STATE: ONE residual branch - the Case-B cut (Kemperman-extremal
menus). T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §135 (2026-08-05) HONEST DOWNGRADE of SS125 after branch (a) dies

With branch (a) eliminated by Dean-Lesniak-Saito, SS125 reduces to:
every minimal counterexample has a CASE-B CUT, i.e. SOME cut with no
mod-4-frozen pair-menu. But menus are generically large and
non-frozen, so such cuts almost certainly exist in any graph =>
BRANCH (b) IS PLAUSIBLY VACUOUS and the Structure Theorem corners
nothing. The earlier phrasing ("one branch from done") is withdrawn.
WHAT SURVIVES: at Case-A cuts no hot cycle crosses (SS122), and hot
cycles now provably exist (DLS) => HOT CYCLES CROSS ONLY CASE-B
CUTS. A real constraint, not a contradiction.
SCOPE NOTE ON SS113: eps_p (parity of cycles crossing at pair p) is
well-defined only when both menus at p are parity-pure; if a menu
has mixed parity, crossing cycles of both parities exist and eps_p
is not a function. The coboundary argument therefore applies exactly
in the parity-pure case - which is the case-split SS125 uses. The
theorem stands; its reach is smaller than stated.
NET AFTER SURVEY - gained: branch (a) dead; hot cycles
unconditional; Markstrom n >= 30 supersedes the internal census;
calibration that k = 8 is the open even-modulus frontier.
NOT gained: any corner on the counterexample.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §136 (2026-08-05) Survey round 2: the expander lever, and the degree-3 wall

RESTATEMENT OF WHAT REMAINS: T(3) <=> every C4-free graph with
min degree >= 3 contains a cycle of length divisible by 8. Minimal
counterexample: cubic, 3-connected, girth >= 5, >= 30 vertices
(Markstrom).
LEVERAGE POINT: FOUR CONSECUTIVE EVEN CYCLE LENGTHS would settle
T(3) instantly (L, L+2, L+4, L+6 with L even cover all four even
residues mod 8, including 0).
IMPORT - MARTINSSON & STEINER, "Cycle lengths modulo k in
expanders" (arXiv:2204.09107): if k > 1 has smallest prime divisor
p, then for alpha > 1/(p-1) every sufficiently large alpha-expanding
graph has cycles of EVERY residue mod k. For k = 8, p = 2, the
threshold is alpha > 1 - live for cubic graphs (which expand up to
alpha ~ 2). CONSEQUENCE: a large minimal counterexample to T(3)
CANNOT be an alpha-expander for alpha > 1; it must contain X with
|X| <= n/2 and |N(X)| <= |X| - a SPARSE CUT. Independent citable
confirmation of the regime SS70 derived by hand.
LIMITS (honest): the cut is sparse, not small - it bounds expansion,
not separator size, so no bounded treewidth follows. And the
Komlos-Szemeredi sublinear-expander paradigm does NOT compose with
Martinsson-Steiner: sublinear expansion is far weaker than
alpha > 1. The two strongest tools do not chain.
THE DEGREE-3 WALL: consecutive-length machinery all needs degree
>> 3 - Liu-Ma need 2k+1 (k=4 => degree 9); Gao-Huo-Liu-Ma need k+1
(degree 3 => only k=2 = Bondy-Vince); Sudakov-Verstraete need
average degree 192(k+1). Nothing delivers four consecutive even
lengths at degree 3.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §137 (2026-08-05) THE SYNTHESIS: three regimes, two closed by literature

Subdividing the residual by structural regime and mapping each onto
the literature:
REGIME 1 (EXPANDING): Martinsson-Steiner 2022 (arXiv:2204.09107) -
for k = 8 (smallest prime divisor 2) every large alpha-expander with
alpha > 1 has cycles of EVERY residue mod 8; cubic graphs can exceed
alpha = 1, so this is live. G0 cannot be such an expander. CLOSED.
REGIME 2 (LARGE TREEWIDTH): Thomassen's subdivided-grid theorem -
every graph of sufficiently large treewidth contains a cycle of
length = 0 (mod k) (the bipartite parity caveat blocks odd residues
only, not residue 0). => tw(G0) <= W(8), explicit. This REPLACES
SS70's hand-derived wall-death with a citable theorem. CLOSED.
REGIME 3 (BOUNDED TREEWIDTH): "cubic, girth >= 5, no cycle = 0 mod
8" is MSO-definable => COURCELLE => the class is recognized by a
finite tree automaton. With Markstrom (n >= 30) and
Dean-Lesniak-Saito (hot cycles unconditional), this is exactly the
regime SS83-84 and the menu/budget theory were built for. OPEN.
NET: T(3) IS DECIDABLE IN PRINCIPLE - regimes 1,2 closed by
published theorems (Dean-Lesniak-Saito 1993, Thomassen 1988,
Martinsson-Steiner 2022), regime 3 a finite automaton-emptiness
question (Courcelle 1990) with Markstrom's computational base.
The pieces genuinely were scattered across five separate papers.
LIMIT (honest): decidable is not decided. The automaton's state
count is non-elementary in the treewidth bound and W(8) is already
exponential in 8, so the check is astronomically infeasible - the
same wall SS83 hit from the other side.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §138 (2026-08-05) HOW THE LITERATURE RESOLVES "DECIDABLE BUT INFEASIBLE"

ANSWER: the unavoidable-set-of-reducible-configurations method
(DISCHARGING). When a problem reduces to checking a bounded-
structure class and the check is astronomical, nobody runs it.
Instead: (1) REDUCIBILITY - local configurations that cannot occur
in a minimal counterexample (surgery gives a smaller member);
(2) UNAVOIDABILITY - a charge-redistribution argument proving every
graph in the class contains one. Assign charges (deg(v) - c plus a
structural term), redistribute locally, show the total is both
invariant and impossible if no configuration appears. Infeasible
global search -> finite local check. This is the Four Colour Theorem
template.
DECISIVE PRECEDENT: Heckman & Krakovski proved EG for 3-CONNECTED
CUBIC PLANAR graphs "employing the Discharging Method in a novel
way", with computer assistance only for small cases - the same
predicament, resolved exactly this way.
DIAGNOSIS OF THIS PROGRAM: it has done only HALF the method.
SS19's Safe-Surgery Lemma, the plug/blob surgeries, menu-replacement
- all REDUCIBILITY. UNAVOIDABILITY was never attempted. That is why
every attack ended in "the configuration survives": configurations
were being killed one at a time instead of proving some member of a
finite set must appear.
THE MISSING INGREDIENT IS A CHARGE. Heckman-Krakovski get theirs
from planarity (Euler / faces). We have no faces - but Thomassen now
gives BOUNDED TREEWIDTH, and a tree decomposition is exactly the
discharging substrate: charge on bags, redistribution along the
decomposition tree, deficiency from girth >= 5 and cubicity.
Modern refinement: AUTOMATIC DISCHARGING (rules found by LP,
e.g. arXiv:2204.05791).
NEXT: build the charge on the tree decomposition and pair it with
the existing reducible surgeries. T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §139 (2026-08-05) The discharging framework built; what it does and does not give

CHARGE (constructed): tree decomposition T of G0 of width <= W0
(Thomassen); charge mu(b) = deg_T(b) - 2 per bag. Then
sum mu = 2|E(T)| - 2|V(T)| = -2: a fixed negative total, no
planarity or Euler needed. Leaves -1, path-bags 0, branch-bags >= 1.
=> LEAF BAGS ARE UNAVOIDABLE, and a leaf bag's private vertices form
a set of size <= W0+1 attached through <= W0 vertices.
UNAVOIDABILITY (proved): G0 contains a bounded piece behind a
bounded separator.
REDUCIBILITY (already in hand, SS18): such a piece is determined by
a finite menu (residues mod 8 per boundary pairing); if it is not
the MINIMUM-SIZE realization of its menu, replacement yields a
smaller counterexample. => every bounded piece in G0 is a
minimum-size realization of its menu.
VERDICT (honest): pairing them makes G0 a tree-like assembly of
irreducible bounded pieces, and splice/pumping then bounds n <= N*.
That is EXACTLY SS83's reduction rediscovered through the discharging
lens - the framework is genuine but reproduces the astronomical
constant, because "minimum realization of its menu" is STATE-BASED
reducibility with exponentially many states.
WHAT REAL DISCHARGING NEEDS: a SMALL set of reducible configurations
- local patterns (a 5-cycle with specified attachment, adjacent
pentagons, a bounded blob shape) each killed by a girth/cubicity/
mod-8 argument - plus rules forcing one to appear. Heckman-Krakovski
have exactly this, with rules drawn from faces. This program has the
charge and the surgeries; it does NOT have the configuration list.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §140 (2026-08-05) STEP BACK: the Erdos-Posa restructuring (better argument)

NEW LEVER (not available earlier): THOMASSEN 1988 Erdos-Posa for
0-mod-m cycles - for every m there is f such that for every k and
every G, either G has k vertex-disjoint cycles = 0 (mod m), or some
X with |X| <= f(k) meets all of them.
Apply with m = 4. In a mod-8-free graph every 0-mod-4 cycle is HOT
(= 4 mod 8). So G0 obeys a dichotomy this program never had:
BRANCH I - k DISJOINT HOT CYCLES for any k. The whole tube programme
(SS8 Tube Cap, SS57 subset-sum/Odd-Octet filling) was built on TWO
disjoint hot cycles; it now runs with unlimited supply. Arithmetic:
threading gives arc-shifts 4 - 2a_i, which are != 0 (mod 8) whenever
a_i != 2 (mod 4), so eight independent threadings fill Z8 and force
a cycle = 0 (mod 8).
BRANCH II - BOUNDED HITTING SET X. Then H = G0 - X has NO cycle
divisible by 4. Literature (arXiv:2507.12798): a 2-connected
n-vertex graph with no 0-mod-4 cycle has <= floor((3n-1)/2) edges,
tight, with extremal families explicitly constructed. Counting:
|E(H)| >= 3n/2 - 3f versus block-wise max (3(n-f) - b)/2 gives
b <= 3f (BOUNDEDLY MANY BLOCKS) and H within 3f/2 edges of extremal.
=> G0 IS A BOUNDED PERTURBATION OF AN EXPLICITLY CHARACTERIZED
EXTREMAL GRAPH: <= f extra vertices on a near-extremal 0-mod-4-free
graph of known structure.
WHY BETTER: earlier routes fought an unstructured residual; both
branches here are structurally concrete - one supplies the exact
object the tube machinery wants, the other pins G0 to a known
family plus bounded noise. Neither is a Kemperman-extremal residue
configuration that absorbs every constraint.
T(3) NOT PROVED - but the architecture is rebuilt on stronger
hypotheses. NEXT: (I) threading/linkage of 8 disjoint hot cycles;
(II) read off the extremal 0-mod-4-free families and check them.

## §141 (2026-08-05) Branch I executed: threading is PARITY-BLOCKED in principle

COMPUTATION: three disjoint hot cycles C1,C2,C3 (Erdos-Posa) and a
cycle threading all three, using arcs a,b,c plus three connecting
paths. Each arc has two choices differing by |C_i| - 2a = 4 - 2a
(mod 8). The eight threading cycles have lengths
L + subset-sums{alpha,beta,gamma}, alpha = 4-2a etc.
ALL THREE SHIFTS ARE EVEN. Hence:
* L odd => every threading cycle is odd, none can be = 0 (mod 8):
  no contradiction;
* L even => subset-sums must avoid -L inside {0,2,4,6}; three shifts
  = 2 (mod 4) would generate all four even residues and force a
  cycle = 0 (mod 8). So every shift must be = 0 or 4 (mod 8), i.e.
  every attachment arc on every hot cycle is EVEN.
RESULT: either all threading cycles are odd, or all attachment
points on every hot cycle lie in ONE CLASS of its alternating
2-colouring.
SIGNIFICANCE: that second alternative is EXACTLY the
class-homogeneity configuration that absorbed SS99-103, SS119's
extremality and the Hot-Crossing analysis. The Erdos-Posa
restructuring gives strictly stronger hypotheses (unlimited disjoint
hot cycles) and reproduces the SAME obstruction from an independent
direction => the obstruction is NOT an artifact of the route.
ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED: parity. Hot cycles are even, so arc-swaps
generate only EVEN shifts, and even shifts can never reach 0 (mod 8)
from an odd base. ANY argument built on hot-cycle arc-swapping is
parity-blocked in principle. To break it one needs ODD-length
structures (odd cycles) interacting with the hot cycles - the
Branch II / non-bipartite side.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §142 (2026-08-05) Following the parity diagnosis: the 2-factor/Kempe handle

If G0 is BIPARTITE then (Konig) it is 3-edge-colourable:
G0 = M1 u M2 u M3, giving three 2-factors M_i u M_j, each a disjoint
union of even cycles partitioning all n vertices, EVERY cycle of
which must avoid = 0 (mod 8).
WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT: it produces cycles in BULK with a GLOBAL
constraint (sum of lengths = n per 2-factor) instead of the local
residue laws that kept saturating. KEMPE SWITCHING on any 2-factor
cycle yields a new 3-edge-colouring, hence new 2-factors and new
cycles - so the family of cycles under the mod-8 restriction is
large and richly connected.
WHY HERE: SS141 showed the obstruction is PARITY (hot cycles even =>
arc-swaps give even shifts => cannot reach 0 mod 8 from an odd
base). The 2-factor/Kempe structure sidesteps that: it re-partitions
the edge set, changing WHICH cycles exist rather than shifting one
cycle's length.
HONEST LIMITS: non-bipartite cubic graphs need not be
3-edge-colourable (snarks), so this handle covers only the bipartite
case; and sum of lengths = n with each length != 0 (mod 8) is
satisfiable on its face - no contradiction derived.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §143 (2026-08-05) FORCING FROM KNOWN-GOOD SUBCASES

Every subcase where T(3)/EG is KNOWN forces structure on G0:
* 3-connected cubic PLANAR (Heckman-Krakovski) => G0 NON-PLANAR
* P13-free (Hu-Shen et al.) => G0 has an INDUCED P13
* diameter 2 => diameter(G0) >= 3
* alpha-expanding, alpha > 1 (Martinsson-Steiner) => sparse cut
* large treewidth (Thomassen) => tw(G0) <= W0
* n <= 30 (Markstrom) => n >= 30
* no 0-mod-4 cycle (Dean-Lesniak-Saito) => HOT CYCLES EXIST
* sunflower (SS16) => TWO DISJOINT HOT CYCLES EXIST
SHARPEST CONSEQUENCE: non-planarity + Kuratowski, and K5 needs
degree-4 branch vertices, so a CUBIC graph can only contain a
K3,3-SUBDIVISION => G0 CONTAINS A SUBDIVIDED K3,3 with nine branch
paths p_ij; its nine 2x2 rectangle sums (4-cycles) and six
S - perm sums (6-cycles) must all be != 0 (mod 8) and >= 5.
This lands on the SS7 K3,3 machinery - now FORCED, not assumed.
HONEST CHECK: that CSP alone is NOT contradictory. All p_ij = 5
gives 4-cycles of length 20 (= 4, hot) and 6-cycles of length 30
(= 6), all legal with girth 20. So non-planarity by itself does not
close it; the subdivision's degree-2 vertices need third edges, and
any contradiction must come from that extra structure.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §144 (2026-08-05) Naming the residual: PUMPABLE CUBIC CHAIN; closing attempt

NAMING: G0 has bounded treewidth (Thomassen), so candidates form a
REGULAR TREE LANGUAGE (bounded-width HR grammar; "no cycle = 0 mod
8" is MSO, Courcelle). Such a language is FINITE or PUMPABLE =>
either T(3)-counterexamples are finitely many sporadic graphs with
30 <= n <= N*, or there is an INFINITE PUMPABLE FAMILY - a repeating
unit spliced arbitrarily often. The object is a PUMPABLE CUBIC CHAIN.
CLOSING ARGUMENT FOR THE PUMPABLE CASE (three ingredients):
(1) JACKSON: a 3-connected cubic graph has circumference >= n^0.8,
so G0 carries a cycle traversing MANY repeated units.
(2) REROUTING: if a unit's through-menu has two routes differing by
delta != 0 (mod 4), the long cycle can be rerouted there, shifting
its length by delta.
(3) SUBSET-SUM FILLING (SS57 Odd-Octet / SS90): eight DISJOINT units
each offering such a delta give subset-sums covering Z8, forcing a
cycle = 0 (mod 8): CONTRADICTION.
Ingredient (2) is owned: SS109/SS111's arc-parity kill (via Tutte's
peripheral-cycle theorem) proves NO CUT SIDE IS MOD-4-FROZEN, so
every unit has two routes differing by != 0 (mod 4); units are
disjoint sections so the choices are independent.
THE ONE GAP (named precisely): SS111 gives a non-frozen menu AT SOME
PAIR of each unit's terminals, not necessarily at the pair the long
cycle uses. This is the PAIR-MATCHING obstruction in its sharpest
form: the long cycle must enter and leave each unit through a rich
pair. SS124's Shift-Covering says a terminal's two menus JOINTLY
cover a parity class - close, but "jointly" is not "at the pair the
cycle uses".
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §145 (2026-08-05) At most one pair per unit is frozen; the gap quantified

PROVED: for a unit U with terminals a,b,c, SS111 (contraction +
Tutte) says both menus at a terminal cannot be mod-4-frozen. So at
a, at most one of M_ab, M_ac is frozen; likewise at b and c. If M_ab
were frozen, a's condition forces M_ac rich and b's forces M_bc
rich. => EVERY UNIT HAS >= 2 RICH PAIRS; AT MOST ONE OF ITS THREE
PAIRS IS FROZEN.
"Rich" is genuine: SS124's Shift-Covering says a terminal's two
menus jointly cover a full parity class, and every parity class
contains values != 0 (mod 4) (e.g. 2, 6 among the evens), so a rich
pair supplies a reroute with shift != 0 (mod 4).
Menus are fuller than they look: M_ab includes EVERY a-b path in U,
including those detouring through c, so "frozen" is strong.
THE GAP, QUANTIFIED: the long cycle (Jackson, >= n^0.8) crosses each
unit's 3-cut exactly twice, so uses exactly one pair per unit. The
argument closes if it uses a RICH pair at eight disjoint units.
Since only one pair in three is ever frozen, this fails only if the
cycle systematically selects the single frozen pair at all but seven
units - a strong coincidence I cannot exclude.
WHY REROUTING FAILS: at a frozen-pair unit the third cut edge is
off-cycle, so switching pairs changes the cycle GLOBALLY and the
length difference involves the uncontrolled exterior rather than a
clean local shift.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §146 (2026-08-05) THE EIGHT EARS LEMMA IS A SOLVED PROBLEM: CGGGLS import

IDENTIFICATION (exact, not analogy): ears of C are A-PATHS for
A = V(C). Label every edge 1 in Z4 and each C-edge by its position
increment; an ear spanning an arc then has weight
|ear| - |arc| (mod 4), so NON-ZERO WEIGHT = UNBALANCED EAR.
THEOREM (Chudnovsky, Geelen, Gerards, Goddyn, Lohman, Seymour,
Combinatorica 26 (2006) 521-532): in a group-labelled graph, for
every k either there are k vertex-disjoint non-zero A-paths, or a
set of AT MOST 2k-2 VERTICES meets all non-zero A-paths.
APPLY WITH k = 8: either eight vertex-disjoint unbalanced ears - and
T(3) follows by subset-sum filling (SS57 Odd-Octet) - or a set X of
AT MOST 14 VERTICES meets every unbalanced ear. An explicit tiny
constant, not an unspecified f(8).
SECOND BRANCH IS RIGID: if every ear avoiding X is balanced, the
position function phi: V(C) -> Z4 extends along every ear, giving
G0 - X a Z4-GRADING: an orientation where every edge goes from level
phi to phi+1, i.e. a FOUR-LAYER CIRCULAR STRUCTURE L0..L3 with edges
only between consecutive layers. Consequences: G0 - X is bipartite;
every odd cycle of G0 meets <= 14 vertices; every monotone cycle has
length = 0 (mod 4) hence = 4 (mod 8); girth >= 5 forbids the short
winding (length 4) and bouncing (length 4) cycles.
WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT IMPORT: CGGGLS is a MIN-MAX theorem, so it
converts "I cannot find eight disjoint good ears" into "then there
is a tiny obstruction set" - no linkage argument needed, which is
exactly where every previous attempt died.
REMAINING: kill the <= 14-vertex hitting-set branch (the Z4-graded
four-layer structure). T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §147 (2026-08-05) The Z4-graded residual, fully specified

G0 - X (|X| <= 14) has levels L0..L3, every edge between consecutive
levels. For a cycle with f forward, b backward edges the grading
forces f - b = 0 (mod 4), hence LENGTH = 2b (mod 4). Consequences:
* b EVEN => length = 0 (mod 4) => (mod-8-free) length = 4 (mod 8):
  every such cycle is HOT; in particular the long cycle C (b = 0).
* G0 - X is BIPARTITE, so with C4-freeness girth >= 6; and GIRTH
  != 8, since a girth-8 graph contains an 8-cycle. Girth is in
  {6, 10, 12, 14, ...}.
* NO 8-CYCLES AT ALL: the natural short graded cycles (f,b) =
  (4,4), (6,2), (8,0) all have length 8 and are banned - a strong
  exclusion, as these are what a layered cubic structure most
  readily produces.
* Two monotone cycles meeting in a single path must share a path
  whose ENDPOINTS LIE ON DIFFERENT LEVELS (else their symmetric
  difference is = 0 mod 8).
LITERATURE CHECKED, DOES NOT CLOSE IT: Bondy-Simonovits (C_2k-free
=> O(n^(1+1/k)) edges) gives O(n^(5/4)) for C8-free, but G0 - X has
only ~3n/2 edges - VACUOUS AT CUBIC DENSITY; the same holds for the
other even-cycle extremal results, which bite only for dense graphs.
EG is NOT known for bipartite graphs (only the experimental study of
Salehi Nowbandegani & Esfandiari), so the forced near-bipartiteness
yields no citable win.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §148 (2026-08-05) SYNTHESIS ON THE GRADED OBJECT: winding parity forces a Z8-grading

PIECE 1 (grading): a MONOTONE cycle (all edges forward) has b = 0,
so length = 0 (mod 4): length = 4m with m its WINDING NUMBER around
the four levels.
PIECE 2 (mod-8-freeness): that length must be = 4 (mod 8), so
4m = 4 (mod 8) => EVERY MONOTONE CYCLE WINDS AN ODD NUMBER OF TIMES.
PIECE 3 (composition): if P1, P2 are monotone u->v paths completing
cycles, oddness of both windings forces w(P1) = w(P2) (mod 2), so
WINDING PARITY IS AN INVARIANT OF THE ENDPOINT PAIR - a Z2-valued
potential psi on top of the Z4-level phi.
PUNCHLINE: (phi, psi) assemble into a single Z8-GRADING, with
length(P) = (phi(v) - phi(u)) + 4 psi (mod 8). But a Z8-grading
makes every monotone cycle have length = 0 (mod 8) - FORBIDDEN. The
long cycle C is monotone, so this is an outright CONTRADICTION.
REMAINING ESCAPE: the argument closes provided psi is GLOBALLY
CONSISTENT, which needs monotone paths joining the relevant
vertices. So the surviving case is: the monotone (directed)
structure of G0 - X is DISCONNECTED, and the contradiction applies
only within each monotone-connected piece. That is a CONNECTIVITY
question about an orientation, not a residue question - far narrower
than anything the residue machinery left.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §149 (2026-08-05) RETRACTION of SS148; salvage: MONOTONE RIGIDITY

RETRACTED (13th): SS148's Z8-grading does NOT follow. Winding parity
psi cannot be a vertex potential: going once around the long cycle C
the winding increases by m, which is ODD, so psi has monodromy 1
around C and is globally inconsistent BY CONSTRUCTION. The very fact
that made Piece 2 work (odd winding) blocks Piece 3 from
globalizing. Equivalently, if Phi = phi + 4 psi existed then
|C| = 0 (mod 8), but |C| = 4 - so Phi does not exist. No
contradiction.
SALVAGE (correct, and clean) - MONOTONE RIGIDITY: in the graded
structure, any two MONOTONE paths with the same endpoints have
lengths CONGRUENT MOD 8. Proof: both have the same level-difference
delta, so lengths are delta + 4w and delta + 4w'; completing each
with a common monotone return path gives monotone cycles, whose
windings are odd by mod-8-freeness, forcing w = w' (mod 2); hence
the lengths differ by 4(w - w') = 0 (mod 8). QED
So the monotone structure of G0 - X is MOD-8-FROZEN: every directed
u->v route has one and the same residue. This is the "frozen"
species killed repeatedly in this program - but always for ALL
paths, never for a DIRECTED sub-structure, so SS109's arc-parity
kill does not apply as it stands.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §150 (2026-08-05) The directed/undirected tension examined; why it does not yet close

SHARED-PATH CONSTRAINT: two monotone cycles meeting in a single path
of length s have symmetric difference of length |Z1|+|Z2|-2s =
-2s (mod 8), so s != 0 (mod 4); since a monotone path's length is
= delta (its endpoints' level-difference), TWO MONOTONE CYCLES MAY
ONLY SHARE PATHS WHOSE ENDPOINTS LIE ON DIFFERENT LEVELS - never a
path completing a full winding.
ODD-WINDING RIGIDITY: every directed cycle has odd winding, so two
directed cycles can never merge into a single directed cycle
(winding w1+w2 would be even). At a shared vertex the union is
Eulerian but yields only a closed WALK, not a simple cycle - checked,
which is why no contradiction falls out there.
WHY THE TENSION DOES NOT CLOSE: SS109's kill produces two undirected
paths differing mod 4, and those necessarily use BACKWARD edges,
since the monotone ones are all congruent (SS149). A path with b
backward edges has length = delta + 4k + 2b (mod 8), so the
non-frozenness is supplied entirely by the 2b term. Frozen directed
skeleton and non-frozen undirected graph COEXIST consistently,
because backward edges carry all the variation.
RESIDUAL: cubic bipartite Z4-graded graph; no 8-cycles; girth >= 6,
!= 8; all directed cycles odd-winding with length = 4 (mod 8);
directed paths mod-8-frozen; undirected paths not mod-4-frozen;
monotone cycles share only different-level paths.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §151 (2026-08-05) EXOTIC IMPORT: Ihara zeta / non-backtracking spectrum

REFRAMING: in girth >= 6, every closed NON-BACKTRACKING walk of
length 8 is a simple 8-cycle (two shorter cycles need >= 12 edges),
so with T the Hashimoto operator: tr(T^8) = 16 c_8 = 0.
BASS-IHARA: spec(T) = {lambda: lambda^2 - a lambda + 2 = 0,
a in spec(A)} u {+-1}^(n/2), giving the exact identity
tr(A^8) - 16 tr(A^6) + 80 tr(A^4) - 128 tr(A^2) + 33n = 16 c_8.
VERIFIED on the HEAWOOD graph (n=14, spectrum +-3, +-sqrt2^(6)):
the formula returns 16c_8 = 336, i.e. c_8 = 21 - the correct count.
The machinery is sound.
CONSEQUENCE: with c_8 = 0 and girth >= 6 (tr A^2 = 3n, tr A^4 = 15n,
tr A^6 = 87n + 12 c_6), the n-terms cancel identically and the
identity fixes tr(A^8) = 543n + 192 c_6. Spectrally: eigenvalues a
with |a| < 2 sqrt 2 give T-eigenvalues of modulus sqrt2 at angle
theta contributing 32 cos(8 theta), so MOD-8-FREENESS <=> CHEBYSHEV
MOMENT IDENTITIES on the adjacency spectrum. The Perron eigenvalue
alone contributes 2^8 + 1 = 257, so the complex part must supply
<= -(257+n)/32 while |sum cos 8theta| <= n/2, forcing n >= 18 from
pure spectral reasoning (weaker than Markstrom's 30, but derived
independently). This is only the FIRST condition: forbidding 16-,
24-, ...-cycles gives an INFINITE FAMILY of Chebyshev moment
constraints.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §152 (2026-08-05) Directing the spectral tools: exact formula, dichotomy, bound

(1) EXACT FORMULA: for a cubic graph of girth >= 6 with NO 8-CYCLES
the Bass-Ihara identity collapses (n-terms cancel identically) to
    tr(A^8) = 543 n + 192 c_6.
The eighth spectral moment is completely determined by n and the
hexagon count. Cross-check: Heawood (which HAS 8-cycles) returns
c_8 = 21 from the same identity - correct.
(2) GIRTH DICHOTOMY: our graph is bipartite with girth != 8, so
GIRTH IS 6 OR >= 10. In either case, with l0 the least multiple of 8
that is >= g, we have l0 < 2g, so every closed non-backtracking walk
of length l0 is a simple l0-cycle and mod-8-freeness gives
    tr(T^{l0}) = 0   (a VANISHING NON-BACKTRACKING MOMENT).
(3) WHAT VANISHING FORCES: T has Perron eigenvalue 2 contributing
2^{l0}, while all non-real T-eigenvalues have modulus exactly
sqrt 2; cancellation needs 3n * 2^{l0/2} >= 2^{l0}, i.e.
    n >= 2^{g/2}/3.
HONEST ASSESSMENT: that is essentially the MOORE BOUND - the
spectral route recovers it rather than beating it; the first moment
identity alone gives only n >= 19 (weaker than Markstrom's 30). The
genuinely new content is the exact hexagon formula and the
VANISHING-MOMENT FRAMING: mod-8-freeness becomes a statement that
specific GLOBAL spectral moments vanish, a constraint no local
rearrangement can satisfy - unlike every configuration-level tool
the obstruction previously absorbed.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §153 (2026-08-05) REVERSE-ENGINEERING: T(3) as an extremal edge bound

IF T(3) IS TRUE, the proof must show the class
F = {C4-free graphs with no cycle = 0 (mod 8)} has NO CUBIC MEMBER.
Since a cubic graph has exactly 3n/2 edges, the route is an
EXTREMAL BOUND:
  TARGET: every 2-connected G in F has |E(G)| <= floor((3n-1)/2).
That is strictly below 3n/2, forcing a vertex of degree <= 2 and
killing cubic members outright.
THIS IS HOW THE NEIGHBOURING CASES WERE PROVED: Chen-Saito (k=3)
shows graphs with no cycle divisible by 3 are 2-DEGENERATE;
Dean-Lesniak-Saito (k=4) IS this edge bound, <= floor((3n-1)/2) for
2-connected graphs, tight, with characterized extremal families.
The template is already written; only the modulus differs.
BRIDGE TO OUR WORK - our results are exactly the lemmas such an
induction consumes:
* INDUCTION SUBSTRATE: the SPQR/2-cut machinery (SS9-10), Universal
  2-Cut Law System, terminal trichotomy.
* THE POTENTIAL (the missing ingredient): replace residue menus by an
  EDGE-COUNT potential phi(H) = |E(H)| - (3|V(H)|-1)/2, shown
  subadditive across cuts. Every menu we ever tracked was
  residue-valued, never edge-counting - this is the gap.
* REDUCIBLE PIECES: SS18 menu-replacement surgery, SS131 Minimal Blob
  Theorem (minimal blob = a single edge), SS127 bridge laws.
* BASE CASES: Markstrom n >= 30; SS128 (m=6) and SS132 analyses.
* COUNTING IDENTITIES: SS152's tr(A^8) = 543n + 192 c_6 gives an
  exact hexagon count for exactly this class.
HONEST ASYMMETRY: mod-8-freeness is WEAKER than mod-4-freeness, so F
is larger and the bound is harder - the C4-free hypothesis must do
the work the stronger modulus did for DLS. That is why the target is
not a corollary of their theorem, and where the difficulty sits.
T(3) NOT PROVED.

## §154 (2026-08-05) DIAGNOSIS: why every route hits the same wall

FIVE WALL-SHAPES, ALL ONE WALL:
1. RESIDUE-LOCAL SYSTEMS SATURATE. SS119: the surviving
   configuration meets every budget with EQUALITY; SS123 exhibits
   explicit consistent data (M^A={0,1,2,3}, M^B={7,0,1,2}). Finitely
   many constraints on subsets of Z8 are satisfiable unless
   something forces scarcity; a local structure sees only finitely
   many cycles.
2. PARITY BLOCKS ARC-SWAPPING (SS141). Hot cycles are even, so
   arc-swaps shift lengths by even amounts, and even shifts never
   reach 0 (mod 8) from an odd base. Any single-cycle rerouting
   argument is dead before it starts.
3. SIMULTANEITY NEEDS CONNECTIVITY WE LACK. Every "k independent
   local modifications on ONE cycle" demand (8 ears, 8 units, 6
   movers) needs k-linkage; cubic graphs are only 3-connected.
   CGGGLS removed this once by min-max; it reappeared as a hitting
   set.
4. FROZEN STRUCTURES REGENERATE. Class-homogeneity, H-periodicity,
   mod-4-frozen menus, the Z4-grading, monotone rigidity - all the
   same object: A POTENTIAL FUNCTION. Kill one, a weaker or directed
   version returns.
5. DECIDABLE BUT INFEASIBLE (SS83-84, SS137): non-elementary
   automaton constants.
THE SINGLE UNDERLYING REASON: mod-8-freeness says the length
function wants to be a Z8-COBOUNDARY (a grading). A counterexample
is a graph that is ALMOST GRADABLE - gradable enough that every
local test passes, not gradable enough to be trivially impossible.
ALL OUR TOOLS DETECT EXACT COBOUNDARIES; NONE DETECTS NEAR-
COBOUNDARIES. The frozen/graded object is the fixed point of the
whole method, which is why it reappears at every level.
NOT AN ARTIFACT: every abundance theorem in the literature needs
degree above 3 - Liu-Ma 2k+1 (degree 9 for four consecutive even
lengths); Gao-Huo-Liu-Ma k+1 (degree 3 gives only Bondy-Vince's
two); Sudakov-Verstraete average degree 192(k+1);
Martinsson-Steiner expansion alpha > 1; Thomassen 4k-1. MINIMUM
DEGREE 3 IS EXACTLY THE THRESHOLD WHERE CYCLE-SPACE RICHNESS STOPS
FORCING RESIDUE COVERAGE. And a T(3)-counterexample IS an
EG-counterexample, so the task inherits a 1976 conjecture's
difficulty in the C4-free sector. T(3) NOT PROVED.

## 155. THE DEGREE FILTRATION: the right algebraic frame (DERIVED + IMPORTED)

STATUS: T(3) and Erdos-Gyarfas remain UNPROVED. This section reframes, it does
not close.

### 155.1 The identity (PROVED, elementary)

For subsets A_1..A_k of a finite set, with A_T = intersection over i in T:

    |symdiff_{i in S} A_i| = sum_{T subset S, T nonempty} (-2)^{|T|-1} |A_T|.

Proof: fix an element e with multiplicity n = #{i in S : e in A_i}. Its
contribution to the RHS is sum_{k=1..n} C(n,k)(-2)^{k-1}
= (-1/2)[(1-2)^n - 1] = (-1/2)[(-1)^n - 1], which is 1 if n odd, 0 if n even.
That is exactly its contribution to the LHS. QED

### 155.2 The filtration (DERIVED - new framing for this program)

Apply 155.1 to a basis B_1..B_r of the cycle space Z(G) over F_2, with
x = sum_{i in S} B_i:

  mod 2 : |x| = sum_i |B_i|                                  LINEAR
  mod 4 : |x| = sum_i |B_i| - 2 sum_{i<j} |B_i ^ B_j|        QUADRATIC
  mod 8 : the above + 4 sum_{i<j<k} |B_i ^ B_j ^ B_k|        CUBIC
  mod 16: the above - 8 sum over 4-subsets                   QUARTIC

because (-2)^{m-1} is divisible by 2^k once m > k. So:

  LENGTH MOD 2^k IS A POLYNOMIAL FUNCTION OF DEGREE k-1 ON THE CYCLE SPACE.

This is the exact algebraic content of the Tower. Level k of Erdos-Gyarfas is
the degree-(k-1) layer of one filtration:

  - degree 1 (mod 2): linear functional. Trivial.
  - degree 2 (mod 4): quadratic. This is DEAN-LESNIAK-SAITO 1993 (every
    3-connected graph has a cycle of length 0 mod 4) - proved, unconditional.
  - degree 3 (mod 8): cubic. OPEN. This is T(3).

So the wall is not accidental: mod 8 is the FIRST layer beyond quadratic, and
quadratic forms over F_2 have a complete classical theory (Arf/Brown, Gauss
sums) while cubic forms do not.

### 155.3 The mod-4 layer is classical and complete (IMPORTED)

On Z(G) put b(x,y) = |x ^ y| mod 2 (the F_2 intersection pairing) and
q(x) = |x| mod 4. Then 155.2 says

    q(x+y) = q(x) + q(y) + 2 b(x,y)   in Z_4,

i.e. q is a Z_4-valued QUADRATIC REFINEMENT of b in the sense of E. H. Brown
(Generalizations of the Arf invariant, Ann. of Math. 1972). Consequences, all
classical:

 (i)  rad(b) = Z ^ Z-perp = Z ^ B = the BICYCLE SPACE of G.
 (ii) Brown's invariant beta(G) in Z_8 is defined by the Gauss sum
      sum_{x in Z} i^{|x|} = 2^{(dim Z)/2} * zeta_8^{beta}.
 (iii) By Greene's theorem this same sum is a Tutte evaluation: with x=1, y=i,
      (x+y)/(x-y) = i and x/y = -i, so the Gauss sum equals
      i^{m-n+c} (1-i)^{n-c} T(i,-i).
 (iv) Vertigan (Bicycle dimension and special points of the Tutte polynomial,
      JCTB 1998) evaluates T at (i,-i) in terms of bicycle dimension, in
      polynomial time.

So the entire mod-4 distribution of cycle-space lengths is controlled by the
bicycle space. That is why the mod-4 theorem (DLS) exists and is provable.
There is NO analogous special point for mod 8: by 155.2 that layer is cubic,
and cubic phases have no closed-form Gauss sum. This is a structural, not
tactical, explanation of the wall diagnosed in section 154.

### 155.4 THE MAC LANE DICHOTOMY (DERIVED - new)

The cubic term in 155.2 is 4 * sum_{i<j<k} |B_i ^ B_j ^ B_k|. It vanishes
identically as soon as no edge lies in three basis cycles.

MAC LANE'S PLANARITY CRITERION: G is planar iff Z(G) has a 2-basis (every edge
in at most two basis cycles).

Hence:

  THEOREM (planar quadratic reduction). If G is planar, take a 2-basis
  (e.g. all but one face of a plane embedding). Then for every x in Z(G),
      |x| = sum_{i in S} |B_i| - 2 sum_{i<j in S} |B_i ^ B_j|
  EXACTLY (not merely mod 8). Length is an honest quadratic form on the
  cycle space.

This explains in one line why HECKMAN-KRAKOVSKI could prove EG for 3-connected
cubic planar graphs by discharging while the general case resists: for planar
graphs the mod-8 problem is only quadratic. NONPLANARITY IS THE CUBIC DEFECT.

Sharper form of the vanishing condition: the cubic term dies iff every triple
of basis cycles shares an EVEN number of edges. Call such a basis an
EVEN-TRIPLE BASIS; Mac Lane's 2-basis is the special case "zero edges". So:

  OPEN SUB-QUESTION (well-posed, apparently not in the literature):
  which graphs admit an even-triple cycle basis? Any graph in that class has
  length-mod-8 quadratic and inherits the whole Arf/Brown apparatus. If the
  class strictly contains the planar graphs, T(3) would follow on a strictly
  larger class than Heckman-Krakovski reach.

### 155.5 The face subspace and the Ising connection (DERIVED + IMPORTED)

For any cellular embedding of G in a surface of genus g, Euler gives
f = dim Z + 1 - 2g, so the face boundaries span a subspace F of Z of
CODIMENSION 2g. Each edge lies in exactly two faces, so on F length is exactly
quadratic. Moreover, for a set S of faces the corresponding element of Z is the
boundary of the region, so

    |x_S| = |delta_{G*}(S)|,

the cut function of the DUAL graph. Two consequences:

 (a) Length on the face subspace is a cut function, hence SUBMODULAR. None of
     our residue menus ever had submodularity available.
 (b) The mod-8 counting function on F is
        sum_{S subset F(G)} zeta_8^{|delta_{G*}(S)|},
     which is exactly the ISING PARTITION FUNCTION of G* at a complex coupling
     (van der Waerden / Kac-Ward expansion). For planar G this is evaluated
     exactly by KASTELEYN's Pfaffian method; for genus g by the
     Galluccio-Loebl / Tesler 4^g-Pfaffian sum.

So mod-8 statistics of face-region boundary lengths are exactly computable in
bounded genus. Regions that are discs have CYCLE boundaries, so this is not
vacuous. Honest limit: it counts all regions, most of whose boundaries are
disconnected.

### 155.6 What category theory gives here: mostly NO-GO (honest)

 (1) Plain cohomology is VACUOUS. A graph is a 1-complex; H^1(G;Z_8) is free and
     every Z_8-cochain is a coboundary on a spanning tree. There is no torsion
     obstruction to find. The obstruction lives in the QUADRATIC structure on
     the cycle space, not in H^1. That is exactly why section 154's
     "near-coboundary" diagnosis was right and why no cohomological tool bit.
 (2) Homomorphism duality does not apply. Hedetniemi / Pultr adjoints / CSP
     dualities need the target property closed under homomorphisms. Cycle
     EXISTENCE is not: homomorphisms do not preserve cycles. EG is a subgraph
     problem, not a CSP. This kills the categorical-graph-theory toolkit here.
 (3) The RECIPE THEOREM (Brylawski; Oxley-Welsh) does apply, as a no-go: any
     invariant obeying the deletion-contraction recursion is a Tutte
     specialization. Our W-class / menu calculus was exactly deletion-closed
     bookkeeping. By 155.3 the only mod-power-of-2 information Tutte carries
     sits at (i,-i), i.e. mod 4. THIS IS WHY THE MENU CALCULUS SATURATED at
     mod 8 (sections 119, 123). It could not have succeeded.
 (4) Where algebra does pay: Brown's classification (the Witt group of
     Z_4-valued quadratic forms is Z_8) is the complete invariant of the
     quadratic layer; and Courcelle / Myhill-Nerode for graph algebras is the
     bounded-treewidth regime already recorded in section 138.

### 155.7 The single remaining obstacle in this frame

Everything above is about the CYCLE SPACE Z(G). Mod-8-freeness is a statement
about CYCLES = the CONNECTED elements of Z(G). All the algebra (Gauss sums,
Arf/Brown, Ising/Pfaffian, submodularity) is blind to connectivity, and
connected elements are an exponentially sparse subset.

This replaces the five-faced wall of section 154 with ONE well-posed question:

  CONNECTIVITY FILTER PROBLEM: control the distribution of |x| mod 8 over the
  CONNECTED elements of Z(G), given exact control over all of Z(G).

That is a cleaner target than anything in sections 100-154, and it is the honest
statement of what is missing. Two partial handles already in hand:

 - K_4 is the unique graph all of whose 7 nonzero cycle-space elements are
   cycles; Dirac gives a K_4-subdivision in every min-degree-3 graph; on it all
   triple intersections are empty, so length mod 8 is exactly quadratic there
   (consistent with 155.4, K_4 being planar). CHECKED: the 7 resulting
   constraints in 6 variables over Z_8 are satisfiable (all branch lengths 1
   gives triangles 3, quadrilaterals 4), so one K_4-subdivision alone is not
   enough - matching every previous saturation.
 - Tutte's peripheral cycles are connected and span Z(G) for 3-connected G, so
   they are the natural place to look for a connected-element-rich subspace.

STATUS RESTATED: T(3) UNPROVED. Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 155 contributes
a frame, two derived structural theorems (155.2 degree filtration, 155.4 Mac
Lane dichotomy), three literature identifications (Brown; Greene/Vertigan;
Kasteleyn/Tesler), one no-go explaining a past failure (155.6.3), and one
sharpened open problem (155.7).


## 156. THE EDGE-COUNTING POTENTIAL: import, derivation, and a CORRECTION to 153

STATUS: T(3) and Erdos-Gyarfas remain UNPROVED.

### 156.1 IMPORT (fresh, July 2025)

Hojin Chu et al., "On 2-connected graphs avoiding cycles of length 0 modulo 4",
arXiv:2507.12798 (July 2025). Main theorem:

  A 2-connected n-vertex graph with no cycle of length 0 mod 4 has at most
  floor((3n-1)/2) edges, and the bound is tight (infinitely many extremal
  examples, built by parallel sums of small gadgets F_4,F_6,F_7,F_8,F_9).

This is EXACTLY the bound that section 153 reverse-engineered as the target,
at the mod-4 level. Their method, from the paper: decomposition along
2-VERTEX CUTS; classification of rooted pieces by "L-types" = the set of
residues of x-y paths; local edge-density accounting per type; small-case
base bounds for n <= 9.

The L-types ARE our MENUS. The paper independently validates the menu
framework and shows what our version was missing: a menu must carry an EDGE
BUDGET, not merely a residue exclusion. That is precisely the diagnosis of
section 153.

### 156.2 The potential and its exact composition rules (DERIVED, new)

For a rooted piece (H,x,y) set

    c(H) := 2|E(H)| - 3|V(H)|      (= 2 * phi(H), phi = e - 3n/2)
    L(H) := { |P| mod 8 : P an x-y path in H }.

PARALLEL SUM (glue at both x and y): n = n1+n2-2, e = e1+e2. Cycles are the
cycles of each part plus P1 u P2, so H is mod-8-free iff both parts are and
(L1 + L2) does not contain 0. Menu of the sum: L = L1 u L2. Potential:

    c = c1 + c2 + 6.

SERIES SUM (identify y1 = x2): n = n1+n2-1, e = e1+e2, no new cycles,
menu L = L1 + L2 (sumset). Potential:

    c = c1 + c2 + 3.

Define the CAPACITY  cap(L) := sup{ c(H) : H 2-connected rooted, mod-8-free,
L(H) = L }. Then the two rules read

    cap(L1) + cap(L2) + 6 <= cap(L1 u L2)   whenever (L1+L2) does not meet 0,
    cap(L1) + cap(L2) + 3 <= cap(L1 + L2).

TARGET RESTATED: every 2-connected mod-8-free G has 2|E| <= 3|V| - 1, i.e.
c(G) <= -1. If G has a 2-cut then c(G) = c1 + c2 + 6, so the target for the
reducible case is exactly

    (*)  cap(L1) + cap(L2) <= -7   for every complementary menu pair.

Note (*) is the quantitative form of MENU COMPLEMENTARITY (|L1| + |L2| <= 8):
complementarity says the menus cannot both be large; (*) says the PIECES
cannot both be dense.

### 156.3 CORRECTION TO SECTION 153 (14th correction; important)

Section 153 named the edge-counting potential phi(H) = |E(H)| - (3|V(H)|-1)/2
as "the missing ingredient" and the bound |E| <= floor((3n-1)/2) as the route
to T(3). That is WRONG AS A ROUTE, for a reason now visible:

The 2-cut induction in 156.2 bottoms out at 3-CONNECTED graphs, which have no
2-cut. But every 3-connected graph has minimum degree 3, hence
2|E| >= 3|V| > 3|V| - 1. So the base case of the induction is precisely the
statement

    NO 3-CONNECTED GRAPH IS MOD-8-FREE,

which is T(3) itself (the minimal counterexample is 3-connected, section 1).
At mod 4 the same base case is DEAN-LESNIAK-SAITO 1993, which the 2025 paper
uses as INPUT. So the edge-counting potential is reduction machinery that
PROPAGATES the 3-connected theorem outward to all 2-connected graphs. It
cannot produce the 3-connected theorem.

CONSEQUENCE: the reverse-engineering of section 153 identified a correct
equivalence but an unusable direction. The extremal bound and T(3) are
equivalent, and the 2-cut route runs from T(3) to the bound, not back.
Section 153's "TARGET" line is hereby downgraded from route to corollary.

### 156.4 Why every candidate "one simple fact" is circular (DERIVED)

Test case, the natural ear statement. Let C be a cycle with |C| = 4 mod 8
(one exists by DLS + mod-8-freeness). Let P be an ear of C: a path with both
ends on C, internally disjoint from C, splitting C into arcs alpha, beta with
alpha + beta = |C|. The two new cycles have lengths |P|+alpha and |P|+beta.

  HINGE FACT (candidate): some ear has |P| = alpha + 4 (mod 8).

It demolishes: |P| + beta = alpha + 4 + (4 - alpha) = 8 = 0 mod 8. But
beta = |C| - alpha = 4 - alpha, so alpha + 4 = -beta (mod 8). Hence the Hinge
Fact says exactly "some ear takes one of the two residues that mod-8-freeness
forbids". It is a restatement, not a lemma.

This is general: any fact that demolishes the obstruction is logically
equivalent to T(3), because T(3) is what is being asserted. "Simple" therefore
cannot mean "logically weaker". It must mean AN EQUIVALENT FORM PROVABLE BY A
DIFFERENT MECHANISM. Sections 154-156 identify the mechanisms already
exhausted: residue-consistency (saturates), potentials/gradings (regenerate),
deletion-contraction bookkeeping (Tutte no-go, 155.6.3), edge-counting
(reduction only, 156.3).

### 156.5 The mechanism not yet tried: non-constructive counting

Every method used so far certifies a 0-mod-8 cycle by EXHIBITING one. Each
fails because a mod-8-free configuration is locally consistent (sections 119,
123, 143, 155.7). The one class of existence proofs blind to local consistency
is ALGEBRAIC / PARITY COUNTING: prove a count is nonzero without producing a
witness.

Precedent that such theorems exist for cubic graphs:
 - SMITH's theorem (via Thomason's lollipop): every edge of a cubic graph lies
   in an EVEN number of Hamiltonian cycles - a parity theorem about connected
   spanning cycle-space elements, i.e. exactly the connectivity filter of
   155.7, which no algebraic tool of 155 could see.
 - Thomason's generalization to graphs with all degrees odd.
 - Combinatorial Nullstellensatz / Alon-Tarsi: existence from a nonzero
   coefficient.

NOMINATED FACT (not proved): let N_j be the number of cycles of length = j
(mod 8) in a 3-connected cubic graph of girth >= 5. Prove N_0 is odd, or more
generally that some explicit algebraic quantity forces N_0 > 0.

Why this is the right shape: N_0 odd would give N_0 > 0 with no reference to
any residue assignment, hence immune to every saturation phenomenon recorded
in sections 119-155. Smith's theorem shows parity statements of exactly this
type are true and provable in cubic graphs. What is missing is a lollipop-style
involution that respects length mod 8.

### 156.6 Also imported this pass

 - Every graph with min degree >= 2 and at most two vertices of degree 2 has a
   cycle of length 0 mod 4 (strengthening of DLS, cited in arXiv:2507.12798).
 - Gao-Shan: EG holds for P_8-free graphs; improved to P_10-free
   (Discrete Math. 2024) and to P_13-free with computer search
   (arXiv:2410.22842).
 - EG holds for graphs of diameter 2 and min degree >= 3: such graphs contain a
   C_4 or a C_8 (arXiv:2508.19302).
 - Counterexample lower bounds: n >= 17 in general, n >= 30 cubic, n >= 30
   bipartite (consistent with Markstrom, already banked).

STATUS RESTATED: T(3) UNPROVED. Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 156 contributes
one literature import that confirms the menu framework at mod 4, two exact
composition rules for the edge potential (156.2), one CORRECTION retiring
section 153's proposed route (156.3), one proof that "simple demolishing fact"
is a category error as usually posed (156.4), and one untried mechanism with
cubic-graph precedent (156.5).


## 157. RETRACTION of 156.5, and the character-sum reformulation

STATUS: T(3) and Erdos-Gyarfas remain UNPROVED.

### 157.1 RETRACTION (15th) - the parity mechanism is DEAD

Section 156.5 nominated: "N_0 (the number of cycles of length 0 mod 8) is odd
in a 3-connected cubic graph of girth >= 5." COMPUTED and REFUTED.

Enumerated every cycle of 47 cubic 3-connected graphs (11 named, 36 random
Hamiltonian C_n + perfect matching, all girth >= 5, n = 10..24). N_0 is EVEN in
21 of them. Explicit counterexamples:

    Mobius-Kantor (n=16, g=6)   N_0 = 36
    Pappus        (n=18, g=6)   N_0 = 270
    Desargues     (n=20, g=6)   N_0 = 390
    Dodecahedron  (n=20, g=5)   N_0 = 120
    Nauru         (n=24, g=6)   N_0 = 1134
    McGee         (n=24, g=7)   N_0 = 568

(also K_4, girth 3: N_0 = 0, even). Parity of N_0 is not a graph invariant:
among the 47, 26 odd and 21 even, with no correlation to bipartiteness, girth,
or n mod anything. The Smith/Thomason lollipop analogy does not transfer.
Section 156.5 is withdrawn in full.

### 157.2 What the enumeration DID show (COMPUTED)

(a) EQUIDISTRIBUTION. Let C = total number of cycles and
    maxdev = max_j |N_j - C/8| / C. For random 3-connected cubic girth-5
    graphs the deviation shrinks steadily with n:

      n=12: .049-.095   n=14: .071-.082   n=16: .046-.068   n=18: .049-.057
      n=20: .038-.043   n=22: .025-.036   n=24: .023-.029

    Cycle lengths mod 8 equidistribute, and fast.

(b) THE PARITY TERM IS THE ONLY LARGE OBSTRUCTION. Every graph in the sample
    with maxdev > 1/8 is bipartite or has a degenerate length spectrum
    (Heawood .269, Mobius-Kantor .295, Pappus .220, Desargues .185,
    Nauru .175, Petersen .226 - the last has spectrum {5,6,8,9} only).
    Every non-bipartite sample with n >= 16 has maxdev < 1/8.
    For a bipartite graph maxdev >= 1/8 automatically, since N_1 = N_3 = N_5 =
    N_7 = 0; there the right statistic is |C|/2 mod 4.

(c) EDGE-LOCAL STRENGTHENING (new conjecture, verified on all 47):
    every edge lies on a cycle of length 0 mod 8. The minimum over edges of
    that count was >= 2 in every graph tested (smallest value 2, at n=14).
    Likewise every vertex: minimum over vertices >= 4.

### 157.3 THE CHARACTER-SUM REFORMULATION (DERIVED - this is the point)

Let z = zeta_8 = e^{2 pi i / 8} and for k = 0..7 set

    S_k := sum over all cycles C of  z^{k |C|}      (so S_0 = C, the total).

Orthogonality gives exactly

    N_0 = ( C + S_1 + S_2 + S_3 + S_4 + S_5 + S_6 + S_7 ) / 8.

Hence

    T(3) for a given graph  <==>  S_1 + ... + S_7 > -C.

This is a QUANTITATIVE statement about character sums over the set of cycles.
It is not a residue-consistency statement, so it is untouched by every
saturation phenomenon recorded in sections 119-156: saturation says a
consistent assignment of residues EXISTS; a character-sum bound does not care
whether one exists, only how the actual cycle lengths distribute.

Structure of the seven terms:
 - S_4 = sum over C of (-1)^{|C|} = (#even cycles) - (#odd cycles). This is the
   ONLY term that can reach magnitude C: it equals C exactly when G is
   bipartite. It is the parity term, and parity is precisely what the proved
   T(1) / All-Odd machinery (section 1) already controls. For bipartite G,
   replace z_8^{|C|} by z_4^{|C|/2} and the whole scheme runs mod 4.
 - S_2, S_6 are the mod-4 layer, which by section 155.3 is the quadratic layer
   controlled by the bicycle space / Tutte at (i,-i).
 - S_1, S_3, S_5, S_7 are the genuinely cubic layer (section 155.2).

SUFFICIENT CONDITION (simple form): |S_k| < C/7 for k = 1,2,3,5,6,7, with the
parity term split off as above. Equivalently: the length distribution of cycles
mod 8 has l-infinity Fourier deviation below 1.

### 157.4 THE SIMPLE FACT, correctly posed

  EQUIDISTRIBUTION FACT. For every 3-connected cubic graph of girth >= 5 on
  n >= 30 vertices, max_j |N_j - C/8| < C/8 (with the bipartite case run on
  |C|/2 mod 4).

This demolishes the obstruction: it gives N_0 > 0 by counting alone, with no
witness, no residue assignment, no potential, no discharging. Combined with
MARKSTROM's census (a cubic counterexample needs n >= 30, already banked) it
yields T(3), hence Erdos-Gyarfas by the Tower.

Why n >= 30 and not all n: the counting bound is genuinely false at small n
(Heawood, n=14, has deviation .151 even after the bipartite reduction, though
N_0 = 21 > 0 anyway). The census covers exactly that range. This is a clean
division of labour, not a fudge.

Why this fact is the right shape: it is the first candidate in the entire
program that is (i) equivalent-strength, (ii) NOT a restatement of
mod-8-freeness in disguise (contrast section 156.4, where the Hinge Fact
collapsed to "some ear takes a forbidden residue"), and (iii) provable in
principle by a mechanism - exponential-sum estimation - that has never been
applied here.

### 157.5 The machinery that would prove it, and its honest limit

Section 155 gives EXACT control of sums over the whole cycle space Z(G):
Greene/Vertigan at the Gaussian point, Kasteleyn/Tesler Pfaffians in bounded
genus, Brown's invariant. Section 155.7 named the gap: those sums run over all
of Z(G), while S_k runs over CONNECTED elements only.

The standard bridge between the two is the CLUSTER (Mayer/polymer) EXPANSION.
In a cubic graph every element of Z(G) is a disjoint union of vertex-disjoint
cycles, i.e. Z(G) is exactly the hard-core polymer gas whose polymers are
cycles. Therefore

    sum over x in Z(G) of  w^{|x|}  =  the polymer partition function,
    sum over cycles C of   w^{|C|}  =  the first Mayer coefficient of its log,

and Kotecky-Preiss gives convergence, hence a bound on S_k, whenever the
activity is small enough.

HONEST LIMIT: the activity here is |w| = |z_8^k| = 1, and the Kotecky-Preiss
condition fails at activity 1 for graphs with many short cycles. So this is a
genuine research programme, not a proof. What it is NOT is another instance of
the wall: it fails for an analytic reason (radius of convergence), not because
a locally consistent mod-8-free configuration exists.

STATUS RESTATED: T(3) UNPROVED. Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 157 contributes
one RETRACTION (156.5, computationally refuted on 47 graphs), one computed
equidistribution table, one new verified conjecture (every edge lies on a
0-mod-8 cycle), one exact reformulation of T(3) as a character-sum inequality
(157.3), and one correctly-posed demolishing fact with its proof mechanism
named and its limit stated (157.4, 157.5).


## 158. THE OBSTRUCTION IS ONE CHARACTER (COMPUTED + DERIVED)

STATUS: T(3) and Erdos-Gyarfas remain UNPROVED. This section localizes the
obstruction to a single quantity. It does not bound it.

### 158.1 What was measured

For 32 cubic 3-connected graphs of girth >= 5 (11 named, 21 random Hamiltonian,
n = 10..24) the full cycle spectrum was enumerated and the normalized character
sums |S_k| / C computed, where

    S_k = sum over cycles C of exp(2 pi i k |C| / M),   C = total cycle count,

with M = 8 for non-bipartite G and M = 4 applied to |C|/2 for bipartite G
(the reduction of 157.3).

### 158.2 THE FINDING: all the mass sits on the primitive character

For every non-bipartite graph tested, the profile is dominated by k = 1 and its
conjugate k = 7; k = 2,3,4,5,6 are an order of magnitude smaller. Example rows:

  McGee     n=24  |S_k|/C = .100 .072 .061 .004 .061 .072 .100
  GP(11,2)  n=22           = .117 .058 .087 .015 .087 .058 .117
  rand n=24                = .092 .026 .017 .002 .017 .026 .092
  rand n=20                = .136 .018 .012 .001 .012 .018 .136

|S_1|/C for random 3-connected cubic girth-5 graphs, by order:

  n=12: .224 .224 .249     n=14: .200 .228 .220     n=16: .203 .192 .203
  n=18: .174 .178 .175     n=20: .136 .139 .143     n=22: .113 .113 .116
  n=24: .092 .098 .086

Monotone decreasing, crossing the threshold 1/7 = .143 at about n = 20 and
sitting at .09 by n = 24.

### 158.3 This confirms the degree filtration of 155.2 by measurement

The characters sort exactly by the polynomial degree of the length function:

  S_4  = (#even cycles) - (#odd cycles)  = the LINEAR layer (mod 2).
         Measured .000-.037 for non-bipartite G: parity is nearly balanced.
         Controlled by the proved T(1) / All-Odd machinery.
  S_2, S_6 = the QUADRATIC layer (mod 4), which by 155.3 is the bicycle-space /
         Tutte-at-(i,-i) layer. Measured .006-.072 for n >= 16. This is the
         quantitative shadow of DEAN-LESNIAK-SAITO being a theorem.
  S_1, S_3, S_5, S_7 = the CUBIC layer (mod 8), 155.2. All the remaining mass.
         Within it the PRIMITIVE character k = 1 dominates.

So the independent measurement reproduces the algebraic stratification derived
in 155.2 from the inclusion-exclusion identity. That is a genuine cross-check
of the framework, obtained without assuming it.

### 158.4 The crude bound already suffices almost everywhere (COMPUTED)

By 157.3, N_0 > 0 iff S_1 + ... + S_{M-1} > -C. The triangle inequality gives
the sufficient condition

    (CRUDE)   sum_{k=1}^{M-1} |S_k|  <  C.

Evaluated on all 32 graphs: it HOLDS for 31. The single failure is PETERSEN
(n = 10, value 2.64), whose spectrum is only {5,6,8,9} - four lengths, hence no
room for cancellation. Petersen is far below Markstrom's n >= 30 census
threshold, so it is not a counterexample to anything; it shows only that the
crude bound needs n to be moderately large.

Selected values of the crude sum: Heawood .72, Mobius-Kantor .80, GP(7,2) .90,
Pappus .55, Desargues .52, Dodecahedron .68, GP(11,2) .54, Nauru .21,
McGee .47; random n=12 .94, n=14 .80, n=16 .57, n=20 .36, n=24 .27.

### 158.5 Consequence: T(3) is now ONE inequality about ONE character

Combining 157.3, 158.2 and 158.4, the whole conjecture reduces to:

  TARGET (unproved). For every 3-connected cubic graph of girth >= 5 with
  n >= 30 vertices,
        2|S_1| + 2|S_2| + 2|S_3| + |S_4|  <  C
  (bipartite case: 2|S_1| + |S_2| < C on |C|/2 mod 4),
  and by 158.2 the only term that is ever close to binding is |S_1|.

This is the narrowest formulation the program has produced. It is a single
exponential-sum estimate over the set of cycles, with a measured safety margin
that grows with n (crude sum .94 at n=12 down to .27 at n=24).

### 158.6 Why it is still not proved - honest accounting

The natural elementary bounds are far too lossy. Abel summation gives
|S_1| <= |1 - zeta_8|^{-1} * sum_l |c_l - c_{l+1}| <= 5.2 * max_l c_l for a
unimodal spectrum, and max_l c_l / C is around .39 for Heawood, .25 for typical
random samples - so the elementary bound gives nothing. The smallness of |S_1|
is genuine cancellation across lengths, not mere smoothness of the spectrum,
and no tool in the program bounds it.

The two candidate mechanisms both have named blockers:
 - Polymer/cluster expansion (157.5): activity |zeta_8| = 1, Kotecky-Preiss
   fails.
 - Non-backtracking spectral (151-152, Ihara/Bass): gives closed-walk counts
   exactly, but converting walk counts to SIMPLE-cycle counts is the same
   connectivity filter as 155.7.

STATUS RESTATED: T(3) UNPROVED. Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 158 contributes
a measured character-sum profile over 32 graphs, an independent confirmation of
the 155.2 degree filtration, the observation that the crude triangle-inequality
bound already suffices for 31 of 32 (all but Petersen), and the reduction of the
entire conjecture to a single exponential-sum estimate on the primitive
character S_1 (158.5). No gap is closed.


## 159. THE DEMOLISHING FACT, NAMED: the even-k case of Lyngsie-Merker

STATUS: T(3) and Erdos-Gyarfas remain UNPROVED.

### 159.1 The fact

LYNGSIE-MERKER (arXiv:1904.05076, "Cycle lengths modulo k in large 3-connected
cubic graphs"), verbatim from the abstract:

  "For all natural numbers m and k where k is odd, there exists a natural
   number N(k) such that any 3-connected cubic graph with at least N(k)
   vertices contains a cycle of length m modulo k."

The paper proves this ONLY for odd k. For even k it gives a counterexample
family at 2-connectivity, and states no theorem at 3-connectivity. Confirmed by
direct reading of the source this pass.

  THE FACT TO PROVE (call it LM-even for k = 8):
  there is N such that every 3-connected cubic graph on at least N vertices
  contains a cycle of length 0 modulo 8.

### 159.2 Why this is the right nomination, unlike every earlier one

 (a) IT IS NOT CIRCULAR. Section 156.4 showed that the natural "one simple
     fact" candidates (the Hinge Fact and its relatives) collapse into
     restatements of mod-8-freeness. LM-even does not: it is a statement about
     ALL large 3-connected cubic graphs with no girth or C4 hypothesis, i.e.
     strictly stronger than T(3), and it is asserted in a form that already has
     a proved sibling.
 (b) HALF OF IT IS ALREADY A THEOREM. The odd-k case is proved and in print.
     The technique therefore exists; what is missing is the even-k adaptation,
     where bipartite graphs obstruct the odd residues. Note that obstruction is
     harmless for us: bipartite graphs have all cycles even, and residue 0 is
     even, so the even-residue version of LM-even still yields T(3).
 (c) IT CLOSES THE PROGRAM AS STATED. LM-even for k = 8 gives a 0-mod-8 cycle
     in every 3-connected cubic graph of order >= N. MARKSTROM's census
     (a cubic Erdos-Gyarfas counterexample needs n >= 30, banked) covers the
     small orders provided N is brought below the census reach; otherwise the
     residual window [30, N) is a finite, explicitly bounded check.
 (d) IT MATCHES THE MEASUREMENTS. Section 158's character-sum profile is
     exactly what LM-even predicts: equidistribution of cycle lengths mod 8
     setting in as n grows, with the deviation |S_1|/C falling from .25 at
     n = 12 to .09 at n = 24.

### 159.3 Supporting measurement (COMPUTED)

Re-reading the section-157 enumeration for residue COVERAGE rather than counts:
every 3-connected cubic girth->=5 graph tested with n >= 12 realizes every
residue class mod 8 that its bipartition class permits -

  non-bipartite (GP(7,2), GP(9,2), GP(11,2), GP(12,2), Dodecahedron, McGee, all
    21 random samples n = 12..24): all EIGHT residues occur;
  bipartite (Heawood, Mobius-Kantor, Pappus, Desargues, Nauru): all FOUR even
    residues occur, including 0.

The single exception is PETERSEN (n = 10), whose spectrum is {5,6,8,9} and which
realizes only residues {0,1,5,6} - it still contains residue 0. So the sample
contains no obstruction to LM-even at k = 8, and the coverage threshold in the
data is n >= 12, far below the census bound n >= 30.

### 159.4 Honest statement of what is NOT done

LM-even for k = 8 is UNPROVED, by me and (as far as this pass could determine)
by anyone. Nominating it does not prove T(3). What sections 155-159 establish is
that it is the correct single target:

  - 155.2: mod 8 is the first CUBIC layer of the degree filtration; mod 4 is
    quadratic and is Dean-Lesniak-Saito.
  - 156.3: the edge-counting/extremal route CANNOT prove it (it needs the
    3-connected case as input) - correction to 153.
  - 156.4: no logically weaker "simple fact" can exist; every candidate is a
    restatement.
  - 157.1: the parity/lollipop mechanism is refuted computationally.
  - 158.5: quantitatively, the entire obstruction is the single primitive
    character S_1.
  - 159.1: the literature has proved the odd-k sibling of exactly the needed
    statement.

STATUS RESTATED: T(3) UNPROVED. Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 159 contributes
the identification of the needed statement with a named, half-solved open
problem in the literature, and the residue-coverage measurement supporting it.
No gap is closed.


## 160. TWO CORRECTIONS, AND THE OBJECT OUTSIDE GRAPH THEORY

STATUS: T(3) and Erdos-Gyarfas remain UNPROVED.

### 160.1 CORRECTION (16th): cycles are NOT exponentially sparse in Z(G)

Sections 155.7 and 157.3 both asserted that the connected elements of the cycle
space are "an exponentially sparse subset". THAT IS FALSE, and the numbers were
already in hand in section 157.

For a cubic graph, dim Z(G) = m - n + 1 = n/2 + 1, so |Z(G)| = 2^{n/2+1}. Every
nonzero element is a disjoint union of vertex-disjoint cycles. Comparing with
the enumerated cycle counts:

  graph          n    |Z|-1    cycles   disconnected   cycles / (|Z|-1)
  Petersen      10      63        57          6            .90
  Heawood       14     255       213         42            .84
  GP(7,2)       14     255       205         50            .80
  MobiusKantor  16     511       400        111            .78
  Pappus        18    1023       783        240            .77
  Dodecahedron  20    2047      1168        879            .57
  Desargues     20    2047      1456        591            .71
  Nauru         24    8191      5442       2749            .66
  McGee         24    8191      5608       2583            .68

Cycles are a CONSTANT FRACTION - between 57% and 90% - of the nonzero cycle
space. The "connectivity filter" of 155.7 is therefore a bounded-factor problem,
not a needle-in-a-haystack problem. Every conclusion drawn from the sparsity
claim is withdrawn.

### 160.2 CORRECTION (17th): the polymer expansion is FINITE, so Kotecky-Preiss
### was the wrong blocker

Section 157.5 declared the cluster-expansion route blocked because the activity
is |zeta_8| = 1 and Kotecky-Preiss fails to converge. That diagnosis is wrong,
because the expansion here does not need to converge - IT TERMINATES.

In a cubic graph of girth g every cycle uses at least g vertices and components
are vertex-disjoint, so no element of Z(G) has more than floor(n/g) components.
With g >= 5 that is at most n/5. Writing S_j for the sum of w^{|x|} over
elements with exactly j components,

    W(w) := sum over x in Z(G) of w^{|x|}  =  1 + S_1 + S_2 + ... + S_{floor(n/g)}

is a FINITE sum, and S_1 - the cycle character sum of 158 - is

    S_1 = W(w) - 1 - S_2 - ... - S_{floor(n/g)}.

For n < 15 with girth 5 it terminates at j = 2 exactly (three disjoint cycles
need 15 vertices). Petersen: W = 1 + S_1 + S_2 with exactly 57 and 6 terms.
Heawood: 213 and 42. No convergence question arises.

Moreover the mean-field relation S_2 = (S_1^2 - sum_C w^{2|C|})/2 + (correction
for non-disjoint pairs) suggests the self-consistent estimate

    S_1  =  log W(w)  + lower order,

i.e. the cycle character sum is the LOGARITHM of a quantity that section 155.3
identifies as a Tutte evaluation (Greene's theorem). At w = i that evaluation is
exactly T(i,-i), computable in polynomial time by Vertigan. At w = zeta_8 it is
T at a generic point.

This does not prove anything, but it replaces a false blocker with a concrete
finite identity.

### 160.3 THE OBJECT: the lattice of integral flows

The faithful translation of our graphs out of graph theory is into the theory of
INTEGRAL LATTICES.

Let G be cubic with a reference orientation and incidence matrix d. Define

    Lambda(G) := ker(d) intersect Z^E,   with the standard inner product.

This is the LATTICE OF INTEGRAL FLOWS (Bacher-de la Harpe-Nagnibeda 1997). Facts,
all classical or immediate:

 (i)  rank Lambda(G) = m - n + 1 = n/2 + 1.
 (ii) A cycle C with an orientation gives the vector v_C with entries +-1 on C
      and 0 elsewhere, and
                        ||v_C||^2 = |C|.
      CYCLE LENGTH IS SQUARED NORM.
 (iii) The vectors of Lambda(G) with entries in {0,+-1} are exactly the oriented
      disjoint unions of directed cycles; a k-component element of Z(G) yields
      2^k of them.
 (iv) The minimal vectors of Lambda(G) are the shortest cycles, so
      min-norm(Lambda(G)) = girth(G).
 (v)  det Lambda(G) = the number of spanning trees of G (Kirchhoff). The
      discriminant group is the JACOBIAN / critical group of G.
 (vi) Lambda(G) is an EVEN lattice if and only if G is bipartite (odd cycles
      give odd norms).

So T(3) restated with no graph theory in it:

  For every rank-(n/2+1) flow lattice Lambda of a 3-connected cubic graph with
  min-norm >= 5, some {0,+-1}-vector of Lambda with connected support has
  squared norm divisible by 8.

### 160.4 Why the lattice is the RIGHT new object: theta series

The theta series of an integral lattice,

    Theta_Lambda(q) = sum over v in Lambda of q^{||v||^2},

is a MODULAR FORM when Lambda is even: weight (rank)/2, level dividing the
lattice level, for a congruence subgroup. By 160.3(v)-(vi):

  For BIPARTITE cubic G, Theta_{Lambda(G)} is a modular form of weight
  (n/2+1)/2 whose level is controlled by the spanning-tree number of G.

And what section 158 established is that everything now hinges on ONE question:
how do the counts of cycles distribute over residue classes mod 8? That is
literally the question "how do the Fourier coefficients of a modular form
distribute in arithmetic progressions" - the single best-developed question in
the subject (Sturm's theorem, Deligne bounds, twists by Dirichlet characters,
Serre's results on lacunarity and on coefficients in residue classes).

The graph-theory literature has no tool for cycle counts in arithmetic
progressions. The modular-forms literature has almost nothing else.

HONEST GAP: Theta_Lambda counts ALL lattice vectors of a given norm, while T(3)
concerns only the {0,+-1}-vectors with connected support. That is the same
filter as 155.7 - but by 160.1 it costs a constant factor, not an exponential
one, and by 160.2 it is a finite correction.

### 160.5 The other translations, with verdicts

 (a) TREE LATTICES / OUTER SPACE. pi_1(G) is free of rank n/2+1 acting freely and
     cocompactly on the 3-regular tree T_3; G = Gamma \ T_3. Cycles correspond to
     conjugacy classes whose axis projects injectively, and cycle length is
     TRANSLATION LENGTH. So a cubic graph is an integral point of CULLER-VOGTMANN
     OUTER SPACE, and mod-8-freeness says the embedded translation-length
     spectrum misses 8Z. Machinery available: the prime geodesic theorem for
     graphs (equidistribution of ALL primitive closed geodesics), Ihara zeta as
     the Selberg analogue, geodesic currents (Kapovich), Out(F_r) dynamics.
     VERDICT: real, and the equidistribution theorems there are exactly the shape
     needed - but they count all closed geodesics, not embedded ones. Same filter.
 (b) CODING THEORY. Z(G) is a binary linear code of length 3n/2 and dimension
     n/2+1; cycles are precisely the MINIMAL CODEWORDS; cycle length is Hamming
     weight. By 160.1 this code has the unusual property that 57-90% of its
     codewords are minimal (Ashikhmin-Barg's sufficient condition
     w_min/w_max > 1/2 is far from met here, so this is not explained by the
     standard criterion). Divisible-code theory (Ward), Gleason-Pierce, and
     Massey secret-sharing all live here.
     VERDICT: the right vocabulary, no theorem yet that bites.
 (c) DESSINS D'ENFANTS. A cubic ribbon graph is a trivalent dessin, hence a curve
     over Qbar with a Belyi map, with Gal(Qbar/Q) acting.
     VERDICT: NO. Cycle lengths are not a dessin invariant; the Galois action does
     not preserve mod-8-freeness. Dead end, recorded so it is not retried.
 (d) GRAPH C*-ALGEBRAS. K-theory of the Cuntz-Krieger algebra is coker(I - A^T).
     VERDICT: NO. It sees the adjacency matrix, not cycle lengths mod 8.

### 160.6 The ZERO-EIGHT resonance (observation, not a theorem)

Section 155.3 derived that q(x) = |x| mod 4 is a Z_4-valued quadratic refinement
of the intersection form on Z(G), whose complete invariant is BROWN'S INVARIANT,
valued in Z_8. Section 160.3 puts the same data in a lattice whose norms are the
cycle lengths, and integral lattice theory is 8-periodic for the same reason
(signature of an even unimodular lattice is 0 mod 8; Witt group of Z_4-quadratic
forms is Z_8).

So the modulus 8 in Erdos-Gyarfas level 3 and the modulus 8 in quadratic-form
theory come from the same 8-fold periodicity. This is a structural resonance, NOT
an identification - Brown's Z_8 classifies the mod-4 form's Witt class, while
T(3) asks for a mod-8 value of an individual vector. Recorded as a reason to
expect the lattice-theoretic route to be natural rather than forced.

STATUS RESTATED: T(3) UNPROVED. Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 160 contributes
two CORRECTIONS (160.1 sparsity claim false; 160.2 Kotecky-Preiss was the wrong
blocker, the expansion is finite), the flow-lattice translation with cycle length
= squared norm (160.3), the modular-forms target (160.4), four further
translations with verdicts including two explicit dead ends (160.5), and one
structural observation (160.6). No gap is closed.


## 161. THE CHOICE: the cycle code / flow lattice. Machine built and validated.

STATUS: T(3) and Erdos-Gyarfas remain UNPROVED.

### 161.1 Why this translation and not the other

Outer space / tree lattices (160.5a) is the more glamorous translation and it has
the equidistribution theorems we want - the prime geodesic theorem for graphs,
via Ihara-Bass, gives tr(B^l) = 2^l + O(rho^l) with rho < 2 for non-bipartite
cubic G, hence exponentially fast equidistribution of closed geodesic lengths
over all residues mod 8. But the filter there is FATAL: closed geodesics of
length <= n number about 2^n / n, while cycles number about 2^{n/2}. Cycles are
EXPONENTIALLY rare among geodesics.

In the cycle code the same filter costs a CONSTANT FACTOR (160.1: cycles are
57-90% of Z(G)). Same theorem shape, exponentially better filter. Therefore:

  CHOSEN TRANSLATION: Z(G) as a binary linear code / Lambda(G) as an integral
  lattice. Cycle length = Hamming weight = squared norm. Cycles = minimal
  codewords = connected {0,+-1}-vectors.

### 161.2 The machine

Let W(z) = sum over x in Z(G) of z^{|x|}  (the weight enumerator of the cycle
code), r = dim Z = n/2 + 1, and S_j(z) = the same sum restricted to elements with
exactly j components. Then, exactly:

  (M1)  N_0 = (1/8) sum_{k=0..7} S_1(zeta_8^k)                    [orthogonality]
  (M2)  S_1(z) = W(z) - 1 - S_2(z) - ... - S_{floor(n/g)}(z)      [finite, 160.2]
  (M3)  W(z) is a Tutte evaluation (Greene's theorem).

So T(3) for one graph is a statement about W at the eight 8th roots of unity,
corrected by at most floor(n/5) component terms.

### 161.3 Four of the eight characters are now in CLOSED FORM

 k = 0:  W(1) = 2^r.                                              [trivial]

 k = 4:  W(-1) = 2^r if G is bipartite, 0 otherwise.              [PROVED]
         Proof: |x| mod 2 is a linear functional on Z(G); it is identically zero
         iff every cycle is even iff G is bipartite. A nontrivial character sums
         to zero over a group.
         VERIFIED 8/8: Petersen 0, Heawood 256, GP(7,2) 0, Mobius-Kantor 512,
         Pappus 1024, GP(9,2) 0, Dodecahedron 0, Desargues 2048.

 k = 2, 6:  let d = dim of the BICYCLE SPACE Z ^ Z-perp. Then
              |W(i)| = 2^{d + (r-d)/2}   if |x| = 0 mod 4 for every bicycle x,
              |W(i)| = 0                 otherwise.
         Proof: by 155.3, q(x) = |x| mod 4 is a Z_4-quadratic refinement of
         b(x,y) = |x^y| mod 2 whose radical is the bicycle space. Split
         Z = B (+) U with b nondegenerate on U. Since B is the radical,
         q(u + beta) = q(u) + q(beta), so the sum factorizes. On B, q is
         additive from F_2^d, hence valued in {0,2}: its factor is 2^d if q|_B
         vanishes and 0 otherwise. The U factor is a nondegenerate Gauss sum of
         modulus 2^{(r-d)/2}.
         VERIFIED 8/8, including the vanishing case:
           Petersen      d=4, r=6   pred 2^4*2^1 = 32     computed 32
           Heawood       d=0, r=8   pred 2^4      = 16     computed 16
           GP(7,2)       d=0, r=8   pred 16               computed 16
           Mobius-Kantor d=3, r=9   pred 2^3*2^3 = 64     computed 64
           Pappus        d=6, r=10  pred 2^6*2^2 = 256    computed 256
           GP(9,2)       d=0, r=10  pred 2^5     = 32     computed 32
           Dodecahedron  d=5, r=11  q nonzero on radical  -> 0, computed 0
           Desargues     d=5, r=11  pred 2^5*2^3 = 256    computed 256

 k = 1, 3, 5, 7:  UNKNOWN. These are exactly the CUBIC layer of 155.2, and
         exactly the characters that 158.2 measured as carrying all the mass.
         The algebra (155.2), the measurement (158.2), and the closed forms
         (this section) agree on which four characters are hard.

### 161.4 THE MACWILLIAMS-ISING IDENTITY (DERIVED, then VERIFIED exactly)

The dual of the cycle code is the CUT code B, of dimension n-1. MacWilliams
gives W_Z(X,Y) = 2^{-(n-1)} W_B(X+Y, X-Y), so with X = 1, Y = z:

    W(z) = (1+z)^m / 2^{n-1}  *  sum over cuts delta(S) of  ((1-z)/(1+z))^{|delta(S)|}.

At z = zeta_8 the ratio is exactly

    (1 - zeta_8)/(1 + zeta_8) = -i tan(pi/8) = -i (sqrt2 - 1),

verified numerically to 1e-16. Hence

  THE CYCLE-CODE CHARACTER SUM AT zeta_8 IS AN ISING PARTITION FUNCTION OF THE
  SAME GRAPH AT THE COMPLEX COUPLING -i(sqrt2 - 1), |coupling| = sqrt2 - 1.

VERIFIED exactly (both sides computed independently, agreement to 1e-6 relative):
    Petersen  W(zeta_8) =  21.6569 + 1.6569i   (both methods)
    Heawood   W(zeta_8) = -76.0000 +32.0000i   (both methods)
    GP(7,2)   W(zeta_8) = -68.0833 +28.4853i   (both methods)
  and at z = i:  Petersen 32i, Heawood -16, GP(7,2) -16i, both methods.

This is exact and it is new to the program. Consequences:
 - For PLANAR G the right-hand side is a Kasteleyn Pfaffian, computable in
   polynomial time; for genus g, a Galluccio-Loebl / Tesler 4^g-Pfaffian sum.
   So W(zeta_8) - and hence, up to the finite component correction of (M2), the
   cycle character sum - is EXACTLY COMPUTABLE in bounded genus.
 - sqrt2 - 1 = tan(pi/8) is subcritical for the cubic Ising model (critical
   coupling near 1/2), so the cut-side sum is in the ordered/low-temperature
   phase, dominated by small cuts.

### 161.5 What is still missing, quantified honestly

The naive route - triangle inequality on the cut side - LOSES BY AN EXPONENTIAL
FACTOR. Taking absolute values gives

    |W(zeta_8)| <= (2 cos(pi/8))^m / 2^{n-1}  *  sum over cuts of (sqrt2-1)^{|delta(S)|}.

For cubic m = 3n/2 the prefactor is 2.512^n / 2^n. If the graph has edge
expansion |delta(S)| >= beta |S| the cut sum is at most 2(1 + (sqrt2-1)^beta)^n,
and the whole bound beats the target 2^r = 2 * 1.414^n only when

    (sqrt2 - 1)^beta < 0.126,  i.e.  beta > 2.35,

which is nearly the maximum conceivable expansion (3) and false for large S. So
MacWilliams gives an exact identity but not, by itself, a bound. The smallness of
|W(zeta_8)| (measured: .34 * 2^r at n=10 falling to .165 * 2^r at n=20) is
cancellation on the cut side, i.e. genuine complex-phase cancellation in the
Ising sum, not a size bound.

  REMAINING TARGET, in final form:
    bound |W(zeta_8)| + |W(zeta_8^3)| below a constant times 2^r, using the
    complex-temperature Ising representation, plus control of the at most
    floor(n/5) component corrections S_2, ..., in (M2).

This is a Lee-Yang / Fisher-zero question: the coupling -i(sqrt2-1) is purely
imaginary of modulus tan(pi/8), and the needed bound says the partition function
does not concentrate there. Lee-Yang theory controls zeros of the Ising partition
function in the complex FIELD; Fisher zeros are the complex-TEMPERATURE analogue,
and this is exactly a complex-temperature question.
