five-attachment criterion; the one-bridge corollary; and the BIPARTITE t = 1 RUNG
for non-Hamiltonian cycles.

OPEN: the two residual cases of 174.3, and every rung with t >= 2.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 174 closes the base case of the
Hensel induction (174.1) and proves the t = 1 induction step whenever a bridge has
five attachments, or three in the bipartite case (174.2), leaving two explicitly
described rigidity cases (174.3) and the t >= 2 rungs (174.4). No gap is closed.


## 175. WHY THE RUNGS ARE NOT UNIFORM, AND THE GENERAL ATTACK

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section answers a methodological
question - why climb rung by rung rather than attack the induction step in
general - and the answer turns out to be a small theorem rather than an excuse.

### 175.1 The uniform form of every rung

By 173.4 the rung at level t asks, for a cycle C with 2^t | |C|:

     find an ear P of C with 2^t | |P| and 2^t | |A|.

Fix a bridge B of C and a vertex w inside it. By Menger (fan version) a
3-connected cubic graph has three internally disjoint paths from w to C, of
lengths mu_1, mu_2, mu_3, landing at attachments y_1, y_2, y_3. Any such STAR gives
ears with EXACT length

     |P_ij| = mu_i + mu_j,

which repairs the defect flagged in 174.4 (for a general Steiner tree
|P_ij| = l_i + l_j - 2*overlap and only the mod-2 statement survives; for a star
the identity is exact). Writing p_i for the position of y_i along C - well defined
mod 2^t because 2^t | |C| - the rung fires as soon as some pair satisfies

     (*)   mu_i + mu_j = 0  (mod 2^t)    and    p_i = p_j  (mod 2^t).

So EVERY rung has the same uniform form. The question is whether one argument
settles (*) for all t at once.

### 175.2 IT DOES NOT, AND HERE IS WHY (PROVED)

  OBSERVATION. In Z_2 one has -x = x, so at t = 1 condition (*) reads
  mu_i = mu_j and p_i = p_j : an EQUALITY condition in F_2 x F_2. Equality
  conditions are pigeonhole conditions, and five attachments force a repeat.
  That is exactly the proof of 174.2, and it is why t = 1 was easy.

  For t >= 2 the map x -> -x is NOT the identity on Z_{2^t}, and (*) becomes a
  ZERO-SUM condition, mu_j = -mu_i. Zero-sum conditions have UNBOUNDED avoiding
  sets: take every mu_i congruent to the same value x with 2x =/= 0 mod 2^t (for
  instance all mu_i = 1). Then mu_i + mu_j = 2x =/= 0 for every pair, no matter how
  many attachments there are, and every position class may be filled arbitrarily.

  CONSEQUENCE. No pigeonhole bound on the number of attachments can prove the rung
  for t >= 2. The ladder is genuinely NON-UNIFORM: rung 1 is a pigeonhole problem
  and rungs t >= 2 are zero-sum problems. Attacking "the induction step" in general
  by a counting argument is therefore not merely hard - it is impossible in that
  form.

This is worth recording as a positive result: it identifies precisely where the
difficulty jumps, and it says the jump is at t = 2, not gradually.

### 175.3 What the general attack must therefore be

Two genuine options, and they are the only two.

 (A) IMPORT ZERO-SUM MACHINERY. The correct general tool for (*) is the theory of
     zero-sum sequences: the DAVENPORT CONSTANT D(Z_{2^t} x Z_{2^t}) = 2^{t+1} - 1
     and ERDOS-GINZBURG-ZIV. These bound the length of a sequence with no zero-sum
     subsequence - but note (*) asks for a zero-sum PAIR with a matching second
     coordinate, which is a restricted and harder question than the classical one.
     The classical constants do not apply directly; what is needed is a
     "zero-sum pair with a constraint" result, which I did not find in the
     literature this session.

 (B) BOUND THE NUMBER OF RUNGS INSTEAD OF PROVING THEM ALL. Since t = 0 and t = 1
     are proved (174.1, 174.2), it suffices to show that the descent can always be
     arranged to finish within those two rungs. This is a GLOBAL statement about
     choosing the starting cycle C_0 and the target exponent m, not a local
     statement about any single rung - which is the "focus generally" the question
     asks for.

     Concretely: after the t = 0 move we hold an even cycle; after the t = 1 move
     we hold a cycle with 4 | |C| - 2^m. To finish we need that cycle to BE 2^m,
     i.e. we need |C| - 2^m = 0 rather than merely divisible by 4. Inside the
     window [3, 2^{m+1}) the possible values of |C| - 2^m divisible by 4 are
     0, +-4, +-8, ..., so this is exactly the demand that the window be tightened
     from 2^{m+1} to 4, i.e. that the two moves be chosen to land within 4 of the
     target.

  TWO-RUNG CONJECTURE (open, and the recommended target). Every graph of minimum
  degree 3 admits a cycle C_0 and an exponent m such that at most two admissible
  ear-moves carry C_0 to a cycle of length exactly 2^m.

  Evidence (173.5): of the 26 descents found by exhaustive backtracking, the
  lengths were e.g. [3,4], [4], [5,6,8], [6,8], [7,8], [8], [10,8], [11,8],
  [12,8], [14,8], [5,8] - all of these are AT MOST TWO MOVES. Only four of the 26
  needed three: [6,12,8], [9,6,12,8], [10,12,8], [11,6,8]. So two rungs suffice in
  22 of 26 cases, and in the remaining four the third move was at t = 2.

### 175.4 Honest assessment of the change of strategy

The rung-by-rung climb was not wrong, but it cannot be completed: 175.2 shows the
method dies at t = 2 for a structural reason. The correct general strategy is (B),
because it uses only the two rungs that ARE proved and moves the remaining
difficulty into a choice problem (which C_0, which m) rather than an existence
problem at every level.

What is still missing for (B) is a way to steer the first two moves so that the
second lands exactly on 2^m rather than merely within 4 of it. That is a window
problem, and the window is the one part of the whole framework that has never been
analysed - every section from 170 onward has treated it as bookkeeping.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 175 contributes the exact
Menger-star form of every rung (175.1), a proof that no pigeonhole argument can
handle t >= 2 because the condition changes from equality to zero-sum at exactly
that point (175.2), and the resulting redirection to the TWO-RUNG CONJECTURE, with
the observation that 22 of 26 computed descents already satisfy it (175.3).
No gap is closed.


## 176. CANONICAL STATEMENT of the Hensel induction (consolidation, no new result)

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Nothing new is proved here; this section
writes the induction of 172-175 in one place, in the exact form it must take.

### 176.1 Setup

G has minimum degree >= 3 (and, after the standard reduction, is 2-connected).
GOAL: G has a cycle of length exactly 2^m for some m.

EAR. A path P with both ends on a cycle C and interior disjoint from C. It splits
C into two arcs A and A'. Rerouting gives the cycles P u A and P u A'. Setting
delta = |P| - |A|, the rerouted cycle has length |C| + delta = |P| + |A'|.

TARGET AND WINDOW. Fix T = 2^m and the window W = [3, 2^{m+1}).

THE INDUCTION MEASURE. For a cycle C in W put

        t(C) = v_2( |C| - T )   in {0,1,2,...} u {infinity},

so t(C) = infinity exactly when |C| = T, i.e. exactly when we are DONE.

### 176.2 The three components

  (1) STARTING POINT  [PROVED, 174.1]
      G has a cycle. Let g be the girth, C_0 a shortest cycle, m = ceil(log_2 g).
      Then g <= 2^m and g < 2^{m+1}, so C_0 lies in W.

  (2) INDUCTION STEP  [the content]

      STEP(t).  Let C be a cycle with C in W and t(C) = t finite. Then there is an
      ear P of C and a choice of arc A with

            v_2( |P| - |A| ) = t        and       |P| + |A'|  in  W.

      By the Hensel Descent Lemma (172.2) the first condition forces
      t(C') > t for the rerouted cycle C'; the second keeps C' in the window.

  (3) TERMINATION  [PROVED, 174.1 B3]
      For C in W with |C| =/= T we have 0 < | |C| - T | < 2^{m+1}, so t(C) <= m-1.
      Since each step strictly increases t and t is capped at m-1, the process
      cannot continue forever; the only way out is t = infinity, i.e. |C| = T.

So the induction runs UPWARD in t through the finite range 0,1,...,m-1, and there
is no "base case" in the schoolbook sense - what plays that role is (1), the
existence of a starting cycle, plus (3), which is what makes the ladder finite.

### 176.3 The step must be EXISTENTIAL, not universal

STEP(t) as written above quantifies over every cycle C at level t. THAT VERSION IS
FALSE: 172.3 exhibits counterexamples - Heawood has a 14-cycle from which no
admissible move exists for T = 8, and Mobius-Kantor fails at T = 4, 8 and 16.

The correct hypothesis is existential:

      STEP'(t). Among the cycles at level t that are REACHABLE from C_0 by
      admissible moves, at least one has an ear satisfying the two conditions of
      STEP(t).

This is what the backtracking search of 173.5 verifies (26 graphs, no failures),
and it is why the descent must be allowed to choose its route rather than follow a
greedy path.

### 176.4 Status of each piece, exactly

  (1) starting point            PROVED  (174.1)
  (3) termination               PROVED  (174.1)
  STEP'(0)                      PROVED  (173.3 Corollary): at t = 0 the sufficient
                                condition of the Rung Lemma is vacuous, so EVERY
                                ear works, and every cycle of a 2-connected
                                minimum-degree-3 graph has an ear.
  STEP'(1)                      PROVED (174.2) when some bridge of C with internal
                                vertices has >= 5 attachments; >= 3 suffice if G is
                                bipartite. Open in the residual cases of 174.3.
  STEP'(t), t >= 2              OPEN. By 175.2 no pigeonhole argument can settle
                                it: at t = 1 the condition is an EQUALITY in F_2^2
                                (because -x = x in Z_2), at t >= 2 it is a ZERO-SUM
                                condition in Z_{2^t}, which admits unbounded
                                avoiding sets.
  THE WINDOW CONDITION          NEVER ANALYSED, in any step. Every section from 170
                                onward has carried "and stay in W" as bookkeeping
                                and never verified that it can be maintained.

### 176.5 The sufficient condition actually used at each step

The Rung Lemma (173.3) replaces the awkward requirement v_2(|P|-|A|) = t by a
divisibility requirement that is easier to search for:

      if 2^t divides |P| and 2^t divides |A|, then ONE of the two moves through P
      is admissible.

Equivalently: C lies in a theta all three of whose branch lengths are divisible by
2^t. In the Menger-star form of 175.1, with legs mu_1, mu_2, mu_3 from an interior
vertex w to attachments at positions p_1, p_2, p_3, the requirement is a pair with

      mu_i + mu_j = 0 (mod 2^t)   and   p_i = p_j (mod 2^t).

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 176 consolidates only; the open
items are STEP'(1) in its residual cases, STEP'(t) for t >= 2, and the window
condition throughout.


## 177. THE EXISTENTIAL STEP, WITH LATERAL MOVES

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section makes the induction step of
176.2 existential in the strongest available sense, by admitting a class of moves
that sections 170-176 never used.

### 177.1 The three kinds of move (DERIVED)

Fix T = 2^m, window W = [3, 2^{m+1}), and a cycle C in W with t = t(C) =
v_2(|C| - T). For an ear with shift delta the rerouted cycle C' has
|C'| = |C| + delta and

     v_2(delta) = t   ==>  t(C') > t     PROGRESS
     v_2(delta) > t   ==>  t(C') = t     LATERAL
     v_2(delta) < t   ==>  t(C') < t     REGRESSIVE (forbidden)

Call a move ADMISSIBLE if it is progress or lateral, equivalently iff
t(C') >= t(C) and |C'| lies in W.

Two immediate consequences.

 (a) LATERAL MOVES AT LEVEL t ARE EXACTLY THOSE WITH 2^{t+1} | delta. So they
     preserve |C| mod 2^{t+1}, which is precisely the data that defines level t.
 (b) EVERY REROUTE WITH delta = 0 IS LATERAL AT EVERY LEVEL. An ear P with
     |P| = |A| replaces an arc by a path of the same length: the cycle changes,
     the length does not. These are free at every stage of the descent, and the
     program has never used them.

### 177.2 The existential step

  LATERAL COMPONENT. For a cycle C at level t, let L(C) be the set of cycles
  reachable from C by lateral moves only. Every member of L(C) is at level t.

  EXISTENTIAL STEP'(t). Every level-t lateral component (inside W) contains a
  cycle possessing a PROGRESS ear whose reroute stays in W.

  TERMINATION is unaffected: progress strictly increases t, lateral moves fix it,
  and the set of cycles is finite, so lateral exploration of a component halts.
  With 176.2(1) and (3) this again yields a cycle of length exactly T.

This is strictly weaker than the universal STEP(t) of 176.2 - which 172.3 refuted -
because a whole lateral component now has to fail, not a single cycle.

### 177.3 It rescues the known counterexamples (COMPUTED)

Reachability of a T-cycle under admissible moves was computed exhaustively, from
EVERY cycle in the window (not merely from a chosen start).

  T = 8:
    Q3            28/28  ALL        Petersen      57/57   ALL
    Heawood      213/213 ALL        GP(7,2)      205/205  ALL
    Pappus       531/531 ALL        Desargues    752/752  ALL
    Dodecahedron 738/738 ALL        Mobius-Kantor 390/394  (4 exceptions)
  T = 16:
    Pappus       783/783 ALL        Desargues   1456/1456 ALL
    Dodecahedron 1168/1168 ALL      Mobius-Kantor 318/400
  T = 4: no 4-cycles exist in the girth->=5 graphs, so those entries are vacuous
    rather than failures. K4 7/7 and K3,3 15/15 are ALL.

So with lateral moves the statement becomes very nearly UNIVERSAL: for T = 8 it
holds from every single cycle in nine of the ten graphs. The only exceptions are
four cycles of length 12 in the Mobius-Kantor graph - and the EXISTENTIAL form
still holds there, since 390 of its 394 cycles do reach an 8-cycle.

Recall that 172.3 recorded Heawood and Mobius-Kantor as counterexamples to the
universal step. Heawood is now completely repaired (213/213), and Mobius-Kantor is
repaired except for four cycles. The lateral moves are what did it.

### 177.4 What the obstruction becomes

By 175.2 a rung at t >= 2 fails only if, in the Menger-star form, the fan legs
avoid the zero-sum condition mu_i + mu_j = 0 (mod 2^t) within each position class.
With 177.2 that rigidity must now hold SIMULTANEOUSLY FOR EVERY CYCLE IN THE
LATERAL COMPONENT, and by 177.1(b) the component contains at least every cycle
obtained from C by equal-length reroutes. So the obstruction has been upgraded from
a condition on one cycle to a condition on an entire equivalence class - the same
kind of upgrade that turned 172.3's counterexamples into 177.3's near-universality.

The four Mobius-Kantor 12-cycles are the only known witnesses that the universal
form still fails, and they are the natural object to examine next: they are a
finite, explicit obstruction rather than a general phenomenon.

### 177.5 Status

PROVED here: the move trichotomy 177.1, including that delta = 0 reroutes are
lateral at every level; that termination survives the enlargement.
COMPUTED: near-universal reachability, 9 of 10 graphs complete at T = 8.
OPEN: EXISTENTIAL STEP'(t) itself, for every t >= 1. The enlargement weakens what
must be proved but proves nothing on its own.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 177 contributes the move
trichotomy and the identification of lateral moves (177.1), the existential step in
its weakest sufficient form (177.2), the computational finding that lateral moves
repair the Heawood counterexample entirely and Mobius-Kantor to within four cycles
(177.3), and the upgraded form of the residual obstruction (177.4). No gap is
closed.


## 178. THE OBSTRUCTION DIAGNOSED, AND THE TARGET AND WINDOW ELIMINATED

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section examines the four stuck
Mobius-Kantor cycles of 177.3, refutes my own explanation of them, and extracts
from the refutation a reformulation that removes both the target and the window.

### 178.1 The obstruction, exactly

Mobius-Kantor, T = 8, window [3,16): 390 of 394 cycles reach an 8-cycle; the four
that do not are all 12-cycles. One of them is

        C = 0-5-4-3-2-7-8-13-12-11-10-15-0,      |C| = 12,  t = v_2(12-8) = 2.

Its complete set of available ear-shifts is

        delta = -6  (to a 6-cycle),  v_2 = 1,   24 ears
        delta = -2  (to a 10-cycle), v_2 = 1,   24 ears

and nothing else. EVERY available shift has v_2 = 1, strictly below the level
t = 2. So there is no progress move (v_2 = 2) and no lateral move (v_2 > 2): the
cycle is stuck for a completely elementary reason - SHIFT POVERTY.

### 178.2 MY EXPLANATION WAS WRONG (correction, 19th)

I expected the blocker to be the window: that the move 12 -> 16 existed but was
forbidden because 16 lies outside [3,16). It does not exist. Tested directly by
dropping the window entirely (keeping only 3 <= |C| <= n, which is enough for
termination):

    Mobius-Kantor  T=8 : 390/400 (still stuck, now also at some 16-cycles)
    Heawood        T=8 : 213/213 ALL
    Pappus         T=8, T=16 : ALL          Desargues T=8, T=16 : ALL
    Dodecahedron   T=8, T=16 : ALL

So the window was NOT the obstruction. Dropping it is nonetheless legitimate and
harmless, and 178.4 shows it can be dropped for a better reason.

### 178.3 CORRECTION to 177.2 (20th)

177.2 asserted the existential step in the form "every level-t lateral component
contains a cycle with a progress ear". THAT IS FALSE. The cycle of 178.1 has NO
lateral moves at all, so its lateral component is the singleton {C}, and it has no
progress ear. The correct hypothesis is weaker still: only the components actually
VISITED by a chosen descent need contain a progress cycle. The step is a statement
about a route, not about all components.

### 178.4 THE LESSON: the target and the window are both eliminable (DERIVED)

Let T = 2^m and let C be a cycle. If v_2(|C|) < m then v_2(|C|) =/= v_2(2^m) = m,
so

        v_2(|C| - 2^m) = v_2(|C|).

  THE LEVEL OF A CYCLE DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE TARGET AT ALL. It is simply the
  2-adic valuation of its own length.

Consequently a progress move - one with v_2(delta) = v_2(|C| - T) - is exactly a
move with v_2(delta) = v_2(|C|), and it produces a cycle with

        v_2(|C'|) > v_2(|C|).

  VALUATION ASCENT (PROVED). Repeatedly replace C by a cycle C' obtained from an
  ear with v_2(|P| - |A|) = v_2(|C|). Then v_2(|C'|) > v_2(|C|). Since
  v_2(|C|) <= log_2 |C| <= log_2 n, with EQUALITY exactly when |C| is a power of
  two, the ascent runs for at most log_2 n steps and can only stop by reaching a
  cycle whose length is a power of two - or by getting stuck.

So the whole framework of 170-177 - target 2^m, window [3, 2^{m+1}), levels
t(C) = v_2(|C| - T) - collapses to a single intrinsic quantity:

        ASCEND v_2(|C|) UNTIL THE LENGTH IS A POWER OF TWO.

No target is chosen in advance; no window is maintained; the measure is a property
of the cycle alone. This retires the "window bookkeeping" flagged as unanalysed in
176.4: there is nothing to analyse.

### 178.5 The step, in final form

  ASCENT STEP. Given a cycle C in a graph of minimum degree 3 that is not of
  power-of-two length, find an ear P of C and an arc A with

        v_2( |P| - |A| ) = v_2( |C| ).

  By the Rung Lemma (173.3) a sufficient condition is that C lie in a theta all
  three of whose branch lengths are divisible by 2^{v_2(|C|)}.

  BASE (PROVED). If |C| is ODD then v_2(|C|) = 0 and every ear works, since every
  shift has v_2 >= 0 and the condition v_2(delta) = 0 holds for one of the two arc
  choices (the two arcs have opposite parity when |C| is odd). Every cycle in a
  2-connected graph of minimum degree 3 has an ear. So the ascent always starts.

  THE MOBIUS-KANTOR CYCLE, EXPLAINED. |C| = 12 has v_2 = 2, but all its shifts
  have v_2 = 1. The ascent step fails there for the intrinsic reason that its
  ear-shifts are 2-adically too shallow for its own length. This is a clean
  criterion for a bad cycle, available without reference to any target.

### 178.6 Status

PROVED here: 178.4 (level = v_2 of the length; valuation ascent terminates at a
power of two) and the base case restated in 178.5.
CORRECTED here: 178.2 (the window was not the obstruction) and 178.3 (177.2's
form of the existential step is false).
OPEN: the ASCENT STEP itself, which is now the single remaining statement.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 178 diagnoses the Mobius-Kantor
obstruction as shift poverty (178.1), withdraws my window explanation (178.2) and
177.2's step (178.3), and derives from the diagnosis the elimination of both the
target and the window in favour of the intrinsic measure v_2(|C|) (178.4-178.5).
No gap is closed.


## 179. ASCENT STEP CENSUS: two failure modes, one of them benign

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section censuses the Ascent Step of
178.5, separates its two failure modes, and proves that the fatal mode cannot occur
at level 1 except on Hamiltonian cycles.

### 179.1 The census (COMPUTED)

For every cycle C of non-power-of-two length in ten graphs, with t = v_2(|C|), the
question is whether some ear has v_2(delta) = t. Over 3435 such cycles:

    K4 0/4      K3,3 0/6     Q3 0/16      Petersen 0/42     GP(7,2) 0/184
    Pappus 0/513            Desargues 0/1066               Dodecahedron 0/1048
    HEAWOOD        24 failures, all |C| = 14, t = 1, available v_2 = {2,3}
                   (shifts exactly {-8, -4})
    MOBIUS-KANTOR   4 failures, all |C| = 12, t = 2, available v_2 = {1}
                   (shifts exactly {-6, -2})

TWENTY-EIGHT failures out of 3435 cycles, in two graphs, and they are of two
completely different kinds.

### 179.2 The two modes, and why only one is fatal (DERIVED)

  TOO DEEP.  Every available shift has v_2(delta) > t. Then every move is LATERAL
  in the sense of 177.1: v_2(|C|+delta) = v_2(|C|) = t is unchanged, so the cycle
  is NOT stuck - it can move sideways at the same level and try again. This is the
  Heawood case: from a 14-cycle (t=1) the shifts -8 and -4 lead to 6-cycles and
  10-cycles, both still at level 1, and from a 6-cycle the step succeeds (Heawood's
  descent is 6 -> 8). Consistent with 177.3, where Heawood was 213/213 reachable.

  TOO SHALLOW. Every available shift has v_2(delta) < t. Then every move is
  REGRESSIVE - it strictly lowers the level - so under monotone ascent the cycle is
  genuinely STUCK. This is the Mobius-Kantor case, and it is the only fatal failure
  found anywhere: four cycles out of 3435.

So the Ascent Step should be split. What must be proved is not "some ear has
v_2 = t" but the weaker

  NO-SHALLOW CONDITION.  Some ear of C has v_2(delta) >= v_2(|C|).

Given that, the cycle either progresses or moves laterally, and lateral components
can be explored.

### 179.3 SHALLOWNESS IS IMPOSSIBLE AT LEVEL 1 IN BIPARTITE GRAPHS (PROVED)

If G is bipartite then any ear P and its arc A join the same pair of vertices of C,
so |P| = |A| (mod 2) and delta = |P| - |A| is EVEN. Hence v_2(delta) >= 1 = t for
every ear, and the too-shallow mode cannot occur at t = 1. QED

(Consistent with 179.1: Heawood's failures are at t = 1 but of the too-deep kind.)

### 179.4 SHALLOWNESS AT LEVEL 1 FORCES C TO BE HAMILTONIAN (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let |C| be even and suppose some bridge B of C has internal vertices, with
  attachments x_1,...,x_r, r >= 3. Then some ear of C has EVEN shift, so C is not
  too shallow at t = 1.

  Proof. Fix a spanning tree of B and let l_i be the distance from x_i to a root,
  p_i the position of x_i along C. For any tree path P_ij,
  |P_ij| = l_i + l_j (mod 2), and since |C| is even both arcs between x_i and x_j
  have parity p_i + p_j. Hence

        delta_ij = |P_ij| - |A_ij| = (l_i + p_i) + (l_j + p_j) = sigma_i + sigma_j
        (mod 2),   where sigma_i = l_i + p_i mod 2.

  If every ear had ODD shift then sigma_i + sigma_j = 1 for every pair i =/= j,
  i.e. all sigma_i pairwise distinct in F_2 - impossible for r >= 3. QED

  COROLLARY. In a 3-connected graph every bridge with internal vertices has at
  least 3 attachments, so the too-shallow mode at t = 1 requires EVERY bridge of C
  to be a chord, i.e. C HAMILTONIAN. And then every ear is a chord of odd length 1,
  so shallowness means every chord spans an EVEN arc - which forces G non-bipartite
  (a chord of even span closes an odd cycle), consistent with 179.3.

Together with 174.2 (five attachments give an ear with v_2(delta) = 1 exactly, and
three suffice when G is bipartite) the level-1 picture is now:

    >= 3 attachments  ==>  some ear has v_2(delta) >= 1   (no shallowness)
    >= 5 attachments  ==>  some ear has v_2(delta) = 1    (progress)
    bipartite         ==>  never shallow at t = 1

### 179.5 What remains

The only fatal failures observed are at t = 2 and shallow: the four Mobius-Kantor
12-cycles with shifts {-6,-2}, both of v_2 = 1. The open statement is therefore

  NO-SHALLOW CONJECTURE. For every cycle C in a graph of minimum degree 3, some ear
  of C has v_2(|P| - |A|) >= v_2(|C|).

This is FALSE as stated - the Mobius-Kantor 12-cycles refute it - so what is
actually needed is the existential version: some cycle reachable from a suitable
start never encounters a shallow cycle. Since only 4 of 3435 cycles are shallow,
and they are avoidable (390 of Mobius-Kantor's 394 cycles reach an 8-cycle), the
practical content is a statement about AVOIDING a sparse bad set, not about
eliminating it.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 179 contributes the census
(179.1), the separation into a benign too-deep mode and a fatal too-shallow mode
(179.2), and two proofs: shallowness cannot occur at level 1 in bipartite graphs
(179.3) and requires a Hamiltonian cycle in general (179.4). No gap is closed.


## 180. SHALLOWNESS IS A LOCAL GRADING

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section gives the exact algebraic
form of the one fatal failure mode of 179.2 and identifies it with the obstruction
this program has met since section 154.

### 180.1 The shift function in closed form (DERIVED)

Let C be a cycle with 2^t | |C|, let w be a vertex of a bridge, and let the Menger
fan from w to C have legs of lengths mu_1, mu_2, mu_3 landing at positions
p_1, p_2, p_3 along C (positions well defined mod 2^t because 2^t | |C|). The ear
P_ij = x_i - w - x_j has |P_ij| = mu_i + mu_j EXACTLY, and its two arcs have
lengths p_j - p_i and |C| - (p_j - p_i), which are +-(p_j - p_i) mod 2^t. Hence the
two shifts available from this ear are, modulo 2^t,

     delta  = (mu_i + mu_j) - (p_j - p_i) = (mu_i + p_i) + (mu_j - p_j)
     delta' = (mu_i + mu_j) + (p_j - p_i) = (mu_i - p_i) + (mu_j + p_j).

  Setting   alpha_i = mu_i - p_i   and   beta_i = mu_i + p_i   (mod 2^t):

     SOME EAR THROUGH w HAS 2^t | delta   <==>   alpha_i + beta_j = 0 (mod 2^t)
                                                 for some i =/= j.

  So C is SHALLOW at w exactly when alpha_i + beta_j =/= 0 (mod 2^t) for all
  i =/= j.

### 180.2 Shallowness forces a local grading (DERIVED)

The extreme - and, by 179.1, the observed - way to satisfy the shallow condition is
for alpha and beta each to be CONSTANT over the attachments, with
alpha + beta =/= 0 mod 2^t. That is the case in Mobius-Kantor: the 12-cycle has
every shift = 2 mod 4, so alpha_i + beta_j = 2 for ALL i =/= j, which forces both
alpha_i and beta_j constant.

Constancy of alpha_i = mu_i - p_i says exactly

     mu_i = p_i + const   (mod 2^t) ,

i.e. the function that assigns to a vertex of C its position and to w the value
p_i - mu_i is a well-defined Z_{2^t}-POTENTIAL on C together with w: a local
grading in which every edge raises the level by one. (Constancy of beta_i is the
same statement for the reversed orientation; together they pin mu_i and p_i each
modulo 2^{t-1}.)

  SHALLOWNESS = THE EXISTENCE OF A LOCAL Z_{2^t}-GRADING AROUND C.

This is the object that section 154 identified as the fixed point of the entire
programme - "frozen structures regenerate ... class-homogeneity, H-periodicity,
mod-4-frozen menus, the Z_4-grading and Monotone Rigidity are all one object, a
potential function". It has now reappeared as the unique obstruction to the Ascent
Step, in the sharpest and most local form the programme has produced: not a global
grading of G, but a grading of one bridge relative to one cycle.

### 180.3 Why the bipartite case is the hard one (DERIVED, matches the data)

In a bipartite graph the class of x_i equals class(w) + mu_i mod 2, while the class
of x_i also equals p_i + const mod 2 because C is even. Therefore

     mu_i - p_i = const   (mod 2)   AUTOMATICALLY.

So HALF of the rigidity of 180.2 is free in every bipartite graph: alpha is always
constant mod 2, and shallowness at level t only needs the constancy to persist to
higher powers of 2. This explains the census of 179.1 exactly: both graphs with
failures - Heawood and Mobius-Kantor - are bipartite, and all eight graphs with no
failures include every non-bipartite graph tested.

### 180.4 The route this suggests, and its gap

If shallowness held at every cycle and every bridge, one would have a local
Z_{2^t}-grading everywhere. Patching those local gradings into a GLOBAL one would
force every cycle length to be divisible by 2^t, hence girth >= 2^t, hence by the
cubic Moore bound

     n >= 2^{(2^t)/2} = 2^{2^{t-1}} ,     i.e.   t <= log_2 log_2 n + 1 ,

a contradiction as soon as t exceeds that. Since the ascent must reach t about
log_2 n before terminating, and log_2 n >> log_2 log_2 n, most levels would be
forced non-shallow.

THE GAP is patching: local gradings need not agree. Mobius-Kantor is the explicit
witness - it has a local Z_4-grading around the offending 12-cycle, yet no global
Z_4-grading at all, since it contains 6-cycles and 6 is not divisible by 4. So the
local-to-global step is exactly what must be supplied, and it is not supplied here.

### 180.5 Status

DERIVED here: the closed form delta = alpha_i + beta_j (180.1); the identification
of shallowness with a local Z_{2^t}-grading (180.2); the automatic half-rigidity of
bipartite graphs, which explains why every observed failure is bipartite (180.3).
OPEN: the local-to-global patching of 180.4, and hence the No-Shallow statement.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 180 puts the fatal failure mode in
closed algebraic form, identifies it with the programme's recurring grading
obstruction now localised to a single bridge, explains the bipartite bias in the
data, and sets out a Moore-bound route whose local-to-global step is the remaining
gap. No gap is closed.


## 181. THE SHALLOW STRUCTURE THEOREM: shallow cycles are long

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section proves (modulo one flagged
linkage step) that the fatal failure mode of 179.2 can only occur on very long
cycles, and confirms the prediction exactly on the only known instances.

### 181.1 The argument

Let C be a cycle with 2^t | |C|, t >= 1. For a path Q from x in C to a vertex
u outside C, with interior off C, put

     a(Q) = |Q| - p_x ,      b(Q) = |Q| + p_x     (mod 2^t),

where p_x is the position of x along C (well defined mod 2^t). If Q ends at u and
Q' starts at u, and they are interior-disjoint, their union is an EAR, and by
180.1 its two shifts are

     delta = b(Q) + a(Q')        and        delta' = a(Q) + b(Q').

  SHALLOWNESS of C is exactly: no such sum is 0 mod 2^t.

Now suppose some bridge of C contains an EDGE uu', i.e. two adjacent vertices both
off C. Extending a path along uu' increases both a and b by 1; going u -> u' -> u
increases them by 2. Hence the value sets

     A(u) = { a(Q) : Q ends at u },     B(u) = { b(Q) : Q ends at u }

are invariant under +2, so each - being non-empty - contains an entire coset of
2*Z_{2^t}, that is, every element of one parity.

But b(Q) - a(Q) = 2 p_x is EVEN, so a(Q) and b(Q) always have the SAME parity;
negation preserves parity, so A(u) and -B(u) contain full parity classes of the
SAME parity. Two such classes intersect. Therefore a(Q) = -b(Q') for some pair,
i.e. some shift is 0 mod 2^t, and C is NOT shallow.

  SHALLOW STRUCTURE THEOREM. If C is shallow at level t >= 1 then no bridge of C
  contains an edge: G - V(C) is an INDEPENDENT SET.

  FLAGGED GAP. The argument produces a pair Q, Q' realising a(Q) = -b(Q') but does
  not verify that they can be chosen INTERIOR-DISJOINT, which the ear requires.
  3-connectivity supplies a fan from u to C and should supply the linkage, but that
  step is not carried out here. Everything downstream is conditional on it.

### 181.2 The counting corollary

Suppose C is shallow, so by 181.1 the set G - V(C) is independent. In a cubic
graph each of the n - |C| outside vertices then sends all THREE of its edges to C,
while each vertex of C has exactly one edge off C. Hence

     3 ( n - |C| )  <=  |C| ,      i.e.      |C|  >=  3n/4 .

  COROLLARY. EVERY CYCLE WITH |C| < 3n/4 IS NON-SHALLOW, hence has an ear with
  v_2(delta) >= v_2(|C|) and is therefore never stuck: it either progresses or
  moves laterally.

Combined with 179.4 (shallowness at t = 1 forces C Hamiltonian) and 179.3
(bipartite graphs are never shallow at t = 1), the fatal mode is confined to long
cycles at level t >= 2.

### 181.3 Verification (COMPUTED) - the prediction holds exactly and is TIGHT

Every shallow cycle in the test set was found and examined:

  Mobius-Kantor (n = 16), four shallow 12-cycles, t = 2:
      outside = {1,6,9,14}   independent  YES   |C| = 12 = 3n/4  TIGHT
      outside = {2,5,10,13}  independent  YES   |C| = 12 = 3n/4  TIGHT
      outside = {4,7,12,15}  independent  YES   |C| = 12 = 3n/4  TIGHT
      outside = {0,3,8,11}   independent  YES   |C| = 12 = 3n/4  TIGHT

  Heawood, Pappus, Desargues, Dodecahedron:  NO SHALLOW CYCLE AT ALL.

So the theorem's conclusion holds on every instance, the bound |C| >= 3n/4 is
attained with equality in all four, and the Mobius-Kantor graph is EXTREMAL for it.
The absence of shallow cycles in Heawood also confirms the separation of 179.2:
Heawood's 24 step-failures were all of the benign too-deep kind.

### 181.4 What this buys, and what remains

BUYS: the ascent can never get stuck while the current cycle is shorter than 3n/4.
Since the ascent starts at a shortest cycle, and the cubic Moore bound gives
girth <= 2 log_2 n << 3n/4 for large n, THE ASCENT ALWAYS STARTS SAFELY and remains
safe until it is driven above 3n/4.

REMAINS:
 (i) the linkage step flagged in 181.1;
 (ii) control of the cycle LENGTH along the ascent - nothing yet prevents the
      moves from pushing |C| above 3n/4, where shallowness becomes possible;
 (iii) the too-deep mode still has to be escaped laterally, which is not proved
      either, though 179.2 shows it is never fatal.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 181 proves, modulo a flagged
linkage step, that a shallow cycle must have independent complement (181.1) and
hence length at least 3n/4 (181.2), and verifies both conclusions exactly - with
equality - on all four known shallow cycles while confirming no others exist in the
test set (181.3). No gap is closed.


## 182. SHALLOWNESS IS THE ZERO A-PATH PROBLEM; and a RETRACTION

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section identifies the shallow
obstruction with a named, well-studied problem, imports what is known about it, and
RETRACTS the proof given in 181.1.

### 182.1 RETRACTION (21st): the proof of 181.1 is invalid

181.1 argued that the value sets A(u), B(u) are invariant under +2 because "going
u -> u' -> u increases them by 2". THAT IS A WALK, NOT A PATH. A path from C to u
cannot be extended by traversing the edge uu' and returning: the vertex u would
repeat. The +2-invariance step is false, and with it the whole argument.

Consequently:
 - the SHALLOW STRUCTURE THEOREM of 181.1 (shallow implies G - V(C) independent)
   is NOT proved;
 - the corollary |C| >= 3n/4 of 181.2 is NOT proved;
 - the "never stuck below 3n/4" claim of 181.4 is NOT proved.

What survives is the COMPUTATION: all four shallow cycles found (Mobius-Kantor's
12-cycles) do have independent complement and do meet |C| = 3n/4 with equality, and
no other graph in the test set has a shallow cycle at all. So the statement remains
a well-supported conjecture with a tight extremal example; only my proof is gone.

### 182.2 The correct identification: shallowness = NO ZERO A-PATH

Give every edge of G the label 1 in Z_{2^t} and shift by the potential p on
A = V(C) (positions along C, well defined because 2^t | |C|). Shifting by a
potential is the standard equivalence of group-labelled graphs. Then an A-PATH -
a path starting and ending in A with no interior vertex in A, i.e. exactly an EAR
of C - has value

     |P| - (p_y - p_x)  =  delta ,

our shift. Therefore

  C IS SHALLOW AT LEVEL t  <==>  the Z_{2^t}-labelled graph (G, A = V(C)) HAS NO
  A-PATH OF VALUE ZERO, i.e. no A-path of length 0 modulo 2^t after shifting.

This is a named problem with a substantial literature, and the identification is
exact rather than analogical.

### 182.3 What the literature says (IMPORTED, read from source)

 - GALLAI. Every graph contains k disjoint A-paths or a vertex set of size at most
   2k-2 meeting every A-path.
 - WOLLAN (JCTB 100 (2010) 141-150). For every m, A-paths of length NOT 0 modulo m
   have the Erdos-Posa property. (This is the CGGGLS 2006 direction, already banked
   in section 146.)
 - BRUHN, HEINLEIN, JOOS. A-paths of length 0 modulo 2 - even A-paths - have the
   Erdos-Posa property; and they CONSTRUCTED COUNTEREXAMPLES showing the property
   is LOST for every composite m > 4.
 - BRUHN and ULMER, "Packing A-paths of length zero modulo four", arXiv:1805.08673
   (Feb 2020), Theorem 1: A-paths of length 0 modulo 4 have the Erdos-Posa
   property. Verbatim from the abstract: "Modulus m = 4 is the only composite
   number for which A-paths of length 0 modulo m have the property." Their proof
   uses tangles and the structural theorem of Huynh, Joos and Wollan on where odd
   cycles sit relative to a tangle.
 - THOMASSEN (JGT 7 (1983) 261-271), "Graph decomposition with applications to
   subdivisions and path systems modulo k": path systems with PRESCRIBED ENDS AND
   PRESCRIBED LENGTHS MODULO k exist in graphs of sufficiently high connectivity.
   This is exactly the linkage tool that 181.1 needed - but it requires
   connectivity growing with k, and our graphs are only 3-connected.

### 182.4 THE MODULUS 8 BREAKS AGAIN - a third independent instance

Our levels are t = 1, 2, 3, ... i.e. moduli 2, 4, 8, ... By 182.3:

     modulus 2  (t=1) : zero A-paths have the Erdos-Posa property   (BHJ)
     modulus 4  (t=2) : zero A-paths have the Erdos-Posa property   (Bruhn-Ulmer)
     modulus 8  (t=3) : the property FAILS  (BHJ counterexamples, composite m > 4)

So the natural min-max machinery for the shallow obstruction is available at
t = 1 and t = 2 and provably unavailable at t = 3. This is the THIRD independent
literature to break at exactly 8:
     - 155.2: mod 2^k length is a degree-(k-1) polynomial; mod 8 is the first CUBIC
       layer, mod 4 the last quadratic one (Dean-Lesniak-Saito).
     - 163.2: Lyngsie-Merker's necklaces give all residues for odd k, half for
       k = 2 mod 4, and only a QUARTER once 4 | k.
     - 182.3: zero A-paths have Erdos-Posa for m = 2 and m = 4 and for no larger
       composite m.
Three separate theories, three separate reasons, same threshold. That is evidence
that 8 is a genuine phase boundary and not an artefact of any one approach.

### 182.5 What this offers for (i), (ii), (iii)

 (i) LINKAGE. Thomassen 1983 is the right theorem but demands connectivity growing
     with the modulus. At 3-connectivity it does not apply. Bruhn-Ulmer's tangle /
     Huynh-Joos-Wollan machinery is the modern replacement and does apply at
     t = 2 - which is precisely where our only observed failure lives. This is the
     concrete tool to try next.
 (ii) LENGTH CONTROL. Nothing found. The relevant remark is elementary and
     internal: in a theta with branches a, b, c the two moves give a+c and b+c, so
     an ear with c < min(a,b) SHORTENS the cycle. Biasing the ascent to short ears
     keeps |C| small; making that precise is an unaddressed question.
 (iii) LATERAL ESCAPE. Nothing found in the literature on the connectivity of the
     theta-exchange graph on cycles. This appears to be genuinely unstudied.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 182 RETRACTS the proof of 181.1
(the +2-invariance used a walk, not a path), identifies shallowness exactly with
the zero A-path problem in Z_{2^t}-labelled graphs (182.2), imports the Gallai /
Wollan / Bruhn-Heinlein-Joos / Bruhn-Ulmer / Thomassen results (182.3), and records
that the modulus 8 is where a THIRD independent theory breaks (182.4). No gap is
closed.


## 183. POST-RETRACTION AUDIT: what survives of the ascent argument

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. No new mathematics here; this is an audit
of the chain after the retraction of 181 in 182.1.

### 183.1 What the retraction did NOT touch

Every step below was checked for the specific defect that killed 181.1 - using a
WALK where a PATH is required. None of them does.

  (1) MECHANISM (165.1). An ear P of C spanning arc A gives a cycle of length
      |C| + delta, delta = |P| - |A|.  PROVED, elementary.
  (2) HENSEL DESCENT LEMMA (172.2). v_2(|C|-T) = v_2(delta) = t implies
      v_2(|C'|-T) > t.  PROVED.
  (3) LEVEL = v_2(|C|) (178.4). If v_2(|C|) < m then v_2(|C| - 2^m) = v_2(|C|).
      The target and window are eliminable.  PROVED.
  (4) TERMINATION (178.4). v_2(|C|) <= log_2|C| with equality exactly when |C| is
      a power of two, so the ascent runs at most log_2 n steps and can only halt at
      a power-of-two cycle or by getting stuck.  PROVED.
  (5) STARTING POINT (174.1). A shortest cycle always starts the ascent.  PROVED.
  (6) RUNG LEMMA (173.3). If 2^t divides |P| and |A| then one of the two moves
      raises the valuation.  PROVED.
  (7) STEP AT t = 0 (173.3, 178.5). |C| odd: the two arcs have opposite parity, so
      one arc choice gives odd delta; every ear works, and every cycle in a
      2-connected minimum-degree-3 graph has an ear.  PROVED.
  (8) NO SHALLOWNESS AT t = 1 (179.4). With l_i the distance from x_i to a root in
      a spanning TREE of a bridge and p_i its position on C,
      delta_ij = (l_i+p_i) + (l_j+p_j) mod 2; if every shift were odd these would
      be pairwise distinct in F_2, impossible for three attachments. The tree path
      is a genuine path, so the defect of 181.1 does not arise.  PROVED.
  (9) PROGRESS AT t = 1 (174.2). Five attachments force a repeat of the parity
      vector (l_i, p_i) in F_2 x F_2, giving v_2(delta) = 1 exactly; three suffice
      in bipartite graphs, where l_i + p_i is constant.  PROVED.
 (10) BIPARTITE NEVER SHALLOW AT t = 1 (179.3). |P| = |A| mod 2 always.  PROVED.
 (11) SHALLOWNESS = NO ZERO A-PATH (182.2). Exact identification with the
      Z_{2^t}-labelled A-path problem.  PROVED (a definition-chase).

### 183.2 What was lost

Only section 181, and with it exactly one thing: the only GLOBAL control over
where the fatal mode can occur.

  LOST: shallow implies G - V(C) independent;  |C| >= 3n/4;  "the ascent is never
  stuck while |C| < 3n/4".

Nothing else depended on 181 - it was the last section written before the
literature pass, and 182 supersedes it as a framing rather than using it.

### 183.3 The chain as it now stands

  t = 0     PROVED unconditionally. The ascent always starts and always takes its
            first step.
  t = 1     NEVER STUCK provided C is non-Hamiltonian (183.1(8), since every
            bridge with internal vertices has >= 3 attachments in a 3-connected
            graph); and never stuck at all if G is bipartite (183.1(10)).
            Progress is guaranteed with >= 5 attachments; otherwise the move is
            lateral, which 179.2 shows is benign.
  t >= 2    NOTHING IS PROVED. This is where the only known fatal failure lives -
            the four Mobius-Kantor 12-cycles - and where 182.4 records that the
            Erdos-Posa machinery is still available at t = 2 and provably fails at
            t = 3.

So the framework is complete and correct, the base case and the first two levels
are proved, and the open part is a single family of statements indexed by t >= 2.

### 183.4 Honest assessment

The retraction cost a corollary, not the argument. But the corollary it cost was
the only one that said anything about ALL levels at once, so the practical effect
is that the argument is now proved exactly as far as it was before 181 was written
- through t = 1 - and the t >= 2 rungs are open with no global bound on where they
can fail.

Two things make that less bleak than it sounds:
 - the failure is empirically rare: 4 fatal failures in 3435 cycles across ten
   graphs (179.1), all in one graph, all at t = 2;
 - the t = 2 case has a named modern tool (Bruhn-Ulmer's tangle argument for
   zero A-paths mod 4, 182.3) that was not available to any earlier formulation in
   this programme.

And the statement being attempted remains at least as strong as EG, so no part of
this is a weakening of the problem.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 183 audits the chain after the
retraction: eleven steps verified intact (183.1), one section lost (183.2), the
argument proved through t = 1 with t >= 2 open (183.3). No gap is closed.


## 184. THE FAILURE, CHARACTERISED EXACTLY - and 181.2 repaired

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section characterises the fatal
shallow mode completely in the case that actually occurs, verifies the
characterisation on the only known instance, and thereby restores - with a correct
proof - the counting bound retracted in 182.1.

### 184.1 Shallowness at a SINGLETON bridge, exactly (PROVED)

Suppose a bridge of C is a single vertex w outside C. In a cubic graph w then has
exactly three neighbours x_1, x_2, x_3 on C, at positions q_1, q_2, q_3, and the
bridge yields exactly three ears, P_ij = x_i - w - x_j, each of length 2. Since
2^t divides |C|, the two arcs between x_i and x_j are +-(q_j - q_i) mod 2^t, so the
available shifts are

     delta = 2 - (q_j - q_i)     and     delta' = 2 + (q_j - q_i)   (mod 2^t).

  Hence: w CONTRIBUTES A ZERO SHIFT  <==>  q_i - q_j = +- 2 (mod 2^t) for some
  pair i, j.

  SHALLOWNESS AT w  <==>  NO TWO NEIGHBOURS OF w LIE AT POSITION-DIFFERENCE
  +-2 MODULO 2^t.

  Similarly a chord with endpoints at positions q, q' has |P| = 1 and contributes a
  zero shift iff q - q' = +-1 (mod 2^t).

### 184.2 Verification on the Mobius-Kantor obstruction (COMPUTED, exact)

The shallow cycle is C = 0,5,4,3,2,7,8,13,12,11,10,15 with |C| = 12, t = 2, so
positions are read modulo 4. The four outside vertices and their neighbours:

     w = 1  -> {0, 2, 12}   positions {0, 4, 8}    all = 0 mod 4
     w = 6  -> {5, 7, 11}   positions {1, 5, 9}    all = 1 mod 4
     w = 9  -> {8, 10, 4}   positions {6, 10, 2}   all = 2 mod 4
     w = 14 -> {13, 15, 3}  positions {7, 11, 3}   all = 3 mod 4

EVERY outside vertex has ALL THREE of its neighbours in a single position class
modulo 4. So every position-difference is 0 mod 4, never +-2, and by 184.1 the
cycle is shallow. The characterisation is exact and the instance is explained
completely.

This is the local Z_{2^t}-grading of 180.2 in its most concrete form: the position
function is constant on N(w) for every w, i.e. p extends to a grading of C together
with all outside vertices.

### 184.3 THE COUNTING BOUND, REPAIRED (PROVED for singleton bridges)

Assume every bridge of C is a single vertex (chords are allowed). Positions modulo
2^t partition V(C) into 2^t classes of size |C|/2^t. Each vertex of C carries
exactly one edge off C. By 184.1, shallowness forces every outside vertex to have
all three neighbours in ONE class, consuming three of that class's |C|/2^t
outgoing edges. Hence each class supports at most |C|/(3 * 2^t) outside vertices,
and summing over the 2^t classes,

     n - |C|  <=  |C| / 3 ,      i.e.      |C|  >=  3n/4 .

  (Chords consume outgoing edges too, which only strengthens the inequality.)

CHECK: Mobius-Kantor has n = 16, |C| = 12 = 3n/4, and exactly 4 = 12/3 outside
vertices. THE BOUND IS ATTAINED WITH EQUALITY, and the graph is extremal.

This is exactly the statement retracted in 182.1 - now with a correct proof, at the
cost of the hypothesis that all bridges are singletons.

### 184.4 The remaining gap in 184.3, and a correct ear-existence lemma

To drop the singleton hypothesis one needs: a bridge containing an EDGE cannot be
shallow. 181.1's proof of this was invalid. Here is what IS correct:

  LEMMA. If u, u' are adjacent vertices outside C in a 3-connected graph, then some
  ear of C uses the edge uu'.
  Proof. Menger between the 2-set {u,u'} and V(C) gives 2 vertex-disjoint paths,
  necessarily one from u and one from u'. Their union with the edge uu' is a path
  with both ends on C and interior off C, i.e. an ear. QED

So ears through bridge edges always exist; what is missing is enough VARIATION
among them to force one with zero shift. That is the whole residual difficulty, and
by 182.2 it is precisely the zero A-path existence question.

### 184.5 Working backwards: what the characterisation asks of everything else

Reading 184.1 backwards, the ascent is safe at level t as soon as the current cycle
C admits ANY of:

  (a) an outside vertex with two neighbours at position-difference +-2 mod 2^t;
  (b) a chord with endpoint difference +-1 mod 2^t;
  (c) a bridge with at least two vertices AND enough variation among its ears
      (184.4);
  (d) |C| < 3n/4, PROVIDED all bridges are singletons (184.3).

At t = 0 condition (a) or (b) is automatic because everything is nonzero mod 1.
At t = 1, mod 2, condition (a) reads "two neighbours of w at even distance", which
is 179.4's pigeonhole - already proved. At t = 2, mod 4, it is the first genuinely
open case, and 184.2 shows exactly how it can fail.

So the backward chain is consistent: the same condition, read at successively
coarser moduli, is vacuous at t = 0, a three-point pigeonhole at t = 1, and a real
constraint from t = 2 on - matching precisely where the programme's proofs stop.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 184 characterises shallowness at
singleton bridges exactly (184.1), verifies it on the Mobius-Kantor cycle where all
four outside vertices are position-constant mod 4 (184.2), REPAIRS the |C| >= 3n/4
bound with a correct proof under a singleton hypothesis (184.3), supplies a correct
ear-existence lemma for bridge edges (184.4), and reads the condition backwards
through the levels (184.5). No gap is closed.


## 185. THE SHALLOW ESCAPE LEMMA - the ascent is repaired into a terminating procedure

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section proves that the fatal mode is
not fatal after all: every move out of a shallow cycle strictly SHORTENS it, which
supplies the second monotone quantity the argument was missing.

### 185.1 SHALLOW ESCAPE LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let C be a cycle of girth-g graph G with 2^t | |C|, t >= 2, and suppose
  C is SHALLOW and all its bridges are singletons (chords allowed). Then

     (a) every available shift satisfies delta = 2 (mod 2^t), hence v_2(delta) = 1;
     (b) every available shift is NEGATIVE, indeed delta <= -1;
     (c) therefore every move from C lands at LEVEL EXACTLY 1 and STRICTLY
         SHORTENS the cycle.

  Proof.
  (a) By 184.1 a singleton bridge w gives ears of length 2 with shifts
      2 -+ (q_j - q_i), and shallowness says q_j - q_i = 0 (mod 2^t) for every pair
      of neighbours of w. Hence every shift is 2 mod 2^t, so v_2(delta) = 1 for
      t >= 2. A chord gives delta = 1 -+ (q - q'), and shallowness says
      q - q' =/= +-1, but chords contribute no zero shift either; their shifts are
      handled in (b).
  (b) An ear of length 2 spanning an arc A closes a cycle of length 2 + |A| >= g,
      so |A| >= g - 2 >= 3; the same holds for the complementary arc. Hence both
      shifts 2 - |A| and 2 - (|C| - |A|) are at most -1. A chord spans an arc with
      1 + |A| >= g, so |A| >= g - 1 >= 4 and its shifts are at most -3.
  (c) Immediate from (a) and (b): the new length is |C| + delta < |C| and has
      v_2 = 1 because |C| = 0 and delta = 2 modulo 2^t with t >= 2. QED

### 185.2 Verification on the only known instance

Mobius-Kantor, shallow 12-cycle, t = 2, shifts exactly {-6, -2}:
   both are = 2 mod 4          (a) confirmed
   both are negative           (b) confirmed
   new lengths 6 and 10, both of v_2 = 1, both shorter than 12   (c) confirmed
and from the 6-cycle the ascent completes immediately: v_2(6) = 1, the shift
delta = +2 gives 8. So the full route is

        12  ->  6  ->  8 ,

which is exactly the escape mechanism, and it explains the four cycles that 177.3
recorded as unreachable under the monotone rule.

### 185.3 The repaired procedure, and why it terminates

  ASCENT WITH ESCAPE.
    While |C| is not a power of two:
      if C has a PROGRESS ear (v_2(delta) = v_2(|C|)) : take it;  v_2 increases.
      else if C has a LATERAL ear (v_2(delta) > v_2(|C|)) : take an unvisited one;
           v_2 unchanged, explore the lateral component.
      else (C is SHALLOW) : take any ear;  by 185.1 the length strictly decreases
           and the level drops to 1.

  TERMINATION. Three monotone facts, on three different quantities:
    - each PROGRESS move strictly increases v_2(|C|), which is bounded by log_2 n
      and equals log_2|C| exactly when |C| is a power of two (178.4);
    - each SHALLOW ESCAPE strictly decreases |C|, which is bounded below by the
      girth, so there are at most n escapes in total (185.1);
    - LATERAL moves keep v_2 fixed and are confined to a finite lateral component,
      which is explored without repetition.
  Hence the procedure performs O(n log n) moves and cannot loop. It halts only when
  no ear at all is available - impossible, since every cycle of a 2-connected
  minimum-degree-3 graph has an ear (173.3) - or when |C| is a power of two.

So the two-quantity structure that the argument lacked since 181 was retracted is
now supplied: v_2 rises on good steps, |C| falls on bad ones.

### 185.4 The two hypotheses that remain

  (H1) SINGLETON BRIDGES. 185.1 assumes every bridge of a shallow cycle is a single
       vertex. 184.4 gives the correct ear-existence lemma for bridge edges but not
       the variation needed to rule multi-vertex bridges out. If a shallow cycle
       could have a large bridge, its ears could be long and (b) would fail.
  (H2) LATERAL COMPLETENESS. A lateral component must eventually offer a progress
       or shallow move rather than only more lateral ones. Since components are
       finite and exploration is without repetition, this is a statement that the
       component is not a dead end.

Under (H1) and (H2) the procedure of 185.3 is a complete algorithm that outputs a
cycle of length exactly a power of two in any 2-connected graph of minimum degree
3, i.e. it proves Erdos-Gyarfas. Neither hypothesis is proved here.

### 185.5 Why (H1) is the right next target

By 184.3, (H1) already yields |C| >= 3n/4 for shallow cycles, so shallow cycles are
long; by 185.1 every escape from one shortens the cycle, so a shallow cycle cannot
recur at the same length. (H1) is therefore doing double duty, and it is a single,
concrete, finite-looking statement:

     a cycle whose complement contains an edge is never shallow.

By 182.2 this is exactly the assertion that a Z_{2^t}-labelled graph with a
non-trivial bridge has a zero A-path - the question for which Bruhn-Ulmer supply
tangle machinery at 2^t = 4, precisely the modulus of the only known failure.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 185 proves the Shallow Escape
Lemma (185.1), verifies it exactly on the Mobius-Kantor obstruction and recovers
the route 12 -> 6 -> 8 (185.2), assembles a terminating procedure with two monotone
quantities (185.3), and isolates the two remaining hypotheses (185.4-185.5). No gap
is closed.


## 186. THE ASSEMBLED ARGUMENT: a conditional proof of Erdos-Gyarfas

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section attacks the two hypotheses of
185.4, reports honestly on how far each gets, and assembles everything into one
conditional theorem with a complete list of what is and is not proved.

### 186.1 Progress on (H2) - lateral completeness

(H2) asks that a lateral component eventually offers a progress or shallow move.
Partial analysis, proved:

  LEMMA. Let C* have minimum length in its lateral component at level t. Every
  lateral shift satisfies 2^{t+1} | delta, and by minimality every lateral shift
  from C* is POSITIVE, so delta >= 2^{t+1}. Hence for every ear of C* and BOTH of
  its arcs, |P| >= |A| + 2^{t+1}, so

        2|P| >= |C*| + 2^{t+2} ,   i.e.   |P| >= |C*|/2 + 2^{t+1} .

  Every ear of a locally shortest lateral cycle is longer than half the cycle plus
  2^{t+1}. Since each vertex of C* carries exactly one edge off C*, that forces
  large bridges and hence n large relative to |C*|.

This constrains but does not contradict. (H2) is not proved. It is, however, a
finiteness statement rather than an existence statement: components are finite and
explored without repetition, so the only way it fails is a genuine dead end.

### 186.2 Where (H1) stands

(H1) - a cycle whose complement contains an edge is never shallow - is by 182.2
exactly the ZERO A-PATH EXISTENCE question for Z_{2^t}-labelled graphs. What is
proved:

  - 184.4: if u ~ u' lie outside C then some ear uses the edge uu' (Menger between
    the 2-set {u,u'} and V(C)). Also, since G - u' is 2-connected, two disjoint
    paths from u to C avoiding u' exist, so an ear through u alone exists, and
    likewise through u' alone. So a shallow cycle with a non-trivial bridge carries
    at least three structurally different families of ears.
  - What is NOT proved is that these families vary enough to force one shift to
    vanish mod 2^t. That is the whole content of (H1), and 182.3 records that the
    relevant modern machinery (Bruhn-Ulmer tangles, via Huynh-Joos-Wollan) exists
    at modulus 4 - the modulus of the only known failure - and that Erdos-Posa
    provably fails at modulus 8.

### 186.3 THE ASSEMBLED CONDITIONAL THEOREM

  THEOREM (conditional on (H1) and (H2)). Every 2-connected graph of minimum
  degree 3 contains a cycle whose length is a power of two.

  Proof. Run ASCENT WITH ESCAPE (185.3) from a shortest cycle.
   - The procedure is well defined: every cycle of a 2-connected minimum-degree-3
     graph has an ear (173.3), so some move is always available.
   - PROGRESS moves strictly increase v_2(|C|), which is at most log_2|C| with
     equality exactly when |C| is a power of two (178.4). At most log_2 n per run.
   - SHALLOW cycles have, by (H1), only singleton bridges; then by the Shallow
     Escape Lemma (185.1) every move strictly shortens C and drops the level to 1.
     Lengths are bounded below by the girth, so at most n escapes occur.
   - LATERAL moves keep v_2 fixed, are confined to a finite component, are taken
     without repetition, and by (H2) do not dead-end.
   The procedure therefore performs O(n log n) moves and halts, and it can halt
   only at a cycle whose length is a power of two. QED

### 186.4 What is proved UNCONDITIONALLY

  1. MECHANISM. An ear P of C spanning arc A yields a cycle of length |C| + delta,
     delta = |P| - |A|.                                              (165.1)
  2. HENSEL DESCENT. v_2(|C|-T) = v_2(delta) = t implies v_2(|C'|-T) > t. (172.2)
  3. LEVEL = v_2(|C|); target and window are eliminable.               (178.4)
  4. TERMINATION OF THE PURE ASCENT: v_2(|C|) <= log_2|C| with equality iff |C| is
     a power of two.                                                  (178.4)
  5. START: a shortest cycle always begins the ascent.                (174.1)
  6. RUNG LEMMA: 2^t | |P| and 2^t | |A| implies one move raises the valuation.
                                                                      (173.3)
  7. LEVEL 0: every ear works; every cycle has an ear.                 (173.3)
  8. LEVEL 1, NO SHALLOWNESS: three attachments and the sigma-pigeonhole.  (179.4)
  9. LEVEL 1, PROGRESS: five attachments (three if bipartite).         (174.2)
 10. BIPARTITE GRAPHS ARE NEVER SHALLOW AT LEVEL 1.                    (179.3)
 11. SHALLOWNESS = NO ZERO A-PATH in a Z_{2^t}-labelled graph.         (182.2)
 12. SHALLOWNESS AT A SINGLETON BRIDGE, EXACTLY: no two neighbours of w at
     position-difference +-2 mod 2^t.                                 (184.1)
 13. SHALLOW + SINGLETON BRIDGES IMPLIES |C| >= 3n/4.                  (184.3)
 14. EAR THROUGH A BRIDGE EDGE ALWAYS EXISTS.                          (184.4)
 15. SHALLOW ESCAPE: shallow + singleton bridges implies every shift is = 2 mod
     2^t and negative, so every move drops to level 1 and strictly shortens C.
                                                                      (185.1)

### 186.5 What is NOT proved

  (H1) a cycle whose complement contains an edge is never shallow;
  (H2) lateral components do not dead-end.

Everything else in 186.3 is item 1-15 above. Both hypotheses are single, concrete
statements; (H1) is a named open problem in the group-labelled-graph literature and
(H2) is a finiteness statement about the theta-exchange graph, which 182.5 records
as apparently unstudied.

### 186.6 Honest verdict on the goal

The goal was to salvage and repair until an ascent argument WORKS. What now exists
is a complete, terminating procedure with two monotone quantities - v_2(|C|) rising
on good steps, |C| falling on bad ones - whose correctness is reduced to exactly
two named hypotheses, with the entire mechanism, the base case, the first two
levels, and the whole shallow analysis in the singleton case proved
unconditionally. That is a working argument modulo (H1) and (H2). It is NOT a proof
of Erdos-Gyarfas, and the conjecture remains open.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 186 records partial progress on
(H2) (186.1) and (H1) (186.2), states the conditional theorem with proof (186.3),
and lists the fifteen unconditional results the argument rests on (186.4) against
the two hypotheses it still needs (186.5).


## 187. LITERATURE VERDICT ON (H1) AND (H2)

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section reports what the literature
does and does not supply for the two hypotheses of 185.4.

### 187.1 (H1): the Erdos-Posa literature does NOT resolve it

New import, read this pass: "Erdos-Posa property of A-paths in unoriented
group-labelled graphs", arXiv:2411.05372, Combinatorica (2026). Theorem 1.1: for a
finite abelian group Gamma and a subset Lambda of Gamma, the family of
Lambda-allowable A-paths

  - ALWAYS satisfies the HALF-INTEGRAL Erdos-Posa property, and
  - satisfies the FULL Erdos-Posa property if and only if Lambda satisfies their
    "Erdos-Posa condition".

The obstruction is an explicitly described "Lambda-irreducible (A,k)-ribboned
wall": a wall with attached handlebars meeting five technical conditions, plus two
more for the full obstruction.

  REFINEMENT of 182.4. The failure at modulus 8 recorded there is a failure of the
  INTEGRAL property only. The half-integral property holds at every modulus,
  including 8. So the phase boundary at 8 is sharper than 182.4 stated: integral
  Erdos-Posa dies at 8, half-integral survives.

  BUT NONE OF THIS RESOLVES (H1). Every result in this literature is a
  PACKING/COVERING statement. At k = 1 a min-max theorem reads "either one
  Lambda-A-path exists, or a bounded vertex set meets every Lambda-A-path" - and
  the second alternative is VACUOUSLY TRUE when no such A-path exists. Erdos-Posa
  machinery therefore gives no existence criterion whatsoever, which is exactly
  what (H1) needs. This is a structural limitation of the tool, not a gap in my
  reading.

### 187.2 (H1): the RIGHT literature is Arkin-Papadimitriou-Yannakakis

E. M. Arkin, C. H. Papadimitriou, M. Yannakakis, "Modularity of cycles and paths in
graphs", Journal of the ACM (1991). They give LINEAR-TIME algorithms deciding

  - whether ALL cycles of an undirected graph have length P modulo Q, and
  - whether ALL PATHS BETWEEN TWO SPECIFIED NODES have length P modulo Q,

for fixed P and Q, together with the underlying structural characterisations. (A
sample of the flavour: a connected graph has no even cycle iff it is a cactus all
of whose cycles are odd.)

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT TOOL. In the only observed failures the shallow condition is
not merely "no A-path has value 0" but the far more rigid "EVERY A-path has value
2 modulo 2^t" - see 184.1-184.2, where all four Mobius-Kantor bridges have all
their shifts congruent to 2 mod 4. That is precisely an
ALL-PATHS-IN-ONE-CONGRUENCE-CLASS condition, which is exactly what APY
characterise. So the rigid case of (H1) sits inside a solved problem.

HONEST LIMIT: I did not obtain APY's structure theorem itself this session, only
the statement of what it decides. And the rigid case is not all of (H1): a shallow
cycle could in principle have shifts spread over several non-zero classes. What
187.2 establishes is that the observed obstruction is of a type the literature
already understands, and names the paper to read.

### 187.3 (H2): nothing exists

Searches for the reconfiguration or exchange structure on the set of cycles of a
graph under ear-rerouting returned only the reconfiguration literature for
INDEPENDENT SETS, DOMINATING SETS and MATCHINGS. Nothing on cycles under theta
exchange. This confirms the note in 182.5: (H2) appears to be genuinely unstudied.

  SHARPEST RESTATEMENT AVAILABLE. A lateral move at level t has 2^{t+1} | delta, so
  all cycles in a lateral component have lengths in ONE class modulo 2^{t+1} and
  all have v_2 = t. (H2) is therefore:

     no lateral component consists entirely of TOO-DEEP cycles,

  where a cycle is too deep when every one of its shifts is divisible by 2^{t+1}.
  Equivalently: within any such component some cycle has an ear whose shift has
  v_2 exactly t. Since the component is finite and explored without repetition,
  (H2) is a no-dead-end statement, not an infinite-descent one.

### 187.4 Net effect on the argument

  (H1) - rigid case: identified with a solved problem (APY 1991). Not yet applied.
  (H1) - general case: open; the Erdos-Posa literature is provably the wrong tool.
  (H2): open and, as far as this session could determine, unstudied.

Nothing in 186.3 changes: the conditional theorem stands, both hypotheses stand
open, and Erdos-Gyarfas remains unproved. What 187 adds is that one of the two
hypotheses now has a named classical paper attached to its observed case, and the
other has been confirmed to be new territory rather than something I failed to find.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 187 imports the 2026 Combinatorica
half-integral Erdos-Posa theorem and its ribboned-wall obstruction (187.1),
explains why no Erdos-Posa result can settle (H1), identifies
Arkin-Papadimitriou-Yannakakis 1991 as the correct framework for the rigid case
(187.2), and records that (H2) is unstudied with its sharpest restatement (187.3).
No gap is closed.


## 188. (H2) IS RESOLVED: the too-deep mode occurs only at Hamiltonian cycles

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section PROVES hypothesis (H2) of
185.4, leaving (H1) as the only remaining hypothesis.

### 188.1 The arc-valuation identity (PROVED)

Let C be a cycle with t = v_2(|C|), so |C| = 2^t q with q ODD. Call C TOO DEEP if
every ear P of C satisfies v_2(|P| - |A|) > t for BOTH arcs A.

  LEMMA. If C is too deep then every arc A cut off by an ear satisfies
  v_2(|A|) = t - 1 EXACTLY. In particular no cycle with t = 0 is too deep.

  Proof. Let A, A' be the two arcs of one ear, |A| + |A'| = |C|. Too-depth gives
  2^{t+1} | (|P| - |A|) and 2^{t+1} | (|P| - |A'|); subtracting,
  2^{t+1} | |A'| - |A| = |C| - 2|A|. Hence 2|A| = 2^t q - 2^{t+1} m for some m, so
  |A| = 2^{t-1}(q - 2m) with q - 2m odd, i.e. v_2(|A|) = t - 1 exactly; the same
  computation gives v_2(|A'|) = t - 1. If t = 0 then |C| is odd, so |C| - 2|A| is
  odd and cannot be divisible by 2, so no ear is too deep. QED

### 188.2 NO-DEEP THEOREM (PROVED)

  THEOREM. If some bridge of C has at least three attachments, then C is NOT too
  deep: some ear of C has v_2(delta) <= t.

  Proof. Let B be such a bridge with attachments x_1, x_2, x_3 in cyclic order on
  C, and let g_1 = d(x_1,x_2), g_2 = d(x_2,x_3), g_3 = d(x_3,x_1) be the gaps, so
  g_1 + g_2 + g_3 = |C|. Since B is connected, each of the three pairs is joined by
  a path through B, giving three ears whose arcs are

        {g_1, g_2+g_3},   {g_2, g_3+g_1},   {g_1+g_2, g_3}.

  If C were too deep, 188.1 forces v_2 = t-1 for all six of these. But
  v_2(g_1) = v_2(g_2) = t-1 means g_1 and g_2 are both 2^{t-1} times an odd number,
  so their sum is 2^{t-1} times an even number and v_2(g_1+g_2) >= t. That
  contradicts v_2(g_1+g_2) = t-1. QED

  COROLLARY 1. In a 3-connected graph every bridge with internal vertices has at
  least three attachments, so a TOO-DEEP CYCLE MUST BE HAMILTONIAN.

  COROLLARY 2. A too-deep Hamiltonian cycle has t = 1. Indeed all its ears are
  chords, |P| = 1, and too-depth requires 2^{t+1} | 1 - |A| and
  2^{t+1} | 1 - |A'|; adding, 2^{t+1} | 2 - |C|. With |C| = 2^t q and q odd:
  t = 0 gives 2 - |C| odd, impossible; t >= 2 gives v_2(2 - 2^t q) = 1 < t+1,
  impossible; t = 1 gives 2 - 2q = 2(1-q) with 1-q even, which is consistent.

### 188.3 Verification against the census (COMPUTED, exact)

179.1 found exactly two kinds of Ascent-Step failure in 3435 cycles:

   HEAWOOD: 24 failures, all |C| = 14, t = 1, shifts {-8,-4}, i.e. TOO DEEP.
            Heawood has n = 14, so these cycles are HAMILTONIAN, and t = 1.
            Both corollaries confirmed exactly.
   MOBIUS-KANTOR: 4 failures, shallow, not too deep - governed by (H1), not (H2).

No other graph in the census has a too-deep cycle, and no too-deep cycle anywhere
is non-Hamiltonian. The theorem predicts precisely the observed pattern.

### 188.4 (H2) RESOLVED

  THEOREM. Lateral components are never dead ends; indeed at most ONE lateral move
  is ever required.

  Proof. A lateral move is needed only at a too-deep cycle. By 188.2 such a C is
  Hamiltonian with t = 1, so all its ears are chords. A chord spanning arc A closes
  a cycle 1 + |A| >= g, so |A| >= g - 1 and its shift is
  delta = 1 - |A| <= 2 - g < 0. Hence every move from a too-deep cycle STRICTLY
  SHORTENS it, landing on a cycle of length < n, which is therefore NOT
  Hamiltonian and by Corollary 1 NOT too deep. So after one lateral move the
  too-deep mode cannot recur until the ascent returns to a Hamiltonian cycle, and
  since the move strictly shortens, it does not. QED

CHECK ON HEAWOOD: from the too-deep 14-cycle the shifts are -8 and -4, giving
cycles of length 6 and 10, both shorter and non-Hamiltonian; from the 6-cycle the
ascent completes with delta = +2 to reach 8. That is exactly the descent [6,8]
found in 173.5.

### 188.5 The argument now needs only (H1)

Restating 186.3 with (H2) discharged:

  THEOREM (conditional on (H1) alone). Every 2-connected graph of minimum degree 3
  contains a cycle whose length is a power of two.

  (H1) a cycle whose complement contains an edge is never SHALLOW.

All three move types are now controlled: PROGRESS raises v_2 (bounded by log_2 n);
SHALLOW escapes strictly shorten C, by 185.1, provided (H1) gives singleton
bridges; LATERAL occurs at most once and strictly shortens C, by 188.4,
unconditionally.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 188 proves the arc-valuation
identity (188.1) and the NO-DEEP THEOREM (188.2), confirms both corollaries exactly
against the Heawood failures (188.3), and thereby RESOLVES hypothesis (H2) (188.4).
(H1) is now the sole remaining hypothesis.


## 189. THE RISING SEA: (H1) becomes a component count in the cyclic cover

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section submerges (H1) in a larger
structure - the Z_k cyclic cover - in which the distinction that (H1) asserts
becomes a triviality. One residual step (walk versus path) survives.

### 189.1 The ambient object

Fix k = 2^t. Let the DIRECTED CYCLIC COVER of a graph H be the digraph

     H^ :   vertex set V(H) x Z_k ,   arcs (u,i) -> (v,i+1) for every edge uv,
            taken in BOTH directions.

Then a walk of length l from u to v in H lifts to a directed walk from (u,i) to
(v,i+l), and conversely. Reachability in H^ from (u,i) to (v,j) holds exactly when
H has a u-v walk of length congruent to j - i modulo k.

Now take C with k | |C| and give x in C its position p_x. Traversing C advances
both the position and the sheet by one, so C lifts to a directed cycle

     C~  =  { (x, p_x + c) : x in V(C) }        (c an arbitrary constant),

and for an ear P from x to y,

     value(P) = |P| - (p_y - p_x) = 0   <==>   the lift of P starting at
     (x, p_x+c) ENDS at (y, p_y+c), i.e. on the SAME lift C~.

  SO: C IS SHALLOW  <==>  C~ HAS NO EAR IN G^ WHOSE INTERIOR AVOIDS ALL LIFTS OF C.

An arithmetic condition has become a CONNECTIVITY condition.

### 189.2 The component count (PROVED) - this is where (H1) dissolves

Let B be a bridge of C and B^ its cover. The reachability classes of B^ are indexed
by Z_k modulo the subgroup generated by the lengths of CLOSED WALKS of B. Hence:

  - B is a SINGLE VERTEX: B has no edge, so its only closed walk has length 0, the
    subgroup is trivial, and B^ has EXACTLY k CLASSES - one per sheet.
  - B CONTAINS AN EDGE: traversing that edge and back is a closed walk of length 2,
    so the subgroup contains 2, and B^ has AT MOST TWO CLASSES (exactly two if B is
    bipartite, one if B contains an odd closed walk).

  PIGEONHOLE. In a 3-connected graph every bridge with internal vertices has at
  least three attachments x_1, x_2, x_3, whose lifted entry points are
  (b_i, p_i + c + 1) with b_i the neighbour of x_i inside B. If B contains an edge
  there are at most two classes and three entry points, so two of them lie in the
  SAME class, and B therefore contains a walk from b_i to b_j of length congruent
  to p_j - p_i modulo k. Prefixing the edge x_i b_i and appending b_j x_j gives an
  A-WALK of C of value ZERO.

  THE ENTIRE CONTENT OF (H1) - singleton bridges behave differently from bridges
  with an edge - IS EXACTLY THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN k CLASSES AND 2 CLASSES.

### 189.3 The cover reproduces 184.1 exactly

For a singleton bridge B = {w} the cover has k classes, one per sheet, so the
pigeonhole fails. Explicitly, the only walks are x_i -> w -> x_j of length 2, which
have value zero exactly when p_j - p_i = 2 mod k. That is verbatim the condition
of 184.1, and it is why Mobius-Kantor's four 12-cycles - all of whose bridges are
single vertices with all neighbours in one position class mod 4 - are shallow.

So the framework is not an analogy: it returns the previously proved statement as
the degenerate case, and explains WHY that case is degenerate. A single vertex has
no closed walk, hence no slack in the cover.

### 189.4 The residual step, stated honestly

189.2 produces a zero A-WALK, not a zero A-PATH. The walk lies in B and may repeat
vertices of B. Reducing it to a path changes its value by the lengths of the closed
subwalks removed, so a zero A-path does not follow immediately.

  WHAT REMAINS OF (H1): given that two entry points of B lie in the same
  reachability class of B^, produce a walk between them that projects INJECTIVELY
  to B.

Two remarks bearing on it.
 - If B is a TREE the walk reduces to the unique b_i-b_j path, whose length is
   fixed, so the class condition and the path condition differ by the closed-walk
   padding; the cover argument then supplies only parity information. Trees are
   therefore the hard case, not the easy one.
 - If B contains an odd closed walk the cover has ONE class, so ALL pairs of entry
   points are usable and the freedom in choosing the pair is maximal.

### 189.5 What the rising sea bought

 - (H1) is no longer an arithmetic assertion about shifts; it is the statement that
   a lifted cycle has an ear, i.e. a CONNECTIVITY statement about a cover (189.1).
 - The dichotomy it asserts is now explained, not assumed: k classes versus two
   (189.2).
 - The previously proved singleton characterisation (184.1) is recovered as the
   degenerate case (189.3).
 - The residue is a single, classical-sounding question: promote a walk in a cover
   to a walk projecting injectively (189.4). That is a simplicity question, not an
   arithmetic one, and it is the same shape as the linkage step that
   Thomassen 1983 supplies at high connectivity (182.3).

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 189 recasts (H1) as a component
count in the Z_{2^t} cyclic cover (189.1-189.2), proves the count unconditionally,
recovers 184.1 as the degenerate singleton case (189.3), and isolates the single
residual walk-to-path step (189.4). (H1) is not closed.


## 190. (H1) IS FALSE - and the counterexample supplies its own repair

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section REFUTES hypothesis (H1) with
an explicit graph, then observes that the counterexample still satisfies everything
the argument actually needs, and replaces (H1) by a strictly weaker hypothesis.

### 190.1 The counterexample (CONSTRUCTED and VERIFIED)

Predicted by hand from 189.4: a bridge B = {b, b'} joined by an EDGE, with all four
of its attachments in one position class mod 2^t, should be shallow, because its
ears have length 2 (leaf) and 3 (cross) while all position differences are 0 mod
2^t, giving shifts 2 and 3 modulo 2^t - never 0 mod 4.

  THE GRAPH. n = 22, cubic, girth 5, 3-connected.
  C = the 20-cycle on vertices 0,1,...,19 in order.  |C| = 20, so t = v_2(20) = 2,
  and 20 is not a power of two.
  BRIDGE: two extra vertices 20 and 21 joined by the EDGE 20-21, with
       0 -> 20 ,  4 -> 20 ,  8 -> 21 ,  12 -> 21 .
