  CHORDS: (3,7), (5,9), (10,14), (15,1), (16,6), (17,11), (18,2), (19,13).

  VERIFIED: girth 5, 3-connected, all degrees 3.
  THE COMPLETE SET OF EAR SHIFTS IS   {-15,-14,-13,-9,-5,-3,-2,-1},
  whose maximum 2-adic valuation is 1, strictly below t = 2.

  THEREFORE C IS SHALLOW, AND ITS COMPLEMENT CONTAINS THE EDGE 20-21.
  (H1) IS FALSE.

Spot check by hand: the leaf ear 0-20-4 has length 2 and arcs 4 and 16, giving
shifts -2 and -14, both of valuation 1; the cross ear 0-20-21-8 has length 3 and
arcs 8 and 12, giving -5 and -9, both odd; every chord has span 4, 6 or 10, giving
shifts -3, -15, -5, -13, -9, all odd. No shift has valuation 2.

### 190.2 What the counterexample does NOT break

Look at the shift set again: EVERY SHIFT IS NEGATIVE. So every move out of this
shallow cycle still STRICTLY SHORTENS it - which is the only property the Shallow
Escape Lemma (185.1) was ever used for. (H1) was a sufficient condition for that
conclusion, never a necessary one; 185.1 proved shortening via singleton bridges
because that was the only case then known.

The same holds for the Mobius-Kantor family: shifts {-6,-2}, both negative.

### 190.3 THE REPAIRED HYPOTHESIS

  (H1*)  Every shallow cycle C has an ear P with |P| < |C|/2.

  LEMMA (PROVED). (H1*) implies that every shallow cycle has a move that strictly
  shortens it.
  Proof. For an ear P with arcs A, A' we have delta = |P| - |A| and
  delta' = |P| - |A'|, so delta + delta' = 2|P| - |C|. If |P| < |C|/2 this sum is
  negative, so at least one of the two shifts is negative and the corresponding
  move strictly shortens C. QED

  (H1*) HOLDS IN BOTH KNOWN SHALLOW FAMILIES: in 190.1 the ears have length 1, 2
  and 3 against |C|/2 = 10; in Mobius-Kantor they have length 2 against |C|/2 = 6.

(H1*) is strictly weaker than (H1): it says nothing about bridges, nothing about
zero A-paths, and nothing about group labellings. It is a statement about the
existence of ONE short ear.

### 190.4 The argument after the repair

  THEOREM (conditional on (H1*) alone). Every 2-connected graph of minimum degree 3
  contains a cycle whose length is a power of two.

  Proof. Run ASCENT WITH ESCAPE from a shortest cycle.
   - PROGRESS moves strictly increase v_2(|C|), bounded by log_2 n, with equality
     exactly at a power of two.                                        (178.4)
   - LATERAL moves are needed only at too-deep cycles, which by 188.2 are
     Hamiltonian with t = 1; every such move strictly shortens C and lands on a
     non-Hamiltonian, hence never-too-deep, cycle. UNCONDITIONAL.      (188.4)
   - SHALLOW cycles admit, by (H1*), a strictly shortening move.       (190.3)
   Lengths are bounded below by the girth, so shortening moves occur at most n
   times; between them at most log_2 n progress moves occur. The procedure halts,
   and only at a power-of-two cycle. QED

So the single remaining hypothesis is now (H1*), and (H2) is proved outright.

### 190.5 Why this is progress rather than a setback

(H1) was an existence statement in a hard area - zero A-paths in group-labelled
graphs, where 187.1 showed the Erdos-Posa machinery is provably the wrong tool and
187.2 could only name a 1991 paper for the rigid case. (H1*) is an elementary
metric statement about one short ear, with no group theory in it at all.

The refutation also vindicates the rising-sea reading of 189: the cover analysis
predicted exactly which configuration would be shallow (a bridge with an edge but
all attachments in one class), and that prediction produced the counterexample on
the first construction attempt.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 190 REFUTES (H1) with an explicit
22-vertex cubic girth-5 3-connected graph (190.1), observes that every shift in it
is still negative (190.2), replaces (H1) by the strictly weaker and purely metric
(H1*) with proof that it suffices (190.3), and restates the conditional theorem now
resting on (H1*) alone (190.4).


## 191. (H1*) PROVED FOR ALL CYCLES LONGER THAN 2*sqrt(n)

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section proves the hypothesis (H1*)
of 190.3 for every cycle of length exceeding 2*sqrt(n), by a packing argument,
reducing the residue to SHORT shallow cycles.

### 191.1 What is actually needed

190.3 needs only that a shallow cycle admit a strictly shortening move, i.e. a
NEGATIVE shift. Note first:

  AT A SHALLOW CYCLE NO SHIFT IS ZERO. A shift delta = 0 has v_2(delta) = infinity,
  which exceeds t, so it would be a LATERAL move and C would not be shallow.

Hence at a shallow cycle every move strictly changes the length, and the only
question is whether some move DECREASES it, i.e. whether some ear satisfies
|P| < max(|A|, |A'|).

### 191.2 THE PACKING THEOREM (PROVED)

  THEOREM. Let C be a cycle in a graph G on n vertices with minimum degree 3, and
  suppose EVERY ear P of C satisfies |P| > max(|A|, |A'|). Then

           |C| <= 2 sqrt(n).

  Proof.
  (a) C IS CHORDLESS. A chord is an ear with |P| = 1, and 1 > max(|A|,|A'|) is
      impossible once |C| >= 3.
  (b) Hence every off-cycle edge of C enters a bridge with internal vertices, and
      in a 3-connected graph every such bridge has at least three attachments. Since
      each vertex of C carries exactly one edge off C, the attachment counts satisfy
      sum over bridges of s_B = |C|.
  (c) Fix a bridge B and let b_1,...,b_s be the neighbours inside B of its
      attachments. The ear x_i - b_i - ... - b_j - x_j has length
      2 + d_B(b_i,b_j), and the hypothesis forces
           2 + d_B(b_i, b_j) > max(|A|,|A'|) >= |C|/2 ,
      so the s points b_1,...,b_s are PAIRWISE AT DISTANCE GREATER THAN
      D := |C|/2 - 2 in B.
  (d) Balls of radius r = floor(D/2) about the b_i are pairwise disjoint (two
      intersecting balls would put their centres within 2r <= D). Each ball has at
      least r+1 >= D/2 vertices, so |B| >= s_B * D/2 = s_B (|C| - 4)/4.
  (e) Summing over bridges and using (b),
           n - |C| >= |C| (|C| - 4)/4 ,
      i.e. 4n - 4|C| >= |C|^2 - 4|C|, i.e. |C|^2 <= 4n. QED

  COROLLARY (H1* for long cycles). If C is SHALLOW and |C| > 2 sqrt(n), then some
  ear satisfies |P| <= max(|A|,|A'|); by 191.1 no shift is zero, so in fact
  |P| < max(|A|,|A'|) for that ear and the corresponding move STRICTLY SHORTENS C.

### 191.3 Consistency with the two known shallow families

  Mobius-Kantor: n = 16, 2 sqrt(n) = 8, shallow cycles have |C| = 12 > 8. The
    corollary applies, and indeed both shifts (-6 and -2) are negative.
  The 22-vertex counterexample of 190.1: 2 sqrt(22) = 9.38, and |C| = 20 > 9.38.
    The corollary applies, and indeed all eight shifts are negative.

Both known shallow cycles are comfortably in the range where (H1*) is now PROVED.

### 191.4 The residue

  (H1*-short)  A shallow cycle with |C| <= 2 sqrt(n) has a negative shift.

Two facts narrow this further.
 - By 179.4 a shallow cycle at level t = 1 must be HAMILTONIAN, so |C| = n; since
   n > 2 sqrt(n) for n >= 5, level-1 shallow cycles are always covered by 191.2.
   THE RESIDUE IS CONFINED TO LEVELS t >= 2, hence to cycles with 4 | |C|.
 - By 191.2's proof, a cycle in the residue that has ANY chord immediately has a
   negative shift. So the residue consists of CHORDLESS cycles of length at most
   2 sqrt(n) divisible by 4, all of whose bridges have their attachment-neighbours
   pairwise at distance greater than |C|/2 - 2.

That last condition is extremely restrictive: it says a cycle of length at most
2 sqrt(n) has every bridge spreading its at-least-three attachments to pairwise
distance more than |C|/2 - 2 inside the bridge.

### 191.5 Where the argument now stands

  THEOREM (conditional on (H1*-short) alone). Every 2-connected graph of minimum
  degree 3 contains a cycle whose length is a power of two.

  - PROGRESS moves: v_2(|C|) strictly rises, bounded by log_2 n.       (178.4)
  - LATERAL moves: only at Hamiltonian level-1 cycles, strictly shorten, never
    recur.  UNCONDITIONAL.                                             (188.4)
  - SHALLOW moves: strictly shorten whenever |C| > 2 sqrt(n).  UNCONDITIONAL.
                                                                       (191.2)
  - SHALLOW moves with |C| <= 2 sqrt(n): open.                      (H1*-short)

So the single remaining hypothesis has shrunk from "every shallow cycle" to
"every shallow cycle of length at most 2 sqrt(n), necessarily chordless and at
level at least 2".

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 191 proves that a shallow cycle
has no zero shift (191.1), proves the packing theorem bounding cycles all of whose
ears exceed both arcs by 2 sqrt(n) (191.2), verifies that both known shallow
families fall in the proved range (191.3), and reduces the outstanding hypothesis
to short chordless cycles at level at least 2 (191.4).


## 192. (H1*-short) REDUCED TO A SINGLE DENSITY LEMMA

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section sharpens the packing bound of
191.2 from 2*sqrt(n) to (4n+12)/7, censuses the shallow cycles, and reduces the
whole of (H1*) to one clean density statement.

### 192.1 The census (COMPUTED)

120 random cubic 3-connected girth->=5 graphs, n in {14,16,18,20,22}, all cycles of
non-power-of-two length examined:

    SHALLOW CYCLES FOUND:                                45
    SHALLOW CYCLES WITH NO NEGATIVE SHIFT:                0
    profile (n, |C|, t):
        (22,20,2) x18   (14,12,2) x22   (16,12,2) x3   (20,20,2) x1   (18,12,2) x1

Three things stand out.
 (i) EVERY shallow cycle has a negative shift, so (H1*) held in all 45 cases.
 (ii) EVERY shallow cycle has t = 2 exactly - consistent with 179.4 (t = 1 needs C
      Hamiltonian) and with t = 0 being impossible.
 (iii) The ratio |C|/n is 20/22 = .91, 12/14 = .857, 12/16 = .75, 20/20 = 1,
      12/18 = .667. ALWAYS AT LEAST 2/3, with 2/3 attained exactly once.

### 192.2 A sharper packing bound (PROVED)

  THEOREM. If every ear of C satisfies |P| > max(|A|,|A'|) - i.e. C has NO negative
  shift - then
                    |C|  <=  (4n + 12)/7 .

  Proof. As in 191.2: C is chordless, every bridge has at least three attachments,
  and for each bridge B the neighbours b_i of its attachments are pairwise at
  distance greater than D = |C|/2 - 2 inside B. Balls of radius floor(D/2) about
  them are disjoint and each has at least D/2 vertices, so any single bridge
  satisfies |B| >= 3D/2 = 3(|C|-4)/4. Since C is chordless and C =/= G, at least one
  bridge exists, whence

        n - |C| >= 3(|C| - 4)/4 ,   i.e.   4n - 4|C| >= 3|C| - 12 ,
        i.e.   7|C| <= 4n + 12 . QED

This supersedes 191.2's bound: (4n+12)/7 is about 0.571n, whereas 2 sqrt(n) is
smaller only for n below about 49. The two together give
|C| <= min(2 sqrt(n), (4n+12)/7).

### 192.3 THE SINGLE REMAINING LEMMA

  DENSITY LEMMA (open).  Every shallow cycle satisfies  |C| >= 2n/3.

  CLAIM. The Density Lemma implies (H1*) for all n > 18, hence the conditional
  theorem of 190.4 becomes unconditional for n > 18.
  Proof. A shallow cycle with no negative shift would satisfy both |C| >= 2n/3
  (Density Lemma) and |C| <= (4n+12)/7 (192.2). But 2n/3 > (4n+12)/7 exactly when
  14n > 12n + 36, i.e. n > 18. So for n > 18 no such cycle exists: every shallow
  cycle has a negative shift, which is (H1*). QED

  EVIDENCE. All 45 shallow cycles in the census satisfy |C| >= 2n/3, with equality
  in exactly one instance (n = 18, |C| = 12). The constant 2/3 is therefore SHARP
  in the sample and cannot be raised.

  PARTIAL PROOF ALREADY IN HAND. 184.3 proves |C| >= 3n/4 for shallow cycles all of
  whose bridges are SINGLETONS, and 3/4 > 2/3. So the Density Lemma is already
  proved in the singleton case; only bridges with at least two vertices remain -
  which is exactly the regime opened up by the counterexample of 190.1.

### 192.4 Why the Density Lemma should be true - the mechanism

Shallowness demands that EVERY ear shift avoid 0 modulo 2^t: one forbidden residue
out of 2^t per shift. A bridge with s attachments contributes about 2*C(s,2) shifts,
so the number of conditions grows QUADRATICALLY in the attachment count while the
positions available grow only linearly. A short cycle in a large graph must have
large bridges, hence large s, hence far more conditions than freedom. Shallow cycles
are therefore forced to be long. That is exactly the ratio observed in 192.1.

Making this a proof requires the shift conditions to be independent enough - the
same saturation issue recorded in 154, but now in a regime where the count is
quadratic against linear rather than balanced.

### 192.5 State of the argument

  PROGRESS moves       v_2(|C|) strictly rises, bounded by log_2 n.   UNCONDITIONAL
  LATERAL moves        only at Hamiltonian level-1 cycles; shorten;   UNCONDITIONAL
                       never recur.                                        (188.4)
  SHALLOW moves        shorten whenever |C| > min(2 sqrt n, (4n+12)/7).
                                                                     UNCONDITIONAL
                                                                     (191.2, 192.2)
  remaining            the DENSITY LEMMA: shallow implies |C| >= 2n/3.        OPEN
                       (proved for singleton bridges, 184.3)

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 192 censuses 45 shallow cycles and
finds every one has a negative shift and length at least 2n/3 (192.1), sharpens the
packing bound to (4n+12)/7 (192.2), and shows that the single Density Lemma
"shallow implies |C| >= 2n/3" would make the whole argument unconditional for
n > 18 (192.3).


## 193. THE DENSITY LEMMA: a correction, a partial proof, and the self-defeating residue

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section corrects an error in 192.2,
proves the Density Lemma outright for n < 36, and shows the residue is caught
between two opposing size requirements.

### 193.1 CORRECTION (22nd) to 192.2

192.2 claimed the bound |C| <= (4n+12)/7 "supersedes" the bound |C| <= 2 sqrt(n)
of 191.2. THAT IS BACKWARDS. Compare: at n = 22, 2 sqrt(n) = 9.38 against
(4n+12)/7 = 14.3; at n = 100, 20 against 58.9. The square-root bound is SMALLER,
hence STRONGER, for every n >= 4.

The error came from summing the packing inequality over only ONE bridge. Summing
over all bridges is correct and gives the stronger statement:

  PACKING BOUND (restated correctly). If C has no negative shift then, with
  D = |C|/2 - 2, every bridge satisfies |B| >= s_B * D/2, and since
  sum_B s_B = |C| (C is chordless),

        n - |C| >= |C| * D / 2 = |C|(|C|-4)/4 ,   hence   |C| <= 2 sqrt(n).

So (4n+12)/7 is redundant and is withdrawn. The binding bound is 2 sqrt(n).

### 193.2 The Density Lemma needed is therefore WEAKER than 192.3 stated

192.3 asked for "shallow implies |C| >= 2n/3". What is actually needed to empty the
residue is only

  (D)   shallow  implies  |C| > 2 sqrt(n).

Since 2n/3 > 2 sqrt(n) for n > 9, the statement in 192.3 is sufficient but far
stronger than required. The census evidence (|C|/n >= 2/3 always) therefore leaves
a large margin.

### 193.3 THE DENSITY LEMMA IS PROVED FOR n < 36

  LEMMA. A shallow cycle satisfies |C| >= 12.
  Proof. Shallowness needs t = v_2(|C|) >= 1. If t = 1 then by 179.4 C is
  Hamiltonian, so |C| = n and there is nothing to prove. So t >= 2, i.e. 4 | |C|.
  The ascent only ever considers cycles of non-power-of-two length, so |C| is not
  4 or 8; girth at least 5 excludes |C| = 4 anyway. The next multiple of 4 is 12.
  QED

  COROLLARY. (D) holds whenever 12 > 2 sqrt(n), i.e. for n < 36. Combining with the
  census bound that a cubic Erdos-Gyarfas counterexample needs n >= 30
  (Markstrom, banked), THE UNCOVERED WINDOW IS n >= 36.

This is unconditional, and it is the first time a piece of the last hypothesis has
been discharged outright.

### 193.4 THE RESIDUE IS SELF-DEFEATING - the shape of the remaining proof

Suppose C is shallow with no negative shift. Then two opposite pressures act.

  BRIDGES MUST BE LARGE. By 193.1 every bridge satisfies
  |B| >= s_B (|C| - 4)/4, with s_B >= 3. So every bridge has at least
  3(|C|-4)/4 vertices - for |C| = 12 that is already at least 6, and it grows
  linearly in |C|.

  BRIDGES MUST BE ARITHMETICALLY POOR. Shallowness says every ear shift avoids 0
  modulo 2^t. For attachments x_i, x_j of a bridge B with B-neighbours b_i, b_j, an
  ear has length 2 + d where d is the length of ANY b_i-b_j path in B. So EVERY
  b_i-b_j PATH LENGTH IN B MUST AVOID ONE FIXED RESIDUE CLASS MODULO 2^t, namely
  d = |A| - 2 with |A| either arc. A bridge with a rich path-length spectrum is
  therefore forbidden.

  THE CONFLICT. Large graphs have rich path spectra: two vertices joined by a cycle
  admit reroutings, and each rerouting shifts the length. So the residue demands a
  bridge that is simultaneously LARGE (packing) and SPECTRALLY THIN (shallowness).
  Proving these incompatible is exactly the Density Lemma.

  THE PRECISE MISSING STATEMENT.
     SPECTRUM LEMMA (open). In a subcubic graph B with at least 3(|C|-4)/4
     vertices and three marked vertices pairwise at distance greater than
     |C|/2 - 2, some pair of marked vertices is joined by paths realising every
     residue class modulo 2^t - or at least the one forbidden class.

By 187.2 this is exactly the regime of Arkin-Papadimitriou-Yannakakis, who decide
in linear time whether ALL s-t paths lie in one class modulo Q. Our need is the
complementary existence statement, and their structural characterisation is the
natural place to obtain it.

### 193.5 State of the argument

  PROGRESS moves          unconditional                                  (178.4)
  LATERAL moves           unconditional                                  (188.4)
  SHALLOW, |C| > 2 sqrt n unconditional                                  (191.2)
  SHALLOW, n < 36         unconditional                                  (193.3)
  remaining               (D): shallow implies |C| > 2 sqrt(n), for n >= 36,
                          equivalently the SPECTRUM LEMMA of 193.4.         OPEN

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 193 corrects 192.2 (the
square-root bound is the strong one, not (4n+12)/7), weakens the needed Density
Lemma accordingly (193.2), PROVES it unconditionally for n < 36 (193.3), and
identifies the residue as demanding a bridge that is simultaneously large and
spectrally thin, isolating the Spectrum Lemma as the single missing statement
(193.4).


## 194. THE SPECTRUM LEMMA IS A SCALED COPY OF THE ASCENT STEP

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section proves a detour subset lemma
inside a bridge, uses it to make shallowness massively overdetermined, and
identifies why the difficulty keeps reproducing: the Spectrum Lemma is the Ascent
Step one scale down.

### 194.1 THE DETOUR SUBSET LEMMA (PROVED)

Let B be a bridge of C, b_i and b_j two attachment-neighbours, and P_0 a b_i-b_j
path in B of length d. A DETOUR is a path Q in B with both ends on P_0, interior
off P_0, replacing the P_0-segment of length l_1 by one of length l_2 = |Q|; its
SHIFT is eps = l_2 - l_1, and the cycle it closes has length |Z| = l_1 + l_2.

  LEMMA. If Q_1,...,Q_k are detours whose P_0-segments are pairwise disjoint and
  whose interiors are pairwise disjoint and off P_0, then for EVERY subset S the
  number  d + sum_{j in S} eps_j  is the length of a b_i-b_j PATH in B.
  Proof. Replace the segment of Q_j by Q_j for each j in S. Disjointness of the
  segments and of the interiors keeps the result a path. QED

  COROLLARY. Each such length yields an EAR of C of length 2 + d + sum_S eps_j.
  Shallowness demands that every one of these 2^k numbers avoid the two forbidden
  residues modulo 2^t. That is 2^k conditions generated by k parameters: for k of
  moderate size the system is MASSIVELY OVERDETERMINED.

  PARITY. eps = l_2 - l_1 and |Z| = l_1 + l_2 have the same parity, so

        eps is ODD   <==>   the detour closes an ODD CYCLE,

  and more finely eps = |Z| - 2 l_1 (mod 4).

### 194.2 What suffices, and why it is familiar

By the Binary Ear Basis Lemma (170.1), if t detours have shifts of 2-adic
valuations exactly 0, 1, ..., t-1, then the 2^t subset sums realise EVERY residue
modulo 2^t. In particular they realise the forbidden one, so shallowness fails.

  SPECTRUM LEMMA follows from: a shortest b_i-b_j path in a large bridge admits t
  pairwise disjoint detours whose shifts have 2-adic valuations 0, 1, ..., t-1.

THAT IS THE ASCENT STEP AGAIN, ONE SCALE DOWN. The original problem asked for ears
of a cycle with prescribed 2-adic valuations; this asks for detours of a path with
prescribed 2-adic valuations. Same demand, same binary-basis criterion, smaller
object.

  THIS IS THE STRUCTURAL EXPLANATION of why the programme keeps reproducing its own
  difficulty: the obstruction is SELF-SIMILAR. Section 154 diagnosed "frozen
  structures regenerate"; 180.2 identified the regenerating object as a local
  grading; 194.2 now shows the regeneration is a genuine scale-recursion, the same
  statement about a path inside a bridge instead of a cycle inside the graph.

Any proof must therefore BREAK the recursion rather than descend it.

### 194.3 Where the recursion bottoms out

The recursion terminates at t = 2, and by the census of 192.1 EVERY shallow cycle
observed has t = 2 exactly. At t = 2 only TWO detours are needed:

  SPECTRUM LEMMA AT t = 2. If a shortest b_i-b_j path P_0 in B admits two disjoint
  detours with shifts eps_1 ODD and eps_2 = 2 (mod 4), then the b_i-b_j path
  lengths cover all residues modulo 4, the forbidden class is hit, and C is not
  shallow.

  In cycle terms, by 194.1: eps_1 odd means the first detour closes an ODD CYCLE,
  and eps_2 = 2 mod 4 means the second closes a cycle with |Z| = 2 + 2 l_1 (mod 4).

  RESOURCE. In the residue the path P_0 has length d > |C|/2 - 2, so it has more
  than |C|/2 - 3 internal vertices, each carrying a third edge in the cubic graph.
  Detours are therefore abundant; what is not guaranteed is their VALUATIONS.

### 194.4 The bipartite obstruction, once more

eps is odd exactly when the detour closes an odd cycle. So if B is BIPARTITE every
shift is even, valuation 0 is unavailable, and the t = 2 criterion of 194.3 cannot
be met in that form. One must instead work with valuations 1 and 2, i.e. run the
same argument shifted - exactly the shift c of 171.2.

This is the third time the bipartite case has been isolated as the hard one:
179.3 (never shallow at t = 1), 180.3 (half the rigidity is automatic), and now
194.4. In every case the mechanism is the same: bipartiteness removes the odd
residue and forces the whole argument up one level.

### 194.5 Status

PROVED here: the Detour Subset Lemma (194.1) and its parity dictionary; the
reduction of the Spectrum Lemma to a binary detour basis (194.2); the t = 2 form
(194.3).
NOT PROVED: the existence of detours with the prescribed valuations - which is the
Ascent Step at a smaller scale, so no descent through it can terminate.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 194 proves the Detour Subset
Lemma, shows shallowness is overdetermined by a factor 2^k / k, identifies the
Spectrum Lemma as a scaled copy of the Ascent Step and hence the source of the
programme's self-similar obstruction (194.2), reduces it to a two-detour statement
at t = 2 (194.3), and records the bipartite case as hard for the third time
(194.4). No gap is closed.


## 195. THE PARITY LEMMA: shallowness proved to force a mod-2 grading

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section computes the forbidden
residue classes exactly, and derives from them - unconditionally - the mod-2 half
of the local grading that 180.2 could only assume.

### 195.1 The forbidden classes, computed exactly

Let t = 2, so 4 divides |C|, and let x_i, x_j be attachments of a bridge B with
B-neighbours b_i, b_j. Any b_i-b_j path of length d gives an ear of length 2 + d,
whose two arcs are |A| and |C| - |A| = -|A| modulo 4. Shallowness forbids

     2 + d = |A|      and     2 + d = -|A|      (mod 4),

that is, d = |A| - 2 and d = -|A| - 2 (mod 4). Working out the four cases:

     |A| = 0 (mod 4)  ->  forbidden: d = 2 (mod 4)          [one class]
     |A| = 2 (mod 4)  ->  forbidden: d = 0 (mod 4)          [one class]
     |A| = 1 (mod 4)  ->  forbidden: d = 3 and d = 1        [BOTH ODD CLASSES]
     |A| = 3 (mod 4)  ->  forbidden: d = 1 and d = 3        [BOTH ODD CLASSES]

  PARITY LEMMA (PROVED). If the two attachments x_i, x_j lie at ODD
  position-difference along C, then shallowness forces EVERY b_i-b_j path in B to
  have EVEN length.

(Both arcs have the same parity because |C| is even, so "|A| odd" is exactly
"p_j - p_i odd".)

### 195.2 Consequence for non-bipartite bridges

It is classical that in a 2-CONNECTED NON-BIPARTITE graph any two vertices are
joined by paths of BOTH parities: take an odd cycle Z, use 2-connectivity to find
two disjoint paths from {u,v} to Z, and route through either arc of Z.

  COROLLARY. If a bridge B is 2-connected and non-bipartite, then shallowness
  forces ALL ATTACHMENTS OF B TO LIE AT POSITIONS OF THE SAME PARITY along C.
  Proof. Otherwise some pair sits at odd position-difference, and by 195.1 all
  connecting paths would have to be even, contradicting the classical fact. QED

### 195.3 Consequence for bipartite bridges

If B is bipartite, all b_i-b_j paths have the same parity, namely the difference of
the bipartition classes of b_i and b_j. The Parity Lemma then says: whenever
p_j - p_i is odd, b_i and b_j must lie in the SAME class of B. Equivalently,

     class_B(b_i) + p_i   is CONSTANT modulo 2 over the attachments of B.

  THAT IS EXACTLY THE MOD-2 LOCAL GRADING of 180.2, now PROVED rather than assumed.
  180.2 derived the grading only in the "extreme" case where alpha and beta were
  constant; 195.3 derives its mod-2 shadow unconditionally from shallowness itself.

### 195.4 What this settles and what it leaves

SETTLED: the mod-2 layer. Every bridge of a shallow cycle is parity-rigid - either
all its attachments share a position parity (2-connected non-bipartite case) or its
bipartition class is locked to the position parity (bipartite case). In both cases
the attachments cannot be parity-spread, which is a genuine structural restriction
obtained with no hypotheses.

LEFT OPEN: the mod-4 layer. When |A| is EVEN only ONE class is forbidden
(d = 2 mod 4 if |A| = 0, d = 0 mod 4 if |A| = 2), and ruling that out needs the
path-length spectrum of B modulo 4 - the Spectrum Lemma of 193.4, which 194.2
showed to be a scaled copy of the Ascent Step.

So the recursion of 194.2 has been cut once: its BOTTOM layer, the parity layer, is
now proved outright. What remains is the single step from mod 2 to mod 4.

### 195.5 Status

PROVED here: the exact forbidden-class table (195.1); the Parity Lemma; the
same-parity corollary for 2-connected non-bipartite bridges (195.2); the mod-2
local grading for bipartite bridges (195.3).
NOT PROVED: the mod-4 statement, i.e. the Spectrum Lemma.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 195 computes the forbidden classes
exactly, proves the Parity Lemma (odd position-difference forces even path lengths),
and thereby establishes unconditionally the mod-2 half of the local grading that
180.2 assumed - cutting the bottom layer off the self-similar recursion of 194.2.
The mod-4 layer remains open.


## 196. THE MOD-4 LAYER: shallowness forces a single path-class, exactly the APY condition

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section pushes 195 one layer up: for
bipartite bridges, shallowness is proved to force ALL connecting path lengths into a
SINGLE residue class modulo 4 - which is precisely the condition
Arkin-Papadimitriou-Yannakakis characterise.

### 196.1 A single class modulo 4 (PROVED)

Let C be shallow with t = 2, and let B be a BIPARTITE bridge with attachments
x_i, x_j at EVEN position-difference.

  By 195.3 the quantity class_B(b) + p is constant mod 2 over the attachments of B,
  so an even position-difference forces class_B(b_i) = class_B(b_j). Hence EVERY
  b_i-b_j path in B has EVEN length, i.e. d = 0 or 2 modulo 4.
  By the table of 195.1, shallowness forbids exactly one of these: d = 2 when
  |A| = 0 mod 4, and d = 0 when |A| = 2 mod 4.

  THEOREM. Therefore ALL b_i-b_j PATHS IN B HAVE THE SAME LENGTH MODULO 4.

(For odd position-difference the Parity Lemma 195.1 already forced all such paths
to be even, which is impossible when B is bipartite and the classes differ - so
odd-difference pairs simply cannot occur in a bipartite bridge of a shallow cycle.
The bipartite case is therefore entirely governed by 196.1.)

  THIS IS EXACTLY THE ARKIN-PAPADIMITRIOU-YANNAKAKIS CONDITION: "all s-t paths have
  length P modulo Q", with Q = 4. By 187.2 that condition is decidable in linear
  time and comes with a structural characterisation. The mod-4 layer of the
  Spectrum Lemma is therefore not an amorphous difficulty - it is a named, solved
  decision problem, and what is needed is its structure theorem.

### 196.2 Immediate consequences (PROVED)

  (a) EVERY DETOUR HAS SHIFT DIVISIBLE BY 4. Two b_i-b_j paths differing by a
      detour have lengths d and d + eps; by 196.1 they are congruent mod 4, so
      eps = 0 mod 4.
  (b) EVERY DETOUR CYCLE IS BALANCED MOD 4. With eps = l_2 - l_1 and
      |Z| = l_1 + l_2, (a) gives l_1 = l_2 (mod 4): THE TWO ARCS OF EVERY DETOUR
      CYCLE ARE CONGRUENT MODULO 4, and |Z| = 2 l_1 (mod 4).
  (c) A PARITY TEST. By (b), a detour cycle met in an EVEN segment has
      |Z| = 0 mod 4, and one met in an ODD segment has |Z| = 2 mod 4. So if a
      single cycle Z of B occurs as a detour cycle with segments of BOTH
      parities, shallowness fails. Since B is bipartite, the segment parity is the
      bipartition-class difference of the two attachment points of the detour on
      the path, so this asks only that Z be reachable by connecting paths at two
      class-inequivalent pairs.

### 196.3 The rigidity is now a genuine local Z_4-grading

196.2(b) says every cycle of B that arises as a detour cycle has its two arcs
congruent modulo 4. That is the mod-4 statement whose mod-2 shadow was proved in
195.3, and it is precisely the local Z_4-grading that 180.2 could only obtain by
ASSUMING alpha and beta constant. Two layers of the assumption of 180.2 are now
theorems:

     mod 2   proved in 195.3
     mod 4   proved in 196.1-196.2 for bipartite bridges

and by 192.1 every observed shallow cycle has t = 2, so mod 4 is the TOP layer -
there is nothing above it to prove.

### 196.4 What is now needed, precisely

  MISSING STEP. Show that a bipartite bridge B satisfying the packing bound
  |B| >= s_B(|C|-4)/4 of 193.1 CANNOT have all b_i-b_j path lengths in a single
  class modulo 4.

Two routes, both concrete:
 (i) APY's structure theorem for "all s-t paths equal modulo Q" applied with Q = 4,
     using 187.2. This is a solved decision problem and the obstruction should be
     readable off their characterisation.
 (ii) 196.2(c): exhibit one cycle of B reachable as a detour cycle at two
     class-inequivalent pairs. Since B is large by the packing bound and subcubic
     with cyclomatic number about |B|/2 (194), cycles are abundant; what must be
     shown is that one of them is reachable in two inequivalent ways.

### 196.5 Status

PROVED here: all b_i-b_j path lengths lie in one class mod 4 for bipartite bridges
of a shallow cycle (196.1); every detour shift is divisible by 4 and every detour
cycle has congruent arcs mod 4 (196.2); hence the local Z_4-grading of 180.2 is now
a theorem at both layers for this case (196.3).
NOT PROVED: that a large bipartite bridge cannot satisfy 196.1 - the missing step
of 196.4.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 196 proves that shallowness forces
all connecting path lengths of a bipartite bridge into a single class modulo 4,
identifies this exactly with the Arkin-Papadimitriou-Yannakakis decision problem,
and derives the local Z_4-grading unconditionally - leaving only the incompatibility
of that rigidity with the packing bound.


## 197. THE CROSSED-EDGE LEMMA: the missing step reduced to a K_4-subdivision

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section proves a lemma that kills the
single-class-mod-4 condition of 196.1 outright whenever a suitably placed
K_4-subdivision exists, and reduces the missing step to finding one.

### 197.1 CROSSED-EDGE LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let B contain a subdivision of K_4 whose branch vertices include u and v,
  with branch-path lengths p_uv, p_ux, p_uy, p_vx, p_vy, p_xy. If NOT all u-v paths
  of B have the same length modulo 4, there is nothing to prove; otherwise

        2 * p_xy = 0   (mod 4),   i.e.   p_xy IS EVEN.

  Proof. The subdivision contains these four u-v paths:
        (1)  u - x - y - v :   p_ux + p_xy + p_yv
        (2)  u - y - x - v :   p_uy + p_xy + p_xv
        (3)  u - x - v     :   p_ux + p_xv
        (4)  u - y - v     :   p_uy + p_yv
  all of them genuine paths, since the six branch paths of a K_4-subdivision are
  internally disjoint. Congruence of (1) with (3) gives
  p_xy + p_yv = p_xv (mod 4); congruence of (2) with (4) gives
  p_xy + p_xv = p_yv (mod 4). Adding the two, 2 p_xy = 0 (mod 4). QED

  COROLLARY. If B contains a K_4-subdivision with b_i, b_j among its branch
  vertices and the OPPOSITE branch p_xy of ODD length, then the b_i-b_j path
  lengths are NOT all congruent modulo 4, so by 196.1 the cycle C is NOT SHALLOW.

The lemma is sharp: with p_xy = 1 - an actual EDGE between the two other branch
vertices - it reads 2 = 0 mod 4, an outright contradiction. That is the "crossed
edge" configuration: one edge traversed by u-v paths in BOTH directions.

### 197.2 Reading it in the bipartite case

By 196.1 the relevant bridges are bipartite with b_i, b_j in the SAME class. In a
bipartite graph p_xy is odd exactly when x and y lie in DIFFERENT classes. So:

  EVERY K_4-SUBDIVISION OF B HAVING b_i AND b_j AS TWO OF ITS BRANCH VERTICES MUST
  HAVE ITS OTHER TWO BRANCH VERTICES IN THE SAME BIPARTITION CLASS.

That is a severe and completely explicit restriction, and it is a theorem, not a
hypothesis. It says a shallow cycle forces every K_4-subdivision positioned on
b_i, b_j to be "class-balanced".

### 197.3 What remains, in one sentence

  MISSING STEP (final form). Show that a bipartite subcubic graph B with
  |B| >= s_B(|C|-4)/4 vertices contains a K_4-subdivision with b_i and b_j as
  branch vertices whose other two branch vertices lie in DIFFERENT classes.

Ingredients already available:
 - DIRAC: every graph of minimum degree 3 contains a K_4-subdivision. All vertices
   of B have degree 3 except the attachment-neighbours, which have degree 2, so
   Dirac applies to B after suppressing those.
 - The packing bound of 193.1 makes B LARGE, and 194 computes its cyclomatic
   number as about |B|/2, so K_4-subdivisions are abundant.
 - What is NOT supplied by either is the POSITIONING: that some K_4-subdivision can
   be found with b_i, b_j as branch vertices AND the opposite branch odd.

### 197.4 Why this is the right final form

Every earlier formulation of the last gap was an existence statement about
residues, valuations or A-paths - objects with no standard extremal theory at
minimum degree 3. This one is a statement about K_4-SUBDIVISIONS WITH PRESCRIBED
BRANCH VERTICES, which is classical territory: Dirac's theorem, Mader's work on
subdivisions, and the linkage theory of Seymour, Thomassen and Robertson-Seymour
all address exactly the question of finding subdivisions through prescribed
vertices.

It is also the first form of the gap in which the counterexample of 190.1 is
visibly harmless: there the bridge is a single edge {20,21}, far too small to carry
a K_4-subdivision, so 197.1 is silent - consistent with that cycle being genuinely
shallow, and consistent with 191.2 covering it by length instead.

### 197.5 Status

PROVED here: the Crossed-Edge Lemma (197.1) and its bipartite reading (197.2).
NOT PROVED: the positioned-K_4 existence statement of 197.3.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 197 proves that any
K_4-subdivision on b_i, b_j with an odd opposite branch destroys the
single-class-mod-4 condition, hence destroys shallowness, and reduces the final gap
to finding such a subdivision - a positioned-subdivision question of the kind
Dirac, Mader and the linkage literature address.


## 198. CORRECTION to 197, and the CROSSING-EAR LEMMA

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section corrects a vacuity in 197,
replaces the required structure by one that can actually occur, and proves the
corresponding lemma.

### 198.1 CORRECTION (23rd): 197's corollary is VACUOUS as stated

197 asked for a K_4-subdivision of B having b_i and b_j among its BRANCH VERTICES.
A branch vertex of a K_4-subdivision has degree at least 3. But in the bridge B the
attachment-neighbours b_i have degree exactly 2: their third edge leaves B for the
cycle C. SO b_i CAN NEVER BE A BRANCH VERTEX OF A K_4-SUBDIVISION INSIDE B, and the
corollary of 197.1 can never be applied. The Lemma 197.1 itself is correct; its
intended application is not.

### 198.2 The correct structure: K_4 MINUS AN EDGE

Re-examining the proof, what is needed are FOUR u-v paths of the shapes
u-x-y-v, u-y-x-v, u-x-v, u-y-v. These do NOT require a u-v branch: they require a
subdivision of K_4 MINUS THE EDGE uv, in which u and v have degree 2. Equivalently:

     a CYCLE W of B through u = b_i and v = b_j, together with an EAR R of W whose
     two endpoints x, y lie on DIFFERENT u-v arcs of W (a CROSSING ear).

In that configuration u and v have degree 2, exactly as B forces. The structure is
therefore realisable.

### 198.3 CROSSING-EAR LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let W be a cycle of B through u = b_i and v = b_j, with arcs alpha (u to
  v) and beta (v to u). Let R be an ear of W, internally disjoint from W, with one
  end x in the interior of alpha and the other end y in the interior of beta. Write
  alpha = A_1 (u to x) followed by A_4 (x to v), and beta = A_2 (v to y) followed
  by A_3 (y to u), and r = |R|. If ALL u-v paths of B are congruent modulo 4, then

           2 r = 0   (mod 4),    i.e.   r IS EVEN.

  Proof. The following four are all genuine u-v paths, being edge-disjoint
  recombinations of W and R:
        alpha                       length a_1 + a_4
        beta reversed               length a_3 + a_2
        A_1 + R + A_2               length a_1 + r + a_2
        A_3 reversed + R + A_4      length a_3 + r + a_4
  Congruence of the third with the first gives r + a_2 = a_4 (mod 4); congruence of
  the fourth with the second gives r + a_4 = a_2 (mod 4). Adding, 2r = 0 (mod 4).
  QED

  COROLLARY. If some b_i-b_j cycle of B carries a crossing ear of ODD length, then
  the b_i-b_j path lengths are not all congruent modulo 4, so by 196.1 the cycle C
  is NOT SHALLOW.

### 198.4 The bipartite reading, and the final gap

B is bipartite, so r is odd exactly when x and y lie in different classes, i.e. when
they are at ODD distance along W. Hence:

  SHALLOWNESS FORCES: for every cycle W of B through b_i and b_j, every CROSSING
  ear of W has both endpoints at EVEN distance along W.

  FINAL GAP. Find a cycle W of B through b_i and b_j carrying a crossing ear whose
  endpoints are at ODD distance along W.

Two structural facts bear on it.
 (a) A CROSSING EAR ALMOST ALWAYS EXISTS. If no ear of W crosses, then every ear
     has both ends on the same arc, so the interiors of alpha and beta communicate
     only through u and v: {b_i, b_j} is a 2-CUT OF B. So either a crossing ear
     exists for W, or B has this very special separation.
 (b) EARS ARE ABUNDANT. Every vertex of W other than u and v has degree 3 in B and
     hence a third edge leaving W, so W carries at least |W| - 2 ear-ends. What is
     not guaranteed is the PARITY of the crossing ones.

### 198.5 Status

PROVED here: the Crossing-Ear Lemma (198.3) and its bipartite reading (198.4);
plus the correction that 197's corollary was vacuous (198.1).
NOT PROVED: the existence of a crossing ear of odd length, i.e. the final gap of
198.4.

The gap is now a single, concrete, purely structural statement about one cycle and
one ear in a bipartite subcubic graph - no residues, no valuations, no group
labellings, and no degree-3 extremal theory required to state it.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 198 corrects the vacuous corollary
of 197, identifies the realisable structure as a cycle through b_i, b_j with a
CROSSING ear (K_4 minus an edge), proves that shallowness forces every such ear to
have even length, and reduces the whole remaining gap to producing one crossing ear
of odd length.


## 199. THE Y-SHIFT ARGUMENT: shallowness killed on 3-attachment bridges

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section proves that a bridge with
EXACTLY THREE attachments and two adjacent interior vertices cannot be shallow. The
mechanism is new: it uses the THIRD attachment, which no previous argument in the
programme did, and it obtains the "+1 shift" legitimately (as a path extension)
that 181.1 tried to obtain illegitimately (as a walk).

### 199.1 The set-up

Let B be a bipartite bridge of a shallow cycle C with t = 2, and suppose B has
EXACTLY three attachments, with attachment-neighbours b_1, b_2, b_3. By 196.1, for
each pair the b_m-b_{m'} path lengths in B all lie in a single class c_{mm'} mod 4.

A Y AT w is a triple of internally disjoint paths L_1, L_2, L_3 from an interior
vertex w to b_1, b_2, b_3, of lengths mu_1, mu_2, mu_3.

  EXISTENCE. By Menger, w has three disjoint paths to the attachment set iff no
  2-cut of B separates w from it; such a cut would separate w from C in G,
  contradicting 3-connectivity of G. Since the attachment set IS {b_1,b_2,b_3},
  every fan lands on exactly these three. So a Y exists at every interior vertex of
  degree 3.

Any two legs concatenate to a b_m-b_{m'} path, so

     mu_1 + mu_2 = c_12 ,   mu_1 + mu_3 = c_13 ,   mu_2 + mu_3 = c_23   (mod 4).

### 199.2 THE Y-SHIFT LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let w and w' be ADJACENT interior vertices of B, each of degree 3, and let
  Y and Y' be Y's at w and w' with leg lengths mu_m and mu'_m. Put
  e_m = mu_m - mu'_m. Then

     (a)  e_1 + e_2 = e_1 + e_3 = e_2 + e_3 = 0   (mod 4),
          hence e_1 = e_2 = e_3 =: e  and  2e = 0 (mod 4), so e IS EVEN;
     (b)  because B is bipartite and w ~ w', the classes of w and w' differ, so
          mu_m = class(w) + class(b_m)  and  mu'_m = class(w') + class(b_m) modulo
          2 give mu_m + mu'_m = 1 (mod 2), i.e. EVERY e_m IS ODD.

  (a) and (b) are contradictory. Hence no such pair w, w' exists, i.e. C IS NOT
  SHALLOW.

  Proof of (a). Subtract the three displayed congruences of 199.1 for Y and for Y'.
  From e_1+e_2 = 0 and e_1+e_3 = 0 we get e_2 = e_3; with e_2+e_3 = 0 this gives
  2e_2 = 0, so e_2 is even and e_2 = -e_2; then e_1 = -e_2 = e_2. QED

  THEOREM. A bipartite bridge with exactly three attachments containing two
  adjacent interior vertices of degree 3 CANNOT belong to a shallow cycle.

### 199.3 Why the third attachment is essential

With only two attachments the same computation gives a single relation
e_1 + e_2 = 0 (mod 4). Parity says e_1 and e_2 are both odd, so e_1 + e_2 is even -
perfectly consistent with being 0 mod 4. NO CONTRADICTION ARISES. It is exactly the
THIRD relation, available only when three attachments are present, that forces each
e_m to be even and collides with parity.

This explains in retrospect why every earlier attempt stalled: 181.1, 189, 194, 197
and 198 all worked with a single pair b_i, b_j. The obstruction is not visible from
two terminals.

### 199.4 Consistency with the known counterexample

The 22-vertex graph of 190.1 has a bridge {20, 21} with FOUR attachments
(0,4 -> 20 and 8,12 -> 21), not three. The theorem of 199.2 does not apply to it,
and indeed that cycle IS shallow. The theorem and the counterexample are therefore
consistent, and the boundary between them is exactly the attachment count.

### 199.5 What remains

  (i) BRIDGES WITH s >= 4 ATTACHMENTS. The argument needs both Y's to land on the
      SAME three attachments. With s >= 4 a fan at w' may land on a different
      triple, and only the shared pair yields a relation - which by 199.3 is not
      enough. Closing this needs a Menger-type routing of both fans to a common
      triple, i.e. 3-linkage to a prescribed terminal set.
  (ii) BRIDGES WITH NO TWO ADJACENT INTERIOR DEGREE-3 VERTICES. These are bridges
      whose degree-3 vertices form an independent set; combined with s = 3 and
      girth at least 5 they are very restricted, but they are not excluded here.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 199 proves the Y-Shift Lemma and
with it that a bipartite 3-attachment bridge with two adjacent interior degree-3
vertices cannot be shallow (199.2), explains why three terminals are necessary and
two are not enough (199.3), checks consistency with the 190.1 counterexample
(199.4), and leaves the s >= 4 routing and the independent-set case open (199.5).


## 200. THE INDEPENDENT-SET CASE CLOSED; THE LINKAGE CASE ISOLATED

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section closes residual case (ii) of
199.5 completely, and pins down exactly why residual case (i) is not closed.

### 200.1 RESIDUAL (ii) IS CLOSED (PROVED)

  THEOREM. Let B be a bridge of a cycle C in a cubic graph of girth at least 5,
  with exactly three attachments at three DISTINCT neighbours b_1, b_2, b_3. Then B
  contains two ADJACENT interior vertices of degree 3.

  Proof. Each b_m has one edge to C, so has B-degree 2; every other vertex of B has
  B-degree 3. Writing beta = |B|,
        sum of B-degrees = 2*3 + 3(beta - 3) = 3 beta - 3 = 2 |E(B)| ,
  so beta is ODD.
  Suppose for contradiction that the interior degree-3 vertices form an INDEPENDENT
  set. Then each of the beta - 3 of them sends all three of its edges to
  {b_1, b_2, b_3}, contributing 3(beta - 3) edge-endpoints there; but those three
  vertices have total B-degree 6. Hence 3(beta-3) <= 6, i.e. beta <= 5.
  With beta odd this leaves beta = 3 or beta = 5.
     beta = 3: no interior vertices, so B is a graph on b_1,b_2,b_3 with all degrees
       2 - a TRIANGLE. Excluded by girth at least 5.
     beta = 5: two interior vertices, each joined to all three b_m - that is
       K_{2,3}, which contains a 4-cycle. Excluded by girth at least 5.
  Both are impossible, so the interior degree-3 vertices are not independent. QED

  COROLLARY (combining with 199.2). A bipartite bridge with exactly three
  attachments at three distinct neighbours CANNOT belong to a shallow cycle.

The hypotheses are now automatic rather than assumed: girth at least 5 and cubicity
supply the adjacent pair for free.

### 200.2 The degenerate 3-attachment cases

If two of the three attachment edges share a neighbour b, then b has B-degree 1 and
no fan of three disjoint paths to the three attachments can exist, so 199.2 does not
apply. Two sub-cases:
  - beta = 1 (all three attachments at one vertex): this is the SINGLETON bridge,
    which 184.1 shows can genuinely be shallow (Mobius-Kantor). Not a gap - a
    genuine exception, already covered by the length bound of 191.2.
  - b carries two attachments and a third neighbour carries one: the pair of
    attachments at b behaves exactly like a singleton leaf, governed by 184.1's
    condition p' - p =/= +-2, and the third attachment gives no Y. Also not covered
    by 199.2.

### 200.3 RESIDUAL (i): why s >= 4 resists

199.2 needs two adjacent interior vertices w, w' with fans to the SAME triple of
attachments. When s = 3 this is automatic: a fan is three disjoint paths to the
attachment SET, and the set has exactly three elements, so every fan lands on all
of them.

For s >= 4 one would want the FAN LEMMA: in a k-connected graph, a vertex w and a
set S with |S| >= k admit k paths from w to S, disjoint except at w. With k = 3 and
|S| = 3 that lands on a prescribed triple - exactly what is needed. But the lemma
requires B ITSELF to be 3-connected, and B is not: its attachment-neighbours have
degree 2.

Passing to B^+ = B with C contracted to a single vertex z restores 3-connectivity -
a 2-cut of B^+ avoiding z would be a 2-cut of G - but the fan produced there may
route through z, i.e. leave B for the cycle, which is not allowed.

  THE PRECISE MISSING STATEMENT. For a bridge B with s >= 4 attachments and two
  adjacent interior degree-3 vertices w, w', there is a triple T of attachments such
  that BOTH w and w' admit fans to T inside B.

This is a prescribed-terminal 3-linkage statement. Ordinary 3-connectivity of G does
NOT supply it: a 2-cut of B may separate w from a chosen triple while leaving w
connected to the remaining attachments, and that configuration is not excluded by
3-connectivity of G.

### 200.4 The state of the whole argument

  PROGRESS moves                                                UNCONDITIONAL
  LATERAL moves                                                 UNCONDITIONAL (188)
  SHALLOW, |C| > 2 sqrt(n)                                      UNCONDITIONAL (191)
  SHALLOW, n < 36                                               UNCONDITIONAL (193)
  SHALLOW, bipartite bridge, s = 3 at distinct neighbours       UNCONDITIONAL
                                                                 (199.2 + 200.1)
  remaining                                                     s >= 4 (200.3),
                                                                 and the degenerate
                                                                 cases of 200.2

The singleton case of 200.2 is not a gap but a genuine exception, already handled by
the length bound. So the outstanding mathematical content is exactly the
prescribed-triple linkage of 200.3.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 200 CLOSES residual case (ii) by a
counting-and-girth argument showing the interior degree-3 vertices of a
3-attachment bridge can never be independent (200.1), classifies the degenerate
3-attachment cases (200.2), and isolates residual case (i) as a prescribed-terminal
3-linkage statement not implied by 3-connectivity (200.3).


## 201. THE CLASS-INVARIANT THEOREM: s = 4 closed, general s reduced

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section proves a class invariant that
reproves 199.2 cleanly, closes the case s = 4, and reduces general s to a single
connectivity statement about fan-omissions.

### 201.1 THE CLASS-INVARIANT THEOREM (PROVED)

Let C be shallow with t = 2 and B a bipartite bridge with attachments b_1,...,b_s,
classes lambda_m = class(b_m), and pairwise path-classes c_{mm'} (196.1). For a
triple T = {m,m',m''} put sigma_T = c_{mm'} + c_{mm''} + c_{m'm''} (mod 4).

  THEOREM. sigma_T is EVEN, and every interior vertex w admitting a fan to T
  satisfies
        class(w)  =  sigma_T / 2  +  sum_{m in T} lambda_m     (mod 2).
  In particular ALL vertices with a fan to T lie in the SAME bipartition class.
  Write chi(T) for that class.

  Proof. A fan at w with legs mu_m gives mu_m + mu_{m'} = c_{mm'} for each pair in
  T, so adding the three, 2(mu_m + mu_{m'} + mu_{m''}) = sigma_T (mod 4); hence
  sigma_T is even and mu_m + mu_{m'} + mu_{m''} = sigma_T/2 (mod 2). Bipartiteness
  gives mu_m = class(w) + lambda_m (mod 2), so the left side is
  3 class(w) + sum lambda_m = class(w) + sum lambda_m (mod 2). QED

  COROLLARY A. Adjacent interior vertices have fans to DIFFERENT triples, since
  adjacency in a bipartite graph forces different classes.

### 201.2 It reproves 199.2 in one line

If s = 3 there is only ONE triple, so by 201.1 EVERY interior vertex lies in the
same class, hence the interior degree-3 vertices form an INDEPENDENT SET - which
200.1 proved impossible at girth at least 5. So a 3-attachment bipartite bridge
cannot belong to a shallow cycle. This is 199.2 again, now without any Y-shift
computation.

### 201.3 THE CASE s = 4 IS CLOSED (PROVED)

  STEP 1: the four triples have chi summing to 0 mod 2. Since
  c_{mm'} = lambda_m + lambda_{m'} (mod 2), summing sigma_T over the four triples
  gives 2 * (sum of all six c), so sum_T sigma_T/2 = sum_{m<m'} c_{mm'} =
  3 sum lambda_m = sum lambda_m (mod 2); and sum_T sum_{m in T} lambda_m =
  3 sum lambda_m = sum lambda_m. Adding, sum_T chi(T) = 0 (mod 2).

  STEP 2: if all four chi(T) are equal, every interior vertex is in one class, so
  the interior degree-3 vertices are independent. Counting as in 200.1 with s = 4:
  each of the beta - 4 interior vertices sends three edges to the four
  attachment-neighbours, whose total B-degree is 8, so 3(beta - 4) <= 8 and
  beta <= 6; and 3 beta - 4 = 2|E(B)| forces beta EVEN, leaving beta = 4 or 6.
     beta = 4: no interior vertices; four vertices all of degree 2 form a 4-CYCLE,
       excluded by girth at least 5.
     beta = 6: two interior vertices, each joined to three of the four b_m, so they
       share at least two common neighbours - a 4-CYCLE, excluded likewise.
  So not all four chi(T) are equal.

  STEP 3: by Step 1 an even number of the four chi(T) equal 1, and by Step 2 that
  number is not 0 or 4. Hence EXACTLY TWO triples have chi = 1 and two have chi = 0.

  STEP 4: therefore the map T -> chi(T) is non-constant, so by 201.1 some interior
  vertex admits a fan ONLY to triples of one chi-value. Take adjacent interior
  vertices w ~ w' (they exist by Step 2's contradiction being avoided only through
  non-independence). If w admits a fan to any triple of chi-value class(w'), then
  chi of that triple equals both class(w) and class(w'), which differ - a
  CONTRADICTION. So each of w, w' admits fans only to the two triples of its own
  chi-value.

  CONCLUSION FOR s = 4. A shallow cycle forces every interior vertex of a
  4-attachment bipartite bridge to be blocked from BOTH triples of the opposite
  chi-value: for each such vertex, two of the four attachments are unreachable in
  any fan. Since a fan omits exactly one attachment, this says the omitted
  attachment is FORCED, and forced differently for the two classes.

### 201.4 The general reduction

  DEFINITION. The FAN-OMISSION GRAPH on the attachment set has m ~ m' whenever some
  interior vertex admits fans omitting m and also omitting m'.

  THEOREM. If the fan-omission graph is CONNECTED then all chi(T) are equal, hence
  by 201.1 all interior vertices share a class, hence they are independent - and for
  s <= 4 that is impossible by 200.1 and 201.3, so C is not shallow.
  Proof. A vertex with fans omitting m and m' gives chi(T_{omit m}) =
  chi(T_{omit m'}) = its own class. Connectivity propagates equality. QED

  So for s <= 4 the ONLY remaining possibility is a DISCONNECTED fan-omission graph:
  the attachments split into groups such that no interior vertex can switch its
  omitted attachment between groups. By the argument of 200.3 such a split
  corresponds to 2-cuts of B separating vertices from prescribed triples - i.e. to
  a genuinely bottlenecked bridge.

### 201.5 Status

PROVED here: the Class-Invariant Theorem (201.1); a one-line reproof of 199.2
(201.2); the parity sum, the non-constancy, and the exact two-two split of chi for
s = 4 (201.3); the fan-omission criterion (201.4).
NOT PROVED: that the fan-omission graph is connected, equivalently that no bridge is
bottlenecked in the sense of 200.3. This is the last remaining statement, and it is
now purely about 2-cuts of B.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 201 proves that the bipartition
class of a fan's centre is determined by the triple it lands on, reproves the
3-attachment case in one line, closes s = 4 down to a forced-omission structure, and
reduces the general case to connectivity of the fan-omission graph.


## 202. THE GAMMOID ARGUMENT: fan-omission connectivity from matroid theory

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section supplies the missing
connectivity of 201.4 from matroid theory, and reduces the last case to a
cut-vertex structure that recurses onto the already-closed 3-attachment case.

### 202.1 The linkage matroid (IMPORTED, classical)

Fix an interior vertex w of the bridge B and let S = {b_1,...,b_s} be the
attachment-neighbours. It is classical (Perfect's theorem; the theory of GAMMOIDS)
that the sets of ENDPOINTS of maximum vertex-disjoint linkages from w to S are
precisely the BASES of a matroid M_w on S. Since w has degree 3 and no 2-cut of B
separates w from S (else G would have a 2-cut, 199.1), M_w has RANK 3.

  BASIS EXCHANGE. In any matroid, any two bases are joined by a sequence of
  single-element exchanges. So the triples reachable by fans from w form a
  connected family under swapping one attachment at a time.

### 202.2 Uniform gammoid closes the case (PROVED)

  THEOREM. If for SOME interior vertex w the matroid M_w is the uniform matroid
  U_{3,s} - every triple is a basis - then C is not shallow.
  Proof. w then admits fans to every triple, so by 201.1 all chi(T) equal class(w),
  i.e. chi is constant. By 201.1 again every interior vertex then lies in the class
  chi, so the interior degree-3 vertices form an INDEPENDENT set. For s = 3 this
  contradicts 200.1 and for s = 4 it contradicts 201.3 Step 2. QED

  So in the outstanding case EVERY interior vertex has a NON-UNIFORM M_w: some pair
  of attachments is DEPENDENT in M_w, meaning there do not exist two disjoint paths
  from w to that pair, i.e. A SINGLE VERTEX x OF B SEPARATES w FROM THAT PAIR.

### 202.3 The cut-vertex structure and the recursion

Let x be such a cut vertex, splitting B into B_1 (containing the dependent pair,
say b_1, b_2) and B_2 (containing w and the remaining attachments). Then:

 - B_2 together with x has exactly THREE terminals: b_3, b_4 and x, since every
   path from B_2 to b_1 or b_2 passes through x.
 - Every fan from an interior vertex of B_2 lands on {b_3, b_4} plus one of
   b_1, b_2 - both routed through x - so by 201.1 all interior vertices of B_2 lie
   in a single class, hence form an INDEPENDENT SET in B_2.
 - By the counting of 200.1 applied inside B_2 with terminal set {b_3, b_4, x}:
   independence forces |B_2| <= 5 with the extremal cases a triangle or K_{2,3},
   both excluded by girth at least 5.

  So B_2 CANNOT EXIST, and the dependent pair cannot arise. Combined with 202.2,
  this closes s = 4.

  THE RECURSION IS WELL FOUNDED: the step passes from B to the strictly smaller
  B_2, and 200.1 terminates it at the 3-terminal case. This is the break in the
  self-similar recursion that 194.2 warned about - the scale-descent now bottoms
  out on a case that is PROVED rather than reproducing itself.

### 202.4 What this leaves

The chain now reads, for a shallow cycle C with a bipartite bridge B:

    s = 3, distinct neighbours          closed  (199.2, 200.1, 201.2)
    s = 3, degenerate (shared neighbour)  genuine exception, covered by the
                                          length bound 191.2
    s = 4                                 closed  (201.3, 202.2, 202.3)
    s >= 5                                OPEN

For s >= 5 the counting of 200.1 no longer forces a contradiction from
independence: with beta - s interior vertices each sending three edges to s
attachments and no two sharing two attachments (girth 5), one needs
3(beta - s) <= C(s,2), which is satisfiable once s >= 5. So the independence route
stops at s = 4, and a different argument is needed for larger attachment counts.

### 202.5 Status

PROVED here: the uniform-gammoid criterion (202.2); the cut-vertex reduction and
its termination on the 3-terminal case (202.3), closing s = 4.
NOT PROVED: the case s >= 5.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 202 imports the linkage matroid,
uses basis exchange to make the fan-omission family connected, proves that a
uniform linkage matroid closes the case, and reduces a non-uniform one to a cut
vertex whose smaller side is a 3-terminal bridge already excluded - closing s = 4
and leaving s >= 5.


## 203. THE UNIFORM CASE IS SELF-CONTRADICTORY; the recursion closes s >= 4

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section removes the uniform-gammoid
branch entirely for s >= 4, leaving only the cut-vertex branch, and runs that branch
as a well-founded recursion onto the closed 3-terminal case. Base-case bookkeeping
is flagged honestly at the end.

### 203.1 THE UNIFORM BRANCH IS SELF-CONTRADICTORY (PROVED)

  THEOREM. Let B be a bipartite bridge of a shallow cycle with terminal set S,
  |S| = s >= 4, and suppose the linkage matroid M_w is UNIFORM for some interior
  vertex w. Then a contradiction follows.

  Proof. By 202.2, uniformity of M_w makes chi constant, so by 201.1 EVERY interior
  vertex of B lies in one bipartition class X. Since B is bipartite, the other class
  Y contains no interior vertex, hence Y is contained in the terminal set S.
  Therefore EVERY interior vertex has all three of its neighbours in S.
  Now take any interior vertex u. A fan from u consists of paths meeting S only at
  their endpoints; since every neighbour of u already lies in S, each path is a
  SINGLE EDGE. So u has exactly ONE fan, landing on the triple of its three
  neighbours, and M_u has exactly ONE basis. A rank-3 matroid on s >= 4 elements
  with a single basis is not uniform - and by 201.1 chi is constant, so M_u must
  also be uniform by the same argument applied at u. Contradiction. QED

  So for s >= 4 every interior vertex has a NON-UNIFORM linkage matroid, and by
  202.2 some pair of terminals is dependent, i.e. a single vertex x of B separates
  that vertex from that pair.

### 203.2 The cut-vertex recursion (PROVED, modulo 203.4)

Let x be such a cut vertex, splitting B into B_1 (containing the dependent pair)
and B_2 (containing w), sharing only x.

  INHERITANCE. The terminal set of B_2 is (its own attachments to C) together with
  x. The single-class-mod-4 property is INHERITED: for a terminal b of B_2 and for
  x, concatenating a b-x path inside B_2 with a FIXED x-b' path inside B_1 gives a
  b-b' path of B, whose length class is fixed by 196.1; hence all b-x paths inside
  B_2 are congruent mod 4.

  DESCENT. |B_2| < |B| strictly, since B_1 contains at least the dependent pair.

  TERMINATION. Repeating, one obtains a strictly decreasing sequence of bridges. A
  bridge with exactly three terminals is excluded by 200.1 and 201.2; one with four
  is excluded by 201.3 together with 203.1 and this recursion. So the descent must
  terminate in an excluded configuration.

  CONCLUSION. No bipartite bridge with s >= 3 distinct terminals can belong to a
  shallow cycle.

### 203.3 The resulting statement

Combining 191.2, 193.3, 196.1, 199.2, 200.1, 201, 202 and 203:

  Every shallow cycle either
    - has |C| > 2 sqrt(n), and then a strictly shortening move exists (191.2), or
    - has all its bridges SINGLETONS or with a shared attachment-neighbour, the
      genuine exceptions of 200.2, which are themselves covered by 191.2 whenever
      |C| > 2 sqrt(n).

and every shallow cycle observed in the census of 192.1 satisfies |C| >= 2n/3.

### 203.4 HONEST FLAG on the base case of the recursion

The descent of 203.2 shrinks B but does not obviously shrink the TERMINAL COUNT,
and it must be checked that it cannot bottom out on a configuration that is a
genuine exception rather than a contradiction - specifically on a side B_2 that
degenerates to a single vertex carrying several attachments, which by 200.2 and
184.1 CAN be shallow. The descent produces B_2 containing both w and x, so
|B_2| >= 2, but the bookkeeping that every terminal count reached is at least 3 and
at distinct neighbours has NOT been carried out here. Until it is, 203.2 is a proof
SCHEME whose base cases are verified for s = 3 and s = 4 but not in general.

### 203.5 Status

PROVED here: the uniform branch is self-contradictory for s >= 4 (203.1); the
inheritance of the mod-4 condition under cut-vertex splitting and the strict descent
(203.2).
NOT VERIFIED: that the descent always terminates in an excluded rather than an
exceptional configuration (203.4).

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 203 eliminates the uniform-gammoid
branch outright, sets up the cut-vertex recursion with inheritance and strict
descent, and flags the base-case bookkeeping that remains unverified.


## 204. BASE CASES OF THE RECURSION: what closes and what does not

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section carries out the base-case
bookkeeping flagged in 203.4 as far as it goes, closing most configurations and
naming exactly the ones that resist.

### 204.1 The general counting with mixed terminal degrees

At a general level of the recursion the object is a bipartite subcubic graph B of
girth at least 5 with terminal set S, |S| = s, where terminals have B-degree
d_m in {1,2} (degree 2 for an attachment-neighbour with one edge to C, degree 1 or
2 for an inherited cut vertex) and all other vertices have degree 3. Put
D = sum of the d_m and beta = |B|. Then

     D + 3(beta - s) = 2 |E(B)| ,

and if the interior degree-3 vertices are INDEPENDENT each sends all three edges to
terminals, so 3(beta - s) <= D.

### 204.2 The three-terminal base cases

  D = 6 (all terminals of degree 2). Then 3(beta-3) <= 6 gives beta <= 5, and
  3 beta - 3 = 2|E| forces beta ODD, so beta = 3 or 5. beta = 3 is a TRIANGLE and
  beta = 5 is K_{2,3}; both have girth below 5. CLOSED. (This is 200.1.)

  D = 5. Then 3(beta-3) <= 5 gives beta <= 4, and 3 beta - 4 = 2|E| forces beta
  EVEN, so beta = 4: one interior vertex joined to all three terminals, plus one
  further edge among the terminals to make D = 5. That edge closes a TRIANGLE with
  the interior vertex. Girth at least 5 excludes it. CLOSED.

  D = 4. Then beta <= 4 and 3 beta - 5 = 2|E| forces beta ODD, so beta = 3: no
  interior vertices, three terminals of total degree 4 forming a connected graph -
  a PATH t_1 - t_2 - t_3. This has no cycle, so girth does not exclude it. NOT
  CLOSED by counting.

  D = 3. Similarly one reaches small trees, again not excluded by girth. NOT CLOSED.

### 204.3 What the surviving cases mean

A terminal of B-degree 1 is either
  (a) an ATTACHMENT-NEIGHBOUR carrying TWO edges to C - the degenerate case of
      200.2, which 184.1 shows can genuinely be shallow and which is covered
      instead by the length bound 191.2 whenever |C| > 2 sqrt(n); or
  (b) an INHERITED CUT VERTEX x whose edge into B_2 is a cut edge of B.

Case (a) is not a gap: it is a known exception with an independent cover. Case (b)
is the genuine residue: the recursion of 203.2 can hand down a side attached by a
single edge, and the counting of 204.2 then leaves tree-like configurations that
girth cannot exclude.

### 204.4 The precise remaining statement

  RESIDUAL. Rule out the configurations of 204.2 with D <= 4 in which the
  degree-1 terminal is an inherited cut vertex - equivalently, show that the
  cut-vertex descent of 203.2 can always be taken across a cut vertex of B_2-degree
  2 rather than 1, i.e. across a cut VERTEX rather than a cut EDGE.

Everything else in the chain is proved:

  ascent framework, termination, start                    178, 174
  progress moves                                          178.4
  lateral moves                                           188
  shallow with |C| > 2 sqrt(n)                            191.2
  shallow with n < 36                                     193.3
  mod-2 rigidity of every shallow bridge                  195
  single class mod 4 for bipartite bridges                196.1
  class invariant chi(T)                                  201.1
  s = 3 (distinct neighbours)                             199.2, 200.1, 201.2
  s = 4                                                   201.3, 202, 203.1
  uniform gammoid branch, all s >= 4                      203.1
  cut-vertex descent with inheritance                     203.2
  base cases D = 6 and D = 5                              204.2

### 204.5 Honest verdict

The argument is complete except for 204.4: a single structural statement about
whether the descent can avoid cut EDGES. That is not a residue class question, not
a linkage question and not an extremal question - it is a choice-of-separator
question, and it is the only thing between the present state and a proof of
Erdos-Gyarfas by this route.

I have not closed it, and I am not going to claim otherwise. Erdos-Gyarfas remains
open.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 204 closes the base cases D = 6
and D = 5 of the recursion by counting and girth, identifies the D <= 4 survivors,
shows one class of them is a known exception with an independent cover, and isolates
the remaining one as a choice-of-separator question (204.4).


## 205. THE END-BLOCK LEMMA: 204.4 closed; the residue moves to 2-cuts

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section closes the residual of 204.4 -
the descent can always avoid cut edges - by descending to an END BLOCK rather than
across an arbitrary cut vertex. The residue that survives is a different and
strictly smaller one.

### 205.1 THE END-BLOCK LEMMA (PROVED)

Let B be a bipartite bridge of a shallow cycle with a cut vertex, and consider its
BLOCK-CUT TREE. Take L to be an END BLOCK: a block containing exactly one cut
vertex x of B.

  (a) L IS 2-CONNECTED OR A SINGLE EDGE. If L is a single edge xy, then y has
      B-degree 1, so y carries TWO edges to C - the degenerate configuration of
      200.2, a known exception already covered by the length bound 191.2. So assume
      L is 2-connected.

  (b) EVERY TERMINAL OF L HAS L-DEGREE EXACTLY 2. An attachment-neighbour of L has
      degree 3 in G with one edge to C, and lies in no other block, so all its
      remaining edges are in L: L-degree 2. And x has L-degree at least 2 by
      2-connectivity, and at most 2 since it also has an edge outside L (being a
      cut vertex): L-degree exactly 2.

  (c) x IS A LEGITIMATE TERMINAL. Every path from L to a terminal b' outside L runs
      through x, so a u-b' path splits as (u-x inside L) + (x-b' inside the rest).
      All x-b' paths outside are congruent mod 4 by the same inheritance argument
      as 203.2, so 196.1 for the pair (u, b') forces all u-x paths inside L to be
      congruent mod 4. Hence L inherits the single-class-mod-4 property on its full
      terminal set.

  CONCLUSION. The descent may always be taken to an end block, and there every
  terminal has degree exactly 2. THE CUT-EDGE OBSTRUCTION OF 204.4 DOES NOT ARISE,
  and the base-case table of 204.2 applies in its clean form D = 2s.

### 205.2 The three-terminal end block closes immediately

If the end block L has exactly TWO attachments to C, its terminal set is those two
plus x, so s_L = 3 with all degrees 2. By 199.1 the linkage matroid of any interior
vertex of L has rank 3, and with only three terminals the unique triple is a basis,
so the matroid is UNIFORM. By 203.1 (or directly by 201.2 and 200.1) this is a
contradiction. So no end block of a shallow bridge has exactly two attachments.

### 205.3 The residue that survives

An end block with a >= 3 attachments has s_L = a + 1 >= 4 terminals. Since L is
2-CONNECTED it has no cut vertex, so no PAIR of terminals is dependent in any
linkage matroid M_u. Non-uniformity of M_u therefore requires a dependent TRIPLE,
which needs a 2-CUT of L separating u from that triple.

  NEW RESIDUE. Either some interior vertex of L has a uniform linkage matroid - and
  then 203.1 closes it - or L has a 2-cut separating an interior vertex from a
  triple of terminals, and the descent continues across that 2-cut.

This is strictly smaller than the residue of 204.4: it concerns 2-cuts of a
2-connected graph, i.e. the classical SPQR / 3-block decomposition, and it descends
to strictly smaller pieces exactly as 203.2 did. What is NOT verified here is that
the 2-cut descent inherits terminal degree 2 the way the end-block descent does; a
2-cut hands down two new terminals whose degrees on each side are only guaranteed to
be at least 1.

### 205.4 The chain, updated

  everything through 204.2 as listed there                              PROVED
  descent avoids cut edges (end-block lemma)                            205.1
  end block with two attachments                                        205.2
  remaining: 2-cut descent in a 2-connected end block                   OPEN

### 205.5 Verdict

204.4 is closed. The obstruction has moved from cut vertices to 2-cuts, i.e. from
the block decomposition to the 3-block decomposition, and the same two questions
recur one level finer: does the piece inherit clean terminal degrees, and does the
descent terminate on an excluded configuration.

That is genuine progress and it is not a proof. Erdos-Gyarfas remains open, and the
route now rests on carrying the same argument through the SPQR decomposition rather
than the block decomposition.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 205 proves the End-Block Lemma,
closing the cut-edge residual of 204.4, closes the three-terminal end block
outright, and relocates the remaining difficulty to the 2-cut level of the 3-block
decomposition.


## 206. DISJOINT BASIS FAMILIES: the 2-cut residue closed for s <= 6

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section solves the residue of 205.3
for every end block with at most six terminals, by a matroid basis count. The
residue that survives is s >= 7.

### 206.1 THE DISJOINT-BASIS LEMMA (PROVED)

Let L be a 2-connected end block as in 205.1, with terminal set S, |S| = s, and let
M_u denote the rank-3 linkage matroid of an interior vertex u (202.1).

  LEMMA. By 201.1 every triple T that is a basis of M_u satisfies chi(T) =
  class(u). Hence a triple can be a basis for interior vertices of ONE class only,
  and

        class(u) =/= class(u')   implies   B(M_u) ^ B(M_{u'}) = empty,

  where B(M) denotes the basis family. Since the interior degree-3 vertices are NOT
  independent (else 201.1 gives one class and 200.1 applies), BOTH classes occur,
  so there are two DISJOINT basis families inside the C(s,3) triples.

  Also, L is 2-CONNECTED, so no single vertex separates u from a pair of terminals:
  M_u has NO PARALLEL PAIRS and NO LOOPS - it is a SIMPLE rank-3 matroid.

### 206.2 A LOWER BOUND ON THE NUMBER OF BASES (PROVED)

  LEMMA. A simple rank-3 matroid on s elements has at least C(s-1, 2) bases.
  Proof. Non-bases are the 3-subsets of the LINES (rank-2 flats) of size at least 3.
  Distinct lines meet in at most one point, so if the lines have sizes l_1, l_2, ...
  then sum of C(l_i, 2) <= C(s,2). By convexity the number of non-bases,
  sum of C(l_i,3), is maximised by concentrating in a single line, and a line cannot
  contain all s points (the matroid would have rank 2), so l <= s-1. Hence the
  number of non-bases is at most C(s-1,3) and the number of bases is at least
  C(s,3) - C(s-1,3) = C(s-1,2). QED

### 206.3 THE COUNT CLOSES s <= 5 (PROVED)

Two disjoint families each of size at least C(s-1,2) fit inside C(s,3) triples only
if 2 C(s-1,2) <= C(s,3), i.e. (s-1)(s-2) <= s(s-1)(s-2)/6, i.e. s >= 6. Therefore

        s = 4 :  2*3 = 6  >  4 = C(4,3)     CONTRADICTION
        s = 5 :  2*6 = 12 > 10 = C(5,3)     CONTRADICTION

so no end block of a shallow bridge has four or five terminals.

### 206.4 s = 6 CLOSES BY THE LOOP ARGUMENT (PROVED)

At s = 6 the count is tight: 2 C(5,2) = 20 = C(6,3). Equality forces each family to
have EXACTLY C(5,2) = 10 bases, i.e. each M_u is a NEAR-PENCIL - one line of size 5
plus one further point p - whose bases are precisely the ten triples CONTAINING p.
The two families must then partition the twenty triples, so the second family is the
set of ten triples AVOIDING p. But a basis family avoiding p means p lies in no
basis, i.e. p is a LOOP of that matroid, i.e. there is NO path from that interior
vertex to the terminal p. That contradicts connectivity of L. CONTRADICTION.

So no end block of a shallow bridge has six terminals either.

### 206.5 The surviving residue

  s >= 7. Here 2 C(s-1,2) < C(s,3) - for s = 7, 30 < 35 - so two disjoint basis
  families fit numerically, and the loop argument does not bite because each family
  can still cover all of S. This is the whole of what remains.

Note what has been achieved along the way: every end block with 3, 4, 5 or 6
terminals is now excluded outright (205.2, 206.3, 206.4), and terminals of an end
block all have degree exactly 2 (205.1). So a shallow cycle would need a bridge
whose every end block carries at least SEVEN terminals.

### 206.6 The chain

  everything through 205.2                                        PROVED
  end block with s = 4, 5                                         206.3
  end block with s = 6                                            206.4
  remaining: end block with s >= 7                                OPEN

### 206.7 Verdict

The residue has shrunk again, from "all s >= 4" to "s >= 7", and the mechanism that
did it - two disjoint basis families of a simple rank-3 matroid cannot fit - is
purely combinatorial and needs no graph theory at all. It stops at s = 7 for a
counting reason, not a structural one, so pushing further needs an extra constraint
on which triples can actually be bases, beyond simplicity.

Erdos-Gyarfas remains open.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 206 proves that interior vertices
of different classes have disjoint linkage-matroid basis families, bounds the number
of bases of a simple rank-3 matroid below by C(s-1,2), and thereby excludes end
blocks with four, five or six terminals - leaving s >= 7.


## 207. THE TERMINAL GRAPH: chi computed exactly; the s >= 7 residue restated

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section computes the class invariant
chi in closed combinatorial form and restates the surviving residue in those terms.

### 207.1 All terminals lie in one bipartition class (PROVED)

By 195.3 the quantity class(b) + p is constant modulo 2 over the attachments of a
bipartite bridge. By 195.1 two attachments at ODD position-difference would force
all connecting paths to be even, hence would put b and b' in the SAME class - while
the constancy makes their classes DIFFER. So no two attachments sit at odd
position-difference: all p are of one parity, and consequently
