  LEMMA. Let Z and Z' be VERTEX-DISJOINT odd cycles of B. Then one of them contains at
  most ONE terminal, and hence there are TWO terminals avoiding it.
  Proof. There are exactly three terminals and Z, Z' are disjoint, so they cannot both
  contain two or more. QED

So relabel: Z contains at most one terminal, and b_i, b_j are two terminals with
b_i, b_j not on Z. Note Z' survives intact in B - V(Z), since Z and Z' are disjoint.

### 255.3 THE TWO-CYCLE LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let Z, Z' be disjoint odd cycles, and b_i, b_j two terminals off Z as supplied
  by 255.2. If b_i and b_j are joined in B - V(Z) by paths of BOTH parities, then (L2**)
  HOLDS.
  Proof. Take an EVEN b_i-b_j path P inside B - V(Z). Its interior avoids V(Z)
  entirely, so it misses the odd cycle Z and is therefore NOT an odd cycle transversal.
  By 250.2 that is exactly the condition under which the pair (b_i,b_j) admits two
  internally disjoint even connecting paths. QED

  So the implication nu_odd >= 2 ==> (L2**), measured at 254.1 on 273 instances without
  exception, reduces to a single connectivity-and-parity condition on B - V(Z), and the
  witness for its non-bipartiteness is HANDED TO US: Z' lies in B - V(Z) untouched.

### 255.4 What is missing, exactly

By the classical fact of 195.2, b_i and b_j have paths of both parities in B - V(Z)
provided some BLOCK OF B - V(Z) ON THE b_i-b_j ROUTE IS NON-BIPARTITE. Two things must
hold and neither is automatic:

  (1) b_i and b_j lie in the same component of B - V(Z);
  (2) the odd cycle Z' lies in a block of that component through which the b_i-b_j route
      passes.

B is 2-connected, so deleting the vertex set of a cycle can disconnect it; and Z' can
sit in a block hanging off the route rather than on it. Choosing Z to be a SHORTEST odd
cycle keeps the deletion small - in a subcubic graph a cycle of length l has exactly l
edges leaving it, so B - V(Z) inherits l attachment points - which makes both conditions
plausible, but plausible is not proved.

  I state this without dressing it up: 255.3 is a genuine reduction of 254.1 to a
  connectivity statement, and that statement is not established.

### 255.5 And (PACK-2) remains

Even with 255.3-255.4 completed, one would still need (PACK-2): that a surviving bridge
HAS two disjoint odd cycles. 254.3 records why k = 2 is the right place to be - the
Lovasz-Slilaty structure theorem is complete there, and its internally-4-connected form
demands a triangle, which girth 5 forbids - but our bridges are subcubic, so only the
low-connectivity part of that characterisation applies and it has not been worked out.

### 255.6 Status

PROVED here: the reduction of the failure of (L2**) to "every even connecting path's
interior meets every odd cycle" (255.1); the pigeonhole that two disjoint odd cycles
cannot both contain two of the three terminals, so one is avoided by two terminals
(255.2); and the Two-Cycle Lemma - an even b_i-b_j path inside B - V(Z) immediately
contradicts the failure (255.3).
NOT PROVED: that b_i and b_j lie in one component of B - V(Z) with Z' on their route
(255.4); and (PACK-2) (255.5). Hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 255 replaces the pigeonhole over
terminal pairs, which has failed since 230, by a pigeonhole over cycles against
terminals: two disjoint odd cycles cannot both contain two of the three terminals, so
some pair avoids one of them entirely. The Two-Cycle Lemma then shows a single even
connecting path inside the complement of that cycle refutes the failure of (L2**),
reducing 254.1's measured implication to the connectivity of that complement - which is
not proved, as (PACK-2) is not.


## 256. THREE SIMPLE FACTS ABOUT THE SURVIVING CASE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Three short proofs, each one line of idea.

### 256.1 THE TRANSVERSAL IS A PATH (PROVED)

If (L2**) fails for a pair, then by 250.3 the interior of every even connecting path
alpha between them is an odd cycle transversal. But interior(alpha) is the interior of a
PATH, hence a CONNECTED set of at most |alpha| - 1 vertices. So

     tau_odd(B) <= |alpha| - 1 ,   and B minus a short PATH is BIPARTITE.

With |alpha| between 6 and 8 throughout the census, that is a connected transversal of at
most seven vertices in a graph of at least twenty-one. Every odd cycle of B must run
through that one short path.

### 256.2 VERTEX-DISJOINT AND EDGE-DISJOINT COINCIDE (PROVED)

  LEMMA. In a subcubic graph, two cycles are vertex-disjoint if and only if they are
  edge-disjoint.
  Proof. Edge-disjoint clearly does not imply vertex-disjoint in general - but in a
  subcubic graph it does. If two cycles share a vertex v, then each uses TWO of v's
  edges, and v has at most three; two pairs from a set of three must overlap, so they
  share an edge at v. Hence sharing a vertex forces sharing an edge, and the converse is
  trivial. QED

  CONSEQUENCE. For B, nu_odd computed with vertex-disjointness equals nu_odd computed
  with EDGE-disjointness. So (PACK-2) may be read either way, and 254's whole discussion
  transfers to the edge version - where the Erdos-Posa theory is better behaved
  (Kawarabayashi-Kobayashi prove the integral edge version for 4-edge-connected graphs,
  though B, being subcubic, is at most 3-edge-connected and so is not covered).

### 256.3 (SC) MAKES ALL ODD CYCLES SHARE EDGES (PROVED)

By 254.2, (SC) forces nu_odd(B) <= 1: no two disjoint odd cycles. By 256.2 that now reads

     EVERY TWO ODD CYCLES OF B SHARE AN EDGE.

  COROLLARY. Let Z be a shortest odd cycle. Then E(Z) meets every odd cycle, so
  B - E(Z) is BIPARTITE: deleting the edges of ONE shortest odd cycle destroys all
  odd cycles at once.

  Combined with 256.1, a surviving bridge admits both a connected VERTEX transversal of
  at most seven vertices and an EDGE transversal of size equal to its odd girth. Its odd
  cycles are packed into a very small part of the graph.

### 256.4 What these do and do not do

They sharpen the description of the surviving case and they make (PACK-2) interchangeable
with its edge version. They do NOT prove (PACK-2), and they do not supply the component
condition of 255.4. The obstruction is unchanged: exhibit one even connecting path whose
interior misses one odd cycle.

### 256.5 Status

PROVED here: the odd cycle transversal produced by a failing pair is the interior of a
path, hence connected and of size at most |alpha| - 1 (256.1); in a subcubic graph
vertex-disjointness and edge-disjointness of cycles coincide (256.2); and (SC) forces
every two odd cycles of B to share an edge, so deleting the edges of one shortest odd
cycle makes B bipartite (256.3).
NOT PROVED: (PACK-2); the component condition of 255.4; hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and
the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 256 records three short facts: the
transversal handed over by a failing pair is a connected path interior of at most seven
vertices; in subcubic graphs vertex-disjoint and edge-disjoint cycles are the same notion,
so (PACK-2) has an edge form; and (SC) forces every two odd cycles of a surviving bridge
to share an edge, so one shortest odd cycle's edge set is a transversal. None of this
closes the gap.


## 257. THE LOVASZ-SLILATY THEOREM APPLIED TO (PACK-2)

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The literature does contain the tool (PACK-2)
needs, in complete form. This section imports it and works out what it says about a
surviving bridge.

### 257.1 The theorem (IMPORTED)

  SLILATY, "Projective-planar signed graphs and tangled signed graphs", J. Combin.
  Theory Ser. B (2007), completing and publishing LOVASZ's unpublished characterisation:

     Every signed graph with NO TWO VERTEX-DISJOINT NEGATIVE CIRCLES and NO BALANCING
     VERTEX is obtained from a PROJECTIVE-PLANAR signed graph, or from a copy of -K_5,
     by taking 1-, 2- and 3-SUMS with BALANCED signed graphs.

  A signed graph is BALANCED when every circle is positive; a BALANCING VERTEX is a
  vertex whose deletion leaves a balanced graph. Taking the all-negative signature,
  negative circles are exactly ODD CYCLES and balanced means BIPARTITE. A projective-
  planar signed graph has no two vertex-disjoint negative circles - that is the source
  of the characterisation.

### 257.2 What it says about B (PROVED, given 254.2)

By 254.2, (SC) forces nu_odd(B) <= 1. Applying the theorem to B with the all-negative
signature, exactly one of the following holds:

  (i)   B has a BALANCING VERTEX v: a single vertex whose deletion leaves B BIPARTITE;
  (ii)  B is built by 1-, 2-, 3-sums of BIPARTITE pieces onto a PROJECTIVE-PLANAR core;
  (iii) B is built the same way onto a -K_5 core.

### 257.3 Branch (i) recurses onto 196-208 - the same move as 242 (PROVED in outline)

If v is a balancing vertex then B - v is BIPARTITE. Its degree-2 vertices are the three
terminals together with the (at most three) neighbours of v, which lose one edge each -
so B - v is a bipartite subcubic graph of girth at least 5 with AT LEAST THREE and at
most six vertices of degree 2. That is precisely the object 205.2 and 208.2 exclude,
PROVIDED the single-class-mod-4 property transfers to it.

  And the transfer is the argument of 242.2 again: vary a connecting path inside B - v
  while holding the rest fixed. What must be checked is that enough connecting paths
  avoid v to make the variation legitimate - the same bookkeeping 243 carried out for
  the fenced case, not yet done here.

  Note also that a balancing vertex means tau_odd(B) = 1, whereas 256.1 gives a
  transversal that is a path interior of up to seven vertices; branch (i) says the
  transversal can be taken to be a SINGLE VERTEX, which is much stronger and should make
  the recursion easier, not harder.

### 257.4 Branches (ii) and (iii), honestly

  (iii) -K_5. I first thought this was immediate: K_5 is 4-regular and B is subcubic. It
  is NOT immediate, because the theorem allows a -K_5 CORE reached through 1-, 2- and
  3-sums, and a K_5 minor can perfectly well live in a subcubic graph - the Petersen
  graph has one, using two-vertex branch sets. So this branch needs the sum structure
  examined, not a degree count. I withdraw the quick argument.

  (ii) PROJECTIVE-PLANAR. Euler does not exclude it: a projective-planar graph of girth
  at least 5 satisfies |E| <= (5/3)(|V| - 1), and B has |E| = (3|B| - 3)/2, which gives
  9n - 9 <= 10n - 10, i.e. n >= 1. No contradiction. Nor does the literature help
  directly: HECKMAN and KRAKOVSKI proved Erdos-Gyarfas for 3-connected cubic PLANAR
  graphs, but there is no projective-planar analogue, and in any case that theorem
  applies to the ambient G rather than to a bridge.

  What is available is 155's Mac Lane dichotomy - planarity is exactly where the mod-4
  layer of the degree filtration is linear - and the projective plane is the first
  surface where it is not. That is suggestive of where to look, not an argument.

### 257.5 The synthesis, stated plainly

The tools ARE in the literature and they are complete at k = 2, which is why 254's move
from three disjoint odd cycles to two mattered. What is needed is:

  - branch (i): finish the 242-style recursion for a balancing vertex, with the 243-style
    hypothesis audit;
  - branch (ii): exclude a projective-planar core of girth at least 5 carrying three
    terminals pairwise at distance at least 5;
  - branch (iii): examine the -K_5 core through the sum decomposition.

None of the three is done here. But this is the first point in the program where the
remaining case analysis is FINITE and named, rather than an open extremal question.

### 257.6 Status

IMPORTED: the Lovasz-Slilaty characterisation of graphs with no two vertex-disjoint odd
cycles, in its complete form (257.1).
PROVED: (SC) plus 254.2 puts B into exactly one of the three branches (257.2); and in
branch (i) the bipartite graph B - v carries at least three degree-2 vertices, the object
205.2/208.2 exclude (257.3).
CORRECTED: my first reaction that -K_5 is excluded by subcubicity is WRONG - K_5 minors
exist in subcubic graphs (257.4).
NOT PROVED: any of the three branches; hence (PACK-2), (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 257 imports the complete
Lovasz-Slilaty characterisation of graphs with no two vertex-disjoint odd cycles and
applies it to a surviving bridge, which must then have a balancing vertex, a
projective-planar core, or a -K_5 core. The balancing-vertex branch recurses onto the
bipartite machinery of 196-208 by the method of 242; the other two are not excluded, and
the quick degree argument against -K_5 is withdrawn as wrong.


## 258. THE DIRECT ROUTE: apply 199-201 to B minus the transversal

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section replaces 257's three-branch
Slilaty analysis by a single route with a single gap. It does not close it.

### 258.1 The idea

250.3 already hands us a bipartite graph. If (L2**) fails for a pair, then
interior(alpha) is an odd cycle transversal, so

     B' := B - interior(alpha)   IS BIPARTITE.

There is no need for Slilaty, no balancing vertex, no projective-planar core: apply the
bipartite machinery of 199-201 directly to B'.

### 258.2 What B' inherits, for free (PROVED)

  (a) ALL THREE TERMINALS LIE IN B'. The endpoints b_1, b_2 of alpha are not in its
      interior, and 251.2 proved b_3 is not either, since b_3 inside alpha would force
      |alpha| >= d(b_1,b_3) + d(b_3,b_2) >= 10 while |alpha| <= 8.

  (b) THE PAIRWISE CLASSES COME FOR FREE. Every path of B' between two terminals is a
      path of B between two terminals, so (SC) applies to it directly. No transfer
      argument of the 242.2 kind is needed - this is the cleanest inheritance in the
      whole programme.

  (c) B' IS BIPARTITE, SUBCUBIC, OF GIRTH AT LEAST 5, and large: |B| >= 21 and
      |interior(alpha)| <= 7 give |B'| >= 14. Each of the at most 7 deleted interior
      vertices had one edge leaving alpha, so at most 7 vertices of B' drop to degree 2,
      and b_1, b_2 drop to degree 1; every other vertex keeps degree 3.

### 258.3 What 199.2 would need

The Y-Shift Lemma 199.2 derives a contradiction from: bipartiteness, the three pairwise
classes c_{mm'} modulo 4, and TWO ADJACENT INTERIOR VERTICES OF DEGREE 3 EACH CARRYING A
Y - a fan of three internally disjoint paths to the three terminals.

  ADJACENT DEGREE-3 VERTICES EXIST. B' has at least 14 vertices of which at most 9 have
  degree below 3, so at least 5 have degree 3; were they independent they would send all
  their edges into the low-degree set, and the counting of 200.1 bounds that immediately.

  So the only missing ingredient is the Y's.

### 258.4 THE TWO GAPS, stated plainly

  (1) THE FANS. A Y at w needs three internally disjoint paths from w to {b_1,b_2,b_3}
      inside B'. By Menger that fails exactly when a 2-cut of B' separates w from the
      terminals. In B the same statement was rescued by the 3-connectivity of G (199.1,
      repaired at 243.3), but B' is B with up to seven vertices DELETED, and that
      argument does not survive the deletion: a 2-cut of B' need not be a 2-cut of B.

  (2) THE PARITIES. (SC) constrains only EVEN connecting paths. In the bipartite B' all
      b_i-b_j paths share a parity, so c_{ij} is pinned modulo 4 only when that parity is
      EVEN. With three terminals in two colour classes, pigeonhole gives at least ONE
      same-class pair, hence at least one genuine c_{ij}; 199.2 needs ALL THREE. So the
      colours must cooperate, and nothing so far forces them to.

  Gap (2) is the sharper of the two: it is a statement about how the three terminals are
  coloured in B', and 240.4 shows what having all three in one class would buy. If all
  three terminals lie in the SAME class of B', all three pairs have even connecting paths,
  all three c_{ij} exist, and 199.2 fires - modulo gap (1).

### 258.5 Why this is better than 257

257 left three branches, two of them - projective-planar and -K_5 cores - with no
obvious attack and with my first argument against -K_5 withdrawn as wrong. 258 leaves
ONE object, B', with two explicit conditions on it, both about B' alone and neither
requiring any structure theorem. The bipartite graph that 250.3 produces is the natural
place to apply machinery built for bipartite graphs, and it took until now to notice.

### 258.6 Status

PROVED here: all three terminals survive in B' (258.2a); the pairwise mod-4 classes
transfer to B' with no argument at all, since its terminal-to-terminal paths ARE
connecting paths of B (258.2b); B' is bipartite, subcubic, of girth at least 5, on at
least 14 vertices with at most 9 of degree below 3 (258.2c); and adjacent degree-3
vertices exist in it (258.3).
NOT PROVED: the existence of the fans in B' (258.4.1), and that the three terminals share
a colour class of B' so that all three mod-4 classes are defined (258.4.2). Hence (L2**),
(INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 258 observes that the failure of (L2**)
directly produces a bipartite graph B' = B - interior(alpha) containing all three
terminals, whose terminal-to-terminal paths are connecting paths of B so that the mod-4
classes transfer for free, and to which the Y-Shift machinery of 199-201 applies. This
replaces 257's three Slilaty branches by a single object with two explicit gaps: the
existence of fans in B', and the colouring of the three terminals within it.


## 259. MANUFACTURED TERMINALS: gap (2) largely closed

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Gap (2) of 258.4 turns out to be attackable by
a device the programme has not used: CREATING new terminals for B' out of the deleted
path's neighbourhood. The device works; the pigeonhole it feeds is tight.

### 259.1 First, the bad news about the obvious three terminals (PROVED)

252.3 proved that when a pair fails, B - interior(alpha) is bipartite and contains the
ODD arc of an odd cycle through b_1 and b_2. So b_1 and b_2 lie in DIFFERENT classes of
B', every b_1-b_2 path in B' is ODD, and c_12 is NOT DEFINED - (SC) constrains only even
paths. The third terminal shares a class with exactly one of them, so at most ONE of the
three classes c_12, c_13, c_23 exists.

  THE ORIGINAL THREE TERMINALS CANNOT FEED 199.2. Gap (2) is not a technicality to be
  arranged; for those three vertices it genuinely fails.

### 259.2 MANUFACTURING TERMINALS (PROVED)

Let x be an interior vertex of alpha. By 251.2 no terminal lies inside alpha, so x has
degree 3 in B and exactly ONE edge leaving alpha, to a vertex u of B'. In B', u has
degree 2. Now:

  LEMMA. u carries a well-defined class modulo 4 relative to b_1. Precisely, all EVEN
  b_1-u paths Q inside B' are congruent modulo 4.
  Proof. Given such a Q, the concatenation

       Q  +  edge u x  +  the tail of alpha from x to b_2

  is a b_1-b_2 path of B: Q lies in B' so avoids interior(alpha) entirely, and the tail
  lies inside alpha, so the two are disjoint and the concatenation is SIMPLE. Its length
  is |Q| + 1 + (length of the tail), with the tail fixed once x is fixed. So (SC) applied
  to the pair (b_1,b_2) forces |Q| to be constant modulo 4. QED

  THE SAME FOR PAIRS OF MANUFACTURED TERMINALS. If u, u' come from interior vertices x,
  x' of alpha with x before x', then for any u-u' path R inside B',

       (head of alpha from b_1 to x) + x u + R + u' x' + (tail of alpha from x' to b_2)

  is again a simple b_1-b_2 path of B, so |R| is constant modulo 4 as well.

  So the neighbourhood of the deleted path supplies B' with terminals of degree 2 whose
  pairwise mod-4 classes are all defined - exactly the input 199-201 need.

### 259.3 How many manufactured terminals there are (PROVED)

alpha has |alpha| - 1 interior vertices, each contributing one edge to B'. A single
vertex u can absorb two of those edges only if its two neighbours on alpha are at
alpha-distance at least 3, since a shorter gap would close a cycle of length below 5. So
each u absorbs AT MOST TWO, and the number of DISTINCT manufactured terminals is at
least ceil((|alpha| - 1)/2).

     |alpha| = 6 : at least 3 manufactured terminals, plus b_3, so at least 4 candidates
     |alpha| = 8 : at least 4 manufactured terminals, plus b_3, so at least 5 candidates

Each candidate lies in one of the two classes of the bipartite B'. Pigeonhole gives THREE
in a common class when there are five candidates, i.e. when |alpha| = 8; with only four
candidates it gives just two.

  So gap (2) CLOSES when |alpha| = 8 and remains open when |alpha| = 6. The census of
  250.1 and 251.1 recorded |alpha| between 6 and 8 with median 6, so the open case is the
  typical one - I am not going to claim the gap is closed.

### 259.4 What is now needed

  - For |alpha| = 6: find a fifth candidate terminal, or a version of 199.2 that runs on
    two same-class terminals plus one of the opposite class. 199.3 explains why two alone
    are useless, but the third terminal there was of the same kind; a mixed triple has not
    been analysed.
  - Gap (1) of 258.4 is untouched: the fans in B'. Deleting up to seven vertices from B
    destroys the 3-connectivity argument of 199.1/243.3, and nothing replaces it.

### 259.5 Status

PROVED here: b_1 and b_2 lie in different classes of B', so the original terminals cannot
feed 199.2 (259.1); manufactured terminals - the B'-neighbours of alpha's interior -
carry well-defined mod-4 classes, both to b_1 and to each other, by concatenating with
pieces of alpha (259.2); and girth at least 5 forces at least ceil((|alpha|-1)/2) distinct
ones (259.3).
NOT PROVED: the case |alpha| = 6, where the pigeonhole yields only two same-class
candidates; and gap (1), the existence of fans in B'. Hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 259 shows the original three terminals
cannot supply the mod-4 classes B' needs, because the failure itself puts b_1 and b_2 in
opposite classes; it then manufactures new terminals from the neighbourhood of the deleted
path, proving their pairwise classes are defined by concatenation with pieces of alpha,
and counts at least ceil((|alpha|-1)/2) of them. That closes gap (2) when |alpha| = 8 but
not when |alpha| = 6, which the census says is the typical case; gap (1) is untouched.


## 260. GAP (1) CLOSED: fans exist in B'

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Reverse-engineering what the fans would REQUIRE
identifies the right terminal set for B', and with that set the fans exist - by the same
3-connectivity argument that 199.1 used and 243.3 repaired, now surviving the deletion.

### 260.1 Reverse-engineering

A fan from an interior vertex w of B' to a set T of terminals exists, by Menger, unless
some 2-CUT {p,q} of B' leaves w in a component containing NO vertex of T. So the fans
exist if and only if EVERY component of B' - {p,q} meets T, for every pair {p,q}.

Working backwards: what would make that automatic? Only that a T-free component be
IMPOSSIBLE - and a component is impossible exactly when its existence would contradict
the 3-connectivity of G. For that, the component must have NO edge to the rest of G. Its
possible escapes are: through p or q; through an edge to the DELETED set interior(alpha);
or through a terminal's edge to C. So T must be chosen to block the last two.

  THAT DICTATES THE CHOICE OF T: take T to consist of EVERY vertex of B' adjacent to
  interior(alpha), together with the terminal b_3.

  Note that b_1 and b_2 belong to T automatically: they are the ENDPOINTS of alpha, so
  each is adjacent to the first, respectively last, vertex of interior(alpha).

### 260.2 THE FAN LEMMA FOR B' (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let T be as in 260.1. Then every vertex w of B' has THREE internally disjoint
  paths to T.

  Proof. Suppose not. By Menger some pair {p,q} of vertices of B' separates w from T, so
  the component K of B' - {p,q} containing w meets T not at all. Consider K inside G.
  - K has no edge to interior(alpha): such an edge would have its B'-end adjacent to
    interior(alpha), hence in T, hence not in K.
  - K contains no terminal of B: b_1, b_2 and b_3 all lie in T. So K has no edge to C.
  - Therefore every edge leaving K ends at p or at q.
  Hence {p,q} separates K from the rest of G, contradicting the 3-CONNECTIVITY OF G. QED

  GAP (1) OF 258.4 IS CLOSED. The 3-connectivity argument of 199.1, which 243.3 repaired
  for the fenced case and which I feared at 258.4 would not survive deleting up to seven
  vertices, DOES survive - provided the terminal set is enlarged to include everything
  adjacent to the deleted path. That enlargement is exactly what 259.2 had already shown
  carries well-defined mod-4 classes.

### 260.3 What the two sections now give together

  259.2: every vertex of T carries a mod-4 class, obtained by concatenating with a piece
         of alpha, and pairs of them do too.
  260.2: every interior vertex of B' has a fan to T.

  So B' is a bipartite, subcubic, girth-5 graph with a terminal set T that is both
  CLASS-BEARING and FAN-REACHABLE - precisely the two hypotheses the machinery of
  199-201 consumes.

### 260.4 The one thing still missing

201.1 assigns chi(T') to a TRIPLE T' of terminals, and its proof needs the three pairwise
classes c_{mm'} to EXIST - which requires the three pairwise connecting paths to be EVEN,
i.e. the triple to lie in ONE class of the bipartite B'. 260.2 delivers a fan to SOME
triple of T, not to a prescribed one.

  So the remaining question is exactly 259.3's pigeonhole, now sharpened: is there a
  same-class triple inside T that every interior vertex can reach by a fan? |T| is at
  least ceil((|alpha|-1)/2) + 3 counting b_1, b_2, b_3, which is at least 6 when
  |alpha| = 6 and at least 7 when |alpha| = 8 - comfortably enough for a same-class
  triple to EXIST by pigeonhole. What is not established is that the fans can be steered
  onto it.

### 260.5 Status

PROVED here: the correct terminal set for B' is everything adjacent to the deleted path
together with b_3, and b_1, b_2 lie in it automatically (260.1); with that set, every
vertex of B' has three internally disjoint paths to it, because a T-free component would
be cut off from interior(alpha), from C and from everything but two vertices,
contradicting the 3-connectivity of G (260.2). GAP (1) IS CLOSED.
NOT PROVED: that the fans can be steered onto a SAME-CLASS triple, which is what 201.1
requires (260.4). Hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 260 reverse-engineers what the fans in
B' would require, finds it dictates enlarging the terminal set to everything adjacent to
the deleted path, and proves that with that set every vertex of B' has a fan - closing
gap (1) of 258.4 by the 3-connectivity of the ambient graph. Combined with 259.2 the
terminal set is both class-bearing and fan-reachable; what remains is to steer the fans
onto a triple lying in one bipartition class.


## 261. THE POSITION FORMULA: the classes of T are explicit

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Reverse-engineering what would put three
terminals of T in one class produces an exact congruence, and the congruence decides the
classes outright by POSITION ALONG alpha.

### 261.1 Reverse-engineering

To steer a fan onto a same-class triple one must first KNOW the classes. A fan from a
degree-3 vertex has only three legs, so no pigeonhole is available at w itself: the
classes of T must be pinned in advance. So the question becomes: what determines whether
u_i, the B'-neighbour of the i-th interior vertex of alpha, lies in b_1's class?

### 261.2 THE POSITION FORMULA (PROVED)

Write alpha = b_1 = a_0, a_1, ..., a_L = b_2 with L = |alpha| EVEN, and let u_i be the
B'-neighbour of a_i for 1 <= i <= L-1.

  Since alpha is itself an even connecting path of length L, (SC) says EVERY even
  connecting path between b_1 and b_2 has length congruent to L modulo 4.

  Now let Q be any b_1-u_i path inside B'. As in 259.2,

        Q  +  u_i a_i  +  alpha[a_i .. b_2]

  is a simple b_1-b_2 path of B, of length |Q| + 1 + (L - i). If that length is EVEN it
  must be congruent to L modulo 4, giving

        |Q|  =  i - 1   (mod 4).

  And it is even precisely when |Q| + 1 + L - i is even, i.e. - since L is even - when
  |Q| = i - 1 modulo 2. So:

     u_i LIES IN THE SAME BIPARTITION CLASS OF B' AS b_1  IF AND ONLY IF  i IS ODD,
     and then every even b_1-u_i path has length exactly i - 1 modulo 4.

  Symmetrically u_i shares b_2's class exactly when i is EVEN. And b_2 itself is in the
  class opposite b_1, which is 259.1 again, now visible as the case i = L.

  THE CLASSES OF T ARE THEREFORE READ OFF FROM POSITION ALONG alpha, with no further
  argument, and the mod-4 class of each is given explicitly by i - 1.

### 261.3 The same-class family (PROVED)

The odd indices in 1..L-1 number exactly L/2, so

     |alpha| = 6 : u_1, u_3, u_5   - three candidates in b_1's class
     |alpha| = 8 : u_1, u_3, u_5, u_7 - four candidates

all with explicitly known mod-4 classes 0, 2, 0, 2 respectively. This is exactly the
same-class triple 260.4 asked for, and it is now identified rather than merely counted.

  DISTINCTNESS, honestly. Two of these can coincide: u_i = u_j requires a common
  neighbour of a_i and a_j, which closes a cycle of length |i-j| + 2, so girth 5 forces
  |i-j| >= 3, and for odd i, j that means |i-j| >= 4. For L = 6 the only possible
  collision is u_1 = u_5; for L = 8 the possible collisions are u_1 = u_5, u_1 = u_7,
  u_3 = u_7. Since 259.3's bound says each vertex absorbs at most two positions, at least
  ceil(L/4) of them are distinct - which is 2 for L = 6 and L = 8. So a same-class TRIPLE
  of distinct vertices is guaranteed only when the collisions do not occur, and I have not
  ruled them out.

### 261.4 The bridge, and what is left of it

  260.2 gives every interior vertex of B' a fan to T.
  261.2 gives every member of T an explicitly known class and mod-4 value.
  261.3 identifies the same-class family inside T as the odd-position neighbours.

  What remains is the conjunction: a fan landing on THREE DISTINCT odd-position
  neighbours. 260.2 guarantees a fan to T but not which members it reaches; 261.3
  guarantees at least two distinct odd-position members but not three when the collisions
  u_1 = u_5 or u_1 = u_7 or u_3 = u_7 occur.

  So the gap has narrowed from "steer the fans onto an unknown same-class triple" to
  "avoid at most three explicit coincidences and land the fan on odd positions". That is
  a finite, concrete residue - but it is a residue.

### 261.5 Status

PROVED here: the Position Formula - u_i shares b_1's class exactly when i is odd, and
then every even b_1-u_i path has length i - 1 modulo 4 (261.2); consequently the
same-class family inside T is exactly the odd-position neighbours, of which there are L/2
(261.3).
NOT PROVED: that three of them are DISTINCT (the collisions u_1 = u_5, u_1 = u_7,
u_3 = u_7 are not excluded), nor that a fan can be steered onto three of them. Hence
(L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 261 reverse-engineers the class question
and answers it exactly: because alpha is itself an even connecting path, (SC) forces every
even b_1-u_i path to have length i - 1 modulo 4, so u_i lies in b_1's class precisely when
i is odd. The same-class family in T is thus explicitly the odd-position neighbours. What
remains is that three of them be distinct and simultaneously reachable by one fan.


## 262. DISTINCTNESS CLOSED; the residue is a single fan statement

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Reverse-engineering the conjunction of 261.4
disposes of the distinctness problem completely and shows that whichever size the
same-class family has, the machinery of 201 closes it. One statement is left.

### 262.1 DISTINCTNESS IS NOT A PROBLEM (PROVED)

261.3 worried that the odd-position neighbours u_1, u_3, u_5, ... might collide. They
might - but b_1 ITSELF belongs to its own class, and b_1 is a vertex of B'. So the
same-class family is

     T1  =  {b_1}  union  {u_i : i odd, 1 <= i <= L-1} .

  LEMMA. b_1, u_1 and u_3 are three DISTINCT vertices of T1.
  Proof. u_1 and u_3 are the neighbours of a_1 and a_3 NOT lying on alpha, so neither is
  b_1 = a_0. And u_1 = u_3 would give a common neighbour of a_1 and a_3, closing a cycle
  of length 4, below the girth. QED

  So a same-class triple of distinct vertices ALWAYS exists, for every L, and 261.3's
  collisions u_1 = u_5, u_1 = u_7, u_3 = u_7 are irrelevant. Distinctness is closed.

### 262.2 The two families, explicitly (PROVED)

By the Position Formula 261.2 the terminal set of B' splits by parity of position:

     T1 = {b_1} + {u_i : i odd}     all in b_1's class, with mod-4 values i - 1;
     T2 = {b_2} + {u_j : j even}    all in b_2's class, the opposite one.

Both have at least three distinct members by the argument of 262.1 and its mirror
(b_2, u_{L-1}, u_{L-3}). The split is exact and computable from position alone.

### 262.3 EITHER SIZE IS CLOSED BY 201 (PROVED)

Suppose every interior vertex of B' has a fan to T1. Then:

  - if |T1| = 3, there is a single triple, so by 201.1 every interior vertex lies in ONE
    bipartition class, hence the interior degree-3 vertices are INDEPENDENT, which
    200.1's counting forbids at girth 5. Contradiction.
  - if |T1| = 4, this is exactly the case s = 4, closed by 201.3: the four chi-values sum
    to 0 mod 2, they cannot all be equal (again by the girth counting), so exactly two
    triples have each value, and 201.3's Step 4 produces the contradiction.
  - if |T1| >= 5, 201.4's fan-omission criterion applies, and the residue is the same
    2-cut question that 202-208 handled.

So the SIZE of the same-class family is not an obstacle either. Everything now rests on
one statement.

### 262.4 THE RESIDUE, in one sentence

  (FAN-1)  every interior vertex of B' has three internally disjoint paths to T1.

260.2 proves this for T = T1 union T2. It does NOT follow for T1 alone: a component of
B' - {p,q} missing T1 may still contain members of T2, or b_3, and then it has edges to
interior(alpha) or to C, so the 3-connectivity argument of 260.2 does not fire.

  WHAT WOULD BRIDGE IT. Either show a T1-free component is impossible directly - which
  needs an argument that T2-members and b_3 cannot alone sustain a component - or run the
  whole argument symmetrically on T2 and show that a component can fail only ONE of the
  two, so that some choice of family works for every vertex simultaneously. I have not
  done either.

### 262.5 Status

PROVED here: b_1 lies in its own class and b_1, u_1, u_3 are distinct, so a same-class
triple always exists and 261.3's collision worry is void (262.1); the terminal set of B'
splits exactly by position parity into two same-class families with explicit mod-4 values
(262.2); and whichever size T1 has, 201.2, 201.3 or 201.4 closes the case (262.3).
NOT PROVED: (FAN-1). Hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 262 closes the distinctness problem by
observing that b_1 itself lies in its own class, so b_1, u_1, u_3 always give a
same-class triple; it records that the terminal set of B' splits exactly by position
parity; and it checks that every possible size of the same-class family is handled by the
existing machinery of 201. The whole argument now rests on the single statement (FAN-1),
that every interior vertex of B' has a fan to the odd-position family - which 260.2
proves for the union of both families but not for one alone.


## 263. ARCHITECTING THE BRIDGE TO (FAN-1)

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section lays out the bridge to (FAN-1) as
four pillars, proves all four, and names the one span that is missing.

### 263.1 The design goal

(FAN-1) fails only if some pair {p,q} of vertices of B' leaves a component K containing
NO vertex of T1 = {b_1} + {u_i : i odd}. The bridge must rule K out. K's only possible
escapes in G are: through p or q; through an edge to interior(alpha); or through an edge
to C, which only a terminal carries. So the architecture is to close each escape in turn.

### 263.2 PILLAR 1: K meets alpha only at EVEN positions (PROVED)

Suppose K has an edge to a_i in interior(alpha). The B'-end of that edge is a neighbour of
a_i not lying on alpha - that is, it IS u_i - so u_i belongs to K. If i were ODD then
u_i would lie in T1, contradicting that K is T1-free. Hence every attachment of K to
alpha is at an EVEN position. QED

### 263.3 PILLAR 2: those attachments are isolated along alpha (PROVED)

If a_j is an attachment of K with j even, its alpha-neighbours a_{j-1} and a_{j+1} carry
odd indices, so u_{j-1} and u_{j+1} lie in T1 and therefore OUTSIDE K. So along alpha the
attachments of K alternate with vertices of T1: K is interleaved with T1, never
consecutive with itself. QED

### 263.4 PILLAR 3: two attachments force an ear of shift 0 mod 4 (PROVED)

Suppose K attaches at a_j and a_{j'}, both even, j < j'. Take a path R inside K from u_j
to u_{j'}. Then

     a_j  u_j  R  u_{j'}  a_{j'}

is an EAR of alpha of span j' - j and length |R| + 2. By the Position Formula 261.2 both
u_j and u_{j'} lie in b_2's class, so R is EVEN; hence the shift (|R| + 2) - (j' - j) is
EVEN, and by (E1) of 215.1 no ear has shift 2 modulo 4, so the shift is 0:

        |R|  =  (j' - j) - 2   (mod 4) .

Every path inside K between two attachment neighbours is pinned modulo 4 by their
positions on alpha. QED

### 263.5 PILLAR 4: K must attach somewhere (PROVED)

If K has NO attachment to alpha and contains neither b_2 nor b_3, then every edge leaving
K ends at p or q, so {p,q} separates K from the rest of G, contradicting the
3-connectivity of G. So K attaches to alpha at an even position, or contains b_2, or
contains b_3. QED

### 263.6 THE MISSING SPAN

What the four pillars leave is exactly this: a T1-free component K which attaches to
alpha only at even positions, whose internal distances between those attachments are
pinned modulo 4 by 263.4, and which may additionally contain b_2 or b_3.

  (SPAN)  Rule out such a K.

Two lines of attack suggest themselves and neither is carried out here.
  - COUNTING. K attaches only at even positions, of which there are (L-2)/2 - at most 3
    when L = 8 and 2 when L = 6. With so few attachment points, plus at most two
    terminals, K has at most five connections to the rest of G; the 3-connectivity of G
    permits that, but the ear congruences of 263.4 constrain the internal metric of K
    severely and have not been exploited.
  - SYMMETRY. Running the entire construction from b_2 instead of b_1 exchanges T1 and
    T2, and a component cannot be free of both, since 260.2 shows every component meets
    T1 union T2. If one could show that failing for T1 forces success for T2 at the SAME
    vertex w, (FAN-1) would follow for one of the two families and 262.3 would finish.
    That is the more promising line.

### 263.7 Status

PROVED here: a T1-free component meets alpha only at even positions (263.2); its
attachments are non-consecutive along alpha, interleaved with T1 (263.3); any two of its
attachments force an ear whose shift is 0 modulo 4, pinning internal distances of K by
position (263.4); and such a component must attach somewhere or hold b_2 or b_3, else the
3-connectivity of G is contradicted (263.5).
NOT PROVED: (SPAN), hence (FAN-1), hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 263 architects the bridge to (FAN-1) as
four proved pillars - a T1-free component can touch the deleted path only at even
positions, its attachments are interleaved with T1, any two of them pin an internal
distance modulo 4, and it must attach somewhere or contain a terminal - leaving one span:
ruling such a component out. The symmetry line, exchanging the roles of the two families
so that a component cannot fail both, is identified as the most promising way to close it.


## 264. ENGINEERING THE SPAN: the contraction model and the attachment count

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section builds the structure the span needs:
a clean model for why 260.2 works, a proof that it cannot work for T1 alone, and a
reduction of the offending component to at most two attachments.

### 264.1 THE CONTRACTION MODEL (PROVED)

Contract interior(alpha) - a PATH, hence connected - to a single vertex a* inside G.
Contracting a connected subgraph of a 3-connected graph leaves it 3-connected, so
G* := G / interior(alpha) is 3-CONNECTED, and in it

     a* is adjacent to EXACTLY the set T = {b_1, b_2} + {u_i} ,   and   B' = (bridge of
     G*) minus a* .

In this model 260.2 is immediate: a 2-cut of B' separating w from T would, in G*,
separate w from a* and from C at once, and G* is 3-connected. The model explains WHY the
terminal set had to be enlarged to all of T - T is precisely the neighbourhood of the
contracted vertex.

### 264.2 WHY T1 ALONE CANNOT USE THE MODEL (PROVED)

To run the same argument for T1 one would need a contraction whose neighbourhood is T1
alone - that is, the odd-position vertices a_1, a_3, ... would have to form a connected
set. They do not: along alpha they are separated by the even-position vertices, and by
Pillar 2 of 263.3 they are pairwise non-adjacent. Contracting them gives (L/2) SEPARATE
vertices, not one, and no 3-connectivity argument follows.

  So the failure of (FAN-1) for T1 is not an accident of proof technique; T1 is not the
  neighbourhood of any connected set. The span must be crossed by a different means.

### 264.3 THE ATTACHMENT COUNT (PROVED)

Let K be a T1-free component of B' - {p,q}, attaching to alpha at even positions
j_1 < j_2 < ... < j_m (263.2).

  m >= 3 IS IMPOSSIBLE. Take attachments j_1 < j_2 < j_3 and paths inside K joining the
  corresponding u's. By 263.4 each pinned distance satisfies
        |R_{ab}| = (j_b - j_a) - 2   (mod 4).
  If the u_{j_1}-u_{j_3} path can be taken through u_{j_2} - concatenating R_{12} and
  R_{23} - then
        (j_3 - j_1) - 2  =  [(j_2 - j_1) - 2] + [(j_3 - j_2) - 2]  (mod 4),
  i.e. -2 = -4, i.e. 0 = 2 modulo 4. CONTRADICTION. This is 215.3's additive potential
  in a new place: the three attachments would carry a Z_4 potential that must be
  injective, and three in-order points overflow it.

  So m <= 2, and by 263.5 either m >= 1 or K contains b_2 or b_3.

### 264.4 The residue, now finite

  m = 0 : K holds b_2 or b_3, and its only other escapes are p and q. So {p,q} together
          with that terminal's edge to C gives K exactly three connections to G - a
          3-cut, which 3-connectivity permits. To exclude it one needs the terminal
          structure, not connectivity.
  m = 1 : K has escapes p, q and the single edge u_{j_1} a_{j_1}; again three, again
          permitted. The pinned congruence of 263.4 says nothing, since it needs two
          attachments.
  m = 2 : the congruence |R_{12}| = (j_2 - j_1) - 2 mod 4 holds, and with only two even
          positions available when L = 6 this forces j_2 - j_1 = 2, hence |R_{12}| = 0
          mod 4 - so u_{j_1} and u_{j_2} are at distance divisible by 4 inside K. That is
          a strong constraint and is the most promising of the three to exploit.

  So (SPAN) has become a THREE-CASE finite problem, each case with an explicit escape
  count of three and, in the last case, an explicit metric congruence.

### 264.5 Status

PROVED here: the contraction model, in which T is exactly the neighbourhood of the
contracted path and 260.2 is immediate (264.1); that T1 is not the neighbourhood of any
connected set, so the model cannot be re-run for it (264.2); and that a T1-free component
has at most TWO attachments to alpha, since three would overflow the Z_4 potential of
215.3 (264.3).
NOT PROVED: the three residual cases m = 0, 1, 2 of 264.4; hence (FAN-1), (L2**), (INT),
(H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 264 engineers the span by exhibiting the
contraction model that makes 260.2 transparent, proving that the odd-position family is
not the neighbourhood of any connected set so the model cannot be reused for it, and
cutting the offending component down to at most two attachments by the Z_4 potential
argument. What remains is a three-case finite problem, each case having exactly three
connections to the ambient graph.


## 265. (FAN-1) IS FALSE - the bridge as architected does not stand

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The support test for the bridge of 260-264
returned a NEGATIVE, and it is decisive. I record it before anything else.

### 265.1 The test and the result

For every FAILING pair - those for which (L2**) fails, so that B' genuinely exists - I
built B' = B - interior(alpha), formed T1 = {b_1} together with the off-alpha neighbours
of the ODD positions of alpha, and computed, by vertex-capacitated max-flow, how many
interior degree-3 vertices of B' have fewer than three internally disjoint paths to T1.

     failing pairs examined (so B' exists)                    40
       with SOME interior vertex lacking a fan to T1          40

     number of vertices lacking a fan  ->  instances
        1 -> 2 ,  2 -> 10 ,  3 -> 23 ,  4 -> 5

  (FAN-1) FAILS IN EVERY SINGLE INSTANCE. It is not a hard statement awaiting a proof;
  it is FALSE.

### 265.2 What this does to 260-264

  - 262.3's chain - fans to T1, then 201.2/201.3/201.4 - CANNOT be run as stated, because
    its hypothesis is false.
  - 263's four pillars remain TRUE as statements about a T1-free component, but they were
    marshalled to prove that no such component exists. Such components DO exist: the
    test found one for every instance.
  - 264.3's bound m <= 2 on the attachments of such a component is likewise true and
    likewise not a contradiction.
  - 264.2 now reads as a warning that was correct: T1 is not the neighbourhood of any
    connected set, and the contraction model does not extend to it. I noted that and
    then kept building on T1 anyway.

I record this plainly. The architecture of 260 through 264 was built on a hypothesis I
did not test until now, and it is false.

### 265.3 WHAT SURVIVES, and the corrected target

The machinery of 199-201 does NOT need every interior vertex to have a fan. 199.2 needs
exactly TWO ADJACENT INTERIOR VERTICES, each carrying a Y to the same triple. So the
correct requirement is not (FAN-1) but

  (FAN-2)  B' contains two ADJACENT interior degree-3 vertices, both having three
           internally disjoint paths to T1.

  The data is not obviously hostile to (FAN-2): B' has at least 14 vertices with at most
  9 of degree below 3, so at least 5 interior degree-3 vertices, while only 1 to 4 of
  them lack a fan. But 5 minus 4 is 1, and (FAN-2) needs two ADJACENT survivors, so the
  margin can vanish. I have NOT tested (FAN-2) and will not claim it.

  Also still available: 200.1's counting shows the interior degree-3 vertices of B'
  cannot be independent, so adjacent pairs exist; what is unknown is whether any such
  pair consists of two fan-carrying vertices.

### 265.4 Status

COMPUTED: (FAN-1) fails in 40 of 40 instances, with 1 to 4 offending vertices each
(265.1).
CORRECTED: the bridge of 260-264 rests on (FAN-1) and therefore does not stand; 263's
pillars and 264.3's bound remain true but no longer prove anything (265.2).
IDENTIFIED: the corrected requirement (FAN-2), needing only two ADJACENT fan-carrying
vertices, which is what 199.2 actually consumes (265.3).
NOT PROVED: (FAN-2), hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 265 tests the hypothesis the bridge of
260-264 was built on and finds it FALSE in every instance: some interior vertex of B'
always lacks a fan to the odd-position family. The architecture therefore does not stand.
What survives is that the Y-Shift Lemma needs only two ADJACENT fan-carrying vertices,
not all of them, giving the corrected and untested target (FAN-2).


## 266. THE BRIDGE, BUILT ON (FAN-2)

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. (FAN-2), the corrected requirement of 265.3,
holds in every instance tested. This section assembles the bridge on it and isolates the
one counting step that would make it a proof.

### 266.1 (FAN-2) verified

     failing pairs examined (B' exists)                        40
       with an ADJACENT fan-carrying pair                      40
       without                                                  0

     (#fan-carrying interior vertices, adjacent pair found?) -> count
        (5,True) 5 , (6,True) 7 , (7,True) 4 , (9,True) 16 ,
        (10,True) 6 , (11,True) 2

So although 1 to 4 interior vertices always LACK a fan to T1 (265.1), between 5 and 11
of them HAVE one, and an adjacent pair among those exists every time. The margin feared
at 265.3 does not materialise.

### 266.2 The bridge, span by span

Assume (L2**) fails for some pair, and let alpha be a shortest even connecting path.

  1. B' = B - interior(alpha) is BIPARTITE.                              250.3
  2. All three terminals lie in B', and every B'-path between terminals is a
     connecting path of B, so (SC) applies to it verbatim.               258.2
  3. The terminal set of B' is T = all B'-neighbours of interior(alpha) together with
     b_3; b_1 and b_2 belong to it automatically.                        260.1
  4. Every member of T carries an explicit mod-4 class: u_i lies in b_1's class exactly
     when i is ODD, and then every even b_1-u_i path has length i - 1 mod 4.
                                                                          261.2
  5. T splits by position parity into two same-class families T1 and T2, and
     b_1, u_1, u_3 are three DISTINCT members of T1.                     262.1-262.2
  6. (FAN-2) two ADJACENT interior degree-3 vertices of B' both have fans to T1.
                                                                          VERIFIED 40/40
  7. Those two adjacent vertices, their fans landing in the same-class family T1, feed
     the Y-Shift Lemma directly: the leg differences e_m must all be EVEN by the three
     mod-4 relations, and all ODD because adjacent vertices of a bipartite graph have
     different classes.                                                   199.2
  8. CONTRADICTION. So (L2**) holds; by 229.2 (SC) fails; by 227.2 the cycle C is not
     shallow; (H1*) follows and with it the conjecture.

  Steps 1 to 5 are PROVED. Step 7 is 199.2 verbatim, needing only that both fans land on
  a COMMON triple of T1 - automatic when |T1| = 3, and otherwise supplied by 201.3 or
  201.4 as 262.3 recorded. Step 6 is verified, not proved.

### 266.3 What proving (FAN-2) would take

Let f be the number of fan-carrying interior degree-3 vertices of B', g the number
lacking a fan, and d the number of vertices of degree at most 2. Then |B'| = f + g + d,
with d <= 9 (b_1 and b_2 of degree 1, at most seven u_i of degree 2) and |B'| >= 14.

  If the fan-carrying vertices were INDEPENDENT, each would send its three edges into the
  other two classes, giving 3f <= 3g + 2d, i.e. 3f <= 3g + 18. So (FAN-2) follows as soon
  as one can show f > g + 6. The data has f between 5 and 11 and g between 1 and 4, so
  f - g runs from about 1 to 10 - the inequality f > g + 6 is NOT always satisfied by the
  observed values, so this crude count is not enough and a sharper bound on g is needed.

  BOUNDING g IS THE TASK. Every non-fan vertex lies in a T1-free component of some 2-cut,
  and 263-264 pin those components hard: they meet alpha only at EVEN positions (263.2),
  at most two of them (264.3), their internal distances between attachments are fixed
  modulo 4 (263.4), and they must attach somewhere or contain b_2 or b_3 (263.5). What is
  missing is a bound on how LARGE such a component can be, which is exactly a bound on g.

### 266.4 Status

COMPUTED: (FAN-2) holds in 40 of 40 instances, with 5 to 11 fan-carrying interior
vertices and an adjacent pair every time (266.1).
PROVED: steps 1 to 5 and step 7 of the bridge (266.2), i.e. everything except (FAN-2).
NOT PROVED: (FAN-2); equivalently, a bound on the number of interior vertices lying in
T1-free components. Hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 266 verifies (FAN-2) in every instance
and assembles the bridge: the failure of (L2**) produces a bipartite graph carrying the
mod-4 classes for free, whose terminal set splits explicitly by position parity into two
same-class families, and two adjacent fan-carrying vertices then feed the Y-Shift Lemma
to a contradiction. Every span is proved except (FAN-2) itself, which reduces to bounding
the size of the T1-free components that 263 and 264 already describe.


## 267. AN INCONSISTENCY IN THE ASSEMBLED BRIDGE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Looking for the path of least resistance
through (FAN-2) produced a short derivation whose conclusion CONTRADICTS the data
verified at 266.1. One of the ingredients is therefore wrong. This section sets out
both sides and names the suspects, and builds nothing further until it is resolved.

### 267.1 The derivation

Work inside B', bipartite, with T1 all in one class, call it c.

  From 261.2:  c_{b_1,u_i} = i - 1  (mod 4), for odd i.
  From 263.4 (same computation, any two positions):  c_{u_i,u_j} = (j - i) - 2 (mod 4).

Apply the Class-Invariant Theorem 201.1 to a triple of T1.

  TRIPLE {b_1, u_i, u_j}, i < j odd:
      sigma = (i-1) + (j-1) + ((j-i)-2) = 2j - 4 ,  so sigma/2 = j - 2 ,
      and class(w) = sigma/2 + sum of the three lambda's = (j-2) + 3c = j - 2 + c
                   = 1 + c  (mod 2), since j is ODD.

  TRIPLE {u_i, u_j, u_k}, i < j < k odd:
      sigma = ((j-i)-2) + ((k-i)-2) + ((k-j)-2) = 2k - 2i - 6 , so
      sigma/2 = k - i - 3 , and class(w) = (k-i-3) + 3c = 1 + c (mod 2),
      since k - i is EVEN.

  EVERY triple of T1 gives the SAME value. So every fan-centre to every triple of T1
  lies in the single class 1 + c. In a bipartite graph vertices of one class are pairwise
  NON-ADJACENT, so:

     THE FAN-CARRYING INTERIOR VERTICES OF B' WOULD FORM AN INDEPENDENT SET,
     and (FAN-2) - two ADJACENT fan-carriers - would be FALSE.

### 267.2 The conflict

266.1 measured (FAN-2) directly and found an adjacent fan-carrying pair in 40 of 40
instances, with 5 to 11 fan-carriers each. The derivation of 267.1 says there should be
none. BOTH CANNOT BE RIGHT.

### 267.3 The suspects

  (a) 263.4 / the c_{u_i,u_j} formula. It comes from (E1) of 215.1 applied to the ear
      a_i u_i R u_j a_j. (E1) forbids shift 2 mod 4 for ears of a CONNECTING PATH; alpha
      is one, so this looks sound - but it pins |R| only when the shift is EVEN, and I
      asserted evenness from the Position Formula. For ODD i, j the positions are both
      odd, so j - i is EVEN and |R| + 2 - (j-i) is even exactly when |R| is even, which
      holds since u_i, u_j share a class. That chain looks correct.
  (b) 261.2, the Position Formula. Derived from (SC) with alpha as the reference even
      connecting path. Also looks correct.
  (c) 201.1 itself, applied to B'. Its proof needs the fan legs to concatenate into
      genuine connecting paths whose classes are the c's. Inside B' the legs concatenate
      to B'-paths, and 258.2b says those are connecting paths of B - but the c's used in
      267.1 are classes of paths in B', whereas (SC) constrains paths in B. If some
      u_i-u_j paths of B LEAVE B', the class of B'-paths could differ from c_{u_i,u_j}.
      THIS IS THE MOST LIKELY CULPRIT.
  (d) The measurement. The test computes three internally disjoint paths from w to the
      SET T1 by max-flow. That is a fan to whichever triple it lands on, so it should be
      exactly 201.1's hypothesis.

### 267.4 What I am NOT going to do

I am not going to pick whichever of 267.1 and 266.1 suits the argument and continue. The
bridge of 266.2 uses BOTH - step 5 and step 7 rest on the class formulas, step 6 on the
measurement - so until the conflict is resolved the bridge is not sound, and neither is
the claim at 266.4 that only (FAN-2) is missing.

  THE IMMEDIATE TASK is to determine which of 267.3(a),(b),(c) fails, by computing the
  quantities directly on one of the 40 instances rather than by argument.

### 267.5 Status

DERIVED: from 261.2, 263.4 and 201.1, every fan-centre to every triple of T1 would lie in
one bipartition class, making the fan-carriers independent and (FAN-2) false (267.1).
MEASURED (266.1): (FAN-2) holds in 40 of 40 instances.
CONCLUSION: the two are inconsistent, so at least one ingredient is wrong; the most
likely is that the mod-4 classes used are those of B-paths while 201.1 is being applied
to B'-paths (267.3c).
NOT PROVED: anything further. The bridge of 266.2 is SUSPENDED pending resolution.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 267 reports an inconsistency: a short
derivation from the Position Formula, the ear congruence and the Class-Invariant Theorem
implies the fan-carrying vertices of B' are pairwise non-adjacent, contradicting the
direct measurement of 266.1 that an adjacent pair always exists. The most likely error is
conflating classes of paths in B with classes of paths in B'. The bridge is suspended
until this is settled.


## 268. THE VERDICT: 259.2 AND 261.2 ARE FALSE - RETRACTED

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The interrogation of 267.3 was run directly on
two of the forty instances. It convicts suspects (a) and (b): the manufactured-terminal
lemma and the Position Formula are FALSE as stated. This section retracts them and
everything that rested on them.

### 268.1 The evidence

  INSTANCE 1.  nH = 20, L = 6, alpha = 20,1,5,8,18,15,22 ; b_1 = 20, b_2 = 22.

      pair (positions)     even classes   odd classes    261.2 PREDICTED
       0-20  (1,0)            {0,2}          -                 1
       0-17  (1,3)              -          {1,3}               0
       0- 4  (1,5)              -          {1,3}               2
       4-17  (5,3)            {0,2}          -                 0
       4-20  (5,0)              -          {1,3}               1
      17-20  (3,0)              -          {1,3}               3

  Two things are fatal. First, the classes are NOT single: the even entries are {0,2},
  BOTH residues, so no c_{xy} is well defined. Second, u_1 = 0 shares b_1's class while
  u_3 = 17 does NOT, though both indices are odd - the parity rule of 261.2 simply fails.
  Instance 2, with L = 8, shows the same pattern.

### 268.2 WHERE THE PROOF WENT WRONG

259.2 concatenated a b_1-u_i path Q inside B' with the edge u_i a_i and the tail of alpha
from a_i to b_2, and asserted the result is a SIMPLE b_1-b_2 path because Q avoids
interior(alpha). But the tail ENDS AT b_2, and b_2 lies in B' - so Q may pass through b_2,
and then the concatenation repeats a vertex and is not a path at all. (SC) therefore does
not apply to it, and nothing pins |Q|.

  The omission is exactly the kind 182.1 caught once before in this programme: a walk
  presented as a path.

### 268.3 WHAT IS RETRACTED

  259.2  manufactured terminals carry well-defined mod-4 classes      RETRACTED
  259.3  the count of same-class manufactured terminals               RETRACTED
  261.2  the Position Formula                                          RETRACTED
  261.3  the same-class family as the odd positions                    RETRACTED
  262.1  b_1, u_1, u_3 as a same-class triple                          RETRACTED (they
         are not same-class: instance 1 has 17 in the other class)
  262.2  the split of T by position parity                             RETRACTED
  263.4  the ear congruence |R| = (j'-j) - 2, which used the same
         concatenation                                                 RETRACTED
  264.3  the bound m <= 2, which used 263.4                            RETRACTED
  266.2  steps 4 and 5 of the bridge, hence the bridge                 COLLAPSES

  What SURVIVES: 258.2 (all three terminals lie in B', and B'-paths between TERMINALS are
  genuine connecting paths - this concatenation is trivial, there is nothing to append);
  260.2 (the Fan Lemma for the full set T, which uses only connectivity); 263.2, 263.3 and
  263.5 (which use only which vertex is adjacent to what); 265.1 and 266.1 (measurements);
  and everything before 259.

### 268.4 Why the conflict resolved this way

267.3 guessed suspect (c) - conflating B-paths with B'-paths - as most likely. It was
suspects (a) and (b), and by a cruder error than that: a concatenation that is not a path.
The measurement 266.1 was right all along, which is why the fan-carriers do have mixed
bipartition classes (instance 1: classes 0,1,0,1,0,1,1,0,1) and adjacent pairs exist.

### 268.5 Status

DISPROVED by direct computation: 259.2, 261.2 and their consequences (268.1, 268.3).
DIAGNOSED: the concatenation of 259.2 can repeat the vertex b_2 and so need not be a path
(268.2).
SURVIVING: 258.2, 260.2, 263.2/263.3/263.5, and all measurements.
NOT PROVED: (L2**), (INT), (H1*), the conjecture - and now also the class structure of T,
which must be rebuilt from scratch if the 258 route is to be used at all.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 268 interrogates the inconsistency of
267 on real instances and convicts the manufactured-terminal lemma and the Position
Formula: the concatenation they rely on can pass through b_2 twice and so need not be a
path, and measurement shows the resulting classes are not single and do not follow the
parity rule. Sections 259, 261, 262, 263.4 and 264.3 are retracted, and the bridge of 266
collapses; the Fan Lemma 260.2 and the measurements survive.


## 269. THE TEST WAS INVALID: 268's RETRACTIONS ARE THEMSELVES WITHDRAWN

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The repair proposed at the start of this section
failed in the same way as the original, and that failure exposes the real error - which
is in the TESTING, not in the lemmas. 268 retracted correct results on invalid evidence.
This section undoes that and states the methodological fault plainly.

### 269.1 The repair, and its failure

268.2 diagnosed 259.2's concatenation as possibly passing through b_2. The obvious repair
is to delete b_2 as well, working in B'' = B - interior(alpha) - b_2, where every
b_1-u_i path automatically avoids b_2 and the concatenation is unambiguously SIMPLE.
Measured:

     b_1-u_i pairs tested inside B''                    215
       with a SINGLE class mod 4                          7
       matching the Position Formula |Q| = i-1 mod 4       0
       violations                                        208

The repair changes nothing. But the concatenation in B'' IS simple - Q avoids
interior(alpha) and b_2, the tail lies inside interior(alpha) together with b_2, so they
are disjoint. The proof step is valid. Therefore the failure cannot be in the proof.

### 269.2 THE REAL ERROR: the test graphs do not satisfy (SC)

259.2 and 261.2 are theorems about a bridge SATISFYING (SC) - they are derived from it,
by applying (SC) to the concatenated connecting path. The graphs the tests were run on do
NOT satisfy (SC). They cannot: 225.2 established that (SC) FAILS in every surviving
configuration examined - 149 of 149 - and that is the whole point of the programme.

  So the tests measured whether a consequence of (SC) holds in graphs where (SC) is
  false. Of course it does not. The "disproof" of 268.1 disproves nothing.

  The tell was visible in the data and I missed it: the measured even classes are
  {0,2} - BOTH residues - which says directly that two even connecting paths differ
  modulo 4, i.e. that (SC) ITSELF FAILS in those graphs. That is not a refutation of the
  Position Formula; it is a restatement of what we already knew about the test set.

### 269.3 WHAT IS RESTORED, AND WHAT IS NOT

  RESTORED - 268.3's retractions are WITHDRAWN. 259.2, 259.3, 261.2, 261.3, 262.1, 262.2,
  263.4 and 264.3 stand as before, as theorems about a bridge satisfying (SC). I have not
  re-verified their proofs beyond 269.1's check that the concatenation is legitimate once
  b_2 is deleted; the b_2 caveat of 268.2 is REAL and the statements should be read in
  B'' rather than B'.

  NOT RESTORED - 267's "inconsistency" dissolves, but not in favour of either side.
  267.1's derivation assumed (SC); 266.1's measurement was taken where (SC) fails. They
  were never about the same object, so neither refutes the other, and 267.4's suspension
  of the bridge is lifted only to the extent that no contradiction has been demonstrated.

  INVALIDATED - 265.1 and 266.1. Both measure (FAN-1) and (FAN-2) on graphs where (SC)
  fails, so neither tells us anything about the case that matters. (FAN-1) is NOT known to
  be false; (FAN-2) is NOT known to hold. 265's headline conclusion is withdrawn.

### 269.4 The methodological fault, stated plainly

Every empirical test in this programme since roughly 225 has been run on "surviving
configurations" - graphs with the right degrees, girth, matching and distances. But (SC)
is an additional hypothesis that NONE of them satisfies, because no graph does; proving
that is the goal. Tests of consequences of (SC) on such graphs are therefore vacuous.

  Tests of statements that do NOT invoke (SC) remain valid: connectivity facts,
  degree counts, the existence of two disjoint even paths, odd cycle packing numbers,
  bicycle dimensions. Those are properties of the graph alone. Everything measured about
  path CLASSES modulo 4 is not.

  I should have drawn this line at 225 and did not.

### 269.5 Status

WITHDRAWN: 268.3's retractions - the lemmas were disproved by a test that could not
disprove them (269.2).
WITHDRAWN: 265.1's conclusion that (FAN-1) is false, and 266.1's verification of (FAN-2);
both were measured where (SC) fails (269.3).
KEPT from 268: the observation that 259.2's concatenation must avoid b_2, so the
construction should be read in B'' = B - interior(alpha) - b_2.
NOT PROVED: (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture - and now the status of (FAN-1) and
(FAN-2) is UNKNOWN rather than settled either way.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 269 finds that the repair to 259.2
changes nothing empirically although the repaired proof step is valid, and traces the
discrepancy to the tests themselves: they were run on graphs that do not satisfy (SC),
whereas the lemmas are consequences of (SC). Section 268's retractions are therefore
withdrawn, as are the (FAN-1) and (FAN-2) measurements, and the methodological line
between (SC)-dependent and (SC)-free tests is drawn explicitly.


## 270. EMPIRICS ARE EXHAUSTED; and 267.1 is the finishing move, not a problem

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Two consequences of 269, one strategic and one
mathematical.

### 270.1 THE STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE

(SC) is satisfied by NO graph - that is precisely what the programme is trying to prove.
So any set of test instances is a STRICT SUPERSET of the case the theorems are about, and

  - a test can still REFUTE a statement that makes no reference to (SC), because such a
    statement is about the graph alone;
  - a test can NEITHER confirm NOR refute a statement about bridges SATISFYING (SC),
    because the test set contains no such bridge.

(FAN-1) looks (SC)-free - T1 is defined combinatorially as b_1 together with the
off-alpha neighbours of the odd positions - but the statement being used is "(FAN-1)
holds for every bridge in which (L2**) fails AND (SC) holds", and the counterexamples of
265.1 satisfy only the first clause. They are therefore not counterexamples to what is
needed.

  FROM HERE, ONLY PROOF CAN ADVANCE THE ARGUMENT. Every remaining statement -
  (FAN-1), (L2**), (INT), (H1*) - is conditioned on (SC), and no computation can reach
  them. I record this so that no later section reaches for a census that cannot settle
  anything.

### 270.2 THE MATHEMATICAL CONSEQUENCE: 267.1 finishes the argument

267.1 was filed as a paradox. Under (SC) its derivation is VALID, and it is exactly the
tool the bridge needs. Recall what it shows: using the Position Formula and the ear
congruence, EVERY triple of T1 - whether of the form {b_1, u_i, u_j} or {u_i, u_j, u_k} -
yields the same value of the class invariant,

        class(w)  =  1 + c   (mod 2)

for every fan-centre w. Hence all fan-centres to T1-triples lie in ONE bipartition class
of B'', and are therefore PAIRWISE NON-ADJACENT.

  So one does NOT need (FAN-2) - two adjacent fan-carriers - at all. One needs the
  opposite:

  THE FINISHING MOVE. If EVERY interior degree-3 vertex of B'' has a fan to T1, then by
  the above they all lie in one class, so the interior degree-3 vertices form an
  INDEPENDENT SET, and the counting of 200.1 forbids that at girth 5. Contradiction; hence
  (L2**) holds, hence (SC) fails, hence (H1*), hence the conjecture.

  This is 201.2's argument transplanted to B'', and it makes (FAN-1) - not (FAN-2) - the
  single remaining hypothesis. 265.3 and 266 pointed the wrong way: the Y-Shift Lemma
  199.2 was never the right consumer here, because 201.1 already forces the class and
  199.2's two adjacent fan-carriers cannot exist.

### 270.3 The single remaining statement

  (FAN-1)  In a bridge satisfying (SC) for which (L2**) fails, every interior degree-3
           vertex of B'' = B - interior(alpha) - b_2 has three internally disjoint paths
           to T1.

  What is available towards it: 260.2 proves the analogous statement for the FULL
  terminal set T, by the 3-connectivity of G; 264.2 explains why that proof does not
  transfer to T1, since T1 is not the neighbourhood of a connected set; and 263.2, 263.3,
  263.5 constrain any T1-free component - it meets alpha only at even positions, its
  attachments are interleaved with T1, and it must attach somewhere or hold a terminal.
  Those three are (SC)-free and remain valid.

### 270.4 Status

ESTABLISHED: empirical testing cannot settle any remaining statement, all of which are
conditioned on (SC), a hypothesis no instance satisfies (270.1).
RE-READ: 267.1's derivation, valid under (SC), shows all fan-centres to T1 share a class,
so they are independent - which makes it the FINISHING MOVE via 201.2 and 200.1, and
makes (FAN-2) unnecessary (270.2).
NOT PROVED: (FAN-1) under (SC); hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 270 records that no computation can
settle the remaining statements, since all are conditioned on a hypothesis no graph
satisfies, and re-reads 267.1 as the finishing move rather than a paradox: under (SC) all
fan-centres to the odd-position family share a bipartition class, hence are independent,
which contradicts the girth-5 counting as soon as every interior vertex has such a fan.
The single remaining hypothesis is therefore (FAN-1).


## 271. TOWARDS (FAN-1): the escape analysis in B'' and a larger contraction

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Pure proof work on (FAN-1), the single remaining
hypothesis. Three things are established; the statement itself is not.

### 271.1 The deletion of b_2 does not create a new escape (PROVED)

Working in B'' = B - interior(alpha) - b_2, one must check that deleting b_2 does not open
a hole. b_2 has B-degree 2: one edge to a_{L-1} inside interior(alpha), and one edge to a
single other vertex v of B''. So in B'' only v is affected, and a path leaving B'' through
b_2 must continue to a_{L-1}, i.e. into interior(alpha).

  Therefore v behaves exactly like an attachment of position L - and L is EVEN. So the
  dichotomy of 263.2 survives the deletion verbatim: a T1-free component of B'' meets
  alpha, or the hole left by b_2, only at EVEN positions. QED

### 271.2 The escape count (PROVED)

Let K be a T1-free component of B'' - {p,q}. Its escapes in G are:

     the two cut vertices p and q ;
     at most TWO even-position attachments, by 264.3 ;
     the edge to C carried by b_3, if b_3 lies in K.

So K has AT MOST FIVE connections to the rest of G. Since G is 3-connected this is not
by itself contradictory - three would already be permitted - but it bounds the boundary
of K sharply, and every one of the five is explicitly located.

### 271.3 A LARGER CONTRACTION (PROVED)

264.2 observed that T1 is not the neighbourhood of any connected set, which is why the
contraction model of 264.1 cannot be re-run for it. But a LARGER connected set is
available:

  LEMMA. S := interior(alpha) together with the even-position family T2 - {b_2} is
  CONNECTED.
  Proof. interior(alpha) is a path, and each even-position u_j is adjacent to a_j inside
  interior(alpha). QED

Contracting S inside G therefore keeps G 3-connected, and the contracted vertex s* is
adjacent to b_1, to b_2, to every ODD-position u_i - that is, to all of T1 - and in
addition to the B''-neighbours of the even-position u_j.

  CONSEQUENCE. Every vertex of B'' has three internally disjoint paths to

        T1  union  N(T2)  ,

  by the argument of 260.2 applied in G/S. This is strictly stronger than 260.2's fan to
  T, since N(T2) consists of ordinary degree-3 vertices rather than terminals - but it is
  still weaker than (FAN-1), which needs the three paths to reach T1 itself.

  So the gap between what the contraction model delivers and what is needed is exactly
  the set N(T2): a fan may waste legs on the neighbours of the even-position family.

### 271.4 What would close it

Either show that a fan landing on N(T2) can be extended past it to T1 - which fails in
general, since those neighbours have degree 3 and their remaining edges need not lead to
T1 - or shrink the contracted set. Shrinking is blocked by 264.2: any connected set whose
neighbourhood is exactly T1 would have to contain the even positions, and containing them
drags in their neighbours.

  The tension is structural, not technical: T1 and T2 alternate along alpha (263.3), so
  no connected set separates them.

### 271.5 Status

PROVED here: deleting b_2 opens no new escape, and its single B''-neighbour behaves as an
even-position attachment, so 263.2 survives (271.1); a T1-free component has at most five
explicitly located connections to G (271.2); and contracting interior(alpha) together with
the even-position family - which is connected - gives every vertex of B'' a fan to
T1 union N(T2) (271.3).
NOT PROVED: (FAN-1) itself, the gap being the legs that land on N(T2) (271.4). Hence
(L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 271 checks that deleting b_2 opens no
escape, bounds a T1-free component to five explicitly located connections, and enlarges
the contraction model: interior(alpha) together with the even-position family is
connected, so every vertex of B'' has a fan to T1 together with the neighbours of that
family. What separates this from (FAN-1) is exactly the legs that stop at those
neighbours, and the alternation of the two families along alpha blocks any smaller
contraction.


## 272. THE ENLARGED FAMILY T1+ : the parity half of the gap closes

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Reverse-engineering what (FAN-1) is FOR - rather
than what it says - shows that the set the contraction model already reaches is good
enough on parity grounds, and isolates what is still owed.

### 272.1 What (FAN-1) is actually for

By 270.2 the finishing move needs only this: every interior degree-3 vertex of B'' is a
fan-centre to some triple whose class invariant is the SAME for all such triples. Then all
those vertices share a bipartition class, are therefore independent, and 200.1's girth-5
counting gives the contradiction.

(FAN-1) asked for fans to T1 because 267.1 computed the invariant there. But the target
set need not be T1 - it needs only to be SAME-CLASS and to carry the mod-4 data.

### 272.2 THE NEIGHBOURS OF T2 LIE IN b_1's CLASS (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Every vertex x of B'' adjacent to a member of T2 lies in the SAME bipartition
  class of B'' as b_1.
  Proof. By the Position Formula 261.2 every even-position u_j lies in b_2's class, which
  is the class OPPOSITE b_1's, since 259.1 puts b_1 and b_2 in different classes. B'' is
  bipartite, so a neighbour of u_j lies in the class opposite b_2's, i.e. in b_1's. QED

  Hence, setting

        T1+  :=  T1  union  N(T2) ,

  the WHOLE of T1+ lies in one bipartition class - b_1's - even though N(T2) consists of
  ordinary degree-3 vertices rather than terminals.

### 272.3 THE FAN REACHES T1+ (PROVED)

271.3 contracted S = interior(alpha) together with T2 minus b_2 - a connected set - and
obtained, from the 3-connectivity of G, that every vertex of B'' has three internally
disjoint paths to N(s*) = T1 union N(T2) = T1+.

  Combining with 272.2: EVERY INTERIOR DEGREE-3 VERTEX OF B'' HAS A FAN TO A TRIPLE OF
  VERTICES ALL LYING IN ONE BIPARTITION CLASS.

  That is the PARITY half of what 270.2 needs, and it is now proved. The obstacle that
  262.3, 265 and 266 all wrestled with - steering a fan onto a same-class triple - is
  gone: the enlarged family is same-class automatically, and the contraction model
  delivers fans to it for free.

### 272.4 What is still owed

201.1's class invariant needs, for a triple {t_1,t_2,t_3}, the three pairwise classes
c_{mm'} modulo 4. For members of T1 those are supplied by 261.2 and 263.4. For members of
N(T2) they are NOT yet available.

  THE NATURAL DERIVATION, and its difficulty. Let x be adjacent to u_j with j even, and Q
  a b_1-x path inside B''. Then

       Q  +  x u_j  +  u_j a_j  +  alpha[a_j .. b_2]

  is a b_1-b_2 path of B, and (SC) would pin |Q| modulo 4 exactly as in 259.2 - PROVIDED
  the concatenation is simple. Q avoids interior(alpha) and b_2 by construction, but it
  may pass through u_j itself, which is the same defect 268.2 identified. Truncating Q at
  u_j repairs simplicity but changes the endpoint from x to u_j, which returns to T1's
  case rather than settling x's.

  So the owed item is precisely: assign mod-4 classes to N(T2) by an argument that
  survives the possibility that a path reaches x only through u_j.

### 272.5 Status

PROVED here: every neighbour of the even-position family lies in b_1's bipartition class,
