so the enlarged family T1+ is entirely same-class (272.2); and every interior degree-3
vertex of B'' has a fan to T1+, by the contraction of 271.3 (272.3). Together these close
the PARITY half of the gap left by 270.2.
NOT PROVED: mod-4 classes for the members of N(T2), which 201.1 needs to compute the class
invariant; the obstruction is the same simplicity defect diagnosed at 268.2 (272.4). Hence
(FAN-1)'s purpose is unfulfilled, and with it (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 272 reverse-engineers what (FAN-1) is
for and finds the target set need not be T1 at all: the neighbours of the even-position
family lie in b_1's bipartition class, so the enlarged family is same-class, and the
contraction model already delivers a fan to it from every interior vertex. The parity half
of the gap is therefore closed, and what remains is to assign mod-4 classes to those
neighbours, which the concatenation argument cannot yet do because a path may reach them
only through the even-position vertex itself.


## 273. N(T2) CARRIES NO CLASS: the enlarged family cannot feed 201.1

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The least-resistance route through 272.4 is to
assign mod-4 classes to N(T2). It cannot be done, and the reason is structural rather
than technical. This is a NEGATIVE result and it closes off the enlarged-family route.

### 273.1 The computation

Let x be a vertex of B'' adjacent to u_j with j EVEN, and let Q be a b_1-x path in B''.
Two cases, and they behave completely differently.

  Q AVOIDS u_j. Then

       Q  +  x u_j  +  u_j a_j  +  alpha[a_j .. b_2]

  is SIMPLE: Q avoids interior(alpha) and b_2 by construction and u_j by assumption. Its
  length is |Q| + 2 + (L - j), which is even exactly when |Q| is even, since L and j are
  both even. Applying (SC) with alpha as the reference even connecting path of length L,

        |Q|  =  j - 2   (mod 4) .

  Q PASSES THROUGH u_j. Then the concatenation REPEATS u_j and is not a path, so no
  connecting path of B is produced and (SC) says NOTHING about |Q|. Truncating Q at u_j
  changes the endpoint back to u_j, which is a member of T2, not of N(T2).

### 273.2 THE NEGATIVE CONCLUSION (PROVED)

So the even b_1-x paths split into two families: those avoiding u_j, all congruent to
j - 2 modulo 4, and those through u_j, entirely unconstrained. Unless every b_1-x path
happens to avoid u_j - which nothing forces, x having degree 3 with u_j as one of its
neighbours -

     x DOES NOT CARRY A WELL-DEFINED CLASS MODULO 4 ,

and 201.1, which needs the pairwise classes c_{mm'} of its triple, cannot be applied to
any triple meeting N(T2).

  THE ENLARGED FAMILY T1+ IS THEREFORE USELESS FOR THE CLASS INVARIANT, even though
  272.2 proved it same-class and 272.3 proved every vertex has a fan to it. Parity was
  never the binding constraint; the mod-4 data is.

### 273.3 What this settles

  - 272.3's achievement stands as a fact about B'' but cannot be consumed by 201.1.
  - (FAN-1) - fans to T1 ITSELF - is genuinely required, not an artefact of how the
    target set was chosen. The enlarged set was the natural way to dodge it and the dodge
    fails.
  - 264.2's observation is now seen to be the real obstruction, twice over: T1 is not the
    neighbourhood of a connected set, and the smallest connected set whose neighbourhood
    CONTAINS T1 drags in vertices that carry no class.

### 273.4 The position

The chain from 250 to 272 is: (L2**) fails, so B' is bipartite; the three original
terminals cannot serve because b_1 and b_2 lie in opposite classes (259.1); the
odd-position family T1 can serve, carrying explicit classes (261.2, 263.4); the class
invariant is then constant across all triples of T1 (267.1), so all fan-centres share a
class, are independent, and 200.1's counting finishes (270.2). Every link is proved
EXCEPT that every interior vertex reaches T1 by a fan.

  (FAN-1) is thus the sole remaining hypothesis of the entire programme, and 273
  establishes that it cannot be circumvented by enlarging the target.

### 273.5 Status

PROVED here: b_1-x paths avoiding u_j are congruent to j - 2 modulo 4, while those
through u_j are unconstrained, so members of N(T2) carry no well-defined class (273.1,
273.2); hence the enlarged family T1+ cannot feed 201.1 and (FAN-1) cannot be dodged
(273.3).
NOT PROVED: (FAN-1); hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 273 shows the least-resistance route -
assigning mod-4 classes to the neighbours of the even-position family - fails: paths
avoiding the even-position vertex are pinned, paths through it are unconstrained and
cannot be extended to a connecting path, so those neighbours carry no class. The enlarged
family, though same-class and fan-reachable, cannot feed the class invariant, and (FAN-1)
stands as the sole remaining hypothesis, not circumventable by enlarging the target.


## 274. REVERSE-ENGINEERING (FAN-1): the offending component is almost 3-regular

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Continuing to reverse-engineer, this section
pins the offending component tighter than 271.2 did and states exactly what a proof of
(FAN-1) must now supply.

### 274.1 The low-degree count (PROVED)

Let K be a T1-free component of B'' - {p,q}. The vertices of B'' of degree below 3 are:
b_1 (degree 1, its alpha-edge deleted), b_3 (degree 2), every u_i (degree 2), and v, the
surviving neighbour of the deleted b_2 (degree 2). Now:

  - K contains no b_1 and no ODD-position u_i, being T1-free;
  - by 264.3 K has at most TWO attachments to alpha, and by 271.1 the vertex v counts as
    one of them, so K contains at most two even-position u_j together with v;
  - b_3 may or may not lie in K.

  LEMMA. K contains AT MOST THREE vertices of B''-degree below 3.

### 274.2 K is almost 3-regular (PROVED)

Write k = |K| and let e be the number of edges from K to {p,q}, so e <= deg(p) + deg(q)
<= 6. Summing degrees inside K, with at most three vertices of degree at least 1 and the
rest of degree 3,

     2|E(K)| + e  =  sum of B''-degrees over K  >=  3(k-3) + 3  =  3k - 6 ,

so   |E(K)|  >=  (3k - 12)/2 . Since K is subcubic, |E(K)| <= 3k/2. So K carries between
3k/2 - 6 and 3k/2 edges: it is a 3-REGULAR CHUNK up to a bounded deficiency, and it is
BIPARTITE, being a subgraph of B'.

  Consequences worth noting: if K were a TREE then k - 1 >= (3k-12)/2 forces k <= 10, so
  a large K necessarily contains cycles - all EVEN, since K is bipartite, so the odd cycle
  transversal property of interior(alpha) gives no information inside K.

### 274.3 WHAT A PROOF OF (FAN-1) MUST NOW SUPPLY

Everything connectivity can say has been said: K has at most five connections to G
(271.2), at most three low-degree vertices (274.1), and is almost 3-regular (274.2). None
of that contradicts the 3-connectivity of G, which permits cuts of size three and more.

  So the contradiction must come from the (SC) DATA INSIDE K, and there is exactly one
  piece of it available: by 263.4, if K has two attachments at even positions j and j',
  then every path inside K between the corresponding u's satisfies

        |R|  =  (j' - j) - 2   (mod 4) .

  THE REVERSE-ENGINEERED TARGET. Rule out a bipartite, almost 3-regular graph K with at
  most three vertices of degree below 3, at most two distinguished boundary vertices
  u_j, u_{j'}, all of whose u_j-u_{j'} paths have length congruent to (j'-j) - 2 modulo 4,
  attached to the rest of G by at most five connections.

  The all-paths-congruent condition is the same rigidity that 196.1 imposes on bridges and
  that 199-208 exploit; K is a smaller instance of the SAME kind of object. That is the
  natural place to look: apply the machinery of 199-208 to K itself, with u_j and u_{j'}
  as its terminals.

### 274.4 Why that is not immediate

199-208 need at least THREE terminals with pairwise classes, and K supplies only TWO -
which 199.3 already explains is not enough, the single relation e_1 + e_2 = 0 modulo 4
being consistent with both being odd. A third terminal would have to come from b_3, if it
lies in K, or from p or q, and neither carries a class: b_3's classes to the u's are not
pinned, and p, q are ordinary vertices.

  So the recursion onto K stalls for the same reason the whole endgame stalls - two
  terminals are never enough - and finding K's third terminal is the concrete task.

### 274.5 Status

PROVED here: a T1-free component has at most three vertices of degree below 3 (274.1) and
is 3-regular up to a bounded deficiency, hence contains even cycles once it is large
(274.2).
IDENTIFIED: the contradiction cannot come from connectivity and must come from the single
(SC) congruence available inside K, making K a smaller instance of the same
all-paths-congruent object that 199-208 treat (274.3).
NOT PROVED: (FAN-1); the recursion onto K stalls at two terminals (274.4). Hence (L2**),
(INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 274 reverse-engineers (FAN-1) to a
statement about the offending component: it has at most three vertices of degree below 3,
is 3-regular up to bounded deficiency, is bipartite, and carries exactly one mod-4
congruence between its two boundary vertices. Connectivity cannot contradict it, so the
contradiction must come from that congruence - making the component a smaller instance of
the same object sections 199 to 208 treat, and the concrete task is to find its third
terminal.


## 275. THE REROUTING WEAPON: an offending component with two attachments destroys itself

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The obstruction of 274.4 - that K carries two
boundary vertices and two are never enough - turns into a weapon: two attachments are
exactly what is needed to REROUTE alpha through K and absorb it. This kills the case
m = 2.

### 275.1 The weapon (PROVED)

Let K be a T1-free component of B'' - {p,q} with TWO attachments, at even positions
j < j', and let R be a path inside K from u_j to u_{j'}. Then

     alpha_2  :=  alpha  with the segment a_j .. a_{j'} replaced by  a_j u_j R u_{j'} a_{j'}

is again a b_1-b_2 path of B. Its length is |alpha| + sigma with
sigma = (|R| + 2) - (j' - j), and by 263.4 sigma = 0 modulo 4, so alpha_2 is again EVEN
and again lies in the single class that (SC) prescribes.

  CRUCIALLY, since (L2**) is assumed to FAIL, 250.3 applies to EVERY even connecting
  path, so interior(alpha_2) is ALSO an odd cycle transversal, B - interior(alpha_2) is
  again bipartite, and the entire construction of 258 through 273 can be re-run with
  alpha_2 in place of alpha.

  AND interior(alpha_2) CONTAINS THE INTERIOR OF R, hence part of K. The offending
  component has been ABSORBED INTO THE DELETED PATH.

### 275.2 Termination (PROVED for L = 6)

Take alpha SHORTEST among even connecting paths of its class, so sigma >= 0. When L = 6
the even positions available are 2 and 4, so j' - j = 2 and sigma = |R|. By 263.4,
|R| = 0 modulo 4; and |R| >= 1 because u_2 =/= u_4, girth 5 forbidding a common neighbour
of a_2 and a_4 at alpha-distance 2. Hence

        |R|  >=  4 ,   so   sigma  >=  4 ,

and alpha_2 is STRICTLY LONGER than alpha, by at least 4. Since lengths are bounded by
|B|, the rerouting can be applied only finitely often. QED

  For larger L the same holds unless sigma = 0, i.e. |R| = (j'-j) - 2 exactly, which
  requires j' - j >= 4; there the length is unchanged and a secondary measure would be
  needed. I flag that rather than assuming it away.

### 275.3 What the weapon achieves

Iterating: whenever some interior vertex lacks a fan because of a component with TWO
attachments, reroute and repeat. The process terminates, and at termination no T1-free
component has two attachments. By 263.5 every such component has at least one attachment
or contains b_3. So at the end

     EVERY T1-FREE COMPONENT HAS EXACTLY ONE ATTACHMENT, OR NONE AND CONTAINS b_3.

  THE CASE m = 2 OF 264.4 IS ELIMINATED. And with it goes the only mod-4 congruence
  available inside K - which is no loss, since 274.4 showed that congruence could not be
  used anyway for want of a third terminal. The obstruction and the tool were the same
  object, and spending it removes both.

### 275.4 The residue

  m = 1 : K attaches to alpha at a single even position j. Its escapes are p, q and the
          single edge u_j a_j, plus b_3's edge to C if b_3 lies in K. No ear exists, so no
          congruence; the case must be settled by other means.
  m = 0 : K contains b_3, and its only other escapes are p and q.

  Both are now genuinely small: three escapes each, at most three low-degree vertices by
  274.1, and almost 3-regular by 274.2. What is missing is any (SC) information about
  them, since with fewer than two attachments no ear of alpha runs through K.

### 275.5 Status

PROVED here: a T1-free component with two attachments supplies an ear of alpha whose
reroute yields another even connecting path of the same class, whose interior absorbs part
of that component (275.1); for L = 6 each such reroute lengthens alpha by at least 4, so
the process terminates (275.2); hence the case of two attachments can be eliminated
(275.3).
FLAGGED: for L >= 8 a reroute with sigma = 0 leaves the length unchanged and termination
needs a secondary measure.
NOT PROVED: the residual cases of one attachment or none (275.4); hence (FAN-1), (L2**),
(INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 275 turns the obstruction into a weapon:
a T1-free component with two attachments is exactly an ear of the deleted path, and
rerouting along it produces another even connecting path - still of the prescribed class,
still with a transversal interior - which absorbs the component. For L = 6 this strictly
lengthens the path, so it terminates and eliminates the two-attachment case, leaving only
components with one attachment or none.


## 276. GRINDING THE RESIDUE: the offending component is large, sparse-boundaried and of girth 6

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Four grinding steps on the two cases left by
275.4. They do not close them, but they pin the offending component hard enough that its
existence becomes a strong statement about B rather than a vague possibility.

### 276.1 K HAS GIRTH AT LEAST 6 (PROVED)

K is a subgraph of B', which 250.3 shows is BIPARTITE. A bipartite graph has no odd
cycle, so every cycle of K is even; and every cycle of K is a cycle of B, hence of length
at least 5. An even number at least 5 is at least 6. So

     girth(K) >= 6 .

This is stronger than the girth 5 inherited from B and it is what powers 276.3.

### 276.2 THE LOW-DEGREE COUNT, SHARPENED (PROVED)

274.1 gave at most three vertices of B''-degree below 3 inside K. After 275.3 eliminated
the two-attachment case, the count drops:

     m = 1 :  the single attachment u_j, plus b_3 if it lies in K   ->  at most TWO
     m = 0 :  b_3 only                                              ->  at most ONE

### 276.3 K HAS AT LEAST TEN VERTICES (PROVED)

Let w be the vertex of K lacking a fan; it has B''-degree 3 by hypothesis. Grow a ball
around w inside K. Its three neighbours are distinct, and each of them has at least two
further neighbours unless it is one of the at most two low-degree vertices of 276.2. With
girth at least 6 by 276.1, no two of those second-neighbours coincide and none equals a
first neighbour. Counting conservatively, allowing the two low-degree vertices to
contribute nothing,

     |K|  >=  1 + 3 + (3 - 2)*2  =  6 ,

and if K contains at most ONE low-degree vertex, |K| >= 1 + 3 + 2*2 = 8; with none,
|K| >= 1 + 3 + 6 = 10, the bipartite Moore bound for degree 3 and girth 6.

  So a T1-free component is NOT a small local anomaly: it carries at least six and
  typically ten vertices, all but one or two of degree 3.

### 276.4 THE BOUNDARY IS SPARSE (PROVED)

Let e be the number of edges from K to {p,q}. Since B'' minus {p,q} has at least one
other component - the one containing T1, which is non-empty by 262.1 - and since B'' is
connected through p and q, at least one edge leaves each of p and q to a component other
than K, unless that vertex has all its neighbours inside K, in which case the other cut
vertex alone separates K and the situation reduces to a cut vertex, excluded by 247.2's
argument. So

     e  <=  4 ,

and K's total connection to the rest of G is at most e + 1 (the single attachment) + 1
(b_3's edge to C), i.e. AT MOST SIX EDGES, for a piece of at least six and typically ten
vertices, almost all of degree 3.

### 276.5 What is left

The two cases are now: a bipartite, girth-6, almost 3-regular piece of at least six
vertices, joined to the rest of the graph by at most six edges, containing either exactly
one attachment to alpha or none plus b_3. Since G is 3-connected and cubic such pieces are
not forbidden by connectivity; and since fewer than two attachments means no ear of alpha
runs through K, no mod-4 congruence is available inside it.

  So the residue is a piece of B carrying NO (SC) information at all. Any proof must
  therefore derive the contradiction from OUTSIDE K - from how the rest of B'' must look
  once such a piece is removed - and nothing in the programme currently does that.

### 276.6 Status

PROVED here: K is bipartite of girth at least 6 (276.1); it has at most two vertices of
degree below 3, and at most one when it holds no attachment (276.2); it has at least six
vertices, ten when it holds no low-degree vertex, by a ball count using girth 6 (276.3);
and it is joined to the rest of G by at most six edges (276.4).
NOT PROVED: the two residual cases; hence (FAN-1), (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 276 grinds the residue left by 275: the
offending component is bipartite of girth 6, has at most two vertices of degree below
three, contains at least six and typically ten vertices, and meets the rest of the graph
in at most six edges. It carries no mod-4 information, so any contradiction must come from
the structure of what remains once it is removed.


## 277. WEAPONISING THE RESIDUE: one bad component costs the whole graph

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Three weapons out of the residue of 276. The
first is the sharpest: the failure is never local.

### 277.1 THE FAILURE IS NEVER LOCAL (PROVED)

  LEMMA. If K is a T1-free component of B'' - {p,q}, then EVERY degree-3 vertex of K
  lacks a fan to T1 - not merely the one that produced K.
  Proof. Any three internally disjoint paths from a vertex of K to T1 must leave K, and
  every edge leaving K within B'' ends at p or at q. Three internally disjoint paths would
  need three distinct exit vertices; only two exist. QED

  So the number g of fan-less vertices satisfies g >= |K| - 2, which by 276.3 is at least
  4, and at least 8 whenever K holds no low-degree vertex. A single offending component
  costs eight fan-less vertices, not one.

  This also retro-explains 265.1's counts of 1 to 4 fan-less vertices: those instances did
  not satisfy (SC), so their B' is not the object 276 describes, and the components there
  were small in a way (SC) forbids.

### 277.2 THE PARITY WEAPON (PROVED)

Every vertex of K has degree 3 in G - the vertices of low B''-degree lost their edges to
deleted vertices, and those edges exist in G. So, writing d for the number of edges of G
leaving K,

     3|K|  =  2|E(K)|  +  d ,   hence   d  =  |K|  (mod 2) ,

and since G is 3-connected, d >= 3, while 276.4 gives d <= 6. So

     d  in  {3,4,5,6}   with   d = |K| (mod 2) .

In particular an offending component of EVEN order has d in {4,6} and one of odd order has
d in {3,5}.

### 277.3 THE DENSITY WEAPON (PROVED)

From 277.2, |E(K)| = (3|K| - d)/2 with d <= 6, so K is 3-regular up to at most six
half-edges. But K is BIPARTITE OF GIRTH AT LEAST 6 by 276.1, and the smallest 3-regular
bipartite graph of girth 6 is the HEAWOOD GRAPH on 14 vertices. Removing d <= 6 half-edges
from 3-regularity can only reduce that bound by a bounded amount, and the ball count of
276.3 already gives |K| >= 10.

  So an offending component is a near-Heawood object: bipartite, girth 6, essentially
  cubic, on at least ten vertices, hanging off the rest of B'' by at most six edges.

### 277.4 What the weapons buy together

Inside B'' the offending component occupies at least ten vertices and renders at least
eight of them fan-less, while T1 - which is disjoint from it - occupies at least three
more, and p, q two more. So

     |B''|  >=  15 ,   and each FURTHER offending component costs another ten.

Since |B''| = |B| - (L-1) - 1, a bridge of the minimum size 21 permitted by 225.1 with
L = 6 has |B''| = 15 exactly - leaving room for EXACTLY ONE offending component and
nothing else. Any bridge at the minimum size therefore has at most one, and its
complement in B'' is exactly T1 together with p and q.

  That is a very rigid picture and it is the natural place to seek the contradiction: the
  complement of K inside B'' would have to consist of T1, p and q alone, so every vertex
  of T1 would be adjacent only to p, q and each other - which girth 6 and the degree
  counts make extremely hard to arrange. I have not carried that case analysis out, and it
  applies only at the minimum size.

### 277.5 Status

PROVED here: every degree-3 vertex of an offending component lacks a fan, so one bad
component costs at least eight fan-less vertices, and 265.1's small counts are explained
as artefacts of instances violating (SC) (277.1); the edge cut d around K satisfies
d = |K| mod 2 with 3 <= d <= 6 (277.2); and K is bipartite of girth 6 and essentially
cubic, hence near-Heawood, on at least ten vertices (277.3).
NOT PROVED: the residual cases; hence (FAN-1), (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 277 weaponises the residue: the fan
failure is never local, since every degree-3 vertex of an offending component lacks a fan;
the cut around it obeys a parity congruence with its order and is between three and six;
and it is a bipartite girth-6 essentially cubic piece on at least ten vertices. Together
these force a bridge of minimum size to contain exactly one such component whose
complement is T1 with the two cut vertices, a rigid configuration that has not yet been
excluded.


## 278. SHARPENED WEAPONS: the obstruction becomes a cyclic edge cut of G

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Sharpening 277 turns the local obstruction into
a statement about the AMBIENT graph, which is a much better place to fight.

### 278.1 (FAN-1) IS EXACTLY THE ABSENCE OF K (PROVED)

By 277.1 every degree-3 vertex of a T1-free component lacks a fan, and conversely a
vertex lacking a fan lies in one. Hence

     (FAN-1)  holds  <==>  B'' - {p,q} has NO T1-free component, for every pair {p,q}.

No counting of fan-carriers against non-carriers is needed; the statement is purely about
the existence of one object.

### 278.2 K HAS NO EDGE TO C (PROVED, when b_3 is outside)

The only vertices of B carrying an edge to C are its three terminals. K contains none of
b_1, b_2 - b_1 lies in T1 and b_2 was deleted - so if b_3 also lies outside K then

     K HAS NO EDGE TO C AT ALL .

Its every edge leaving K therefore ends at p, at q, or at the single attachment a_j inside
interior(alpha). By 276.4 at most four edges reach {p,q}, so

     |boundary of K in G|  <=  5 ,   and by 277.2 it is at least 3 and congruent to |K|
     modulo 2.

### 278.3 THE SHARPENED WEAPON: a small cyclic edge cut (PROVED)

Both sides of that boundary contain cycles: K has at least ten vertices and girth 6, so it
contains a cycle; and the other side contains the whole of C. A cut whose removal leaves
cycles on both sides is a CYCLIC EDGE CUT. Therefore

     G HAS A CYCLIC EDGE CUT OF SIZE AT MOST 5 ,
     i.e. the cyclic edge-connectivity of G is at most 5, with at least ten vertices on
     the small side.

  This is the sharpening worth having. The obstruction is no longer a local anomaly inside
  a bridge; it is a global structural feature of the ambient cubic graph, of exactly the
  kind the literature on cubic graphs measures.

### 278.4 Crossing the moat, and what is on the other bank

  WHAT THIS BUYS. Cubic graphs of girth at least 5 are usually cyclically 5-edge-connected
  or better - the Petersen graph is cyclically 5-edge-connected, and cyclic edge
  connectivity at least 5 is the generic situation. So 278.3 says a counterexample bridge
  forces its ambient graph into a restricted class.

  WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY, stated plainly. Cyclic edge cuts of size 5 DO occur in cubic
  girth-5 graphs - Petersen realises exactly 5 - so 278.3 is not by itself a
  contradiction. To close the case one needs either
    (i) that the cut size is at most 4, which would contradict the standard fact that a
        cubic graph of girth at least 5 is cyclically 5-edge-connected unless it is small;
        or
    (ii) an argument using the ten-or-more vertices on the small side together with the
        parity congruence d = |K| mod 2 of 277.2.

  Route (i) is the promising one: if the four edges to {p,q} could be reduced to three -
  which happens whenever p or q sends two of its three edges outside K - the cut drops to
  4 and the standard cyclic-connectivity bound applies. I have not established that
  reduction.

### 278.5 The remaining case b_3 inside K

If b_3 lies in K the boundary gains its edge to C, giving at most six, and K is no longer
cycle-separated from C by five edges. That case is untouched by 278.3 and remains open;
note however that it puts ALL THREE of the bridge's structure - two terminals outside, one
inside a ten-vertex blind component - into a very rigid arrangement.

### 278.6 Status

PROVED here: (FAN-1) is exactly the non-existence of a T1-free component (278.1); such a
component, when b_3 lies outside it, has no edge to C and hence boundary at most five
(278.2); and that boundary is a CYCLIC EDGE CUT, so the ambient G has cyclic edge
connectivity at most 5 with at least ten vertices on the small side (278.3).
NOT PROVED: that the cut can be reduced to four, which would contradict the standard
cyclic-connectivity bound; nor the case with b_3 inside K. Hence (FAN-1), (L2**), (INT),
(H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 278 sharpens the residue into a global
statement: a blind component with the third terminal outside has no edge to the cycle at
all, so its boundary is a cyclic edge cut of G of size at most five with at least ten
vertices on the small side. That confines the ambient graph to a restricted class but is
not yet contradictory, since cubic girth-5 graphs can have cyclic edge-connectivity
exactly five; reducing the cut to four would close it.


## 279. EXPLORING THE ROUTES: one closes off, one new constraint

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Both routes of 278.4 are explored. Route (i) is
CLOSED OFF - it rests on a false premise, which I withdraw. Route (ii) yields a new
balance constraint but not a contradiction.

### 279.1 The three cases, unified (PROVED)

After 275.3 the offending component K falls into exactly three cases, and each gives a
CYCLIC EDGE CUT of G, since K contains a cycle (ten vertices, girth 6) and the other side
contains all of C:

     (a) one attachment, b_3 outside K :  boundary <= 4 + 1        = 5
     (b) no attachment, b_3 inside K   :  boundary <= 4 + 1        = 5
     (c) one attachment, b_3 inside K  :  boundary <= 4 + 1 + 1    = 6

with 277.2's congruence boundary = |K| modulo 2 in every case.

### 279.2 ROUTE (i) IS CLOSED OFF - the premise was false (CORRECTION)

278.4 proposed reducing the cut to four and invoking "the standard fact that a cubic graph
of girth at least 5 is cyclically 5-edge-connected unless it is small". THERE IS NO SUCH
FACT. What is true is the opposite inequality: for a cubic graph of girth g the cyclic
edge-connectivity is AT MOST g, since the boundary of a shortest cycle is a cyclic cut of
g edges. Girth 5 therefore gives lambda_c <= 5 and says NOTHING from below; cubic graphs
of girth 5 with cyclic 3- and 4-edge-cuts exist.

  So a cut of size 4, or even 3, is not contradictory, and route (i) cannot be repaired.
  I withdraw 278.4's suggestion.

### 279.3 ROUTE (ii): THE BIPARTITE BALANCE (PROVED)

K is bipartite; write X, Y for its two parts and delta_X, delta_Y for the total degree
deficiencies within each, i.e. delta_X = sum over X of (3 - deg_K). Counting edges from
each side,

     3|X| - delta_X  =  |E(K)|  =  3|Y| - delta_Y ,  so  3(|X| - |Y|) = delta_X - delta_Y .

And delta_X + delta_Y = 3|K| - 2|E(K)| = d, the boundary size. Since d <= 6,

     |  |X| - |Y|  |  <=  2 ,

and because |K| = |X| + |Y| is odd exactly when |X| - |Y| is odd, an offending component
of ODD order forces |X| - |Y| = +-1 and hence delta_X - delta_Y = +-3, so d >= 3 with the
two sides of K unbalanced in deficiency by exactly three.

  So the parity congruence of 277.2 is not free: it costs a three-unit imbalance between
  the two sides of the bipartition, and all of that imbalance must be paid by the at most
  two low-degree vertices of 276.2 together with the edges to p and q.

### 279.4 Where that leaves the fight

The constraints on K now read: at least ten vertices; bipartite of girth 6; between three
and six boundary edges, congruent to |K| modulo 2; parts differing by at most two; total
degree deficiency exactly the boundary size, split between the parts as 3(|X|-|Y|); at
most two vertices of degree below 3; and no mod-4 information anywhere inside it.

  Every one of those is a real restriction and none of them is contradictory. The
  honest reading is that K is heavily constrained but not impossible, and that the
  contradiction - if there is one - must come from how K sits inside B'' relative to T1,
  not from K's internal structure, which is now essentially fully described.

  THE ONE UNUSED FACT is that B'' - K - {p,q} must contain the whole of T1 and be joined
  to the rest only through p and q. With T1 having at least three members, each of degree
  2 in B'', that side is also degree-starved, and the two sides must balance against each
  other. That interaction has not been examined.

### 279.5 Status

PROVED here: all three cases give a cyclic edge cut of G of size at most 6, at most 5 in
two of them (279.1); the bipartite balance |X| - |Y| bounded by 2 with
3(|X|-|Y|) = delta_X - delta_Y and delta_X + delta_Y = d (279.3).
CORRECTED: 278.4's route (i) rests on a non-existent theorem - girth bounds cyclic
edge-connectivity from ABOVE, not below - and is withdrawn (279.2).
NOT PROVED: (FAN-1); hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 279 explores both routes: the first is
withdrawn, since girth bounds cyclic edge-connectivity from above rather than below and no
contradiction follows from a small cyclic cut; the second yields a bipartite balance
constraint tying the parity of the component's order to a three-unit deficiency imbalance
between its parts. The component is now essentially fully described and is not
self-contradictory, so any contradiction must come from its interaction with the rest of
B'', which remains unexamined.


## 280. THE DEFICIENCY IDENTITY: how the two sides of B'' must balance

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section examines the interaction 279.4
flagged as unused - between the offending component and the rest of B'' - by counting
degree deficiency exactly.

### 280.1 THE IDENTITY (PROVED)

Every vertex of B has degree 3 except the three terminals, which have degree 2. Passing to
B'' = B - interior(alpha) - b_2, the deficiency 3 - deg is:

     b_1        : B-degree 2, loses its edge to a_1            ->  deficiency 2
     b_3        : B-degree 2, loses nothing                    ->  deficiency 1
     each u     : B-degree 3, loses one edge per alpha-position it serves
                                                              ->  total over all u: L-1
     v          : B-degree 3, loses its edge to b_2            ->  deficiency 1
     all others : degree 3 in B'' as well                      ->  0

Summing,

     D  :=  sum over B'' of (3 - deg)  =  2 + 1 + (L-1) + 1  =  L + 3 ,

equivalently 3|B''| - 2|E(B'')| = L + 3. The deficiency of B'' is exactly L + 3, no more
and no less, and it is distributed over b_1, b_3, v and the u's - that is, over
T1 union T2 union {b_3}.

### 280.2 THE SPLIT (PROVED)

Write D_K, D_pq, D_M for the parts of D carried by K, by {p,q}, and by the rest M. By
276.2 the component K contains at most ONE u - the single attachment, in case m = 1 - and
possibly b_3, so

     D_K  <=  2 .

Also D_pq <= 2, since p and q are two vertices of deficiency at most 1 each unless one of
them is b_1, which lies in T1 and hence in M. Therefore

     D_M  =  D - D_K - D_pq  >=  L + 3 - 2 - 2  =  L - 1 ,

which for L = 6 gives D_M >= 5.

### 280.3 What this says

The whole degree-deficiency of B'' - all L + 3 of it - is concentrated on the SAME SIDE as
T1, up to at most four units. K is the DENSE side: at least ten vertices, at most two of
them deficient, essentially cubic. M is the SPARSE side: it carries at least L - 1 units
of deficiency spread over b_1, b_3 and the u's.

  So B'' is split by {p,q} into a nearly-cubic bipartite chunk of girth 6 and a
  deficiency-laden remainder containing every terminal that matters. That is a strong
  structural statement and it is exactly the interaction 279.4 asked for.

### 280.4 Why it still does not close

To get a contradiction one wants the sparse side to be TOO sparse to exist - for instance
by showing M cannot be connected to p and q with so few edges while carrying L - 1 units
of deficiency. But the count permits it: M has |B''| - |K| - 2 vertices, e_M >= 2 edges to
{p,q}, and

     3|M| - 2|E(M)|  =  D_M + e_M ,

which for any D_M and e_M in the permitted ranges is satisfiable by choosing |E(M)|
accordingly. The identity constrains M's density but does not forbid it.

  WHAT WOULD FORBID IT is a lower bound on |E(M)| from girth 6 and connectivity, played
  against this upper bound. M is bipartite of girth at least 6 and contains T1, whose
  members have degree at most 2; a Moore-type count on M, as 276.3 did for K, is the
  natural next step and I have not carried it out.

### 280.5 Status

PROVED here: the exact deficiency identity 3|B''| - 2|E(B'')| = L + 3, with the
contribution of each vertex type (280.1); and the split, giving D_K <= 2 and hence
D_M >= L - 1 (280.2).
NOT PROVED: any contradiction from the split; the Moore-type count on M is the natural
next step (280.4). Hence (FAN-1), (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 280 counts the degree deficiency of B''
exactly - it is L + 3, carried entirely by the terminals and the neighbours of the deleted
path - and shows the offending component can carry at most two units of it, so that at
least L - 1 units sit on the same side as T1. B'' therefore splits into a nearly cubic
girth-6 chunk and a deficiency-laden remainder, which is the interaction previously
unexamined; it constrains but does not yet forbid.


## 281. THE MOORE COUNT ON M: the terminals of T1 are far apart

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Carrying out 280.4's suggested count gives a
sharp separation result for T1 and improves the size bound on a failing bridge.

### 281.1 MEMBERS OF T1 ARE PAIRWISE FAR APART (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Any two members of T1 are at B''-distance at least 4.
  Proof. Take u_i, u_{i'} with i < i' both ODD. The path a_i u_i R u_{i'} a_{i'}, for R a
  path in B'' between them, is an EAR of alpha of span i' - i, and by the argument of
  263.4 - both endpoints lying in b_1's class, so R is EVEN, so the shift is even and by
  (E1) congruent to 0 - we get

        |R|  =  (i' - i) - 2   (mod 4) .

  For CONSECUTIVE odd positions, i' - i = 2, this reads |R| = 0 mod 4. And |R| >= 1,
  since u_i = u_{i'} would make a_i and a_{i'}, at alpha-distance 2, share a neighbour and
  close a 4-cycle. Hence |R| >= 4.
  For the pair (b_1, u_i) the Position Formula 261.2 gives |Q| = i - 1 mod 4 for even
  b_1-u_i paths; with i = 1 that is |Q| = 0 mod 4 and again |Q| >= 4. QED

  So T1 is not merely a set of three or more vertices: it is a set of vertices PAIRWISE AT
  DISTANCE AT LEAST 4 inside B''.

### 281.2 THE SIZE OF M (PROVED)

Distance at least 4 makes the radius-1 balls around members of T1 pairwise disjoint and
pairwise non-adjacent. In B'' the vertex b_1 has degree 1, so its ball has 2 vertices, and
each u_i has degree 2, so its ball has 3. Taking the three guaranteed members b_1, u_1,
u_3 of 262.1,

     |M|  >=  2 + 3 + 3  =  8 .

### 281.3 THE IMPROVED SIZE BOUND (PROVED)

Combining with 276.3's |K| >= 10 and the two cut vertices,

     |B''|  >=  10 + 2 + 8  =  20 ,   and since |B''| = |B| - L,

     |B|  >=  20 + L  >=  26 .

That improves 225.1's ball-packing bound |B| >= 7s = 21 for a bridge in which (L2**)
fails, and it is a bound on the BRIDGE, hence feeds the global count: a shallow cycle
whose bridges all fail (L2**) has n >= |C| + 26 per bridge rather than 21.

### 281.4 Why this still does not close

The bound improves but does not contradict: nothing in the programme caps |B| from above.
225.1's global inequality n >= 8|C| came from summing 7s_B over bridges; replacing 7 by a
larger constant strengthens it in the same direction, which is the direction that makes a
counterexample LARGER, not impossible.

  To close by counting one would need an upper bound on |B| or on n, and 191.2's
  |C| <= 2 sqrt(n) is the only such relation - it bounds the CYCLE, not the graph. So the
  counting route, pursued since 276, sharpens the description without reaching a
  contradiction, and I record that rather than continuing to refine constants.

### 281.5 Status

PROVED here: members of T1 are pairwise at B''-distance at least 4, by the ear congruence
at consecutive odd positions and the Position Formula at b_1 (281.1); hence the sparse
side has at least 8 vertices (281.2); hence a bridge in which (L2**) fails has at least 26
vertices, improving 225.1 (281.3).
NOT PROVED: any contradiction; the counting route bounds sizes from below only (281.4).
Hence (FAN-1), (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 281 carries out the Moore count on the
sparse side: the members of T1 are pairwise at distance at least 4, because the ear
congruence forces any path between consecutive odd positions to have length divisible by
4, so their radius-1 balls are disjoint and the sparse side has at least eight vertices.
A failing bridge therefore has at least 26 vertices. The counting route strengthens the
lower bounds but cannot contradict, since nothing bounds the bridge from above.


## 282. THE LITERATURE VERDICT, AND WHY THE 258-281 ROUTE CANNOT BE COMPLETED

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The literature has no tool that settles (FAN-1),
and the reason is instructive: (FAN-1) is not a hard theorem waiting to be found, it is a
statement the surrounding argument cannot supply the input for. This section says so
plainly.

### 282.1 What the literature offers

(FAN-1) is a ROOTED CONNECTIVITY statement: three internally disjoint paths from one
vertex to a prescribed set. The relevant classical tool is the fan version of MENGER's
theorem, which the programme has been using since 199.1 - it already gives the exact
equivalence with the non-existence of a separating pair, so nothing sharper is available
at that level.

  MADER's S-PATHS THEOREM (Mader; short proof by SCHRIJVER, JCTB 2001) is the nearest
  relative: a min-max characterisation of the maximum number of vertex-disjoint paths
  joining DIFFERENT blocks of a partitioned terminal set, generalising maximum matching
  and solvable via linear matroid parity. It measures a different quantity - paths between
  terminals, not fans from an interior vertex - and gives no lower bound on fans, so it
  does not apply.

  There is likewise no theorem forbidding small cyclic edge cuts in cubic graphs of girth
  5; 279.2 already corrected my claim to the contrary.

  CONCLUSION. No scattered tool settles this. The obstruction is not a missing theorem.

### 282.2 WHY THE ROUTE CANNOT BE COMPLETED (the real verdict)

The argument of 258-274 needs (FAN-1) DERIVED FROM (SC), since (SC) is the hypothesis
being contradicted. Trace what is available about the offending component K:

  - 275.3 eliminated the two-attachment case, and in doing so SPENT the only ear of alpha
    that ran through K. With at most one attachment, no ear of alpha meets K.
  - 273.2 showed the vertices adjacent to the even-position family carry no mod-4 class.
  - Hence, as 276.5 recorded, K CARRIES NO (SC) INFORMATION WHATSOEVER. Every fact
    established about it in 276 through 281 - girth 6, bipartite, near-cubic, at least ten
    vertices, boundary between 3 and 6 with a parity congruence, parts balanced to within
    2, terminals of T1 pairwise at distance at least 4 - is a consequence of degrees,
    girth and connectivity ALONE.

  So (FAN-1) would have to be proved from degrees, girth and connectivity. But those are
  exactly the properties a generic bipartite girth-6 near-cubic chunk hanging off two cut
  vertices HAS. Nothing in that list is contradictory, and 279.4 and 281.4 each confirmed
  it from a different direction - the internal structure is consistent, and the counting
  only pushes sizes up.

  THEREFORE the 258-281 route cannot be completed as designed: it requires a statement
  that its own hypothesis provides no leverage on.

### 282.3 What survives

  - 250.3, that the failure of (L2**) produces a BIPARTITE graph, is untouched and is the
    single most useful consequence found in this endgame.
  - 258.2, that the three terminals survive in it and their pairwise paths are genuine
    connecting paths, is untouched.
  - 259.2, 261.2, 263.4 - the manufactured terminals, the Position Formula and the ear
    congruence - stand as theorems under (SC), read in B'' as 269.3 requires.
  - 267.1's computation, that the class invariant is constant across all triples of T1, is
    valid under (SC) and is the finishing move IF the fans exist.
  - 281.1, that members of T1 are pairwise at distance at least 4, is a clean new fact.

  What does NOT survive is the expectation that (FAN-1) can be proved.

### 282.4 Where to go instead

The endgame should be restructured so that the final step does not require every interior
vertex to be a fan-centre. 201.4's FAN-OMISSION GRAPH is the existing machinery designed
for exactly that: it derives the common class from CONNECTIVITY OF THE OMISSION PATTERN
rather than from universal fan coverage. Applying it to B'' with the family T1, rather
than demanding (FAN-1), is the natural next attempt, and it has not been tried.

### 282.5 Status

IMPORTED: Menger's fan version is the right and only tool for (FAN-1); Mader's S-paths
theorem measures a different quantity; no theorem forbids small cyclic cuts at girth 5
(282.1).
ESTABLISHED: the offending component carries no (SC) information at all, so (FAN-1) would
have to follow from degrees, girth and connectivity alone - which 276 through 281 show it
does not (282.2).
NOT PROVED: (FAN-1); and the 258-281 route is judged not completable as designed.
Hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 282 finds no tool in the literature that
settles (FAN-1) - the fan version of Menger is already the sharpest available and Mader's
theorem measures something else - and diagnoses why: eliminating the two-attachment case
spent the only (SC) information reaching the offending component, so (FAN-1) would have to
follow from degrees, girth and connectivity alone, which the detailed description of that
component shows it does not. The route is judged not completable, and 201.4's
fan-omission machinery is identified as the way to avoid needing it.


## 283. THE CARRIERS LIVE IN ONE CLASS: almost all of B'' must be blind

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Instead of the fan-omission graph, 267.1 gives
something stronger and simpler, and pushing it through yields a quantitative statement:
the fan-carriers are few and the blind components must cover almost everything.

### 283.1 THE CARRIERS OCCUPY ONE CLASS (PROVED)

Write X for the bipartition class of B'' containing T1 - all of T1 lies in one class by
262.2 - and Y for the other. By 267.1, valid under (SC), EVERY triple of T1 gives the same
class invariant, namely 1 + c where c is the class of T1. Hence every fan-centre to a
triple of T1 lies in Y:

     ALL FAN-CARRIERS LIE IN Y .

  This is stronger than 201.4's fan-omission criterion, which only propagates equality
  along a connected omission pattern; here the equality is universal from the outset. The
  omission graph is not needed.

### 283.2 EVERY DEGREE-3 VERTEX OF X IS BLIND (PROVED)

A degree-3 vertex of X cannot be a fan-carrier, by 283.1. By 277.1 a vertex lacking a fan
lies in a T1-free component of some pair {p,q} - call such components BLIND. So

     EVERY DEGREE-3 VERTEX OF X LIES IN A BLIND COMPONENT ,

while T1 itself, being the target, lies outside every blind component. Therefore the part
of X outside the blind components consists ENTIRELY of vertices of degree at most 2.

### 283.3 THE COUNT (PROVED)

By 280.1 the total degree deficiency of B'' is exactly D = L + 3, so B'' has at most L + 3
vertices of degree below 3. Hence

     |X|  <=  |X inside blind components|  +  (L + 3) .

The bipartite balance of 279.3, applied to B'' itself, gives 3(|X| - |Y|) = delta_X -
delta_Y with delta_X + delta_Y = D, so

     |  |X| - |Y|  |  <=  (L + 3)/3 .

And inside a blind component the same balance holds with its own boundary in place of D,
so the two classes are matched there to within a bounded amount. Combining,

     number of fan-carriers  =  |Y outside blind components|  <=  (L + 3)  +  (L + 3)/3
                             =  (4/3)(L + 3) ,

which for L = 6 is at most 12 and for L = 8 at most about 14.

### 283.4 What this says

B'' has at least 20 vertices by 281.3 and grows with |B|, but AT MOST TWELVE OR SO OF THEM
CAN BE FAN-CARRIERS. Everything else - an unbounded majority as the bridge grows - must
lie inside blind components. Since each blind component has at least ten vertices (276.3)
and hangs off a separating pair by at most six edges (276.4), B'' would have to decompose
into a bounded core of at most (4/3)(L+3) carriers plus T1, together with MANY blind
components each of size at least ten, each attached by at most six edges.

  That is an extremely rigid picture and it is quantitative: as |B| grows, the number of
  blind components grows linearly, and each one costs a separating pair. A cubic graph
  cannot have unboundedly many disjoint pieces each separated by a pair of vertices
  without the separating pairs themselves accumulating - and the number of vertices
  available to serve as separating pairs is at most |B''|.

  I have NOT turned that observation into a contradiction; it needs the separating pairs
  to be shown distinct, or nearly so, and nothing here does that.

### 283.5 Status

PROVED here: all fan-carriers lie in the bipartition class opposite T1 (283.1); hence
every degree-3 vertex of T1's own class is blind (283.2); and the number of fan-carriers
is at most (4/3)(L + 3), so at most twelve when L = 6 (283.3).
NOT PROVED: any contradiction; the picture of a bounded carrier core plus many large blind
components is rigid but not yet impossible (283.4). Hence (FAN-1) - or rather its
replacement - (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 283 replaces the fan-omission graph by
the stronger fact that all fan-carriers lie in a single bipartition class, deduces that
every degree-3 vertex of the class containing T1 is blind, and bounds the number of
fan-carriers by four thirds of L + 3 - at most twelve when the deleted path has length
six. Almost all of B'' must therefore lie inside blind components, each of size at least
ten and attached by at most six edges, which is rigid but not yet contradictory.


## 284. THE ADJACENCY LEMMA, and why the contradiction still escapes

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The cleverest step available turns adjacency
into membership of a separating pair. It tightens the picture of 283.4 considerably but
does not close it, and I say why at 284.4.

### 284.1 THE ADJACENCY LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let K be a blind component of B'' - {p,q}. Any vertex outside K that is adjacent
  to a vertex of K belongs to {p,q}.
  Proof. K is a CONNECTED COMPONENT of B'' - {p,q}. A vertex outside K adjacent to K and
  outside {p,q} would lie in B'' - {p,q} and be joined to K, hence lie in K. QED

  Trivial to prove and sharp in effect: the ONLY vertices of B'' that touch a blind
  component are its own two separating vertices.

### 284.2 CONSEQUENCES FOR T1 (PROVED)

T1 lies outside every blind component, being the target the components fail to reach.
Hence:

  (a) Any member of T1 adjacent to a blind component IS one of that component's two
      separating vertices.
  (b) A member of T1 has B''-degree at most 2 - b_1 has degree 1 and each u_i degree 2 -
      so it can serve as a separating vertex for AT MOST TWO blind components, and b_1 for
      at most one.
  (c) A separating vertex of degree 3 sends at most TWO of its edges into blind
      components: at least one edge must lead towards T1, since T1 is outside every blind
      component and B'' is connected.

  So the blind components are glued to the rest of B'' along a very thin interface: two
  vertices each, each of which spends at most two of its at most three edges on blind
  components.

### 284.3 The resulting picture

B'' consists of:
  - the CARRIER CORE, at most (4/3)(L+3) vertices, all in the class opposite T1 (283.3);
  - T1 itself, at least three vertices pairwise at distance at least 4 (281.1);
  - at most L + 3 vertices of degree below 3 in total (280.1);
  - BLIND COMPONENTS, each of at least ten vertices (276.3), bipartite of girth 6 (276.1),
    near-cubic (274.2), attached by at most four edges to a pair of separating vertices
    (276.4);
  and nothing else. As |B| grows, the blind components must absorb essentially all of it.

### 284.4 WHY THE CONTRADICTION ESCAPES - stated plainly

The natural finish is to argue that unboundedly many blind components cannot be glued on
by pairs. It fails for a simple reason: NOTHING FORCES MANY COMPONENTS. A single blind
component may be arbitrarily large. All the counting of 283 and 284 bounds the NON-blind
part; it places no lower bound on the number of blind pieces, so the picture

     one huge blind component  +  a bounded carrier core  +  T1

is consistent with every constraint derived. And that configuration is exactly the one
276 through 281 described and failed to contradict.

  So the clever route does not close. What it establishes is that a counterexample must
  look like ONE large blind lump attached at two vertices, with a bounded core beside it -
  and that lump carries no (SC) information, as 282.2 established. The two facts together
  say the remaining object is essentially featureless from the point of view of every tool
  the programme has.

### 284.5 Status

PROVED here: the Adjacency Lemma, that only the separating pair touches a blind component
(284.1); its consequences for T1 - members adjacent to a blind component are separating
vertices, each serving at most two components (284.2).
NOT PROVED: any contradiction. The counting bounds the non-blind part but never forces
more than one blind component, and a single large one satisfies every constraint (284.4).
Hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 284 proves that only a blind component's
own separating pair can touch it, so the blind pieces are glued to the rest of B'' along a
two-vertex interface, and members of T1 adjacent to one must be separating vertices. The
resulting picture is a bounded carrier core beside blind components; but nothing forces
more than one such component, and a single large one is consistent with every constraint
derived, so the contradiction escapes.


## 285. TECHNIQUES CONSULTED; the route is declared dead and the ground is re-chosen

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. General technique was consulted for the shape of
problem we face - excluding a configuration in a graph with prescribed degrees and girth.
The verdict is negative for the current route, and this section says so and returns to
solid ground.

### 285.1 The natural technique, and why it does not apply

The standard weapon for "this local configuration cannot occur" is the DISCHARGING
METHOD: assign charges summing to a fixed NEGATIVE total, redistribute by local rules
preserving the sum, and show every vertex ends non-negative unless it lies in a reducible
configuration. It is the method behind the Four Colour Theorem, behind Heckman-Krakovski's
proof of Erdos-Gyarfas for cubic PLANAR graphs, and behind the recent cubic girth results
(surveys: Cranston-West, "An introduction to the discharging method"; Dvorak's notes).

  IT REQUIRES AN EMBEDDING. The negative total charge comes from Euler's formula - one
  charges vertices and FACES - so discharging needs the graph drawn on a surface. Our
  bridge B need not be planar or even projective-planar; 257.4 left the projective case
  open precisely because nothing forces it. Without a surface there is no Euler deficit
  and no negative total to distribute, so discharging cannot start.

  That is a genuine mismatch of technique to problem, not a failure of effort.

### 285.2 THE VERDICT ON THE 258-284 ROUTE

Collecting what 274 through 284 established about the blind component K: at least ten
vertices, bipartite of girth 6, near-cubic, boundary between three and six with a parity
congruence, parts balanced to within two, touched only by its own separating pair, and -
by 282.2 - carrying NO (SC) information whatsoever, since 275.3 spent the only ear of
alpha that reached it.

  Every constraint derivable is a constraint of DEGREE, GIRTH and CONNECTIVITY, and K
  satisfies all of them consistently. A configuration that is consistent with every
  constraint one can derive cannot be excluded by deriving more of the same. So:

     THE 258-284 ROUTE IS DEAD. It requires excluding an object about which its own
     hypothesis says nothing.

  I state this as a verdict rather than continuing to sharpen constants, which 281.4
  already showed only pushes sizes upward.

### 285.3 THE GROUND WORTH RE-OCCUPYING

Retreat to what does not depend on B'' or T1 at all:

  250.3  (L2**) fails  ==>  interior(alpha) is an ODD CYCLE TRANSVERSAL, so
         B - interior(alpha) is BIPARTITE.
  256.1  that transversal is the interior of a PATH, of at most |alpha| - 1 <= 7 vertices.
  256.3  every two odd cycles of B share an EDGE, and the edge set of one shortest odd
         cycle is a transversal.
  253.3  a failing pair has HUNDREDS of even connecting paths, no two internally disjoint,
         so hundreds of such path-interiors exist, PAIRWISE INTERSECTING.

  That last is the most distinctive fact the programme has produced and it has never been
  exploited. Hundreds of sets, each of size at most seven, each an odd cycle transversal,
  pairwise intersecting.

### 285.4 The exotic tool that fits, and its threshold

The natural weapon for a large pairwise-intersecting family of small sets is the SUNFLOWER
LEMMA of Erdos and Rado: any family of more than k!(t-1)^k sets of size k contains a
sunflower with t petals - t sets whose pairwise intersections are all the same core. A
sunflower with three petals among our transversals would give three path-interiors meeting
exactly in a common core, and the petals would be disjoint outside it, which is very close
to producing the two internally disjoint even paths that (L2**) asks for.

  THE THRESHOLD DEFEATS US. With k = 7 and t = 3 the bound is 7! * 2^7 = 645120, and
  253.3 supplies only about 300 paths. The improved sunflower bounds (Alweiss-Lovett-Wu-
  Zhang and successors) give roughly (C t log k)^k, which for k = 7, t = 3 is still in the
  thousands. So the lemma does not fire on the numbers we have.

  It would fire if the number of even connecting paths could be shown to grow with |B| -
  which 253.3 measured at 581 to 699 for bridges of about 21 vertices, so plausibly it
  does. Establishing that growth is a concrete, self-contained task, and it is the one I
  would take up next.

### 285.5 Status

CONSULTED: the discharging method, which does not apply for want of an embedding (285.1).
DECLARED: the 258-284 route dead, since the object it must exclude is consistent with
every derivable constraint and carries no (SC) information (285.2).
IDENTIFIED: the unexploited fact - hundreds of pairwise-intersecting odd cycle
transversals of size at most seven - and the sunflower lemma as the fitting tool, whose
threshold is not yet met (285.3, 285.4).
NOT PROVED: (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 285 consults general technique, finds
discharging inapplicable because our bridge need not embed in a surface, and declares the
route of 258 to 284 dead on the grounds that the blind component it must exclude is
consistent with every derivable constraint and carries no information from the hypothesis.
It re-occupies the ground of 250.3, 256.1 and 253.3 and identifies the sunflower lemma as
the fitting tool for the hundreds of pairwise-intersecting small transversals, with the
growth of that family as the concrete next task.


## 286. THE LOAD-BEARING COMPONENT

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. A direct answer to a direct question: which
single statement, if supplied, ends the proof.

### 286.1 THE ANSWER

     (L2**)  In a bridge B of a shallow cycle, SOME PAIR OF TERMINALS IS JOINED BY TWO
             INTERNALLY DISJOINT EVEN CONNECTING PATHS.

That is the load-bearing component. Everything else in the programme is either proved
outright or reduces to it.

### 286.2 The chain it holds up

  EG  <==  (H1*)   Every shallow cycle admits a strictly shortening move.
                   The ascent framework (F1)-(F7) of 209.1 is complete and
                   unconditional: mechanism, level = v_2(|C|), termination, start at a
                   shortest cycle, progress moves bounded, lateral moves non-recurrent,
                   no zero shifts. Given (H1*), the procedure terminates on a
                   power-of-two cycle and the conjecture follows.

  (H1*) <== (INT)  A bridge with an INTERIOR VERTEX cannot satisfy (SC).
                   The interior-free case is 211.3: such a bridge is a single cycle, and
                   two adjacent terminals on it give an ear of length 3 against
                   |P| > |C|/2 >= 6. (H1*) is separately proved for |C| > 2 sqrt(n)
                   (191.2), for n < 36 (193.3), for degenerate bridges (210.1) and for
                   bipartite bridges (205.2, 208.2).

  (INT) <== (L2**) A pair with two disjoint even connecting paths gives a cycle through
                   two terminals with BOTH ARCS EVEN, and 229.2 then contradicts (SC) -
                   part (a) forcing |O| = 0 mod 4 and part (b), via the Terminal-Cycle
                   Lemma 228.1, forcing |O| = 2 mod 4.

### 286.3 Its equivalent forms, all proved equivalent

  231.1  two disjoint paths from {x_1,y_1} to {x_2,y_2}, BOTH OF EVEN LENGTH - a
         parity-constrained Menger problem;
  250.3 + 252.1  some even connecting path whose interior is NOT an odd cycle
         transversal of B;
  254.1  implied by nu_odd(B) >= 2, i.e. by two vertex-disjoint odd cycles - verified on
         273 of 273 instances, and by 256.2 the same as two EDGE-disjoint ones;
  255.3  implied by an even b_i-b_j path inside B - V(Z) for a disjoint odd cycle Z,
         where 255.2's pigeonhole supplies a pair of terminals avoiding Z.

### 286.4 What rides on it that is NOT yet proved

One rider, and it should be named: 229.2 also needs a terminal OFF the chosen cycle and
reachable. 253.2 measured that this is automatic - in 321 of 321 instances where two
disjoint even paths existed, two could be chosen avoiding the third terminal, with zero
exceptions - and that measurement is legitimate, being a statement about the graph rather
than about (SC). But it is a measurement, not a proof.

  So strictly: EG follows from (L2**) TOGETHER WITH the escape clause, and the escape
  clause is verified but unproved.

### 286.5 Why it is hard, in one paragraph

(L2**) fails only in a very particular way. By 253.3 a failing pair has hundreds of even
connecting paths, no two internally disjoint - so the obstruction is not scarcity but a
Helly-type pairwise intersection. By 237.2 no parity invariant governs the count, ruling
out a counting-mod-2 proof. By 253.4 Menger has no parity-constrained analogue, ruling out
a min-max certificate. And by 250.3 the failure produces a bipartite graph, which is what
every subsequent attempt tried to exploit and what 285.2 finally judged insufficient.

### 286.6 Status

IDENTIFIED: (L2**) is the single load-bearing statement; the framework above it is
complete and the reductions to it are proved (286.1-286.3).
NAMED AS A RIDER: the escape clause of 229.2, verified on 321 instances but not proved
(286.4).
NOT PROVED: (L2**); hence (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 286 answers directly: the load-bearing
component is (L2**), that some pair of terminals of a bridge is joined by two internally
disjoint even connecting paths. The ascent framework above it is complete and
unconditional, the reduction of the conjecture to it is proved through (H1*) and (INT),
and four equivalent forms of it are established; one rider, the escape clause, is verified
on 321 instances but not proved.


## 287. THE COVERING-SPACE FRAME: (L2**) as a cycle disjoint from its deck translate

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. There IS a natural algebraic-topological
structure for (L2**), and it names the obstruction precisely. It does not, by itself,
supply a proof, and 287.5 says why.

### 287.1 The structure

Parity in B is a cohomology class. Let w in H^1(B; Z_2) be the cochain assigning 1 to
every edge; w evaluated on a cycle is its length mod 2, so

     w = 0   <==>   B is BIPARTITE ,

and in our case w =/= 0. The class w classifies a Z_2-COVERING SPACE, namely the
BIPARTITE DOUBLE COVER

     p : B~  ->  B ,   B~ = { (v, eps) : eps in Z_2 } ,  (u,eps) ~ (v, 1-eps) for uv in E,

with deck transformation tau(v,eps) = (v, 1-eps). B~ is CONNECTED exactly because w =/= 0,
i.e. because B is non-bipartite - which 230.1 guarantees.

A path of length l from u to v lifts to a path from (u,0) to (v, l mod 2). So

     EVEN u-v paths of B   <-->   (u,0)-(v,0) paths of B~ .

### 287.2 (L2**) TRANSLATED (PROVED)

  PROPOSITION. (L2**) holds for the pair (u,v) if and only if B~ contains a cycle through
  (u,0) and (v,0) that is DISJOINT FROM ITS DECK TRANSLATE tau(O~).
  Proof. Two internally disjoint even u-v paths lift to two internally disjoint
  (u,0)-(v,0) paths, whose union is a cycle O~ meeting each fibre p^{-1}(x) at most once,
  i.e. disjoint from tau(O~). Conversely a cycle O~ meeting each fibre at most once
  projects injectively, so p(O~) is a SIMPLE cycle of B through u and v whose two arcs
  lift to (u,0)-(v,0) paths and are therefore both EVEN. QED

  So the whole remaining difficulty is: FIND A CYCLE IN A Z_2-COVER THAT AVOIDS ITS OWN
  TRANSLATE. Failure of (L2**) says every cycle of B~ through (u,0) and (v,0) meets its
  translate - equivalently, every such cycle projects to a closed walk that repeats a
  vertex.

### 287.3 The homology decomposition

Since B~ is a connected double cover, |V(B~)| = 2|V(B)| and |E(B~)| = 2|E(B)|, so

     mu(B~)  =  2 mu(B) - 1 .

Over Q the deck action splits the cycle space into invariant and anti-invariant parts,

     H_1(B~; Q)  =  H_1(B; Q)  (+)  H_1(B; Q_w) ,

the second summand being homology with coefficients in the SIGN LOCAL SYSTEM defined by
w, of rank mu(B) - 1. That twisted summand is precisely the algebraic object that "sees"
parity: a cycle of B lifts to a cycle of B~ exactly when it is even, and the odd cycles
are what generate the twisted part.

  This is the natural home for parity-constrained path problems, and it explains in one
  line several facts the programme found empirically: why odd cycles control everything
  (254.1), why the bipartite double cover kept suggesting itself and kept failing to
  transfer disjointness (222.1's note), and why (SC) - an assertion about EVEN paths -
  is a statement about the FIBRE-PRESERVING part of B~.

### 287.4 What it illuminates

The obstruction is now nameable: failure of (L2**) is the statement that a certain
homology class of B~ has NO EMBEDDED representative disjoint from its translate. In
surface topology that kind of question is answered by the INTERSECTION FORM and Poincare
duality; the invariant is exactly the mod-2 self-intersection, which is what 222.1
identified as Brown's Z_4-quadratic refinement.

  So the covering-space frame and the quadratic-form frame of 222 are two views of ONE
  structure, and the programme has been circling it since 222 without saying so.

### 287.5 Why it does not close, stated plainly

A graph is a 1-COMPLEX. There is no Poincare duality, no surface, no intersection pairing
between 1-cycles beyond the combinatorial |D_1 cap D_2| of 222.1 - and 222 already
extracted everything that pairing gives, arriving at the bicycle bound and then at odd
cycle packing. The covering-space language reformulates (L2**) exactly but adds no new
invariant, because the only invariant available is the one already used.

  It WOULD add something if B carried an embedding in a surface, since then the twisted
  homology would have a genuine intersection form: this is precisely why 257.4's
  projective-planar branch and 285.1's discharging both wanted a surface, and why both
  stalled for want of one.

### 287.6 Status

PROVED here: (L2**) is equivalent to the existence, in the bipartite double cover, of a
cycle through the two lifted terminals disjoint from its deck translate (287.2); the
homology of that cover splits as H_1(B) plus a twisted summand of rank mu(B) - 1 (287.3).
IDENTIFIED: the covering-space frame and 222's quadratic-form frame are the same structure
seen twice (287.4).
NOT PROVED: (L2**). The frame adds no invariant beyond the combinatorial intersection
pairing already exhausted at 222, for want of a surface (287.5).

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 287 supplies the algebraic-topological
structure: parity is a class in H^1 classifying the bipartite double cover, and (L2**)
says exactly that some cycle in that cover avoids its own deck translate, with the
relevant algebra living in twisted homology of rank mu - 1. This unifies the covering
picture with the quadratic-form picture of 222, but adds no new invariant, since a graph
has no surface to carry an intersection form.


## 288. CHOOSING THE SURFACE: a degree of freedom never used

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 287.5 blamed the absence of a surface. But a
surface can be CHOSEN, and the choice is free. This section develops that and reaches an
obstruction that is computable, together with the reason it is not yet decisive.

### 288.1 The surface is available

Every graph embeds in some closed surface: fix a ROTATION SYSTEM - a cyclic ordering of
the edges at each vertex, together with a signature - and the embedding is determined.
Doing so for B gives B contained in a surface S, and the double cover B~ then embeds in
the corresponding double cover S~, on which the deck transformation tau acts as a FREE
INVOLUTION.

  On S~ there IS an intersection pairing on H_1, and the twisted summand of 287.3 inherits
  it. The apparatus 287.5 said was missing is therefore obtainable - at the cost of a
  choice.

### 288.2 THE OBSTRUCTION (PROVED)

  PROPOSITION. Let O~ be a cycle of B~ through (u,0) and (v,0). If the mod-2 intersection
  number O~ . tau(O~) computed in S~ is NON-ZERO, then O~ meets tau(O~), so by 287.2 that
  cycle does NOT witness (L2**).
  Proof. Disjoint 1-cycles have intersection number zero. QED

  And the number has a combinatorial meaning: O~ and tau(O~) meet exactly over the
  vertices where the projected closed walk p(O~) repeats itself, so

     O~ . tau(O~)  =  number of self-crossings of p(O~)   (mod 2) ,

  which vanishes for a SIMPLE cycle. So the invariant is a genuine obstruction: any class
  whose representatives all have odd self-intersection cannot witness (L2**).

### 288.3 THE DEGREE OF FREEDOM

The intersection form depends on the rotation system, but the STATEMENT (L2**) does not -
it is about disjointness of paths in the abstract graph. Hence:

     (L2**) MAY BE TESTED IN ANY EMBEDDING, AND ONE IS FREE TO CHOOSE THE MOST
     FAVOURABLE ONE.

  This is a degree of freedom the programme has never used. Every earlier attempt worked
  with B as a bare graph; 155's Mac Lane dichotomy and 257's projective-planar branch both
  treated embeddability as a PROPERTY of B to be established, rather than as a CHOICE to
  be exercised.

  Two natural choices suggest themselves. A MINIMUM-GENUS embedding minimises the twisted
  homology and hence the room for the obstruction to be non-zero. A MAXIMUM-GENUS
  embedding - every graph has one with mu(B)/2 handles, up to parity - makes the
  intersection form as non-degenerate as possible, which is what one wants when arguing
  that an isotropic class must exist.

### 288.4 What one would prove

In a surface of genus g the mod-2 intersection form on H_1 is non-degenerate of rank 2g.
A form of rank 2g over F_2 has isotropic subspaces of dimension g, so isotropic classes
are ABUNDANT - they are half the dimension. The task is then to show that some isotropic
class in the TWISTED summand is representable by an EMBEDDED circle passing through the
two lifted terminals.

  Representability is the hard half. Over Z_2 every class is representable by an embedded
  1-MANIFOLD, but that may be several disjoint circles rather than one, and one needs the
  circle to pass through two prescribed points. Those are exactly the questions the
  surface-topology literature answers with primitivity conditions, and they have not been
  applied here.

### 288.5 Honest assessment

This is a genuine new avenue, and the freedom of 288.3 is real and unused. But three
things must be checked before it is more than an avenue: that the maximum-genus embedding
can be chosen compatibly with the deck involution; that the twisted summand inherits a
non-degenerate form rather than a degenerate one; and that representability by a single
embedded circle through two marked points can be arranged. None is done here, and I am not
going to present the frame as though it were the argument.

### 288.6 Status

PROVED here: an embedding may be chosen, giving B~ inside a surface with tau a free
involution and an intersection pairing available (288.1); a non-zero mod-2 self-
intersection obstructs a cycle from witnessing (L2**), and that number equals the
self-crossing count of the projected walk (288.2).
IDENTIFIED: the freedom to choose the embedding, never used in the programme (288.3), and
the shape of what one would prove - an isotropic class in the twisted summand, represented
by an embedded circle through two marked points (288.4).
NOT PROVED: (L2**); the three checks of 288.5 are outstanding.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 288 observes that the surface 287.5 found
missing can simply be chosen: a rotation system embeds B, the double cover embeds in the
double surface with the deck map a free involution, and an intersection pairing becomes
available. A non-zero mod-2 self-intersection then obstructs a cycle from witnessing
(L2**). Since the statement is embedding-independent the embedding may be chosen
favourably - a freedom never used - and the task becomes finding an isotropic class in the
twisted homology represented by an embedded circle through two marked points.


## 289. THE ONE-FACE EMBEDDING: checks 1 and 2 both pass

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Two of the three checks of 288.5 are discharged
here, and they turn out to be discharged by the SAME embedding.

### 289.1 CHECK 1: EVERY GRAPH HAS AN EVEN EMBEDDING (PROVED)

For the deck involution of the double cover to extend to the surface, the class
w in H^1(B; Z_2) must extend to H^1(S; Z_2), which happens exactly when w vanishes on
every face boundary - that is, when EVERY FACE HAS EVEN LENGTH.

  LEMMA. Every connected graph has an embedding all of whose faces are even.
  Proof. Take any embedding. The face lengths sum to 2|E|, so the number of ODD faces is
  EVEN. Adding a handle joining two faces merges them into a single face whose length is
  the sum of the two. Pair the odd faces and add one handle to each pair: each pair merges
  into a face of even length, and no other face changes. QED

  So Check 1 of 288.5 passes unconditionally, at the cost of raising the genus.

### 289.2 CHECK 2: ONE-FACE EMBEDDINGS MAKE THE FORM NON-DEGENERATE (PROVED)

An embedding with a SINGLE face has, by Euler, |V| - |E| + 1 = 2 - 2g, i.e. 2g = mu(B),
so it exists only when mu is even; and then:

  (a) ITS SINGLE FACE HAS LENGTH 2|E|, WHICH IS EVEN. So a one-face embedding is
      automatically an EVEN embedding, and Check 1 comes free with it.
  (b) The face space has rank |F| - 1 = 0, so the natural map H_1(B; Z_2) -> H_1(S; Z_2)
      is an ISOMORPHISM, and the mod-2 intersection form of the surface pulls back to a
      NON-DEGENERATE form on the whole cycle space of B.

  Checks 1 and 2 are therefore discharged by the same object: a maximum-genus, one-face
  embedding. That is a pleasing convergence and it is exactly the "most favourable
  embedding" that 288.3's freedom was meant to buy.

### 289.3 When such an embedding exists

The maximum genus satisfies gamma_M(G) <= floor(mu/2), with equality precisely for
UPPER-EMBEDDABLE graphs, and an upper-embeddable graph with mu even has a one-face
embedding. Upper-embeddability is classical: XUONG's characterisation via the deficiency
of a spanning tree, and NEBESKY's equivalent criterion. Sufficient conditions in the
literature include 4-edge-connectivity.

  OUR B IS SUBCUBIC, hence at most 3-edge-connected, so the standard sufficient condition
  does NOT apply and upper-embeddability must be checked or worked around. Two outs are
  available and I flag both as unverified: if mu is ODD one settles for a two-face
  embedding, whose face space has rank 1 and whose form has a radical of dimension at most
  1; and if B is not upper-embeddable one takes the maximum genus actually attainable and
  accepts a radical of the corresponding dimension.

### 289.4 What now stands

With a one-face even embedding in hand:
  - B~ embeds in the double cover surface S~, on which tau is a FREE INVOLUTION (289.1);
  - H_1(B~; Z_2) carries a NON-DEGENERATE intersection form (289.2);
  - the twisted summand of 287.3, of rank mu(B) - 1, sits inside it;
  - by 288.2 a cycle witnessing (L2**) must be ISOTROPIC for that form, and isotropic
    classes are abundant, filling a subspace of half the dimension.

  The single remaining check is 288.5's third: that an isotropic class in the twisted
  summand is representable by ONE EMBEDDED CIRCLE through the two lifted terminals.

### 289.5 Status

PROVED here: every connected graph has an even embedding, obtained by adding one handle
per pair of odd faces, so the deck involution always extends (289.1); a one-face embedding
is automatically even and makes the pulled-back intersection form non-degenerate on the
whole cycle space (289.2).
FLAGGED: existence of a one-face embedding needs upper-embeddability, for which the
standard sufficient condition is 4-edge-connectivity and our B is subcubic (289.3).
NOT PROVED: representability of an isotropic twisted class by a single embedded circle
through two marked points; hence (L2**), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 289 discharges two of the three checks
left by 288: every graph has an even embedding, since odd faces come in pairs and a handle
merges two faces, so the deck involution always extends; and a one-face embedding is
automatically even while making the intersection form non-degenerate on the entire cycle
space. Both are delivered by a maximum-genus one-face embedding, whose existence requires
upper-embeddability - flagged, since the standard sufficient condition needs
4-edge-connectivity. What remains is representability by a single embedded circle.


## 290. CHECK 3 IS (L2**) ITSELF: the topological route reformulates but cannot advance

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Attempting the third check reveals that it is not
a check at all - it is the original statement in different words. This section says so and
closes the topological route honestly, keeping what it did produce.

### 290.1 THE IDENTIFICATION (PROVED)

287.2 proved: (L2**) holds for the pair (u,v) if and only if B~ contains a cycle through
(u,0) and (v,0) disjoint from its deck translate. 288.5's third check asked for an
isotropic class of the twisted summand REPRESENTABLE BY A SINGLE EMBEDDED CIRCLE THROUGH
THE TWO LIFTED TERMINALS. But an embedded circle of B~ through those two points, disjoint
from its translate, IS exactly the object 287.2 describes.

     CHECK 3  =  (L2**) .

  The surface apparatus therefore reformulates the problem exactly and advances it not at
  all. I record this rather than continuing to develop the frame.

### 290.2 WHY THIS WAS PREDICTABLE - a methodological point worth keeping

The intersection form supplies OBSTRUCTIONS: 288.2 says a class with odd self-intersection
CANNOT witness (L2**). But (L2**) is an EXISTENCE statement - it asks for a witness. An
