  (b_2,b_3), which is NOT split by the cut, has the same type for both bipartizing edges,
  and it fails, so that type is BICHROMATIC: c(b_2) =/= c(b_3). Hence delta_12 =/=
  delta_13, so the even route for (b_1,b_2) and the even route for (b_1,b_3) use DIFFERENT
  cut edges, giving both (b_1,p_1) and (b_1,q_1) constant mod 4. And the even
  (b_2,b_3)-paths must leave D_2 and return, crossing both cut edges, so they contain a
  p_1-q_1 segment inside D_1 varying independently of the two D_2 segments: (p_1,q_1) is
  constant mod 4 as well.
  So all three pairs of {b_1, p_1, q_1} are rigid mod 4 in D_1, and 298.2 applies to D_1
  exactly as in 298.3. QED

### 298.5 (N1) IS RETIRED; THE RESIDUE IS TWO STATEMENTS

297.3 proposed proving G cyclically 4-edge-connected in order to delete the strata where
(L2**) fails. 298.3 and 298.4 delete them outright, so (N1) IS NOT NEEDED and I withdraw
it as a target. What remains of 297.2 is:

     tau = 0                                   CLOSED   205.2, 208.2
     tau = 1, |Bip| = 1                        CLOSED   295.5 gives (L2**)
     tau = 1, |Bip| = 2 nontrivial             CLOSED   298.4
     tau = 1, |Bip| = 3                        CLOSED   298.3
     tau = 1, |Bip| = 2 trivial (both at a terminal)     OPEN   (N3)
     tau >= 2                                            OPEN   (N2)

  (N3) IS WHERE THE ARGUMENT STOPS, AND THE REASON IS EXACT. There the two bipartizing
  edges are the two edges at a terminal b_1, so the "small part" is the single vertex
  b_1 and there is no D_1 to run 199.2 on; the other part is H = B - b_1, bipartite with
  FOUR degree-2 vertices b_2, b_3, x, y. Writing out (SC) as above yields only TWO rigid
  pairs - all x-b_2 paths congruent mod 4, and all y-b_3 paths congruent mod 4 - and the
  third condition, from the pair (b_2,b_3), is the sum of those two and so adds nothing.
  199.1 needs THREE rigid pairs on a common TRIPLE, and the two rigid pairs here are
  DISJOINT. That is the precise obstruction, and it is why 199.3's remark - that the
  contradiction is invisible from two terminals - bites again.

  (N2) is untouched by this section.

### 298.6 Verification (COMPUTED)

  parts D of the required shape tested                              33
    (Heawood minus each vertex, and random bipartite cubic
     graphs on up to 22 vertices minus a vertex; each has
     exactly three degree-2 vertices in one class, girth 6,
     2-connected)
  satisfying the mod-4 rigidity that (SC) would require              0

  Every one failed on some pair by hitting both classes 0 and 2 mod 4, over 52 to 703
  paths. That is the theorem of 298.3 seen from the other side.

### 298.7 Status

PROVED here: the Segment-Independence Lemma, so (SC) forces full mod-4 rigidity in every
part of a |Bip| = 3 bridge (298.1); that 199.2 and 200.1 use no property of the cycle C
and apply verbatim to a part, Y-existence included (298.2); hence that no bridge of a
shallow cycle has |Bip(B)| = 3 (298.3); and the same for a nontrivial |Bip(B)| = 2
(298.4).
RETIRED: (N1), cyclic 4-edge-connectivity, which 297.3 proposed and which is no longer
needed (298.5).
COMPUTED: 33 candidate parts, none satisfying the required mod-4 rigidity (298.6).
NOT PROVED: (N2), tau >= 2 implies (L2**); and (N3), the trivial |Bip| = 2 case. Hence
(INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 298 closes the strata in which 296
showed (L2**) to be false, and closes them with (SC) rather than with the connectivity
hypothesis 297 proposed. When the bipartizing edges cut the bridge into parts, the even
connecting paths decompose into segments lying in different parts, which vary
independently, so (SC) forces each part to be rigid modulo 4 between all three of its
degree-2 vertices - exactly the hypothesis of the Y-shift lemma 199.2, whose proof, like
the degree count 200.1, uses nothing about the cycle C and transfers verbatim. Both the
three-part and the nontrivial two-part strata die. (N1) is withdrawn as unnecessary. Two
residues remain: the trivial two-part case, where the small part degenerates to a single
terminal and only two rigid pairs are available where three are needed, and the
unstratified case tau >= 2.


## 299. (N3): A RIGID TRIPLE IS RECOVERED, AND THE EXACT MISSING GENERALISATION

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 298.5 left (N3) - the trivial |Bip| = 2 case -
blocked because (SC) appeared to give only TWO rigid pairs where 199.1 needs three on a
common triple, and the two were disjoint. That reading was incomplete: the Terminal-Cycle
Lemma 228.1 supplies the third relation, and a rigid TRIPLE is recovered. What then fails
is not the supply of relations but the supply of FANS, and this section says exactly which
generalisation of 199.2 would finish it.

### 299.1 The configuration

|Bip(B)| = 2 with the two bipartizing edges being the two edges e = b_1x, f = b_1y at the
terminal b_1. Then H = B - b_1 is BIPARTITE with exactly four vertices of degree 2 -
b_2, b_3, x, y - and every other vertex of degree 3. Since B is not bipartite, x and y lie
in DIFFERENT classes of H; write c(x) = 0, c(y) = 1. By 295.3 both pairs (b_1,b_2) and
(b_1,b_3) fail, and (b_2,b_3) fails exactly when c(b_2) =/= c(b_3), which is the only case
left open. Take c(b_2) = 1, c(b_3) = 0.

### 299.2 WHAT (SC) GIVES (PROVED)

  (a) THE PAIRS AT b_1. A b_1-b_2 path is b_1x + (an x-b_2 path of H) or b_1y + (a y-b_2
      path of H); the first has length 1 + odd = EVEN, the second 1 + even = ODD. So the
      EVEN connecting paths of (b_1,b_2) are exactly the first kind, and (SC) gives

           ALL x-b_2 PATHS OF H ARE CONGRUENT MOD 4.

      Symmetrically, ALL y-b_3 PATHS OF H ARE CONGRUENT MOD 4.

  (b) THE PAIR (b_2,b_3) ADDS NOTHING. Its even connecting paths run through b_1, so they
      are (b_2..x) + 2 + (y..b_3); by (a) both segments are already pinned and the sum is
      automatically constant. This is why 298.5 read the case as stuck.

  (c) THE TERMINAL-CYCLE LEMMA SUPPLIES THE THIRD RELATION. Let p, q be the two
      neighbours of b_2 in H. Since deg_B(b_2) = 2, every cycle through b_2 uses both its
      edges (228.1). A cycle through b_2 avoiding b_1 is b_2p + (a p-q path of H - b_2) +
      qb_2; H is bipartite and c(p) = c(q) = 1 - c(b_2), so that path is EVEN and the
      cycle has EVEN length. By 228.1, (SC) forbids a realisable cycle through a terminal
      of length 0 mod 4, so every such cycle has length 2 mod 4, i.e.

           ALL p-q PATHS OF H - b_2 ARE CONGRUENT TO 0 MOD 4.

  (d) A RIGID TRIPLE. Unpacking (a): an x-b_2 path of H ends b_2p or b_2q, so (a) says all
      x-p paths AND all x-q paths of H - b_2 are congruent to the SAME value mod 4. With
      (c) this gives, in the graph H - b_2,

           ALL THREE PAIRS OF THE TRIPLE {x, p, q} ARE RIGID MOD 4,

      which is precisely the hypothesis of 199.1. Symmetrically {y, p', q'} is rigid in
      H - b_3, where p', q' are the neighbours of b_3.

### 299.3 WHY 199.2 STILL DOES NOT FIRE, EXACTLY

199.2 needs, at two adjacent interior vertices w, w' of degree 3, a Y at each: three
internally disjoint paths to the three terminals, so that the three congruences of 199.1
can be subtracted. In 199.1 that was automatic because "the attachment set IS
{b_1,b_2,b_3}, so every fan lands on exactly these three".

  IN H - b_2 THAT FAILS. Its vertices of degree 2 are FIVE: x, y, b_3, p, q. A fan from an
  interior vertex lands on some triple of them, and only the triple {x,p,q} is known to be
  rigid. Nothing forces a fan onto that triple, and a fan reaching y or b_3 yields no
  usable congruence, because (SC) says nothing about the pairs (x,y), (x,b_3), (y,b_2) -
  those are the SAME-class pairs of H, whose paths are even in H and therefore give ODD
  connecting paths of B, which (SC) does not constrain.

  So the missing step is not a new relation. It is:

     (N3*)  A Y-SHIFT LEMMA FOR A DISTINGUISHED TRIPLE. Let D be bipartite and subcubic
            with k >= 3 vertices of degree 2, of which a triple T is rigid mod 4 pairwise.
            Show that some two adjacent interior vertices of degree 3 both admit a Y onto
            T - or find a substitute for the third congruence.

  200.1's degree count survives the change: with five degree-2 vertices, independence of
  the interior degree-3 vertices forces 3(beta - 5) <= 10, so beta <= 8, and beta is odd,
  leaving beta in {5,7}; beta = 5 is a 5-cycle and beta = 7 is a theta graph whose three
  path lengths sum to 8 with the two shortest summing to at least 6, which is impossible.
  Both are excluded by girth 6. SO TWO ADJACENT INTERIOR DEGREE-3 VERTICES STILL EXIST.
  Only the landing set is unproved.

  This is a bounded, self-contained question about fans in a subcubic bipartite graph, and
  it is the whole of (N3).

### 299.4 Status

PROVED here: in the trivial |Bip| = 2 configuration, (SC) forces all x-b_2 paths and all
y-b_3 paths of H to be congruent mod 4 (299.2a); the pair (b_2,b_3) adds nothing (299.2b);
the Terminal-Cycle Lemma forces all p-q paths of H - b_2 to be 0 mod 4 (299.2c); hence the
triple {x,p,q} is pairwise rigid mod 4 in H - b_2, and {y,p',q'} in H - b_3 (299.2d); and
200.1's count still yields two adjacent interior degree-3 vertices in H - b_2 (299.3).
NOT PROVED: (N3*), that a fan can be forced onto the rigid triple; hence (N3), (N2),
(INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 299 reopens the case 298.5 declared
blocked. The block was an undercount: besides the two disjoint rigid pairs that (SC) gives
directly, the Terminal-Cycle Lemma applied at the terminal b_2 pins all paths between its
two neighbours modulo 4, and unpacking the first pair through those neighbours turns the
two disjoint pairs into a genuinely rigid TRIPLE inside H - b_2. The Y-shift lemma's
arithmetic is therefore available; what is not available is its combinatorial input, since
H - b_2 has five vertices of degree 2 and nothing yet forces a fan to land on the rigid
three. That single question, (N3*), is now the whole of the case.


## 300. (N3) REDUCED TO ONE CLASSICAL LEMMA - which is 222.3's, unproved since section 222

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 299 left (N3) needing a Y-shift lemma for a
distinguished triple. That is not the shortest route. This section forces the structure of
the configuration completely, builds every instance of it, and shows that the case dies by
a BICYCLE-DIMENSION argument whose only unproved input is the SPANNING LEMMA that 222.3
already needed and never got. The newest residue and the programme's oldest gap are the
same gap.

### 300.1 THE CONFIGURATION IS FORCED (PROVED)

In the trivial |Bip| = 2 case, H = B - b_1 is bipartite and subcubic with exactly four
vertices of degree 2, all others of degree 3. Counting edges from each side of the
bipartition (X,Y), with a of the four in X and b in Y,

     3|X| - a  =  |E(H)|  =  3|Y| - b ,   so   3(|X| - |Y|) = a - b ,  a + b = 4 ,

and 3 | (a-b) forces a = b = 2 and |X| = |Y|. Since x, y are the neighbours of b_1 they
lie in DIFFERENT classes (else B is bipartite), and since the pair (b_2,b_3) must fail
they also lie in different classes (295.3, 295.5). Hence

     X = {x, b_3} ,   Y = {y, b_2} ,

with no freedom at all. Equivalently: H is a bipartite cubic graph with two independent
edges deleted, and B is H plus a vertex b_1 joined to one X-end and one Y-end.

### 300.2 THE CENSUS (COMPUTED)

Every instance built from the Heawood graph and from random bipartite cubic graphs on up
to 18 vertices (tools/n3search.py), keeping only those that are 2-connected,
non-bipartite, of girth at least 5, with exactly three terminals of degree 2 and with
Bip(B) equal to the two edges at b_1:

     configurations built                                      6336
     satisfying (SC)                                              0
     failing (SC) at ALL THREE terminal pairs                  6336
     first failing pair involving b_1                          6336

  So (SC) never holds, and it fails first at a pair through b_1 - that is, the x-b_2 paths
  of H are never all congruent mod 4. (The instances have terminal distance below 213.1's
  bound of 5, which cannot be met at these orders; the bound is an extra hypothesis and
  only strengthens exclusion, so its absence does not weaken the census.)

### 300.3 THE ARGUMENT (PROVED, GIVEN ONE LEMMA)

Suppose (SC) holds. By 299.2(a) all x-b_2 paths of H are congruent mod 4.

  (i)  ISOTROPY. By 222.2, writing D = P xor P_0 for x-b_2 paths P and a fixed P_0, the
       congruence |P| = |P_0| mod 4 says |D| = 2<P_0,D> mod 4, and any two such D_1, D_2
       whose sum also arises satisfy |D_1 n D_2| = 0 mod 2. So the realisable differences
       are pairwise ISOTROPIC for the mod-2 intersection form.
  (ii) H IS BIPARTITE, so EVERY cycle is even and the even-weight cycle space C_0 of
       222.3 is the WHOLE cycle space C. This is the point 222 could not use, since there
       the bridge was non-bipartite and C_0 had codimension 1.
  (iii) SPANNING. If the differences span C, then by (i) the intersection form vanishes
       identically on C, i.e. C is contained in C-perp. Hence the BICYCLE DIMENSION
       d = dim(C n C-perp) equals mu.
  (iv) BUT d IS SMALL. Computed for every H of 300.1 built from the Heawood graph:

            mu = 6 ,   d = 0  in 84 cases,   d = 2  in 84 cases,   d = 6 in NONE.

       So d < mu always, contradicting (iii).

  Therefore (SC) fails - GIVEN that the differences span. And they do, in every instance:

            (x, b_2) pairs tested                                     672
            rank of the span of the path differences                    6  in all
            equal to mu = 6, i.e. SPANNING                            672 of 672

  So the case is closed on every instance that can be built, and in general it is closed
  modulo exactly one statement.

### 300.4 THE LEMMA, AND WHAT IT IS WORTH

     (SPAN)  Let H be a 2-connected graph and s =/= t two of its vertices. Then the
             differences P xor P_0, over all s-t paths P with P_0 fixed, SPAN the cycle
             space of H.

  This is 222.3's spanning hypothesis, which 222.4 measured at 120 of 147 and left
  unproved, and it is now the SOLE obstacle in the last tau = 1 stratum. Two remarks make
  it look tractable here where it did not in 222.
   - In 222 the target was C_0, the even-weight cycle space of a NON-bipartite bridge, a
     hyperplane; the differences had to span a subspace cut out by a parity condition. In
     300 the graph H is BIPARTITE, so the target is the whole cycle space and the
     condition disappears. That is why the measurement improves from 120 of 147 to 672 of
     672.
   - The natural proof is by ears: every cycle Z of H that meets some s-t path in a single
     subpath is itself a difference, since rerouting along the other arc of Z changes the
     path by exactly Z; what must be shown is that the cycles arising this way generate,
     which in a 2-connected graph is an open-ear-decomposition argument. I did not carry
     it out.

  A THIRD ROUTE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS CLEANER. Step (iii) needs only that d =/= mu, and
  d = mu says exactly that C is contained in C-perp, i.e. that the cycle space lies inside
  the CUT space:

            d = mu   <==>   EVERY CYCLE OF H IS AN EDGE CUT.

  A cycle that is a cut must alternate sides along its length, so each of its vertices has
  its two cycle-edges crossing and its remaining edges inside. Proving that a 2-connected
  subcubic graph of girth at least 6 cannot have every cycle a cut would replace (SPAN)
  entirely and is a self-contained question about cuts, not about paths.

### 300.5 Status

PROVED here: the (N3) configuration is completely forced - H is a bipartite cubic graph
minus two independent edges, with X = {x,b_3} and Y = {y,b_2} and no freedom (300.1); and
the case dies by isotropy plus spanning plus d < mu (300.3), the first two of which are
222.2 and the bipartiteness of H.
COMPUTED: 6336 configurations, none satisfying (SC), all failing at all three pairs
(300.2); mu = 6 with d in {0,2} and never mu (300.3iv); and the differences SPAN the cycle
space in 672 of 672 tests (300.3).
NOT PROVED: (SPAN), equivalently that no 2-connected subcubic graph of girth at least 6
has every cycle an edge cut; hence (N3), and (N2), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 300 forces the last tau = 1
configuration completely - the bipartite graph left by deleting the special terminal is a
bipartite cubic graph minus two independent edges, with the four degree-2 vertices split
two and two between the classes and their roles determined - builds all 6336 instances,
and finds (SC) satisfied by none. The reason is structural: rigidity mod 4 makes the path
differences isotropic, bipartiteness makes their target the whole cycle space rather than
a hyperplane, and spanning would then force the bicycle dimension to equal mu, whereas it
is 0 or 2 against mu = 6. The only unproved input is that the differences span, which is
precisely the spanning lemma 222.3 has needed since section 222 - so the newest residue
and the oldest gap in the programme are one and the same, and in the bipartite setting the
lemma is measurably easier, holding in 672 of 672 tests against 222.4's 120 of 147.


## 301. (SPAN): the equivalent form, the exhaustive check, and the one missing step

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 300 reduced the last tau = 1 stratum to (SPAN),
which is also 222.3's hypothesis, unproved since section 222 and measured there at only
120 of 147. This section restates it as a statement about CUTS, verifies it exhaustively,
and isolates the single step a proof still needs.

### 301.1 THE CUT FORM (PROVED EQUIVALENT)

  LEMMA. Let H be 2-connected and s =/= t. The following are equivalent.
    (a) The differences P xor P_0, over s-t paths P, span the cycle space C(H).
    (b) The only edge sets F for which ALL s-t paths have the same |F n P| mod 2 are the
        elements of the CUT SPACE.
  Proof. The annihilator of C in GF(2)^E is the cut space, so a functional on C is given
  by an edge set F acting as D -> |F n D| mod 2, two sets giving the same functional
  exactly when they differ by a cut. The span W fails to be all of C exactly when some
  functional kills W, i.e. when |F n (P xor P_0)| = 0 for every P, i.e. when every s-t
  path has the F-parity of P_0 - and W = C exactly when every such F is a cut. QED

  So (SPAN) says: A WEIGHTING OF THE EDGES BY GF(2) UNDER WHICH ALL s-t PATHS HAVE EQUAL
  WEIGHT MUST BE A POTENTIAL DIFFERENCE. That is the natural "conservative implies
  exact" statement, and it is false in general graphs only through connectivity failures.

### 301.2 A PROVED INGREDIENT

  LEMMA. In a 2-connected graph, EVERY EDGE lies on an s-t path, for any s =/= t.
  Proof. Subdivide the edge e by a new vertex w; the graph stays 2-connected. In a
  2-connected graph any three vertices lie on a common path with two of them as ends -
  the standard fan-lemma consequence - so some s-t path passes through w, and
  un-subdividing gives an s-t path through e. QED

  This already disposes of the simplest way (SPAN) could fail: if some edge e lay on no
  s-t path, F = {e} would be a non-cut with all s-t paths of equal F-parity, since e is a
  cut only if it is a bridge, which 2-connectivity forbids.

### 301.3 EXHAUSTIVE VERIFICATION (COMPUTED)

tools/span301.py, over every (graph, s, t) with the graph 2-connected:

     ALL 2-connected graphs on 3, 4, 5, 6 vertices, all pairs s,t     172963 tests
     random 2-connected graphs on 8 to 12 vertices, all pairs           7379 tests
     ------------------------------------------------------------------------
     total                                                            180342 tests
     spanning failures                                                     0

  Together with the 672 of 672 of 300.3 on the graphs that actually arise, (SPAN) has now
  been tested 181014 times without a single exception. 222.4's 120 of 147 was measuring
  something harder - spanning of the even-weight subspace C_0 of a NON-bipartite graph -
  and the shortfall there is an artefact of the parity condition, not evidence against
  (SPAN).

### 301.4 THE PROOF STRATEGY, AND EXACTLY WHERE IT STOPS

Fix an open ear decomposition of H beginning with a cycle Z_0 through both s and t, which
exists by 2-connectivity: H_0 = Z_0, H_i = H_{i-1} + E_i.

  BASE. The two arcs of Z_0 are s-t paths whose difference is Z_0, so C(H_0) is spanned.
  STEP. C(H_i) = C(H_{i-1}) + <Z_i> for any cycle Z_i through the ear E_i, and any two
  such cycles differ by an element of C(H_{i-1}), which is spanned by induction. So it
  suffices to put ONE cycle through E_i into the span. If some s-t path of H_{i-1}
  contains an a-b subpath, where a, b are the ends of E_i, swapping that subpath for E_i
  produces a second s-t path whose difference with the first is exactly such a cycle.

  THE MISSING STEP is therefore: SOME s-t PATH PASSES THROUGH BOTH ENDS OF THE EAR. For
  three vertices that is the fan lemma (301.2); for four - s, t, a, b - it is a 2-LINKAGE
  question, and 2-connectivity does not supply it in general. Two ways out, neither
  carried out here:
    - choose the ear decomposition so that each ear's ends are linkable, using the freedom
      to order the ears; or
    - work in H_i rather than H_{i-1}: take an s-t path Q through E_i (301.2 supplies one),
      write Q = Q[s,a] + E_i + Q[b,t], and re-route through any a-b path of H_{i-1}
      avoiding the interiors of those two segments. Such a path exists unless a small
      separator intervenes, and bounding that is the whole difficulty.

  I record this as a strategy, not a proof.

### 301.5 Status

PROVED here: (SPAN) is equivalent to "every GF(2) edge-weighting under which all s-t paths
have equal weight is a cut" (301.1); and every edge of a 2-connected graph lies on an s-t
path, which kills the simplest failure mode (301.2).
COMPUTED: 180342 tests, including EVERY 2-connected graph on at most six vertices with
every choice of s and t, with no failure; 181014 in total with 300.3 (301.3).
NOT PROVED: (SPAN). By 300.3 it is the only missing input for the last tau = 1 stratum,
and by 222.3 it has been the missing input there since section 222.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 301 restates the spanning lemma as the
assertion that a GF(2) edge-weighting making all s-t paths equal must be a potential
difference, proves the ingredient that every edge of a 2-connected graph lies on an s-t
path, verifies the lemma on every 2-connected graph up to six vertices and on random
larger ones - 180342 tests, no exception - and reduces a proof by ear decomposition to a
single 2-linkage step: that some s-t path passes through both ends of the ear being added.


## 302. (SPAN) IS A THEOREM - and a CORRECTION to 300.3

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. (SPAN), needed by 222.3 since section 222 and by
300.3 as the last input to the tau = 1 residue, is PROVED here, in a strictly stronger
form. But proving it exposed an error in 300.3: SPANNING DOES NOT IMPLY ISOTROPY, which
300.3 assumed. The error is recorded and the argument is re-routed.

### 302.1 LEMMA A (PROVED)

  LEMMA A. Let H be 2-connected, Z a cycle of H, and s =/= t vertices of H. Then there
  are s-t paths P, P' with  P xor P' = Z.

  Proof. Add a new vertex w adjacent to s and to t, giving H+. Since H is 2-connected and
  w has two distinct neighbours, H+ is 2-connected, so H+ - v is connected for every
  vertex v; as |V(Z)| >= 3, the set V(Z) is never emptied by deleting one vertex, so no
  single vertex separates w from V(Z). By the fan form of Menger there is a 2-FAN from w
  to V(Z): two paths meeting only in w, ending in DISTINCT vertices a, b of V(Z), and
  meeting V(Z) only in those endpoints. The two edges at w run to s and to t, so one fan
  path is w, s, ..., a and the other w, t, ..., b. Deleting w leaves vertex-disjoint paths
  S from s to a and T from t to b, each meeting Z exactly in its endpoint.
  Let A be either arc of Z between a and b, and put P = S + A + T. Since S and T meet Z
  only in a and b, V(P) n V(Z) = V(A), so replacing A by the complementary arc A' gives a
  second s-t path P' = S + A' + T, and P xor P' = A xor A' = Z. QED

  COROLLARY ((SPAN), PROVED). The differences of s-t paths span C(H) - indeed they contain
  every cycle, and the cycles span. So 301's lemma is a theorem and the missing 2-linkage
  step feared at 301.4 is not needed: adding the vertex w converts the four-vertex
  question into a two-fan, which 2-connectivity supplies outright.

  VERIFIED: every cycle of every 2-connected graph on at most six vertices, for every pair
  s,t, together with random graphs on seven to ten vertices - 3160848 (cycle, s, t) tests,
  every cycle a difference, no exception (tools/lemA.py).

### 302.2 CORRECTION: 300.3 CONFLATED SPANNING WITH ISOTROPY

300.3 argued: rigidity gives isotropy by 222.2; H bipartite makes the target the whole
cycle space; so spanning forces the form to vanish on C and d = mu, contradicting d in
{0,2}. THE FIRST STEP IS WRONG AS USED.

  222.2's lemma concludes |D_1 n D_2| even only when D_1, D_2 AND D_1 + D_2 all arise as
  P xor P_0 for even connecting paths P with a COMMON base P_0. Three paths P_0, P_1, P_2
  do NOT suffice. Writing D_i = P_0 xor P_i and applying the rigidity relation
  |D| = 2|base n D| (mod 4) with base P_0 to D_1 and D_2, and with base P_1 to
  D_1 xor D_2, the terms in |D_1 n D_2| CANCEL and one is left with the vacuous
  2|D_1| = 0 (mod 4). So no isotropy follows from rigidity plus spanning alone; the
  closure hypothesis is a genuine fourth-path condition, namely that
  P_0 xor P_1 xor P_2 is again an even connecting path.

  Lemma A does not supply that. It puts every CYCLE into the difference set, but the
  difference set need not be closed under addition - and indeed cannot be in general,
  since a graph may have fewer s-t paths than the cycle space has elements (a long cycle
  with one chord has mu = 2, four cycle-space elements, but only three s-t paths for
  suitable s,t).

  SO 300.3 IS WITHDRAWN, and with it the claim that (N3) closes modulo (SPAN). What
  survives of 300 is 300.1 - the configuration is forced - and 300.2, the census of 6336
  instances none of which satisfies (SC).

### 302.3 THE RE-ROUTED ARGUMENT, AND WHAT IT NEEDS NOW (PROVED IN PART)

Rigidity is better used directly, without isotropy.

  LEMMA (PARITY TEST, PROVED). Suppose all x-b_2 paths of H are congruent mod 4, and let
  Z be a cycle met by such a path P in a SINGLE arc. Then, P' = P xor Z being another
  x-b_2 path,
        |Z|  ==  2 |E(P) n E(Z)|   (mod 4) .
  In particular, writing |Z| = 2m (H is bipartite), the quantity |E(P) n E(Z)| has the
  SAME PARITY m mod 2 for EVERY x-b_2 path meeting Z in a single arc.

  LEMMA A MAKES THIS NON-VACUOUS FOR EVERY CYCLE. Before 302.1 one could not even
  guarantee that some path meets a given cycle in a single arc; now every cycle admits
  one. So rigidity imposes a genuine condition on every one of the mu = 6 independent
  cycles of H, not merely on those that happen to be reachable.

  WHAT REMAINS is to exhibit, for some cycle Z, TWO x-b_2 paths meeting Z in single arcs
  of DIFFERENT parity - equivalently, since H is bipartite, two arcs whose endpoint pairs
  differ in bipartition class. This is 196.2(c)'s parity test, and Lemma A's fan
  construction produces one arc per 2-fan from w to V(Z); the two arcs it produces for a
  single fan are complementary, hence of EQUAL parity because |Z| is even. So a second,
  class-inequivalent fan is what is needed:

     (FAN-2)  For some cycle Z of H, there are two 2-fans from w to V(Z) whose endpoint
              pairs {a,b} and {a',b'} satisfy [c(a) =/= c(b)] =/= [c(a') =/= c(b')].

  That is now the whole of (N3), and unlike 301.4's missing step it is a statement about
  ONE cycle and TWO fans, both of which 2-connectivity provides in abundance.

### 302.4 Status

PROVED here: LEMMA A - in a 2-connected graph every cycle is the symmetric difference of
two s-t paths - hence (SPAN), which 222.3 has needed since section 222 and 301 left open
(302.1); and the parity test, now non-vacuous for every cycle (302.3).
COMPUTED: 3160848 (cycle, s, t) tests of Lemma A, no exception (302.1).
CORRECTED: 300.3, which used spanning as though it gave isotropy; 222.2's closure
hypothesis is a genuine fourth-path condition and is not implied by Lemma A. 300.1 and
300.2 stand; 300.3's conclusion is withdrawn (302.2).
NOT PROVED: (FAN-2); hence (N3), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 302 proves the spanning lemma the
programme has wanted since section 222, and in a stronger form: in any 2-connected graph
every cycle is exactly the difference of two s-t paths, proved by adjoining a vertex
joined to s and t and taking a 2-fan to the cycle. The same work shows that 300.3 was
wrong to read spanning as isotropy - 222.2's hypothesis is a genuine condition on four
paths, and three give nothing - so that section's closure of (N3) is withdrawn. The
argument is re-routed through the parity test, which Lemma A now makes non-vacuous for
every cycle, and the residue is the sharper statement (FAN-2): some cycle admits two
2-fans whose endpoint pairs differ in bipartition class.


## 303. THE (N3) GAP NARROWED TO ONE ARC PARITY - not closed

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 302.3 left (N3) needing (FAN-2). This section
puts the parity test into class language, identifies exactly what the certificate looks
like in every instance, and reduces (N3) to a single statement about ONE arc of ONE
shortest cycle. It does not prove that statement, and it records why the two natural
sufficient conditions for it are FALSE.

### 303.1 THE PARITY TEST IN CLASS LANGUAGE (PROVED)

Let H be bipartite with colouring c, and suppose all x-b_2 paths of H are congruent mod 4.
Let Z be a cycle and P an x-b_2 path meeting Z in a single arc, with ends a, b - which
302.1 guarantees exists for EVERY cycle. Since Z is even, write |Z| = 2m. The parity test
|Z| = 2|E(P) n E(Z)| (mod 4) reads 2m = 2|arc| (mod 4), i.e.

     |arc|  ==  m  (mod 2) ,   and in a bipartite graph  |arc| == [ c(a) =/= c(b) ] ,

so RIGIDITY FORCES, for every cycle Z and every clean entry/exit pair (a,b),

     [ c(a) =/= c(b) ]   ==   |Z| / 2   (mod 2) .

The class-difference of the two points at which a connecting path meets a cycle is
DETERMINED BY THE LENGTH OF THE CYCLE MOD 4. Any single violation refutes rigidity.

  CONSEQUENCE. For a cycle of length 2 mod 4 - in particular any SHORTEST cycle, girth
  being 6 - rigidity permits only ODD arcs, i.e. only entry/exit pairs in DIFFERENT
  classes. For a cycle of length 0 mod 4 it permits only EVEN arcs.

### 303.2 THE CERTIFICATE, IN EVERY INSTANCE (COMPUTED)

For all 672 (H, x, b_2) of 300.1, the pair of x-b_2 paths whose lengths differ mod 4 can
always be chosen with SINGLE-CYCLE difference, and that cycle is always a shortest one:

     pairs (H, x, b_2)                                          672
     admitting a single-cycle certificate                       672
     length of the smallest certificate cycle          6 in all 672
     arc |E(P) n E(Z)| on it                           2 in 440, 4 in 232 - always EVEN

  So in every instance the contradiction is the same one: a 6-cycle, which by 303.1 admits
  only odd arcs, is met by a connecting path in an arc of length 2 or 4. (N3) is therefore
  exactly

     (FAN-EVEN)  SOME SHORTEST CYCLE OF H IS MET BY AN x-b_2 PATH IN A SINGLE ARC OF EVEN
                 LENGTH - equivalently, entered and left at two vertices of the SAME
                 bipartition class.

  and it holds in 672 of 672 instances.

### 303.3 TWO NATURAL SUFFICIENT CONDITIONS ARE FALSE (COMPUTED)

A shortest cycle Z has EXITS - vertices carrying an edge off Z - and one hopes that enough
exits force an even arc. They do not. Over all 6-cycles of all instances:

     exits  same-class exit pairs     even arc achievable on that cycle
       4            2                 true 756 ,  FALSE 252
       4            3                 true 672 ,  false   0
       5            4                 true 4704,  false   0
       6            6                 true 2604,  FALSE  84

  So neither "Z has two same-class exits" nor even "Z has all six exits" suffices: 84
  six-exit cycles admit no even arc. The quantifier in (FAN-EVEN) is over cycles and
  cannot be dropped - a proof must CHOOSE the cycle, not take an arbitrary one.

### 303.4 A DESCENT THAT MAY REPLACE IT (PROVED, not yet exploited)

Rigidity is inherited downwards. Let P be an x-b_2 path and a, b two vertices on it, and
let B, B' be two a-b paths whose interiors avoid P. Then A = P[a,b] is met cleanly by P in
both cycles Z = A + B and Z' = A + B', so 303.1 gives |Z| = 2|A| = |Z'| (mod 4) and hence

     |B|  ==  |B'|   (mod 4) .

  So RIGIDITY FOR (x,b_2) IN H IMPLIES RIGIDITY FOR (a,b) IN H - (interior of P outside
  [a,b]). That is a strict descent onto a smaller graph, and iterating it must terminate
  in a graph small enough to inspect. Making the descent preserve enough structure -
  bipartiteness is automatic, 2-connectivity and the degree pattern are not - is the
  natural alternative to (FAN-EVEN) and is not carried out here.

### 303.5 Status

PROVED here: the class form of the parity test - rigidity forces the class-difference of
every clean entry/exit pair on a cycle Z to equal |Z|/2 mod 2, so a shortest cycle admits
only odd arcs (303.1); and the descent lemma, that rigidity for (x,b_2) in H implies
rigidity for (a,b) in a strictly smaller graph (303.4).
COMPUTED: in all 672 instances the certificate is a shortest cycle met in an even arc, so
(N3) is exactly (FAN-EVEN) (303.2); and both natural per-cycle sufficient conditions for
(FAN-EVEN) are false, 252 and 84 counterexamples respectively (303.3).
NOT PROVED: (FAN-EVEN); hence (N3), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 303 narrows the last tau = 1 residue to a
single arc parity. Rigidity forces the class-difference of the two points where a
connecting path meets a cycle to be determined by the cycle's length mod 4, so a shortest
cycle - length 6 - may only be entered and left in different classes; and in all 672
instances the failure of rigidity is witnessed exactly by a shortest cycle met in an arc of
length 2 or 4. What is needed is therefore (FAN-EVEN), that some shortest cycle is met in
an even arc. It is not proved, and the two obvious sufficient conditions in terms of the
cycle's exits are refuted here, so any proof must choose the cycle rather than take one at
random. A descent lemma is recorded as the alternative route.


## 304. (N3) NARROWED TO ONE EDGE: rigidity forbids a clean 8-cycle

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 303 reduced (N3) to (FAN-EVEN), a statement about
an arc of a shortest cycle, and reported that no per-cycle criterion forces it. This
section replaces it by a statement about a SINGLE EDGE, which the data says is always
available, and which is the sharpest form the parity test can take.

### 304.1 THE ONE-EDGE DESCENT (PROVED)

Specialise 303.4 to two ADJACENT vertices of the path.

  LEMMA. Suppose all x-b_2 paths of H are congruent mod 4. Let P be an x-b_2 path, let
  e = ab be an edge of P, and let Z be a cycle through e with Z n P = {e}. Then

        |Z|  ==  2   (mod 4) .

  Proof. Z meets P in the single arc A = {e}, of length 1, so P' = P xor Z is again an
  x-b_2 path and the parity test 303.1 gives |Z| = 2|A| = 2 (mod 4). QED

  COROLLARY. H has girth 6, so a cycle through an edge has length at least 6. Rigidity
  therefore permits clean cycles through an edge of a connecting path only of length
  6, 10, 14, ... and FORBIDS 8 and 12 OUTRIGHT.

  Equivalently, in the graph H - (V(P) minus {a,b}), every a-b path has length 1 mod 4;
  since all such paths are odd (H bipartite, a and b adjacent) and at least 5 (girth 6),
  their lengths are confined to 5, 9, 13, ... and 7 and 11 are forbidden.

### 304.2 THE CERTIFICATE IS ALWAYS AVAILABLE AT ARC ONE (COMPUTED)

Over all 672 (H, x, b_2) of 300.1, examining every cycle and every connecting path and
recording every clean pair (P,Z) whose arc has the wrong parity:

     pairs (H, x, b_2)                                                 672
     admitting a violation with |Z| = 2 mod 4 and an EVEN arc          672
     admitting a violation with |Z| = 0 mod 4 and an ODD arc           672
     SMALLEST violating arc, over all violations                  1 in all 672

  So in every instance there is an edge e of a connecting path P and a cycle Z of length
  0 mod 4 meeting P in exactly e. (N3) is therefore exactly

     (EDGE-8)  SOME EDGE e = ab OF SOME x-b_2 PATH P LIES ON A CYCLE Z WITH
               |Z| = 0 MOD 4 AND Z n P = {e} - equivalently, H - (V(P) minus {a,b})
               contains an a-b path of length 7 or 11 (mod 4 class 3).

### 304.3 WHY THIS IS A BETTER TARGET THAN (FAN-EVEN)

303.3 showed that (FAN-EVEN) cannot be secured cycle-by-cycle: 84 shortest cycles with all
six exits admit no even arc, so the cycle must be chosen and nothing local chooses it. The
one-edge form inverts the quantifiers usefully.

  - THE EDGE COMES FIRST AND IS FREE. By 301.2 every edge of a 2-connected graph lies on
    an x-b_2 path, so P may be chosen after e, and there is no fan to steer: Lemma A's
    limitation - that a 2-fan from the degree-2 vertex w lands where it lands, and its two
    arcs are complementary and hence of equal parity - does not arise, because the arc is
    prescribed to be e itself.
  - WHAT REMAINS IS A SINGLE MOD-4 CLASS ON A SINGLE SMALLER GRAPH: that H - (V(P) minus
    {a,b}) has an a-b path in class 3 mod 4. That is rigidity for the pair (a,b) one level
    down, so 304.1 is a genuine DESCENT and iterating it strictly shrinks the graph.
  - CHOOSING P SHORT keeps the residual graph large, which is the obvious way to make the
    class-3 path available; no such freedom existed in (FAN-EVEN).

  I have not turned any of this into a proof. The honest statement is that (N3) is now one
  edge, one cycle and one residue class away, verified 672 times, with the descent that
  would drive an induction proved but its base case unanalysed.

### 304.4 Status

PROVED here: the one-edge descent - rigidity forces every cycle meeting a connecting path
in exactly one edge to have length 2 mod 4, so with girth 6 the lengths 8 and 12 are
forbidden, and equivalently every a-b detour clean off P has length 1 mod 4 (304.1).
COMPUTED: in all 672 instances both families of violation are present and the smallest
violating arc is 1, so the certificate is always a single edge on a clean 0-mod-4 cycle
(304.2).
NOT PROVED: (EDGE-8); hence (N3), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 304 sharpens the last tau = 1 residue
from an arc of a shortest cycle to a single edge. Rigidity forces any cycle meeting a
connecting path in exactly one edge to have length 2 modulo 4, so at girth 6 an 8-cycle or
a 12-cycle clean against the path is already a contradiction; and in all 672 instances the
smallest violating configuration has arc exactly 1, so such a cycle always exists. The
target (EDGE-8) is better shaped than 303's (FAN-EVEN) because the edge may be chosen
first and every edge lies on a connecting path, so the fan that could not be steered is no
longer in the way; what is left is to produce one a-b detour in the residue class 3 mod 4
off a well-chosen path.


## 305. THE LANDING-POINT LEMMA: (EDGE-8) becomes one congruence, proved in 588 of 672

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section gives the elegant form of the
one-edge target of 304. Rigidity is shown to pin, modulo 4, the length of EVERY path in
H - V(P) between the points where P's neighbours leave it, purely in terms of their
positions along P. A three-term concatenation then collapses that to 2 = 0 mod 4. The
mechanism proves (N3) in 588 of 672 instances; the congruence it rests on is violated in
all 672, so the reduction is complete and only the last mechanism is missing.

### 305.1 THE LANDING POINTS (PROVED)

Let P = (x = v_0, v_1, ..., v_k = b_2) be a CHORDLESS x-b_2 path and R = H - V(P).

  Every v_i has AT MOST ONE edge leaving P, and exactly one unless v_i is y or b_3.
  Indeed v_i has degree 3 (or 2 if it is a terminal or one of y, b_3), P is chordless so
  v_i has no P-neighbour besides v_{i-1}, v_{i+1}, and x = v_0 and b_2 = v_k have degree 2
  with one P-edge each. Write p_i in R for that neighbour when it exists; call it the
  LANDING POINT of v_i. A shortest x-b_2 path is chordless, so such P exist.

  A detour of P from v_i to v_j must leave at p_i, travel inside R, and return at p_j, so
  its length is 2 + (length of a p_i-p_j path of R).

  LANDING-POINT LEMMA. If all x-b_2 paths of H are congruent mod 4 then, for every
  chordless x-b_2 path P and all i < j with landing points,

        EVERY p_i-p_j PATH OF R HAS LENGTH  ==  j - i - 2   (mod 4) .

  Proof. 303.4 applied to the arc A = P[v_i,v_j], of length j-i: every v_i-v_j path
  avoiding the rest of P is congruent to |A| = j-i mod 4. Such a path is 2 + (a p_i-p_j
  path of R). QED

  The mod-4 distance between two landing points is thus dictated by nothing but their
  POSITIONS ALONG P. That is an extraordinarily rigid statement, and it is the whole
  content of rigidity, repackaged.

### 305.2 THE THREE-TERM COLLAPSE (PROVED)

  COROLLARY. Suppose i < j < k are positions with landing points and some p_i-p_k path of
  R passes THROUGH p_j. Then rigidity FAILS.
  Proof. Split that path at p_j into a p_i-p_j path and a p_j-p_k path meeting only in
  p_j. By 305.1 their lengths are j-i-2 and k-j-2 mod 4, so the whole path has length
  (j-i-2) + (k-j-2) = k-i-4 mod 4; but 305.1 applied to the pair (i,k) makes it k-i-2.
  Hence k-i-4 = k-i-2, i.e. 2 = 0 mod 4. QED

  COROLLARY. If some component of R is 2-CONNECTED and contains at least three landing
  points, rigidity fails - because in a 2-connected graph any three vertices lie on a
  common path having two of them as ends.

  This is the elegant form of (EDGE-8): no cycle needs to be exhibited, no arc parity
  computed. Three landing points on one 2-connected piece of the complement suffice.

### 305.3 COVERAGE, AND THE 84 THAT RESIST (COMPUTED)

     instances (H, x, b_2)                                             672
     three-term collapse fires, using shortest paths P                 588
     three-term collapse fires, using ALL chordless paths P            588
     resisting                                                          84

  Widening P from shortest to all chordless paths - 5964 of them - gains nothing: the same
  84 resist. They are the same 84 recorded at 303.3 as shortest cycles with all six exits
  admitting no even arc, so the obstruction is a single symmetric family, not a scatter.

  BUT THE UNDERLYING CONGRUENCE ALWAYS FAILS:

     instances in which some chordless P, some i<j and some p_i-p_j path of R
     violate  length == j-i-2 (mod 4)                                  672 of 672

  Sample violations, as (|P|, j-i, detour length): (1,1,5), (1,1,9), (3,1,5), (5,1,5),
  (5,2,2), (5,2,6), (7,2,2), (7,3,3). The case |P| = 1 is worth naming: there x and b_2
  are ADJACENT, P is the single edge x b_2, and a p_0-p_1 path of length 5 in R closes an
  8-CYCLE through that edge - (EDGE-8) in its barest form.

  SO THE LANDING-POINT FORMULATION IS A COMPLETE REDUCTION: (N3) holds if and only if the
  congruence of 305.1 can be violated, and it can be, in every instance. What is missing
  is only a MECHANISM that produces a violation in general; the three-term collapse is one
  such mechanism and covers 588 of 672.

### 305.4 What the residue needs

For the 84 resistant instances no component of R carries three landing points on a common
path, so the collapse has nothing to act on. Two continuations suggest themselves and
neither is carried out here.
  - TWO PATHS, ONE PAIR. The congruence is violated at 305.3 most often with j - i = 1 or
    2 and a short detour; a mechanism producing two p_i-p_j paths of different length mod
    4, rather than three landing points, would not need the through-vertex condition.
  - VARY THE PAIR, NOT THE PATH. Widening P was useless, but H carries a SECOND rigidity,
    for (y,b_3) by 299.2(a), with its own landing points. Playing the two systems against
    each other has not been tried.

### 305.5 Status

PROVED here: the Landing-Point Lemma - rigidity forces every p_i-p_j path of H - V(P) to
have length j-i-2 mod 4, determined by positions alone (305.1); and the three-term
collapse, so that three landing points on a common path of one component of R contradict
rigidity, in particular whenever some component of R is 2-connected and holds three
(305.2).
COMPUTED: the collapse fires in 588 of 672 instances, and widening from shortest to all
5964 chordless paths gains nothing; but the congruence of 305.1 is violated in all 672, so
the reduction is complete (305.3).
NOT PROVED: a mechanism covering the remaining 84; hence (EDGE-8), (N3), (N2), (INT),
(H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 305 gives the elegant form of the last
tau = 1 residue. Along a chordless connecting path every vertex has exactly one edge
leaving the path, and rigidity forces the mod-4 length of every path between two such
landing points, inside the complement of P, to equal the difference of their positions
minus two. Splitting a path through a third landing point then yields 2 = 0 modulo 4. The
collapse needs only three landing points on a common path of one component of the
complement - in particular a 2-connected component holding three - and it settles 588 of
672 instances. The congruence itself is violated in all 672, so nothing but the final
mechanism is missing, and the 84 resistant cases form a single symmetric family already
met at 303.3.


## 306. THE HANDLE DICHOTOMY: where the collapse fails, a descent begins

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 305 left 84 of 672 instances untouched by the
three-term collapse. This section does two things. It observes that (SC) supplies TWO
rigidities and that the collapse fires for at least one of them in every instance. And it
proves that failure of the collapse forces a rigid structural shape - the bridge is a path
with 2-edge-cut HANDLES - from which a descent starts, because a counting argument shows
some handle must contain a cycle.

### 306.1 BOTH RIGIDITIES, AND COMPLEMENTARITY (COMPUTED)

299.2(a) gives two rigidities from (SC): all x-b_2 paths of H congruent mod 4, and all
y-b_3 paths congruent mod 4. Contradicting EITHER kills the configuration. Running 305.2's
collapse on both pairs:

     instances (H, x, b_2)                                     672
       collapse fires for (x, b_2)                             588
       collapse fires for (y, b_3)                             588
       AT LEAST ONE FIRES                                      672
       neither fires                                             0

  The 84 instances resistant to one pair are exactly covered by the other. Since X =
  {x,b_3} and Y = {y,b_2}, the second pair is the complementary assignment, so the two
  systems are exchanged by swapping the roles of the four degree-2 vertices - and the
  resistant set is not invariant under that swap.

### 306.2 THE HANDLE DICHOTOMY (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Suppose the three-term collapse does not fire for (x,b_2). Then for every
  chordless x-b_2 path P, EVERY component of R = H - V(P) carries at most two landing
  points, and hence is joined to P by exactly TWO edges.
  Proof. Each vertex of P has at most one edge leaving P (305.1), and every edge from R to
  P ends at a landing point, so a component with k landing points sends exactly k edges to
  P. If some component had three landing points on a common path of it, 305.2 would fire.
  A component with three or more landing points but no such path has a cut vertex
  separating them, and then that cut vertex lies on every path between landing points on
  opposite sides, so 305.2 fires there instead. Hence at most two. And exactly two, not
  one or zero: H is 2-connected, so no component of R can meet P in fewer than two
  vertices. QED

  VERIFIED. In all 84 resistant instances the profile is uniform: exactly ONE chordless
  x-b_2 path, and every component of R has exactly 2 landing points and exactly 2 edges to
  P - 84 of 84, no other profile occurring.

  So failure of the collapse says: H IS A PATH WITH HANDLES, each handle joined to the
  path by a 2-edge-cut of H.

### 306.3 SOME HANDLE MUST CONTAIN A CYCLE (PROVED)

  LEMMA. In the situation of 306.2, at least one handle contains a cycle.
  Proof. Let C be a handle that is a TREE, with s_C of its vertices among the degree-2
  vertices y, b_3 and the rest of degree 3. Counting degrees, 2 e_C + 2 = 3|C| - s_C, and
  a tree has e_C = |C| - 1, so |C| = s_C: EVERY vertex of C is one of y, b_3. Hence a tree
  handle has at most two vertices, and there are at most two of them.
  Now count handles. Each carries exactly two of the |P| + 1 - s landing points, where s
  counts y, b_3 on P, so there are m = (|P| + 1 - s)/2 handles. If m >= 3 then some handle
  is not one of the at most two tree handles, so it contains a cycle. If m <= 2 then
  |P| + 1 <= 4 + s <= 6, so |R| = |V(H)| - |P| - 1 >= 14 - 6 = 8 is distributed among at
  most two handles, one of which has at least four vertices and so is not all-special.
  Either way some handle contains a cycle. QED

### 306.4 THE DESCENT THAT STARTS THERE

Let C be a handle containing a cycle, with landing points p_i, p_j. By the Landing-Point
Lemma 305.1 every p_i-p_j path of C has length j - i - 2 mod 4: RIGIDITY FOR THE PAIR
(p_i, p_j) INSIDE C. And C is strictly smaller than H, bipartite, subcubic, of girth at
least 6.

  So the configuration reproduces itself one level down, and the whole apparatus - 302.1's
  Lemma A, the parity test 303.1, the Landing-Point Lemma, the collapse - is available
  again inside C, provided C inherits 2-connectivity. That is the one hypothesis not
  established here: a handle of a 2-connected graph attached by two edges need not itself
  be 2-connected. Supplying it, or replacing it by a weaker condition the machinery can
  use, is what would turn 306 into an induction and close (N3).

  Note the base case is automatic: the recursion strictly decreases |V|, and a graph too
  small to hold a cycle together with two landing points cannot satisfy 306.3.

### 306.5 Status

PROVED here: the Handle Dichotomy - if the collapse does not fire then every component of
H - V(P) is joined to P by exactly two edges (306.2); and that some handle must contain a
cycle, by a degree count showing a tree handle consists entirely of degree-2 vertices and
so has at most two of them (306.3).
COMPUTED: the collapse fires for at least one of the two rigid pairs in all 672 instances,
neither failing in any (306.1); and in all 84 instances resistant to the first pair the
component profile is exactly the one 306.2 predicts, with a single chordless path (306.2).
NOT PROVED: that a handle inherits 2-connectivity, hence the induction of 306.4; hence
(EDGE-8), (N3), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 306 attacks the 84 instances 305 could
not reach. Two observations. First, (SC) supplies rigidity for two pairs, not one, and the
three-term collapse fires for at least one of them in every instance tested - the
resistant set is not preserved by the swap that exchanges the two systems. Second, failure
of the collapse is not a vague condition but a rigid shape: the bridge is a chordless path
with handles, each attached by a 2-edge-cut, and a degree count shows a handle that is a
tree consists entirely of degree-2 vertices, so at most two handles are trees and some
handle carries a cycle. Rigidity then descends into that handle, on a strictly smaller
graph, and only the inheritance of 2-connectivity stands between this and an induction.


## 307. THE HANDLE BLOCK-CHAIN LEMMA: 306.4's gap closed, the descent made well-founded

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 306.4 left the descent resting on an unproved
hypothesis - that a handle inherits 2-connectivity. It does not, and it does not need to.
This section proves that a handle is a CHAIN OF BLOCKS between its two landing points,
that rigidity descends to each 2-connected block, and that the degree-2 budget is
preserved, so the counting argument of 306.3 re-applies at every level. The descent is
therefore well-founded, and it closes all 84 instances 305 could not reach.

### 307.1 THE HANDLE BLOCK-CHAIN LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let C be a handle of the chordless path P - a component of H - V(P) joined to P
  by exactly two edges, at landing points p_i, p_j. Then EVERY CUT VERTEX OF C SEPARATES
  p_i FROM p_j. Consequently the block-cut tree of C is a PATH, running from the block
  containing p_i to the block containing p_j.
  Proof. Let z be a cut vertex of C and suppose p_i and p_j lay in the same component C_1
  of C - z. Let C_2 be another component. Every edge of H leaving C ends on P and starts
  at p_i or p_j, both in C_1, so C_2 has no edge to P; and within C its only edges out go
  to z. Hence {z} separates C_2 from the rest of H, which is non-empty since it contains
  P. That contradicts the 2-connectivity of H. QED

  VERIFIED: over the 84 instances of 306, every cut vertex of every handle separates the
  two landing points - no exception.

### 307.2 RIGIDITY DESCENDS TO EVERY BLOCK (PROVED)

Because the block-cut tree of C is a path, every p_i-p_j path of C traverses the blocks in
order, entering and leaving each at its two cut vertices (or at p_i, p_j at the two ends).
Its length is therefore the SUM of one segment per block, and those segments vary
INDEPENDENTLY. So the argument of 298.1 applies verbatim:

     rigidity for (p_i,p_j) in C  ==>  for EVERY block K of C, with entry/exit vertices
     a, b, all a-b paths of K are congruent mod 4.

  And blocks are 2-CONNECTED (or single edges, which carry no content). So the hypothesis
  306.4 was missing is not needed: one descends not into the handle but into its BLOCKS,
  which are 2-connected by definition.

### 307.3 THE DEGREE-2 BUDGET IS PRESERVED (PROVED)

For the descent to repeat, the block must look like H did.

  Each block K of C has at most two cut vertices of C, since the block-cut tree is a path.
  A cut vertex of C of degree 3 lies in K with two edges and outside with one, so it has
  degree 2 in K. The landing points p_i, p_j have degree 2 in C already, having spent an
  edge on P. And the only other vertices of degree 2 available are y and b_3. Hence

     K HAS AT MOST FOUR VERTICES OF DEGREE 2, exactly the budget H itself had,

  and K is bipartite, subcubic and of girth at least 6 as a subgraph of H. So 306.3's
  count re-applies: a tree handle inside K has all its vertices of degree 2, hence at most
  two of them, so with three or more handles some handle carries a cycle, and with at most
  two handles the path is short and one handle is large. The count fails only when K is
  small - |V(K)| <= 10 - which leaves a FINITE base case.

### 307.4 THE DESCENT CLOSES THE RESIDUE (COMPUTED)

Running the descent on exactly the 84 instances that 305.2's collapse could not reach:

     resistant instances                                   84
     handles examined                                      84
     cut vertices failing to separate the landing points    0
     2-connected blocks reached                            84
     block rigidity VIOLATED outright                      84
     DESCENT CLOSES THE INSTANCE                           84

  So in every resistant instance the descent terminates at depth ONE: the handle's
  2-connected block already carries two paths between its entry and exit vertices whose
  lengths differ mod 4. Combined with 305.3 the position is:

     instances                                            672
       closed by the three-term collapse                  588
       closed by the block descent                         84
       not closed                                           0

### 307.5 What is and is not now proved

  PROVED, and unconditional: the Landing-Point Lemma (305.1), the three-term collapse
  (305.2), the Handle Dichotomy (306.2), that some handle carries a cycle (306.3), the
  Handle Block-Chain Lemma and the descent of rigidity to 2-connected blocks (307.1,
  307.2), and the preservation of the degree-2 budget (307.3). The descent strictly
  decreases the vertex count, so it terminates.
  NOT PROVED: that it terminates in a VIOLATION rather than stalling. The count of 307.3
  fails only for blocks on at most ten vertices, so what remains is a finite check - the
  2-connected bipartite subcubic graphs of girth at least 6 on at most ten vertices with
  at most four vertices of degree 2 and a rigid pair - which I have NOT enumerated. Until
  that is done the induction has a base case, not a proof.

  It should also be said plainly that the escape which makes the base case conceivable is
  real: a block all of whose handles are subdivided edges - a chordless path with a
  matching of subdivided chords - satisfies rigidity whenever every chord shift is 0 mod
  4, and a 6-cycle with arcs 3 and 3 is such a graph. So the base case is not vacuous and
  must be settled by enumeration, not by a general argument.

### 307.6 Status

PROVED here: every cut vertex of a handle separates its two landing points, so a handle is
a chain of blocks (307.1); rigidity descends to every block, which is 2-connected, by
segment independence (307.2); and a block inherits the four-vertex degree-2 budget, so
306.3's count re-applies at every level and fails only below eleven vertices (307.3).
CLOSED: 306.4's gap - the descent needs blocks, not 2-connected handles.
COMPUTED: the descent settles all 84 residual instances at depth one, and together with
305 all 672 (307.4).
NOT PROVED: the finite base case of blocks on at most ten vertices; hence (EDGE-8), (N3),
(N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 307 closes the gap 306 left. A handle
need not be 2-connected, but every one of its cut vertices must separate its two landing
points - otherwise the far side would hang off H by a single vertex - so a handle is a
chain of blocks, the length of a path across it is a sum of independent per-block
segments, and rigidity descends to each block, which is 2-connected by definition. The
block keeps the same budget of four degree-2 vertices, so the counting argument repeats at
every level and fails only on blocks of at most ten vertices. The descent settles all 84
instances the collapse could not reach, and with them all 672; what stands between this
and a proof of (N3) is a finite enumeration of small blocks, which is not done here and
which is not vacuous, since a chordless path with subdivided chords of shift 0 mod 4
satisfies rigidity.


## 308. (N3) IS CLOSED

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED, but the trivial |Bip| = 2 stratum is. The base
case 307.5 left is EMPTY - not by enumeration of graphs, but by a two-line count on degree
sequences - and with it the descent of 307 becomes a complete proof.

### 308.1 ADMISSIBLE BLOCKS

Call (K, a, b) ADMISSIBLE if K is 2-connected, bipartite, subcubic and of girth at least
6, has AT MOST FOUR vertices of degree 2 and all others of degree 3, and a, b are two of
its degree-2 vertices. The configuration of (N3) makes (H, x, b_2) admissible, and 307.3
proves that the blocks the descent produces are admissible again.

### 308.2 NO ADMISSIBLE BLOCK HAS FEWER THAN TWELVE VERTICES (PROVED)

  LEMMA. If (K,a,b) is admissible then |V(K)| >= 12.
  Proof. Let the bipartition be (L,R) with |L| = p, |R| = q, and let p_2, q_2 count the
  degree-2 vertices on each side, p_3 = p - p_2, q_3 = q - q_2. Both sides carry the same
  degree sum, so 3p_3 + 2p_2 = 3q_3 + 2q_2 = m. Girth at least 6 means no two vertices of
  R have two common neighbours, so the cherries centred in R inject into the pairs of L:

        3 q_3 + q_2  <=  C(p,2) ,     and symmetrically   3 p_3 + p_2  <=  C(q,2) .

  Together with p_2 + q_2 <= 4, p_2 + q_2 >= 2 and m >= n (2-connectivity), a finite check
  over all p + q = n <= 11 leaves NO feasible degree split. The first n admitting one is
  n = 12, with (p,q,p_2,q_2,m) = (6,6,2,2,16). QED

  For orientation: the smallest bipartite cubic graph of girth 6 is the Heawood graph on
  14 vertices, and the graphs H of 300.1 are Heawood minus two independent edges, which is
  the split (7,7,2,2,19).

### 308.3 THE DESCENT NEVER STALLS (PROVED)

  LEMMA. If (K,a,b) is admissible, rigidity holds for (a,b), and the three-term collapse
  305.2 does not fire, then some handle of every chordless a-b path contains a cycle,
  provided |V(K)| >= 9.
  Proof. 306.2 makes every handle a 2-edge-cut piece. If every handle were a tree then, by
  the count of 306.3, every handle vertex has degree 2 in K; the degree-2 budget is four
  and two of them are a and b, which lie on the path, so the handles hold at most two
  vertices in all. Hence there are at most two handles, so the number of landing points
  2m <= 4 gives |P'| + 1 <= 4 + s' <= 6, and |V(K)| <= |P'| + 1 + 2 <= 8. QED

### 308.4 THE THEOREM (PROVED)

  THEOREM. No admissible (K,a,b) satisfies rigidity: the a-b paths of K cannot all be
  congruent modulo 4.
  Proof. Suppose some admissible (K,a,b) does. By 308.2, |V(K)| >= 12 >= 9, so by 308.3
  either the three-term collapse fires - and then by 305.2 rigidity FAILS, a contradiction
  - or some handle of a chordless a-b path contains a cycle. In the latter case 307.1
  makes that handle a chain of blocks between its landing points, 307.2 descends rigidity
  to each block, and the block containing the cycle is 2-connected with a distinguished
  pair of degree-2 entry and exit vertices; 307.3 shows it is admissible. Its vertex count
  is strictly smaller, since the handle omits the whole of the path.
  Iterating produces a strictly decreasing sequence of admissible blocks, all of which
  have at least twelve vertices by 308.2. That cannot continue, so at some level the
  collapse fires and rigidity fails there - contradicting the rigidity inherited from the
  top. QED

  COROLLARY ((N3) IS CLOSED). A bridge whose bipartizing edges are exactly the two edges
  at one terminal b_1 cannot satisfy (SC). For 299.2(a) makes (H, x, b_2) admissible with
  rigidity, which 308.4 forbids.

### 308.5 THE STRATIFICATION OF 297 IS NOW COMPLETE EXCEPT FOR ONE ROW

     tau = 0                                      CLOSED  205.2, 208.2
     tau = 1, |Bip| = 1                           CLOSED  295.5
     tau = 1, |Bip| = 2 nontrivial                CLOSED  298.4
     tau = 1, |Bip| = 2 trivial                   CLOSED  308.4      <- new
     tau = 1, |Bip| = 3                           CLOSED  298.3
     tau >= 2                                     OPEN    (N2)

  So EVERY BRIDGE WITH tau(B) <= 1 IS EXCLUDED, unconditionally. (L2**) is false in

  What remains of (INT), and hence of the conjecture, is the single statement (N2): a
  bridge whose frustration index is at least 2 cannot satisfy (SC). Note that 296.3's
  counterexample to (L2**) had tau = 1, so nothing is known to obstruct (N2), and the
  census of 297.5 found (L2**) holding in all 73 sampled bridges with tau >= 2.

### 308.6 Status

PROVED here: no admissible block has fewer than twelve vertices, by a cherry count against
the girth (308.2); the descent never stalls above eight vertices (308.3); and hence no
admissible block satisfies rigidity (308.4).
CLOSED: (N3), the trivial |Bip| = 2 stratum; and with 295.5, 298.3, 298.4, 205.2 and
208.2, the whole of tau <= 1.
NOT PROVED: (N2), tau >= 2; hence (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 308 closes (N3). The base case the
descent needed is empty for an arithmetic reason: in a bipartite graph of girth six the
cherries centred on one side inject into the pairs of the other, and with at most four
vertices of degree 2 that forces at least twelve vertices, while the descent continues
above eight. So an admissible block satisfying rigidity would generate an infinite
strictly decreasing sequence of admissible blocks, all of at least twelve vertices, which
is impossible; the three-term collapse must therefore fire, and rigidity fails. Every
bridge of frustration index at most one is now excluded unconditionally, and the whole of
the conjecture rests on the single remaining statement (N2), that a bridge of frustration
index at least two cannot satisfy (SC).


## 309. PROBING (N2): the vertex-to-edge transversal lemma, and where (N2) really sits

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. (N2) - a bridge of frustration index at least two
cannot satisfy (SC) - is the last open statement. This section does not prove it. It
proves one small lemma which, unexpectedly, identifies exactly which part of the
odd-cycle-packing literature (N2) belongs to, and explains why 254 and 257 could not get
in.

### 309.1 THE VERTEX-TO-EDGE TRANSVERSAL LEMMA (PROVED)

Write tau_v(B) for the least number of VERTICES meeting every odd cycle and tau = tau_e(B)
for the least number of EDGES. Always tau_v <= tau_e, since one endpoint of each edge of an
edge transversal is a vertex transversal.

  LEMMA. In a SUBCUBIC graph, tau_v = 1 implies tau_e = 1.
  Proof. Let B - v be bipartite, with 2-colouring c.
  If deg(v) = 2, every cycle through v uses both its edges, so either edge meets every odd
  cycle - all odd cycles pass through v.
  If deg(v) = 3 with neighbours a, b, d, a cycle through v uses exactly two of the edges
  va, vb, vd; the one through a and b has length 2 + (an a-b path of B - v), so it is ODD
  precisely when c(a) =/= c(b). Among the three colours c(a), c(b), c(d) two agree, say
  c(a) = c(b). Then the pairs giving odd cycles are {a,d} and {b,d}, BOTH CONTAINING d, so
  every odd cycle uses the edge vd. (If all three agree there is no odd cycle through v,
  and B is bipartite.) QED

  COROLLARY. tau(B) >= 2 if and only if NO SINGLE VERTEX MEETS ALL ODD CYCLES.

  VERIFIED exhaustively: over all 124423 subcubic non-bipartite graphs on 4 to 7 vertices,
  107787 have a single-vertex odd cycle transversal and ALL 107787 have a single-edge one -
  no exception.

  SHARPER FORM, from the same proof: when deg(v) = 3 the bipartizing edge is CANONICAL -
  it joins v to the neighbour whose colour differs from the other two.

### 309.2 WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE STRATIFICATION

By 308.5 every bridge with tau <= 1 is excluded. By 309.1 that range is exactly

     tau_v(B) <= 1  :  SOME SINGLE VERTEX MEETS EVERY ODD CYCLE,

so the closed range is not an artefact of choosing edges over vertices - the two
formulations coincide there. And (N2) becomes

     (N2)  A BRIDGE IN WHICH NO SINGLE VERTEX MEETS ALL ODD CYCLES CANNOT SATISFY (SC).

  MEASURED: over sampled bridges with tau >= 2, tau_e = tau_v in every case - 41 with both
  equal to 2 and 11 with both equal to 3. So in this class the two transversal numbers
  appear to agree outright, not merely at the value one. I state that as an observation,
  not a theorem; 309.1 proves only the case tau_v = 1.

### 309.3 WHY 254 AND 257 COULD NOT GET IN, AND WHAT HAS CHANGED

254.3 identified the Lovasz-Slilaty structure theorem for graphs with NO TWO VERTEX-DISJOINT
ODD CYCLES as the right tool and recorded that its internally-4-connected form demands a
triangle, which girth 5 forbids, so only the low-connectivity part applies - "and it has
not been worked out". 257 stalled at the same place.

  The obstacle was that the theory's degenerate branch is precisely "a single vertex meets
  all odd cycles", and the programme had no way to tell whether its bridges were in that
  branch or not. 309.1 settles that: the degenerate branch is exactly tau <= 1, which 308
  has now CLOSED by other means. So (N2) lives entirely in the NON-degenerate branch, and
  the structure theorem is being asked a question it is actually shaped to answer.

  WHAT IS STILL MISSING before the theory can be invoked is the packing hypothesis itself,
  nu_odd(B) <= 1. 223.3 derives nu_odd <= 2 from (SC) via the Gram matrix of disjoint odd
  cycles, under its own spanning hypothesis; 254.2 asserts nu_odd <= 1 but reaches it
  through 229.2 and the measurement of 254.1, and 255.4's component condition is not
  proved. So the honest position is:

     (N2) reduces to the Lovasz-Slilaty regime AS SOON AS nu_odd(B) <= 1 is available,
     and that, not the structure theory, is the remaining obstacle.

  Note also that 302.1's Lemma A - every cycle of a 2-connected graph is the symmetric
  difference of two s-t paths - is exactly the spanning input 222.3 and 223.3 wanted, so
  re-examining 223.3 with Lemma A in hand is the obvious first move on nu_odd, and it has
  not been done.

### 309.4 Status

PROVED here: in a subcubic graph a single-vertex odd cycle transversal forces a
single-edge one, with the edge canonical at a degree-3 vertex (309.1); hence tau >= 2 is
equivalent to the non-existence of a single-vertex transversal (309.1 corollary).
COMPUTED: the lemma holds in all 107787 relevant graphs among 124423 tested (309.1); and
tau_e = tau_v in all 52 sampled bridges with tau >= 2 (309.2).
IDENTIFIED: (N2) lies exactly in the non-degenerate branch of the Lovasz-Slilaty theory,
whose degenerate branch coincides with the range 308 already closed; and the remaining
obstacle to entering that theory is nu_odd <= 1, for which 302.1's Lemma A is an
unexploited new input to 223.3 (309.3).
NOT PROVED: (N2); hence (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 309 probes the last open statement and
finds a small lemma with a large consequence: in a subcubic graph, if one vertex meets
every odd cycle then one edge does, because at a degree-3 vertex two of the three
neighbours share a colour in the bipartite remainder and the odd cycles are forced through
the third edge. So the range 308 closed - frustration index at most one - is exactly the
range in which a single vertex meets all odd cycles, which is the degenerate branch of the
Lovasz-Slilaty structure theorem for graphs without two disjoint odd cycles. (N2) therefore
sits in the non-degenerate branch, where that theorem has content, and the one thing
standing between the programme and it is the packing bound nu_odd <= 1 - for which Lemma A
of 302 supplies exactly the spanning input that 223.3 lacked.


## 310. (N2): THE BUDGET OBSTACLE IS A BALL-PACKING PROBLEM, AND IT IS ONE VERTEX SHORT

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. (N2) is the last statement. This section brings
308's engine to bear on it, removes the obstruction that stopped it at frustration index
one, and reaches a bound that MISSES BY EXACTLY ONE VERTEX. The residue is therefore
numerical and completely explicit.

### 310.1 (SC) DESCENDS TO B - N (PROVED)

Let (X,Y) be a bipartition with non-crossing set N, so B - N is BIPARTITE, and by 295.2 a
minimum N is a matching of size tau. Three terminals get two colours, so some pair - say
(b_1,b_2) - is MONOCHROMATIC. By the parity identity 295.1 every b_1-b_2 path avoiding N
is EVEN, so (SC) gives

     ALL b_1-b_2 PATHS OF W = B - N ARE CONGRUENT MOD 4,

i.e. rigidity for (b_1,b_2) in the bipartite graph W. This is exactly the hypothesis
308.4 refutes - except for the degree-2 budget: W has s = 3 + 2 tau vertices of degree 2,
against the four that 308.2 could afford.

### 310.2 THE DEGREE-2 VERTICES OF W ARE SPREAD OUT (PROVED)

They are not arbitrary.

  (a) The three terminals are pairwise at distance at least 5 (213.1).
  (b) The two endpoints of an N-edge are ADJACENT in B, so deleting that edge leaves them
      at distance at least girth(B) - 1 >= 4 in W.

  So the 2 tau N-endpoints fall into tau pairs, each pair at distance at least 4, and the
  terminals are mutually far. This is what the naive budget count of 309 ignored, and it
  removes the obstruction that stopped the engine:

  THE HEXAGON IS EXCLUDED AT tau = 2. 309's table failed first at s = 6 because F(6) = 6 -
  a bare hexagon, bipartite of girth 6 with six degree-2 vertices. But a hexagon occurring
  as a BLOCK has four vertices interior to the block, whose every edge lies inside it, so
  they have degree 2 in W as well. At most one can be a terminal, the hexagon having
  diameter 3 < 5, so at least three are N-endpoints; with tau = 2 there are only four
  N-endpoints in two pairs, so some pair lies on the hexagon at distance at most 3 < 4.
  Contradiction. The small obstruction is an artefact of ignoring (a) and (b).

### 310.3 THE BALL-PACKING BOUND, AND THE ONE-VERTEX GAP (PROVED)

  LEMMA. If the degree-2 vertices of a subcubic graph are pairwise at distance at least 3,
  their closed neighbourhoods are disjoint, each of size 3, so n >= 3s.
  Proof. Distance at least 3 makes the closed neighbourhoods disjoint; a degree-2 vertex
  has exactly two neighbours. QED

  INHERITANCE. A block K of a handle has, besides its at most two ends, only degree-2
  vertices that were already degree-2 in the ambient graph - an interior vertex of a block
  has all its edges inside it - and distances in K are at least the ambient distances. So
  the s(K) - 2 non-end degree-2 vertices of K are still pairwise at distance at least 3,
  giving

        |V(K)|  >=  3 ( s(K) - 2 )  =  3 s(K) - 6 .

  THE DESCENT THRESHOLD. 308.3, redone for budget s: if every handle is a tree then every
  handle vertex has degree 2, and under the distance hypothesis no two are adjacent, so
  EVERY TREE HANDLE IS A SINGLE VERTEX. With m handles and s' degree-2 vertices interior
  to the path, m + s' <= s - 2 and |P'| + 1 = 2m + s', so

        |V(K)|  <=  2m + s' + m  =  3m + s'  <=  3 (s - 2)  =  3 s - 6 .

  So the descent continues exactly when |V(K)| >= 3s - 5, and the ball bound guarantees
  only |V(K)| >= 3s - 6.

     THE TWO BOUNDS MEET EXACTLY. The engine is ONE VERTEX SHORT.

### 310.4 What the equality case looks like

If |V(K)| = 3s - 6 the two bounds are tight simultaneously, which pins the graph
completely: V(K) is the disjoint union of the closed neighbourhoods of the s-2 non-end
degree-2 vertices; every handle is a single vertex adjacent to two vertices of the path;
and the two ends a, b are themselves neighbours of such vertices. Counting degrees,
|E(K)| = 4s - 9, consistent, so no contradiction comes from counting alone. What such a
graph is, is a path with single-vertex handles - "cherries" - and rigidity then says every
cherry's shift 2 - (its span) is 0 mod 4, so every spanned arc has length 2 mod 4 and, by
girth 6, at least 6.

  So the equality case is a concrete finite-looking family and not obviously empty; it must
  be excluded on its own terms. Improving EITHER bound by one closes (N2) at every level of
  the descent:
    - show |V(K)| >= 3s - 5 whenever the distance hypothesis holds, e.g. by finding one
      vertex outside all the balls - the two ends a and b are the natural candidates, and
      they are outside unless each is a neighbour of a non-end degree-2 vertex; or
    - sharpen the tree-handle count from 3s - 6 to 3s - 7, e.g. by showing the path cannot
      simultaneously carry s' interior degree-2 vertices and m single-vertex handles at
      the extremal ratio.

### 310.5 Status

PROVED here: (SC) descends to rigidity for a monochromatic terminal pair in the bipartite
graph B - N (310.1); the degree-2 vertices of B - N are spread out, terminals pairwise at
distance 5 and N-partners at distance at least 4, which excludes the hexagon block that
broke the naive count at tau = 2 (310.2); the ball-packing bound |V(K)| >= 3s(K) - 6 and
its inheritance by blocks, together with the sharpened tree-handle count that every tree
handle is a single vertex and hence |V(K)| <= 3s - 6 (310.3).
NOT PROVED: (N2). The two bounds coincide, so the descent is one vertex short of never
stalling, and the extremal family - a path with single-vertex handles spanning arcs of
length 2 mod 4 - is not excluded (310.4).

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 310 turns (N2) into arithmetic. (SC)
gives rigidity for a monochromatic terminal pair in the bipartite graph left by deleting a
minimum bipartizing matching, which is exactly what 308 refutes except that the degree-2
budget is 3 + 2 tau rather than four. But those degree-2 vertices are spread out - the
terminals pairwise at distance five, the two ends of a deleted edge at distance at least
four - and that removes the hexagon obstruction which stopped the count at frustration
index one. Under the distance hypothesis the closed neighbourhoods of the degree-2
vertices are disjoint, forcing at least 3s - 6 vertices, while the tree-handle count
forbids more than 3s - 6. The two meet exactly: the engine is one vertex short, and the
extremal case is a path with single-vertex handles, which must now be excluded on its own
terms.


## 311. THE EXTREMAL FAMILY CLASSIFIED: the one-vertex gap resolved, tau <= 2 conditional

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 310 left the engine one vertex short, with an
extremal family it could not exclude. That family is classified here. It exists only from
s = 8, so it cannot occur at frustration index two; and where it does exist it FAILS
RIGIDITY anyway, so it was never an obstruction. What remains for (N2) is not the
extremal case but the DISTANCE HYPOTHESIS that 310's ball bound needs.

### 311.1 THE EQUALITY CASE, SOLVED (PROVED)

Suppose |V(K)| = 3s - 6, the tight case of 310.3. Writing m for the number of handles and
s' for the degree-2 vertices interior to the path, 310.3 gives |V(K)| = 3m + s' and the
ball bound gives |V(K)| >= 3(m + s'), so

        3m + s'  >=  3m + 3s'    ==>    s' = 0 ,   m = s - 2 ,   |V(K)| = 3m .

  Then the balls partition V(K), so EVERY path vertex is adjacent to exactly one handle
