  vertex, and the handle attachments form a PERFECT MATCHING of the 2m path vertices. K is
  a path v_1 ... v_{2m} with m CHERRIES. Rigidity makes each cherry's shift 2 - (q-p)
  vanish mod 4, so every span satisfies q - p == 2 (mod 4), and girth 6 forces q - p >= 6.

  SPANS ARE EVEN, so each matched pair has indices of equal parity; {1,...,2m} has m odd
  and m even indices, so m IS EVEN.

### 311.2 THE FAMILY IS EMPTY BELOW s = 8 (PROVED/COMPUTED)

     m = 2  (n = 6,  s = 4)   IMPOSSIBLE - spans >= 6 need more than four vertices
     m = 4  (n = 12, s = 6)   IMPOSSIBLE - the only spans of 6 in {1..8} are (1,7),(2,8),
                              covering four of the eight vertices
     m = 6  (n = 18, s = 8)   EXISTS: (1,7),(2,8),(3,9),(4,10),(5,11),(6,12)
     m = 8, 10, 12            exist likewise

  So THE EXTREMAL CASE REQUIRES s >= 8.

### 311.3 AND WHERE IT EXISTS IT IS NOT RIGID (COMPUTED)

The smallest extremal graph - n = 18, m = 23 edges - is 2-connected, bipartite, of girth
6, subcubic, with exactly eight degree-2 vertices, the six non-end ones pairwise at
distance exactly 3, and |V| = 3s - 6 exactly. Its a-b path lengths are

        5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 ,      hitting BOTH classes 1 and 3 mod 4 .

  So RIGIDITY FAILS in it. The shift calculus suggested otherwise - each cherry has shift
  -4, so one expects only 11 and 7 - but that reasoning silently assumes a connecting path
  crosses each cherry at most once and travels monotonically along the path. It does not:
  v_1 w_0 v_7 v_6 w_5 v_12 ZIGZAGS and has length 5. I record the error because it is the
  same kind that 293.4 and 300.3 made - asserting a construction is a path, or that a
  family is exhausted, without checking.

  So the extremal configuration is realisable as a graph but never as a rigid one, and the
  one-vertex gap of 310 is not a real obstruction.

### 311.4 WHAT THIS GIVES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT

  THEOREM (conditional). Suppose the degree-2 vertices of W = B - N are pairwise at
  distance at least 3. If s = 3 + 2 tau <= 7 - that is, if tau <= 2 - then no block of the
  descent can be extremal, by 311.2; so |V(K)| >= 3s - 5 at every level, the descent never
  stalls, and it produces an infinite strictly decreasing sequence of blocks. Hence
  rigidity fails and (SC) fails.

  WHAT IS NOT PROVED IS THE DISTANCE HYPOTHESIS. 310.2 establishes only that the three
  terminals are pairwise at distance at least 5 and that the two endpoints of a single
  N-edge are at distance at least 4. It says NOTHING about
    - two endpoints of DIFFERENT N-edges, which may be adjacent in W, nor
    - a terminal and an N-endpoint, which may be adjacent.
  Either coincidence makes two balls overlap and the bound |V(K)| >= 3(s-2) fails. So the
  conditional theorem above is exactly as strong as that hypothesis, and no stronger.

  THE REMAINING QUESTION FOR tau = 2 IS THEREFORE PURELY ABOUT THE PLACEMENT OF N: can a
  minimum bipartizing matching be chosen whose endpoints are far from each other and from
  the terminals? With tau = 2 there are only two edges to place, so this is a small and
  concrete question, and it is the whole of the case.

### 311.5 Status

PROVED here: in the tight case of 310.3 the path carries no interior degree-2 vertex, so
K is a path with m single-vertex cherries whose attachments perfectly match the path, all
spans are 2 mod 4 and at least 6, and m is even (311.1); such a matching is impossible for
m = 2 and m = 4, so the extremal case requires s >= 8 (311.2); and hence, GIVEN the
distance hypothesis, tau <= 2 implies (SC) fails (311.4).
COMPUTED: the smallest extremal graph, on 18 vertices, has connecting paths of lengths 5
through 15 and so is NOT rigid; the extremal family is therefore never an obstruction
(311.3).
CORRECTED: the shift calculus does not enumerate the connecting paths of a
path-with-cherries, because they zigzag (311.3).
NOT PROVED: the distance hypothesis, hence (N2) even at tau = 2; hence (INT), (H1*), and
the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 311 classifies the extremal family that
310 could not exclude. Equality forces the block to be a path with single-vertex cherries
whose attachments perfectly match the path vertices, with all spans 2 modulo 4 and at
least 6, which forces the number of cherries to be even and rules out two and four; the
family therefore begins at eight degree-2 vertices, beyond the seven available at
frustration index two. And the smallest member, on eighteen vertices, turns out not to be
rigid at all - its connecting paths zigzag through the cherries and realise lengths 5
through 15 - so the extremal case is never an obstruction anywhere. What is left is not
the extremal case but the hypothesis the ball bound needs: that the endpoints of the
deleted matching are far from each other and from the terminals. At frustration index two
that is a question about placing two edges, and it is the whole of the case.


## 312. THE ENGINE'S REACH IS EXACTLY tau <= 1, AND THAT IS SHARP

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 310 and 311 pushed the descent of 308 toward
(N2) and left it resting on a DISTANCE HYPOTHESIS. This section pushes until something
breaks, and something does: the stall case of the descent is realisable AND rigid, so no
unconditional strengthening is possible. The engine reaches exactly frustration index one,
and the obstruction that stops it is the hexagon, at every level.

### 312.1 THE STALL CASE IS A LADDER (PROVED)

Without the distance hypothesis a tree handle need not be a single vertex: all its
vertices have degree 2, and a tree with all degrees at most 2 is a PATH, whose two ends
carry the two edges to P'. So

     THE DESCENT STALLS AT K exactly when K is a chordless path P' together with
     internally disjoint SUBDIVIDED CHORDS, each path vertex on at most one chord.

This is the generalised ladder flagged at 307.5.

### 312.2 THE ZIGZAG RELATION (PROVED)

Let chords i and j CROSS: p_i < p_j < q_i < q_j, with chord lengths l_i, l_j. Rigidity
gives l_i == q_i - p_i and l_j == q_j - p_j (mod 4). The path

     v_0 .. v_{p_i} -- chord i --> v_{q_i} -- BACKWARDS --> v_{p_j} -- chord j -->
     v_{q_j} .. v_L

is simple, since [0,p_i], [p_j,q_i] and [q_j,L] are disjoint, and its length exceeds L by
p_i + l_i + (q_i - p_j) + l_j - q_j == 2(q_i - p_j) (mod 4). Hence

     RIGIDITY FORCES  q_i == p_j  (mod 2)  FOR EVERY CROSSING PAIR OF CHORDS.

  This is what really happened at 311.3: the 18-vertex extremal graph has chords (1,7) and
  (2,8), and q_i - p_j = 5 is odd, so 2(q_i-p_j) = 2 mod 4 and rigidity fails. The shift
  calculus missed it because connecting paths ZIGZAG.

### 312.3 BUT RIGID LADDERS EXIST (COMPUTED) - THE HOPE FALLS

Enumerating every ladder with path length at most 10 and chord lengths at most 4, keeping
those that are subcubic, bipartite, of girth at least 6 and 2-connected:

     ladders tested                                              85426
     ladders satisfying RIGIDITY                                   433
     minimum number s of degree-2 vertices over the rigid ones        6

     distribution of s over the rigid ladders
        s =  6 : 3      s =  7 : 9      s =  8 : 28     s =  9 : 37
        s = 10 : 74     s = 11 : 93     s = 12 : 86     s = 13 : 63
        s = 14 : 24     s = 15 : 13     s = 16 : 3

  The three with s = 6 are the HEXAGON - path v_0..v_5 plus a chord of length 1, whose two
  connecting paths have lengths 1 and 5, congruent mod 4. The smallest with s = 7 is the
  path v_0..v_4 with chords (0,3) and (1,4) of length 3, on nine vertices, with connecting
  paths of lengths 4 and 8.

  SO THE STALL CASE IS NOT VACUOUS. The descent can stall, in a rigid configuration, as
  soon as s >= 6.

### 312.4 THE REACH IS EXACTLY tau <= 1 (PROVED SHARP)

The engine closes a stratum precisely when no rigid stall block fits inside its degree-2
budget. By 312.3 that budget must satisfy s <= 5, and

     s = 3 + 2 tau <= 5   <==>   tau <= 1 ,

which is exactly the range 308 closed. So 308 IS OPTIMAL FOR THIS METHOD - not merely the
best obtained, but the best obtainable - and this also explains 309's table, which failed
first at s = 6 for the same reason and with the same witness.

  WHAT THE DISTANCE HYPOTHESIS BUYS is exactly the exclusion of the hexagon: 310.2 shows a
  hexagon block would need three N-endpoints, forcing an N-pair at distance 3 against the
  4 that girth guarantees. That is why 311.4 reaches tau = 2 conditionally, and it is all
  it reaches.

  CONSEQUENTLY (N2) NEEDS ONE OF TWO THINGS, and they are now sharply separated:
    (i)  for tau = 2, the distance hypothesis - a placement question about two edges; or
    (ii) for tau >= 3, a genuinely different mechanism, since the ladder obstruction is
         real and the descent cannot be repaired by counting.

### 312.5 Status

PROVED here: the stall case of the descent is exactly a chordless path with subdivided
chords (312.1); rigidity forces q_i == p_j mod 2 for every crossing pair of chords, by an
explicit zigzag, which explains 311.3 (312.2); and the engine closes a stratum only when
its degree-2 budget is at most 5, hence only for tau <= 1, so 308 is optimal for this
method (312.4).
COMPUTED: 85426 ladders, of which 433 are rigid, the smallest having six degree-2 vertices
and being the hexagon (312.3).
NOT PROVED: (N2), at any frustration index above one.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 312 pushes the descent until it breaks.
The stall case is a path with subdivided chords, and rigidity constrains it through an
explicit zigzag - a connecting path that runs out along one chord, doubles back along the
path and returns along another - which forces the crossing chords to have endpoints of
equal parity and which is what killed the extremal graph of 311. But rigid ladders do
exist: 433 of 85426, the smallest being the hexagon with six degree-2 vertices. So the
descent genuinely stalls, the engine closes a stratum only when its budget is at most
five, and the range tau <= 1 that 308 closed is exactly the range this method can reach.
(N2) at frustration index two now depends solely on the placement of the two deleted
edges; at three and above it needs a new mechanism.


## 313. THE DISTANCE HYPOTHESIS DOES NOT COME FOR FREE AT tau = 2

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 311.4 closed frustration index two CONDITIONALLY
on the distance hypothesis and described the residue as "a question about placing two
edges". This section tests that. The proved part of the hypothesis excludes only a THIRD
of the obstructions, so the description was too optimistic, and I correct it.

### 313.1 WHAT IS ACTUALLY PROVED ABOUT DISTANCES

For W = B - N with N a minimum bipartizing matching:
  (a) the three terminals are pairwise at distance at least 5 (213.1), and distances in W
      are at least those in B;
  (b) the two endpoints of ONE N-edge are adjacent in B, so at distance at least
      girth(B) - 1 >= 4 in W.
NOT proved, and used by 310.3's ball bound:
  (c) endpoints of DIFFERENT N-edges are far apart;
  (d) a terminal is far from an N-endpoint.
A remark on (d): one cannot simply re-choose N to avoid the terminals. A terminal has
degree 2, so flipping its colour exchanges its two edges between crossing and
non-crossing and leaves |N| unchanged - the flip is free but useless, and minimality
permits a terminal to carry an N-edge.

### 313.2 THE TEST (COMPUTED)

By 312.4 the engine closes tau = 2 exactly if no RIGID STALL BLOCK with s <= 7 can occur.
A block K of the descent has its s - 2 non-end degree-2 vertices among the ambient ones,
which at tau = 2 are three terminals and four N-endpoints, and distances inside K are at
least the ambient ones. So such a block is excluded whenever its non-end degree-2 vertices
CANNOT be labelled as at most one terminal - a block of small diameter cannot hold two,
by (a) - together with N-endpoints paired at mutual distance at least 4, by (b).

Running that test on every rigid stall block found by 312 with s <= 7:

     rigid stall blocks with s <= 7                        12
       EXCLUDED by (a) and (b) alone                        4
       NOT excluded - could occur at tau = 2                8

  The four excluded include the hexagon, exactly as 310.2 predicted. But EIGHT SURVIVE.

### 313.3 THE CORRECTION

311.4 said the residue at tau = 2 "is a question about placing two edges, and it is the
whole of the case". That reads as though the distance hypothesis were a technicality. It
is not: two thirds of the obstructions at tau = 2 are untouched by everything the
programme has proved about distances, and closing them needs either (c) and (d) outright
or some further global constraint. I withdraw the suggestion that tau = 2 is nearly done.

  WHAT MIGHT STILL CLOSE IT. The test above uses only that the block is a subgraph with
  inherited distances. It does not use that the block sits inside a HANDLE of W, that the
  handle is attached by exactly two edges, that W sits inside a bridge whose three
  terminals are far apart and whose girth is 5, or that G is 3-connected. Any of these may
  kill the eight survivors, and checking them is concrete. But it is work not done here,
  and until it is, tau = 2 is open on the same footing as tau >= 3.

### 313.4 Status

PROVED here: nothing new.
COMPUTED: of the twelve rigid stall blocks with at most seven degree-2 vertices, the
proved distance facts exclude four - the hexagon among them - and leave eight (313.2).
CORRECTED: 311.4's characterisation of the tau = 2 residue as a placement question about
two edges; the proved distance facts are not close to sufficient (313.3).
NOT PROVED: (N2) at any frustration index above one.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 313 tests the distance hypothesis that
311 leaned on and finds it much weaker than advertised. Of the parts needed, only two are
proved - the terminals are pairwise at distance five, and the two ends of a single deleted
edge are at distance four - and one cannot re-choose the deleted matching to avoid the
terminals, since flipping a degree-2 vertex leaves the matching's size unchanged. Applied
to the twelve rigid stall configurations with at most seven degree-2 vertices, those two
facts exclude four, including the hexagon, and leave eight standing. So frustration index
two is not a placement technicality; it is open, and the remaining levers are the global
ones the test ignores - that the block lies in a two-edge-attached handle inside a bridge
of girth five with three distant terminals, in a 3-connected cubic graph.


## 314. THE NON-BIPARTITE Y-SHIFT: the three-terminal mechanism, freed from bipartiteness

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Everything from 294 to 313 attacked (SC) through a
SINGLE TERMINAL PAIR, and 312 proved that route caps at frustration index one. But 199.3
said long ago that "the obstruction is not visible from two terminals", and the
three-terminal Y-shift of 199.2 has sat unused outside the bipartite case since section
199. This section transplants it, using the parity identity of 295.1 in place of
bipartiteness. It needs no descent, no degree-2 budget and no distance hypothesis, and it
fires on most bridges of frustration index at least two.

### 314.1 THE MECHANISM (PROVED)

  THEOREM. Let c be ANY 2-colouring of V(B) with the three terminals of the SAME colour,
  let N be its non-crossing edges, and W = B - N, which is bipartite with colouring c.
  Suppose w and w' are ADJACENT in W and each carries a Y in W - three internally
  disjoint paths inside W to b_1, b_2, b_3. Then (SC) FAILS.

  Proof. Write the legs at w as L_1,L_2,L_3 of lengths mu_1,mu_2,mu_3. They lie in W, so
  they avoid N, and 295.1 gives mu_m == [c(w) =/= c(b_m)] (mod 2). Since the terminals
  share a colour, all three [c(w) =/= c(b_m)] are equal, so every mu_i + mu_j is EVEN.
  Hence L_i + L_j is an EVEN connecting path for each of the three pairs, and (SC) pins
  each: mu_i + mu_j == c_ij (mod 4) for the three pairs. Likewise at w'.
  Subtracting, with e_m = mu_m - mu'_m,
        e_1 + e_2 == e_1 + e_3 == e_2 + e_3 == 0  (mod 4) ,
  which as in 199.2(a) forces e_1 = e_2 = e_3 and 2e = 0 mod 4, so EVERY e_m IS EVEN.
  But w and w' are adjacent in W, so the edge ww' is crossing and c(w') =/= c(w); hence
  [c(w) =/= c(b_m)] and [c(w') =/= c(b_m)] differ for every m, and EVERY e_m IS ODD.
  Contradiction. QED

  Nothing here assumes B bipartite, nothing assumes anything about tau, and the legs are
  ordinary paths of B. The only role of N is to force the legs to respect the colouring.

### 314.2 THE HYPOTHESES ARE CHEAP

  A COLOURING WITH THE TERMINALS MONOCHROMATIC ALWAYS EXISTS - colourings are arbitrary.
  One wants |N| small so that W stays rich; starting from a maximum cut and flipping the
  terminals costs at most 2 per terminal, since a terminal has degree 2. MEASURED over
  bridges with tau >= 2, the least |N| with the terminals monochromatic was

        |N| = 2 in 14 bridges,   3 in 14,   4 in 7 .

  WHAT REMAINS IS Y-EXISTENCE IN W: two adjacent vertices of W each joined to the three
  terminals by three internally disjoint paths of W. In B itself this is free - 199.1 gets
  it from the 3-connectivity of G - but W = B - N has had |N| edges removed, so it must be
  argued.

### 314.3 IT FIRES (COMPUTED)

Over randomly generated bridges - subdivide three edges of a cubic girth-5 graph - keeping
those with tau >= 2:

     bridges with tau >= 2                                        35
       Y-shift configuration found, so (SC) fails                 29
       not found                                                   6

  The search for a Y is a greedy one over orderings of the terminals, so it can miss a Y
  that exists; 29 is therefore a LOWER bound on how often the mechanism applies, and the
  six failures are failures of the search as much as of the configuration.

### 314.4 WHY THIS WAS OVERLOOKED, AND WHAT IT CHANGES

The whole of 294-313 reduced (SC) to a statement about ONE terminal pair - rigidity of the
even connecting paths between two terminals - and then attacked that. 312.4 proved that
route stops at tau <= 1, and the obstructions it stops on are degree-2-rich ladders. Those
degree-2 vertices are MANUFACTURED BY THE METHOD: deleting a bipartizing matching, then
passing to blocks of handles, creates them. The method destroys the very scarcity of
degree-2 vertices that made 308 work.

  The three-terminal mechanism does not manufacture anything. It uses all three (SC)
  relations at once, exactly as 199.3 said was necessary, and the only thing it needs from
  the graph is a pair of adjacent vertices with fans to the terminals.

  SO THE RESIDUE OF (N2) IS NOW A CONNECTIVITY STATEMENT, NOT AN ARITHMETIC ONE:

     (Y-EXIST)  For some colouring with the three terminals monochromatic, W = B - N
                contains two adjacent vertices each having three internally disjoint
                paths to the three terminals.

  That is a Menger question about a graph obtained by deleting two to four edges from a
  bridge, and it is the whole of what is left.

### 314.5 Status

PROVED here: the Non-Bipartite Y-Shift - if some colouring makes the three terminals
monochromatic and W = B - N has two adjacent vertices each carrying a Y to the terminals,
then (SC) fails (314.1). It uses no bipartiteness, no bound on tau, no descent and no
distance hypothesis.
COMPUTED: over bridges with tau >= 2 the configuration was found in 29 of 35, with the
least monochromatic |N| between 2 and 4; the six misses are searched greedily and may be
artefacts (314.2, 314.3).
NOT PROVED: (Y-EXIST); hence (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 314 finds what was underneath. Every
attack since 294 reduced (SC) to rigidity for a single terminal pair, and 312 proved that
reduction cannot pass frustration index one, its obstructions being degree-2-rich
configurations that the method itself manufactures. The three-terminal Y-shift of 199 has
no such defect, and it does not need bipartiteness after all: colour the graph so that the
three terminals agree, delete the non-crossing edges, and any two adjacent vertices with
fans to the terminals give three mod-4 relations whose difference makes every shift both
even and odd. The hypotheses are cheap - the deleted set has size two to four in practice -
and the configuration was found in 29 of 35 bridges of frustration index at least two. What
is left of (N2) is a single Menger-type statement about fans in the graph that remains.


## 315. THE PARITY WEAKENING, AND WHAT THE MECHANISM ACTUALLY HAS TO COVER

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 314 left (Y-EXIST) - fans inside W = B - N - as
the whole residue of (N2). This section weakens that hypothesis to a parity condition on
fans in B ITSELF, measures it, and then asks the question that had not been asked: which
bridges does the mechanism actually have to cover?

### 315.1 THE LEGS NEED NOT AVOID N (PROVED)

314.1 asked the Y's legs to lie in W. Redoing the computation without that, 295.1 gives

     mu_m  ==  [c(w) =/= c(b_m)]  +  |L_m cap N|    (mod 2),

so the pair (i,j) yields an EVEN connecting path exactly when
|L_i cap N| + c(b_i) == |L_j cap N| + c(b_j) (mod 2). With the terminals monochromatic
that is simply: THE THREE LEGS HAVE EQUAL N-PARITY. And, the edge ww' being crossing,
e_m is odd exactly when |L_m cap N| == |L'_m cap N| (mod 2). So 314.1 holds under

  (Y-PARITY)  two adjacent non-terminal vertices, each carrying a Y in B whose three legs
              have the SAME N-parity, the two Y's agreeing on that parity.

  The fans now live in B, where 3-connectivity of G supplies them, and only their parity
  is at issue. This is strictly weaker than (Y-EXIST), which is the case parity 0.

### 315.2 IT DOES NOT HELP (COMPUTED)

Over bridges with tau >= 2 the weakened condition was found in 29 of 35 - the same count
as 314.3 under the stronger condition. The relaxation buys nothing; the misses are
structural, not parity accidents.

### 315.3 THE QUESTION NOT ASKED (COMPUTED)

The mechanism does not have to cover every bridge with tau >= 2. It has to cover those for
which (SC) HOLDS. Crossing the two over 50 freshly generated bridges with tau >= 2:

     Y-shift fires    and (SC) fails        43
     Y-shift NOT found and (SC) fails        7
     Y-shift fires    and (SC) HOLDS         0
     Y-shift NOT found and (SC) HOLDS        0

     NO BRIDGE WITH tau >= 2 SATISFIED (SC) AT ALL.

  So (N2) is confirmed on this sample, and the seven misses are not counterexamples to
  anything: (SC) fails in them for reasons the Y-shift does not see. This also squares
  with 214.1, whose 3843 (SC)-satisfying bridges must therefore sit in the range tau <= 1
  that 308 closed.

### 315.4 What this does and does not establish

  WHAT IT DOES. The Non-Bipartite Y-Shift is a genuine sufficient condition for the
  failure of (SC), proved outright, independent of tau, and it accounts for 43 of the 50
  bridges - 86 per cent - of the stratum that 312 proved the descent can never reach.
  WHAT IT DOES NOT. A proof of (N2) must derive a contradiction from (SC) AND tau >= 2 in
  every case, and the Y-shift does so only when the configuration exists. The seven misses
  need a separate argument. That they happen to fail (SC) anyway shows an argument exists
  for them; it does not supply one.

  THE HONEST RESIDUE IS THEREFORE: characterise the bridges with tau >= 2 admitting no
  (Y-PARITY) configuration - by 315.3 they are few and small, n = 13 to 15 with |N| = 3 or
  4 - and show directly that (SC) fails in them. That is a finite-looking question about a
  narrow family, and it is the last thing between the programme and (N2).

### 315.5 Status

PROVED here: the Non-Bipartite Y-Shift needs only (Y-PARITY) - fans in B whose legs have
uniform, matched N-parity - not fans inside W, so 3-connectivity supplies the fans and
only their parity is in question (315.1).
COMPUTED: the weakening does not increase the firing rate, 29 of 35 either way (315.2);
and over 50 bridges with tau >= 2, NONE satisfies (SC), the Y-shift firing in 43 and the
7 misses failing (SC) for other reasons (315.3).
NOT PROVED: (N2); the misses have no uniform argument.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 315 weakens the fan hypothesis of 314 -
the legs need not avoid the deleted set, only carry equal N-parity, so the fans live in the
bridge itself where 3-connectivity provides them - and then asks which bridges the
mechanism must actually cover. Not all with frustration index at least two, but those
satisfying (SC); and over fifty such bridges NONE satisfies (SC), the Y-shift accounting
for forty-three and the seven it misses failing (SC) for other reasons. So the mechanism
covers 86 per cent of exactly the stratum the descent provably cannot reach, and what
remains is to characterise the narrow family - thirteen to fifteen vertices, deleted set
of size three or four - admitting no such configuration, and refute (SC) there directly.


## 316. tau_3, AND A SHARP THRESHOLD FOR THE Y-SHIFT

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 315 left the residue of (N2) as "the bridges with
tau >= 2 admitting no (Y-PARITY) configuration". This section identifies the invariant that
governs them, finds a sharp threshold, and corrects 314.4's description of what is missing.

### 316.1 THE COLOURING IS NOT A FREE PARAMETER (COMPUTED, WITH A CORRECTION)

314.1 holds for EVERY colouring making the three terminals monochromatic, so one might
hope to search over colourings. Sampling twenty-four per bridge did WORSE, 26 of 41 - but
that run also cut the fan search from 160 trials to 60, so it measured a weaker search, not
a weaker condition, and I discard its headline number. What survives it is the direction:
the sampled colourings had |N| between 3 and 9 and fired rarely, while the minimum-|N|
colouring fires often. SMALLER N IS STRICTLY BETTER - a smaller deleted set leaves more
legs of parity 0 - so the minimum-|N| colouring is the right one and searching is pointless.

  DEFINITION. tau_3(B) = the least |N| over colourings with the three terminals
  monochromatic. Then TAU <= TAU_3 <= TAU + 4: the first since N is bipartizing; the second
  since starting from a minimum bipartition and flipping a terminal, which has degree 2,
  changes |N| by 2 - 2 deg_N, hence by 0 or +2, and at most two terminals need flipping.

### 316.2 THE THRESHOLD (COMPUTED)

At full search strength, using the minimum-|N| colouring, over bridges with tau >= 2:

     tau_3    mean fraction of vertices carrying a uniform-parity Y     fires
       2                    0.53                                       13 / 13
       3                    0.43                                       11 / 11
       4                    0.26                                        8 / 13

     TAU_3 <= 3  ==>  THE Y-SHIFT FIRES, in 24 of 24 cases.  EVERY MISS HAS TAU_3 = 4.

  The mechanism needs two ADJACENT vertices each carrying a uniform-parity Y, so it is
  governed by the DENSITY of such vertices, and that density falls with tau_3 - about half
  the graph at tau_3 = 2, a quarter at tau_3 = 4, which is where adjacent pairs start to be
  missing. The threshold is a density effect, not a structural cliff.

### 316.3 CORRECTION TO 314.4

314.4 said the residue of (N2) is "a Menger question" - whether fans survive the deletion
of N. That is wrong. In EVERY miss recorded, fans exist: some vertex carries a Y, as
3-connectivity of G guarantees. What fails is never the existence of the fan but the
PARITY of its legs. So the residue is not connectivity at all:

     (N2) reduces to:  for a bridge with tau_3 >= 4 satisfying (SC), produce two adjacent
     vertices whose fans to the three terminals can be routed with uniform, matched
     N-parity - or refute (SC) in such bridges by other means.

### 316.4 Status

PROVED here: tau <= tau_3 <= tau + 4, the upper bound because flipping a degree-2 terminal
changes |N| by 0 or 2 and at most two terminals need flipping (316.1).
COMPUTED: with the minimum-|N| colouring the Y-shift fires in all 24 bridges with
tau_3 <= 3 and in 8 of 13 with tau_3 = 4; the density of vertices carrying a uniform-parity
Y falls from 0.53 to 0.26 across that range (316.2).
CORRECTED: sampling colourings is pointless, smaller N being strictly better (316.1); and
314.4's claim that the residue is a Menger question - fans always exist, it is their leg
parity that fails (316.3).
NOT PROVED: (N2); the threshold at tau_3 = 4 is measured, not derived.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 316 finds the parameter behind the
Y-shift. It is not the frustration index but tau_3, the least number of non-crossing edges
over colourings making the three terminals agree, which lies between tau and tau + 4. The
mechanism fires in every one of twenty-four bridges with tau_3 at most three and in eight
of thirteen with tau_3 equal to four, and the reason is density: the vertices carrying a
fan whose three legs have equal N-parity make up about half the graph when tau_3 is two and
a quarter when it is four, at which point two adjacent such vertices start to be missing.
The residue is therefore not the connectivity question 314 advertised - fans always exist -
but a routing question about parity, confined to bridges with tau_3 at least four.


## 317. ADJACENCY WAS NEVER NEEDED - AND 316's THRESHOLD DOES NOT SURVIVE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section removes the adjacency hypothesis from
the Non-Bipartite Y-Shift, which is a strict improvement and is proved; and it retests
316's threshold on a fresh sample, where it fails. Both matter, and the second is a
correction to the previous section.

### 317.1 THE ADJACENCY HYPOTHESIS IS SPURIOUS (PROVED)

  THEOREM. Let c be a colouring with the three terminals monochromatic and N its
  non-crossing edges. Suppose w and w' have OPPOSITE COLOURS and each carries a Y whose
  three legs have the same N-parity, the two parities being equal. Then (SC) fails.

  Proof. (SC) attaches to each terminal pair (i,j) a CONSTANT c_ij with |P| == c_ij (mod 4)
  for every even connecting path P from b_i to b_j. The constant belongs to the pair, not
  to any vertex. At w the legs are internally disjoint, so L_i + L_j is a path; by 295.1
  and the uniform leg parity its length mu_i + mu_j is EVEN, so mu_i + mu_j == c_ij (mod 4).
  The same at w'. Subtracting the three relations,
        e_1 + e_2 == e_1 + e_3 == e_2 + e_3 == 0  (mod 4),  e_m = mu_m - mu'_m,
  whence e_1 = e_2 = e_3 and 2e_1 == 0 (mod 4), so every e_m is EVEN.
  On the other hand 295.1 gives e_m == [c(w) =/= c(b_m)] + [c(w') =/= c(b_m)] +
  |L_m cap N| + |L'_m cap N| (mod 2); the first two brackets DIFFER because c(w') =/= c(w),
  and the last two agree because the two parities are equal, so every e_m is ODD.
  Contradiction. QED

  NOTHING IN THE ARGUMENT TOUCHES THE EDGE ww'. Adjacency merely forced opposite colours,
  which is all that was ever used, and the two fans need not be related in any way.

### 317.2 IT IS STRICTLY BETTER (COMPUTED)

Over 34 bridges with tau >= 2, using the minimum-|N| colouring:

     adjacency version fires                   26
     OPPOSITE-COLOUR version fires             28

and the opposite-colour version fires in every case the adjacency version does, as it must.
The two extra cases are at tau_3 = 3.

### 317.3 CORRECTION: 316's THRESHOLD WAS SAMPLING LUCK

316.2 reported that the Y-shift fires in all 24 bridges with tau_3 <= 3 and called
tau_3 <= 3 a threshold. On this fresh sample:

     tau_3 = 2      13 fire,  0 miss
     tau_3 = 3       5 fire,  3 miss
     tau_3 = 4      10 fire,  3 miss

  So THREE OF EIGHT BRIDGES WITH tau_3 = 3 MISS, under the weakest hypothesis now
  available. 316's "24 of 24" was an artefact of its sample, and I withdraw the threshold.
  What survives is the correlation - tau_3 = 2 has fired in every bridge seen, 26 of 26
  across both samples - and the density explanation of 316.2, which predicts a gradual
  decline and not a cliff. The cliff was mine, not the data's.

### 317.4 Where (N2) stands

The mechanism, in its weakest proved form, leaves 6 of 34 bridges with tau >= 2 untouched.
Those are the whole residue. They are small - the generator produces 13 to 15 vertices -
and by 315.3 they fail (SC) anyway, so each is refutable; what is missing is a UNIFORM
reason. The two obvious directions are to allow the two fans to have DIFFERENT uniform
parities, which changes the parity bookkeeping by a known amount and may be recoverable,
or to use more than two fan-vertices at once.

### 317.5 Status

PROVED here: the Non-Bipartite Y-Shift needs only two vertices of OPPOSITE COLOUR carrying
uniform-parity fans of equal parity - adjacency is spurious, and the two fans may be
unrelated (317.1).
COMPUTED: the weakened form fires in 28 of 34 bridges against 26 for the adjacency form,
dominating it everywhere (317.2).
CORRECTED: 316.2's threshold tau_3 <= 3; on a fresh sample three of eight such bridges
miss, and the threshold is withdrawn, the density argument of 316.2 having predicted a
gradual decline all along (317.3).
NOT PROVED: (N2); six of thirty-four bridges are untouched.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 317 strips the Non-Bipartite Y-Shift to
what it actually uses. The subtraction of the three (SC) relations is legitimate between
ANY two vertices, since the mod-4 constants belong to the terminal pairs; the only thing
the argument needs of the second vertex is that its colour differ, which adjacency was
supplying gratuitously. The weakened mechanism dominates the old one and fires in
twenty-eight of thirty-four bridges of frustration index at least two. It also disposes of
the threshold claimed in the previous section: on a fresh sample three of eight bridges
with tau_3 = 3 miss, so tau_3 <= 3 is not a cutoff and the correlation is the gradual one
that the density argument predicted.


## 318. THE BALANCED FAN THEOREM: the uniform reason, with the scaffolding removed

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Sections 314 to 317 built the Non-Bipartite
Y-Shift out of a colouring, a deleted set N and the parity identity. Studying the misses
shows all of that was scaffolding. The mechanism is a statement about B alone.

### 318.1 sigma IS THE LEG PARITY (PROVED)

For a fan at v whose three legs have equal N-parity p, 295.1 gives
mu_m == [c(v) =/= c(b_m)] + |L_m cap N| (mod 2), and the terminals are coloured 0, so

     mu_1 == mu_2 == mu_3 == c(v) + p == sigma   (mod 2).

SIGMA IS SIMPLY THE COMMON PARITY OF THE THREE LEG LENGTHS. It does not depend on the
colouring, on N, or on p separately. Call a fan BALANCED if its three legs have equal
length parity, and write sigma(Y) for that parity.

### 318.2 THE THEOREM, COLOURING-FREE (PROVED)

  BALANCED FAN THEOREM. If B carries two balanced fans of DIFFERENT leg parity, then (SC)
  fails. The two fans may sit at the same vertex.

  Proof. Let Y have legs L_m of lengths mu_m, all of parity sigma, and Y' legs L'_m of
  lengths mu'_m, all of parity sigma'. The legs of Y are internally disjoint, so L_i + L_j
  is a PATH from b_i to b_j, of length mu_i + mu_j, which is EVEN since mu_i == mu_j. So
  (SC) applies: mu_i + mu_j == c_ij (mod 4), where c_ij is the constant (SC) attaches to
  the pair (i,j). The same for Y'. Subtracting the three relations, with e_m = mu_m - mu'_m,
        e_1 + e_2 == e_1 + e_3 == e_2 + e_3 == 0 (mod 4),
  so e_1 = e_2 = e_3 and 2e_1 == 0 (mod 4): EVERY e_m IS EVEN.
  But e_m = mu_m - mu'_m == sigma + sigma' == 1 (mod 2): EVERY e_m IS ODD. QED

  NO COLOURING, NO DELETED SET, NO PARITY IDENTITY, NO ADJACENCY, NO BOUND ON tau. The
  entire apparatus of 314 to 317 was a way of not noticing that mu_m's parity is the whole
  content. Equivalently:

     (SC) FORCES ALL BALANCED FANS OF B TO HAVE THE SAME LEG PARITY.

### 318.3 WHAT THE MISSES LOOK LIKE (COMPUTED)

Over 33 bridges with tau >= 2 the test fires in 27 - matching the opposite-colour form of
317 exactly, as it must, since sigma differs precisely when that form fires - and the six
misses are strikingly uniform:

     (n, tau, tau_3, sigma-values present, number of balanced fans)
     (13, 2, 3, [1], 1)   (13, 2, 4, [1], 1)   (17, 2, 4, [1], 2)
     (13, 2, 4, [1], 1)   (15, 2, 4, [1], 3)   (13, 2, 4, [1], 1)

  IN EVERY MISS sigma == 1: every balanced fan has ODD legs, and there are only one to
  three balanced fans in the whole graph. So the residue of (N2) is now a single sentence:

     (ODD-FAN)  Can a bridge satisfying (SC) have balanced fans, all of odd leg parity,
                and no balanced fan of even leg parity?

  UNBALANCED FANS GIVE NOTHING, and this is worth recording so the direction is not
  retried: if a fan's leg parities are not all equal, exactly one pair (i,j) has
  mu_i == mu_j, so it yields ONE (SC) relation rather than three; two such fans give
  e_i + e_j == 0 (mod 4), and mod 2 that is automatic from 295.1. No contradiction survives.

### 318.4 Status

PROVED here: sigma is the common parity of the three legs, independent of the colouring
(318.1); and the BALANCED FAN THEOREM - two balanced fans of different leg parity, at the
same vertex or not, refute (SC) - proved from (SC) and internal disjointness alone, with
none of the machinery of 314 to 317 (318.2).
COMPUTED: the test fires in 27 of 33 bridges with tau >= 2, and in all six misses every
balanced fan has ODD legs, there being only one to three balanced fans in total (318.3).
RECORDED AS DEAD: unbalanced fans yield one (SC) relation instead of three, and the
resulting congruence is automatic (318.3).
NOT PROVED: (ODD-FAN), hence (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 318 removes the scaffolding. The
invariant sigma that governed the Y-shift is nothing but the common parity of the three
legs of a fan, so the colouring, the deleted matching and the parity identity all cancel,
and what remains is a statement about the bridge alone: if two fans to the three terminals
each have their three legs of equal length parity, and those two parities differ, then
(SC) fails - because the three concatenations are even connecting paths whose mod-4
constants belong to the terminal pairs, forcing every shift even, while the parities force
every shift odd. So (SC) forces all balanced fans of a bridge to share one leg parity. It
fires in twenty-seven of thirty-three bridges of frustration index at least two, and in
every miss the balanced fans are few and all odd. Whether a bridge satisfying (SC) can have
odd balanced fans and no even one is the whole of what is left.


## 319. (ODD-FAN) IS A delta > 0 PHENOMENON

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section investigates (ODD-FAN) and finds the
parameter that governs it. It is not tau, and not tau_3, but their DIFFERENCE.

### 319.1 THE BIPARTITE CASE, RECOVERED (PROVED)

If B is bipartite with colouring c, then mu_m == c(v) + c(b_m) (mod 2) for every path, so:
  - if the three terminals AGREE in colour, EVERY fan is balanced, with sigma = c(v) +
    c(b_1); as v ranges over both classes sigma takes both values, and 318.2 refutes (SC)
    at once;
  - if they do not agree, NO fan is balanced and 318.2 says nothing.
So the Balanced Fan Theorem contains 205 and 208 as its bipartite special case, and it
already shows what governs it: WHETHER THE TERMINALS CAN BE MADE TO AGREE.

### 319.2 THE PARAMETER (DEFINED, WITH ONE DIRECTION PROVED)

     tau    = least |N| over all colourings          (the frustration index)
     tau_3  = least |N| over colourings with the three terminals MONOCHROMATIC
     delta  = tau_3 - tau ,   so delta = 0 exactly when SOME MINIMUM bipartition already
              has the three terminals agreeing.

  PROVED, ONE DIRECTION. Suppose delta = 0 and fix a minimum N with the terminals
  monochromatic. A fan whose legs AVOID N is balanced with sigma = c(v), by 318.1. So if
  such fans exist at vertices of BOTH colours, sigma takes both values and (SC) fails. At
  delta = 0 the Balanced Fan Theorem therefore reduces to: DO N-AVOIDING FANS EXIST AT
  VERTICES OF BOTH COLOURS - a far weaker demand than 314's (Y-EXIST), which wanted a
  specific adjacent pair.

### 319.3 THE MEASUREMENT

Over 35 bridges with tau >= 2:

     delta    fires / total    mean number of balanced fans
       0        24 / 25                 6.6
       1         3 /  4                 5.0
       2         3 /  6                 3.3

  The balanced-fan population thins as delta grows, exactly as 319.1 predicts: at delta = 0
  the terminals agree in a minimum bipartition and almost every N-avoiding fan is balanced;
  at delta > 0 a leg must detour around an odd cycle to correct its parity, and balanced
  fans become scarce and - as 318.3 recorded - all of one parity.

  SO (ODD-FAN) IS A delta > 0 PHENOMENON. Of the ten bridges with delta > 0, four miss; of
  the twenty-five with delta = 0, ONE misses. That one exception matters and I do not
  explain it: it shows that even at delta = 0 the existence of N-avoiding fans at both
  colours is not automatic, so 319.2's reduction is a reduction and not a proof.

### 319.4 The shape of what is left

     (a) At delta = 0: show N-avoiding fans exist at vertices of both colours. B is
         2-connected and G is 3-connected, and only |N| = tau edges are missing, so this is
         the most tractable statement the programme has reached. One counterexample in the
         sample means it needs a hypothesis, not just an argument.
     (b) At delta > 0: the terminals cannot be aligned by any minimum bipartition, balanced
         fans are scarce, and all observed ones are ODD. This is (ODD-FAN) proper, and
         nothing here touches it.

  A REMARK ON delta. Since flipping a degree-2 terminal changes |N| by 0 or +2 (316.1),
  delta is EVEN whenever it is forced by flips alone - yet delta = 1 occurs, so the minimum
  N with monochromatic terminals is not always obtained by flipping terminals in a minimum
  bipartition. That is a small structural fact worth having: the two minimisations do not
  nest.

### 319.5 Status

PROVED here: the bipartite case of 318.2 - terminals agreeing makes every fan balanced with
sigma = c(v), refuting (SC), which recovers 205 and 208 (319.1); and at delta = 0 the
Balanced Fan Theorem reduces to the existence of N-avoiding fans at vertices of both
colours (319.2).
COMPUTED: firing rates 24/25, 3/4 and 3/6 at delta = 0, 1, 2, with mean balanced-fan counts
6.6, 5.0, 3.3 (319.3); and delta = 1 occurs, so tau_3 is not always reached by flipping
terminals in a minimum bipartition (319.4).
NOT EXPLAINED: the single delta = 0 miss.
NOT PROVED: (ODD-FAN), hence (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 319 finds what (ODD-FAN) depends on. The
Balanced Fan Theorem is really a statement about whether the three terminals can be made to
agree in colour: in a bipartite bridge, agreeing terminals make every fan balanced and
refute (SC) immediately, which is the old bipartite result. The right parameter is
therefore delta, the excess of the least bipartizing set with agreeing terminals over the
least bipartizing set outright. At delta zero every N-avoiding fan is balanced with sigma
equal to the colour of its centre, so two colours suffice, and the mechanism fired in
twenty-four of twenty-five such bridges; as delta grows the balanced fans thin out - 6.6,
5.0, 3.3 on average - and the misses concentrate there. (ODD-FAN) is thus a delta-positive
phenomenon, and the delta-zero case has been reduced to a fan-existence question that one
counterexample in the sample says still needs a hypothesis.


## 320. THE MISSES WERE NOT REAL: exhaustive enumeration removes them all

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section studies the misses of 314 to 319 and
finds they do not exist. They were failures of a randomized fan search, not of the
mechanism. Several conclusions of the preceding six sections fall with them, and I set out
which.

### 320.1 THE MEASUREMENT (COMPUTED)

Every firing rate from 314 onwards used a randomized fan search - 160 attempts per vertex,
each a random BFS reroute. The misses are small, so the fans can instead be enumerated
EXHAUSTIVELY: all simple paths to the first terminal, then all avoiding those, then all
avoiding both. Over 27 bridges with tau >= 2:

     delta = 0     20 fire,  0 miss
     delta = 1      2 fire,  0 miss
     delta = 2      5 fire,  0 miss

     ALL 27 FIRE. THERE ARE NO MISSES.

### 320.2 WHAT FALLS

  - 314.3's "29 of 35", 315.2's repeat of it, 317.2's "28 of 34" and 318.3's "27 of 33"
    were all UNDERSTATEMENTS produced by the search, not properties of the bridges.
  - 316.2's threshold at tau_3 <= 3 was already withdrawn in 317.3 as sampling luck; it was
    worse than that - the quantity it thresholded was search difficulty.
  - 319.3's table - 24/25, 3/4, 3/6 against delta - measured HOW HARD THE SEARCH WAS, not
    how often the mechanism applies. The associated balanced-fan counts, 6.6, 5.0 and 3.3,
    are real and do decline with delta; a randomized search finds a scarce fan less often,
    and that is the whole of the effect. THE CONCLUSION THAT MISSES CONCENTRATE AT delta > 0
    IS WITHDRAWN.
  - 318.3's observation that every miss had sigma = 1 is void: there are no misses.
  - (ODD-FAN), posed in 318.3 and investigated in 319, HAS NO INSTANCE IN ANY SAMPLE TAKEN.

  What survives untouched is everything PROVED: the Balanced Fan Theorem itself (318.2),
  sigma being the leg parity (318.1), the bipartite specialisation recovering 205 and 208
  (319.1), the reduction at delta = 0 (319.2), the bounds tau <= tau_3 <= tau + 4 (316.1),
  and the fact that delta = 1 occurs so the two minimisations do not nest (319.4).

### 320.3 THE LESSON, AND THE CORRECTED TARGET

I generalised from a randomized search three times - 314.4 called the residue a Menger
question, 316.2 announced a threshold, 319.3 built a theory of delta on it - and each time
the residue was an artefact. The rule the programme already had, from 293.4 and 300.3 and
311.3, is that a negative result from an incomplete search is not a negative result. A
randomized path search is an incomplete search.

  With the misses gone the target is a single clean statement:

     (BAL)  EVERY BRIDGE WITH tau >= 2 CARRIES BALANCED FANS OF BOTH LEG PARITIES.

  By 318.2 this implies (N2) outright, hence (INT), (H1*) and the conjecture. It has held
  in every bridge tested exhaustively. It is not proved, and the exhaustive samples are
  small - bridges of 13 to 17 vertices, from cubic graphs on 10 to 12.

### 320.4 Status

COMPUTED: with exhaustive fan enumeration the Balanced Fan Theorem fires in all 27 bridges
with tau >= 2, at every value of delta (320.1).
CORRECTED: the firing rates of 314.3, 315.2, 317.2 and 318.3; the threshold of 316.2; the
delta-dependence of 319.3; and the sigma = 1 pattern of 318.3. All were artefacts of a
randomized fan search. (ODD-FAN) has no known instance (320.2).
NOT PROVED: (BAL), hence (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 320 studies the misses that the last six
sections were built around and finds they are not there. Enumerating fans exhaustively
rather than by randomized search, the Balanced Fan Theorem fires in every one of
twenty-seven bridges of frustration index at least two, at every value of delta. So the
Menger residue of 314, the threshold of 316, the odd-parity pattern of 318 and the
delta-theory of 319 were all measuring how hard it is to find a scarce fan at random, not
any property of the bridges - though the scarcity itself is real and does grow with delta.
What remains is one statement: every bridge of frustration index at least two carries
balanced fans of both leg parities. That implies (N2) and everything above it, it has held
in every bridge enumerated exhaustively, and it is unproved.


## 321. THE ANATOMY OF (BAL)

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. (BAL) - every bridge with tau >= 2 carries balanced
fans of both leg parities - is the single statement left. This section enumerates fans
exhaustively and reports what the balanced ones look like. One natural strengthening dies;
three facts come out; and (BAL) reduces to a Menger statement.

### 321.1 THE MEASUREMENT (COMPUTED, EXHAUSTIVE)

For each bridge with tau >= 2, over every interior vertex, all fans were enumerated and
their leg-parity triples recorded.

     n   tau   sigma=0 vertices   sigma=1 vertices   both   no fan   all 8 triples
    13    2          3                  5             0       0           0
    17    2          8                 14             8       0           0
    15    2          4                  6             0       0           0
    17    3          8                 10             4       0           2
    15    3          6                  9             3       0           0
    13    3          4                  7             1       0           0
    17    2          6                 13             5       0           0
    17    3          9                 11             7       0           2
     ...  (23 bridges in all)

     (BAL)  holds  23 / 23
     (BAL+) holds  14 / 23

### 321.2 THREE FACTS, AND ONE DEAD END

  (i) EVERY INTERIOR VERTEX CARRIES A FAN. The "no fan" column is ZERO in every bridge.
      So the Menger half costs nothing - 3-connectivity of G delivers it - and (BAL) is
      purely about PARITY, never about existence. This confirms 316.3 and settles it.

  (ii) (BAL+) IS FALSE. The strengthening "some single vertex carries balanced fans of
      BOTH parities" fails in 9 of 23 bridges. RECORDED AS DEAD so it is not retried:
      (BAL) genuinely needs two different centres, and no argument that flips all three
      legs at one vertex can work.

  (iii) THE POPULATIONS ARE ASYMMETRIC. In every one of the 23 bridges there are STRICTLY
      MORE sigma = 1 vertices than sigma = 0 vertices - (3,5), (8,14), (4,6), (8,10),
      (4,7), (6,9), (7,11), (6,13), (9,11), and so on without exception. Odd-balanced fans
      outnumber even-balanced ones always. I have no explanation for this and record it as
      an observation; it suggests the even side is the binding constraint, and the least
      count observed there is 3.

  (iv) FAN PARITY IS RIGID. Only about 1 per cent of interior vertices realise all eight
      parity triples. A fan's parities are heavily constrained by where the odd cycles sit,
      which is why (BAL) is a real statement and not a counting triviality.

### 321.3 THE REDUCTION (PROVED)

  Fix ANY colouring with the three terminals monochromatic - one always exists - and let N
  be its non-crossing edges. By 318.1 a fan whose legs AVOID N is balanced with
  sigma = c(v). Hence

     (BAL-W)  for some such colouring, W = B - N contains vertices of BOTH colours
              carrying fans to the three terminals inside W
     implies  (BAL),  hence (N2) by 318.2, hence (INT), (H1*) and the conjecture.

  This is the same Menger question 314 raised, stripped of adjacency and of the parity
  bookkeeping: not a specific adjacent pair, not matched parities, just SOME vertex of each
  colour whose fan survives the deletion of N. By 321.2(i) fans exist everywhere in B; only
  their survival in W is at issue, and |N| is between tau and tau + 4.

### 321.4 Status

COMPUTED, EXHAUSTIVELY: (BAL) holds in all 23 bridges tested with tau >= 2; every interior
vertex carries a fan, in every bridge; sigma = 1 vertices strictly outnumber sigma = 0
vertices, in every bridge, the latter never falling below 3; and about 1 per cent of
vertices realise all eight parity triples (321.1, 321.2).
RECORDED AS DEAD: (BAL+), the single-vertex strengthening, false in 9 of 23 (321.2ii).
PROVED here: (BAL-W) implies (BAL), since an N-avoiding fan is balanced with sigma equal to
the colour of its centre (321.3).
NOT PROVED: (BAL), hence (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.
UNEXPLAINED: why odd-balanced fans always outnumber even-balanced ones (321.2iii).

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 321 dissects (BAL). Exhaustive
enumeration shows it holding in every bridge tested, and shows why it is not trivial: fan
parity is rigid, only one vertex in a hundred realising all eight parity triples. The
obvious strengthening - that one vertex carries balanced fans of both parities - is FALSE,
failing in nine of twenty-three, so any proof must use two centres. What is free is
existence: every interior vertex carries a fan, in every bridge, so the Menger content
costs nothing and (BAL) is purely a parity statement. And there is an unexplained
asymmetry - odd-balanced fans outnumber even-balanced ones in every bridge without
exception, the even count never dropping below three, which points at the even side as the
binding one. (BAL) reduces to asking that fans of both colours survive the deletion of a
bipartizing set of size between tau and tau + 4.


## 322. (BAL-W): the colouring must be chosen for CONNECTIVITY, not for size

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. (BAL-W) implies (BAL) by 321.3 and hence (N2). This
section attacks it, finds it true in every bridge tested, identifies the real obstruction -
which is not what 316 said - and gives a sufficient condition.

### 322.1 THE MEASUREMENT (COMPUTED, EXHAUSTIVE FANS)

Over 22 bridges with tau >= 2, searching 14 colourings with monochromatic terminals per
bridge and enumerating fans in W = B - N exhaustively:

     (BAL-W) holds for SOME colouring                22 / 22
     the MINIMUM-|N| colouring suffices              20 / 22
     W disconnected for at least one colouring       22 / 22

### 322.2 CORRECTION TO 316.1

316.1 concluded that "smaller N is strictly better, so the minimum-|N| colouring is the
right one and searching is pointless". BOTH HALVES ARE WRONG.
  - The evidence for it was a randomized fan search, which 320 showed to be unreliable.
  - And the conclusion is false on its own terms: the minimum-|N| colouring FAILS (BAL-W)
    in 2 of 22 bridges, where another colouring with a LARGER N succeeds.
Smaller N leaves more legs of parity 0, which is what 316 was looking at, but it also
deletes edges wherever they are cheapest, and that is not where they can be spared.
SEARCHING THE COLOURINGS IS NECESSARY.

### 322.3 THE REAL OBSTRUCTION

W was disconnected for at least one colouring in EVERY bridge tested. That is the thing to
avoid: a component of W missing a terminal carries no fan at all, so its vertices are lost
whatever their colour, and if one colour class survives only in such a component, (BAL-W)
fails for that colouring. The binding quantity is therefore THE CONNECTIVITY OF W, not the
size of N, and the two are not aligned - a minimum N is a maximum cut, which is precisely
the deletion most likely to cut W in two.

### 322.4 A SUFFICIENT CONDITION (PROVED)

Let W* be W with its degree-2 vertices SUPPRESSED, except the three terminals, each
suppression replacing two edges by one; paths of W* lift to paths of W.

  CLAIM. If W* is 3-connected then (BAL-W) holds for that colouring.
  Proof. In a 3-connected graph the fan lemma gives, for any vertex v and any three other
  vertices, three internally disjoint paths from v to them. So every vertex of W* carries a
  fan to the three terminals, and lifting gives a fan in W at every branch vertex of W. The
  branch vertices are all but the 3 + 2|N| vertices of degree 2, so both colour classes of
  the bipartite graph W contain one, and their colours differ. QED

  SO (BAL-W), HENCE (N2), HENCE THE CONJECTURE, FOLLOWS FROM:

     (CONN)  every bridge admits a colouring with the three terminals monochromatic for
             which the suppression of B - N is 3-connected.

  That is a statement about choosing a cut, with no parity in it at all. It is the first
  time the programme's residue has been free of mod-4 arithmetic.

### 322.5 Status

COMPUTED, with exhaustive fan enumeration: (BAL-W) holds for some monochromatic colouring
in all 22 bridges tested with tau >= 2; the minimum-|N| colouring suffices in only 20 of
them; and W is disconnected for at least one colouring in all 22 (322.1).
CORRECTED: 316.1's claim that the minimum-|N| colouring is the right one and searching is
pointless - it rested on the unreliable search of 320 and is false in 2 of 22 bridges
(322.2).
PROVED here: if the suppression of W is 3-connected then (BAL-W) holds, by the fan lemma
and the fact that all but 3 + 2|N| vertices are branch vertices (322.4).
NOT PROVED: (CONN), hence (BAL-W), (BAL), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 322 attacks (BAL-W) and finds it true in
every bridge tested, but not for the reason the programme expected. The minimum-|N|
colouring - the one earlier sections insisted was optimal - fails in two of twenty-two,
because a minimum N is a maximum cut and a maximum cut is exactly the deletion most likely
to disconnect what is left; and a component of W missing a terminal carries no fan at all.
So the colouring must be chosen for the CONNECTIVITY of B - N rather than the smallness of
N, and searching the colourings is necessary, contrary to 316. With that understood, the
fan lemma finishes the job: if the suppression of B - N is 3-connected then every branch
vertex carries a fan, both colour classes contain branch vertices, and (BAL-W) follows.
What is left is a pure connectivity statement, free of mod-4 arithmetic for the first time
in the programme: some colouring with agreeing terminals leaves B - N 3-connected after
suppression.


## 323. (CONN) CORRECTED, AND WHAT A MAXIMUM CUT GIVES FOR FREE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section corrects the statement of (CONN),
which as posed in 322.4 has no instances, replaces it with the right one, and proves the
part of it that comes from a single elegant observation about maximum cuts.

### 323.1 CORRECTION: 322.4's (CONN) IS UNSATISFIABLE

322.4 formed W* by suppressing the degree-2 vertices of W "except the three terminals" and
asked for W* to be 3-connected. But a terminal has degree 2 in B, hence AT MOST 2 in
W = B - N, so W* always contains a vertex of degree at most 2 and is NEVER 3-connected. The
condition is empty and the claim built on it, though correctly argued from its hypothesis,
was vacuous. The error was using the fan lemma, which wants 3-connectivity of the whole
graph, where the natural tool is Menger.

### 323.2 THE RIGHT OBJECT (PROVED)

Adjoin an APEX: let W+ be W together with a new vertex T* joined to b_1, b_2 and b_3. A fan
at v to the three terminals inside W is precisely a set of three internally disjoint
v-T* paths in W+, so BY MENGER it exists if and only if no 2-cut of W+ separates v from T*.
Suppressing degree-2 vertices preserves this. Hence

  CLAIM. If the suppression of W+ is 3-CONNECTED, every branch vertex of W carries a fan,
  so both colour classes are represented and (BAL-W) holds.

  (CONN+)  every bridge admits a colouring with the three terminals monochromatic for which
           the suppression of W+ = (B - N) + apex is 3-connected.

  The terminals are no longer an obstruction: with two crossing edges each they have degree
  3 in W+, and with fewer they are suppressed away.

### 323.3 THE LOCAL OPTIMALITY LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let the colouring maximise the cut SUBJECT TO the three terminals agreeing. Then
    (a) every non-terminal vertex has at least half its edges crossing - so every degree-3
        vertex has AT LEAST TWO, and W has minimum degree 2 away from the terminals;
    (b) cross(b_1) + cross(b_2) + cross(b_3) >= 3.
  Proof. (a) Flipping a single non-terminal vertex preserves the constraint and changes the
  cut by (non-crossing at v) - (crossing at v), which must be at most 0.
  (b) The terminals are pairwise at distance at least 5 (213.1), hence pairwise
  non-adjacent, so flipping ALL THREE - which preserves the constraint - changes each
  terminal's edges independently: cross(b_i) becomes 2 - cross(b_i), and the cut changes by
  6 - 2 sum cross(b_i), which must be at most 0. QED

  MEASURED: the minimum crossing-degree at non-terminals was exactly 2 in all 21 bridges
  tested, so (a) is tight and W really does sit at minimum degree 2.

### 323.4 The gap, stated exactly

  (CONN+) holds for some colouring in ALL 21 bridges tested; a LOCALLY MAXIMUM cut suffices
  in 16 of them, and in the other 5 some other colouring is needed.

  So the elegant argument delivers MINIMUM DEGREE 2 and no more, while (CONN+) needs
  3-CONNECTIVITY AFTER SUPPRESSION. That is the whole gap, and it is the familiar one:
  local moves control degrees, not connectivity. Two things would close it -
    - a global exchange argument: given a 2-cut of the suppressed W+, exhibit a flip that
      strictly increases the cut or reduces the number of 2-cuts, so that a suitably chosen
      extremal colouring has none; or
    - a proof that minimum degree 2 plus girth 5 in B plus 3-connectivity of G forces the
      suppressed W+ to be 3-connected, which is false in general graphs but may hold here.

### 323.5 Status

CORRECTED: 322.4's (CONN) is unsatisfiable, a terminal having degree at most 2 in W, so
the suppressed W* is never 3-connected; the claim resting on it was vacuous (323.1).
PROVED here: a fan in W is three internally disjoint paths to an apex, so by Menger
3-connectivity of the suppressed W+ gives fans at all branch vertices and hence (BAL-W)
(323.2); and, for a cut maximum subject to agreeing terminals, every non-terminal has at
least two crossing edges and the three terminals have at least three between them, the
second by flipping all three at once, which is legitimate because they are pairwise
non-adjacent (323.3).
COMPUTED: (CONN+) holds for some colouring in all 21 bridges with tau >= 2; a locally
maximum cut suffices in 16; the minimum crossing-degree at non-terminals is exactly 2 in
all 21 (323.3, 323.4).
NOT PROVED: (CONN+), hence (BAL-W), (BAL), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 323 repairs the statement the previous
section left. Keeping the terminals unsuppressed made 3-connectivity impossible, since a
terminal has only two edges to begin with; adjoining an apex joined to the three terminals
turns a fan into three disjoint paths to a single vertex, and then Menger asks exactly for
3-connectivity of the suppressed graph, with the terminals no longer in the way. The
elegant half is then immediate: take the cut maximum among those with agreeing terminals,
and flipping one non-terminal shows every such vertex keeps two crossing edges, while
flipping all three terminals at once - legal because they are pairwise far apart - shows
they retain three between them. So the deleted set never strips a vertex below degree two,
and measurement confirms that bound is tight. What local optimality cannot deliver is
3-connectivity, and that single step is now the whole of the distance to the conjecture.


## 324. BOTH EXCHANGE ROUTES TO (CONN+) ARE BLOCKED

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 323.4 proposed two ways to close the gap between
minimum degree 2 and 3-connectivity: a flip that improves the cut, or a greedy improvement
of connectivity. This section shows the first cannot exist and the second does not work,
and records the one structural fact that survives.

### 324.1 THE MAXIMUM CUT CANNOT BE REPAIRED (PROVED)

Suppose the suppressed W+ has a 2-cut and one wants a flip that removes it while keeping
the cut maximum. No such flip exists. At a maximum cut every non-terminal v has at most one
non-crossing edge (323.3a), so flipping v changes the cut by (non-crossing) - (crossing)
<= 1 - 2 = -1: EVERY FLIP STRICTLY DECREASES THE CUT. So a repairing flip always leaves the
maximum, and the first route of 323.4 is not merely unproved but IMPOSSIBLE. This is the
same lesson as 322.2 - a maximum cut is a worst case for connectivity, not a best one - and
it should have been drawn there.

### 324.2 WHAT SURVIVES: 2-CUTS COST AN N-EDGE (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let {x,y} be a 2-cut of W+ separating a set K from the apex T*. Then K contains no
  terminal, since a terminal is adjacent to T*. Hence EITHER {x,y} is already a 2-cut of B
  separating K, OR some edge of N leaves K.
  Proof. If no edge of N leaves K then all edges of B leaving K lie in W, hence run to
  {x,y}, so {x,y} separates K in B. QED

  So every 2-cut of W+ that is not inherited from B consumes an N-edge, and |N| <= tau + 4
  by 316.1. The obstructions are FEW. This is the quantitative handle the problem offers.

### 324.3 GREEDY CONNECTIVITY FAILS TOO (COMPUTED)

The second route was to hill-climb on
     f(c) = number of branch vertices of W carrying a fan to the three terminals,
computed by Menger as a unit-vertex-capacity flow to the apex. Over 17 bridges with
tau >= 2, starting from random monochromatic colourings:

     local search reaches a colouring witnessing (BAL-W)        6
     local search STUCK                                        11
       of which stuck at ZERO fan-carrying vertices             7

  The landscape is bad: from a random start with no fan-carrying vertex, no single flip
  creates one, so the search never leaves zero. THE OBJECTIVE HAS SPURIOUS LOCAL OPTIMA and
  greedy improvement is not an argument. Note this does NOT bear on the truth of (CONN+),
  which held for some colouring in 21 of 21 bridges by search over random colourings
  (323.4); it bears on the METHOD.

### 324.4 What is left, and what it now needs

Both routes proposed in 323.4 are closed: the cut-improving flip cannot exist, and the
connectivity-improving flip does not reach the optimum. (CONN+) is true in every bridge
tested and unreachable by any local move so far tried, which means the proof must be
NON-LOCAL. The one asset is 324.2: the bad 2-cuts number at most |N| <= tau + 4, so a
counting or averaging argument over colourings - showing that no single colouring can be
bad in every place at once - is the shape that remains, rather than an exchange.

### 324.5 Status

PROVED here: at a maximum cut every flip strictly decreases the cut, so 323.4's first route
is impossible (324.1); and every 2-cut of W+ is either inherited from B or crosses an
N-edge, so the obstructions number at most |N| (324.2).
COMPUTED: greedy local search on the number of fan-carrying vertices reaches (BAL-W) in
only 6 of 17 bridges and stalls at zero in 7, the objective having spurious local optima
(324.3).
NOT PROVED: (CONN+), hence (BAL-W), (BAL), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 324 closes both routes the previous
section proposed. A cut-improving repair cannot exist, because at a maximum cut every
vertex has at most one non-crossing edge and so every flip strictly loses ground - the
maximum cut is the worst case for connectivity, not the best, which 322 had already
signalled. And a connectivity-improving repair fails in practice: hill-climbing on the
number of fan-carrying vertices stalls in eleven of seventeen bridges, seven of them at
zero, because from a colouring with no such vertex no single flip creates one. What
survives is a counting handle: a 2-cut of the apexed graph either came from the bridge
itself or must be crossed by one of the at most tau + 4 deleted edges, so the obstructions
are few and located. The proof of (CONN+), which holds in every bridge tested, will have to
average over colourings rather than exchange within one.


## 325. WHAT THE FAILURES TEACH, AND THE ONE MOVE THAT KEPT WORKING

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Sections 294 to 324 contain more retracted claims
than any comparable stretch of this programme. This section sorts them, extracts the rule
each violated, and applies the one technique that never failed.

### 325.1 THE FAILURES, SORTED

  (A) NEGATIVE RESULTS FROM INCOMPLETE SEARCHES - five times.
      311.3 predicted the extremal graph rigid, by a shift calculus that silently assumed
      connecting paths do not zigzag. 314.3, 315.2, 317.2 and 318.3 reported miss rates
      produced by a randomized fan search; 320 enumerated exhaustively and found NO MISSES,
      voiding the Menger residue of 314.4, the threshold of 316.2 and the whole delta
      theory of 319. 316.2's "24 of 24" was additionally a small sample.
      RULE VIOLATED: the programme's own, from 293.4 and 300.3 - an incomplete search
      yields no negative result. A randomized path search is incomplete. The exhaustive
      enumeration that settled it cost minutes and could have been run at 314.

  (B) OPTIMISING THE WRONG QUANTITY - twice, in the same direction.
      316.1 declared the minimum-|N| colouring optimal and searching pointless; 322.2 found
      it fails outright. 323.4 proposed repairing a cut while keeping it maximum; 324.1
      proved no such repair can exist. Both times the quantity that is easy to optimise -
      the SIZE of the deleted set - was chosen over the one that matters, its effect on
      CONNECTIVITY, and the two are anti-correlated: a minimum N is a maximum cut, which is
      the deletion most likely to disconnect.
      RULE: before adopting an extremal principle, check it correlates with the target.

  (C) A CONDITION WITH NO INSTANCES - once.
      322.4's (CONN) asked a graph containing a degree-2 vertex to be 3-connected. The
      argument from it was valid and the hypothesis unsatisfiable.
      RULE: instantiate a sufficient condition on one example before building on it.

  (D) GENERALISING FROM ONE WITNESS - twice. 311.3 from a single 18-vertex graph; 319 from
      a single sample.

### 325.2 THE MOVE THAT NEVER FAILED

Every advance in this stretch came from REMOVING A HYPOTHESIS, never from adding one:
     315.1  the fan's legs need not avoid N, only carry equal parity
     317.1  the two fan-centres need not be adjacent, only differently coloured
     318.1  sigma is just the leg parity - the colouring, N and the parity identity all
            cancel, and the Balanced Fan Theorem is a statement about B alone
Each time the question "what does the proof actually USE?" returned "less than assumed",
and each time the result got stronger AND shorter. The failures all came from the opposite
motion - extrapolating structure from computation.

### 325.3 THE LENS APPLIED ONCE MORE (PROVED)

Sum the three (SC) relations of a SINGLE balanced fan:
     (mu_1+mu_2) + (mu_1+mu_3) + (mu_2+mu_3) = 2(mu_1+mu_2+mu_3) == c_12+c_13+c_23 (mod 4),
and mu_1+mu_2+mu_3 == 3 sigma == sigma (mod 2), so writing mu_1+mu_2+mu_3 = sigma + 2k the
left side is 2 sigma + 4k. Hence, with S := c_12 + c_13 + c_23,

     S == 2 sigma  (mod 4),   that is   SIGMA == S/2  (mod 2).

  ONE BALANCED FAN ALREADY PINS SIGMA TO AN INVARIANT OF B. So 318.2's two-fan comparison
  was itself a hypothesis too many: (SC) does not merely force all balanced fans to agree,
  it DETERMINES the value they must take, from the three mod-4 constants alone. (BAL) is
  then the assertion that a determined quantity takes two values.

### 325.4 WHAT TO DO NEXT

  (i) ATTACK ONLY THE EVEN SIDE. 321.2(iii) found odd-balanced fans outnumbering
      even-balanced ones in every bridge, the even count never below 3. With sigma now
      pinned by S, the target is a single existence statement:
         SOME VERTEX OF B CARRIES A FAN WHOSE THREE LEGS ARE ALL EVEN,
      together with the same for odd. The odd side is the abundant one; the even side binds.
  (ii) DROP (CONN+) UNLESS IT SIMPLIFIES. It was reached by three successive strengthenings
      - 321.3, 322.4, 323.2 - and 324 blocked both routes to it. By 325.2 the productive
      direction is the reverse: ask what the even-fan statement actually needs.
  (iii) NEVER AGAIN REPORT A MISS FROM A RANDOMIZED SEARCH.

### 325.5 Status

PROVED here: S = c_12 + c_13 + c_23 == 2 sigma (mod 4), so a single balanced fan determines
sigma from the (SC) constants, and 318.2 follows without comparing two fans (325.3).
COMPUTED: of 195 bridges generated, NONE satisfies (SC) - every one has an interior vertex,
which is exactly what (INT) predicts, so the formula had no non-vacuous instance to be
tested against (325.3).
NOT PROVED: the existence of an even balanced fan, hence (BAL), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 325 sorts this stretch's retractions. Five
came from treating an incomplete search as a negative result - the programme's own rule,
broken repeatedly, and one exhaustive enumeration voided six sections at a stroke. Two came
from optimising the size of the deleted set when connectivity was what mattered, quantities
that pull against each other. One came from posing a condition that a degree-2 vertex makes
unsatisfiable. Against that, every genuine advance came from removing a hypothesis rather
than adding one, and applying that lens once more shows even the Balanced Fan Theorem
carried a redundant assumption: summing the three relations of a SINGLE balanced fan gives
c_12 + c_13 + c_23 == 2 sigma modulo 4, so (SC) does not merely make all balanced fans
agree, it fixes the value they must take. What is left is one existence statement - that
some vertex carries a fan with all three legs even - and by the counts of 321 that is the
binding half.


## 326. PARITY IS FREE PER LEG; THE DIFFICULTY IS DISJOINTNESS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 325.4 set the target: some vertex of B carries a
fan whose three legs are all EVEN. This section tests three candidate characterisations of
such vertices. One is refuted; the other two turn out to be UNIVERSAL, and both are
provable, which relocates the difficulty precisely.

### 326.1 THE MEASUREMENT

Over interior vertices of bridges, with fans enumerated exhaustively:

     H1  d(v,b_m) even for all three m        REFUTED as a characterisation: of the 17
         vertices carrying an even balanced fan, 15 fail H1
     H2  both parities of v-b_m path achievable, for all three m
                                              TRUE at all 50 vertices tested
     H3  v lies on an odd cycle               TRUE at all 50 vertices tested

  And all 5 bridges carried an even balanced fan, as (BAL) requires.

### 326.2 BOTH UNIVERSALS ARE THEOREMS (PROVED)

  LEMMA A. In a 2-connected NON-BIPARTITE graph every vertex lies on an odd cycle.
  Proof. Let C be an odd cycle and v a vertex not on it. By 2-connectivity there are two
  disjoint paths from v to C, of lengths p and q, meeting C exactly at their endpoints
  x =/= y. These split C into arcs A_1, A_2 with |A_1| + |A_2| = |C| ODD, so the arcs have
  different parities, and the two cycles of lengths p + q + |A_1| and p + q + |A_2| differ
  in parity. One is odd, and both pass through v. QED

  LEMMA B (PARITY FREEDOM). In a 2-connected non-bipartite graph, for any two vertices v
  and t there are v-t paths of BOTH parities.
  Proof. By Lemma A, v lies on an odd cycle C. Since the graph is 2-connected, B - v is
  connected and C \ {v} is non-empty, so there is a t-to-(C \ {v}) path in B - v; truncate
  it at its first vertex of C to get Q with Q meeting C exactly at one endpoint u =/= v.
  The two arcs of C from v to u have DIFFERENT parities, C being odd, and each meets Q only
  at u. So arc_1 + Q and arc_2 + Q are v-t paths of different parities. QED

  B is 2-connected and, having tau >= 2, non-bipartite, so both apply to every bridge in
  question. This explains H2 and H3 completely: they are not properties of the sigma = 0
  vertices, they hold everywhere.

### 326.3 WHERE THE DIFFICULTY ACTUALLY IS

Lemma B says each leg's parity can be set FREELY AND INDEPENDENTLY. If the three legs could
be chosen independently, an even balanced fan would exist at EVERY vertex and (BAL) would
be immediate. They cannot, because a fan requires the legs to be INTERNALLY DISJOINT.

     SO THE EVEN-FAN STATEMENT CONTAINS NO PARITY DIFFICULTY AT ALL. It is entirely a
     question of realising three prescribed parities SIMULTANEOUSLY under disjointness.

  This also explains 321.2(iv), which found only about 1 per cent of vertices realising all
  eight parity triples: per leg the parity is free, but the parity-flipping detours of
  Lemma B compete for the same vertices, and disjointness couples them. It also explains
  321.2(ii), that no single vertex need carry both parities - the coupling can forbid it -
  and 321.2(iii)'s asymmetry, since the odd triple is reachable by shorter detours.

  THE TARGET IS THEREFORE A PARITY-CONSTRAINED DISJOINT PATHS PROBLEM: in a 2-connected
  subcubic graph of girth 5 with three degree-2 terminals pairwise at distance at least 5,
  find a vertex admitting three internally disjoint EVEN paths to them. Parity-constrained
  disjoint paths is hard in general; here there are only three paths, the graph is subcubic,
  and Lemma B supplies a flip at every leg individually.

### 326.4 Status

PROVED here: Lemma A, every vertex of a 2-connected non-bipartite graph lies on an odd
cycle; and Lemma B, both path parities are available between any two vertices of such a
graph (326.2). Together they show the per-leg parity of a fan is completely free.
COMPUTED: H1 is refuted as a characterisation, 15 of 17 even-fan vertices failing it; H2
and H3 hold at all 50 vertices tested, as the lemmas require; all 5 bridges carry an even
balanced fan (326.1).
NOT PROVED: the simultaneous realisation - that some vertex admits three internally
disjoint even legs - hence (BAL), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 326 tests what distinguishes a vertex
carrying an all-even fan and finds that nothing does: the two properties that hold at every
such vertex hold at every vertex whatever, and both are theorems. Every vertex of a
2-connected non-bipartite graph lies on an odd cycle, because two disjoint paths from the
vertex to an odd cycle split it into arcs of opposite parity; and consequently any two
vertices are joined by paths of both parities, by detouring around that cycle. So the
parity of each leg of a fan is free and independent, and if the legs could be chosen
separately every vertex would carry an all-even fan. They cannot: the legs must be
