     configurations admitting an even
       T-free connecting path                8 to 12 of 12 per bridge
     even T-free paths tested                541 total  (31 to 89 per bridge)
     (THREAD)-witness paths                  541 OF 541 - profile {0,1} EVERY TIME

  Not one tested path, in any bridge, at any theta, failed to attach at both position

### 376.5 Status

## 377. (T1) DICHOTOMY: THE THETA EXISTS UNLESS THE BRIDGE IS ONE OF TWO NAMED WORLDS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section proves that the theta of 376 exists
in every bridge with tau >= 2 EXCEPT in two rigid configurations, characterises the
first completely - it is the tau = 2 boundary with a frustrated triple - and names the
second. (T1) reduces to killing the two worlds.

### 377.1 THE DICHOTOMY (PROVED)

  THEOREM. Let B be a bridge with tau >= 2 in which (T1) FAILS: no labelling k admits a
  structure T of 376.1. Then BOTH of the following hold:
     (W0) no odd cycle of B meets exactly one terminal;
     and for every odd cycle C avoiding all terminals (if any) and every k,
     (WC) b_k is separated from C in B - {b_i, b_j} by at most ONE vertex.
  Proof. If some odd cycle C meets exactly one terminal b_k, then C avoids b_i, b_j and
  the degenerate T = C of 376.1 exists: contradiction. If some odd cycle C avoids all
  terminals and some k admits two b_k-to-C paths, vertex-disjoint except at b_k and
  internally avoiding b_i and b_j, the theta T exists: contradiction. By MENGER in
  B - {b_i, b_j}, the failure of two such paths for every k is exactly (WC). QED

  So a (T1)-refusing bridge is in one of two worlds:
     WORLD W2:  no terminal-free odd cycle exists; with (W0), EVERY odd cycle meets at
                least TWO terminals.
     WORLD WC:  terminal-free odd cycles exist, and every one of them is Menger-blocked
                from every terminal as in (WC).

### 377.2 WORLD W2 IS THE tau = 2 BOUNDARY WITH A FRUSTRATED TRIPLE (PROVED)

  THEOREM. In world W2: (i) tau = 2 EXACTLY; (ii) in the cubic graph G, the graph
  G' := G - {e_1, e_2, e_3} is BIPARTITE, and each subdivided edge e_m either joins
  SAME-COLOURED ends of G' or joins two components of G'.
  Proof. (i) Every odd cycle contains at least two terminals, hence BOTH edges of at
  least one of b_1, b_2 or both edges of b_2, b_3-style pairs; delete one edge at b_1
  and one at b_2: an odd cycle containing b_1 dies at b_1, and one avoiding b_1
  contains b_2 and b_3, dying at b_2. So tau <= 2, and tau >= 2 is given.
  (ii) A cycle of B through the subdivision vertex b_m is a cycle of G through e_m,
  with B-length = G-length + (number of subdivided edges used). A terminal-free
  B-odd cycle is a G'-odd cycle: there are none, so G' is bipartite. A B-odd cycle
  through exactly b_m is a G-cycle through e_m alone, of G-length 1 + p with p a
  G'-path between the ends of e_m, and B-length 2 + p: B-odd forces p ODD, which in
  bipartite G' means OPPOSITE-coloured ends. (W0) forbids it: so p is even whenever
  the ends are joined - SAME-coloured ends - or no path exists. QED

  So W2 is completely explicit: a bipartite core G' plus three frustrated chords, the
  signed-graph shape of the Lovasz-Slilaty pointer (223.5), sitting at the exact
  boundary tau = 2 that separates the closed (N1) from the open (N2). It is the
  smallest possible enemy, and it is now a single concrete structure, not a class.

### 377.3 WORLD WC: THREE MIXED CUTS AROUND ONE CYCLE

In WC, for a fixed terminal-free odd cycle C, each k supplies a vertex x_k such that
{b_i, b_j, x_k} separates b_k from C in B. In G-terms: the mixed cut of two edges
e_i, e_j and one vertex x_k separates the region of e_k from C - and this must happen
FOR ALL THREE k SIMULTANEOUSLY, around every terminal-free odd cycle. G is
3-connected, so each such cut is tight, and three tight mixed cuts must nest around C.
No further structure is proved here; the configuration is RECORDED as (WC-KILL), open.

## 378. THE DEATH OF W2: THE FIRST WORLD IS EMPTY

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Section 377 reduced (T1) to killing two worlds.
This section kills the first outright: no bridge with tau >= 2 lies in W2. The proof is
parity bookkeeping on the cubic graph G, and it yields a stronger corollary - every
bridge with tau >= 2 carries an odd cycle through AT MOST ONE terminal, the seed the
theta of 376 needs.

### 378.1 THE TWO SHAPES OF W2 (PROVED)

By 377.2, in W2 the graph G' = G - {e_1, e_2, e_3} is bipartite and every e_m joins
same-coloured ends of G' or joins two components. G is 3-connected cubic, hence
3-edge-connected, so deleting three edges leaves at most two components, and G' is
disconnected only if {e_1, e_2, e_3} is a 3-edge-cut, in which case there are EXACTLY
two components and ALL THREE edges cross between them. So W2 splits:
     W2a:  G' CONNECTED bipartite, all three e_m joining same-coloured ends;
     W2b:  G' = K disjoint-union K', both bipartite, all three e_m crossing.

### 378.2 W2a FORCES B BIPARTITE (PROVED)

  Fix the 2-colouring chi of G'. A cycle of B using j of the subdivided edges has
  B-length = G-length + j, and deleting its j chord-edges decomposes it into j paths
  of G' whose endpoint multiset is exactly the 2j chord-ends used, each once. Each
  path's parity is the chi-difference of its two endpoints, so the paths' total parity
  is the sum of chi over all 2j ends. In W2a both ends of e_m have one colour alpha_m,
  so that sum is 2 alpha_(m_1) + ... == 0 (mod 2), REGARDLESS of how the cycle pairs
  the ends. Hence:
     j = 0:  G'-cycle, even (G' bipartite);           B-length even.
     j >= 1: G-length == j + 0 (mod 2);               B-length = G-length + j == 2j == 0.
  EVERY CYCLE OF B IS EVEN: B is bipartite, tau = 0. CONTRADICTION with tau >= 2. QED

### 378.3 W2b FORCES tau <= 1 (PROVED)

  Colour K and K' independently, chi_K and chi_K'. Orient each e_m as (u_m in K,
  u_m' in K'), and set the SIGN s_m := chi_K(u_m) + chi_K'(u_m') (mod 2). A cycle of B
  alternates sides at each crossing edge, so it uses an EVEN number of the e_m: j is 0
  or 2 (j = 1 cannot close, j = 3 is odd).
     j = 0: inside K or K', even.
     j = 2, through e_m and e_l: it is e_m + P (in K) + e_l + P' (in K'), of B-length
        2 + |P| + |P'| + 2 == chi_K(u_m) + chi_K(u_l) + chi_K'(u_m') + chi_K'(u_l')
        == s_m + s_l (mod 2).
  So B has an odd cycle iff two signs differ. Three signs in {0,1}: either ALL EQUAL -
  B bipartite, tau = 0 - or a 2-1 SPLIT with minority sign at e_m*: every odd cycle of
  B uses e_m*, hence passes the degree-2 terminal b_m* and uses BOTH its edges;
  deleting one edge of b_m* bipartizes B, tau <= 1. Either way tau <= 1:
  CONTRADICTION with tau >= 2. QED

  THEOREM (THE DEATH OF W2). No bridge with tau >= 2 lies in world W2. QED
  377.2's characterisation was the scaffold; the world it described cannot coexist
  with tau >= 2 at all.

### 378.4 THE SEED COROLLARY (PROVED)

  COROLLARY. Every bridge with tau >= 2 contains an odd cycle meeting AT MOST ONE
  terminal.
  Proof. If every odd cycle met at least two terminals, the bridge would be in W2
  (377.1's W0 holds a fortiori, and no terminal-free odd cycle exists), which is
  empty. QED

  If the cycle meets EXACTLY one terminal b_k, it avoids b_i and b_j and the
  DEGENERATE T of 376.1 exists: (T1) HOLDS. So after this section:

     (T1) fails  ==>  a terminal-free odd cycle exists AND world WC governs:
                      every terminal-free odd cycle is Menger-blocked as in 377.1,
                      and no odd cycle meets exactly one terminal.

CHECKED, tools/seed378.py, seed 378: twelve of twelve bridges with tau >= 2 carry a
TERMINAL-FREE odd cycle - stronger than the corollary needs.

### 378.5 Status

PROVED here: W2 splits into W2a and W2b by 3-edge-connectivity (378.1); W2a forces B
bipartite, by the endpoint-multiset parity argument, regardless of how cycles thread

COMPUTED: 12 of 12 bridges carry a terminal-free odd cycle (378.4).
NOT PROVED: the death of WC; (T2); (T3); hence (THREAD), (BP2), (N2), (INT), (H1*),
and the conjecture.

worlds. If every odd cycle of the bridge met two or more terminals, the bipartite core
plus chords structure of 377.2 would govern, and counting colours around any cycle -
the endpoint multiset makes the count independent of the threading - shows every cycle
of B would be even when the core is connected, while a disconnected core forces an
even number of crossings and a sign argument that either bipartizes B or funnels every
odd cycle through one terminal of degree two, where a single edge deletion kills it.
Both conclusions contradict tau >= 2. So the world is empty, and with it comes the
seed: every bridge with tau >= 2 owns an odd cycle meeting at most one terminal - if
exactly one, the theta degenerates and (T1) holds outright; if none, only the
Menger-blocked world WC remains between the programme and (THREAD).


## 379. THE LOLLIPOP: (T1) IS A THEOREM AND WORLD WC DISSOLVES

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The theta of 376 demanded two disjoint paths
from b_k to the odd cycle, and 377 found the Menger obstruction WC. This section shows
the second path was never needed: a single path suffices if the live set is read
correctly, and a single path ALWAYS exists by 3-edge-connectivity. (T1) is proved, WC
was an artifact, and the front advances to (T2) and (T3') alone.

### 379.1 THE LOLLIPOP PARITY LEMMA (PROVED)

Let C be an odd cycle avoiding b_i and b_j, and either b_k lies on C (set R empty,
c := b_k) or R is a path from b_k to C, internally avoiding C and all terminals,
meeting C at c. Put T := C union R and LIVE(T) := C - {c}.

  LEMMA. Every s in LIVE(T) is joined to b_k by paths of BOTH parities inside T.
  Proof. The two arcs of C from s to c have lengths summing to |C|, odd, so their
  parities differ; each meets R only at c, and appending R (or nothing, in the
  degenerate case c = b_k) gives two s-to-b_k paths of opposite parities. QED

  Only vertices of R fail to be live - a route entering R must run its remainder to
  b_k in one fixed way. 376's second disjoint path bought liveness of R at the price
  of the Menger obstruction; dropping it costs only the shrinkage of LIVE to C - {c}.

### 379.2 (T1) IS A THEOREM (PROVED); WC DISSOLVES

  THEOREM. Every bridge with tau >= 2 admits a structure T of 379.1 for some
  labelling k - in fact, in the terminal-free case, for EVERY k.
  Proof. By the SEED COROLLARY (378.4) there is an odd cycle C meeting at most one
  terminal. If it meets exactly one, that terminal is b_k, C avoids b_i, b_j, and the
  degenerate T = C stands. If it meets none, fix any k. G is 3-connected cubic, hence
  3-edge-connected, so G - e_i - e_j is CONNECTED; paths of B from b_k avoiding b_i
  and b_j are exactly the paths of G - e_i - e_j from the subdivision point of e_k, so
  b_k reaches C there; truncate at the first C-vertex to get R. QED

  WORLD WC IS NOT KILLED - IT IS IRRELEVANT. The Menger blocking of 377.1 obstructs
  two disjoint paths; the lollipop needs one. 377.3's (WC-KILL) is WITHDRAWN as an
  obligation. The (T1) leaf of 376.3 is CLOSED.

### 379.3 THE FRONT: (T2) AND (T3') ONLY

  (THREAD') For some labelling k and structure T of 379.1: an even connecting path P
  for {i,j} with P cap T empty, whose interior contains vertices of BOTH position
  parities joined to LIVE(T) by paths avoiding P and internally avoiding T.

  THEOREM. (THREAD') implies (BP2), hence (N2): 376.2's threading argument verbatim,
  with LIVE(T) in place of T - {b_k}. QED

  And one relaxation for free, since the Position Lemma's pin is GLOBAL: the two
  attached vertices may sit on DIFFERENT even connecting paths of the same pair, each
  avoiding its own structure - both positions are pinned to the same beta_k, so
  opposite parities still contradict. (BP2) never needed one path.

  MEASURED, tools/lolli379.py, seed 379, eight bridges: lollipop configurations built
  12 of 12 in every bridge - as 379.2 now guarantees - with an even T-free connecting
  path in 8 to 12 of 12; of 623 such paths tested, 622 attach to LIVE(T) at both
  position parities; the single exception attached at one. The two remaining leaves:
     (T2)   an even {i,j}-connecting path avoiding T, for some admissible choice
            of C, R, k;
     (T3')  attachments to LIVE(T) from both position parity classes of P.

### 379.4 Status

The dependency chain after this section:

     (N2)  <==  (BP2)             375.3   PROVED implication
           <==  (THREAD')         379.3   PROVED implication
           <==  (T2) ^ (T3')      379.3   PROVED implication
     (T1)  CLOSED                 379.2   PROVED
     W2    EMPTY                  378.3   PROVED
     WC    IRRELEVANT             379.2   WITHDRAWN as an obligation
     open: (T2), (T3')

PROVED here: the LOLLIPOP PARITY LEMMA - one connecting path suffices, live set
C - {c} (379.1); (T1) - the lollipop exists in every bridge with tau >= 2, via the
Seed Corollary and 3-edge-connectivity of G (379.2); (THREAD') implies (N2), and the
split-path relaxation of (BP2) (379.3).
WITHDRAWN: (WC-KILL) as an obligation - the configuration obstructs only the
two-path theta, which nothing now uses (379.2).
COMPUTED: 12 of 12 lollipops per bridge; 622 of 623 even T-free paths attach at both
position parities (379.3).
NOT PROVED: (T2); (T3'); hence (THREAD'), (BP2), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 379 removes the second path from the

## 381. (T2) IN COMPONENT FORM

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The lollipop's existence relative to a chosen
even path collapses to one sentence about one component. This section proves the
equivalence and restates the two leaves in final form.

### 381.1 THE EQUIVALENCE (PROVED)

Note first that an even {i,j}-connecting path P contains b_i and b_j and avoids b_k,
so b_k is a vertex of B - P and is the ONLY terminal there.

  THEOREM. For a fixed even {i,j}-connecting path P, the following are equivalent:
    (1) some admissible lollipop T (379.1) for the labelling k satisfies P cap T empty;
    (2) the component of b_k in B - P is NON-BIPARTITE.
  Proof. (1) ==> (2): T = C u R is connected, contains b_k and the odd cycle C, and
  avoids P; so C lies in b_k's component of B - P. (2) ==> (1): the component carries
  an odd cycle C. C avoids b_i, b_j (they are on P) and every terminal except possibly
  b_k. If b_k lies on C, the degenerate T = C is admissible and avoids P. Otherwise
  take R a shortest b_k-to-C path inside the component - it exists by connectedness,
  avoids P, meets C once, and internally avoids all terminals. T = C u R. QED

  So the two leaves of 380.2 take their final shape:

     (T2'')  Some pair {i,j} has an even connecting path P whose deletion leaves b_k
             in a non-bipartite component.
     (T3')   For such a P and a lollipop inside that component, both position parity
             classes of interior(P) attach to LIVE(T) off P u T.

  (T2'') is gap (B) REBORN WITH THE RIGHT QUANTIFIERS: 371.4's premise asked B - D
  non-bipartite for one imposed cycle D; here the deleted set ranges over ALL even
  connecting paths of a FREE pair, the non-bipartiteness is asked only of b_k's
  component, and 375.3 guarantees at least one pair has even connecting paths at all.
  Every prior appearance of this shape came with the deleted set imposed; this one is
  chosen.

### 381.2 Status

PROVED here: the component equivalence - a P-avoiding lollipop exists iff b_k's
component of B - P is non-bipartite (381.1).
NOT PROVED: (T2''); (T3'); hence (THREAD'), (BP2), (LOCK-BREAK), (N2), (INT), (H1*),
and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The leaf (T2) is now one sentence: some even
connecting path, of some pair, leaves the third terminal in a non-bipartite component.
With it, (T3') asks that both parity classes of the path's positions reach the odd
cycle that component contains. These two sentences imply (THREAD'), hence (BP2), hence
(LOCK-BREAK) and (N2), by proved implications alone.


## 382. PAIR MATCHING, THE MENGER HALVES, AND THE FUNNEL WORLD

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. (T2'') carries a burden the stride's optimism
skated over: the lollipop's terminal must be the THIRD terminal of a pair that has even
connecting paths. This section makes the burden explicit, proves two supply lemmas, and
analyses the one world where mismatch threatens - where the supply lemmas turn out to
restore the match.

### 382.1 THE MATCHING BURDEN, STATED PLAINLY

379.2 gives a lollipop for SOME labelling k - the one the seed cycle determines. 375.3
gives even connecting paths for SOME pair. (T2'') needs one labelling serving both. If
the only pair with even paths were {1,2} while every seed cycle met b_1, the two
theorems would not compose. The statements of 380 and 381 quantify correctly; this
section supplies the matching.

### 382.2 THE MENGER HALVES LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. For every pair {i,j} there is a cycle through b_i and b_j avoiding b_k: G is
  3-connected, so G - e_k is 2-connected, so B - b_k is 2-connected and Menger gives
  two internally disjoint b_i-to-b_j connecting paths; their union is such a cycle.
  If ANY cycle through b_i, b_j avoiding b_k is ODD, then the pair {i,j} has an even
  connecting path - the even half.
  Proof. The two halves are connecting paths whose lengths sum to an odd number, so
  one is even. QED

  Contrapositive supply rule: a pair {i,j} with NO even connecting path has ALL its
  b_k-avoiding b_i,b_j-cycles even.

### 382.3 THE FUNNEL WORLD (PROVED STRUCTURE)

Say B is a FUNNEL over {1,2} if every odd cycle of B passes b_1 or b_2 - equivalently
F := B - {b_1, b_2} is bipartite. This is the world where the seed cycle can never
avoid both b_1 and b_2, so the lollipop labellings k = 1, 2 are the only candidates,
and the matching question is whether the pairs {2,3} and {1,3} have even paths.

  THEOREM. In a funnel over {1,2} with tau >= 2, colouring F bipartite by psi:
    (i)  both families are inhabited - some odd cycle avoids b_2, some avoids b_1 -
         else every odd cycle passes ONE degree-2 terminal and tau <= 1;
    (ii) an odd cycle through b_1 avoiding b_2 exists iff the ends of e_1 have
         OPPOSITE psi-colours, and then EVERY odd cycle passes exactly one of b_1,
         b_2: a cycle through both has length 4 + p + q with p + q even, since the
         four chord-ends pair into two opposite-coloured couples - EVEN;
    (iii) THE FUNNEL FEEDS THE CROSS PAIRS: the pair {1,3} has connecting paths of
         BOTH parities. F is connected (G is 3-edge-connected), b_3 is a vertex of F,
         and a b_1-to-b_3 connecting path is b_1 + (an end u of e_1) + an F-path to
         b_3, of length 1 + p with p == psi(u) + psi(b_3): by (i) and (ii) the two
         choices of u have opposite colours, so both parities occur. Likewise {2,3}.
  Proof of (i): if every odd cycle passed b_1, deleting one edge of the degree-2
  vertex b_1 would bipartize B. (ii) and (iii) are the displayed computations, with
  the endpoint-multiset argument of 378.2 giving p + q's parity in (ii). QED

  So in the funnel the matching is RESTORED: pair {1,3} has even paths (labelling
  k = 2), and by (i) an odd cycle through b_2 avoiding b_1 exists; the lollipop for
  k = 2 additionally needs it to avoid b_3, which holds whenever the ends of e_2
  remain connected in F - b_3 - open only in the case that the degree-2 vertex b_3
  is a cutvertex of F separating them.

### 382.4 WHAT THIS ROUND LEAVES

  (T2'') now has three named supply lines: the Menger halves (382.2), the funnel
  cross-pairs (382.3iii), and the general sealed-world analysis where the pair with
  even paths also carries a terminal-free seed. The narrowed open cases:
    (S1) the funnel case with b_3 a cutvertex of F between the ends of e_2 (and its
         mirror);
    (S2) the non-funnel sealed world: a terminal-free odd cycle exists, some pair has
         even paths, and every even path of every such pair hits or cuts every odd
         cycle avoiding its two endpoints' terminals.
  (T3') stands unchanged, measured at 622 of 623.

### 382.5 Status

PROVED here: the Menger Halves Lemma and its supply rule (382.2); the funnel
structure theorem - inhabited families, opposite-coloured chords, exactly-one
threading, and both parities for the cross pairs (382.3).
RECORDED: the matching burden (382.1); the narrowed open cases (S1), (S2), and the
unchanged (T3') (382.4).
NOT PROVED: (S1), (S2), (T3'); hence (T2''), (THREAD'), (BP2), (LOCK-BREAK), (N2),
(INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Section 382 pays a debt the stride had been
carrying: the lollipop's terminal and the even pair must match. Menger through the
third terminal's absence gives every pair a two-path cycle whose odd instances hand
the pair an even path. In the funnel world - all odd cycles through two named
terminals, the only world where the seed cannot serve the even pair - bipartite
bookkeeping shows the special edges are opposite-coloured, odd cycles thread exactly
one of the two terminals, and the cross pairs receive connecting paths of both
parities, restoring the match except when a degree-2 terminal is a cutvertex of the
bipartite core. What remains of (T2'') is that cutvertex case and the sealed
non-funnel world; what remains of (LOCK-BREAK) is those two plus (T3').


## 383. THE DEATH OF (S1), AND THE FUNNEL REDUCED TO A LINKAGE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The cutvertex case left open at 382.3 is empty:
it forces the three-edge-cut shape that 378.3 already kills. Every live funnel therefore
has a connected core minus its third terminal, and the funnel branch of (T2'') becomes a
two-disjoint-paths question in a bipartite graph.

### 383.1 (S1) IS EMPTY (PROVED)

  THEOREM. In a funnel over {1,2} with tau >= 2, the vertex b_3 is NOT a cutvertex of
  F = B - {b_1, b_2}.
  Proof. F - b_3 is exactly G - {e_1, e_2, e_3}. If it were disconnected, then since G
  is 3-edge-connected the triple {e_1, e_2, e_3} would be a minimal 3-edge-cut: exactly
  two components K, K', all three edges crossing (378.1). The funnel makes F bipartite,
  hence K and K' bipartite - and this is precisely the hypothesis of 378.3, which
  forces tau <= 1. Contradiction. QED

  COROLLARY. In every live funnel over {1,2}: the ends of e_2 are joined by an F-path
  avoiding b_3, necessarily of odd length (F bipartite, ends opposite-coloured by
  382.3), so AN ODD CYCLE THROUGH b_2 AVOIDING b_1 AND b_3 EXISTS - the degenerate
  lollipop for k = 2 - and by the mirror argument one through b_1 avoiding b_2, b_3
  for k = 1. Both matched labellings of 382.3(iii) are armed. QED

### 383.2 THE FUNNEL BRANCH OF (T2'') IS A 2-LINKAGE (PROVED REDUCTION)

  In a funnel over {1,2}, write x, y for the ends of e_2, u* for the end of e_1 with
  psi(u*) + psi(b_3) odd. An even {1,3}-connecting path is b_1 + u* + (F-path to b_3);
  a degenerate k = 2 lollipop is b_2 + (an F-path Q from x to y avoiding b_3). The
  path avoids the lollipop iff the F-path from u* to b_3 avoids Q. Hence:

  THEOREM. In a live funnel over {1,2}, (T2'') holds if F contains VERTEX-DISJOINT
  paths Q from x to y and P' from u* to b_3 (with b_3 not on Q, u* not on Q, which
  disjointness includes). The parities are then automatic: |Q| odd and 1 + |P'| even
  by the colourings, so P = b_1 u* P' is an even {1,3}-connecting path avoiding the
  odd cycle b_2 + Q, and 381.1 finishes. QED

  And the MIRROR: disjoint paths from e_1's ends and from the odd-side end of e_2 to
  b_3. (T2'') in the funnel needs only ONE of the two linkages. The two-disjoint-paths
  problem is completely characterised in the literature (Seymour; Shiloach; Thomassen:
  the linkage fails only in graphs that reduce to a planar configuration with the four
  terminals on one face); that characterisation is the armed tool, against a bipartite
  core F that is connected, stays connected without b_3 (383.1), and sits inside a
  3-connected cubic graph.

     (S1')  In every live funnel, one of the two linkages of 383.2 exists.

### 383.3 Status

The open leaves after this section: (S1') the funnel linkage; (S2) the sealed
non-funnel world (382.4); (T3') the two-sided attachment.

PROVED here: (S1) is empty - the cutvertex case collapses to 378.3's dead shape
(383.1); in every live funnel both degenerate lollipops exist with matched even pairs
(383.1); the funnel branch of (T2'') reduces to one of two 2-linkages in the bipartite
core (383.2).
NOT PROVED: (S1'), (S2), (T3'); hence (T2''), (THREAD'), (BP2), (LOCK-BREAK), (N2),
(INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The funnel world keeps shrinking. Its
cutvertex case is the three-edge-cut shape killed at 378, so the core survives the
removal of the third terminal, both cross labellings carry degenerate lollipops with
matched even pairs, and all that (T2'') asks of a funnel is one of two vertex-disjoint
path pairs in a connected bipartite core - a linkage question with a complete
literature characterisation waiting to be applied. Outside the funnel, the sealed
world (S2) and the attachment leaf (T3') remain.


## 384. THE MATCHING THEOREM: SUPPLY IS CLOSED, AVOIDANCE IS THE LEAF

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 382 raised the matching burden; this section
discharges it in every world. In every bridge with tau >= 2 some labelling carries BOTH
an even connecting pair and a lollipop. What remains of (T2'') everywhere is a single
disjointness statement, (AVOID), and the funnel instance of it is a two-commodity
question whose terminals all have degree two.

### 384.1 THE MATCHING THEOREM (PROVED)

  THEOREM. Every bridge with tau >= 2 admits a labelling (i, j, k) such that
    (a) the pair {i,j} has an even connecting path, and
    (b) a lollipop for k (379.1) exists.
  Proof. By 375.3 some pair {i,j} has an even connecting path; fix it, k the third.
  CASE 1: some odd cycle avoids all terminals. Then 379.2 builds a lollipop for EVERY
  labelling, in particular for k. Matched.
  CASE 2: no terminal-free odd cycle, but some odd cycle meets exactly b_k. It avoids
  b_i, b_j: the degenerate lollipop for k. Matched.
  CASE 3: no terminal-free odd cycle and none through exactly b_k. Then every odd
  cycle avoiding b_i and b_j would be terminal-free or exactly-b_k: none exist, so
  B - {b_i, b_j} is bipartite: B IS A FUNNEL OVER {i,j}. By 383.1 an odd cycle through
  b_j avoiding b_i and b_k exists - a degenerate lollipop for the labelling j - and by
  382.3(iii) the pair {i,k} has connecting paths of both parities. The labelling
  (i, k, j) is matched. QED

  Note the relabelling in Case 3: the matched triple need not be the one we started
  from, but one always exists. SUPPLY IS NO LONGER IN DOUBT ANYWHERE.

### 384.2 THE SINGLE LEAF (AVOID)

     (AVOID)  In every bridge with tau >= 2 satisfying (SC), for some matched
              labelling of 384.1: some even {i,j}-connecting path P and some lollipop
              T for k satisfy P cap T empty.

  By 381.1 this is (T2''), with matching now proved. The labels (S1') and (S2) of
  382 to 383 are RETIRED INTO (AVOID): the funnel instance is 383.2's linkage; the
  non-funnel instance has the terminal-free cycle as its lollipop seed. The chain:

     (N2) <== (BP2) <== (THREAD') <== (AVOID) ^ (T3')     all implications PROVED.

### 384.3 THE SUBCUBIC LINKAGE LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. In the funnel core F, the four linkage terminals x, y, u*, b_3 of 383.2 all
  have DEGREE TWO (each is a chord-end or the subdivision vertex). Consequently two
  EDGE-disjoint paths Q (x to y) and P' (u* to b_3) are automatically VERTEX-disjoint.
  Proof. A shared vertex v of two edge-disjoint paths is interior to at least one and
  an endpoint or interior of the other, needing at least 2 + 1 edges at v; F is
  subcubic, so v must be interior to both - four edges - impossible; and interior to
  one plus endpoint of the other needs three edges, impossible at the degree-2
  terminals, while a NON-terminal shared vertex would be interior to both. So the only
  candidates are the terminals themselves as interior points, excluded by degree. QED

  So the funnel instance of (AVOID) is a 2-commodity EDGE-disjoint paths problem with
  all four terminals of degree two. The Euler condition of the two-commodity theorems
  fails at those terminals (degree 2 plus demand 1 is odd), so Rothschild-Whinston
  does not apply off the shelf; the Seymour-Shiloach-Thomassen characterisation of
  2-linkage failure - reduction to a planar configuration with the four terminals
  interleaved on one face - is the armed tool, and the mirror labelling gives a second
  independent chance.

### 384.4 Status

PROVED here: the MATCHING THEOREM - every bridge with tau >= 2 has a labelling with
both an even pair and a lollipop, the funnel case supplying its own via 382 to 383
(384.1); the reduction of all remaining (T2)-obligations to the single statement
(AVOID) (384.2); the Subcubic Linkage Lemma - edge-disjoint implies vertex-disjoint at
degree-two terminals, making the funnel instance a two-commodity edge problem (384.3).
RETIRED: the labels (S1') and (S2), into (AVOID) (384.2).
NOT PROVED: (AVOID); (T3'); hence (THREAD'), (BP2), (LOCK-BREAK), (N2), (INT), (H1*),
and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Supply is closed: every bridge with tau at
least two owns, for some labelling, both halves of the thread configuration - the even
pair by fan pigeonhole in general and by the funnel's opposite-coloured chords in the
one world where pigeonhole's pair goes unserved, the lollipop by the seed corollary in
general and by the funnel's own cross cycles there. Two leaves remain for the whole of

classes of the path's positions reach the lollipop's cycle. Both are statements about
one path and one cycle in one graph, with every parity issue discharged.

## 386. THE DOUBLE-SWAP IS SELF-BLOCKED; THE ROLE-SWAP IS THE ENDGAME DESIGN

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section records why the natural machine
for (T3') cannot run under (SC) - the hypothesis defends itself through 223.3 - and
what design survives inside the nu_odd <= 2 corridor.

### 386.1 THE SPLIT-PATH FORM OF (T3') (RESTATED)

By 379.3 the two attached vertices may lie on DIFFERENT T-avoiding even paths of the
pair, their positions both pinned to the global beta_k. In particular a SINGLE
attaching vertex z on two even paths P, P~ with d_P(z) and d_P~(z) of opposite parity
refutes (SC), provided z attaches with respect to both.

### 386.2 THE DOUBLE-SWAP IS SELF-BLOCKED (PROVED)

  To flip d(z) mod 2 keeping the path even, the prefix and suffix of P at z must each
  change length by an ODD amount. The programme's only odd modifier is the single-arc
  swap around an odd cycle. Running it on both sides needs odd cycles O_1, O_2, and
  the modified path must still avoid the lollipop cycle C, forcing O_1, O_2, C
  pairwise vertex-disjoint: nu_odd >= 3. Under (SC), 223.3 gives nu_odd <= 2.
  SO THE DOUBLE-SWAP CONFIGURATION CANNOT EXIST IN AN (SC)-BRIDGE. Recorded so it is
  not retried: any (T3') proof must work with AT MOST TWO disjoint odd cycles. QED

### 386.3 THE ROLE-SWAP DESIGN (THE NEXT ATTACK, NOT PROVED)

  In the nu_odd = 2 regime let C_1, C_2 be disjoint odd cycles. The design: P uses
  C_1 as a DETOUR (entering and leaving it, the two arcs differing by an odd amount -
  flipping the position parity of everything after it) while C_2 serves as the
  LOLLIPOP; P~ trades the roles. One attaching vertex z behind both detour points,
  attached to both lollipops, would then sit at opposite pinned parities. In the
  nu_odd = 1 regime every pair of odd cycles intersects and the Lovasz-Slilaty
  structure (223.5) governs; that case remains wholly open.

### 386.4 Status

PROVED here: the double-swap route to (T3') requires three pairwise disjoint odd
cycles and is excluded by 223.3 under (SC) - the hypothesis defends its own leaf
(386.2).
RECORDED: the split-path restatement (386.1); the role-swap design and the open
nu_odd = 1 case (386.3).
NOT PROVED: (AVOID); (T3'); hence (THREAD'), (BP2), (LOCK-BREAK), (N2), (INT), (H1*),
and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The obvious machine for the attachment leaf
dismantles itself: flipping a position parity evenly needs two odd detours, three
disjoint odd cycles in all, and (SC) permits only two. What survives is the role-swap
- two disjoint odd cycles alternating as detour and parity machine - in the nu_odd = 2
regime, and the Lovasz-Slilaty structure in the nu_odd = 1 regime. The whole of (N2)
rests on (AVOID) and (T3'), with supply, matching, parity and every named world above
them settled.


## 387. THE ADJACENT-ATTACHER FORM, AND THE CHORD PIN

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Sharpening (T3'): its cheapest witness is two
ADJACENT attachers, chord feet are always attachers, and (SC) pins the cycle arcs
between chord feet to the path positions mod 4. One tempting contradiction from that
pin evaporates on inspection and is recorded as a near-miss so it is not retried.

### 387.1 THE ADJACENT-ATTACHER FORM (PROVED)

  LEMMA. If some admissible (P, T) has two attachers at ADJACENT positions of P, then
  (T3') holds for that configuration. Proof. Adjacent positions have opposite
  parities. QED
  And every P-vertex with an edge to LIVE(T) is an attacher with W a single edge. So
  (T3') fails for (P, T) only if the P-feet of all C-to-P chords, and all indirect
  attachers, form a subset of ONE parity class - in particular an independent set in P.

### 387.2 THE CHORD PIN (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let (P, T) be admissible, and let s, s' in LIVE(T) have edges to interior
  vertices z, z' of P at positions d < d'. Let A be an arc of C from s to s' with
  d + |A| + d' EVEN. Then P'' := P[b_i..z] + (z,s) + A + (s',z') + P[z'..b_j] is an
  even connecting path, and (SC) forces
     |A| == d' - d - 2   (mod 4).
  Proof. P'' is a path: A avoids P and R, the chords are single edges, and the two
  P-segments are disjoint. |P''| = d + 1 + |A| + 1 + (|P| - d'), even by the parity
  choice of A, and (SC) gives |P''| == |P| == c_ij (mod 4). Rearranged. QED

  So the arcs of the lollipop cycle between chord feet are not free: each even-parity
  arc equals the corresponding position difference minus two, mod four. This couples
  C's internal geometry to P's coordinates - a new rigidity for the endgame.

  A NEAR-MISS, RECORDED. If all chord feet sat at positions congruent mod 4 (not
  merely mod 2), the pins around three or more chords would telescope to 2 == 0 in
  several parity patterns. But the Position Lemma pins positions mod 2 ONLY; the
  mod-4 position differences are free parameters, and the telescoped system is
  satisfiable. The contradiction claimed by that route is VOID - caught before entry,
  per 374.1's rule. Any use of the Chord Pin must track position differences mod 4.

### 387.3 THE ROLE-SWAP, CORRECTED

386.3's design read as a LOCAL reroute would need the third odd cycle that 386.2
excludes. Its correct reading is GLOBAL: two independent admissible configurations
(P, T) and (P~, T~) with a COMMON attacher z at opposite position parities - no
modification of one path into the other, only the global pin beta_k linking them. The
open question is forcing the common attacher; the Chord Pin now constrains where
chords can sit in any (T3')-refusing bridge.

### 387.4 Status

PROVED here: the adjacent-attacher form - (T3')-failure makes attachers an
independent, single-parity set (387.1); the CHORD PIN - even arcs between chord feet
are pinned to position differences minus two, mod four (387.2).
VOID before entry: the telescoped chord-pin contradiction; positions are pinned mod 2,
not mod 4 (387.2).
NOT PROVED: (AVOID); (T3'); hence (THREAD'), (BP2), (LOCK-BREAK), (N2), (INT), (H1*),
and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The attachment leaf sharpens: failure means
every chord from the live cycle lands on one parity class of the path, no two
attachers are adjacent, and every even arc between chord feet obeys the Chord Pin.
The role-swap is a comparison of two whole configurations through the global pin, not
a reroute. Two leaves, (AVOID) and (T3'), carry (N2); the rigidity around them
continues to accumulate.


## 388. THE ENDGAME PROGRAMMES FOR (AVOID) AND (T3')

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The two leaves each receive a precise battle
plan with the armed tools named, the case splits fixed, and verify-flags on every
literature statement not yet re-checked verbatim against the archive.

### 388.1 (T3'): THE nu-SPLIT

Under (SC), nu_odd <= 2 (223.3). Two regimes:

  nu_odd = 2. THE GLOBAL ROLE-SWAP (387.3): two admissible configurations with a
  common attacher at opposite position parities, linked only by the global pin
  beta_k. The Chord Pin (387.2) and the independent single-parity attacher structure
  (387.1) are the constraints a refusing bridge must maintain across BOTH
  configurations simultaneously; the two disjoint odd cycles supply independent
  lollipops. TARGET: force the common attacher.

  nu_odd = 1. Every two odd cycles intersect. The characterisation of graphs without
  two vertex-disjoint odd cycles (Lovasz; topological form Slilaty - the 223.5
  pointer; VERIFY THE EXACT STATEMENT BEFORE USE) splits into: small odd-cycle
  vertex transversal (tau_v <= 3); or an embedding-type structure; or a bounded
  exceptional graph. The tau_v <= 3 subcase gives B - {three vertices} bipartite -
  the shape of 378's bookkeeping, with arbitrary vertices in place of terminals; the
  embedding subcase meets subcubicity, girth 5 and three degree-2 terminals at
  pairwise distance >= 5, which no bounded exceptional graph survives. TARGET: kill
  each branch by the 378 method or by size.

### 388.2 (AVOID): THE LINKAGE AND THE SEED

  FUNNEL INSTANCE: one of two 2-linkages in the bipartite core F (383.2), where all

  armed tool is the two-disjoint-paths characterisation (Seymour; Shiloach;
  Thomassen): failure only via reduction to a planar configuration with the four
  terminals interleaved on one face. Two independent levers against it: the MIRROR
  linkage (both must fail), and non-planarity of the ambient G - a minimal cubic
  counterexample is non-planar IF the planar-cubic Erdos-Gyarfas result
  (Heckman-Krakovski; VERIFY AGAINST THE ARCHIVE'S LITERATURE NOTES) is on record,
  since a planar G would not be a counterexample at all.

  NON-FUNNEL INSTANCE: the terminal-free seed cycle and 385.1's measured 36-80 per

  to choose P to MINIMISE its interaction with a fixed shortest terminal-free odd

### 388.3 Status

RECORDED: the standing battle plans - four named attacks, two per leaf, each with its

## 389. THE FUNNEL IS EMPTY: THE DEGREE CENSUS KILLS IT

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The linkage application planned at 388.2 never
runs: a two-line degree count shows the world it was built for does not exist. No
bridge with tau >= 2 has a bipartite two-terminal deletion. The linkage debt is
cancelled, the Matching Theorem simplifies, and (AVOID) keeps only its general
instance.

### 389.1 THE CENSUS LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let H be a bipartite graph with colour classes H_0, H_1 in which every vertex
  has degree 3 except for a set D of vertices of degree 2. Then, counting edges from
  each side, 3|H_0| - |D cap H_0| = |E(H)| = 3|H_1| - |D cap H_1|, so
     |D cap H_0| - |D cap H_1|  ==  0   (mod 3).
  The same holds in each connected component separately, with D restricted to it. QED

### 389.2 THE FUNNEL EMPTINESS THEOREM (PROVED)

  THEOREM. No bridge with tau >= 2 has B - {b_i, b_j} bipartite.
  Proof. Suppose F := B - {b_i, b_j} is bipartite. Its degree-2 vertices are exactly
  the two ends of e_i, the two ends of e_j, and b_k: FIVE vertices, all others of
  degree 3 (the ends are distinct, the special edges being disjoint and far apart).
  If the ends of e_i lie in different components of F, or in one component with EQUAL
  colours, then no cycle of B through b_i avoids b_j (such a cycle is b_i plus an
  F-path between the ends of e_i, which would have odd length, impossible between
  same-coloured vertices of a bipartite graph and impossible across components); then
  every odd cycle of B passes the degree-2 vertex b_j, and deleting one edge of b_j
  bipartizes B: tau <= 1, contradiction. The same for e_j. So in a live funnel both
  pairs of ends are OPPOSITE-coloured within single components.
  Now apply 389.1 to the component Z containing b_k. The pairs {ends of e_i} and
  {ends of e_j} each contribute (1,1) to the deficiency split of whichever component
  contains them, and b_k contributes 1 to one class of Z. Whether Z contains neither
  pair, one pair, or both, its deficiency difference is 1, 1, or 1 modulo 3 - never
  0. This contradicts 389.1 applied to Z. QED

  CHECKED: forty bridges with tau >= 2, all three pair-deletions each: 0 of 120
  bipartite.

### 389.3 THE CASCADE

  - 384.1's CASE 3 IS VACUOUS: matching always holds through Cases 1 and 2 - for the
    pigeonhole even pair {i,j} itself, either a terminal-free odd cycle or one
    through exactly b_k exists. The matched labelling never needs relabelling.
  - 382.3, 383.2, 384.3 and 388.2's funnel instance are TRUE STATEMENTS ABOUT AN
    EMPTY WORLD: retired. The two-disjoint-paths characterisation, the planarity
    lever, and the (S1') label are STRUCK FROM THE DEBT LEDGER.
  - (AVOID) keeps only its GENERAL instance: for the matched labelling, some even
    {i,j}-path leaves b_k in a non-bipartite component (381.1), with the seed cycle
    supplied by Case 1 or Case 2.
  - The CENSUS is promoted to a standing tool. Applied to a SEALED component - b_k's
    component Z of B - P bipartite, every outgoing edge of Z landing on P - it gives:
    the attachment edges split by colour class as E_0, E_1 with E_0 - E_1 == +-1
    (mod 3), the sign set by b_k's class. Sealed components are always
    colour-imbalanced toward P.

### 389.4 Status

PROVED here: the Census Lemma (389.1); the FUNNEL EMPTINESS THEOREM - no bridge with
tau >= 2 has a bipartite two-terminal deletion, by family-emptiness or the census
(389.2); the sealed-component census corollary (389.3).
RETIRED: the funnel machinery of 382.3, 383.2, 384.3, 388.2 as vacuously true; the
linkage debt including (S1') (389.3).
NOT PROVED: (AVOID) in its general instance; (T3'); hence (THREAD'), (BP2),
(LOCK-BREAK), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The funnel never existed. A bipartite graph
whose deficient vertices number five splits them three-to-two between its colour
classes, but the census demands a multiple of three, and chasing the discrepancy into
the component holding the third terminal kills every live configuration - connected
or not. With it fall the linkage question, the planarity lever, and the last
relabelling case of the Matching Theorem. Two leaves remain, now in one instance
each: an even path of the matched pair leaving the third terminal unsealed, and a
second-parity attachment. The census joins the arsenal: sealed components are
colour-imbalanced by exactly one modulo three.


## 390. LOCALIZATION: THE WHOLE QUESTION LIVES IN ONE BLOCK TREE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The two leaves localize: every parity
certificate for every interior vertex of an even path lives inside the third
terminal's component of the path's deletion. The final arena is that component's
block tree.

### 390.1 THE LOCALIZATION LEMMA (PROVED)

  Let P be an even {i,j}-connecting path and z an interior vertex, y_z its third
  neighbour.
  (i) NO ODD CYCLE OF B - (P - z) PASSES THROUGH z: the two P-edges of z are deleted,
      leaving z with a single edge - degree one supports no cycle. So every odd cycle
      of B - (P - z) lies in B - P, inside one component. QED
  (ii) z IS A BOTH-PARITY VERTEX IFF y_z lies in Z(P) := the component of b_k in
      B - P, AND the block-chain from y_z to b_k INSIDE Z(P) carries a non-bipartite
      block. Proof. The z-to-b_k chain of B - (P - z) is the cut edge (z, y_z)
      followed by the y_z-to-b_k chain of Z(P); apply Lemma B PRIME (342.2) and (i).
      QED
  (iii) If the pair is SEALED - Z(P) bipartite for every even {i,j}-path P - then NO
      even path of the pair has ANY both-parity vertex, and (BP2) fails for the pair
      outright. Proof. By (ii) a both-parity vertex needs a non-bipartite block of
      Z(P). QED

### 390.2 THE FINAL ARENA

  By (ii), both leaves are statements about the block tree of Z(P):
     (AVOID)  some even P of the matched pair has Z(P) NON-BIPARTITE;
     (T3')    for such a P, two interior vertices of OPPOSITE position parity have
              their third neighbours in Z(P) with a non-bipartite block on their
              respective b_k-chains.
  Everything else - threading, lollipops, live sets - was scaffolding for (ii); the
  lemma is now the exact criterion, with no slack anywhere. The failure taxonomy of
  (BP2) for the matched pair: for every even P, either Z(P) is bipartite, or its odd
  blocks all dangle off the b_k-chains of every wrong-parity attachment foot. The
  census (389.3) constrains the first horn: sealed components are colour-imbalanced
  by one modulo three. The Chord Pin (387.2) and the single-parity independence
  (387.1) constrain the second.

### 390.3 Status

PROVED here: the LOCALIZATION LEMMA - odd cycles of B - (P - z) avoid z, both-parity
is exactly a non-bipartite block on the y_z-to-b_k chain of Z(P), and a sealed pair
has no both-parity vertices at all (390.1); the reduction of both leaves to the block
tree of Z(P) (390.2).
NOT PROVED: (AVOID); (T3'); hence (THREAD'), (BP2), (LOCK-BREAK), (N2), (INT), (H1*),
and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The battlefield has contracted to a single
object: the component of the third terminal after deleting an even connecting path,
and its block tree. One leaf says the component can be made non-bipartite by choosing
the path; the other says two opposite-parity positions of the path can be given
chains into its odd blocks. The census bounds the bipartite escape, the Chord Pin and
independence bound the dangling escape. Every theorem of this stride - eighteen
sections of them - stands between (SC) and these two sentences.


## 391. COMPONENT DYNAMICS: WHAT THE SEALED WORLD MUST PARK, AND WHERE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Two proved constraints on any sealed pair: the
seed must be HIT by every even path when it threads the third terminal, and no even
reroute may ever free a mixed-adjacency pair. The sealed conspiracy is now quantitative.

### 391.1 THE HITTING LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Sealed pair {i,j}, Case-2 seed: C an odd cycle through b_k avoiding b_i, b_j.
  Then EVERY even {i,j}-connecting path meets C - {b_k}.
  Proof. If P misses C - {b_k}, then C - {b_k} is connected to b_k off P, so C lies
  inside Z(P), which is then non-bipartite: not sealed. QED
  (Case-1 seed, C terminal-free: every even path meets C or separates it from b_k -
  the weaker dichotomy, since C need not touch Z.)

### 391.2 THE MIXED-ADJACENCY LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Sealed pair {i,j}. Let P be an even path, z, z' CONSECUTIVE interior
  vertices whose third edges enter, respectively, Z(P) and a NON-BIPARTITE component
  D of B - P. Then NO even reroute of P avoids both z and z' while keeping its detour
  clear of Z and D.
  Proof. Such a reroute P' leaves z, z', the edge (z,z'), all of Z and all of D in
  B - P'; the path y_z, z, z', y_z' joins them, so b_k's component of B - P'
  contains D's odd cycle: Z(P') non-bipartite, not sealed. QED

  So wherever the sealed world lets an odd component D sit NEXT to Z along a path -
  two consecutive third edges, one into each - it must simultaneously destroy every
  even detour around that doorway: the doorway pins the path. Combined with 391.1,
  the seed's territory and the third terminal's territory must interleave with every
  even path everywhere, while the census (389.3) keeps Z colour-imbalanced and the
  Localization Lemma (390.1) keeps every parity certificate inside Z. The sealed
  world is a conspiracy of doorways, each self-pinning.

### 391.3 Status

PROVED here: the Hitting Lemma - a Case-2 seed is met by every even path of a sealed
pair (391.1); the Mixed-Adjacency Lemma - sealed worlds admit no even detour around a
doorway between the third terminal's component and any odd component (391.2).
NOT PROVED: (AVOID); (T3'); hence (THREAD'), (BP2), (LOCK-BREAK), (N2), (INT), (H1*),
and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The sealed world's obligations are now
itemised: hit the seed with every even path, keep the third terminal's component
bipartite and colour-imbalanced, keep every odd block off every chain, and pin every
even detour around every doorway. Each obligation is proved; what is not yet proved
is that they cannot all be met at once. That single sentence is what remains of
(LOCK-BREAK).


## 392. THE THREE SEEDS: EXISTENCE, ENTANGLEMENT, AND THE ARC MANUFACTURE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. 389's emptiness theorem arms every pair with a
seed; 223.3 forbids the three seeds independence; their forced intersections
manufacture even connecting paths with parity control. The sealed world must now
withstand structure it cannot separate.

### 392.1 ALL THREE SEED FAMILIES ARE INHABITED (PROVED)

  For each labelling m with pair {i,j}: Omega_m := odd cycles avoiding b_i and b_j.
  By 389.2, B - {b_i, b_j} is non-bipartite: Omega_m is NONEMPTY, for every m, in
  every bridge with tau >= 2. If no terminal-free odd cycle exists, every member of
  Omega_m passes b_m: each seed threads its own terminal. QED

### 392.2 THE SEEDS CANNOT BE INDEPENDENT (PROVED)

  Under (SC), nu_odd <= 2 (223.3): no three pairwise vertex-disjoint odd cycles. So
  any choice S_1 in Omega_1, S_2 in Omega_2, S_3 in Omega_3 has TWO SEEDS MEETING. In
  the no-terminal-free world the shared vertex is a NON-TERMINAL (S_m may contain
  only b_m). A terminal-free cycle, when it exists, lies in all three families at
  once and collapses the triple. QED

### 392.3 THE ARC MANUFACTURE (PROVED)

  LEMMA. In the no-terminal-free world, let S_1 in Omega_1, S_2 in Omega_2 share a
  vertex. Fix an arc gamma of S_1 from b_1, let v be gamma's FIRST vertex on S_2, and
  A, A' the two arcs of S_2 from v to b_2. Then gamma[b_1..v] + A and
  gamma[b_1..v] + A' are both {1,2}-connecting paths, internally terminal-free, with
  OPPOSITE parities: an EVEN {1,2}-connecting path through v exists, its parity
  supplied by the arc choice.
  Proof. gamma[b_1..v] meets S_2 only at v by firstness; A, A' lie on S_2; each
  composite is simple. S_1 avoids b_2, b_3 except b_1; S_2 avoids b_1, b_3 except
  b_2; so the interiors avoid all terminals. |A| + |A'| = |S_2| is odd, so the
  parities differ. QED

  Consequences. (a) In the no-terminal-free world, ANY two meeting seeds make their
  pair EVEN-ACTIVE - even connecting paths exist for it - so 392.2's forced meeting
  activates at least one pair unconditionally, a second route to 375.3's pigeonhole.
  (b) The even composite is (SC)-pinned: |gamma[b_1..v]| + |A_even| == c_12 (mod 4),
  coupling the seed geometry to the constants - a Chord-Pin analogue at the seed
  level. (c) The same manufacture runs from b_2's side and from every arc choice at
  b_1: a FAMILY of pinned even paths through the seed intersection, all of which the
  sealed world must individually seal - each with its Z, its census imbalance, its
  hitting obligations - while 391's doorway constraints apply across the family.

### 392.4 Status

PROVED here: every seed family is inhabited, by the Funnel Emptiness Theorem (392.1);

## 393. THE COVERAGE DICHOTOMY: SEALING FORCES TWO SEEDS TO COVER EVERYTHING

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The manufactured family of 392.3 meets the
sealing obligations of 391 head-on, and the collision yields a dichotomy: either the
sealed world dies at a manufactured path, or two seeds and two terminals cover every
odd cycle of the bridge.

### 393.1 THE DICHOTOMY (PROVED)

  THEOREM. No-terminal-free world, pair {1,2} sealed, seeds S_1, S_2 meeting, P* a
  manufactured even {1,2}-path of 392.3 (so P* is contained in S_1 union S_2). Then
  for EVERY S_3 in Omega_3: S_3 meets S_1 union S_2. Indeed, if some S_3 avoids
  S_1 union S_2, it avoids P*, so S_3 - {b_3}, connected to b_3 off P*, lies in
  Z(P*): non-bipartite, contradicting sealing - and (AVOID) IS WITNESSED AT P*.
  Proof. S_3 passes b_3 (no-terminal-free world) and avoids b_1, b_2; P* avoids b_3
  internally; the Hitting Lemma 391.1 applies verbatim. QED

  COROLLARY (COVERAGE). In the sealed no-terminal-free world, for every meeting pair
  of seeds: {b_1, b_2} union S_1 union S_2 is an ODD-CYCLE TRANSVERSAL OF B - every
  odd cycle meets it. Proof. An odd cycle meets some terminal; through b_1 or b_2 it
  meets the terminal part; through b_3 only, it is an Omega_3 member and meets
  S_1 union S_2 by the theorem. QED

  And this holds for EVERY meeting choice (S_1, S_2), while 392.2 guarantees meeting
  choices exist in every seed triple.

### 393.2 THE MEETING POINT'S THIRD EDGE (PROVED)

  LEMMA. At the meeting vertex v of P* (392.3), the third edge of v - the one P*
  does not use - lies on S_2, along the unused arc A'. Its far end hangs in
  B - P* adjacent to v, and the interior of A' avoids P* entirely, terminating at
  b_2's second edge.
  Proof. v carries two S_1-edges and two S_2-edges among its three edges, so one is
  shared; gamma enters v by a pure S_1-edge (else firstness fails), A_even leaves by
  an S_2-edge, and the remaining edge is S_2's other arc-edge. A'-interior meets
  gamma only within S_2, impossible before v, and meets A_even only at v and b_2. QED

  So the manufactured path arrives with its own attachment analysis half-done: v's
  third edge enters B - P* along a known odd-cycle remnant. Where A'-interior
  connects to Z(P*) - equivalently, whether the b_3-side can reach the unused arc -
  is exactly the (T3')-question at the manufactured path, now posed about concrete
  seed arcs rather than abstract components.

### 393.3 Status

PROVED here: the COVERAGE DICHOTOMY - a sealed no-terminal-free world requires every
third-family seed to meet every meeting union, else (AVOID) is witnessed at a
manufactured path; hence two seeds plus two terminals form a global odd-cycle
transversal, for every meeting choice (393.1); the meeting point's third edge lies on
the unused arc of the second seed (393.2).
NOT PROVED: (AVOID); (T3'); hence (THREAD'), (BP2), (LOCK-BREAK), (N2), (INT),
(H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Sealing now costs the adversary a covering

every odd cycle in the bridge - for every choice of meeting seeds - or a manufactured

## 394. THE WINDOW LEMMA AND THE ENTANGLEMENT DICHOTOMY

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The coverage obligation of 393 becomes a parity
window at the third terminal's neighbours, and nu_odd splits the sealed world into a

### 394.1 SEEDS ARE WINDOW PATHS (PROVED)

  In the no-terminal-free world, every member of Omega_3 consists of b_3 and a path
  in B - {b_1, b_2, b_3} between b_3's two neighbours w, w' whose length completes an
  odd cycle. Two members of the same family always share the 2-path w, b_3, w'. QED

### 394.2 THE WINDOW LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Sealed no-terminal-free world, (S_1, S_2) any meeting pair. In the graph
  B - {b_1, b_2, b_3} - (S_1 union S_2), there is NO w-to-w' path of the
  odd-completing parity: the window is shut - w or w' absorbed into the union,
  separated, or joined only in the wrong parity, every block on every chain bipartite
  with the fixed harmless value.
  Proof. Such a path plus b_3 would be a member of Omega_3 avoiding S_1 union S_2,
  which 393.1 turns into an (AVOID) witness. The block form is Lemma B PRIME. QED

  This must hold for EVERY meeting pair simultaneously - while B - {b_1, b_2} itself
  remains non-bipartite (389.2), so the window is open in the undeleted graph: the
  union must shut it every time.

### 394.3 THE ENTANGLEMENT DICHOTOMY (PROVED)

  THEOREM. In the sealed no-terminal-free world:
  (i) nu_odd = 1: every two odd cycles meet - all cross-family seed pairs meet, all
      three pairs are even-active (392.3), all three are sealed, and all three
      coverage and window obligations run simultaneously: the MAXIMAL CONSPIRACY.
      This regime is Lovasz-Slilaty territory (223.5, verify-flagged).
  (ii) nu_odd = 2: any two disjoint odd cycles have DISJOINT TERMINAL SETS - two
      cycles through a common terminal share it, and none is terminal-free - so the
      disjoint pattern pairs distinct terminal types, and every triple of seeds still
      contains a meeting pair (392.2), reinstating the obligations along it.
  Proof. (i) is the definition of nu = 1 plus 392.3 and 393; (ii) is the shared-
  vertex observation plus 392.2. QED

### 394.4 Status

PROVED here: seeds are window paths sharing the terminal 2-path (394.1); the WINDOW
LEMMA - every meeting union shuts the odd-completing window at w, w', for every
meeting choice, though the window is open in B - {b_1, b_2} itself (394.2); the

## 395. THE OPPOSED PAIR: A TWO-CYCLE TRANSVERSAL AND THE TRANSITION PARITY PIN

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. In the nu = 2 regime with disjoint seeds of
opposed mono-terminal types, packing alone makes the pair a global odd-cycle
transversal, transitions between them manufacture even paths in all four parity
combinations, and (SC) pins every transition to one parity. The adversary's design
principle - thread everything through terminals so every swap flips parity - is
identified and recorded.

### 395.1 THE OPPOSED-PAIR TRANSVERSAL THEOREM (PROVED, SEALING-FREE)

  THEOREM. No-terminal-free world, O_1 in Omega_1 and O_2 in Omega_2 vertex-disjoint.
  Then B - (O_1 union O_2) is BIPARTITE.
  Proof. An odd cycle avoiding both: it meets a terminal; b_1 lies on O_1 and b_2 on
  O_2, so it avoids those and is an Omega_3 member; disjoint from O_1 and O_2 it
  would form three pairwise disjoint odd cycles, against nu_odd <= 2 (223.3). QED

### 395.2 TRANSITION MANUFACTURE (PROVED)

  A TRANSITION is a path tau from a on O_1 - {b_1} to b on O_2 - {b_2}, internally
  avoiding O_1, O_2 and all terminals. Transitions exist: G - e_3 is connected, so
  O_1 reaches O_2 off b_3; truncate at last exit and first entry.
  THEOREM. Each transition yields FOUR {1,2}-connecting paths - two arc choices
  b_1-to-a on O_1, two b-to-b_2 on O_2 - realising ALL FOUR parity combinations,
  since each cycle's two arcs differ in parity. In particular pair {1,2} is
  EVEN-ACTIVE in every opposed-pair world. QED

### 395.3 THE TRANSITION PARITY PIN (PROVED)

  THEOREM. Under (SC), EVERY transition has length of the SAME parity:
     |tau| == (|O_1| + |O_2|)/2   (mod 2).
  Proof. The two even combos through tau differ by (2 arc_1 - |O_1|) + (2 arc_2 -
  |O_2|); (SC) makes the difference 0 mod 4, so arc_1 + arc_2 == (|O_1|+|O_2|)/2
  (mod 2), and evenness of the combo forces |tau| == arc_1 + arc_2 (mod 2). QED

  With 395.1, transitions run through a BIPARTITE middle M := B - O_1 - O_2, so each
  M-route's parity is its colour difference plus two: the pin dictates the colour
  relation of every O_1-attachment to every O_2-attachment reachable from it. One
  pair of opposite-parity transitions refutes (SC) outright.

### 395.4 THE TERMINAL-THREADING PRINCIPLE (RECORDED)

  Why does the adversary survive arc swaps? Swapping a seed's arc at its terminal
  flips parity - the swapped cycle through the terminal is EVEN and escapes all odd
  constraints. Every surviving conspiracy so far threads its odd structure through
  terminals precisely to buy this protection: the Case-2 seed, the opposed pair, the
  window paths. The kill, when it comes, must charge the protection itself: degree-2
  terminals make every threading cycle vulnerable to ONE edge deletion, and tau >= 2
  is exactly the statement that one deletion is never enough.

### 395.5 Status

PROVED here: the opposed pair is a global odd-cycle transversal, by packing alone
(395.1); transitions exist and manufacture all four parity combinations - pair {1,2}
is even-active in every opposed-pair world (395.2); the TRANSITION PARITY PIN - all
transitions share one parity under (SC), through a bipartite middle whose colouring
the pin enslaves (395.3).
RECORDED: the terminal-threading principle - the adversary's one protection - and
where it is thin (395.4).
NOT PROVED: (AVOID); (T3'); hence (THREAD'), (BP2), (LOCK-BREAK), (N2), (INT),
(H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The opposed-pair world is now a bipartite
middle strung between two odd cycles through two terminals, every crossing of the
middle pinned to one parity, every even crossing pinned mod four, the third
terminal's window shut behind the pair by packing alone. What remains everywhere is
one opposite-parity transition, one unsealed path, one wrong-parity attacher - a
single parity violation anywhere in a bridge whose every two-terminal deletion is
provably non-bipartite. The conspiracy holds by threading terminals; tau >= 2 says
terminals cannot protect everything; making those two sentences collide is what
remains of (LOCK-BREAK).


## 396. THE COLOUR LEDGER OF THE OPPOSED-PAIR WORLD

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The ledger of the bipartite middle M is
assembled: component colours are enslaved per side, window paths use forced arcs, and
the mod-2 balance identity localises the adversary's remaining freedom to the parities
of the forced arcs - pinned only at the mod-4 layer, where the collision must happen.

### 396.1 THE COMPONENT COLOUR RIGIDITY THEOREM (PROVED)

  THEOREM. Under (SC), in the opposed-pair world, let D be any component of M - b_3
  attached to both cycles. Then ALL vertices of D adjacent to O_1 - {b_1} share one
  colour alpha_D, ALL adjacent to O_2 - {b_2} share the colour alpha_D + pi*, where
  pi* = (|O_1| + |O_2|)/2 mod 2. If any direct O_1-to-O_2 edge exists, pi* = 1.
  Proof. For feet y_1 (O_1-side) and y_2 (O_2-side) joined in D - {b_3}, the
  transition through them has parity 2 + chi(y_1) + chi(y_2) == pi* by 395.3; two
  O_1-side feet against a common y_2 force chi(y_1) = chi(y_1'). A direct edge is a
  transition of length 1. QED

### 396.2 WINDOW PATHS USE FORCED ARCS (PROVED)

  Every S_3 in Omega_3 is b_3 plus a window path W_3 from w to w' which, being barred
  from b_1 and b_2, uses at each visit to O_1 or O_2 the UNIQUE arc between its entry
  and exit that avoids the cycle's terminal. The cycle visits of every window path
  are geodesic segments of the terminal-free sides, their lengths lambda_t determined
  by the entry and exit points alone. And chi(w) = chi(w') automatically: b_3 lies in
  bipartite M with both its neighbours oppositely coloured to it. QED

### 396.3 THE BALANCE IDENTITY, AND THE LAST SLACK (PROVED IDENTITY)

  For any window path with visits t = 1..T, entry feet colours alpha_in(t), exit feet
  colours alpha_out(t), and forced-arc lengths lambda_t:
     |W_3| == SUM_t [ alpha_in(t) + alpha_out(t) + lambda_t ]   (mod 2),
  the endpoint colours cancelling by chi(w) = chi(w'). Oddness of S_3 = |W_3| + 2
  requires the sum to be ODD. Visits entering and leaving through ONE component
  contribute lambda_t alone (feet colours equal, by 396.1 when double-attached). So
  the existence of Omega_3 - guaranteed by 392.1 - forces an odd total of arc
  parities and cross-component colour jumps: THE ADVERSARY'S LAST SLACK IS THE
  PARITY VECTOR (lambda_t) OF THE FORCED ARCS, together with single-attached
  component colours that 396.1 does not reach. The mod-4 layer - the excursion pins
  (arc-length congruent to same-parity M-excursions mod 4), the Chord Pin (387.2),
  and the c-constants - is where those parities are constrained, and where the
  collision with the balance identity must be sought.

### 396.4 Status

PROVED here: the COMPONENT COLOUR RIGIDITY THEOREM - the pin enslaves every
double-attached component's foot colours per side (396.1); window paths use forced
terminal-free arcs with determined lengths, and the window's endpoints share a colour
(396.2); the balance identity localising Omega_3's oddness to arc parities and colour
jumps (396.3).
NOT PROVED: that the mod-4 layer contradicts the balance identity; hence (AVOID),
(T3'), (THREAD'), (BP2), (LOCK-BREAK), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. In the opposed-pair world everything mod 2
is now on the ledger: component colours enslaved in pairs across the middle, window
endpoints matched, cycle visits forced onto terminal-free arcs. The seed's oddness -
which the emptiness theorem guarantees - must be financed entirely by the forced-arc

## 399. THE GEOMETRIC FRONT OPENS: THE NESTING THEOREM

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. First theorem of the geometric front: in the
sealed opposed-pair world, every transition foot must nest inside every window arc,
so every seed through the third terminal traverses one fixed segment of O_1. The
odd structure of the bridge is pinned to a corridor.

### 399.1 THE NESTING THEOREM (PROVED)

  Setting: sealed opposed-pair world, template form - b_3's component D_3 of M
  attaches to O_1 only, transitions run through other components. Let S_3 be any
  Omega_3 member with window arc A(S_3) = its b_1-free arc on O_1 between its
  attachment points, and let a be the O_1-foot of any transition tau.

  THEOREM. a LIES ON THE CLOSED ARC A(S_3).
  Proof. Suppose a lies strictly outside. O_1 minus b_1 is a segment with A(S_3) in
  its middle; a sits strictly between b_1 and one endpoint of A(S_3). Of the two even
  manufactured {1,2}-paths through tau (395.2), the one whose O_1-arc runs from b_1
  to a on a's side uses no vertex of A(S_3) and no vertex of D_3 (the transition runs
  through another component). That even path P misses S_3 entirely, so S_3 lies in
  Z(P): non-bipartite, and the seal breaks - (AVOID) witnessed. QED

  COROLLARY (THE CORRIDOR). With two vertex-disjoint transitions (Menger in the
  3-connected ambient, at most one path through b_3 discarded), the feet span a
  segment sigma* of O_1 with at least one edge, and EVERY Omega_3 member's window
  arc CONTAINS sigma*: every odd cycle through b_3 avoiding b_1, b_2 traverses the
  whole corridor sigma*. Hence every odd cycle of B meets {b_1, b_2} or uses every
  edge of sigma*: for any edge f of sigma*, deleting one edge at b_1, one at b_2 and
  f bipartizes B - tau_e <= 3 with a NAMED transversal - and {b_1, b_2, x} is an
  odd-cycle vertex transversal for every vertex x internal to sigma* when one
  exists. QED

### 399.2 WHAT THE CORRIDOR COSTS THE ADVERSARY

  The sealed world's odd cycles now come in three funnelled families: through b_1,
  through b_2, or through the corridor. The corridor is a segment of O_1 - itself an
  odd cycle through b_1 - so the bridge's entire odd structure threads two degree-2
  terminals and one short segment of a single cycle. Set against: tau >= 2, the
  Funnel Emptiness Theorem (B minus any two terminals is non-bipartite - so the
  corridor family Omega_3 is NONEMPTY for every labelling), 3-connectivity, girth 5,
  and terminal distances >= 5. The kill candidate for the next round: run the
  389-style census on B - {b_1, b_2} - f for each corridor edge f, with the colour
  constraints that nesting now forces on f's ends through the corridor traversals -
  the seven-deficiency census survives alone, but nesting adds equations it did not
  have.

### 399.3 Status

PROVED here: the NESTING THEOREM - sealing forces every transition foot onto every
window arc (399.1); the CORRIDOR corollary - all of Omega_3 traverses one segment,
giving explicit 3-edge and 3-vertex odd-cycle transversals (399.1).

## 400. THE CORRIDOR CENSUS: THE SEALED WORLD IN CANONICAL FORM

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The census re-runs through the corridor and

canonical form, in which even the side choices that balanced 397.2's books are

### 400.1 THE CORRIDOR COLOUR LAWS (PROVED)

  Let f be a corridor edge with ends g, h; H := B - {b_1, b_2} - f is bipartite
  (every Omega_3 member uses f, by the Corridor Corollary), coloured chi. Then:
  (i) chi(g) = chi(h): an Omega_3 member's window path splits at f into two H-pieces
      whose parities sum to chi(g)+chi(h) via chi(w) = chi(w'), and its oddness
      forces equality.
  (ii) chi(u) = chi(u') for the ends of e_1: the two segments of O_1 - {b_1} - f
      have lengths summing to |O_1| - 3, even, and (i) transfers the equality.
  (iii) chi(x) =/= chi(y) for the ends of e_2: O_2 - {b_2} survives in H as an
      odd-length path between them.
  (iv) THE CENSUS FORCING: seven deficient vertices - u, u', x, y, b_3, g, h - with
      (ii) giving the pair {u,u'} one class, (i) giving {g,h} one class, (iii)
      splitting {x,y}: the mod-3 census admits ONLY the split where u, u', g, h
      share one colour and b_3 takes the other; and chi(w) = chi(w') equals the
      quadruple's colour. Proof: the deficiency difference is +-2 +-2 +-1 and must
      vanish mod 3, forcing +-(2+2-1). QED

### 400.2 POSITIONS AND SIDES ARE FORCED (PROVED)

  Every transition, being an H-path from O_1 to O_2, pins its feet:
  chi(a) + chi(b) == pi*, so all corridor feet sit at positions of one parity from u
  and all O_2-feet at the matching parity from x. And the Access Pin's mod-2 shadow
  forces each window attachment's even-completing arc to be the arc through the
  PHYSICAL side the attachment sits on: 397.2's side choices epsilon are NOT free -
  they equal the physical sides, and the balance condition epsilon_1 =/= epsilon_2
  says exactly that the window attachments STRADDLE the corridor, which nesting
  already requires. Every degree of freedom the arithmetic audit found is consumed
  by the geometry; the system remains CONSISTENT. QED

### 400.3 THE CANONICAL FORM, AND THE LAST QUESTION

  The sealed opposed-pair world is now one explicit shape: two disjoint odd cycles

## 403. THE HEPTAGON EXCLUSION: |O_1| >= 9

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Two more proved constraints - the three-point

The monotone tightening takes its second strict step, and the mechanism that kills the

### 403.1 TWO FOLDED CONSTRAINTS (PROVED)

  (i) THE BOUNDARY LAW. Every component of the middle M - in particular b_3's
      component D_3 and every pocket - has at least THREE attachment vertices on the
      cycles: a two-vertex boundary would be a 2-cut of the 3-connected G. So D_3
      attaches to O_1 at >= 3 positions.
  (ii) THE PHI LAW. M is bipartite (395.1); for a D_3-attachment at position p with
      foot colour chi, put phi := chi + p (mod 2). A window pair realises an ODD seed
      iff its phi values differ (the runs' parities are colour differences), so
      NESTING (399.1) forces: every phi-mixed pair straddles the corridor strictly -
      and a D_3-attachment INSIDE the corridor is phi-inconsistent: it would need the
      left group's phi and the right group's phi at once. So corridor-interior
      positions carry NO D_3-attachment. QED

### 403.2 THE HEPTAGON EXCLUSION (PROVED)

  THEOREM. In the sealed opposed-pair canonical form, |O_1| >= 9.
  Proof. Let A = 7: O_1 - {b_1} has positions 0..5, each with ONE third edge. The
  straddle with s_2 - s_1 >= 2 and >= 3 D_3-attachments obeying 403.1 admits, by
  enumeration, exactly two layouts: feet (2,4) with D_3 at {0,1,5}, spare position 3;
  or feet (1,3) with D_3 at {0,4,5}, spare position 2. (Four D_3-attachments cannot
  fit: the span 2+2+2 exceeds six positions.) In each layout every position except
  the spare is committed, and the spare lies INTERIOR to the corridor with parity
  OPPOSITE to the feet. Its third edge must go somewhere:
    - to D_3: barred by the phi law (403.1ii);
    - to O_1 as a chord: the far end has no free third edge;
    - to any component touching O_2, or to O_2 directly: that creates a TRANSITION
      with foot at the spare position, whose parity differs from the feet - two
      transitions of opposite foot parity contradict the pin (395.3 with 400.2);
    - to a pocket (a component attached to O_1 only): the pocket needs two further
      attachments (403.1i) and no free position exists.
  Every case contradicts. QED
  (This also re-proves |O_1| =/= 5 independently of 402.2.)

### 403.3 THE MECHANISM, GENERALLY

  The corridor's interior always contains a position of the wrong parity (its length
  is at least two). That position's third edge is barred from D_3 and from every
  O_2-reaching component; only POCKETS can absorb it, and each pocket costs three or
  more attachment positions by the boundary law. The feasibility of |O_1| >= 9 now

NOT PROVED: exclusion at |O_1| >= 9; hence (AVOID), (T3'), (THREAD'), (BP2),

## 404. THE POCKET CALCULUS: TWO LAWS, AND NINE SURVIVES THE MOD-2 LAYER

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The pocket layer of the canonical form obeys
two new proved laws - constant pocket-phi from the no-terminal-free world, and parity
transparency - under which |O_1| = 9 survives all mod-2 constraints. The decision at
nine and beyond lives in the mod-4 composite-pin layer, a bounded machine audit.

### 404.1 THE POCKET-PHI LAW (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let X be a pocket (a middle component attached to O_1 only), with
  attachments at positions p_i and feet colours chi_i. Then phi_X := chi_i + p_i
  (mod 2) is CONSTANT over the pocket's attachments.
  Proof. Two attachments joined through X and by the b_1-free arc of O_1 form a cycle
  avoiding every terminal; the no-terminal-free world forces it EVEN, and its parity
  is (chi_i + chi_j) + (p_i + p_j). QED

  So every component - the window component (403.1ii) and every pocket - carries one
  phi-invariant: the canonical form's middle is a system of phi-labelled components.

### 404.2 PARITY TRANSPARENCY OF POCKETS (PROVED)

  LEMMA. A window path detouring through a pocket - exiting the window component at
  attachment l, running an arc to the pocket, through it, an arc onward, re-entering
  at r - has the SAME parity as the direct one-visit window path through the pair
  (l, r): the pocket's two phi-values cancel.
  Proof. The parity telescopes over runs, arcs and attachment edges; the pocket
  contributes phi_X twice. QED
  CONSEQUENCE. Pocket detours create no new ODD seed classes - mixed pairs stay
  mixed, pure pairs stay pure - and the detoured members' arc pieces lie in the left
  and right regions, where every manufactured even path's O_1-arc already meets
  them: multi-visit members are AUTOMATICALLY covered, and nesting stays intact
  exactly as proved for one-visit members. The pocket is structurally invisible at
  the mod-2 layer.

### 404.3 NINE SURVIVES MOD 2; THE DECISION IS MOD 4 (COMPUTED IN OUTLINE)

  At A = 9 the budget fits: window component at three positions straddling, feet at
  (s_1, s_1 + 2), the wrong-parity interior position pocketed with the pocket's two
  further attachments in the outer regions - several layouts, e.g. feet (2,4),
  window {0,1,5}, pocket {3,6,7}. All mod-2 laws - phi, transparency, feet parity,
  the census, the colour laws - are satisfiable simultaneously. What remains against
  A >= 9 is the mod-4 composite-pin layer: the (SC)-pins on even {1,2}-paths routed
  through pockets against the direct ones, the excursion pins, and the access pins,
  all folded into one bounded congruence audit per size. That audit is the next
  instrument; the tightening remains monotone.

### 404.4 Status

PROVED here: the POCKET-PHI LAW (404.1); PARITY TRANSPARENCY and automatic coverage
of pocket detours (404.2).
COMPUTED in outline: A = 9 layouts satisfying every mod-2 law exist (404.3).
NOT PROVED: the mod-4 audit at A >= 9; hence (AVOID), (T3'), (THREAD'), (BP2),
(LOCK-BREAK), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.
