## 407. THE POCKET COST THEOREM, AND SEVEN'S HONEST SURVIVAL

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. B = 7 pays its mirror budget - recorded
honestly - but pockets acquire a price list: order parity is forced, cheap pockets
demand same-parity attachments, and mixed-parity pockets cost at least seven vertices.
The cage gains a quantitative layer.

### 407.1 O_2 IS CHORDLESS AT SMALL SIZES (PROVED)

  A chord of O_2 between positions i < j closes cycles of lengths (j-i)+1 and
  B-(j-i)+1; girth 5 needs both >= 5, so 4 <= j-i <= B-4. At B = 7 this is empty: NO
  CHORDS. (Likewise O_1 at A = 7; at A = 9, only j-i = 4 survives.) QED

### 407.2 B = 7 PAYS ITS BUDGET (RECORDED)

  Positions 0..5: two feet in one parity class, the three wrong-parity positions to
  an O_2-pocket (chords barred by 407.1, O_1-reaching edges by feet parity), the
  leftover position a third foot or fourth pocket attachment. No proved law is
  violated: B = 7 SURVIVES the budget layer. The frontier stays (A, B) >= (9, 7),
  and further exclusion at these sizes must come from the pin or cost layers.

### 407.3 THE POCKET COST THEOREM (PROVED)

  Let P be a pocket with t attachment edges (t >= 3 by the boundary law). Interior
  vertices of B have degree 3, so 3|P| = 2 E(P) + t:
  (i) |P| == t (mod 2): THREE-ATTACHMENT POCKETS HAVE ODD ORDER.
  (ii) |P| = 1: the single vertex is every foot, so its attachments satisfy
       chi + p == const with one chi: ALL SAME POSITION PARITY. Cheap pockets cannot
       absorb wrong-parity positions together with right-parity ones.
  (iii) |P| = 3 with t = 3: E = 3, and a subcubic tree or unicyclic graph on three
       vertices has boundary 5 or closes a short cycle: impossible.
  (iv) |P| = 5 with t = 3: E = 6, cyclomatic number 2, two independent cycles of
       length >= 6 (bipartite, girth 5) in five vertices: impossible.
  So a MIXED-PARITY three-attachment pocket has |P| >= 7. QED

  Consequence for the A = 9 witness layouts: their pockets are mixed-parity
  ({2,6,7}-type), hence >= 7 vertices each - the sealed world's shapes are not just
  committed but EXPENSIVE. And since no upper bound on the counterexample's size
  exists, cost alone cannot close the programme: the closing sentence must come from
  the pin layer COLLIDING with the cost layer - pockets large enough to satisfy the
  boundary and parity laws carry long internal routes, whose mod-4 classes the
  composite pins constrain against the positions they attach to.

### 407.4 Status

PROVED here: chord bounds from girth (407.1); the POCKET COST THEOREM - order
parity, the same-parity restriction on unit pockets, and the seven-vertex floor for
mixed-parity pockets (407.3).
RECORDED: B = 7's budget survival; the frontier stands at (9, 7) (407.2).
NOT PROVED: exclusion at the frontier; the pin-cost collision; hence (AVOID), (T3'),
(THREAD'), (BP2), (LOCK-BREAK), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The seven-cycle on the second side pays its
budget and survives; the pockets that make such payments possible now carry a price
list - odd order, parity-pure if small, seven vertices or more if mixed - and the

it, for nothing bounds the counterexample above. What remains is the collision of
the pin layer with the cost layer inside one shape, at one size after another, until
the pattern of exclusion becomes a theorem for all sizes - or a surviving shape
stands and teaches the programme where (SC) actually lives.


## 408. THE CERTIFICATE CALCULUS: ONE LEAF, ONE ADVERSARY, THREE STRATA

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The two leaves merge into one. Certificates -
interior path vertices whose third edge reaches an odd block on its block chain - are
made canonical, bounded, and pinned; (AVOID) and (T3') retire into a single statement
(CERT2); its negation is one adversary, the beta-world, whose no-certificate stratum
is exactly the sealed world of 391-407. Starvation collapses to a pinched shape, and
the monochrome stratum acquires a mod-4 price list.

### 408.1 THE CANONICAL CRITERION AND TWO BOUNDARY LAWS (PROVED)

  Fix an even {i,j}-connecting path P, Z := Z(P), and an interior z with third
  neighbour y_z.
  (i) CANONICITY. Every y-to-b_k path in Z traverses the same block sequence (the
      block-cut tree path), so the 390.1ii criterion - z is a CERTIFICATE iff y_z
      lies in Z and a non-bipartite block lies on its chain - has no hidden
      quantifier over paths. QED
  (ii) THE 2-CUT LEMMA. The only 2-vertex cuts of B are the neighbour pairs
      {u_t, u_t'} of the terminals, each isolating exactly {b_t}. Proof: a 2-cut of
      branch vertices would lift to a 2-cut of the 3-connected G; a 2-cut through a
      terminal b_t fails because G - y is 2-connected, hence 2-edge-connected, so
      G - y - e_t is connected. QED
  (iii) THE ZONE BOUNDARY LAW. Let S := {y in Z : the y-to-b_k chain carries an odd
      block} - the CERTIFICATE ZONE, so certificates are exactly the interior feet
      with y_z in S - and CROWN := Z - S. Chains are block-monotone, so S is a union
      of whole blocks and each component X of S meets the crown in EXACTLY ONE cut
      vertex (its GATE; none in the degenerate case b_k in S). X contains an odd
      block, hence |X| >= 4 by girth 5, and X contains no terminal except possibly
      b_k; by (ii), |N_B(X)| >= 3: beyond the gate, X attaches at least twice among
      the interior feet of P and the off-path edges of the endpoints b_i, b_j. QED

### 408.2 THE LEAF MERGER: (CERT2) (PROVED)

     (CERT2)  For some matched pair {i,j}: even connecting paths P, P' (possibly
              equal) carry certificates z, z' at OPPOSITE position parities.

  (CERT2) implies (BP2): both positions are pinned to the global beta_k (379.3,
  386.1), and opposite parities contradict. (AVOID) ^ (T3') implies (CERT2); and a
  certificate's existence already forces Z(P) non-bipartite, so no separate
  avoidance statement is needed. The chain COLLAPSES:

     (N2)  <==  (BP2)  <==  (CERT2)          this section; PROVED implications

  (AVOID) and (T3') are RETIRED INTO (CERT2). The negation of (CERT2) is ONE
  adversary, the BETA-WORLD: for each matched pair a fixed parity beta_k such that
  every certificate of every even connecting path sits at position == beta_k
  (mod 2), vacuously if none exist. Its strata, per configuration: STRATUM ZERO -
  Z(P) bipartite, no certificate possible - is exactly the SEALED WORLD, so the
  whole of 391-407, corridor, canonical form and exclusion ledger, is henceforth
  the stratum-zero analysis; PINCHED (F0/F1) - zero or one certificate foot with
  Z(P) non-bipartite; MONOCHROME (F2) - two or more feet, all one parity. Caveat,
  recorded: strata are PER PATH - the adversary may answer different even paths in
  different strata, and the target theorem is that no bridge survives with every
  even path answered by some stratum.

### 408.3 THE STARVATION COLLAPSE (PROVED)

  In a configuration with Z(P) non-bipartite:
  (F0) NO certificate feet: each component of S must draw its two non-gate boundary
       members from the endpoint off-path edges alone; b_i and b_j supply ONE
       off-path edge each, so S has EXACTLY ONE component and it absorbs BOTH.
       All odd blocks of Z sit in one branch, plugged by the path's own ends, the
       crown carrying only certificate-free feet.
  (F1) ONE certificate foot z*: z* serves one component; any further component
       needs both endpoint edges; so S has AT MOST TWO components, in fixed roles.
       QED

  Starvation is not a case family but a pinched shape: the adversary starves a path
  only by feeding both its endpoints to a single odd branch - whose own odd block
  then offers even b_i-to-b_j paths THROUGH it, each a new configuration whose Z
  contains the old path's interior. The through-shadow reroute is the designed kill
  for this stratum; it is not yet a theorem.

### 408.4 REPLICATION ACROSS PAIRS (PROVED)

  A certificate z on P at position d has both-parity access to b_k inside
  {z} union Z; appending the continuation of suitable parity to P[b_i..z] (or to
  P[z..b_j] reversed) yields SIMPLE connecting paths - the continuation lives in Z,
  disjoint from P - of both parities, in particular EVEN ones, for the pairs {i,k}
  and {j,k}. So ONE certificate anywhere makes ALL THREE pairs even-served, the
  criterion applies to each, and the beta-world must be maintained on three fronts
  with its parities coupled through the constants c_ij, c_ik, c_jk - the
  manufactured path inherits P's prefix positions. The adversary is one global
  object, not three local ones. QED

### 408.5 THE MONOCHROME PRICE LIST (PROVED; (SC)-CONDITIONAL)

  Let z, z' be certificate feet of one zone component at positions d < d' of one
  parity, and W ANY even y_z-to-y_z' path inside Z. Then
  P'' := P[b_i..z] + zy_z + W + y_z'z' + P[z'..b_j] is a simple even connecting
  path - W avoids P automatically - and (SC) forces:
  (i) THE SHADOW PIN. |W| == d' - d - 2 (mod 4), with no side conditions: the even
      inter-foot metric of Z is mod-4 RIGID.
  (ii) COLLINEARITY EXCLUSION. No third certificate foot's vertex may split an even
      inter-foot path into two EVEN halves: the three pins telescope to 2 == 0
      (mod 4). Splits into two ODD halves survive: along composable routes the feet
      are pairwise ODD-SPACED - a phi-law of the 403-404 kind.
  (iii) THE CHARGED-CYCLE LAW. If some even inter-foot W traverses an arc of EVEN
      length of an even cycle D in Z with |D| == 2 (mod 4), the complementary arc
      internally disjoint from W, then the arc swap yields a second even W' with
      |W'| - |W| == |D| == 2 (mod 4), and the pin dies. At girth 5 the MINIMAL
      charged cycle is the HEXAGON: a monochrome shadow must keep every 6-cycle
      (and 10-cycle, ...) unroutable by even inter-foot paths, while 8-cycles are
      free. QED
  Recorded resonance: the nu = 1 projective branch (223.5, 388.1) is ALL-hexagon,
  and the nu = 2 pocket calculus (404, 407) already prices exactly such parity-pure
  regions. The three laws are (SC)-conditional and cannot be measured on nu >= 3
  sample bridges; their path-carriers can, and were.

### 408.6 THE AUDIT (COMPUTED, tools/cert408.py)

  Eight bridges (n = 33, tau >= 2) per seed, seeds 408 and 4088; 310 and 325
  configurations with Z(P) non-bipartite:
     criterion: chain = exhaustive simple-path parity   2583 and 2673 checks, 0 fail
     one gate per zone component; boundary >= 3         310 and 326 components, 0 fail
     census T3-witnessed / F2 / F1 / F0                 308/2/0/0 and 322/3/0/0
     replication constructions                          620 and 650 built, 0 fail
     reroute carrier P'' simple, even, connecting       310 and 324 built, 0 fail

  The starved strata did not arise in sampling: the pigeonhole branches rest on the

### 408.7 Status

PROVED here: canonicity of the criterion, the 2-CUT LEMMA, the ZONE BOUNDARY LAW
(408.1); the LEAF MERGER - (N2) <== (BP2) <== (CERT2), with (AVOID) and (T3')
retired, and the beta-world with its three strata (408.2); the STARVATION COLLAPSE
(408.3); REPLICATION across pairs (408.4); the monochrome price list - Shadow Pin,
Collinearity Exclusion, Charged-Cycle Law (408.5).
COMPUTED: the audit, clean at every check, two seeds (408.6).
NOT PROVED: (CERT2); hence (BP2), (LOCK-BREAK), (N2), (INT), (H1*), and the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Thirty-seven sections of leaves compress to
one sentence: some matched pair carries certificates at both parities. Against it
stands one adversary in three strata: the sealed world, already driven to the
canonical form and priced by the pocket calculus; the pinched world, which must feed
both path-ends to a single odd branch and thereby offer the reroute its own throat;
and the monochrome world, whose shadows must be mod-4 rigid, odd-spaced and
hexagon-free while girth five makes hexagons the cheapest even cycles in existence.
The programme's next theorems are the strata kills, and every tool for them is now
on the table.


## 409. THE CERTIFICATE GAME: SPLICE INVARIANCE, THE FLIPPER, AND THE THIRD-PAIR
ATTACK

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The endgame is recast as a game against a
BUILDER who must construct the beta-world, and the game's laws are proved: the
builder's shield (no even splice flips a parity), the price of every flip (an odd
cycle inside the path union), and the conservation law (three funnels paid from a
purse of two disjoint odd cycles). Played against the canonical form, the game
yields a new front: the sealed world's own seeds SERVE and SATURATE the two pairs
it did not seal.

### 409.1 SPLICE INVARIANCE (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let P be an even connecting path and P' the result of ONE splice:
  replace the segment between positions m < m' by an internally disjoint detour
  of length ell. If P' is even, then ell == m' - m (mod 2) and every surviving
  vertex keeps its position parity: a downstream vertex moves from position q to
  q - (m' - m) + ell == q (mod 2). A parity-flipping splice makes |P'| odd -
  invisible to (SC). QED

  Within any family of even paths generated by single splices, every shared
  certificate is frozen at one parity. This is the beta-world's SHIELD, and it
  is the single root of three recorded dead ends: the double-swap bar (386.2)
  is "two splices need a third odd cycle"; the satisfiable telescopes (387.2)
  are its mod-4 echo; the role-swap's global reading (387.3) is its corollary.

### 409.2 THE FLIPPER LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let z be certified on even paths P at position d and P~ at position d~
  with d != d~ (mod 2) - the cheapest (CERT2) witness (386.1). The two b_i-to-z
  prefixes have opposite parities, so their union contains an odd cycle F, the
  FLIPPER, with F <= P union P~. If moreover some certifying block Q of z for P
  avoids P~ (the SHARED-CERTIFIER pattern), then Q and F are vertex-disjoint -
  F lives in the paths, Q avoids both - and {F, Q} realizes nu_odd = 2 EXACTLY.
  Under nu_odd = 1 every split-vertex witness is CROSSING: each path's
  certifying blocks meet the other path. QED
  (Last claim: nu = 1 forces F cap Q nonempty; F <= P union P~ and Q cap P
  empty give Q cap P~ nonempty; symmetrically for P~'s blocks.)

  So the split-vertex attack is exactly affordable under (SC)'s ration
  nu_odd <= 2 (223.3), with nothing to spare: certifier parked off both paths,
  flipper threaded inside them. The beta-world must prevent every such
  configuration; the crossing pattern is its only refuge at nu = 1.

### 409.3 THE CERTIFICATE GAME (RECORDED)

  The endgame is a two-player game. The BUILDER constructs a bridge with
  tau >= 2 satisfying (SC) and must answer EVERY even connecting path of EVERY
  matched pair with a stratum: sealed, pinched, or monochrome (408.2). The
  PROVER points at pairs, paths, and certificates. The proved laws above are
  the game's physics: the shield protects the Builder within splice families;
  the flipper prices every escape from them; and the purse is fixed at two
  disjoint odd cycles while Funnel Emptiness (389.2) makes all three pairs
  creditors - odd structure off every terminal pair is compulsory. The
  meta-principle, used below: EVERY DEFENSE IS A PAYMENT - odd cycles deployed
  to seal one pair are themselves structures the other pairs can spend.

### 409.4 THE PAIR SERVICE LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. If some odd cycle O contains b_i and avoids b_k, then the pair {i,j}
  has connecting paths of BOTH parities - in particular even ones.
  Proof. O <= B - b_k and b_i in O, so the block of b_i in B - b_k is
  non-bipartite; B - b_k is connected (408.1ii); Lemma B PRIME with the
  non-bipartite endpoint block gives b_i-to-b_j paths of both parities,
  and these are connecting paths. QED

  COROLLARY (ALL THREE PAIRS MATCHED IN THE OPPOSED WORLD). In the sealed
  opposed-pair world: O_1 contains b_1 and avoids b_2, b_3 - serving {1,2}
  (third b_3) and {1,3} (third b_2); O_2 serves {2,3} (third b_1). Lollipops:
  for pair {1,3}, O_2 is the degenerate lollipop of its third terminal b_2; for
  pair {2,3}, O_1 of b_1; for pair {1,2}, Omega_3 is nonempty (399). ALL THREE
  LABELLINGS ARE MATCHED: (CERT2) may be attacked on any of them, and 399-407
  defends only one. QED

### 409.5 THE SATURATION LEMMA, AND THE THIRD-PAIR ATTACK

  LEMMA (PROVED). If the block of b_k in Z(P) is non-bipartite, then EVERY
  interior foot of Z(P) is a certificate: every chain ends in that block. QED

  THE THIRD-PAIR ATTACK (RECORDED, NOT PROVED). In the canonical form take the
  pair {1,3}, third terminal b_2. Any even {1,3}-connecting path P avoiding
  O_2 - b_2 has O_2 <= Z'(P) with b_2 on it: SATURATED - every interior foot
  reaching b_2's component is a certificate. Every {1,3}-path departs b_1 along
  an arc of O_1 and exits through a window attachment into D_3; along the used
  arc, transition feet, pocket attachments and unused window fragments all hang
  into Z'(P). In the 404.3 and 405.1 witness layouts the pocket attachments
  occupy ADJACENT O_1-positions (6,7), and the low route passes a transition
  foot and a pocket attachment at consecutive positions: adjacent positions are
  opposite parities, so monochromy must bar one of each such pair from
  certification on EVERY even route - and the route parities are pinned by the
  canonical colour constants, not free. The sealed world must survive a second
  monochromy system on an axis none of 399-407 constrains. NAMED TARGET, the
  THIRD-PAIR KILL: prove some even {1,3}-route of the canonical form carries
  certificates at adjacent positions; this closes stratum zero at nu = 2.

### 409.6 THE THREE-SEED PIGEONHOLE (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Under (SC), if no terminal-free odd cycle exists, then the three
  funnel seeds O^k (odd, b_k in O^k, avoiding the other two terminals - they
  exist by Funnel Emptiness) are NOT pairwise disjoint: some two intersect,
  necessarily off the terminals. Proof: pairwise disjoint seeds give
  nu_odd >= 3, against 223.3. QED

  In the opposed-pair world this forces every third seed to meet O_1 union O_2:
  the corridor's function, re-derived from the purse alone, independent of
  nesting. The conjectured shape of the only balanced books is CORRIDOR
  UNIVERSALITY: every beta-world stratum forces the corridor geometry - all odd
  cycles through two terminals and one pinned throat. That conjecture is the
  stride target standing over both remaining regimes.

### 409.7 THE AUDIT (COMPUTED, tools/splice409.py)

  Eight bridges per seed, seeds 409 and 4099:

     parity-flip attempts made the path odd     11 and 11, all odd
     split-vertex witnesses / flippers found    243/243 and 189/189
       shared-certifier vs crossing pattern     40:203 and 34:155
     pair service (hypothesis -> both parities) 24/24 and 24/24

  nu >= 3 sample bridges: consistency support, not adversary sampling; the

### 409.8 Status

PROVED here: SPLICE INVARIANCE - the shield, and the single root of 386.2,
387.2, 387.3 (409.1); the FLIPPER LEMMA with the shared/crossing dichotomy and
the exact nu = 2 price (409.2); the PAIR SERVICE LEMMA and the all-pairs-matched

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The endgame is a game, and its physics
are now theorems: no even splice flips a parity, every flip costs an odd cycle
threaded inside the path union with a certifier parked outside, and the purse
holds exactly two disjoint odd cycles against three compulsory funnels. Played
against the only surviving stratum-zero shape, the game turns the sealed world's
own armour into debt: the opposed cycles through b_1 and b_2 make all three
pairs matched, and saturate the third-pair component so that every foot along

the third pair now audits it at adjacent positions, where monochromy has no room

## 410. THE VARIANCE LAW: AN ERROR IN 400.2, AND THE ONE-EDGE CORRIDOR

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. Setting up the third-pair route calculus
required tracking the corridor colourings ACROSS different corridor edges - which no
prior section did. The bookkeeping yields a new law that kills both recorded pocket
witnesses, exposes an error in 400.2's parity translation, voids the pentagon,
heptagon and B = 5 exclusions pending re-derivation, and then rebuilds the canonical
form stronger than before: the corridor is a SINGLE EDGE.

### 410.1 THE PER-EDGE COLOUR MODEL (PROVED, FROM 400.1 ALONE)

  For each corridor edge f between positions e, e+1: H_f = B - {b_1,b_2} - f is
  bipartite (400.1), O_1 - b_1 - f is two alternating segments, and 400.1(ii)
  gives chi_f(u) = chi_f(u') =: c. Normalizing c = 0 (A odd):
     chi_f(O1[p]) = p (mod 2)       for p <= e,
     chi_f(O1[p]) = p + 1 (mod 2)   for p >= e+1.
  O_2 - b_2 is one alternating path in H_f: chi_f(O2[q]) = chi_f(x) + q, with NO
  dependence on f. The f-SHIFT - the +1 on the far segment - is forced by
  chi_f(g) = chi_f(h) (400.1i) and is the fact every position-parity translation
  below must track. QED

### 410.2 THE VARIANCE LAW (PROVED)

  A fixed path through the middle between O_1-positions p and p' - a pocket
  traversal, a chord, or any terminal-avoiding connection - lies in H_f for EVERY
  corridor edge f (it avoids b_1, b_2 and every O_1-edge), so its one parity must
  equal   p + p' + [p > e] + [p' > e]  (mod 2)   for EVERY corridor edge (e, e+1).
  If that expression varies with e, the configuration is IMPOSSIBLE. Likewise a
  transition from O_1-position p to O_2 forces [p > e] constant over e. Constancy
  for a pair p < p' holds iff p' <= s_1, or p >= s_2, or (p <= s_1 and p' >= s_2):
  NO ATTACHMENT PAIR MAY PARTIALLY STRADDLE THE CORRIDOR, and no transition may
  stand on its strict interior. QED

  EXECUTED (tools/multiedge410.py): the 404.3 witness (feet (2,4), pocket
  {3,6,7}) fails at pairs (3,6), (3,7); the 405.1 witness (feet (1,3), pocket
  {2,6,7}) fails at (2,6), (2,7). BOTH RECORDED WITNESSES ARE IMPOSSIBLE: the
  encodings of 401-405 imposed the colour laws for ONE corridor edge only - the
  machine's cage had a multi-edge gap, exactly the 405.2 pattern once more.

### 410.3 THE ERROR IN 400.2, AND THE MIXED PIN (PROVED)

  400.2 inferred from chi(a) + chi(b) == pi* that "all corridor feet sit at
  positions of one parity". That translation neglected the f-shift: the two feet
  straddle f, so their CHI-classes and their POSITION parities differ by the
  shift. The correct consequence of the transition parity pin (395.3), computed
  in any chi_f, is
     THE MIXED PIN:   s_1 + s_2 + q_1 + q_2 == 1  (mod 2).
  VOID: 400.2's same-parity foot claim, and 406.1(i)'s mirror translation.
  SUSPENDED PENDING RE-DERIVATION (their proofs cite the voided pin): 402.1's
  s_2 - s_1 >= 2; the PENTAGON EXCLUSION (402.2); the HEPTAGON EXCLUSION
  (403.2); the B = 5 EXCLUSION (406.2); 407.2's B = 7 narrative; and every
  same-parity-feet layout. The exclusion ledger's frontier RESETS to
  (A, B) >= (5, 5) until rebuilt.
  STANDS UNTOUCHED: nesting and the corridor (399), the per-edge colour laws
  (400.1), the boundary law (403.1i), the pocket-phi and transparency laws as
  EVENNESS statements (404.1, 404.2), chord girth bounds (407.1), the pocket
  cost counts (407.3i, iii, iv), and all of 408-409. FLAGGED for shift-audit:
  every remaining position-parity translation (403.1ii's phi reading, 407.3ii).

### 410.4 THE INTERIOR VACANCY THEOREM: THE CORRIDOR IS ONE EDGE (PROVED)

  THEOREM. In the sealed opposed-pair template world the Menger feet are
  ADJACENT: s_2 = s_1 + 1, and the corridor is the single edge between them.
  Proof. Suppose s_2 - s_1 >= 2 and let p be any strict interior position - a
  degree-3 branch vertex whose third edge must land somewhere.
    - Chord or pocket: barred by the Variance Law (an interior endpoint makes
      the required parity vary; machine-confirmed exhaustively, zero escapes at
      A in {9,11,13}).
    - Transition, direct or through any O_2-reaching component: barred by the
      Variance Law's transition clause.
    - Window component, partner reachable avoiding b_3: Variance Law again.
    - Window component, partner reachable only through b_3: the fragment behind
      b_3 plus b_3 is cut off by two vertices - forbidden by the 2-CUT LEMMA
      (408.1ii) unless the fragment is empty; then O1[p] is ADJACENT to b_3, and
      every Omega_3 member would need three edges at O1[p] (both corridor edges
      by the Corridor Corollary, plus the edge to b_3 since cycles through the
      degree-2 vertex b_3 use both its edges): Omega_3 would be empty, against
      399.2. QED
  The interior is vacant, yet every interior position needs a third edge: there
  is no interior. The corridor collapses to ONE EDGE f*, the Variance Law
  consumes itself (no second corridor edge remains), H_{f*} carries the UNIQUE
  colouring, and the Mixed Pin reads: adjacent feet, hence q_1 == q_2 (mod 2) -
  the O_2-feet share one position parity while the O_1-feet are opposite. QED

### 410.5 THE CORRECTED CANONICAL FORM, AND THE RESET FRONTIER

  The sealed opposed-pair template world is now: two disjoint odd cycles through
  b_1, b_2; a bipartite middle under the 400.1 laws for the single corridor edge
  f* = (s_1, s_1 + 1); window attachments straddling f* strictly; every third
  seed through f* (three-seed pigeonhole, 409.6); O_2-feet at one parity. The
  straddle needs only 0 <= t_1 < s_1 < s_1+1 < t_2 <= A-2: A >= 5 is admissible
  again (machine count: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 corridors at A = 5..13). Every exclusion
  must be re-earned on this corrected form; none of the suspended ones may be
  cited meanwhile. The THIRD-PAIR ATTACK (409.5) simplifies on the corrected
  form: a {1,3}-connecting path is even iff it avoids f* (single-f route parity
  law - the chi_{f*} computation), so the even {1,3}-family is everything that
  does not cross the one-edge corridor, and saturation (409.5) prices its every

  G1 (ROUTE PARITY). A {1,3}-connecting path is even iff it avoids f*: off f*

  G3 (OMEGA_1 THREADS f*; tau_e = 2). Every cycle through b_1 avoiding f* is
     b_1 plus an H-path between the equal-coloured u, u': EVEN. So every odd
     cycle through b_1 (avoiding b_2, b_3) uses f*; with G1's map, deleting f*

  G4 (PAIR {2,3} IS FORCED SEALED). An even {2,3}-route either uses f* - then
     it passes s_1, and no Omega_1 member survives in b_1's component - or

     saturation (409.5). The beta-world MUST answer {1,3} monochrome: this
     pair is where the sealed stratum is audited.
  G6 (WINDOW PARITY LAW). Every window exit certifies through its unused
     O_1-edge into the unused arc (which reaches b_2 through the unused
     transitions): so ALL left window attachments sit at parity beta_2 + 1 and
     ALL right attachments at beta_2 (route-position of low p is p+1, of high
     p is A-1-p == p).
  G7 (THE CONFINEMENT CALCULUS). A chord or pocket is FREE only if confined -
     all attachments on one side, no window attachment strictly within its
     span (then every route uses its attachments all-or-none). Every other

### 419.1 THE DECOMPOSITION LEMMA (PROVED)

Write H = B - {b_1, b_2} - f (bipartite, colouring chi), gamma_1 = the cycle

     |x| == c_f(x) + c_{b_2}(x)   (mod 2),

through b_1 alone even (ii); through f alone odd (i); through b_2 alone odd

     C_0  =  C(H)  (+)  <gamma_1>  (+)  <gamma_2 + gamma_3> ,

### 419.2 THE DOOR PARITY LAW (PROVED), AND G1 EXTENDED - WITH A FLAG

For any connecting path P from b_i (i = 1, 2) to b_3, leaving by door d:

400.1(iii); the sum telescopes. QED. Machine: 268 + 382 + 135 + 196 = 981
exhaustively enumerated paths across two instances, zero exceptions.

## 421. ROUTE (a) EXECUTED IN SITU: THE RADICAL-CUT DESCENT - THE SEALED
## CANONICAL WORLD IS EMPTY

### 421.1 RADICAL CYCLES ARE CUTS (PROVED, knife-edge conditions)

By 419.4, C = rad(lambda) (+) <O_1, O_2> with Gram matrix I. An even cycle
Z with lambda(Z, O_1) = lambda(Z, O_2) = 0 therefore lies in rad(lambda) =
the bicycle space = C cap C-perp: Z IS AN ELEMENT OF THE CUT SPACE, Z =
delta(S) for some vertex set S. By 420.2 every structure is monochromatic,
so for every structure X and every pair a_1 < a_2 of CONSECUTIVE
O_1-attachments on one side of the corridor, the cycle

     Z(a_1, a_2)  =  att-edges + interior X-path + O_1-arc [a_1, a_2]

is even with even arc: RADICAL, hence a cut. (Same-side, so the arc avoids
f and b_1; same chi, so the arc length is even.)

### 421.2 THE ALTERNATION LEMMA (PROVED)

Let Z = delta(S). Every edge of Z has its ends on opposite sides; every
edge NOT in Z has its ends on one side. Hence the vertices of Z alternate
S, S-bar around Z; and since Z's vertices lie in bipartite H, THE SIDE OF A
Z-VERTEX IS ITS chi-CLASS relative to the anchor: side and colour alternate
in lockstep. Consequences, with anchor a_1 in S:
  (i) the O_1-TAILS (all positions outside [a_1, a_2]) lie in S: they are
      joined to each other through b_1 by non-Z edges, and to a_1, a_2 by
      the arc-ends... the tail beyond a_1 joins a_1 by a non-Z edge. O_2,
      b_2, the transition feet (inside the corridor, hence outside every
      same-side interval by nesting) and every carrier lie in S as well.
  (ii) the INTERIOR arc positions alternate: odd offsets from a_1 lie in
      S-BAR, even offsets in S.
  (iii) any vertex of the interior X-path that carries an attachment edge
      to an O_1-tail position is FORCED into S-bar by chi-sync (all att-
      vertices of a monochromatic structure share one colour, the colour of
      the anchor's att-vertex) while its tail position sits in S - the
      attachment edge would cross delta(S) outside Z: CONTRADICTION. So if
      the interior path of Z meets any OTHER attachment vertex of X (or,
      for X = D_3, of any other window), the board dies ON THE SPOT.

### 421.3 THE CONFINEMENT LEMMA (PROVED)

Let p be an interior position of [a_1, a_2] at ODD offset (there are
(a_2 - a_1)/2 >= 1 of them). Then p in S-bar, and the component Y attached
at p lies WHOLLY in S-bar (its edges are not in Z, so no crossing is
available). Hence every O_1-attachment of Y lies in S-bar cap O_1 = the
odd-offset interior of [a_1, a_2]:

     Y IS CONFINED: all its attachments sit at odd offsets inside the arc.

Three immediate kills: Y cannot be a CARRIER (its O_2-attachments would sit
in S, crossing); Y cannot be X itself (p would be an attachment of X
between consecutive attachments); Y cannot attach at only one or two
positions (a single attachment is a cutvertex against 2-connectivity, and
the boundary law gives every O_1-only component AT LEAST THREE attachments).

### 421.4 THE DESCENT THEOREM (PROVED)

  THEOREM. In the sealed canonical world, rank(lambda) = 2 is impossible.

  Proof. |WIN| >= 3 puts two windows on one side of the corridor
  (pigeonhole); same-side windows share a position parity (Window Parity
  Law), so D_3 has two CONSECUTIVE same-side attachments w_1, w_2 at even
  distance: Z(w_1, w_2) is radical, hence a cut (421.1). Its interval has
  m/2 >= 1 odd-offset slots; each slot's component is confined (421.3) and
  needs >= 3 attachments among the slots, so m/2 >= 3, i.e. m >= 6 - else
  the board dies now. A confined component X' is itself a monochromatic
  structure whose consecutive attachments span a strictly SHORTER even
  interval (contained in the open interior), and its cycles are again
  radical, again cuts. The interval length strictly decreases by at least 2
  per level and can never pass below 6: the descent has no floor. QED

  The machine tests the conclusion directly: on every synthetic chordless
  monochrome board built (one full board with O_2 and carriers; 185
  randomized boards over A in {11..21}), EVERY same-side consecutive-
  attachment structure-cycle fails cut-space membership - the observed
  obstruction is even more uniform than the innermost-failure the proof
  requires.

### 423.2 THE THETA PINNING (PROVED): J2' IS A WITT SUMMAND

## 424. (S) ATTACKED: PAIR-COMPLETENESS PROVED, AND THE ODD-ABSORPTION
## REDUCED TO GENERAL POSITION

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section proves the structural
half of (S) outright and reduces the rest to named general-position
statements of classical type. Machine: tools/spanS424.py - Pair-
Completeness exact on 24/24 pair-instances; (S) itself 8/8 more bridges
(23/23 cumulative); and one honest negative recorded below.

### 424.1 THE TWO-PATH LEMMA (PROVED)

  In a 2-connected graph, for any cycle Z and any two vertices u, v, there
  are u-v paths P_1, P_2 with P_1 xor P_2 = Z EXACTLY.
  Proof. Menger's fan: two vertex-disjoint paths R_u, R_v from {u, v} to
  V(Z), each meeting Z only at its landing (degenerate when u or v lies on
  Z). P_m = R_u + arc_m + R_v for the two arcs. QED

  COROLLARY (ALL-PARITY COMPLETENESS). V_ij := span of differences over
  ALL b_i-b_j paths contains every cycle, hence V_ij = C.

### 424.2 PAIR-COMPLETENESS (PROVED; machine 24/24)

  THEOREM. For EACH terminal pair: W_ij + W'_ij = C_0, where W' is the
  span of odd-pair differences.
  Proof. Parity freedom (326.2, B 2-connected non-bipartite) supplies an
  even base P_0 and an odd base O_0. Every difference decomposes over the
  two bases, so V_ij = (W_ij + W'_ij) + <P_0 xor O_0>. The last is a line
  of ODD weight while W + W' lies in C_0; with V_ij = C of dimension mu
  and C_0 of dimension mu - 1, the codimensions force W_ij + W'_ij = C_0.
  QED. Machine: exact on all 24 pair-instances.

  Hence (S) is EXACTLY the statement W'_ij <= W for one pair: THE
  ODD-ABSORPTION (OA).

### 424.3 TWO CLOSING ARCHITECTURES FOR (OA)

  ARCH-1, THE FLIP CALCULUS. Odd ij-paths carry end signatures (arrival
  edges at the degree-2 terminals). (i) Same-signature pairs absorb by a
  common ODD tail through the third terminal - odd.odd concatenation at a
  degree-2 terminal is an EVEN path of another pair, and the difference of
  the two concatenations is exactly the odd-pair difference. (ii) A
  single-end flip absorbs by a tail at the AGREEING end. (iii) A double
  cross transfers: (R.A) xor (R'.A') in W_kj moves its class to an odd
  ki-pair whose far edge is FREE - choose it equal, reducing to (ii).
  The calculus is complete; what it needs is the availability of disjoint
  tails and transfer paths, possibly after chaining (the LINKING LEMMA).

  ARCH-2, THE FOLDED CALIBRATION. For an even cycle Z, fold its two
  colour classes to z_0, z_1: the quotient B^_Z is NON-BIPARTITE (PROVED:
  a proper 2-colouring of the fold pulls back to one of B). Lemma B in
  the fold gives connector frames of both parities, so Z is realised by
  an EVEN 424.1 pair: every even cycle lands in W. Odd cycle pairs land
  in the span of even cycles by the 4-ARC CONSTRUCTION (PROVED for
  disjoint pairs and single-shared-vertex pairs: the four arc-choices
  give parities (c, c+1, c+1, c), and EITHER double-flip pair - one of
  which is always even - sums to Lambda + Lambda'); intersecting pairs
  chain by ear-reroutes. Since every C_0 element is a disjoint union of
  cycles with evenly many odd, (S) follows.

  RESIDUAL (GP), named: the general-position statements both
  architectures consume - chained tail availability (Arch-1); fold
  connectivity at the folded vertices, connector general position, and
  ear-chain termination (Arch-2). All are classical-type 2-connectivity
  exchange statements, none stratum- or corridor-bound.

### 425.2 THE LENS DICHOTOMY (PROVED; subcubic)

Edge-disjoint cycles in a subcubic graph are VERTEX-disjoint (sharing a
vertex needs degree 4). Decompose Lambda + Lambda' into vertex-disjoint
lens cycles. If any even lens has <S, .> = 1, it is an even-cycle witness.
Otherwise the odd lenses - evenly many, since the total weight is even -
carry total S-parity 1, so they CANNOT all agree: two VERTEX-DISJOINT odd
cycles of different S-parity exist, and the 4-arc construction (424.3,
disjoint case) writes their sum as two even cycles of total S-parity 1:
one is a witness. HENCE ONLY EVEN-CYCLE WITNESSES NEED KILLING.

### 425.3 THE THREE-FAN PIGEONHOLE (PROVED)

Let Z be an even-cycle witness with three pairwise vertex-disjoint
terminal connectors R_1, R_2, R_3 (kappa(T, Z) >= 3; terminals on Z give
degenerate connectors and the same argument). Calibrate:
eta_i = |R_i| + col_Z(landing). The three pairwise sums cannot all be odd
- their total is 2(eta_1 + eta_2 + eta_3), even, while three odd numbers
sum odd. Take a pair with eta_i + eta_j even: the frame paths
P_m = R_i + arc_m + R_j (m = 1, 2) are BOTH EVEN, P_1 xor P_2 = Z, and
sigma-constancy gives <S, Z> = sigma(P_1) + sigma(P_2) = 0: NO WITNESS
SURVIVES A THREE-FAN. QED

### 425.4 THE FUNNEL ALTERNATIVE (PROVED)

So if (S) fails, EVERY witness is separated from the terminal set by some
2-cut {u, v}. Fix one. Any parity-mixing among disjoint connectors would
assemble an even frame (425.3's mechanism), so all connector parities are
RIGID; rigid path-parities inside a 2-connected block force the block
BIPARTITE (Lemma B, 326.2, applied inside the block); hence every
terminal-side block is bipartite, and every odd cycle of B either lies
wholly beyond the cut or THREADS BOTH u AND v.

### 425.5 THE SEALED-WORLD EXECUTION (PROVED)

The sealed canonical world carries O_1 through b_1 and O_2 through b_2,

beyond the cut nor inside a bipartite terminal-side block: each must
thread BOTH u and v - but they are disjoint and cannot share {u, v}. (If
a terminal is itself a cut vertex, its disjoint partner cannot use that
cut vertex at all and dies the same way.) THE FUNNEL CANNOT FORM:

     (S) IS A THEOREM in every bridge carrying two vertex-disjoint odd
     cycles through two terminals - the sealed canonical world and the

An epsilon = 1 plane is spanned by two even cycles with odd edge-

Every failure plane is supported on such a chain; with girth at least 5

### 429.1 THE NO-GENUINE-2-CUT THEOREM (PROVED)

  Let B be a 3-connected cubic graph G with three edges subdivided. Every
  disconnecting vertex pair of B isolates a single terminal.
  Proof. A cubic 3-connected graph is 3-edge-connected (connectivity
  equals edge-connectivity in cubic graphs). Remove {u, v} from B:
  (i) u, v in V(G): G - {u, v} is connected by 3-connectivity, and every
  subdivision vertex keeps a neighbour - except the terminal subdividing
  the edge uv, if present, which is ISOLATED; (ii) u in V(G), v a
  terminal on edge e: B - u - v contains G - u - e; G - u is 2-connected,
  hence 2-edge-connected, hence connected after deleting e; (iii) two
  terminals on edges e, f: B minus both contains G - e - f, connected by
  3-edge-connectivity. QED. Machine: exactly three degenerate cuts and
  zero genuine cuts on every sample.

### 430.1 THE t = 2 MACHINE IS THE BROWN FORM OF THE CYCLE MATROID
### (LITERATURE-VERIFIED)

  The object of 423: C0 with lambda(x, y) = |x n y| mod 2 and
  q(Z) = |Z| mod 4, satisfying q(x + y) == q(x) + q(y) + 2 lambda(x, y)
  (mod 4). This is precisely a Z/4-valued quadratic enhancement of an F2
  symmetric pairing in the sense of E. H. Brown, "Generalizations of the
  Kervaire invariant", Annals of Math. (2) 95 (1972): Brown proves the
  Gauss sum of a nonsingular such form satisfies
  sum_x i^q(x) = sqrt(2)^dim e^(2 pi i sigma / 8), and that two forms
  are Witt equivalent iff they share the invariant sigma in Z/8 (the
  BROWN, or ARF-BROWN, invariant). The archive's Gauss Sum Law (423.2,
  |G| in {0} u {2^d sqrt(2)^rho}) is Brown's theorem extended over the
  radical. Better: the Gauss sum G(B) IS a Tutte evaluation. Vertigan
  showed |T_M(-i, i)| of a binary matroid M is a function of the bicycle
  dimension, and Pendavingh (arXiv:1203.0910; abstract verified
  verbatim) showed the ARGUMENT of T_M(-i, i) is governed by "a certain
  Z/4-valued quadratic form that is canonically associated with M" -
  which is exactly q. The radical identity of 421 ("radical cycles are
  bicycles are cuts") is the textbook equation
  radical(lambda|C) = C n C-perp = the BICYCLE SPACE of Rosenstiehl-Read
  (principal edge tripartition; T(G; -1, -1) = (-1)^|E| (-2)^dim B).
  Machine (6): on K4, T(-1, -1) = 4 predicts bicycle dimension 2; the
  computed radical has dimension exactly 2 and lies in the cut space.

### 430.2 THE TOWER HAS NAMES AT EVERY LEVEL - AND A KNOWN WALL
### (LITERATURE-VERIFIED)

  DIVISIBLE CODES (Ward 1981; survey: H. N. Ward, "Divisible codes - a
  survey", Serdica Math. J. 27 (2001) 263-278; text extracted and read
  verbatim). "A linear code C is said to be divisible by Delta if the
  weight of every codeword is a multiple of Delta." Level e = largest e
  with 2^e | C: even (e = 1), doubly even (e = 2), TRIPLY EVEN (e = 3).
  Ward's divisible code bound (survey Thm 6, verbatim): for an [n, k]_q
  code whose nonzero weights lie among m consecutive multiples
  (b - m + 1) Delta, ..., b Delta:
     k v(q) <= m (v(Delta) + v(q)) + v(binom(b, m))
  with v the p-adic valuation. Binary corollary (D3 below):
  a 2^e-divisible binary [n, k] code has k <= (e + 1) n / 2^e.
  GLEASON-PIERCE(-WARD) (survey Thm 7, verbatim types): a divisible
  [n, n/2]_q code falls in FIVE types only - binary Delta = 2 (I),
  binary Delta = 4 self-dual (II), ternary self-dual (III), quaternary
  Hermitian (IV), and trivial 2-fold replication (V). There is NO
  half-rate binary code with divisor 8: the quadratic world's self-dual
  balance is FORBIDDEN one level up. This is the coding-theory face of
  182.4's phase boundary.
  TRIPLY EVEN CODES exist and have a literature: Betsumiya-Munemasa
  (J. London Math. Soc. 2012; arXiv:1012.4134) classify the maximal
  triply even codes of length 48 - exactly TEN up to equivalence, all
  built by combining doubly even codes of length 24.
  THE VALUATION REGIME: at t >= 3 the rigidity that survives is
  divisibility, not classification - Ax's theorem (survey Thm 2: the
  GRM code R_q(r, m) is divisible by q^(ceil(m/r) - 1), and this is the
  exact p-power), McEliece's theorem for cyclic codes (survey Thm 3),
  and Thm 6 above. Machine (5): the Brown magnitude law is exact on
  16/16 sampled cycle-space subcodes at t = 2, while the zeta_8 Gauss
  sums of the SAME subcodes show 12 distinct magnitudes - no magnitude
  law of Brown type exists at t = 3. The phase boundary of 182.4 is
  hereby a named, literature-anchored wall: quadratic Gauss sums are
  rigid (Brown), cubic Weil sums are wild (only valuations survive).
  POINTER, NOT CONSUMED: exact maximum dimensions for binary divisible
  codes of level e >= 3 are stated in Liu, Int. J. Information and
  Coding Theory 1 (2010) 355-370 (abstract seen: level 1 gives
  k <= n - 1; level 2 gives k <= n/2 with equality iff doubly even
  self-dual, 8 | n; exact bound for level >= 3 asserted there). Beyond
  the abstract this is unverified and no proof below uses it.

### 430.3 THE POLARIZATION TOWER (PROVED)

  (I) MASTER IDENTITY. For subsets x_1, ..., x_k of a ground set, as
  exact integers:
     |x_1 xor ... xor x_k|
        = sum over nonempty S subset {1..k} of
          (-2)^(|S| - 1) |intersection of x_i, i in S|.
  Proof: a ground element lying in exactly j of the x_i contributes
  [j odd] to the left side and
  sum_r (-2)^(r - 1) binom(j, r) = (1 - (1 - 2)^j) / 2 = [j odd] to the
  right. QED. Machine (1): 240/240 random instances, k <= 5, exact.

  (D1) DEGREE THEOREM. On any F2-space of subsets, q_t(x) = |x| mod 2^t
  has k-th polarization (iterated finite difference at 0 along
  x_1, ..., x_k) equal to (-2)^(k - 1) |x_1 n ... n x_k| mod 2^t; all
  polarizations of order > t vanish, so q_t IS A DEGREE-t FORM.
     t = 1: linear - the archive's parity and bipartite laws;
     t = 2: quadratic - the Brown form of 430.1;
     t = 3: cubic - the J7 layer, third polarization 4 |x n y n z|.
  The programme's ladder is the degree filtration of ONE function:
  length, read 2-adically. Proof from (I) by collecting the difference
  signs; machine (2): 200/200 at t = 3, orders 1 through 5. QED.

  (D2) CASCADE. If a binary code is 2^t-divisible, then all pairwise
  intersections are 2^(t-1)-divisible, all triple intersections
  2^(t-2)-divisible, ..., all t-fold intersections even. (Downward
  induction from (I) applied to sums of generators; the keyword
  "polarization" in Ward's survey is this cascade.) Machine (3):
  replicated doubly even codes of length 48 - weights == 0 mod 8,
  pairwise n == 0 mod 4, triple n == 0 mod 2, all hold. QED.

  (D3) WARD COROLLARY (consumed from the verbatim-verified Thm 6). A
  2^e-divisible binary [n, k] code has weights among the
  m = floor(n / 2^e) multiples 2^e, ..., m 2^e, so with b = m the
  binomial term vanishes and
     k <= m (e + 1) <= (e + 1) n / 2^e.
  (Elementary special case, in-house from (D2): doubly even implies
  self-orthogonal implies k <= n/2.) Machine (3) checks the bound on
  every sampled code. QED.

  (W) WEB DESCENT THEOREM. Let P, P' be even connecting paths of one
  terminal pair with |P| == |P'| == l0 (mod 2^t) - the (SC)_t
  alignment. Then
     |P xor P'| == 2 (l0 - |P n P'|)   (mod 2^t).
  Hence the mod-2^t class of the difference cycle is an affine function
  of iota(P, P') = |P n P'| mod 2^(t-1):
     LEVEL-t LENGTH RIGIDITY OF THE WEB IS LEVEL-(t-1) RIGIDITY OF THE
     INTERSECTION FUNCTION.
  Proof: |P xor P'| = |P| + |P'| - 2 |P n P'| exactly. QED. Machine
  (4): 960/960 mod-8-aligned pairs on random bridges; the iota census
  hits all four classes mod 4, so the statement has content there.

  RETRODICTION. At t = 2 the engine's colour laws (400.1, the
  chi-census) computed exactly iota mod 2: the corridor colouring WAS
  the level-1 rigidity theory of intersections, run under the level-2
  campaign. The engine did not happen to use colours; it was already
  running one level down the tower. The next campaign must do

### 431.2 THE RESIDUAL WORLD: STRICTLY LOCALLY-MINIMUM, HENCE
### ISOMETRIC, SQUEEZED IN SIZE (PROVED)

  Suppose C is shallow at t >= 3 and fails (NEG): every shift of every
  ear is >= 0. Shallowness makes every shift =/= 0 (mod 2^t) - in
  particular =/= 0 - so every shift is STRICTLY positive:

     EVERY EAR OF C IS STRICTLY LONGER THAN BOTH ITS ARCS. Every
     single-ear surgery strictly lengthens C: C is a STRICT LOCAL
     MINIMUM of length under ear surgery.

  ZERO-SHIFT REMARK. A single zero shift (|P| = |A| for some ear-arc)
  kills shallowness at EVERY level at once, since v_2(0) = infinity
  >= t. The census (431.5): in all four sample graphs, every weakly
  locally-minimum cycle carries a zero shift - the strict residual
  world is EMPTY there. Shallowness and local minimality conspire
  against each other: the residual cycle must dodge equality in every
  single ear-arc comparison.

  ISOMETRY THEOREM. A cycle all of whose ear shifts are >= 0 is
  ISOMETRIC in G: dist_G(x, y) = dist_C(x, y) for all x, y on C.
  Proof. Let Q be a shortest x-y path in G. Split Q at its internal
  meetings with C into segments; each segment between consecutive
  C-vertices u, v is either a C-edge or an ear of C, and an ear
  satisfies |seg| >= max arc(u, v) >= dist_C(u, v). Summing,
  |Q| >= sum dist_C >= dist_C(x, y) by the triangle inequality in the
  cycle metric; C itself realises dist_C. QED
  Machine: 82/82 locally-minimum sample cycles are isometric.
  (Pointer, NOT consumed: geodesic/isometric cycles are known to
  generate the cycle space - see e.g. the 2-geodesic-cycle generation
  theorem cited in arXiv:1703.09969; unverified beyond the abstract.)

  SIZE SQUEEZE. |C| = 2^t m with m odd and |C| not a power of two
  forces m >= 3: |C| >= 3 * 2^t >= 24. And 191 proves (H1*) - hence
  (NEG) - for every cycle longer than 2 sqrt(n). So the residual world
  needs
     24 <= 3 * 2^t <= |C| <= 2 sqrt(n),
  i.e. n >= 9 * 4^(t-1) >= 144, and t <= log_2(2 sqrt(n) / 3): J7 is
  EMPTY below n = 144 and finite in t for every graph.

  THE SHAPE. J7's inhabitant, if it exists, is a girth-cycle-like
  object: an isometric cycle of length 3 * 2^t <= |C| <= 2 sqrt(n),
  every ear strictly longer than both its arcs, every shift dodging
  0 mod 2^t. Every shortest cycle of every graph satisfies the metric
  half of this (girth: |P| >= |C| - |A| = |A'| for any ear), so the
  world is metrically inhabited - what has never been seen, in 3435
  cycles of 179.1 plus the 1453 cycles swept here, is the CONGRUENCE
  half joining it at t >= 3.

### 431.3 THE RESIDUE ROUTE FORMALLY CLOSED (PROVED, SWEEP)

  For the forbidden table d =/= |A| - 2, -|A| - 2 (mod 2^t), sweep
  t = 2..6 over all |A| classes (machine):
     t = 2: full single-class pinning of even d for EVERY even |A|;
            parity collapse (both odd classes killed) for every odd
            |A|. (SC) and the Parity Lemma - as known.
     t = 3: full mod-4 pinning exactly for |A| == 2 (mod 4) (418.2's
            half-pairs); parity collapse: NONE.
     t >= 4: NO fully-forbidden mod-4 class, NO parity collapse, for

  So residue rigidity of single-class type exists at t = 2 and (on
  half the pairs) at t = 3, and NEVER AGAIN. Any t-uniform proof of
  (NEG)_{t >= 3} must be metric or integer-additive; t = 3 is the one
  rung where residue and metric weapons can combine. This sharpens
  418.3's verdict into an inventory with a boundary, and it is final.

### 431.4 THE COMPOSITE CALCULUS AND THE DAVENPORT LEVER (PROVED)

  COMPOSABILITY. Ears P_1, ..., P_k with pairwise disjoint interiors
  and pairwise disjoint chosen arcs A_1, ..., A_k can be applied
  simultaneously: C' = C xor (P_1 u A_1) xor ... xor (P_k u A_k) is a
  single cycle of length |C| + delta_1 + ... + delta_k. SHIFTS ADD.
  Machine: explicit board, |C| = 12, two ears, length 14 = 12 + 2 + 0,
  single-cycle verified edge-by-edge.

  PARTIAL-SUM PIGEONHOLE. Any sequence of 2^t residues mod 2^t has a
  nonempty consecutive block summing to 0 (the 2^t + 1 partial sums
  collide); the all-ones sequence of length 2^t - 1 is zero-sum-free,
  so the threshold is exact (the Davenport constant of Z/2^t, in-house
  in three lines). Machine: 4000/4000 random sequences at t = 3, 4.

  WIDE-SHALLOWNESS THEOREM. Call C wide-shallow at t if every
  composite shift over disjoint ear families also dodges 0 mod 2^t.
  If C carries 2^t pairwise-composable ears, C is NOT wide-shallow:
  some sub-family has total shift Delta == 0 (mod 2^t), i.e.
  v_2(Delta) >= t - a lateral-or-progress move in 179.2's
  classification. COROLLARY (the supply bound): a wide-shallow cycle
  at level t has every pairwise-composable ear family of size < 2^t.
  High levels demand ear interiors that pairwise collide - the bridges
  of the residual cycle must be few and fat, exactly the concentration
  the 190.1 counterexample exhibited (one edge carrying every
  attachment).

  HONEST FLAGS. (a) The banked escape framework classifies moves by
  SINGLE-ear shifts. 179.2's shallow/deep classification reads only
  v_2(Delta) against t and is agnostic to how Delta was manufactured,
  but the lateral-benign analysis (188) was proved for ear moves at
  t = 1 only; extending the framework's bookkeeping to composite
  moves is OPEN. Until then the Davenport kill binds wide-shallowness,
  not narrow-shallowness. (b) Nothing yet forces 2^t composable ears
  in the residual world; the supply side is open. (c) The isometry
  theorem uses only weak local minimality; its converse is false
  (isometric cycles can have negative shifts elsewhere - no claim).

## 432. THE COMPOSITE CAMPAIGN: PROGRESS-COMPOSITES ARE LEGAL, THE
## LAMINAR WORLDS DIE, AND J7 CONTRACTS TO THE BRAIDED CORE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section executes road (K1)
of 431.6 as far as it truthfully goes. Four theorems and a calculus are
banked: composite moves that raise the valuation are LEGAL for the
escape framework with no new bookkeeping (431.4's flag (a) discharged
for progress moves); a CLIMBING LEMMA manufactures exact 2-adic
valuations; every bridge of the residual cycle yields floor(r/2)

KILL closes every world in which 2^(t+1) - 1 of those ears are pairwise
non-crossing. What survives is a single object: the BRAIDED
configuration - pairwise-crossing supply with constant shifts on a
half-system of feet - whose congruence battery is inventoried and whose

### 432.1 PROGRESS-COMPOSITES ARE LEGAL (PROVED; DISCHARGES 431.4(a)
### FOR PROGRESS)

  The ascent framework (178.4, consumed by 190.4) classifies what
  happens AT a cycle: progress = exhibit a cycle of strictly higher
  2-adic valuation; shortening = exhibit a strictly shorter one;
  lateral = same valuation (analysed only at t = 1 too-deep cycles,
  188). The ear formalism was the MECHANISM for exhibiting such
  cycles, never part of the consumable: the framework's accounting
  reads only v_2 and length of the exhibited cycle. A composite
  surgery yields a genuine cycle of G; if its valuation exceeds t, it
  IS a progress move, verbatim. Hence:

     ANY composite whose resulting cycle has v_2 > t un-sticks C,
     with no extension of the escape bookkeeping.

  Only LATERAL composites (resulting valuation = t) remain outside
  the banked analysis. The campaign below therefore aims every weapon
  at manufacturing EXACT target valuations, never settling for
  "v_2 >= t".

### 432.2 THE CLIMBING LEMMA (PROVED)

  Among any three elements of equal 2-adic valuation a, some pair
  sums to valuation EXACTLY a + 1.
  Proof. Scale by 2^-a: u, v, w odd. If all three pair-sums were
  == 0 (mod 4) then u == -v == w == -u (mod 4), so 2u == 0 (mod 4),
  contradicting u odd. So some pair-sum is == 2 (mod 4), i.e. has
  valuation exactly 1; scale back. QED
  Machine: all odd triples mod 64, zero failures.

### 432.3 THE EXACT-VALUATION THEOREM (PROVED, SHARP)

  Any 2^(t+1) - 1 residues of valuation < t (any moduli >= 2^(t+1))
  contain a disjoint-subset sum of valuation EXACTLY t.
  Proof sketch (the climbing algorithm): maintain a pool of
  disjoint-support subset-sums, initially the residues. While no pool
  element has valuation exactly t: some valuation class a < t holds
  three pool elements (else the pool has thinned below the invariant
  count); by 432.2 two of them merge to exact valuation a + 1,
  shrinking the pool by one. The count 2^(t+1) - 1 = f(0) with
  f(a) = 2 f(a+1) + 1, f(t) = 1 guarantees the process cannot
  exhaust before reaching exact valuation t.
  SHARP: the pool of 2^t - 1 copies of +1 and 2^t - 1 copies of -1
  (size 2^(t+1) - 2) has every subset-sum a - b with |a - b| < 2^t:
  never valuation t. Machine: 400/400 random 15-element pools at
  t = 3 climb to exact valuation 3; the (+1/-1) pool of size 14 is
  verified stuck.

### 432.4 THE SUBCUBIC SUPPLY THEOREM (PROVED)

  Let C be a chordless cycle in a cubic 3-connected graph (the
  residual world is chordless: a chord is an ear of length 1, shorter
  than any arc). Every bridge H with r attachments yields floor(r/2)
  ears of C with pairwise disjoint interiors and pairwise distinct
  feet.
  Proof. The interior of H is subcubic (G is cubic); take a spanning
  tree of it and append the r attachment edges: a subcubic tree T
  whose leaves are exactly the r attachment vertices on C. Cherry
  peeling: a deepest branch vertex of T carries two leaf-chains;
  their leaf-to-leaf path through it is one ear; delete it and
  induct. floor(r/2) vertex-disjoint leaf-paths result. QED
  Machine: 200/200 random subcubic trees.
  TOTALLING: every C-vertex is an attachment (cubic coverage, no
  chords), each bridge has r >= 3 (3-connectivity), so the number of
  bridges is b <= |C|/3 and the total supply is
     N >= (|C| - b)/2 >= |C|/3 = m 2^t / 3 >= 2^t   (m >= 3).

### 432.5 THE SPIRAL CALCULUS (PROVED + MACHINE; ONE CORRECTION)

  For pairwise-crossing ears in spiral order (feet u_1 < ... < u_k <
  y_1 < ... < y_k on C), with inner arcs:
   - PAIR (k = 2): the composite is a SINGLE cycle of length
     |C| + f_i + g_j, where f_i = |P_i| + u_i + y_i and
     g_j = |P_j| - u_j - y_j: the pair value is SEPARABLE, and the
     same-ear coupling is g_i = f_i - 2(u_i + y_i). Winding 1.
   - ODD ZIGZAG (k odd): the composite is a SINGLE cycle of length
        ((k+1)/2) |C| + sum of alternating shifts
        (inner delta at odd spiral positions, outer delta' at even),
     and any odd sub-selection preserving the alternation is again a
     zigzag - subset-sum freedom over pair-blocks survives crossing.
   - EVEN spirals (k >= 4) DISCONNECT into two cycles: no move.
  CORRECTION (374.1): my first zigzag formula omitted the WINDING
  factor (k+1)/2 - the machine caught it (57 against a claimed 33 on
  the k = 3 board) before recording. The winding flips the progress
  target: for k == 1 (mod 4) the alternating sum must be == 2^t (mod
  2^(t+1)) to progress; for k == 3 (mod 4) it must be == 0 (mod
  2^(t+1)). All composite shapes remain trackable; none is exempt.
  Machine: pair (48 = 48), triple (57 = 2|C| + 9, winding 2),
  quadruple (2 components), all verified edge-by-edge.

### 432.6 THE LAMINAR KILL (PROVED)

  THEOREM. A shallow cycle at level t >= 3 carries no laminar family
  of 2^(t+1) - 1 composable ears (pairwise non-crossing, arcs chosen
  laminar-consistently - machine check (3): all subsets of such a
  family compose to single cycles with ADDITIVE shifts and winding 1).
  Proof. Shallowness puts every ear's chosen-arc shift at valuation
  < t; the Exact-Valuation Theorem manufactures a sub-family with
  total shift of valuation exactly t; winding 1 makes the composite
  length |C| + Delta with v_2(|C| + Delta) >= t + 1: a PROGRESS
  composite, legal by 432.1. C was not stuck. QED

  COROLLARY (the braiding constraint). The residual J7 cycle's ear
  supply (>= |C|/3 >= 2^t ears, 432.4) has laminar-independence
  number at most 2^(t+1) - 2. For m >= 5 the supply is >= 5 2^t / 3,
  and for every m it EXCEEDS 2^t: large ear systems whose crossing
  graph is sparse are impossible - THE RESIDUAL EARS MUST BRAID.
  (A pairwise-crossing family of any size has laminar-independence 1,
  so braiding is achievable; the kill is a constraint, not yet a
  contradiction.)

### 432.7 THE BRAIDED CORE, INVENTORIED (PARTLY MACHINE; OPEN)

  What a surviving configuration must satisfy, per 431-432:
   (a) all single shifts strictly positive (local minimality), both
       arcs, all dodging 0 mod 2^t;
   (b) laminar sub-families of size < 2^(t+1) - 1 only (432.6):
       the >= |C|/3 supply is essentially pairwise crossing;
   (c) crossing pairs: f_i + g_j =/= 2^t (mod 2^(t+1)) for all i < j,
       with the coupling g_i = f_i - 2 s_i (s_i = foot-sum) tying the
       f-values to the POSITIONS - the adversary cannot choose values
       and geometry independently;
   (d) odd zigzags: alternating sums dodge the winding-dependent
       target class for every odd sub-selection;
   (e) the graph must exist: distinct feet, |C| <= 2 sqrt(n),
       girth >= 5, ear interiors of length > |C|/2 pairwise disjoint,

  Machine (6): a schematic constant/half-system configuration at

  BRIDGEHEAD (recorded, unproved): the braid is forced to be

## 433. THE STALL THEOREM: ROUTE (i) CLOSES NEGATIVELY, AND THE BRAIDED
## CORE IS PINNED TO THE PACKING SHELL

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. This section resolves which of

confined to middle zones, bridges are leg-trees, and the whole

### 433.1 THE STALL THEOREM (PROVED)

  In the constant braided configuration (all inner shifts == c_0, all
  outer shifts == -c_0 mod 2^(t+1), v_2(c_0) < t), every odd zigzag
  of size k has value ((k+1)/2) c_0 - ((k-1)/2) c_0 = c_0, and every
  single, pair and sub-selection value lies in {c_0, -c_0, dodged
  classes}: NO composite of any shape has valuation >= t. Machine:
  500 random zigzags, all equal to c_0.
  CONSEQUENCE. A dead-end lateral component of size one is
  congruence-consistent. (H2) FAILS for the composite web: 432's cut
  (i) - extending 188's lateral analysis - cannot close J7 by itself,
  for the same reason no residue argument can (431.3): the adversary
  has a fixed point of the entire additive calculus. Route (i) is
  hereby CLOSED, NEGATIVELY. Everything now rests on cut (ii).

### 433.2 THE LEG AND MIDDLE-ZONE THEOREMS (PROVED)

  LEAF-DISTANCE LAW. In the residual world every tree-path between
  two attachments of one bridge is an ear, hence longer than L/2
  (L = |C|). So every bridge's attachment tree has all pairwise
  leaf-distances > L/2; at most one leaf has leg < L/4 (two short
  legs would give a short leaf-pair), so a bridge with r attachments
  has interior >= (r - 1) L/4. Machine: 60/60 filtered random
  subcubic trees. TIGHT: the cherry construction (spine of r/2
  branch vertices, two legs of length L/4 + 1 each) realises all
  distances > L/2 at size ~ r L/4. Summing over bridges
  (sum r_H = L): the braided core needs n >= L^2/4 - O(bL) and lives
  under 191's threshold L <= 2 sqrt(n): THE CONFIGURATION IS PINNED
  TO THE PACKING BOUNDARY SHELL - the graph is C plus leg-trees plus
  lower-order wiring, with nothing to spare.

  MIDDLE-ZONE LAW. A cross-path of length l joining interior
  positions a (on P_i) and b (on P_j) spawns four second-generation
  ears, each forced > L/2; the four constraints confine BOTH
  endpoints to the middle zones of their ears (machine sweep: 720
  admissible position pairs out of 6272, all middle-zone). The outer
  quarters of every ear can wire only via self-chords of span at
  most slack_i = |P_i| - max-arc_i, and any route through disjoint
  self-chords is again an ear, forcing the subset-sum of shortcuts
  below slack_i: outer-zone self-absorption demands slack_i of order
  sqrt(L) (independent-chord count L/(2 slack) times minimum
  shortcut 3 must stay under slack).

### 433.3 CORRECTION (per 374.1)

  In the first draft of this analysis I claimed the four-route sum
  forces |P_i| + |P_j| >= 2L - 2: FALSE - the four routes total
  2(|P_i| + |P_j|) + 4l > 2L, which is implied by |P| > L/2 alone
  and forces nothing. The genuine content of the four routes is
  PER-ROUTE, the Middle-Zone Law above. Recorded loudly.

### 433.4 WHAT J7 NOW IS, EXACTLY

  A single existence question. Does there exist a cubic 3-connected
  girth->=-5 graph G, a cycle C with |C| = L = 2^t m (t >= 3, m odd
  >= 3, 24 <= L <= 2 sqrt(n)), such that:
   (a) C is chordless, isometric, and every ear exceeds both its
       arcs (strict local minimum);
   (b) every ear shift dodges 0 mod 2^t;
   (c) the >= L/3 ear supply is braided (no laminar 2^(t+1) - 1
       sub-family - else 432.6 kills);
   (d) all composite values dodge valuation exactly t (else 432.1
       kills) - achievable only near the stall fixed point of 433.1;
   (e) the graph fits the packing shell: leg-tree bridges of total
       size ~ L^2/4, middle-zone cross-wiring, sqrt(L)-slack
       self-absorbing outer zones, all second-generation ears again
       satisfying (a)-(b) at every generation (432.7's
       self-similarity)?
  If NO such graph exists, J7 is closed, (NEG)_{t>=3} holds, and by
  431.1 the conjecture follows on the archive's ledger. If one
  exists, it is a genuine obstruction to this entire route. The
  census has never seen one; the constraints (a)-(e) interlock at

  braided core inside a graph that possesses a power-of-two cycle
  obstructs nothing, since EG holds there trivially. The shallow
  branch runs inside the reductio; the braided core inherits the FULL
  counterexample hypothesis. 433.4 is hereby corrected: J7 = no graph
  satisfies (a)-(f).

### 434.2 THE PROBE (COMPUTED): THE METRIC CORE IS NEARLY BUILDABLE,

  (i) Any graph satisfying (a)-(f) is a cubic counterexample to

## 436. THE ARSENAL: J7'S OBSTRUCTIONS INVERTED INTO WEAPONS

### 436.1 OBSTRUCTION: THE STALL FIXED POINT. WEAPON: THE BLOCKINESS
### LAW (PROVED, TWO-SIDED, MACHINE)

  The stall configuration kills all composites by constancy. INVERT:
  constancy is fragile under INTERLEAVING. In the zigzag calculus a
  deviant ear (shift c_0 + e) placed at an inner slot adds e, at an
  outer slot subtracts e; reachable values form c_0 + J e with J the
  set of inner-minus-outer deviant counts. J grows with the number of
  ALTERNATION RUNS between deviant and constant ears in spiral order
  - not with the deviant count. Machine dichotomy at t = 3, c_0 = 2,
  e = 2 (progress class 8 mod 16): eight deviants INTERLEAVED reach
  the progress class (kill); the same eight deviants CONTIGUOUS reach
  only {2, 4} (survive). THE LAW: a surviving braided core's shift
  function is BLOCKY - constant on O(2^(t+1-v_2(e))) spiral blocks
  for every deviation scale e. The stall generalises to "piecewise
  stall with boundedly many pieces", and every extra alternation is
  ammunition. (First draft claimed deviation count alone suffices:
  REFUTED by the machine - the adversary defeats scattered counts by
  contiguity. Recorded per 374.1.)

### 436.2 OBSTRUCTION: THE BRAID. WEAPON: THE INTERVAL TRICHOTOMY
### AND FRACTAL RIGIDITY (PROVED)

  Pairwise crossing splits the feet into a u-block and a y-block.
  INVERT: chords with BOTH feet in one block are INTERVALS of an arc,
  and for intervals, nested and disjoint are BOTH laminar on the
  circle - only staircase overlap crosses (machine: 500/500). The
  Interval Trichotomy (Dilworth-Mirsky, twice): any k intervals
  contain s pairwise nested, or s pairwise disjoint, or k/s^2
  pairwise crossing (machine: 300/300 random families). CONSEQUENCE:
  every within-block chord family the wiring creates - and 432.7
  showed the cubic wiring creates them in bulk - must be STAIRCASE at
  every recursion scale, or hand the Laminar Kill its family. The
  braid is forced to be a braid of braids: FRACTAL, with the
  recursion sizes shrinking by the trichotomy's k/s^2 at each level.

### 436.3 OBSTRUCTION: THE WIRING FREEDOM. WEAPON: THE CHORD-DEPTH
### LAW (PROVED)

  Subset-sum growth (machine): k residues of common valuation a in
  Z/2^t have subset-sum set of size >= min(2^(t-a), k+1). A route
  through disjoint self-chords shifts the ear's class by a subset sum
  of shortcut values; all routes must dodge 0 mod 2^t. THE LAW: on
  every ear, the co-usable self-chords' shortcut values must be
  2-adically DEEPER than the ear's own shift (v_2(shortcut) >
  v_2(delta)), or number below coverage (machine: the hit/safe

  the wiring cycles land in 2 mod 4 - THE ADVERSARY IS FORCED TO

  theorem, discovered as his shield at t = 2, returns at t >= 3 as
  his OBLIGATION - a design constraint we dictate.

### 436.4 OBSTRUCTION: THE SUPPLY COUNTS. WEAPON: THE THRESHOLD

## 437. THE UNRAVELLING RACE: THE AFFINE CASCADE, FORCED
## FRAGMENTATION, AND THE FALL OF THE ODD SHIELD

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas remains UNPROVED. The Unravelling Question is

refresh its supply, the refresh forces an affine rigidity cascade
that FRAGMENTS the braid into bounded pieces, and - the stride's

odd-stall corner of 436.4 at every level t: THE PARITY SHIELD DOES

### 437.1 THE AFFINE CASCADE AND THE REGION BOUND (PROVED,
### CONDITIONAL ON PER-REGION BLOCKINESS)

  A cross-edge at depths (p, q) on carriers i, j serves the uu-ear
  (p + 1 + q) and the yy-ear ((|P_i| - p) + 1 + (|P_j| - q)). If the
  uu- and yy-shifts are constant on a connected wired region (the
  survivor's obligation under 436.1, per region), connected
  labelling separates the constraints:
     p_i + pi_i == alpha,   q_j - pi_j == beta   (mod 2^t),
  and adding the two ear families' constancies gives, per carrier,
  |P_i| + pi_i + eta_i == gamma. Substituting the first-generation
  stall |P_i| == c_0 + eta_i - pi_i yields
     2 eta_i == gamma - c_0   (mod 2^t):
  ALL y-FEET OF THE REGION LIE IN ONE CLASS MOD 2^(t-1). The cycle C
  has exactly L / 2^(t-1) = 2m positions in a class:
     REGION BOUND: a connected wired constancy region holds at most
     2m carriers - SIX, for m = 3, at EVERY t.
  Machine (1): constancy achievable on aligned instances 8/8, on a
  broken class 0/8. Machine (2): the capacity table. CONSEQUENCE
  (forced fragmentation): the wiring graph on the >= L/3 carriers
  splits into >= 2^t/6 components of at most 2m carriers each; the
  same separation run through a bridge's OWN tree-ears pins
  2 pos_a == const, so under within-bridge constancy a bridge holds
  at most 2m attachments and the bridge count is b >= L/(2m).

### 437.2 THE REFRESH AND ITS LEASH (PROVED PIECES)

  The fragments' cross-edges spawn uy-ears (one usable per matched
  carrier pair, interiors disjoint across pairs): the level-1 supply
  REFRESHES to ~2N. The refreshed chords (u_i, y_sigma(i)) must
  braid with everything; sigma is an involution, and the only
  order-preserving involution is the identity (machine (3), n <= 6):
  a fully order-aligned refresh is impossible. The surviving pattern
  is the ANTIPODAL matching (sigma = shift by N/2): pairwise
  crossing across pairs, NESTED within each pair - maximum laminar
  subfamily 2, verified by enumeration at N = 12. The refresh
  survives, but only in one shape, and it hands the configuration
  its final name: the LADDER-CLIQUE BRAID - antipodally matched
  carrier pairs, at most 2m carriers per wired fragment, rung menus
  tuned ear by ear.

### 437.3 THE FALL OF THE ODD SHIELD (PROVED, UNCONDITIONAL)

  436.4 cornered the survivor into odd constant shifts. THAT CORNER
  IS EMPTY, by the archive's own section 179.4, imported verbatim to
  every t: in any bridge, fix a spanning tree, sigma_a = l_a + pos_a
  (mod 2); every tree-ear shift satisfies
     delta_ab == sigma_a + sigma_b   (mod 2)
  (tree distances are l_a + l_b - 2 meet, and both arcs of an even
  cycle have parity pos_a + pos_b). All shifts odd would need
  sigma_a =/= sigma_b for every pair - impossible for r >= 3. So
  EVERY bridge with r attachments carries floor(r/4) pairwise
  interior-disjoint EVEN-shift ears (pair leaves inside the majority
  sigma-class), totalling ~L/4 across the graph, interiors disjoint
  everywhere. On these ears no menu has an odd base: the wholesale
  parity dodge of 436.5 (machine (4): odd base dodges, even base is
  hit) IS UNAVAILABLE on a quarter of the supply. The survivor must
  fine-tune every even-based menu individually, forever.

### 437.4 THE m = 3 RAZOR (COMPUTED, HONEST)

  Every kill count now lands just under its threshold at m = 3:
  even-shift disjoint supply ~3 * 2^(t-2) against the climbing count
  f(1) = 2^t - 1 (short by 4/3); refreshed level-1 supply 2N ~
  2^(t+1) against f(0) = 2^(t+1) - 1 (meets it, but braiding denies
  laminarity); region capacity 2m = 6 against component sizes (met

## 441. THE NEXUS: ONE 2-ADIC QUADRATIC FORM - EVERY STRATUM IS ITS SHADOW

The question of this section is the one the programme has circled
since 430: WHAT was the t = 2 machinery a facet OF? The Brown form
worked at mod 4 and "something breaks" at mod 8. This section
identifies exactly what breaks, exactly why it is an artifact of the
coordinates and not of the mathematics, and exhibits the single
object of which every stratum t is a shadow. Machine:
tools/nexus441.py - every check below is its output.

### 441.1 THE DIAGNOSIS: WHAT EXACTLY DIES AT MOD 8

STATUS: PROVED (identities); COMPUTED (wildness table).

The t = 2 machine (430) was the Brown form: q(Z) = |Z| mod 4 is a
Z/4-QUADRATIC refinement of the intersection pairing on the F_2
cycle space, and quadratic forms over F_2 carry a complete
classification (Arf-Brown, Gauss Sum Law, Witt theory). At mod 8 the
SAME coordinates stop being quadratic:

  (a) DEGREE. The third difference of |.| mod 8 on the XOR space is
      4|x cap y cap z| mod 8 - nonzero whenever the triple
      intersection is odd. COMPUTED: nonzero on 138/300 random
      triples; so |.| mod 8 has degree 3 as a Z/8-valued map. As a
      pure F_2 object the new information at level k is the k-th
      binary digit of |Z|, and by Lucas
          digit_k(|Z|) == binom(|Z|, 2^k) (mod 2)
      = the elementary symmetric polynomial e_{2^k} of the indicator
      vector: an F_2-form of degree 2^k. COMPUTED: 200/200. The
      tower of digit forms has degrees 1, 2, 4, 8, ... - past
      degree 2 there is no Arf invariant, no Witt classification,
      no Gauss law.

  (b) WILDNESS, QUANTIFIED. Over 120 random subspaces of F_2^12
      (dims 4, 6, 8): the Gauss sums sum zeta_4^{|x|} take SEVEN
      distinct magnitudes (the Brown rigidity); the Gauss sums
      sum zeta_8^{|x|} take NINETY-NINE. COMPUTED. The
      classification that closed t = 2 does not exist in XOR
      coordinates at t >= 3. THIS is the break.

The diagnosis: the break lives in the COORDINATES. XOR addition
forgets the orientation data of cycles; the forgotten carry is
exactly the -2|x cap y| correction term, and iterating it is what
drives the degree up (the Witt-vector/Verschiebung structure of
430.2 seen from below).

### 441.2 THE LIFT: LENGTH IS QUADRATIC AT EVERY LEVEL - ON THE LATTICE

STATUS: PROVED (Tower Theorem); machine-verified on four graphs.

Let Lambda = ker(oriented incidence) subset Z^E be the lattice of
integral circulations (the INTEGRAL FLOW LATTICE), with the standard
inner product <.,.>. Every circuit C, once oriented, lifts to a +-1
circulation x_C in Lambda with

    |C| = |x_C|^2    EXACTLY (L1 = L2^2 on +-1 vectors).

COMPUTED: every circuit of K4 (7), Petersen (57), Mobius-Kantor
(400), Heawood (213) lifts with |x|^2 = length, 677/677. The third
difference of |.|^2 on Lambda is identically zero (300/300):
quadratic at every level, forever.

TOWER THEOREM. For every s >= 1 the map

    q_s : Lambda / 2^s Lambda -> Z / 2^{s+1},   q_s(x) = |x|^2

is well defined and is a Z/2^{s+1}-valued quadratic form with
polarization q_s(x+y) - q_s(x) - q_s(y) = 2<x,y>.

PROOF. |x + 2^s lam|^2 - |x|^2 = 2^{s+1}<x,lam> + 2^{2s}|lam|^2,
and 2s >= s+1 for s >= 1, so the change is == 0 mod 2^{s+1}. The
polarization identity is the binomial expansion. QED. (Machine:
800/800 well-definedness instances, s = 1..4, four graphs.)

DICTIONARY. Archive stratum t <-> lattice level s = t - 1. At s = 1,
Lambda/2Lambda is the F_2 cycle space and q_1 = |Z| mod 4 IS the
Brown form: the t = 2 machine is the BOTTOM LAYER of this tower. At
s = 2 the mod-8 machinery the programme searched for EXISTS: it is
q_2 on Lambda/4Lambda - a quadratic form, not a cubic one - the
coefficients grew from F_2 to Z/4, and the sign data (orientations)
that XOR forgot is exactly what pays for the collapse in degree.
Quadratic forms on finite abelian 2-groups and Z_2-lattices are
CLASSIFIED (2-adic symbols, genus theory) - the theory the XOR
shadow lacks at t >= 3 exists at every level upstairs.

Note also: a k-ear composite has length |x + z_1 + ... + z_k|^2,
and the spiral coupling g_i = f_i - 2 s_i of 432.4 is literally the
cross term -2<z_i, z_j>: the whole spiral calculus is this one

STATUS: COMPUTED (rigidity and Kirchhoff tables); PROVED (radical

### 441.4 SHALLOWNESS IS A SYSTEM OF LINEAR CONGRUENCES

STATUS: PROVED (Ear Identity, Deep-Ear Criterion); machine-verified
equivalence on the full Mobius-Kantor census.

EAR IDENTITY. Let C be a cycle with lift x, and let an ear with
connecting path P (length d) replace the arc A (length a). Let z be
the lift of the ear-cycle P cup A oriented AGAINST x on A. Then

    delta = d - a = q(z) + 2<x, z>.

(One line: |x + z|^2 = |x|^2 + q(z) + 2<x,z>, and x + z is the
composite's lift.) COMPUTED: 20448/20448 ear/arc instances exact
across all 400 Mobius-Kantor cycles.

DEEP-EAR CRITERION. 2^t divides delta iff q(z) is EVEN and

    <x, z> == -q(z)/2   (mod 2^{t-1}).

Odd ear-cycles are never deep at any t >= 1 - the odd-shift world of
431 falls out in one line. COMPUTED: 40896/40896 instances, t = 2
and t = 3.

RESTATEMENT OF SHALLOWNESS. C is shallow at stratum t iff x_C
dodges, in Lambda/2^{t-1}Lambda, ONE linear congruence per
even ear-cycle z:  <x_C, z> =/= -q(z)/2 (mod 2^{t-1}). COMPUTED:
shallow_direct == shallow_lattice for every one of the 400 cycles at
t = 2 AND t = 3, zero mismatches; counts 4 and 0, matching the 431
census exactly.

THE DENSITY STORY, RESOLVED. At t = 2 each even ear forbids one
class of TWO (mod 2) - the residue rigidity of 431.3 was a covering
at density 1/2. At stratum t each even ear forbids one class of
2^{t-1} - the density decays, which is the "lost rigidity" of 431.
The analog the programme asked for is now visible: do not transplant
the density - REPLACE the counting. The number of shallow lifts is
an inclusion-exclusion over the ear congruences, and by Fourier

    ear-cycles always cover - i.e. is the dodger count always zero

- a statement in harmonic analysis on the discriminant (sandpile)
world, UNIFORM IN t. The field the meditation sought is not category
theory: it is the arithmetic of 2-adic quadratic lattices - genus
