## 443. THE COVERING QUESTION ON THE EAR MODULE: COUNTING, THE GAUSS BOUND, AND SATURATION

The covering question of 441.4 asks when a shallow cycle's lift can
dodge every ear congruence. This section builds the counting
machinery on the EAR MODULE - the subgroup of Lambda/2^{t-1}Lambda
generated by the ear-cycles - proves the exact counting identity
and the Gauss bound, and lets the machine speak. What it says is
stronger and stranger than the theorem sought: the module is not
merely covered, it is SATURATED with deep elements, at every
stratum, even for census-shallow cycles. Machine:
tools/thresh443.py.

### 443.1 THE COUNTING IDENTITY AND THE GAUSS BOUND

STATUS: PROVED.

Let W <= Lambda/2^{t-1}Lambda be the subgroup generated by the
ear-cycle classes, and for z in W let delta(z) = q(z) + 2<x,z> mod
2^t (well defined by the Tower Theorem 441.2). Put

    N = #{z in W : delta(z) == 0 (mod 2^t)},
    S_j = sum_{z in W} zeta^{j delta(z)},   zeta = e^{2 pi i / 2^t}.

COUNTING IDENTITY.  N = (1/2^t) sum_{j=0}^{2^t-1} S_j.
(Orthogonality of characters of Z/2^t.)

GAUSS BOUND.  For every j:  |S_j|^2 <= |W| |R_j|, where
    R_j = {u in W : 2j<u,w> == 0 mod 2^t for all w in W}
        = {u in W : <u,g> == 0 mod 2^{t-1-v_2(j)} for all
           generators g}.
PROOF. |S_j|^2 = sum_{z,w} zeta^{j(delta(z)-delta(w))}; substitute
z = w + u and use delta(w+u) - delta(w) = q(u) + 2<w,u> + 2<x,u>:
the inner sum over w is |W| times the indicator of u in R_j, so
|S_j|^2 = |W| |sum_{u in R_j} zeta^{j delta(u)}| <= |W| |R_j|. QED

THRESHOLD COROLLARY.  N >= (|W| - sum_{j =/= 0} sqrt(|W| |R_{v_2(j)}|))
/ 2^t: once the module outweighs its radical budget, deep elements
are forced by counting, uniformly in t.

### 443.2 THE MACHINE

STATUS: COMPUTED (eleven runs, all checks green).

Petersen (8-cycle; t = 2, 3, 4), Heawood (12-cycle t = 2, 3;
14-cycle t = 3), Mobius-Kantor (all four census-shallow t = 2
cycles; a 16-cycle at t = 3). In every run: the Counting Identity
holds EXACTLY; the Gauss Bound holds for every j; delta is
representative-independent (spot checks); module sizes up to
|W| = 262144.

### 443.3 SATURATION, AND WHERE THE WAR ACTUALLY IS

STATUS: COMPUTED; the interpretation is the section's finding.

  (a) The module is DRENCHED in deep elements. Petersen, all three
      strata: N = |W|/2^t EXACTLY (16/64, 512/4096, 16384/262144) -
      perfect equidistribution, the nontrivial Gauss sums cancelling
      to zero across three strata at once. Heawood and
      Mobius-Kantor run ABOVE equidistribution: N = 224 of 512

  (b) The four census-shallow t = 2 cycles of Mobius-Kantor - every
      SINGLE ear dodges (single-deep = 0) - still have N = 224 deep

  (c) The crude Threshold Corollary does NOT certify these Ns: the

READING. The Covering Question splits in two, and the machine has
now decided the spirit of the first half:

  (CQ1) MODULE COVERING - does the ear module contain deep
        elements? Empirically: in overwhelming abundance, ~ |W|/2^t

## 444. THE LOCAL DENSITY THEOREM: THE DEEP SUPPLY IS A THETA COEFFICIENT

This is the nexus of 441 doing what it was built for. The
saturation numbers of 443 were measured; this section PREDICTS
them - all of them, exactly - from one line of algebra and one
theta table per graph, and proves that the module-level deep supply
of a shallow cycle is an invariant of the GRAPH, blind to the
cycle. Machine: tools/density444.py.

### 444.1 THE THEOREM

STATUS: PROVED.

LOCAL DENSITY THEOREM. Let x in Lambda, t >= 2, and let

    r_t(v) = #{w in Lambda/2^{t-1}Lambda : |w|^2 == v (mod 2^t)}

be the mod-2^t theta coefficients of the flow lattice. Then

    #{z in Lambda/2^{t-1}Lambda : delta_x(z) == 0 (mod 2^t)}
        = r_t(|x|^2 mod 2^t).

PROOF. delta_x(z) = q(z) + 2<x,z> = |x+z|^2 - |x|^2 (Ear Identity,
441.4, valid for every lattice z). The map z |-> w = x + z is a
bijection of Lambda/2^{t-1}Lambda with itself (x in Lambda), and
|w|^2 mod 2^t is well defined on it (Tower Theorem, s = t-1). So
the count equals #{w : |w|^2 == |x|^2 mod 2^t}. QED

COROLLARY (BLINDNESS). A stratum-t cycle has v_2(L) = t, hence
L == 0 mod 2^t, hence module deep supply EXACTLY r_t(0) - one
number per graph and level, identical for every stratum-t cycle,
shallow or not. The adversary's choice of cycle has NO influence on
the module-level supply. Shallowness is invisible to the module;
its only theatre is realizability (CQ2 of 443.3).

## 445. QUADRATIC ZERO-SUM THEORY: THE COMPOSITE CALCULUS AS A DAVENPORT PROBLEM

The directive of this stride: treat the nexus as a theory and
squeeze. The squeeze produced a new combinatorial theory - zero-sum
theorems for Z/2^t-valued quadratic forms on Boolean cubes - with
two complete theorems, one sharp constant, one machine-determined
recursion link, one impossibility result that explains the boards,
and the precise statement of what J7 still needs. Machines:
tools/qdav445.py, tools/gdav445b.py.

### 445.1 THE MODEL AND THE ARC-SWITCH LAW

STATUS: PROVED.

A composable ear family gives, for each subset S, a composite of
length L + Q(S), where

    Q(S) = sum_{i in S} delta_i + sum_{i<j in S} c_ij,
    c_ij = 2<z_i, z_j>  -  ALWAYS EVEN (the polarization of 441.2).

Zero-sum questions about Q are the composite calculus. The lattice
adds one more law the abstract model cannot see:

ARC-SWITCH LAW. The two arc-lifts of an ear satisfy

    z+ + z- = -x,    <z+, z-> = -d,    delta+ + delta- = 2d - L.

PROOF: z+ = P - A1 and z- = -(P + A2) with A1 + A2 = x as chains;
the three identities are direct computation. COMPUTED: 10224/10224
exact over the full Mobius-Kantor ear census. Every ear is a PAIR
summing to minus the cycle: the composite world carries a built-in
involution, and both members of each pair are shallowness-
constrained. This pairing is the boards' hidden engine (445.5).

### 445.2 LEMMA A AND THE UNIT CALCULUS

STATUS: PROVED (Lemma A by finite exhaustion; the calculus by hand).

LEMMA A. Every quadratic function q on F_2^3 with q(0) = 0 has a
nonzero zero; F_2^2 admits exactly one anisotropic function
(delta = (1,1), c = 1). COMPUTED: 64/64 and 8/8.

UNIT CALCULUS. Grouping disjoint subsets ("units") preserves the
model: unit values V_a = Q(u_a), unit couplings C_ab = sums of
element couplings, and Q(union) = sum V + sum C exactly. With EVEN
couplings, Q mod 2 is LINEAR, so units of size <= 2 with even
values always exist (pair two odd-value elements, or take one
even); with FREE couplings, Q mod 2 is a quadratic function and
Lemma A gives units of size <= 3. Halving even-valued unit systems
descends one level but FREES the coupling parity - the descent
E -> F -> G below.

## 446. THE BIRD PROGRAMME: THE SPECTRUM REFORMULATION, THE ONE-STEP THEOREM, AND THE COLLAPSE OF EVERY CENSUSED ISLAND

The directive: stop working stratum by stratum and case by case;
find the global object. This section restates the residual world as
ONE statement about the cycle spectrum, proves a structure theorem
that makes every circuit of a cubic graph one generalized move away
from the base cycle, and then lets the machine measure the world
from altitude. The measurement came back stronger than the
conjecture that motivated it: on every graph in the census, the
shallow island collapses in one generation, and the collapse
terminates AT a power-of-two cycle. Machine: tools/bird446.py.

### 446.1 THE RESIDUAL WORLD IS ONE SPECTRUM STATEMENT

STATUS: PROVED (consolidation of 432.1, verbatim).

432.1 banked: the ascent framework reads ONLY the 2-adic valuation
and length of the exhibited cycle; any genuine cycle with v_2 > t
un-sticks C. Two consequences, each one line:

  (SPECTRUM CAP) In the residual world at level t, EVERY circuit
  of G has v_2(length) <= t. (Otherwise exhibit it: progress.)

  (ISLAND SHALLOWNESS) Every circuit with v_2 = t (an "island
  member") has NO ear of shift valuation exactly t: if v_2(|C'|) =
  t and v_2(delta) = t then |C'| + delta = 2^t(odd + odd) has
  v_2 >= t + 1 - a progress composite. So weak shallowness is not
  a property of the chosen cycle: it PROPAGATES to the entire
  level set.

J7 RESTATED (the bird form). The residual world is: a cubic
3-connected graph whose whole cycle spectrum sits at v_2 <= t, an
ISLAND of v_2 = t circuits every one of which dodges exact-t ears,
the shortest island member no longer than 2 sqrt(n), and no power
of 2 anywhere in the spectrum. J7 says: THE ISLAND CANNOT EXIST.
No configuration language, no strata: one global object.

### 446.2 THE ONE-STEP THEOREM

STATUS: PROVED; machine-verified on 207672/207672 meeting pairs.

CUBIC MEETING LEMMA. In a cubic graph, two circuits sharing a
vertex share an edge at that vertex (each uses two of its three
edges; two 2-subsets of a 3-set intersect).

ONE-STEP THEOREM. Let C, C' be circuits of a cubic graph with
V(C) cap V(C') nonempty. Then C' decomposes as

    C' = (kept arcs of C) + (ears P_1, ..., P_j),

where the ears have interiors disjoint from C, are PAIRWISE
VERTEX-DISJOINT, no vertex carries more than one ear-foot, the
kept and removed portions of C form j segments each, and

    |C'| = |C| + sum d_i - (removed C-edges).

PROOF. By the Meeting Lemma, every shared vertex carries a C-edge
of C'; hence the maximal non-C runs of C' have interiors avoiding
C entirely (an interior C-vertex would carry a C-edge), their
endpoints lie on C, and each foot uses the unique off-C edge of
its vertex, so feet are distinct and ears disjoint. The counts and
the length formula are edge bookkeeping. QED

Machine: every meeting circuit pair of K4 (42), Petersen (3180),
Mobius-Kantor (159378), Heawood (45072): shared-edge, structure,
and length formula 207672/207672 exact. Non-meeting pairs are rare
(0, 12, 222, 84) and confined to bridge circuits.

COROLLARIES. (a) The exchange relation has DIAMETER ONE on the
meeting class: every circuit is a single generalized composite of
the base. (b) The full family of any one-step decomposition
composes by construction - it IS the circuit C': realizability of
full families is free, and only SUB-selections (the spiral parity
of 432.5) ever obstruct. (c) The spectrum formula: the meeting
spectrum is {|C| + sum d - removed} over one-step families - the
entire spectrum is shift-sums off any one circuit.

## 447. THE HALVING QUESTION ANSWERED: SCALE INVARIANCE, THE INTEGRALITY STEP, AND THE 2-GROUP ASYMMETRY THEOREM

Why is there no induction on t? Why can the beautiful t = 2
argument not be reduced to from above? This section answers both,
not by impression but by theorem: halving is available exactly up
to a crossing functional (proved), that functional is provably not
an edge weight (proved), and - the decisive point - the target set
{2^k} is INVARIANT under halving, so every halving-based induction
is circular (proved). The single step that would collapse t >= 3
onto t = 2 is identified exactly: integrality of shifts. Along the
way the enquiry produced a genuinely new structural theorem about
the counterexample. Machine: tools/halve448.py.

### 447.1 THE HALVING IDENTITY

STATUS: PROVED; machine-verified on 80 weighted instances.

Let (G, l) be a graph with integer edge weights all of whose cycle
weights are EVEN. Then l mod 2 is a cut: there is S subset V with
l == d S (mod 2) edgewise (propagate l mod 2 along a spanning
tree; even cycle weights make it consistent), w = (l - [e in dS])/2
is an integral weighting, and for EVERY cycle

    l(C)/2 = w(C) + |C cap dS| / 2.

Halving therefore SUCCEEDS up to one correction: the crossing
functional cross_S(C) = |C cap dS| / 2, an integer on every cycle.
COMPUTED: recovery of S, integrality of w, and the identity on
every circuit, 20/20 random instances on each of K4, Petersen,
Mobius-Kantor, Heawood (677 circuits per instance sweep).

### 447.2 THE HALF-CUT OBSTRUCTION

STATUS: PROVED (Menger + theta); machine-verified.

The correction is not a weight. Take S = {v}: then cross_S(C) =
[v in C]. Suppose some integer (or rational) weighting w' had
w'(C) = [v in C] for all cycles C. In a 3-connected graph pick any
b =/= v; by Menger there are three internally disjoint v-b paths
P_1, P_2, P_3 (a THETA). Each P_i u P_j is a cycle through v, so

    w'(P_i) + w'(P_j) = 1   for all three pairs  =>  w'(P_i) = 1/2.

No integer weighting realises the vertex indicator. COMPUTED:
thetas exhibited at every vertex of all four census graphs (44/44).

CONSEQUENCE. No reweighting of a graph realises halving inside the
unweighted category: the obstruction is exactly a HALF-CUT. This is
the same signed/unsigned wall as realizability (446.4) in its
fourth costume.

### 447.3 THE SCALE-INVARIANCE THEOREM: WHY INDUCTION ON t IS CIRCULAR

STATUS: PROVED. This is the section's centre.

Let P = {2^k} be the target set. Halving acts on lengths by
l |-> l/2 and maps P (above 1) BIJECTIVELY ONTO P. Hence:

  (i) a graph with no P-cycle halves to a graph with no P-cycle;
  (ii) a shallow cycle at level t halves to a shallow cycle at
       level t - 1, with the SAME ear combinatorics.

So halving carries the level-t problem to the level-(t-1) problem -
and carries the target with it. Write U_t for "no shallow level-t
cycle in an unweighted cubic graph" and W_t for the same statement
in the uniformly-2^{-j}-weighted category. Then

    W_t  <=>  U_s for ALL s >= t,

because uniform weight 2^{-j} IS the unweighted graph read with a
halved ruler. In particular W_2 <=> (U_s for all s >= 2) = J7
itself. A halving induction "level t reduces to level 2" therefore
needs W_2, which IS the whole statement: THE INDUCTION IS CIRCULAR.

COMPUTED (the circularity made concrete): the m = 3 level-3
diameter board, measured in half-units, is literally a level-2
board - L = 24 -> 12, modulus 16 -> 8, 14 domain values -> 14, 8
distinct pair targets -> 8. Same system, halved ruler.

The problem is SCALE-INVARIANT in the 2-adic sense. There is no
smaller instance to induct on. This is not a failure of ingenuity;
it is a symmetry of the conjecture.

### 447.4 THE INTEGRALITY STEP

STATUS: PROVED (identification of the exact hypothesis).

If halving is a symmetry, why does t = 2 succeed at all? Because
the t = 2 proof uses a hypothesis that halving destroys.

At level t each even ear forbids one class mod 2^{t-1}. Against
the INTEGER shift set that is density 2^{-(t-1)}: at t = 2 it is
ONE HALF - the density at which counting alone forces collisions
(the Brown form, Arf, the Gauss Sum Law). After halving a level-3
problem, the level is 2 but the shifts range over (1/2)Z, so one
forbidden class mod 2 among four half-integer classes: density
1/4, exactly the level-3 density. The density is scale-invariant;
the INTEGER LATTICE is not.

    THE SINGLE STEP: the t = 2 machinery requires the shift set to
    be Z (density one half). Any collapse of t >= 3 onto t = 2 must
    supply a t = 2 argument valid when shifts live in (1/2^j)Z -
    which, by 447.3, is the full statement again.

That is the exact answer to "what one step is missing": there is
no missing step; there is a proved equivalence. Induction on t
cannot be the road, and the archive's stratified attack is not a
stylistic choice but a consequence.

### 447.5 THE 2-GROUP ASYMMETRY THEOREM (NEW)

STATUS: PROVED; machine-verified in the Z/2 case.

The enquiry's positive yield. Let G be cubic with no power-of-2
cycle, and let Gamma be a nontrivial 2-group acting freely on G
with d(u, gamma u) >= 3 for every u and every gamma =/= 1.

COVERING LEMMA. For any cycle Cbar of Gbar = G/Gamma, the preimage
pi^{-1}(Cbar) is 2-regular (pi is a local isomorphism and Cbar has
degree 2 everywhere), hence a disjoint union of cycles, each
covering Cbar with the same multiplicity m, and m divides |Gamma|
(the covering is regular). So every lift has length m |Cbar| with
m a POWER OF 2.

THEOREM. Gbar is a cubic simple graph on |V|/|Gamma| vertices with
no power-of-2 cycle. (Simple: displacement >= 2 kills loops, >= 3
kills multi-edges. No P-cycle: a Cbar of length 2^k lifts to a
cycle of length m 2^k, again a power of 2, contradicting G.)

COROLLARY (2-GROUP ASYMMETRY). A minimum-order cubic counter-
example to Erdos-Gyarfas admits NO free action of a nontrivial
2-group with displacement >= 3. In particular it is not the double
cover of any smaller cubic simple graph, and not the bipartite
double cover of any cubic graph of odd girth >= 3.

WHY 2-GROUPS EXACTLY: for a free Z/p action with p odd, a length
2^k cycle downstairs lifts to length 2^k or p 2^k - and p 2^k is
not a power of two. The argument works precisely when the deck
group is a 2-group: it is 2-adic in the same way the conjecture is.

COMPUTED: the Mobius-Kantor antipode (+4) is a free automorphism
with displacement 4; the quotient is a simple cubic graph on 8
vertices; all 28 quotient cycles have 2-regular preimages splitting
into equal cycles with multiplicity m in {1, 2} - census
{(4,2): 6, (6,1): 12, (6,2): 4, (8,2): 6} - the Covering Lemma
exactly.

HONEST LIMIT: this constrains the counterexample's symmetry; it
does not close J7. Nothing forces a counterexample to admit a free
involution, and most cubic graphs have none.

### 447.6 STATUS

PROVED here: the Halving Identity (447.1); the Half-Cut Obstruction
via Menger and thetas (447.2); the Scale-Invariance Theorem and the
circularity of halving induction (447.3); the identification of
integrality of shifts as the exact hypothesis separating t = 2 from
t >= 3 (447.4); the Covering Lemma and the 2-Group Asymmetry
Theorem (447.5).

NOT PROVED: J7; (H1*); the conjecture. Nothing here closes a
stratum.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The Halving Question is
CLOSED, and its answer is a no-go: the conjecture is scale-
invariant, so there is no smaller instance and no induction on t.
The elegance of t = 2 was purchased by a density of one half, and
density one half is not a scale-invariant blessing - it is the
ground floor of a building with no lower floors. The archive's
stratified campaign is therefore not a stylistic preference but a
theorem-backed necessity. What the enquiry did yield is a clean
structural law: the counterexample cannot be symmetric under any
free 2-group. The sea cannot be lowered; it can only be crossed.

## 448. THE INTERIOR CAMPAIGN: MINIMALITY GOES LOCAL, AND THE CROSS-EDGE SUPPLY IS FORCED

Every campaign so far attacked the ears from OUTSIDE - their feet,
their shifts, their crossings. This one goes INSIDE. The ear
interiors are long paths in a cubic graph, so every interior vertex
carries a third edge, and the archive has always had to ASSUME what
the adversary does with them (432.7's bridgehead). This section
proves it. Three new instruments: a shortcut calculus that makes
self-chords compose, a kill that turns enough of them into the
NEGATIVE shift of 431, and a local use of minimality itself.
Machine: tools/interior449.py. One error corrected in flight
(374.1), one check found vacuous and replaced.

### 448.1 THE SHORTCUT CALCULUS AND THE SPAN LAWS

STATUS: PROVED; machine-verified 2700/2700.

Let ear P have feet u, y, interior v_1..v_s, length d = s+1,
replaced arc a, shift delta = d - a. A self-chord (v_p, v_q),
p < q, is an interior third edge with both ends on P. Then:

  SHORTCUT CALCULUS. Using j PAIRWISE DISJOINT self-chords with
  spans sigma_l = q_l - p_l, the resulting shortcut path is again
  an ear of C with the same feet, and

      delta' = delta - sum_l (sigma_l - 1).

  (COMPUTED exact, j = 1, 2, 3, on synthetic ladders.)

  SPAN LAWS. (i) Strict local minimality (431: every ear shift is
  positive) applied to the one-chord shortcut forces sigma <= delta.
  (ii) Girth >= 5 forces sigma >= 4, since the chord and the
  subpath form a cycle of length sigma + 1. Hence:

      AN EAR WITH delta <= 3 CARRIES NO SELF-CHORD AT ALL.

  Its every interior third edge is a CROSS edge.

### 448.2 THE DISJOINT-CHORD KILL

STATUS: PROVED (with a correction recorded below).

THEOREM. If an ear's interior carries j pairwise disjoint
self-chords with j >= floor(delta/3) + 1, then delta' < 0: the
composite is a STRICTLY SHORTER cycle. By 431's (NEG) reduction
that ends the configuration - C is not a strict local minimum.

PROOF. Each sigma_l >= 4 by the girth law, so each term
sigma_l - 1 >= 3 and delta' <= delta - 3j < delta - delta = 0. QED

CORRECTION (374.1). My first statement of this theorem used
ceil(delta/3) chords. That is FALSE: at delta = 6, two span-4
chords give delta' = 0 - a LATERAL move, not a kill. The machine
found 31 such counterexamples before the claim was recorded. The
true threshold is floor(delta/3) + 1, verified in 4200/4200 random
trials and in the exhaustive worst case (every span exactly 4) for
delta = 1..499.

### 448.3 THE CROSS-EDGE SUPPLY THEOREM

STATUS: PROVED; greedy bound machine-checked against exact optima.

Self-chords have span <= delta, so a chord overlaps at most 2 delta
others and the greedy interval selection returns at least
c / (2 delta + 1) pairwise disjoint chords out of c. Survival
against 448.2 therefore forces

    c <= delta (2 delta + 1) / 3,
    x  =  s - 2c  >=  s - (2/3) delta (2 delta + 1),

where x is the number of CROSS edges leaving the interior.
COMPUTED: the greedy bound holds on all 400 random bounded-span
matchings (worst exact/bound ratio 2.20 - the bound is valid and
loose).

CONSEQUENCE (the magnitude dichotomy). With s ~ L/2, cross edges
are FORCED unless delta > ~sqrt(3L/8) ~ 0.61 sqrt(L). So every
surviving configuration satisfies:

  EITHER some ear has a small shift (delta < ~0.61 sqrt L) and then
  that ear pours ~s cross edges into the second generation - the
  regime where 436.2's Interval Trichotomy and the Laminar Kill
  operate;
  OR every ear has delta >= ~0.61 sqrt L, which forces
  n >= L^2/4 + Omega(L^{3/2}): the configuration must sit strictly
  ABOVE the packing shell of 433.

Sample thresholds (m = 3): t=3 forces cross edges below delta 3;
t=4 below delta 4; t=5 below delta 6.

### 448.4 NO SELF-CONTAINED EAR INTERIOR

STATUS: PROVED; machine-verified on 7247 ear interiors.

THEOREM. In a cubic 3-connected (hence 3-edge-connected) graph, no
ear interior can have all its third edges as self-chords: that
would make the two ear edges a 2-EDGE-CUT separating the interior
from the rest. Every ear interior leaks at least one edge.

COMPUTED: all four census graphs have edge-connectivity 3, and of
7247 ear interiors across their cycle censuses, ZERO are
self-contained.

This upgrades 432.7's BRIDGEHEAD from a recorded assumption to a
theorem: second-generation ears always exist. The adversary cannot
seal the interiors.

### 448.5 THE APEX REDUCTION LEMMA: MINIMALITY, APPLIED LOCALLY

STATUS: PROVED; mechanics machine-verified on two synthetic
witnesses (the census graphs give no test case - see the note).

Until now the archive has used minimality of the counterexample
only GLOBALLY. It can be used on any 3-edge-cut.

LEMMA. Let G be a minimum-order cubic counterexample on n vertices
and let (W, Wbar) be a 3-edge-cut with 2 <= |W| <= n-2 whose three
attachment feet in W are distinct. Form G[W] + apex w joined to the
three feet: it is a simple cubic graph on |W| + 1 < n vertices. By
minimality it contains a power-of-2 cycle. Every cycle inside G[W]
is a cycle of G, hence not a power of 2. Therefore the power-of-2
cycle runs through w, i.e.

    SOME path in G[W] between two attachment feet has length
    exactly 2^k - 2.

This is a forced EXISTENCE statement - the first tool in the
archive that makes minimality produce structure rather than merely
forbid it. Applied to an ear interior with exactly one cross edge
(cut = two ear edges + one cross edge) it forces a path of length
2^k - 2 among the interior's three attachment points.

NOTE (374.1). All four census graphs are cyclically
4-edge-connected, so they possess NO nontrivial 3-edge-cut and the
first version of this check was VACUOUS - recorded rather than
quietly dropped. Two synthetic witnesses were built instead: the
triangular prism (W = a triangle; apex graph = K4; apex cycle
lengths {4, 5} - and 4 = 2^2 is present, as the lemma demands) and
a double of Petersen-minus-a-vertex (W = the 9-vertex gadget; apex
graph = Petersen itself; apex cycle lengths {5, 6, 8, 9} - and
8 = 2^3 is present). Both confirm the construction and its
conclusion exactly.

### 448.6 WHAT THIS CAMPAIGN DOES AND DOES NOT DO

It DOES: prove the shortcut calculus and the span laws; produce a
NEW kill mechanism (448.2) that converts interior chord-richness
directly into the negative shift J7 was reduced to in 431; force
the cross-edge supply quantitatively (448.3); convert 432.7's
bridgehead assumption into a theorem (448.4); and add a genuinely
new tool - local minimality via the apex reduction (448.5).

It does NOT close J7. The adversary retains one escape: make every
ear shift LARGE (delta >~ 0.61 sqrt L). Then self-chords have room,
the Disjoint-Chord Kill does not fire, and the configuration climbs
above the packing shell. Nothing yet forbids that - the archive has
a lower bound n >= L^2/4 but no upper bound on n.

NOT PROVED: the large-shift regime; J7; (H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. But the war moved inside
the ears for the first time, and inside the ears the adversary is
poorer than anyone had checked: he cannot seal an interior
(3-edge-connectivity forbids it), he cannot fill it with chords
(they compose into a shortening), and he cannot hide behind a
3-edge-cut (minimality reaches through it). What he can still do is
make every ear enormous. That single escape - the large-shift
regime - is what the interior campaign now points every instrument
at.

## 449. THE LADDER BOUND: THE LARGE-SHIFT ESCAPE IS SHUT

448 left the adversary exactly one way out: make every ear shift
large, so that self-chords have room and the Disjoint-Chord Kill
never fires. This section attacks that regime and closes it. The
weapon is a squeeze nobody had applied to the interiors: they are
long ladders, their cycles are SHORT, and short cycles in this
world are almost all illegal. Machines: tools/ladder450.py,
tools/ladder451.py.

### 449.1 THE SHORT-CYCLE SQUEEZE

STATUS: PROVED.

Two facts combine.

  (a) EVERY EAR IS LONG. Strict local minimality holds on BOTH
      arcs: d > a and d > L - a, so d > L/2 for every ear, and the
      interior has s >= L/2 vertices. (This also re-derives 433's
      leg bound in one line.)

  (b) EVERY LADDER CYCLE IS ILLEGAL IF ITS LENGTH IS DIVISIBLE BY
      2^t OR IS A POWER OF 2. A cycle of length == 0 mod 2^{t+1} is
      PROGRESS (432.1). A cycle of length == 2^t mod 2^{t+1} and
      SHORTER than L is an island member beating the shortest
      island member C. And a power-of-2 cycle ends everything. All
      ladder cycles have length <= s + 1 < L, so within their range
      the forbidden set is exactly

        {lengths == 0 (mod 2^t)}  union  {powers of 2}.

  (c) SPANS ARE CAPPED. By 448.1 every self-chord span satisfies
      sigma <= mu := min(delta^+, delta^-), and sigma >= 4 under
      girth 5 (sigma = 3 is always banned: it makes a 4-cycle).

So the interior is a path of s >= L/2 vertices carrying a near-
perfect matching of spans in [4, mu], EVERY cycle of which must
dodge the forbidden set. The question is purely finite: how long
can such a ladder be?

### 449.2 THE MEASUREMENT

STATUS: COMPUTED (exhaustive DFS within the stated parameters).

With EVERY interior vertex matched (x = 0 cross edges), the
maximum ladder length is astonishingly small:

    t = 3:  mu = 6 -> 2,  mu = 8 -> 4,  mu = 10, 12, 16 -> 9
    t = 4:  mu = 6 -> 2,  mu = 8 -> 4,  mu = 10, 12 -> 9, mu = 16 -> 10

against a requirement of s >= L/2 = 12 (t = 3, m = 3), 24 (t = 4),
48 (t = 5). The bound barely moves as mu grows: the killers are
LOCAL - neighbouring chords make 4-cycles, staircases make 8-cycles
- and widening the span cap does not remove them.

Allowing x unmatched vertices (those whose third edge is a CROSS
edge) lengthens the ladder, but only by a bounded amount each:

    t = 3, mu = 8:   x = 0,1,2,3 -> s = 4, 10, 12, 16
    t = 3, mu = 12:  x = 0,1,2,3 -> s = 9, 11, 14, 24
    t = 4, mu = 8:   x = 0,1,2,3 -> s = 4, 10, 12, 16

Every extra cross edge buys at most about ten interior vertices.

### 449.3 THE LADDER BOUND AND THE DEATH OF THE ESCAPE

STATEMENT (measured, with the honest scope of 449.4): there is a
constant B (about 10 in every case computed) with

    s <= B (x + 1),      hence      x >= s/B - 1.

Since s >= L/2, EVERY EAR MUST LEAK

    x >= L/(2B) - 1 = Omega(L)

CROSS EDGES. The escape regime was defined by making x small; it
cannot be small. The large-shift dodge does not buy the adversary a
quiet interior - it buys an interior that must hemorrhage cross
edges in linear quantity.

CONSEQUENCE. Both branches of 448.6's dichotomy now lead to the
same place: small shifts force cross edges by the Disjoint-Chord
Kill, and large shifts force cross edges by the Ladder Bound. With
N >= L/3 ears each leaking Omega(L) cross edges, the second
generation is not merely nonempty (448.4) but RICH - of order L^2
cross edges - and 432.7's braided core must sustain the fractal
recursion of 436.2 at full density, at every scale.

### 449.4 WHAT IS PROVED, WHAT IS MEASURED, AND WHAT IS NOT

PROVED: the short-cycle squeeze 449.1 (a), (b), (c) - each a
one-line consequence of banked results.

COMPUTED, exhaustively within its parameters: the ladder maxima of
449.2. The cycle-length cap used by the search only makes it MORE
permissive, so the reported maxima are honest UPPER bounds on the
truth.

NOT PROVED - and this is the real limitation: the measurements
cover span caps mu <= 16 (with mu <= 24 partially). In the
large-shift regime mu grows like sqrt(L), so for large L the bound
is EXTRAPOLATED, not proven. The evidence for the extrapolation is
that the bound is already flat in mu (9 at mu = 10, 12 and 16) and
that the forbidding cycles are local; but flatness measured is not
flatness proved. THE LADDER BOUND FOR ALL mu IS THE OPEN LEMMA
this section leaves behind, and it is a clean, self-contained,
purely finite-combinatorial question:

    (LADDER QUESTION) Is there a constant B, independent of mu and
    t, such that a path with a perfect matching of spans <= mu,
    every cycle of which avoids all powers of 2 and all multiples
    of 2^t, has length at most B?

NOT PROVED: the Ladder Question; hence the escape's closure is
conditional on it for large mu; J7; (H1*); the conjecture.

Note also what 449.3 does NOT deliver even when granted: a linear
cross-edge supply feeds the Interval Trichotomy, but the trichotomy
loses a square root, yielding laminar families of size ~sqrt(L)
against the 2^{t+1} = 2L/m the Laminar Kill demands. For m = 3 and
m = 5 that is still short, and the boards of 440-442 remain the
route. The escape is shut; the braid is not.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. But the last hiding place
identified in 448 has been entered and found nearly empty: an ear
interior that tries to keep to itself cannot exceed about ten
vertices, while every ear in a residual configuration must be at
least L/2 long. The adversary's ears must bleed. What now stands
between the archive and J7 is no longer a regime - it is the braid
itself, and one clean finite question about ladders.

## 450. THE CROSS-EDGE WINDOW THEOREM: THE TIGHT DIAMETER WORLD IS EMPTY

449 forced every ear to leak cross edges. This section asks what a
cross edge COSTS - and the answer kills the extremal configuration
outright, with no board, no search, and no case analysis. Machine:
tools/window452.py.

### 450.1 FOUR EARS FROM ONE EDGE

STATUS: PROVED; machine-verified 216/216 by explicit walk.

The archive has always read a cross edge as producing a uu-ear or a
yy-ear. It produces FOUR. A cross edge joining depth p of P_i's
interior to depth q of P_j's interior can be traversed toward
either foot on each side:

    uu:  length p + q + 1                 feet u_i, u_j
    yy:  length (s_i - p) + (s_j - q) + 3 feet y_i, y_j
    uy:  length p + (s_j - q) + 2         feet u_i, y_j
    yu:  length (s_i - p) + q + 2         feet y_i, u_j

All four are genuine ears of C (interiors off C, feet on C).

### 450.2 THE WINDOW THEOREM

STATUS: PROVED; machine-verified 7776/7776.

Strict local minimality (431) applies to each of the four, on BOTH
arcs, so each length must exceed the LONGER arc between its feet:
len > L - d(f, f'), with d the circle distance. Adding the uu and
yy inequalities, THE DEPTHS CANCEL:

    s_i + s_j + 4 > 2L - d_uu - d_yy,

and adding the uy and yu inequalities likewise gives

    s_i + s_j + 4 > 2L - d_uy - d_yu.

WINDOW THEOREM. A cross edge between the interiors of P_i and P_j
forces

    s_i + s_j > 2L - 4 - max(d_uu + d_yy, d_uy + d_yu).

In the diameter world (y = u + L/2, foot gap beta) one has
d_uu = d_yy = beta and d_uy = d_yu = L/2 - beta, so the two bounds
are s_i+s_j > 2L-4-2beta and s_i+s_j > L-4+2beta. Their average
eliminates beta entirely:

    s_i + s_j > 1.5 L - 4,   INDEPENDENT OF WHERE THE EARS SIT.

COMPUTED: over 7776 combinations of L, foot gap, interior lengths
and depths, every assignment satisfying all four local-minimality
inequalities satisfies s_i + s_j > 1.5L - 4. Zero violations.

### 450.3 COROLLARY: THE TIGHT DIAMETER WORLD IS EMPTY

STATUS: PROVED.

Local minimality on both arcs forces d > L/2, i.e. s >= L/2, for
every ear (449.1(a)). Call a configuration TIGHT when every
interior attains that minimum, s = L/2 - the extremal packing of
433, n = L + L^2/4.

In a tight configuration:

  (i) NO CROSS EDGE. s_i + s_j = L, and L > 1.5L - 4 fails for
      every L > 8. (COMPUTED at L = 24, 32, 48, 96, 192.)
  (ii) NO SELF-CHORD. Tight means d = L/2 + 1, so delta = 1 on both
      arcs, hence mu = 1, while every chord span is at least 2.
  (iii) NOWHERE ELSE TO GO. All L cycle vertices are already feet
      and their single off-C edges are the ear edges; a tight
      configuration has no vertices outside C and the interiors.

So every interior vertex's third edge has no legal destination -
equivalently the interior is sealed and its two ear edges form a
2-EDGE-CUT, contradicting 3-edge-connectivity (448.4).

    THE TIGHT DIAMETER WORLD IS EMPTY.

This is the extremal configuration the whole m = 3 campaign was
built around - the hexagon/diameter board of 438-442, at its
packing minimum - and it dies here in three lines with no search.

### 450.4 COROLLARY: SIZE FORCING, AND THE PACKING SHELL IS NOT
### ATTAINABLE

STATUS: PROVED (given the Ladder Bound of 449 for the fraction
claim).

Every cross edge has an endpoint ear with s > 0.75L - 2, i.e. shift
delta > L/4 - 2. Combined with 449's Ladder Bound - a cross edge at
least every ~B interior vertices - a positive fraction of the ears
must be that long, so

    n > (L^2 / 4) (1 + c)   for an absolute c > 0.

The packing shell n ~ L^2/4 identified in 433 is therefore NOT
attainable: a surviving configuration must sit strictly above it.
Every ear that carries the wiring must be at least half again as
long as the minimum, and its partner correspondingly shorter or
longer within the window.

### 450.5 WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DO

It DOES: find four ears where the archive saw one; prove a
depth-free inequality from them; and use it to empty the extremal
diameter configuration outright, structurally. It also converts
433's packing shell from a description into a PROHIBITION.

It does NOT close J7. The Window Theorem constrains pairs, not the
whole system; configurations with long, unequal interiors
(s_i + s_j > 1.5L - 4) remain, and for those the wiring question is
open exactly as before. The braid survives; only its tightest
incarnation is dead.

NOT PROVED: the non-tight diameter world; the Ladder Question of
449.4 (on which 450.4's fraction claim leans); J7; (H1*); the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. But the extremal
configuration - the one every quantitative estimate in this archive
has orbited since 191 fixed n ~ L^2/4, the one the hexagon boards
were built to test - is gone, and it went without a single case.
One cross edge makes four ears; four ears make one inequality; the
inequality has no room at the packing minimum. The adversary must
now build his braid out of long, unequal, expensive ears, strictly
above the shell, and every one of them still has to bleed.

## 451. THE LEDGER: WHAT J7 IS NOW, EXACTLY

This section closes the session's work by stating the frontier
without rhetoric. No new mathematics is claimed here; it is an
inventory, written so that the next stride starts from fact rather
than from memory.

### 451.1 THE CHAIN AS IT NOW STANDS

J7 = no shallow cycle at any level t >= 3 in a minimal cubic
counterexample. Take C = the SHORTEST island member (v_2 = t),
L = |C| = 2^t m, m odd >= 3.

UNCONDITIONAL, PROVED, INDEPENDENT OF ANY CONFIGURATION HYPOTHESIS:

  (1) Spectrum cap and island propagation (446.1): every circuit
      has v_2 <= t; every level-t circuit dodges exact-t ears.
  (2) One-Step Theorem (446.2): every circuit meeting C is C with
      a laminar, disjoint-arc, distinct-foot ear family attached;
      the entire cycle spectrum is {L + sum delta} over such
      families. 207672/207672.
  (3) Supply (432.4): at least L/3 ears with disjoint interiors.
  (4) Laminar Kill (432.6) + Exact-Valuation (432.3): a laminar
      family of 2^{t+1}-1 ears is fatal. So laminar independence
      of the WHOLE ear system is at most 2^{t+1}-2.
  (5) Both arcs are minimal (449.1): d > L/2 for every ear, so
      every interior has s >= L/2.
  (6) No sealed interior (448.4): 3-edge-connectivity forces every
      ear interior to leak.
  (7) Interior chord laws (448.1-448.3): spans lie in
      [4, mu], mu = min(delta+, delta-); floor(mu/3)+1 disjoint
      self-chords give a NEGATIVE shift and end the configuration;
      hence a quantitative cross-edge supply.
  (8) Ladder Bound (449, measured for mu <= 16): a self-chorded run
      exceeds ~10 vertices for no mu tested, so cross edges recur
      at bounded intervals along every interior.
  (9) Window Theorem (450.2): a cross edge makes FOUR ears, and
      their local-minimality inequalities cancel the depths:
      s_i + s_j > 2L - 4 - max(d_uu+d_yy, d_uy+d_yu); in the
      diameter world, s_i + s_j > 1.5L - 4.
 (10) Tight diameter world empty (450.3); packing shell not
      attainable, n > (L^2/4)(1+c) (450.4).
 (11) 2-group asymmetry (447.5): no free 2-group action with
      displacement >= 3.
 (12) Arithmetic side, complete: the flow-lattice nexus - Tower
      Theorem (441.2), Ear Identity (441.4), Counting Identity and
      Gauss Bound (443.1), Local Density and Blindness (444.1).
      The deep supply is the theta coefficient r_t(0), massive and
      adversary-independent. The arithmetic never protects the
      adversary; only geometry does.

CONDITIONAL CHAIN (m = 3, under per-region blockiness and wiring
connectivity): Blockiness (436.1) -> Affine Cascade and Region
Bound (437.1) -> Hexagons (438.2) -> Diameters (439) -> boards
UNSAT at t = 3, both branches, every placement (440, 442).

### 451.2 WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT

Exactly five statements. Nothing else is missing.

  (A) THE LADDER QUESTION (449.4). Is the self-chorded-run bound B
      independent of the span cap mu? Verified mu <= 16; the escape
      regime has mu ~ sqrt(L). PURELY FINITE COMBINATORICS.
  (B) THE NON-TIGHT DIAMETER WORLD (450.5). 450 kills s_i = s_j =
      L/2. Configurations with long unequal interiors satisfying
      s_i + s_j > 1.5L - 4 survive. Known structure: the short ears
      (s <= 0.75L - 2) form an INDEPENDENT SET in the cross-edge
      graph - every short ear wires only to tall ears - and a
      minimum-length short ear (s = L/2, mu = 1) has NO self-chords,
      so all L/2 of its interior vertices wire out to tall ears.
      That is the live configuration.
  (C) THE TWO DICHOTOMY BRANCHES at m = 3 (Theorem I of 445.6):
      wiring-fragmented regions, and the contiguous-deviant branch
      of Blockiness - the latter provably immune to the zigzag
      battery (436.1), so it needs a genuinely new instrument.
  (D) m = 5 (Theorem II). The 10-slot analogue; 3 does not divide
      10, which is the crack, but the argument is unwritten.
  (E) UNIFORMITY IN t (Theorem V). The t = 4 one-extra board did
      not decide within this session's compute; t = 3 is UNSAT in
      both branches (442, re-verified 447-run). The t-free
      pigeonhole (all t) and the Constancy Dichotomy are proved,

### 451.3 THE HONEST VERDICT

J7 is not closed and this session did not close it. What changed is
the character of the remainder. At the session's start the frontier
was a regime - an open-ended search through strata and
configurations. It is now five named finite statements, four of
which are ordinary mathematics (one finite combinatorial lemma, one
configuration analysis, one divisibility argument, one uniformity
proof) and one of which - (C)'s contiguous-deviant branch - is
known to require a new idea, because the existing instrument is
proved not to reach it.

Two structural facts should govern any continuation. First, by the
Scale-Invariance Theorem (447.3) there is no induction on t: the
problem has no smaller instance, so uniformity must be proved
directly, never by descent. Second, by the Constancy Dichotomy
(447) and the asymmetric impossibility (445.5), no purely
arithmetic theorem can finish this: the surviving adversary is
position-dependent, and the last mile is geometric by proof, not by
preference.

NOT PROVED: (A), (B), (C), (D), (E); J7; (H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The arithmetic half of
this problem is finished and belongs to the flow lattice. The
geometric half is down to five statements about long, unequal,
bleeding ears above a packing shell that can no longer be reached.
That is the whole of what remains, written out, with nothing hidden
behind an ellipsis.


## 452. THE TRACE FRAME: CYCLES AS A SPECTRAL QUANTITY

### 452.0 WHY A DIFFERENT FRAME AT ALL

Sections 191 through 451 all live in one frame: fix a minimal
counterexample, fix a shallow cycle, study its ears. Every theorem
in that frame is a constraint on a configuration, and the frame's
own no-go results now say what it can and cannot end in. By 447.3
there is no induction on t. By 447 and 445.5 no purely arithmetic
theorem can finish. What is left inside the frame is a global count
against a configuration, and 451 measured the slack in the only
global count the frame owns.

There is a second, blunter reason to leave. The infinite 3-regular
tree has minimum degree 3 and no cycles at all. So NO statement
about bounded neighbourhoods can imply Erdos-Gyarfas: every proof
must at some point use the fact that the graph closes up. Ear
inequalities are local; they can only ever bite through a global
quantity. This section computes the global quantity directly and
never assumes a counterexample.

### 452.1 THE NON-BACKTRACKING TRACE

Let G be cubic on n vertices, m-th power taken of the Hashimoto
(non-backtracking) matrix T on the 3n directed edges,

    T[(u,v)][(v,w)] = 1   iff   w != u.

tr(T^m) counts closed non-backtracking TAILLESS walks of length m
with a marked starting directed edge. By Ihara's theorem for a
(q+1)-regular graph with q = 2, the spectrum of T consists of the
roots of z^2 - lam z + 2 for each lam in spec(A), together with +1
and -1 each with multiplicity |E| - |V| = n/2. Writing
p_m(lam) = alpha^m + beta^m for alpha + beta = lam, alpha beta = 2:

    (IDENTITY)   tr(T^m) = SUM_lam p_m(lam) + (n/2)(1 + (-1)^m).

p_m is an integer polynomial, p_0 = 2, p_1 = X,
p_m = X p_{m-1} - 2 p_{m-2}, so the right side is tr(p_m(A)) plus a
constant: EXACT integer arithmetic, no floating point anywhere.

PROVED (452.1). The identity, verified in tools/spectral453.py
against direct integer powers of T on eleven cubic graphs (K4, K3,3,
prism, cube, Petersen, Heawood, Moebius-Kantor, GP(9,2),
dodecahedron, Desargues, Nauru) for every m below 2g. All rows
agree exactly.

### 452.2 THE CUBIC GEODESIC SIMPLICITY LEMMA

LEMMA. In a cubic graph of girth g, every closed non-backtracking
tailless walk of length m < 2g is a simple cycle traversed once.

PROOF. Let W = v_0 v_1 ... v_{m-1} (indices mod m, v_{i+1} != v_{i-1}
for every i) and suppose W is not a simple cycle. Some vertex
repeats, say v_i = v_j with i != j. The two passes through that
vertex use the edge pairs {v_{i-1}v_i, v_i v_{i+1}} and
{v_{j-1}v_j, v_j v_{j+1}}; each pair has two distinct edges because W
does not backtrack. The vertex has degree 3, so two 2-subsets of a
3-set intersect: the passes share an edge e. Hence e is traversed
twice.

Case 1: e is traversed twice in the same direction. Then W revisits
a directed edge, so W is a proper power of a shorter closed
non-backtracking tailless walk of length l = m/j, j >= 2. The
support of such a walk has minimum degree 2, hence contains a cycle,
hence l >= g and m >= 2g.

Case 2: e = xy is traversed once as (x,y) and once as (y,x). Cut W
at those two steps. The arc A between them is a closed walk at y of
length a, non-backtracking internally; its first edge differs from e
(no backtrack after arriving along e) and its last edge differs from
e (no backtrack before leaving along e reversed), and its first and
last edges differ from each other (no backtrack at that visit to y).
So A is a closed non-backtracking tailless walk and a >= g. The
complementary arc B is the same at x, b >= g. Since
m = a + b + 2, m >= 2g + 2.

Either way m >= 2g. QED

COROLLARY. For g <= m < 2g,   tr(T^m) = 2m c_m,  where c_m is the
number of cycles of length m. Hence in that range c_m is a purely
spectral quantity:

    c_m = [ SUM_lam p_m(lam) + (n/2)(1 + (-1)^m) ] / 2m.

SHARP. Any girth cycle traversed twice is a closed non-backtracking
tailless walk of length exactly 2g, so the bound 2g cannot be
raised for any graph.

COMPUTED (452.2). tools/sieve454.py enumerates EVERY closed
non-backtracking tailless walk and classifies it by the cycle rank
of its support. On all seven test graphs the census total equals
the spectral trace exactly, the rank-1 total equals the divisor
prediction SUM_{j|m} 2(m/j) c_{m/j} exactly, and the first
non-simple geodesic appears at m = 2g exactly - never earlier,
never later.

### 452.3 THE DOUBLING LAW: POWERS OF TWO ARE A DYNAMICAL SYSTEM

    p_{2m}(lam) = p_m(lam)^2 - 2^{m+1}.

Normalising q_m = p_m / 2^{m/2} this is

    q_{2m} = q_m^2 - 2,

the Chebyshev / Lucas-Lehmer map, conjugate to the doubling map
z -> 2z on the circle via q = 2 cos theta. So the power-of-two
subsequence of the cycle counts is the ORBIT OF THE GRAPH'S SPECTRUM
UNDER A QUADRATIC DYNAMICAL SYSTEM. This is what the 2-adic tower of
441 was a shadow of: the tower is the arithmetic trace of an
iteration, and the reason "something breaks at mod 8" is that the
second iterate of a quadratic map is where a quadratic map stops
being determined by its linearisation.

Under this map lam = 3 ESCAPES: p_m(3) = 2^m + 1 exactly. Every
lam in [-2 sqrt 2, 2 sqrt 2] stays BOUNDED: |p_m(lam)| <= 2 . 2^{m/2}.
Every lam outside that interval contributes a POSITIVE amount when m
is even. The escape rate of the Perron eigenvalue against the
bounded orbit of everything else is the whole content of 452.4.

COMPUTED: doubling identity checked for lam = -3..3 and
m = 1,2,4,8,16 with zero violations; p_m(3) = 2^m + 1 for m = 0..32;
|p_m(lam)| <= 2 . 2^{m/2} for lam in -2..2, m = 1..24.

### 452.4 THE SPECTRAL WINDOW THEOREM

THEOREM. Let G be cubic on n vertices with girth g. For every EVEN
m satisfying

    (W)   2^m + 1 + n > 2(n-1) 2^{m/2}      and      m < 2g,

G contains a cycle of length m, and in fact

    c_m >= [ 2^m + 1 + n - 2(n-1) 2^{m/2} ] / 2m.

PROOF. Bound the n-1 non-Perron eigenvalues below by -2 . 2^{m/2}
each (valid: those inside the bounded interval satisfy it, those
outside contribute positively for even m), add p_m(3) = 2^m + 1 and
the constant n from (IDENTITY), and divide the corollary of 452.2.
QED

COROLLARY (unconditional Erdos-Gyarfas for an explicit class). If
some power of 2 satisfies (W), then G has a cycle of that length and
Erdos-Gyarfas holds for G. The test depends only on (n, g).

COMPUTED (452.4), tools/verify455.py, LCF constructions with girth
verified:

  graph            n    g   forced m   forced c_m >=   actual c_m
  Heawood         14    6      10             11            84
  Moebius-Kantor  16    6      10              5            96
  McGee           24    7      12             50           164
  Tutte-Coxeter   30    8      12             18           300
  Tutte-Coxeter   30    8      14            322          1080
  Foster          90   10      16            627          4860
  Foster          90   10      18           4753         12600

The Foster row is the corollary firing: 16 is a power of two, it
satisfies (W), and the graph is therefore forced to contain a
16-cycle. c_16 = 4860 confirmed independently by brute-force
enumeration and by the trace formula. Erdos-Gyarfas for the Foster
graph, proved by spectrum alone, with no combinatorics.

Sweeping Moore-extremal sizes, the criterion fires at
n = 58, 70, 90, 102, 126 (the (3,9) through (3,12) cages), at
n = 1022, 2046, 4094, 8190, 16382, and at n = 262142, 1048574; it
fails at n = 258, 510, 65534. So it settles the conjecture for a
large, explicitly identifiable, infinite family of the very graphs
that are hardest for every other method - the cages.

### 452.5 THE GEODESIC SIEVE AND THE EXACT BARRIER

Above 2g the trace picks up non-simple geodesics, classified by the
cycle rank of the support:

  rank 1: a cycle of length l traversed j times, m = jl; total
          contribution SUM_{j|m} 2(m/j) c_{m/j}  (exact, verified).
  rank 2: theta traversals, length a + b + 2c on branch paths
          a,b,c; and dumbbell traversals, length |C1| + |C2| + 2 x
          (bar). Both first occur at m = 2g exactly.
  rank>=3: first occur later; observed from m = 12 on Petersen.

MEASURED (452.5). The rank >= 2 corrections at m >= 2g are of the
same order as the main term: corr/2^m lies between 0.66 and 2.53
across the census. They are NOT a lower-order error term.

THE BARRIER, EXACTLY. Let m* be the least even m at which (W)
holds. Because c_m = 0 for m < g, (W) must fail for every even
m < g, which gives 2^{m/2} < 2n there and hence

    m* >= g - 1,       g < 2 log2(2n) + 2.

The second inequality is the Moore bound, rederived spectrally -
a consistency check, and the reason the method cannot be pushed:
the window is (m*, 2g) with m* >= g - 1, so it is contained in
(g-1, 2g). That interval has multiplicative ratio just over 2, so
it MAY contain a power of two, but nothing forces one into it, and
when m* is much larger than g the window is empty outright. The
threshold cannot be improved by better spectral estimates either:
for even m < g the identity forces SUM_{lam != 3} p_m(lam) to equal
exactly -(2^m + 1 + n), i.e. the non-Perron eigenvalues conspire to
cancel the main term to the last unit, all the way up to the girth.
The crude bound is achieved.

So the frame's reach is exactly m < 2g, and extending it requires
cancellation-level accounting of rank >= 2 geodesics, not a cruder
estimate.

### 452.6 ERRORS RECORDED (374.1)

FALSE, RETRACTED: "the unique power of two in [g, 2g) is always a
cycle length" (call it the weak form). It would imply
Erdos-Gyarfas immediately. It is refuted by truncation: replacing
every vertex of a cubic graph by a triangle gives girth 3 and no
4-cycles at all. Verified on truncated K4 (n=12), truncated cube
(n=24) and truncated Petersen (n=30): each has girth 3 and exactly
zero 4-cycles.

FALSE, CORRECTED: an earlier draft of tools/verify455.py asserted
that the Tutte-Coxeter graph has no 10-cycle and billed this as
showing (W) is tight. It has 72 ten-cycles, confirmed twice. (W)
is a CONSERVATIVE forcing threshold, not the onset of cycles: on
Tutte-Coxeter cycles exist at m = 8 and 10 while (W) first fires at
m = 11. The gap between onset and forcing is precisely the slack a
sieve would have to recover.

### 452.7 WHAT THIS CHANGES

It does not close J7. The five statements of 451.2 stand
untouched; nothing here bears on ear geometry.

What it changes is the shape of the problem. Erdos-Gyarfas now has
a second, independent line of attack that assumes no counterexample,
performs no surgery, and produces cycles instead of contradictions;
that line proves the conjecture outright for an infinite explicit
family including the (3,9) to (3,12) cages; and its single point of
failure is identified exactly and quantitatively - the rank >= 2
geodesic corrections above m = 2g, which are Theta(2^m) rather than
o(2^m).

It also reinterprets the nexus. The 2-adic tower of 441 is the
arithmetic shadow of the Chebyshev iteration q -> q^2 - 2 acting on
the graph spectrum. Powers of two are hard here for the same reason
they are hard in the Lucas-Lehmer test: they are not an arithmetic
progression but the orbit of a chaotic quadratic map.

PROVED: (IDENTITY); the Cubic Geodesic Simplicity Lemma and its
sharpness; c_m spectral for g <= m < 2g; the Doubling Law; the
Spectral Window Theorem and its corollary; the rank-1 divisor
formula; Erdos-Gyarfas for every cubic graph passing the (n, g)
test, in particular for the Foster graph and the (3,9) to (3,12)
cages.

NOT PROVED: any control of the rank >= 2 corrections above 2g;
E-G for graphs failing the (n,g) test; J7; (H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. But it is no longer being
attacked from one direction only, and the new direction's failure
point is a single measured quantity rather than a list of
configurations.


## 453. J7 IN GENERATING FUNCTIONS

### 453.0 THE QUESTION

Can J7 be cast in the language of generating functions, in a way
that does not require settling the five statements of 451.2? The
answer is that J7 casts exactly - three different ways - that two of
the three castings are already in this archive under other names,
that one of them yields a new unconditional theorem, and that the
casting does NOT bypass 451.2. The reason it does not is a single
number, computed in 453.5, and that number explains the whole
predicament of this programme better than any of the five statements
do.

### 453.1 GF1: THE ZETA, AND CYCLES AS A PRIME COUNT

    1/zeta_G(u) = (1 - u^2)^{n/2} det(I - uA + 2u^2 I),
    SUM_m N_m u^m = -u d/du log zeta_G(u),      N_m = tr(T^m),
    N_m = SUM_{l | m} l P_l,      P_l = # prime geodesic classes.

Moebius inversion recovers P_l, and by 452.2, P_l = 2 c_l for
l < 2g. So below twice the girth the cycle counting function is
literally the prime counting function of an explicit rational
function of degree 3n.

COMPUTED (453.1), tools/gf456.py: Moebius inversion is integral in
every case, and P_l = 2 c_l holds for every l < 2g on K4, Petersen,
Heawood, Moebius-Kantor, Pappus, Desargues and McGee. The first
disagreement occurs at l = 2g exactly (Desargues, l = 12: P = 540
against 2c = 300 - the surplus of 240 is the non-simple primes),
matching 452.5.

### 453.2 GF2: THE ROOTS-OF-UNITY FILTER, AND AN EXISTENCE THEOREM

Let E_G(y) = SUM_{Z even subgraph} y^{|Z|}, an Ising/Tutte
specialisation. The condition "2^k divides |Z|" is a CONGRUENCE, so
the filter exists:

    #{Z even : 2^k | |Z|} = 2^{-k} SUM_{j < 2^k} E_G(w^j),
    w = exp(2 pi i / 2^k).

This is 443's Counting Identity in standard notation; the Gauss sums
of 443 and the theta coefficients r_t(v) of 444 are the same objects.
Because the condition is a congruence rather than an exact value, the
GF frame is not merely descriptive here: Ax's theorem applies.

THEOREM (Ax existence). Let G be any graph of cycle rank
mu >= 2^k. Then G has a NONEMPTY even subgraph Z with
|Z| == 0 mod 2^k.

PROOF. Parametrise the cycle space by y in F_2^mu, x = By. By
Lucas, bit j of the weight is the elementary symmetric polynomial
e_{2^j}(x) over F_2, so "2^k divides |x|" is the system
e_1 = e_2 = e_4 = ... = e_{2^{k-1}} = 0, polynomial conditions in y
of degrees 1, 2, ..., 2^{k-1}, with degree sum 2^k - 1 and maximum
degree 2^{k-1}. By Ax's theorem the number N of common zeros is
divisible by 2^b with b = ceil((mu - (2^k - 1)) / 2^{k-1}), and
b >= 1 exactly when mu >= 2^k. Since y = 0 is a solution, N >= 1,
hence N >= 2. QED

For a cubic graph mu = n/2 + 1, so the hypothesis is
n >= 2^{k+1} - 2. (The technique is standard Chevalley-Warning /
Ax; whether this exact corollary is in the literature has NOT been
checked, per 388.1, and it is not relied on below.)

COMPUTED (453.2): the divisibility 2^b | N verified for
2^k = 4, 8, 16 on all seven graphs by full enumeration of the cycle
space; nonempty solutions forced and found wherever mu >= 2^k
(Petersen, Heawood, Moebius-Kantor, Pappus, Desargues, McGee).

WHAT IT IS NOT. This produces an even subgraph of size DIVISIBLE by
2^k, not a CIRCUIT of size EQUAL to 2^k. Both gaps are real. J7 is
precisely the exactness gap of this theorem.

### 453.3 GF3: J7 AS AN INDEPENDENCE POLYNOMIAL

By the One-Step Theorem (446.2) the lengths reachable in one step
from the shallow cycle C are exactly L + SUM_{i in S} delta_i, where
S ranges over independent sets of the CONFLICT GRAPH H on the ears
(two ears conflict when their interiors meet). Hence

    J7  <=>  the weighted independence polynomial
             Z_H(u) = SUM_{S indep in H} u^{SUM_{i in S} delta_i}
             has no monomial whose exponent is a forbidden length.

This is an exact casting of J7 and it is the honest one: the
arithmetic content sits in the delta_i, which 441-445 have already
finished, and ALL remaining content sits in the edge set of H. The
five statements of 451.2 are, one for one, statements about the edge
set of H. Casting J7 as a generating function does not remove them;
it collects them into a single object.

### 453.4 WHAT PROVABLY DOES NOT CAST

"Length == 0 mod 2^t" is a finite Fourier condition and casts
perfectly (453.2). "Length == 2^k exactly" does not, and the
obstruction is structural rather than technical:

  - Roots-of-unity filters exist for arithmetic progressions. The
    set {2^k} is not one, and is not a finite union of them.
  - The natural detector SUM_k u^{2^k} is a Hadamard lacunary
    series: by the Hadamard gap theorem it has the unit circle as a
    natural boundary, so it cannot be an algebraic operator acting
    on a rational zeta.
  - Consequently no rational/algebraic manipulation of GF1 can
    extract the power-of-two section.

This is exactly the Scale-Invariance Theorem (447.3) restated
analytically: {2^k} is the fixed set of doubling, and doubling is
not a group operation on Z that Fourier analysis can see. The
archive proved the no-go combinatorially in 447; the GF frame
explains why it had to be true.

There is a second, quieter limitation. The GF SUM_m N_m u^m has
radius of convergence 1/2, but SUM_m c_m u^m is a POLYNOMIAL (of
degree at most n). All of the analytic mass therefore lives in the
sieve corrections, so singularity analysis cannot separate cycles
from non-simple geodesics. The GF frame gives exact identities and
no asymptotic leverage.

### 453.5 THE CRITICAL DENSITY: WHY THE BYPASS FAILS

The one route by which GF language could have skipped 451.2: bound
the DEGREE of the conflict graph H rather than analyse its
structure, extract a large independent family of ears by Turan, and
run the zero-sum theory of 445 on that family - for which no
geometry is needed, since independence means all subsets are
simultaneously realisable.

Count the configuration with the archive's own parameters. C has L
vertices, each carrying exactly one third edge, so the ear system
has exactly N = L/2 ears. Every interior is at least L/2 (450) and
n > L^2/4 (450, Corollary 2), so the interiors hold about L^2/4
vertices, each with one spare edge; that is about L^2/8 cross edges.
The number of PAIRS of ears is C(L/2, 2), also about L^2/8.

COMPUTED (453.5):

     L    ears N   cross edges   pairs C(N,2)   cross/pairs
    24        12            72             66        1.091
    48        24           288            276        1.043
    96        48          1152           1128        1.021
   192        96          4608           4560        1.011
   384       192         18432          18336        1.005
  4096      2048       2097152        2096128        1.000

THE CONFLICT GRAPH CARRIES EXACTLY ONE CONFLICT PER PAIR OF EARS,
asymptotically to the last digit. This is not a coincidence to be
tuned away: it is forced by n ~ L^2/4 together with N = L/2.

Consequences, both negative and clarifying:

  - Turan sees only the average degree, which is ~N. It returns
    alpha >= N/(N+1) < 1. It gives NOTHING.
  - Since the count of conflicts equals the count of pairs, whether
    a large compatible family of ears exists depends entirely on how
    the cross edges are DISTRIBUTED, never on how many there are.
  - That distribution question is statement (B) of 451.2.

So the degree-bound bypass does not escape the five statements; it
reduces to one of them. And it does so for a reason that is now
quantitative: the J7 configuration sits exactly at the critical
density of its own conflict graph, the one density at which every
counting argument is silent.

### 453.6 VERDICT

PROVED: the three castings GF1, GF2, GF3; the Ax existence theorem
(nonempty even subgraph of size divisible by 2^k whenever
mu >= 2^k); the identification of 443's Counting Identity as a
roots-of-unity filter and of 444's densities as theta coefficients;
the critical-density identity cross edges ~ pairs of ears.

NOT PROVED, AND NOT REACHABLE THIS WAY: extraction of the
power-of-two section of any of these generating functions. J7;
(H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. J7 casts into generating
functions exactly and gains one theorem by doing so, but the casting
is faithful: it carries the five statements of 451.2 across intact,
and it explains why - the configuration sits at the exact density
where counting cannot decide and only distribution can.


## 454. THE FIRST-MOMENT ATTACK ON THE SIEVE GAP

### 454.0 THE GAP, AND WHY IT WAS MISMEASURED

452.5 measured the non-simple geodesic corrections above m = 2g,
found corr/2^m between 0.66 and 2.53, and concluded that they are
"NOT a lower-order error term". That conclusion is WRONG, and this
section overturns it. Every graph in that census had m comparable
to n. The correction was never measured in the regime that matters.

### 454.1 THE FIRST-MOMENT PREDICTION

In the configuration model the expected number of copies of a fixed
subgraph F in a random cubic graph scales as
(d-1)^{e(F)} n^{v(F)-e(F)}, with d - 1 = 2.

  - A CYCLE has v = e, giving Theta(2^a). This is the main term:
    the expected number of a-cycles is ~ 2^a/2a, so 2a c_a ~ 2^a,
    exactly matching p_a(3) = 2^a + 1.
  - A THETA and a DUMBBELL both have v = e - 1, giving
    Theta(2^{e}/n). A rank-r support gives n^{1-r}.

So EVERY correction carries a factor 1/n that the main term does
not. Summing the shapes, with SUM_{a+b=m-2l} 1/(ab) = O(log m / m),

    rank-2 contribution  =  O( 2^m log m / n ).

PREDICTION: corr(m) . n / 2^m is roughly constant in n, while
corr(m)/2^m decays like 1/n.

### 454.2 THE MEASUREMENT, AND AN ERROR RECORDED (374.1)

tools/moment457.py, random cubic graphs, m = 12 fixed:

     n    2m c_m / 2^m    corr / 2^m    corr . n / 2^m
    20        0.4517        0.6016           12.03
    30        0.5972        0.3784           11.35
    40        0.7075        0.3022           12.09
    60        0.8472        0.1838           11.03
    80        0.9170        0.1211            9.69
   120        0.8994        0.0742            8.91
   160        0.8799        0.1152           18.44
   240        0.9648        0.0410            9.84

The middle column decays by a factor of fifteen; the right column is
flat (the n = 160 row is a six-sample fluctuation). At n = 320,
m = 12 the main term ratio is 0.9824.

CORRECTED (374.1): the sieve corrections are Theta(2^m / n), NOT
Theta(2^m). The verdict of 452.5 is withdrawn. Consequently THE
CAP AT m = 2g IS NOT THE REAL BARRIER of the trace frame; the real
barrier is the size of the correction, and for graphs whose short
cycles are not clustered the correction is negligible and the window
of 452.4 extends far past 2g.

### 454.3 WHAT THE CORRECTION ACTUALLY IS

A theta subgraph with branch paths a, b, c carries the two cycles
x = a + c and y = b + c, and its closed geodesic that doubles the
shared path has length a + b + 2c = x + y. So thetas contributing at
length m are exactly PAIRS OF CYCLES THAT SHARE A PATH AND WHOSE
LENGTHS SUM TO m. Counting the marked-start walks on such a theta
gives two orientations times m rotations.

COMPUTED (454.3). Writing T_m for the number of such pairs, the
rank-2 census of 452.5 equals 2m T_m exactly:

  graph            m    T_m    rank-2 census    ratio    2m
  Petersen        10     60           1200       20.0    20
  Heawood         12    336           8064       24.0    24
  Moebius-Kantor  12    216           5184       24.0    24

(At these m no dumbbell fits, since two disjoint cycles need
|C1| + |C2| + 2l = m with l >= 1.)

THE SIEVE IDENTITY. Dividing the trace identity by 2m,

    c_m  =  N_m / 2m  -  T_m  -  D_m  -  (proper-power terms),

with N_m the spectral trace, T_m the theta count and D_m the
dumbbell count. T_m is a GEOMETRICALLY WEIGHTED ADDITIVE ENERGY of
the cycle spectrum: pairs (x, y) with x + y = m, counted only when
the two cycles actually meet in a path.

That is the whole content of the trace frame in one line, and it is
exact, not asymptotic.

### 454.4 THE DICHOTOMY AT m = 2^k

Take m = 2^k. The Spectral Window Theorem (452.4) bounds the first
term below, so the identity splits into two cases, with no
counterexample assumed and no configuration analysis anywhere:

  EITHER   2^k T_{2^k} + 2^k D_{2^k}  <  2^{2^k} + 1 + n
                                          - 2(n-1) 2^{2^{k-1}},
           in which case c_{2^k} > 0 and Erdos-Gyarfas holds for G;

  OR       the graph carries at least

               [ 2^{2^k} - 2n . 2^{2^{k-1}} ] / 2^{k+1}

           pairs of cycles that meet in a path and whose lengths sum
           to exactly 2^k. Each such theta, with shared path of
           length c, also carries the third cycle a + b = 2^k - 2c.

The first horn is the generic case: by 454.1 and 454.2 the left side
is O(2^m log m / n) while the right side is ~2^m, so the inequality
holds with enormous room whenever the short cycles are not clustered.
The second horn is a strong positive structure - an additively
saturated, geometrically incident cycle spectrum - not a
configuration to be case-analysed.

### 454.5 STATUS

PROVED: the first-moment scaling of rank-r corrections; the exact
identification of the rank-2 correction as 2m T_m with T_m the
geometric additive energy at m; the Sieve Identity; the dichotomy at
m = 2^k.

CORRECTED: 452.5's verdict that the corrections are Theta(2^m). They
are Theta(2^m / n). The 2g cap on the trace frame is therefore an
artifact, not a barrier.

NOT PROVED: any worst-case upper bound on T_m. The 1/n saving is a
first-moment (typical-case) phenomenon; an adversary is free to
cluster its short cycles, and no deterministic bound recovers the
factor n. Horn two of the dichotomy is open. J7; (H1*); the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. But the trace frame's
failure point has moved: it is no longer "the corrections are the
same size as the main term", which was false, but the single
inequality T_{2^k} < 2^{2^k - k - 1} - a bound on the additive
energy of the cycle spectrum, with nothing geometric in it and
nothing from 451.2 in it.


## 455. THE ENERGY INEQUALITY: HALF PROVED, REMAINDER ISOLATED

### 455.1 THE DETERMINISTIC THETA BOUND

Target: T_m < 2^m / 2m, which for m = 2^k is T_{2^k} < 2^{2^k-k-1}.

Two exact facts do most of the work.

FACT 1. c_x <= N_x / 2x, for every x, with no hypothesis. Every
term of the sieve identity is non-negative and the simple x-cycles
contribute 2x c_x to N_x.

FACT 2. T_m <= (1/2) SUM_{x+y=m, x,y >= g} c_x c_y. A theta at m is
a pair of cycles whose lengths sum to m; dropping the requirement
that the pair actually meets in a path only increases the count.

Put kappa = max_{g <= x <= m-g} N_x / 2^x. Combining, and using
SUM_{x=g}^{m-g} 1/(x(m-x)) = (2/m)(H_{m-g} - H_{g-1})
                           <= (2/m)(1 + ln((m-g)/g)):

  THEOREM (theta bound).
      T_m  <=  (kappa^2 / 4) (2^m / m) (1 + ln((m-g)/g)).
  Hence T_m < 2^m / 2m whenever
      kappa^2 (1 + ln((m-g)/g)) < 2,
  which for kappa = 1 reads  m < (1 + e) g = 3.72 g.

This is a worst-case bound with no clustering hypothesis and no
probabilistic input.

WHAT IT WOULD BUY, IF ITS HYPOTHESIS EVER HELD. A power of two is
guaranteed inside (m*, Bg) once Bg/m* >= 2, and m* ~ 2 log2(2n).
With B = 2 (452) that demanded g >= 2 log2(2n), i.e. girth AT the
Moore bound; with B = 3.72 only g >= 0.54 x Moore.

RETRACTED (374.1), see 456.1: the sentence "it breaks the 2g cap
outright" stood here and is WRONG. The bound needs kappa < 1.41 even
in the limit ln -> 0, and kappa was subsequently MEASURED at 3.4 to
5.6 on every cage, and shown to be unbounded (Theta(n)) in general.
The theta bound of this section is valid but its hypothesis is never
met. The looseness is FACT 2, which throws away the requirement that
the two cycles actually meet - and that requirement is exactly the
factor 1/n. See 456 for the repaired version.

### 455.2 WHY THE ZOO CANNOT TEST THIS

tools/bound458.py measured the FULL correction against the main term
on seven Moore-extremal graphs past 2g. It collapses at once:

  graph            g    m    m/g   2m c_m / N_m
  Petersen         5   10   2.00      0.0000
  Heawood          6   12   2.00      0.1379
  Moebius-Kantor   6   12   2.00      0.3049
  Desargues        6   12   2.00      0.5357
  McGee            7   14   2.00      0.4079
  Tutte-Coxeter    8   16   2.00      0.3564

This is NOT evidence against 455.1, and reading it that way would be
an error. Petersen's cycle spectrum is {5, 6, 8, 9}: it has no cycle
of any length above 9, so at m = 12 the entire trace mass MUST be
non-simple. The method cannot prove what is false. Moore-extremal
graphs are exactly the graphs whose n is as small as possible for
their girth, so m ~ 2g is comparable to n and the 1/n saving of 454
has no room to act. The regime that matters for Erdos-Gyarfas is
m ~ 2 log2 n, which is m << n, and that regime is the one
tools/moment457.py measured: corr/2^m = 0.041 at n = 240.

### 455.3 THE RESIDUE, ISOLATED EXACTLY

The theta bound is not the whole correction. At Petersen, m = 12:

    rank 1 = 120,  rank 2 = 2160,  rank 3 = 1080,  N_12 = 3360.

The pair bound gives T_12 <= 45 (the only split is 6 + 6, and
C(10,2) = 45), so thetas carry at most 24 x 45 = 1080 of the rank-2
mass. The other half is DUMBBELLS - two disjoint pentagons joined by
a single edge, 5 + 5 + 2 = 12.

So exactly two terms remain uncontrolled: the dumbbell count D_m and
the rank >= 3 mass. And the obstruction in both is the SAME single
quantity. A dumbbell is (C1, bar, C2); the bar leaves C1 at a vertex
v by v's unique third edge and then has at most 2 choices per step,
so there are at most |C1| 2^{l-1} bars - but that bound ignores the
requirement that the bar LANDS on C2. Summing over the landing
vertex w,

    D_m^{(l)} = SUM_w (# bars ending at w) . c_y(w),

where c_y(w) is the number of y-cycles through w. Averaged,
c_y(w) = y c_y / n, which is exactly the factor 1/n of 454. Bounding
it in the worst case requires precisely one hypothesis:

  (NC)  no vertex lies on more than K . y c_y / n cycles of
        length y.

That is the ENTIRE residue. It is a statement about how evenly the
cycles of a fixed length are spread over the vertices - no ears, no
configurations, no counterexample, nothing from 451.2.

### 455.4 STATUS

PROVED: FACT 1 and FACT 2; the theta bound
T_m <= (kappa^2/4)(2^m/m)(1 + ln((m-g)/g)); hence the target
inequality T_m < 2^m/2m for the theta term alone whenever
kappa^2 (1 + ln((m-g)/g)) < 2, in particular for m < 3.72 g when
kappa = 1. This is unconditional and worst-case.

MEASURED: on Moore-extremal graphs the total correction dominates
immediately past 2g, for the honest reason that those graphs have no
long cycles at all; the regime m << n behaves as 454 predicts.
Dumbbells carry about half the rank-2 mass at Petersen, m = 12.

NOT PROVED: any bound on kappa; the dumbbell count D_m; the
rank >= 3 mass; hypothesis (NC). J7; (H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The energy inequality is
now half a theorem. Its theta half is proved outright; its remaining
half is a single spreading hypothesis (NC) on how many cycles of a
given length pass through one vertex. (455.1 as first written
overstated the reach of the theta half; corrected in place and in
456.1.)


## 456. kappa AND (NC): BOTH UNBOUNDED, AND WHAT SURVIVES

### 456.1 kappa, MEASURED AND RETRACTED

PROVED (upper control, above the threshold). From
N_x = 2^x + 1 + n + E_x with |E_x| <= 2(n-1) 2^{x/2},

    kappa_x  =  N_x / 2^x  <=  1 + (1+n)/2^x + 2(n-1) 2^{-x/2},

so kappa_x <= 1 + 2^{-s} + o(1) once x >= m* + 2s, m* = 2 log2(2n).
kappa is pinned to 1 ABOVE the window threshold and says nothing
below it. The theta sum runs over x in [g, m-g], which is exactly
the range below m* where nothing is pinned. That is the structural
problem, stated once and for all.

MEASURED (tools/kappa459.py), kappa_x = 2x c_x / 2^x on the cages:

  graph              n   g    kappa_g   max kappa_x   at x
  Petersen          10   5      3.750        3.750      5
  Heawood           14   6      5.250        5.250      6
  Moebius-Kantor    16   6      4.500        4.500      6
  Pappus            18   6      3.375        3.375      8
  Desargues         20   6      3.750        3.750      6
  McGee             24   7      3.500        3.500      7
  Tutte-Coxeter     30   8      5.625        5.625      8

kappa peaks at x = g in every case and never drops below 3.3. The
theta bound of 455.1 tolerates kappa < 1.41. IT IS OFF BY A FACTOR
OF ABOUT SIXTEEN IN kappa^2, ON EVERY CAGE. Retracted accordingly.

NO ABSOLUTE BOUND EXISTS. For the truncation of any cubic graph
(replace each vertex by a triangle) there is exactly one triangle per
original vertex, so c_3 = n/3 and kappa_3 = 6c_3/8 = n/4:

  truncated Petersen  n=30, kappa_3 = 7.50
  truncated Heawood   n=42, kappa_3 = 10.50
  truncated McGee     n=72, kappa_3 = 18.00
  truncated T-Coxeter n=90, kappa_3 = 22.50

### 456.2 (NC) IS FALSE, AND FREE

FREE FOR VERTEX-TRANSITIVE GRAPHS. If G is vertex-transitive then
c_y(w) = y c_y / n for EVERY w, so (NC) holds with K = 1 exactly, by
symmetry, with no argument. Verified: Petersen, Heawood,
Moebius-Kantor, Pappus all return K_obs = 1.00 to machine precision.
The same argument gives the edge version free for edge-transitive
graphs, and the standard cubic cages are arc-transitive.

FALSE IN GENERAL. Splice a Petersen graph onto random cubic blocks
(delete an edge from each, cross-join; the result stays cubic and
connected). All the 5-cycles stay in the ten Petersen vertices while
n grows:

  Petersen + 1 block   n= 40   c_5=10   max c_5(w)=5   K_obs=4.00
  Petersen + 3 blocks  n=100   c_5=17   max c_5(w)=4   K_obs=4.71
  Petersen + 6 blocks  n=190   c_5=21   max c_5(w)=4   K_obs=7.24

K_obs grows with n. A bounded region carrying all the y-cycles forces
K_obs = Theta(n/y). (NC) is therefore FALSE as a universal statement
and cannot be proved. Random cubic graphs also show K_obs = 5 to 13
at girth scale.

### 456.3 THE REPAIR, AND WHAT IT COSTS

The looseness in 455.1 is FACT 2, which counts ALL pairs of cycles
with lengths summing to m instead of only the pairs that meet. Put
the incidence back. Counting theta pairs by their shared edge,

    T_m  ~  SUM_e (# x-cycles through e)(# y-cycles through e)
         =  (1/|E|) SUM_{x+y=m} x y c_x c_y    (edge-transitive),

which for arbitrary graphs is an equality up to the edge-spreading
constant. With kappa_x <= K on [g, m-g] and |E| = 3n/2 this gives
T_m < 2^m / 2m as soon as

    m (m - 2g + 1)  <  3n / K^2.

For a cage, n ~ 2^{g/2+1}, so with K = 5.6 the admissible m runs to
about 2.15 g at g = 20 and about 3.8 g at g = 30: the extension past
2g is real and GROWS WITH THE GIRTH, but it is worthless at the sizes
that can be computed, which is why 455.2's zoo saw nothing.

### 456.4 WHAT THIS SETTLES

The two residues of 455 are the same phenomenon - CYCLE
CONCENTRATION - and neither admits a universal bound:

  - kappa is Theta(n) for truncations; (NC) fails by Theta(n/y) for
    spliced graphs. Both failures are built the same way: put all
    the short cycles of one length into a bounded region.
  - Both are FREE under symmetry: vertex-transitivity gives (NC)
    with K = 1, edge-transitivity gives the theta version, and the
    cubic cages are arc-transitive.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the one durable thing here. The trace frame
is a TYPICAL-CASE and SYMMETRIC-CASE instrument. It cannot be made
worst-case, because the worst case genuinely exists. What it does
deliver, unconditionally, is a structural constraint on any
counterexample:

  ANY CUBIC GRAPH WITH NO POWER-OF-TWO CYCLE MUST HAVE ITS SHORT
  CYCLES CLUSTERED - concentrated on a vanishing fraction of the
  vertices at the relevant scale. If they are spread, in the precise
  sense that kappa = O(1) and the edge-incidence is within a constant
  of uniform, then the sieve converges, cycles exist at every even
  length in a window of multiplicative width greater than 2, and that
  window contains a power of two.

PROVED: the upper control on kappa above m*; (NC) with K = 1 for
vertex-transitive graphs and its edge analogue for edge-transitive
graphs; the incidence-corrected theta bound and its criterion
m(m-2g+1) < 3n/K^2.

DISPROVED: (NC) as a universal statement; any absolute bound on
kappa.

RETRACTED: 455.1's claim that the theta bound breaks the 2g cap
outright.
