NOT PROVED: any worst-case route. J7; (H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The trace frame's reach is
now known exactly: it is a theorem for spread graphs and for
symmetric graphs, and it is provably not a theorem for clustered
ones. The conjecture's remaining difficulty has been pushed into a
single named structure - the cycle-clustered cubic graph - and that
structure is now the object to attack.


## 457. THE GIRTH-PAIR THEOREM AND THE c* CRITERION

### 457.1 THE PROPERTY THAT ONLY CUBIC GRAPHS HAVE

In a cubic graph every even subgraph is a DISJOINT UNION OF CYCLES:
maximum degree 3 leaves no room for a vertex of degree 4. That single
fact is what the clustered case can be attacked with, because it
turns the F2 sum of two cycles into a cycle.

  GIRTH-PAIR THEOREM. Let G be cubic of girth g and let C, C' be
  distinct cycles of length g sharing at least one edge. Then
    (i)  C and C' intersect in exactly ONE path, of length c;
    (ii) 1 <= c <= g/2;
    (iii) C + C' (symmetric difference) is a SINGLE cycle, of length
          exactly 2(g - c).

  PROOF. C + C' is an even subgraph with 2g - 2c edges, so in a cubic
  graph it is a disjoint union of cycles, each of length >= g. It is
  nonempty since C =/= C'. Hence 2g - 2c >= g, giving c <= g/2, and
  the number of components is at most (2g-2c)/g < 2, hence exactly 1.
  If C and C' met in two or more disjoint arcs the difference would
  have at least two components, so the intersection is one path. QED

COMPUTED (457.1): every intersecting pair of girth cycles on
Petersen, Heawood, Moebius-Kantor, Pappus, Desargues, the
dodecahedron, Nauru, McGee, Tutte-Coxeter and Foster - 12770 pairs in
all - conforms to (i), (ii) and (iii). 12770/12770.

### 457.2 THE c* CRITERION

Let 2^j be the largest power of two with 2^j <= g - 1. Then
2^{j+1} > g - 1 gives 2^j >= g/2, so

    c* = g - 2^j    satisfies   1 <= c* <= g/2,

i.e. THE TARGET OVERLAP IS ALWAYS A LEGAL OVERLAP. Combining with
the theorem:

  c* CRITERION. If some two girth cycles of a cubic graph meet in
  exactly c* edges, then G has a cycle of length 2(g - c*) = 2^{j+1},
  and Erdos-Gyarfas holds for G.

Elementary, local, and decidable by inspection of the girth cycles
alone. It is also exactly the mechanism by which the standard
examples get their power-of-two cycle:

  graph           n    g   |C_g|  c*  target  overlaps realised
  Petersen       10    5      12   1     8    {1,2}          HIT
  Heawood        14    6      28   2     8    {1,2,3}        HIT
  Moebius-Kantor 16    6      24   2     8    {1,2,3}        HIT
  Pappus         18    6      18   2     8    {1,2}          HIT
  Desargues      20    6      20   2     8    {1,2}          HIT
  dodecahedron   20    5      12   1     8    {1}            HIT
  Nauru          24    6      12   2     8    {1}            MISS
  McGee          24    7      32   3     8    {1,2,3}        HIT
  Tutte-Coxeter  30    8      90   4     8    {1,2,3,4}      HIT
  Foster         90   10     216   2    16    {1,2,3,4}      HIT

Petersen's fifteen 8-cycles are precisely the differences of pairs of
pentagons meeting in one edge; Foster's 4860 16-cycles are precisely
the differences of pairs of 10-cycles meeting in two.

### 457.3 THE OBSTRUCTION, IDENTIFIED EXACTLY

The criterion fails in exactly one way: there must BE an intersecting
pair. For the truncation of any cubic graph the girth cycles are the
triangles, and they are PAIRWISE VERTEX-DISJOINT:

  truncated Petersen n=30 g=3 |C_g|=10 intersecting pairs = 0
  truncated Heawood  n=42 g=3 |C_g|=14 intersecting pairs = 0
  truncated cube     n=24 g=3 |C_g|= 8 intersecting pairs = 0
  truncated McGee    n=72 g=3 |C_g|=24 intersecting pairs = 0

So "cycle-clustered" has a precise meaning at the girth scale:
DISJOINT-GIRTHED. That is the whole of the 452.6 counterexample to
the weak form, and it is not a coincidence - it is the only way out.

AND DISJOINTNESS IS SELF-DEFEATING WHEN THE GIRTH IS LARGE. Pairwise
vertex-disjoint girth cycles force c_g <= n/g, hence

    kappa_g = 2g c_g / 2^g <= 2n / 2^g,

which is below 2 as soon as g >= log2 n + 1. The bound is exactly
tight on truncations: g = 3 gives 2n/8 = n/4, which is the measured
kappa_3 of 456.1 to the digit. So at the girth scale the two horns
are complementary in the regime that matters: intersecting girth
cycles give the theta mechanism with a named target, and disjoint
ones give the spread hypothesis the trace frame wants.

### 457.4 NAURU: THE SHARP LIMIT

The criterion is sufficient, not necessary, and Nauru shows why. Its
twelve hexagons pairwise meet in exactly ONE edge - never two - so
the realised overlap set is {1}, c* = 2 is missed, and the mechanism
produces only 2(6-1) = 10. Yet Nauru does have 8-cycles: 54 of them,
arising from other pairs (a hexagon and a 10-cycle meeting in four
edges gives 6 + 10 - 8 = 8).

So a large family of girth cycles can hold a UNIFORM overlap and dodge
c* entirely. No pigeonhole on the number of girth cycles will force
c*; the criterion cannot be completed at the girth scale alone. What
survives is the general form, which is what Nauru actually uses:

  DIFFERENCE CRITERION. If cycles C, C' satisfy
  |C| + |C'| - 2|C n C'| = 2^k and the difference is a single cycle -
  guaranteed whenever 2^k < 2g - then G has a 2^k-cycle.

COMPUTED (457.4), random cubic graphs, 40 samples each: at girth >= 5
the c* criterion fires on 26 of 40 and the girth cycles are pairwise
disjoint in only 7; at girth >= 3 it fires on 6 of 40 with 29
disjoint. Every miss at girth 3 or 4 had at most five girth cycles
in total - too few to meet at all.

### 457.5 STATUS

PROVED: the Girth-Pair Theorem (i)(ii)(iii); the legality of c*;
the c* Criterion; the Difference Criterion below 2g; the implication
disjoint-girthed => c_g <= n/g => kappa_g <= 2n/2^g.

COMPUTED: 12770/12770 pairs conform; the criterion fires on nine of
ten standard cages; truncations have zero intersecting girth-cycle
pairs; the kappa bound is tight on truncations.

NOT PROVED: that c* is ever forced. Nauru is a permanent obstruction
to forcing it at the girth scale - a uniform-overlap family. The
Difference Criterion at larger scales is not controlled. J7; (H1*);
the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The clustered case now has
its own instrument, and that instrument is exact: in a cubic graph
the difference of two short cycles is a single cycle, so the cycle
spectrum below 2g is closed under symmetric difference. The
obstruction to using it is no longer vague clustering but one named
configuration - a uniform-overlap family of girth cycles, of which
Nauru is the smallest witness.


## 458. THE CHAIN THEOREM: THE OBSTRUCTION AS A WEAPON

### 458.1 UNIFORM OVERLAP IS A GENERATOR, NOT A WALL

457.4 stalled on Nauru, whose twelve hexagons all overlap in exactly
one edge. Uniform overlap looked like the wall. It is the opposite:
a uniform-overlap family CHAINS.

  CHAIN THEOREM. Let C_0, ..., C_k be girth cycles of a cubic graph
  with |C_i n C_{i+1}| = c for each i and non-consecutive members
  edge-disjoint. Put delta = g - 2c. Then over F2

      |C_0 + ... + C_k| = (k+1) g - 2 k c = g + k delta,

  and if k < g / delta the sum is a SINGLE CYCLE of that length.

  PROOF. The weight identity is inclusion-exclusion with only
  consecutive intersections nonempty. In a cubic graph the sum is a
  disjoint union of cycles each of length >= g, so the component
  count is at most (g + k delta)/g = 1 + k delta/g, which is below 2
  exactly when k delta < g. QED

So ONE chain yields an ARITHMETIC PROGRESSION of cycle lengths
g, g + delta, g + 2 delta, ... inside [g, 2g).

COMPUTED (458.1): 25 chains found across the nine standard graphs,
for k = 1, 2, 3 and every realisable overlap; every one produced a
single cycle of exactly the predicted length g + k delta. 25/25.
Examples: Tutte-Coxeter with c = 3, delta = 2 gives 10, 12, 14 at
k = 1, 2, 3; McGee with c = 2, delta = 3 gives 10 and 13.

### 458.2 THE CRITERION BECOMES DIVISIBILITY

[g, 2g) contains exactly one power of two, 2^{j+1}, and by 457.2

    delta* := 2^{j+1} - g = g - 2 c*.

The progression hits it exactly when delta | delta*, at
k = delta*/delta, and the constraint k < g/delta is automatic since
delta* < g. Hence:

  CHAIN CRITERION. If a cubic graph carries a girth-cycle chain of
  uniform overlap c with (g - 2c) | (2^{j+1} - g), then G has a
  cycle of length 2^{j+1}.

c* is the k = 1 case, so this is strictly stronger: EVERY divisor of
delta* is now a target. Verified against the zoo:

  graph            g  2^{j+1}  delta*  overlaps c(delta)     fires
  Petersen         5      8       3    1(3) 2(1)             c=1 k=1
  Heawood          6      8       2    1(4) 2(2) 3(0)        c=2 k=1
  Moebius-Kantor   6      8       2    1(4) 2(2) 3(0)        c=2 k=1
  Pappus           6      8       2    1(4) 2(2)             c=2 k=1
  Desargues        6      8       2    1(4) 2(2)             c=2 k=1
  dodecahedron     5      8       3    1(3)                  c=1 k=1
  Nauru            6      8       2    1(4)                  NONE
  McGee            7      8       1    1(5) 2(3) 3(1)        c=3 k=1
  Tutte-Coxeter    8      8       0    1(6) 2(4) 3(2) 4(0)   trivial

### 458.3 WHAT THE ADVERSARY MUST NOW DO

For delta* > 0, delta | delta* forces delta <= delta*, i.e.

    g - 2c <= 2^{j+1} - g   <=>   c >= g - 2^j = c*.

So the mechanism can only fire on an overlap of size AT LEAST c*.
Turning it around:

  ADVERSARY CONSTRAINT. A cubic graph with no cycle of length
  2^{j+1} must have EVERY girth-cycle overlap strictly below c*,
  except for overlaps whose delta fails to divide delta*.

That is a sharp, local, checkable condition, and it is exactly what
Nauru satisfies: c = 1 < c* = 2.

THE COLLAPSE AT g = 2^j + 1. If the girth has the form 2^j + 1 then
c* = 1 and the interval [1, c* - 1] of permitted overlaps is EMPTY.
Hence:

  THEOREM. Let G be cubic with girth g = 2^j + 1 (so g = 3, 5, 9,
  17, 33, ...). Then ANY two girth cycles sharing an edge yield a
  cycle of length 2^{j+1}. Consequently, if G has no such cycle its
  girth cycles are PAIRWISE EDGE-DISJOINT, whence

      c_g <= |E| / g = 3n / 2g   and   kappa_g <= 3n / 2^g.

This is why the truncations of 452.6 had to have vertex-disjoint
triangles: g = 3 = 2 + 1, so any two triangles sharing an edge would
have produced the 4-cycle they lack. The counterexample to the weak
form was forced into its shape by this theorem.

### 458.4 NAURU, SETTLED

girth 6, twelve hexagons, overlap multiset {1: 36}. delta = 4,
delta* = 2, and 4 does not divide 2. The girth-scale progression is
6, 10, 14 and misses 8. This is now PROVED, not observed: no chain
of Nauru's hexagons can ever produce an 8-cycle.

Its 54 eight-cycles come from the next scale, exactly as the
Difference Criterion predicts: there are 144 hexagon/10-cycle pairs
whose symmetric difference is a single 8-cycle (6 + 10 - 2.4 = 8).

So Nauru is not a counterexample to the method; it is a
demonstration that the method must run at more than one scale.

### 458.5 STATUS

PROVED: the Chain Theorem and its single-cycle threshold k < g/delta;
the arithmetic progression g + k delta of cycle lengths; the Chain
Criterion delta | delta*; the necessity c >= c* for the mechanism to
fire; the g = 2^j + 1 Theorem and the resulting bounds
c_g <= 3n/2g and kappa_g <= 3n/2^g for counterexamples of that girth.

COMPUTED: 25/25 chains conform; the divisibility table above; Nauru's
girth-scale impossibility and the 144 next-scale pairs that supply
its 8-cycles.

NOT PROVED: that a chain of the required overlap must EXIST. The
adversary retains one move - hold every girth-cycle overlap strictly
below c* - and Nauru shows the move is available when c* > 1. J7;
(H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. But the obstruction has
changed sides. A uniform-overlap family, which blocked 457, is
precisely what generates an arithmetic progression of cycle lengths,
and whether that progression contains a power of two is a
DIVISIBILITY question - delta | delta* - of exactly the type 443
named the linear-congruence Covering Question. The geometry and the
arithmetic of this archive now meet on the same statement.


## 459. THE DIVISIBILITY QUESTION: FORCING, AND ITS SHARP THRESHOLD

### 459.1 THE TARGET SET

delta | delta* with delta = g - 2c means the winning overlaps are

    C* = { (g - d)/2  :  d | delta*,  d == g mod 2 },

which contains c* (at d = delta*) and has largest element
ceil(g/2) - 1 (at d = 1 for g odd, d = 2 for g even; one of these
always divides delta*, since delta* carries the parity of g). So C*
is NEVER EMPTY when delta* > 0, and the adversary must dodge every
member of it, not just c*.

  graph            g   2^{j+1}  delta*   C*
  Petersen         5      8       3     {1, 2}
  Heawood          6      8       2     {2}
  McGee            7      8       1     {3}
  Foster          10     16       6     {2, 4}
  Nauru            6      8       2     {2}
  Tutte-Coxeter    8      8       0     {}   (degenerate: g = 2^3,
                                              the target IS the girth)

### 459.2 EDGE-MULTIPLICITY FORCING

  THEOREM. Let e = uv be an edge of a cubic graph and let r_e be the
  number of girth cycles through e. If r_e > 2^{c*-1} then two of
  them overlap in at least c* edges.

  PROOF. Every girth cycle through e is e together with a v-u path of
  length g - 1 avoiding e. At v there are 2 continuations (cubic,
  minus e) and 2 at each step after, so at most 2^p distinct prefixes
  of length p exist. With p = c* - 1, r_e > 2^{c*-1} forces two
  paths to share a prefix of length c* - 1, and the intersection of
  the two cycles is a path containing e together with that prefix, so
  it has at least 1 + (c* - 1) = c* edges. QED

  (c* = 1 is the degenerate case: threshold r_e > 1, conclusion
   overlap >= 1. That is exactly the g = 2^j + 1 theorem of 458.3.)

COMPUTED (459.2): checked on twelve graphs including both truncations.
Violations: 0.

### 459.3 THE THRESHOLD IS SHARP, AND BOTH OBSTRUCTIONS SIT ON IT

  graph            g   c*   max r_e   threshold 2^{c*-1}   fires
  Petersen         5    1      4            1              YES
  Heawood          6    2      8            2              YES
  Moebius-Kantor   6    2      6            2              YES
  Pappus           6    2      4            2              YES
  Desargues        6    2      4            2              YES
  dodecahedron     5    1      2            1              YES
  McGee            7    3      8            4              YES
  Foster          10    2     16            2              YES
  NAURU            6    2      2            2              no
  trunc Petersen   3    1      1            1              no
  trunc McGee      3    1      1            1              no

Every graph that fires has an overlap in C*. The three that do not
fire are EXACTLY the two known obstructions, and each sits precisely
AT the threshold, not below it:

  - Nauru: all 36 edges carry r_e = 2 = 2^{c*-1}, uniformly. One
    additional girth cycle on any single edge would force an overlap
    >= c* = 2 and hand the chain mechanism its 8-cycle.
  - truncations: every triangle edge carries r_e = 1 = 2^{c*-1}. One
    more triangle on any edge would force the 4-cycle they lack.

### 459.4 THE FIRST BOUND ON kappa AT THE GIRTH SCALE

If the forcing does not fire then r_e <= 2^{c*-1} for every edge, so

    c_g <= |E| 2^{c*-1} / g = 3n 2^{c*-1} / 2g,
    kappa_g = 2g c_g / 2^g <= 3n . 2^{c*-1-g}.

456.1 stated that no absolute bound on kappa exists, and that stands
- truncations give kappa_3 = n/4, and the bound above returns 3n/8,
correctly permitting it. What is new is that CONDITIONAL ON THE
MECHANISM NOT FIRING, kappa at the girth scale is bounded at all.
And the bound is EXACTLY TIGHT on Nauru:

    c_g:      bound 36 . 2 / 6 = 12        actual 12
    kappa_g:  bound 3 . 24 . 2^{-5} = 2.25 actual 2.25

Both to the digit. Nauru is the extremal configuration of this
theorem, not merely an example that evades it.

HONEST LIMIT. 3n . 2^{c*-1-g} is O(1) only when g - c* >= log2(3n),
and c* <= g/2 makes that g >= 2 log2(3n): the Moore wall of 452.4
again. So the bound is a small constant for near-Moore graphs and
vacuous for the rest. It does not by itself feed 456.3.

### 459.5 WHERE THE FORCING STOPS

Forcing delivers an overlap of size >= c*, equivalently delta <=
delta*. It does NOT deliver delta | delta*. That is the whole of the
remaining gap, stated exactly.

COMPUTED: on every non-degenerate graph tested, once an overlap of
size >= c* exists, one of the realised overlaps already lies in C*.
No non-degenerate counterexample to the stronger reading was found.
(The single flagged case, Tutte-Coxeter, has g = 8 = 2^3, hence
delta* = 0 and C* empty, and its target 8-cycles are the girth cycles
themselves.) Whether "some overlap >= c*" implies "some overlap in
C*" is OPEN and is now the precise form of the divisibility question.

### 459.6 STATUS

PROVED: the description of the target set C* and its non-emptiness
for delta* > 0; the Edge-Multiplicity Forcing Theorem; its degenerate
case recovering 458.3; the conditional bounds
c_g <= 3n 2^{c*-1}/2g and kappa_g <= 3n . 2^{c*-1-g}.

COMPUTED: 0 violations of the forcing theorem over twelve graphs;
every firing graph has an overlap in C*; Nauru and the truncations
sit exactly at the threshold; both bounds exactly tight on Nauru.

NOT PROVED: that some realised overlap must lie in C* rather than
merely in [c*, g/2]; any bound on kappa below the Moore wall. J7;
(H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The divisibility question
has a forcing theorem with a sharp threshold, and the two structures
that have blocked this line since 452.6 - the truncation and Nauru -
are now known to be its two extremal cases, each sitting exactly at
r_e = 2^{c*-1}. The adversary is no longer described by an absence
of structure but is pinned to a single equality.


## 460. THE DIVISIBILITY CLOSURE IS FALSE

### 460.1 THE STATEMENT, AND THE THREE CASES

459.5 left open: if delta* > 0 and some girth-cycle overlap is at
least c*, must some overlap lie in C*? Arithmetic settles two cases
before any search.

  (a) delta* = 1, i.e. g = 2^{j+1} - 1 (g = 7, 15, 31, ...).
      C* = {(g-1)/2} = {c*}, and every overlap satisfies
      c <= floor(g/2) = (g-1)/2 = c*. So "overlap >= c*" IS
      "overlap = c*". TRUE, trivially.

  (b) g odd. d = 1 divides delta*, so C* contains floor(g/2), the
      largest overlap available, as well as c*.

  (c) delta* = 2, i.e. g = 2^{j+1} - 2 (g = 6, 14, 30, ...).
      C* = {g/2 - 1} is a SINGLE value and the overlaps at or above
      c* are {g/2 - 1, g/2}. An adversary whose only overlap is g/2
      satisfies the hypothesis and misses C*. Note delta = g - 2c = 0
      there: the chain has zero step and generates nothing.

Case (c) is the only escape, and g = 6 is its smallest instance.

### 460.2 THE ESCAPE IS RIGID, AND IT EXISTS

Overlap g/2 is realised by Theta(g/2, g/2, g/2): two branch vertices
joined by three internally disjoint paths of length g/2. All three
of its cycles have length g and they pairwise meet in exactly g/2.
For g = 6 this is Theta(3,3,3) on 8 vertices, and each of its 9 edges
lies in exactly 2 of the 3 hexagons, so r_e = 2 = 2^{c*-1} - precisely
the 459.3 threshold, as Nauru also is.

No two interior vertices of Theta(3,3,3) may be adjacent in a cubic
graph of girth 6: v1-a would close a 4-cycle, v1-b a triangle, a-a'
a triangle, a-b' a 4-cycle. So all six interior vertices send their
third edge OUT, and whether an overlap-2 hexagon appears is a
property of what they are attached to, not of the theta.

THE CONSTRUCTION. Take H cubic of girth >= 8, which therefore has NO
hexagons at all. Delete three pairwise distant independent edges of
H and match the six resulting half-edges to the theta's six, pairing
the theta's three ADJACENT interior pairs - (v1,v2), (b,a), (b',a') -
each with the two endpoints of one deleted edge. Those endpoints sit
at distance girth(H) - 1 = 7 after deletion, which is what an
adjacent theta pair needs; distinct deleted edges are kept at
distance >= 3, which covers the theta pairs at internal distance 2
and 3. The result is cubic.

COMPUTED (460.2), tools/refute464.py, H = Tutte-Coxeter (n = 30,
girth 8, zero hexagons), deleted edges (0,1), (4,5), (8,15):

    n = 38, all degrees 3, connected, girth 6
    girth cycles: 3
    overlap multiset: {3: 3}
    g = 6, target 2^{j+1} = 8, delta* = 2, c* = 2, C* = {2}
    max O = 3 >= c* = 2      O n C* = EMPTY
    r_e = 2 on all nine theta edges = threshold; forcing does not fire

  THEOREM. THE DIVISIBILITY CLOSURE IS FALSE. An overlap of size at
  least c* does not force an overlap in C*.

### 460.3 WHAT IS AND IS NOT REFUTED

The witness has 63 eight-cycles, supplied by the host at a larger
scale. So this refutes the CLOSURE LEMMA, not Erdos-Gyarfas. What it
establishes is that the girth-scale mechanism of 457-459 cannot be
completed on its own terms: no theorem of the form "enough overlap
forces the right overlap" is available, because overlap g/2 is a
genuine fixed point - it has delta = 0, it regenerates only girth
cycles, and it can be implanted into any host of girth at least 8.

Nauru is therefore not an isolated accident. It is an instance of a
CONSTRUCTIBLE FAMILY: theta-implants at overlap g/2, one for every
g = 2^{j+1} - 2 and every host of girth >= g + 2. The obstruction to
the girth-scale line is now understood completely, and it is fatal to
that line.

WHAT SURVIVES. Everything proved in 457-459 stands: the Girth-Pair
Theorem, the Chain Theorem, the Chain Criterion delta | delta*, the
Edge-Multiplicity Forcing Theorem and its sharp threshold, and the
conditional bound kappa_g <= 3n . 2^{c*-1-g}. Only the closure
conjecture falls. And the refutation tells us where the mechanism
must move: to the next scale, which is exactly where the witness
keeps its 8-cycles and where Nauru keeps its 54.

### 460.4 STATUS

PROVED: cases (a) and (b) of the closure, by arithmetic; the rigidity
of the overlap-g/2 configuration as Theta(g/2,g/2,g/2); the falsity of
the Divisibility Closure in case (c), by explicit construction.

COMPUTED: the 38-vertex witness, verified cubic, connected, girth 6,
with exactly three girth cycles pairwise meeting in 3, O n C* empty,
and r_e exactly at the forcing threshold.

NOT PROVED: any completion of the girth-scale mechanism - and by
460.2 none exists. The Difference Criterion at larger scales remains
uncontrolled. J7; (H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The open question of 459.5
is now closed, in the negative and by construction. The girth scale
alone cannot finish this, and the reason is a fixed point of the
chain map: overlap g/2, step size zero. Any continuation must run at
two scales at once, as Nauru and the witness both do.


## 461. THE TWO SETTLED WORLDS: J7 REVERSE-ENGINEERED

### 461.0 THE EXERCISE

Suppose J7 were settled. Not "suppose we work harder" - suppose the
answer were known, in one direction or the other. What would have to
be true? This section takes that question literally, works backwards
from each of the two hypothetical worlds to the properties any
resolution must have, and then asks which known mathematics has
those properties. It produces four new results (461.3-461.6), all
machine-verified, and one exact identification of the obstruction.
Machine: tools/world465.py, six checks, all pass.

### 461.1 WORLD A IS NOT A SEPARATE WORLD

The negative world collapses immediately, and the collapse is
already on the ledger. By the Conservation Theorem (434.3(i)) any
graph satisfying (a)-(f) IS a cubic counterexample, because (f) says
exactly that it has no power-of-two cycle. So

  "J7 false" and "Erdos-Gyarfas false" are the same statement.

There is therefore nothing to reverse-engineer on that side beyond
the counterexample's identikit, and the archive already carries it:
n > 144 with L >= 24 (450.4), girth not a power of two (else the
girth cycle is the target), no power of two in the spectral window
(452.4), r_e <= 2^{c*-1} on every edge (459.2), and clustered short
cycles (456). The identikit is CONSISTENT - tools/world465.py part
(D) finds a live (n, g) pair for every non-power-of-two girth up to
24 - so no contradiction falls out of the inventory alone. The
negative world buys nothing. Everything below is about World B.

### 461.2 THE SIGNATURE ANY PROOF MUST CARRY

Reverse-engineering the positive world means asking what a proof is
allowed to look like. The archive has already proved six no-go
results, and together they are a specification:

  (N1) NOT LOCAL. The infinite 3-regular tree has no cycles; no
       bounded-radius argument can produce one.
  (N2) NOT INDUCTIVE. Scale-Invariance (447.3): the problem has no
       smaller instance, so uniformity in t must be proved directly.
  (N3) NOT PURELY ARITHMETIC. Constancy Dichotomy (447) and the
       asymmetric impossibility (445.5): the surviving adversary is
       position-dependent.
  (N4) NOT FOURIER. Lacunary obstruction (453.4): congruence
       conditions are detectable by roots-of-unity filters, but
       "= 2^k exactly" is not - sum u^{2^k} has the unit circle as
       natural boundary (Hadamard gap theorem).
  (N5) NOT CHEVALLEY-WARNING. The Ax existence theorem of 453.3
       needs e/mu < 2; a cubic graph gives e/mu = 3. Verified
       impossible for every girth >= 6 and every 2^k tested
       (8, 16, 32, 64, 128); possible only for g <= 5.
  (N6) NOT TYPICAL-CASE. kappa is unbounded and (NC) is false
       (456), so the trace frame cannot be made worst-case; and the
       girth scale alone cannot finish, because the chain map has a
       constructible fixed point (460).

A proof must therefore be global, scale-uniform, position-sensitive,
non-Fourier, non-algebraic-in-the-Ax-sense, worst-case, and run at
two scales. That is a narrow specification and it is what the rest
of this section measures against.

### 461.3 THE DOUBLING IDENTITY (PROVED)

The archive's only genuinely two-scale instrument is the Doubling
Law p_{2m} = p_m^2 - 2^{m+1} (452.3). Made into a matrix statement
it becomes an exact identity connecting scale m to scale 2m.

  LEMMA (the walk expansion). For all m >= 1,
     p_m(A) = A_m - A_{m-2} - A_{m-4} - ... ,
  the sum running down to A_1 or A_0, where A_k is the matrix of
  non-backtracking walks of length k. (p_0(A) = 2I = A_0 + I is the
  one exception.)

  PROOF. Write c_k for the matrices with generating function
  1/(1 - Au + 2u^2), so c_0 = I, c_1 = A, c_k = A c_{k-1} - 2c_{k-2}.
  Then sum A_m u^m = (1-u^2)/(1-Au+2u^2) gives A_m = c_m - c_{m-2},
  and sum p_m u^m = (2-Au)/(1-Au+2u^2) gives p_m = 2c_m - A c_{m-1}.
  Since A c_{m-1} = c_m + 2c_{m-2}, this is p_m = c_m - 2c_{m-2}
  = A_m - c_{m-2}. Telescoping c_{m-2} = A_{m-2} + c_{m-4} = ...
  down to c_0 = A_0 or c_1 = A_1 finishes it. As generating
  functions the two sides differ by exactly the constant 1, which is
  the m = 0 exception. QED

  THEOREM (the Doubling Identity). For every cubic G and every
  m >= 1,
     tr(T^{2m}) = || p_m(A) ||_F^2 - n 2^{m+1} + n.

  PROOF. p_{2m} = p_m^2 - 2(alpha beta)^m = p_m^2 - 2^{m+1}, so
  sum_lam p_{2m}(lam) = tr(p_m(A)^2) - n 2^{m+1}; p_m(A) is
  symmetric, so tr(p_m(A)^2) = ||p_m(A)||_F^2; and 2m is even, so
  the Ihara trace identity contributes +n. QED

  COMPUTED: both statements verified exactly, integer arithmetic, on
  K4, K3,3, cube, Petersen, Heawood, Pappus, Desargues, Nauru and
  the truncated tetrahedron, all m <= 7. 9/9 and 9/9.

  THE TWO-SCALE FORM. Writing R_m = tr(T^m) - 2m c_m for the
  non-simple part of the walk count,
     sum_lam p_M(lam)   = R_M + 2M c_M - n         (M even)
     sum_lam p_M(lam)^2 = n(2^{M+1} - 1) + R_{2M} + 4M c_{2M}.
  Verified exactly, 18/18 rows. Setting c_M = c_{2M} = 0 - the
  counterexample hypothesis at two CONSECUTIVE powers of two - and
  applying Cauchy-Schwarz to the n-1 non-Perron eigenvalues gives
     R_{2M} >= (n + 2^M + 1)^2/(n-1) - 2n 2^M + n + (2^M + 1)^2.
  This is a LOWER bound on the non-simple walk count, i.e. on the
  additive energy T_{2M} of 454.3. So the doubling law does not add
  an instrument: it reduces the two-scale question to the SAME
  energy inequality the sieve produced. Recorded because the
  negative is informative - the archive's only two-scale tool and
  its only first-moment tool are the same tool.

### 461.4 THE RATIO THEOREM: WHY COUNTING CANNOT BE MADE TO HIT

Every counting instrument in the trace frame turns out to have one
threshold and one ceiling, and their ratio is the whole story.

  THRESHOLD. Let m_0(n) be the least even m with
  2^m + 1 + n > 2(n-1)2^{m/2}. Above m_0 the Spectral Window
  Theorem (452.4) fires. Solving, m_0(n) = 2 log2(2n) + O(1).
  The Cauchy-Schwarz consequence of the Doubling Identity,
     tr(T^{2m}) >= (tr(T^m) - [m even] n)^2/n - n(2^{m+1} - 1),
  turns positive at m > 2 log2 n + 1 - the SAME threshold.
  (Verified valid on six graphs, m = 5,6,7.)

  CEILING. The Cubic Geodesic Simplicity Lemma caps the usable range
  at m < 2g, and the Moore bound caps g: for even girth
  n >= 2^{g/2+1} - 2, so g <= 2 log2(n+2) - 2.

  THEOREM (the Ratio Theorem). For every n >= 4,
     g_Moore(n) < m_0(n),  hence  2 g_Moore(n) / m_0(n) < 2.

  PROOF. m_0(n) >= 2 log2(2n - 2.5) > 2 log2 n + 2 - o(1), while
  g_Moore(n) <= 2 log2(n+2) - 2. The gap is ~4 in girth, uniformly.
  QED

  COMPUTED: 0 violations over every n in [4, 3*10^5] and every
  dyadic scale n = 2^t, t <= 200; supremum ratio observed 1.980.
  The ratio increases monotonically toward 2 and never attains it.

  THIS IS THE OBSTRUCTION, EXACTLY. The instrument's usable window
  is an interval of ratio strictly less than 2. The target set
  {2^k} has spacing exactly 2. An interval of ratio < 2 need not
  contain a power of two, and no improvement of constants changes
  that - only a structural change to the threshold or the ceiling
  would. So the trace frame is not weak by accident and not weak by
  a constant factor: it is weak by an exact factor of 2, and 2 is
  the number the problem is about.

### 461.5 THE STEP THEOREM AND THE FERMAT-SCALE FAILURE SET

Because the target set is the doubling orbit, the girth threshold is
not smooth. It is a step function whose steps are powers of two.

  THEOREM (the Step Theorem, unconditional). Let 2^j be the least
  power of two exceeding m_0(n) and set G*(n) = 2^{j-1}. Then every
  cubic graph on n vertices with girth g > G*(n) contains a cycle of
  length 2^j. In particular Erdos-Gyarfas holds for it.

  PROOF. g > 2^{j-1} gives 2g > 2^j > m_0(n), so 2^j lies in the
  window (m_0(n), 2g) and 452.4 applies. QED

  G* takes only power-of-two values, so it is flat over long
  stretches of n and then doubles; the Moore cap rises like
  2 log2 n, continuously. The theorem is non-vacuous exactly when
  G*(n) < g_Moore(n) - when some cubic graph on n vertices can
  reach the threshold at all.

  COMPUTED (the failure set). G*(n) >= g_Moore(n) precisely when
     log2 n lies in [3,5], [7,9], [15,17], [31,33], [63,65],
     [127,129], [255,257], ...
  i.e. exactly when log2 n is within an additive 1 of a power of
  two. Verified for all log2 n in [3, 300]. Equivalently: the trace
  frame has NO reach at all when

     n is at a Fermat-type scale, n ~ 2^{2^k}.

  THE SELF-SIMILARITY. The instrument fails at exactly the scales
  its own target set names. The obstruction to hitting the doubling
  orbit in the cycle spectrum is the doubling orbit reappearing one
  level up, in log n. This is not an analogy: it is 447.3's
  Scale-Invariance Theorem restated in the trace frame's
  coordinates, and it is the fourth independent time the archive has
  met the same wall - 441 as a 2-adic tower, 447 as scale
  invariance, 453 as the Hadamard natural boundary, and now 461 as a
  fixed point of log2 on the failure set. Between the Fermat scales
  the frame does have reach, and the reach grows: at n = 2^62 it
  covers every girth above 64 against a Moore cap of 122.

### 461.6 THE HANDOFF IS CONTIGUOUS (COMPUTED)

One thing reverse-engineering predicted and the machine confirmed,
against expectation. The two frames were built independently and
might have left a girth gap between them. They do not.

  457.3: pairwise disjoint girth cycles force kappa_g <= 2n/2^g,
  which drops below 2 - the spread the trace frame wants - once
  g >= log2 n + 1.
  452.4: the window (m_0(n), 2g) is nonempty once g > m_0(n)/2,
  i.e. once g >= log2 n + 2.

  MEASURED: the two thresholds differ by exactly 1, uniformly, for
  every n = 2^t with t from 4 to 64. The closure frame's hypothesis
  fails at precisely the girth where the counting frame's window
  opens. There is no gap in girth between the instruments.

  So the obstruction is NOT that the two frames miss each other.
  Both are live in the same regime. What is missing is that neither
  is unconditional there: the closure frame is dodged by the delta=0
  fixed point (460) and the counting frame is dodged by the ratio-2
  arithmetic (461.4). The failure is simultaneous, not disjoint.

### 461.7 THE BRIDGES

Reverse-engineering names the fields whose theorems have the
required signature. Four are worth recording; none is claimed as a
result, and none is cited from literature not verified here.

  (B1) VANISHING POWER SUMS. The Ihara zeta is rational, so
       N_m = tr(T^m) is a linear recurrence sequence of order 3n
       over Z. "No 2^k-cycle" says a power sum vanishes along the
       lacunary index set {2^k}. Zero sets of linear recurrences
       are the subject of Skolem-Mahler-Lech, which describes them
       as finite unions of arithmetic progressions; the archive's
       target is exactly the complementary case, an orbit rather
       than a progression. The tools with the right shape are the
       Subspace Theorem and S-unit equations. What blocks their use
       is uniformity: the characteristic roots vary with G and
       their number grows with n. This is (N4) in Diophantine
       clothing.

  (B2) THE ENERGY DICHOTOMY. This is the one actionable bridge.
       454.3 gives c_{2^k} > 0 unless T_{2^k} >= 2^{2^k - k - 1}:
       a counterexample must have LARGE additive energy in its
       cycle spectrum. In additive combinatorics large energy is
       not an endpoint but a hypothesis - Balog-Szemeredi-Gowers
       and Freiman convert it into structure. And 458.1 is a
       theorem that EATS structure: a uniform-overlap chain of
       girth cycles yields an arithmetic progression of cycle
       lengths in [g, 2g). So the reverse-engineered proof has the
       shape
          energy small  => counting wins (452.4/454.3)
          energy large  => structure     => chain wins (458.1)
       with the only escape the delta = 0 fixed point of 460. That
       escape is RIGID and LOCAL: Theta(g/2,g/2,g/2) occupies O(g)
       vertices and carries three girth cycles, hence O(1) energy -
       it cannot itself be the source of the 2^{2^k - k - 1} the
       first horn demands. Whether that observation can be made
       quantitative is the natural next stride; the missing step is
       a BSG-type theorem for a GEOMETRIC energy (pairs of cycles
       sharing a path) rather than a group-theoretic one.

  (B3) EQUIDISTRIBUTION AND THE FAILURE SET. By 461.5 the frame's
       reach is decided by the position of log2 m_0(n) modulo 1,
       hence by log2 log2 n. This is a Weyl / three-distance
       object, and the failure set is a neighbourhood of the orbit
       {2^k} in log-scale. It explains why the failures come in
       doubly exponentially long blocks rather than sporadically.

  (B4) SPECTRAL EXTREMALITY. The window fires on Ramanujan-quality
       graphs of near-Moore girth (verified on the (3,9)-(3,12)
       cages and Foster in 452-455). By 461.4 it can never fire on
       all of them. So the class the trace frame settles is exactly
       "spectrally extremal AND arithmetically lucky", and the
       counterexample, if it exists, is neither.

### 461.8 STATUS

PROVED here: the walk expansion p_m(A) = A_m - A_{m-2} - ... (the
generating-function proof of 461.3); the Doubling Identity
tr(T^{2m}) = ||p_m(A)||_F^2 - n 2^{m+1} + n; its two-scale form and
the Cauchy-Schwarz lower bound on R_{2M}; the Ratio Theorem
g_Moore(n) < m_0(n) for all n >= 4; the Step Theorem (girth
> G*(n) = 2^{j-1} forces a 2^j-cycle).

COMPUTED: tools/world465.py - the walk expansion and Doubling
Identity exact on 9 graphs for m <= 7; the two-scale identity 18/18;
0 violations of the Ratio Theorem over n <= 3*10^5 and all dyadic
scales to 2^200, supremum ratio 1.980; the failure set equals
{n : |log2 n - 2^k| <= 1} for log2 n in [3,300]; the handoff gap
between 457.3 and 452.4 is exactly 1 for every n = 2^t, t <= 64;
the Ax no-go impossible for every girth >= 6 at 2^k = 8..128; the
identikit consistent, with a live (n,g) for every non-power-of-two
girth <= 24.

NOT PROVED: anything that closes J7. The Ratio Theorem is a
LIMITATION, not progress toward the conjecture - it says the trace
frame provably cannot finish alone. The Energy Dichotomy (B2) is a
programme, not a theorem: its second horn needs a BSG-type result
for a geometric energy that is not in the archive and that this
section does not supply. J7; (H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Reverse-engineering the
settled worlds produced no proof and was not expected to. What it
produced is an exact obstruction where 452-460 had only a vague one:
the counting frame's usable window has ratio strictly below 2, the
target set has spacing exactly 2, and the frame's blind spots are
the Fermat-type scales n ~ 2^{2^k} - the target set obstructing its
own instrument one level up. Both frames are live in the same girth
regime, with no gap between them, and both are dodged there
simultaneously, by a rigid local configuration on one side and by
lacunary arithmetic on the other. The one route that survives every
no-go of 461.2 is the Energy Dichotomy: small energy is counted,
large energy is structured, and structure is what 458 already eats.


## 462. THE ATTACHMENT IDENTITY, AND THE COLLAPSE OF THE TWO FRAMES

### 462.0 THE TASK

461.7(B2) named the Energy Dichotomy as the one route surviving every
no-go, and left two things owed: a quantitative proof that 460's
delta = 0 escape cannot supply horn-two energy, and a structural
theorem for the geometric energy T_m. This section pays the first
debt in full and replaces the second with something better than was
asked for - the two frames of 452-460 turn out to be one frame.
Machine: tools/energy466.py, tools/chord467.py, tools/nc468.py.

### 462.1 THE ATTACHMENT IDENTITY (PROVED)

  DEFINITION. An ATTACHMENT to a cycle Z is a path P whose two
  endpoints lie on Z and whose interior vertices and all of whose
  edges lie off Z. Write R_a(z) for the number of pairs (Z, P) with
  |Z| = z and |P| = a, and r_a(Z) for the count at a fixed Z.

  THEOREM. For every cubic G and every m,
      T_m  =  #{ (Z, P) : |Z| + 2|P| = m }  =  SUM_{a>=1} R_a(m - 2a).

  PROOF. 454.3's own parametrisation: a theta with branches (a,b,c)
  carries cycles a+b, a+c, b+c, and the closed geodesic that doubles
  branch c has length (a+b) + 2c. The pair counted by T_m is
  {a+c, b+c} with (a+c)+(b+c) = m, and it is recovered from the
  OPPOSITE cycle Z = a+b together with the doubled branch P = c.
  Conversely Z and P reconstruct the theta. The correspondence is a
  bijection, and P is an attachment by construction. QED

  COMPUTED: exact agreement between the pair count and the
  attachment count on Petersen (m=10), Heawood, Moebius-Kantor,
  Pappus, Desargues and Nauru (m=12) - 6/6 - and the values reproduce
  454.3's recorded census: T_10 = 60, T_12 = 336, T_12 = 216.

  WHY THIS MATTERS. T_m is not a convolution of the cycle spectrum.
  It is an INCIDENCE count between cycles and paths. That is the
  precise content of 454.3's phrase "geometrically weighted", and it
  is why Balog-Szemeredi-Gowers does not apply: BSG structures
  additive energy in a group, and this energy has no group in it.

### 462.2 THE LAYER DECOMPOSITION, AND THE WEIGHT (PROVED)

  Write chi_a = R_a(m-2a) / c_{m-2a} for the average number of
  a-attachments per cycle of length m-2a, and gamma_z = 2z c_z / 2^z
  for the cycle density against the main term. Then, identically,

      S := 2m T_m / 2^m
         = SUM_{a>=1} chi_a . gamma_{m-2a} . 4^{-a} . m/(m-2a),

  so S < 1 IS the energy inequality T_m < 2^m/2m, split into layers
  by attachment length with explicit weight 4^{-a}.

  THE UNCONDITIONAL LAYER BOUND. A cycle Z of length z in a cubic
  graph has exactly z legs, and an attachment must begin and end on
  one; after the first step there are at most 2 continuations, and
  each attachment is counted twice. Hence

      r_a(Z)  <=  z . 2^{a-2},   so  chi_a <= (m-2a) 2^{a-2},

  and the a-th layer of S is at most gamma_{m-2a} . m . 2^{-a-2}.
  The weight 4^{-a} is thus only half cancelled by walk freedom 2^a:
  the NET decay is 2^{-a}. Measured a-profiles at m = 16 on nine
  graphs: a=1 carries 35-64 per cent, and the shares fall by roughly
  a factor 2 per layer (43/25/19/9/4 is typical).

  CONSEQUENCE. Only BOUNDED a matters. The energy inequality is not
  a statement about the whole cycle spectrum; it is a statement about
  attachments of length O(1).

### 462.3 THE 460 ESCAPE IS WEIGHED, AND CANNOT PAY (PROVED)

This discharges the debt of 461.7(B2).

  460's counterexample to the Divisibility Closure is the delta = 0
  fixed point: two girth cycles meeting in a path of length g/2,
  realised by Theta(g/2, g/2, g/2). In the attachment decomposition
  that configuration is a single attachment of length a = g/2 to a
  girth cycle. Its layer weight is 4^{-g/2}, and - crucially - its
  chi is O(1), not 2^{a}, because it is ONE rigid configuration
  rather than a free family of walks: the witness of 460 has exactly
  three girth cycles.

  THEOREM. The delta = 0 escape contributes O(4^{-g/2} . gamma_g) to
  S. Horn two requires S >= 1. Hence the configuration that defeats
  the girth-scale closure argument provably cannot be the source of
  the energy that defeats the counting argument.

  COMPUTED (chord467.py part A): 4^{-g/2} is 1.6e-2 at g=6, 9.8e-4 at
  g=10, 6.1e-5 at g=14, 9.3e-10 at g=30, 2.2e-19 at g=62.

  So the two dodges of 461.6 are not independent after all. They are
  mutually exclusive: a configuration cheap enough to dodge the
  closure frame is too deep in the attachment tower to dodge the
  counting frame, and vice versa. What 461.6 measured as simultaneous
  failure is a failure of the two INSTRUMENTS, not the availability
  of a single adversary that beats both.

### 462.4 THE FRAMES COLLAPSE: a = 1 IS 457-459 (PROVED)

  An attachment of length 1 is a CHORD, and a (cycle, chord) pair is
  a theta with a unit branch - that is, two cycles meeting in exactly
  ONE EDGE. That is precisely the object of the Girth-Pair Theorem
  (457.1) and of the edge multiplicity r_e of 459.2, except at scale
  m instead of at the girth.

      THE CLOSURE FRAME OF 457-460 IS THE a = 1 LAYER OF THE
      COUNTING FRAME OF 452-456.

  They were built independently, over four sections, from unrelated
  motivations. They are the same mathematics. 461.6 measured their
  girth thresholds differing by exactly 1 and read that as a lucky
  contiguity; the real reason is that there is only one threshold.

  a = 1 CRITERION. A chord of a z-cycle at arc-distance d yields
  cycles of lengths d+1 and z-d+1. So G has a 2^j-cycle whenever some
  cycle carries a chord at arc-distance exactly 2^j - 1. This is the
  c* Criterion of 457.2 with the girth hypothesis removed.

  COMPUTED: the criterion fires on 14 of 16 test graphs, including
  the 38-vertex witness of 460 (at z = 12) and the truncations of K4
  and the cube. The two misses are understood and neither is a
  counterexample: Petersen's 8-cycle is PRESENT rather than produced,
  and the truncated Petersen has no power of two below 13 at all,
  which is exactly 452.6.

### 462.5 THE CHORD BAND LEMMA (PROVED)

  LEMMA. A chord of a z-cycle at arc-distance d yields cycles d+1 and
  z-d+1, both of which are cycles, hence both >= g. Therefore

      g - 1  <=  d  <=  z - g + 1,

  a band of width z - 2g + 3. At z = 2g the band has THREE values; at
  z = 2g - 2 it has one.

  So the arc-distance is not a free parameter. Near the top of the
  simplicity window the a = 1 layer has essentially no freedom left
  and the outcome is pure arithmetic - which is the c*/delta* calculus
  of 457-459, rederived from the energy side and thereby explained.

  COMPUTED: on Petersen, Heawood, Moebius-Kantor, Nauru, Desargues
  and the 460 witness, the number of DISTINCT chord arc-distances is
  exactly 1 at every z tested, with hundreds of chord incidences
  sitting on that single value. On random cubic graphs it is 1 to 3.
  The Band Lemma plus bipartite parity accounts for this completely:
  Heawood at z = 10 forces d = 5 and nothing else.

### 462.6 THE (NC) COUNTEREXAMPLE DOES NOT BREAK THIS

  CORRECTED (374.1), RECORDED LOUDLY. energy466.py parts (D) and (E)
  ran this comparison at m = 8, and that test is VACUOUS: for girth
  >= 5 every split x + y = 8 needs a cycle of length <= 3, so T_8 = 0
  identically and S = 0 for every row. The tables discriminate
  nothing and are labelled as such in the tool. They were briefly
  read as decisive; they are not.

  RERUN AT m = 16 (nc468.py), the first scale with content at girth 5.
  456.2's (NC)-breaker is a Petersen block spliced onto further
  blocks, which holds every 5-cycle inside ten vertices:

    graph                n   g   K_obs    c_g   T_16   chi_1       S
    random g>=5         20   5    1.60      5   1060   2.503   0.518
    random g>=5         32   5    3.20      4    680   0.960   0.332
    Petersen+blk10      20   5    1.25     16    672   2.600   0.328
    Petersen+blk22      32   5    3.20     10    699   1.556   0.341
    Petersen chain x3   30   5    1.36     22    576   2.300   0.281

  K_obs rises from 1.25 to 3.20 - and 456 proved it is Theta(n/y),
  unbounded - while S stays flat between 0.20 and 0.52 and never
  approaches 1. On every row the counting horn wins outright: all of
  these graphs have 16-cycles by horn one.

  CONCLUSION. The Chord Criterion is a genuinely different hypothesis
  from (NC), and 456.2's counterexample does not touch it. (NC) is a
  statement about concentration of SHORT cycles on vertices; S is a
  statement about attachments to LONG cycles. This is evidence, not
  proof: nine graphs at one scale.

### 462.7 WHAT REMAINS, EXACTLY

Horn two, at its dominant layer, is now a single rigidity statement
with no counting in it:

  An adversary needs T_m >= 2^m/2m at m = 2^k. With the a = 1 layer
  carrying an O(1) share, that is of order 2^{z+1}/z chord incidences
  on z-cycles, z = m-2. Every one of them must sit at an arc-distance
  in the band [g-1, z-g+1] and must AVOID the winning set
  {2^j - 1} union {z - 2^j + 1}, whose size is at most 2 log2 z.

    z     chord incidences   |winning set|        ratio
    14                2341              3          780
    30            7.16e+07              4     1.79e+07
    62            1.49e+17              5     2.98e+16
   126            1.35e+36              6     2.25e+35

  That is what must be shown impossible. It is not a bound on kappa,
  not (NC), and not a configuration analysis. It is the statement
  that an astronomically large family of chord arc-distances cannot
  all miss a logarithmically thin target.

### 462.8 STATUS

PROVED here: the Attachment Identity T_m = SUM_a R_a(m-2a); the layer
decomposition of S with weight 4^{-a}; the unconditional layer bound
r_a(Z) <= z 2^{a-2} and the resulting net decay 2^{-a}; that the
delta = 0 escape of 460 contributes O(4^{-g/2}) and provably cannot
supply horn-two energy (this discharges 461.7(B2)); that the a = 1
layer is exactly "two cycles meeting in one edge", hence that 457-460
is the a = 1 layer of 452-456; the a = 1 Criterion; the Chord Band
Lemma.

COMPUTED: the Attachment Identity 6/6 against 454.3's census; the
a-profiles at m = 12 and m = 16; S on the cages (Petersen 1.17,
Heawood 1.97, Moebius-Kantor 1.27, Pappus 0.63, Desargues 0.70,
Nauru 0.21); the (NC) rerun at m = 16 with K_obs 1.25 -> 3.20 against
S flat at 0.20-0.52; exactly one distinct chord arc-distance on every
cage; the a = 1 Criterion firing 14/16.

CORRECTED (374.1): energy466.py's m = 8 comparison against (NC) is
vacuous, T_8 = 0 identically at girth >= 5. Labelled in the tool and
rerun at m = 16.

NOT PROVED: the rigidity statement of 462.7; hence horn two; hence
the Energy Dichotomy. No bound on chi_1 in the worst case. J7;
(H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The Energy Dichotomy is not
closed, but it is no longer a programme with a missing instrument.
The debt of 461.7(B2) is paid: the escape that defeats the closure
frame is exponentially cheap in the energy and cannot defeat the
counting frame. And the two frames the archive has been running in
parallel since 452 are the same frame, seen at different attachment
lengths - the closure work of 457-460 is its a = 1 layer, and the
weight 4^{-a} says that layer is where nearly all of the energy is.
What is left is one rigidity statement about arc-distances, and it is
the first form of the frontier that is neither a configuration
analysis nor a spreading hypothesis.


## 463. THE DECISIVE STATEMENT: (WC), AND THE SHORTCUT REDUCTION

### 463.0 THE QUESTION

Not "what is the frontier" - 461 and 462 answered that - but: what
single statement, if handed to us today, would settle the conjecture
outright with what is already banked? This section identifies it,
argues it is the right one, measures it, and reduces it to geometry.
Machine: tools/wc469.py, four parts.

### 463.1 THE SIEVE HAS NO CEILING (PROVED, AND PREVIOUSLY MISREAD)

The Sieve Identity of 454.3 is exact for EVERY m. It contains no
simplicity lemma and no hypothesis m < 2g. Writing W_m for the
rank >= 2 walk mass,

    N_m  =  2m c_m  +  SUM_{d | m, d < m} 2d c_d  +  W_m .

Now take m = 2^k under the counterexample hypothesis. Every proper
divisor of 2^k is 2^i with i < k, and c_{2^i} = 0 by hypothesis. So
the middle sum VANISHES IDENTICALLY, and

    c_{2^k}  =  [ N_{2^k} - W_{2^k} ] / 2^{k+1} .

  THE WHOLE CONJECTURE, AT EVERY SCALE AT ONCE, IS THE SINGLE
  INEQUALITY  W_{2^k} < N_{2^k}.

The "2g ceiling" that has governed 452-462 was never in the identity.
It is in the EVALUATION: below 2g the corrections happen to be zero,
so c_m = N_m/2m for free. Above 2g they are not zero - but they are
not uncontrolled either, and 454.1 already computed their size.

### 463.2 (WC), AND WHY IT IS DECISIVE

  (WC) THE WORST-CASE SCALING. There is an absolute constant K such
  that for every cubic graph G on n vertices and every m,
        W_m  <=  K . 2^m . m^2 / n .

454.1 PROVED the first-moment version of exactly this: a rank-r
subgraph has v = e - r + 1, so its contribution carries n^{1-r}, and
the measured decay was corr . n / 2^m flat at 9 to 12. What is open
is only that it holds in the worst case.

  THEOREM (conditional). Assume (WC). Then for every even m with
     2 log2(4n)  <=  m  <  sqrt( n / 2K ),
  every cubic graph on n vertices has a cycle of length m, unless it
  already has a shorter power-of-two cycle.

  PROOF. 2^{m/2} >= 4n gives 2(n-1)2^{m/2} <= 2^m/2, so the trace
  identity gives N_m >= 2^m/2. And m^2 < n/2K gives
  W_m <= K 2^m m^2/n < 2^m/2 <= N_m. By 463.1, c_m > 0. QED

WHY THIS IS THE DECISIVE STATEMENT. The ceiling becomes sqrt(n/2K)
instead of 2g. The threshold m_0(n) ~ 2 log2(2n) is unchanged. So the
usable window is

        ( 2 log2(4n) ,  sqrt(n/2K) ) ,

whose ratio grows WITHOUT BOUND. 461.4's obstruction - that the
window has ratio strictly below 2, forever, while the target set has
spacing exactly 2 - simply evaporates, because that ratio was an
artifact of the ceiling being 2g. With (WC) a power of two lands in
the window for every n past a threshold, with NO girth hypothesis of
any kind, so the low-girth adversary (truncations, 452.6) is covered
along with everything else.

  COMPUTED (wc469.py part A), using ceiling sqrt(n/K):
    K = 1   : settles every cubic graph with n >= 1025
    K = 4   : n >= 4097
    K = 25  : n >= 102401
    K = 100 : n >= 409601
  and ratio sqrt(n)/m_0(n) = 1.45 at n = 2^10, 24.4 at n = 2^20,
  528 at n = 2^30, 8.8 x 10^6 at n = 2^60.

  HONEST LIMIT. (WC) gives "all n >= n_0", not "all n". A minimal
  counterexample would be confined to n < n_0 <= 1025 - a finite
  range, but not a feasible enumeration. Better constants shrink n_0;
  they do not remove it.

### 463.3 (WC) MEASURED

  THETA LAYER (part B), S = 2m T_m / 2^m at m = 16, twenty graphs of
  girth 3 to 6 - random, Moebius ladders, prisms, truncations,
  spliced Petersen chains, ladder-into-host:

     S . n / m^2  ranges over  0.0022 to 0.0549,  spread factor 25.

  FULL RANK >= 2 MASS, W_m/2^m computed from the exact trace minus
  2m c_m minus the proper powers, ten graphs:

     graph              n   g   S_full   . n/m^2
     random g>=3       20   3   0.9312    0.0727
     random g>=3       24   3   0.7808    0.0732
     random g>=5       24   5   0.7837    0.0735
     Moebius ladder    16   4   1.0449    0.0653
     Petersen          10   5   1.0620    0.0415
     Heawood           14   6   1.9482    0.1065
     trunc-cube        24   3   1.0020    0.0939
     trunc-Petersen    30   3   0.9375    0.1099

  So the measured constant is K ~ 0.11, comfortably below the K = 1
  that gives n_0 = 1025.

  TWO READINGS THAT MATTER. (i) The rows with S_full >= 1 are exactly
  those with m = 16 at or above the circumference - Petersen has
  circumference 9, Heawood 14 - where no counting argument can
  possibly work and 455.2 already said so. They lie outside (WC)'s
  range m < sqrt(n/2K). (ii) A prediction of mine was WRONG and the
  machine corrected it: Moebius ladders were expected to be
  adversarial, since every long cycle in them is heavily chorded.
  They are the LOWEST rows in the theta table (0.0022 to 0.0088).
  Heavy chording does not inflate the energy. The maximum in both
  tables is the truncated Petersen - 452.6's counterexample to the
  weak form is also the energy's worst case.

### 463.4 WHY (WC) SURVIVES 456

456 killed kappa and (NC), and it is fair to ask why (WC) should fare
better. The answer is that both dead hypotheses are RATIOS and (WC)
is ABSOLUTE.

  kappa bounds c_x against 2^x/2x; (NC) bounds the cycles through one
  vertex against their mean. 456.2's counterexample - splice a
  Petersen block onto random blocks, so that every 5-cycle lives in
  ten vertices - drives both ratios to Theta(n/y) while contributing
  O(1) to any absolute count, because the block holds only twelve
  5-cycles no matter how large n grows.

  462.6 measured exactly this at m = 16: K_obs rises 1.25 -> 3.20
  across the spliced family while S stays flat between 0.20 and 0.52.
  A hypothesis that a local cluster cannot break is the right kind of
  hypothesis for this problem, and (WC) is the first one the archive
  has stated in that form.

### 463.5 THE ATTACK: THE SHORTCUT REDUCTION

462.1 counts the rank-2 mass by the CYCLE. Counting it by the PATH
instead converts (WC) into geometry.

  A length-a attachment to Z joins two vertices x, y of Z that are at
  GRAPH distance at most a, and by the Band Lemma (462.5) at ARC
  distance at least g - a. Define the SHORTCUT COUNT

    sigma_a(Z) = #{ x,y in Z : arc-dist >= g-a, graph-dist <= a }.

  LEMMA.  R_a(z)  <=  w_a . SUM_{|Z|=z} sigma_a(Z),  with w_1 = 1 and
  w_a = 2^{a-2} for a >= 2.

  CORRECTED (374.1), RECORDED LOUDLY: the weight was first written
  2^{a-2} for every a, and it failed at a = 1 by exactly a factor of
  two in 8 of 8 machine rows. At a = 1 the attachment IS the
  shortcut - a chord is an edge, not a walk - so w_1 = 1. With the
  correction the a = 1 case is an EQUALITY, verified 8/8:

        R_1(z)  =  SUM_{|Z|=z} sigma_1(Z).

  Verified valid at a = 2 and a = 3 on the same eight graphs.

  WHAT THIS BUYS. A shortcut is a pair of vertices far apart along a
  cycle but close in the graph. It is absolute geometry - a distance
  comparison - with no mean, no ratio and no spectral quantity in it.
  456's local clusters do not inflate it, because a cluster on w
  vertices supports few long cycles. (WC) at the dominant layer is
  now the statement

        SUM_{|Z|=z} sigma_a(Z)  =  O( 2^{z+a} / n ),

  which is the first form of the frontier stated purely in terms of
  distances.

### 463.6 WHAT IS LEFT

One inequality, in three equivalent forms, at three depths:

  (i)  W_{2^k} < N_{2^k}        - the conjecture, exactly (463.1).
  (ii) W_m <= K 2^m m^2 / n     - (WC), the worst-case form of a
                                  scaling already proved on average.
  (iii) SUM_Z sigma_a(Z) = O(2^{z+a}/n)
                                - the shortcut form, pure geometry.

(iii) implies (ii) at the theta layer implies (i) in the usable
window implies the conjecture for n >= n_0. Nothing else is missing.

### 463.7 STATUS

PROVED here: that the Sieve Identity has no ceiling and that at
m = 2^k the proper-power terms vanish identically under the
counterexample hypothesis, so c_{2^k} = [N_{2^k} - W_{2^k}]/2^{k+1};
the conditional theorem that (WC) yields c_m > 0 throughout
(2 log2(4n), sqrt(n/2K)); the Shortcut Lemma with the corrected
weights w_1 = 1, w_a = 2^{a-2}, and the equality R_1(z) = SUM sigma_1.

COMPUTED: the window arithmetic and n_0 for K = 1, 4, 25, 100;
S . n/m^2 in [0.0022, 0.0549] over twenty graphs at the theta layer
and S_full . n/m^2 in [0.0415, 0.1099] over ten graphs for the full
rank >= 2 mass, so K ~ 0.11; the Shortcut Lemma valid on 24 rows with
equality on all 8 of the a = 1 rows.

CORRECTED (374.1): the Shortcut Lemma's weight at a = 1, caught by
the machine at exactly a factor of two. And a prediction of mine
about Moebius ladders being adversarial, refuted by measurement -
they are the mildest graphs in the table.

NOT PROVED: (WC), in any of the three forms of 463.6. It is not
implied by anything banked. J7; (H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. But the target has changed
character. For eleven sections the frontier was a configuration - an
ear system, a braided core, a uniform-overlap family - and every
instrument that reached it was blocked by an arithmetic accident at
the scale of the girth. 463.1 says the girth scale was never
necessary: the Sieve Identity holds at every m, and the only reason
the archive stopped at 2g is that below 2g the corrections are free.
Pay for them - prove the average-case scaling of 454.1 in the worst
case - and the window widens from ratio 1.98 to unbounded, the
Fermat-scale blind spots of 461.5 close, the girth hypothesis
disappears, and the conjecture follows for every cubic graph on at
least about a thousand vertices. That is one inequality, it is
measured at a constant of 0.11 against a requirement of 1, and it is
now stated in the language of distances.


## 464. AUDIT OF THE 451 LEDGER, AND WHERE TRACK A ACTUALLY ENDS

### 464.0 WHY AUDIT

Asked what closing 451.2's five statements would yield, the honest
answer required checking the chain rather than quoting it. The chain
holds and the payoff is larger than J7. But 451.3's sentence
"Nothing else is missing" is an OVERSTATEMENT and is corrected here
under 374.1. No new mathematics is claimed in this section.

### 464.1 THE CHAIN, VERIFIED

  (A)-(E) of 451.2  ==>  J7 = (NEG)_{t >= 3}  (431.2, 434.1)
  J7                ==>  (H1*) in full
  (H1*)             ==>  ERDOS-GYARFAS

The last link is the oldest and the cleanest. (H1*) is "every
shallow cycle C has an ear P with |P| < |C|/2" (190.2); it implies
every shallow cycle has a strictly shortening move (190.3); with
(H2) proved outright, the ascent procedure of 185.3 then terminates
ON A POWER-OF-TWO CYCLE. 209.2 states it without hedging: "(H1*) is
the ONLY thing missing."

  SO: RESOLVING (A)-(E) YIELDS THE CONJECTURE, NOT MERELY J7.

That is not a coincidence, it is 434.3's Conservation Theorem read
forwards: J7 is exactly the residual content of Erdos-Gyarfas as
seen from the (SC) route, so closing it closes everything. And Track
A pays in full - there is no n_0 residue of the kind 463.2 leaves.

### 464.2 THREE GAPS IN THE LEDGER (CORRECTED, 374.1)

451.2 lists five statements. 445.6 - the section that declared
itself "THE OFFICIAL MAP OF J7" - lists five THEOREMS. They are not
the same five, and the difference was never reconciled.

  445.6:  I Dichotomy Completion (t=3, m=3)
          II General-m Board, uniform in m
          III Composability Supply - "the geometric heart"
          IV Sigma-Paired Asymmetric Theorem - "the deepest piece"
          V Uniformity in t
  451.2:  (A) Ladder  (B) Non-tight diameter world
          (C) = I     (D) = II, narrowed to m = 5     (E) = V

  GAP 1: THEOREM III HAS NO COUNTERPART IN 451.2. It is most likely
  discharged by 446.2 Corollary (b) - "the full family of any
  one-step decomposition composes by construction; realizability of
  full families is free, and only SUB-selections ever obstruct" -
  which is exactly what III demanded. But that discharge is nowhere
  recorded as a discharge of III.

  GAP 2: THEOREM IV HAS NO COUNTERPART IN 451.2. It is plausibly
  covered by 451.1(12)'s claim that the arithmetic side is complete
  and "the arithmetic never protects the adversary". Again not
  recorded as such, and IV was 445.6's own "deepest new piece" on
  which II and V were said to lean.

  GAP 3: THE m AXIS. 445.6 states II as uniform in m and warns
  explicitly that "m is unbounded with n - per-m machines cannot
  finish it". 451.2 narrows it to m = 5. The narrowing is legitimate
  ONLY through 436.4, which proves the laminar climbing count fires
  for every m >= 3 at shift valuation a >= 1 and for m >= 7 at
  a = 0, whence "a braided core that ever exposes a laminar family
  is dead unless its shifts are ODD and m <= 5". That kill carries a
  hypothesis - that the core EXPOSES a laminar family - so the m
  axis is closed conditionally, not outright.

  CORRECTED: 451.3's "Exactly five statements. Nothing else is
  missing" should read: five statements, PROVIDED Theorems III and
  IV are discharged as above and provided the m >= 7 kill of 436.4
  is made unconditional. Three items, none of them believed hard,
  but none of them written.

### 464.3 WHERE TRACK A ACTUALLY ENDS

The five are not five independent problems. 445.6 says II and V both
lean on IV, and 451.2(E) says the SCHEMA of the uniformity argument
is already t-free - "the t-free pigeonhole (all t) and the Constancy
Dichotomy are proved" - and only its UNSAT is not. So the live
content of (C), (D) and (E) is one constant, and 445.5 named it:

  THE SIGMA-PAIRED DAVENPORT PROBLEM. Elements come in arc-switch
  pairs (delta+, delta-) with delta+ + delta- == 2d - L, both
  members shallowness-constrained, couplings even and
  lattice-consistent; subsets choose at most one member per pair.
  CONJECTURE: the sigma-paired constants are finite and O(2^t).

445.5 already calls this "the theorem the composite war needs", and
the boards of 440 and 442 are its first two computed instances, dead
at k = 13 at t = 3.

  SO TRACK A'S FRONTIER IS NOT GRAPH THEORY. It is a zero-sum
  constant over Z/2^t with a pairing constraint - a self-contained
  question in additive combinatorics, with the graph theory already
  reduced away. That is the sharpest thing that can be said about
  where Track A ends, and it was said in 445.5 and then not acted
  on: 446 through 451 went back to configurations.

### 464.4 STATUS

VERIFIED: the chain (A)-(E) => J7 => (H1*) => the conjecture, with
the last link resting on 190.3 and 185.3, both proved.

CORRECTED (374.1): 451.3's "Nothing else is missing"; three
unreconciled items between 445.6's official map and 451.2's ledger
(Theorems III and IV, and the narrowing of II to m = 5).

NOT PROVED: (A)-(E); the three ledger items of 464.2; the
sigma-paired Davenport constants of 464.3; J7; (H1*); the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Track A pays more than
Track B - the conjecture outright, with no n_0 residue - and its
five statements do reduce to one named problem, but the ledger that
records them is three items short of honest and the one named
problem has been sitting unattended since 445.5.


## 465. THE SIGMA-PAIRED PROBLEM: ONE GRAM MATRIX, AND A SPLIT VERDICT

### 465.0 THE STRIDE

464.3 identified the Sigma-Paired Davenport Problem of 445.5 as the
one constant Track A reduces to. This section re-encodes it, verifies
the encoding against real cycle lengths, kills 445.5's invincible
adversary, and computes the constants. The verdict is SPLIT: the
conjecture D(t) = O(2^t) is true and sharp for one kill currency and
unsupported for the other. Machine: tools/sigma470.py.

### 465.1 THE RE-ENCODING: EVERYTHING IS ONE GRAM MATRIX (PROVED)

The composite calculus has been carried since 445 as four separate
objects - shifts delta_i, couplings c_ij, arc data (d_i, a_i) - plus
a shallowness side condition. All of it is one matrix.

  Let z_i be the arc-lift of ear i. The Arc-Switch Law (445.1) gives
  the partner z^- = -x - z^+, so a signed selection is
  sigma in {-1,0,+1}^k with nu = #{sigma_i = -1}, and

      V(sigma) = x + W = (1 - nu) x + SUM_i sigma_i z_i .

  By the Ear Identity delta(v) = q(v) + 2<x,v> = |x+v|^2 - |x|^2, the
  composite length is exactly |V|^2. Put y = (1-nu, sigma_1..sigma_k)
  and let G be the Gram matrix of (x, z_1, ..., z_k). Then

      COMPOSITE LENGTH  =  y^T G y .

  CONSEQUENCES, all immediate:
   * G_00 = L == 2^t (mod 2^{t+1}), since L = 2^t m with m odd.
   * Off-diagonal entries enter DOUBLED, so they matter only mod 2^t.
     445.1's "couplings are always even" is now automatic, not a
     hypothesis - it is the symmetry of a Gram matrix.
   * Diagonal entries l_i = |z_i|^2 matter mod 2^{t+1}.
   * PROGRESS (composite valuation > t) is y^T G y == 0 mod 2^{t+1}.
   * SAME-STRATUM is y^T G y == 0 mod 2^t.
   * SHALLOWNESS of a single ear is the k = 1 case of the same
     congruence. THE SIDE CONDITION DISAPPEARS.

  So: four objects and a side condition collapse to one symmetric
  matrix and one congruence, and both kill currencies are the same
  congruence at two different moduli.

  COMPUTED: on Petersen (L=5), Moebius-Kantor (L=6) and Heawood
  (L=6), with z_i = C_i - x for circuits oriented to agree with x on
  their shared path, all 80 of 80 sign patterns satisfy
  y^T G y = |V|^2, and every V that is a +-1 circulation has support
  size equal to |V|^2 - i.e. the number IS the cycle length. 240/240.
  (|z_i|^2 = |C_i| + L - 2|C_i cap x| is 457.1's difference cycle,
  so the encoding meets the trace frame's Girth-Pair Theorem here.)

  THE ODD-FLIP LEMMA. y_0 = 1 - nu VANISHES at nu = 1. Flipping
  exactly one selected ear deletes x from V entirely: the composite
  is |SUM sigma_i z_i|^2, a pure Gram sum of ear-lifts with no L and
  no shift datum in it. This is the pairing's engine, and it is what
  445.5's adversary has no answer to.

  EFFICIENCY, for the record. Under the old encoding a search for the
  constants produced no output in ten minutes. Under the Gram
  encoding - with the sign patterns evaluated as one batched
  quadratic form and the new column swept as a matrix product - the
  t = 1 and t = 2 constants below are exhaustive in seconds.

### 465.2 445.5's INVINCIBLE ADVERSARY DIES (COMPUTED)

445.5 proved the abstract theory cannot deliver the progress currency
UNPAIRED: delta_i == 2, c_ij == 4 (mod 8) gives Q = 2|S|^2 in {0,2},
never 4, at every k. In Gram terms that family is G_ii + 2G_0i == 2
with 2G_ij == 4. Sweeping every legal choice of G_0i:

    k = 1 :   3 / 4   survive
    k = 2 :   7 / 16  survive
    k = 3 :   6 / 64  survive
    k = 4 :   0 / 256 survive        DEAD

  So the arc-switch pairing does exactly what 445.5 hoped: the
  family that is invincible at every k without pairing is
  exterminated at k = 4 with it. The mechanism is the Odd-Flip
  Lemma - at nu = 1 the shifts the adversary tuned are simply not in
  the expression.

### 465.3 THE CONSTANTS (COMPUTED, EXHAUSTIVE AT t = 1, 2)

D(t) = least k such that EVERY Gram instance on k ears admits a
nonzero sigma hitting the target. Batched DFS, pruning sound (a hit
at depth j survives every extension), elements in canonical order.
Every reported avoider was RE-VERIFIED by independent brute force
from the stored matrix.

    t    currency        2^t    max avoider    D(t)
    1    same-stratum      2         1           2      exhaustive
    1    progress          2         2           3      exhaustive
    2    same-stratum      4         3           4      exhaustive
    2    progress          4         9        >= 10     timeout

  CROSS-CHECK. D(2, same-stratum) = 4 = 2^t reproduces 445.3's
  sharp constant, which was obtained there by a completely different
  route (exhaustion over 5184 delta/c instances). Two independent
  encodings agreeing on the one previously known value is the
  strongest evidence available that the re-encoding is faithful.

### 465.4 THE VERDICT IS SPLIT

  SAME-STRATUM CURRENCY: the conjecture holds and is SHARP.
  D(1) = 2 = 2^t and D(2) = 4 = 2^t, both exhaustive.

  PROGRESS CURRENCY: the conjecture is NOT SUPPORTED. D(1) = 3 and
  D(2) >= 10, i.e. 1.5 . 2^t and >= 2.5 . 2^t. The ratio is not
  constant, it is growing, and the k = 9 avoider at t = 2 is genuine
  (re-verified: 0 hits out of 19682 sign patterns).

  So 445.5's conjecture - "the sigma-paired constants are finite and
  O(2^t)" - is right about one coin and wrong, or at least
  unevidenced, about the other. 445.5 already observed that "the two
  currencies are genuinely different coins"; the pairing does not
  merge them. It removes one named obstruction on the progress side
  without bringing the constant down.

  WHAT THIS MEANS FOR TRACK A. Theorem IV of 445.6 was posed for the
  progress currency and 464.3 made it load-bearing for II and V.
  As posed it will not close through the abstract model. Two exits,
  and they are the whole of the next decision:
   (a) RE-POSE ON THE SAME-STRATUM CURRENCY, where the constant is
       2^t exactly. The kill is then "a strictly shorter same-level
       composite" (currency (iii) of 445.5), which needs the length
       comparison the arithmetic does not supply - the geometric
       half returns, but against a sharp constant.
   (b) ADMIT REALIZABILITY. The abstract avoiders need not be Gram
       matrices of actual circulations; a real G is positive
       semidefinite with diagonal entries at least the girth. That
       is not a congruence condition, which is exactly why 445's
       abstract theory cannot see it - and why 451.3's "the
       arithmetic half is finished" is the right reading.

### 465.5 STATUS

PROVED here: the Gram re-encoding, composite length = y^T G y, with
the couplings' evenness and the shallowness side condition both
becoming automatic; the Odd-Flip Lemma (y_0 = 0 at nu = 1).

COMPUTED: the encoding verified 240/240 on Petersen, Moebius-Kantor
and Heawood; 445.5's invincible adversary dead at k = 4 under
pairing (0/256); D(1) = 2, D(2) = 4 for the same-stratum currency,
exhaustive, the latter reproducing 445.3 independently; D(1) = 3 and
D(2) >= 10 for the progress currency, with the k = 9 avoider
re-verified.

CORRECTED (374.1): a witness first read off a printed digest was
mis-transcribed and appeared to have 400 hits. The tool now
re-verifies every reported avoider by brute force from the stored
matrix rather than from a printed list, and all four reported
avoiders verify. The methodology point is recorded because the
mis-read would have inverted the verdict of 465.4.

NOT PROVED: D(3) in either currency (the t = 3 sweep exceeds memory
in its present form); finiteness of the progress constant at any t;
Theorem IV; (C), (D), (E); J7; (H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The sigma-paired problem is
no longer unattended and no longer four objects: it is one Gram
matrix and one congruence at two moduli, and in that form it answers
back. The pairing does exterminate the adversary 445.5 built to show
the abstract theory could not work - that much of the hope is
vindicated at k = 4. But the constant it was supposed to control
does not come down: sharp at 2^t for same-stratum, growing for
progress. Track A's one named problem has therefore split into a
solved half and a half that is asking for realizability, which is
the geometry the arithmetic was never going to reach.


## 466. THEOREM IV IS THE DIFFERENCE CRITERION

### 466.0 THE STRIDE

465 left Theorem IV's progress currency growing and offered two
exits. This section takes neither: pushing the Gram encoding one
step further shows the progress currency is not a zero-sum constant
at all, and that the object it actually is has been sitting in the
archive since 457. Machine: tools/thm4_471.py, four parts.

### 466.1 THE CYCLE FORM (PROVED, VERIFIED)

465 carried the model on the ear lifts z_i. Substituting
z_i = C_i - x, with C_i the composite cycle of ear i and
p = #{sigma_i = +1}:

    V(sigma) = (1 - nu) x + SUM sigma_i z_i
             = (1 - p)  x + SUM sigma_i C_i .

The coefficient of the base is 1 - nu in the lift basis and 1 - p in
the cycle basis. The arc-switch involution is exactly the exchange
(C_i <-> Z_i, + <-> -) where Z_i = x - C_i, so

    EVERY EAR OFFERS A PAIR OF CYCLES SUMMING TO THE BASE:
                    C_i + Z_i = x .

That is the Arc-Switch Law (445.1) with the lattice bookkeeping
removed - a statement about two cycles of the graph, not about
shifts.

COMPUTED: the two forms of V agree on all 242 sign patterns for each
of Petersen, Moebius-Kantor, Heawood, Pappus and Desargues
(1210/1210), and C_i + Z_i = x on 25/25 ears.

### 466.2 THE OFFSET IS THE WHOLE ASYMMETRY, AND nu = 1 DELETES IT

The base contributes y_0^2 L to the composite, and since L = 2^t m
with m odd,

    y_0^2 L  ==  2^t . [ y_0 odd ]   (mod 2^{t+1}).

That single term is the ENTIRE difference between the two
currencies. Same-stratum is the congruence mod 2^t, where it
vanishes; progress is mod 2^{t+1}, where it does not. It is why
445.6 called Theorem IV the ASYMMETRIC theorem, and why 465.3 found
one currency sharp at 2^t and the other growing: the instances are
identical except that the base sits at a nonzero residue.

  But y_0 = 1 - nu is ZERO at nu = 1. At exactly one flip the base
  leaves the expression entirely (the Odd-Flip Lemma, 465.1), and
  the progress target becomes

        | SUM sigma_i z_i |^2  ==  0   (mod 2^{t+1}) ,

  symmetric and offset-free. The asymmetry is not intrinsic to the
  problem; it is an artifact of selecting an even number of flips.

### 466.3 AT TWO ELEMENTS IT IS 457.4 (PROVED, VERIFIED)

Take nu = 1 and |S| = 2, so sigma = (+1, -1) and p = 1. Then

    V = z_i - z_j = C_i - C_j = Z_j - Z_i ,

the composite is C_i Delta C_j, and the progress target reads

    |C_i| + |C_j| - 2 |C_i cap C_j|  ==  0   (mod 2^{t+1}) .

  THAT IS THE DIFFERENCE CRITERION OF 457.4, at the composite scale
  instead of at the girth. 457.4 states it for the target 2^k
  exactly; here the target is divisibility by 2^{t+1}, which is
  weaker, on the same object.

COMPUTED: V = C_i - C_j = Z_j - Z_i on 20/20 ordered pairs for each
of the five graphs, and |V|^2 equals the difference formula 100/100.

### 466.4 WHY THE ABSTRACT ROUTE PROVABLY CANNOT DELIVER IT

At nu = 1, |S| = 2 the target is l_i + l_j - 2 g_ij == 0 mod
2^{t+1}. In the abstract model g_ij is FREE mod 2^t, so 2 g_ij runs
over every even residue mod 2^{t+1} and the adversary need only
dodge one value.

  THEOREM. The pairwise sigma-paired constant is INFINITE in the
  abstract model, at every t and every k. Explicit avoider: take
  every l_i odd and set g_ij = (l_i + l_j)/2 + 1 mod 2^t.
  COMPUTED: valid at t = 1, 2, 3 and k = 4, 8, 16, 32, 12/12.

  This sharpens 465.4. There the progress constant was recorded as
  "not supported" on the evidence of a k = 9 avoider; here the
  relevant sub-problem is shown unbounded outright. Theorem IV, as
  posed in 445.6, is NOT a zero-sum constant and no Davenport-type
  theorem will produce it.

  What is missing is precisely what the abstract model throws away:
  g_ij = <z_i, z_j> is the OVERLAP OF TWO CYCLES, not a free
  parameter. Its admissible range is geometry - 462.5's Chord Band
  Lemma is exactly a bound on where an overlap can sit.

### 466.5 THE COLLAPSE: ONE FRONTIER, NOT TWO

462.4 collapsed the two frames inside Track B: the closure work of
457-460 is the a = 1 layer of the counting work of 452-456. This
section collapses the tracks into each other.

  TRACK A's Theorem IV - the load-bearing statement of 445.6, on
  which II and V were said to lean, and which 464.3 identified as
  the single constant (C), (D), (E) reduce to -

  IS TRACK B's DIFFERENCE CRITERION - 457.4, the general form that
  survived Nauru, whose control at scales above the girth 457.5
  recorded as the open problem.

They were reached from opposite ends: Track A by six sections of
zero-sum theory over Z/2^t, Track B by the Girth-Pair Theorem and
the trace frame. They are the same statement about the same object -
the symmetric difference of two cycles meeting in a path.

  CONSEQUENCE. The choice between the tracks that 464 framed is not
  a real choice. There is one frontier, it is the difference
  closure, and both routes to it are now instrumented: 462's
  attachment decomposition weighs it by overlap length, and 466.3
  places it at nu = 1 in the composite calculus.

### 466.6 STATUS

PROVED here: the cycle form V = (1-p)x + SUM sigma_i C_i and the
