pairing law C_i + Z_i = x; that y_0^2 L == 2^t [y_0 odd] is the sole
source of the two currencies' asymmetry and that nu = 1 deletes it;
that at nu = 1, |S| = 2 the composite is C_i Delta C_j, so the
progress target is 457.4's Difference Criterion mod 2^{t+1}; that
the pairwise abstract constant is infinite at every t and k.

COMPUTED: the cycle form 1210/1210 on five graphs; C_i + Z_i = x
25/25; the nu = 1 identification 100/100 pairs; the abstract
avoider valid 12/12 across t = 1,2,3 and k = 4..32.

NOT PROVED: the Difference Criterion at scales above the girth -
which is now known to be Theorem IV as well, so it carries (C), (D),
(E) with it. J7; (H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Theorem IV does have a
nicer form, and the nicer form is that it is not its own theorem.
The asymmetry that made it hard is a single term y_0^2 L that
vanishes as soon as exactly one ear is flipped; with it gone the
progress currency is a symmetric question about signed sums of ear
lifts, and at two elements that question IS the difference of two
cycles meeting in a path. No zero-sum constant can settle it - the
couplings are free abstractly and the pairwise constant is
unbounded - because the content was never arithmetic. Six sections
of Track A and nine of Track B have converged on one object, and
the archive should stop maintaining two frontiers for it.


## 467. THE SOAK: THE NUT DOES NOT SPLIT, AND THE RACE IS NAMED

### 467.0 THE QUESTION

466 collapsed both tracks onto one object - the difference of two
cycles meeting in a path. If the archive's whole accumulation is now
pointed at a single nut, does it open? This section soaks it and
reports what happens. It does not open. What the soak produces
instead is the first quantitative account of WHY, with every term
named. Machine: tools/soak472.py.

### 467.1 THE DIMENSION-COLLAPSE HOPE, REFUTED (COMPUTED)

466.4 blamed the unbounded abstract constant on the couplings being
free. Geometrically they are not free: ears on the base cycle have
disjoint interiors (432.4), so two ears meet only along x and

    Z_i cap Z_j = A_i cap A_j ,  an INTERVAL OVERLAP,
    |Z_i D Z_j| = l_i + l_j - 2 |A_i cap A_j| .

The adversary therefore holds 3k numbers - two feet and one path
length per ear - against k(k-1)/2 pairwise conditions. Quadratic
against linear: the system looked massively over-determined, and
that was the hope.

  IT IS NOT OVER-DETERMINED, BECAUSE THE CONDITIONS ARE CONGRUENCES.
  Each kill removes only a 2^{-(t+1)} fraction of the space, so the
  right accounting is entropy, not rank.

  COMPUTED. Largest avoiding family found, greedy with restarts:

    L    t   m   ear options   max avoider   = L/2 ?
    12   2   3         1164          6         yes
    20   2   5         5700         10         yes
    28   2   7        16044         14         yes
    24   3   3        11352         12         yes
    40   3   5        53960         20         yes

  The avoider saturates the DISTINCT-FEET CEILING L/2 in every case:
  the arithmetic does not bind at all. And the escape is not
  degenerate. At L = 24, t = 3 the winning 12-ear family has 21
  disjoint-arc pairs, 3 two-piece pairs and FORTY-TWO genuine
  single-path pairs - 42 real difference cycles, every one dodging
  0 mod 16. At L = 40 it is 125 single-path pairs, all dodged.

  Imposing 449.1's strict local minimality (d > L/2 on every ear,
  proved unconditionally for the residual world) does NOT shrink the
  avoider - it stays at L/2, merely converting disjoint pairs into
  single-path ones (21 -> 8 disjoint, 42 -> 50 single-path at
  L = 24).

### 467.2 THE RACE, NAMED (HEURISTIC, LABELLED AS SUCH)

First-moment accounting for the pairwise level. The adversary has
~L^{3k} configurations; each of the ~k^2/2 pairwise kills removes a
2^{-(t+1)} fraction. Avoiders survive while

    3k ln L  >  (k^2/2) 2^{-(t+1)} ,   i.e.   k  <  c . 2^t ln L .

Against that threshold the archive's supply is 432.4's L/3, i.e.
2^t m / 3. The two cross when

    m  ~  c' . ln L .

  436.4 has ALREADY cornered the adversary at m in {3, 5}. So the
  pairwise race is lost precisely in the strata that survive - not
  by a little, and not for want of a better argument. At L = 24,
  t = 3 the threshold is in the hundreds and the supply is 8.

  This is the sharpest statement the archive has about why the
  difference criterion resists: it is not a missing lemma, it is a
  supply shortfall of a factor ln L, in exactly the corner 436.4
  drove the adversary into.

### 467.3 WHAT WOULD TURN IT

The same accounting at selection order 3 - triples rather than
pairs, which the sigma-model supplies for free since sigma ranges
over all of {-1,0,1}^k - replaces k^2/2 conditions by ~k^3/6 and
gives

    k  <  c . 2^{(t+1)/2} sqrt(ln L) ,

so supply beats threshold once  m  >  c' . 2^{-(t-1)/2} sqrt(ln L).
The right-hand side FALLS with t. At t = 3 it still exceeds 5; by
t = 7 it is below 5. So the race turns as t grows, and m in {3,5}
survives only for finitely many strata - which is exactly the job
the boards of 440 and 442 already do at t = 3.

  That is a concrete programme and a concrete prediction, and it is
  the first time uniformity in t (Theorem V, 451.2(E)) has had a
  mechanism attached rather than a hope. It is also HEURISTIC: first
  moments do not prove existence of a kill, and the constants are
  not computed. Recorded as a direction, not a result.

### 467.4 VERDICT

  THE NUT DOES NOT SPLIT.

The soak was still worth taking, because the frontier has changed
character again. Before 466 the archive maintained two frontiers and
did not know they were one. After 466 it knew, but the shared object
was still a qualitative statement. After 467 it is a race between
two named quantities - supply 2^t m/3 against a congruence-dodging
threshold that depends on the selection order - and the loss is
localised to small m, where 436.4 had independently already put the
adversary.

  What the soak rules out: the pairwise difference criterion, alone,
  at any t. 42 genuine single-path pairs dodged at L = 24 is not a
  search that needs more compute.

  What it leaves: higher-order selections, where the count of
  conditions grows faster than the adversary's freedom, and where
  the crossing point moves the right way in t.

### 467.5 STATUS

COMPUTED: the interval model; avoider size = L/2 (the distinct-feet
ceiling) at (L,t) = (12,2), (20,2), (28,2), (24,3), (40,3); the
escape mechanism broken down into disjoint, two-piece and
single-path pairs, with 42 and 125 genuine single-path pairs dodged
at L = 24 and L = 40; strict local minimality imposed and shown not
to shrink the avoider.

HEURISTIC (labelled): the pairwise threshold c . 2^t ln L and the
order-3 threshold c . 2^{(t+1)/2} sqrt(ln L); the crossing
conditions on m; the prediction that the race turns with t.

NOT PROVED: any kill. The Difference Criterion above the girth;
Theorem IV; (C), (D), (E); J7; (H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. Soaking the collapsed
frontier does not open it. The pairwise level of the difference
criterion is now closed off by measurement rather than by intuition:
the adversary saturates the trivial distinct-feet bound, keeps
dozens of genuine single-path pairs, and dodges every one, and
449.1's minimality does not disturb him. The reason is that kills
are congruences and congruences are cheap to dodge - the accounting
is entropy against supply, and at m in {3,5} the supply is short by
a logarithm. That is a race, it has two named sides, and the side
the archive is on improves with selection order and with t. The nut
is wet, not open.


## 468. THE BLITZ PLAN: CONSTRAIN, ENCODE, EXHAUST - AUDITED

### 468.0 THE DIRECTIVE

Drive the residual space down until it is tiny, then encode it so
the whole of it can be swept in minutes. This section audits both
halves against measurement rather than hope, and reports which one
is actually the bottleneck. Machine: tools/blitz473.py.

### 468.1 WHAT THE BANKED CONSTRAINTS ACTUALLY BUY (COMPUTED)

Per-ear admissible types at each stratum, applying the constraints
in the order the archive proved them. An ear is (foot u, arc length
a, interior length d), with d taken mod 2^{t+1}:

    L    t   m      raw   +shallow  +both-arc  +girth 5
   24    3   3      368       325        311       241
   40    3   5      624       551        537       467
   48    4   3     1504      1413       1383      1233
   80    4   5     2528      2375       2345      2195
   96    5   3     6080      5893       5831      5521

  THE WHOLE BANKED APPARATUS REMOVES 35 PER CENT. Island shallowness
  (446.1) costs the adversary 12%, strict local minimality on both
  arcs (449.1) another 4%, girth 5 another 22%. Nothing else in the
  ledger touches a single ear at all.

  This is 467.1 for the third time and it should now be treated as a
  law of the archive: CONSTRAINTS THAT ARE CONGRUENCES REMOVE A
  2^{-t} SLIVER, AND THE ARCHIVE'S CONSTRAINTS ARE CONGRUENCES. No
  further arithmetic will make this space small. The per-ear count
  stays at ~2 L^2 / m however much more of the same is proved.

### 468.2 THE ENCODING IS SOUND AND IS NOT THE BOTTLENECK

For every stratum that matters - t <= 5, m in {3,5} - the base cycle
has L <= 96, and for t <= 4 it has L <= 80. So the ARC OF AN EAR IS
ONE MACHINE WORD: bit e set iff edge e of x lies in the arc. Then
for any signed selection sigma,

    arc part  =  XOR of the chosen arc masks
    length    =  popcount(XOR) + SUM_{i in S} d_i
    kill      =  length == 0  (mod 2^{t+1})
    is a cycle=  runs(XOR) == |S|, alternation closes up

and the arc-switch sign of 465 is just "mask or its complement".
This is 465's Gram matrix stored as bits - popcount(XOR) IS |V|^2
for a +-1 circulation - and every operation is a word op.

  MEASURED (pure Python, L = 24, t = 3): 87 396 selections/s at
  k = 8, 76 023/s at k = 10. Gray-coding the ternary sweep removes
  the inner loop, and meet-in-the-middle replaces 3^k by 3^{k/2},
  which is 6561 at k = 16 and 1.6e6 at k = 26.

  So a single family is decided in microseconds, and will be decided
  in nanoseconds once the sweep is written properly.

### 468.3 THE BOTTLENECK IS THE FAMILY COUNT, AND ENUMERATION IS THE
### WRONG FRAME

With ~L . (per-ear count) / 2 ear types and k = L/3 ears per family,
the number of families is beyond 10^20 at every stratum, including
t = 3, m = 3. No encoding closes that gap; 35 per cent off the
per-ear count moves nothing.

  AND ENUMERATION IS NOT WHAT IS WANTED. 467 already established
  that avoiders EXIST at the pairwise level, of size L/2 against a
  supply of L/3. There is nothing to exhaust there: the answer is
  known and it is "the adversary survives". The exhaustive frame
  only pays where the answer is UNSAT, which is what 440 and 442
  achieved at t = 3, m = 3 - by SEARCH WITH PROPAGATION, not by
  enumeration. The tree is small even when the space is not.

  So the blitz plan is right in shape and misdirected in target. The
  thing to blitz is not the configuration space; it is the BOARDS -
  the finite constraint systems of 438-442 - and the blocker there
  is recorded in the archive's own assault state: the t = 4 one-extra
  board, L = 48, 25 ears, 57785 constraints, generated in 224 s and
  left mid-solve.

### 468.4 THE DIAGNOSIS

  57785 constraints is a SMALL instance. Modern CDCL solvers dispose
  of structured instances two orders of magnitude larger routinely.
  The t = 4 board did not stall because the mathematics is hard
  there; it stalled because it was handed to a hand-rolled
  forward-checking engine written in Python.

  THE HIGHEST-VALUE MOVE AVAILABLE IS THEREFORE INFRASTRUCTURAL, NOT
  MATHEMATICAL: re-encode the boards of 438-442 as CNF and give them
  to a real solver. The bit-parallel arc encoding of 468.2 is the
  natural front end - each kill condition is a popcount congruence on
  an XOR of masks, which linearises into cardinality constraints over
  the ear-selection variables.

  If that lands, (E) - uniformity in t, 451.2's fifth statement -
  becomes a compute question at t = 4, 5, 6 rather than an open
  problem, and 467.3's estimate says the counting race turns on its
  own by about t = 7. Finitely many strata between the two, which is
  exactly the shape 451.3 said any continuation must have.

### 468.5 STATUS

COMPUTED: per-ear admissible counts at five strata, before and after
each banked constraint - 35% total reduction; the bit-parallel arc
encoding, benchmarked at 76-87 thousand selections/s in pure Python;
family counts beyond 10^20 at every stratum.

PROVED (as an accounting, not a theorem): that congruence
constraints cannot shrink the per-ear space below ~2L^2/m, so the
"constrain until tiny" half of the plan cannot be completed with the
tools the archive has.

NOT PROVED: anything new about J7. (A)-(E); Theorem IV; the
Difference Criterion above the girth; J7; (H1*); the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The plan survives the audit
with one correction: the space cannot be made tiny, and it does not
need to be. Every constraint the archive owns is a congruence, and
congruences take 35 per cent, not orders of magnitude - so
enumeration of configurations is out of reach at every stratum and
will stay out of reach. But the boards of 438-442 were never
enumerations; they were propagating searches, and they are small.
The bit-parallel encoding built here is the right front end for
them, and the recorded blocker at t = 4 is 57785 constraints handed
to the wrong engine. Close that and uniformity in t stops being a
theorem to prove and becomes a job to run.


### 468.6 ADDENDUM: THE SOLVER IS IN, AND THE CLAIM IS QUALIFIED

RESOLVED. The note in 468.4 that no solver was present is superseded.
`pip install python-sat` fails on this machine - it builds CaDiCaL

    pip install --only-binary :all: python-sat

fetches a prebuilt wheel and works. Six CDCL solvers are now

CORRECTED (374.1), THE FIRST BENCHMARK WAS VACUOUS. Timing random

0.00-4.77 s, and that measures nothing: those clause-to-variable
ratios are 58 to 193, far above the 3-SAT threshold of 4.27, so the
instances are massively over-constrained and refute instantly. It
was recorded as a scale check and it is not one.

THE HONEST REACH TEST, random 3-SAT AT the threshold ratio 4.27 -
the hardest known regime, hence a LOWER bound on structured
performance:

      vars   clauses   result      time
       100       426    UNSAT      0.02 s
       200       853      SAT      0.62 s
       300      1280    UNSAT     96.43 s

So CaDiCaL is not magic: at the threshold it stalls by 300
variables. 468.4's sentence "57785 constraints is a SMALL instance"
therefore stands only for STRUCTURED instances, and is asserted, not

WHAT IS NOW UNBLOCKED: the boards of 438-442 can be re-encoded as

## 469. J7 STRIPPED: DESCENT ON THE ODD PART

### 469.0 THE STRIDE

Everything built since 452 set aside; the question is what J7 says
when nothing is assumed but the statement itself, and what the
shortest route to it looks like. The answer is a one-line
reformulation and a descent that 447.3 does not forbid.
Machine: tools/simple474.py.

### 469.1 WHERE THE HYPOTHESIS ACTUALLY ENTERS (PROVED)

G cubic, no cycle length a power of two. Put
t = max{ v_2(|C|) : C a cycle of G }, and let C be a shortest cycle
with v_2(|C|) = t, so |C| = 2^t m with m odd. Then:

  * the SPECTRUM CAP (every cycle has v_2 <= t) is free - it is the
    definition of t, not a hypothesis;
  * ISLAND SHALLOWNESS is free - an ear of shift valuation exactly t
    would produce a cycle of valuation t+1, contradicting the cap;
  * m = 1 would make |C| = 2^t, a power of two. So m >= 3, AND THAT
    IS THE ONLY PLACE THE COUNTEREXAMPLE HYPOTHESIS IS USED.

Hence, with 446.1's island form stripped of everything derivable:

  J7.  There is no cubic graph in which no cycle length is a power
       of two and some cycle length is divisible by 8.

  (J7')  If a cubic graph has a cycle of length divisible by 8, then
         it has a cycle whose length is a power of two.

No islands, no shifts, no shallowness, no lattice, no braiding. The
2 sqrt(n) bound of 446.1 is not part of the statement either; it is
191's reduction, available but not needed to state it.

### 469.2 THE DESCENT, AND WHY 447.3 DOES NOT FORBID IT

The natural induction for (J7') is on the ODD PART, not on t.

  (DESC)  In a cubic graph, the SHORTEST cycle whose length is
          divisible by 2^t is itself a power of two.

  (DESC) => (J7') at once: take t = 3.

  (STEP)  In a cubic graph, if there is a cycle of length 2^t m with
          t >= 3 and m odd >= 3, there is a STRICTLY SHORTER cycle
          whose length is divisible by 2^t.

  (STEP) => (DESC): let C be shortest with 2^t | |C| and write
  |C| = 2^t q. If q is even then 2^{t+1} | |C| and C is also shortest
  for t+1, so recurse upward - the recursion terminates since
  lengths are bounded. So q = m is odd. If m = 1, |C| = 2^t and we
  are done. If m >= 3, (STEP) contradicts minimality. QED

  THE POINT. The induction parameter is m, which STRICTLY DECREASES,
  while t STAYS FIXED throughout. 447.3's Scale-Invariance Theorem
  forbids induction on t - "the problem has no smaller instance, so
  uniformity must be proved directly, never by descent" - and it
  says nothing about m. So this route sidesteps 451.2(E), uniformity
  in t, ENTIRELY: t is a spectator.

  That is the first route in the archive with that property.

### 469.3 TESTED (COMPUTED)

(DESC), 29 cubic graphs - cages, generalized Petersen, truncations,
Moebius ladders, prisms, dodecahedron, random at girth 3 and 5:

    HOLDS 29/29 at t = 3, 4, 5.

  The sharp row is the TRUNCATED PETERSEN, which is 452.6's
  counterexample to the archive's weak form: it has girth 3, no
  4-cycle and no 8-cycle, so its least multiple of 8 is 16 - and 16
  is a power of two. (DESC) survives precisely where the weak form
  died.

(STEP), tested on every length in every spectrum:

    HOLDS 9/9 instances.

  HONEST LIMIT, recorded per 374.1: all nine instances are the same
  one, (l, t) = (24, 3). With n <= 30 the only length satisfying
  v_2(l) = t >= 3 and l/2^t >= 3 is 24; the next is 40, needing
  n >= 40 and cycle enumeration to length 40. So (STEP) has been
  confirmed at one point, not swept. The (DESC) table is the broader
  evidence.

### 469.4 WHAT (STEP) IS, IN THE ARCHIVE'S OWN TERMS

(STEP) asks for a shorter cycle of length divisible by 2^t. That is
exactly 465.4(a)'s SAME-STRATUM-PLUS-SHORTNESS kill, and the archive
already knows both halves separately:

  * the congruence half - forcing a composite of length == 0 mod 2^t
    - has constant EXACTLY 2^t, proved sharp at t = 1, 2 in 465.3
    and reproducing 445.3 independently;
  * the shortness half is a length inequality, and 449-450 are a
    battery of length inequalities (d > L/2 on both arcs; the
    cross-edge window; the tight diameter world empty).

So the two halves of (STEP) are the two halves the archive has, and
what has never been done is to run them together. 465.4 offered
"re-pose on the same-stratum currency" as exit (a) and did not take
it; 469 says that exit is not merely available but is the whole of
the simplest route.

### 469.5 STATUS

PROVED here: the reformulation J7 <=> (J7'), with the counterexample
hypothesis isolated to the single inference m >= 3; the implications
(STEP) => (DESC) => (J7') => J7, including the upward recursion that
disposes of the even-quotient case.

COMPUTED: (DESC) on 29 cubic graphs at t = 3, 4, 5, holding
everywhere, including the truncated Petersen where the least
multiple of 8 is 16; (STEP) on all 9 available instances.

NOT PROVED: (STEP), at any t. Hence (DESC), (J7'), J7, (H1*), the
conjecture. And the (STEP) evidence is one instance repeated, not a
sweep - the honest strength of the test is the (DESC) table.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. But J7 is now one sentence
with no machinery in it, the counterexample hypothesis has been
traced to a single inference, and there is a descent that reaches it
whose induction parameter is the odd part rather than the level - so
uniformity in t, which 451.2 listed as the fifth open statement and
464.3 made load-bearing, is simply not on the path. What remains is
one step: a cycle of length 2^t m with m odd at least 3 must have a
shorter companion divisible by 2^t. Its congruence half is a sharp
constant the archive has measured; its shortness half is the kind of
inequality 449 and 450 exist to supply. They have never been run
together, and that is now the whole of the job.


## 470. THE ODD PART AS THE TRANSVERSE COORDINATE

469 proposed a descent whose induction parameter is the odd part m
rather than the level t. This section keeps the coordinate and
discards the descent. The coordinate is right, and 470.0-470.3 make
it permanent structure. The descent is WRONG: 470.4 exhibits three
explicit cubic graphs refuting it, including one that refutes it at
t = 3, the level J7 needs. 470.5 turns that refutation into a no-go
of the same kind as 447.3.

### 470.0 THE FIBRE PICTURE: WHY t CANNOT AND m CAN

STATUS: PROVED. This is 447.3 explained rather than restated.

Write every length uniquely as

        l  =  2^t . m ,     m odd .

447.3's halving map H : l |-> l/2 is, in these coordinates,

        H : (t, m)  |->  (t - 1, m) .

It MOVES t and FIXES m. Its orbits are the sets {m . 2^s : s >= 0},
one per odd m, so the odd part is exactly the invariant of the
halving action, and

        THE TARGET SET  P = {2^k}  IS THE FIBRE  m = 1 .

That single sentence contains 447.3. Membership in P is the
condition m = 1; halving never changes m; therefore no motion along
the halving direction can ever bring a length closer to the target.
An induction on t is an induction ALONG the orbits of a symmetry
that preserves the target fibre setwise - it is not merely circular,
it is transverse to nothing. The odd part m is the unique coordinate
on the quotient, hence the only induction parameter that can see P
at all.

Two consequences follow at once.

  (i)  447.3 is not a no-go against induction as such. It is a
       SELECTION PRINCIPLE: it names m as the only admissible
       induction parameter and rules out every other.

  (ii) 447.4's integrality obstruction never fires on an m-descent.
       That obstruction says the t = 2 machinery needs the shift set
       to be Z, and that halving pushes shifts into (1/2^j)Z. An
       m-descent holds t FIXED, hence holds the modulus 2^{t+1} and
       the shift lattice Z fixed. Nothing is halved, so nothing
       leaves the integers.

The correct object attached to a graph is therefore the image of its
cycle spectrum under the odd-part map,

        M(G)  =  { odd part of l  :  l in Spec(G) } ,

and Erdos-Gyarfas reads

        min degree >= 3   ==>   1 in M(G) .

M(G) is precisely the halving-invariant of the spectrum: it is what
survives 447.3's symmetry, and it is the coarsest invariant that
still determines whether the conjecture holds. Any statement about
the spectrum that is not a statement about M(G) is either strictly
stronger than the conjecture or blind to it.

### 470.1 THE DESCENT QUANTUM IN (t, m) COORDINATES

STATUS: PROVED. Elementary, and it is the whole arithmetic of the
frame.

Let C be a cycle of length L = 2^t q in a cubic graph, and let an ear
have feet on C at arc-distance a (so the two arcs have lengths a and
L - a) with interior path length d. The two cycles through the ear
have lengths a + d and (L - a) + d. Exchanging the a-arc for the ear
gives the cycle of length L - a + d. Then:

  (a) IN-STRATUM.  2^t divides L - a + d  iff  d == a (mod 2^t).
  (b) STRICTLY SHORTER.  L - a + d < L  iff  d < a.
  (c) THE QUANTUM.  Under (a) and (b) the new cycle has
          q'  =  q  -  (a - d) / 2^t ,
      so q drops by the positive integer (a - d)/2^t.
  (d) VALUATION-PRESERVING.  If q is odd, q' is odd - the new cycle
      has valuation exactly t - iff (a - d)/2^t is even, that is iff
          d == a  (mod 2^{t+1}) ,
      and then the drop in q is EVEN, hence at least 2.

(d) is where the archive's modulus enters. The whole mod-2^{t+1}
calculus of 465.3 and 445.3 is exactly the condition that a descent
step stay inside the valuation-t stratum rather than fall into a
deeper one. The archive has been computing the descent quantum for
sections without naming it as such.

### 470.2 THE BASE-CASE COLLAPSE AT m = 3

STATUS: PROVED.

CLAIM. For every t >= 0 the multiples of 2^t strictly below 3 . 2^t
are exactly 2^t and 2 . 2^t, and both are powers of two.

Immediate: the multiples in question are j . 2^t for j = 1, 2.

CONSEQUENCE (the collapse). At q = 3 the descent target set IS the
goal set. Any cycle strictly shorter than 3 . 2^t and divisible by
2^t has length 2^t or 2^{t+1} - already a power of two. So at m = 3,

        "descend one step"   and   "win outright"

are the SAME event. At q = 5, by contrast, the admissible landing
sites are 2^t, 2 . 2^t, 3 . 2^t and 4 . 2^t, and 3 . 2^t is not a
power of two: descending is strictly weaker than winning.

So the induction on m is easy above the base and equivalent to the
whole problem at the base. That is a prediction about difficulty,
and it matches 451.2 exactly: (D), the m = 5 case, is recorded there
as an argument that is merely "unwritten" - a STEP; (C), the m = 3
case, is recorded as "provably immune to the zigzag battery", the
one item "known to require a new idea" - a BASE. The m-frame
explains the shape of the archive's own ledger.

### 470.3 THE BASE CASE IS UNIVERSAL IN THE HARD WORLD

STATUS: PROVED.

Let G be cubic with no power-of-two cycle, and let t be a level whose
stratum is non-empty. The two multiples of 2^t below 3 . 2^t are
2^t and 2^{t+1}, both powers of two, both absent by hypothesis.
Hence

        q_t  :=  min { l / 2^t  :  l in Spec(G),  2^t | l }   >=  3

for EVERY such t simultaneously. The counterexample world sits at or
above the base case at every level at once, and the only terminus an
m-descent can have is q = 3.

This is why the frame cannot remove anything from 451.2 on its own.
Choosing the shallow cycle minimal in its stratum gives m = m_t, the
least odd part present, and 470.3 gives only m_t >= 3, not m_t = 3:
the length 3 . 2^t need not occur. The reduction of (D) to (C) is
therefore exactly the descent step - and 470.4 shows that step is
false.

### 470.4 THE ROUTE IS DEAD: THREE EXPLICIT REFUTATIONS

STATUS: COMPUTED, and re-verified from stored adjacency by a second
algorithm.

Recall the two statements of 469:

  (STEP)  a cycle of length 2^t m, m odd >= 3, has a strictly
          shorter companion of length divisible by 2^t;
  (DESC)  the shortest cycle divisible by 2^t is a power of two.

(i) t = 1. The truncated Petersen graph, n = 30. Exact per-length
tests: no cycle of length 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9; cycles of length 3 and
10 exist. So the shortest even cycle has length 10 = 2 . 5, giving
q_1 = 5 with NO shorter even cycle. (STEP) and (DESC) both fail.

(ii) t = 2. Same graph. Its multiples of 8 are {16, 24} and it has
no 4-cycle and no 8-cycle, so the shortest multiple of 4 is 12 =
4 . 3, giving q_2 = 3. (DESC) fails.

(iii) t = 3 - THE LEVEL J7 NEEDS. An explicit cubic graph on 24
vertices, found by two-edge-swap search on #C8 + #C16 with a
24-cycle pinned as a hard constraint:

  adj = [[2,3,22],[5,17,21],[0,12,18],[0,20,22],[7,10,21],[1,11,14],
         [9,12,18],[4,10,21],[10,15,23],[6,14,17],[4,7,8],[5,16,19],
         [2,6,18],[14,17,20],[5,9,13],[8,16,23],[11,15,19],[1,9,13],
         [2,6,12],[11,16,23],[3,13,22],[1,4,7],[0,3,20],[8,15,19]]

Re-verified independently by exhaustive cycle enumeration (a
different algorithm from the per-length existence test that produced
it): 3-regular, simple, connected, 1202 simple cycles, complete
spectrum

  {3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24}.

Its cycle lengths divisible by 8 are EXACTLY {24}. So q_3 = 3, the
shortest multiple of 8 is 24, and the 24-cycle has no strictly
shorter companion divisible by 8. (DESC) is false at t = 3 and
(STEP) is false at t = 3, m = 3.

Erdos-Gyarfas is NOT refuted: the spectrum contains 4. The witness
escapes by paying in a DIFFERENT stratum from the one being
descended.

CORRECTED (374.1). 469.4 reported "(DESC) holds 29/29" and treated
it as the evidential basis of the route. That table is VACUOUS. In
every one of its 29 rows q_t was 1 or 2 - the graph carried the
power of two 2^t or 2^{t+1} at the very bottom of the stratum, so
(DESC) held there for the trivial reason that the required power of
two was sitting exactly where it was needed. Not one row tested the
regime q_t >= 3 that 470.3 shows a counterexample is FORCED into.
The first configuration ever constructed that does sit at q_3 = 3
refutes the statement. The measured 29/29 was a measurement of
nothing, and the sharpest row of that table - truncated Petersen at
t = 3, praised in 469.4 for surviving where 452.6's weak form died -
is the very graph that refutes (DESC) at t = 1 and t = 2.

469's implication chain (STEP) ==> (DESC) ==> (J7') ==> J7 remains
valid as an implication. Its hypothesis is now known false. It is
not a route, and 469.5's closing claim that "what remains is one
step" is WITHDRAWN.

### 470.5 THE STRATUM-LOCALITY NO-GO

STATUS: PROVED. This is the section's positive yield, and it is an
obstruction of the same kind as 447.3.

Let G* be the 24-vertex graph of 470.4(iii). Its set of cycle
lengths divisible by 8 is {24}. Now ask what the t = 3 data of a
genuine counterexample would have to look like. If G were cubic with
no power-of-two cycle and with maximal valuation t = 3, its
8-divisible cycle lengths would be multiples of 8 with valuation
exactly 3, that is lengths == 8 (mod 16), none of them a power of
two. The set {24} is such a set: 24 == 8 (mod 16) and 24 is not a
power of two.

  THE NO-GO. The level-3 stratum data of a putative counterexample
  is REALISABLE in an actual cubic graph. Hence no theorem of the
  form "a cubic graph whose 8-divisible cycle lengths avoid the
  powers of two has property X" can produce a contradiction: G*
  satisfies the hypothesis. Any proof of J7 must use the
  no-power-of-two hypothesis at some level BELOW t, not only at t
  and above.

This is why the descent failed, and it is a sharper statement than
"the descent failed". The descent is stratum-local by construction:
it looks only at multiples of 2^t. 470.0 says the target is the
fibre m = 1, and the fibre meets the spectrum at some level nobody
gets to choose - in G*, at t = 2, via the 4-cycle - while the
descent is running its column at t = 3. A single-column argument
cannot see it.

Restated in the frame of 470.0: EG is a statement about M(G), and
the 8-stratum determines only the part of M(G) coming from lengths
of valuation >= 3. G* has 8-stratum {24}, so that part of its M is
{3} - no 1 anywhere - and yet 1 in M(G*) because 4 contributes it.
M(G*) = {1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 19, 21, 23}, and the 1 comes
from valuation 2.

  THE DEMAND. What must be supplied is a mechanism COUPLING levels:
  a reason why emptiness of the fibre m = 1 at low levels forces
  something at high levels, or conversely. 447.5's 2-group
  asymmetry, which lifts a cycle of Gbar to cycles of length
  2^k . |Cbar| - a pure motion along a halving orbit, m fixed - is
  the only instrument in the archive that moves between levels while
  controlling m, and it needs a free 2-group action to run.

### 470.6 WHAT SURVIVES, AND WHAT THE LEDGER NOW SAYS

PROVED in this section: the fibre picture and the selection
principle (470.0); the descent quantum, including the identification
of the archive's modulus 2^{t+1} as the valuation-preserving
condition (470.1); the base-case collapse at m = 3 (470.2); the
universality of the base case in the counterexample world (470.3);
the stratum-locality no-go (470.5).

COMPUTED: three refutations of 469's descent, one at each of
t = 1, 2, 3, with the t = 3 witness re-verified by exhaustive
enumeration.

CORRECTED (374.1): 469.4's 29/29 table is vacuous; 469.5's claim
that one step remained is withdrawn.

NOT PROVED: J7; (A), (B), (C), (D), (E) of 451.2 - the m-frame
explains the shape of that ledger but removes no item from it, since
the reduction of (D) to (C) was exactly the false descent step; the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. J7 is unchanged and the
451.2 ledger is unchanged. What changed is that the odd part is now
established as the only admissible induction coordinate, with the
target set identified as one of its fibres; that the archive's
mod-2^{t+1} arithmetic is identified as the condition for a descent
step to stay in its stratum; and that stratum-local arguments are
now provably dead, by an explicit 24-vertex graph realising the
level-3 data of a counterexample. The frontier moves from "find the
descent step" to "find the coupling between levels".


## 471. LEVEL COUPLING: THE THETA VALUATION LEMMA

470.5 left the frontier at "couple two levels" and asked for a
theorem of the shape

  (CPL_t)  no power-of-two cycle at levels >= t  ==>  a power-of-two
           cycle at some level < t.

471.0 proves that EVERY instance of that schema is equivalent to the
conjecture, so it cannot be obtained as a weakening. 471.1 supplies
what can be obtained instead: an exact transport rule between
levels. 471.2-471.3 specialise it and say when it is silent. 471.4
measures how tightly the levels are in fact coupled.

### 471.0 THE SCHEMA COLLAPSES: EVERY (CPL_t) IS THE CONJECTURE

STATUS: PROVED. A one-line no-go, and it must be stated before any
work is done in this direction.

The cycle lengths that are powers of two are 2^k for k >= 2. For
t >= 2 write

  (CPL_t)  a cubic graph with no cycle of length 2^k for any k >= t
           has a cycle of length 2^j for some 2 <= j < t.

CLAIM. (CPL_t) is equivalent to Erdos-Gyarfas for cubic graphs, for
every t >= 2.

Proof. EG implies (CPL_t) trivially. Conversely let G be a cubic
counterexample to EG: G has NO power-of-two cycle at all. Then G
satisfies the hypothesis of (CPL_t) vacuously - it has no cycle of
length 2^k for k >= t because it has none for any k - and it fails
the conclusion, again because it has none. So (CPL_t) fails. QED

The counterexample satisfies every hypothesis in the family at once,
which is exactly why no member of the family is weaker than the
whole. In particular (CPL_3) - "no 8-, 16-, 32-, ... cycle implies a
4-cycle" - looks like a modest fragment and is the conjecture.

  CONSEQUENCE. Level coupling cannot be a LEMMA one proves and then
  applies. It can only be a MECHANISM operating inside a proof: a
  rule that transports information between levels, whose hypotheses
  are structural rather than "no power of two up there".

The rest of this section supplies such a rule.

### 471.1 THE THETA VALUATION LEMMA

STATUS: PROVED (hand proof below; machine-checked on all 1 771 561
triples in [1,120]^3, zero violations).

Let theta be a subgraph consisting of three internally disjoint u-v
paths of lengths p, q, r. Its three cycles have lengths

        A = p + q,   B = p + r,   C = q + r.

Put alpha = min(v_2 p, v_2 q, v_2 r) and let mu in {1,2,3} be the
number of paths attaining alpha. Then

        min(v_2 A, v_2 B, v_2 C)  =  alpha       if mu = 1 or 2,
                                  =  alpha + 1   if mu = 3.

Proof. mu = 1, say v_2 p = alpha < v_2 q, v_2 r. Then v_2(p+q) =
v_2(p+r) = alpha and v_2(q+r) > alpha; the minimum is alpha.
mu = 2, say v_2 p = v_2 q = alpha < v_2 r. Then v_2(p+r) = v_2(q+r)
= alpha while v_2(p+q) >= alpha + 1; the minimum is alpha.
mu = 3. Write p = 2^alpha p', q = 2^alpha q', r = 2^alpha r' with
p', q', r' odd. Each pairwise sum has an even cofactor, so v_2 of
each of A, B, C is at least alpha + 1. And A + B - C = 2p has
v_2 exactly alpha + 1; if all three of A, B, C had v_2 >= alpha + 2
then so would A + B - C. Hence the minimum is exactly alpha + 1. QED

This is an EQUALITY, not an estimate, and it is the transport rule:
the LEVELS of a theta's three cycles are determined by the
VALUATIONS of its three paths, and the paths are shared between
cycles sitting at different levels. That sharing is the coupling.

  LEVEL DESCENT (contrapositive form). If every cycle of a theta
  sits at level >= s, then every path of the theta has length
  divisible by 2^{s-1}. Equivalently: ONE path of low valuation
  drags one of the theta's cycles down to a low level.

The archive already had the parity shadow of this - "a theta's three
cycles sum to 2(a+b+c)", used at 3047 to force an even cycle. The
lemma above is the full 2-adic statement of which that is the s = 1
case.

### 471.2 THE EAR SPECIALISATION

STATUS: PROVED; machine-checked for L in {24, 40, 48, 96} and all
a, d < 200, zero violations.

Let C be a cycle of length L with v_2(L) = t, and let an ear have
feet at arc-distance a and interior length d. The theta is (a, L-a,
d) and its three cycles are C itself, a + d, and (L-a) + d.

If v_2(a) < t then v_2(L-a) = v_2(a) =: beta, so a and L-a already
share a valuation and

        min level  =  min(beta, v_2 d)   if v_2 d =/= beta,
                   =  beta + 1           if v_2 d  = beta.

Since the third cycle of the theta is C, at level t, WHENEVER THAT
MINIMUM IS LESS THAN t IT IS ATTAINED BY AN EAR CYCLE. So:

  COROLLARY (level descent along an ear). A cycle at level t
  carrying an ear whose arc-distance has valuation beta < t - 1
  forces a cycle at level exactly min(beta, v_2 d), or beta + 1 when
  those agree. In particular an ear of ODD arc-distance on any cycle
  forces a cycle at level 0 or level 1.

This is a genuine two-level inference with a purely structural
hypothesis, which is what 471.0 says is the only admissible kind.

### 471.3 WHEN THE COUPLING IS SILENT: 2-ADIC RIGIDITY

STATUS: PROVED, plus a measurement.

The corollary is silent only if every ear of C has arc-distance of
valuation >= s. Call C then s-RIGID. Since arc-distance is the
difference of foot positions, s-rigidity says every ear joins feet
CONGRUENT MOD 2^s; so no bridge of C has feet in two different
residue classes mod 2^s, and hence no component of G - V(C) does.

  RIGIDITY BOUND. Let G be cubic and 3-connected and C chordless, so
  432.4 applies: every C-vertex is an attachment and every bridge has
  r >= 3 attachments, giving b <= L/3 bridges. If C is s-rigid then
  each bridge lies in a single class mod 2^s, so every non-empty
  class needs its own bridge and
              2^s  <=  b  <=  L/3 .
  With L = 2^t m this is 2^s <= 2^t m / 3, so at m = 3 the ear system
  can be rigid only up to s <= t: rigidity cannot outrun the level
  of the cycle it sits on.

MEASURED (tools/couple479.py PART 2). For each graph in a zoo of
cages, generalized Petersen graphs and truncations, take a cycle at
the graph's maximal level and list v_2(arc-distance) over all its
ears:

  Petersen        |C|=8  t=3  16 ears   0:8  1:4  2:4
  Heawood         |C|=8  t=3  28 ears   0:16 1:8  2:4
  Moebius-Kantor  |C|=16 t=4  24 ears   0:24
  Pappus          |C|=16 t=4  28 ears   0:26 1:1  3:1
  Desargues       |C|=16 t=4  33 ears   0:24 1:4  2:2  3:3
  Dodecahedron    |C|=16 t=4  32 ears   0:26 1:4  2:2
  Nauru           |C|=16 t=4  58 ears   0:38 1:12 2:6  3:2
  McGee           |C|=16 t=4  53 ears   0:33 1:12 2:5  3:3
  trunc-cube      |C|=16 t=4  33 ears   0:23 1:8       3:2
  trunc-Petersen  |C|=16 t=4  45 ears   0:29 1:12 2:2  3:2

Valuation 0 occurs in every row - the coupling fires immediately on
every graph tested, and Moebius-Kantor is the extreme case in which
ALL 24 ears have odd arc-distance. No 1-rigid example was found.

### 471.4 THE AVOIDANCE LATTICE: THE COUPLING, MEASURED

STATUS: COMPUTED (tools/couple479.py PART 3, tools/couple480.py).

A power-of-two cycle at level s is the single length 2^s, by 470.2.
So ask directly which SETS of powers of two a cubic graph can avoid.
Two-edge-swap descent on the capped count, with restarts:

  subset      n=16   n=20   n=24   n=28
  {4}         yes    yes    yes    yes
  {8}         yes    yes    yes    yes
  {16}        yes    yes    yes    yes
  {4,8}       no(3)  no(2)  yes    yes
  {4,16}      yes    yes    yes    no(15)
  {8,16}      yes    yes    yes    yes
  {4,8,16}    no(3)  no(3)  no(3)  no(15)

  AT n = 24 EVERY TWO OF {4, 8, 16} CAN BE KILLED SIMULTANEOUSLY AND
  ALL THREE CANNOT. The levels are pairwise free and jointly
  constrained. That is the coupling in measured form.

Pushing the decisive row (couple480.py): minimising the total number
of power-of-two cycles gives, at n = 16, 20 and 24, a best value of
exactly 3 in every case, realised by a graph with NO 8-cycle, NO
16-cycle, and exactly THREE 4-cycles. The survivor is always the
LOWEST power of two, never the highest.

374.1 HONEST LIMITS, recorded because they bound what the table
means.
  (a) The objective caps each length's count at 30, so once a graph
      has 30 or more 16-cycles there is no gradient. The n = 28 and
      n = 30 rows plateau at exactly 30 with 313 and 321 sixteen-
      cycles respectively: those two rows are CAP ARTIFACTS and say
      nothing about avoidability.
  (b) The n = 32 run completed only 2 restarts in 120 s - counting
      32-cycles dominates - so it is undersearched and excluded.
  (c) couple479's closing report line called count_len(G, L, 1), and
      count_len returns tot//2, so a cap of 1 always returns 0 and
      the "still carries" line printed [] unconditionally. That line
      was junk; the lattice rows themselves use cap 30 and stand.
      The counterexample gate read only the {4,8,16} row, which
      never reached 0, so no false alarm was raised.
  (d) The reliable content is the n = 16, 20, 24 columns.

A FURTHER LIMIT, and it is structural rather than computational. The
finite statement "every cubic graph has a 4-, 8- or 16-cycle" is
FALSE: any cubic graph of girth >= 17 has none of those three, and
such graphs exist. So no fixed finite window of powers of two can
carry the coupling; a true coupling must SCALE with n. That is
461.4's Ratio Theorem again - the achievable window has ratio below
2, so it need not contain a power of two - and it is the reason the
n <= 24 measurements above cannot be extrapolated.

### 471.5 STATUS

PROVED: the schema collapse - every (CPL_t) is equivalent to the
conjecture, so coupling must be a mechanism and not a lemma (471.0);
the Theta Valuation Lemma, an exact determination of the minimum
level of a theta's cycles from the valuations of its paths (471.1);
the ear specialisation and the level-descent corollary, a two-level
inference with a purely structural hypothesis (471.2); the rigidity
bound 2^s <= L/3 (471.3).

COMPUTED: the lemma on 1 771 561 triples and the ear form on four
strata, zero violations; the ear-valuation profile of ten graphs, in
all of which the coupling fires; the avoidance lattice, in which
every proper subset of {4,8,16} is avoidable at n = 24 and the full
set is not, with the surviving power of two always the lowest.

NOT PROVED: any instance of (CPL_t) - and by 471.0 that is not a
shortfall of this section but a theorem about the schema; J7; the
five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The request that opened
this section - a theorem of the form "no power of two at levels
>= t implies a contradiction below t" - is answered in the negative
as a matter of logic: every such statement IS the conjecture. What
exists instead is a transport rule, proved and exact, which converts
the valuations of a theta's paths into the levels of its cycles, and
which fires on every graph so far examined. The frontier is now to
run that rule against a supply theorem - 432.4 gives at least L/3
ears - and extract a contradiction from the ear-valuation profile of
a counterexample, whose rigidity is bounded by 2^s <= L/3.


## 472. FIELD SURVEY: WHERE ELSE J7 COULD LIVE

A survey of mathematical fields the archive has NOT used, filtered
against the no-go results it has proved. Most of the obvious imports
turn out to be already mined - the archive is far deeper in coding
theory, zeta functions and lattice theory than a fresh reader would
guess - so 472.1 lists those explicitly to stop them being proposed
again. Three candidates survive the filter; they are 472.2 to 472.4.
472.5 records two new no-goes generated by the survey itself.

### 472.0 THE FILTER: SEVEN STANDING NO-GOES

Each kills a whole class of methods. A field is worth importing only
if all seven are silent on it.

  (N1) SCALE INVARIANCE (447.3, sharpened at 470.0). Lengths are
       l = 2^t m; halving is (t,m) |-> (t-1,m); the target P = {2^k}
       IS the fibre m = 1. Anything that moves along halving orbits
       cannot approach the target. NEW HERE: this kills COVERING
       SPACES. A regular Gamma-cover with Gamma a 2-group (447.5)
       gives lifts of length 2^k |Cbar| - pure motion along a
       halving orbit, m fixed. The one on-target topological
       instrument is provably in the blocked direction.

  (N2) THE CONSTANCY DICHOTOMY (447) and the asymmetric
       impossibility (445.5). No purely arithmetic theorem finishes:
       {2^k} is not a union of congruence classes. Modulo p it is
       the multiplicative subgroup <2> of F_p^*, so any F_p method
       concludes at best "some length lies in <2> mod p", of density
       ord_p(2)/(p-1). Kills the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz,
       Chevalley-Warning, Ax-Katz.

       SHARPENED (COMPUTED, tools/cn481.py). Ask which congruence
       conclusions are even TRUE for cubic graphs:
         Q(k): every cubic graph has a cycle of length divisible by k.
       Search over cubic graphs at n = 12, 16, 20, 24 by 2-edge-swap
       descent on the capped count of multiples of k:
         k = 3 : survives (best 4, 6, 6, 11)
         k = 4 : survives (best 4, 5, 3, 7)
         k = 5 : REFUTED at n = 16, spectrum {4,6,7,9,12,14,16}
         k = 6 : REFUTED at n = 16, spectrum {3,4,5,7,8,9,10,11}
         k = 8 : REFUTED at n = 12, spectrum {3,4,5,6,7}
       Each refuting witness re-verified by exhaustive enumeration.
       So the ENTIRE reachable output of any F_p method here is
       "divisible by 3" and "divisible by 4". Q(4) is the strongest
       available and says exactly "level 2 is never empty" - which
       is not the conjecture, since a 12-cycle satisfies it. Note
       the convergence with 471.4: the surviving power of two in the
       avoidance lattice is always the one at level 2.

  (N3) THE TREE NO-GO (452.0). The infinite 3-regular tree has
       minimum degree 3 and no cycles, so NO statement about bounded
       neighbourhoods can imply Erdos-Gyarfas. Kills every local or
       limit method AS AN ATTACK ON EG. It is silent on (WC) - see
       472.3.

  (N4) THE RATIO THEOREM (461.4). The achievable window has ratio
       below 2 (sup 1.980), so no interval method can guarantee a
       power of two inside it.

  (N5) STRATUM-LOCALITY (470.5). An explicit 24-vertex cubic graph
       realises the level-3 data of a counterexample, so no
       single-level argument can conclude.

  (N6) SCHEMA COLLAPSE (471.0). Every level-coupling statement of
       the form "no power of two above t implies one below t" is
       equivalent to the conjecture.

  (N7) THE DEGREE-3 BARRIER. The whole cycle-length literature -
       Bondy-Vince, Liu-Ma, Gao-Huo-Liu-Ma, Sudakov-Verstraete,
       Martinsson-Steiner, Thomassen, Chen-Saito, Dean-Lesniak-Saito
       - needs minimum degree strictly above 3 and is already
       surveyed and rejected in the archive with reasons.

### 472.1 ALREADY MINED - DO NOT RE-PROPOSE

Recorded so that a later session does not spend a day rediscovering
them. Each has a section and, where relevant, a recorded gap.

  coding theory: the cycle code, its weight enumerator, MacWilliams
    duality, the zeta_8 character sum and its Ising closed form
    (160-161); the Delsarte LP bound, tried and recorded as too weak,
    with SDP strengthening explicitly noted as out of reach (162.2);
  Ihara zeta and the non-backtracking spectrum: Bass-Ihara, prime
    geodesics, the prime geodesic theorem for graphs and exponential
    equidistribution of closed geodesic lengths (151-152, 157, and
    the whole trace frame 452-463);
  lattice theory: the integral flow lattice with length = norm
    squared, its theta series as a modular form, and the recorded
    HONEST GAP that theta counts all lattice vectors while we need
    circuit vectors (160.4, 441);
  quadratic forms over Z_2: the Brown form, Arf invariant, Gauss
    sums, Witt group of Z_4-forms, signature mod 8 (430, 441, 447.4);
  statistical mechanics: Ising via MacWilliams, polymer and cluster
    expansions, Kotecky-Preiss and its recorded misdiagnosis
    (157.5, 161.4);
  Tutte polynomial and Vertigan's algorithm at the relevant point
    (157);
  structural graph theory: treewidth, Thomassen's subdivided-grid
    theorem, the bounded-treewidth arm;
  matroid theory: the linkage matroid and gammoids (202);
  additive combinatorics: Davenport constants, the sigma-paired
    Davenport problem, and the recorded fact that Balog-Szemeredi-
    Gowers does not apply because the attachment count is an
    incidence not a convolution (462.1, 465);
  entropy accounting (467); SAT and CDCL (438-442, 468);
  Combinatorial Nullstellensatz, assessed and rejected under (N2).

### 472.2 CANDIDATE 1: PROOF COMPLEXITY - CERTIFICATE DEGREE

STATUS: PROPOSED. Untouched: no occurrence of proof complexity,
polynomial calculus, Nullstellensatz degree, sum-of-squares,
Positivstellensatz or Lasserre anywhere in the archive.

The target is NOT the conjecture but 451.2(E), UNIFORMITY IN t,
which 451.2 states in exactly the right words: "the SCHEMA is
uniform; its UNSAT is not." The boards of 438-442 are a family of
finite unsatisfiable constraint systems indexed by t. Proof
complexity asks a question the archive has never asked of them:

  is there a REFUTATION whose DEGREE is bounded independently of t?

A Nullstellensatz or Polynomial Calculus refutation of degree d is a
finite algebraic identity; if d is constant across t = 2, 3, 4 then
the same identity schema refutes every t, and (E) closes. This is
computable: for fixed degree d the existence of a Nullstellensatz
certificate is a LINEAR PROGRAM in the coefficients, and an SOS
certificate is a semidefinite program. So the degree can be MEASURED
at t = 2, 3, 4 and the trend read off, without proving anything
first.

Why it evades the filter. It does not induct on t, so (N1) is
silent. Its conclusion is the unsatisfiability of a specific finite
system, not an arithmetic theorem about {2^k}, so (N2) is silent.
It is global, so (N3) is silent. (N4)-(N7) concern the shape of
statements about cycle lengths, not certificates.

Distinguish it sharply from 162.2. That section tried the Delsarte
LP on the WEIGHT DISTRIBUTION OF THE CYCLE CODE and recorded that a
rate-.36 code of relative distance .11 sits deep inside the feasible
region, so deleting one weight cannot make the LP infeasible. That
is a different object entirely: an LP over 26 weight variables, not
a certificate over the board's own constraints. 162.2's verdict does
not transfer.

The most valuable outcome may not be a proof but a READING: the
coefficients of a low-degree certificate usually expose the
combinatorial identity driving the refutation, which is precisely
what a uniform argument would need to be built from.

### 472.3 CANDIDATE 2: LOCAL WEAK CONVERGENCE - FOR (WC), NOT FOR EG

STATUS: PROPOSED. Untouched: no occurrence of Benjamini-Schramm,
local weak convergence or unimodular random graphs.

(N3) forbids local methods as an attack on EG, and the reason is
airtight: the 3-regular tree has minimum degree 3 and no cycles at
all. But (N3) is a statement about EG. It is SILENT ON (WC), and
(WC) is the archive's own best target (463.2).

(WC) asserts W_m <= K . 2^m . m^2 / n, where W_m is the rank >= 2
walk mass - the closed non-backtracking walks of length m that are
NOT simple cycles. That quantity is governed by the density of short
cycles around a root, which is exactly a LOCAL functional. Cubic
graphs converge in the Benjamini-Schramm sense to unimodular random
rooted 3-regular graphs, whose extreme point is the tree, where
W_m = 0 below the girth. So (WC) is the statement that a specific
local functional is uniformly bounded over all unimodular measures
on rooted cubic graphs - a question in precisely the form that
theory is built to answer.

Why it matters more than the other two candidates: with (WC) the
sieve ceiling becomes sqrt(n/2K) instead of 2g, and the ratio of
that ceiling to the floor 2 log2(4n) GROWS without bound. So (WC)
is the one statement in the archive that defeats (N4): the Ratio
Theorem bounds the window ratio below 2 only for the 2g ceiling.
K is measured at about 0.11 against K = 1 sufficing - a factor of
nine of room on a measured quantity, and at K = 1 the conditional
theorem of 463.2 settles every cubic graph with n >= 1025.

CAVEAT (388.1). No theorem from that literature has been verified
verbatim here. This is a proposal about where the statement lives,
not a claim that a usable theorem exists off the shelf.

### 472.4 CANDIDATE 3: TROPICAL GEOMETRY AND VALUATED MATROIDS

STATUS: PROPOSED, with one proved point of contact. Untouched: no
occurrence of tropical geometry or valuated matroids.

The defining axiom of tropical geometry is that the minimum of a
tropical expression is attained AT LEAST TWICE. The Theta Valuation
Lemma of 471.1 is exactly such a statement about the 2-adic
valuations of a theta's three cycles - and it satisfies the axiom in
some cases and violates it in exactly one.

  COMPUTED (all (p,q,r) in [1,160]^3, 4 096 000 triples). Let
  alpha = min(v_2 p, v_2 q, v_2 r) and mu the number of paths
  attaining it, and count how often the minimum of
  (v_2 A, v_2 B, v_2 C) is attained just once:

      mu = 1 : attained once        0 ,  twice or more  1 755 414
      mu = 2 : attained once        0 ,  twice or more  1 755 432
      mu = 3 : attained once  438 858 ,  twice or more    146 296

  So the tropical balance axiom HOLDS WITHOUT EXCEPTION when mu <= 2
  and FAILS in three quarters of the mu = 3 cases. Smallest failure:
  (p,q,r) = (1,1,3), cycles (2,4,4), valuations (1,2,2).

That is not a curiosity. mu = 3 - all three paths of equal
valuation - is precisely the VALUATION-BOOSTING case, the only one
in which the theta's cycles sit strictly above the level of its
paths, and therefore the only place powers of two can be
manufactured. Example: paths (1,3,5) give cycles 4, 6, 8 - two
powers of two out of three.

  THE READING. The circuits of a graph, valued by v_2 of their
  length, form a structure that is tropical away from mu = 3 and
  breaks the balance axiom exactly at the configurations that
  generate the target set. Whatever the right axiomatics is, it must
  be one in which balance failure is the interesting event rather
  than a defect.

HONEST ASSESSMENT: this names and isolates the phenomenon; it does
not come with a theorem that would deliver EG. It is proposed
because it is the only field on the list whose central axiom makes
direct contact with a PROVED result of this archive.

### 472.5 TWO NEW NO-GOES GENERATED BY THE SURVEY

STATUS: PROVED.

(a) NO SECOND ACTION, SO NO RIGIDITY. Ergodic-theoretic rigidity of
the Furstenberg x2-x3 type needs two multiplicatively independent
actions. Here there is only x2: 470.0's halving. The natural
candidate for a x3 is subdivision - subdividing every edge k-fold
multiplies every cycle length by k - but subdivision creates
vertices of degree 2 and so LEAVES the minimum-degree-3 class, in
which the conjecture is false for trivial reasons. There is no
length-scaling operation preserving the class. Rigidity is therefore
unavailable in principle, not merely unproved.

(b) DIOPHANTINE METHODS ANSWER THE WRONG QUESTION. S-unit equation
theory, the subspace theorem and their relatives are exactly adapted
to powers of two: {2^k} is the S-unit group for S = {2}, and the
theta identity A + B - C = 2p is a linear relation among lengths.
But those theorems bound the NUMBER of solutions from above, and
what is needed here is existence of ONE. A counterexample has no
power-of-two cycle at all, so there is nothing to feed in. The
direction of the conclusion is wrong, permanently.

REMARK (why (WC) is the whole game, at the cheapest possible level).
Closed walks at a vertex concatenate, so their lengths form a
numerical semigroup; it contains 2 - go out along an edge and back -
so it contains every sufficiently large even number, and in
particular 2^k for all large k. Power-of-two closed WALKS are free
and unconditional. Every difficulty in the conjecture is the passage
from walk to simple cycle, and that passage is measured by exactly
one quantity, W_m. The archive's spectral count (452, 463) is
strictly stronger than this remark, but the remark shows the split
without any spectral input at all.

### 472.6 STATUS

PROVED in this section: the covering-space direction is the blocked
fibre direction (472.0, N1); the congruence ceiling at minimum
degree 3 is k = 4, with Q(5), Q(6), Q(8) refuted by re-verified
explicit witnesses (472.0, N2); the tropical balance axiom holds for
mu <= 2 and fails only at mu = 3 (472.4); ergodic rigidity is
unavailable for want of a second action, and Diophantine methods
conclude in the wrong direction (472.5).

PROPOSED, in order of expected value:
  1. LOCAL WEAK CONVERGENCE, aimed at (WC) - the only target that
     defeats the Ratio Theorem, with a measured factor of nine of
     room;
  2. PROOF COMPLEXITY, certificate degree, aimed at 451.2(E) -
     measurable today at t = 2, 3, 4 by LP and SDP;
  3. TROPICAL GEOMETRY, as the axiomatics of 471.1.

NOT PROVED: J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The survey's main finding
is convergence: three independent lines of reasoning - the Ratio
Theorem's ceiling, the walk-versus-cycle split, and the search for a
field where the tree no-go is silent - all terminate at the same
statement, (WC). No new field displaces it. The correct reading of
this section is not that a new import is needed, but that the import
already identified in 463 is the only one whose resolution is
blocked by none of the seven no-goes.


## 473. J7 IN THE LANGUAGE OF MANIFOLDS

The question: is there an EQUIVALENT restatement of J7 in manifold
language, and what would it buy? The answer is yes, there is exactly
one such dictionary not already in the archive - tropical curves and
their Jacobians - and what it buys is a cleaner name for the one gap
this problem has. Two further dictionaries are written out and shown
to buy nothing, each yielding a new no-go. Two of the archive's own
statements are corrected.

### 473.0 WHAT IS ALREADY THERE

160.5 already surveyed the geometric translations and gave verdicts,
and they must not be re-proposed:

  (a) TREE LATTICES / OUTER SPACE. pi_1(G) is free of rank n/2+1
      acting freely cocompactly on T_3, so G = Gamma \ T_3 and a
      cubic graph is an integral point of Culler-Vogtmann Outer
      space, with CYCLE LENGTH = TRANSLATION LENGTH. Verdict
      recorded: the equidistribution theorems are the right shape but
      count all closed geodesics, not embedded ones.
  (c) DESSINS D'ENFANTS. A cubic ribbon graph is a trivalent dessin.
      Verdict recorded: NO - cycle lengths are not a dessin
      invariant and the Galois action does not preserve
      mod-8-freeness.

160.3 gives the flow lattice with cycle length = squared norm; 160.4
gives the theta series and the modular-forms target, with the gap
recorded; 161.1 gives the reason the code was chosen over Outer
space; 444 proves a Local Density Theorem for the mod-2^t theta
coefficients of that lattice. So the manifold question is narrow:
what is left is the object 160.3's lattice is the Jacobian OF.

### 473.1 THE DICTIONARY NOT YET WRITTEN: TROPICAL CURVES

STATUS: exact, and the identification is standard (Mikhalkin-Zharkov
tropical Jacobians; recorded as an identification of objects, not as
an imported theorem - no result from that literature is used below).

Give every edge of a cubic G length 1. The resulting metric graph IS
a tropical curve of genus

        g  =  |E| - |V| + 1  =  n/2 + 1 ,

and its Jacobian is the real torus

        Jac(Gamma)  =  H_1(Gamma, R) / H_1(Gamma, Z) ,

principally polarised by the quadratic form Q(x) = SUM_e l_e x_e^2,
which at unit lengths is exactly ||x||^2. That is 441's flow lattice,
verbatim - so the archive has been computing on a Jacobian since 160
without saying which manifold it was.

  THE DICTIONARY.
      cubic graph                 trivalent tropical curve, genus n/2+1
      cycle space                 H_1, the period lattice Lambda
      cycle length                squared norm, the polarisation
      girth                       the lattice minimum
      a cycle                     an INDECOMPOSABLE +-1 lattice vector
      an even subgraph            any +-1 lattice vector
      the cycle spectrum          the norms of indecomposable +-1 vectors

  J7 RESTATED. The principally polarised tropical Jacobian of a
  trivalent tropical curve carries an indecomposable +-1 lattice
  vector of norm a power of two, whenever it carries one of norm
  divisible by 8.

  THE ONE PLACE THE DICTIONARY IS TIGHT (PROVED). min(Lambda) = g,
  the girth, and the minimal vectors are exactly the girth cycles
  with their two orientations.
  Proof. A nonzero integral flow has support of minimum degree >= 2,
  hence containing a cycle, so ||x||^2 >= |supp x| >= girth. Equality
  forces every entry to be 0 or +-1 and |supp x| = girth, so the
  support has minimum degree >= 2 with exactly girth many edges: a
  single girth cycle. QED
  Verified on K4, K3,3, cube, Petersen: minimum norm equals girth and
  the minimal-vector count equals 2 c_g in all four.

### 473.2 THE SIMPLICITY GAP, MEASURED

STATUS: COMPUTED (tools/manifold482.py). 160.4's recorded gap - the
theta series counts ALL lattice vectors of a given norm while cycles
are only the indecomposable +-1 ones - had never been quantified.
Enumerating the flow lattice directly, with

    a_N = lattice vectors of norm N          (theta coefficient)
    u_N = those with all entries in {-1,0,1} (even subgraphs)
    s_N = those that are a single circuit    (= 2 c_N, what J7 needs)

  cube (rank 5, girth 4)          Petersen (rank 6, girth 5)
    N    a_N   u_N   s_N            N    a_N   u_N   s_N
    4     12    12    12            5     24    24    24
    6     32    32    32            6     20    20    20
    8     24    24    12            8     30    30    30
   10     24     0     0            9     40    40    40
   12     48     0     0           10     24    24     0
                                   12     60     0     0

  THE SHARPEST ROW IS PETERSEN AT N = 10: twenty-four lattice
  vectors of norm ten, and NOT ONE CYCLE. Petersen is not
  Hamiltonian, so c_10 = 0, while the six disjoint pairs of 5-cycles
  supply 24 unit flows. Every lattice-theoretic invariant - theta
  series, Voronoi cell, Torelli data - reads 24 there and is blind to
  the 0. Petersen at N = 8 is the contrast: a_8 = u_8 = s_8 = 30,
  the gap fully closed, because 8 admits no decomposition into
  Petersen cycle lengths (no 3-cycles, no 4-cycles) and no vector
  with an entry of modulus 2.

  THE READING. The gap is not a uniform loss factor. It is exactly
  zero at N = girth and at every N admitting no decomposition, and it
  is TOTAL at N admitting one. Whether it is open at N = 2^k is a
  question about the additive structure of the cycle spectrum - which
  is 454.3's theta count T_m again, arriving from the lattice side.

### 473.3 CORRECTED (374.1): THE MINIMALITY RATE IS NOT A CONSTANT

STATUS: COMPUTED (tools/manifold483.py), and it corrects the archive.

161.1 chose the cycle-code translation over Outer space with this
argument: among closed geodesics cycles are exponentially rare
(2^{n/2} against 2^n/n), whereas "in the cycle code the same filter
costs a CONSTANT FACTOR (160.1: cycles are 57-90% of Z(G))".

The comparison is sound and stands. The constant-factor phrase does
not. Computing the minimality rate WEIGHT BY WEIGHT - A_w codewords
of weight w, M_w of them single circuits:

  graph            n  rank  codewords  minimal   rate   dead weights
  K4               4     3          7        7   100%   none
  cube             8     5         31       28    90%   none
  Petersen        10     6         63       57    90%   10
  Heawood         14     8        255      213    84%   none
  Moebius-Kantor  16     9        511      400    78%   none
  Pappus          18    10       1023      783    77%   none
  Desargues       20    11       2047     1456    71%   none
  Dodecahedron    20    11       2047     1168    57%   19
  McGee           24    13       8191     5608    68%   none
  trunc-Petersen  30    16      65535    15114    23%   6, 9, 28, 29, 30

A "dead weight" has codewords but none minimal. They exist:
Petersen weight 10 (6 codewords, none minimal), Dodecahedron weight
19 (120), trunc-Petersen weights 6 (45), 9 (120), 28 (1680), 29
(480), 30 (64).

  TWO CORRECTIONS.
  (i) The aggregate rate does not transfer to a single weight. At a
      dead weight the filter is TOTAL, so a theorem delivering "the
      code has a codeword of weight 2^k" does not deliver a cycle of
      length 2^k. J7 uses the code at one weight, and one weight is
      exactly where the aggregate says nothing.
  (ii) The band "57-90%" is not a floor. trunc-Petersen sits at 23%,
      far below it. The low rows are the low-girth rows, and low
      girth - truncations - is the archive's own known adversary
      (452.6). So the filter is worst precisely on the graphs that
      have already broken other arguments.

  NOT A REFUTATION. No dead weight in this zoo is a power of two, and
  where a power of two is dead in the CYCLE spectrum the code sees it
  too: trunc-Petersen has no 8-cycle and also no weight-8 codeword at
  all, since 8 is not a sum of its cycle lengths {3, 10, 12, 16, 24}.
  161.1's choice of translation is not overturned; its stated reason
  is.

### 473.4 TWO MORE DICTIONARIES, AND TWO NEW NO-GOES

STATUS: PROVED.

(A) BRUHAT-TITS. The 3-regular tree is exactly the Bruhat-Tits tree
of PGL_2(Q_2), since that tree is (q+1)-regular with q = 2. For a
hyperbolic element with eigenvalues lambda_1, lambda_2 the
translation length on the tree is |v_2(lambda_1) - v_2(lambda_2)|.
So for an arithmetic quotient A CYCLE LENGTH IS ITSELF A 2-ADIC
VALUATION.

  NO-GO. J7 asks about v_2 of the length. In this dictionary that is
  the 2-adic valuation OF a 2-adic valuation: the two occurrences of
  the prime 2 sit at different levels of the tower and do not
  interact. Nested valuations carry no structure to exploit. The
  apparent resonance between "power of two" and "2-adic tree" is
  an accident of notation.
  Second, weaker point: only arithmetic quotients arise from
  PGL_2(Q_2) at all. A general cubic graph is Gamma \ T_3 with Gamma
  merely in Aut(T_3), which is vastly larger, so the dictionary is
  not even available in general.

(B) RIBBON GRAPHS AND SURFACES. A rotation system thickens G to a
surface of some genus gamma with F faces, and

    F = 2 - 2 gamma + n/2 ,   SUM_f l_f = 2|E| = 3n ,
    hence  SUM_f (6 - l_f)  =  6F - 3n  =  12 - 12 gamma .

  At gamma = 0 this forces a face of length at most 5, which is how
  the planar case is reachable. But among 3, 4, 5 only 4 is a power
  of two, so even at genus 0 the Euler mechanism forces a SHORT face,
  not a power-of-two one. The dodecahedron is the clean witness:
  every face has length 5, the Euler count is 12 x 1 and yields
  nothing, while the graph's power-of-two cycle is a 16-CYCLE, which
  is not a face at all.
  At gamma >= 1 the sum is 12 - 12 gamma <= 0 and forces nothing.

  NO-GO. The Euler-characteristic mechanism is exhausted at genus 0,
  is silent at every positive genus, and even at genus 0 does not
  reach the target. And the genus is not ours to choose: minimum
  genus is a property of the graph.

### 473.5 WHAT THE MANIFOLD SIDE ACTUALLY BUYS

One thing, and it is real but not new in substance. Naming the
lattice as a Jacobian makes a_N a REPRESENTATION NUMBER of a
positive definite integral quadratic form in g = n/2 + 1 variables -
a theta-series coefficient - rather than a spectral trace. That
main term comes with the apparatus of quadratic forms: Siegel-type
asymptotics with a product of local densities, of which the factor
at p = 2 is exactly the one that governs N = 2^k. 444 already proves
a Local Density Theorem for the mod-2^t theta coefficients of this
lattice, so half the apparatus is in the archive already; what is
missing is the global asymptotic for a_N itself.

But the shape of the argument is unchanged. Where 463 has

    N_m  =  2m c_m  +  proper powers  +  W_m ,

the Jacobian has

    a_N  =  s_N  +  decomposable +-1 vectors  +  vectors of modulus >= 2 ,

with a main term one can hope to estimate and an excess one must
bound. It is (WC) with a different main term. The manifold language
supplies a better-understood main term and does NOT touch the
excess, which 473.2 shows can swallow the whole count.

  THE UNIFICATION, AND IT IS THE SECTION'S POINT. This archive has
  now recorded the same obstruction from four independent
  directions: 160.4's theta series counting all lattice vectors
  rather than circuits; 161.1's geodesics counting all closed
  geodesics rather than embedded ones; 463's W_m separating closed
  non-backtracking walks from simple cycles; and 473.2's a_N
  separating lattice vectors from indecomposable ones. THEY ARE ONE
  GAP. Call it the SIMPLICITY GAP: every frame supplies a main term
  it can estimate and an excess of non-simple objects it cannot
  bound. No reformulation has ever removed it, and the manifold
  reformulation does not either.

### 473.6 STATUS

PROVED: the tropical-Jacobian dictionary and the identification of
441's flow lattice as the period lattice of a genus-(n/2+1) tropical
curve (473.1); min(Lambda) = girth with the minimal vectors exactly
the girth cycles (473.1); the Bruhat-Tits nested-valuation no-go and
the ribbon-graph Euler no-go (473.4).

COMPUTED: the simplicity gap per norm, with Petersen at N = 10
showing 24 lattice vectors and zero cycles (473.2); the per-weight
minimality rate on ten graphs, with seven dead weights exhibited
(473.3).

CORRECTED (374.1): 161.1's "the filter costs a constant factor" is
false for the single-weight use J7 makes of the code - at a dead
weight the filter is total; and 160.1's 57-90% band is not a floor,
trunc-Petersen sitting at 23%. The CHOICE of translation stands; the
REASON given for it does not.

NOT PROVED: J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. J7 can be cast in manifold
language exactly, as a statement about indecomposable minimal-norm
data on a principally polarised tropical Jacobian, and the cast is
faithful rather than analogical. What it buys is a better main term
and a name for the obstruction. What it does not buy is any purchase
on the obstruction itself, which 473.5 identifies as the single gap
this problem has had all along, now seen from four frames at once.


## 474. THE FAMILY AS AN OBJECT: THE CYCLE SEMIGROUP

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. This section answers a question the
archive had never asked: can the FAMILY of graphs, rather than any
one graph, be made into a single mathematical object whose structure
settles J7? It (a) exhibits the object and PROVES that it satisfies
J7 unconditionally, before any graph is examined (474.1); (b) PROVES
the exact spectrum identity that makes a family carry the structure,
machine-verified (474.2); (c) PROVES that all seven standing no-goes
of 472.0 are silent on it, which no previous criterion in this
archive has managed (474.3); (d) PROVES the exact price - the
counterexample class is closed under the operation if and only if it
is empty, and the failure of closure is an explicit finite
certificate (474.4). 474.5 isolates the one non-equivalent form and
shows it is 473.5's simplicity gap. 474.6 records a new standing
no-go.

### 474.0 WHAT THE QUESTION DEMANDS, AND THE FREE STRUCTURE

To say "the family IS an object O" is worth something only if three
conditions hold at once.

  (R1) O-hood must PRODUCE the theorem. "Every O satisfies J7" must
       be provable from the definition of O alone, with no graph
       theory beyond what the definition names. This has to be
       settled FIRST; otherwise O is decoration.
  (R2) The family must plausibly carry the structure.
  (R3) The structure must not be a restatement. By (N6) - schema
       collapse, 471.0 - every level-coupling statement about cycle
       lengths is equivalent to the conjecture, and a restated
       conjecture dressed as an algebraic axiom is the trap this
       section has to avoid naming as progress.

Before proposing anything, record what the family already has. Let

    X  =  the class of finite graphs with minimum degree >= 3 and no
          cycle whose length is a power of two,

so Erdos-Gyarfas says exactly that X is empty, and let

    Sigma  =  union of S(H) over all H in X,

the set of cycle lengths realisable by counterexamples. By
construction Sigma is disjoint from P = {2^k : k >= 2}.

LEMMA 474.0 (THE FREE STRUCTURE IS A SEMILATTICE, AND IT IS USELESS).
  (i)   X is closed under DISJOINT UNION.
  (ii)  X is closed under passing to a subgraph of minimum degree >= 3.
  (iii) X is closed under Whitney 2-isomorphism, within minimum
        degree >= 3.
  (iv)  On cubic graphs (ii) is VACUOUS: a subgraph of minimum degree
        >= 3 of a cubic graph is a union of its connected components.
  (v)   Under (i)-(iii) alone, Sigma is closed under UNION and
        nothing else, and no union-closed hypothesis can force a
        power of two.

PROOF. (i) S(H1 + H2) = S(H1) U S(H2) and no degree changes.
(ii) every cycle of a subgraph is a cycle of the host.
(iii) 2-isomorphic graphs have the same cycle matroid, hence the same
circuits, hence the same multiset of cycle lengths.
(iv) if v in V(H) has deg_H(v) >= 3 while deg_G(v) = 3, then every
edge of G at v already lies in H; so V(H) is closed under adjacency
in G and H is a union of components.
(v) the three operations are respectively spectrum-union,
spectrum-nonincreasing and spectrum-preserving, so they generate no
length not already present; and a single set disjoint from P is
already union-closed, so union closure is consistent with Sigma
disjoint from P. QED

READING. Two things follow, and both were tacit in the archive
without ever being written down. First, the closures the family
carries for free make it a JOIN-SEMILATTICE - a poset with unions -
and a semilattice cannot see a power of two, because the semilattice
axioms are satisfied by the answer "no". Second, (iv) says the
subgraph order is FLAT on cubic graphs: there is no descent in it at
all. That is the precise reason every descent in this archive - 165,
185, 447, 469, 470 - had to be built by hand on some invented
parameter rather than read off an order. To settle J7 the family must
be given an operation that ADDS lengths.

### 474.1 THE OBJECT, AND THE PROOF THAT IT SATISFIES J7

DEFINITION (EDGE AMALGAM). Let H1 and H2 be disjoint graphs, e1 =
u1v1 an edge of H1 and e2 = u2v2 an edge of H2. The AMALGAM is

    H1 (+) H2  =  (H1 - e1)  +  (H2 - e2)  +  u1u2  +  v1v2 .

Every degree is preserved: u1 and v1 each lose one edge and gain
one, and no other vertex is touched. The two new edges form an edge
cut of size 2. Iterating gives the m-block CHAIN: delete e_i from
each of H_1, ..., H_m and add v_i u_{i+1} cyclically; the amalgam is
the case m = 2.

DEFINITION (CYCLE SEMIGROUP). A class F of finite graphs of minimum
degree >= 3 is a CYCLE SEMIGROUP if for all H1, H2 in F - disjoint
copies allowed, including a disjoint copy of H1 itself - and all
e1 in E(H1), e2 in E(H2), the amalgam H1 (+) H2 lies in F.

THEOREM A. Every NONEMPTY cycle semigroup contains a member with a
cycle whose length is a power of two.

PROOF, in three steps.

STEP 1 - ADDITIVITY. Write Sigma_F for the union of S(H) over H in F.
Claim: Sigma_F + Sigma_F is contained in Sigma_F.

  Let a be in S(H1), realised by a cycle C1, and b in S(H2), realised
  by C2; pick e1 in E(C1) and e2 in E(C2), taking a disjoint copy if
  H1 = H2. Then a is in S_{e1}(H1) and b in S_{e2}(H2), where S_e(H)
  denotes the set of lengths of cycles of H through e.

  In H = H1 (+) H2 the pair {u1u2, v1v2} is an edge cut of size 2, so
  every cycle meets it 0 or 2 times. A cycle meeting it twice enters
  H1 at one endpoint of e1 and leaves at the other, so its H1-part is
  a u1-v1 path of H1 - e1 and its H2-part is a u2-v2 path of H2 - e2;
  conversely any such pair of paths closes into a cycle. Since the
  cycles of H1 through e1 are exactly e1 plus a u1-v1 path of
  H1 - e1, the crossing lengths are exactly the SUMSET. The cycles
  meeting the cut 0 times are exactly the cycles of H1 - e1 and of
  H2 - e2. Hence, as an EQUALITY of sets,

    S(H1 (+) H2) = S(H1-e1) U S(H2-e2) U ( S_{e1}(H1) + S_{e2}(H2) ),

  and moreover the cycles through the new edge u1u2 are exactly the
  crossing ones, so S_{u1u2}(H1 (+) H2) = S_{e1}(H1) + S_{e2}(H2) and
  the construction ITERATES: an m-block chain realises the m-fold
  sumset. In particular a + b lies in S(H1 (+) H2), and H1 (+) H2 is
  in F, so a + b is in Sigma_F. QED Step 1.

STEP 2 - THE gcd IS A POWER OF TWO. Bondy-Vince 1998, as already
recorded verbatim in this archive at 3, 169.3 and 472.0(N7): every
graph with minimum degree at least three contains two cycles whose
lengths differ by one or two. No stronger form is used, and none is
available at degree exactly 3 (that is (N7)).
