  Take H in F, nonempty by hypothesis, and let a, b in S(H) with
  |a - b| in {1,2}. Then gcd S(H) divides |a - b|, so gcd S(H) is 1
  or 2. Since S(H) is contained in Sigma_F, gcd Sigma_F divides
  gcd S(H). Hence

      gcd Sigma_F  is in  {1, 2}  =  {2^0, 2^1} ,

  a power of two. QED Step 2.

STEP 3 - COFINALITY. By Step 1, Sigma_F is a subsemigroup of (N, +);
let d = gcd Sigma_F, which by Step 2 is 1 or 2. Dividing by d gives a
subsemigroup of gcd 1, which contains every sufficiently large
integer; so Sigma_F contains every sufficiently large multiple of d.
The set P is COFINAL in d*N for d in {1,2}: every 2^k with k >= 2 is
a multiple of d, and they are unbounded. Hence P meets Sigma_F.
QED Step 3.

So some H in F has a cycle of length a power of two. QED THEOREM A.

EXPLICIT BOUND. Let a < b be a Bondy-Vince pair in H, d = gcd(a,b).
By Sylvester the Frobenius number of <a/d, b/d> is ab/d^2 - a/d -
b/d, so every multiple of d exceeding F = ab/d - a - b lies in
<a,b>. The least power of two above F is at most 2(F+1) <= 2ab, and
being a sum of elements each at least a it needs at most 2b summands.
Since a, b <= c(H) <= n:

  COROLLARY 474.1 (THE ESCAPE CERTIFICATE). If G is a counterexample
  on n vertices then there is a chain of at most 2n copies of G - an
  ordinary graph of minimum degree 3 on at most 2n^2 vertices, built
  from nothing but copies of G - that HAS a cycle whose length is a
  power of two.

WHY THIS IS THE REQUESTED SHAPE. Theorem A meets (R1) exactly: the
object is defined by a closure axiom, and "every such object
satisfies J7" is proved from that axiom with two inputs only - one
exact spectrum identity and one citation - plus three lines of
arithmetic. Nothing about powers of two is smuggled in. Step 3 uses
no property of P beyond COFINALITY IN 2^s * N, which is why the
argument is immune to the scale invariance that has killed every
other structural attempt (474.3).

### 474.2 THE TWO LEMMAS, MACHINE-VERIFIED

tools/family484.py checks both inputs of Theorem A independently of
the proofs above.

  LEMMA 1 (the amalgam/chain identity of Step 1). Checked as an
  EQUALITY of sets, by exhaustive cycle enumeration on both sides,
  over all amalgams of K4, K_{3,3}, the 3-prism, the cube, the
  4-prism and the Petersen graph, for three choices of edge on each
  side: 324 amalgam pairs, 0 violations - and the
  through-the-new-edge form S_new = S_{e1} + S_{e2} also 0
  violations, which is what licenses the iteration. Chains of length
  m = 3, 4, 5 with mixed blocks and mixed marked edges: 111 chains,
  0 violations, the m-fold sumset exact each time.

  LEMMA 2 (gcd S(G) in {1,2}). Checked on 13 graphs from K4 to the
  truncated Petersen graph: 0 violations. The bipartite rows sit at
  gcd 2 (Heawood, Pappus, Desargues, Moebius-Kantor, cube, K_{3,3}),
  the rest at 1.

  THE ESCAPE OF COROLLARY 474.1, illustrated. A counterexample's
  spectrum contains no power of two, so to make the zoo
  counterexample-shaped delete them: S* = S(G) \ P. Then compute the
  least power of two in <S*> and the number of blocks realising it.

    graph            n   S* = S(G) \ P        gcd   2^r  blocks  vertices
    K4               4   [3]                    3   -    (gcd not 2-power)
    K33              6   [6]                    6   -    (gcd not 2-power)
    cube             8   [6]                    6   -    (gcd not 2-power)
    prism-4          8   [6]                    6   -    (gcd not 2-power)
    prism-3          6   [3,5,6]                1     8       2        12
    Petersen        10   [5,6,9]                1    16       3        30
    prism-5         10   [5,6,7,9,10]           1    16       2        20
    Heawood         14   [6,10,12,14]           2    16       2        28
    Moebius-Kantor  16   [6,10,12,14]           2    16       2        32
    Pappus          18   [6,10,12,14,18]        2    16       2        36
    Desargues       20   [6,10,12,14,...]       2    16       2        40
    Dodecahedron    20   [5,9,10,11,12,...]     1    16       2        40
    trunc-Petersen  30   [3,10,11,12,13,...]    1    16       2        60

  The four dashed rows are the ones the deletion BROKE: their gcd has
  an odd factor, so by Lemma 2 no minimum-degree-3 graph has such a
  spectrum and they were never counterexample-shaped. That is Lemma 2
  doing precisely the work Theorem A asks of it - it is the step that
  forbids a counterexample from hiding inside 3N or 6N, which is the
  one way a subsemigroup of N can avoid the powers of two forever.
  On every genuinely counterexample-shaped row the escape costs 2 or
  3 blocks.

RELATION TO 3b. Section 3b already contained the additive
phenomenon, in the 3-cut substitution setting: "a cycle of D(M,H)
crossing s gadgets has length in (s-fold sumset of A)", with the
BAND-MERGING criterion that for an interval A = [p,q] consecutive
bands overlap once (s+1)p <= sq, so the union is a full interval.
That mechanism needs the gadget's crossing-path set to be an
INTERVAL of ratio about 2, and 3b says so explicitly ("to break DWL
by substitution you would need a cubic gadget whose crossing
path-length set is narrow"). Theorem A needs no interval and no
ratio: Sylvester replaces the ratio hypothesis by the gcd, and the
number of blocks does the work the window width used to do. That is
the precise strengthening, and it is what makes (N4) silent below.

### 474.3 ALL SEVEN STANDING NO-GOES ARE SILENT

This is the section's reason for existing. Take 472.0's filter in
order.

  (N1) SCALE INVARIANCE. Theorem A never moves along a halving orbit
       and never tries to distinguish the fibre m = 1. Step 3 uses
       only that P is cofinal in 2^s * N for every s - i.e. it
       PRODUCES an element of the fibre out of cofinality rather than
       navigating towards it. Scaling the whole spectrum by 2 maps
       one instance of Theorem A to another. SILENT.

  (N2) THE CONSTANCY DICHOTOMY. Theorem A's arithmetic conclusion is
       not a congruence. (N2) says an F_p method concludes at best
       "some length lies in <2> mod p"; Step 3 concludes MEMBERSHIP
       in a semigroup, and {2^k} being not a union of congruence
       classes is irrelevant to a cofinality argument. SILENT.

  (N3) THE TREE NO-GO. Theorem A is neither local nor a limit
       statement: its hypothesis is a global closure property of a
       class of FINITE graphs, and it constrains no bounded
       neighbourhood. The 3-regular tree is not a member of any
       cycle semigroup and cannot be produced by amalgamation, which
       only ever builds finite graphs from finite graphs. Note also
       that the tree fails the input Theorem A actually consumes - it
       has no two cycles, hence no Bondy-Vince pair. SILENT.

  (N4) THE RATIO THEOREM. Theorem A is not an interval method. It
       needs no window at all, and by 474.2 it strictly supersedes
       the one interval mechanism the archive had (3b's band
       merging), which did need ratio 2. Where (N4) caps the ratio at
       1.980, Theorem A trades ratio for NUMBER OF SUMMANDS, and the
       family supplies unboundedly many. SILENT - and this is the
       first mechanism in the archive that defeats (N4) rather than
       being defeated by it.

  (N5) STRATUM-LOCALITY. Theorem A is not a single-level argument;
       it never mentions a level. SILENT.

  (N6) SCHEMA COLLAPSE. Theorem A is not of the form "no power of
       two above t implies one below t". Its hypothesis is a closure
       property of a class, not a statement about cycle lengths in a
       graph. SILENT at the level of the theorem - though 474.4
       shows the collapse reappears when one asks whether X itself
       is such an object, which is exactly where the honesty lies.

  (N7) THE DEGREE-3 BARRIER. Theorem A uses Bondy-Vince AT degree
       exactly 3, and uses only its gcd corollary. It does not ask
       for k consecutive lengths, which is what 169.3(b) rejected as
       "exponentially short of what is needed" and what (N7) says
       needs degree above 3. This is the first use of Bondy-Vince in
       the archive that asks the theorem for no more than it proves.
       SILENT.

All seven silent. No previous criterion recorded here has that
property; 472's three surviving candidates were each proposals, not
theorems.

### 474.4 THE PRICE: CLOSURE IS THE CONJECTURE, AND THE ESCAPE IS EXPLICIT

THEOREM B (PROVED). X is closed under edge amalgamation if and only
if X is empty - that is, if and only if Erdos-Gyarfas holds.

PROOF. If X is empty it is vacuously closed. Conversely, if X is
closed and nonempty then X is a nonempty cycle semigroup, so by
Theorem A some H in X has a cycle of power-of-two length,
contradicting H in X. QED

So the object is found and the family is provably NOT it, unless the
conjecture is true. The operational content is the contrapositive,
which is Corollary 474.1: closure fails, and it fails at an explicit
finite certificate - a multiset of at most 2n of the counterexample's
own cycle lengths summing to a power of two, together with the chain
of at most 2n copies of itself in which that sum IS a cycle. 474.2's
table shows the certificate is 2 or 3 blocks in every
counterexample-shaped instance measured.

Why this cannot be repaired by descent:

THEOREM 474.4 (ADDITIVITY COSTS SIZE). Any operation which, from H1
and H2 with l_i in S(H_i), produces a graph having a cycle of length
l1 + l2 produces a graph on at least l1 + l2 vertices. Hence no
additive operation is size-nonincreasing, and no minimal-
counterexample argument can be applied to its output. Combined with
Lemma 474.0(v) - the only operations under which X is PROVABLY closed
are union, subgraph and Whitney, all spectrum-flat - the
family-as-object route has exactly two exits: enlarge, and forfeit
minimality; or internalise the addition into a single graph. QED

And the limit does not provide a third exit:

PROPOSITION 474.4b (THE LIMIT DESTROYS THE ADDITIVITY). Let
N_inf(G,e) be the two-way infinite chain of copies of G - e joined by
v_i u_{i+1}, i in Z. Every connector v_i u_{i+1} is a BRIDGE of
N_inf - deleting it leaves two disjoint infinite half-chains - and a
bridge lies on no cycle. Hence no cycle of N_inf crosses a block
boundary and S(N_inf) = S(G - e). QED

So the additive part of the spectrum is carried entirely by the
CLOSING UP of the chain, which is finite and global. There is no
infinite object in which the semigroup is realised internally: the
semigroup lives on the inverse system {N_m} with its covering maps
N_{km} -> N_m, not on any limit of it. That is a precise statement of
why the family's additive structure cannot be internalised, and it
is the same fact from the other side that makes (N3) silent in
474.3: the object Theorem A applies to is not a limit of local data.

### 474.5 THE SECOND EXIT: INTERNAL ADDITIVITY IS THE SIMPLICITY GAP

The remaining exit of Theorem 474.4 is to make one graph's own
spectrum additive within its window:

  (SEMI)  for all a, b in S(G) with a + b <= c(G),  a + b in S(G),

where c(G) is the circumference.

THEOREM 474.5 (PROVED). Let G have minimum degree >= 3 and satisfy
(SEMI), and suppose G has a Bondy-Vince pair a < b (so |a-b| <= 2)
with 2ab <= c(G). Then G has a cycle whose length is a power of two.

PROOF. Let d = gcd(a,b), which divides |a-b|, so d is 1 or 2. Under
(SEMI) every value xa + yb that is at most c(G) lies in S(G): induct
on x + y, all partial sums of positive terms being at most the total.
By Sylvester every multiple of d exceeding F = ab/d - a - b lies in
<a,b>. Take r minimal with 2^r > F; then 2^r <= 2(F+1) <= 2ab <=
c(G), and r >= 1 so d divides 2^r. Hence 2^r is in S(G). QED

So on the internal exit the conjecture costs exactly (SEMI) plus a
QUANTITATIVE Bondy-Vince - a pair whose product is at most half the
circumference. The second half is open and is squarely inside (N7).
The first half is FALSE, and it fails at 473.3's adversary:

  THE TRUNCATED PETERSEN GRAPH REFUTES (SEMI). Its spectrum is
  exactly {3} U [10, 27] (30 vertices, girth 3, circumference 27,
  computed in tools/family484.py). So 3 is in S(G) and 3 + 3 = 6 is
  at most c(G), yet 6 is NOT in S(G). 473.3 measured A_6 = 45
  codewords of weight 6 in its cycle code with M_6 = 0 of them
  minimal - and 45 = C(10,2) is exactly the number of PAIRS OF
  DISJOINT TRIANGLES, one pair for each pair of the 10 vertices of
  the Petersen graph. The weight-6 element of the cycle space exists;
  it is not a cycle.

READING, AND IT IS THE SECTION'S FINDING. The external route and the
internal route fail at the SAME place, for the same reason. Addition
of cycle lengths is free in the CYCLE SPACE, where it is symmetric
difference of disjoint supports; it is not free in the SPECTRUM,
where the sum must be a single circuit. Externally the family buys
additivity with SIZE, and size is exactly what a minimality argument
needs. Internally it must buy it with SIMPLICITY, and simplicity is
exactly what 473.5 says is not for sale. 3 + 3 = 6 holds in the cycle
space of the truncated Petersen graph and fails in its spectrum: that
is the simplicity gap in its smallest possible instance, and it is
the whole obstruction.

The cycle semigroup is therefore the sharpest statement so far of
what this conjecture costs. Not a congruence, not a window, not a
level coupling: ONE ADDITION, REALISED BY ONE CYCLE.

### 474.6 STATUS

PROVED here: Lemma 474.0, the free closures of X and the flatness of
the subgraph order on cubic graphs; Lemma 1, the exact amalgam and
m-chain spectrum identity, together with its through-the-new-edge
form which licenses iteration; Lemma 2, gcd S(G) in {1,2} for
minimum degree >= 3, as a corollary of Bondy-Vince; THEOREM A, every
nonempty cycle semigroup contains a member with a power-of-two cycle;
Corollary 474.1, the explicit escape certificate at most 2n blocks
and 2n^2 vertices; THEOREM B, X is amalgamation-closed iff EG;
Theorem 474.4, additivity costs size; Proposition 474.4b, the
two-way infinite chain has S = S(G-e); Theorem 474.5, (SEMI) plus a
quantitative Bondy-Vince implies EG for G.

COMPUTED (tools/family484.py): Lemma 1 exact on 324 amalgam pairs and
on 111 chains of length 3 to 5, 0 violations, in both the full-
spectrum and the new-edge form; Lemma 2 on 13 graphs, 0 violations;
the escape certificate 2 or 3 blocks on every counterexample-shaped
spectrum in the zoo, with the four rows whose gcd is not a power of
two exhibited as the ones Lemma 2 forbids.

REFUTED here: (SEMI), by the truncated Petersen graph - spectrum
{3} U [10,27], so 3 is in S and 6 is not, though 6 < c = 27.

NEW STANDING NO-GO, to be carried with 472.0's seven.

  (N8) ADDITIVITY COSTS SIZE OR SIMPLICITY (474.4, 474.5). Any
       operation adding two cycle lengths either enlarges the graph,
       forfeiting every minimal-counterexample argument, or must
       realise the sum as a single circuit, which is 473.5's
       simplicity gap. The only closures X provably has - union,
       subgraph, Whitney - are all spectrum-flat, and the subgraph
       order is flat outright on cubic graphs. Any future proposal
       to give the FAMILY an algebraic structure must say which of
       these two prices it pays.

NOT PROVED: J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. The family of graphs CAN be
made into a single object, and the right object is a CYCLE
SEMIGROUP - a class of minimum-degree-3 graphs closed under edge
amalgamation. That object satisfies J7 unconditionally, by a
three-step proof whose only inputs are one exact spectrum identity
and Bondy-Vince's gcd corollary, and it is the first criterion in
this archive on which all seven standing no-goes are silent: it
defeats (N3) by being global over finite graphs, and (N4) by trading
window ratio for number of summands. What it does not do is close.
"The counterexample class is closed under edge amalgamation" is
equivalent to the conjecture, the failure of closure is an explicit
certificate of at most 2n blocks, and the internal repair (SEMI) is
refuted by the truncated Petersen graph. The object is found; the
family is provably not it unless the conjecture is true; and the one
addition that would make it so is 473.5's simplicity gap, now met
for the fifth time and for the first time as a single arithmetic
sum.


## 475. THE CHAIN DESCENT: 474's ENGINE RUN DOWNWARD

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. 474 proved (N8): additivity costs
SIZE, and size is exactly what a minimal-counterexample argument
needs, so the chain was useless as an attack. This section observes
that the cost is affordable in one place - when the block being
chained is SMALL - and turns the same engine into a DESCENT. It
lands on the archive's own named load-bearing open step (section 3:
"the load-bearing open step in the whole programme is the reduction
of EG-for-cubic to EG-for-cyclically-4-edge-connected-cubic") and
settles the 2-edge-cut notch of it up to an explicitly identified
surviving configuration. 475.3 PROVES the method's reach is exactly
the narrow blocks; 475.4 explains why the 3-cut is genuinely harder
and what the difference is.

### 475.0 THE OBSERVATION

Let G be a counterexample of MINIMUM order n. Minimality gives EG for
every graph on fewer than n vertices. The m-block chain of 474 over a
block on n_1 vertices has m*n_1 vertices. So

    m * n_1  <  n   ==>   the chain is not a counterexample.

The chain's spectrum is EXACTLY (474 Lemma 1) the block's own cycles
together with the m-fold sumset of its transit lengths. If the block
comes from inside G, its own cycles are cycles of G and are therefore
clean automatically. So the entire content lands on the sumset, and
the descent fires the moment that sumset misses the powers of two.

(N8) is not evaded, it is PAID: the enlargement is real, but it is
paid out of the gap between n_1 and n. That gap is the resource this
section spends, and it is the only place in the archive where
enlargement has ever been affordable.

DEFINITION (2-TERMINAL BLOCK, and its CHAIN). A 2-terminal block is a
triple (H; x, x') with x != x', every vertex other than x, x' of
degree >= 3 in H, and deg_H(x), deg_H(x') >= 2. Its TRANSIT SET is

    A(H; x, x')  =  { t + 1 : t is the length of an x-x' path in H } .

The m-CHAIN is m disjoint copies H_1, ..., H_m with the edges
x'_i x_{i+1} added cyclically. It is simple for m >= 2, and every
degree is at least 3: each terminal has degree >= 2 in its copy and
gains exactly one new edge.

LEMMA 475.0 (chain spectrum; this is 474's Lemma 1 restated so that
no edge is ever added to a block, which removes every simplicity
caveat). For m >= 2,

    S( m-chain )  =  S(H)  U  mA ,     A = A(H; x, x') ,

where mA is the m-fold sumset. PROOF. Each copy H_i meets the rest of
the chain in exactly two edges, at x_i and at x'_i. A cycle entering
H_i by one of them must leave by the other, so a cycle either stays
inside one copy - giving S(H) - or traverses every copy in turn,
contributing an x_i-x'_i path of length t_i in copy i plus one
connector, i.e. total sum over i of (t_i + 1). Conversely every such
choice of paths closes up. QED

### 475.1 THE DESCENT THEOREM

THEOREM 475.1 (CHAIN DESCENT). Let G be a counterexample of minimum
order n, and suppose G has a 2-edge-cut {x_1 y_1, x_2 y_2} with
x_1 != x_2 in V_1 and y_1 != y_2 in V_2. Put H = G[V_1], n_1 = |V_1|,
and A = A(H; x_1, x_2). Then

    for every m >= 2 with m * n_1 < n :   mA  meets  P .

PROOF. The m-chain over (H; x_1, x_2) is a simple graph of minimum
degree >= 3 on m*n_1 vertices, with spectrum S(H) U mA by Lemma
475.0. Now H = G[V_1] is a subgraph of G, so S(H) is a subset of S(G)
and is disjoint from P. If mA were also disjoint from P the chain
would be a counterexample on m*n_1 < n vertices, contradicting the
minimality of G. QED

Three remarks fix the picture.

  (a) G ITSELF IS THE 2-CHAIN of (G[V_1]; x_1,x_2) and
      (G[V_2]; y_1,y_2), so S(G) = S(G[V_1]) U S(G[V_2]) U (A_1 + A_2)
      and the hypothesis "G is a counterexample" is exactly
      "A_1 + A_2 misses P".
  (b) The usable range is m < n/n_1 = 1 + n_2/n_1, so the descent has
      room precisely when one side is much smaller than the other.
      It has NO room when the cut is balanced.
  (c) min A >= 2, with equality iff the two cut edges have adjacent
      feet inside V_1.

### 475.2 FOUR KILLS

Write alpha = min A, beta = max A, d = gcd(A - alpha), and note
alpha >= 2, beta <= n_1, d <= beta - alpha < n_1. Each kill below
exhibits an m with mA disjoint from P; by Theorem 475.1 the
configuration is then impossible provided m*n_1 < n. All are PROVED.

  (K0) EMPTY. If A is empty - x_1 and x_2 lie in different components
       of H - then mA is empty for every m, so the 2-chain is itself a
       counterexample. Kill at m = 2.
       REACH: 2 n_1 < n. So A is nonempty and alpha, beta, d are
       defined.

  (K1) SINGLETON. If |A| = 1, say A = {a}, then mA = {ma}, and
       3a is never a power of two. Kill at m = 3.
       REACH: 3 n_1 < n.

  (K2) ODD gcd. Let p be an odd prime dividing d. Every element of A
       is congruent to alpha mod d, hence mod p; so every element of
       pA is congruent to p*alpha, i.e. to 0, mod p. Thus pA lies in
       pZ and contains no power of two. Kill at m = p.
       REACH: p n_1 < n. Since every odd prime factor of d is at most
       d < n_1, a blanket sufficient condition is n_1^2 < n.

  (K3) NARROW. Suppose beta < 2 alpha. The set of m for which
       [m alpha, m beta] contains a power of two is the union over r
       of the intervals [2^r/beta, 2^r/alpha]; since beta < 2 alpha
       these are pairwise disjoint, with gaps
           (2^r/alpha, 2^(r+1)/beta),
       of length 2^r (2 alpha - beta)/(alpha beta).
       Taking r least with 2^r >= 2 alpha beta/(2 alpha - beta) makes
       the gap longer than 1, so it contains an integer m, and then
       [m alpha, m beta] lies strictly inside (2^r, 2^(r+1)) and
       mA, being a subset of that interval, misses P. Kill at
           m  <=  8 alpha / (2 alpha - beta) .
       REACH: that m times n_1 below n; blanket 8 n_1^2 < n. In
       practice far cheaper - see 475.3.

  (K4) 2-ADIC. Suppose d = 2^s with s > v_2(alpha). Every element of
       mA is congruent to m*alpha mod 2^s. A power of two 2^r in mA
       with r >= s forces 2^s | m*alpha, i.e. 2^(s - v_2(alpha)) | m;
       and one with r < s forces 2^r >= m*alpha, i.e. m <= 2^(s-1)/alpha.
       So any m exceeding 2^(s-1)/alpha and not divisible by
       2^(s - v_2(alpha)) kills. Such an m exists below
       2^(s-1)/alpha + 2^s < n_1/4 + n_1.
       REACH: blanket 5 n_1^2 / 4 < n.

COROLLARY 475.2. In a minimal counterexample, every 2-edge-cut whose
small side satisfies 8 n_1^2 < n has

    |A| >= 2,   gcd(A - min A) a power of two dividing min A,
    and   max A  >=  2 min A .

That is: the small side of a small 2-edge-cut must be WIDE. Its
longest transit is at least twice its shortest.

### 475.3 SHARPNESS: THE METHOD REACHES EXACTLY THE NARROW BLOCKS

THEOREM 475.3. If beta >= 2 alpha then [m alpha, m beta] contains a
power of two for EVERY m >= 1.
PROOF. The interval contains [m alpha, 2 m alpha], and for any x >= 1
the least power of two that is at least x is at most 2x. It is at
least 4 because m alpha >= 2, and when m alpha = 2 the interval
reaches 4 anyway. QED

So the interval test - the only test available once the congruence
tests (K2), (K4) are exhausted - fires if and only if the block is
narrow. The dichotomy of Corollary 475.2 is therefore not an artefact
of the proof: it is the exact reach of the method.

COMPUTED (tools/descent485.py). For every graph of the zoo and every
edge, A = the transit set, and the least m <= 64 with mA disjoint
from P. Worst edge shown; alpha, beta, d as above.

    block            n   alpha  beta   d   least m   verdict
    K4               4     3      4    1      3      narrow, fires
    K33              6     4      6    2      5      narrow, fires
    Petersen        10     5      9    1      7      narrow, fires
    prism-3          6     3      6    1      -      WIDE
    cube             8     4      8    2      -      WIDE
    prism-4          8     4      8    2      -      WIDE
    prism-5         10     4     10    1      -      WIDE
    Heawood         14     6     14    2      -      WIDE
    Moebius-Kantor  16     6     16    2      -      WIDE
    Pappus          18     6     18    2      -      WIDE
    Desargues       20     6     20    2      -      WIDE
    Dodecahedron    20     5     20    1      -      WIDE

Twelve blocks, twelve agreements: the descent fires on exactly the
three narrow ones and on none of the nine wide ones, and where it
fires it fires EARLY - m = 3, 5, 7 against the proved bounds 6, 8, 20
from (K3). So the reach requirement in practice is about m <= 7, i.e.
7 n_1 < n, not the blanket 8 n_1^2 < n.

The nine wide rows also show why: beta = 2 alpha exactly, or more, in
every one of them. A block on n_1 vertices whose shortest transit is
alpha has beta up to n_1, so wideness is the generic state as soon as
n_1 >= 2 alpha. That is the same fact section 3b recorded from the
other side - "cubicity works against you: the terminals have degree 2
and every internal vertex has degree 3, so a gadget with a cycle in
it offers many internally disjoint routes of differing lengths".

### 475.4 WHY THE 3-CUT IS DIFFERENT, AND IT IS NOT A DETAIL

The 2-cut chain is RIGID: by Lemma 475.0 a crossing cycle must
traverse EVERY block, because each copy meets the rest in exactly two
edges. Hence the crossing spectrum is the single sumset mA, and it
can be made to miss P.

At a cyclic 3-edge-cut the substitution D(M,H) of section 3b attaches
each gadget by THREE edges, so a cycle may enter a gadget, leave it,
and SKIP others through the base. The crossing spectrum is therefore
the UNION over s of the s-fold sumsets, and 3b PROVED those bands
merge from s = 2 onward whenever the transit set is an interval,
giving a full integer interval - which contains a power of two. In
other words:

  at a 2-cut the constructed graph can be a counterexample, and the
  descent has something to contradict;
  at a 3-cut the constructed graph is forced NOT to be one, and there
  is nothing to contradict.

The rigidity that makes the 2-cut chain a descent engine is exactly
what the 3-cut lacks. This is a structural reason, not a gap in
effort, and it says where the load-bearing step will have to be
attacked from: the 3-cut reduction cannot be done by substitution at
all, because substitution destroys the very cleanliness the descent
needs.

### 475.5 STATUS

PROVED here: Lemma 475.0, the chain spectrum in terminal form, with
every simplicity caveat removed; THEOREM 475.1, the chain descent -
in a minimal counterexample, every 2-edge-cut with small side n_1
forces mA to meet P for all m with m n_1 < n; the four kills (K1)
singleton, (K2) odd gcd, (K3) narrow, (K4) 2-adic, each with its
explicit reach; COROLLARY 475.2, the small side of a small 2-edge-cut
must be wide with 2-power gcd dividing its minimum; THEOREM 475.3,
the interval test fires if and only if the block is narrow, so the
dichotomy is the exact reach of the method.

COMPUTED (tools/descent485.py): the least firing m over 12 zoo blocks
and every edge of each; the narrow/wide dichotomy holds 12 out of 12,
with firing at m = 3, 5, 7 well inside the proved bounds.

NOT PROVED: the wide case; the 3-cut notch; J7; the five statements
of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED. 474's engine, proved useless
upward by (N8), runs DOWNWARD on the small side of a 2-edge-cut,
because chaining a small block keeps the result below a minimal
counterexample's order. That gives the first genuine progress in this
archive on the named load-bearing step: in a minimal counterexample
the small side of any sufficiently unbalanced 2-edge-cut must be
WIDE, with transit set of 2-power gcd - singleton, odd-gcd and narrow
small sides are all impossible. The reach is proved sharp: the method
sees exactly the narrow blocks. What survives is the wide case, which
is also the generic case, and the 3-cut, which 475.4 shows cannot be
reached by this construction at all because substitution merges the
bands and destroys the cleanliness a descent needs.


## 476. THE J7 FAMILY AS AN OBJECT: COMPLETE EAR SYSTEMS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. This section corrects
474-475's scope (374.1, loudly) and then does for J7 what 474 did for
EG: names an object that satisfies J7 by its own structure, PROVES
that first, and reduces J7 to the single statement that the family is
that object. The correction matters because 475 in particular is
VACUOUS on J7, and its framing invited the opposite conclusion.

### 476.0 CORRECTION (374.1): 474 AND 475 WERE BUILT FOR EG, NOT J7

  (i) 474's object - a class of minimum-degree-3 graphs closed under
      edge amalgamation - has as its subject X, the class of EG
      counterexamples. J7's family is not X; it is the class of
      (a)-(f) configurations of 433.4 as corrected by 434.1. Theorem
      A of 474 is a theorem about EG's family. Nothing in 474 was
      claimed for J7 and nothing should be read into it for J7,
      except 476.1 below.

 (ii) 475 IS VACUOUS ON J7. Theorem 475.1 assumes a 2-EDGE-CUT. By
      433.4 the J7 configuration lives in a cubic 3-CONNECTED graph,
      and a cubic graph is 3-connected if and only if it is
      3-edge-connected, so it has no 2-edge-cut at all. 475 speaks
      about the architecture's GAP 2 of section 3f ("bridgeless, not
      3-connected"); J7 lives in GAP 3 ("3-connected, general"), of
      which the architecture itself says "Gap 3 is the one that
      matters".

(iii) 475's claim to land on "the named load-bearing open step" is
      WRONG. That step (section 3) is the reduction of EG-for-cubic
      to EG-for-cyclically-4-EDGE-CONNECTED-cubic - the cyclic
      3-edge-cut notch - and 475.4 proves this construction cannot
      reach it. 475 does the 2-edge-cut notch, a different one.

The MATHEMATICS of 475 is unaffected: Lemma 475.0, Theorem 475.1, the
five kills and the sharpness theorem stand as proved. Its correct
description is narrower and still worth having: PROVED kills on Gap
2, valid at every order, complementing the Leaf Database of section
3f, which is a finite verification (12,783,477 pairs, |H| <= 20) and
open above it. It is not progress on J7.

### 476.1 THE ONE THING J7 INHERITS FROM 474, AND IT IS THE POINT

474.5's finding was that the conjecture costs ONE ADDITION REALISED
BY ONE CYCLE, and that the internal form (SEMI) is false in general.
On the J7 branch that bill is ALREADY PAID, by a theorem the archive
proved long ago. Quoting 451.1(2) verbatim:

  "One-Step Theorem (446.2): every circuit meeting C is C with a
   laminar, disjoint-arc, distinct-foot ear family attached; the
   entire cycle spectrum is {L + sum delta} over such families.
   207672/207672."

So for a J7 configuration

    S(G)  =  L + D ,     D = { sum_{e in F} delta_e : F admissible } ,

with 0 in D (the empty family gives C itself). D is a set of SUBSET
SUMS. That is exactly the additivity 474 had to buy with size and
(N8) said could not be had for free - and here 446.2 gives it inside
a single graph, because the admissibility conditions are precisely a
certificate that the sum IS a single circuit.

THIS IS WHY J7, NOT EG, IS THE RIGHT PLACE FOR THE OBJECT. On the EG
branch the simplicity gap blocks the addition; on the J7 branch the
One-Step Theorem discharges it, and what remains is arithmetic on D.

DEFINITION (EAR SYSTEM). A quadruple (L; E, delta, K) where E is a
finite set, delta : E -> Z, and K is a DOWNWARD-CLOSED family of
subsets of E containing every singleton. Its shift set is
D = {sum_F delta : F in K} and its spectrum is Spec = L + D. Every
J7 configuration yields one, by 446.2, and admissibility is downward
closed because a sub-family of a laminar, disjoint-arc, distinct-foot
family is again one.

### 476.2 THE OBJECT, AND THE PROOF THAT IT SATISFIES J7

DEFINITION (COMPLETE EAR SYSTEM, at scale g). Let g be a power of two
dividing L. The ear system is COMPLETE at scale g if some F in K,
with shifts sorted a_1 <= a_2 <= ... <= a_k, satisfies

    (C1)  every a_i is a positive multiple of g, and a_1 = g;
    (C2)  a_{j+1} <= g + sum_{i <= j} a_i   for every j < k;
    (C3)  sum_{i <= k} a_i  >=  L.

FILLING LEMMA (PROVED; the finite, scaled form of Brown's
completeness criterion for sequences). Under (C1)-(C2) the subset sums
of a_1, ..., a_k cover EVERY multiple of g in [0, S_k], where
S_j = sum_{i <= j} a_i.

  PROOF by induction on j. For j = 1 the subset sums are {0, g},
  which is every multiple of g in [0, g]. Assume the subset sums of
  a_1..a_j cover every multiple of g in [0, S_j]. Adjoining a_{j+1}
  adds the translate a_{j+1} + (multiples of g in [0, S_j]), i.e.
  every multiple of g in [a_{j+1}, a_{j+1} + S_j]. The first multiple
  of g not already covered is S_j + g, and (C2) gives
  a_{j+1} <= S_j + g, so the two ranges abut or overlap and the union
  is every multiple of g in [0, S_{j+1}]. QED

THEOREM A(J7). A complete ear system has a power of two in its
spectrum.

  PROOF. All subsets of F are admissible (K is downward closed), so
  D contains every subset sum of a_1..a_k, hence by the Filling Lemma
  every multiple of g in [0, S_k]. Since g divides L,

      Spec = L + D  contains every multiple of g in [L, L + S_k],

  and by (C3) that range contains [L, 2L]. Let 2^r be the least power
  of two with 2^r >= L; then 2^r <= 2L, because the least power of two
  at least x is at most 2x. Finally g = 2^s divides 2^r: g divides L
  so 2^s <= L <= 2^r, whence s <= r. Therefore 2^r lies in Spec, and
  2^r >= L >= 24, so it is a genuine power-of-two cycle length. QED

COROLLARY. No J7 configuration has a complete ear system: (C1)-(C3)
contradict condition (f) of 433.4/434.1. Hence

    THEOREM B(J7) (the main work).  Every J7 ear system is complete
    at some scale g.  This statement implies J7.

That is the whole reduction, and it is of the requested shape: the
OBJECT ("complete ear system") satisfies J7 by structure, proved
before any graph is examined; what remains is to show the family is
one.

### 476.3 WHAT KIND OF OBJECT THIS IS, AND WHY IT IS A FAMILY STATEMENT

An ear system is a weighted downward-closed set family - a weighted
SIMPLICIAL COMPLEX on the ear set, with D the image of its faces
under the additive map F |-> sum_F delta. Completeness is not a
property of any one face; it is a property of the complex AS A WHOLE,
namely that the poset of faces is rich enough that its image has no
gap below L. So the family-of-graphs question the programme asked has
turned into: the J7 family maps functorially to weighted complexes,
and the object that settles J7 is the class of COMPLETE ones.

Three no-goes to check, since that is what 472.0 is for.

  (N8) SILENT, and this is the decisive difference from 474. (N8)
       says additivity costs size or simplicity. Here nothing is
       enlarged - the addition happens inside one fixed graph - and
       the simplicity is paid by 446.2, which is a theorem, not a
       hypothesis. J7 is the one branch of this problem where (N8)
       has no bill to present.
  (N6) SILENT. Completeness is not of the form "no power of two
       above t implies one below t"; it is a growth condition on a
       shift multiset and mentions no level.
  (N4) NOT SILENT, and this is the price. (C3) demands a shift total
       of at least L, i.e. it demands filling a window of ratio 2 -
       exactly what the Ratio Theorem says the trace frame cannot
       supply. The resource here is different (subset sums of the
       432.4 ear supply, not geodesic counts), so (N4) does not
       apply as a theorem, but it is a warning that (C3) is where
       the weight sits.

### 476.4 THE STANDING WARNING: SECTION 3d, AND WHICH OF ITS THREE
### DIAGNOSES TRANSFER

Section 3d recorded a REFUTED conjecture of exactly this family: "for
a longest cycle C of a 3-connected cubic graph, some family of
pairwise independent ears has all decrements delta_i <= 2 and sum
delta_i >= c/2". It was refuted by every Hamiltonian cubic graph of
girth >= 5, with the Heawood graph as witness, and three design
errors were diagnosed. Theorem B(J7) must be judged against them.

  (D1) "Decrements off a longest cycle are large, not small."
       DOES NOT TRANSFER VERBATIM. 3d's C is a LONGEST cycle, so
       every ear is a CHORD, |P| = 1, and girth >= 5 forces decrement
       at least g - 2. J7's C is the SHORTEST island member, with
       L <= 2 sqrt(n), and by 449.1 every ear has interior d > L/2:
       these are long bridges through the rest of the graph, not
       chords, and a balanced ear (d = a + 1, shift 1) is not
       excluded by 3d's Proposition. This is the hypothesis (C1)
       needs, and it is OPEN, not refuted. It must be checked, not
       assumed.
  (D2) "Independence is scarce." DOES NOT TRANSFER. 3d's setting had
       at most c/3 bridges and Petersen had exactly one usable
       exchange. J7's setting has 432.4, which PROVES a supply of at
       least L/3 ears with disjoint interiors. The resource 3d
       lacked is a theorem here.
  (D3) "Crossing ears are the ones that matter." TRANSFERS, and it is
       the live risk. 446.2 licenses LAMINAR, disjoint-arc,
       distinct-foot families only, while J7's surviving branch is
       the BRAIDED - i.e. crossing - core (433, 436). If completeness
       can only be realised by crossing families, 446.2 does not
       license the sum as a single circuit and the simplicity gap
       re-opens inside J7.

So Theorem B(J7) enters with two of the three historical failure
modes disarmed by theorems already on the ledger, and one live. That
is the honest position, and (D3) is where the next work goes.

### 476.5 STATUS

PROVED here: the Filling Lemma, the finite scaled form of Brown's
completeness criterion, elementary and self-contained; THEOREM A(J7),
a complete ear system has a power of two in its spectrum; the
corollary that Theorem B(J7) - every J7 ear system is complete -
implies J7.

CORRECTED (374.1, loudly): 474 and 475 are statements about EG's
counterexample class, not about J7. 475.1 is VACUOUS on J7, whose
ambient graph is cubic 3-connected and therefore 3-edge-connected;
475 addresses GAP 2 of the section 3f architecture while J7 is GAP 3;
and 475's claim to address the named load-bearing open step is
withdrawn, that step being the cyclic 3-edge-cut notch which 475.4
itself proves unreachable by that construction.

IDENTIFIED: 446.2 is the reason J7, and not EG, is where this object
belongs - the One-Step Theorem discharges 473.5's simplicity gap on
this branch by certifying that an admissible sum of ear shifts IS a
single circuit. (N8) therefore has nothing to charge here, which no
other branch of the programme can say.

NOT PROVED: Theorem B(J7); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked for a
single object whose structure settles J7, the answer is the COMPLETE
EAR SYSTEM: a weighted downward-closed complex whose shift multiset
starts at a power of two dividing L, never more than doubles, and
totals at least L. Theorem A(J7) proves such an object cannot satisfy
condition (f), so J7 reduces exactly to showing every J7 ear system
is complete. The reduction is legitimate rather than circular because
the additivity it needs is supplied by 446.2 rather than assumed, and
it is the only place in this programme where (N8) presents no bill.
The three conditions are not equally hard: (C2), the doubling
condition, is a statement about the shape of the shift multiset;
(C3), the total, is where (N4)'s ratio-2 weight sits; and (C1), the
small starting shift, is precisely what section 3d refuted for a
LONGEST cycle and what remains open for J7's SHORT one.


## 477. TOWARDS THEOREM B(J7): THE ARC BUDGET

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED, Theorem B(J7) UNPROVED.
This section attacks Theorem B(J7) - "every J7 ear system is
complete" - and does three things. It records loudly that Theorem
B(J7) is EQUIVALENT to J7, not merely sufficient for it (477.0). It
PROVES the first quantitative theorem in the archive about the SIZES
of J7's ear shifts, the Arc Budget (477.1). And it uses that theorem
to PROVE a hard scope limit on 476's route: Brown-completeness at a
scale dividing L forces m <= 23, so 476's Theorem A as stated can
never reach the tail m >= 25 (477.2). 477.3 diagnoses why, and
repairs Theorem A into a form the Arc Budget does not cap.

### 477.0 CORRECTION (374.1): THEOREM B(J7) IS EQUIVALENT TO J7

476 presented Theorem B(J7) as "the main work" implying J7. It should
have said, as 474 did for its own Theorem B, that the implication
runs both ways:

  Theorem B(J7) => J7 by Theorem A(J7); and J7 => Theorem B(J7)
  vacuously, since if no J7 configuration exists then every J7 ear
  system is complete by emptiness.

So Theorem B(J7) IS J7. That does not make the reduction worthless -
it converts a configuration-existence question into a growth
condition on a multiset of integers, which is a different kind of
object - but it does mean no proof of J7 can be obtained by
"verifying" Theorem B on anything short of the full family. Recorded
so no later session mistakes the reduction for progress.

### 477.1 THE ARC BUDGET THEOREM (PROVED)

Fix a J7 configuration: C the shortest island member, L = |C| = 2^t m
with t >= 3 and m odd >= 3. Two facts already on the ledger:

  449.1(a), PROVED: strict local minimality holds on BOTH arcs, so
  every ear has d > a and d > L - a.
  446.2, PROVED: an admissible family has pairwise DISJOINT chosen
  arcs and pairwise distinct feet, and the composite length is
  L + sum of shifts, where an ear replacing its chosen arc alpha
  contributes sigma = d - alpha.

THEOREM (ARC BUDGET). Let F be an admissible family with chosen arcs
alpha_1, ..., alpha_k and shifts sigma_i = d_i - alpha_i. Then for
every theta in (0,1),

    #{ i : sigma_i <= theta L }   <   2/(1 - theta)  +  1 .

  PROOF. The chosen arcs are pairwise disjoint arcs of C, so their
  lengths sum to at most L; in particular AT MOST ONE of them exceeds
  L/2. Discard that one if present. For every remaining index,
  alpha_i <= L/2, so L - alpha_i >= alpha_i, and 449.1(a) gives
  d_i > L - alpha_i, whence

      sigma_i  =  d_i - alpha_i  >  (L - alpha_i) - alpha_i
               =  L - 2 alpha_i .

  Therefore sigma_i <= theta L forces alpha_i > (1 - theta) L / 2.
  Disjoint arcs of total length at most L admit fewer than
  L / ((1 - theta) L / 2) = 2/(1 - theta) arcs of that size. Adding
  back the discarded index gives the bound. QED

Two instances, which are the ones used below:

  theta = 1/3 :  at most 3 ears of an admissible family have shift
                 below L/3.
  theta = 1/2 :  at most 4 ears have shift at most L/2.

COROLLARY (CONCENTRATION). Summing sigma_i > L - 2 alpha_i over the
at most one long arc and the rest, and using sum alpha_i <= L,

    sum_{i} sigma_i   >   (k - 2) L ,

so an admissible family of k ears has average shift exceeding
(1 - 2/k) L. THE SHIFTS OF AN ADMISSIBLE FAMILY ARE CONCENTRATED
JUST BELOW AND ABOVE L, not spread over [1, L].

This is the first statement in the archive about the MAGNITUDE of the
ear shifts. Everything before it - 432.3, 432.6, 444, 447 - is about
their VALUATION. The two are independent, and the magnitude side
turns out to be the binding one for 476.

### 477.2 THE SCOPE LIMIT ON 476's THEOREM A (PROVED)

Recall 476's completeness conditions at scale g, g a power of two
DIVIDING L: sorted shifts sigma_1 <= ... <= sigma_k with (C1) all
multiples of g and sigma_1 = g; (C2) sigma_{j+1} <= g + sum_{i<=j}
sigma_i; (C3) sum sigma_i >= L.

THEOREM. A J7 ear system that is complete at a scale g dividing L has
m <= 23.

  PROOF. Since g divides L = 2^t m with m odd and g is a power of
  two, g <= 2^t = L/m.

  Case k >= 4. Iterating (C2) from sigma_1 = g gives sigma_2 <= 2g,
  sigma_3 <= 4g, sigma_4 <= 8g. By the Arc Budget at theta = 1/3, at
  most 3 shifts lie below L/3, so sigma_4 >= L/3. Hence 8g >= L/3,
  i.e. g >= L/24. Combined with g <= L/m this gives m <= 24, so
  m <= 23 as m is odd.

  Case k <= 3. The subset sums number at most 2^k <= 8, and
  completeness requires them to cover every multiple of g in
  [0, Sigma], which needs Sigma/g + 1 <= 8, i.e. Sigma <= 7g. With
  (C3), L <= Sigma <= 7g <= 7L/m, so m <= 7. QED

So 476's route, exactly as stated, is capped at m <= 23 and can never
reach the tail. It is not vacuous - m = 3, the branch 445.6 Theorem I
and the t = 3 boards of 440/442 are about, sits well inside the cap -
but it is not a proof of J7, and 476 should not be read as offering
one.

### 477.3 THE DIAGNOSIS, AND THE REPAIR

WHY IT CAPS. Brown's criterion needs the multiset to START SMALL and
then grow at most geometrically. The Arc Budget says the opposite:
small shifts are structurally scarce, because a small shift needs a
long chosen arc (sigma > L - 2 alpha), and the arcs of an admissible
family live in a budget of total length L. At most three ears can be
small; every further ear is at least L/3, and on average they are
just under L. J7's shift multiset is CONCENTRATED, and Brown's
criterion is a hypothesis about SPREAD multisets. The mismatch is
structural, not incidental.

WHAT COMPLETENESS ACTUALLY NEEDED. Theorem A(J7) only ever used
completeness to conclude that the shift set D contains a long enough
run. The clean form drops g altogether:

  THEOREM A(J7)'' (PROVED). If D contains every integer of some
  interval [X, 2X + L], then Spec = L + D contains a power of two.
  PROOF. L + D contains [L + X, 2(L + X)], and for any y >= 1 the
  least power of two at least y is at most 2y. QED

This hypothesis is not capped by the Arc Budget, and the reason is
the point of the section:

  FINE GRANULARITY COMES FROM SHIFTS THAT ARE CLOSE TOGETHER, NOT
  FROM SHIFTS THAT ARE SMALL.

A family of ears whose shifts are sigma, sigma+1, sigma+2, ... has
subset sums of size j filling an interval of length about j, no
matter how large sigma is; the Arc Budget forbids small sigma and
says nothing whatever about small DIFFERENCES. Indeed the Arc Budget
pushes towards closeness: with sum alpha_i <= L and k ears, most arcs
are short, so most shifts sit in the narrow band (L - 2 alpha_max, L),
and a narrow band of many shifts is exactly a source of small
differences.

AND ONE SMALL DIFFERENCE IS FREE. By 474's Lemma 2 (the Bondy-Vince
gcd corollary), S(G) contains two lengths differing by 1 or 2; since
S(G) = L + D by 446.2, D contains two elements differing by 1 or 2.
If G is bipartite the difference is exactly 2 and D lies in 2Z.

So the repaired target is:

  THEOREM B(J7)'' - the shift differences of J7's admissible families
  generate a run of length 2X + L - X = X + L inside D.

which is a statement about the DIFFERENCE set of a concentrated
multiset rather than about the multiset itself. That is the right
next question, and it is not the one 476 asked.

### 477.4 STATUS

PROVED here: the ARC BUDGET THEOREM - in any admissible family, fewer
than 2/(1-theta) + 1 ears have shift at most theta L, so at most 3
lie below L/3 and at most 4 at or below L/2; its CONCENTRATION
corollary, sum sigma_i > (k-2) L, so the average shift of an
admissible k-family exceeds (1 - 2/k) L; the SCOPE LIMIT, that
Brown-completeness at a scale dividing L forces m <= 23; and THEOREM
A(J7)'', the g-free interval form.

CORRECTED (374.1, loudly): 476 presented Theorem B(J7) as sufficient
for J7 without recording that it is EQUIVALENT to J7. It is. And
476's completeness hypothesis, though sound, is capped at m <= 23 by
the Arc Budget; the route as stated cannot reach the tail.

IDENTIFIED: the Arc Budget is the first statement in this archive
about the MAGNITUDE of ear shifts rather than their valuation, and it
is the binding constraint on 476. Its content is that J7's shift
multiset is CONCENTRATED just below and above L. Concentration defeats
Brown, whose hypothesis is spread; but concentration FEEDS the
difference-based form, because many shifts in a narrow band is exactly
a supply of small differences.

NOT PROVED: Theorem B(J7) in any form; J7; the five statements of
451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Theorem B(J7)
was set as the target and it is not proved; what this section
establishes is where it can and cannot be attacked. Theorem B(J7) is
equivalent to J7, so it cannot be verified piecemeal. The completeness
form of 476 is capped at m <= 23 by a new proved theorem about the
arc budget, which shows J7's shifts are concentrated near L rather
than spread from 1 to L. The same concentration that kills the
completeness form is what makes the difference form plausible, and
Theorem A(J7)'' is stated in that form, free of the scale g and
uncapped. The honest position is that the object of 476 is correct
and its hypothesis was the wrong one; the next attempt should be on
the difference set, with Bondy-Vince's guaranteed pair as its seed.


## 478. POST-MORTEM: WHY 474-477 DID NOT ANSWER THE QUESTION ASKED

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. This section records two
failures and proves that they were one failure. It contributes no new
mathematics about cycles; it contributes a no-go about a METHOD, and
that no-go is what any future attempt at the same question must clear.

THE QUESTION THAT WAS ASKED. Take the FAMILY of graphs satisfying or
failing J7, equip it with structure, and find a single mathematical
object - a group, a topology, a manifold, an algebra - such that:
  (A) the object satisfies J7 by its own structure, PROVED FIRST;
  (B) the remaining work is showing the family IS such an object,
      and (B) should be strictly easier than J7.

### 478.0 FAILURE 1 (474, 475): WRONG FAMILY

474 built its object - the CYCLE SEMIGROUP, a class closed under edge
amalgamation - over X, the class of Erdos-Gyarfas counterexamples.
That is not J7's family. J7's family is the class of (a)-(f)
configurations of 433.4 as corrected by 434.1.

475 compounded it. Theorem 475.1 assumes a 2-EDGE-CUT, and J7's
ambient graph is cubic 3-connected, hence 3-edge-connected: the
hypothesis is VACUOUS on J7. 476.0 recorded that correction.

Root cause: the family was never written down before an object was
chosen. The nearest tractable family was substituted for the one
asked about.

### 478.1 FAILURE 2 (476, 477): RIGHT FAMILY, WRONG KIND OF OBJECT

476 did use J7's family, and the object - the COMPLETE EAR SYSTEM -
was correctly built on 446.2's One-Step Theorem, which is the right
piece of structure to build on. Theorem A(J7) was proved in three
lines. But Theorem B(J7) turned out to be EQUIVALENT to J7 (477.0),
so nothing was gained: (A) was easy exactly to the extent that (B)
absorbed the whole difficulty. 477 then proved the Arc Budget, which
caps that route at m <= 23 - a genuine theorem, but a theorem about
why the route is too narrow, not a step along it.

### 478.2 THE TWO FAILURES ARE ONE: THE CONCLUSION-DEFINED FAMILY TRAP

THEOREM (PROVED). Let S be a statement about objects satisfying
hypotheses H, and let

    F  =  { X : X satisfies H and X violates S }

be the class of COUNTEREXAMPLES to S. Let Pi be ANY property, of
members of F or of F itself, for which the following holds:

    (A)  Pi  implies  some member of F satisfies S.

Then

    (B)  "F has Pi"   is equivalent to   S .

PROOF. Assume (B). By (A) some member of F satisfies S; but every
member of F violates S by definition, so F is empty, which is S.
Conversely if S holds then F is empty and Pi holds of F vacuously.
QED

The theorem does not mention cycles, powers of two, ears or graphs.
It says: WHENEVER THE FAMILY IS DEFINED AS THE COUNTEREXAMPLES, THE
TWO-STEP SCHEME COLLAPSES, FOR EVERY CHOICE OF OBJECT. The cleverness
of the object is irrelevant; the collapse is forced by the shape of
the definition. Both failures are instances:

  474: F = X, Pi = "closed under edge amalgamation". B <=> EG.
  476: F = the (a)-(f) configurations, Pi = "complete ear system".
       B <=> J7.

This is (N6) - the schema collapse of 471.0 - in a new costume.
471.0 said every LEVEL-COUPLING statement is equivalent to the
conjecture. 478.2 says every OBJECT-HOOD statement about the
counterexample family is too, and for a reason that has nothing to do
with levels. Record it as a strengthening.

  (N9) THE CONCLUSION-DEFINED FAMILY TRAP (478.2). No property of
       the counterexample class can be both sufficient for the
       conjecture and easier than it. Any "the family is an object
       O" programme must first replace the counterexample class by a
       family whose definition does not mention the conclusion.

### 478.3 WHAT THE FIX HAS TO BE

J7's conditions split into two kinds, and 474-477 never made the
split:

  STRUCTURAL, satisfied by graphs that DO have power-of-two cycles:
    (a) C chordless, isometric, every ear exceeds both arcs;
    (c) the >= L/3 ear supply is braided;
    (e) the packing shell.
  AVOIDANCE, which are the conclusion in disguise:
    (b) every ear shift dodges 0 mod 2^t;
    (d) all composite values dodge valuation exactly t;
    (f) G has no cycle of length 2^k.

The family to equip with structure is the STRUCTURAL one - all
(a)+(c)+(e) configurations, most of which are perfectly ordinary
graphs with power-of-two cycles. On that family:

    (A) must become a substantive theorem: every object of type O has
        a power-of-two cycle. It will NOT be three lines, and it
        should be an application of known mathematics rather than a
        definition unpacked.
    (B) becomes a verification against GEOMETRY - do (a), (c), (e)
        force O-hood? - and a verification against geometry can be
        strictly easier than J7, because the geometry is not the
        conclusion.

The burden has to sit somewhere. 474-477 put it all on (B) and (B)
became the conjecture. The correct architecture puts the burden on
(A), where known mathematics can be brought to bear, and leaves (B) a
structural check. THE TEST TO APPLY TO ANY PROPOSED OBJECT: do its
DEFINING AXIOMS mention cycle lengths, shifts, valuations or powers
of two? If yes, it will collapse by 478.2. Sylow does not mention
powers of two; it produces them.

### 478.4 WHAT SURVIVES FROM 474-477

Not everything is withdrawn. These stand as proved and independent of
the failed architecture:

  474 Lemma 1, the exact amalgam/chain spectrum identity, machine
      verified; Lemma 2, gcd S(G) in {1,2} at minimum degree 3, the
      Bondy-Vince gcd corollary - the first use of Bondy-Vince in the
      archive that does not ask it to be stronger than it is.
  475 Lemma 475.0 and the five kills, correctly rescoped in 476.0 as
      proved kills on GAP 2 of the section 3f architecture.
  476 The identification that 446.2 discharges 473.5's simplicity gap
      on the J7 branch: an admissible sum of ear shifts IS a single
      circuit. This is why J7, not EG, is where an additive object
      belongs, and it survives the collapse of the object built on it.
  477 THE ARC BUDGET THEOREM and its concentration corollary - the
      first statement in this archive about the MAGNITUDE of ear
      shifts rather than their valuation. J7's shifts are concentrated
      just below and above L. This is a fact about the structural
      family, not about the counterexample family, so 478.2 does not
      touch it, and it is the one piece of 474-477 that the corrected
      architecture can build on.
  477 Theorem A(J7)'', the g-free interval form.

### 478.5 STATUS

PROVED here: 478.2, the conclusion-defined family trap, recorded as
standing no-go (N9).

RECORDED (374.1): two failures. FAILURE 1 (474, 475) answered a
question about EG when the question was about J7, and 475's central
hypothesis is vacuous on J7. FAILURE 2 (476, 477) used the right
family but an object whose defining property was an unpacking of the
conclusion, so Theorem A was easy and Theorem B was the conjecture.
By 478.2 the second failure was not bad luck - it was forced.

NOT PROVED: J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The programme
asked for an object that settles J7 with the residual work in showing
the family is that object. Two attempts failed, and 478.2 proves they
failed for one reason: both equipped the COUNTEREXAMPLE class, whose
definition already contains the conclusion, so object-hood was
equivalent to the conjecture no matter what object was chosen. The
correction is not a better object but a better family: split (a)-(f)
into the structural conditions (a), (c), (e) and the avoidance
conditions (b), (d), (f), equip the structural family, and require of
any candidate object that its defining axioms mention no cycle
length, no shift, no valuation and no power of two.


## 479. THE STRUCTURAL FAMILY, WRITTEN DOWN; BRAID RIGIDITY; AND THE
## FIRST OBJECT REJECTED BY ITS OWN ACCEPTANCE TEST

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. This section executes
478.3 in order. It WRITES THE FAMILY DOWN before any object is
chosen (479.0); proves the first structure theorem about that family
- BRAID RIGIDITY, which says the braid of J7 is not an arbitrary
chord system but a MOBIUS LADDER (479.1); computes the numerics that
rigidity forces (479.2) and the cycle forms it carries (479.3); and
then applies 478.3's acceptance test to the object so obtained and
REJECTS IT, by an explicit twelve-rung witness that a reader can
check by hand (479.4). The rejection is the useful part: it names
the one ingredient any object built on the braid must import, and
where in the archive that ingredient already lives (479.5).

### 479.0 THE FAMILY (DEFINITION; NO OBJECT YET)

DEFINITION (STRUCTURAL J7 CONFIGURATION). A pair (G, C) with

  G cubic, 3-connected, of girth at least 5, on n vertices;
  C a cycle of G of length L with 24 <= L <= 2 sqrt(n);
  (a) C is chordless and isometric, and every ear of C is strictly
      longer than BOTH arcs of C between its two feet;
  (e) G fits the packing shell of 433.2/433.4.

Write F_str for the class of all structural J7 configurations.

Three things are ABSENT from that definition, deliberately: no t, no
2^t, no shift, no valuation, no condition (f). By 433.4 as corrected
by 434.1, a J7 configuration is a member of F_str that satisfies in
addition (b), (d), (f) and whose length factors as L = 2^t m. Hence

  THE REDUCTION. If every member of F_str has a cycle of length a
  power of two, then J7 holds.
  PROOF. A J7 configuration is a member of F_str carrying (f), which
  says exactly that it has no such cycle. QED

and, decisively, THE CONVERSE FAILS: F_str contains perfectly
ordinary graphs that do have power-of-two cycles, so "every member of
F_str has a power-of-two cycle" is strictly stronger than J7 and is
not implied by it. That is precisely what 478.2 demands of a usable
family, and it is the whole difference from 474-477:

  (N9) IS SILENT ON F_str. F_str is not the counterexample class of
  anything; its definition mentions no conclusion.

Condition (c) of 433.4 is deliberately NOT part of the definition.
Half of it is a theorem already - 432.4 proves unconditionally that a
chordless cycle in a cubic 3-connected graph carries at least L/3
ears with pairwise disjoint interiors and pairwise distinct feet - and
the other half, braiding, is a property of a SUBfamily. So braiding
enters below as a parameter, not as a hypothesis: for k >= 2 say that
(G, C) CARRIES A k-BRAID if some k of its ears are pairwise disjoint
in their interiors, have 2k distinct feet, and pairwise CROSS on C.

### 479.1 BRAID RIGIDITY (PROVED)

LEMMA (ANTIPODAL PATTERN). Let E_1, ..., E_k be ears of a cycle C
with 2k distinct feet, pairwise crossing. List the feet in cyclic
order around C as p_1, ..., p_{2k}. Then, after relabelling the ears,
E_i has feet p_i and p_{i+k} for i = 1, ..., k.

  PROOF. Fix one ear and let its feet cut the remaining 2k - 2 feet
  into two open arcs holding s and 2k - 2 - s of them. Every other
  ear crosses it, so contributes exactly one foot to each arc; there
  are k - 1 other ears, so s = k - 1. Thus every ear joins two feet
  that are exactly k apart in the cyclic order of feet, which is the
  stated pairing. QED

THEOREM (BRAID RIGIDITY). Let (G, C) carry a k-braid E_1, ..., E_k
with k >= 3 and put H = C union E_1 union ... union E_k. Then H is a
SUBDIVISION OF THE MOBIUS LADDER

    ML_k  =  Cay( Z/2k , { +1, -1, k } )

- the 2k-cycle with all k main diagonals - and every cycle of H is a
cycle of G.

  PROOF. By the Lemma the feet are p_1, ..., p_{2k} in cyclic order
  with E_i joining p_i to p_{i+k}. The 2k arcs of C cut by the feet
  are internally disjoint paths, the ear interiors are disjoint from
  C and from one another, and no vertex carries two feet; so
  suppressing the degree-2 vertices of H contracts each arc to one
  edge p_j p_{j+1} and each ear to one edge p_i p_{i+k}. That
  multigraph is ML_k, and it is simple for k >= 3. A subgraph's
  cycles are cycles of G. QED

REMARK. 432.5 does its spiral calculus under the HYPOTHESIS that the
feet appear in spiral order u_1 < ... < u_k < y_1 < ... < y_k. The
Lemma shows this is not a hypothesis at all: it is forced. The
braided core of J7 has one combinatorial shape and only one.

### 479.2 THE RIGID NUMERICS (PROVED)

Notation, fixed for the rest of the section. Feet p_1, ..., p_{2k} in
cyclic order; arc lengths a_j = d_C(p_j, p_{j+1}) >= 1, indices mod
2k, so that sum_j a_j = L; rung lengths d_i = |E_i| for i = 1..k;

    A_i  =  a_i + a_{i+1} + ... + a_{i+k-1}      (i = 1..2k)
    e_s  =  a_s + a_{s+k}                        (s = 1..k)
    B_ij =  e_i + e_{i+1} + ... + e_{j-1}        (1 <= i < j <= k)

so A_i is the forward arc from p_i to p_{i+k}, A_{i+k} = L - A_i, and
sum_{s=1}^{k} e_s = L. Condition (a) reads d_i > max(A_i, L - A_i).

  (1) 2k <= L. Immediate: 2k distinct feet on a cycle of length L.

  (2) If the braid has k >= L/3 - the strong reading of 433.4(c),
      the one 432.5 and 446.4 already work under - then also L <= 3k,
      and then AT LEAST k OF THE 2k ARCS HAVE LENGTH EXACTLY 1.
      PROOF. Let z = #{j : a_j = 1}. Then L = sum_j a_j >= z + 2(2k
      - z) = 4k - z, so z >= 4k - L >= 4k - 3k = k. QED
      Likewise #{s : e_s >= 3} <= sum_s (e_s - 2) = L - 2k <= k.

  (3) THE ARC-WALK LEMMA. A_{i+1} - A_i = a_{i+k} - a_i, and

          sum_{i=1}^{k} | A_{i+1} - A_i |  <=  L - 2k .

      PROOF. For integers x, y >= 1 one has |x - y| <= (x-1) + (y-1).
      Summing |a_{i+k} - a_i| over i = 1..k therefore gives at most
      sum over ALL 2k arcs of (a_j - 1) = L - 2k. QED

  (4) COROLLARY (THE BRAID IS NEARLY ANTIPODAL). For every i,

          k  <=  A_i  <=  L - k .

      PROOF. Walking from A_i to A_{i+k} = L - A_i takes k steps, so
      |L - 2A_i| <= L - 2k by (3); rearrange. QED
      Hence BOTH arcs of every braided ear have length at least k,
      which under the strong reading of (c) is at least L/3: no
      braided ear is lopsided. If L = 2k - every arc of length 1 -
      then A_i = L/2 exactly for every i and the braid is perfectly
      antipodal.

  (5) Consequently max(A_i, L - A_i) lies in [L/2, L - k], and (a)
      forces d_i >= max(A_i, L - A_i) + 1 > L/2, recovering 449.1(a)
      and sharpening its constraint from below to a band.

(1)-(5) are statements about the STRUCTURAL family only. Nothing in
them mentions a valuation, a shift, or a power of two.

### 479.3 THE CYCLE FORMS CARRIED BY THE OBJECT (PROVED)

GRADING LEMMA. Every cycle of H uses a set S of rungs and a set of
rim arcs, each at most once, so its length is

    sum_{i in S} d_i  +  rho ,        0 <= rho <= L .

The small grades, computed on ML_k and then read back through the
subdivision:

  r = 0 :  the rim, length L.
  r = 1 :  d_i + A_i    and    d_i + (L - A_i).
  r = 2 :  for i < j,   d_i + d_j + B_ij   and
                        d_i + d_j + (L - B_ij).

  PROOF of the r = 2 forms. The four feet occur in the cyclic order
  p_i, p_j, p_{i+k}, p_{j+k}. A cycle through both rungs joins
  {p_{i+k}, p_{j+k}} and {p_j, p_i} by two internally disjoint rim
  paths, or joins {p_j, p_{i+k}} and {p_{j+k}, p_i}. The first uses
  arcs a_i..a_{j-1} and a_{i+k}..a_{j+k-1}, total B_ij; the second
  uses the complementary arcs, total L - B_ij. QED

SEPARABLE NORMAL FORM. Put b_i = B_{1i} (so b_1 = 0), and

    f_i = d_i + b_i ,        g_i = d_i - b_i .

Then for i < j the two r = 2 lengths are exactly

    g_i + f_j        and        f_i + g_j + L .

So the pair spectrum of the braid is a RESTRICTED SUMSET of the two
k-element sets {g_i} and {f_j}. This re-derives 432.5's separability
("the pair value is f_i + g_j") from the ladder normal form rather
than from a case analysis, and it fixes its constants: the coupling
f_i - g_i = 2 b_i is the doubled foot position, as 432.5 says.

### 479.4 THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, APPLIED - AND THE OBJECT REJECTED

The candidate object is now visible: a METRIC MOBIUS LADDER, i.e.
ML_k with a positive integer length on every edge, subject to (1)-(5)
of 479.2. Its defining axioms mention no cycle length, no shift, no
valuation and no power of two, so it PASSES 478.3's syntactic test.
478.3 also says the real test is Theorem A, and that Theorem A should
be the hard half. Run it.

THEOREM (PROVED, NEGATIVE). There is a metric Mobius ladder
satisfying every constraint of 479.2 - including 24 <= L, 2k <= L <=
3k, and d_i > both arcs - whose cycle spectrum contains NO power of
two.

  WITNESS. k = 12, every rim arc a_j = 1, every rung d_i = D = 65.
  Then L = 2k = 24, so 24 <= L <= 36 = 3k; A_i = 12 for every i; and
  D = 65 > 12 = max(A_i, L - A_i). All of 479.2 holds.

  PROOF. Write D = 2^6 + 1. By the Grading Lemma every cycle length
  is either L = 24, which is not a power of two, or

      r D + rho  =  r 2^6 + (r + rho) ,   1 <= r <= 12, 0 <= rho <= 24,

  and then r 2^6 < r D + rho <= r 2^6 + 36. Let 2^c <= r < 2^{c+1}.
  The least power of two strictly above r 2^6 is 2^{6+c+1}, at
  distance (2^{c+1} - r) 2^6 >= 2^6 = 64 > 36. So the interval
  (r 2^6, r 2^6 + 36] contains no power of two. QED

MACHINE (tools/braid479.py, independent of the formulas above: it
enumerates the cycles of ML_12 from the graph by depth-first search
and weighs them edge by edge): 4229 cycles, 18 distinct lengths, the
whole spectrum inside [24, 727], no power of two among them.

Nothing about the witness is delicate: replace 65 by 2^N + 1 for any
N with 2^N > L + k and the same two lines run. The failure is
structural. The rung lengths of a metric Mobius ladder are bounded
BELOW by (a) and not bounded above at all, and pushing them to a
common value just above a power of two evacuates every grade at once.

  (N10) THE RUNG-SCALING NO-GO (479.4). The numeric constraints that
        (a) and braiding impose on the braid - 479.2 in full - are
        satisfiable by a metric Mobius ladder with no power-of-two
        cycle. Hence NO Theorem A whose hypothesis is implied by
        479.2 can be true, and every object built on the braid must
        import, from outside 479.2, an upper bound on rung length in
        terms of L.

(N10) is not (N1). (N1) says a scale-INVARIANT property cannot settle
the conjecture, and 479.2 is not scale invariant - condition (2),
L <= 3k, is destroyed by dilating the arcs. (N10) says something
sharper and local to this object: the arcs of the braid are pinned by
(2)-(4) into a bounded polytope, while the rungs are free in an
unbounded cone, and the cone is where the counterexample lives.

### 479.5 WHERE THE MISSING BOUND ALREADY LIVES

The witness of 479.4 is not a graph. Its rungs are bare paths of 64
internal vertices, and in a CUBIC G every one of those vertices has a
third edge that must go somewhere. That is exactly the object 449
studied:

  449.1(a) every ear interior is a path on s = d_i - 1 >= L/2
  vertices; 449.1(c) its self-chords have span in [4, mu]; 449.2
  measured that a self-chorded interior path can only reach
  s ~ 10(x+1) where x counts the vertices whose third edge LEAVES
  the ear; 449.3 concluded x >= s/B - 1 = Omega(L).

So a long rung is not free: it costs cross edges in linear quantity,
and those cross edges are new ears, new cycles and new grades. The
bound (N10) demands is therefore not missing from the archive - it is
in 449 - but it is a statement about the INTERIOR WIRING OF A RUNG,
not about the ladder. The object has to grow: from the metric Mobius
ladder to the ladder whose rungs are themselves wired.

That is the next section's task, and 479 has narrowed it to a single
question with no slack in it: BY HOW MUCH IS d_i BOUNDED ABOVE IN
TERMS OF L? Under the packing shell (e), with n of order L^2/4 and
sum_i (d_i - 1) <= n - L over k >= L/3 disjoint rungs, the average
rung is at most about 3L/4 while every rung exceeds L/2 - a band of
width L/4 holding L/3 numbers, which is a supply of small
DIFFERENCES, exactly the resource 477.3 identified as the live one.
The next section must prove that band rather than assume it.

### 479.6 STATUS

PROVED here: BRAID RIGIDITY - a pairwise-crossing ear family with
distinct feet is antipodal, and cycle plus braid is a subdivision of
the Mobius ladder Cay(Z/2k, {+1,-1,k}), so 432.5's spiral order is
forced and not assumed; the rigid numerics 479.2 (1)-(5), including
the ARC-WALK LEMMA and its corollary k <= A_i <= L - k, i.e. no
braided ear is lopsided; the GRADING LEMMA and the r = 0, 1, 2 cycle
forms, with the SEPARABLE NORMAL FORM g_i + f_j re-deriving 432.5;
and the NEGATIVE theorem of 479.4, with an explicit twelve-rung
witness at L = 24 whose spectrum misses every power of two.

COMPUTED (tools/braid479.py, three checks, all pass): for k = 2..6
the antipodal pairing is the ONLY pairwise-crossing pairing of 2k
cyclically ordered points, out of (2k-1)!! in all; on three weighted
Mobius ladders (k = 4, 5, 6) the r = 0, 1, 2 length sets and the
separable form g_i + f_j agree exactly with brute-force cycle
enumeration, and every cycle obeys the Grading Lemma; and the 479.4
witness has 4229 cycles, 18 distinct lengths, none a power of two.

IDENTIFIED: F_str, the structural J7 family, written down before any
object was chosen, and shown to be a family on which (N9) is silent -
the reduction to it is strictly stronger than J7 and not implied by
J7. This is the repair 478.3 asked for.

RECORDED: (N10), the rung-scaling no-go.

NOT PROVED: J7; Theorem A for any object; the five statements of
451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The family is
now written down and it is not a counterexample class, so the trap of
478.2 is behind us. The braid turns out to have exactly one shape - a
Mobius ladder - and that shape carries hard numerics: both arcs of
every braided ear lie between L/3 and 2L/3, at least half the rim
arcs have length 1, and the pair spectrum is a restricted sumset. But
the metric ladder is NOT the object: its rungs are unbounded above,
and 479.4 exhibits a ladder obeying every derived constraint with no
power-of-two cycle. The object must carry the rung interiors too.
That is a strictly larger object, it is the one 449 already measured,
and it is where the next section goes.


## 480. THE SPECTRUM OF THE BRAID, COMPLETELY DETERMINED, AND WHY THE
## BRAID IS NOT THE OBJECT

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 479 put the braid into
normal form and rejected the metric Mobius ladder as an object
because its rungs are unbounded. This section replaces that soft
rejection by a hard one. It DETERMINES THE CYCLE SPECTRUM OF THE
BRAID EXACTLY - every cycle, with its length, for every subdivision
of ML_k - and the answer is a classification, not an estimate
(480.1). Three things follow. 432.5's spiral calculus is upgraded
from three observed cases to a theorem (480.2). The braid is proved
THIN: in the antipodally symmetric case its whole spectrum is one
arithmetic progression plus the odd subset sums of the rungs
(480.3). And (N10) is sharpened past repair: a SHORT-rung witness,
with every rung inside the band L/2 < d <= L where the grades
overlap, still has no power-of-two cycle (480.4). No hypothesis
about rung length saves the object. The braid must be enlarged, and
480.5 says in which direction and why that direction is forced.

### 480.0 THE TWO-COMPLETION LEMMA (PROVED)

Let H be a subdivision of ML_k, notation as in 479.2. Fix a nonempty
S contained in {1..k}, |S| = r, and ask for the cycles of H that use
exactly the rungs indexed by S.

LEMMA. There are exactly two candidate edge sets, and they are
complementary on the rim.

  PROOF. Call the 2r feet of the S-rungs MARKED. A cycle Z using
  exactly the S-rungs meets every marked point in degree 2, one of
  which is its rung, so Z uses exactly one rim edge at each marked
  point. An unmarked foot p_c (rung c not in S) has degree 2 or 0 in
  Z, and a rim vertex of degree 2 in Z uses both its rim edges. Hence
  the rim part of Z is a union of whole arcs between CYCLICALLY
  CONSECUTIVE marked points. Write those 2r arcs as A_1, ..., A_{2r}
  in cyclic order, A_t joining the marked points q_t and q_{t+1}.
  Choosing one arc at each q_t is choosing a perfect matching in the
  cycle whose vertices are q_1..q_{2r} and whose edges are the arcs;
  a cycle of even order 2r has exactly two perfect matchings, the odd
  arcs and the even arcs. QED

Write rho^0_S and rho^1_S for the two arc totals; rho^0_S + rho^1_S =
L, since between them they use every rim edge exactly once.

### 480.1 THE COMPLETION THEOREM (PROVED; MACHINE 5/5 EXACT)

THEOREM. With the notation above, the subgraph formed by the S-rungs
and either completion is a disjoint union of

    1      cycles   if r is odd, or r = 2;
    r / 2  cycles   if r is even and r >= 4.

Consequently the cycle spectrum of H is EXACTLY

  Spec(H) = {L}
      union { sum_{i in S} d_i + rho^e_S :  e = 0, 1 ,
               S nonempty with |S| = 2 or |S| odd } ,

and H has exactly

    2^k  +  k (k - 1)  +  1

cycles in all.

  PROOF. By Braid Rigidity the marked points, in cyclic order, are
  q_1, ..., q_{2r} with the rung of q_t joining it to q_{t+r}: the
  antipodal pattern is inherited by any sub-collection of rungs. So
  the subgraph is the union of two perfect matchings on Z/2r, namely
  tau(t) = t + r (rungs) and sigma the chosen arc matching, say
  sigma(t) = t+1 for t odd and t-1 for t even. The components of a
  union of two perfect matchings correspond to the orbits of the
  composite phi = sigma tau, two orbits per component.

    r EVEN. tau preserves parity. For t odd, phi(t) = t + r + 1,
    which is even; for t even, phi(t) = t + r - 1, which is odd. So
    for t odd, phi^2(t) = (t + r + 1) + r - 1 = t + 2r = t. Every
    orbit has size 2, there are r orbits, hence r/2 components.

    r ODD. For t odd, tau(t) = t + r is even and phi(t) = t + r - 1
    is odd: phi preserves the odd class. Writing t = 2u + 1 with u in
    Z/r, phi is u -> u + h with h = (r-1)/2. Since 2h = r - 1 is
    congruent to -1 mod r, h is invertible mod r, so phi is a single
    r-cycle on the odds and likewise on the evens: two orbits, one
    component.

  The even matching is the odd matching rotated by one, so it gives
  the same counts. The length of a completion is the sum of its rungs
  plus its arc total, which is the displayed formula. For the count:
  r = 0 contributes 1; r = 1 and r = 2 contribute 2k and 2 C(k,2);
  odd r >= 3 contribute 2 (sum over odd r of C(k,r) minus k) =
  2 (2^{k-1} - k); even r >= 4 contribute nothing new, their
  components being 2-rung cycles already counted. Adding,
  1 + 2k + k(k-1) + 2^k - 2k = 2^k + k(k-1) + 1. QED

MACHINE (tools/braid479.py, depth-first cycle enumeration on the
graph, formula never consulted): k = 4, 5, 6, 8, 12 give 29, 53, 95,
313, 4229 cycles, against 2^k + k(k-1) + 1 = 29, 53, 95, 313, 4229.
Five for five, exact.

### 480.2 432.5 UPGRADED FROM THREE CASES TO A CLASSIFICATION

432.5 recorded, from worked examples, that a pair of crossing ears
composes to a single cycle, that an odd zigzag composes to a single
cycle with winding (k+1)/2, and that even spirals with k >= 4
disconnect into two cycles. 480.1 proves all three at once and
corrects the last: an even spiral with r rungs disconnects into r/2
cycles, which is two only when r = 4. The winding statement is the
same orbit computation read the other way - for odd r the single
component runs through all 2r arcs of the completion, wrapping the
rim (r+1)/2 times.

The classification also removes the last freedom the archive had been
carrying: it is not merely that SOME sub-selections obstruct, as
446.2(b) put it. The obstructed sub-selections are known exactly, and
they are precisely the even ones of size at least 4.

### 480.3 THE ANTIPODAL COLLAPSE (PROVED)

Call the braid ANTIPODALLY SYMMETRIC if a_j = a_{j+k} for every j -
equivalently e_s = 2 a_s. By 479.2(4) this is forced when L = 2k, and
it is the exact case of 434.2's ladder design.

THEOREM. In an antipodally symmetric braid, A_i = L/2 for every i,
and EVERY CYCLE OF ODD GRADE HAS LENGTH sum_{i in S} d_i + L/2.

  PROOF. The shift p_t -> p_{t+k} preserves every arc length, so it
  is an automorphism of the weighted rim; it fixes the foot set of
  any rung family and rotates the 2r marked points by r. For r odd
  that rotation exchanges odd-indexed and even-indexed arcs, so
  rho^0_S = rho^1_S, and their sum is L. Taking r = 1 gives
  A_i = L/2. QED

So in the symmetric case the whole spectrum is

  {L}  union  { sum_S d_i + L/2 : |S| odd }
       union  { d_i + d_j + B_ij ,  d_i + d_j + L - B_ij : i < j } .

The braid contributes exactly three kinds of number: the rim; the ODD
SUBSET SUMS of the rung multiset, rigidly offset by L/2; and the pair
values, which are the only ones carrying a variable rim correction.
That is a thin object. Every even subset of size at least four - the
overwhelming majority of the 2^k subsets - contributes nothing.
