### 480.4 (N10) SHARPENED: SHORT RUNGS DO NOT SAVE THE OBJECT

479.4's witness had rungs of length 65 against L = 24 and could be
dismissed as an artefact of unbounded rungs. It cannot. Put the rungs
INSIDE the band L/2 < d <= L, which is exactly the band in which
consecutive grade windows [r d, r d + L] overlap and the union
[d, 3d + L] has ratio at least 4 - the regime that ought to be the
favourable one.

WITNESS. k = 12, every arc a_j = 1 (so L = 24, antipodally
symmetric), every rung d = 16, so 12 < 16 <= 24. By 480.3 the
spectrum is

    {24}  union  {16 r + 12 : r odd, 1 <= r <= 11}
          union  {32 + 2 s : 1 <= s <= 11}
  = {24, 28, 34, 36, 38, ..., 52, 54, 60, 92, 124, 156, 188},

eighteen values, and NO POWER OF TWO: 32 falls one step below the
pair progression, which starts at 34, and 64 falls above its top, 54.
MACHINE (tools/braid479.py): the same eighteen values, obtained by
enumerating all 4229 cycles of the graph. Confirmed.

  (N10) SHARPENED (480.4). The metric Mobius ladder fails Theorem A
        in BOTH regimes: with rungs far above L (479.4) and with
        rungs inside L/2 < d <= L (480.4). The failure is not a
        missing bound on rung length. It is thinness: by 480.1 the
        braid has only 2^k + k(k-1) + 1 cycles and, when symmetric,
        only the pair grade carries a variable rim correction, so its
        spectrum is one arithmetic progression of step 2 and length
        k-1 together with a sparse tail. A progression of step 2 and
        length k-1 spans 2k - 4 < L, a window of ratio below 2, and
        (N4) then applies verbatim. NO PROPERTY OF THE BRAID ALONE
        CAN SETTLE J7.

Note how sharply the failure is localised. The pair grade DOES
produce an arithmetic progression of consecutive even numbers - the
run that 477.3 said was the right thing to look for - but its length
is capped by the rim: the corrections B_ij are the interval sums of
the e_s, which total L, so the run cannot be longer than L/2 terms
and cannot span a ratio-2 window when it sits at height 2d > L. The
run exists; the rim is too short to pay for it.

### 480.5 THE DIRECTION THAT IS NOW FORCED

Two facts from 480 point the same way.

  (i) The braid is thin because its grades are FIXED: adding a rung
      does not lengthen any existing cycle, it only offers new
      subsets, and the even ones of size >= 4 are wasted.
 (ii) What J7 needs is a long run of consecutive lengths, and the
      only run the braid has is capped by the rim.

Both say: stop looking for the object inside a fixed subgraph and
look at how the graph is BUILT. The relevant filtration is the EAR
DECOMPOSITION. If G = G_0 + P_1 + ... + P_N with G_0 a cycle and each
P_j an ear of the current graph, then

    Spec(G_0) subset Spec(G_1) subset ... subset Spec(G_N) = Spec(G),

because attaching an ear never destroys or lengthens an existing
cycle - the spectrum only ACCUMULATES. This is the structural
opposite of 479.4's failure mode, and it is the reason the filtration
and not the subgraph is the right carrier. The accumulation step is
explicit: if P_j has length p and ends u, v, then

    Spec(G_j) = Spec(G_{j-1})  union  ( p + Path(u, v ; G_{j-1}) ) ,

where Path(u, v; X) is the set of lengths of u-v paths in X. So the
object to equip is the pair (spectrum, path spectra), the operation
is a translated union, and the question becomes whether a monotone
system of this shape can grow from Spec(C) = {L} to its final state
while dodging every power of two. THAT is a question about a
FILTERED object with an increasing family of subsets of Z, it uses
the cubic hypothesis through the ear decomposition rather than
through a local count, and nothing in its statement mentions a
valuation. It is the next section's target.

### 480.6 STATUS

PROVED here: the TWO-COMPLETION LEMMA - each rung set admits exactly
two rim completions, complementary on the rim; the COMPLETION
THEOREM - a rung set of size r closes into a single cycle exactly
when r is odd or r = 2, and into r/2 cycles when r is even and at
least 4, whence the exact spectrum of a subdivided Mobius ladder and
the closed form 2^k + k(k-1) + 1 for its number of cycles; the
ANTIPODAL COLLAPSE - a symmetric braid has A_i = L/2 and every
odd-grade length equal to a rung subset sum offset by L/2; and the
SHORT-RUNG WITNESS, which fails Theorem A inside the favourable band.

COMPUTED (tools/braid479.py, cycles enumerated from the graph, the
formulas never consulted): the cycle counts 29, 53, 95, 313, 4229 for
k = 4, 5, 6, 8, 12 against the closed form, five for five; and the
eighteen-value spectrum of the 480.4 witness, with no power of two.

CORRECTED (374.1): 432.5's "even spirals with k >= 4 disconnect into
TWO cycles" - the correct count is k/2 components, which is two only
at k = 4.

RECORDED: (N10) sharpened - the braid is thin, and no hypothesis
about rung length can make it satisfy Theorem A.

NOT PROVED: J7; Theorem A for any object; the five statements of
451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The braid is
now a solved object: its cycles are classified, counted in closed
form, and its spectrum written down. The verdict is negative and it
is final for this object - the braid has 2^k + k(k-1) + 1 cycles but
only O(k^2) lengths, its one run of consecutive values is capped by
the rim at a ratio below 2, and explicit witnesses defeat Theorem A
both above and below the rung band. What 479 and 480 together buy is
therefore a family written down correctly, a normal form for its
central object, a complete calculation of that object, and a proof
that the object must be replaced by the FILTRATION that builds it.
The ear-decomposition filtration is the candidate, its accumulation
law is exact, and it is where the next section goes.


## 481. THE TAXICAB THEOREM: A CHORD SYSTEM IS A PACKING IN THE L^1
## PLANE, AND THE FIRST OBJECT TO PASS ITS ACCEPTANCE TEST

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 480 forced the search
off the braid and onto the wiring inside it. This section supplies
the normal form for that wiring. Its content is one theorem, THE
TAXICAB THEOREM (481.1): the chords of a path or cycle are POINTS OF
THE PLANE, girth is a packing radius, and cycle lengths are TAXICAB
DISTANCES between the points, shifted by 2. Under that dictionary
448-449's exhaustive DFS measurements become a question about the
distance set of an L^1 packing, and J7's demand becomes: the distance
set must avoid the lacunary set {2^m - 2}. 481.4 then runs the
acceptance test on the resulting object and, for the first time in
479-481, IT PASSES as far as it can be checked - with an exact
statement of how far that is.

### 481.0 THE ACCUMULATION LAW AND THE CUBIC EAR NORMAL FORM (PROVED)

Let G be 2-connected with an ear decomposition G_0, G_1, ..., G_N,
G_0 a cycle and G_j = G_{j-1} + P_j, P_j an ear of length p_j with
ends u_j, v_j. Attaching an ear neither destroys nor lengthens an
existing cycle, so

    Spec(G_0) subset Spec(G_1) subset ... subset Spec(G_N) = Spec(G),

and the step is exact:

  ACCUMULATION LAW.  Spec(G_j) = Spec(G_{j-1}) union
                    ( p_j + Path(u_j, v_j ; G_{j-1}) ),
  where Path(u,v;X) is the set of lengths of u-v paths in X.

So the family, ordered by ear-extension, is a DIRECTED SYSTEM and
Spec is a MONOTONE FUNCTOR from it to the subsets of Z. That is the
family-level object 478.3 asked for, and unlike 476's it is not a
property of a counterexample class: it is the shape of the family
itself.

CUBIC EAR NORMAL FORM (PROVED). If G is cubic then every vertex is an
endpoint of exactly one ear; hence the decomposition has exactly n/2
ears and the cyclomatic number is n/2 + 1.
  PROOF. Every vertex enters the construction with degree 2 - on the
  initial cycle, or in the interior of its ear - and the only later
  degree increase is being the endpoint of a subsequent ear, each of
  which raises two degrees by one. Final degree 3 forces exactly one
  such event per vertex, so 2 (number of ears) = n. Then
  1 + n/2 = m - n + 1 with m = 3n/2. QED

### 481.1 THE TAXICAB THEOREM (PROVED; MACHINE 249/249)

Let R be a path v_0 v_1 ... v_s (the case of a cycle is identical
with arcs in place of segments) and let X be a set of chords, no two
sharing an endpoint - automatic when the host graph is cubic. Write a
chord as the point c = (i, j) of Z^2 with i < j.

THEOREM.
  (i) A chord c = (i,j) lies on exactly one cycle using no other
      chord, of length (j - i) + 1.
 (ii) Two chords c = (i,j) and c' = (i',j') lie on a common cycle
      using no other chord if and only if they are NOT DISJOINT,
      i.e. not (j < i') and not (j' < i); and then that cycle is
      unique, with length

          | i - i' | + | j - j' | + 2   =   || c - c' ||_1  +  2 .

  PROOF. (i) The chord plus the segment between its ends. (ii) If
  c, c' are disjoint the two chords and the path form a dumbbell, and
  a cycle through both would have to traverse the segment between
  them twice. Otherwise c, c' either cross (i < i' < j < j') or nest
  (i < i' < j' < j). Crossing: the cycle is v_i..v_{i'}, the chord c'
  to v_{j'}, v_{j'}..v_j backwards, the chord c to v_i, of length
  (i'-i) + 1 + (j'-j) + 1. Nesting: v_i..v_{i'}, the chord c' to
  v_{j'}, v_{j'}..v_j, the chord c back, of length
  (i'-i) + 1 + (j-j') + 1. Both equal |i-i'| + |j-j'| + 2.
  Uniqueness: every chord endpoint has degree 2 on the cycle, one of
  which is its chord, so the segment used at each endpoint is
  determined. QED

MACHINE: 249 random girth-legal chorded paths, s between 8 and 13;
the one-chord and two-chord cycle sets produced by depth-first
enumeration of the graph agree with (i) and (ii) exactly, 249 out of
249. (An earlier run disagreed on 157 of 300 instances; every
disagreement came from chords of span 1 or 2, which do not make
cycles at all and are excluded by girth. Recorded per 374.1.)

COROLLARY (CROSSING FAMILIES ARE INTERVAL SUMS). If the chords
pairwise cross then i_1 < ... < i_c and j_1 < ... < j_c, and writing
gamma_t = (i_{t+1} - i_t) + (j_{t+1} - j_t) the two-chord lengths are
exactly the INTERVAL SUMS gamma_t + ... + gamma_{u-1}, plus 2.

### 481.2 GIRTH IS A PACKING RADIUS

Immediately from 481.1: for a host of girth at least 5,

    every chord has span j - i >= 4 ;
    every non-disjoint pair has  || c - c' ||_1  >=  3 .

So THE CHORD SYSTEM IS A PACKING IN THE TAXICAB PLANE, of minimum
distance 3, whose points have all their 2|X| coordinates distinct.
And the conclusion J7 must avoid becomes a DISTANCE-AVOIDANCE
condition on that packing:

    no span equals 2^m - 1 ,   no distance equals 2^m - 2 .

A packing whose distance set avoids a lacunary set. That is a
recognisable kind of object, its axioms mention no valuation and no
shift, and by 478.3's test it is admissible.

### 481.3 WHAT THIS DOES TO 448 AND 449

448.1 capped self-chord spans by sigma <= mu; in the dictionary that
is a bound on the distance from a point to the diagonal. 449.2
measured by exhaustive DFS that a self-chorded interior path dodging
the forbidden set reaches only s of order 10, and 449.3 concluded
that every ear must leak Omega(L) cross edges. 481.1 says what those
searches were searching: the set of L^1 packings in a triangle whose
distance set avoids a prescribed set. The "killers are LOCAL"
phenomenon 449.2 reported is exactly the minimum-distance constraint,
and the reason widening mu did not help is that mu bounds the
diameter of the packing and not its density.

### 481.4 THE CLOSED LADDER, AND THE FIRST POSITIVE ACCEPTANCE TEST

DEFINITION. A CLOSED LADDER of length s is a path v_0 ... v_s
together with a PERFECT matching of its interior vertices by chords.
Equivalently: a graph with a Hamiltonian path in which every internal
vertex has degree 3. It is the rung of a braid whose interior is
entirely self-wired.

MEASURED, EXHAUSTIVELY (search over all perfect matchings, girth
tested on the graph and cycle lengths obtained by depth-first
enumeration, never from a formula):

  s <= 11 : NO girth-legal closed ladder exists at all.
  s = 13  :    34 girth-legal closed ladders, ALL 34 contain an
               8-cycle.
  s = 15  :   792 girth-legal closed ladders, ALL 792 contain an
               8-cycle.
  s = 17  : 15306 girth-legal closed ladders, ALL 15306 contain an
               8-cycle; 15114 of them also contain a 16-cycle.
  s = 19  : exhaustive search with the power-of-two constraint
               enforced during the search closes after 1117 complete
               matchings: NONE is power-of-two-free.

So for every length at which the question can be decided by
exhaustion, THE CLOSED LADDER SATISFIES THEOREM A. This is the first
candidate object in 479-481 whose acceptance test does not fail.

THE HONEST SCOPE OF THAT (374.1). The uniform appearance of 8 cannot
persist, and the reason is not subtle: a graph of girth 9 has no
8-cycle at all, cubic graphs of arbitrarily large girth exist, and a
cubic graph of girth 9 needs at least 1 + 3 + 6 + 12 + 24 = 46
vertices by the Moore bound. So the mechanism behind the
measurement - girth 5 forces short cycles and 8 lies inside their
range - runs out at some s below 46, and beyond that the adversary
has room to push the girth past 8 and must be defeated by 16, 32 and
the rest. The measurement therefore establishes that the closed
ladder has NO SMALL COUNTEREXAMPLE. It does not establish Theorem A,
and this archive does not record it as established.

What the measurement does establish is the SHAPE of Theorem A for
this object:

  THEOREM A(LADDER), NOT PROVED. Every graph with a Hamiltonian path
  whose internal vertices all have degree 3, and of girth at least 5,
  has a cycle of length a power of two.

which is Erdos-Gyarfas restricted to the cubic graphs carrying a
Hamiltonian path. Three things recommend it as the Theorem A that
478.3 was asking for. It is substantive rather than a definition
unpacked. Its class is closed under nothing and defined by geometry
alone - a Hamiltonian path and a girth - so (N9) is silent on it. And
by 481.1 it is a statement about a planar point set, which is a place
where known mathematics has purchase, whereas "no cycle of length
2^k" on a bare cubic graph is not.

### 481.5 WHERE (B) STANDS, EXACTLY

(B) for this object reads: every rung interior of an F_str braid is a
closed ladder. THAT IS FALSE, and the archive already proved it
false: 449.3 shows every ear must leak Omega(L) cross edges, so no
rung is entirely self-wired. The leak is not a perturbation - it is
linear in L.

So the true object is the LEAKY LADDER: a path with a PARTIAL
matching of its interior, the unmatched vertices carrying edges out
of the rung. And the leaks are not lost information - by 432.4 they
are themselves ears of the ladder H, with feet on rung interiors, and
by 433.2's Middle-Zone Law their feet are confined. The object to
carry Theorem A is therefore the taxicab packing of ONE rung TOGETHER
WITH the ear system its leaks generate, which is a packing in a
higher-dimensional taxicab space - one coordinate pair per rung.

That is a precise next target, and 481 has earned the right to state
it in one line: THE J7 BRAID IS A TAXICAB PACKING IN Z^{2k}, ITS
GIRTH IS A MINIMUM DISTANCE, AND J7 SAYS ITS DISTANCE SET AVOIDS
{2^m - 2}.

### 481.6 STATUS

PROVED here: the ACCUMULATION LAW and the monotone-functor framing of
the family under ear-extension; the CUBIC EAR NORMAL FORM - every
vertex ends exactly one ear, n/2 ears, cyclomatic number n/2 + 1; the
TAXICAB THEOREM - one-chord cycles have length span + 1, two-chord
cycles exist exactly for non-disjoint pairs and have length equal to
the L^1 distance of the two chords-as-points plus 2, and the cycle is
unique in both cases; the corollary that a pairwise-crossing family
contributes exactly the interval sums of its gap sequence; and the
identification of girth with a packing radius.

COMPUTED (exhaustive, cycles enumerated from the graph): no
girth-legal closed ladder for s <= 11; 34, 792 and 15306 of them at
s = 13, 15, 17, every single one containing an 8-cycle; and no
power-of-two-free closed ladder at s = 19.

CORRECTED (374.1): a first machine run appeared to refute the Taxicab
Theorem on 157 of 300 instances. Every failure was a chord of span 1
or 2, which bounds no cycle and is excluded by girth 5; with the
girth hypothesis enforced the agreement is 249 out of 249. The
theorem needs the hypothesis and the first run did not supply it.

IDENTIFIED: the closed ladder is the first object of this series to
pass its acceptance test as far as exhaustion reaches, and its
Theorem A - Erdos-Gyarfas for cubic graphs with a Hamiltonian path -
is a substantive open statement of exactly the shape 478.3 demanded.
Its (B) is FALSE as stated, by 449.3, and the repair is the leaky
ladder.

NOT PROVED: Theorem A(LADDER); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Three objects
have now been put to 478.3's acceptance test. The metric Mobius
ladder failed twice, above and below the rung band, because it is
thin (480). The chord system passes, as far as exhaustion reaches,
and it comes with a normal form that is genuinely geometric: a
packing of minimum distance 3 in the taxicab plane whose distance set
must dodge {2^m - 2}. The burden now sits where 478.3 said it should
sit - on Theorem A - and Theorem A is a statement about planar point
sets rather than about the absence of a cycle. What is not yet in
hand is (B): the rungs leak, by a theorem of this archive, so the
object must be widened from one rung's packing to the braid's
packing in Z^{2k}. That widening, and Theorem A for it, is the work.


## 482. WHY THE BRAID: ANTIPODALITY IS SPECTRUM-EXTREMAL, AND THE
## SHALLOW GRADES ARE THE ONES THAT CAN BE DODGED

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 480 proved the braid
thin. This section proves WHY, and the answer is not an accident of
the braid's arithmetic: ANTIPODALITY IS EXACTLY THE CHORD PATTERN
THAT FRAGMENTS EVERY EVEN COMPOSITE AS MUCH AS A CHORD PATTERN CAN
(482.1). It then shows, by a measurement whose design is the point,
that the resource the braid destroys is the ONLY resource that
matters: a Hamiltonian cubic graph can be built to dodge every
power of two at grades 0, 1 and 2, and grade 3 defeats the dodge
immediately (482.4). Put together: J7's condition (c) is not one
hypothesis among six. It is the hypothesis that removes the deep
grades, and 449.3 says it cannot be maintained (482.5).

### 482.0 THE COMPONENT LEMMA (PROVED, GENERAL)

Let R be a cycle carrying a family of chords or ears with distinct
feet. Fix a sub-family S of size r and one of its two arc
completions (480.0). On the 2r feet, write tau for the pairing
induced by the ears and sigma for the pairing induced by the chosen
arcs; both are perfect matchings of a 2r-set.

LEMMA. The chosen edge set has exactly (number of orbits of the
permutation sigma tau) / 2 components.

  PROOF. The union of two perfect matchings is a disjoint union of
  cycles alternating between them. On a component
  v_1 - v_2 - ... - v_{2j} - v_1 with v_1 v_2 in tau, one has
  sigma tau (v_1) = v_3, so sigma tau permutes the odd-indexed
  vertices in a j-cycle and, symmetrically, the even-indexed ones:
  exactly two orbits per component, of size j each. (For j = 1, tau
  and sigma pair the same two feet and the two orbits are the two
  fixed points.) QED

This is the general statement behind 480.1, and it needs no
hypothesis about the chord pattern.

### 482.1 BRAID EXTREMALITY (PROVED)

THEOREM. Let S be a sub-family of size r >= 2 no chord of which
joins two CYCLICALLY CONSECUTIVE feet of S. Then every completion of
S has at most r/2 components. The ANTIPODAL family - a
pairwise-crossing braid, by 479.1 - attains r/2 for every even
r >= 4 and for both of its completions.

  PROOF. A component alternates ears and arcs, so it uses j >= 1
  ears; j = 1 forces the ear's two feet to be paired by an arc, i.e.
  to be consecutive, which the hypothesis excludes. So every
  component uses at least two ears and there are at most r/2 of
  them. The antipodal case is the orbit computation of 480.1: for r
  even, sigma tau has order 2 and hence r orbits, giving r/2
  components. QED

So the braid is EXTREMAL. Among all chord patterns it fragments the
even composites as finely as any pattern can - it converts every
even sub-family of size at least four into a pile of two-ear cycles
already counted at grade 2, and contributes nothing new.

And the fragmentation is genuinely a property of ANTIPODALITY, not
of evenness. Take r = 4 with feet q_1..q_8 and the non-antipodal
pairing tau = (q_1 q_3)(q_2 q_5)(q_4 q_7)(q_6 q_8) against the odd
arc matching sigma = (q_1 q_2)(q_3 q_4)(q_5 q_6)(q_7 q_8). Then
sigma tau sends 1 -> 4 -> 8 -> 5 -> 1 and 2 -> 6 -> 7 -> 3 -> 2: two
orbits, ONE component. A four-ear composite exists. It is antipodal
patterns, and not even ones, that die.

### 482.2 THE CYCLE-HOST TAXICAB THEOREM (PROVED)

481.1 was stated for a path host. On a cycle host of length n, with
chords c = (a,b) and c' = (a',b') of spans sigma, sigma':

  one chord   :  sigma + 1   and   n - sigma + 1 ;
  two CROSSING chords :  || c - c' ||_1 + 2   and
                         n + 2 - || c - c' ||_1 ;
  two NON-CROSSING chords :  n + 2 - sigma - sigma' , one cycle only.

  PROOF. The completions are the two arc matchings of 480.0, whose
  totals sum to n. For crossing chords the feet in cyclic order are
  a, a', b, b' and the odd completion uses the arcs (a,a') and
  (b,b'), of total (a'-a) + (b'-b) = || c - c' ||_1. For
  non-crossing chords the feet are a, b, a', b' and the odd
  completion pairs each chord with its own arc, giving two separate
  one-chord cycles rather than a composite; the even completion uses
  the arcs (b,a') and (b',a), of total n - sigma - sigma'. QED

### 482.3 A FAMILY BUILT TO DODGE, AND WHAT DEFEATED IT (COMPUTED)

Take the cubic Hamiltonian graph

    H(n, s)  =  C_n  +  { {2t, 2t+s mod n} : t = 0, ..., n/2 - 1 } ,

s odd - a Hamiltonian cycle plus a perfect matching of chords of
constant odd span. It is cubic and, for the parameters below, has
girth 6. Its shallow grades are computable in closed form by 482.2:
the chord spans are all s, and two chords cross exactly when their
left feet differ by less than s/2, with || c - c' ||_1 = 4 |t - t'|.
So grade 1 is {s+1, n-s+1}, and grade 2 consists of numbers
4v + 2, n + 2 - 4v and n + 2 - 2s.

CHOOSE n = 28, s = 5. Then grade 1 is {6, 24} and grade 2 is
{6, 10, 20, 22, 26}: EVERY LENGTH AT GRADES 0, 1 AND 2 IS 28, or is
congruent to 2 modulo 4, and NONE IS A POWER OF TWO. The dodge at
the shallow grades is complete and it is by design.

MEASURED (all cycles enumerated from the graph and sorted by the
number of chords they use):

    grade 0 : 28
    grade 1 : 6, 24
    grade 2 : 6, 10, 20, 22, 26                 <- no power of two
    grade 3 : 8, 10, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26 <- 8 AND 16
    grades 4-14 : ... , and the full spectrum is
    every even number from 6 to 28.

Thirty members of the family, n in {20,24,28,32,36,40} and s in
{5,7,9,11,13}, were measured: every one has spectrum equal to all
even numbers from its girth to n, and every one contains 8 and 16
(and 32 once n >= 32).

  THE LESSON, and it is the reason for recording the measurement:
  THE SHALLOW GRADES CAN BE DODGED; THE DEEP GRADES CANNOT. Grades
  0-2 of a cubic Hamiltonian graph are a handful of numbers that an
  adversary can push into a single residue class. Grade 3 alone
  already supplied two powers of two.

### 482.4 WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT J7

Read 480 and 482 together.

  480.1  the braid contributes at grades 0, 1, 2 and the ODD grades
         only; every even grade from 4 up fragments into grade-2
         cycles.
  482.1  that fragmentation is maximal, and it is caused by
         antipodality, which by 479.1 is FORCED by braiding.
  482.3  the shallow grades are exactly the ones an adversary can
         dodge, and the deep grades are what defeats a dodge.

So condition (c) of 433.4 is not one hypothesis among six. IT IS THE
HYPOTHESIS THAT DELETES THE DEEP EVEN GRADES, and 482.3 says that is
precisely the resource a counterexample has to delete. That is why
the braided core is the residual case, and it is a much sharper
answer than "large ear systems whose crossing graph is sparse are
impossible" (432.6).

It also says where the proof has to come from, and the archive has
already proved the ingredient.

  THE RE-POPULATION PRINCIPLE. 449.3 shows every ear of the braid
  must leak Omega(L) cross edges. A cross edge between rung i at
  depth x and rung j at depth y produces four ears of C, with feet
  {p_i, p_j}, {p_i, p_{j+k}}, {p_{i+k}, p_j}, {p_{i+k}, p_{j+k}} and
  lengths x+1+y, x+1+(d_j - y), (d_i - x)+1+y, (d_i - x)+1+(d_j - y).
  Except when j = i + k these feet are NOT antipodal. By 482.1 a
  family containing such an ear is not the extremal pattern, so its
  even grades need not fragment - the deep grades that 480 emptied
  are back.

WHAT IS NOT YET PROVED, stated exactly. 446.2 licenses only families
with DISTINCT feet, and a leak-route through rung i has p_i as a
foot, which rung i also has. So a composite may use the rung or the
leak-route through it, not both, and re-population must be carried
out inside that constraint. Whether the surviving mixed families are
numerous enough, and whether their grade-3 and grade-4 values run
through a ratio-2 window as they do in 482.3, is the open step. It
is a counting question about admissible mixed families, not a
question about valuations, and that is a different kind of question
from any the archive has previously reduced J7 to.

### 482.5 STATUS

PROVED here: the COMPONENT LEMMA, that the completion of an r-ear
sub-family has (orbits of sigma tau)/2 components, with no hypothesis
on the pattern; BRAID EXTREMALITY, that a family no ear of which
joins consecutive feet has at most r/2 components and that the
antipodal - i.e. braided - family attains this for every even
r >= 4, so braiding fragments even composites maximally; the explicit
non-antipodal four-ear pattern whose completion is a SINGLE cycle,
showing the fragmentation is caused by antipodality and not by
parity; and the CYCLE-HOST TAXICAB THEOREM in its three cases.

COMPUTED: the family H(n,s) = C_n plus constant-span-s chords. At
n = 28, s = 5 grades 0, 1, 2 are {28}, {6,24} and {6,10,20,22,26} -
no power of two, by design - while grade 3 is
{8,10,14,16,18,20,22,24,26} and contains 8 and 16; the full spectrum
is every even number from 6 to 28. Thirty members measured, all
bipancyclic in this sense. Also, extending 481.4: exhaustive search
at s = 21 (6796 complete matchings) again finds no power-of-two-free
closed ladder.

IDENTIFIED: the shallow grades can be dodged and the deep ones cannot;
braiding is exactly the deletion of the deep even grades; and the
leaks that 449.3 forces are non-antipodal, so they re-populate what
braiding deleted.

NOT PROVED: that the mixed rung-and-leak families are numerous enough
to supply a ratio-2 window; Theorem A(LADDER); J7; the five
statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The question
"why is the braided core the residual case?" now has a structural
answer rather than a historical one: among all chord patterns the
braid is the unique kind that fragments every even composite of size
four or more, and a measurement designed for the purpose shows that
the deep composites are the only part of a cubic graph's spectrum
that cannot be dodged. The two facts meet at 449.3, which proves the
braid cannot be pure: every rung leaks, every leak is a non-antipodal
ear, and non-antipodal ears un-fragment the even grades. The
remaining work is to count the mixed families that 446.2's
distinct-feet rule allows, and that is the first time in this archive
that J7 has been reduced to a counting question with no valuation in
it.


## 483. THE RE-POPULATION THEOREM: ONE LEAK RESTORES EVERY EVEN GRADE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 480.1 proved that in a
PURE braid every even sub-family of size at least four fragments and
contributes no new cycle; 482.3 measured that the deep grades are the
only part of a cubic spectrum that cannot be dodged; 449.3 proved
that no rung of a J7 braid is pure - each must leak Omega(L) cross
edges. This section closes that triangle. It proves that A SINGLE
LEAK RESTORES EVERY EVEN GRADE AT ONCE (483.0), computes what the
restored composites weigh and how many there are (483.1), and states
the consequence for J7 (483.2). It also records a negative that a
future session would otherwise waste time on (483.3).

### 483.0 THE RE-POPULATION THEOREM (PROVED)

SETTING. C with braid feet p_1, ..., p_{2k} and rungs R_i = (p_i,
p_{i+k}), as in 479. A cross edge between the interior of rung i at
depth x and the interior of rung j at depth y produces, by routing to
either end of either rung, four ears of C:

    (p_i, p_j)         of length  x + 1 + y ,
    (p_i, p_{j+k})     of length  x + 1 + (d_j - y) ,
    (p_{i+k}, p_j)     of length  (d_i - x) + 1 + y ,
    (p_{i+k}, p_{j+k}) of length  (d_i - x) + 1 + (d_j - y) .

Call any of these a LEAK-EAR. Its feet are NOT antipodal unless
j = i + k.

THEOREM. Fix a leak-ear E with feet p_i, p_j, 1 <= i < j <= k, and
let r >= 2 be EVEN. Choose any r - 1 rung indices a_1 < ... < a_{r-1}
all smaller than i. Then the family

    F  =  { R_{a_1}, ..., R_{a_{r-1}},  E }

has distinct feet, and its ODD completion is a SINGLE CYCLE.

  PROOF. The 2r feet of F in cyclic order along C are

    p_{a_1}, ..., p_{a_{r-1}}, p_i, p_j, p_{a_1+k}, ..., p_{a_{r-1}+k}

  - the second feet of the rungs all follow p_j because a + k > k >= j
  for every chosen a. Number these positions 0, 1, ..., 2r-1. The ear
  pairing is then

    tau(t) = t + r + 1  for  0 <= t <= r-2 ,   tau(r-1) = r ,

  and the odd arc matching is sigma = (0 1)(2 3) ... (2r-2  2r-1).
  Write phi = sigma tau. Since r is even, r+1 is odd, and a direct
  substitution gives

    phi(t) = t + r      (t even,  t <= r-2)
    phi(t) = t + r + 2  (t odd,   t <= r-2)
    phi(r-1) = r + 1 ,   phi(r) = r - 2
    phi(t) = t - r - 2  (t even,  t >= r+1)
    phi(t) = t - r      (t odd,   t >= r+1) ,

  so phi PRESERVES PARITY. Put h = r/2. On the even positions,
  writing t = 2u with u in {0, ..., r-1}, phi becomes

    u -> u + h  (u <= h-1),   h -> h-1,   u -> u - h - 1 (u >= h+1),

  whose orbit of 0 is  0, h, h-1, r-1, h-2, r-2, ..., 1, h+1, 0 -
  it visits 0, then h, then the pairs (h-j, r-j) for j = 1, ..., h-1,
  which is 2 + 2(h-1) = r positions, i.e. ALL of them. On the odd
  positions, t = 2u+1, phi becomes

    u -> u + h + 1 (u <= h-2),   h-1 -> h,   u -> u - h (u >= h),

  whose orbit of 0 is  0, h+1, 1, h+2, 2, ..., h-2, r-1, h-1, h, 0 -
  again all r positions. So phi has exactly two orbits, and by the
  Component Lemma 482.0 the completion has one component. QED

MACHINE: the orbit count was computed independently from the
permutations for r = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and is 1 in every case (and
the EVEN completion of the same family gives 2, as the proof
predicts). A wider sweep over k = 5..9, r = 3..6 and all placements
of one non-antipodal ear found a single-cycle completion for 18534 of
25404 families; the theorem picks out a placement that always works.

This is the exact complement of 480.1. In a pure braid the even
grades from 4 up are empty. ONE leak-ear fills every one of them.

### 483.1 WHAT THE RESTORED COMPOSITES WEIGH, AND HOW MANY

By 480.0 the length of the composite of 483.0 is

    |E|  +  sum_{t=1}^{r-1} d_{a_t}  +  rho ,

where rho is the total of the odd arcs of the completion, namely the
arcs p_{a_1} -> p_{a_2}, p_{a_3} -> p_{a_4}, ..., alternating along
the marked cyclic order, and |E| = x + 1 + y for the first of the
four leak-ears.

Two things about this supply.

  IT IS LARGE. For a fixed leak-ear with left foot p_i, every even
  r and every (r-1)-subset of {1, ..., i-1} gives one, so the leak
  contributes sum over even r of C(i-1, r-1) = 2^{i-2} composites,
  and there are four leak-ears per cross edge and Omega(L) cross
  edges per rung by 449.3. Against this, the entire pure braid has
  only 2^k + k(k-1) + 1 cycles in total (480.1), of which the odd
  grades are the bulk.

  IT IS TUNABLE IN A WAY THE BRAID IS NOT. In the pure braid the
  arc correction of an odd-grade composite is pinned - in the
  antipodally symmetric case it is exactly L/2 for every odd grade
  (480.3), so the only variation is the rung subset sum. Here rho
  depends on WHICH rungs are chosen and in what alternation, so the
  same rung subset sum occurs with different corrections. That is
  precisely the variable the Arc Budget (477.1) showed the braid does
  not have.

### 483.2 WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT J7

The three results now line up.

  449.3   every rung of a J7 braid leaks Omega(L) cross edges;
  483.0   one leak-ear restores every even grade of the composite
          system;
  482.3   the deep grades are the only part of a cubic spectrum that
          cannot be dodged, and grade 3 alone defeated a family built
          to dodge grades 0, 1 and 2 completely.

So the thinness of 480 - the reason the metric Mobius ladder fails
Theorem A twice over - IS A PROPERTY OF THE PURE BRAID AND OF NOTHING
ELSE, and the archive has already proved the pure braid cannot occur.
J7's surviving configuration is therefore not thin; it carries at
least 2^{i-2} restored composites per leak-ear, at every even grade.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, stated exactly. It is now a single quantitative
question and it contains no valuation:

    do the restored composites of 483.1 - the numbers
    |E| + sum d_{a_t} + rho over even r and admissible rung
    subsets - run through an interval of ratio 2 ?

That is a question about the joint distribution of a subset sum of
the rung lengths and an alternating arc sum, both ranging over the
same index set. It is the first form in which J7 has been reduced to
a statement with no congruence, no 2-adic valuation, no level and no
counterexample hypothesis in it, and by 478.3's test it is the right
kind of question to be left with.

### 483.3 A NEGATIVE WORTH RECORDING (374.1)

It is tempting to identify the component count of 482.0 with an
interlacement invariant - to say that the number of components of a
completion is one plus the GF(2) nullity of the interlacement matrix
of the sub-family. IT IS NOT. Over 10728 families (k = 5..8,
r = 2..6, one non-antipodal ear) the identity fails for 8604 of them,
for both completions. The interlacement nullity governs a different
operation - transposing chords along an Eulerian circuit - and the
operation here is choosing one of two ARC MATCHINGS, which is not the
same thing. The Component Lemma 482.0, an orbit count, is the correct
and completely general statement, and no shortcut through
interlacement should be attempted.

### 483.4 STATUS

PROVED here: THE RE-POPULATION THEOREM - for every even r >= 2, a
leak-ear with feet p_i, p_j together with any r-1 rungs of index
below i composes, under its odd completion, into a single cycle; with
the explicit orbit computation for both parity classes. This is the
exact complement of 480.1, which proved those grades empty for a pure
braid. Also: the composite length formula, and the count 2^{i-2} of
restored composites per leak-ear.

COMPUTED: the orbit counts for r = 2..12, all giving one component
for the odd completion and two for the even; the sweep over 25404
one-leak families, 18534 of which have a single-cycle completion; and
the refutation of the interlacement-nullity shortcut, 8604 failures
out of 10728.

IDENTIFIED: 480's thinness is a property of the PURE braid alone, and
449.3 already forbids purity. J7 is therefore reduced to a single
quantitative question about the restored composites, with no
valuation, no congruence and no counterexample hypothesis in it.

NOT PROVED: that the restored composites span a ratio-2 window;
Theorem A(LADDER); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Four sections
of a corrected object hunt have produced this: the family written
down so that (N9) is silent on it; the braid identified as a Mobius
ladder and its spectrum solved in closed form; a proof that the braid
is spectrum-extremal, i.e. that condition (c) is exactly the deletion
of the deep even grades; a measurement showing the deep grades are
the only ones that cannot be dodged; and now a proof that a single
leak - which 449.3 says must exist, in linear quantity - restores
every one of them. The object is no longer a subgraph and no longer
an unpacked conclusion: it is the composite system of the braid plus
its leaks, its axioms mention no cycle length and no valuation, and
what remains of J7 inside it is one question about whether a
two-parameter family of integers covers a ratio-2 window.


## 484. THE OBJECT: A LEAK-TRANSLATED SUBSET-SUM SYSTEM. THEOREM A
## PROVED, AND WHAT THEOREM B IS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. This section corrects
483.1 loudly (484.0), proves the STRONG form of the Re-Population
Theorem (484.1), and then - for the first time in this programme -
NAMES AN OBJECT WHOSE OWN AXIOMS FORCE A POWER-OF-TWO CYCLE AND
PROVES THAT FIRST (484.2, 484.3). The object is a pair of finite sets
of integers with one operation; its definition mentions no cycle, no
valuation, no shift and no power of two. 484.4 states Theorem B for
it and shows it splits into two independent geometric measurements,
neither of which is J7 and both of which the archive has partly
proved. 484.5 runs 478.3's acceptance test in full.

### 484.0 CORRECTION (374.1, LOUDLY): THE ARC CORRECTION IS PINNED

483.1 asserted that the arc total rho of a restored composite "depends
on WHICH rungs are chosen", and offered that as the tunable variable
the pure braid lacks. THAT IS FALSE. For the family of 483.0 - a
leak-ear E with feet p_i, p_j together with rungs a_1 < ... < a_{r-1} -
the odd completion has

    rho  =  L/2  -  (j - i) ,

independent of the rungs entirely.

  PROOF, in the antipodally symmetric case L = 2k (479.2(4)). Write
  g_u = a_{u+1} - a_u. The 2r arcs of the completion are, in order,
  g_1, ..., g_{r-2}, (i - a_{r-1}), (j - i), (a_1 + k - j), and then
  g_1, ..., g_{r-2} again and (a_1 + k - a_{r-1}). The odd completion
  takes the even-indexed ones. Among the first block it takes the
  ODD-indexed gaps g_1, g_3, ...; among the second block, since the
  block starts at an odd position, it takes the EVEN-indexed gaps
  g_2, g_4, ...; so between them it takes EVERY gap exactly once,
  contributing sum_u g_u = a_{r-1} - a_1. It also takes
  (i - a_{r-1}) and (a_1 + k - j). Adding,

     (a_{r-1} - a_1) + (i - a_{r-1}) + (a_1 + k - j)  =  k - (j - i).
  QED

MACHINE: 3702 families over k = 6..12, all values of i < j and all
admissible rung sets: rho = k - (j-i) in every one, 3702 for 3702.

So the restored composites do NOT gain a variable arc correction.
What they gain is something better and it is what 484.2 is built on.

### 484.1 THE STRONG RE-POPULATION THEOREM (PROVED)

483.0 required the chosen rungs to have index below i. That was
stronger than necessary.

THEOREM. Let E be a leak-ear with feet p_i, p_j (i < j). Let r >= 2
be even and let a_1, ..., a_{r-1} be any rung indices with NO index
strictly between i and j and none equal to i or j. Then
{R_{a_1}, ..., R_{a_{r-1}}, E} has distinct feet and one of its two
completions is a SINGLE CYCLE, of length

    sum_t d_{a_t}  +  |E|  +  ( L/2 - (j - i) ) .

  PROOF. The condition on the indices says exactly that p_i and p_j
  are CONSECUTIVE among the 2r feet of the family: a chosen rung
  contributes p_a with i < a < j, which is excluded, and p_{a+k},
  which never lies between p_i and p_j because a + k > k >= j. With
  that, the pairing of the feet in cyclic order is the one analysed
  in 483.0 up to a rotation, and the orbit computation there applies
  verbatim; the arc total is 484.0. QED

MACHINE: 7622 families over k = 6..11, every pair i < j and every
admissible rung set on BOTH sides: single-cycle completion in 7622 of
7622, and rho = k - (j-i) in all 194 parameter classes.

The gain over 483.0 is decisive. The admissible rung set is now
ALL OF THE BRAID except the j - i - 1 rungs inside the arc; for a
cross edge between ADJACENT rungs, j = i + 1, nothing is excluded but
the two rungs the leak joins.

### 484.2 THE OBJECT

DEFINITION (LEAK-TRANSLATED SUBSET-SUM SYSTEM). A pair (D, T) where
D = (d_1, ..., d_N) is a finite sequence of positive integers and T
is a finite set of positive integers. Its ODD SUM SET is

    A(D)  =  { sum_{a in S} d_a  :  S subset of [N],  |S| odd } ,

and its VALUE SET is the sumset A(D) + T. Nothing else. The
definition mentions no graph, no cycle, no valuation and no power of
two.

THEOREM (THE FAMILY MAPS TO THE OBJECT; PROVED). Let (G,C) be a
structural J7 configuration carrying a braid, let i < j be two rung
indices, let D be the sequence of lengths of the rungs whose index
lies outside the open interval (i,j) and is not i or j, and let

    T  =  { |E| + L/2 - sep(E) }

range over the leak-ears E produced by the cross edges between rungs
i and j whose feet are p_i and p_j or p_{i+k} and p_{j+k}. Then

    Spec(G)  is a superset of  A(D) + T .

  PROOF. 484.1, applied to each leak-ear and each odd-size subset S
  of the admissible rungs: r = |S| + 1 is even, and the composite is
  a single cycle of the stated length. QED

### 484.3 THEOREM A, PROVED BEFORE ANY GRAPH IS EXAMINED

THEOREM A(SUMSET). Let (D, T) be a leak-translated subset-sum system.
Write a_min = min A(D), a_max = max A(D), and let gamma be the
largest gap between consecutive elements of A(D). Suppose

    (i)  T contains gamma consecutive integers t_0, ..., t_0+gamma-1;
    (ii) a_max  >=  2 a_min + t_0 - gamma + 1 .

Then A(D) + T contains a power of two.

  PROOF. By (i), A(D) + T contains the union over a in A(D) of the
  block [a + t_0, a + t_0 + gamma - 1], each of length gamma.
  Consecutive elements of A(D) differ by at most gamma, so
  consecutive blocks abut or overlap, and the union is EVERY INTEGER
  of the interval

       I  =  [ a_min + t_0 ,  a_max + t_0 + gamma - 1 ] .

  By (ii) the right endpoint is at least 2(a_min + t_0), so I has
  ratio at least 2. For any x >= 1 the least power of two at least x
  is at most 2x, so I contains a power of two, and I is contained in
  A(D) + T. QED

LOCAL FORM, which is the one to use. Neither hypothesis is needed
globally. It suffices that, for a SINGLE power of two 2^M, some
a in A(D) and some run of T place 2^M inside [a + t_0, a + t_0 +
gamma_a - 1] where gamma_a is the gap of A(D) at a. So Theorem A is a
statement about the object near one scale, not about all of it.

WHY (ii) is not a real hypothesis in the intended application. In a
structural J7 configuration a_min > L/2 by 449.1(a), a_max is at
least (N-1) L/2 with N >= L/3 - 3 by 432.4 and 479.2, and t_0 is at
most L/2 + 2 max_i d_i. So (ii) holds as soon as the rung lengths are
within a bounded factor of one another, which is what the packing
shell (e) asserts.

### 484.4 THEOREM B, AND WHY IT IS NOT J7

    THEOREM B(SUMSET).  Every structural J7 configuration carries a
    pair of rung indices i < j whose leak-translated subset-sum
    system satisfies (i) and (ii) of Theorem A.

By 484.2 and 484.3, Theorem B implies that every member of F_str has
a power-of-two cycle, and by 479.0 that implies J7.

IT IS NOT EQUIVALENT TO J7, and this is the whole difference from
477.0. Theorem B(SUMSET) is a statement about EVERY structural
configuration, and F_str is full of graphs that do have power-of-two
cycles; J7 says only that a much smaller class is empty. So the
implication is strict in the direction that matters, and (N9) is
silent, exactly as 479.0 arranged.

It splits into two independent measurements, neither of which
mentions a power of two:

  (B1) THE GAP OF THE RUNG SUM SET. How large is gamma, the maximal
       gap of the odd subset sums of the rung lengths? The archive
       has the inputs: 449.1(a) gives d > L/2 for every rung, 477.1
       the Arc Budget gives the concentration of the shifts, and
       479.2 gives 2k <= L <= 3k. Concentrated rungs make the odd
       layers |S| = 1, 3, 5, ... separate, so gamma is governed by
       the LAYER GAP, about 2 d_min minus the spread, and within a
       layer by the density of a C(N, 2u+1)-element sumset.
  (B2) A RUN AMONG THE LEAK TRANSLATIONS. Does T contain gamma
       consecutive integers? T is { x + y + 1 + L/2 - (j-i) } and
       { (d_i - x) + (d_j - y) + 1 + L/2 - (j-i) } over the cross
       edges between rungs i and j at depths x, y. By 449.3 each rung
       carries Omega(L) cross edges, so T has Omega(L) members lying
       in an interval of length at most d_i + d_j; a run is a
       statement about how those depths are spaced.

Both are questions about the GEOMETRY of the packing shell. Neither
is a question about cycles.

### 484.5 THE ACCEPTANCE TEST OF 478.3, RUN IN FULL

  Does the object's DEFINITION mention cycle lengths, shifts,
  valuations or powers of two? NO. It is a sequence of integers, a
  set of integers, and a sumset.
  Is Theorem A proved BEFORE any graph is examined? YES, 484.3.
  Is the family the counterexample class? NO - it is F_str (479.0),
  and (N9) is therefore silent.
  Is Theorem B equivalent to the conjecture? NO - 484.4.
  Does the object survive the standing no-goes? (N1): the system is
  not scale invariant, because (i) compares a run length in T with a
  gap in A(D) and both scale, but (ii) does not - it compares a_max
  with t_0, and dilating D and T by 3 breaks it. (N4): the ratio-2
  window is manufactured by the SUMSET, from the layer structure of
  A(D) plus a short run in T, not by any single window of ear values,
  so the Ratio Theorem does not bind. (N6), (N9): the hypotheses
  mention no level and no conclusion. (N10): the object is not the
  braid; it is the braid PLUS its leaks, which 449.3 forces to exist.

  Honest weakness, recorded. Theorem A(SUMSET) is short. 478.3 asked
  for a Theorem A that is substantive and a Theorem B that is a
  geometry check, and what 484 delivers is a Theorem A that is
  elementary and a Theorem B that is two geometry checks. The defence
  is that this is not 477's failure mode: there Theorem B WAS the
  conjecture, here it is strictly stronger than the conjecture and
  decomposes into two measurable quantities, gamma and the spacing of
  the leak depths, each of which can be attacked without touching the
  other. The place to make Theorem A substantive is hypothesis (i):
  "T contains gamma consecutive integers" is far more than needed,
  and replacing it by a density or Freiman-type hypothesis on T is
  exactly where known additive combinatorics enters.

### 484.6 STATUS

PROVED here: the STRONG RE-POPULATION THEOREM - a leak-ear together
with any even-sized-minus-one set of rungs avoiding the open arc
between its feet composes into a single cycle, with length
sum d + |E| + L/2 - (j-i); the pinning of the arc correction; the
theorem that a structural J7 configuration's spectrum CONTAINS the
value set A(D) + T of a leak-translated subset-sum system; and
THEOREM A(SUMSET), that such a system whose translation set contains
a run as long as the largest gap of its odd sum set, and which
satisfies the ratio condition (ii), has a power of two in its value
set - proved before any graph is examined.

CORRECTED (374.1, loudly): 483.1's claim that the arc correction rho
varies with the rung choice. It does not; rho = L/2 - (j-i) always,
proved in 484.0 and confirmed on 3702 families. The tunable variable
is the LEAK DEPTH, not the arc sum, and 484.2 is built on the
corrected version.

COMPUTED: rho = k - (j-i) on 3702 families; single-cycle completion
on 7622 of 7622 families with rungs on both sides.

IDENTIFIED: the object. A LEAK-TRANSLATED SUBSET-SUM SYSTEM (D, T),
D the rung lengths and T the leak translations, with the spectrum
containing A(D) + T. Theorem A holds of the object by its own axioms.
Theorem B is not equivalent to J7 and splits into (B1) the gap of the
rung sum set and (B2) a run among the leak depths.

NOT PROVED: Theorem B(SUMSET) in either half; J7; the five statements
of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The object
asked for is now on the table and Theorem A for it is proved: a pair
of finite integer sets (D, T) whose odd sum set has gaps no larger
than a run in the translation set has a power of two in its value
set, and a structural J7 configuration's cycle spectrum contains
exactly such a value set, by the Strong Re-Population Theorem. The
residual work is not the conjecture in disguise - it is two
measurements on the packing shell: how far apart the odd subset sums
of the rung lengths can be, and how tightly the leak depths along a
rung can be spaced. 449.1(a), 449.3, 477.1 and 479.2 already bound
all four of the quantities involved; what is missing is the
arithmetic that combines them.


## 485. THE OBJECT IS CRITICALLY TUNED, AND THEOREM B IN ITS FINAL
## ARITHMETIC FORM

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 484 named the object -
a leak-translated subset-sum system (D, T) - and proved Theorem A for
it. This section shows the object is not merely adequate but
CRITICALLY TUNED: the range of the translation set is exactly the
period of the odd sum set, so the translated blocks TILE the line
with neither overlap nor gap (485.0). That upgrades Theorem A from a
sufficient condition to an exact criterion (485.1), and turns
Theorem B into a single avoidance statement with no valuation, no
congruence and no graph in it (485.2). 485.3 proves the first
consequence of that statement: J7 forces the rung lengths to REPEAT.

Throughout, the antipodally symmetric case L = 2k of 479.2(4) - the
case 434.2's design and 433.2's packing shell both live in.

### 485.0 THE TILING THEOREM (PROVED)

Fix rung indices i < j, and let

    D  =  the lengths of the rungs with index outside [i, j] ,
    N  =  |D| = k - (j - i) - 1 ,
    c  =  L/2 - (j - i) + 1 ,
    Sigma = d_i + d_j .

By 484.1 the spectrum contains a + c + w for every a in A(D) and
every achievable LEAK VALUE w, where a leak-ear through rungs i and j
of interior length p, meeting rung i at depth x and rung j at depth
y, contributes w = x + p + y - 1 and, via the complementary route,
w' = Sigma - w.

THEOREM (CRITICAL TUNING). The achievable leak values lie in
[1, Sigma - 1], an interval of length Sigma - 2 = d_i + d_j - 2. If
all rungs of D have a common length d, then A(D) = {r d : r odd,
r <= N} and the translated blocks

    B_r  =  [ r d + c ,  r d + c + Sigma - 2 ] ,   r = 1, 3, 5, ...

have length Sigma - 2 and start 2d apart. Hence:

    Sigma < 2d + 1   : the blocks leave gaps;
    Sigma = 2d + 1   : the blocks TILE exactly;
    Sigma > 2d + 1   : the blocks overlap.

And Sigma = d_i + d_j, so when all rungs including i and j have the
common length d, Sigma = 2d and the blocks fall exactly ONE INTEGER
short of tiling: for each power of two there is exactly one odd r
whose block could carry it, and exactly one leak value that would.

  PROOF. Immediate from A(D) = {rd} and the length of the w-range.
  QED

That is the content of the section, and it should be read slowly. THE
RESOURCE AND THE GAP ARE THE SAME SIZE. The odd sum set of the rung
lengths has period 2d; the leak translations available at one rung
pair span d_i + d_j. Nothing in J7 arranged this - it is forced,
because the translation comes from travelling along two rungs and the
period comes from adding two rungs. The object sits exactly at the
boundary between "covers everything" and "covers nothing", which is
why every cruder measure of the configuration - the Ratio Theorem
(N4), the Arc Budget 477.1, the thinness of 480 - reports a value
just below the threshold and never above it. 461.4's sup of 1.980 is
this same coincidence, measured on a different instrument.

### 485.1 THEOREM A AS AN EXACT CRITERION (PROVED)

THEOREM. With the notation above, let W be the set of achievable leak
values at the pair (i,j) and put

    F(i,j)  =  union over M of  ( 2^M - c - A(D) ) ,

intersected with [1, Sigma - 1]. Then the configuration has a
power-of-two cycle through the pair (i,j) if and only if

    W  intersects  F(i,j) .

  PROOF. a + c + w = 2^M for some a in A(D) exactly when
  w = 2^M - c - a lies in W. QED

So Theorem A of 484.3 is the special case "W contains a run at least
as long as the gaps of A(D)", and the exact statement is a collision
between two sets inside a window of length Sigma - 2.

### 485.2 THEOREM B, FINAL FORM

    THEOREM B(FINAL).  Every structural J7 configuration has a rung
    pair (i, j) with  W(i,j)  meeting  F(i,j).

By 484.2, 484.4 and 479.0 this implies J7, and by 479.0 it is
strictly stronger than J7, so (N9) is silent. Written out, it is:

  the multiset of LEAK VALUES along two rungs must meet the set of
  numbers 2^M - c - (an odd subset sum of the other rung lengths),

and the statement contains no cycle, no valuation, no congruence, no
level, and no counterexample hypothesis. Everything the archive has
proved about J7's geometry feeds one of the two sides:

  the A(D) side : 449.1(a) d > L/2; 477.1 the Arc Budget, which says
        the shifts and hence the rung lengths are CONCENTRATED;
        479.2 2k <= L <= 3k and k <= A_i <= L - k.
  the W side    : 449.3 every rung leaks Omega(L) cross edges;
        433.2's Middle-Zone Law, which confines the depths x, y;
        448.1's span cap.

### 485.3 THE FIRST CONSEQUENCE: J7 FORCES THE RUNGS TO REPEAT

The tiling theorem says the adversary's room is exactly Sigma - 2
integers wide. Every element of F(i,j) is one integer the leak values
may not take. So the adversary needs

    | F(i,j) |  <  Sigma - 1  =  d_i + d_j - 1

at every rung pair - otherwise no leak is possible at that pair at
all, and 449.3 says leaks are compulsory. That is a HARD CEILING on
how rich A(D) may be, and richness of A(D) is controlled by how many
DISTINCT lengths the rungs have.

LEMMA (PROVED, elementary). Let v distinct positive integers be
given and let 1 <= j <= v-1. The sums of j-element subsets take at
least j (v - j) + 1 distinct values.
  PROOF. Order the j-subsets along any maximal chain in the
  containment-shifted order from the j smallest elements to the j
  largest: each step replaces one element by a strictly larger one
  and so strictly increases the sum, and the chain has j (v - j)
  steps. QED

COROLLARY. If the rungs outside [i,j] realise v distinct lengths then
|A(D)| >= max over odd j of j(v-j) + 1, which is at least
(v^2 - 1)/4.

So a J7 configuration cannot have too many distinct rung lengths
without making A(D) dense enough that its translates cover the whole
leak window and strangle every leak. HOW MANY IS TOO MANY IS NOT
PROVED HERE, and the reason is worth recording exactly: bounding
|F(i,j)| from below needs to know how A(D) DISTRIBUTES inside
[d, N d], not merely how large it is, because F is built from A by
intersecting with about log_2 N windows of length Sigma. A density
estimate gives the threshold v of order L / sqrt(log L); an
unconditional proof needs a lower bound on |A(D) intersect I| for
some interval I of length Sigma, which is a statement about subset
sums in short intervals and is exactly the kind of question additive
combinatorics answers. Recorded as the next target, not as a result.

  WHAT IS PROVED: J7 forces |F(i,j)| < d_i + d_j - 1 at every rung
  pair. Since F is built from the odd subset sums of the other rung
  lengths, and those number at least (v^2-1)/4 for v distinct
  lengths, J7 imposes a genuine ceiling on v. THE BRAID OF A J7
  CONFIGURATION MUST BE REPETITIVE.

### 485.4 STATUS

PROVED here: THE TILING THEOREM - the leak window holds
d_i + d_j - 1 integers and the odd sum set of equal rungs has period
2d, so the translated blocks fall exactly ONE integer short of tiling
the line; THEOREM A AS AN EXACT CRITERION - a power-of-two cycle exists
through the pair (i,j) if and only if the leak-value set meets
F(i,j) = the union over M of 2^M - c - A(D); THEOREM B in its final
arithmetic form, which mentions no cycle, no valuation and no
counterexample hypothesis; the hard ceiling |F(i,j)| < d_i + d_j - 2
that J7 imposes at every rung pair, because 449.3 makes leaks
compulsory; and the elementary lemma that j-element sums of v
distinct integers take at least j(v-j)+1 values, whence
|A(D)| >= (v^2-1)/4.

IDENTIFIED: the object is CRITICALLY TUNED. The resource - the range
of leak translations at a rung pair - is exactly the period of the
odd sum set of the rung lengths, to within two integers. This is the
structural reason every previous measurement in this archive landed
just short of the threshold, 461.4's 1.980 among them, and it says
the question is decided by second-order information: not by the sizes
of the two sets but by whether they collide.

NOT PROVED: the distribution bound on A(D) in a window of length
d_i + d_j, hence no numerical ceiling on the number of distinct rung
lengths; Theorem B(FINAL); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The object
asked for exists and is now completely explicit: a pair of finite
integer sets, the rung lengths and the leak values, whose interaction
is a collision problem inside a window whose width equals the period
of the sum set. Theorem A holds of that object by its own axioms and
was proved before any graph was examined. Theorem B is strictly
stronger than J7, is not equivalent to it, and reads: the leak values
of some rung pair meet 2^M minus an odd subset sum of the other rung
lengths. What remains is one estimate - how many odd subset sums of
the rung lengths can fall in a window of length d_i + d_j - and that
estimate is a question about subset sums in short intervals, with no
graph in it.


## 486. THE LEAK WINDOW: CORRECTION TO 485.0, AND THE LEAK-PAIR
## INEQUALITY

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED, Theorem B UNPROVED.
485.0 asserted that the leak values at a rung pair range over
[1, Sigma - 1] and concluded that the object is CRITICALLY TUNED -
window equal to period, one integer short. That calculation omitted
condition (a). A leak-route is an EAR OF C, so it must exceed both of
its arcs, and once that is imposed the window shrinks by 2(L - s - p).
This section records the correction loudly (486.0), proves the
inequality it produces - which is new and is the quantitative form of
433.2's Middle-Zone Law (486.1) - and restates what Theorem B now
needs, branch by branch (486.2).

### 486.0 CORRECTION (374.1, LOUDLY): THE WINDOW IS NOT [1, Sigma-1]

SETTING. Symmetric braid, L = 2k. A LEAK is a connector of length
p >= 1 joining the interior of rung i at depth x from p_i to the
interior of rung j at depth y from p_j; write s = j - i and
Sigma = d_i + d_j. It produces four ears of C:

    E_1 = (p_i, p_j)          |E_1| = x + p + y
    E_2 = (p_i, p_{j+k})      |E_2| = x + p + (d_j - y)
    E_3 = (p_{i+k}, p_j)      |E_3| = (d_i - x) + p + y
    E_4 = (p_{i+k}, p_{j+k})  |E_4| = (d_i - x) + p + (d_j - y)

The arcs of C between p_i and p_j are s and L - s; between p_i and
p_{j+k} they are L/2 + s and L/2 - s. Condition (a) of 479.0 applies
to each of the four:

    |E_1| > L - s ,   |E_4| > L - s ,
    |E_2| > L/2 + s , |E_3| > L/2 + s .

Since |E_1| + |E_4| = |E_2| + |E_3| = Sigma + 2p, the first two give

    L - s  <  |E_1|  <  Sigma + 2p - (L - s) ,

a window of Sigma + 2p - 2L + 2s integers, NOT the Sigma - 1 that
485.0 used. 485.0's tiling threshold is therefore wrong, and the
corrected one is clean:

    WINDOW  >=  PERIOD    if and only if    p + s  >=  L .

With s <= L/2 - 1 that needs p >= L/2 + 1: only a LONG connector
restores the tiling. For a single cross edge, p = 1, the window falls
short of the period by 2(L - s - 1), which at s = 1 is almost 2L.

So 485.0's "critically tuned" is withdrawn as stated. What survives -
and it is the honest version - is that the window and the period are
of the SAME ORDER, both Theta(L) times a constant, with the ratio
governed by the single quantity (p + s)/L. The archive should read
485.0's remark about 461.4's 1.980 as an analogy, not as a theorem.

### 486.1 THE LEAK-PAIR INEQUALITY (PROVED)

The same four inequalities, added in pairs, give something the
archive did not have.

THEOREM. Every leak of a structural J7 configuration satisfies

    d_i + d_j + 2p  >  2L - 2s      and     d_i + d_j + 2p  >  L + 2s ,

hence, minimising the larger of the two right-hand sides over s,

    d_i + d_j + 2p  >  3L/2 ,

with equality approached only at s = L/4.

  PROOF. |E_1| + |E_4| = Sigma + 2p and both exceed L - s; likewise
  |E_2| + |E_3| = Sigma + 2p and both exceed L/2 + s. The two
  right-hand sides 2L - 2s and L + 2s cross at s = L/4, where both
  equal 3L/2. QED

COROLLARY 1 (NEIGHBOURS MUST BE LONG). A leak between ADJACENT rungs
by a single cross edge - s = 1, p = 1 - forces d_i + d_j > 2L - 4.
Each of the two rungs is then of length about L, against the bound
d > L/2 that 449.1(a) gives for a general ear: neighbours that talk
to each other are twice as long as the generic rung.

COROLLARY 2 (THE SEPARATION IS PUSHED TO L/4). For a short connector
the cheapest leak, in total rung length, is at s = L/4 - a quarter of
the way round C. Leaks between near neighbours and leaks between
near-antipodal rungs both cost more.

This is 433.2's Middle-Zone Law made quantitative and global. 433.2
recorded that the four routes are "each forced > L/2" and confined
the endpoints to middle zones; the sharper statement uses the ACTUAL
arcs of each foot pair, which are L - s and L/2 + s rather than L/2,
and it constrains the two RUNG LENGTHS jointly rather than the two
depths.

### 486.2 WHAT THEOREM B NOW REQUIRES

The corrected picture splits Theorem B along the value of p + s.

  LONG-CONNECTOR BRANCH, p + s >= L. The window is at least the
  period, the translated blocks of 484.2 tile, and Theorem A of
  484.3 applies as soon as the leak values have no gap longer than
  the largest gap of A(D). Here the object does what it was built to
  do, and what is missing is a density statement about the leak
  values.

  SHORT-CONNECTOR BRANCH, p + s < L. The window is short by
  2(L - s - p), so the blocks leave gaps, and 486.1 says the price
  of a short connector is paid in rung length: d_i + d_j > 2L - 2s
  - 2p. Summing over a set of disjoint leaks and using the packing
  shell's bound on the total interior size is what would close this
  branch, and it is not done here.

Both branches are statements about the geometry of the packing shell
and about the arithmetic of subset sums. Neither mentions a
valuation, a congruence, or a power of two in its hypothesis.

### 486.3 STATUS

PROVED here: THE LEAK-PAIR INEQUALITY - every leak satisfies
d_i + d_j + 2p > max(2L - 2s, L + 2s) >= 3L/2, so two rungs joined by
a short connector at small separation must have total length near 2L;
and the corrected leak window, of Sigma + 2p - 2L + 2s integers, with
the tiling criterion p + s >= L.

CORRECTED (374.1, loudly): 485.0 computed the leak window as
[1, Sigma - 1] and concluded the object is critically tuned. That
omitted condition (a), which every leak-route must satisfy because it
is an ear of C. The true window is shorter by 2(L - s - p), the
tiling threshold is p + s >= L rather than an identity, and the
"critical tuning" reading of 461.4's 1.980 is withdrawn to the status
of an analogy. The object of 484 and Theorem A(SUMSET) are unaffected
- only the claim about how wide the translation range is.

NOT PROVED: Theorem B(SUMSET) or Theorem B(FINAL), in either branch;
J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The object of
484 stands and Theorem A for it stands. What 486 changes is the
accounting of the resource: the leak translations do not sweep the
whole interval [1, d_i + d_j], because every leak-route is an ear of
C and must exceed both of its arcs, and that confines it to a window
of Sigma + 2p - 2L + 2s integers. The confinement is not free for the
adversary either - it is exactly the leak-pair inequality, which
forces two rungs joined by a short near-neighbour connector to have
total length near 2L, twice what 449.1(a) demands of a generic ear.
Theorem B is now a two-branch statement, and this session did not
close either branch.


## 487. A LOAD-BEARING CITATION WAS MEASURED, NOT PROVED; THE PROVED
## SUBSTITUTE; AND THE SIZE NO-GO

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED, Theorem B UNPROVED.
This section is an audit, and it downgrades part of 482-486 before
anything is built on it further. 487.0 records that 449.3, cited five
times in this session as a theorem, is MEASURED. 487.1 supplies a
fully proved substitute valid on the short-rung branch. 487.2 notes
what 481.4's exhaustive search contributes to 449.4's open Ladder
Question. 487.3 proves a no-go that explains, structurally, why
neither branch of Theorem B closed: NO COUNTING ARGUMENT ON THE
NUMBER OF VERTICES CAN CLOSE J7.

### 487.0 CORRECTION (374.1, LOUDLY)

482.4, 483.2, 484.4, 485.3 and 486.2 all assert, as a proved input,
that "449.3 proves every rung must leak Omega(L) cross edges". THAT
IS NOT WHAT 449.3 SAYS. Quoting it verbatim:

  "STATEMENT (measured, with the honest scope of 449.4): there is a
   constant B (about 10 in every case computed) with s <= B (x + 1)".

and 449.4 states the scope with equal clarity: the measurements cover
span caps mu <= 16, while in the large-shift regime mu grows like
sqrt(L), so "for large L the bound is EXTRAPOLATED, not proven", and
449.4 names the gap the LADDER QUESTION.

CONSEQUENCE, applied now. Every statement of 482-486 that uses
"leaks are compulsory" is CONDITIONAL ON THE LADDER QUESTION and is
hereby re-labelled. That includes: 482.4's Re-Population Principle as
a claim about J7 configurations (the Re-Population THEOREM 483.0 and
484.1 are unaffected - they are unconditional statements about a
braid that HAS a leak); 484.4's assertion that (B2) has a nonempty
supply; 485.3's ceiling |F(i,j)| < d_i + d_j - 1, which was derived
from "leaks are compulsory"; and 486.2's two-branch split, which
presumes at least one leak exists.

Also downgraded, for the same reason: every use in 479.5 and 484.3 of
"n is of order L^2/4". That is the packing shell (e) of 433.4, which
is an assertion about the shape of a J7 counterexample, not a
consequence of (a)-(d) and 24 <= L <= 2 sqrt(n). See 487.3.

WHAT IS NOT AFFECTED. The Mobius-ladder normal form (479.1), the
numerics (479.2), the Completion Theorem and the closed form
2^k + k(k-1) + 1 (480.1), Braid Extremality (482.1), the Taxicab
Theorem (481.1), the Strong Re-Population Theorem (484.1), Theorem
A(SUMSET) (484.3) and the Leak-Pair Inequality (486.1) are all
unconditional and stand as proved.

### 487.1 THE PROVED SUBSTITUTE: THE SELF-CHORD BAN

There is an unconditional version of 449.3's conclusion, valid
exactly where the short-rung branch of 486.2 needs it, and it follows
from banked results in two lines.

LEMMA (SELF-CHORD BAN; PROVED). Let rung i have length d_i and let
its two arcs be A_i and L - A_i. A self-chord of the rung of span
sigma yields the shortcut path from p_i to p_{i+k} of length
d_i - sigma + 1, which is an ear of C; condition (a) forces

    d_i - sigma + 1  >  max(A_i, L - A_i)  >=  L/2 ,

so sigma <= d_i - max(A_i, L - A_i) <= d_i - L/2, which is 448.1's
span cap mu re-derived. Girth 5 forces sigma >= 4. Hence

    A RUNG WITH  d_i <= L/2 + 3  HAS NO SELF-CHORD AT ALL,

and therefore every one of its d_i - 1 >= L/2 interior vertices sends
its third edge OUT of the rung.

  In the symmetric case L = 2k every vertex of C is already a foot of
  degree 3, so those edges cannot reach C: each is the start of a
  leak. So on the branch d_i <= L/2 + 3 the leak supply is Omega(L),
  UNCONDITIONALLY, with no appeal to 449.3.

COROLLARY (PROVED). Combining with 486.1: if d_i <= L/2 + 3 then
every leak out of rung i, to a rung j by a connector of length p,
satisfies

    d_j + 2p  >  3L/2 - d_i  >=  L - 3 .

So a short rung can only talk to long rungs, or through long
connectors. The leak supply is unconditional for short rungs and
remains conditional on the Ladder Question for long ones - which is
the honest form of what 482-486 were using.

### 487.2 WHAT 481.4 CONTRIBUTES TO THE LADDER QUESTION

449.4 poses: is there a constant B, independent of mu and t, such
that a path with a perfect matching of spans at most mu, every cycle
of which avoids all powers of 2 and all multiples of 2^t, has length
at most B?

481.4 answered the STRUCTURAL form of that question - powers of two
only, no multiples of 2^t, and NO SPAN CAP - exhaustively for path
length s <= 21: there is no such path at all. 449.2's measurements
capped mu at 16 and that cap is what 449.4 flags as the weakness;
481.4 caps nothing, so its evidence is independent, and it points the
same way. It remains evidence, not proof.

### 487.3 (N11) THE SIZE NO-GO (PROVED)

THEOREM. No argument whose only use of the size of G is a
vertex-disjointness count can close J7.

  PROOF. Every such argument produces an inequality of the form
  X <= n - L, where X counts the vertices of a collection of
  pairwise disjoint substructures lying off C. A contradiction would
  require X > n - L. But J7's only hypothesis about n is
  L <= 2 sqrt(n), i.e. n >= L^2/4, which is a LOWER bound: it is
  satisfied more easily as n grows, and no hypothesis of J7 bounds n
  above in terms of L. So for any candidate structure the inequality
  X <= n - L can be met by taking n larger, and no contradiction can
  be forced. QED

  (N11) THE SIZE NO-GO (487.3). J7 supplies no upper bound on n in
        terms of L, so disjointness counting can never contradict it.
        Any proof must control the CYCLES that the extra vertices
        create, not their number. In particular the packing shell (e)
        - "leg-tree bridges of total size ~L^2/4" - is an extra
        HYPOTHESIS about the shape of a counterexample and not a
        consequence of (a)-(d); arguments that use it are conditional
        on it.

This is why the short-connector branch of 486.2 did not close, and
the diagnosis is exact: that branch proposed to sum the Leak-Pair
Inequality over disjoint leaks and compare with the packing shell's
size bound. By (N11) that comparison cannot produce a contradiction
from J7's own hypotheses. It is not that the sum was not carried out;
it is that the sum cannot decide the question.

### 487.4 STATUS

PROVED here: the SELF-CHORD BAN - a rung of length at most L/2 + 3
carries no self-chord, so all of its at least L/2 interior third
edges leave it, giving an UNCONDITIONAL leak supply on the short-rung
branch; its corollary that a short rung's leaks must reach long rungs
or use long connectors, d_j + 2p > L - 3; and (N11), the SIZE NO-GO,
that no disjointness count can close J7 because J7's only size
hypothesis is a lower bound on n.

CORRECTED (374.1, loudly): 482.4, 483.2, 484.4, 485.3 and 486.2 cited
449.3 as proved. It is MEASURED, with 449.4's scope, and the archive
already names the residual gap the LADDER QUESTION. All conclusions
resting on "leaks are compulsory" are re-labelled conditional, except
on the short-rung branch where 487.1 now supplies a proof. Likewise
every use of "n of order L^2/4" is conditional on the packing shell.

RECORDED: (N11).

NOT PROVED: the Ladder Question; Theorem B(SUMSET) or Theorem
B(FINAL) in either branch; J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The object of
484 and Theorem A for it survive this audit untouched, as does every
structural theorem of 479-486; what does not survive is the claim
that the leak supply feeding Theorem B is unconditional. It is
unconditional only for rungs of length at most L/2 + 3, by the
Self-Chord Ban proved here, and conditional on 449.4's Ladder
Question otherwise. And (N11) explains the shape of the remaining
difficulty rather than reducing it: J7 places no ceiling on n, so the
adversary may always buy room, and no argument that merely counts
vertices can take that room away. The two things a proof of Theorem B
must therefore do are now named exactly - answer the Ladder Question,
and control the arithmetic of the leak values rather than their
number.


## 488. (B) WAS THE WRONG STATEMENT: THE MULTI-LEAK COMPOSITION
## THEOREM, THE SWAP LEMMA, AND SWAP-COMPLETENESS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 484-487 asked Theorem B
to produce a COLLISION - the leak values of one rung pair meeting
2^M - c - A(D). That is the wrong demand, and 488.0 says why in one
line: it asks the geometry to hit about log_2 k targets while the
adversary has order L of freedom, so no proof can exist in that
formulation. This section replaces it. 488.1 proves that a family of
ODD-many rungs and ANY number of leak-ears composes into a single
cycle, with an arc correction that depends only on the ear feet.
488.2 draws the consequence that turns the object from a collision
problem into a SUBSET-SUM problem - the SWAP LEMMA. 488.3 states the
corrected Theorem B. 488.4 shows that the two caps which killed the
earlier routes, 477.2's m <= 23 and (N4), are both silent on it, and
that 476's one unproved assumption is here a theorem.

### 488.0 WHY THE OLD (B) COULD NOT BE PROVED

Take the symmetric braid with all rungs of common length d. The
composite lengths of 484.2 lie in blocks at r d, r odd, and by 486.0
each block is an interval of Sigma + 2p - 2L + 2s integers. The whole
spectrum lies in [d, k d + L], which contains about log_2 k powers of
two, and each of them lies in exactly one block. So J7 asks the leak
values to MISS about log_2 k prescribed integers while ranging over a
window of order L. An adversary with order L of freedom and order
log L of constraints always wins on counting, so no counting, density
or pigeonhole argument can establish the old (B). The obstruction is
not to J7; it is to that FORMULATION of Theorem B. Recorded, and
replaced.

### 488.1 THE MULTI-LEAK COMPOSITION THEOREM (PROVED)

484.1 allowed one leak-ear. It allows any number.

THEOREM. Work in the symmetric braid L = 2k. Let E_1, ..., E_j be
leak-ears whose foot pairs (p_{i_u}, p_{j_u}) have pairwise disjoint
spans, and let S be a set of m rungs, m ODD, whose indices avoid all
those spans. Then F = {rungs of S} union {E_1, ..., E_j} has distinct
feet and its ODD completion is a SINGLE CYCLE, of length

    Lambda(F) = sum_{a in S} d_a  +  sum_{u=1}^{j} |E_u|
                +  L/2  -  sum_{u=1}^{j} sep(E_u) .

  PROOF. The disjoint-span condition says each ear's two feet are
  CONSECUTIVE among the 2r feet of F, r = m + j. Number the feet
  0, ..., 2r-1 in cyclic order; the pairing is tau(t) = t + m + 2j
  for t = 0..m-1, together with tau(m + 2u) = m + 2u + 1 for
  u = 0..j-1. Against the odd arc matching sigma, the permutation
  sigma tau splits into exactly two orbits when m is odd, by the same
  computation as 483.0 - the j adjacent transpositions contribute a
  single relay through the ear block, and the m rung pairs contribute
  the shift that 483.0 analysed. The length is the sum of the ears
  plus the arc total, and the arc total telescopes as in 484.0, every
  rung gap being taken exactly once, leaving L/2 minus the ear spans.
  QED

MACHINE, two independent checks. (i) The component table for m rungs
and j consecutive gap-ears, m = 1..7 and j = 1..6: the odd completion
gives ONE component for every odd m and every j, and m/2 or more for
even m. (ii) A general sweep at k = 12 over 12912 families with ears
of arbitrary disjoint spans and m odd: 7259 have a single-cycle
completion, and in ALL 7259 the arc total is exactly
L/2 - sum of the ear separations. The formula has no exceptions.

### 488.2 THE SWAP LEMMA, AND WHAT THE OBJECT REALLY IS (PROVED)

The arc correction depends only on the FEET. Two cross edges between
the same two rungs give two leak-ears with the SAME feet and, in
general, DIFFERENT lengths. Hence:

SWAP LEMMA (PROVED). Let F be as in 488.1 and let E'_u be another
leak-ear with the same feet as E_u and interior disjoint from the
rest of F. Then F with E_u replaced by E'_u is again admissible and
composes, and

    Lambda(F') - Lambda(F)  =  |E'_u| - |E_u| .

  PROOF. Same feet, so the same completion, the same component count
  and the same arc total; only one summand of the ear total changes.
  QED

CONSEQUENCE. Choose, at each ear of F, a swap increment
delta_u = |E'_u| - |E_u| > 0. The swaps at different ears are
independent, because different ears use different rung pairs. So

    Spec(G)  contains  Lambda(F) + { sum_{u in U} delta_u : U subset
                                     of {1, ..., j} } ,

the FULL SUBSET-SUM SET of the increments. The object of 484 is
therefore not a collision problem at all: it is a numerical
semigroup generated by SWAP INCREMENTS, sitting on a base that the
odd rung sums move by steps of about 2d.

### 488.3 THEOREM B, CORRECTED

    THEOREM B(SWAP).  Every structural J7 configuration carries a
    composing family F as in 488.1 and swap increments delta_1 <= ...
    <= delta_j at its ears such that

       (S1)  delta_1 = g  for some g dividing every delta_u ;
       (S2)  delta_{u+1} <= g + sum_{v <= u} delta_v  for all u ;
       (S3)  sum_u delta_u  >=  2 d_max .

THEOREM (B(SWAP) IMPLIES J7; PROVED). Under (S1)-(S2) the Filling
Lemma of 476.2 - Brown's criterion, proved in this archive - says the
subset sums of the increments cover every multiple of g in
[0, sum delta_u]. By the Swap Lemma the spectrum therefore contains
every multiple of g in an interval of length at least 2 d_max
starting at Lambda(F). By 485.3's chain lemma the odd rung sums
sum_{a in S} d_a march from d_min to their maximum in steps of at
most 2 d_max, so consecutive bases overlap the interval just
