TOTAL saving of a disjoint-span family by the slack (498.0). That one
inequality supersedes 496.2, removes its distinctness hypothesis,
improves its constant fourfold, and derives 433.2's square-root slack
unconditionally (498.1). Applied to (C2) it gives a complete
conditional proof (498.2) - and the condition turns out to sit
EXACTLY at the unconditional bound, which is 489.3's borderline
pattern appearing for the fifth time.

### 498.0 THE SHORTCUT BUDGET THEOREM (PROVED)

Symmetric braid, L = 2k, rung of length d with feet p_i, p_{i+k}, so
both arcs equal L/2 and the slack is mu = d - L/2 >= 1. Let F be ANY
family of self-chords of the rung with pairwise disjoint spans,
sigma_1, ..., sigma_r.

THEOREM.    sum_{t in F} ( sigma_t - 1 )   <   mu .

  PROOF. Traversing the rung and taking every chord of F replaces
  sigma_t edges by one edge for each t, the spans being disjoint, so
  the resulting path from p_i to p_{i+k} has length
  d - sum_t (sigma_t - 1). Its interior avoids C, so it is an EAR of
  C with the rung's own feet, and condition (a) requires every ear to
  exceed both arcs:
      d - sum_t (sigma_t - 1)  >  L/2 .
  Subtract. QED

COROLLARY (THE CHORD-COUNT CAP). Girth 5 gives sigma_t >= 4, so

      r  =  |F|   <   mu / 3

for every disjoint-span family. In particular the maximum
disjoint-span family has fewer than mu/3 members.

This supersedes 496.2. That theorem gave r <= 4(mu - 1)/3 and needed
the spans to be pairwise DISTINCT; 498.0 gives r < mu/3 - four times
smaller - with no hypothesis at all. 496.2 is not withdrawn, it is
absorbed.

Note what made it work: condition (a) had previously been applied to
the rung and to the leak-ears, never to the rung's own SHORTCUTS.
They are ears too, and they are the ears that the disjoint-span
families produce.

### 498.1 THE SLACK IS AT LEAST OF ORDER sqrt(L), UNCONDITIONALLY

LEMMA (COVERING, 496.2 restated). Let F be a MAXIMUM disjoint-span
family of a fully self-chorded rung, U the union of its spans. Every
chord's span meets U by maximality, and every interior position lies
on a chord of span at most mu (448.1), so every interior position is
within mu of U. Hence

      d - 1   <=   |U|  +  2 r mu ,      |U| = sum sigma_t
                                              = sum (sigma_t - 1) + r .

THEOREM. A fully self-chorded J7 rung satisfies

      2 mu^2  +  4 mu   >   3 (d - 1) ,   hence
      mu  >  ( sqrt( 4 + 6(d-1) ) - 2 ) / 2  =  Omega( sqrt d ) ,

and, substituting d = L/2 + mu,

      2 mu^2  +  mu   >   3 (L/2 - 1) ,   i.e.   mu > sqrt(3L)/2
      asymptotically.

  PROOF. By 498.0, |U| < mu + r and r < mu/3; substitute both into
  the covering lemma and clear denominators. QED

433.2 obtained the same exponent from the packing side - "outer-zone
self-absorption demands slack of order sqrt(L)", by the count
3 L/(2 mu) <= mu, i.e. mu >= sqrt(3L/2). 498.1 reaches sqrt(3L)/2 by
a completely different route, from condition (a) applied to
shortcuts. TWO INDEPENDENT DERIVATIONS OF THE SAME EXPONENT, and
496.3's remark now stands without its distinctness hypothesis.

### 498.2 (C2), PROVED UNDER A SLACK CEILING

(C2) asked whether a J7 rung can have all the spans of its
disjoint-span family congruent modulo a common g >= 3, i.e. all
v_t = sigma_t - 1 divisible by g.

THEOREM. Suppose every v_t is divisible by g. Then

      g   <   ( 4 mu^2 + 2 mu ) / ( L - 2 ) .

  PROOF. Divisibility and positivity give v_t >= g, so by 498.0
  r g <= sum v_t < mu, i.e. r < mu/g. Feed that and |U| < mu + r into
  the covering lemma: d - 1 < mu + r(1 + 2 mu) < mu + (mu/g)(1+2mu).
  Since d - 1 - mu = L/2 - 1, multiply out. QED

COROLLARY ((C2) HOLDS BELOW THE CEILING). If

      mu   <=   sqrt( 3 (L-2) ) / 2       (asymptotically sqrt(3L)/2)

then g < 3, contradicting g >= 3. SO (C2) IS TRUE FOR EVERY J7 RUNG
WHOSE SLACK IS AT MOST sqrt(3L)/2, AND FALSE-OR-UNDECIDED ONLY ABOVE
THAT CEILING. For larger g the ceiling is higher: g >= 4 needs
mu > sqrt(L), g >= 8 needs mu > sqrt(2L), and so on - the ceiling
grows like sqrt(gL)/2.

### 498.3 THE FIFTH BORDERLINE

Compare the two theorems just proved.

    498.1 (unconditional):   2 mu^2 + mu  >  3 (L/2 - 1) .
    498.2 (with g = 3):      2 mu^2 + mu  >  3 (L/2 - 1) .

THEY ARE THE SAME INEQUALITY. The bound that forces the slack to be
at least sqrt(3L)/2 is exactly the bound that would refute (C2) below
sqrt(3L)/2. There is no margin: (C2) at g = 3 is true precisely up to
the point where the slack is forced to exceed it, and not one unit
beyond.

489.3 recorded four independent near-misses in this programme, all by
the slack mu: the ratio 1.980 of 461.4, the L-4 versus L of 480.4,
the window-versus-period gap of 486.0, and the pigeonhole deficit of
489.2. THIS IS THE FIFTH, and it is the sharpest: not a deficit of
mu, but a deficit of ZERO. Whatever is true about J7, the quantity
that decides it is mu = d - L/2, and the decision is made at
mu = sqrt(3L)/2.

### 498.4 WHAT (C2) NOW NEEDS, EXACTLY

One statement, and it contains no cycles, no valuations and no
congruences:

  (CEIL) A J7 rung satisfies  mu = d - L/2  <=  sqrt(3L)/2 .

With (CEIL), 498.2 proves (C2) outright, 498.0 caps every
disjoint-span family at fewer than sqrt(3L)/6 chords, and 493.3's
ladder branch collapses. Without it, a rung of very large slack
evades everything - and by (N11) no vertex count forbids one, because
J7 bounds n only from below.

So the programme's last question is an UPPER bound on the slack, and
the archive currently has none: 448.1 bounds spans BY mu, 449.1(a)
bounds d from below, 479.2 bounds the rung COUNT above but not the
rung LENGTH. The one place an upper bound could come from is the
packing shell (e) of 433.4, which was stated as a hypothesis and has
never been derived. Deriving it - or replacing it - is the task.

### 498.5 STATUS

PROVED here: THE SHORTCUT BUDGET THEOREM - for every disjoint-span
self-chord family of a J7 rung, sum (sigma_t - 1) < mu, because the
shortcut is itself an ear and condition (a) applies to it; its
COROLLARY r < mu/3, which supersedes 496.2's r <= 4(mu-1)/3 and drops
its distinctness hypothesis; THE SLACK LOWER BOUND 2 mu^2 + 4 mu >
3(d-1), hence mu = Omega(sqrt L) unconditionally for a fully
self-chorded rung, a second independent derivation of 433.2's
square-root slack; and (C2) UNDER A CEILING - if every v_t is
divisible by g then g < (4 mu^2 + 2 mu)/(L-2), so (C2) holds whenever
mu <= sqrt(3(L-2))/2, and the ceiling for larger g grows like
sqrt(gL)/2.

IDENTIFIED: the conditional proof of (C2) at g = 3 and the
unconditional slack lower bound are THE SAME INEQUALITY. The fifth
and sharpest instance of 489.3's borderline pattern, with deficit
exactly zero.

NOT PROVED: (CEIL), hence (C2) in full; (LQ3); the Ladder Question;
(R); Theorem B(SWAP); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture. (C1) was REFUTED in 497.0 and cannot be proved.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked to prove
(C1) and (C2): (C1) is false, and 497 exhibits the failures. (C2) is
proved for every rung of slack at most sqrt(3L)/2, by a new
inequality - the shortcut budget - that comes from applying condition
(a) to an ear nobody had applied it to. Above that ceiling (C2) is
open, and the ceiling is exactly where the same inequality forces the
slack to live. The programme therefore ends this session on a single
missing fact of a kind it has never had: an UPPER bound on the slack
of a rung. Everything else it needs is now proved.


## 499. (C1) AND (C2) RESOLVED: ONE IS FALSE, THE OTHER VIOLATES (N9)

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 496.4 set two targets.
This section resolves both, and neither survives. (C1) is FALSE, by
the measurement of 497.0. (C2) is worse than false: IT IS A PROPERTY
OF THE COUNTEREXAMPLE CLASS, so by this archive's own standing no-go
(N9) it cannot be a step towards J7 - only a restatement of it. I
proposed it in 496.4 without applying (N9) to it, and that is
recorded here loudly under 374.1. 499.2 shows the ceiling route to
(C2) is closed for a second, independent reason: (CEIL) contradicts a
theorem proved one section earlier. 499.3 says what survives and what
the correct target is.

### 499.0 (C1): FALSE

Settled in 497.0. Over 250 random ladders, enumerating ALL
disjoint-span families, 196 power-of-two even-subgraph weights were
reached and only 113 had a connected representative. (C1) asserted
that a connected one always exists; it does not. A false statement
cannot be proved, and the refutation is its resolution.

### 499.1 (C2) VIOLATES (N9) (PROVED)

(C2) reads: "A J7 rung cannot have all the spans of its maximum
disjoint-span family equal, or congruent modulo a common g >= 3."

A J7 RUNG IS AN OBJECT OF THE COUNTEREXAMPLE CLASS. By 433.4 as
corrected by 434.1, a J7 configuration satisfies (f) - the ambient
graph has no cycle of length 2^k - and every statement whose subject
is "a J7 rung" is therefore a statement about graphs that violate the
conclusion. Now recall the standing no-go:

  (N9) THE CONCLUSION-DEFINED FAMILY TRAP (478.2). Let F be the class
  of counterexamples to a statement S. For ANY property Pi such that
  "Pi implies some member of F satisfies S", the assertion "F has Pi"
  is EQUIVALENT to S.

Here Pi is (C2). By 498.2, (C2) together with the shortcut budget
would collapse 493.3's ladder branch and hence close J7 - that is
exactly the hypothesis of (N9). Therefore

    (C2)   is equivalent to   J7 ,

and no proof of it can be easier than the conjecture. (C2) IS
WITHDRAWN AS A TARGET.

RECORDED (374.1). 496.4 proposed (C1) and (C2) as the two statements
on which the programme rests. (C1) was legitimate - it is a statement
about arbitrary perfect matchings, with no (f) in it - and it turned
out false. (C2) was NOT legitimate, and the error is exactly the one
478.2 was written to prevent: I equipped the counterexample class
again, three sections after proving that one must never do so. The
lesson of 478.3 has to be applied to every proposed target, not only
to the choice of object.

### 499.2 THE CEILING ROUTE IS CLOSED ANYWAY (PROVED)

Even setting (N9) aside, 498's conditional proof of (C2) cannot be
completed. It required

  (CEIL)   mu  =  d - L/2   <=   sqrt(3L)/2 .

But 498.1 PROVES the opposite inequality for exactly the rungs in
question. For a fully self-chorded rung, the shortcut budget gives
r < mu/3 and |U| < mu + r, and the covering lemma then yields
2 mu^2 + 4 mu > 3(d-1); substituting d = L/2 + mu gives

    2 mu^2 + mu  >  3 (L/2 - 1) ,   i.e.   mu  >  sqrt(3L)/2
    asymptotically.

So (CEIL) is FALSE on the ladder branch, and 498.2's corollary - "(C2)
holds whenever mu <= sqrt(3(L-2))/2" - is VACUOUS there. 498.3 had
already noticed that the two inequalities coincide; the correct
reading is not that the margin is zero but that THE CONDITIONAL
PROOF HAS NO DOMAIN. Recorded as a correction to 498.2's presentation,
not to its mathematics: the inequality g < (4 mu^2 + 2 mu)/(L-2)
stands, and it still forbids LARGE g - it gives g < 4 as soon as
mu <= sqrt(L) - but it can never reach g = 3.

### 499.3 WHAT SURVIVES, AND THE CORRECT TARGET

Two theorems of 498 are statements about the STRUCTURAL family - they
use condition (a), girth 5 and the chord geometry, and no (f) - so
(N9) is silent on them and they stand:

  THE SHORTCUT BUDGET (498.0). For every disjoint-span self-chord
  family of a rung with both arcs L/2,
      sum (sigma_t - 1) < mu ,   hence   |F| < mu/3 .
  Proof: the shortcut is an ear with the rung's own feet, and
  condition (a) applies to it.
  THE SLACK LOWER BOUND (498.1). A fully self-chorded rung satisfies
  2 mu^2 + 4 mu > 3(d - 1), so mu = Omega(sqrt L).

Both are (N9)-safe, both are new, and the second is a second
independent derivation of 433.2's square-root slack, which had been a
hypothesis of condition (e) since 433.

THE CORRECT TARGET IS (LQ3) OF 497.4, and it is (N9)-safe because its
subject is an arbitrary perfect matching, not a J7 rung:

  (LQ3) For a perfect matching of [1, 2N] with all spans at least 4
        and all non-disjoint pairs at L^1 distance at least 3, some
        chord subset T with connected completion has
        |T| + alt(endpoints of T) a power of two.

497.1 shows T must be allowed three chords; 497.0 shows T cannot be
restricted to complements of disjoint families; 495.0 shows T alone
determines the even subgraph; 494.1 pins the first and last four
positions; and 498.0 now adds that any disjoint-span sub-family of T
has total saving below the slack. Exhaustive to s = 21 and randomised
to s = 27, nothing contradicts it.

### 499.4 STATUS

PROVED here: that (C2) is equivalent to J7, by (N9) applied to it -
its subject is the counterexample class - so it is withdrawn as a
target; and that the ceiling route to it is independently closed,
because (CEIL) contradicts 498.1 on the very rungs it was needed for.

REFUTED: (C1), in 497.0.

CORRECTED (374.1), loudly: 496.4 proposed (C2) without checking it
against (N9). The check fails. Proposing a property of the
counterexample class as a step is the exact error 478.2 was written
to prevent, and it recurred three sections after that no-go was
strengthened. Every future target must be tested: DOES ITS SUBJECT
MENTION THE CONCLUSION? For (LQ3) the answer is no; for (C2) it was
yes.

IDENTIFIED: what survives of 498 is the SHORTCUT BUDGET and the SLACK
LOWER BOUND, both statements about the structural family, both new,
and together a derivation of the sqrt(L) slack that condition (e) had
only assumed.

NOT PROVED: (LQ3); the Ladder Question; (R); Theorem B(SWAP); J7; the
five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked to prove
(C1) and (C2), the honest answer is that neither can be: the first is
false and 497.0 exhibits the failures, and the second is a property
of the counterexample class, so by 478.2 it is the conjecture wearing
a different hat. The session's gain is not those two statements but
what fell out of trying: condition (a) applied to a rung's own
shortcuts, which caps every disjoint-span family below mu/3 and
forces the slack above sqrt(3L)/2 - the first derivation of the
packing shell's square root from outside the packing analysis. The
programme's target is (LQ3), it is (N9)-safe, and it is the smallest
statement this archive has ever reduced J7 to.


## 500. (LQ3) REVERSE-ENGINEERED: THE ZIGZAG FAMILY, AND THE FACTS
## THAT WOULD SETTLE IT

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 499 left (LQ3) as the
programme's only (N9)-safe target. This section does not attack it
frontally; it asks what a settled (LQ3) would have to rest on, and
works backwards. The answer is sharper than expected. 500.0 identifies
what (LQ3) actually is. 500.1 replaces the alternating sum by a better
formula. 500.2 proves a NEW NO-GO (N12): the route of 495 fails for a
second reason, independent of the connectivity failure of 497.0 - it
cannot even reach the right WEIGHTS at a positive density of scales,
so any proof must produce cycles in the MIDDLE of the spectrum. 500.3
then exhibits a family of mid-spectrum cycles that is CONNECTED BY
CONSTRUCTION - the zigzag families - which removes from (LQ3) the
exact ingredient that killed (C1). 500.4 shows the family cannot be
enlarged in the two obvious ways. 500.6 states the strengthening
(LQ4), which has no connectivity clause at all and which every ladder
tested satisfies, and 500.7 is the chart of provable facts that
deliver it.

### 500.0 WHAT (LQ3) IS (PROVED)

Let H be the graph on vertices 1, ..., 2N whose edges are the path
edges (j, j+1) and a perfect matching M. Every interior vertex has
degree 3; the ends have degree 2.

LEMMA. The two hypotheses of (LQ3) - every span at least 4, every
non-disjoint pair at L^1 distance at least 3 - hold if and only if H
has girth at least 5.
  PROOF. Chords are a basis of the cycle space of H (495.0), so every
  cycle is E(T) for a unique chord set T, and by 495.0 again the
  completion is unique. A cycle with r chords uses at least one host
  segment per chord, so its length is at least 2r; hence r >= 3 forces
  length at least 6, and only r = 1 and r = 2 can produce a cycle
  shorter than 5. Those are exactly w = sigma + 1 and, for
  non-disjoint pairs, w = 2 + L^1 (494.0). Disjoint pairs give
  disconnected completions and no cycle. QED

So, in one line:

  (LQ3) IS THE ERDOS-GYARFAS CONJECTURE FOR GRAPHS THAT ARE A
  HAMILTONIAN PATH PLUS A PERFECT MATCHING AND HAVE GIRTH AT LEAST 5.

That is the honest statement of the programme's target: a cubic graph
(bar its two ends) carrying a Hamiltonian path. It contains no t, no
2^t, no valuation, no shift, no packing shell, and above all no (f) -
so (N9) is silent on it, as 499.3 said.

TWO FREE REDUCTIONS. Let x_j be the number of chords straddling the
gap between j and j+1. Counting endpoints below j gives
x_j = j - 2 (chords inside [1,j]), so

    x_j  is congruent to  j  modulo 2 ,

hence x_j >= 1 for every odd j automatically. If x_j = 0 for some even
j the ladder SPLITS: [1, j] and [j+1, 2N] are girth-legal ladders in
their own right and every chord subset of either has the same weight
computed inside it, so (LQ3) for the pieces gives (LQ3) for the whole.
WE MAY THEREFORE ASSUME x_j >= 1 FOR ALL j - call such a ladder
IRREDUCIBLE. (Machine: the congruence held on 240 of 240 random
girth-legal ladders, N = 5..11.)

### 500.1 THE STRADDLE-PARITY FORMULA (PROVED)

The alternating sum of 497.2 is correct but blind. Here is the same
weight in a form that shows what it measures.

THEOREM. For any chord set T, the completion of T contains the host
edge (j, j+1) IF AND ONLY IF an odd number of chords of T straddle
gap j. Consequently

    w(T)  =  |T|  +  #{ j : k_T(j) is odd } ,

where k_T(j) is the number of chords of T straddling gap j.
  PROOF. The completion uses (j, j+1) exactly when an odd number of
  endpoints of T lie at or below j; that number is
  2 (chords of T inside [1, j]) + k_T(j). QED

  MACHINE: 118740 subsets over 300 girth-legal ladders, N = 5..10,
  every subset of every ladder; agreement 118740 of 118740, the weight
  recomputed each time from the explicit edge list.

Three corollaries, all verified, all used below.

  (i) THE TOGGLE FORMULA. Adding a chord c to T flips the parity of
      k on exactly the gaps inside c's span, so
          w(T + c) - w(T)  =  1 + sigma_c - 2 u_c(T) ,
      u_c(T) being the number of host edges inside c's span already
      used by T. (Machine 7200 of 7200.)
 (ii) THE PARITY INVARIANT. Hence w(T) is congruent to
      |T| + sum_{c in T} sigma_c modulo 2: A POWER-OF-TWO CYCLE MUST
      USE AN EVEN NUMBER OF EVEN-SPAN CHORDS. (Machine 7200 of 7200.)
(iii) THE DELETION CONSTANT. For T = M all straddle counts have the
      parity of j, so w(M) = 2N; deleting one chord c = (a, b) gives
          w(M - c)  =  2N - eps(c) ,
          eps(c)  =  1 + [a odd] - [b odd]  in  {0, 1, 2} ,
      and for a family S of PAIRWISE DISJOINT spans the deletions are
      independent, w(M - S) = 2N - sum_{c in S} eps(c). (Machine 2040
      of 2040 and 2931 of 2931.)

### 500.2 (N12) THE REACH LIMIT (PROVED)

497.0 refuted (C1) by showing the disjoint-family route of 495 fails
on CONNECTIVITY. It fails for a second and completely independent
reason, and this one is a theorem rather than a measurement.

THEOREM (REACH LIMIT). For every girth-legal ladder and every family
S of chords with pairwise disjoint spans,

    sum_{c in S} eps(c)   <=   (2/5) (2N - 1) ,

so every weight obtainable by the route of 495 lies in

    [ (6N + 2)/5 ,  2N ] ,

an interval of ratio 5/3 < 2.
  PROOF. eps(c) = 2 forces a odd and b even, so sigma_c is odd and,
  being at least 4, at least 5; eps(c) = 1 forces sigma_c even, hence
  at least 4. In both cases eps(c) <= (2/5) sigma_c, and eps = 0 is
  trivial. The spans of S are disjoint subintervals of [1, 2N], so
  sum sigma_c <= 2N - 1. QED

COROLLARY (THE ROUTE CANNOT REACH). Take 2N = 2^{k+1} - 2 with N > 3.
The largest power of two not exceeding 2N is 2^k = N + 1, and
N + 1 < (6N + 2)/5 exactly when N > 3. SO NO DISJOINT FAMILY, IN ANY
GIRTH-LEGAL LADDER OF THAT SIZE, REACHES A POWER-OF-TWO WEIGHT - let
alone a connected one. More generally, writing 2^{k+1} for the least
power of two above 2N, the route is blind exactly when
2^k < (6N + 2)/5, that is when

    2N / 2^{k+1}   lies in   ( 5/6 ,  1 ) :

WHENEVER THE LADDER SIZE FALLS IN THE TOP SIXTH OF ITS DYADIC
INTERVAL. At 2N = 30 the route reaches only [19, 30], and the nearest
powers of two are 16 and 32.

  MACHINE: over 240 girth-legal ladders the maximum of sum eps over
  all disjoint families of size at most 4 never exceeded the bound;
  240 of 240.

(N12) IS RECORDED AS A STANDING NO-GO. THE TOP OF THE SPECTRUM IS NOT
ENOUGH. Whatever proves (LQ3) must manufacture cycles of length near
HALF the maximum, not near the maximum - and 497.0 says it must do so
with connectivity in hand. That is the specification the rest of this
section answers.

### 500.3 ZIGZAG FAMILIES ARE CYCLES (PROVED)

DEFINITION. A ZIGZAG FAMILY is a set of chords which, listed by left
endpoint as c_1, ..., c_m with c_t = (a_t, b_t), satisfies

    a_1 < a_2 < b_1 < a_3 < b_2 < a_4 < b_3 < ... < a_m < b_{m-1} < b_m

- that is, consecutive chords CROSS and non-consecutive chords are
DISJOINT. The interleaving pattern is completely rigid.

THEOREM. The completion of a zigzag family is a single cycle, of
length

    W  =  m  +  (b_m - a_1)  -  sum_{t=1}^{m-1} o_t ,
    o_t  =  b_t - a_{t+1}   (the overlap of c_t and c_{t+1}) .

  PROOF. The sorted endpoints are a_1, a_2, b_1, a_3, b_2, ..., a_m,
  b_{m-1}, b_m, so the completion pairs them as (a_1, a_2),
  (b_1, a_3), (b_2, a_4), ..., (b_{m-2}, a_m), (b_{m-1}, b_m): the
  used host segments are exactly the m intervals between consecutive
  chords, and their total length is (b_m - a_1) minus the overlaps.
  For connectivity, follow the two threads
      a_1 - b_1 - a_3 - b_3 - a_5 - ...      (odd chords)
      a_1 - a_2 - b_2 - a_4 - b_4 - ...      (even chords)
  where each dash is alternately a chord and a host segment. They
  start together at a_1 and are joined at the top by the segment
  (b_{m-1}, b_m), so the union is one cycle. QED

  MACHINE: 13174 zigzag families over 360 girth-legal ladders,
  N = 5..11, every subset of every ladder tested; CONNECTED 13174 OF
  13174, zero exceptions, connectivity decided by union-find on the
  explicit edge list.

THIS IS THE POINT OF THE WHOLE SECTION. Connectivity is what refuted
(C1) and what 496.0 measured at 54 per cent. On zigzag families it is
not a hypothesis to be verified but a theorem, and it costs nothing.

EXISTENCE. Every irreducible ladder HAS a long one. Take c_1 to be the
chord at position 1 and, given c_t, let c_{t+1} be the straddling
chord of gap b_t with the LARGEST right endpoint; irreducibility
guarantees one exists until b_t = 2N.
  This greedy chain is a zigzag family. Consecutive chords cross by
  construction. If a_{t+2} <= b_t then c_{t+2} straddles gap b_t and
  has a larger right endpoint than c_{t+1}, contradicting the greedy
  choice at step t+1; so b_t < a_{t+2}. If a_{t+1} < a_t then c_{t+1}
  straddles gap b_{t-1} with a larger right endpoint than c_t,
  contradicting the choice at step t; so the left endpoints increase.
  (Machine: 240 of 240 greedy chains were zigzag families.)

### 500.4 THE FAMILY CANNOT BE ENLARGED THE TWO OBVIOUS WAYS

Both natural weakenings of the zigzag condition are FALSE, and both
were tested before anything was recorded.

  (i) NESTING BREAKS IT. Drop "non-consecutive disjoint" and allow
      nesting: the girth-legal triple (1, 20), (3, 12), (5, 9) has
      pairwise L^1 distances 10, 5, 15 and a connected overlap graph,
      but its completion is the 4-cycle 1 - 3 - 12 - 20 and a separate
      digon on {5, 9}. Two components. This is 496.1(i) again, now
      with a girth-legal witness.
 (ii) STAIRCASES ARE NOT ENOUGH. Drop only the non-consecutive
      disjointness, keeping both endpoint sequences increasing and
      consecutive pairs crossing - call these STAIRCASES, so that
      nesting is impossible. Of 17379 staircases over 300 girth-legal
      ladders, 1278 have DISCONNECTED completions. The smallest
      pattern is four pairwise crossing chords: in the ladder
      (1,5) (2,9) (3,7) (4,10) (6,11) (8,12) the staircase
      (2,9) (4,10) (6,11) (8,12) splits into the two 4-cycles
      2-4-10-9 and 6-8-12-11. Three pairwise crossing chords are
      connected; four are not. A parity obstruction, and the reason
      the zigzag condition asks for DISJOINTNESS at distance two.

  A THIRD MOVE FAILS FOR A STRUCTURAL REASON. Inserting a chord
  BETWEEN c_t and c_{t+1} of a zigzag chain - the "shortcut" move of
  492 - never yields a zigzag family, because c_t and c_{t+1} become
  non-consecutive while still crossing. So the shortcut calculus of
  492 to 498 and the zigzag calculus are DIFFERENT calculi on the same
  ladder; a length change of 1 - sigma for an insertion, which the
  overlap formula would suggest, is wrong, and the machine rejected it
  on the first ladder tested. The correct statement for insertions is
  the toggle formula 500.1(i), where u_c is not zero.

### 500.5 THE ZIGZAG DIFFERENCE FORMULA AND THE TWO MOVES (PROVED)

Fix a zigzag chain c_1, ..., c_m. Every consecutive sub-chain c_i,
..., c_j is again a zigzag family, hence a cycle. Put
O_s = o_1 + ... + o_s, O_0 = 0, and

    R_j  =  j + 1 + b_j - O_{j-1} ,      L_i  =  i + a_i - O_{i-1} .

THEOREM (DIFFERENCE FORMULA).  W(i, j)  =  R_j  -  L_i  for all
i <= j, the case i = j giving the one-chord cycle sigma_i + 1.
  PROOF. W(i,j) = (j-i+1) + (b_j - a_i) - (O_{j-1} - O_{i-1}); regroup
  the terms carrying j and those carrying i. QED

  MACHINE: over 240 greedy chains, all 901 sub-chains were connected
  and all 901 weights matched both W(i,j) and R_j - L_i.

So the lengths available from ONE chain are the DIFFERENCE SET of two
explicit integer sequences, and the prefix walk has steps

    R_{j+1} - R_j  =  1 + e_j - o_j ,     e_j = b_{j+1} - b_j .

MOVE 1 (TRUNCATE / EXTEND). Move i or j; the length changes by the
corresponding step of L or R.

MOVE 2 (SWAP). Replace an interior chord c_t by another chord c'
crossing c_{t-1} and c_{t+1} and disjoint from c_{t-2} and c_{t+2}.
Only o_{t-1} and o_t change, and

    DELTA W   =   sigma_t  -  sigma_{c'}   :

THE LENGTH CHANGES BY EXACTLY THE DIFFERENCE OF THE TWO SPANS.
(Machine 156 of 156.) Spans avoid only 2^M - 1, so consecutive span
values 4, 5, 6 and 8, ..., 14 and 16, ..., 30 are all legal: a slot
with two alternatives of adjacent spans tunes the length by ONE.

### 500.6 (LQ4): (LQ3) WITH THE CONNECTIVITY CLAUSE DELETED

Everything above supports one strengthening.

  (LQ4) Every girth-legal ladder has a ZIGZAG FAMILY of power-of-two
        weight; equivalently, chords c_1, ..., c_m with
        a_1 < a_2 < b_1 < ... < a_m < b_{m-1} < b_m and
            m + (b_m - a_1) - sum (b_t - a_{t+1})   =   2^k .

  (LQ4) IMPLIES (LQ3), by 500.3.

  MACHINE: of 360 girth-legal ladders, N = 5..11, every one has a
  power-of-two cycle, and 360 OF 360 realise one with a ZIGZAG FAMILY.
  Zero misses. (For comparison, staircases missed one of 300.)

(LQ4) is strictly better posed than (LQ3): it has no connectivity
condition, no even-subgraph language and no completion. It is a
statement about an interleaving pattern of m chords and one integer.
Its subject is an arbitrary perfect matching, so it is (N9)-safe.

AN EQUIVALENT WALK FORM. Since
W(1, j+1) - W(1, j) = 1 + a_{j+1} + b_{j+1} - 2 b_j depends only on the
PAIR (c_j, c_{j+1}), a zigzag chain is a walk in a digraph on the N
chords with arc weights g(c, c') = 1 + e - o, and

    W  =  (sigma_1 + 1)  +  sum of the arc weights along the walk .

(LQ4) SAYS THAT SOME WALK IN THAT DIGRAPH HAS PATH-SUM A POWER OF TWO.
The only non-local constraint is that the walk be 2-disjoint, which is
a condition on consecutive triples, so the walks are the paths of a
line-digraph. This is a finite, purely order-theoretic problem with no
graph theory left in it.

### 500.7 THE CHART: WHAT WOULD SETTLE (LQ3)

Reverse-engineered, the target rests on four facts about ARBITRARY
girth-legal ladders. None mentions (f); all are (N9)-safe.

  (F1) CAPTURE. If the set of realisable zigzag lengths contains every
       integer of an interval [x, 2x] then it contains a power of two.
       PROVED, trivially - and this is the only place the arithmetic
       of powers of two is used in the whole chart.

  (F2) CROSSING. Some zigzag chain has a sub-chain of length at most x
       and a sub-chain of length at least 2x. By 500.5 the prefix
       walk starts at sigma_1 + 1 >= 5 and ends at W(1, m), so this
       asks for one chain whose full length is at least twice one of
       its own one-chord cycles - a statement about the greedy chain
       of 500.3 and nothing else. NOT PROVED.

  (F3) STEP BOUND. Consecutive prefixes of that chain differ by at
       most B, i.e. |1 + e_j - o_j| <= B. NOT PROVED, and B is the
       quantity to minimise: with B = 1 the walk sweeps an interval
       and (F1) finishes alone.

  (F4) FINE TUNING. Within B of a power of two, a swap lands exactly
       on it: some interior slot of the chain has two admissible
       chords whose spans differ by the required amount at most B.
       By 500.5 the length then moves by exactly that difference.
       NOT PROVED.

  (F1) and the two calculus theorems 500.3 and 500.5 are proved.
  (F2), (F3), (F4) are the whole remaining content, and they are
  statements about ONE explicitly constructed chain.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT DECOMPOSITION, AND NOT ANOTHER. (N12) forbids
the top of the spectrum, so the proof must live in the middle; 497.0
forbids paying for connectivity afterwards, so it must be free in
advance; 500.4 shows the zigzag family is the largest natural family
for which it is free. The three open facts are exactly what remains
once those two no-goes are respected.

AND (C2) IS REBORN (N9)-SAFE. 499.1 withdrew (C2) - "a J7 rung cannot
have all its disjoint-span values congruent modulo g >= 3" - because
its subject was the counterexample class. (F4) is its legitimate
descendant: "SOME ZIGZAG SLOT OF SOME GIRTH-LEGAL LADDER HAS TWO
ADMISSIBLE CHORDS OF NEARLY EQUAL SPAN". Same arithmetic content -
values that refuse to differ by a small amount - with the subject
changed from the counterexample class to an arbitrary ladder. That is
what the test of 499.4 was for, and it is passed here.

### 500.8 STATUS

PROVED here: that (LQ3) IS THE ERDOS-GYARFAS CONJECTURE FOR A
HAMILTONIAN PATH PLUS A PERFECT MATCHING OF GIRTH AT LEAST 5, the two
numeric hypotheses being exactly girth 5, and that the ladder may be
assumed irreducible; THE STRADDLE-PARITY FORMULA w(T) = |T| + #{j :
k_T(j) odd}, with the toggle formula, the parity invariant "a
power-of-two cycle uses an even number of even-span chords", and the
deletion constant eps(c) = 1 + [a odd] - [b odd]; THE ZIGZAG THEOREM,
that a zigzag family's completion is a single cycle of length
m + (b_m - a_1) - sum o_t, together with the greedy construction of a
zigzag chain spanning any irreducible ladder; THE DIFFERENCE FORMULA
W(i,j) = R_j - L_i; and THE SWAP LEMMA, that exchanging an interior
chord changes the cycle length by exactly the difference of the two
spans.

PROVED here as a NO-GO: (N12) THE REACH LIMIT. Every disjoint family
of a girth-legal ladder has sum eps <= (2/5)(2N-1), so the route of
495 reaches only the weights in [(6N+2)/5, 2N], a window of ratio 5/3;
at 2N = 2^{k+1} - 2 with N > 3 that window contains no power of two at
all. The route of 495 was therefore doomed twice over - by 497.0's
connectivity failure and, independently, by arithmetic reach. ANY
PROOF OF (LQ3) MUST PRODUCE CYCLES NEAR HALF THE MAXIMUM LENGTH.

COMPUTED: 118740 of 118740 straddle-parity checks; 13174 of 13174
zigzag families connected; 901 of 901 sub-chain difference formulas;
156 of 156 swaps; 240 of 240 reach-limit and straddle-parity-of-j
checks; and, decisively, 360 OF 360 girth-legal ladders realise a
power-of-two cycle with a ZIGZAG FAMILY.

REFUTED before recording: the staircase hypothesis (1278 of 17379
staircases disconnect, four pairwise crossing chords being the
smallest pattern); the overlap-graph criterion for connectivity, with
the girth-legal witness (1,20), (3,12), (5,9); and the insertion rule
DELTA W = 1 - sigma, which fails because inserting into a zigzag chain
destroys the zigzag property.

IDENTIFIED: (LQ4), the strengthening of (LQ3) with the connectivity
clause deleted, verified on every ladder tested; and its walk form,
which turns the programme's target into a path-sum problem in a
digraph on N chords with arc weights 1 + e - o.

NOT PROVED: (LQ4); (F2), (F3), (F4); (LQ3); the Ladder Question; (R);
Theorem B(SWAP); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked what a
settled (LQ3) would rest on, this section works backwards and finds
that the two things (LQ3) most needed are now in hand. It needed
mid-spectrum cycles, because (N12) proves the top of the spectrum
cannot reach a power of two at a positive density of scales; and it
needed them CONNECTED WITHOUT PAYING FOR IT, because that is what
refuted (C1). The zigzag families supply both: their completions are
single cycles by a two-thread argument, every irreducible ladder
carries one spanning it, their lengths form the difference set of two
explicit sequences, and swapping one chord moves the length by exactly
the difference of two spans. What is left is (LQ4) - the same target
with the connectivity clause DELETED - and three quantitative facts
about a single explicitly constructed chain.


## 501. (LQ4) IS FALSE. THE HARD CASE, THE THREE-CHORD CRITERION, AND
## (TRI)

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 500.6 proposed (LQ4) -
(LQ3) with the connectivity clause deleted - on the strength of 360 of
360 random ladders. IT IS FALSE, and the way it is false is the most
useful thing in this section: the 360 ladders were GENERIC, and a
generic girth-legal ladder already has a one- or two-chord power-of-two
cycle, which is a zigzag of length one or two. The test never entered
the case that matters. 501.0 defines THE HARD CASE and refutes (LQ4)
there. 501.1 checks, exhaustively, that (LQ3) itself survives - which
was not automatic, because the ladder has two vertices of degree 2 and
Erdos-Gyarfas does not apply to it. 501.2 proves the THREE-CHORD
CRITERION, 501.3 states (TRI) - three chords always suffice - 501.4
gives the four closed weight formulas and the MIXED-CROSSER THEOREM,
501.5 isolates the two-parameter family that has never failed, and
501.7 reports what the literature does and does not offer.

### 501.0 (LQ4) IS FALSE (REFUTED, 374.1)

DEFINITION. A girth-legal ladder is in the HARD CASE if it has no
one-chord and no two-chord power-of-two cycle, i.e. no span equals
2^M - 1 and no non-disjoint pair has L^1 distance 2^M - 2. This is
exactly the class 497.1 searched, and it is the only class in which
(LQ3) has any content: outside it a power-of-two cycle is exhibited by
a single chord or a single pair.

EXHAUSTIVELY, by backtracking over all perfect matchings of [1, 2N]:

    2N          10   12    14    16     18     20      22
    hard-case    0    0    14   120   1117   6796   52546
    no zigzag
    power of 2   -    -     2    32    202    970    4869

SO (LQ4) IS FALSE FROM 2N = 14, and the failure rate does not decay:
it is 14 per cent at 2N = 14 and 9 per cent at 2N = 22. The smallest
witness is

    (1,7) (2,11) (3,9) (4,13) (5,10) (6,14) (8,12) ,

spans 6, 9, 6, 9, 5, 8, 4. No zigzag family has power-of-two weight.

CORRECTED (374.1), loudly, and the correction is METHODOLOGICAL. The
"360 of 360" of 500.6 was measured on ladders drawn at random from the
girth-legal class. In that class almost every ladder has a span equal
to 2^M - 1 or a crossing pair at L^1 distance 2^M - 2, and those ARE
zigzag families of size one and two. The measurement therefore
confirmed nothing about the zigzag family; it confirmed that generic
ladders are easy. NEW STANDING RULE, to sit beside the (N9) test of
499.4: EVERY CONJECTURE ABOUT LADDERS MUST BE TESTED IN THE HARD CASE.
Generic sampling in this problem measures the one- and two-chord
layers and nothing else.

### 501.1 (LQ3) SURVIVES (COMPUTED, EXHAUSTIVE)

This had to be checked, and it was not a formality. The ladder graph
has TWO VERTICES OF DEGREE 2 - positions 1 and 2N - so it does not
satisfy the hypothesis of Erdos-Gyarfas, and nothing outside this
archive forbids a girth-legal ladder with no power-of-two cycle at
all. (In a J7 rung those two vertices are joined to the feet on C; the
ladder abstraction of 500.0 drops that, and 500.0's reading of (LQ3)
as "Erdos-Gyarfas for a Hamiltonian path plus a perfect matching"
must be qualified accordingly - the two ends have degree 2.)

MEASURED: for every hard-case ladder at 2N = 14, 16, 18 and 20 - 8047
ladders, exhaustive, all chord subsets, connectivity by union-find on
the explicit edge list - THE FULL CONNECTED SPECTRUM CONTAINS A POWER
OF TWO. Zero exceptions. (LQ3) stands.

### 501.2 THE THREE-CHORD CRITERION (PROVED)

THEOREM. Let T be three chords with endpoints q_1 < ... < q_6. The
completion of T is a single cycle IF AND ONLY IF none of the three
pairs {q_1,q_2}, {q_3,q_4}, {q_5,q_6} is itself a chord. Its length is
then

    w  =  3  +  (q_2 - q_1)  +  (q_4 - q_3)  +  (q_6 - q_5) .

  PROOF. By the contraction criterion 496.1 the components are the
  cycles of the multigraph on the three blocks {q_1,q_2}, {q_3,q_4},
  {q_5,q_6} whose edges are the chords. Each block has degree 2, so
  the multigraph is 2-regular on three nodes with three edges: either
  a triangle, or a digon plus a loop. A loop is exactly a chord lying
  inside a block. Excluding loops leaves the triangle, which is
  connected. The length is the straddle-parity formula 500.1. QED

  MACHINE: 7210 of 7210 triples over the exhaustive hard-case ladders
  at 2N = 14 and 16, criterion and weight both.

Note what this says: {q_1,q_2} can only be a chord of span q_2 - q_1,
so ANY BLOCK OF TWO ADJACENT POSITIONS IS AUTOMATICALLY LEGAL, since
girth forbids spans below 4. That observation is the whole of 501.5.

### 501.3 (TRI): THREE CHORDS ALWAYS SUFFICE

In every one of the 236 hard-case ladders at 2N = 14, 16, 18 that
defeat the zigzag family, the SMALLEST winning chord set has exactly
three chords - never four. That is the shape of the target:

  (TRI) Every girth-legal ladder has three chords whose six sorted
        endpoints q_1 < ... < q_6 satisfy: none of {q_1,q_2},
        {q_3,q_4}, {q_5,q_6} is a chord, and
            3 + (q_2-q_1) + (q_4-q_3) + (q_6-q_5)  =  2^k .

  (TRI) IMPLIES (LQ3), by 501.2. Its subject is an arbitrary perfect
  matching, so it is (N9)-safe.

  MACHINE: EXHAUSTIVE over all 60593 hard-case ladders at
  2N = 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, and 3000 sampled hard-case ladders at each
  of 2N = 24, 26, 28, 30, 32, 34. ZERO FAILURES.

(TRI) is smaller than (LQ3) in every direction: no even subgraphs, no
completions, no connectivity to verify, no unbounded chord set. Six
positions and one equation.

### 501.4 THE FOUR WEIGHT FORMULAS, AND THE MIXED-CROSSER THEOREM

Write sigma = b - a and phi = a + b for a chord. Sorting the three
chords A, B, C by left endpoint, each interleaving pattern collapses
the alternating sum to a formula in sigma and phi (all PROVED by
substitution into 501.2, all machine-checked):

  A, B, C pairwise crossing:      w = 3 + sigma_A - sigma_B + sigma_C
  A nests B and C, B crosses C:   w = 3 + sigma_A + phi_B - phi_C
                                    = 3 + sigma_A - L^1(B, C)
  A crosses B and C, B nests C:   w = 3 + sigma_A + phi_B - phi_C
  A nests B, A and B cross C:     w = 3 + phi_B + sigma_C - phi_A

The first says a pairwise crossing triple has length 3 plus the
ALTERNATING SUM OF ITS SPANS - so a ladder whose chords all have the
same span has every such triple at the same length, which is exactly
how the near-parallel ladders dodge.

MIXED-CROSSER THEOREM (PROVED). Let A = (a, b) be ANY chord, X a chord
crossing A on the left (y < a < p < b) and X' a chord crossing A on
the right (a < p' < b < y'). Then {A, X, X'} is ALWAYS a single cycle,
of length

    w  =  3  +  (a - y)  +  |p - p'|  +  (y' - b) .

  PROOF. The six endpoints sort as y, a, min(p,p'), max(p,p'), b, y',
  so the blocks are {y,a}, {p,p'}, {b,y'}. None is a chord: y is
  matched to p, a to b, and p' to y'. Apply 501.2. QED
  MACHINE: 4010 of 4010, connectivity and weight.

This is a second connectivity-free family, and unlike the zigzags it
needs no ordering discipline at all - one chord and one crosser on
each side, in any position.

THE MINIMUM-SPAN CHORD (PROVED). Let A have the minimum span
sigma_min. No chord is nested inside A, since a nested chord has span
at most sigma_min - 2. Hence EVERY ONE of the sigma_min - 1 interior
positions of A belongs to a chord crossing A. Two corollaries: no
girth-legal ladder is laminar, and the minimum-span chord has at least
three crossers. If they occur on both sides, the mixed-crosser theorem
applies with p and p' ranging over ALL of a+1, ..., b-1, so the
lengths 3 + lambda + rho + |p - p'| are available for every left
offset lambda = a - y and right offset rho = y' - b.

### 501.5 THE ADJACENT-BLOCK FAMILY: TWO PARAMETERS

By the remark closing 501.2, a block of two ADJACENT positions is
always legal. Fix p and let c = M(p), c' = M(p+1); these are distinct,
because a chord of span 1 is illegal. So TWO OF THE THREE CHORDS ARE
FORCED, and the family has only two parameters: the position p and a
third chord D.

Let u = mu(p), v = mu(p+1) and let d_1 < d_2 be the endpoints of D.
If {p, p+1} is a block - equivalently an even number of u, v, d_1, d_2
lie below p - then the other four sort as r_1 < r_2 < r_3 < r_4 and

    w  =  4  +  (r_2 - r_1)  +  (r_4 - r_3) .

Four sub-cases, writing I for the interval between u and v:

    D straddles I :   w = 4 + sigma_D - |u - v|
    D inside I :      w = 4 + |u - v| - sigma_D
    D interleaves :   w = 4 + (d_1 - min I) + (d_2 - max I)  or
                      w = 4 + (min I - d_1) + (max I - d_2) .

So along this family the third chord's SPAN is the tuning knob, and
|u - v| = |mu(p) - mu(p+1)| is the offset - a quantity girth already
controls, since the chords at p and p+1 overlap and therefore
1 + |u - v| >= 3.

  (ADJ) Every girth-legal ladder has such a triple of power-of-two
        weight.
  (ADJ) IMPLIES (TRI) IMPLIES (LQ3).

  MACHINE: 3200 hard-case ladders at 2N = 18, 22, 26, 30, 36, 42 and
  50. ZERO FAILURES. By contrast the mixed-crosser family alone fails
  on 14 of 200 ladders at 2N = 18, falling to 0 by 2N = 36, so it is
  not sufficient on its own at small size.

### 501.6 THE SPECTRUM GAP, AND WHAT A COUNTEREXAMPLE MUST DO

MEASURED, over 3000 hard-case ladders at 2N = 18 to 50: the set of
three-chord cycle lengths runs from 6 or 7 up to within a few units of
2N, and its LARGEST INTERNAL GAP is 2, 3 or 4 - never more. So the
three-chord spectrum is an interval of ratio far above 2, punctured
only by gaps of size at most 4.

That converts (TRI) into a placement statement. Write the target
(GAP3): the three-chord spectrum of a girth-legal ladder has no
internal gap exceeding 3. Then a counterexample to (TRI) must have, for
EVERY power of two in [8, 2N], an internal gap of the spectrum
containing it - at least log_2(2N) - 2 separate gaps, each of size at
most 3, each positioned exactly on a power of two, and no gap wasted
anywhere else. That is the precise shape of what has to be excluded,
and it is the first time this archive has been able to say what a
counterexample must look like rather than what it must not.

### 501.7 THE LITERATURE: WHAT IT OFFERS, AND WHY IT STOPS

The (F2), (F3), (F4) of 500.7 are MOOT - they were statements about
zigzag chains, and 501.0 refutes the family. The right question is
what the literature offers for (TRI), (ADJ) and (GAP3). Verified
sources, per 388.1:

  B. Sudakov and J. Verstraete, "Cycle lengths in sparse graphs",
  Combinatorica 28 (2008) 357-372. Motivated by Erdos-Gyarfas, they
  bound the average degree of an n-vertex graph having NO cycle of
  length in a prescribed infinite sequence; for many sequences,
  INCLUDING THE POWERS OF TWO, the bound is e^{O(log* n)}. This is the
  state of the art on the conjecture itself, and it says precisely why
  degree 3 is out of reach: the threshold grows, however slowly, and 3
  is below it.

  J. A. Bondy and A. Vince, "Cycles in a graph whose lengths differ by
  one or two", J. Graph Theory 27 (1998) 11-15. Every graph of minimum
  degree at least three has two cycles whose lengths differ by one or
  two. Already used in 474. It is the ONLY unconditional
  consecutive-length statement available at degree 3 - and it supplies
  one pair, where (GAP3) needs the whole spectrum.

  C.-H. Liu and J. Ma, "Cycle lengths and minimum degree of graphs",
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B. For minimum degree at least k+1 a graph
  has floor(k/2) cycles of consecutive even lengths, and if it is
  2-connected and non-bipartite, floor(k/2) of consecutive odd
  lengths; this confirms Thomassen's two 1983 conjectures for even k.
  AT k = 2, WHICH IS THE CUBIC CASE, floor(k/2) = 1 AND THE THEOREM IS
  VACUOUS. S. Chiba, "Minimum degree conditions for the existence of a
  sequence of cycles whose lengths differ by one or two", J. Graph
  Theory (2023), is degree-scaled in the same way.

  J. Tranquilli, "A 60-Vertex Lower Bound for Cubic Bipartite
  Counterexamples to the Erdos-Gyarfas Conjecture", arXiv:2608.02675,
  2 August 2026: every simple cubic bipartite graph on at most 58
  vertices has a cycle of length 4, 8 or 16, so a cubic bipartite
  counterexample needs at least 60 vertices, doubling the previous
  bound of 30. Computer-assisted, via the Levi graph of a linear
  symmetric configuration.

  Heckman and Krakovski proved Erdos-Gyarfas for 3-connected cubic
  PLANAR graphs; the conjecture is also known for P_8-free and
  P_10-free graphs and for graphs of diameter 2.

  The Cohn-Lempel equality - the number of orbits of a cyclic
  permutation composed with transpositions is one plus the GF(2)
  nullity of the interlacement matrix - and Traldi's extension to
  arbitrary circuit partitions of 4-regular graphs are the general
  theory behind 501.2. They do not contradict 496.1(i): the
  Cohn-Lempel circuit partition keeps ALL arcs of the circle, whereas
  a ladder completion keeps ALTERNATE arcs, which is a different
  transition system.

VERDICT. NOTHING IN THE LITERATURE CLOSES (TRI), AND THE REASON IS
STRUCTURAL, NOT ACCIDENTAL: every general theorem producing many
cycle lengths scales with the minimum degree, and at degree 3 they all
degenerate - Liu-Ma to a single cycle, Bondy-Vince to a single pair,
Sudakov-Verstraete to a threshold that 3 sits under. This is (N7), the
degree-3 barrier, confirmed from outside the archive. What the
literature does supply is the correct expectation: Tranquilli's bound
and the Royle-Markstrom searches say a counterexample must be large,
which is consistent with the scale premises of 433.

### 501.8 STATUS

REFUTED (374.1), loudly: (LQ4) of 500.6. Hard-case girth-legal ladders
with no zigzag family of power-of-two weight exist from 2N = 14, at a
rate of 2 in 14 there and 4869 in 52546 at 2N = 22. The witness
(1,7) (2,11) (3,9) (4,13) (5,10) (6,14) (8,12) has seven three-chord
power-of-two cycles and no zigzag one; the first of them is
{(1,7), (2,11), (6,14)}, pairwise crossing, of length
3 + 6 - 9 + 8 = 8.

CORRECTED (374.1), methodologically: 500.6's evidence was drawn from
GENERIC girth-legal ladders, where a one- or two-chord power-of-two
cycle almost always exists and is itself a zigzag. NEW STANDING RULE:
TEST IN THE HARD CASE. Sampling the generic class in this problem
measures only the first two layers.

PROVED here: THE THREE-CHORD CRITERION - a triple is a cycle iff no
block of two consecutive endpoints is a chord, with length
3 + (q_2-q_1) + (q_4-q_3) + (q_6-q_5) - and its corollary that a block
of two ADJACENT POSITIONS is always legal; the FOUR PATTERN FORMULAS,
in particular that a pairwise crossing triple has length 3 plus the
alternating sum of its spans; THE MIXED-CROSSER THEOREM, that one
chord together with one crosser on each side is always a cycle, of
length 3 + (a-y) + |p-p'| + (y'-b); and THE MINIMUM-SPAN CHORD LEMMA,
that a chord of minimum span has all of its interior positions on
crossers, so no girth-legal ladder is laminar.

COMPUTED: hard-case ladders exhaustively to 2N = 22 (60593 of them);
(LQ3) verified exhaustively for all 8047 hard-case ladders to 2N = 20;
(TRI) verified exhaustively to 2N = 22 and on 18000 sampled ladders to
2N = 34, zero failures; (ADJ) verified on 3200 hard-case ladders to
2N = 50, zero failures; the three-chord spectrum's largest internal
gap measured 2 to 4 throughout.

IDENTIFIED: (TRI), and inside it the two-parameter family (ADJ) -
position p and one further chord - which has never failed; and (GAP3),
which turns (TRI) into the statement that a counterexample must place
a spectrum gap of size at most three exactly on every power of two in
[8, 2N] simultaneously.

NOT PROVED: (TRI); (ADJ); (GAP3); (LQ3); the Ladder Question; (R);
Theorem B(SWAP); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.
(LQ4) is REFUTED and cannot be proved.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked to settle
(LQ4), the answer is that it is false, and the section's value is in
what the refutation forced: the HARD CASE, where alone the question
has content, and in which the archive had never systematically
searched. There the picture is sharp. Three chords always suffice;
connectivity for three chords is decided by a one-line criterion; the
weight is an alternating sum of six positions with four closed forms;
one chord with a crosser on each side is always a cycle; and the
family with a block of two adjacent positions - two parameters in all
- has never failed on any of the 3200 hard ladders tested up to
2N = 50. The literature confirms that no external theorem will close
it, because every one of them degenerates at degree three. The
programme's target is now (TRI), and (ADJ) is the smallest sufficient
statement it has ever had.


## 502. (ADJ) TARGETED: THE VIRTUAL CHORD, AND THE MIRROR PATH

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED, (ADJ) NOT PROVED. 501.5
gave (ADJ) as four sub-cases with a case analysis attached. This
section collapses all four into ONE identity (502.0), which turns
(ADJ) into a statement with no graph theory, no completions and no
case distinctions left in it: a single L^1 distance between two point
sets in the taxicab plane (502.1). 502.2 says where the two sets live,
502.3 exhibits the mechanism that the extremal examples actually use,
and 502.4 reports an adversarial search that could not destroy (ADJ)
and could not drive its witness count below five.

### 502.0 THE VIRTUAL-CHORD THEOREM (PROVED)

DEFINITION. For 1 <= p <= 2N-1 the VIRTUAL CHORD at p is

    Q_p  =  ( min(mu(p), mu(p+1)),  max(mu(p), mu(p+1)) ) ,

the pair of partners of the two adjacent positions p and p+1. It is
never a real chord, and by girth its span is at least 2.

THEOREM. Let D be a chord other than M(p) and M(p+1). The triple
{M(p), M(p+1), D} is a cycle WITH {p, p+1} AS A BLOCK if and only if

  (a) D overlaps Q_p as an interval, and
  (b) D and Q_p contain the same number of endpoints below p, modulo
      two,

and in that case its length is

      w   =   4  +  L^1( Q_p , D ) .

  PROOF. The six endpoints are p, p+1 and the four endpoints of Q_p
  and D. {p,p+1} is a block exactly when an even number of the other
  four lie below p, which is (b). Given (b), the remaining four sort
  as r_1 < r_2 < r_3 < r_4 and the other two blocks are {r_1,r_2} and
  {r_3,r_4}, so by 501.2 the length is
  4 + (r_2-r_1) + (r_4-r_3) and the triple is a cycle unless one of
  those two blocks is a chord. Neither can be a sub-pair of Q_p and D
  mixed - the partners of mu(p), mu(p+1) are p, p+1 - so the only
  failure is {r_1,r_2} = D or {r_3,r_4} = D, which happens exactly
  when D lies wholly below or wholly above Q_p, i.e. when (a) fails.
  Finally, for two overlapping pairs A_1<A_2 and B_1<B_2,
      (r_2-r_1) + (r_4-r_3)  =  |A_1-B_1| + |A_2-B_2| ,
  by the crossing/nested split of 494.0: crossing A_1<B_1<A_2<B_2
  gives (B_1-A_1)+(B_2-A_2), nested A_1<B_1<B_2<A_2 gives
  (B_1-A_1)+(A_2-B_2), and the mirror cases likewise. QED

  MACHINE: 8240 admissible pairs over hard-case ladders at
  2N = 16, 18, 20. Weight and connectivity correct in 8240 of 8240,
  and - the completeness half - ZERO pairs accepted by the raw
  three-chord criterion of 501.2 were rejected by (a) and (b). The
  rule is both sound and complete.

This supersedes the four sub-cases of 501.5. There is one formula.

### 502.1 (ADJ) IS A TAXICAB STATEMENT ABOUT THE MIRROR PATH

Q_p is the image of the host-path edge {p, p+1} under the matching.
So the 2N-1 virtual chords are the edges of

    THE MIRROR PATH     mu(1) - mu(2) - mu(3) - ... - mu(2N) ,

a Hamiltonian path on the positions, and (ADJ) reads:

  (ADJ) Some edge of the mirror path lies at L^1 distance exactly
        2^k - 4 from some admissible real chord.

The target distances are 2^k - 4, that is

        4,  12,  28,  60,  124,  252,  ...

and by 494.0 the distance is |phi(Q_p) - phi(D)| when Q_p and D cross
and |sigma(Q_p) - sigma(D)| when one nests the other. Nothing else is
left: two finite point sets in the plane, one forbidden geometry, one
lacunary list of distances.

### 502.2 WHERE THE TWO SETS LIVE (PROVED)

Call position q LEFT if mu(q) > q and RIGHT otherwise. Then t_1 = L
and t_{2N} = R, so THE TYPE SEQUENCE MUST CHANGE, and the number of
LR changes exceeds the number of RL changes by exactly one. The
admissibility rule (b) reads off the types:

    p, p+1 both LEFT :   D lies entirely above p+1 ;
    p, p+1 both RIGHT:   D lies entirely below p ;
    types differ     :   D straddles the gap (p, p+1) .

Three consequences, all proved:

  (i) p = 1 is always an LL adjacency and p = 2N-1 always an RR one,
      because a span of 1 is illegal. AT THOSE TWO POSITIONS RULE (b)
      IS VACUOUS - no position lies below 1 - so every chord
      overlapping Q_1 other than M(1), M(2) is admissible.
 (ii) At an LR change, M(p) and M(p+1) CROSS and
      L^1(M(p), M(p+1)) = sigma(Q_p) - 1. So girth forces
      sigma(Q_p) >= 4, and in the hard case sigma(Q_p) is not
      2^M - 1: THE VIRTUAL CHORD AT AN LR CHANGE HAS A GIRTH-LEGAL
      SPAN, exactly as if it were real.
(iii) At an LL or RR adjacency, L^1(M(p), M(p+1)) = sigma(Q_p) + 1,
      so sigma(Q_p) >= 2 and, in the hard case, sigma(Q_p) avoids
      2^M - 3, i.e. avoids 1, 5, 13, 29, 61, ... .

### 502.3 THE MECHANISM THE EXTREMAL EXAMPLES USE (PROVED)

THE MIDPOINT LEMMA. Suppose sigma(Q_p) = 2, so Q_p = (m-1, m+1) for
the single interior position m. The chord M(m) has its partner z
outside [m-1, m+1], since |z - m| >= 4; hence M(m) CROSSES Q_p, never
nests in it, and

    phi(Q_p) = 2m ,   phi(M(m)) = m + z ,
    L^1(Q_p, M(m)) = |z - m| = sigma(M(m)) ,

so, whenever M(m) is admissible,

      w   =   4  +  sigma( M(m) ) .

THE SPAN OF ONE CHORD IS THE WHOLE ANSWER: (ADJ) holds at such a p as
soon as some span equals 2^k - 4, that is 4, 12, 28, 60, ... - and
those values are all LEGAL spans, since the hard case forbids only
2^M - 1.

Of the 31 witnesses surviving in the five extremal ladders of 502.4,
EVERY ONE sits at L^1 distance 4 or 12, and two are the Midpoint
Lemma firing verbatim: at 2N = 32, p = 13 has Q = (24,26), midpoint
25, M(25) = (25,29) of span 4, weight 8; at 2N = 26, p = 24 has
Q = (14,16), midpoint 15, M(15) = (11,15) of span 4, weight 8. The
optimiser could not remove those without creating others.

### 502.4 (ADJ) SURVIVES ADVERSARIAL SEARCH

TWO MEASUREMENTS, both on hard-case ladders.

  SURPLUS, on ladders drawn at random. The number of witnessing pairs
  (p, D) grows linearly:

     2N        18   22   26   30   36   42   50   60
     minimum    4    8   12   10   18   21   28   46
     median    13   16   20   21   32   35   40   56

  over 150 ladders at each size. (ADJ) failed on none of them, and the
  largest internal gap of the (ADJ) weight set was 2 to 5 throughout.

  ADVERSARIAL FLOOR. A hill-climb whose only objective is to MINIMISE
  the witness count - moves re-pair the four endpoints of two chords
  in the two other ways, keeping the ladder hard-case - could not
  reach zero at any size, and could not get below

     2N        20   26   32   40   50
     floor      5    5    7    8    6 .

  The floor does not decay with 2N. Every extremal ladder found is
  recorded in 502.3's examples; the one at 2N = 40 is the interesting
  one, because it has NO witness at distance 4 at all - all eight of
  its witnesses sit at distance 12, weight 16.

So (ADJ) is not merely true on samples; it resists an optimiser
pointed straight at it. That is the strongest evidence this archive
has produced for any of its targets, and it is still not a proof.

### 502.5 WHAT (ADJ) NOW NEEDS, EXACTLY

One statement, in the plane, with no graph theory in it:

  (TX) Let M be a perfect matching of [1, 2N] whose chords, viewed as
       points (a, b), have all spans at least 4 and all overlapping
       pairs at L^1 distance at least 3. Let Q_1, ..., Q_{2N-1} be the
       edges of the mirror path, Q_p = {mu(p), mu(p+1)}. Then some
       admissible pair (Q_p, D) has L^1(Q_p, D) in {4, 12, 28, 60,...}.

What is proved towards it: the reduction itself (502.0); that the two
endpoints p = 1 and p = 2N-1 are unconditioned (502.2(i)); that the
virtual chords at LR changes are girth-legal (502.2(ii)) and those at
LL and RR adjacencies avoid the spans 5, 13, 29, ... (502.2(iii));
and the Midpoint Lemma (502.3), which settles (TX) at any p where the
mirror-path edge has span 2 and the midpoint chord has span 2^k - 4.

What is missing is a reason why the mirror path cannot dodge a
lacunary set of distances from the chord set. The archive has met this
shape before - 490.2's congruence reframe, 497.3's bounded Bezout -
and (TX) is the smallest instance of it yet: one point set of size
2N-1, one of size N, and six target distances below 256.

### 502.6 STATUS

PROVED here: THE VIRTUAL-CHORD THEOREM. With Q_p the pair of partners
of p and p+1, the triple {M(p), M(p+1), D} is a cycle with {p,p+1} as
a block if and only if D overlaps Q_p and matches its parity of
endpoints below p, and then its length is exactly 4 + L^1(Q_p, D).
Sound and complete, 8240 of 8240 with zero pairs missed. Also: the
type-change lemma, that the type sequence runs from L to R so LR
changes exceed RL changes by one, with the three admissibility rules
it dictates; that p = 1 and p = 2N-1 carry no parity condition at all;
that the virtual chord at an LR change has a girth-legal span, and at
an LL or RR adjacency has span avoiding 2^M - 3; and THE MIDPOINT
LEMMA, that a virtual chord of span 2 gives w = 4 + sigma(M(m)) for
the chord at its midpoint, so that (ADJ) holds there as soon as some
span is 4, 12, 28 or 60.

COMPUTED: the (ADJ) witness count grows linearly in 2N, median 13 at
2N = 18 rising to 56 at 2N = 60, minimum over 150 random hard-case
ladders never below 4; and an adversarial hill-climb minimising the
witness count could not reach zero at 2N = 20, 26, 32, 40 or 50, its
floor being 5, 5, 7, 8, 6. Every surviving witness in the five
extremal ladders sits at L^1 distance 4 or 12.

IDENTIFIED: (TX), the taxicab form of (ADJ) - the mirror path, whose
edges are the matching's images of the host-path edges, must come
within exactly 2^k - 4 of some admissible chord. It contains no graphs,
no cycles and no completions.

NOT PROVED: (TX); (ADJ); (TRI); (GAP3); (LQ3); the Ladder Question;
(R); Theorem B(SWAP); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED, (ADJ) NOT
PROVED. Targeting (ADJ) removed its case analysis entirely: one
identity, w = 4 + L^1(Q_p, D), replaces the four configurations of
501.5, and with it the target becomes a distance problem between the
mirror path and the chord set. The section adds the Midpoint Lemma,
which converts the smallest virtual chords into a bare condition on a
single span, and it adds the first adversarial evidence in this
archive: an optimiser told to destroy (ADJ) cannot, and cannot push it
below five witnesses at any size tested. What is still absent is the
one thing this programme has never found - a reason why a lacunary set
of distances cannot be dodged.


## 503. (ADJ) IS FALSE. THE COUNTEREXAMPLE THAT 501.6 PREDICTED, AND
## PANCYCLICITY

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. (ADJ) IS SETTLED: IT IS
FALSE. 502.4 reported that an adversarial hill-climb could not drive
the (ADJ) witness count below five and called that the strongest
evidence in the archive. It was worthless. 501.6 had already said
exactly what a counterexample must look like - an internal gap of the
weight set sitting on every power of two at once - and the right move
was to SEARCH FOR THAT, not to sample around it. Doing so finds a
counterexample at 2N = 22 and proves there is none below (503.0). What
survives is recorded in 503.1, and 503.2 reports the observation that
the failure exposed: the FULL cycle spectrum of a hard-case ladder
appears to be GAPLESS, which would give (LQ3) in one line.

### 503.0 (ADJ) IS FALSE (REFUTED, 374.1)

THE SEARCH. Build the matching left to right, pruning on two things:
the hard case of 501.0, and (ADJ)-FAILURE - no fully determined
admissible pair (Q_p, D) may have 4 + L^1(Q_p, D) a power of two. The
second prune is sound because a pair is determined as soon as mu(p),
mu(p+1) and D are placed, and it then survives into every completion.
So the search enumerates exactly the hard-case ladders that violate
(ADJ).

  RESULT. Exhausted with no survivor at 2N = 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20
  (search trees of 21, 79, 354, 1632, 5673 and 20366 nodes). AT
  2N = 22 IT SUCCEEDS:

    (1,9) (2,12) (3,15) (4,22) (5,14) (6,17) (7,20) (8,18) (10,16)
    (11,19) (13,21) .

  INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, with no use of the virtual-chord rule: it is
  a perfect matching of [1,22]; its spans are 6, 8, 8, 8, 9, 10, 10,
  11, 12, 13, 18, all legal, and it has ZERO hard-case violations; it
  has 93 CONNECTED ADJACENT-BLOCK TRIPLES, found by sorting the six
  endpoints and testing 501.2 directly, with completions rebuilt from
  the parity of endpoints below each gap and connectivity decided by
  union-find; and their weight set is exactly

      { 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19 }
        =  [6, 19]  minus  {8, 16} .

THAT IS 501.6's PREDICTION, REALISED VERBATIM. The adjacent-block
spectrum is an interval of length fourteen with exactly two holes, and
the two holes are exactly the two powers of two in range. Nothing is
wasted, and nothing else is missing.

CORRECTED (374.1), and this correction is worth more than the
counterexample. 502.4 measured a linearly growing witness count and an
adversarial floor of five to eight, and read that as evidence. It was
not evidence: the hill-climb's moves - re-pairing the four endpoints
of two chords - cannot reach this configuration, and no amount of
sampling in a neighbourhood tests a statement whose counterexamples
are isolated. NEW STANDING RULE, beside the (N9) subject test of 499.4
and the hard-case rule of 501.0: WHEN YOU CAN SAY WHAT A COUNTEREXAMPLE
MUST LOOK LIKE, BUILD THAT INTO THE SEARCH. A structural prediction is
a search specification, not a rhetorical flourish. 501.6 wrote the
specification and 502 ignored it for a section.

### 503.1 WHAT SURVIVES THE COUNTEREXAMPLE

The chain of 501 was (ADJ) implies (TRI) implies (LQ3). Only the first
link breaks. On the witness of 503.0:

  (TRI) HOLDS. There are exactly four connected triples of
  power-of-two weight, all of weight 16, and NONE of them has an
  adjacent block:

    {(1,9), (6,17), (13,21)}   blocks (1,6) (9,13) (17,21)
    {(2,12), (4,22), (6,17)}   blocks (2,4) (6,12) (17,22)
    {(3,15), (7,20), (8,18)}   blocks (3,7) (8,15) (18,20)
    {(3,15), (7,20), (10,16)}  blocks (3,7) (10,15) (16,20)

  (LQ3) HOLDS. The full connected spectrum is 5, 6, ..., 22 - every
  integer from the girth to 2N - and it contains 8 and 16.

So the two-parameter family of 501.5 was too small, exactly as the
zigzag family of 500.6 was too small, and for the same reason: each
was a proper sub-family chosen for the convenience of its
connectivity, and the hard case punishes any such choice. (TRI) itself
remains exhaustively verified to 2N = 22 and is untouched.

### 503.2 THE SPECTRUM IS GAPLESS (COMPUTED)

The witness's spectrum is the whole interval [5, 22]. That is not an
accident of one example.

  MEASURED, exhaustively over every hard-case ladder to 2N = 20, and
  on 60 sampled ladders at each larger size:

     2N                       14    16    18    20  |  22   26   30
     ladders                  14   120  1117  6796  |  60   60   60
     spectrum NOT an interval  0     0     0     0  |   0    0    0
     circumf/girth, min      2.80  3.00  3.00  3.33  |4.20 5.20 6.00
     circumf/girth, median   2.80  3.20  3.60  4.00  |4.40 5.20 6.00

  EVERY hard-case ladder tested - 8047 of them exhaustively - has a
  cycle of EVERY length between its girth and its circumference. The
  ratio grows like 2N/5, and at 2N = 30 every sampled ladder had
  girth exactly 5 and circumference exactly 2N: it was HAMILTONIAN.

That suggests the statement the programme should have been chasing all
along, and it is a classical one:

  (PAN) A girth-legal ladder has a cycle of every length between its
        girth and its circumference.
  (CIRC) Its circumference is at least twice its girth.

  (PAN) AND (CIRC) IMPLY (LQ3) IMMEDIATELY, by the capture lemma
  500.7(F1): an interval [g, c] with c >= 2g contains a power of two.

The appeal of (PAN) is that it is not a statement about powers of two
at all. Every no-go in this archive - (N7)'s degree-3 barrier,
(N12)'s reach limit, the lacunary-dodging obstruction named at the end
of 502 - is an obstruction to hitting a SPARSE target. (PAN) has no
sparse target in it. The 2-adic content of J7 would be discharged
entirely by the one-line capture lemma, and what remains is a
pancyclicity question about a cubic graph with a Hamiltonian path.

It is not proved, and it is not cheap: pancyclicity statements of this
kind are hard, and (PAN) is certainly false without girth-legality -
a matching with a span-1 chord has an isolated 2-cycle in its
spectrum. What (PAN) has that (ADJ), (TRI) and (LQ4) did not is that
it names no sub-family, so there is no sub-family for the hard case to
break.

### 503.3 STATUS

REFUTED (374.1): (ADJ) of 501.5. Exhaustively there is no hard-case
counterexample below 2N = 22, and at 2N = 22 there is one:
(1,9) (2,12) (3,15) (4,22) (5,14) (6,17) (7,20) (8,18) (10,16)
(11,19) (13,21), independently verified, whose 93 connected
adjacent-block triples realise exactly the weights [6,19] minus
{8, 16}.

CORRECTED (374.1), loudly and methodologically: 502.4's adversarial
hill-climb and linear surplus were presented as the strongest evidence
in the archive and were not evidence at all. 501.6 had already
specified the counterexample's shape - a spectrum gap on every power
of two - and the search that finds it is that specification turned
into a prune. NEW STANDING RULE: WHEN A COUNTEREXAMPLE'S SHAPE IS
KNOWN, SEARCH FOR THE SHAPE. Local search around random instances
tests nothing when the counterexamples are isolated.

COMPUTED: the (ADJ) counterexample search, exhausted at 2N <= 20 and
successful at 22; the witness's full spectrum, [5,22] with no gaps;
its four surviving (TRI) witnesses, all of weight 16 and none with an
adjacent block; and pancyclicity over all 8047 hard-case ladders at
2N = 14, 16, 18 and 20, and 60 sampled at each of 22, 26 and 30, with
ZERO spectra having a gap anywhere and circumference at least 2.8
times girth throughout.

IDENTIFIED: (PAN) and (CIRC). Together they give (LQ3) through the
capture lemma alone, and unlike every target since 496 they contain no
powers of two, so none of the archive's lacunary-dodging no-goes
applies to them.

NOT PROVED: (PAN); (CIRC); (TRI); (GAP3); (LQ3); the Ladder Question;
(R); Theorem B(SWAP); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture. (ADJ) and (LQ4) are REFUTED and cannot be proved. (TX) of
502.5 is withdrawn with (ADJ).

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED, (ADJ) SETTLED
AND FALSE. The section that targeted (ADJ) had already written down
what its counterexample must look like and then spent its evidence
budget on a local search that could not reach one. Building the
prediction into the search finds the counterexample in twelve thousand
nodes. The gain is a rule - search for the predicted shape - and a
better target: the hard-case ladders tested are all PANCYCLIC between
girth and circumference, which would settle (LQ3) with no 2-adic
argument at all, the capture lemma doing the whole of the work that
every failed target since 496 was trying to do by hand.


## 504. (CIRC) IS PROVED. (PAN) IS FALSE. THE CAPTURE WINDOW

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 503.2 named two targets.
(CIRC) IS NOW A THEOREM, in the sharp form c >= 2g - 2 (504.0), which
is exactly what the capture needs and not one unit more (504.1).
(PAN) IS FALSE (504.2) - and what exposed it was the (N9) subject test
of 499.4, applied before the target was adopted: 503.2 had measured
pancyclicity only on HARD-CASE ladders, and the hard case is defined
by a condition naming powers of two. Restated for all girth-legal
ladders, as (N9) demands, the statement is refuted by the bipartite
ones. 504.3 gives the repaired target (PAN*), which needs only a
window of length g - 1, and 504.4 proves it still implies (LQ3).

### 504.0 THE CIRCUMFERENCE THEOREM (PROVED)

THEOREM. Every girth-legal ladder H, of girth g and circumference c,
satisfies

        c   >=   2g - 2 .

  PROOF. Every vertex has degree 3 except the two ends 1 and 2N, of
  degree 2, and H HAS A HAMILTONIAN PATH - the host path - so every
  longest path is Hamiltonian and every neighbour of an endpoint of a
  longest path lies on it.

  STEP 1: A HAMILTONIAN PATH ENDING AT A VERTEX OF DEGREE 3. Label the
  host path v_j = j+1, so v_0 = 1, v_k = 2N, k = 2N-1. The neighbours
  of v_0 are v_1 = 2 and mu(1) = v_i with i = mu(1) - 1. The cycle
  v_0 v_1 ... v_i v_0 has length i+1, so i >= g-1 >= 4. ROTATE at v_0:

     P' = v_{i-1}, v_{i-2}, ..., v_1, v_0, v_i, v_{i+1}, ..., v_k

  uses the host edges below i, the chord v_0 v_i, and the host edges
  above i; it covers all 2N vertices, so it is Hamiltonian. Its
  endpoint w_0 = v_{i-1} = mu(1) - 1 is not 1, since i >= 4, and not
  2N, since that would need i-1 = k while i <= k. SO w_0 HAS DEGREE 3.

  STEP 2: COUNT ITS THREE NEIGHBOURS. Write P' = w_0 w_1 ... w_k; the
  three neighbours of w_0 lie on P', at indices 1 = j_1 < j_2 < j_3.
  Three cycles:

     w_0 w_1 ... w_{j_2} w_0                length  j_2 + 1 ,
     w_0 w_{j_2} w_{j_2+1} ... w_{j_3} w_0  length  j_3 - j_2 + 2 ,
     w_0 w_1 ... w_{j_3} w_0                length  j_3 + 1 .

  The first two are cycles, so j_2 >= g-1 and j_3 - j_2 >= g-2, and
  the third has length at least (g-1) + (g-2) + 1 = 2g-2.       QED

The count is the classical longest-path argument. What the ladder
needed is Step 1: BOTH ends of the obvious Hamiltonian path have
degree 2, and the count needs three neighbours. The rotation produces
an interior endpoint, and it always can, because mu(1) - 1 is neither
end.

  MACHINE: c >= 2g-2 held on every one of the 317964 girth-legal
  ladders at 2N = 12, 14, 16 and 18 - the last exhaustive class
  alone has 301832 members - with zero exceptions.

### 504.1 THE CAPTURE LEMMA, AND THE SHARPNESS OF 504.0 (PROVED)

LEMMA. For every integer g >= 2, the interval [g, 2g-2] contains a
power of two.
  PROOF. Take k with 2^k < g <= 2^{k+1}. Then 2^{k+1} >= g and
  2^{k+1} = 2 * 2^k <= 2(g-1) = 2g-2. QED

AND 2g-2 IS EXACTLY THE RIGHT BOUND: for g = 2^k + 1 the interval
[g, 2g-3] misses 2^{k+1} and contains no power of two at all. So
504.0 is sharp against 504.1, with no margin - the sixth appearance of
489.3's borderline pattern, and again with deficit zero.

### 504.2 (PAN) IS FALSE (REFUTED, 374.1)

503.2 proposed

  (PAN) The cycle spectrum of a girth-legal ladder is the whole
        interval [g, c].

THE (N9) TEST CAME FIRST, and it is what broke this. 503.2's evidence
was gathered on HARD-CASE ladders, and the hard case is defined by "no
span 2^M - 1 and no non-disjoint pair at L^1 distance 2^M - 2" - a
condition that names powers of two. By 499.4, a target whose subject
names the conclusion may not be adopted. So (PAN) had to be restated
for ALL girth-legal ladders. In that form it is FALSE.

  THE BIPARTITE OBSTRUCTION (PROVED). H is bipartite if and only if
  every span is odd, because the host path is bipartite by the parity
  of the position and a chord (a,b) joins the two classes exactly when
  b - a is odd. A bipartite H has only even cycles, so its spectrum
  omits every odd number in (g, c) - and c > g by 504.0. EVERY
  BIPARTITE GIRTH-LEGAL LADDER REFUTES (PAN).

  MEASURED, exhaustively over ALL girth-legal ladders:

     2N                  12      14      16       18
     ladders             34     792   15306   301832
     bipartite            0       2      12      208
     (PAN) failures       0       3      12      250

  At 2N = 16 the failures are exactly the bipartite ladders; at
  2N = 18, 208 of the 250 are bipartite and 42 are not. At 2N = 14
  there is one more than the bipartite count, and it is NOT
  bipartite:

     (1,5) (2,7) (3,9) (4,11) (6,12) (8,13) (10,14) ,

  whose spectrum is 5, 6, ..., 12 together with 14 - complete up to 12
  and then missing 13. So (PAN) fails for two independent reasons, one
  of them a parity obstruction and one of them not.

RECORDED (374.1). (PAN) was proposed one section earlier on hard-case
evidence and is false. The test of 499.4 did its work: it forced the
restatement, and the restatement is what fell. THE LESSON IS THAT THE
SUBJECT TEST MUST BE RUN BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT, NOT AFTER - had 503.2
measured the (N9)-safe form, it would have found the bipartite
counterexamples at 2N = 14 immediately.

### 504.3 (PAN*): LOCAL PANCYCLICITY IN THE CAPTURE WINDOW

Both failure modes are outside the window that 504.1 actually uses.
The repaired target asks for pancyclicity only on [g, 2g-2], and only
within the parity that the graph admits:

  (PAN*) Let H be a girth-legal ladder of girth g. If H is bipartite,
         its spectrum contains EVERY EVEN integer in [g, 2g-2]; if H
         is not bipartite, its spectrum contains EVERY integer in
         [g, 2g-2].

  MACHINE: exhaustively over ALL 16132 girth-legal ladders at
  2N = 12, 14, 16 - bipartite and not, hard-case and not - (PAN*) has
  ZERO FAILURES. Every one of them also has a power-of-two cycle.

(PAN*) is (N9)-safe: its subject is an arbitrary perfect matching with
two metric conditions, and neither the hypothesis nor the window
mentions a power of two.

### 504.4 (PAN*) IMPLIES (LQ3) (PROVED)

Let H be girth-legal, g its girth, and k with 2^k < g <= 2^{k+1}. By
504.1, 2^{k+1} lies in [g, 2g-2], and by 504.0 that interval lies
inside [g, c].

  If H is not bipartite, (PAN*) puts 2^{k+1} in the spectrum.
  If H is bipartite then g is even, hence g >= 6 since g >= 5, hence
  2^{k+1} >= 8 is EVEN, and (PAN*) again puts it in the spectrum.

Either way H has a cycle of length 2^{k+1}. QED

So the frontier now rests on ONE statement, (PAN*), and its window has
length g - 1 - a constant, since g = O(log N) by the Moore bound. The
entire 2-adic content of J7 at this frontier is carried by the two
lines of 504.1.

### 504.5 WHAT (PAN*) NEEDS

(PAN*) is a descent inside the window: it suffices that for every
cycle Z with g < |Z| <= 2g-2 there is a cycle of length |Z| - 1, or of
length |Z| - 2 in the bipartite case.

  (i) THE THETA-SPLIT CANNOT DO IT. If e is an edge of H with both
      ends on Z but not in Z, then Z + e yields cycles of lengths
      ell_1 + 1 and ell_2 + 1 with ell_1 + ell_2 = |Z|. Both are at
      least g, so each is at most |Z| - g + 1 <= |Z| - 4. THE
      CLASSICAL PANCYCLICITY MOVE JUMPS STRAIGHT OVER |Z| - 1.
 (ii) THE TOGGLE CHARACTERISES IT EXACTLY. By 500.1(i), adjoining a
      chord c to the chord set of Z changes the length by
      1 + sigma_c - 2 u_c, where u_c is the number of host edges
      inside c's span already used by Z. A step of -1 is available
      precisely at a chord with

          sigma_c EVEN     and     u_c = sigma_c / 2 + 1 ,

      a step of -2 at a chord with sigma_c odd and
      u_c = (sigma_c + 3)/2 - and in each case the toggle must leave
      the completion connected.

So (PAN*) reduces to a HALF-CONSUMED CHORD LEMMA: every cycle in the
window has, among the chords it does not use, one whose span it has
consumed just past half, with the toggle preserving connectivity.
Note that (ii) already explains the bipartite case correctly: if every
span is odd, no chord gives a step of -1, and only steps of -2 exist -
which is exactly the parity restriction (PAN*) builds in. The
characterisation and the counterexample agree.

### 504.6 STATUS

PROVED here: THE CIRCUMFERENCE THEOREM, c >= 2g-2 for every
girth-legal ladder, via a rotation of the host path at vertex 1 that
produces a Hamiltonian path ending at mu(1) - 1, which has degree 3,
followed by the three-neighbour count; THE CAPTURE LEMMA, that
[g, 2g-2] contains a power of two for every g >= 2, together with the
observation that [g, 2g-3] does not, so the circumference bound is
exactly sharp; THE BIPARTITE CHARACTERISATION, that H is bipartite iff
every span is odd; and the COROLLARY (PAN*) IMPLIES (LQ3), in both the
bipartite and the non-bipartite case.
