or a self-matched arc, every bridge has exactly two attachments, and
what is wanted is two SKEW BRIDGES. That - not (EAR+) - is the correct
residue:

  (YSK) Every cycle of a closed girth-legal ladder has a bridge with
        three attachments, or two skew bridges.

(YSK) is what (LQ3) implies (K4) actually requires. It is strictly
weaker than (EAR+): by the corollary of 514.0 its entire content is
the self-matched-arc case, 3905 of 83978 cycles at 2N = 14, and unlike
(EAR+) it survives the dodecahedron.

### 514.3 WHAT SURVIVES OF 511 TO 513

Three results, all true, none of them now needed for (K4). All are
stated in the closed ladder with girth 5 OF THE CLOSED GRAPH, which
511 to 513 did not impose; that is why the residual counts below
differ from 513's.

OUTSIDE NON-LAMINARITY THEOREM (PROVED). For every residual one-chord
cycle of a closed ladder of girth at least 5, the outside chord system
has a crossing pair.
  PROOF, in ord. (a) Every outside chord has ord-span at least 4,
  since the chord together with the outside path is a cycle of length
  span + 1. (b) No two ord-consecutive positions are both ports: two
  ports at t and t+1 have no port between them, so by the
  monotonicity of f they belong to crossers p and p+1, and then
  p, p+1, mu(p+1), mu(p) is a 4-cycle. (c) Suppose the outside chords
  are pairwise non-crossing and there is at least one; take one of
  minimum span, (alpha, beta). Each of its beta - alpha - 1 >= 3
  interior vertices is matched either into Z, making it a port, or to
  another outside vertex w - and w outside [alpha, beta] would cross
  the chord while w inside would have smaller span. So every interior
  vertex is a port, at least three of them, two consecutive, against
  (b). (d) If there is no outside chord at all then every outside
  vertex is a port and there are at least three, since the span of
  (a,b) is at most n - 4; against (b) again. QED
  MACHINE: 1190 of 1190 residual instances at 2N = 14 to 24, and all
  three of the dodecahedron's.

(GEN), THE GENERAL LINKAGE CRITERION (PROVED). Let two outside chords
cross, gamma < alpha < delta < beta, and cut ord into five zones
  Z0 = [0, gamma], Z1 = (gamma, alpha), Z2 = (alpha, delta),
  Z3 = (delta, beta), Z4 = [beta, max].
If terminals w, x, y, z can be chosen with w in Z0 or Z1, x in Z1 or
Z2, y in Z2 or Z3, z in Z3 or Z4 and no zone used twice, then
  w ... gamma -chord- delta ... y   and   x ... alpha -chord- beta ...z
occupy four pairwise disjoint intervals of ord, so they are disjoint
ears, and w < x < y < z with pairs {w,y} and {x,z} interleaved. The
terminal 0 always lies in Z0 and max always in Z4, so the condition is
only ever about the three middle zones. (XC*) of 513.0 is one case.
  MACHINE: (GEN) settles 1190 of 1190 - every residual one-chord cycle
  at 2N = 14 and 16 exhaustively and at 18 to 24 on samples -
  INCLUDING the six that (XC*) missed. 513's first gap is closed by a
  single proved criterion, and (EAR*) itself was re-verified on the
  1002 instances at 2N = 14, 16 and 18.

THE PLANARITY DICHOTOMY (PROVED). In the interlacement graph of the
matching on the host cycle: (a,b) is adjacent to every crosser chord
and to no outside chord; the crossers are pairwise non-adjacent, by
the monotonicity of f; and an outside chord is adjacent to the crosser
at p exactly when it straddles the port f(p). So in any 2-colouring of
that graph, (a,b) and every port-straddling outside chord take one
colour and every crosser the other. Since a graph carrying a
Hamiltonian cycle is planar exactly when this interlacement graph is
bipartite,

  TWO CROSSING PORT-STRADDLING CHORDS IMPLY G IS NON-PLANAR,

and the obstruction 513.1 was hunting is planarity and nothing else.
  MACHINE: on all 1190 residual instances two straddlers cross; on all
  three of the dodecahedron's the straddlers are perfectly NESTED and
  no two cross. The criterion sees the dichotomy exactly.

### 514.4 THE LITERATURE (388.1)

THE PLANAR BRANCH IS ALREADY A THEOREM. C. C. Heckman and R.
Krakovski, "Erdos-Gyarfas Conjecture for Cubic Planar Graphs",
Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 20(2) (2013), article P7. Abstract,
read from the journal's own article page: "In 1995, Paul Erdos and
Andras Gyarfas conjectured that for every graph of minimum degree at
least 3, there exists a non-negative integer m such that G contains a
simple cycle of length 2^m. In this paper, we prove that the
conjecture holds for 3-connected cubic planar graphs." A closed ladder
is cubic, so on the planar branch of 514.1 the conjecture needs
nothing from this programme as long as the ladder is 3-connected - and
the dodecahedron, the only planar closed ladder of girth 5 at 2N = 20,
is 3-connected.

(NONLAM) IS IN THE LITERATURE, ON THE WRONG SIDE. What 513.1 reduced
to - can two interleaved pairs of terminals be joined by disjoint
paths - is the two-paths problem, settled independently by Seymour, by
Shiloach and by Thomassen in 1980: there is no such pair exactly when
the graph can be drawn in a disc with the four terminals on the
boundary in the interleaved order. (NONLAM) is therefore not a
laminarity lemma waiting for a proof; it is the assertion that this
configuration is never disc-drawable, and the dodecahedron is a
configuration that is. Bibliographic data confirmed, statements NOT
read from the sources: P. D. Seymour, "Disjoint paths in graphs",
Discrete Mathematics 29 (1980) 293-309; C. Thomassen, "2-linked
graphs", European Journal of Combinatorics 1 (1980) 371-378.

### 514.5 THE TWO RULES THIS FAILURE EARNS

  (IFF) AN EQUIVALENCE IS TWO THEOREMS. 509.0 proved that a
  quadrilateral presentation yields two skew ears, and asserted the
  converse for all seven cycles. The direction that was not argued was
  the one every later section depended on, and it was false. Never
  record an "if and only if" unless both directions have been argued
  separately, and never build on the half that was not.

  (EMPTY) BEFORE TRUSTING A SWEEP, COUNT THE COUNTEREXAMPLE CLASS.
  501.0 said: test in the hard case. This is sharper. The class of
  planar closed ladders of girth 5 is EMPTY below 2N = 20 and is one
  graph at 2N = 20, and Euler's formula says so in a single line.
  124769 cycles were checked in a range where the answer could not
  have been no. A one-line count of the class would have shown that
  before any of them was computed.

### 514.6 STATUS

CORRECTED (374.1): the Presentation Lemma of 509.0 and 509.5 is NOT an
equivalence. Two disjoint interleaving ears characterise Z as a
QUADRILATERAL of a K_4-subdivision; a Y characterises Z as a TRIANGLE;
Z lies in a K_4-subdivision if either holds.

REFUTED (374.1): (EAR+) of 510.2, and with it (EAR*) of 511 and
(NONLAM) of 513.1. Witness: the dodecahedron, on which 432 of 1168
cycles - including all three residual one-chord cycles - have no two
disjoint interleaving ears, verified by direct ear enumeration in G.

PROVED here: the corrected Presentation Lemma; the Y-LEMMA, that a
bridge with three attachments carries a Y, so in a cubic graph one
such bridge puts Z in a K_4-subdivision; that a residual one-chord
cycle has exactly one bridge and therefore bounds a face whenever G is
planar; that a cubic planar graph of girth 5 has at least 20 vertices,
with equality only for the dodecahedron; the characterisation of the
cycles with no three-attachment bridge as those whose outside host
arcs are all self-matched; the OUTSIDE NON-LAMINARITY THEOREM; (GEN),
the general linkage criterion; and that two crossing port-straddling
chords force G to be non-planar.

COMPUTED: the dodecahedron's 1168 cycles all lie in K_4-subdivisions,
1138 by a Y and 30 by skew bridges; exhaustively at 2N = 14, all 83978
cycles of all 408 closed girth-5 ladders lie in K_4-subdivisions,
80073 by a Y and 3905 by skew bridges, none failing, and the
self-matched-arc characterisation holds on all 83978; (GEN) settles
all 1190 residual one-chord cycles found at 2N = 14 to 24 in the
closed-girth-5 model, and outside non-laminarity holds on all of them.

IDENTIFIED: (YSK) - every cycle of a closed girth-legal ladder has a
bridge with three attachments or two skew bridges - as the correct and
strictly weaker replacement for (EAR+), whose entire content is the
case where every outside host arc is self-matched.

NOT PROVED: (YSK); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); the Ladder Question; (R);
Theorem B(SWAP); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.
(EAR), (EAR+), (EAR*) and (NONLAM) are REFUTED.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The programme
asked for (NONLAM) and got its refutation, which is the better answer:
the lemma the last five sections were built on was never an
equivalence, the half that was assumed is false, and the half that is
true was never needed, because a cycle sits in a K_4-subdivision as a
triangle far more cheaply than as a quadrilateral. (K4) is where 510
left it - equivalent to (LQ3) on everything measured - but the bridge
between them is now (YSK), which is weaker than (EAR+), survives the
graph that killed (EAR+), and has only one case left in it. The 2-adic
weight of the problem is still in (LQ3) alone.

## 515. (K4) IS EQUIVALENT TO THE CONJECTURE, AND THE TEMPLATE LIST
## IS COMPLETE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. (K4) IS NOW A THEOREM-
GRADE REFORMULATION AND (YSK) IS PROVED. 514 left (YSK) as the
frontier and left "(K4) is equivalent to (LQ3)" resting on
measurement, the earlier derivation having gone through the false
509.0. One short theorem settles both: IN A 3-CONNECTED GRAPH EVERY
CYCLE IS ONE OF THE SEVEN CYCLES OF A K_4-SUBDIVISION. 515.0 proves
it and names the only obstruction, 515.1 draws (YSK) and the
equivalence, 515.2 shows the connectivity cannot be dropped. 515.3
then closes the template line for good: K_4 and K_{3,3} are the ONLY
cubic graphs every element of whose cycle space is a cycle, so
fifteen targets from nine parameters is the most any template can
ever offer. 515.4 shows that the crossing triple of 508.2 IS a
K_{3,3} as soon as the host cycle is kept, so 508 was looking at
seven of its fifteen values; 515.5 shows the K_{3,3} template is
LOCAL, which condemns it under (N16). 515.6 is the arithmetic normal
form, 515.7 the literature map.

### 515.0 THE K_4-UBIQUITY THEOREM (PROVED)

THEOREM. Let G be a simple 2-connected graph of minimum degree at
least 3 and let Z be a cycle of G. If Z is one of the seven cycles of
no K_4-subdivision of G, then some edge ab of Z has {a, b} a 2-cut of
G, and the bridge of Z attached at {a, b} contains a cycle.

  PROOF. By the corrected Presentation Lemma (514.6) Z lies in a
  K_4-subdivision if and only if some bridge of Z has three
  attachments or two bridges of Z are skew; assume neither.
  (a) G is 2-connected, so every bridge has at least two attachments,
      hence exactly two.
  (b) Every vertex of Z is an attachment of some bridge: it has
      degree at least 3 and only two of its edges lie on Z.
  (c) Among all pairs (B, A) with B a bridge with attachments {u, v}
      and A one of the two arcs of Z from u to v, take one with the
      fewest vertices of Z interior to A. No interior vertex w of A
      is an attachment. For let w belong to the bridge with
      attachments {w, w'}. If w' is interior to A, that bridge with
      the sub-arc from w to w' beats the choice. If w' lies strictly
      outside A then {w, w'} and {u, v} interleave, so those two
      bridges are skew. If w' is u or v, the sub-arc of A from w to
      w' again beats the choice. By (b), A has no interior vertex at
      all, so uv is an edge of Z.
  (d) B is not the edge uv, which lies on Z, and G is simple, so B
      has an interior vertex. Its interior meets Z only in u and v
      and Z has at least three vertices, so {u, v} is a 2-cut.
  (e) B is not a tree. Every interior vertex of B has all three of
      its G-neighbours inside B, so degree at least 3 there; a tree
      would have all its leaves in {u, v}, hence at most two leaves,
      hence be a path, whose interior vertices have degree 2. So B
      contains a cycle. QED

COROLLARY 1. IN A 3-CONNECTED GRAPH EVERY CYCLE IS ONE OF THE SEVEN
CYCLES OF A K_4-SUBDIVISION.

COROLLARY 2. In a cubic graph a and b each send exactly one edge into
B, so those two edges form a 2-edge-cut with a cycle on each side.
Hence IN A CYCLICALLY 3-EDGE-CONNECTED CUBIC GRAPH EVERY CYCLE LIES
IN A K_4-SUBDIVISION.

  MACHINE, by the bridge criterion: Petersen 57 of 57 cycles, Heawood
  213 of 213, dodecahedron 1168 of 1168, all 83978 cycles of all 408
  closed girth-5 ladders at 2N = 14, and 311971 of 311971 over 801
  sampled closed girth-5 ladders at 2N = 16. No failure anywhere.
  MACHINE, INDEPENDENTLY, by exact enumeration of subdivisions rather
  than of bridges - in a cubic graph a subgraph of degrees 2 and 3 is
  exactly (G - O) - M for an omitted set O and a matching M inside the
  surviving degree-3 part, so every K_4- and K_{3,3}-subdivision can
  be listed with no bridge or ear machinery at all: K_4 itself 7 of 7,
  K_{3,3} 15 of 15, Petersen 57 of 57 (160 K_4-subdivisions).

### 515.1 (YSK) IS PROVED, AND SO IS THE EQUIVALENCE

(YSK) OF 514.2 IS PROVED for every 3-connected closed ladder, by
Corollary 1. The hypothesis costs nothing in the measured range:

LEMMA. A closed girth-legal ladder with 2N at most 20 is 3-connected,
and a counterexample to (YSK) in a closed girth-legal ladder needs
2N at least 22.
  PROOF. In a cubic graph vertex connectivity equals edge
  connectivity, and a Hamiltonian cycle meets a 2-edge-cut exactly
  twice, so both cut edges are host edges and the host splits into
  two arcs each matched within itself. By 515.0 a (YSK) failure is
  sharper still: the bridge found there is a self-matched host arc A
  whose two host-neighbours a, b are matched to each other, and then
  the rest of the host is self-matched too. A self-matched arc is a
  perfect matching of an interval with every span at least 4 and
  every non-disjoint pair at L^1 distance at least 3, and the
  smallest such interval has TEN vertices (exhaustive; none at 2, 4,
  6, 8; at 10, (1,5)(2,7)(3,9)(4,8)(6,10)). Two self-matched arcs
  give 2N >= 20, and the extra matched pair gives 2N >= 22. QED

So (YSK) holds on every ladder the archive has ever measured, and
514.2's residue is closed. Consequently, and now as a theorem rather
than as a report of 124769 measurements:

  (K4) IS EQUIVALENT TO THE ERDOS-GYARFAS CONJECTURE FOR 3-CONNECTED
  CUBIC GRAPHS OF GIRTH AT LEAST 5.

  PROOF. (K4) implies the conjecture because the seven values of a
  K_4-subdivision of G are lengths of cycles of G. Conversely a
  power-of-two cycle of such a G is, by Corollary 1, one of the seven
  cycles of a K_4-subdivision, so that subdivision witnesses (K4).
  QED

This restores the conclusion of 510.3 - which was drawn from the
false half of 509.0 and therefore had to be withdrawn - on a proof
that does not mention ears at all. It also confirms 509.2's reading:
(K4) LOCATES NOTHING. It is the conjecture, reparametrised.

### 515.2 SHARPNESS: THE CONNECTIVITY CANNOT BE DROPPED (COMPUTED)

Take a 6-cycle 0-1-2-3-4-5 and hang on each of the consecutive pairs
(0,1), (2,3), (4,5) a copy of PETERSEN MINUS AN EDGE, joining the two
degree-2 vertices of the copy to the two vertices of the pair. The
result is cubic on 36 vertices with girth 5, and it is not
3-connected.

  MACHINE: the 6-cycle has exactly three bridges, with attachment
  pairs {0,1}, {2,3}, {4,5} - two attachments each, pairwise
  non-interleaving - so by 514.6 IT LIES IN NO K_4-SUBDIVISION, and
  the 2-cut predicted by 515.0 is exhibited: {0,1}, separating 10
  vertices.

So the general statement "every cycle of a cubic graph of girth 5 has
a bridge with three attachments or two skew bridges" is FALSE; what is
true is Corollary 2, and the ladders satisfy its hypothesis.

### 515.3 TEMPLATE COMPLETENESS: ONLY K_4 AND K_{3,3} (PROVED)

Call a graph a TEMPLATE if every non-zero element of its cycle space
is a cycle. A template of cycle-space dimension d has 2^d - 1 cycles
and every edge lies in exactly 2^(d-1) of them, so its cycle lengths
sum to 2^(d-1) S. The known templates are the cycle (d = 1), the
theta graph (d = 2), K_4 (d = 3, seven cycles, 4S) and K_{3,3}
(d = 4, fifteen cycles - nine quadrilaterals and six hexagons - 8S,
each half summing to 4S).

THEOREM. THE ONLY SIMPLE CUBIC TEMPLATES ARE K_4 AND K_{3,3}.
  PROOF. Two vertex-disjoint cycles are edge-disjoint and their sum
  is their disjoint union, which is not a cycle; so a template has no
  two vertex-disjoint cycles. Let H be a cubic template, C a shortest
  cycle, g = |C| and R = V(H) - V(C). H[R] has no cycle, so at most
  |R| - 1 edges. Each vertex of C has exactly one edge off C, so at
  most g edges join R to C. Summing degrees in R,
      3|R| <= 2(|R| - 1) + g ,  so  |R| <= g - 2  and  n <= 2g - 2 .
  A cubic graph of girth g has at least 3*2^k - 2 vertices for
  g = 2k+1 and at least 2^(k+1) - 2 for g = 2k, and for g >= 5 that
  exceeds 2g - 2 (g = 5: 10 > 8; g = 6: 14 > 10; and the bound
  doubles while 2g - 2 grows by 4). So g <= 4. If g = 3 then n <= 4
  and H = K_4. If g = 4 then n <= 6, and the only cubic graph of
  girth 4 on at most 6 vertices is K_{3,3}. Both are templates. QED

  MACHINE, exhaustive over labelled connected cubic graphs: n = 4,
  1 graph, a template (7 cycles, 4 triangles, girth 3); n = 6, 70
  graphs, exactly 10 templates, all with 15 cycles, no triangle and
  girth 4 - the ten labellings of K_{3,3}, 6!/|Aut| = 720/72 = 10;
  n = 8, 19320 graphs, NO template.

COROLLARY. In a cubic graph the only all-cycles templates are the
K_4-subdivision - seven targets from six parameters - and the
K_{3,3}-subdivision - fifteen targets from nine. NOTHING BEATS 15/9.
The route 508.0 opened is therefore bounded, and the bound is small.

### 515.4 THE CROSSING TRIPLE IS A K_{3,3}, NOT A K_4 (PROVED)

508.2 took three pairwise crossing chords c_i = (a_i, b_i) with
a_1 < a_2 < a_3 < b_1 < b_2 < b_3 and read off a K_4-subdivision with
branch vertices a_2, a_3, b_1, b_2, "a_1 and b_3 having degree 2 in
the subgraph". They have degree 2 only because the subgraph THROWS
AWAY the host arc from b_3 back to a_1. Keep it. Then all six chord
ends have degree 3, and the six-cycle a_1 a_2 a_3 b_1 b_2 b_3 with
its three main diagonals is exactly K_{3,3}. So:

  THE CROSSING TRIPLE OF 508.2 IS A K_{3,3}-SUBDIVISION OF THE CLOSED
  LADDER, WITH NINE BRANCH PATHS AND FIFTEEN CYCLES.

The fifteen split by how many chords they use: one uses none (the
host cycle), six use one, six use two and two use three - and the
K_4 of 508.2 saw one of each complementary pair. Writing sigma_i for
the spans and L_ij for the L^1 distances,

    2N ;
    sigma_i + 1        and   2N + 1 - sigma_i ;
    2 + L_ij           and   2N + 2 - L_ij ;
    XXX                and   2N + 6 - XXX ,   XXX = 3 + sigma_1
                                              - sigma_2 + sigma_3 .

  MACHINE: 10071 crossing triples over 200 closed girth-5 ladders at
  each of 2N = 14, 16, 18 and 20 - 1699, 2162, 2830 and 3380 - every
  one is a K_{3,3}-subdivision, every one has exactly these fifteen
  lengths, and every one sums to 8S with S = 2N + 3. (A first pass
  predicted 2N + 3 - XXX for the second three-chord cycle and matched
  0 of 1409; the complement of a cycle with t chords adds 2t, not 3.)

THE COMPLEMENT LAW (PROVED). Chords are a basis of the cycle space of
the OPEN ladder, which is why 495.0 and 500.0 could say that a chord
set T determines its completion. In the CLOSED ladder the dimension
is N + 1, the host cycle being the extra generator, and the ends of T
cut the host into an even number of arcs, of which either alternating
class completes T. When both completions are connected their lengths
satisfy
    ell + ell'  =  2N + 2|T| .

  MACHINE: 180955 chord sets with two connected completions at
  2N = 12, 14 and 16 - the law holds for every one, no exception. Of
  the 50670 chord sets with at least one completion at 2N = 14, 33308
  have two; the closed ladder carries 83978 cycles against 50670
  open-model targets, a ratio of 1.657 (1.717 at 2N = 12, 1.603 at
  2N = 16). Two independent enumerations - depth-first search and
  the completion algebra above - agree on 83978.

CONSEQUENCE. 508.3 concluded that the short-branch template "is
already fully exploited" because its seven values were the one-chord,
two-chord and XXX lengths the archive already computes. That was
computed in the OPEN ladder. In the closed ladder - the faithful J7
rung of 510.2 - the same configuration carries EIGHT MORE lengths,
every one of them involving 2N. The caveat is that 510.2 models the
return path through C by a single edge; if that path has length p the
complement of a cycle using it is longer by p - 1, so the eight extra
values are a shifted family, not a fixed one.

### 515.5 THE K_{3,3} TEMPLATE IS LOCAL, SO (K33) IS CONDEMNED

The natural successor target is

  (K33) Every 3-connected non-planar cubic graph of girth at least 5
        has a K_{3,3}-subdivision one of whose fifteen lengths is a
        power of two,

and it is forced on exactly the graphs that remain: by Heckman and
Krakovski the planar case is a theorem, and a non-planar graph of
maximum degree 3 contains no K_5-subdivision - K_5 needs degree 4 -
so by Kuratowski it contains a K_{3,3}-subdivision. Fifteen targets
from nine parameters, and the template is unavoidable. But (N16)
requires the safety test that 509.1 ran for (K4), and (K33) FAILS it.

THEOREM. There is a 3-connected cubic graph of girth 5 with cycles
that lie in no K_{3,3}-subdivision.
  CONSTRUCTION. Let A be the dodecahedron minus a vertex and B the
  Petersen graph minus a vertex; each has exactly three vertices of
  degree 2. Join the two triples by a perfect matching. The result G
  is cubic on 28 vertices, of girth 5, and 3-connected (machine), and
  non-planar because B has 9 vertices, 12 edges and girth 5, while a
  planar graph of girth 5 on 9 vertices has at most (5/3)(9-2) < 12.
  PROOF. The three matching edges form a 3-edge-cut. Let H be a
  K_{3,3}-subdivision of G. K_{3,3} is 3-edge-connected and its only
  3-edge-cuts are the six vertex stars, so H either keeps all six
  branch vertices on one side of the cut, or has exactly one branch
  vertex on one side and five on the other with its three legs
  crossing. If all six are in A, H crosses the cut in branch-path
  segments, each using two cut edges, so at most one segment;
  contracting it to an edge puts a K_{3,3}-subdivision inside A plus
  one edge joining two of its three degree-2 vertices, which is
  planar because those three lie on the face left by the deleted
  vertex. If five are in A and one in B, contracting the B side to a
  single vertex joined to those three puts a K_{3,3}-subdivision
  inside the dodecahedron, which is planar. Both are impossible, so
  every K_{3,3}-subdivision of G has at least five branch vertices in
  B; and every cycle of K_{3,3} runs through at least four branch
  vertices, so every cycle of H meets B. NO CYCLE LYING INSIDE A IS A
  CYCLE OF ANY K_{3,3}-SUBDIVISION - for instance none of the eleven
  pentagonal faces of the dodecahedron that avoid the deleted vertex.
  QED

  MACHINE, on the small analogue, fully enumerated: splice a triangle
  (K_4 minus a vertex) to the Petersen graph minus a vertex, giving a
  3-connected cubic graph on 12 vertices. It has 100 cycles and 64
  K_{3,3}-subdivisions, which cover 99 of the 100 cycles. THE SINGLE
  EXCEPTION IS THE PLANAR-SIDE TRIANGLE, exactly as the theorem says.

So (K33) is a STRENGTHENING of the conjecture, not a reformulation:
a graph may satisfy Erdos-Gyarfas by a cycle that no K_{3,3} can
reach. Under (N16) it is condemned, and it is withdrawn as a target
here rather than after three sections. K_4 IS THE UNIQUE UBIQUITOUS
TEMPLATE.

  MACHINE, and this is why the distinction had to be tested rather
  than guessed: on the ladder family K_{3,3} IS ubiquitous. Every one
  of the 83978 cycles of all 408 closed girth-5 ladders at 2N = 14,
  and every one of the 31130 cycles of 80 sampled at 2N = 16, lies in
  a K_{3,3}-subdivision - 0 exceptions, by the exact subdivision
  listing of 515.0 - so the fifteen values of 515.4 are available
  there even though (K33) is not a reformulation in general.

### 515.6 THE Y-FORM OF THE SEVEN VALUES (PROVED)

515.0 supplies the K_4 through a Y in every case where a bridge has
three attachments - which is 80073 of the 83978 cycles at 2N = 14 -
so the seven values deserve to be written in the Y's own parameters.
Let Z have length g, let the Y have legs p, q, r from its hub to
three feet, and let the feet cut Z into arcs x, y, z with
x + y + z = g. Put e_1 = p + q, e_2 = q + r, e_3 = p + r and
a_1 = x, a_2 = y, a_3 = z. Then the seven cycles are

    g ,  and  e_i + a_i  and  e_i + (g - a_i)   for i = 1, 2, 3 .

  PROOF. With hub w and feet u_1, u_2, u_3, S = p + q + r + g and the
  seven values are S minus the seven cuts: S - star(w) = x+y+z = g;
  S - star(u_1) = q+r+y; S - star(u_2) = p+r+z; S - star(u_3) =
  p+q+x; and S - (p+y) = (q+r) + (x+z), S - (q+z) = (p+r) + (x+y),
  S - (r+x) = (p+q) + (y+z). Since x+y+z = g the quadrilaterals are
  e_2 + (g-y), e_3 + (g-z), e_1 + (g-x). QED

So (K4) is not six parameters and seven targets but THREE INDEPENDENT
PAIRS PLUS THE CYCLE ITSELF, the i-th pair summing to 2e_i + g and
differing by |g - 2a_i|. The three differences sum to g. Choosing the
feet so that one arc is floor(g/2) makes one pair differ by 0 or 1,
which is where the freedom in the template actually lives.

### 515.7 THE LITERATURE MAP (388.1)

Five results, from five papers, meet at (K4); this is the map.

  SUPPLY. G. A. Dirac (1960): every graph of minimum degree at least
  3 contains a subdivision of K_4. Verified at 388.1 and used at
  508.4. This is what makes the template exist at all.

  UBIQUITY. The language of 515.0 - bridges of a cycle, their
  attachments, and skewness - is Tutte's. W. T. Tutte, "How to Draw a
  Graph", Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (3) 13
  (1963) 743-767. Bibliographic data confirmed from the publisher's
  article page; the statement of 515.0 is proved here and was not
  found in the literature.

  COUNTING. The nearest published statement about K_4-subdivisions
  and 3-connectivity is T. Miltzow, J. M. Schmidt and M. Xia,
  "Counting K_4-Subdivisions", Discrete Mathematics 338 (2015), issue
  12, 2387-2392; from the arXiv abstract page, they show a
  3-connected graph on n vertices has "Omega(n^3) such
  K_4-subdivisions and show that the order of this bound is tight for
  infinitely many graphs", and that exact counting is "#P-hard".
  They count subdivisions; 515.0 places a PRESCRIBED CYCLE in one.

  THE TEMPLATE LIST. 515.3's proof needs only the Moore bound, but
  the ambient classification is L. Lovasz, "On graphs not containing
  independent circuits", Matematikai Lapok 16 (1965) 289-299 (in
  Hungarian), which describes the graphs in which any two circuits
  meet. Bibliographic data confirmed; the statement is NOT read from
  the source, and 515.3 does not use it.

  THE SECOND TEMPLATE. Kuratowski's theorem plus maximum degree 3
  forces the K_{3,3}-subdivision, since a K_5-subdivision needs four
  branch vertices of degree 4. Combined with C. C. Heckman and R.
  Krakovski (2013), verified at 514.4, this says the only cubic
  graphs left are exactly the ones carrying the larger template -
  which is why 515.5's locality theorem had to be proved before the
  template could be believed.

  AND (NONLAM), at 514.4, was the two-paths theorem of Seymour and of
  Thomassen (1980) read from the wrong side. The pattern across 509
  to 515 is consistent: every structural statement this programme has
  needed about a cycle and its bridges was either classical or
  provable in a page. THE ARITHMETIC IS WHERE THE CONJECTURE LIVES.

### 515.8 STATUS

PROVED here: THE K_4-UBIQUITY THEOREM - in a 3-connected graph every
cycle is one of the seven cycles of a K_4-subdivision, the only
obstruction under minimum degree 3 and 2-connectivity being a 2-cut
{a,b} with ab an edge of the cycle and a cycle behind it; its cubic
form, that cyclic 3-edge-connectivity suffices. (YSK) OF 514.2, for
every 3-connected closed ladder, and unconditionally for 2N <= 20,
since a self-matched host arc needs ten vertices. THE EQUIVALENCE
(K4) = the Erdos-Gyarfas conjecture for 3-connected cubic graphs of
girth at least 5, now a theorem and no longer a report of
measurements. TEMPLATE COMPLETENESS - K_4 and K_{3,3} are the only
simple cubic graphs every element of whose cycle space is a cycle, so
fifteen targets from nine parameters is the ceiling. THE CROSSING
TRIPLE OF 508.2 IS A K_{3,3}-SUBDIVISION of the closed ladder, whose
fifteen lengths are 508.2's seven, the host cycle 2N, and seven
complements. THE COMPLEMENT LAW ell + ell' = 2N + 2|T| in the closed
ladder, where chords are not a basis. THE LOCALITY THEOREM - a
3-connected cubic graph of girth 5 with cycles in no
K_{3,3}-subdivision. THE Y-FORM of the seven values.

COMPUTED: no failure of Corollary 1 anywhere tested - Petersen 57,
Heawood 213, dodecahedron 1168, all 83978 cycles of all 408 closed
girth-5 ladders at 2N = 14, 311971 over 801 sampled at 2N = 16 -
with a second, independent verification by exact enumeration of
subdivisions as (G - O) - M. Template completeness exhaustive at
n = 4, 6, 8 (1, 70, 19320 labelled connected cubic graphs; 1, 10, 0
templates). The fifteen-length formula on 10071 crossing triples at
2N = 14 to 20. The complement law on 180955 chord sets. Every one of
the 83978 cycles at 2N = 14 and of 31130 sampled at 2N = 16 lies in a
K_{3,3}-subdivision as well. The 12-vertex splice:
64 K_{3,3}-subdivisions, 100 cycles, 99 covered, the exception the
planar-side triangle.

CORRECTED (374.1): 508.2 and 508.4 present the crossing triple as a
K_4-subdivision and conclude that "the short-branch template is
already fully exploited". The configuration is a K_{3,3}-subdivision;
the K_4 reading discards the host arc from b_3 to a_1 and with it
eight of the fifteen lengths. The conclusion stands for the open
ladder, where the discarded arc is not there, and fails for the
closed ladder, which is the faithful rung.

WITHDRAWN: (K33), as a strengthening condemned by (N16) - 515.5.

IDENTIFIED: that the structural side of the K_4 programme is now
finished. K_4 is the unique ubiquitous template; K_{3,3} is the only
larger one and it is local; the ratio 15/9 is the ceiling; and the
seven values reduce to three pairs and the cycle. What is left is
what 509.2 said was left: SIX POSITIVE INTEGERS AND SEVEN PRESCRIBED
SUMS, one of which must be a power of two.

NOT PROVED: (LQ3), equivalently (K4); the Ladder Question; (R);
Theorem B(SWAP); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED, (K4) equivalent
to the conjecture for 3-connected cubic graphs of girth at least 5 AS
A THEOREM. Asked to attack (K4) head on, the honest report is that
its structural half collapses in a page and its arithmetic half does
not move at all. Every cycle of a 3-connected graph sits in a
K_4-subdivision; the seven values are three pairs plus the cycle; no
template larger than K_{3,3} exists; and the one template that is
larger cannot see cycles in the planar part of a graph. Six sections
of ear geometry, 509 through 515, end where 509.2 predicted: (K4) is
the conjecture, written with six parameters instead of one cycle, and
the power of two is still not located.


## 516. THE LAYERED LEDGER: WHAT EVERY ATTACK ON J7 MISSES TOGETHER,
## AND EXACTLY HOW FAR THE PLANAR THEOREM REACHES

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked to lay every
approach this archive has thrown at J7 on top of every other and read
off what the union does not cover, the answer is sharper than an
inventory. 516.0 proves that the conjecture factors exactly into one
2-adic and one Archimedean condition. 516.1 sorts every instrument in
the archive by which of the two it controls, and finds that all but
two control exactly one - and that the two exceptions are precisely
the archive's only two theorems that produce a power-of-two cycle in
a graph not assumed to be a counterexample. 516.2 is the
track-by-track ledger with each stopping point named. 516.3 measures
the residue in the ladder world and finds it non-empty from 2N = 20.
516.4 corrects (N16): its sharpest instance was refuted in the open
ladder, and the witness dies on closing. 516.5 answers the planar
question with a formula. 516.6 says what would actually wrap J7 up.
Machine: scratch hard516.py, kstar.py, kstar2.py, shape516.py,
resid516.py, capture516.py, cage516.py, lc516.py, gen516.py.

### 516.0 THE TARGET FACTORISATION (PROVED)

THEOREM. For a positive integer x put t = floor(log_2 x). Then x is a
power of two if and only if 2^t divides x. Consequently, for any set
S of positive integers,

    S contains a power of two
      <=>  for some t, S meets [2^t, 2^{t+1}) in a multiple of 2^t,

and the block [2^t, 2^{t+1}) contains EXACTLY ONE multiple of 2^t.
  PROOF. If 2^t | x and 2^t <= x < 2^{t+1} then x / 2^t is an integer
  in [1, 2), so x = 2^t; the converse is immediate. QED

The arithmetic is trivial. What it says about PROOFS is not. To
produce a power-of-two cycle one must produce a cycle meeting two
conditions of different type:

    (2ADIC)   its length is divisible by 2^t ;
    (ARCH)    its length is below 2^{t+1} .

Neither has content alone. Every cubic graph has lengths divisible by
2^t for many t, and every graph with a cycle has lengths below any
bound one likes; the conjecture is that the two can be met AT THE
SAME t BY THE SAME CYCLE. And the conditions cannot be traded: a
length divisible by 2^t and just past 2^{t+1} is exactly as far from
a power of two as an odd number is.

  COROLLARY (WHY NEITHER HALF OF THE ARCHIVE CAN FINISH). 445.5 and
  447 record that no purely arithmetic theorem can close J7; 450 and
  the packing counts record that no purely metric one can. The
  factorisation says both at once, and says why. An argument in the
  2-adic coordinate proves (2ADIC) and is SILENT on (ARCH); an
  argument in lengths proves (ARCH) and is SILENT on (2ADIC). The
  two no-goes are one no-go.

  AND IT IS 470.5's DEMAND, RENAMED. 470.5 proves the stratum-local
  no-go and states the demand as "a mechanism COUPLING levels". A
  level IS a valuation, and the reason a single stratum cannot decide
  is that the stratum fixes (2ADIC) and says nothing about (ARCH):
  G* of 470.4(iii) has 8-divisible spectrum exactly {24}, which
  satisfies (2ADIC) at t = 3 and fails (ARCH) since 24 > 16. The
  witness is not an accident of that search - it is the general shape
  of the gap.

### 516.1 THE INSTRUMENT LEDGER: EVERY THEOREM CONTROLS ONE COORDINATE

Sorted by coordinate, with the archive's own citations.

  CONTROLS (2ADIC), SILENT ON (ARCH):
    the flow-lattice nexus and the Tower Theorem            441.2
    the Ear Identity                                        441.4
    the Counting Identity and the Gauss Bound               443.1
    residue rigidity, and its death past t = 3              431.3
    Exact-Valuation and the Laminar Kill               432.3/432.6
    the increment congruence under (Q)                    490, 492
    the sigma-paired Davenport constants               464.3, 465-6
    the theta valuation lemma                                 471
    the 2-group asymmetry                                   447.5

  CONTROLS (ARCH), SILENT ON (2ADIC):
    the ear supply bound                                    432.4
    the packing shell and the Middle-Zone Law               433.2
    both-arcs-minimal                                       449.1
    the Cross-Edge Window Theorem                           450.2
    the arc budget                                          477.1
    the shortcut budget                                       498
    the slack-growth theorem                                  493
    the Circumference Theorem c >= 2g - 2                   504.0
    the Moore bound
    K_4-UBIQUITY, the Y-form, template completeness   515.0-515.6

  CONTROLS BOTH - and each of these IS a cycle-producing theorem:
    the non-backtracking trace in its window g <= m < 2g       452
    the cycle semigroup, THEOREM A                             474

THE LEDGER'S ONE OBSERVATION, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THIS SECTION.
The archive contains exactly two theorems that produce a power-of-two
cycle in a graph NOT assumed to be a counterexample:

  (i) 452.4's corollary - if a power of two satisfies (W) then G has
      a cycle of that length - which settles the (3,9) to (3,12)
      cages, the Foster graph, and an infinite explicit family;
 (ii) 474's THEOREM A - every nonempty cycle semigroup contains a
      member with a power-of-two cycle.

Both are in the coupling row, and neither could be anywhere else.
(i) pins the scale by computing c_m exactly in a window and then
observes that the unique power of two in that window is the target;
(ii) pairs the exact amalgam spectrum identity with Bondy-Vince's
gcd corollary, size against divisibility. EVERYTHING ELSE IN THE
ARCHIVE PRODUCES CONTRADICTIONS, NOT CYCLES, AND EVERYTHING ELSE
LIVES IN ONE COLUMN.

Each of the two also pays a stated price, and the price is the other
coordinate bought from outside: (i) pays the (n, g) spectral test,
which is an Archimedean hypothesis on the graph; (ii) pays SIZE, and
(N8) proves it must.

### 516.2 THE FOUR TRACKS, LAYERED, WITH EACH STOPPING POINT

TRACK A - THE (SC) / EAR FRAME (191-451, 464-470).
  COVERS. Everything about a shallow cycle in a minimal counter-
  example except one configuration: J7 = the non-existence of the
  braided packing-shell graph (a)-(f), 433.4 with 434.1's correction,
  and by 434.3 that is exactly the residual content of the conjecture
  as seen from this route.
  STOPS AT. The five statements of 451.2, corrected by 464.2's three
  ledger items and reduced by 464.3 to the sigma-paired Davenport
  problem, which 465-467 measured and which does not come down.
  COORDINATE. (2ADIC). Its supply theorems are Archimedean but they
  bound the NUMBER of ears, never the LENGTH of the companion
  produced - and 477.1's arc budget proves the shifts are
  concentrated near L, that is, on the wrong side of 2^{t+1}.

TRACK B - THE TRACE FRAME (452-463).
  COVERS. c_m exactly for g <= m < 2g, hence Erdos-Gyarfas for every
  cubic graph passing the (n, g) test.
  STOPS AT. m = 2g. The rank >= 2 geodesic corrections are
  Theta(2^m) - measured between 0.66 and 2.53 of the main term
  (452.5) - and the barrier is m* >= g - 1 with the usable window
  (m*, 2g).
  COORDINATE. BOTH, which is why it is a theorem.

TRACK C - THE OBJECT (474-494).
  COVERS. The braid is a Mobius ladder with a solved spectrum
  (479, 480); the chord system is a taxicab packing of minimum
  distance 3 (481); the leak object (D, T) satisfies Theorem A by its
  own axioms (484).
  STOPS AT. Theorem B in each successive form - (B1) the gap of the
  rung sum set and (B2) a run among the leak depths (485), replaced
  in 488 by a Brown-completeness condition on a resource no theorem
  in the archive bounds.
  COORDINATE. (2ADIC), by way of 490: the increments need not be
  small and their gcd need not be a power of two; what is needed is a
  congruence, and 467 measured what congruences cost the adversary -
  about 35 per cent, a constant factor, not a decay.

TRACK D - THE LADDER AND THE TEMPLATE (494-515).
  COVERS. The cycle space is the power set of the chords (495); the
  three-chord criterion and the four weight formulas (501); (CIRC),
  c >= 2g - 2 (504.0); (K4) equivalent to the conjecture for
  3-connected cubic graphs of girth at least 5, as a theorem
  (515.0-515.2); the template list is K_4 and K_{3,3} and nothing
  else (515.3).
  STOPS AT. (LQ3) itself, unlocated, with six strengthenings refuted
  (507.1).
  COORDINATE. (ARCH). And the ledger can be counted: the largest
  template supplies FIFTEEN values, while the dyadic block that must
  be hit at level t contains 2^t integers. A fixed fifteen-element
  set is not a covering of a block of width 2^t for t >= 4. That is
  the arithmetic content of 509.2's "(K4) locates nothing", and it
  is why 515 ended where 509.2 predicted.

  THE LAYERS DO NOT ADD UP. Stacking A, B, C and D gives: one scale
  covered conditionally (B, under the (n,g) test); valuation control
  at the shallow level with no bound on the companion's length
  (A, C); and fifteen numbers per template (D). The union is not a
  covering of even one dyadic block, and 516.3 shows that in the one
  world where it can be measured exactly, the union is literally
  empty on a non-empty set of graphs.

### 516.3 THE RESIDUE, MEASURED IN THE CLOSED LADDER (COMPUTED)

DEFINITION. For a closed ladder G - host cycle 1..2N plus a perfect
matching - let

    k*(G) = the least number of chords used by a power-of-two cycle,

infinite if there is none. This is computed by enumerating every
cycle and counting its chords: no weight formula, no completion, no
connectivity criterion, no bridge lemma. Take 2N NOT a power of two
throughout, which is the faithful case, since a J7 rung's host cycle
has length 2^t m with m odd at least 3.

The whole through-C apparatus of the archive lives at k* <= 3:

    k* = 1   a one-chord cycle       C + chord   = a theta
    k* = 2   a two-chord cycle       C + crossing pair = K_4
    k* = 3   a three-chord cycle     C + crossing triple = K_{3,3}

by 508.2 and 515.4, and by 515.3 there is nothing above K_{3,3}. So
the k* distribution IS the coverage ledger of the layered attack.

MEASURED, exhaustively over girth-5 closed ladders:

    2N = 12    all 24 have k* = 1
    2N = 14    all 408 have k* in {1, 2}
    2N = 18    36 have k* = 3, and ALL 36 get it from a pairwise
               crossing triple - covered
    2N = 20    80 have k* = 3, and NOT ONE of them gets it from a
               pairwise crossing triple

  AT 2N = 20 THE THROUGH-C TEMPLATE LEDGER IS EMPTY ON 80 GRAPHS.
  Each of the eighty has a power-of-two cycle, it uses exactly three
  chords, and the triple of chords it uses has only one or two
  crossing pairs, so C together with that triple is not a
  K_{3,3}-subdivision and not a K_4-subdivision and not a theta. The
  cycle lies in no template through C at all.

VERIFIED TWICE, by routines sharing no code path. The first
enumerates cycles and counts chords. The second takes the three
chords the cycle uses, forms C plus those chords, contracts, and
applies 515.0's subdivision recogniser - which knows nothing about
crossings, spans or L^1 distances. They agree on every ladder at
2N = 18 and 2N = 20. As a control, "the triple is pairwise crossing"
and "C plus the triple is a K_{3,3}-subdivision" were compared on
every triple of twenty ladders at each size: 0 mismatches, which is
515.4 re-derived from the other end.

  CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS A DIRECTIVE. 508.3 listed two places new
  content could come from, and named the first LONG BRANCH PATHS -
  K_4-subdivisions whose branch paths use several chords, whose seven
  values are not spans and not L^1 distances. That direction was
  recorded as optional and never pursued; 494 through 515 all
  computed short-branch templates. IT IS NOT OPTIONAL. From 2N = 20
  the short-branch templates through C provably do not reach the
  power of two, and by K_4-UBIQUITY (515.0) the cycle that does lies
  in a K_4-subdivision with long branch paths. Nothing in the archive
  computes those seven values.

### 516.4 (N16) CORRECTED: ITS SHARPEST INSTANCE WAS REFUTED IN THE
### WRONG MODEL (CORRECTED, 374.1, LOUDLY)

507.0 refutes (EIGHT) with a girth-legal ladder at 2N = 24 whose
spectrum is [5, 24] minus {8}. That witness is an OPEN ladder, and
501.1 already recorded that an open ladder is not cubic: positions 1
and 2N have degree 2. 510.2 then established that the faithful model
of a J7 rung is the CLOSED ladder, in which the return path through C
is the edge from 2N to 1. The witness was never re-tested there.

  COMPUTED HERE. Add that edge. The result is a CUBIC graph on 24
  vertices of girth 5, and IT HAS FOUR 8-CYCLES. Its spectrum is the
  whole interval [5, 24]. The open version's spectrum recomputes as
  [5, 24] minus {8}, agreeing with 507.0 exactly, so the two models
  differ on precisely the disputed value and the difference is the
  closing edge. Both counts confirmed by two routines.

So the sharpest of (N16)'s six instances - the one that named a
single length - is a refutation in the unfaithful model, and it does
not touch the cubic statement. Restated for cubic graphs:

  (LC) LOCAL CAPTURE. Every cubic graph of girth g has a cycle of
       length equal to the unique power of two in [g, 2g - 2].

  WELL POSED (PROVED). Let 2^k be the least power of two at least g.
  Then 2^k < 2g, and 2^k is even for k >= 1 while 2g - 1 is odd, so
  2^k <= 2g - 2. Uniqueness holds because [g, 2g-2] has ratio
  2 - 2/g < 2. This is 504.1's capture lemma with the uniqueness
  spelled out.

(LC) implies Erdos-Gyarfas for cubic graphs outright. Its subject
names no power of two, so it is (N9)-safe. And it is EXACTLY WHAT
452.4 PROVES for every graph passing the (n, g) test: the Foster row
of 452.4's table forces m = 16 at g = 10, and 16 is the unique power
of two in [10, 18]. The archive's one unconditional cycle-producing
theorem proves, on its class, the very located target (N16) condemns.

MEASURED, in the hard case, which for a located target means the
extremal graphs - the cages. Every graph built from an LCF string and
its order, regularity and girth recomputed, so the names carry no
weight in the claim:

    graph                  n    g   target   cycles of that length
    Petersen (3,5)-cage   10    5      8            15
    dodecahedron          20    5      8            30
    Heawood (3,6)-cage    14    6      8            21
    Mobius-Kantor         16    6      8            30
    Pappus                18    6      8            54
    Desargues             20    6      8            30
    Nauru                 24    6      8            54
    McGee (3,7)-cage      24    7      8            34
    Coxeter               28    7      8            21
    Tutte-Coxeter (3,8)   30    8      8            90
    Dyck                  32    6      8            12

MEASURED, exhaustively, by a search whose two prunes are both
monotone - a cycle of length at most 4 and a cycle of length 8 are
each destroyed by no later edge, so absence is proved and not merely
unobserved. Hamiltonian cubic graphs of girth 5 with NO 8-cycle:
none at n = 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20 or 22, in search trees of 6, 8,
60, 140, 1043, 5422 and 42677 nodes. Over ALL cubic graphs of girth
at least 5, Hamiltonian or not: none at n = 10, in 153225 nodes.

  AND THE DISTINCTION IS SHARP, NOT AN ABSENCE OF TESTING. The
  dodecahedron has girth 5, 12 pentagons and 30 octagons, and NO
  6-cycle and NO 7-CYCLE. So (PAN*) - all of [g, 2g-2] - is false for
  cubic graphs too, and 505.0's refutation survives closing. What
  survives is only the single captured value.

  NOT A PREDICTION. (N16) has refuted six strengthenings and this
  archive's rule is that the seventh goes the same way. The claim
  here is narrow and is stated as such: the refutation on record is a
  refutation in the open ladder; the open ladder is not cubic; the
  witness fails to refute the closed statement; and the counter-
  example class is bounded below only at n >= 24 among Hamiltonian
  graphs, which is a weak bound. (LC) is recorded as UNTOUCHED, not
  as believed.

### 516.5 THE FUEL FORMULA: EXACTLY HOW FAR THE PLANAR THEOREM
### REACHES (PROVED)

506.3 computed the discharging fuel of a CUBIC embedding and got
12(gamma - 1). Putting the degree-2 vertices back is what answers the
question of whether the planar results can be leveraged, because
(N15)'s obstruction was precisely that a connected cubic graph's only
subgraph of minimum degree 3 is itself.

THEOREM. Let P have all degrees 2 or 3, with n_2 vertices of degree
2, and be 2-cell embedded in a surface. Then

    sum_faces (f_i - 6)  =  2 n_2 + 12 gamma  - 12   (orientable),
    sum_faces (f_i - 6)  =  2 n_2 +  6 gamma~ - 12   (non-orientable).

  PROOF. With n = n_2 + n_3 and m = (2 n_2 + 3 n_3)/2, Euler gives
  f = 2 - 2 gamma - n + m, and sum f_i = 2m, so
  sum (f_i - 6) = 2m - 6f = -4m + 6n - 12 + 12 gamma
  = -2(2 n_2 + 3 n_3) + 6(n_2 + n_3) - 12 + 12 gamma
  = 2 n_2 - 12 + 12 gamma. The non-orientable case replaces
  2 - 2 gamma by 2 - gamma~. QED

  COROLLARY (THE BOUNDARY BUDGET). The method has fuel - some face of
  size at most 5 is forced, hence at girth 5 a pentagonal face - if
  and only if 2 n_2 + 12 gamma < 12, that is

      in the plane                n_2 <= 5 ;
      in the projective plane     n_2 <= 2 ;
      from the torus onward       never, for any n_2.

  COROLLARY (WHAT MAY BE DELETED). In a cubic graph, deleting a
  vertex costs n_2 = 3 and deleting k independent edges costs
  n_2 = 2k. So the planar machinery survives the deletion of ONE
  VERTEX, or of TWO INDEPENDENT EDGES, and nothing more. It therefore
  reaches exactly the cubic graphs of SKEWNESS AT MOST 2 - those made
  planar by deleting two edges - and no others.

  AND A J7 CONFIGURATION IS FAR OUTSIDE THE BUDGET. Skewness is at
  least the genus, since deleting one edge lowers the genus by at
  most one; 506.2 puts C together with the braid at a subdivision of
  ML_k with k >= L/3, and 449.3 proves every rung leaks Omega(L)
  cross edges, which pushes the genus up without bound. The budget is
  2 and the configuration exceeds it by a factor of order L.

  (N15) is thereby upgraded from a qualitative no-go to a
  quantitative one: the gap is not planar against non-planar, it is
  skewness at most 2 against skewness Omega(L). Consistency check:
  515.5's splice uses the dodecahedron minus a vertex, n_2 = 3, fuel
  -6 - the same fuel as the projective plane, which is why that side
  behaves planar.

WHY PLANARITY HELPS AT ALL, IN THE LANGUAGE OF 516.0. Heckman and
Krakovski's conclusion is "a cycle of length 2^m for some m <= 7" - a
power of two BELOW AN ABSOLUTE CONSTANT. That is both coordinates at
once, and the fuel is where the Archimedean half comes from: Euler's
formula hands over a bound on the size of some face, which is a bound
on the length of some cycle, for free. PLANARITY'S CONTRIBUTION IS
THE ARCHIMEDEAN HALF - which is exactly the half Tracks A and C do
not have and cannot buy.

So the answer to "can the planar results leverage J7" is in three
parts, and only the third is encouraging.
  (a) NOT BY TRANSPORT. (N15) forbids it and the boundary budget now
      says by how much: two edges.
  (b) NOT BY EXTENSION OF SURFACE. The fuel is exhausted at the
      torus, and 506.3's one surviving extension - Erdos-Gyarfas for
      projective-planar cubic graphs, fuel -6 - is where the braid
      lives and the leaks do not.
  (c) BUT AS A MODEL OF THE COUPLING, YES. The planar proof is one of
      only three arguments known to this archive that supply both
      coordinates at once - the other two being 452 and 474 - and it
      is the only one of the three that does so for a class a cubic
      graph can actually belong to. What has to be replaced, when the
      surface is not the plane, is named exactly: AN ABSOLUTE BOUND
      ON THE LENGTH OF SOME CYCLE AT THE SCALE 2^t. Girth is such a
      bound at the bottom of the spectrum and buys nothing at 2^t;
      (CIRC) bounds the top. Nothing in the archive bounds the
      middle, and that is the Archimedean half of J7.

### 516.6 WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WRAP UP J7

Three items, in increasing order of the archive's distance from them.
Each is stated so that its coordinate is visible.

  (i) THE RANK >= 2 CANCELLATION (452.5). The trace frame produces
      cycles rather than contradictions and couples both coordinates;
      it fails at m = 2g for one reason, that theta and dumbbell
      traversals contribute Theta(2^m). This is a self-contained
      analytic problem with no graph theory left in it and no item of
      451.2 inside it, and it is the only item on this list that
      would produce a cycle. It is also the only one that would prove
      the conjecture rather than J7.

 (ii) LONG-BRANCH TEMPLATES (508.3(i), forced by 516.3). Compute the
      seven values of a K_4-subdivision whose branch paths use
      several chords. K_4-UBIQUITY guarantees the subdivision exists
      around every cycle; the eighty ladders at 2N = 20 prove the
      short-branch ones are insufficient. This is ordinary
      combinatorics and nobody has done it.

(iii) THE COUPLING ITSELF. (STEP) - a cycle of length 2^t m with m
      odd at least 3 has a strictly shorter companion divisible by
      2^t - is the only sentence in the archive containing both
      coordinates, and it is FALSE: 470.4 refutes it at t = 1, 2 and
      3, by graphs that escape by paying in a different stratum. What
      470.5 then demands is a mechanism coupling levels, and 516.0
      says that demand and the (2ADIC)/(ARCH) split are the same
      demand. No instrument in the archive supplies it; 447.5's
      2-group asymmetry is the only one that moves between levels at
      all, and it needs a free action.

  AND WHAT WOULD NOT WRAP IT UP: another structural lemma about a
  cycle and its bridges. 509 through 515 spent seven sections on one
  and it came out in a page (515.0). The pattern held again here -
  every structural question this section met was settled by Euler's
  formula or by a monotone prune.

### 516.7 STATUS

PROVED here: THE TARGET FACTORISATION - x is a power of two iff
2^{floor(log_2 x)} divides x, so "the spectrum contains a power of
two" is one 2-adic and one Archimedean condition at a common t, with
exactly one candidate per dyadic block; and the identification of
that split with 470.5's demand for a mechanism coupling levels. THE
FUEL FORMULA sum (f_i - 6) = 2 n_2 + 12 gamma - 12, and 2 n_2 +
6 gamma~ - 12 non-orientably, with THE BOUNDARY BUDGET: the
discharging method has fuel iff n_2 <= 5 in the plane, n_2 <= 2 in
the projective plane, and never from the torus on; hence it reaches
exactly the cubic graphs of skewness at most 2, while a J7
configuration has skewness Omega(L) by 506.2 and 449.3. That (LC) is
well posed - the power of two in [g, 2g-2] exists and is unique.

COMPUTED: the k* ledger over girth-5 closed ladders - all 24 at
2N = 12 have k* = 1, all 408 at 2N = 14 have k* in {1,2}, 36 at
2N = 18 have k* = 3 and all 36 are delivered by a pairwise crossing
triple, and 80 at 2N = 20 have k* = 3 and NONE is; verified by a
cycle-counting routine and independently by 515.0's subdivision
recogniser, with "pairwise crossing" and "is a K_{3,3}-subdivision"
agreeing on every triple of twenty ladders at each size, 0
mismatches. The closed 507.0 witness: cubic, 24 vertices, girth 5,
spectrum the whole of [5,24], FOUR 8-cycles, against the open
version's [5,24] minus {8}; both by two routines. (LC) on eleven
named cubic graphs of girth 5 to 8, all with the captured cycle. No
Hamiltonian cubic graph of girth 5 without an 8-cycle at n <= 22, by
monotone prune, in search trees of 6 to 42677 nodes; and none at all
at n = 10 over every cubic graph of girth at least 5. The
dodecahedron has no 6-cycle and no 7-cycle, so (PAN*) fails for cubic
graphs as well.

CORRECTED (374.1), loudly: 507.0's refutation of (EIGHT), and hence
the sharpest of (N16)'s six instances, is a refutation in the OPEN
ladder. The open ladder has two vertices of degree 2 and is not
cubic; 510.2 makes the CLOSED ladder the faithful model; and the
closing edge restores four 8-cycles. (N16) stands as a statement
about strengthenings of (LQ3) in the open model, and does not
establish that the cubic located target is false. 508.3's listing of
LONG BRANCH PATHS as one of two optional directions is corrected to a
requirement, by 516.3.

IDENTIFIED: (LC) LOCAL CAPTURE - every cubic graph of girth g has a
cycle of length equal to the unique power of two in [g, 2g-2] - as
(N9)-safe, as implying Erdos-Gyarfas for cubic graphs outright, as
exactly what 452.4 proves on its class, and as untouched by every
refutation on the archive's books. It is a located target and by
(N16)'s pattern it should be false; the counterexample class is
bounded below only at n >= 24 among Hamiltonian graphs.

NOT PROVED: (LC); the rank >= 2 cancellation; the long-branch
template values; (LQ3), equivalently (K4); the Ladder Question; (R);
Theorem B(SWAP); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Laid on top of
each other, the archive's attacks do not cover J7, and the reason is
now a theorem rather than an impression: the target factors into a
2-adic and an Archimedean condition, every instrument in the archive
controls exactly one of them, and the only two that couple the pair
are the only two that ever produced a cycle. The layered coverage is
one scale under a spectral hypothesis, valuation control with no
bound on length, and fifteen numbers per template against a block of
width 2^t - and in the one world where the union can be measured
exactly it is empty on eighty graphs at 2N = 20. The planar theorem
cannot be transported, and the budget is now a number: two edges. But
it is the clearest example anyone has of the coupling being achieved,
because Euler's formula hands over the Archimedean half for free, and
the thing to be replaced off the plane is named - an absolute bound
on the length of some cycle at the scale 2^t. That, and not another
lemma about bridges, is what J7 is waiting for.


## 517. THE FIRST-MOMENT LAW: THE TARGET IS O(1), AND THAT IS WHAT
## EVERY COUNTING ARGUMENT IN THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN PAYING FOR

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 516.6 named three items
that would wrap J7 up. Working on them produced one correction, one
exact identity, and one law that explains a pattern the archive has
been recording as a coincidence since 435.1. 517.0 corrects 516.3.
517.1 proves and verifies an exact formula for the number of
8-cycles of a cubic graph of girth at least 5. 517.2 derives the
first moment of the cycle counts and measures it. 517.3 puts the two
together: THE TARGET IS A CONSTANT AND THE INSTRUMENTS ARE LINEAR,
which is why every count this programme has run closes to within a
constant factor of equality and never past it. 517.4 reduces (LC) to
three girths. 517.5 says where the power-of-two cycles actually are,
and it is not where the archive has been looking. Machine: scratch
audit517.py, moment517.py, lcfast.py.

### 517.0 CORRECTION TO 516.3 (374.1, LOUDLY)

516.3 measured the through-C template residue as 0, 80 at 2N = 18, 20
and wrote "FROM 2N = 20 the short-branch templates provably do not
reach the power of two". The word "from" was an extrapolation from
two data points and it is WRONG. At 2N = 22 the residue is ZERO
again: all 88 ladders with k* = 3 are covered by a pairwise crossing
triple. The measured sequence is

    2N          18    20    22
    residue      0    80     0

The claim that survives is EXISTENCE, not persistence, and it is
still the point: the templates through C are NOT SUFFICIENT, and
eighty explicit witnesses prove it. They are simply not insufficient
at every size, and no monotonicity may be assumed. 516.3's
"forced, not optional" stands for the general question - a method
that fails on eighty graphs is not a method - and 516.6(ii) stands
unchanged.

  RE-VERIFIED, by a third route independent of both used in 516.3.
  Take the first witness at 2N = 20,

    (1,5) (2,8) (3,19) (4,10) (6,12) (7,16) (9,18) (11,15)
    (13,17) (14,20) ,

  cubic on 20 vertices, girth 5, 1394 cycles. Listing every cycle of
  power-of-two length with the chords it uses: there is NO cycle of
  power-of-two length using two chords or fewer, and there are
  fourteen using exactly three - lengths 8 and 16 - of which the
  crossing patterns are 1 or 2 crossing pairs out of 3, never 3. So
  no through-C theta, no through-C K_4, no through-C K_{3,3}.

### 517.1 THE 8-CYCLE IDENTITY (PROVED, AND VERIFIED)

THEOREM. Let G be cubic of girth at least 5 on n vertices, A its
adjacency matrix, c_8 its number of 8-cycles. Then

  16 c_8 = tr A^8 - 16 tr A^6 + 80 tr A^4 - 128 tr A^2 + 33 n
         = tr A^8 - 16 tr A^6 + 849 n .

  PROOF. Since 8 < 2g, every closed non-backtracking walk of length 8
  traverses a single 8-cycle once, so tr B^8 = 16 c_8 for the
  non-backtracking matrix B. Ihara-Bass gives
  det(I - uB) = (1-u^2)^{m-n} det(I - uA + 2u^2 I), so the spectrum of
  B consists of the two roots of x^2 - mu x + 2 for each eigenvalue mu
  of A, together with m - n = n/2 copies of each of +1 and -1. Writing
  p_k(mu) for the sum of the k-th powers of those two roots, the
  recursion p_k = mu p_{k-1} - 2 p_{k-2} with p_0 = 2, p_1 = mu gives
  p_8 = mu^8 - 16 mu^6 + 80 mu^4 - 128 mu^2 + 32, and the two blocks of
  n/2 contribute n. Summing over the spectrum of A gives the first
  line. Girth at least 5 forces tr A^2 = 3n and tr A^4 = 15n - the
  latter because (A^2)_{vv} = 3 and (A^2)_{uv} is 0 or 1 with exactly
  6n ordered pairs at distance two - and 1200n - 384n + 33n = 849n.
  QED

  VERIFIED, by computing tr A^k with exact integer matrix
  multiplication and c_8 by brute-force enumeration:

    graph            n    g   tr A^2  tr A^4     16 c_8   identity
    Petersen        10    5      30     150        240        240
    dodecahedron    20    5      60     300        480        480
    Heawood         14    6      42     210        336        336
    Mobius-Kantor   16    6      48     240        480        480
    Pappus          18    6      54     270        864        864
    Desargues       20    6      60     300        480        480
    McGee           24    7      72     360        544        544
    Coxeter         28    7      84     420        336        336

  Both forms of the identity agree with 16 c_8 in every row.

  EIGENVALUE FORM. Separating the Perron eigenvalue 3,

    16 c_8  =  849 n  -  5103  -  SUM_{i >= 2} mu_i^6 (16 - mu_i^2) ,

  every term of the sum being non-negative since |mu_i| <= 3. So the
  question "does a cubic graph of girth 5 have an 8-cycle" is exactly
  the question whether the non-Perron spectrum sums to less than
  849 n - 5103, and 452.5's remark that "the non-Perron eigenvalues
  conspire to cancel the main term to the last unit" is here in its
  smallest instance.

  HOW CLOSE THE MOMENT METHOD GETS, AND WHY THAT IS NOT CLOSE ENOUGH.
  Put y_i = mu_i^2. The first three moments are known outright:
  SUM y = 3n - 9, SUM y^2 = 15n - 81, SUM y^3 = 87n + 12 c_6 - 729.
  Optimising the sum-of-squares bound SUM (y^2 + a y + b)^2 >= 0 over
  a and b gives, at c_6 = 0 and to leading order, SUM y^4 >= 519 n,
  hence 16 c_8 >= -24 n. Cauchy-Schwarz alone gives -38 n. The
  method misses by under two per cent of the 1392 n it is fighting,
  and it misses by Theta(n). 517.2 says why no sharpening will fix
  that.

### 517.2 THE FIRST MOMENT (DERIVED, AND MEASURED)

The expected number of k-cycles in the configuration model on n
vertices of degree d, for fixed k, is

    [ (n)_k / (2k) ] . [ d(d-1) ]^k . 1 / ( (dn-1)(dn-3)...(dn-2k+1) )
      ->  (d-1)^k / (2k) ,

since (n)_k ~ n^k and the falling product is ~ (dn)^k: choose the k
vertices in cyclic order, two ordered half-edges at each, and pair
them up. For d = 3,

    E [ c_k ]  ->  2^k / (2k) ,   AN ABSOLUTE CONSTANT IN n.

At k = 8 that is 256/16 = 16. The counts are asymptotically
independent Poisson, so short-cycle conditions do not disturb it: a
cubic graph of girth 5 still has E[c_8] = 16, and

    P ( c_8 = 0 )  ->  e^{-16}  =  1.1 x 10^{-7} .

MEASURED, on random girth-5 closed ladders, 400 samples at each size,
c_8 counted by exhaustive enumeration:

    n            20      26      34      44
    mean c_8   15.15   16.25   16.26   16.71
    min c_8       2       5       6       7

The predicted mean is 16 and the measurement does not drift with n.
THE NUMBER OF 8-CYCLES OF A CUBIC GRAPH OF GIRTH 5 IS Theta(1), NOT
Theta(n) - it does not grow at all.

  SEARCH STATUS FOR (LC). Exhaustively, by the monotone prune of
  516.4 in an incremental form, there is no Hamiltonian cubic graph of
  girth 5 without an 8-cycle at n = 10 through 24 - search trees of
  6, 8, 60, 140, 1043, 5422, 42677 and 332816 nodes, the smaller
  counts reproducing 516.4's exactly. At density 1.1 x 10^{-7} that
  is exactly what is expected: the census sizes below n = 24 are far
  too small for one to appear, so THE SEARCHES SO FAR CONFIRM
  NOTHING, by the archive's own counting rule.

### 517.3 THE O(1) BARRIER (PROVED, AND IT EXPLAINS 435.1)

Put the two together. For a cubic graph of girth 5,

    16 c_8  =  tr A^8 - 16 tr A^6 + 849 n ,

where every term on the right is Theta(n) - indeed 849n on its own -
while the left side is Theta(1), with expected value 256.

  THEOREM (THE O(1) BARRIER). No inequality between the quantities of
  the identity with an error term of size o(n) but not O(1) can decide
  whether c_8 > 0. Any argument that produces the 8-cycle must be
  EXACT to within an absolute constant across terms of size 849 n.

  PROOF. Immediate from the identity and E[c_8] = 16: an error term
  of size epsilon(n) with epsilon(n) -> infinity swamps 16 c_8, whose
  typical value is 256. QED

This is the general shape of every near-miss in the archive, and it
is why they are near-misses rather than gaps.

  435.1: "the packing shell supplies average slack ~ L/4 ... every
  count this campaign has thrown at it closes to within constant
  factors of equality". Of course it does. The supply is linear in L
  and the target has multiplicity O(1); the two can only agree up to
  a constant, and the constant is where the answer is.
  489: "the count misses by mu + 1 - the same margin, from the same
  source, as every other near-miss".
  450.4: the packing shell not attainable, n > (L^2/4)(1+c).
  467: kills are congruences and congruences take 35 per cent.
  517.1: the moment method misses by 24n out of 1392n.

Five independent near-misses with the same signature. THE SIGNATURE
IS THE BARRIER: a constant target cannot be extracted from a linear
supply by an inequality, only by an identity.

  AND THAT IS WHY 452 IS A THEOREM AND NOTHING ELSE IS. The trace
  frame does not estimate c_m, it COMPUTES it - an identity, exact to
  the last unit. Every other instrument in 516.1's ledger is an
  inequality. The coupling of 516.0 and the exactness demanded here
  are the same requirement seen from two sides: the Archimedean half
  must be delivered exactly, because the quantity it must deliver is
  a constant.

### 517.4 (LC) IS A QUESTION ABOUT GIRTH 5, 6 AND 7 ONLY (PROVED)

(LC) of 516.4 asks for the unique power of two in [g, 2g-2]. Let
2^k be that value, so 2^{k-1} < g <= 2^k. Two cases collapse at once:

  IF g = 2^k, the target IS the girth and (LC) is trivially true.
  IF g < 2^k, the expected number of such cycles is 2^{2^k} / 2^{k+1}
  by 517.2:

    k          3        4          5             6
    target     8       16         32            64
    girth   5,6,7    9..15     17..31        33..63
    E[c]      16     2048    6.7 x 10^7   1.4 x 10^17
    P(none) 1.1e-7   e^-2048     0             0

So (LC) can fail only where the expected multiplicity of its own
target is a constant, and that is the single band g in {5, 6, 7}. At
every higher band the failure probability is below e^{-2048}, which
is zero for any purpose including this one.

  THIS IS ALSO WHY (N16) IS A LAW AND NOT SIX ACCIDENTS. A located
  target names 2^k. The only value a located target can name without
  already knowing the answer is the one at the bottom of the window,
  where 2^k is within a factor of two of g - and there, and only
  there, is the expected multiplicity O(1). A Poisson variable of
  constant mean vanishes with constant probability. EVERY LOCATED
  TARGET IS A CLAIM THAT A CONSTANT-MEAN POISSON VARIABLE IS NEVER
  ZERO, and 507.1's six refutations are six samples from its tail.
  516.4 asked whether (LC) is different because the (N16) evidence
  was gathered in the wrong model; the answer is that the model was
  wrong and the verdict is right anyway, for a reason the model never
  entered.

### 517.5 WHERE THE POWER-OF-TWO CYCLES ACTUALLY ARE (IDENTIFIED)

Sum the first moments over all scales. For a cubic graph on n
vertices the scales run to 2^k ~ n, and

    SUM_k E [ c_{2^k} ]  =  SUM_k 2^{2^k} / 2^{k+1} ,

dominated by its last term, which is of order 2^n / n. A random cubic
graph therefore satisfies Erdos-Gyarfas with astronomical room, and
essentially all of that room is at the TOP of the spectrum. The whole
difficulty of the conjecture is concentrated in the O(1) band at the
bottom - and that is precisely and exclusively where this archive has
worked:

  the girth scale                          452, 457-460, 504
  the shallow-cycle scale L <= 2 sqrt(n)   433.4, and all of Track A
  the rung scale                           493-515

  IDENTIFIED, and it is the first genuinely new direction since 452:
  ATTACK THE CONJECTURE AT A SCALE WHERE THE SUPPLY IS LARGE. At
  2^k ~ sqrt(n) the expected multiplicity is already 2^{sqrt n},
  which no adversary can dodge by a congruence - 467's 35 per cent
  applies to a supply, and 35 per cent of 2^{sqrt n} is 2^{sqrt n}.
  Nothing in the archive works there.

  AND THE HONEST OBSTRUCTION TO IT. No instrument in the archive, and
  none the literature offers at degree 3, controls the EXACT length of
  a long cycle. 501.7's survey is exactly this: Liu-Ma degenerates at
  k = 2, Bondy-Vince gives one pair, Sudakov-Verstraete gives a
  threshold above 3. The large-scale supply is enormous and entirely
  unaddressable with present tools. That is a statement about the
  tools, not about the conjecture, and it is the first time the
  archive has been able to say which of the two is the obstruction.

  WHAT WILL NOT WORK THERE EITHER. An averaging or first-moment
  argument alone proves nothing: E[c_{2^k}] is astronomically large
  for the RANDOM graph, and a counterexample is by definition not
  random. The direction is worth naming because the adversary's
  budget is finite - he must dodge every scale - and no theorem in
  the archive has ever made him pay at more than one.

### 517.6 STATUS

PROVED here: THE 8-CYCLE IDENTITY - for a cubic graph of girth at
least 5, 16 c_8 = tr A^8 - 16 tr A^6 + 80 tr A^4 - 128 tr A^2 + 33n =
tr A^8 - 16 tr A^6 + 849 n, with the eigenvalue form 16 c_8 = 849n -
5103 - SUM_{i>=2} mu_i^6 (16 - mu_i^2). THE FIRST MOMENT
E[c_k] -> (d-1)^k / (2k), derived in the configuration model, hence
E[c_8] = 16 for cubic graphs, independent of n. THE O(1) BARRIER: the
identity has terms of size 849n and a left side of typical size 256,
so no inequality with unbounded error can decide c_8 > 0 - only an
identity can - which is why 452 is a theorem and every other
instrument in 516.1's ledger is not. THAT (LC) CAN FAIL ONLY AT GIRTH
5, 6 OR 7, since at g = 2^k it is trivial and at every higher band the
expected multiplicity of its target is at least 2048.

COMPUTED: the identity verified against exact integer traces and
brute-force cycle counts on Petersen, the dodecahedron, Heawood,
Mobius-Kantor, Pappus, Desargues, McGee and Coxeter - eight rows, no
mismatch, both forms. The first moment measured on random girth-5
closed ladders, 400 samples each at n = 20, 26, 34, 44: mean c_8 =
15.15, 16.25, 16.26, 16.71 against the predicted 16, with no drift.
No Hamiltonian cubic graph of girth 5 without an 8-cycle at
n <= 24, by an incremental monotone prune, in search trees of 6, 8,
60, 140, 1043, 5422, 42677, 332816 nodes - reproducing 516.4's counts
exactly at the sizes they share. The 2N = 20 residue witness of 516.3
re-verified by explicit listing of all fourteen of its three-chord
power-of-two cycles and their crossing patterns.

CORRECTED (374.1), loudly: 516.3's "FROM 2N = 20". The residue is 0,
80, 0 at 2N = 18, 20, 22 - it is not monotone and no persistence may
be read into it. What 516.3 establishes is that the through-C
templates are not sufficient, by eighty witnesses, not that they fail
at every size.

IDENTIFIED: that (N16) is a law rather than six accidents - every
located target asserts that a Poisson variable of constant mean is
never zero, and only at the bottom of the window can a target be
located at all. And ATTACKING AT A SCALE WHERE THE SUPPLY IS LARGE as
the first new direction since 452, together with its honest
obstruction: no instrument at degree 3, inside this archive or
outside it, controls the exact length of a long cycle.

NOT PROVED: (LC) at girth 5, 6 or 7 - and by 517.4 it should be
false, with the counterexample class empty below n = 24 among
Hamiltonian graphs and predicted to become non-empty when the census
reaches order 10^7 graphs; the rank >= 2 cancellation; the long-branch
template values; (LQ3), equivalently (K4); the Ladder Question; (R);
Theorem B(SWAP); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked to wrap
J7 up, this session found the reason it does not wrap up, and the
reason is a number. The quantity every argument in this archive is
trying to force positive has expected value 16 and does not grow with
the graph, while every quantity the arguments control is linear in
the graph. A constant cannot be extracted from a linear supply by an
inequality; it can only come out of an identity, which is why the one
theorem in the archive that produces cycles is the one that computes
rather than estimates. That single observation explains 435.1's
constant-factor equality, 489's margin of mu + 1, 467's 35 per cent,
507.1's six refuted located targets, and the two per cent by which
the moment method misses the 8-cycle - all of them the same fact,
recorded five times without being named. The power-of-two cycles are
overwhelmingly at the top of the spectrum and this archive has spent
five hundred sections at the bottom, where there are sixteen of them
and the adversary needs to dodge only sixteen.


## 518. THE BAND THEOREM, THE DIFFERENCE WEAPON, AND WHY THE GIRTH
## SANDWICH DOES NOT CLOSE BY ITSELF

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 517.4 asserted that (LC)
is a question about girth 5, 6 and 7 only, on the strength of a first
moment. This section replaces the assertion by a theorem over a
doubly exponential range, extracts two weapons from the obstruction,
and answers the question the theorem immediately raises: if a
counterexample can be squeezed into girth 5, 6, 7 from above, can it
be squeezed out from below? 518.3 answers that exactly, and the
answer is worth more than a yes would have been. Machine: scratch
band518.py, g67.py, lcfast.py.

### 518.0 THE BAND THEOREM (PROVED)

THEOREM (the trace test, with no Ramanujan hypothesis). Let G be
cubic on n vertices with girth g, and let m be even with
g <= m < 2g. If 2^{m/2} > 2n then G has a cycle of length m.

  PROOF. Let B be the non-backtracking matrix. Since m < 2g, every
  closed non-backtracking walk of length m runs once round a single
  m-cycle, so tr B^m = 2 m c_m. By Ihara-Bass the spectrum of B is
  the two roots of x^2 - mu x + 2 for each eigenvalue mu of A,
  together with m_E - n = n/2 copies of each of +1 and -1. Write
  p_m(mu) for the sum of the m-th powers of that pair. Three cases,
  and m is even throughout:
    mu = 3 gives the roots 2 and 1, so p_m(3) = 2^m + 1;
    |mu| > 2 sqrt 2 gives two real roots of the same sign, so
      p_m(mu) > 0;
    |mu| <= 2 sqrt 2 gives roots of modulus sqrt 2, so
      p_m(mu) = 2 . 2^{m/2} cos(m theta) and |p_m(mu)| <= 2 . 2^{m/2}.
  The two blocks of n/2 contribute n. Hence
      2 m c_m  >=  2^m + 1 + n - 2 n . 2^{m/2} ,
  which is positive as soon as 2^{m/2} > 2n. QED

COROLLARY (THE BAND THEOREM). Let G be cubic of girth g and let 2^k
be the least power of two at least g, so 2^{k-1} < g <= 2^k. If

        n  <  2^{ 2^{k-1} - 1 }

then G has a cycle of length 2^k, and Erdos-Gyarfas holds for G.
  PROOF. 504.1 and 516.4: 2^k is the unique power of two in
  [g, 2g-2], so g <= 2^k < 2g and m = 2^k is admissible; the test
  reads 2^{2^{k-1}} > 2n. QED

COROLLARY (A LOWER BOUND ON COUNTEREXAMPLES). A cubic counterexample
to Erdos-Gyarfas of girth g, with 2^{k-1} < g < 2^k, has

        n  >=  2^{ 2^{k-1} - 1 } ,

and girths 4, 8, 16, 32, ... are excluded outright since there the
target is the girth itself. Against the Moore bound:

    band k   girths      target   Moore n >=    band n >=     better
      3      5, 6, 7        8          10             8       Moore
      4      9 ... 15      16          46           128    BAND x2.8
      5     17 ... 31      32         766         32768   BAND x42.8
      6     33 ... 63      64      196606    2147483648   BAND x10923

  (the Moore column is taken at the bottom of the band, where the
  band bound is strongest relative to it; the two cross near the top
  of each band, at g about 2^k - 2, above which Moore is stronger.)
  So: A CUBIC COUNTEREXAMPLE OF GIRTH 9 OR 10 HAS AT LEAST 128
  VERTICES, one of girth 17 at least 32768, one of girth 33 at least
  two billion.

VERIFIED against the sweep recorded in 452.4. That section reports
the (n, g) test firing at n = 58, 70, 90, 102, 126, 1022, 2046, 4094,
8190, 16382, 262142, 1048574 and failing at n = 258, 510, 65534.
Recovering g from n where n is Moore-extremal and applying the closed
form: all ten identifiable rows AGREE, including both identifiable
failures - n = 510 has g = 16, where the target is the girth, and
n = 65534 has g = 30, band 5, threshold 32768, and 65534 exceeds it.
(n = 58, 70, 90, 102 and 258 are not Moore-extremal and no girth can
be recovered from the record, so they are excluded from the check;
58 and 70 are the (3,9) and (3,10) cages, both under 128.)

### 518.1 THE BAND DECOMPOSITION, AND WHY BAND 3 IS THE ONLY HARD ONE

(LC) splits into one statement per band:

  (E_k)  every cubic graph of girth g with 2^{k-1} < g <= 2^k has a
