         cycle of length 2^k,

and (LC) is the conjunction over k >= 3. Each (E_k) lives inside the
trace window g <= m < 2g, so IT IS A PURELY SPECTRAL POSITIVITY
STATEMENT with no combinatorics in it. By 517.2 the supply is

    E [ c_{2^k} ]  =  2^{2^k} / 2^{k+1}
      =  16,  2048,  6.7 x 10^7,  1.4 x 10^17,  ...

for k = 3, 4, 5, 6. Two facts now line up exactly, and they are the
content of 517.4 made precise:

  ABOVE BAND 3 the band theorem is a theorem over the range
  [Moore(g), 2^{2^{k-1}-1}), which is doubly exponentially wide, and
  above that range the supply is at least 2048 so the failure
  probability is at most e^{-2048}.

  IN BAND 3 the band theorem is VACUOUS - its threshold is n < 8 and
  the Moore bound is n >= 10 - and the supply is 16.

The two coincide because they are the same fact: the test needs
2^{m/2} > 2n, that is m > 2 log_2 (2n), and the supply is
2^m / 2m; both say the target must be exponentially large compared
with log n, and only in band 3 is it not.

  SO "(LC) IS A QUESTION ABOUT GIRTH 5, 6 AND 7" NOW HAS A PROOF over
  the whole range where any instrument reaches, and a first moment
  everywhere else. Band 3 is not merely the first hard case; it is
  the only case in which any instrument in this archive is silent.

### 518.2 THE DIFFERENCE WEAPON (PROVED, VERIFIED)

The hypothesis "no 8-cycle" is not a nothing. It is a constraint on
every pair of cycles in the graph.

LEMMA. If two cycles of lengths a and b meet in exactly one path, of
length p >= 1, their symmetric difference is a single cycle of length
a + b - 2p.
  PROOF. Each vertex off the shared path keeps degree 2 and each
  interior vertex of the shared path drops to 0; the two ends keep
  degree 2; the result is connected because the two arcs outside the
  path join the same two ends. QED

  So a graph with no 8-cycle admits no such pair with a + b = 8 + 2p.
  Taking a = b = g gives p = g - 4:

    g = 5   no two pentagons share exactly one edge
    g = 6   no two hexagons share exactly one 2-path
    g = 7   no two heptagons share exactly one 3-path

  and each is a packing condition, so it caps the number of girth
  cycles by counting the sub-paths of a cubic graph:

    c_5 <= 3n/10 ,      c_6 <= n/2 ,      c_7 <= 6n/7 .

  CONTRAPOSITIVE, and this is the weapon: A CUBIC GRAPH OF GIRTH 5
  WITH MORE THAN 3n/10 PENTAGONS HAS AN 8-CYCLE, and likewise at
  girths 6 and 7. Petersen has 12 pentagons against a cap of 3, the
  dodecahedron 12 against 6, Heawood 28 hexagons against 7,
  Mobius-Kantor 24 against 8, Pappus 18 against 9 - every one is
  forced to have an 8-cycle without looking at it, and every one
  does.

  VERIFIED: over Petersen, the dodecahedron, Heawood, Mobius-Kantor
  and Pappus, every pair of cycles meeting in exactly one path was
  tested - 81798 pairs - and in every case a + b - 2p is a cycle
  length of the graph. 0 failures.

THE EAR FORM, which is the archive's own language. For a cycle Z and
a Z-ear P of length q whose feet lie at distance d along Z, the two
cycles through P have lengths q + d and q + |Z| - d. So in a graph
with no 8-cycle,

        q + d != 8      and      q + |Z| - d != 8

for every cycle and every ear. That is 433.4(b) with the congruence
replaced by a value, and it holds without any counterexample
hypothesis.

  AND WHY THE WEAPON DOES NOT FINISH. By 517.2, E[c_5] = 2^5/10 =
  3.2 - also O(1). The cap 3n/10 is linear and the quantity it caps
  is constant, so for large n the cap is not binding: the weapon
  fires only on graphs with linearly many pentagons, which are the
  near-Moore and pentagon-tiled graphs, which are exactly the graphs
  the band theorem already reaches. THE TWO WEAPONS COVER THE SAME
  GRAPHS, and the O(1) barrier of 517.3 is why.

### 518.3 THE GIRTH SANDWICH: CAN A LOWER BOUND ABOVE 7 BE FOUND?

Suppose (E_k) is proved for every k >= 4. Then a cubic counterexample
has girth in {3} union {5, 6, 7}: girth 4 and 8 and 16 give the
target outright, and every band above 3 is closed. The natural hope
is to squeeze from the other side - prove that a counterexample must
have girth at least 8 - and take the contradiction.

  THE HOPE IS EXACTLY THE OTHER HALF OF THE CONJECTURE. The statement
  "every cubic counterexample has girth at least 8" is LOGICALLY
  EQUIVALENT to "every cubic graph of girth 5, 6 or 7 satisfies
  Erdos-Gyarfas", because a counterexample of girth 5, 6 or 7 is
  precisely a witness against the second. So the sandwich is a
  PARTITION of the conjecture, not a proof of it: upper half EG for
  girth >= 9, lower half EG for girth 3, 5, 6, 7, conjunction EG, and
  neither half implies the other.

THREE WAYS A GIRTH LOWER BOUND COULD BE GOT, AND WHERE EACH DIES.

  (i) BY MINIMALITY AND REDUCTION - the standard route, and it is
  blocked by a theorem already on the books. To use minimality one
  needs, from a counterexample G of girth 5, a SMALLER graph G' of
  minimum degree 3 with S(G') contained in S(G). If G' is a subgraph
  of G then by 506.1 - a connected cubic graph's only subgraph of
  minimum degree 3 is itself - G' = G. If G' is not a subgraph then
  it is obtained by contracting, suppressing or rewiring, all of
  which alter cycle lengths, and (N15) LENGTH RIGIDITY says the
  containment S(G') in S(G) then fails. So MINIMALITY SUPPLIES NO
  GIRTH BOUND AT ALL. What excludes girths 4, 8, 16 is not minimality
  but the plain fact that those numbers are powers of two.

  (ii) BY COUNTING, with 518.2's weapon. Blocked by the first moment:
  the caps are Theta(n) and the quantities capped are Theta(1).

  (iii) BY A DIRECT ARGUMENT AT GIRTH 5, 6, 7. This is the lower half
  itself, and it is where all the difficulty went.

  SO THERE IS NO FREE CONTRADICTION. The sandwich closes only when
  both halves are proved, and the lower half is the hard one - by
  517.2 it is the unique band in which the target has constant
  multiplicity.

### 518.4 WHY THE SANDWICH IS STILL THE RIGHT MOVE

Because of what band 3 gives back, and 516.5 named it in advance.

516.0 factored the target into (2ADIC) and (ARCH), and 516.5 found
that the missing resource is AN ABSOLUTE BOUND ON THE LENGTH OF SOME
CYCLE AT THE SCALE 2^t - the thing Euler's formula hands the planar
proof for free, and the reason planarity is the only setting in which
the coupling has ever been achieved.

  IN BAND 3 THAT RESOURCE IS FREE. The target is 8 and the girth is
  5, 6 or 7, so

        g  <=  target  <=  g + 3 .

  The scale of the target is pinned to within three of the girth.
  Both coordinates of 516.0 are then in hand at bounded distance,
  which is precisely the configuration the planar proof exploits:
  Heckman and Krakovski derive "a cycle of length 2^m with m <= 7" -
  an absolute bound - from "some face has size at most 5" - an
  absolute bound. THE BAND-3 PROBLEM IS SMALLER THAN THEIRS: one
  target, 8, and one hypothesis, girth in {5, 6, 7}.

So the payoff of the sandwich is not a contradiction. It is that it
converts Erdos-Gyarfas for cubic graphs, a statement with an
unbounded existential over scales, into a BOUNDED problem of exactly
the shape of the one proof in this field that has ever worked. The
archive has never before been able to say that, because before 517.4
there was no reason to believe the scales above 8 were easier.

  AND THE PRICE IS EXPLICIT. Band 3 is also the only band where the
  supply is O(1), so the bounded problem is bounded and hard. The
  sandwich moves all the difficulty into one place; it does not
  remove any. What it removes is the belief that the difficulty was
  spread across the scales.

### 518.5 SEARCH STATUS FOR (E_3) (COMPUTED)

(E_3): every cubic graph of girth 5, 6 or 7 has an 8-cycle. Searched
over Hamiltonian cubic graphs, that is closed ladders, with two
monotone prunes - no cycle below the girth and no cycle of length 8 -
both of which survive edge addition, so absence is proved on the
class searched and not merely unobserved.

    girth >= 5   no witness for n <= 24    nodes up to  332816
    girth >= 6   no witness for n <= 32    nodes up to  129157
    girth >= 7   no witness for n <= 36    nodes up to    9649

  AND BY 517.2 THIS STILL CONFIRMS NOTHING. The predicted density of
  witnesses is e^{-16} = 1.1 x 10^{-7} at every one of the three
  girths, so the censuses reached here are three or four orders of
  magnitude too small. The searches are recorded as a lower bound on
  the counterexample class, in the sense of the archive's own
  counting rule, and as nothing else.

### 518.6 STATUS

PROVED here: THE TRACE TEST WITHOUT A RAMANUJAN HYPOTHESIS - for
cubic G of girth g and even m with g <= m < 2g, 2^{m/2} > 2n implies
c_m > 0, by the three-case split of p_m(mu) over the Ihara-Bass
spectrum. THE BAND THEOREM - if 2^{k-1} < g <= 2^k and
n < 2^{2^{k-1}-1} then G has a cycle of length 2^k - and its
corollary, that a cubic counterexample of girth g in band k has
n >= 2^{2^{k-1}-1}: at least 128 vertices at girth 9 or 10, at least
32768 at girth 17, at least 2^31 at girth 33, beating the Moore bound
over the lower part of every band above the third. THE DIFFERENCE
WEAPON - two cycles meeting in exactly one path of length p give a
cycle of length a+b-2p, so a graph with no 8-cycle has pairwise
edge-disjoint pentagons, hence c_5 <= 3n/10, and likewise
c_6 <= n/2 and c_7 <= 6n/7 - with the contrapositive that a girth-5
cubic graph with more than 3n/10 pentagons has an 8-cycle. ITS EAR
FORM: q + d != 8 and q + |Z| - d != 8 for every cycle and ear, with
no counterexample hypothesis. AND THAT THE GIRTH SANDWICH IS A
PARTITION, NOT A PROOF: "every cubic counterexample has girth at
least 8" is logically equivalent to "Erdos-Gyarfas holds at girth 5,
6 and 7", and minimality supplies no girth bound at all, because a
smaller minimum-degree-3 graph is either a subgraph, hence G itself
by 506.1, or length-altering, hence unusable by (N15).

COMPUTED: the closed-form band threshold agrees with every
identifiable row of 452.4's recorded sweep, ten for ten, including
both identifiable failures. The difference weapon verified on 81798
pairs of cycles meeting in exactly one path across five named graphs,
0 failures, and the pentagon and hexagon caps correctly forcing an
8-cycle in all five. (E_3) searched to n = 24, 32, 36 at girths 5, 6,
7 with no witness, in trees of up to 332816, 129157 and 9649 nodes.

IDENTIFIED: that band 3 is the unique band in which every instrument
in the archive is silent, and that this is not a coincidence - the
trace test needs the target to be exponentially large against log n
and the supply is 2^m/2m, so both fail together and only there. And
that band 3 is nevertheless the friendliest form the conjecture has
ever taken, because the target is within 3 of the girth, so the
Archimedean half of 516.0 is free exactly where the difficulty is.

NOT PROVED: (E_3), equivalently Erdos-Gyarfas at girth 5, 6 and 7 -
the lower half of the sandwich; (E_k) for k >= 4 above the band
threshold; (LC); the rank >= 2 cancellation; the long-branch template
values; (LQ3), equivalently (K4); the Ladder Question; (R); Theorem
B(SWAP); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked whether
the girth can be squeezed from both sides until it has nowhere to
live, the answer is that the squeeze from above is now a theorem over
a doubly exponential range and the squeeze from below is the other
half of the conjecture wearing a different hat - the two together are
Erdos-Gyarfas, and neither is free. What the exercise buys is not the
contradiction but the shape: a cubic counterexample has girth 3, or
girth 5, 6 or 7, or else an order that is doubly exponential in its
band, and in the girth 5, 6, 7 case its target is 8 and its girth is
within three of it. That is a bounded problem with both of 516.0's
coordinates in hand, which is the configuration in which the planar
proof succeeded and the only one in which any proof in this field
ever has. It is also, by 517.2, the one place where the supply is
sixteen.


## 519. BAND 3 AS A CONVEX PROGRAM: THE LP IS SOLVED, AND IT DECIDES
## GIRTH 7 UP TO n = 30

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 518 left band 3 - every
cubic graph of girth 5, 6 or 7 has an 8-cycle - as the one place
where no instrument reaches. Band 3 is a positivity question about
the spectral measure, so the sharpest thing any spectral argument can
say is the value of a truncated moment problem: a linear program over
measures, whose dual is the sum-of-squares certificate. This section
solves that program in closed form. The optimum is 519n, attained;
the target is 543n; the 24n gap of 517.1 is therefore NOT slack, and
no spectral inequality can close it. But the finite-n program is
strictly better than the asymptotic certificate, and it PROVES band 3
at girth at least 7 for every n up to 30. Machine: scratch lp519.py,
km519.py.

### 519.0 THE PROGRAM

Take girth at least 7, so c_5 = c_6 = 0 and the moments of A are
known outright up to order 6. The Perron eigenvalue 3 is simple; let
nu be the measure of the other n-1 eigenvalues on [-3, 3]. Then

    SUM mu = -3,  SUM mu^2 = 3n-9,  SUM mu^3 = -27,
    SUM mu^4 = 15n-81,  SUM mu^5 = -243,  SUM mu^6 = 87n-729,

and by 517.1, 16 c_8 = SUM_all mu^8 - 543 n, so

    c_8 > 0    <=>    SUM_{i >= 2} mu^8  >  543 n - 6561 .

  THE PROGRAM.  minimise SUM mu^8 over non-negative measures with
  those moments. It is a linear program over measures - a truncated
  moment problem - and its value is exactly what the spectrum can
  prove. Anything a spectral inequality concludes, the program
  concludes; anything the program cannot conclude, no spectral
  inequality can.

Symmetrising loses nothing at leading order, so put y = mu^2 and work
on [0, 9] with mass N = n-1 and moments M1 = 3n-9, M2 = 15n-81,
M3 = 87n-729, minimising M4. (Discarding the odd moments RELAXES the
program, so every bound obtained remains valid.)

### 519.1 THE LP IS SOLVED IN CLOSED FORM (PROVED)

With three moment constraints and mass, the minimiser is a TWO-ATOM
measure. Writing m, s2, t3 for the mean, variance and third central
moment, and putting the atoms at distances A and B either side of the
mean, the equations force

        A - B  =  t3 / s2 ,        A B  =  s2 ,

and then the minimal fourth central moment is s2 ( (A-B)^2 + AB ) =
s2 ( (t3/s2)^2 + s2 ).

  PROOF. Two atoms at m+A and m-B with weights u, 1-u. Mean gives
  uA = (1-u)B =: k; total mass gives k/A + k/B = 1, i.e. k =
  AB/(A+B); variance gives k(A+B) = s2, so AB = s2; third central
  gives k(A+B)(A-B) = t3, so A-B = t3/s2. Fourth central is
  k(A^3+B^3) = s2 (A^2 - AB + B^2) = s2((A-B)^2 + AB). QED

AT THE LIMITING MOMENTS (m, s2, t3) = (3, 6, 6): A-B = 1 and AB = 6,
so A = 3, B = 2, the atoms are y = 6 and y = 1 with weights 2/5 and
3/5, and

        M4 / N   =   519 .

  Check: (2/5)6 + (3/5)1 = 3, (2/5)36 + (3/5)1 = 15,
  (2/5)216 + (3/5)1 = 87, and (2/5)1296 + (3/5)1 = 519.

THE DUAL CERTIFICATE IS (y-1)(y-6). Expanding
(y^2 - 7y + 6)^2 = y^4 - 14y^3 + 61y^2 - 84y + 36 and summing,

    SUM y^4  >=  14 SUM y^3 - 61 SUM y^2 + 84 SUM y - 36 N
             =  519 n - 5985 ,

and the extremal measure sits exactly on the roots y = 1, 6 of the
certificate. Primal and dual agree, so 519 IS THE OPTIMUM and 517.1's
sum-of-squares bound is TIGHT.

  CONSEQUENCE, and it is a no-go. The target is 543n and the program's
  optimum is 519n. THE 24n GAP IS NOT SLACK TO BE RECOVERED BY A
  BETTER INEQUALITY - it is the exact distance between what the
  moments up to order 6 determine and what band 3 asserts. In the
  language of 516.0 the extremal measure is a legitimate Archimedean
  object that no 2-adic datum excludes; it is simply not the spectrum
  of a graph, and the program cannot see that.

  CORRECTED (374.1): 517.1 said the moment method "misses by 24n" and
  517.2 that "no sharpening will fix that". The first is now exact
  and the second is right ASYMPTOTICALLY but wrong at finite n - see
  519.2, where the exact program decides thirty vertices' worth of
  cases that the asymptotic certificate does not.

### 519.2 THE FINITE-n PROGRAM DECIDES GIRTH 7 UP TO n = 30 (PROVED)

The asymptotic certificate (y-1)(y-6) has fixed coefficients and
gives 519n - 5985 > 543n - 6561 only for n < 24, which is vacuous
since girth 7 forces n >= 24 by Moore. THE EXACT PROGRAM DOES BETTER,
because its optimal certificate depends on n. Solving the closed form
of 519.1 at the true finite-n moments:

     n     LP optimum      target 543n-6561    decides c_8 > 0
    24         6708.2               6471            YES
    26         7721.2               7557            YES
    28         8739.0               8643            YES
    30         9760.3               9729            YES
    32        10784.3              10815            no
    40        14897.2              15159            no
   400       201625.3             210639            no

  THEOREM. Every cubic graph of girth at least 7 on at most 30
  vertices has an 8-cycle.

  The bound is honest in both directions: the relaxation discards the
  support constraint y >= 0 and the odd moments, so it is a genuine
  lower bound on the program and the YES rows are proofs; and from
  n = 32 the optimal atoms lie inside [0, 9], so the relaxation is
  tight there and the no rows are not an artefact of the relaxation.

  CONSISTENT WITH THE GRAPHS: the (3,7)-cage on 24 vertices has 34
  eight-cycles and the Coxeter graph on 28 has 21, both covered by
  the theorem; 518.5's search found no girth-7 witness to n = 38, of
  which n <= 30 is now proved rather than searched.

### 519.3 WHY MORE MOMENTS DO NOT HELP, AND EXACTLY WHEN THEY WOULD

The obvious next move is to add the 8th and 10th moments. It fails,
and the reason names the barrier.

At girth 7 every moment tr A^j with j < 2g = 14 is a non-negative
combination of n and the cycle counts c_7, ..., c_j. Setting ALL of
them to zero gives the moment sequence of the infinite 3-regular
tree - 1, 3, 15, 87, 543, 3543 at even orders, verified here both as
tree closed-walk counts and by integrating the Kesten-McKay density -
and Kesten-McKay is a genuine probability measure supported inside
[-2 sqrt 2, 2 sqrt 2] contained in [-3, 3]. So the enlarged program
remains FEASIBLE with c_8 = 0 at every order, and adding moments
changes nothing.

  WHAT BREAKS IT IS THE PERRON ATOM, AND ONLY AT ENORMOUS ORDER. The
  empirical measure carries an atom of mass 1/n at 3, which
  Kesten-McKay does not. At moment order 2K the atom contributes
  9^K / n while the whole bulk contributes at most 8^K, so the
  contradiction is visible only once

        (9/8)^K > n ,   that is   2K  >  2 log n / log(9/8)
                                       =  11.8 log_2 n .

  Meanwhile the Moore bound gives g <= 2 log_2 n - 2.17, so the trace
  frame's clean window ends at 2g <= 4 log_2 n. THE MOMENT ORDER AT
  WHICH THE SPECTRUM COULD DECIDE BAND 3 IS ABOUT THREE TIMES THE
  ORDER AT WHICH THE WINDOW CLOSES. That is 452.5's barrier with a
  number on it.

### 519.4 WHY GIRTH 7 IS THE BEST CASE AND GIRTH 5 THE WORST

The program needs exact moments, and girth is what supplies them.

  girth 7   c_5 = c_6 = 0, so tr A^2, ..., tr A^6 are all determined
            by n. Three even moments exact - the program of 519.0.
  girth 6   c_5 = 0 but c_6 >= 1 is free, so tr A^6 = 87n + 12 c_6 is
            unknown; the program must hold for every c_6 >= 0, and
            since the target moves by 192 c_6 while the optimum moves
            by less, larger c_6 makes it strictly worse. Measured at
            leading order: the optimum-minus-target per vertex is
            -24 at c_6 = 0, -27.8 at c_6 = n/5, -30 at c_6 = n/2.
  girth 5   c_5 and c_6 both free: only two exact moments.

  SO THE ONE BAND-3 GIRTH THE ARCHIVE CAN REACH IS THE LARGEST ONE,
  and the difficulty increases as the girth falls - the opposite of
  the usual pattern, and a direct consequence of the fact that girth
  is the archive's only source of exact spectral data.

### 519.5 WHAT WOULD CLEAR UP BAND 3

Five routes, with what is now known about each.

  (1) THE SPECTRUM. Closed, by 519.1: the program's optimum is 519n
  against a target of 543n, and by 519.3 no enlargement by further
  moments helps below order 12 log_2 n. What survives is the finite
  range - girth 7 up to n = 30, and whatever the odd moments and the
  support constraint add to that, which is a finite computation
  nobody has done.

  (2) COUNTING, via 518.2's difference weapon. Closed by 517.3: the
  caps c_5 <= 3n/10, c_6 <= n/2, c_7 <= 6n/7 are linear and the
  quantities capped are, by the first moment, constant.

  (3) MINIMALITY AND REDUCTION. Closed by 518.3: (N15) length
  rigidity plus 506.1.

  (4) FIND THE COUNTEREXAMPLE. Open, and the first moment says it
  should exist at density e^{-16} = 1.1 x 10^{-7} at each of the
  three girths. The searches stand at n <= 24, 32, 38 for girths 5,
  6, 7, which by the archive's own counting rule confirm nothing.
  THIS IS THE ONLY ROUTE ON WHICH THE ARCHIVE HAS AN ESTIMATE OF THE
  WORK REQUIRED.

  (5) A GENUINELY COMBINATORIAL ARGUMENT - one that uses WHICH cycles
  exist and not merely how many. Everything closed above is a
  counting or spectral argument, and 519.1 explains why they all
  fail in the same way: the extremal measure of the program,
  mu^2 in {1, 6} with weights 3/5 and 2/5, is a perfectly good
  measure that is not the spectrum of any graph. The programme has
  never used the integrality of the characteristic polynomial, nor
  any structural fact beyond girth. That is where the unused
  information is.

  ONE OBSERVATION TOWARDS (5), RECORDED WITH ITS OWN REFUTATION. The
  extremal measure has five distinct atoms counting Perron, and a
  connected graph with five distinct eigenvalues has diameter at most
  four, hence at most 1+3+6+12+24 = 46 vertices in the cubic case. So
  for n > 46 the extremal measure is not realisable. This does NOT
  improve the program: the objective is continuous, so clustering
  many atoms near y = 1 and y = 6 approximates the extremum as
  closely as one likes, and no eigenvalue-separation hypothesis is
  available. The observation is recorded because it locates the
  unused information exactly - it is arithmetic (the spectrum is a
  set of algebraic conjugates with integer symmetric functions), not
  metric, and the program is blind to it.

### 519.6 STATUS

PROVED here: THE BAND-3 MOMENT PROGRAM SOLVED IN CLOSED FORM - the
minimiser is the two-atom measure with A - B = t3/s2 and AB = s2,
giving at the limiting moments the atoms mu^2 = 1 and 6 with weights
3/5 and 2/5 and the value 519n; the dual certificate is (y-1)(y-6),
primal and dual agree, so 519 is the optimum and 517.1's bound is
tight. Hence NO SPECTRAL INEQUALITY USING THE MOMENTS UP TO ORDER SIX
CAN PROVE BAND 3, the 24n gap being the exact distance between the
data and the assertion. AND THE FINITE-n PROGRAM IS STRICTLY
STRONGER: every cubic graph of girth at least 7 on at most 30
vertices has an 8-cycle. That the Kesten-McKay measure keeps the
enlarged program feasible at every moment order, so the Perron atom
is the only obstruction and it is invisible below moment order
11.8 log_2 n, about three times the trace window 2g.

COMPUTED: the tree closed-walk counts 1, 3, 15, 87, 543, 3543 by
transfer recursion and independently as Kesten-McKay moments by
numerical integration, agreeing to six figures; the exact LP optimum
against the target at n = 10 to 400, deciding for n <= 30 and failing
from n = 32; the girth-6 degradation, optimum-minus-target per vertex
-24, -27.8, -30 at c_6 = 0, n/5, n/2.

CORRECTED (374.1): 517.2's "no sharpening will fix that" is right
asymptotically and wrong at finite n - the exact program decides
girth 7 for 24 <= n <= 30, which the fixed asymptotic certificate
does not. And a draft of this section asserted that Kesten-McKay is
the extremal measure of the program; it is FEASIBLE but NOT extremal,
the optimum being 519 and not 543. The error would have made the gap
look like zero.

IDENTIFIED: that the one band-3 girth reachable by any instrument is
the largest, 7, and that the difficulty rises as the girth falls,
because girth is the archive's only source of exact spectral data;
and that the unused information is arithmetic - the spectrum of a
graph is a set of algebraic conjugates with integer symmetric
functions - to which every convex relaxation is blind.

NOT PROVED: band 3 at girth 5 or 6, or at girth 7 for n >= 32;
(E_k) above the band threshold; (LC); the rank >= 2 cancellation; the
long-branch template values; (LQ3), equivalently (K4); the Ladder
Question; (R); Theorem B(SWAP); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Convex
optimisation was the right instrument for band 3 and it has now been
run to the end rather than approximated: the program's value is
519n, the target is 543n, and the extremal measure is written down.
That settles what the spectrum can prove - girth 7 up to thirty
vertices, and nothing beyond - and it settles it by exhibiting the
adversary rather than by failing to defeat him. The adversary is a
four-point measure that no graph has, and the reason the program
cannot rule it out is that the program never learns the spectrum is
a set of algebraic conjugates. Band 3 is now the smallest and
best-understood open statement in this archive: one target, 8; three
girths, 5, 6 and 7; every counting and spectral route closed by
theorem; and a counterexample predicted at density e^{-16} that
nobody has looked for at the sizes where it should live.


## 520. WHAT WOULD RESCUE BAND 3: THREE AUGMENTATIONS, AND THE
## LOCAL-CONTINUITY NO-GO

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 519 solved the band-3
convex program and found its value 519n against a target of 543n.
This section asks what could be added to it. 520.0 identifies the
obstruction and proves it is not specific to convexity. 520.1, 520.2
and 520.3 try the three natural augmentations - edge mass, higher
moments, and the counterexample hypothesis - and report two failures
with numbers and one new lemma. Machine: scratch serre520.py,
hankel520.py, lcfast.py.

### 520.0 KESTEN-MCKAY IS THE TREE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OBSTRUCTION
### (PROVED)

The measure that defeats the program is not an accident of the
relaxation. Kesten-McKay for d = 3 IS THE SPECTRAL MEASURE OF THE
INFINITE 3-REGULAR TREE - its moments are the tree's closed-walk
counts 1, 3, 15, 87, 543, 3543, verified two ways in 519 - and the
tree is the Benjamini-Schramm limit of any sequence of cubic graphs
whose girth tends to infinity. Hence:

  THEOREM (LOCAL-CONTINUITY NO-GO). Let P be any graph parameter that
  is continuous under Benjamini-Schramm convergence, or equivalently
  under convergence of the normalised moments tr A^k / n. Then P
  cannot decide band 3. For the 3-regular tree is a limit of cubic
  graphs of girth 7 and has no 8-cycle at all, so P takes the same
  value on the hypothesis and on its negation.
    Every convex relaxation over spectral measures, local statistics,
  homomorphism densities or tracial states is such a parameter.

This is 452.0's tree no-go - "the infinite 3-regular tree has minimum
degree 3 and no cycles at all, so no statement about bounded
neighbourhoods can imply Erdos-Gyarfas" - in analytic form, and it is
the same fact as 519.1's extremal measure. The archive has now met it
in three languages: combinatorial (452.0), spectral (519.1) and
measure-theoretic (here).

  SO THE RESCUE MUST USE A FEATURE THAT IS NOT LOCAL, AND THERE ARE
  EXACTLY TWO. (i) THE PERRON ATOM: mass exactly 1/n at exactly 3,
  which the tree does not have, and which 519.3 shows is invisible
  below moment order 11.8 log_2 n. (ii) INTEGRALITY: the spectrum is
  a set of algebraic conjugates whose symmetric functions are
  integers, to which no convex relaxation is sensitive.

### 520.1 AUGMENTATION 1 - EDGE MASS. QUANTIFIED, AND IT IS THE WRONG
### CONSTRAINT (COMPUTED)

519's extremal measure has its atoms at y = mu^2 = 1 and 6 and NO
MASS ABOVE 6 - in particular nothing near the Ramanujan edge
y = 8. Serre-type theorems assert that a finite d-regular graph
carries a positive proportion of its spectrum near that edge, which
is exactly the kind of statement the program lacks. How much is
needed? Solving the program with the extra constraint "mass at least
c above y = Y":

    Y = 8.0   (the Ramanujan edge)     c = 0.080
    Y = 7.5                            c = 0.120
    Y = 7.0                            c = 0.195
    Y = 6.5                            more than 0.30
    Y = 6.0                            never - the atom sits there

  EIGHT PER CENT OF THE SPECTRUM AT OR ABOVE THE RAMANUJAN EDGE
  CLOSES BAND 3.

  AND IT IS UNAVAILABLE, not because the literature is missing but
  because the statement is false. Kesten-McKay is supported on
  [-2 sqrt 2, 2 sqrt 2], so a typical cubic graph has NO spectrum
  above the edge except the Perron eigenvalue itself - one
  eigenvalue, mass 1/n. The augmentation asks for 0.08n eigenvalues
  where the typical graph has one. Recorded as measured and refuted
  in principle: the program's adversary sits inside the Kesten-McKay
  support, so no edge-mass hypothesis can dislodge it.

### 520.2 AUGMENTATION 2 - MORE MOMENTS. TRIED; IT CANNOT TIGHTEN
### (COMPUTED)

Recast the program as FEASIBILITY, which is the sharper form. Assume
c_8 = 0 and girth at least 7. Then in y = mu^2 over the n-1
non-Perron eigenvalues,

    M0 = n-1, M1 = 3n-9, M2 = 15n-81, M3 = 87n-729, M4 = 543n-6561

are all DETERMINED, and the question is whether any measure on [0,9]
has them - the truncated Hausdorff problem, decided by two Hankel
semidefiniteness conditions. That is precisely 519.2's test, and it
gives n <= 30.

  ADDING THE TENTH MOMENT DOES NOTHING, and the reason is structural:
  M5 = 3543n + 20 c_10 - 59049 is NOT determined, c_10 being free and
  non-negative, and an unconstrained moment never tightens a
  feasibility problem.

  THE FIX IS TO CAP c_10, AND THE DIFFERENCE WEAPON SUPPLIES ONE: by
  518.2 no two 10-cycles meet in exactly a 6-path, and a cubic graph
  has 48n paths of length 6, so c_10 <= 4.8 n. With that cap:

     n     Hankel forces M5 >=     cap permits     contradiction
    24            30975.0            28287.0            YES
    30            50409.0            50121.0            YES
    32            57127.9            57399.0            no
    50           118992.4           122901.0            no
   200           642441.8           668751.0            no

  THE THRESHOLD IS AGAIN EXACTLY n = 30. The sharpest available cap
  on the next cycle count moves it by nothing, and the asymptotics
  say why: the Hankel bound is 3212n, the cap permits 3639n, and the
  tree value 3543n LIES BETWEEN THEM. The bound is below the tree and
  the cap is above it, so the test can never fire. 519.3 predicted
  this by argument; here it is by computation.

### 520.3 AUGMENTATION 3 - RUN THE TRACE FRAME INSIDE THE REDUCTIO
### (PROVED, AND NEW)

452 works OUTSIDE the reductio: it assumes no counterexample and
produces cycles. That is a deliberate strength, and it costs
something that has never been counted.

  LEMMA. Let G be cubic with no cycle of power-of-two length. Then
  for every k the RANK-ONE contribution to tr B^{2^k} is zero.
    PROOF. A closed non-backtracking walk whose support is a single
    cycle of length l runs 2^k / l times round it, so l divides 2^k,
    and the total rank-one contribution is SUM_{l | 2^k} 2 l c_l.
    Every divisor of 2^k is a power of two; c_1 = c_2 = 0 in a simple
    graph and c_4 = c_8 = ... = 0 by hypothesis. QED

  CONSEQUENCE. In a counterexample, for every k,
      tr B^{2^k} = the number of closed non-backtracking walks of
      length 2^k whose support has cycle rank at least two,
  while Ihara-Bass gives tr B^{2^k} >= 2^{2^k} + 1 + n -
  2 n 2^{2^{k-1}}.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. 452 stops at m = 2g because
the identity tr B^m = 2 m c_m there acquires two families of
corrections, rank one and rank two. Inside the reductio, AT THE ONLY
LENGTHS THAT MATTER, HALF OF THEM VANISH: the extension asked for in
516.6(i) needs only the theta and dumbbell terms. That is a real
simplification of the archive's one live analytic problem.

  IT DOES NOT RESCUE BAND 3, and the reason should be recorded before
  anyone hopes otherwise. 517.5 recommended attacking where the
  supply is large, and the supply at a target of length m is
  2^m / 2m, which is large only when m grows. In band 3 the girth is
  5, 6 or 7 - BOUNDED - so every target the trace frame can reach is
  bounded too: widening the window from 2g to 4g at girth 5 reaches
  m <= 20, where the supply is at most 2^20/40, still a constant
  against a Theta(n) error. THE SUPPLY BECOMES POLYNOMIAL IN n ONLY
  WHEN THE GIRTH GROWS WITH n, that is in the HIGH bands - which are
  the bands 518.0 already settles. The two easy regimes coincide and
  band 3 is outside both.

### 520.4 WHERE THAT LEAVES BAND 3

  CLOSED BY THEOREM: every convex relaxation over local or spectral
  data (520.0); the plain moment program beyond n = 30 (519.1); the
  edge-mass augmentation (520.1, refuted in principle); the
  higher-moment augmentation (520.2, threshold unmoved); counting via
  the difference weapon (517.3); minimality and reduction (518.3).

  OPEN, AND NOW THE ONLY TWO: (a) an argument using INTEGRALITY - the
  spectrum of a graph is a set of algebraic conjugates with integer
  symmetric functions, and 519.1's adversary, mu in {+-1, +-sqrt 6},
  is a measure no graph has; (b) FINDING THE COUNTEREXAMPLE, whose
  density the first moment puts at e^{-16}.

  SEARCH STATUS, updated: no Hamiltonian cubic graph without an
  8-cycle at girth 5 for n <= 26 - the n = 26 sweep needed 3910411
  nodes - at girth 6 for n <= 32, at girth 7 for n <= 38, and girth 7
  is PROVED for n <= 30 by 519.2. The girth-5 search tree is growing
  by a factor of about twelve per step, so n = 30 is reachable and
  n = 34 is not, by this method, on this machine.

### 520.5 STATUS

PROVED here: THE LOCAL-CONTINUITY NO-GO - Kesten-McKay is the
spectral measure of the 3-regular tree, the tree is a
Benjamini-Schramm limit of cubic graphs of girth 7, and it has no
8-cycle; hence no parameter continuous under local convergence, and
in particular no convex relaxation over spectral measures, local
statistics or tracial states, can decide band 3. This identifies
452.0's tree no-go and 519.1's extremal measure as one obstruction in
three languages, and leaves exactly two non-local features: the
Perron atom and integrality. THE RANK-ONE VANISHING LEMMA - in a
graph with no power-of-two cycle, tr B^{2^k} counts only walks of
cycle rank at least two, so the extension of 452 past 2g needs only
the theta and dumbbell corrections at the lengths that matter.

COMPUTED: the edge-mass requirement - 8.0 per cent of the spectrum at
or above the Ramanujan edge y = 8 closes band 3, rising to 19.5 per
cent at y = 7 and unattainable at y = 6.5; the Hankel feasibility
test with the tenth moment and the difference weapon's cap
c_10 <= 4.8n, which leaves the threshold at exactly n = 30, the
Hankel bound 3212n and the cap 3639n straddling the tree value 3543n;
and the girth-5 search extended to n = 26 in 3910411 nodes with no
witness.

IDENTIFIED: that 517.5's advice - attack where the supply is large -
does NOT apply inside band 3, because the girth there is bounded, so
every target the trace frame can reach has bounded supply. The
large-supply regime and the regime already settled by 518.0 are the
same regime, and band 3 lies outside both.

NOT PROVED: band 3 at girth 5 or 6, or at girth 7 for n >= 32; (LC);
(E_k) above the band threshold; the rank >= 2 cancellation; the
long-branch template values; (LQ3), equivalently (K4); the Ladder
Question; (R); Theorem B(SWAP); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked what
would rescue band 3 from the convex program, the answer is that
nothing convex will, and the proof is short: the program's adversary
is the 3-regular tree, the tree is a limit of the very graphs in
question, and every convex relaxation is continuous along that limit.
The two augmentations that looked most promising were measured rather
than guessed - the edge-mass hypothesis needs eight per cent of the
spectrum in a place where the typical graph has one eigenvalue, and
the tenth moment with the sharpest cap available moves the threshold
by zero. What survives is one new lemma, that the counterexample
hypothesis annihilates half the corrections in the only analytic
problem the archive has left; and two routes that are not analysis at
all - the integrality of the spectrum, and the search.


## 521. THE SPECTRAL CEILING, AND TWO COMBINATORIAL LEMMAS AT GIRTH 5

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 518.3 left the sandwich
as a partition whose lower jaw is band 3, and 519-520 closed the
convex routes to it. This section takes the two remaining directions
named in 519.5. On the spectrum side it proves an exact identity that
turns the scattered evidence of 452.4, 518.0, 519.2 and 520 into ONE
theorem with ONE threshold. On the combinatorial side it proves two
lemmas about pentagons that use no spectral input at all, one of
which kills the Petersen graph in a line. Machine: scratch
ceiling521.py, ear521.py, match521.py.

### 521.0 THE TREE IDENTITY (PROVED)

THEOREM. Let KM be the Kesten-McKay measure for d = 3 - the spectral
measure of the infinite 3-regular tree - and let p_m be the
polynomial with p_m(mu) = lam^m + lam'^m for lam lam' = 2,
lam + lam' = mu. Then for every even m >= 2,

        INTEGRAL  p_m  dKM   =   -1 .

  PROOF. Substitute mu = 2 sqrt 2 cos theta, so lam = sqrt 2 e^{i
  theta} and p_m = 2 . 2^{m/2} cos(m theta). The Kesten-McKay density
  d sqrt(4(d-1) - x^2) / (2 pi (d^2 - x^2)) at d = 3 becomes, with
  phi = 2 theta, (6/pi) (1 - cos phi)/(5 - 4 cos phi) . dphi/2 on
  (0, 2pi). The Poisson kernel gives
  1/(5 - 4 cos phi) = (1/3) SUM_k 2^{-|k|} e^{i k phi}, whence for
  m = 2r
     INT_0^{2pi} cos(r phi)/(5 - 4 cos phi) dphi = (2 pi/3) 2^{-r}
  and
     INT_0^{2pi} cos(r phi) cos phi/(5-4 cos phi) dphi
        = (pi/3)(5/2) 2^{-r} .
  Assembling, INT p_m dKM = 2 . 2^{r} . (6/pi) . (1/2) .
  [ (2pi/3) 2^{-r} - (pi/3)(5/2) 2^{-r} ] = 12 . (-1/12) = -1. QED

  VERIFIED exactly, in integer arithmetic, by expanding p_m in the
  monomial basis and pairing with the tree walk counts W_j: the value
  is -1 for every even m from 2 to 20.

  WHAT IT SAYS. For a cubic graph, tr B^m = SUM_i p_m(mu_i) + n, and
  for g <= m < 2g that equals 2 m c_m. A graph whose spectral measure
  were exactly KM would therefore have SUM p_m = -n and hence
  c_m = 0 - AT EVERY m, not merely at m = 8. The tree does not sit on
  the boundary of band 3 by accident; it sits on the boundary of
  every band at once, and the identity INT p_m dKM = -1 is the exact
  statement of that.

### 521.1 THE SPECTRAL CEILING (PROVED AND MEASURED)

Separate the Perron eigenvalue. For even m,

    2 m c_m  =  (2^m + 1)  +  SUM_{i >= 2} p_m(mu_i)  +  n ,

and by 521.0 the second term is about -(n-1) when the non-Perron
spectrum resembles the tree. THE ONLY MECHANISM THE SPECTRUM HAS IS
FOR THE PERRON TERM 2^m TO BEAT THE WORST CASE OF THE SECOND, and the
worst case is bounded by |p_m| <= 2 . 2^{m/2} on the bulk
|mu| <= 2 sqrt 2, giving 520's test 2^{m/2} > 2n.

  IS THAT CRUDE STEP LOSSY? Minimise INT p_m dnu over probability
  measures on [-3, 3] matching the tree moments below the girth - the
  most any spectral argument may assume - against the crude value
  -2 . 2^{m/2}:

     girth 5, m = 8    LP min  -31.0   crude  -32.0   ratio 0.97
     girth 6, m = 8    LP min  -31.0   crude  -32.0   ratio 0.97
     girth 7, m = 8    LP min  -24.4   crude  -32.0   ratio 0.76

  THE CRUDE BOUND IS THE TRUTH UP TO A FACTOR BELOW 4/3. So:

  THE SPECTRAL CEILING. For every girth and every admissible target,
  the spectral route decides c_m > 0 exactly in the regime where the
  Perron term beats the bulk, that is n = O(2^{m/2}), and no
  refinement using the moments below the girth improves the threshold
  by more than a constant factor.

  THAT IS ONE THEOREM WHERE THE ARCHIVE HAD FOUR OBSERVATIONS. 452.4's
  sweep firing at n = 58, 70, 126, 1022, ..., 1048574 and failing at
  510 and 65534; 518.0's band theorem n < 2^{2^{k-1}-1}; 519.2's
  girth-7 threshold n <= 30; and 520.2's finding that the tenth
  moment moves it by zero - all four are the single inequality
  2^{m/2} > 2n, and 521.0 says why nothing else is available.

### 521.2 THE EAR DICHOTOMY AT GIRTH 5 (PROVED, VERIFIED)

Now the other direction, with no spectrum in it at all. Let G be
cubic of girth 5, C = v_1..v_5 a pentagon, u_1..u_5 the five third
neighbours, distinct by girth. A path from u_i to u_j internally
disjoint from C, of length s, is an ear of C of length q = s + 2 with
feet v_i, v_j, and it creates cycles of lengths q + d and
q + 5 - d, where d is the distance from v_i to v_j along C.

  LEMMA. If G has no 8-cycle then, writing d(u_i, u_j) for the
  distance in G - V(C),

      v_i, v_j ADJACENT on C     =>   d(u_i,u_j) >= 3 and != 5 ,
      v_i, v_j at DISTANCE 2     =>   d(u_i,u_j) <= 2 or >= 5 .

  PROOF. q + d != 8 and q + 5 - d != 8 with q = s + 2; at d = 1 this
  bars s = 5 and s = 2, and girth bars s <= 1; at d = 2 it bars s = 4
  and s = 3. QED

  So adjacent feet have their neighbours FAR and never at exactly 5,
  while feet at distance two have them CLOSE or FAR and never at 3 or
  4. The forbidden values are the only obstruction: everything else
  is permitted.

  VERIFIED, by the only direction a graph with 8-cycles can test:
  over Petersen, the dodecahedron and six random cubic girth-5 graphs
  on 14 to 24 vertices, every foot pair realising a forbidden
  distance - 254 of them - occurs in a graph that does have an
  8-cycle. No inconsistency.

### 521.3 THE PENTAGRAM MATCHING LEMMA (PROVED, VERIFIED)

Girth 5 already forces u_i ~ u_j only when v_i and v_j are at
distance TWO along C - adjacency at distance one would close a
4-cycle - so the possible adjacencies among the u's form the
pentagram 1-3-5-2-4-1.

  LEMMA. If G has no 8-cycle then those adjacencies form a MATCHING
  in the pentagram: no u_i has two u-neighbours, and at most two of
  the five occur.

  PROOF. Suppose u_1 ~ u_3 and u_1 ~ u_4, the two distance-two
  partners of v_1. Then
      C'  = v_1 u_1 u_3 v_3 v_2      and
      C'' = v_1 u_1 u_4 v_4 v_5
  are both pentagons, and they meet in exactly the edge v_1 u_1,
  their remaining vertices being v_2, v_3, u_3 and v_4, v_5, u_4, all
  distinct. Two cycles meeting in exactly one path of length 1 have a
  symmetric difference that is a single cycle, here of length
  5 + 5 - 2 = 8. QED

  COROLLARY, IN ONE LINE: the Petersen graph, whose five u's form a
  full 5-cycle in the pentagram, must contain an 8-cycle.

  VERIFIED: on Petersen all twelve pentagons violate the matching
  condition, and in all twelve the symmetric difference C' delta C''
  was computed and confirmed to be a genuine 8-cycle. On the
  dodecahedron and eight random girth-5 graphs to n = 30 no pentagon
  violates it, so the lemma is not vacuous only on the extremal
  graph.

  WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT GIVE. It is a genuine local obstruction
  and it is sharp on the (3,5)-cage. It does not iterate to a
  contradiction: applying it to the pentagon C' shows that C' has one
  forced u-adjacency of its own - the outside neighbours of v_1 and
  v_3 are v_5 and v_4, which are adjacent - so the matching on C''s
  pentagram is non-empty, and the lemma then only bars the two
  pentagram edges meeting it. The recursion sustains itself instead
  of closing.

  AND A WARNING RECORDED BEFORE IT COSTS ANYONE A SECTION. A first
  draft of 521.3 argued from paths such as v_5 - v_1 - u_1 - u_3 - w_3
  that 521.2's dichotomy forces four further pairs to distance at
  most 2. IT DOES NOT: 521.2 measures distance in G - V(C'), and that
  path runs through three vertices of C'. The forced-closeness
  corollary is WITHDRAWN; what survives is the matching lemma, which
  needs no distances at all.

### 521.4 WHERE THE SANDWICH STANDS

  UPPER JAW, girth >= 9. Theorem for n < 2^{2^{k-1}-1} (518.0), and
  by 521.1 that threshold is the ceiling of the spectral route, not
  an artefact.

  LOWER JAW, girth 5, 6, 7, target 8. Convex routes closed (519,
  520); spectral ceiling reached at n = 30 for girth 7 (519.2) and
  never for girths 5 and 6, where fewer moments are exact. What is
  live is combinatorial, and 521.2 and 521.3 are the first two
  instruments of that kind the archive has for band 3. Both are
  local, both are sharp on the cage, and neither closes.

  THE HONEST SHAPE. The upper jaw is spectral and is at its ceiling.
  The lower jaw is combinatorial and has just been opened. They meet,
  as 518.3 proved they must, at exactly the conjecture.

### 521.5 STATUS

PROVED here: THE TREE IDENTITY INT p_m dKM = -1 for every even m,
analytically by the Poisson kernel and verified in integer arithmetic
for m = 2 to 20 - so the 3-regular tree sits exactly at c_m = 0 at
EVERY target, which is why 520.0's local-continuity no-go applies to
every band and not only to band 3. THE SPECTRAL CEILING: the only
mechanism available to the spectrum is the Perron term beating the
bulk, with threshold 2^{m/2} > 2n, and the bulk bound is within a
factor below 4/3 of optimal at every band-3 girth - so 452.4's sweep,
518.0's band theorem, 519.2's n <= 30 and 520.2's null result are one
theorem. THE EAR DICHOTOMY AT GIRTH 5: adjacent feet force
d(u_i,u_j) >= 3 and != 5; feet at distance two force d <= 2 or >= 5.
THE PENTAGRAM MATCHING LEMMA: the u-adjacencies of any pentagon form
a matching, so at most two of five occur - and hence the Petersen
graph has an 8-cycle, in one line.

COMPUTED: the tree identity for m = 2, 4, ..., 20, exactly; the
minimum of INT p_m over measures with the tree moments below the
girth, giving -31.0, -31.0, -24.4 against the crude -32.0 at
(g,m) = (5,8), (6,8), (7,8); the ear dichotomy on 254 forbidden-
distance instances across eight graphs, all consistent; the matching
lemma on all twelve pentagons of Petersen with the 8-cycle exhibited
explicitly each time, and on eight further girth-5 graphs to n = 30.

CORRECTED (374.1): a draft forced-closeness corollary of 521.2 is
WITHDRAWN - it applied the dichotomy along paths that run through the
very pentagon the dichotomy excludes. The matching lemma of 521.3 is
unaffected, using no distances.

IDENTIFIED: that the recursion in 521.3 sustains itself - the
pentagon C' produced by a u-adjacency has a forced u-adjacency of its
own - so a proof of band 3 by iterating local pentagon lemmas will
need an entry point those lemmas do not supply.

NOT PROVED: band 3 at any girth beyond the ranges already recorded;
(LC); (E_k) above the band threshold; the rank >= 2 cancellation; the
long-branch template values; (LQ3), equivalently (K4); the Ladder
Question; (R); Theorem B(SWAP); J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Circling back
to the sandwich with the two routes 519.5 left open, the spectrum
side is now finished rather than merely blocked: one identity,
INT p_m dKM = -1, explains why the tree sits on the boundary of every
band, and one inequality, 2^{m/2} > 2n, is the whole of what the
spectrum can ever prove, tight to a factor below 4/3. The
combinatorial side has been opened instead of surveyed: two lemmas
about a pentagon and its five outside neighbours, proved from the
symmetric difference of two cycles and nothing else, one of which
disposes of the extremal graph in a line. Neither closes band 3, and
the second explains why the obvious iteration will not - but they are
the first instruments the archive has that the tree cannot see, which
by 520.0 is the only kind that can ever work.


## 522. THE COMBINATORIAL ROUTE: THE INVOLUTION, TWO MORE LEMMAS,
## AND A PACKING BOUND THAT BEATS THE SPECTRUM

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 521 opened the
combinatorial attack on band 3 and hit an obstruction: the pentagon
recursion does not iterate. This section identifies that obstruction
exactly, converts it into a directive, and follows the directive to a
theorem that does what no convex method managed - it beats the
spectral ceiling. Machine: scratch band522.py, pack522.py.

### 522.0 THE OBSTRUCTION IS AN INVOLUTION (PROVED, VERIFIED)

521.3 observed that the pentagon C' produced by a u-adjacency has a
forced u-adjacency of its own. The exact statement is stronger.

  THEOREM. Let C = v_1..v_5 be a pentagon of a cubic girth-5 graph
  with u_i ~ u_j at C-distance two and common C-neighbour v_x, and
  let C' = v_i u_i u_j v_j v_x. Then C' has a u-adjacency of its own -
  the outside neighbours of v_j and v_i, which are the two remaining
  C-vertices and are adjacent - AND APPLYING THE CONSTRUCTION TO IT
  RETURNS C. The map C -> C' IS AN INVOLUTION.

  PROOF. In C' the vertices v_j and v_i are at distance two with
  common C'-neighbour v_x, and their outside neighbours are their
  C-neighbours other than v_x. Those two are adjacent on C, and the
  construction applied to that pair rebuilds v_j, (its C-neighbour),
  (v_i's C-neighbour), v_i, v_x - which is C. QED

  VERIFIED: over Petersen, the dodecahedron and four random cubic
  girth-5 graphs, all 78 u-adjacency instances return C. 78 of 78.

  THE INVARIANT IS A THETA. C union C' is the theta with branch
  vertices v_i, v_j and paths of lengths 2, 3, 3 - seven vertices,
  eight edges, cycles 5, 5, 6. So a u-adjacency in a girth-5 graph
  with no 8-cycle is exactly a Theta(2,3,3), and the recursion is the
  theta's own symmetry exchanging its two 3-paths. THERE IS NOTHING
  TO ITERATE.

### 522.1 THE OBSTRUCTION AS A DIRECTIVE

Why did the iteration have to fail? Because of the tree, again. 452.0
and 520.0 say a bounded-radius argument cannot decide band 3, and the
combinatorial form is immediate: a large cubic graph of girth 5 looks,
around any pentagon, like a pentagon with trees hanging off it, and
that configuration has no 8-cycle and is completable. NO ARGUMENT
THAT EXAMINES ONLY A BOUNDED NEIGHBOURHOOD WILL EVER PRODUCE A
CONTRADICTION.

  BUT IT CAN PRODUCE A COUNT. The tree is infinite; a counterexample
  is not. A bounded-radius analysis cannot contradict the hypothesis,
  but it CAN force the neighbourhood to be large, and that is a lower
  bound on n. THE RIGHT USE OF LOCAL COMBINATORICS IN BAND 3 IS TO
  PACK, NOT TO CONTRADICT. 522.3 does exactly that and beats every
  spectral bound the archive has.

### 522.2 THE GIRTH-6 AND GIRTH-7 LEMMAS (PROVED, VERIFIED)

GIRTH 6. Let H = x_0..x_5 be a hexagon with outside neighbours
y_0..y_5. An adjacency y_i ~ y_j closes a cycle of length 3 + d, so
girth 6 permits only d = 3: three candidate ANTIPODAL pairs.

  LEMMA. If G has no 8-cycle then AT MOST ONE of the three occurs.
    PROOF. Given y_0 ~ y_3 and y_1 ~ y_4, the hexagons
    H1 = x_0 y_0 y_3 x_3 x_4 x_5 and H2 = x_1 y_1 y_4 x_4 x_5 x_0
    meet in exactly the 2-path x_4 x_5 x_0, so their difference is a
    cycle of length 6 + 6 - 4 = 8. Given y_0 ~ y_3 and y_2 ~ y_5,
    take H1 and H3 = x_2 y_2 y_5 x_5 x_4 x_3, meeting in exactly
    x_3 x_4 x_5. QED

  VERIFIED: Heawood and Mobius-Kantor violate it at every one of
  their 28 and 24 hexagons, and both have 8-cycles; Pappus,
  Desargues, Nauru and Dyck satisfy it. The lemma is sharp on the
  (3,6)-cage.

GIRTH 7. Here girth alone forbids every y-adjacency, since 3 + d <= 6.
The hypothesis constrains distances instead. Writing s for the
distance in G - V(H) between the outside neighbours of two heptagon
vertices at distance d:

    d = 1 :  admissible q = 6, 8, 9, ...   so s >= 4
    d = 2 :  admissible q = 5, 7, 8, ...   so s >= 3
    d = 3 :  admissible q = 6, 7, 8, ...   so s >= 4

  (q + d and q + 7 - d must both be at least 7 and neither may be 8;
  the table is exhaustive over q.) So EVERY pair of outside
  neighbours is at distance at least 3, and the distance-three pairs
  at least 4 - the last needing the hypothesis, girth alone giving 2.

  VERIFIED: McGee violates the distance-3 requirement at all 224
  tested pairs and Coxeter at all 168, and both have 8-cycles.
  Coxeter satisfies the weaker "all pairs at distance >= 3", so the
  two requirements are genuinely different.

### 522.3 THE GIRTH-7 PACKING THEOREM (PROVED)

  THEOREM. A cubic graph of girth 7 with no 8-cycle has at least 34
  vertices. Equivalently, EVERY CUBIC GRAPH OF GIRTH 7 ON AT MOST 32
  VERTICES HAS AN 8-CYCLE.

  PROOF. Fix a heptagon H, seven vertices. Its outside neighbours
  Y = {y_0..y_6} are seven more, distinct because a shared one would
  put two H-vertices at distance 2, closing a cycle of length at most
  6.
    LEVEL TWO. By 522.2 every pair of y's is at distance at least 3,
  so no two share a neighbour; each y_i has two neighbours off H, all
  14 distinct. None lies in H - a path of length 2 between two
  H-vertices needs d >= 5 > 3 - and none in Y, distance being at
  least 3. So far 7 + 7 + 14 = 28 vertices.
    LEVEL THREE IS NON-EMPTY, AND LARGE. A level-three vertex cannot
  lie in Y: that would give a path of length 4 between two
  H-vertices, hence cycles 4 + d and 11 - d; girth forces d = 3, and
  then 11 - d = 8. It cannot lie in H, since a path of length 3
  between H-vertices needs d >= 4 > 3.
    EDGES INSIDE LEVEL TWO. If z ~ z' with feet at H-distance d, the
  cycles are 5 + d and 12 - d; girth kills d = 1 and the hypothesis
  kills d = 3, leaving d = 2 exactly. For a fixed such foot pair
  there is at most ONE such edge: two sharing an endpoint close a
  4-cycle, and two disjoint ones close a 6-cycle. There are seven
  H-distance-2 foot pairs, so at most seven edges inside level two.
    COUNT. Level two offers 14 x 2 = 28 edge-slots; at most 7 edges
  consume 14 of them, so at least 14 slots reach level three, and a
  level-three vertex, having degree 3, absorbs at most 3. Hence level
  three has at least ceiling(14/3) = 5 vertices, and

        n  >=  7 + 7 + 14 + 5  =  33 ,

  and n is even for a cubic graph, so n >= 34. QED

  EVERY CASE OF THE THREE TABLES WAS CHECKED EXHAUSTIVELY OVER THE
  POSSIBLE (d, q) BY MACHINE, and the two real girth-7 graphs
  available, McGee at n = 24 and Coxeter at n = 28, both lie below 34
  and both have 8-cycles, as they must.

  THIS BEATS THE SPECTRUM. 519.2's convex program proves band 3 at
  girth 7 for n <= 30; the packing theorem proves it for n <= 32, in
  half a page, with no eigenvalues in it. It is the first time in
  this archive that a combinatorial argument has overtaken the
  spectral one on the same statement.

  COMBINED WITH THE SEARCH: no Hamiltonian cubic graph of girth 7
  without an 8-cycle at n <= 38 (518.5), so such a graph, if
  Hamiltonian, has at least 40 vertices; and unconditionally at least
  34.

### 522.4 WHY GIRTH 5 AND 6 DO NOT PACK

The packing works at girth 7 because the outside neighbours are
forced APART. At the lower girths they are not.

  GIRTH 5, pentagon: the dichotomy of 521.2 permits s <= 2 at every
  distance-two foot pair, so two u's may be adjacent or share a
  neighbour, and level two can collapse from 10 to as few as 5.
  GIRTH 6, hexagon: the antipodal pairs permit s = 1 and s = 2, and
  by 522.2 only ONE adjacency is barred, not the sharing.

  So the packing bound is a girth-7 phenomenon, and the reason is
  exactly the reason band 3 gets harder as the girth falls (519.4):
  girth is the resource, and there is less of it. THE THREE GIRTHS OF
  BAND 3 ARE NOT ONE PROBLEM - girth 7 is now settled to n = 32,
  girth 6 to n = 32 by search only, girth 5 to n = 26 by search only.

### 522.5 STATUS

PROVED here: THE INVOLUTION - the pentagon map C -> C' of 521.3 is an
involution whose invariant is the theta Theta(2,3,3), so 521.3's
obstruction is a symmetry and not a shortage of ideas. THE GIRTH-6
LEMMA - at most one antipodal adjacency among the outside neighbours
of a hexagon. THE GIRTH-7 EAR TABLE - every pair of outside
neighbours of a heptagon is at distance at least 3, and the
distance-three pairs at least 4. THE GIRTH-7 PACKING THEOREM - a
cubic graph of girth 7 with no 8-cycle has at least 34 vertices,
hence every cubic graph of girth 7 on at most 32 vertices has an
8-cycle, which is strictly stronger than 519.2's spectral n <= 30 and
is proved in half a page without eigenvalues.

COMPUTED: the involution on all 78 u-adjacency instances of six
graphs, returning C every time; the girth-6 lemma sharp on Heawood
and Mobius-Kantor, where all 28 and all 24 hexagons violate it and
8-cycles are present, and satisfied by Pappus, Desargues, Nauru and
Dyck; the girth-7 distance requirement violated at all 224 tested
pairs of McGee and all 168 of Coxeter, both with 8-cycles; and the
three case tables of 522.3 verified exhaustively over the possible
(d, q).

IDENTIFIED, and it reframes the whole route: A BOUNDED-RADIUS
COMBINATORIAL ARGUMENT CANNOT CONTRADICT THE BAND-3 HYPOTHESIS,
because the tree satisfies it, BUT IT CAN PACK - the tree is infinite
and a counterexample is not, so local analysis converts directly into

here, and following it produced 522.3. Also identified: that the
three girths of band 3 are three different problems, girth 7 being
the one with enough girth to pack.

NOT PROVED: band 3 at girth 5 or 6, or at girth 7 for n >= 34; (LC);

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Pursuing the
combinatorial route and turning its obstruction around has paid
exactly once, and the once is worth recording precisely. The
obstruction was that the pentagon recursion is an involution; the
lesson drawn from it was that local combinatorics in band 3 must pack
rather than contradict, because the object it is competing against is

reason that is now also precise, and they remain where the search
left them.

girth >= 6 was a girth >= 7 run and every run labelled girth >= 7 was
a girth >= 8 run. The girth-5 searches used a different routine and

AND THE MISLABELLING FOUND THE OBJECT. The run labelled girth >= 6 at
n = 36 - in truth a girth >= 7 run - returned witnesses.

### 523.1 THE RANK >= 2 CORRECTION, MEASURED (COMPUTED)

516.6(i) named the rank >= 2 cancellation as the archive's one live
analytic problem - the only item that would produce cycles rather
than contradictions. It is now measured exactly rather than
estimated. With tr B^m computed from the integer traces of A by
Ihara-Bass, and the rank-one part SUM_{l | m} 2 l c_l subtracted:

  Petersen (g=5)      R(m)/2^m at m = 10, 12, 14, 16, 18:
                      1.17, 0.79, 0.97, 1.06, 0.98
  Heawood  (g=6)      at m = 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22:
                      1.97, 1.87, 1.95, 2.05, 1.99, 1.99
  dodecahedron (g=5)  at m = 10, 12, 14, 16, 18:
                      0.59, 0.35, 0.51, 1.03, 0.96

  and R(m) = 0 for EVERY m < 2g on all three - the identity of 452
  confirmed exactly, by a second route.

  CORRECTED (374.1): a first pass added n to tr B^m at every m. The
  two blocks of n/2 eigenvalues +1 and -1 cancel at ODD m and give n
  only at even m; the error showed as a spurious R(m) = n at m = 5,
  7, 9. Fixed, after which R(m) vanishes below 2g as it must.

  THE VERDICT ON WIDENING THE WINDOW. The natural hope is to bound
  R(m) by the number of theta subgraphs, each carrying O(1) walks.
  At m = 2g exactly that works - R(2g) divided by the number of
  thetas with at most 16 edges is 0.75, 0.54 and 0.03 on the three
  graphs. It fails immediately after: R(m) grows like 2^m while the
  theta count is polynomial, and the ratio passes 1 by m = 2g + 2 and
  reaches 43 by m = 2g + 6 on Petersen. SO THE WINDOW CANNOT BE
  WIDENED FROM 2g TOWARDS 4g BY COUNTING RANK-2 SUBGRAPHS, and
  520.3's rank-one vanishing lemma, while true, removes a term that
  452.5 had already computed exactly and does not touch the term that
  blocks.

### 523.2 THE LADDER QUESTION, RE-RUN AT THE ARCHIVE'S OWN MODEL

The model was read from the archive's own tools/ladder450.py rather
than reconstructed: positions are decided left to right, the least

    t = 3:  mu = 6, 8, 10, 12, 16  ->  2, 4, 9, 9, 9
    t = 4:  mu = 6, 8, 10, 12, 16  ->  2, 4, 9, 9, 10
  All bounded; none reaches the cap.

### 524.1 THE LADDER BOUND IS NOT FLAT IN mu (CORRECTED, 374.1)

449.4 records the honest limitation of the Ladder Question - "the
measurements cover span caps mu <= 16 ... for large L the bound is
EXTRAPOLATED, not proven" - and offers as evidence "that the bound is
already flat in mu (9 at mu = 10, 12 and 16)". Running the archive's
own model past 16:

    t \ mu    10   12   16   20   24
      3        9    9    9   10   10
      4        9    9   10   11   13
      5        -    -   10   11    -

  every entry BOUNDED, none reaching the cap. THE BOUND IS NOT FLAT.
  At t = 4 it climbs 9, 9, 10, 11, 13 as mu goes 10, 12, 16, 20, 24 -
  three steps of growth over the range the archive did not measure.
  The flatness seen at mu <= 16 was the flat part of a rising curve.

  Note also that the DFS is exhaustive left to right, so each entry
  is a PROOF for all lengths at that mu, not a bound to s = 60: any
  longer ladder would contain a longer valid prefix.

  THE CONSEQUENCE FOR 449.3, RESTATED HONESTLY. 449.3 reads s <= B(x+1)
  with B "about 10 in every case computed", hence x >= s/B - 1 =
  Omega(L) cross edges per ear, hence Theta(L^2) at the second
  generation. If instead B(mu) = Theta(mu) and the escape regime has
  mu ~ sqrt(L), then

      x  >=  (L/2) / (c sqrt L)  -  1  =  Omega( sqrt L ) ,

  and the second generation carries Theta(L^{3/2}) cross edges, not
  Theta(L^2). 449.3's ESCAPE IS STILL SHUT - any B(mu) = o(mu^2)
  suffices for x > 0, and the data is far below that - but its
  quantitative corollary is overstated and is corrected here.

  AND THE QUESTION ITSELF SHOULD BE RESTATED. "Is there a constant B
  independent of mu?" now looks false. What 449.3 actually needs is

    (LADDER BOUND*)  B(mu) = o(mu^2) ,

  which is weaker, is consistent with everything measured, and is the
  statement a proof should target.

### 524.2 WHAT THE CLOSED LADDER HAS THAT NOBODY HAS USED

Four properties, each tested rather than asserted, over the 60
girth-5 closed ladders at 2N = 14.

  (i) 3-EDGE-COLOURABILITY, AND SO NO SNARKS. A closed ladder is a
  Hamiltonian cubic graph on an even number of vertices, so colouring
  host edge {i, i+1} with 1 for i odd and 2 for i even, and every
  chord with 3, is proper. 60 of 60. NO CLOSED LADDER IS A SNARK, so
  every obstruction in the literature that runs on non-3-edge-
  colourability is inapplicable to the faithful J7 rung - a fact the
  archive has never recorded and which rules out a whole family of
  imports in one line.

  (ii) THE TWO ALTERNATING 2-FACTORS. The colouring hands over two
  canonical 2-factors, colours {1,3} and {2,3}: the N chords plus the
  N host edges of one parity. Each covers all 2N vertices, so ITS
  CYCLE LENGTHS PARTITION 2N. These are not completions of any chord
  subset - they use alternate host edges - so the entire calculus of
  495 to 515 cannot see them.

  (iii) THE SPAN PARITY. Summing spans over the matching counts every
  label once, so it is N(2N+1), whence THE NUMBER OF ODD-SPAN CHORDS
  IS CONGRUENT TO N MODULO 2. 60 of 60. Combined with 504.2 - the
  ladder is bipartite iff every span is odd - this says a bipartite
  closed ladder needs N even.

  AND TWO THAT DO NOT TRANSFER, recorded so nobody tries them again.
  501.7 set aside the Cohn-Lempel equality because "a ladder
  completion keeps ALTERNATE arcs, which is a different transition
  system". The hope here was that closing the ladder repairs the
  mismatch, since the all-arcs transition is then a genuine subgraph.
  IT DOES NOT: the identity c = 1 + nullity of the interlacement
  matrix holds on 16 of 60 and fails on 44. The chord-diagram genus,
  defined by 1 - N + c = 2 - 2 gamma, fails for the same reason - the
  count c it needs is the all-arcs one, and the 2-factor supplies the
  alternate-arcs one. 501.7's caution stands in the closed model too.

### 524.3 THE TARGET THE CATALOGUE SUGGESTS, AND ITS REFUTATION

(ii) has an obvious consequence to try, and it costs nothing to test.

  (2F) Does at least one of the two alternating 2-factors of a
       girth-legal closed ladder contain a cycle of power-of-two
       length?

(2F) would imply Erdos-Gyarfas for closed ladders, names no length so
it is (N16)-safe, and names no power of two in its subject so it is
(N9)-safe. It is also free to test - two subgraphs per ladder, no
completions and no connectivity search.

  REFUTED, immediately and overwhelmingly:

    2N = 12    24 ladders,     0 with a power-of-two part,  24 fail
    2N = 14   408 ladders,   182 succeed,                  226 fail
    2N = 16  8002 ladders,  7346 succeed,                  656 fail
    2N = 18  168802 ladders, 42696 succeed,             126106 fail

  The smallest witness is the very first girth-5 closed ladder at
  2N = 12: chords (1,5) (2,7) (3,9) (4,11) (6,10) (8,12), both
  2-factors being single 12-cycles. (2F) IS FALSE AT EVERY SIZE AND
  FAILS ON THE MAJORITY OF LADDERS AT 2N = 18.

  Recorded because the object is worth keeping even though the target

  2N that no instrument in 495-515 can express, and 524.3 only shows

## 525. (LQ3) WITHOUT SEARCH: THE DECOMPOSITION THEOREM, AND WHERE
## THE DIFFICULTY ACTUALLY SITS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 494 through 524 attacked
(LQ3) by enumeration, and the enumerations have been getting more
expensive while the statement has not moved. This section puts (LQ3)
in algebraic form, proves one structural theorem about it, and uses
the two together to say what a proof must and must not target. One
verification is run and no more. Machine: scratch decomp525.py.

### 525.0 (LQ3) IS A STATEMENT ABOUT AN INTERVAL CODE

Fix the open ladder on [1, 2N] with matching M. For a chord set T let
f_T be the PREFIX PARITY: f_T(i) = 1 iff an odd number of endpoints
of T lie in [1, i]. The completion Z(T) is the unique even subgraph
with chord set T (495.0), and it consists of the chords of T together
with the host edges at the positions where f_T = 1. Hence

        w(T)   =   |T|   +   wt( f_T ) .

Algebraically: let v_e in GF(2)^{2N-1} be the indicator of the
half-open interval [a_e, b_e). The v_e are linearly independent - the
leftmost endpoint of any non-empty S makes f_S non-zero there - so
they generate a code V of dimension N, which is the cycle code of the
ladder. The difference operator carries v_e to the pair e_{a_e} +
e_{b_e}, so the encoder T -> f_T is the PREFIX SUM of the endpoint
indicator of T, and

  w(T) = (weight of the message T) + (weight of the codeword f_T).

  SO (LQ3) IS A QUESTION ABOUT THE INPUT-OUTPUT WEIGHT ENUMERATOR OF
  AN INTERVAL CODE - a standard object - restricted to the messages
  whose codeword has connected support-with-chords. Writing it this
  way separates the two contributions, and 525.1 shows the second is
  the whole story.

  (This recovers 497.2's alternating-sum formula: the support of f_T
  is the union of the odd blocks [q_1,q_2), [q_3,q_4), ..., so
  wt(f_T) = SUM (q_{2i} - q_{2i-1}).)

### 525.1 THE DECOMPOSITION THEOREM (PROVED)

THEOREM. Let T be a chord set and let Z(T) have components
Z_1, ..., Z_k with chord sets T_1, ..., T_k. Then

  (a) each Z_j is the completion Z(T_j);
  (b) the parity supports supp f_{T_1}, ..., supp f_{T_k} are
      PAIRWISE DISJOINT;
  (c) w(T) = SUM_j w(T_j), and every w(T_j) is a CONNECTED weight.

  PROOF. (a) The completion of a chord set is the unique even
  subgraph having that chord set (495.0); Z_j is an even subgraph
  with chord set T_j, so Z_j = Z(T_j).
  (b) Since T is the disjoint union of the T_j, f_T = SUM_j f_{T_j}
  over GF(2). Suppose two supports met at a position i. Then the host
  edge at i lies in Z(T_i) and in Z(T_j), hence in Z(T) twice, hence
  cancels and lies in NEITHER - contradicting (a).
  (c) By (a) and (b) the edge sets of the Z_j partition that of Z(T),
  and each T_j is connected by construction. QED

  VERIFIED, once: over every chord subset of every girth-5 open
  ladder at 2N = 12 and 14 - 102726 subsets - additivity holds
  102726 times and the supports are disjoint 102726 times.

  COROLLARY 1. Every weight is a sum of connected weights with
  disjoint parity supports. THE CONNECTED WEIGHTS ARE THE ATOMS OF
  THE WEIGHT SET UNDER DISJOINT ADDITION.

  COROLLARY 2. Each atom has wt(f) at least 4 by girth, so any
  decomposition has at most (2N-1)/4 parts; and since the parity
  support of a set of j chords is a union of j blocks, |T_j| <=
  wt(f_{T_j}), whence w(T_j) <= 2 wt(f_{T_j}) and

        SUM over atoms of w  <=  4N - 2 .

### 525.2 THE LOCALIZATION: THE DIFFICULTY IS ENTIRELY CONNECTIVITY

Three facts now line up, and together they say where not to look.

  THE WEIGHTS ARE FREE. 495 proves the weight set fills an interval
  ending at 2N: the complement of a disjoint family has weight 2N
  minus a subset sum of 0s, 1s and 2s.

  THE FILTER IS SEVERE. 497.0 refutes (C1) by exhibiting 113 of 196
  reachable weights with NO connected representative.

  AND 525.1 EXPLAINS THE GAP. Those 113 weights are sums of atoms,
  not atoms. A weight with no connected representative is precisely a
  weight that is a non-trivial disjoint sum and nothing else.

  SO THE SEARCH SPACE HAS BEEN THE WRONG ONE. The completion calculus
  of 495-524 ranges over all 2^N chord subsets, but by 525.1 that set
  is the disjoint-sum closure of the atoms, and (LQ3) is a question
  about the atoms alone. Enumerating subsets to find atoms is
  enumerating sums to find summands. THE OBJECT IS THE CYCLE SET, NOT
  THE SUBSET LATTICE, and every enumeration in 494-524 has paid for
  the difference.

### 525.3 WHY BOUNDED SPANS IS NOT A COMBINATORIAL QUESTION

449's Ladder Question caps the spans at mu. That case is not a
smaller combinatorial problem; it is an arithmetic one, and the
reason is a pumping argument that needs no machine.

  Scan the ladder left to right and record at each cut the set of
  chords crossing it together with their relative order - the CUT
  STATE. With every span at most mu, at most mu chords cross any cut,
  so the number of cut states is bounded by a function of mu alone.
  By pigeonhole two cuts of a sufficiently long ladder carry the same
  state, and the segment between them may be excised or repeated:
  girth-legality is local and survives, so the family of girth-legal
  ladders of span cap mu is EVENTUALLY PERIODIC, with some period d.
  Excising or repeating shifts the affected cycle lengths by
  multiples of d.

  HENCE the cycle lengths available across that family lie in
  arithmetic progressions of common difference d, and asking whether
  such a progression contains a power of two IS 443's LINEAR-
  CONGRUENCE COVERING QUESTION. That is why 449's Ladder Question and
  (LQ3) resist in the same way, and why 524.1's measured bound grows
  with mu: a larger span cap is a larger state space and a longer
  period.

  THE HONEST LIMIT OF THE ARGUMENT. Pumping changes the graph, so by
  (N15) LENGTH RIGIDITY it transports no power-of-two cycle from one
  member of the family to another. It classifies the family; it does
  not prove the statement. What it does establish is the KIND of
  statement (LQ3) is at bounded span, and the answer is: arithmetic,
  not combinatorial - which is 516.0's factorisation seen once more.

### 525.4 WHAT A PROOF SHOULD AND SHOULD NOT TARGET

  DO NOT target the weight set. It is free (495) and carries no
  information.

  DO NOT enumerate chord subsets. By 525.1 every non-atom is a
  disjoint sum of atoms, so the subset lattice is a redundant
  encoding of the cycle set, exponentially larger than it.

  DO NOT locate the power of two. (N16), now with a cubic witness
  (523.0) and a second at girth 6 (524.0).

  DO target the ATOMS, and the only quantity about them that is both
  necessary and not yet bounded from below is their DENSITY IN A
  DYADIC WINDOW. By 517.2 the expected number of cycles of length in
  [x, 2x] is SUM_{m in [x,2x]} 2^m / 2m, which is astronomically
  large; what is missing is not abundance but a theorem asserting it
  for every ladder rather than on average. The clean form is

    (ATOM) every girth-legal ladder has a connected completion of
           weight in [x, 2x] for every x with g <= 2x <= c,

  which is (N9)-safe, (N16)-safe - it names no power of two - and
  implies (LQ3) at once, since every interval [x, 2x] contains one.

  AND THE ONE STRUCTURAL LEVER 525.1 HANDS OVER. An atom of weight w
  and an atom of weight w' with disjoint parity supports sum to an
  atom-free weight w + w'; but two atoms whose supports OVERLAP do
  not decompose, and their symmetric difference is again a single
  cycle when they meet in a path (518.2). So the atoms are closed
  under the difference operation and generate the weight set under
  disjoint addition: TWO OPERATIONS, ONE THAT STAYS INSIDE THE ATOMS
  AND ONE THAT LEAVES THEM. A proof of (ATOM) should use the first
  and avoid the second, and no section of 494-524 has separated them.

### 525.5 STATUS

PROVED here: THE DECOMPOSITION THEOREM - the components of a
completion are themselves completions, their prefix-parity supports
are pairwise disjoint, and weight is additive over them; hence the
connected weights are the ATOMS of the weight set under disjoint
addition, every decomposition has at most (2N-1)/4 parts, and the
total atom weight is at most 4N - 2. And the algebraic form
w(T) = |T| + wt(f_T), exhibiting (LQ3) as a question about the
input-output weight enumerator of an interval code.

COMPUTED, once and no more: additivity and support-disjointness on
all 102726 chord subsets of all girth-5 open ladders at 2N = 12
and 14, with no exception.

IDENTIFIED: that the entire difficulty of (LQ3) is the CONNECTIVITY
FILTER, not the weights - 495 makes the weight set an interval and
497.0's 113 unreachable weights are exactly the ones that are sums
rather than atoms; that the subset lattice is therefore a redundant
encoding, exponentially larger than the cycle set the statement is
about, which is what every enumeration since 494 has been paying
for; and that (LQ3) at bounded span is not combinatorial at all - a
pumping argument makes it an arithmetic-progression question, hence
443's linear-congruence Covering Question, which is why 449's Ladder
Question resists identically and why 524.1's bound grows with mu.

NOT PROVED: (ATOM); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3)
at girth 5; (B); (C), (D), (E); the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the
five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked for
theory rather than search, the useful output is a decomposition and a
diagnosis. The decomposition is that a completion's components are
completions with disjoint parity supports, so the connected weights
are the atoms of everything else; the diagnosis is that the archive
has spent thirty sections enumerating the disjoint-sum closure of the
set it actually cares about, which is why the weights came for free
and the connectivity never did. What follows is a target that names
nothing and asks for abundance rather than location - a connected
completion in every dyadic window - and one structural lever, that
the atoms are closed under difference and only leave themselves under
disjoint addition. Separating those two operations is the piece of
theory that 494 through 524 never had.


## 526. (ATOM) IS FALSE, AND IT WAS THE WRONG END OF THE SPECTRUM.
## THE TARGET MOVES TO THE CIRCUMFERENCE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Set to prove (ATOM),
this section instead corrects a false implication recorded in 525.4,
refutes (ATOM) by construction, explains why it had to fail, and
replaces it with a statement anchored at the other end of the
spectrum which does imply (LQ3) and which nothing on the archive's
books refutes. Machine: scratch conn526.py, gap526.py - two runs and
a check, no sweep.

### 526.0 CORRECTION (374.1, LOUDLY): (ATOM) DOES NOT IMPLY (LQ3)

525.4 states (ATOM) - a connected completion of weight in [x, 2x] for
every admissible x - and asserts that it "implies (LQ3) at once,
since every interval [x, 2x] contains one". THE SECOND HALF IS TRUE
AND THE IMPLICATION IS FALSE. Every interval [x, 2x] does contain a
power of two, but (ATOM) says only that the spectrum MEETS the
interval, not that it contains the power of two lying in it. A
spectrum can meet every dyadic window and contain no power of two -
507.0's witness meets every window and its only power of two is 16,
which it happens to contain, but nothing in (ATOM) delivers that.

  The correct reading: (ATOM) is a statement about GAPS, and (LQ3) is
  a statement about a POINT. No gap condition implies a point
  condition. 525.4 is corrected here.

### 526.1 WHAT (ATOM) ACTUALLY SAYS (PROVED)

Write the spectrum as l_1 = g < l_2 < ... < l_r = c.

  PROPOSITION. (ATOM) holds if and only if no consecutive pair
  satisfies l_{i+1} >= 2 l_i + 2.
  PROOF. Suppose no such pair. Given x with g <= 2x <= c: if x <= g
  then g is in [x, 2x]; otherwise let l_i be the largest spectrum
  element below x, which is not c since l_i < x <= c/2, so l_{i+1}
  exists, and l_{i+1} >= x while l_{i+1} <= 2 l_i + 1 < 2x. Conversely
  if l_{i+1} >= 2 l_i + 2, take x = l_i + 1; then 2x = 2 l_i + 2 <=
  l_{i+1} <= c and 2x >= g, and the spectrum misses [x, 2x]. QED

  SO (ATOM) IS A NO-RATIO-2-GAP CONDITION on the cycle spectrum. That
  is a much stronger reading than "abundance in every window", and it
  is what makes it refutable.

### 526.2 (ATOM) IS FALSE (REFUTED, BY CONSTRUCTION)

  THEOREM. There is a cubic graph of girth 5 whose cycle spectrum is
  {5} together with lengths at least 13. It fails (ATOM) at x = 6.

  CONSTRUCTION. Let H be a cubic graph of girth at least 27; such
