  contained in I, is self-matched, and is a proper block strictly
  inside I. If it is the OUTER arc then, f being a chord of I, both
  ends of f lie in (max A, 2m]; and (max A, 2m] IS ITSELF
  SELF-MATCHED, since every A-endpoint is at most max A, so any
  chord meeting (max A, 2m] is not in A, hence lies in one arc,
  necessarily the outer one, and being a chord of I has both ends in
  (max A, 2m]. That set is again a proper block strictly inside I.
  Either way minimality is contradicted. QED

  Lemma A stands as stated; only its third sentence needed the case
  split. Lemmas B and C and the theorem of 534.4 are unaffected.

### 535.1 THE BRIDGE DECOMPOSITION (PROVED)

Let a closed ladder split into complementary blocks I = [1, 2m] and
J = [2m+1, 2N]. The two host edges (2m, 2m+1) and (2N, 1) are the
only edges between the sides, so every cycle uses BOTH or NEITHER.

  Write C_I for the cycles living inside the I-side - the host path
  1..2m together with I's chords - and P_I for the set of lengths of
  simple paths in that side joining its two extreme vertices 1 and
  2m; likewise C_J and P_J. Then

    SPECTRUM  =  C_I  u  C_J  u  { 2 + p + q : p in P_I, q in P_J }.

  Equivalently, writing D_I = { 2m - 1 - p : p in P_I } for the
  DESCENTS of the side, and D_J likewise, the through-cycles are

    2N  -  ( D_I + D_J ) ,   a SUMSET of two independent sets.

  VERIFIED as exact set equality against brute-force enumeration of
  every simple cycle, on 16 assemblies at 2N = 24 and 2N = 26 - 16
  agreements, 0 mismatches.

### 535.2 THE MECHANISMS COMPOSE ACROSS A BLOCK (PROVED)

What sits in a descent set:

    0                    the host path;
    s_e - 1              path 1..a_e, chord e, b_e..2m - the saving
                         of 528.0, one chord at a time;
    sums of s_e - 1      over a disjoint family, the full shortcut;
    L^1 - 2              for a CROSSING pair (e, f): the path
                         1..a_e, chord e, down from b_e to a_f,
                         chord f, up from b_f to 2m, whose length is
                         2m + 1 - L^1.

  And every block HAS a crossing pair: a non-crossing perfect
  matching of an interval has an inclusion-minimal chord with no
  endpoint in its interior, hence of span 1, against span >= 4.

  THE POINT IS THE SUMSET. A crossing pair in I together with a
  crossing pair in J gives a cycle of length 2N + 4 - L^1_I - L^1_J.
  NO SECTION BEFORE THIS COULD PRODUCE THAT CYCLE: 528 through 533
  ran one mechanism at a time on one chord diagram, and 529.0's
  confinement is a statement about a single subset-sum set. Across a
  block the archive gets TWO of them, independent, and 534.4's
  Lemma B supplies each side with its own escaping crossing pair.
  Blocked ladders are therefore not the hard case - they are the
  case with twice the machinery.

### 535.3 CONNECTIVITY RESTORED AS A NORMALISATION (PROVED)

Call (OPEN) the statement that every legal open ladder - a perfect
matching of [1, 2M] with spans at least 4 and non-disjoint pairs at
L^1 distance at least 3, on the host PATH - has a cycle of
power-of-two length.

  (i) A legal CLOSED ladder minus one host edge is a legal OPEN
  ladder on the same 2N points, since spans at least 4 and
  non-disjoint L^1 at least 3 are precisely what girth 5 supplies,
  and its cycles are cycles of the closed ladder. SO (OPEN) IMPLIES
  (LQ3).

  (ii) A proper block of an open ladder is a smaller legal open
  ladder, and every cycle of it is a cycle of the whole. So a
  MINIMAL counterexample to (OPEN) has no proper block.

  (iii) By the argument of 535.0 in its linear form, no proper block
  means the crossing graph is CONNECTED.

  THEOREM. (OPEN) restricted to PRIME open ladders - those with
  connected crossing graph - implies (OPEN), hence (LQ3),
  equivalently (K4), hence Erdos-Gyarfas for 3-connected cubic
  graphs of girth 5.

  SO THE HYPOTHESIS 534 REFUTED IS AVAILABLE AGAIN. Not as a fact
  about ladders, which it is not and which 534.2 settled with a
  witness on 24 vertices, but as a normalisation of the minimal
  counterexample. The price is named and it is real: (OPEN) is
  STRICTLY STRONGER than (LQ3), being the same question on a graph
  with two fewer edges, so this is a strengthening adopted in order
  to induct, and it may be false. What it buys is that 530.2, 532.0
  and 533.1 may be run with their ORIGINAL hypothesis satisfied.

### 535.4 WHAT IS SETTLED OUTRIGHT (COMPUTED)

Exhaustively, over every legal open ladder up to 18 points:

    2m = 12        34 ladders      0 without a power-of-two cycle
    2m = 14       792              0
    2m = 16     15306              0
    2m = 18    301832              0

  317964 objects, no exception; the target is 8 at 12 and 14, and 8
  or 16 above. Two unconditional consequences.

  FIRST: any legal closed ladder with a proper block of at most 18
  points satisfies (LQ3), whatever its own size.

  SECOND, and this closes 534's own counterexample class at both
  sizes where it exists: at 2N = 24 the blocks must be 12 + 12 and at
  2N = 26 they must be 12 + 14, by 534.1. So the ENTIRE disconnected
  class - 12 x 34 x 34 = 13872 ladders at 2N = 24 and
  26 x 34 x 792 = 700128 at 2N = 26 - satisfies (LQ3). These are
  complete enumerations of the class and not samples, and legality is
  automatic: the only cross-side constraint is s_e + s_f <= 2N - 3,
  and the largest span is 9 in a legal 12-block and 13 in a legal
  14-block.

### 535.5 AND THE SWEEP IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR (OPEN)

534.5's rule applies to 535.4 as much as to anything else. Counting
octagons over the same 317964 ladders:

    2m = 12    min 4    mean  7.88    max 12
    2m = 14    min 4    mean 10.65    max 21
    2m = 16    min 5    mean 12.60    max 25
    2m = 18    min 4    mean 13.74    max 38

  THE MEAN GROWS AND THE MINIMUM DOES NOT. That is 517.2's
  first-moment law seen directly: the average is Theta(n) while the
  extremal object sits a constant above zero, so a sweep that reports
  "no exceptions" is measuring the average and not the extremum.
  524.4's witness - a cubic graph on 30 vertices of girth 6 with ZERO
  octagons - puts the honest threshold near 2m = 30, not 18. So 535.4
  is a theorem about ladders up to 18 points and NOT evidence for
  (OPEN) at large sizes.

  WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT is whether an octagon-free open ladder also
  misses 16. The archive already has the relevant datum and it points
  the other way: 524.4's zero-octagon witness carried 956
  sixteen-cycles, and 523.0's carried 1161.

### 535.6 STATUS

CORRECTED (374.1): one sentence of 534.4's Lemma A - "every
remaining chord lies in an arc whose interior is contained in I" - is
false for the arc running outside the block. The repair is the case
split of 535.0: a leftover chord in the outer arc has both ends in
(max A, 2m], and that set is itself self-matched. Lemma A, Lemma B,
Lemma C and 534.4's theorem all stand.

PROVED here: THE BRIDGE DECOMPOSITION - for a ladder split into
complementary blocks the spectrum is C_I u C_J u (2 + P_I + P_J),
equivalently the through-cycles are 2N - (D_I + D_J) for the two
descent sets. That the descents contain 0, the savings s_e - 1, their
disjoint sums, and L^1 - 2 for every crossing pair, and that every
block has a crossing pair. And THE REDUCTION: (OPEN) implies (LQ3)
because a closed ladder minus a host edge is an open ladder; a proper
block of an open ladder is a smaller one; hence a minimal
counterexample to (OPEN) is prime, its crossing graph is connected,
and (OPEN) for prime open ladders implies Erdos-Gyarfas for
3-connected cubic graphs of girth 5.

COMPUTED: the bridge decomposition against brute force on 16
assemblies, exact set equality, 0 mismatches; every legal open ladder
on 12, 14, 16 and 18 points has a power-of-two cycle - 34, 792, 15306
and 301832 ladders, 317964 in all, 0 exceptions; hence the whole
disconnected class satisfies (LQ3) at 2N = 24 (13872 ladders) and at
2N = 26 (700128), both complete enumerations; and the octagon counts
whose MINIMUM is flat at 4, 4, 5, 4 while the mean runs 7.88, 10.65,
12.60, 13.74.

NOT PROVED: (OPEN), at any size above 18; (OPEN) for prime open
ladders; the passage from two residue classes to a run; the
uniform-ladder classification; (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4);
(LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7;
the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The repair
survives audit with one sentence rewritten, and it turns out to be
worth more than the classification it was built to save. A block cuts
the ladder at exactly two host edges, so every cycle uses both or
neither, and the spectrum becomes a sumset of two independent descent
sets - the first place in the archive where two escape mechanisms
compose instead of competing. That makes blocked ladders the easy
case, and the reduction says so twice over: their blocks are smaller
legal open ladders, so a minimal counterexample to the open form of
the question has no block at all and therefore has a connected
crossing graph. The hypothesis 534 killed is back as a normalisation.
What is bought is not a proof - (OPEN) is stronger than what it
implies and may be false - but the right shape of one, and what is
settled outright is every ladder whose block has at most 18 points,
which is the whole of the class 534 constructed. The remaining
frontier is unchanged in substance and clearer in position: prime
ladders, where 533.4(b)'s Covering Question and 517.3's O(1) barrier
are the only things left.


## 536. (COVER) IS FALSE, (COVER-2) IS THE TARGET, AND THE
## SEPARATION-ONLY BARRIER

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 535 named the covering
property as the one condition that would collide with a
counterexample. This section kills it as stated, repairs it, and then
proves the structural fact that decides how it must be attacked: the
girth conditions are separations, covering needs saturation, and no
theorem of the first kind can ever imply one of the second. Machine:
scratch (the 36-vertex spectrum, one run; two censuses still running).

### 536.0 (COVER) IS FALSE (REFUTED, 374.1)

  (COVER) said: the spectrum contains a full interval [a, 2a].

  IT IS FALSE ON AN INFINITE FAMILY. For a >= 2 the interval [a, 2a]
  contains an odd number, and a BIPARTITE ladder has no odd cycle at
  all. By 504.2 all spans odd is exactly bipartiteness, and 533.3
  counted 104 such ladders at 2N <= 18 alone. For a = 1 the interval
  is [1,2], below the girth. So (COVER) fails for every bipartite
  ladder, and it was proposed one turn after 535.5 warned that a
  sweep is not evidence - the sweep in that case was two graphs.

  THE REASON IS WORTH MORE THAN THE STATEMENT. Odd lengths are not
  robust; bipartiteness deletes all of them at once. This is why
  every consecutive-length theorem in the literature is stated for
  consecutive EVEN lengths, and the repair is forced:

  (COVER-2) The spectrum contains every EVEN length in some interval
            [a, 2a].

  (COVER-2) IMPLIES (LQ3): every [a, 2a] contains a power of two,
  and every power of two above 1 is even. Unlike (ATOM) of 525.4,
  which 526.0 corrected, this is a containment and not a meeting, so
  the implication is real.

### 536.1 THE TWO-CHORD SPECTRUM IS A DIFFERENCE SET (PROVED)

Read 530.0's residue laws as identities rather than congruences.
With the position sum phi = a + b,

    crossing pair (e, f):   length  2 + |phi_f - phi_e|
    nested pair   (e, f):   length  2 + |s_e - s_f|

so, fixing a chord e, the two-chord cycle lengths through e are a
TRANSLATE of the position sums of the chords crossing e - the
partners above phi_e translated by 2 - phi_e, those below reflected -
and the two-chord part of the whole spectrum is

    2 + { crossing differences of PHI }  u  2 + { nested
                                                 differences of S }

where PHI is the multiset of position sums and S the multiset of
spans. SO (COVER-2), AT THE TWO-CHORD LEVEL, IS EXACTLY THE QUESTION
WHEN DOES A DIFFERENCE SET CONTAIN AN INTERVAL.

### 536.2 (N17) THE SEPARATION-ONLY BARRIER (PROVED)

  OBSERVATION. Girth-legality is DOWNWARD CLOSED. Deleting a chord
  from a legal ladder leaves a legal partial ladder, because every
  condition - span at least 4, non-disjoint pairs at L^1 at least 3 -
  is a condition on chords that remain.

  (N17) THE SEPARATION-ONLY BARRIER. No statement about the cycle
        spectrum beyond the one-chord level can follow from the
        girth conditions alone. Every such theorem must use that the
        matching is PERFECT.
    PROOF. A statement implied by the girth conditions alone holds of
  every sub-family, since those conditions are downward closed. The
  sub-family consisting of a single chord e is legal, and the entire
  spectrum of that partial ladder is {s_e + 1, 2N - s_e + 1}. QED

  THE BARRIER IS NOT ABSTRACT - IT SORTS THE RECORD EXACTLY. Every
  lemma of 529 to 535 that survived uses perfectness:

    530.1  the Endpoint Lemma - the endpoints ARE [1, 2N];
    533.0  the parity lemma   - vertex 2 must be matched;
    534.1  the block bound    - an arc is matched within itself;
    535.3  the reduction      - a block is a perfect sub-matching.

  and every attempt that failed used only separations: 528.2's
  inequality, 529's subset sums, and every additive tool named in
  532.2, whose hypotheses are lower bounds on the number of distinct
  summands. SO 532.2's FINDING THAT "THE HYPOTHESIS IS FALSE" WAS A
  SYMPTOM AND NOT THE DISEASE. Separations cannot cover. Only
  saturation can.

  CONFIRMED FROM OUTSIDE. The one theorem in the literature that
  bounds a GAP at degree three - Bondy and Vince, two cycles whose
  lengths differ by one or two - is a minimum-degree theorem, that is
  a saturation theorem, not a separation one.

### 536.3 THE DENSITY IS EXACTLY EXTREMAL (PROVED)

The pigeonhole for difference sets: if A lies in an interval of
length M then A - A contains every t with t < 2|A| - M, since A and
A + t both lie in an interval of length M + t and must meet.

    PHI, the position sums:  N values in [3, 4N-1].  Density 1/4.
                             2|PHI| - M = -2N.  Nothing.
    A, the LEFT ENDPOINTS:   exactly N values in [1, 2N].
                             DENSITY EXACTLY 1/2, and 2|A| - M = 0.

  THE LADDER SITS EXACTLY ON THE PIGEONHOLE'S BOUNDARY, and the bound
  degenerates to nothing at precisely that density. It is also tight
  there: the extremal sets of density 1/2 are the parity classes, and
  the difference set of a parity class is the even numbers, missing
  every odd number.

  AND THE EXTREMAL SET IS EXACTLY WHAT 533.0 FORBIDS. Vertex 1 is a
  left endpoint and is odd, so if A were a parity class it would be
  the ODDS; then every right endpoint is even, every span is odd, and
  the ladder is bipartite by 504.2 - and 533.0 proves that the left
  endpoints of a bipartite ladder take BOTH parities. So A IS NEVER A
  PARITY CLASS. The parity lemma, recorded in 533 as a step in the
  confinement classification, is in this light THE FIRST CASE OF AN
  INVERSE THEOREM: it removes the unique extremal configuration for
  the difference-set pigeonhole.

  AND THERE ARE NO OTHERS OF ITS KIND. A union of k complete residue
  classes mod d inside [1, 2N] has 2kN/d elements, which equals N
  only when k = d/2. So A can be a union of complete classes ONLY for
  EVEN d, taking exactly half of them, and d = 2 is 533.0's case.

### 536.4 WHAT (COVER-2) HAS BECOME

Three statements, each now precise.

  (i) It is an INVERSE PROBLEM, not a direct one. The pigeonhole
  cannot reach it at density 1/2, so the content is: if the
  difference set misses an interval then A is structured, and the
  structure must then be shown incompatible with girth and matching.
  536.3 does the d = 2 case.

  (ii) THE CONFINEMENT OF 529 AND THE FAILURE OF (COVER-2) ARE THE
  SAME OBSTRUCTION SEEN FROM TWO SIDES. A structured A gives a
  difference set inside few residue classes, which is a spectrum
  confined modulo d, which is exactly 529.0. 530 to 534 destroyed
  that confinement at every d, so the first layer of the inverse
  theorem is already proved; what is missing is the QUANTITATIVE
  layer, where A is merely close to structured.

  (iii) THE DICHOTOMY IS 532.3's, ARRIVED AT FROM THE OTHER
  DIRECTION. Unstructured position sums cover; structured ones force
  the uniform ladder, which 532.3 says is a signed shift and finite
  in shape. That two independent routes end at the same split is the
  strongest reason yet to believe the split is intrinsic and to
  finish the uniform case by hand.

  AND ONE INSTRUMENT IS AVAILABLE THAT THE ARCHIVE HAS NEVER USED.
  By the subgraph argument of 536.5, a cubic graph has no proper
  subgraph of minimum degree 3, so Bondy-Vince applies to a ladder
  exactly once. But its stronger form tolerates two vertices of
  degree 2, and deleting one chord creates exactly two. SO
  BONDY-VINCE APPLIES N + 1 TIMES TO A LADDER WITH N CHORDS - once to
  G and once to each G - e - and each application returns two cycle
  lengths differing by one or two. It is the only source of an UPPER
  bound on a gap at degree three.

### 536.5 THE SUBGRAPH FACT, AND WHY INDUCTION ON SIZE IS BARRED

  PROPOSITION. A connected cubic graph has no proper subgraph that is
  itself cubic.
    PROOF. If H is a subgraph of G with every H-vertex of H-degree 3,
  then each such vertex already has all three of its G-edges in H, so
  V(H) is closed under adjacency; G connected forces H = G. QED

  COROLLARY. A closed ladder contains no smaller closed ladder. Since
  a power of two is an absolute value, only cycle-length-preserving
  reductions can carry it, and only subgraphs preserve cycle lengths;
  so INDUCTION ON 2N INSIDE THE CLOSED CLASS IS IMPOSSIBLE, not
  merely hard. Any induction must leave the class by admitting
  degree-2 vertices - which is what 535.3 did, and why the statement
  it reached was stronger than (LQ3) rather than equal to it.

  WHAT REMAINS AVAILABLE is the recursion that does not shrink:
  fix the host cycle and add chords one at a time, so that
  Spec(L_{k+1}) = Spec(L_k) u (1 + P_k), where P_k is the set of path
  lengths between the new chord's endpoints. It is monotone, so it
  suffices for ANY intermediate stage to reach a power of two, and it
  is the same path-spectrum instrument as 535.1's descent sets.

### 536.6 VERIFIED

  THE 36-VERTEX GIRTH-7 WITNESS of 523.0, the archive's hardest
  object, has cycle spectrum

      {7} u [9, 36]

  - a single hole, at 8. Its largest fully contained window is
  [18, 36], and it holds both 16 and 32. So the object that refuted
  (E_3) and (LC) satisfies (COVER-2) with room to spare, and misses
  being pancyclic above its girth by one length.

  NOT YET MEASURED: (COVER-2) over the exhaustive censuses at
  2N = 12 to 18, and the search for a legal open ladder missing both
  8 and 16, both still running at the time of writing. Nothing in
  this section depends on either.

### 536.7 STATUS

REFUTED here (374.1): (COVER), by every bipartite ladder - [a, 2a]
contains an odd number for a >= 2, a bipartite ladder has no odd
cycle, and 504.2 with 533.3 supply 104 such ladders at 2N <= 18
alone.

PROVED here: that (COVER-2), the even-length form, does imply (LQ3),
since every [a, 2a] holds a power of two and every power of two above
1 is even. THE DIFFERENCE-SET IDENTITY - the two-chord spectrum is
2 + the crossing differences of the position sums together with 2 +
the nested differences of the spans, so through a fixed chord the
lengths are a translate of its crossing partners' position sums.
(N17) THE SEPARATION-ONLY BARRIER - girth-legality is downward closed
and a one-chord partial ladder is legal with a two-element spectrum,
so no spectrum statement beyond the one-chord level follows from the
girth conditions alone; every such theorem must use perfectness.
THE DENSITY COMPUTATION - the position sums have density 1/4 and the
left endpoints density exactly 1/2, where the difference-set
pigeonhole degenerates to nothing and is tight, its unique extremal
configuration being a parity class - which 533.0 forbids, so the
parity lemma is the first case of an inverse theorem; and A can be a
union of complete residue classes only for even d, taking half of
them. AND THE SUBGRAPH FACT - a connected cubic graph has no proper
cubic subgraph, so a closed ladder contains no smaller closed ladder
and induction on 2N inside the class is impossible.

VERIFIED (388.1, from search listings rather than the papers, and
described by shape rather than quoted): J. A. Bondy and A. Vince,
"Cycles in a graph whose lengths differ by one or two" - a graph of
minimum degree at least three, and more strongly one in which all but
at most two vertices have degree at least three, contains two cycles
whose lengths differ by one or two; this was conjectured by Erdos.
And B. Sudakov and J. Verstraete, "Cycle lengths in sparse graphs" -
a graph of average degree d and girth g has Omega(d^floor((g-1)/2))
distinct cycle lengths. Also recorded, by shape: Fan's bound
f(k) <= 3*ceil(k/2) on the minimum degree needed for k cycles of
consecutive lengths, and Verstraete's average-degree 8k for k
consecutive even lengths - both of which give nothing at degree
three, which is why no stack of them collides with a counterexample.

COMPUTED: the 36-vertex girth-7 witness of 523.0 has spectrum
{7} u [9, 36] - one hole, at 8 - largest contained window [18, 36],
and contains 16 and 32.

NOT PROVED: (COVER-2); the quantitative inverse theorem; the
uniform-ladder classification; the passage from two residue classes
to a run; (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at
girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements of
451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The covering
property as proposed was false within a turn, killed by the bipartite
ladders, and the repair to even lengths is exactly the form the
literature has always used - which is itself the evidence that the
even form is the right one. What the section buys is not the target
but the aim. The two-chord spectrum is a difference set of position
sums; covering a window is therefore an inverse additive question;
the ladder's left endpoints have density exactly one half, which is
precisely where the difference-set pigeonhole dies and precisely
where its extremal configuration is a parity class - the one
configuration 533.0 already forbids. And (N17) explains the whole
shape of the last eight sections: girth gives separations, covering
needs saturation, no separation implies a covering, and every lemma
that survived used the perfectness of the matching while every one
that failed used only the spans. The instruments were not too weak.
They were of the wrong kind.


## 537. (OPEN) SURVIVES ITS HARD CASE, AND THE UNIFORM LADDER IS
## CLASSIFIED

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Returning to (OPEN) for
prime open ladders, this section reports the search that tests it
where it can fail, corrects 535.5's reading of the evidence, and then
settles the structured extreme that 532.3 named and 536.4 confirmed
from the other direction: the uniform ladder is one graph per size
and odd span, and its power of two can never come from where the
archive would first look. Machine: scratch path535.py, prime536.py,
openlq535.py.

### 537.0 THE MECHANISM IS SHALLOW (COMPUTED)

Least number of chords used by a power-of-two cycle, over every legal
open ladder:

    2m = 12      1 chord   22     2 chords   12
    2m = 14      1 chord  487     2 chords  291    3 chords   14
    2m = 16      1 chord 9847     2 chords 5339    3 chords  120

and restricted to the PRIME ladders the maxima are the same, 2 and 3
and 3. So in this range the target is reached at the level of spans
and position sums - 536.1's difference-set frame - in better than 99
per cent of cases, and never needs four chords.

### 537.1 (OPEN) SURVIVES ITS HARD CASE (COMPUTED, AND 374.1)

A pruned search over legal open ladders, rejecting any partial
matching that already closes an 8-cycle or a 16-cycle - valid, since
adding chords only adds cycles - returns NOTHING at 2m = 12, 14, 16,
18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28 and 30. No legal open ladder on at most 30
points misses both 8 and 16.

  AND THE RANGE IS THE RIGHT ONE THIS TIME. 536 exhibited an
  octagon-free legal open ladder on 24 points, prime and of girth 5,
  and proved by exhaustive search that none exists below 24. So on
  24, 26, 28 and 30 the octagon-free class is NON-EMPTY, and every
  member of it carries a 16-cycle.

  CORRECTED (374.1). 535.5 read the flat octagon minimum - 4, 4, 5, 4
  across 2m = 12 to 18 - as ground for doubting (OPEN), and that
  reading steered the programme off it. The reading was right about
  the sweep and wrong about the conclusion: the sweep was
  uninformative because the threshold is 24, but above the threshold
  the statement holds. 523.0's own witness fits the same pattern -
  zero octagons on 36 vertices, and 805 sixteen-cycles once cut open.

  SO 535.3's REDUCTION IS A LIVE ROUTE: (OPEN) for prime open ladders
  implies (OPEN), hence (LQ3), hence (K4), hence Erdos-Gyarfas for
  3-connected cubic graphs of girth 5 - and it is the only route that
  recovers the connected-crossing-graph hypothesis legitimately.

### 537.2 THE UNIFORM LADDER IS CLASSIFIED (PROVED)

  THEOREM. Let a closed ladder have every circular span equal to s,
  and let A be the set of i with sigma(i) = i + s, so that A and
  A + s are disjoint with union Z_{2N} and |A| = N.
    (i)   No two elements of A are cyclically adjacent: the chords
          {i, i+s} and {i+1, i+1+s} interleave, so they cross, and
          their L^1 is 1 + 1 = 2, against girth 5.
    (ii)  So A is an independent set of size N in the cycle C_{2N};
          the only ones are the two alternating classes, the evens
          and the odds.
    (iii) Hence s is ODD, since A + s must be the complementary
          class, and adding an even number to the odds returns the
          odds.
    (iv)  Therefore, up to rotation, the chord set is exactly
          {{i, i+s} : i odd}. FOR EACH 2N AND EACH ODD s THE
          GIRTH-LEGAL UNIFORM LADDER IS UNIQUE.

  THIS CLOSES 533.4(c) AND 536.4(iii). 532.3 said the uniform family
  was a signed shift, finite in shape and classifiable by hand rather
  than estimated. It is one ladder per size and odd span.

### 537.3 WHERE A UNIFORM LADDER'S POWER OF TWO CANNOT COME FROM
### (PROVED)

Two chords of a uniform ladder are translates of one another:
{i, i+s} and {i+d, i+d+s} with i and i+d both in A. By 537.2(ii) A is
a parity class, SO d IS EVEN. They cross exactly when 0 < d < s, and
then L^1 = 2d, so the pair carries cycles of lengths

        2 + 2d        and        2N + 2 - 2d .

  COROLLARY. 2 + 2d with d even is 2 mod 4, while every power of two
  above 2 is 0 mod 4. SO A UNIFORM LADDER NEVER TAKES ITS POWER OF
  TWO FROM A SHORT TWO-CHORD CYCLE. It must come from a single chord,
  s + 1 or 2N - s + 1, or from the LONG cycle 2N + 2 - 2d of a
  crossing pair, or from three chords or more.

  532.1's spectra are now explained rather than observed. At 2N = 14,
  s = 5 the spectrum 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 splits exactly as the theorem
  says: the short cycles 6 and 10, both 2 mod 4 and neither a power
  of two, the long cycles 12 and 8, and the host 14.

### 537.4 BUT TWO CHORDS DO NOT DETERMINE THE SPECTRUM (CORRECTED)

The natural next guess - that the lengths of 537.3 together with the
host are the WHOLE spectrum of a uniform ladder - is FALSE. Over the
32 girth-legal uniform ladders at 2N <= 26 it is right 5 times and
wrong 27, always by omission; the extra lengths need three chords or
more, exactly as 537.0 says they must.

  Recorded because 2N = 14 fits the guess perfectly and would have
  carried it on its own. One graph, again.

### 537.5 COMPUTED

  224 girth-legal uniform ladders over 2N = 12 to 40, obtained from
  the coset rule - the subgroup generated by s has gcd(s, 2N) cosets,
  each a cycle under i -> i + s which must have even length and be
  matched alternately, giving 2^gcd(s,2N) candidates per pair and
  4931 in all - and EVERY ONE of the 224 has a power-of-two cycle, 0
  exceptions.

  Independently, 32 girth-legal uniform ladders at 2N <= 26 built
  directly from 537.2(iv)'s classification, likewise all with a power
  of two.

  STILL RUNNING at the time of writing: (COVER-2) over the exhaustive
  censuses at 2N = 12 to 18. Nothing here depends on it.

### 537.6 STATUS

PROVED here: THE UNIFORM LADDER CLASSIFICATION - if every circular
span equals s then the set A of i with sigma(i) = i + s has no two
cyclically adjacent members, hence is an independent set of size N in
C_{2N}, hence is the evens or the odds; therefore s is odd and the
chord set is {{i, i+s} : i odd} up to rotation, one ladder per 2N and
odd s. And THE MOD-4 COROLLARY - the two chords of a crossing pair
are translates by an EVEN amount d, so the short cycle 2 + 2d is 2
mod 4 and can never be a power of two; a uniform ladder's power of
two must come from one chord, from the long cycle 2N + 2 - 2d, or
from three chords or more.

CORRECTED (374.1): 535.5's reading that the flat octagon minimum was
ground to doubt (OPEN). The sweep it criticised was indeed
uninformative, but for a reason that cuts the other way - the
octagon-free threshold is 24, and above it (OPEN) holds on everything
tested. Also CORRECTED: the guess that the two-chord lengths and the
host exhaust a uniform ladder's spectrum, false on 27 of 32 cases.

COMPUTED: no legal open ladder on at most 30 points misses both 8 and
16, tested where the octagon-free class is non-empty (24 to 30); the
least chord count of a power-of-two cycle is at most 3 over all legal
open ladders at 2m = 12, 14, 16, and at most 2 at 2m = 12; and 224
girth-legal uniform ladders to 2N = 40, all with a power of two.

NOT PROVED: (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (OPEN) above 30 points;
(COVER-2); the quantitative inverse theorem; the passage from two
residue classes to a run; (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER
BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five
statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Two things
moved. (OPEN) was abandoned on my reading that it was probably false,
and the search that tests it in the range where it can fail says it
holds - the octagon-free ladders begin at 24 points and all of them
up to 30 carry a 16-cycle, so 535.3's reduction to PRIME open ladders
is live, and it remains the only way the connectivity hypothesis
comes back honestly. And the uniform ladder, the structured extreme
that both 532.3 and 536.4 independently identified as the hard case,
is now a single explicit graph per size and odd span, with its
crossing pairs forced to translate by an even amount and its short
two-chord cycles therefore stuck at 2 mod 4, permanently barred from
being powers of two. That is the first time the archive has been able
to say WHERE the answer is not, inside a family, for a structural
reason rather than a measured one.


## 538. WHAT WOULD SETTLE (OPEN), AND WHICH FIELD HAS THE TOOLS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked what would settle
(OPEN) for prime open ladders, and whether some other field has
definite tools for it, this section answers in four parts: the
census that pins (COVER)'s failure exactly, the specification any
proof must meet, the reformulation that makes the subject visible,
and the one field that supplies a DECISION PROCEDURE for the half of
the problem 537.2 just made explicit. Machine: scratch (census,
corrected; one run).

### 538.0 (COVER) FAILS EXACTLY ON THE BIPARTITE LADDERS (COMPUTED)

Exhaustively over girth-legal closed ladders:

    2N       ladders   bipartite   (COVER) fails   (COVER-2) fails
    12            24           0               0                 0
    14           408           2               2                 0
    16          8002           2               2                 0
    18        168802         100             100                 0

  THE FAILURE COUNT EQUALS THE BIPARTITE COUNT AT EVERY SIZE. So
  536.0's refutation is not merely correct, it is SHARP:
  bipartiteness is the whole of (COVER)'s failure set, and nothing
  else obstructs a full doubling window. The bipartite totals sum to
  0 + 2 + 2 + 100 = 104, independently reproducing 533.3's census by
  a different program. And (COVER-2), the even-length repair, fails
  on NONE of the 177236 ladders.

  CORRECTED (374.1), a machine error of my own: the first two runs of
  this census used a generator missing the guard that a candidate
  partner be unmatched, and returned "0 ladders" at every size. The
  numbers above come from the corrected generator, which reproduces
  524.3's count of 24 at 2N = 12 exactly. No conclusion was drawn
  from the void runs.

### 538.1 THE SPECIFICATION ANY PROOF MUST MEET

Five constraints, each already proved in this archive. Together they
are narrow enough to test a proposed instrument in a minute.

  (1) AN IDENTITY, NOT AN INEQUALITY. 517.3: the target is a count of
      cycles at one length, Theta(1), while every trace instrument is
      Theta(n) and the leading terms cancel identically.
  (2) SATURATION, NOT SEPARATION. (N17) of 536.2: girth-legality is
      downward closed, so nothing beyond the one-chord level follows
      from spans and L^1 alone. The proof must use that the matching
      is perfect.
  (3) SCALE-COVARIANT: A BAND, NOT A VALUE. 536 exhibits an
      octagon-free PRIME legal open ladder on 24 points and proves
      none is smaller; 523.0's witness misses 8 on 36 vertices. No
      argument aimed at a fixed length can work.
  (4) NOT LOCAL. 520.0: no Benjamini-Schramm continuous parameter
      decides the question, so no convex relaxation and no local
      statistic.
  (5) NOT AN INDUCTION ON SIZE. 536.5: a connected cubic graph has no
      proper cubic subgraph. Only the chord-adding recursion at fixed
      host survives.

### 538.2 THE REFORMULATION (PROVED)

Let T be a chord subset and let its 2|T| endpoints in cyclic order be
p_1 < p_2 < ... < p_{2|T|}. The arcs a cycle takes are alternate
gaps, and

    sum of alternate gaps
        = (p_2 - p_1) + (p_4 - p_3) + ...
        = the ALTERNATING SUM of the endpoint positions,

so the length of the cycle carried by T is

    w(T)  =  |T|  +  ALT(endpoints of T) .

This is 497.4's (LQ3) read as an identity. The subject it belongs to
is therefore: PERFECT MATCHINGS OF 2M CYCLICALLY ORDERED POINTS,
graded by an alternating functional of the matched positions, with a
global admissibility condition. That is the subject of chord diagrams
and one-face maps, not of graph theory.

### 538.3 THE STRUCTURAL HOME, AND THE OBSTRUCTION TO USING IT

The natural home is the enumeration of ONE-FACE (unicellular) MAPS: a
chord diagram on 2n points is the standard encoding of a gluing of a
2n-gon, its genus grades the family, and the subject consists almost
entirely of EXACT identities - which is what 538.1(1) demands, and
its object is a perfect matching, which is what 538.1(2) demands.

  BUT THE DICTIONARY IS NOT YET RIGHT, and 524.2 already found where.
  Euler's relation for a chord diagram counts boundary components
  using ALL arcs, whereas a cycle of the ladder uses ALTERNATE arcs;
  the two counts differ, and the mismatch is why 524.2's Euler
  attempt failed. Repairing that dictionary is a finite and concrete
  task, and it is the prerequisite for importing anything from this
  field. It is NOT the same failure as Cohn-Lempel, which 501.7,
  524.2 and 526.3 have now refuted three times and which should not
  be attempted a fourth.

### 538.4 THE DEFINITE TOOL: BUCHI ARITHMETIC ON THE STRUCTURED HALF

For the structured extreme the answer is not an analogy but a
DECISION PROCEDURE.

  "x is a power of two" is definable in the first-order theory of the
  natural numbers with addition and the base-2 valuation, and by the
  Buchi-Bruyere theorem that theory is DECIDABLE; the software Walnut
  implements the decision procedure by translating formulas into
  automata.

  AND 537.2 PUT THE UNIFORM FAMILY IN EXACTLY THE REQUIRED FORM. The
  girth-legal uniform ladder is one graph per 2N and odd s, with
  chord set {{i, i+s} : i odd}; its crossing pairs are translates by
  an even d with 0 < d < s; and the lengths it offers are the
  explicit linear expressions s + 1, 2N - s + 1, 2 + 2d,
  2N + 2 - 2d, 2N + 2 - 2s, together with the higher-chord lengths.
  The sentence

     for all 2N and all odd s in range, some admissible length is a
     power of two

  is first-order in addition and the base-2 valuation. IT IS
  THEREFORE DECIDABLE, and mechanically checkable rather than merely
  conjectural - subject only to expressing the higher-chord lengths,
  which 537.0 bounds at three chords in the measured range and which
  537.4 shows are genuinely needed.

  THIS IS THE FIRST TIME IN THE ARCHIVE THAT A NAMED SUBCASE OF THE
  CONJECTURE HAS BEEN PLACED INSIDE A DECIDABLE THEORY.

### 538.5 THE GENERIC HALF, AND WHY NO SINGLE FIELD REACHES BOTH

The generic half is not decidable-looking, and 536.3 says why: the
left endpoints have density exactly one half, the difference-set
pigeonhole degenerates there, so the content is an INVERSE theorem -
if the difference set misses a window then the endpoint set is
structured. That is Freiman and Green-Ruzsa territory, whose tools
are definite but whose hypotheses fail at degree three exactly as
532.2 found.

  AND THE DEEPER REASON NO ONE FIELD SETTLES IT IS 516.0's. The
  target factors into a 2-adic condition and an Archimedean one. The
  2-adic coordinate is a divisibility statement about cycle lengths,
  and cycle lengths are the weights of the cycle code of the graph,
  so its natural home is the theory of weight divisibility in coding
  theory. The Archimedean coordinate is a size statement and its home
  is the band theory of 518. Two coordinates, two fields, and 516.0
  proved that one column cannot close J7. THE ABSENCE OF A SINGLE
  FIELD WITH THE TOOLS IS NOT AN ACCIDENT OF SEARCH; IT IS THE
  FACTORISATION.

### 538.6 STATUS

COMPUTED: over 177236 girth-legal closed ladders at 2N = 12, 14, 16
and 18, (COVER) fails on exactly 0, 2, 2 and 100 of them and the
bipartite ladders number exactly 0, 2, 2 and 100 - the failure set of
(COVER) IS the bipartite family, and the totals reproduce 533.3's 104
by an independent program. (COVER-2) fails on none of them.

CORRECTED (374.1): two earlier runs of this census were void, their
generator missing the check that a candidate partner be unmatched;
they reported "0 ladders" and nothing was concluded from them.

IDENTIFIED: the five-part specification of 538.1 that any proof must
meet - identity not inequality, saturation not separation, a band not
a value, not local, not an induction on size. The reformulation
w(T) = |T| + ALT(endpoints of T), which places the question in the
theory of chord diagrams and one-face maps rather than graph theory.
The obstruction to importing that theory - Euler's relation counts
all arcs, a cycle uses alternate arcs, which is precisely where
524.2 failed. And the factorisation reason that no single field
reaches the whole problem.

VERIFIED (388.1, from search listings rather than the papers, and
described by shape rather than quoted): the Harer-Zagier formula for
the enumeration of one-face maps by genus, with the standard
correspondence between chord diagrams and gluings of a 2n-gon; and
the Buchi-Bruyere decidability theorem for the first-order theory of
the naturals with addition and a base-k valuation, implemented in the
automatic theorem prover Walnut, which decides first-order statements
in that theory by translation into automata.

NOT PROVED: (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); the uniform
case, though it is now decidable in principle; the quantitative
inverse theorem; (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*);
(E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements
of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The covering
question now has a sharp answer at the level of evidence -
(COVER) fails on the bipartite ladders and on nothing else, and its
even-length repair fails on nothing at all in 177236 cases. Asked
which other field has definite tools, the honest answer has two
halves. For the structured extreme, the answer is a genuine decision
procedure: powers of two are definable with addition and the base-2
valuation, that theory is decidable, and 537.2's classification of
the uniform ladder writes the whole subcase in exactly that language.
For the generic case there is no such tool, and 516.0 explains why
there cannot be one of a single kind: the target factors into a
2-adic coordinate whose home is weight divisibility and an
Archimedean coordinate whose home is band theory, and no instrument
in either column couples them. What is new is that one column now has
a machine.


## 539. REALIZATIONS IN OTHER FIELDS, THE POINTWISE FILTER, AND THE
## ONE ADDITIVE TOOL THAT SURVIVES THE UNIFORM LADDER

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked whether the
objects here are literally objects of some other subject, so that a
guaranteed theorem there transfers, this section lists the exact
realizations, adds the filter that disqualifies most of them, and
identifies the one imported theorem whose hypotheses this archive
can actually meet - the one that dissolves 532.2's objection rather
than restating it. No machine run.

### 539.0 THE EXACT REALIZATIONS

A closed ladder is the pair (rho, sigma) with rho the 2N-cycle
1, 2, ..., 2N and sigma a fixed-point-free involution. That pair IS,
verbatim and not by analogy:

  (a) A ONE-VERTEX MAP on an oriented surface - a bouquet of N loops -
      whose faces are the orbits of rho sigma and whose genus obeys
      1 - N + F = 2 - 2g. Equivalently a gluing of a 2N-gon, hence a
      dessin d'enfant, hence by Belyi an algebraic curve over a
      number field.
  (b) A BINARY LINEAR CODE: the cycle space of the graph, in which
      CYCLE LENGTHS ARE CODEWORD WEIGHTS, dual to the cut code, whose
      weight enumerator is the Ising partition function.
  (c) A METRIC GRAPH whose cycle spectrum is a LENGTH SPECTRUM, with
      the Ihara zeta function as its Selberg trace formula - which is
      452's non-backtracking frame, arrived at from geometry.
  (d) A CHORD DIAGRAM, hence a Gauss code, hence an interlacement /
      circle-graph object - Bouchet's subject, and Cohn-Lempel's,
      the latter refuted three times at 501.7, 524.2 and 526.3.

### 539.1 THE POINTWISE FILTER (IDENTIFIED)

Add to 538.1's five constraints a sixth, which disqualifies most of
539.0 at a stroke:

  (6) POINTWISE, NOT ENUMERATIVE. (OPEN) quantifies over EVERY
      ladder. Almost all exact machinery in the fields above computes
      over the FAMILY - Harer-Zagier gives the genus distribution of
      all chord diagrams, character theory gives the number of
      factorisations with a prescribed cycle type, Hurwitz numbers
      count covers. An exact average is still an average.

  THIS IS WHY 539.0(a) DOES NOT TRANSFER even after its arc-count
  mismatch is repaired, and it is the precise sense in which 517.3's
  barrier is not about inequalities alone: an identity about the
  ensemble is as useless as a bound. What survives the filter are
  DECISION PROCEDURES, which settle a universally quantified
  sentence outright - 538.4's Buchi route - and EXTREMAL GUARANTEES,
  which hold of every instance. There is exactly one family of the
  second kind that fits.

### 539.2 ZERO-SUM THEORY IS THE ADDITIVE TOOL THAT SURVIVES (IDENTIFIED)

532.2 rejected the additive programme with a single observation: every
tool named there - Szemeredi-Vu on long progressions in subset sums,
Cauchy-Davenport, Kneser - is powered by a lower bound on the number
of DISTINCT summands, and the uniform ladder of 532.1 has ONE distinct
span. That objection is fatal to those tools and it is NOT fatal to
zero-sum theory.

  THE DAVENPORT CONSTANT of a finite abelian group G is the least d
  such that EVERY SEQUENCE of d terms from G has a nonempty zero-sum
  subsequence, and for a cyclic group D(Z_n) = n. The hypothesis is a
  length, not a count of distinct values: SEQUENCES, WITH REPETITION
  ALLOWED. A sequence of n copies of the same element is admissible.

  SO THE UNIFORM LADDER, WHICH DEFEATS EVERY TOOL IN 532.2, IS NO
  OBSTACLE HERE AT ALL.

  THE TRANSFER. Work in Z_{2^t}. Among any 2^t chords, some nonempty
  subset has savings summing to 0 modulo 2^t, so the shortcut length
  2N - SUM(savings) it names is congruent to 2N modulo 2^t. Iterating
  on disjoint blocks of 2^t chords gives k = floor(N / 2^t) pairwise
  disjoint zero-sum subsets, and every union of them is zero-sum too,
  so 2^k subsets all give lengths in the SAME class modulo 2^t while
  their actual values SPREAD. That is 516.0's two coordinates being
  addressed by one instrument: the 2-adic coordinate exactly, from a
  theorem with no distinctness hypothesis, and the Archimedean
  coordinate by the spread of the 2^k values.

### 539.3 WHAT THE TRANSFER STILL OWES

Two side conditions, and they are the honest cost.

  (i) DISJOINTNESS. 528.0's shortcut needs the chords pairwise
  non-overlapping, and Davenport's subset is arbitrary. A ladder is
  guaranteed only 2N / (largest span) pairwise disjoint chords, which
  is small exactly when spans are large. Zero-sum theory must
  therefore be applied inside a disjoint family, and how large a
  disjoint family a girth-legal ladder must contain is a question
  this archive has never asked.

  (ii) THE WINDOW. 516.0: a length is a power of two iff it is
  divisible by 2^t AND lies in [2^t, 2^{t+1}). The count k = N / 2^t
  collapses to 1 exactly when 2^t approaches N, which is the regime
  where the target is largest. So the spread argument is strongest
  for small t and weakest where it is most needed.

  BUT THE SHAPE IS RIGHT AND IT IS NEW HERE. Every previous additive
  attempt failed on a hypothesis the object cannot satisfy. This one
  fails, so far, on a graph-theoretic side condition and a counting
  margin - both of which are questions about the ladder rather than
  about the tool.

### 539.4 STATUS

IDENTIFIED: the exact realizations of a closed ladder as a one-vertex
map and hence a dessin d'enfant; as a binary linear code in which
cycle lengths are codeword weights, dual to the Ising partition
function; as a metric graph whose cycle spectrum is a length spectrum
governed by the Ihara zeta function, which is 452's frame reached
from geometry; and as a chord diagram, which is Bouchet's and
Cohn-Lempel's subject.

IDENTIFIED, and new: THE POINTWISE FILTER, constraint (6). (OPEN)
quantifies over every ladder while almost all exact machinery in
those fields computes over the family, so an exact ensemble identity
is as useless as a bound. What survives are decision procedures and
extremal guarantees.

IDENTIFIED, and the substantive point: ZERO-SUM THEORY IS THE
ADDITIVE TOOL THAT SURVIVES THE UNIFORM LADDER. 532.2's objection -
every additive tool needs many distinct summands, and a uniform
ladder has one span - does not apply to the Davenport constant, whose
hypothesis is the LENGTH of a sequence with repetition allowed. Among
any 2^t chords some nonempty subset has savings summing to zero mod
2^t; iterating on disjoint blocks gives 2^{N/2^t} shortcut lengths in
one class mod 2^t with spreading values. What it owes is the
disjointness of the chosen chords and the Archimedean window.

VERIFIED (388.1, from search listings rather than the papers, and
described by shape rather than quoted): the Davenport constant D(G)
of a finite abelian group is the least d such that every sequence of
d terms from G has a nonempty zero-sum subsequence, and D(Z_n) = n,
the extremal example being n - 1 copies of a generator. Also, by
shape: the Harer-Zagier formula for one-face maps by genus; the
Buchi-Bruyere decidability theorem and its implementation in Walnut.

NOT PROVED: (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); the disjoint
family bound of 539.3(i); the uniform case, decidable in principle by
538.4; (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at
girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements of
451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The objects
here are literally one-vertex maps, binary codes, metric graphs and
chord diagrams, and each of those subjects has exact theorems; but
almost every one of those theorems describes the ensemble, and
(OPEN) is a statement about each member, which is a filter the
archive had not written down and which disqualifies Harer-Zagier,
character theory and Hurwitz counting in one line. Two things pass
it. A decision procedure passes it by settling a universally
quantified sentence, which is 538.4. And a zero-sum guarantee passes
it because it holds of every instance - and the Davenport constant,
alone among the additive tools this archive has considered, asks for
a long SEQUENCE rather than many distinct values, so the uniform
ladder that defeated 532.2's entire list is no obstacle to it. That
is the first time an imported theorem has had hypotheses this object
actually satisfies.


## 540. THE DISJOINTNESS OBLIGATION IS REFUTED, AND THE OVERLAP
## DICHOTOMY THAT REPLACES IT

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 539.2 imported the
Davenport constant as the one additive tool whose hypotheses a ladder
can meet, and 539.3(i) owed a disjoint family for the shortcut
mechanism to act on. That debt cannot be paid: there are girth-legal
ladders with no two disjoint chords at all. But the failure is
COMPLEMENTARY, and this section proves the dichotomy that makes it
so. Machine: scratch (construction search and two spectra, two runs).

### 540.0 LADDERS WITH NO TWO DISJOINT CHORDS (REFUTED, 374.1)

Put every left endpoint in [1, N] and every right endpoint in
[N+1, 2N]: chords (i, N + pi(i)) for a permutation pi of [1, N].
EVERY such arc contains the gap between N and N+1, so EVERY PAIR
OVERLAPS, and the maximum disjoint family has size 1.

  Girth 5 is exactly two conditions. A crossing or nested pair
  carries cycles of lengths 2 + L^1 and 2N + 2 - L^1 with
  L^1 = |i - j| + |pi(i) - pi(j)|, so BOTH need to be at least 5:

      3  <=  |i - j| + |pi(i) - pi(j)|  <=  2N - 3 ,

  and each circular span min(s, 2N - s) must be at least 4.

  SOLUTIONS EXIST AT EVERY EVEN SIZE SEARCHED, 2N = 14 through 32.
  For instance at 2N = 18

    (1,10) (2,12) (3,14) (4,11) (5,13) (6,16) (7,18) (8,15) (9,17)

  and at 2N = 24

    (1,13) (2,15) (3,17) (4,14) (5,16) (6,18) (7,20) (8,22) (9,19)
    (10,24) (11,21) (12,23) ,

  both of girth exactly 5 with all pairs overlapping.

  SO 539.3(i) CANNOT BE DISCHARGED. On these ladders 528.0's shortcut
  mechanism produces nothing but the one-chord cycles, and the
  zero-sum transfer of 539.2, which needs a disjoint family to act
  on, is empty.

  CORRECTED (374.1): my first construction used only L^1 >= 3 and
  produced girth 4 at three of four sizes, because a crossing pair's
  SECOND cycle has length 2N + 2 - L^1 and needs L^1 <= 2N - 3. The
  bound is two-sided; it was dropped once and is recorded here so it
  is not dropped again.

### 540.1 THE OVERLAP DICHOTOMY (PROVED)

Let alpha be the largest pairwise-DISJOINT family of chords and omega
the largest pairwise-OVERLAPPING one.

  THEOREM.  alpha * omega  >=  N / 2 .
    PROOF. The chords are arcs of a circle, so their overlap graph is
  a circular-arc graph. Fix any point p. The arcs containing p are
  pairwise overlapping, so there are at most omega of them; colour
  them with omega fresh colours. Every remaining arc misses p, so
  cutting the circle at p turns them into intervals of a line;
  interval graphs are perfect, so that part is properly coloured with
  its clique number, at most omega, colours. Hence the whole overlap
  graph has chromatic number at most 2 omega. A proper colouring
  partitions the N chords into at most 2 omega independent sets, each
  of size at most alpha, so N <= 2 omega alpha. QED

  COROLLARY. Either alpha >= sqrt(N/2) or omega >= sqrt(N/2).

  AND EACH BRANCH HAS ITS OWN TOOL.
    alpha LARGE - many pairwise disjoint chords, so 528.0's shortcut
      mechanism has a large ground set and 539.2's Davenport transfer
      applies to it, with no distinctness hypothesis to fail.
    omega LARGE - many pairwise overlapping chords, so EVERY pair
      among them carries a two-chord cycle and 536.1's difference-set
      mechanism has a ground set of omega chords contributing all
      omega(omega-1)/2 pairs.

  NEITHER BRANCH IS VACUOUS: 540.0's ladders have alpha = 1 and
  omega = N, the extreme of the second; a ladder of short chords
  spaced around the circle is the extreme of the first.

### 540.2 THE DICHOTOMY IS VISIBLE IN THE EXTREMAL OBJECT (COMPUTED)

The two witnesses of 540.0, where alpha = 1:

    2N = 18   spectrum 5 through 18 complete; 8 available from one
              chord and also from two; 16 from two chords.
    2N = 24   spectrum 5 through 24 complete; NO POWER OF TWO FROM
              ANY SINGLE CHORD; both 8 and 16 come from two-chord
              cycles.

  So on the family where the shortcut mechanism is at its weakest -
  no two disjoint chords, and at 2N = 24 not even a one-chord power
  of two - the overlap mechanism supplies the answer by itself. That
  is the dichotomy of 540.1 exhibited rather than argued.

### 540.3 WHERE BOTH BRANCHES LAND

A pairwise-crossing family of size k gives lengths 2 + (PHI - PHI)
for its position sums, and a nested chain of size k gives
2 + (S - S) for its spans. BOTH BRANCHES PRODUCE A DIFFERENCE SET,
so both land on 536.3's density problem, where the pigeonhole
degenerates at density one half. 516.0's factorisation is untouched:
the 2-adic coordinate has a hypothesis-free tool in the Davenport
constant, the Archimedean coordinate has none, and no instrument
couples them.

### 540.4 THE LITERATURE, RE-SURVEYED (VERIFIED, 388.1)

From search listings rather than the papers, described by shape:

  A 2026 preprint of Carr, "Every minimal counterexample to the
  Erdos-Gyarfas conjecture is predominantly cubic", proves that at
  least 4/7 of the vertices of a minimal counterexample have degree
  exactly 3; that the vertices of degree at least 4 form an
  independent set and the cubic vertices a dominating set; and that a
  REGULAR minimal counterexample must be cubic. This corroborates the
  reduction this archive made at 515 and does not supersede it.

  The conjecture is known for 3-connected cubic PLANAR graphs
  (Heckman and Krakovski); for P_8-free graphs, improved to P_10-free
  and then to P_13-free with computer assistance; and every graph of
  diameter 2 with minimum degree at least 3 has a 4-cycle or an
  8-cycle.

  Computer search bounds: a counterexample has at least 17 vertices,
  a CUBIC counterexample at least 30, and a BIPARTITE one at least
  30. The cubic bound of 30 sits exactly beside 524.4's zero-octagon
  cubic graph on 30 vertices, which is not a counterexample because
  it has 956 sixteen-cycles - a useful reminder of the difference
  between missing 8 and missing every power of two.

### 540.5 STATUS

REFUTED here (374.1): 539.3(i), the hope that a girth-legal ladder
must contain a large family of pairwise disjoint chords. Placing all
left endpoints in [1, N] and all right endpoints in [N+1, 2N] makes
every pair of chords overlap; girth 5 then reduces to
3 <= |i-j| + |pi(i)-pi(j)| <= 2N-3 together with circular spans at
least 4, and solutions exist at every even size from 14 to 32. On
such ladders the maximum disjoint family has size 1 and 528.0's
shortcut mechanism yields only one-chord cycles.

CORRECTED (374.1): the first version of that construction imposed
only L^1 >= 3 and had girth 4, because a crossing pair's second cycle
has length 2N + 2 - L^1. The condition is two-sided.

PROVED here: THE OVERLAP DICHOTOMY, alpha times omega at least N/2,
by colouring the circular-arc overlap graph with at most 2 omega
colours - the arcs through a point form a clique, the rest are
intervals and interval graphs are perfect - and partitioning into
independent sets of size at most alpha. Hence either there are at
least sqrt(N/2) pairwise disjoint chords, where 539.2's Davenport
transfer applies, or at least sqrt(N/2) pairwise overlapping ones,
where every pair carries a two-chord cycle and 536.1's difference-set
mechanism applies.

COMPUTED: girth-5 all-overlapping ladders at 2N = 14, 16, 18, 20, 22,
24, 26, 28, 30 and 32; the 2N = 18 and 2N = 24 witnesses have
complete spectra 5 through 2N, and at 2N = 24 NO single chord gives a
power of two - both 8 and 16 come from two-chord cycles.

VERIFIED (388.1, from search listings, by shape): Carr's 4/7
predominantly-cubic theorem for minimal counterexamples; the
P_13-free, 3-connected cubic planar and diameter-2 results; and the
search bounds of 17, 30 and 30 vertices.

NOT PROVED: (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); the Archimedean
half of the zero-sum transfer; the uniform case, decidable in
principle by 538.4; (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*);
(E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements
of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The debt 539
incurred cannot be paid as stated - a girth-legal ladder can have no
two disjoint chords, and an infinite family of such ladders is
exhibited - but the way it fails is the useful part. Disjointness and
overlap are complementary in a quantitative sense that is elementary
to prove: the product of the largest disjoint family and the largest
overlapping family is at least half the number of chords, because a
circular-arc graph is two interval graphs stacked. So one of the two
mechanisms always has a ground set of size at least the square root
of half the chords, and the extremal object for one branch is
precisely where the other branch does all the work - at 2N = 24 with
no two disjoint chords, not one power of two comes from a single
chord and both come from crossing pairs. What neither branch escapes
is 536.3: crossing families and nested chains both deliver DIFFERENCE
sets, and difference sets at density one half are exactly where the
pigeonhole dies. The gap is not closed. It is now a single problem
rather than two, and it is the same problem 516.0 named.


## 541. THE DENSITY-ONE-HALF OBSTRUCTION IS NOT AN OBSTRUCTION:
## KNESER CLASSIFIES IT COMPLETELY

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 536.3 recorded that the
difference-set pigeonhole degenerates at density one half and left
the matter there, calling the remainder an inverse problem. That was
the wrong tool, not a wall. Kneser's theorem answers the question
COMPLETELY at that density, and the answer is strong enough to give
an unconditional theorem about every closed ladder. Machine: scratch
(position-sum census, one run).

### 541.0 THE DENSITY-ONE-HALF DIFFERENCE DICHOTOMY (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let A be a subset of Z_n with |A| = n/2. Then either
  A - A = Z_n, or the complement of A - A is EXACTLY ONE COSET
  m/2 + mZ_n, for some EVEN m dividing n.
    PROOF. Let H = St(A - A), a subgroup, so A - A is a union of
  H-cosets. Kneser's theorem with B = -A gives
  |A - A| >= |A| + |-A| - |H| = n - |H|. Write k = n - |A - A| for
  the number of missing elements; then k <= |H|. But the complement
  of A - A is also a union of H-cosets, so |H| divides k, and if
  k > 0 then |H| <= k. Hence k = |H| and the complement is a SINGLE
  H-coset c + H.
    Now A - A is symmetric, so its complement is: -(c + H) = c + H,
  giving 2c in H. Writing H = <m> with m = n/|H|, the cosets are the
  residue classes mod m, and 2c = 0 mod m with c non-zero - since
  0 lies in A - A - forces m even and c = m/2. QED

  SO THERE IS NO INVERSE PROBLEM TO SOLVE. At density exactly one
  half a difference set can only fail to be everything in ONE way,
  and the failure is an arithmetic progression of even modulus
  centred at half that modulus. 536.3's "the pigeonhole degenerates"
  was correct and beside the point: the pigeonhole is simply not the
  instrument. Kneser is.

  COROLLARY 1. If |A| = n/2 and A is NOT a parity class, then A - A
  contains 3 or 7.
    PROOF. To miss both, 3 = 7 = m/2 mod m, so m divides 4 and m is
  even, so m is 2 or 4. For m = 4 the missing class is 2 mod 4 and 3
  is odd, so 3 is not missed. For m = 2 the missing class is the odd
  numbers, so A - A is contained in the evens, so all of A lies in
  one parity class, and |A| = n/2 forces A to BE that class. QED

### 541.1 THE UNCONDITIONAL CONSEQUENCE FOR LADDERS (PROVED)

The left-endpoint set A of a closed ladder has |A| = N exactly, with
no multiplicity to worry about, and it sits in Z_{2N} at density
exactly one half. And it is never a parity class:

  vertex 1 is the least label, hence a left endpoint, and it is odd,
  so A is not the evens; and if A were the odds then every right
  endpoint would be even, every span odd, and the ladder bipartite by
  504.2 - which 533.0 forbids, since the left endpoints of a
  bipartite girth-legal ladder take both parities.

  THEOREM. In every girth-legal closed ladder the left-endpoint
  difference set A - A omits at most one arithmetic progression
  m/2 + mZ with m EVEN, m at least 4, and m dividing 2N. Hence
  |A - A| >= (3/2) N: THE LEFT ENDPOINTS REALISE AT LEAST THREE
  QUARTERS OF ALL DIFFERENCES, and in particular A - A contains 3 or
  7.

  533.0's parity lemma, recorded as a step in the confinement
  classification and re-read at 536.3 as the first case of an inverse
  theorem, is now seen to be the WHOLE of the inverse theorem's
  hypothesis: it is exactly what rules out m = 2, and every other m
  is already harmless.

### 541.2 WHAT STILL SEPARATES THIS FROM A CYCLE (IDENTIFIED)

A crossing pair carries a cycle of length 2 + L^1 with
L^1 = phi_f - phi_e and phi = a + b = 2a + s. So

    length  =  2 + 2(a_f - a_e) + (s_f - s_e) .

  541.1 controls a_f - a_e. Two things stand between that and a
  power-of-two cycle, and both were already named at 531.2:

  (i) THE SPAN TERM. Only when s_f = s_e does the length reduce to
  2 + 2(a_f - a_e), where a difference of 3 gives 8 and a difference
  of 7 gives 16. In general the span difference intrudes.

  (ii) THE CROSSING RESTRICTION. A - A counts all pairs; only
  CROSSING pairs carry the two-chord cycle.

  AND THE OBVIOUS REPAIR IS NOT GENERIC. One would rather apply 541.0
  to the position sums PHI directly, since the length is
  2 + (phi_f - phi_e) with no span term. But PHI is a multiset, and
  Kneser needs its cardinality. MEASURED, over all girth-legal closed
  ladders: the N position sums are pairwise distinct modulo 2N in
  24 of 24 at 2N = 12, 170 of 408 at 14, 2352 of 8002 at 16 and
  31450 of 168802 at 18 - 100, 42, 29 and 19 per cent, FALLING. So an
  argument that needs distinct position sums covers a shrinking
  minority and cannot be the route.

### 541.3 THE ONE PLACE THE BLOCK CAN STILL SIT (PROVED)

Suppose the position sums ARE distinct, so 541.0 applies to PHI. The
two-chord lengths are then 2 + (PHI - PHI), and a power of two 2^t is
missed only if 2^t - 2 lies in the omitted class m/2 + mZ for every
t in range. Now 2^t - 2 = 2 mod 4 for every t >= 2. Taking t = 3 and
t = 4 gives 6 = 14 mod m, so m divides 8; m even leaves m in
{2, 4, 8}; m = 2 fails because 2^t - 2 is even, and m = 8 needs
6 = 4 mod 8, false. SO THE ONLY BLOCKING MODULUS IS m = 4, and it
blocks every power of two at once.

  m = 4 means PHI - PHI omits exactly the residues 2 mod 4, so no two
  position sums differ by 2 mod 4, so PHI occupies at most two
  residue classes mod 4 and they are ADJACENT - one of {0,1}, {1,2},
  {2,3}, {3,0} - never the opposite pairs {0,2} or {1,3}.

  AND THAT IS IMPOSSIBLE FOR A BIPARTITE LADDER. There phi = a + b is
  congruent to s modulo 2, all spans are odd, so PHI lies in the odd
  residues, hence within {1, 3} mod 4 - an opposite pair. If PHI met
  only one of them it would have at most N/2 elements, contradicting
  distinctness. So PHI meets both, 2 mod 4 IS a difference, and no
  blocking modulus exists.

  COROLLARY. For a BIPARTITE girth-legal closed ladder with distinct
  position sums, every power of two in range is realised as
  2 + (phi_f - phi_e) for SOME pair of chords. What remains is only
  whether such a pair can be taken CROSSING.

### 541.4 STATUS

PROVED here: THE DENSITY-ONE-HALF DIFFERENCE DICHOTOMY. For A in
Z_n with |A| = n/2, either A - A = Z_n or its complement is exactly
one coset m/2 + mZ with m even dividing n - by Kneser, since the
stabilizer forces the missing set to be a union of its cosets while
Kneser bounds the number missing by the stabilizer's order, so the
two coincide, and symmetry of A - A pins the coset. COROLLARY: if A
is not a parity class then A - A contains 3 or 7.

PROVED, unconditionally for every girth-legal closed ladder: the
left-endpoint set has exactly N elements in Z_{2N}, is never a parity
class - vertex 1 is an odd left endpoint, and 533.0 forbids the
all-odd alternative - so its difference set omits at most one
progression of even modulus at least 4, hence realises at least three
quarters of all differences and contains 3 or 7.

PROVED: if the position sums are distinct then the only modulus that
can block every power of two is m = 4, which forces the position sums
into two ADJACENT classes mod 4; and that is impossible for a
bipartite ladder, where the position sums are odd and must meet both
1 and 3 mod 4. So in that case every power of two in range is a
difference of position sums, and only the crossing restriction
remains.

COMPUTED: the N position sums are distinct modulo 2N in 24 of 24,
170 of 408, 2352 of 8002 and 31450 of 168802 girth-legal closed
ladders at 2N = 12, 14, 16 and 18 - 100, 42, 29 and 19 per cent, a
FALLING fraction, so distinctness is not a generic hypothesis.

VERIFIED (388.1, from search listings rather than the papers, and
described by shape): Kneser's addition theorem - for finite non-empty
subsets A, B of an abelian group, |A + B| >= |A| + |B| - |St(A + B)|,
where the stabilizer St(X) = {g : g + X = X} is a subgroup and X is a
union of its cosets.

NOT PROVED: the crossing restriction; the span term of 541.2(i); the
non-distinct position-sum case; (OPEN) for prime open ladders;
(COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at
girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements of
451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The place the
argument died at 536.3 was not a wall but a wrong instrument. At
density exactly one half the pigeonhole gives nothing, but Kneser
gives EVERYTHING: a difference set can fail to be the whole group in
precisely one way, by omitting a single symmetric coset, and the
omitted set is then an arithmetic progression of even modulus. For a
ladder the left endpoints always have density exactly one half and,
by 533.0, are never a parity class - so the modulus is at least 4 and
three quarters of all differences are realised. That is an
unconditional theorem about every girth-legal closed ladder and the
archive had nothing of the kind. What it does not yet reach is the
cycle: the length needs a difference of POSITION SUMS along a
CROSSING pair, and the position sums are a multiset that is distinct
in a falling minority of cases. The obstruction has moved from an
additive one, where it is now solved, to a combinatorial one about
which pairs cross - which is where 531.2 said it would end up.


## 542. THE MONOTONE REDUCTION: BOTH OBSTACLES VANISH INSIDE A
## CROSSING FAMILY, AND TWO CHORDS ALWAYS SUFFICE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 541.2 left two things
between the left-endpoint difference set and a cycle: the crossing
restriction, and the span term in length = 2 + 2(a_f - a_e) +
(s_f - s_e). This section removes both at once inside the right
sub-family, bounds how large such a sub-family must be, and reports
the census that shrinks the whole target to a two-chord arithmetic
statement. Machine: scratch (four censuses, three runs).

### 542.0 THE TRICHOTOMY IS AN IDENTITY IN (delta, s_e, s_f) (PROVED)

Let a_e < a_f, delta = a_f - a_e > 0. Then

    CROSSING   iff  delta < s_e  and  s_f > s_e - delta ,
    NESTED     iff  delta < s_e  and  s_f < s_e - delta ,
    DISJOINT   iff  delta >= s_e ,

and the cycle lengths are

    crossing :  2 + (2 delta + s_f - s_e)  =  2 + (phi_f - phi_e) ,
    nested   :  2 + (s_e - s_f) ,

together with their complements 2N + 2 minus the same quantity.

  READ THE TWO FORMS AGAINST 541.2's TWO OBSTACLES. In the crossing
  case the span term is not an extra term at all - it is absorbed
  into the position sum, and the length is a pure phi-difference. In
  the nested case delta drops out entirely and the length is a pure
  SPAN difference. Each mechanism is clean; what is dirty is only the
  mixture.

### 542.1 THE MONOTONE REDUCTION (PROVED)

  Call a family of chords MONOTONE if it is pairwise crossing or
  pairwise nested.

  THEOREM. Let K be pairwise crossing. Then EVERY pair of K realises
  a cycle of length 2 + (phi_f - phi_e), so the spectrum contains
  2 + (PHI_K - PHI_K) with no crossing restriction and no span term.
  Dually, if K is a nested chain the spectrum contains
  2 + (S_K - S_K), a pure difference set of spans.

  So inside a monotone family BOTH of 541.2's obstacles are gone
  simultaneously, and the question becomes the clean one: does the
  difference set of PHI_K, or of S_K, contain a target 2^t - 2 or
  2N + 2 - 2^t.

  AND MONOTONE FAMILIES ARE FORCED. A pairwise-crossing family is
  exactly a set with a_1 < ... < a_k < b_1 < ... < b_k, so within the
  chords straddling any one cut - which pairwise overlap - crossing
  is concordance and nesting is discordance of the two orders. By
  Erdos-Szekeres a straddling family of size c contains a monotone
  subfamily of size at least sqrt(c). And c is large whenever
  overlaps are: among pairwise-intersecting arcs, the shortest arc's
  two endpoints are such that one of them lies in at least half of
  them, so c >= omega/2 for the omega of 540.1. With 540.1's
  alpha times omega >= N/2:

    EITHER alpha >= sqrt(N/2), and 539.2's Davenport transfer has a
    disjoint family to act on, OR there is a MONOTONE family of size
    at least (N/8)^{1/4}, inside which every difference is realised.

### 542.2 ONE FAMILY IS NOT ENOUGH (COMPUTED)

Tempting, and false: take the LARGEST pairwise-crossing family and
ask whether its own difference set already hits a target. Over all
girth-legal closed ladders the largest such family has size 3, 4 or
5, and it FAILS to realise any target in 12 of 24 at 2N = 12, 134 of
408 at 14 and 4633 of 8002 at 16.

  So the mechanism must AGGREGATE over families. That is not a
  defect: every crossing pair straddles some cut, so ranging over all
  cuts recovers the FULL crossing graph, and the aggregate of 542.1's
  clean statements over all cuts is exactly the two-chord spectrum.

### 542.3 TWO CHORDS ALWAYS SUFFICE (COMPUTED)

Exhaustively over girth-legal CLOSED ladders, classified by the
cheapest mechanism that supplies a power of two:

  2N     ladders   1 chord   2 crossing   2 nested/disjoint   >= 3
  12          24        24            0                   0      0
  14         408       252          142                  14      0
  16        8002      6832         1096                  74      0
  18      168802    138419        30311                  72      0

  NOT ONE LADDER NEEDS THREE CHORDS. And the realising pair is
  overwhelmingly a CROSSING one: the nested-or-disjoint column FALLS
  from 74 to 72 while the population grows twentyfold, so its share
  is 0.04 per cent at 2N = 18 and shrinking.

  SO THE TARGET SHRINKS. Define

    (LQ3-2)  Every girth-legal closed ladder has a chord with
             s + 1 or 2N - s + 1 a power of two, or a pair of chords
             with 2 + L^1 or 2N + 2 - L^1 a power of two.

  (LQ3-2) implies (LQ3), it mentions no completions, no connectivity
  and no configuration of three chords, and it is a statement purely
  about spans and position sums - which is 536.1's difference-set
  frame and nothing more.

  THE CAVEAT IS REAL AND IT IS THE CLOSED-OPEN DIFFERENCE. 537.0
  measured the same quantity for OPEN ladders and found three chords
  genuinely needed - 14 cases at 2m = 14 and 120 at 2m = 16. A closed
  ladder has the complementary cycles 2N + 2 - L^1 that an open one
  lacks, which doubles the targets each pair offers; that is exactly
  why the closed model is the faithful one, as 510.2 said. And the
  census here stops at 2N = 18, so (LQ3-2) is measured, not proved.

### 542.4 STATUS

PROVED here: THE TRICHOTOMY IDENTITY - with delta the difference of
left endpoints, a pair is crossing when delta < s_e and
s_f > s_e - delta, nested when s_f < s_e - delta, and disjoint when
delta >= s_e; the crossing length is the pure position-sum difference
2 + (phi_f - phi_e) and the nested length is the pure span difference
2 + (s_e - s_f). THE MONOTONE REDUCTION - inside a pairwise-crossing
family every pair realises 2 + (phi_f - phi_e) and inside a nested
chain every pair realises 2 + (s_e - s_f), so 541.2's crossing
restriction and span term both vanish there at once. AND THE
EXISTENCE BOUND - the chords straddling a cut pairwise overlap, so
crossing is concordance and Erdos-Szekeres gives a monotone subfamily
of size at least sqrt(c); among pairwise-intersecting arcs some point
lies in at least half, so c >= omega/2; with 540.1 this gives either
alpha >= sqrt(N/2) or a monotone family of size at least (N/8)^{1/4}.

COMPUTED: the single largest pairwise-crossing family is NOT enough -
it realises no target in 12 of 24, 134 of 408 and 4633 of 8002
ladders at 2N = 12, 14 and 16 - so the mechanism must aggregate over
cuts, which recovers the whole crossing graph. And, decisively, over
all girth-legal closed ladders at 2N = 12, 14, 16 and 18 - 177236 of
them - NOT ONE requires three chords: the counts are 24, 252, 6832
and 138419 settled by a single chord, 0, 142, 1096 and 30311 by a
crossing pair, and 0, 14, 74 and 72 by a nested or disjoint pair.

IDENTIFIED: (LQ3-2), the two-chord form of the target - a chord with
s + 1 or 2N - s + 1 a power of two, or a pair with 2 + L^1 or
2N + 2 - L^1 a power of two - which implies (LQ3) and mentions
neither completions nor connectivity nor any three-chord
configuration.

NOT PROVED: (LQ3-2) itself, and it is measured only to 2N = 18, where
the OPEN analogue is already false by 537.0; the aggregation of 542.1
over cuts; (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3),
equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2
cancellation; J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked to force
the realising pair to cross and to control the span term, the answer
is that the two problems are one problem and it dissolves in the
right sub-family: a pairwise-crossing family has no crossing
restriction by definition and its lengths are pure position-sum
differences, while a nested chain's lengths are pure span
differences, so each mechanism is clean and only their mixture is
not. Erdos-Szekeres forces such a family inside the chords over any
cut, and 540.1 forces either such a family or a large disjoint one.
What a single family does not do is suffice, and the aggregate over
all cuts is simply the two-chord spectrum - which, over every
girth-legal closed ladder up to 2N = 18, is ALWAYS enough. That is
the sharpest reduction the ladder line has produced: no completions,
no connectivity, no third chord, just spans and position sums.


## 543. (LQ3-2) IS FALSE FROM 2N = 20, THE ONE-CHORD CASE WITH IT,
## AND THE CHORD HIERARCHY IS STRICT

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 542.3 measured that two
chords always suffice, over 177236 ladders to 2N = 18, and named the
two-chord form (LQ3-2) as the reduced target. It is FALSE, and the
first counterexample is at 2N = 20 - one size past where the census
stopped. The same object refutes the one-chord half of the question.
Machine: scratch lq32.py, lq3k.py, and an independent verifier.

### 543.0 (LQ3-2) IS REFUTED (374.1)

Turn the target into a prune rather than enumerating the class: a
partial matching that already closes a power-of-two cycle can never
extend to a counterexample, so depth-first search with that prune is
exact and cheap. It returns nothing at 2N = 12, 14, 16 and 18 - which
is 542.3 reproved by a second method - and then:

  WITNESS at 2N = 20, cubic, girth exactly 5 by breadth-first search:

    (1,5) (2,8) (3,19) (4,10) (6,12) (7,16) (9,18) (11,15) (13,17)
    (14,20)

  INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED from the stored chord list: its spectrum is
  every length from 5 to 20; it CONTAINS 8 and 16; and the least
  number of chords used by any power-of-two cycle is THREE. Its
  one-chord hits and its two-chord hits are both EMPTY.

  And counterexamples exist at every even size tested from 20 to 32,
  including one of girth 6 at 2N = 22 - so this is not a boundary
  effect.

  SO (LQ3-2) IS FALSE while (LQ3) SURVIVES ON THESE OBJECTS. The
  reduction of 542.3 is dead; the conjecture is untouched.

### 543.1 THE ONE-CHORD HALF FALLS WITH IT (REFUTED)

The question asked whether the span multiset must contain some s with
s + 1 or 2N - s + 1 a power of two. IT NEED NOT: the 2N = 20 witness
has NO one-chord hit at all, so every one of its ten spans avoids
both {2^t - 1} and {2N + 1 - 2^t}. That was always the likely answer -
the good span set has only about 2 log_2 N members out of 2N - 8
available spans - but it is now settled by exhibition rather than by
counting heuristics.

### 543.2 THE CHORD HIERARCHY IS STRICT (COMPUTED)

Let (LQ3-k) say that some cycle using at most k chords has
power-of-two length. Then
