  extracting a constant from a linear supply.

### 554.3 STATUS

PROVED here: THE FILTER IDENTITY. The interval (N, 2N] contains
exactly one power of two 2^t, and since 2^{t+1} exceeds 2N the
root-of-unity filter of order 2^t applied to the cycle-length
generating polynomial equals c_{2^t} exactly. This is a
cross-mechanism invariant in the sense of 553.2 - it sees all |T| at
once, isolates one length, and is an identity.

IDENTIFIED, and it corrects the reading of a barrier quoted
throughout 517 to 553: 517.3's O(1) barrier is a statement about
SMALL powers of two. E[c_k] = 2^k / 2k is exponentially large for k
of order N, so the largest power of two below 2N has an
exponentially large expected count and the barrier does not apply to
it. The conjecture needs only one power of two.

COMPUTED: on 543's witnesses at 2N = 20 and 22, on the dodecahedron,
and from 523.0's record for the n = 36 girth-7 graph, the counts are
c_8 = 11, 21, 30 and 0 against c_16 = 196, 346, 90 and 1161, with
c_32 = 12285 on the n = 36 witness; the length distributions peak
near 0.85 of 2N, so the large power of two sits near the maximum
while 8 sits in the lower tail.

IDENTIFIED: that the large target is blocked only by the m < 2g
restriction of 452 on the non-backtracking trace, not by counting -
518.0's threshold 2^{m/2} > 2n is satisfied with room to spare at
m of order N.

NOT PROVED: c_{2^t} > 0 for the large target; any control of the
filter's terms; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2);
(RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5;
the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The
cross-mechanism invariant asked for exists and is exact: because
(N, 2N] holds exactly one power of two and twice it exceeds 2N, the
root-of-unity filter of that order applied to the cycle generating
polynomial returns the count at that single length, with no
decomposition by mechanism and no inequality. Using it exposes
something that should have been seen at 517. The first-moment law
gives E[c_k] = 2^k / 2k, which is a constant only because k is; at
k of order N it is exponential, so the O(1) barrier - cited in this
archive for thirty-odd sections as though it were a fact about the
conjecture - is a fact about BAND 3 alone. Every hard object here
confirms it: the n = 36 graph with no octagon whatever carries 12285
cycles of length 32. The conjecture asks for some power of two, the
largest one in range is the abundant one, and the only thing standing
in front of it is the m < 2g restriction that stops the trace formula
from counting simple cycles - a narrower and more concrete obstacle
than the one that has been fought since 517.


## 555. THE NON-SIMPLE PART IS THE TRACE: THE SPECTRAL FRAME REACHES
## ONLY BELOW TWICE THE GIRTH

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 554.2 identified 452's
m < 2g restriction as the single obstacle in front of the large power
of two and suggested bounding the non-simple contribution to tr B^m,
observing that 518.0's numerical threshold holds with exponential
room. The observation was right and the inference was wrong. Above
twice the girth the non-simple walks are not a correction to the
trace; they are essentially all of it. Machine: scratch (exact
spectral decomposition of the 2N = 20 witness, one run).

### 555.0 THE MEASUREMENT (COMPUTED)

For 543's 2N = 20 witness, of girth 5, computing tr B^m from the
adjacency spectrum - the eigenvalues of the non-backtracking matrix
being the roots of x^2 - mu x + 2 for each adjacency eigenvalue mu,
together with +1 and -1 each with multiplicity |E| - |V| = 10 - and
comparing with 2 m c_m, the simple-cycle contribution:

    m      tr B^m      2 m c_m    simple share    non-simple
     5          40          40      100.00 %              0
     6         132         132      100.00 %              0
     7         154         154      100.00 %              0
     8         176         176      100.00 %              0
     9         702         702      100.00 %              0
    10        1080        1000       92.59 %             80
    12        3996        2400       60.06 %           1596
    14       16422        4928       30.01 %          11494
    16       67632        6272        9.27 %          61360
    18      260358        4608        1.77 %         255750
    20     1052120         800        0.08 %        1051320

  BELOW 2g = 10 THE SHARE IS EXACTLY 100 PER CENT, confirming 452's
  theorem to the digit and by an independent route. At m = 10 it
  breaks immediately, and thereafter the simple share roughly halves
  at every step.

### 555.1 THE PROPOSAL IS DEAD AT LEADING ORDER (REFUTED)

To use 518.0's test at m one needs the non-simple part to be SMALLER
than tr B^m, since the test only shows tr B^m is positive and the
non-simple walks are counted with a positive sign. At the large
target m = 16 the non-simple part is 61360 of 67632 - ninety-one per
cent - and at m = 2N it is 99.92 per cent.

  SO THE QUANTITY TO BE BOUNDED IS THE TRACE ITSELF. No bound on it
  can be smaller than the thing it is being compared to, and 554.2's
  "exponential room" is room in the wrong direction: the margin
  2^{m/2} > 2n is enormous precisely because tr B^m is enormous, and
  tr B^m is enormous because of the non-simple walks.

  THE HEURISTIC SAYS SO TOO, and should have been checked first. A
  non-backtracking walk of length m on 2N vertices repeats a vertex
  with probability about 1 - exp(-m^2/4N), which at m of order N is
  essentially 1. Almost every long closed walk is non-simple. 554.2's
  claim that only "a narrow technical restriction" stood in the way
  is CORRECTED: the restriction m < 2g is not technical, it is the
  exact point at which the trace stops measuring cycles.

### 555.2 THE CEILING OF 521.1, MADE QUANTITATIVE (IDENTIFIED)

521.1 proved a spectral ceiling and called it tight to a factor below
4/3. 555.0 gives its shape: the fraction of tr B^m attributable to
simple cycles runs

    1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0.93, 0.75, 0.60, 0.45, 0.30, 0.16, 0.093,
    0.053, 0.018, 0.005, 0.0008

  from m = 5 to m = 20. THE SPECTRAL FRAME'S REACH IS THE INTERVAL
  [g, 2g) AND NOTHING BEYOND IT, and the decay past 2g is geometric,
  not polynomial. Any future proposal to read cycle counts off traces
  above twice the girth can be dismissed by this table.

### 555.3 WHAT SURVIVES OF 554 (IDENTIFIED)

The route dies; the reframing does not.

  554.0's FILTER IDENTITY stands: (N, 2N] contains exactly one power
  of two 2^t and the root-of-unity filter of that order returns
  c_{2^t} exactly. It is still the only cross-mechanism invariant on
  the books.

  554.1's CORRECTION OF THE O(1) BARRIER stands, and is the durable
  gain of the last two sections: E[c_k] = 2^k / 2k is a constant only
  because k is, the barrier is a fact about band 3, and the power of
  two in (N, 2N] is exponentially abundant - c_16 = 196 on this very
  witness against c_8 = 11, and c_32 = 12285 on 523.0's octagon-free
  graph.

  WHAT 555 REMOVES is the hope that the spectrum can certify the
  large target. The target remains the right one; the instrument was
  never able to see it.

### 555.4 STATUS

REFUTED here: 554.2's proposal to bound the non-simple contribution
to tr B^m and apply 518.0's test at the large power of two. The
non-simple part is 91 per cent of the trace at m = 16 and 99.92 per
cent at m = 2N, so it is not a correction to be bounded but the trace
itself; and the exponential margin in 2^{m/2} > 2n exists precisely
because the trace is exponentially large, which is because of those
walks. 554.2's description of m < 2g as a narrow technical
restriction is CORRECTED - it is the exact threshold at which the
trace ceases to count cycles.

COMPUTED: on the 2N = 20 witness, the simple share of tr B^m is
exactly 100.00 per cent for m = 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 - an independent
confirmation of 452 - then 92.59, 75.00, 60.06, 44.95, 30.01, 16.42,
9.27, 5.26, 1.77, 0.47 and 0.08 per cent at m = 10 through 20.

IDENTIFIED: the quantitative form of 521.1's ceiling. The spectral
frame reaches exactly [g, 2g) and the simple share decays
geometrically beyond it, so no trace argument can certify a cycle
count above twice the girth.

SURVIVING from 554: the filter identity of 554.0, still the only
cross-mechanism invariant available; and 554.1's correction of the
O(1) barrier, which remains the substantive gain - the large power of
two is the abundant target and band 3 was never where the conjecture
is decided.

NOT PROVED: c_{2^t} > 0 for the large target by any means; (LQ3-3);
(OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently
(K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation;
J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The proposal to
push the trace test past twice the girth fails at leading order, and
the table that kills it is worth keeping: below 2g the simple cycles
are one hundred per cent of the non-backtracking trace, at 2g the
share breaks immediately, and by the large power of two it is nine
per cent and by the Hamiltonian length eight hundredths of one per
cent. The exponential room in 518.0's threshold was never room to
work in - the trace is large because the non-simple walks are many,
and those are exactly what must be subtracted. What survives is the
part of 554 that matters: the root-of-unity filter is still an exact
cross-mechanism invariant, and the correction of the O(1) barrier
still stands, so the large power of two is still the right target.
It simply cannot be certified by a spectrum, and after 518, 521, 552
and now 555 that should be treated as settled.


## 556. LONG CYCLES AS DEVIATIONS, THE TRANSFER MATRIX, AND THE
## CUTWIDTH DICHOTOMY

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 555 closed the spectral
route for good and 555.3 left the large power of two as the right
target with no instrument able to see it. This section reads long
cycles combinatorially instead, finds the parameter that decides
whether a transfer matrix can count them, and measures it on the
counterexamples - where it is small and shrinking. Machine: scratch
(cutwidth of six objects, one run).

### 556.0 A CYCLE OF LENGTH 2N - r OMITS r VERTICES (PROVED)

Let C use the chord set T, |T| = k. Its 2k endpoints cut the circle
into 2k gaps and C takes alternate ones, so C consists of k chords
and k arcs. Writing g_1, ..., g_k for the edge-lengths of the SKIPPED
gaps,

    vertices omitted by C  =  SUM (g_i - 1)  =  2N - m ,

so a cycle of length m = 2N - r omits exactly r vertices, and c_{2N-r}
counts the chord subsets whose skipped gaps satisfy SUM (g_i - 1) = r
and whose completion is connected. At r = 0 every skipped gap is a
single edge and these are the HAMILTONIAN cycles, the host being the
case k = 0.

  SO LONG CYCLES ARE DEVIATIONS FROM THE HOST, not rare
  configurations, and the natural way to count them is to scan the
  host once - which is what a transfer matrix does.

### 556.1 THE TRANSFER MATRIX AND WHAT LIMITS IT (IDENTIFIED)

Scanning the circle vertex by vertex, the state needed to continue is
the set of chords already begun and not yet closed, together with the
partial-path connectivity among them. So the state space has size
about 2^w, where

    w = CUTWIDTH = max over cuts of the number of chords spanning it

  which is 531's c(p) maximised. THE TRANSFER-MATRIX METHOD IS
  POLYNOMIAL IF AND ONLY IF THE CUTWIDTH IS BOUNDED, and for a
  periodic family of bounded cutwidth the cycle-length generating
  function is RATIONAL - at which point 538.4's Buchi decidability
  applies to it verbatim, since "is a power of two" is definable with
  addition and the base-2 valuation.

  AND THE CUTWIDTH IS NOT BOUNDED IN GENERAL: 540.0's all-overlapping
  ladders have every chord across one cut, so w = N.

### 556.2 THE COUNTEREXAMPLES HAVE SMALL CUTWIDTH (COMPUTED)

    object            N    cutwidth   state space   spans
    2N = 20 witness  10        6          64        4,4,4,4,6,6,6,6,9,9
    2N = 22          11        6          64        5..11
    2N = 24          12        6          64        5..12
    2N = 28          14        4          16        mostly 4 and 5
    2N = 32          16        4          16        mostly 4 and 5
    dodecahedron     10        7         128        4,4,4,4,7,7,7,7,10,10

  THE CUTWIDTH FALLS AS 2N GROWS - 6, 6, 6, 4, 4 - so the objects
  that evade every mechanism become MORE quasi-one-dimensional, not
  less. At 2N = 32 the transfer matrix has sixteen states.

  THE CAVEAT IS REAL AND MUST BE RECORDED. 543's search returns the
  FIRST counterexample in lexicographic order, which favours small
  spans early, so the low cutwidth may be an artefact of the search
  order rather than a property of counterexamples. Nothing here shows
  a counterexample must have small cutwidth; it shows the ones we
  have do.

### 556.3 THE CUTWIDTH DICHOTOMY (IDENTIFIED)

Both extremes are tractable, and for opposite reasons.

  SMALL CUTWIDTH. The transfer matrix is polynomial, the generating
  function of a periodic family is rational, and 538.4's decision
  procedure applies. This is the regime the counterexamples occupy.

  LARGE CUTWIDTH. 540.0's family has w = N, every pair of chords
  overlapping, and 540.2 measured their spectra COMPLETE - 5 to 18 at
  2N = 18 and 5 to 24 at 2N = 24 - so (LQ3) holds on them with room
  to spare. Overlap is what makes the two-chord difference set rich,
  which is 536.1 and 542.1.

  SO THE DIFFICULTY, IF IT LIVES ANYWHERE, LIVES IN THE MIDDLE - and
  that is a new place to look, with a parameter attached to it. Every
  split this archive has drawn since 528 has been by MECHANISM, and
  553.2 proved no mechanism can suffice alone. This one is by a
  property of the object.

### 556.4 STATUS

PROVED here: THE DEVIATION IDENTITY - a cycle of length 2N - r omits
exactly r vertices, since the omitted vertices are the interiors of
the skipped gaps and those satisfy SUM (g_i - 1) = 2N - m. At r = 0
the cycles are the Hamiltonian ones and the host is the empty chord
set.

IDENTIFIED: that the transfer matrix counting long cycles has state
space about 2^w with w the CUTWIDTH, so it is polynomial exactly when
the cutwidth is bounded, and that for a periodic family of bounded
cutwidth the generating function is rational and 538.4's Buchi
decision procedure applies verbatim.

COMPUTED: the cutwidths of 543's counterexamples are 6, 6, 6, 4 and 4
at 2N = 20, 22, 24, 28 and 32, and 7 for the dodecahedron - small and
FALLING as the objects grow, so the transfer matrix has sixteen
states at 2N = 32. Recorded with the caveat that 543's search is
lexicographic and may favour short spans.

IDENTIFIED: the CUTWIDTH DICHOTOMY. Small cutwidth is decidable by
transfer matrix; large cutwidth is 540.0's all-overlapping family,
whose spectra 540.2 measured complete. The first split this archive
has drawn by a property of the OBJECT rather than by mechanism, which
is what 553.2 says is required.

NOT PROVED: that a counterexample must have small cutwidth; the
transfer-matrix computation itself; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open
ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*);
(E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements
of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Counting long
cycles from the host rather than from the spectrum gives a clean
picture - a cycle of length 2N - r is one that omits r vertices, and
the omitted vertices are the interiors of the gaps the cycle skips -
and it identifies the parameter that decides whether the count is
computable: the cutwidth, the largest number of chords across any
cut, which is the size of the transfer-matrix state. The measurement
is the interesting part. The counterexamples of 543 have cutwidth 6,
6, 6, 4, 4 as 2N runs from 20 to 32, falling as they grow, so the
objects that defeat every mechanism are quasi-one-dimensional and sit
squarely in the regime where exact machinery works; while at the
other extreme 540.0's ladders have cutwidth N and complete spectra.
Both ends are tractable and for opposite reasons, which is the first
dichotomy here drawn by a property of the object instead of by which
mechanism is being asked to do the work - and 553.2 is the reason
that matters.


## 557. BOUNDED CUTWIDTH GIVES A BOUNDED WINDOW: THE FIRST CLOSURE
## FROM BOTH ENDS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 556.3 drew the first
dichotomy in this archive by a property of the object rather than by
mechanism, and asked which regime counterexamples need. The answer,
at the two-chord level, is neither end: for a FIXED cutwidth the
counterexamples occupy a bounded window of sizes and then stop.
Machine: scratch cutw.py, two runs completed and one still going.

### 557.0 THE EXPERIMENT

543's prune for (LQ3-2) - no power-of-two cycle from one chord or
from any pair - with a CUTWIDTH CAP added. Both prunes are monotone
under adding chords: a partial matching that already closes a
power-of-two cycle can never be repaired, and the number of chords
spanning a cut only grows. So the depth-first search is exact.

### 557.1 CUTWIDTH THREE IS ALWAYS SAFE (COMPUTED)

    cutwidth <= 3 :  NO counterexample at 2N = 16, 18, 20, 22, 24,
                     26, 28, 30, 32, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44 .

  Fifteen sizes, none. Every girth-legal closed ladder of cutwidth at
  most three has a power-of-two cycle using at most two chords.

### 557.2 CUTWIDTH FOUR GIVES A WINDOW (COMPUTED)

    cutwidth <= 4 :  2N = 20, 22, 24            none
                     2N = 26, 28, 30, 32        COUNTEREXAMPLE
                     2N = 34, 36, 38, 40        none

  A BOUNDED WINDOW, closed at both ends. The witnesses at 26 to 32
  are the same objects 543 found without any cap - 556.2 measured
  their cutwidth as 4 - so the cap is not distorting them; it is
  telling us where they can live.

  WHY BOTH ENDS CLOSE. Below the window there is too little room: a
  width-four ladder on twenty vertices cannot arrange its spans to
  dodge 8 and 16 at once. Above it there are too many targets: the
  number of powers of two below 2N grows like log 2N, a third one
  enters at 2N = 32, and the structural freedom of a width-four
  quasi-one-dimensional ladder does not grow with 2N at all.

### 557.3 WHAT THIS MEANS (IDENTIFIED)

Put it beside 540.2. At the other extreme - cutwidth N, every pair of
chords overlapping - the spectra were measured COMPLETE, so (LQ3)
holds there outright. Now the narrow end is closing too:

    cutwidth <= 3       no two-chord counterexample, any size
    cutwidth 4          counterexamples only for 26 <= 2N <= 32
    cutwidth ~ N        spectra complete (540.2)

  SO A COUNTEREXAMPLE MUST HAVE CUTWIDTH GROWING WITH 2N, and it must
  keep growing - each fixed width is exhausted at some size. That is
  the first statement in this archive that closes from BOTH ends, and
  it does so with a parameter of the object rather than a choice of
  mechanism, which is what 553.2 demanded.

  AND IT MATCHES THE PUMPING INTUITION. A ladder of cutwidth w has a
  bounded transfer-matrix state, so for 2N large two cuts repeat a
  state and a segment can be excised or repeated. The spectrum then
  contains arithmetic progressions, and the freedom to dodge a
  growing set of targets with a fixed period runs out. 556.1 already
  observed that bounded cutwidth makes the generating function
  rational for a periodic family, at which point 538.4's decision
  procedure applies; 557.2 is that principle showing up as data.

### 557.4 THE CAVEATS, STATED PLAINLY

  These are counterexamples to (LQ3-2), the TWO-CHORD form of 542.3,
  not to (LQ3). 543 already showed (LQ3-2) is false in general, so
  what 557.2 bounds is the two-chord evasion, not the conjecture.

  The cutwidth-5 and cutwidth-6 searches are still running; only
  w <= 3 and w <= 4 are complete. The window for larger w is expected
  to be larger and is not yet measured.

  And nothing here proves the pattern continues. "Each fixed width is
  exhausted" is measured at w = 3 and w = 4 and is exactly the kind
  of claim 543 taught this archive not to extrapolate.

### 557.5 STATUS

COMPUTED: with the (LQ3-2) prune and a cutwidth cap, both prunes
monotone so the search is exact - at cutwidth at most 3 there is NO
counterexample at any of the fifteen sizes 2N = 16 through 44; at
cutwidth at most 4 there are counterexamples at 2N = 26, 28, 30 and
32 and NONE at 20, 22, 24 or at 34, 36, 38, 40. The window is closed
at both ends, and its members are the same objects 543 found
uncapped.

IDENTIFIED: that a two-chord counterexample must have cutwidth
growing with 2N, since each fixed width is exhausted at some size,
while at the opposite extreme 540.2 measured the spectra of the
cutwidth-N ladders COMPLETE. This is the first closure from both ends
in this archive, and the first argument organised by a parameter of
the object rather than by a choice of mechanism.

NOT PROVED: that the pattern continues to larger widths; anything
about (LQ3) as opposed to (LQ3-2); (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open
ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*);
(E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements
of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Capping the
cutwidth and re-running 543's prune answers 556.3's question in a way
neither branch of the dichotomy predicted. Counterexamples do not
prefer the narrow regime or the wide one; for a FIXED width they
occupy a bounded window and then stop. At width three there is no
two-chord counterexample at any size tested, at width four they exist
only for 2N between 26 and 32, and at width N the spectra are
complete by 540.2. The reason both ends close is visible: the number
of power-of-two targets grows like log 2N while the freedom of a
width-w quasi-one-dimensional ladder does not grow at all, and below
the window there is simply not enough room to dodge two targets at
once. So a counterexample must have cutwidth growing with the size -
which is the first thing this programme has proved to be forced from
both directions, and it is a statement about the object rather than
about which mechanism is being asked to work.


## 558. THE PUMPING LEMMA IS BLOCK THEORY, AND 557.3 IS WITHDRAWN

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 557.5 asked for a
pumping lemma at bounded cutwidth and claimed each fixed width is
exhausted at some size. The lemma, worked out, is 534's block theory
under another name; and the claim is refuted by the cutwidth-5
search, which was still running when 557 was written. Machine:
scratch cutw.py (cutwidth 5 to 2N = 38), span statistics.

### 558.0 EXCISION REQUIRES A BLOCK (PROVED)

To excise the segment (p, q] from a ladder and leave a ladder, every
vertex in (p, q] must be matched within it - otherwise a chord loses
an endpoint. Equivalently, no chord has exactly one endpoint inside,
so the SAME chords span the cut at p and the cut at q.

  BUT A SELF-MATCHED ARC IS A BLOCK, 534.0's notion exactly. So

    "two cuts share a transfer state, so a segment can be excised"
     =  "the ladder has a proper block" ,

  and the pumping lemma requested at 557.5 is 534.0 restated. It is
  already developed: 534.1 shows a block has at least 12 vertices,
  535.4 shows a block of at most 18 forces a power of two, and 534.2
  exhibits the ladders that have blocks at all. THERE IS NO NEW LEMMA
  HERE, and the transfer-state language adds nothing to it for a
  SINGLE ladder. It would add something for a FAMILY, where a state
  may repeat across different members, but that is a statement about
  a sequence of ladders and not about one.

### 558.1 557.3 IS WITHDRAWN (CORRECTED, 374.1)

557.3 read the cutwidth-4 window - counterexamples only for
26 <= 2N <= 32 - as evidence that each fixed cutwidth is exhausted at
some size, and called it the first closure from both ends. THE
CUTWIDTH-5 SEARCH, still running when that was written, says
otherwise:

    cutwidth <= 5 :  2N = 16, 18       none
                     2N = 20           COUNTEREXAMPLE
                     2N = 22, 24       none
                     2N = 26 ... 38    COUNTEREXAMPLE at every size

  Seven consecutive sizes with no sign of stopping. So width five is
  NOT exhausted in the range searched, the pattern seen at widths
  three and four does not continue, and "a counterexample must have
  cutwidth growing with 2N" is not supported.

  557.4 flagged exactly this risk - "measured at w = 3 and w = 4 and
  is exactly the kind of claim 543 taught this archive not to
  extrapolate" - and then 557.3 and 557.5 extrapolated anyway. The
  caveat was right and the headline was wrong.

  WHAT SURVIVES of 557: the measurements. Cutwidth at most 3 admits
  no two-chord counterexample at any of the fifteen sizes 16 to 44,
  and cutwidth 4 admits them only for 26 <= 2N <= 32. Those stand.
  The inference drawn from them does not.

### 558.2 A SECOND CORRECTION: 2N = 32 (374.1)

At 2N = 32 the HOST CYCLE has length 32, a power of two, so that
ladder satisfies (LQ3) outright. The (LQ3-2) prune never inspects the
zero-chord cycle, so it reports a counterexample there; the report is
correct for (LQ3-2) as stated at 542.3 and misleading as evidence
about the conjecture. Any size 2N that is itself a power of two is
trivial for (LQ3) and should be excluded from these censuses.

### 558.3 WHAT BOUNDED CUTWIDTH DOES GIVE (PROVED)

Not a pumping lemma, but a span bound and a local forcing rule.

  (i) SUM over chords of s_e = SUM over cuts of c(p) <= 2N w, so with
  N chords the MEAN SPAN is at most 2w. Measured on the width-4
  witnesses: mean spans 5.9, 5.4 and 5.2 against the bound 8.

  (ii) By 546.1 equal spans are never nested, so two chords of equal
  span that overlap must CROSS, and then L^1 = 2 delta where delta is
  their left-endpoint gap. Hence

      TWO CHORDS OF EQUAL SPAN WHOSE LEFT ENDPOINTS DIFFER BY 3
      GIVE AN OCTAGON,

  since L^1 = 6 and the cycle is 2 + 6 = 8, and delta = 3 < 4 <= s
  makes them cross.

  (iii) So a counterexample must have EVERY SPAN CLASS avoiding
  left-endpoint difference 3, and by (i) bounded cutwidth forces many
  chords into few span classes.

  WHY IT DOES NOT CLOSE. A subset of [1, 2N] avoiding difference 3 can
  have density one half - take two residues out of every six - so the
  pigeonhole from (i) and (iii) never contradicts itself. This is
  536.3's density-one-half wall in yet another costume.

### 558.4 STATUS

CORRECTED here (374.1), twice. FIRST, 557.3's claim that each fixed
cutwidth is exhausted, and the "closure from both ends" drawn from
it, are WITHDRAWN: the cutwidth-5 search finds counterexamples at
2N = 20 and at every size from 26 to 38, seven consecutive, with no
sign of stopping. SECOND, at 2N = 32 the host cycle is itself a power
of two, so such sizes are trivial for (LQ3) and should be excluded
from these censuses; the (LQ3-2) prune does not inspect the
zero-chord cycle.

IDENTIFIED: that the pumping lemma requested at 557.5 does not exist
as a new statement. Excising a segment requires the same chords to
span both cuts, which makes the segment a self-matched arc - a BLOCK
in the sense of 534.0 - so single-ladder pumping is block theory,
already developed at 534 and 535.

PROVED here: at cutwidth w the sum of spans is at most 2Nw, so the
mean span is at most 2w; and two chords of EQUAL SPAN whose left
endpoints differ by 3 must cross, giving L^1 = 6 and an octagon.
Hence a counterexample has every span class avoiding left-endpoint
difference 3.

COMPUTED: cutwidth at most 5 admits counterexamples at 2N = 20 and at
26, 28, 30, 32, 34, 36 and 38; the width-4 witnesses have mean spans
5.9, 5.4 and 5.2 against the bound 8.

NOT PROVED: any exhaustion of a fixed cutwidth; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for
prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4);
(LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7;
the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The pumping
lemma asked for turns out to be a theorem this archive already has:
a segment can be excised only when the same chords span both of its
cuts, which means every vertex inside is matched inside, which is
exactly a block, and blocks were classified at 534 and disposed of up
to eighteen points at 535. And the conclusion 557 drew from the
cutwidth windows is false - width five carries counterexamples at
seven consecutive sizes up to 2N = 38, so widths are not exhausted
one by one and nothing closes from both ends. What survives is
smaller and true: bounded cutwidth forces the mean span below 2w, and
two chords of the same span with left endpoints three apart must
cross and make an octagon, so a counterexample keeps every span class
free of the difference 3. That is a genuine local forcing rule, and
it fails to close for the reason everything in this line fails to
close - a set can avoid one difference at density one half.

## 560. THE TRANSFER MATRIX, BUILT - AND AN INFINITE FAMILY SETTLED

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 556.1 described a
transfer matrix and 559.5 named building it as the one concrete thing
never attempted. It is built here, validated against brute force, and
run on the uniform family - where it exposes an explicit octagon
valid at every size, settling (LQ3) for an infinite family by
exhibition. Machine: scratch tm.py.

### 560.0 THE MACHINE, AND ITS VALIDATION (COMPUTED)

Treat the wrap edge (1, 2N) as an extra chord, so every vertex has
exactly three incident edges, and scan the host once. The state after
each vertex is a MATCHING on the used open strands crossing the cut -
which pairs of strand-ends are already joined by a built path -
together with a flag recording that the cycle has closed. A vertex
uses none or exactly two of its three edges; joining two ends whose
partners are each other closes the cycle, and is allowed only when no
other strand is open, which is what forces a SINGLE cycle rather than
a 2-factor.

  VALIDATED: on 543's 2N = 20 witness the machine returns
  4, 11, 11, 11, 39, 50, 66, 100, 138, 176, 181, 196, 199, 128, 64,
  20 at lengths 5 through 20 - IDENTICAL to the brute-force
  enumeration of 554.

  AND IT SCALES: on the 2N = 32 witness it returns the whole spectrum
  at once, 49483 cycles, with c_8 = 13, c_16 = 424 and c_32 = 48. The
  last of these confirms 558.2 - that ladder satisfies (LQ3) outright
  because 32 is a power of two and the host is a 32-cycle.

### 560.1 THE UNIFORM FAMILY, FAR PAST ENUMERATION (COMPUTED)

Running it on 537.2's uniform ladders with span 5 - chords {i, i+5}
for odd i - at every even 2N from 14 to 120:

    54 girth-legal ladders, EVERY ONE with a power-of-two cycle,
    0 exceptions.

  537.5 had reached 2N = 40 by enumeration; this reaches 120 in
  seconds. And the counts are eventually LINEAR in N:

    c_8  = N          at 2N = 40, 60, 80, 100, 120  (20,30,40,50,60)
    c_16 = 19 N       at 2N = 60 and beyond  (570, 760, 950, 1140)

  which is exactly what translation invariance predicts: the uniform
  ladder admits the shift i -> i + 2 as an automorphism, so cycles of
  a FIXED length fall into orbits of size N once 2N is large enough
  that none of them wraps, and c_m is N times the number of orbits.

### 560.2 AN EXPLICIT OCTAGON, AT EVERY SIZE (PROVED)

The machine reports exactly one orbit of octagons. Extracting it:

    1 - 6   chord      6 - 5   host
    5 - 10  chord     10 - 9   host
                       9 - 8   host
    8 - 3   chord      3 - 2   host
                       2 - 1   host

  THEOREM. In the uniform ladder with span 5 - chords {i, i+5} for i
  odd - the eight vertices 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 with the three
  chords (1,6), (3,8), (5,10) and the five host edges 1-2, 2-3, 5-6,
  8-9, 9-10 form an OCTAGON, for every 2N at which the ladder is
  defined.
    PROOF. The three chords are of the form {i, i+5} with i = 1, 3, 5
  all odd, so all three are present. Every listed vertex has degree
  exactly two in the configuration: 1 by (1,6) and 1-2; 2 by 1-2 and
  2-3; 3 by 2-3 and (3,8); 5 by 5-6 and (5,10); 6 by (1,6) and 5-6;
  8 by (3,8) and 8-9; 9 by 8-9 and 9-10; 10 by 9-10 and (5,10). It is
  connected, traversed as 1, 6, 5, 10, 9, 8, 3, 2 and back to 1. All
  labels lie in [1, 10], so the configuration never wraps once
  2N >= 12. QED

  COROLLARY. (LQ3) HOLDS FOR EVERY UNIFORM LADDER OF SPAN 5. By the
  shift automorphism the octagon has N translates, so c_8 = N exactly
  - matching the machine - and in particular c_8 > 0 for all 2N.

  THIS IS THE FIRST INFINITE FAMILY THIS PROGRAMME HAS SETTLED. The
  uniform ladders were named as the hard case at 532.1, classified at
  537.2, and identified as the structured extreme by 536.4 arriving
  from the other direction. They are now done at span 5.

### 560.3 A CORRECTION OF MY OWN (374.1)

A quick check-enumeration of the octagons in U(40,5) reported 40
where the machine reported 20. THE MACHINE WAS RIGHT: the check
explored both directions from each least vertex and so counted every
cycle twice. Recorded because the instinct on seeing a discrepancy
was to doubt the new machine, and the new machine was correct.

### 560.4 STATUS

BUILT and VALIDATED: 556.1's transfer matrix. The wrap edge is
treated as an extra chord so every vertex has three incident edges;
the state is a matching on used open strands plus a closed flag; a
closure is admitted only into the empty state, which forces one cycle
rather than a 2-factor. It reproduces the brute-force spectrum of the
2N = 20 witness exactly at all sixteen lengths, and returns the whole
2N = 32 spectrum - 49483 cycles, c_8 = 13, c_16 = 424, c_32 = 48.

PROVED here: THE UNIVERSAL OCTAGON. In the uniform ladder of span 5,
the vertices 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 with chords (1,6), (3,8), (5,10)
and host edges 1-2, 2-3, 5-6, 8-9, 9-10 form an 8-cycle at every
size, since the three chords are {i, i+5} for odd i and every label
lies in [1,10]. Hence (LQ3) HOLDS FOR THE WHOLE UNIFORM SPAN-5
FAMILY, and by the shift automorphism c_8 = N exactly.

COMPUTED: 54 girth-legal uniform span-5 ladders at 2N = 14 to 120,
all with a power of two, 0 exceptions - against 537.5's previous
reach of 2N = 40; and the eventual linearity c_8 = N, c_16 = 19N,
which is translation invariance made exact.

CORRECTED (374.1): a check-enumeration that double-counted cycles by
traversing each in both directions; the machine's count was correct.

NOT PROVED: the uniform families of other spans; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for
prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4);
(LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7;
the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The transfer
matrix works. It reproduces brute force exactly where brute force can
reach, it returns whole spectra in seconds where brute force cannot,
and pointed at the uniform ladders it does something better than
verify them: it reports a single orbit of octagons, and reading that
orbit off gives an explicit eight-cycle - three chords {1,6}, {3,8},
{5,10} and five host edges, all inside the first ten vertices - which
exists in the span-5 uniform ladder at EVERY size. That settles (LQ3)
for an infinite family, the first this programme has closed, and it
closes the family that 532.1 named as the hard case and 536.4
independently identified as the structured extreme. The method that
did it is the one 539.1 said was needed and 553.2 said was the only
kind left: exact, pointwise, and blind to which mechanism supplies
the answer.


## 561. THE UNIFORM FAMILY BY SPAN: TWO TEST-DESIGN ERRORS, AND THE
## WINDING CRITERION

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 560.4 asked whether
560.2's universal octagon generalises to every odd span. It does not,
and finding that out cost two errors of my own, both caught here.
What replaces it is a displacement criterion for the whole uniform
spectrum, stated but not yet verified. Machine: scratch (span scans
and a criterion check, the last still running).

### 561.0 THE CUTWIDTH-5 SEARCH, COMPLETED (COMPUTED)

Finishing the run 558.1 quoted in part:

    cutwidth <= 5 :  2N = 16, 18        none
                     2N = 20            COUNTEREXAMPLE
                     2N = 22, 24        none
                     2N = 26 ... 38     COUNTEREXAMPLE at every size
                     2N = 40            none
                     2N = 42, 44        COUNTEREXAMPLE

  SO IT IS NOT EVEN A WINDOW. The class is irregular, with a hole at
  40 and counterexamples on both sides of it. 558.1's withdrawal of
  557.3 is confirmed a second time and more sharply: widths are not
  exhausted, and the shape of the class is not monotone either.

### 561.1 A TEST-DESIGN ERROR (CORRECTED, 374.1)

Scanning the uniform family by span, I tested each odd s at the
single size 2N = 4s and found an octagon every time, s = 5 to 31.
THAT WAS AN ARTEFACT OF THE TEST POINT. Extracting the octagons shows
them to be four chords alternating with four host steps, with
displacements

    +s, +1, +s, -1, +s, -1, +s, +1     summing to 4s ,

so they close only because 4s = 2N. They WIND ONCE AROUND, and they
exist precisely when 2N is about 4s. Choosing 2N = 4s handed the
search the configuration it then reported.

  RETESTED at generic sizes - every even 2N from 2s + 6 to 6s with
  4s not a multiple of 2N - the family still has a power of two in
  every case, s = 5 through 15, but THE LENGTH VARIES: 8 while 2N is
  at most about 4s, then 16 beyond. At s = 9 the octagon is present
  to 2N = 40 and gone from 42, where 16 takes over; at s = 11 it
  survives to 48 and 16 takes over at 50.

  SO NO SINGLE CONFIGURATION SETTLES THE FAMILY. 560.2's octagon
  remains genuinely universal, because its three chords (1,6), (3,8),
  (5,10) have all eight vertices inside [1, 10] and it does not wind;
  SPAN 5 IS STILL SETTLED. Nothing similar holds for general s.

### 561.2 THE WINDING CRITERION, AND A SECOND ERROR (374.1)

Traversing a cycle of U(2N, s): each chord jumps s, and each maximal
host run has some length. Writing k for the number of chords, h for
the number of host edges and w for the winding number, the closure
condition is that the displacements sum to w times 2N.

  MY FIRST VERSION ASSUMED EVERY CHORD CONTRIBUTES +s, giving
  |w 2N - k s| <= L - k with a parity condition. IT IS WRONG, and the
  check said so: 22 of 38 uniform ladders mismatched, always by
  MISSING lengths the graph really has. At s = 7 it missed the
  6-cycle, which is the crossing pair of chords at i and i + 2 - one
  chord traversed forwards and one backwards.

  THE CORRECTION. From an ODD vertex the chord goes +s; from an EVEN
  vertex it goes -s. So the net chord displacement is c s where

      |c| <= k    and    c = k  (mod 2) ,

  and the criterion becomes: a cycle of length L = k + h exists only
  if for some such c and some w

      |w 2N - c s| <= h    and    h - (w 2N - c s)  is even .

  At s = 7, 2N = 26, L = 6 this is satisfied with k = 2, c = 0, w = 0,
  which is the missing hexagon.

  THIS CORRECTED FORM IS NOT YET VERIFIED. The check was still
  running when this section was written, and it is recorded as a
  candidate, not a result. The first version's failure is recorded
  because it is the same mistake in miniature that 547.0 found in
  544.2 - assuming a uniformity (all chords one way, all pairs
  crossing) that the object does not have.

### 561.3 WHAT STANDS FROM THE SPAN SCAN (COMPUTED)

  Every uniform ladder tested has a power-of-two cycle: s = 5 through
  15 at every girth-legal even 2N from 2s + 6 to 6s, and s = 5 at
  every even 2N from 14 to 120 by 560.1. NO EXCEPTIONS ANYWHERE.

  The length is 8 when 2N is at most about 4s and 16 above that,
  which is the winding picture: an octagon needs four chords whose
  spans nearly close the circle, and once the circle is too big for
  four it takes eight.

### 561.4 STATUS

COMPUTED: the cutwidth-5 search completed - counterexamples at
2N = 20 and at 26 through 38 and at 42 and 44, with NONE at 40. The
class is irregular, not a window, confirming 558.1 again.

CORRECTED (374.1), twice, both my own test design. FIRST, scanning
the uniform family at the single size 2N = 4s produced an octagon at
every odd span, and the octagons turn out to be four chords and four
host steps with displacements summing to 4s - they wind once and
exist only because the test point made them close. Retested at
generic sizes the family still always has a power of two, but the
length varies with 2N, so no single configuration settles it.
SECOND, the winding criterion in its first form assumed every chord
contributes +s and missed 22 of 38 spectra; from an even vertex a
chord contributes -s, so the net chord displacement is c s with
|c| <= k and c congruent to k modulo 2.

STANDING: 560.2's universal octagon for span 5, whose three chords
lie inside the first ten vertices and which does not wind, so SPAN 5
REMAINS SETTLED for the whole infinite family.

NOT PROVED, and explicitly not yet verified: the corrected winding
criterion; the uniform family at spans other than 5; (LQ3-3); (OPEN)
for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4);
(LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7;
the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked whether
560.2's octagon generalises across spans, the answer is no, and the
route to it went through two errors of my own making. Testing each
span at 2N = 4s guaranteed the very configuration it then found - a
four-chord octagon that winds once around and closes only because
four spans make a full turn - and retesting at generic sizes shows
the family still always has a power of two but not always an octagon:
eight while the circle is small enough for four chords to close it,
sixteen after. Then the criterion meant to explain that assumed all
chords are traversed in the same direction, which is false whenever a
run has even length, and it missed a fifth of the spectra it was
tested against. What survives is 560.2 - span five is settled, by a
configuration that does not wind and sits inside ten vertices - and a
corrected criterion that is written down here as a candidate and left
unverified until its check returns.


## 562. THE UNIFORM LADDER HAS CUTWIDTH s: WHAT THE MACHINE CAN AND
## CANNOT REACH

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 560 built the transfer
matrix and 561 set it to work across spans. This section records why
that stalls, and it is not a defect of the program: the uniform
ladder's cutwidth is exactly its span, so the state space is the
number of involutions on s+1 points. Two encodings are given that
buy the size direction outright and the span direction not at all.
Machine: scratch tm.py, ftm.py, ctm.py.

### 562.0 THE CUTWIDTH OF A UNIFORM LADDER IS ITS SPAN (COMPUTED)

For U(2N, s) with chords {i, i+s} at odd i, the number of chords
spanning a cut is measured at

    s  =  5, 7, 9, 11, 13   ->   cutwidth  =  5, 7, 9, 11, 13 ,

that is, CUTWIDTH EQUALS SPAN. Every second vertex in a window of
length s starts a chord that crosses the far end of it.

  SO THE UNIFORM FAMILY IS NOT A BOUNDED-CUTWIDTH FAMILY. 556.2
  measured cutwidth 4 to 6 on 543's counterexamples and 556.3 built a
  dichotomy on that parameter; the uniform ladders sit in the
  UNBOUNDED regime once the span grows, and only the small spans lie
  in the tractable one. 538.4's decidability, which needs a periodic
  family of bounded cutwidth, therefore applies to each FIXED s and
  not to the family as a whole.

### 562.1 THE WALL, MEASURED

The transfer-matrix state is a matching on the frontier - the open
chords plus the host edge, so s+1 slots - and the number of such
matchings is the involution number:

    s     frontier    states      one spectrum at 2N = 4s
    5        6            76        0.04 s
    7        8           764        0.54 s
    9       10          9496        4.44 s
   11       12        140152       37.72 s
   13       14       2390480      328.97 s

  A FACTOR OF ABOUT NINE PER SPAN STEP. This is the pathwidth of the
  object showing through, not an inefficiency, and no encoding
  removes it.

### 562.2 TWO ENCODINGS THAT DO HELP (IN THE SIZE DIRECTION)

  POLYNOMIALS AS BIG INTEGERS. Store the generating polynomial
  SUM c_L x^L as the single integer SUM c_L 2^{96 L}. Then
  multiplying by x^a is a bit shift and adding two polynomials is one
  integer addition, both executed at machine speed rather than by a
  Python loop over lengths. Effect: the span-5 spectrum at 2N = 400 -
  319 distinct lengths, 4.9 times 10^30 cycles - in 1.76 seconds,
  where the dictionary version is not usable at that size.

  MEMOISED TRANSITIONS. The transition relation depends only on the
  state and on the vertex's signature - which slots open and close -
  and both repeat constantly, so computing each once and reusing it
  turns the inner loop into table lookups.

  AND A CORRECTION OF MY OWN (374.1): the first fast version reused
  one identifier for the host edge entering a vertex and the host
  edge leaving it. At an interior vertex both are present at once, so
  the matching could not tell them apart and the counts were wrong.
  Distinct identifiers per host edge fix it; the check against the
  slow version then agrees exactly.

### 562.3 THE RIGHT TOOL IN EACH DIRECTION (IDENTIFIED)

  FOR THE SIZE 2N, at fixed span: the ladder is periodic under
  i -> i+2, so the transfer matrix of one period is the SAME at every
  step, and the whole family is governed by powers of one fixed
  matrix. Computing that power by repeated squaring gives any 2N in
  a logarithmic number of matrix multiplications, and the generating
  function of the family is rational with denominator the
  characteristic polynomial. This is 556.1's promise, and it is
  available for every fixed s where the state space fits.

  FOR THE SPAN s: nothing in this line of attack scales, and the
  transfer matrix should not be asked to. The instrument for the span
  direction is 561.2's displacement criterion, which is polynomial in
  s and 2N. The matrix's job is to VERIFY that criterion at the spans
  where it fits - 5, 7, 9, perhaps 11 - after which the criterion
  itself runs instantly at every span.

  SO THE VERIFICATION SHOULD BE RESTRICTED TO s AT MOST 11. Run at
  s = 13 it costs five minutes per ladder and returns nothing the
  smaller spans do not already say.

### 562.4 STATUS

COMPUTED: the cutwidth of the uniform ladder U(2N, s) equals s, at
s = 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13; the transfer-matrix state count is the
involution number on s+1 points - 76, 764, 9496, 140152, 2390480 -
and one spectrum costs 0.04, 0.54, 4.44, 37.72 and 328.97 seconds.

IDENTIFIED: that the uniform family is therefore NOT of bounded
cutwidth, so 556.3's tractable regime and 538.4's decidability apply
to each fixed span and not to the family as a whole; and that the
wall is the object's pathwidth rather than an inefficiency.

RECORDED, as method: polynomials stored as single big integers, so
that shifting and adding are machine operations - which puts the
span-5 spectrum at 2N = 400 within two seconds - and memoised
transitions keyed by state and vertex signature. Together with the
observation that at fixed span the ladder is periodic, so the family
is powers of one fixed matrix and any 2N costs a logarithmic number
of multiplications.

CORRECTED (374.1): a first fast implementation gave one identifier to
both host edges at a vertex; they coexist there, so the state could
not distinguish them. Fixed, and checked against the slow version.

NOT PROVED: 561.2's corrected criterion, whose check is still
running; the uniform family at spans other than 5; (LQ3-3); (OPEN)
for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4);
(LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7;
the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asked to make
the machine fast, the useful finding is where it cannot be. The
uniform ladder's cutwidth is exactly its span, so the transfer
matrix's state space is the number of involutions on s+1 points and
grows by a factor of nine with every step of s - 76 states at span 5
and 2390480 at span 13, five minutes for a single spectrum. That is
the pathwidth of the object and no encoding touches it. What
encodings do buy is the other direction entirely: storing the
generating polynomial as one big integer makes shifting and adding
machine operations and puts a 400-vertex spectrum inside two seconds,
and at fixed span the periodicity means the whole family is powers of
a single fixed matrix, so any size costs a logarithmic number of
multiplications. The division of labour is therefore clean - the
matrix owns the size direction and should be capped at span 11, and
the span direction belongs to 561.2's criterion, which the matrix
exists only to check.


## 563. THE DIRECTION-CHANGE CRITERION: THE UNIFORM SPECTRUM IN
## CLOSED FORM, AND A SCAN OF 111870 LADDERS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 561.2 proposed a
displacement criterion for the uniform spectrum and left it
unverified. Two forms of it were wrong; the third is exact on every
ladder tested, it is pure arithmetic, and it moves the uniform family
out of reach of the transfer matrix and into a scan that costs
seconds. Machine: scratch ctm.py and a criterion scan.

### 563.0 THE CRITERION (VERIFIED EXACT WHERE TESTED)

In U(2N, s) with s odd, traverse a cycle. Each chord runs odd to even
(+s) or even to odd (-s); between chords lie maximal host runs. To
take a +s chord one must stand on an ODD vertex and to take a -s
chord on an EVEN one, so the parity of a run is decided by the pair
of chord directions on either side of it:

    + then +   run ODD        + then -   run EVEN
    - then +   run EVEN       - then -   run ODD

  So the EVEN runs are exactly those at a DIRECTION CHANGE, and an
  even run has length at least 2. Writing k for the number of chords,
  k+ and k- for the two directions, c = k+ - k-, t for the number of
  direction changes and h = L - k for the host edges:

    CRITERION. A cycle of length L exists only if L is even and for
    some k >= 1, some split k+ + k- = k, some even t with
    0 <= t <= 2 min(k+, k-) - and t = 0 exactly when one direction is
    absent - and some integer w:

        h >= k + t ,      h = k - t   (mod 2) ,
        |w 2N - c s| <= h  and  h - (w 2N - c s) even .

  VERIFIED, as an exact characterisation and not merely a necessary
  condition: over 24 girth-legal uniform ladders at spans 5, 7, 9 and
  11 and every even 2N from 2s+6 to 4s+2, the criterion's predicted
  length set equals the true cycle spectrum EXACTLY - 0 mismatches in
  either direction.

### 563.1 THE TWO WRONG FORMS (CORRECTED, 374.1)

  FIRST FORM assumed every chord contributes +s. It missed 22 of 38
  spectra, always by omission - at s = 7 it missed the hexagon, which
  is two chords traversed in opposite directions. From an EVEN vertex
  a chord contributes -s.

  SECOND FORM fixed that but ruled that a run preceding a +s chord is
  odd and one preceding a -s chord is even. That is also wrong: what
  matters is where the run STARTS as well as where it ends, so the
  parity depends on BOTH neighbouring chord directions. It predicted
  a 4-cycle in every ladder - 38 mismatches, all the same spurious
  length - and separately missed the hexagon again in 10 of 24.

  BOTH ERRORS ARE THE SAME ERROR: assuming a uniformity the object
  does not have, which is what 547.0 found in 544.2 and 561.2 found
  in itself. Three times now. The tell each time was a mismatch set
  consisting of a single length repeated across every ladder.

### 563.2 THE SCAN (COMPUTED)

The criterion needs no graph. Taking only its simplest branch -
t = 0, all chords one direction, where c = k and the parity condition
holds automatically because 2N is even and s is odd, so
w 2N - k s = k = h modulo 2 - the test reduces to

    does some multiple of 2N lie within L - k of k s,
    for some k between 1 and L/2 ?

  Run over every uniform ladder with odd span from 5 to 201 and every
  girth-legal even 2N up to 24s:

      111870 pairs (s, 2N) tested,
      pairs admitting NO power of two:  0 ,
      elapsed:  5.6 seconds.

  FOR SCALE, 562.1 measured a single spectrum at span 13 at 329
  seconds. The criterion covers a hundred and eleven thousand ladders
  in under six, and it does it at spans the matrix cannot enter at
  all.

### 563.3 WHAT IS AND IS NOT ESTABLISHED

  ESTABLISHED: the criterion is exact on the 24 ladders where the
  matrix can check it, and on the t = 0 branch it admits a power of
  two for all 111870 pairs scanned.

  NOT ESTABLISHED: that the criterion is exact beyond s = 11 and
  2N = 4s+2. The scan is CONDITIONAL on it, and the direction that
  needs proof is SUFFICIENCY - that the arithmetic condition really
  produces a cycle. The construction is clear enough: k chords all
  taken forwards, with k host runs of odd lengths summing to h and
  signs chosen so the total displacement is w 2N. What is not clear
  is that the run lengths can always be chosen so that the walk is
  SIMPLE. That is the gap, and it is a packing question about odd
  compositions rather than an arithmetic one.

### 563.4 STATUS

PROVED here, as a structural fact about traversal: in a uniform
ladder the parity of a host run is determined by the directions of
the chords on either side of it, even runs occurring exactly at
direction changes and having length at least 2. Hence the run-length
bound h >= k + t and the parity h = k - t modulo 2.

VERIFIED: the resulting criterion reproduces the cycle spectrum
EXACTLY - zero mismatches in either direction - on all 24 girth-legal
uniform ladders at spans 5, 7, 9, 11 with 2N from 2s+6 to 4s+2.

COMPUTED: 111870 pairs (s, 2N), odd spans 5 to 201 and girth-legal
even sizes to 24s, every one admitting a power of two on the t = 0
branch alone, in 5.6 seconds - against 329 seconds for one spectrum
at span 13 by transfer matrix.

CORRECTED (374.1), twice more: the criterion's first form assumed all
chords are traversed forwards, and its second form assigned run
parity by the following chord alone. Both are the error of 547.0 -
assuming a uniformity the object lacks - and both announced
themselves as a single spurious or missing length repeated across
every ladder.

NOT PROVED: sufficiency of the criterion, hence the scan is
conditional; the uniform family at spans above 11 unconditionally;
(LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3),
equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2
cancellation; J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The uniform
spectrum has a closed form. A cycle is a sequence of chords, each
taken forwards or backwards, separated by host runs whose parities
are forced by the directions on either side - odd between like
directions, even and therefore at least two at every direction change
- and the whole thing closes when the signed displacement is a
multiple of 2N. That gives an arithmetic criterion which reproduces
the true spectrum exactly wherever the transfer matrix can check it,
and which then runs without any graph at all: a hundred and eleven
thousand ladders, spans up to two hundred and one, in under six
seconds, with a power of two admitted every single time. What remains
is the sufficiency proof, and its difficulty is not arithmetic but
combinatorial - the odd run lengths must be chosen so the walk does
not revisit a vertex.


## 564. SUFFICIENCY BY CONSTRUCTION: THE SKIPPED-INTERVAL ARGUMENT,
## AND THE UNIFORM FAMILY SETTLED ON THE SCANNED RANGE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 563.3 left sufficiency
open - the criterion's arithmetic had to be turned into a SIMPLE
cycle. It can be, by an argument that costs one observation, and the
resulting construction plus 560.2's octagon covers every uniform
ladder in the scanned range. Nothing here is conditional on the
criterion. Machine: scratch (coverage scans, three runs).

### 564.0 THE SKIPPED-INTERVAL ARGUMENT (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Take k chords of U(2N, s), all traversed FORWARD, separated
  by host runs r_1, ..., r_k with signs, each r_j ODD and every
  BACKWARD run of length less than s. If

      SUM over j of ( s + eps_j r_j )  =  2N ,

  then the closed walk is a SIMPLE cycle, of length k + SUM r_j.
    PROOF. Write v_0, v_1, ... for the vertices at which the chords
  start. Then v_{j+1} = v_j + s + eps_j r_j, and since a backward run
  is shorter than s the increment is positive, so the chord starts
  STRICTLY INCREASE. The walk covers, at step j, the chord from v_j
  to v_j + s - whose interior it SKIPS - and then the run. If the run
  is forward it covers (v_j + s, v_{j+1}], which lies beyond
  everything seen. If it is backward it covers [v_{j+1}, v_j + s),
  which lies INSIDE the interval (v_j, v_j + s) that the chord had
  just skipped, and is therefore untouched. Either way no vertex
  repeats, and the displacements sum to exactly one lap, so the walk
  closes. Each v_j is odd, since s and every r_j are odd, so every
  chord used exists. QED

  THE POINT IS THE SKIPPED INTERVAL. A chord leaps over s - 1
  vertices; a backward run of length less than s can only land among
  them, and they are precisely the ones the cycle has not used.

### 564.1 THE ARITHMETIC OF THE CONSTRUCTION

Let m runs be backward and k - m forward, with P the total forward
run length and M the total backward. Then

    P - M = 2N - k s ,      P + M = L - k ,

so P and M are determined by k and L. The construction exists iff for
some k and some m,

    M >= m ,   M <= m (s - 2) ,   M = m  (mod 2) ,
    P >= k - m ,                  P = k - m  (mod 2) ,

the upper bound on M because each backward run is odd and less than
s, hence at most s - 2.

### 564.2 COVERAGE (COMPUTED)

Over every uniform ladder with odd span 5 to 201 and girth-legal even
2N up to 24s - 111870 pairs:

    all runs forward, one lap      10945 pairs      9.8 per cent
    backward runs allowed         111849 pairs     99.98 per cent
    RESIDUAL                          21 pairs

  and the twenty-one residuals are ALL AT SPAN 5:

    2N = 26, 28, 30, 50, 52, 54, 56, 58, 60, 62,
         98, 100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114, 116, 118 .

### 564.3 THE RESIDUE FALLS TO 560.2 (PROVED)

Every residual has s = 5 and 2N at least 12, which is exactly the
hypothesis of 560.2's UNIVERSAL OCTAGON - the eight vertices 1, 2, 3,
5, 6, 8, 9, 10 with chords (1,6), (3,8), (5,10), which exists in the
span-5 uniform ladder at every size and does not wind.

  SO THE UNIFORM FAMILY IS SETTLED ON THE WHOLE SCANNED RANGE, by two
  explicit constructions and nothing else:

    the skipped-interval construction of 564.0, for 111849 pairs,
    560.2's universal octagon, for the remaining 21 .

  NEITHER IS CONDITIONAL ON 563's CRITERION. Both exhibit a simple
  cycle. The criterion's role was to say where to look.

### 564.4 WHAT IS STILL MISSING

The range is finite: spans to 201 and sizes to 24s. To make this a
theorem for ALL uniform ladders one must show the conditions of 564.1
are satisfiable in general, which is a statement about choosing k.
The range for k is already known to be wide - taking L the largest
power of two below 2N, so that L exceeds N, the conditions P >= 0 and
M >= 0 give

    (2N - L)/(s - 1)   <=   k   <=   (L + 2N)/(s + 1) ,

an interval which is non-empty for every s at least 3, since
(s + 1) < 3 (s - 1) there. What remains is to show that some k in
that interval also meets the parity and representability conditions
on P and M - a counting argument over an interval of length of order
N/s, with two parities to match.

### 564.5 STATUS

PROVED here: THE SKIPPED-INTERVAL LEMMA - k forward chords with odd
host runs, every backward run shorter than s, and total displacement
one lap, give a SIMPLE cycle of length k plus the sum of the runs;
because the chord starts strictly increase and a backward run lands
only among the vertices the preceding chord skipped.

COMPUTED: over 111870 uniform ladders with odd span 5 to 201, the
all-forward case covers 10945, the construction with backward runs
covers 111849, and the 21 residuals all have span 5 - where 560.2's
universal octagon applies. SO EVERY UNIFORM LADDER IN THE SCANNED
RANGE HAS A POWER-OF-TWO CYCLE, BY EXPLICIT CONSTRUCTION, WITH NO
DEPENDENCE ON 563'S CRITERION.

NOT PROVED: that 564.1's conditions are satisfiable for every s and
2N, which is what would turn the scan into a theorem; the criterion's
sufficiency in general; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open ladders;
(COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at
girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements of
451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Sufficiency
turns on one observation. A chord of a uniform ladder leaps over s-1
vertices, and those vertices are exactly the ones the cycle does not
use; so a backward host run shorter than s lands among them and
cannot collide with anything. That makes the walk simple for free,
and the only remaining condition is that the displacements make one
lap - which is arithmetic, not geometry. The construction so obtained
covers 111849 of the 111870 uniform ladders scanned, spans up to two
hundred and one, and every one of the twenty-one exceptions has span
five, where 560.2's octagon already applies at every size. So the
uniform family - named as the hard case at 532.1, classified at
537.2, reached independently as the structured extreme at 536.4 - now
has an explicit power-of-two cycle at every size and span tested, by
construction rather than by criterion. What is left is to replace the
scan by a counting argument: show that among the roughly N/s
admissible values of k, one always meets the two parity conditions.


## 565. THE PARITY CONDITION IN CLOSED FORM, AND WHERE THE LAST CASE
## SITS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 564.4 left one step
between the scan and a theorem: show 564.1's conditions are always
satisfiable. This section reduces them to a single parity question,
verifies the reduction exactly, and settles all but one congruence
class. One simplification was tried and was too strong; it is
recorded. Machine: scratch (reduction checks, three runs).

### 565.0 THE CONDITIONS COLLAPSE (PROVED)

Write D = 2N - L, so D is even and D >= 0 when L is a power of two
below 2N. With k chords,

    M = ( k(s-1) - D ) / 2 ,      P = L - k - M .

  (i) M IS ALWAYS AN INTEGER. Both s-1 and D are even, so no parity
      condition falls on k at all.
  (ii) THE TWO PARITY CONDITIONS OF 564.1 ARE ONE. If M = m mod 2
      then P = (L-k) - M = (L-k) - m, and P = k - m demands
      L = 2k mod 2, which holds because L is even. So only
      m = M (mod 2) is a constraint.
  (iii) M <= m(s-2) AT m = M IS AUTOMATIC for s >= 5, and more
      generally M <= k(s-2) reduces to -D <= k(s-3), true always.
  (iv) P >= k - m at m = M reduces to 2k <= L, and the lower bound
      m >= 2k - L + M is exactly P >= 0.

  SO THE WHOLE OF 564.1 IS: choose k with M >= 0, P >= 0 and
  2k <= L, then find m congruent to M modulo 2 in the interval

      [ max( ceil(M/(s-2)), 2k - L + M, 0 ) ,  min(M, k) ] .

  VERIFIED EXACT: over 35424 triples (s, 2N, L) with s odd from 5 to
  59, this closed form agrees with the full search in EVERY case - 0
  disagreements - and reproduces 564.2's coverage exactly, 111849 of
  111870 with the 21 residuals all at span 5.

### 565.1 A SIMPLIFICATION THAT WAS TOO STRONG (CORRECTED, 374.1)

I first claimed the interval condition reduces to M <= k, on the
ground that m = M then works. That IS a sufficient case, and I then
wrote it down as if it were the whole condition. It is not: when
M > k one must take m < M, with m at least ceil(M/(s-2)).

  The check caught it at once - 4605 disagreements in 35424 triples,
  and the coverage fell from 99.98 to 83.29 per cent. Recorded
  because the error is the familiar one in yet another dress:
  a sufficient case mistaken for the criterion.

### 565.2 THE PARITY, IN CLOSED FORM (PROVED)

When M <= k the choice m = M settles it. So the question is the case
M > k, where the interval is [lo, k] with lo = max(ceil(M/(s-2)),
2k - L + M) - both bounds already known to be at most k - and one
needs a member congruent to M modulo 2. Taking m = k works when
k = M mod 2, and m = k-1 works otherwise provided k-1 >= lo.

  NOW THE KEY COMPUTATION. Increasing k by one increases M by
  (s-1)/2, so the parity of k - M shifts by 1 - (s-1)/2 modulo 2:

    s = 1 (mod 4):  (s-1)/2 is EVEN, so k - M ALTERNATES with k, and
                    one of any two consecutive admissible k has
                    k = M (mod 2). The case is settled.
    s = 3 (mod 4):  (s-1)/2 is ODD, so k - M is CONSTANT in k, equal
                    to D/2 modulo 2. If D = 0 (mod 4) every k works;
                    if D = 2 (mod 4) NO k has k = M (mod 2), and the
                    argument must fall back on m = k-1, needing
                    k - 1 >= ceil(M/(s-2)) and k + M <= L - 1.

  SO EXACTLY ONE CASE REMAINS OPEN: spans congruent to 3 modulo 4
  together with D = 2N - L congruent to 2 modulo 4. Everywhere else
  the parity is free.

### 565.3 STATUS

PROVED here: that 564.1's conditions reduce to a single parity
requirement. M is always an integer, because s-1 and D are both even;
the two parity conditions of 564.1 are the same condition; the bound
M <= m(s-2) and the lower bound on m are automatic given P >= 0 and
2k <= L. What is left is to find m congruent to M modulo 2 in an
interval whose endpoints are explicit.

PROVED: the parity of k - M shifts by 1 - (s-1)/2 when k increases by
one. Hence for s congruent to 1 modulo 4 the difference alternates
and one of any two consecutive k succeeds; for s congruent to 3
modulo 4 it is constant and equal to D/2 modulo 2, so every k
succeeds when D is divisible by 4 and none does when D is 2 modulo 4.

VERIFIED: the closed form agrees with the full search on all 35424
triples tested, 0 disagreements, and reproduces the 99.98 per cent
coverage with the same 21 span-5 residuals.

CORRECTED (374.1): the claim that the interval condition is just
M <= k. That is the sufficient case m = M; when M > k a smaller m is
required. The mistaken form disagreed on 4605 triples and lost
sixteen points of coverage.

NOT PROVED: the case s congruent to 3 modulo 4 with 2N - L congruent
to 2 modulo 4, where the fallback m = k-1 must be justified; hence
the uniform family is still settled only on the scanned range;
(LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3),
equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2
cancellation; J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The conditions
that 564 left to be checked collapse almost entirely. M is an integer
for every k, the two parities are one parity, and both awkward bounds
are consequences of P >= 0 and 2k <= L, so all that survives is
finding one m of the right parity in an explicit interval. That in
turn depends on how the parity of k - M moves with k, and it moves by
1 - (s-1)/2: when s is 1 modulo 4 it alternates and consecutive k
cover both parities, and when s is 3 modulo 4 it is frozen at D/2. So
three of the four congruence classes are free and one - span 3 modulo
4 with 2N - L equal to 2 modulo 4 - needs the fallback argument. The
closed form was verified against the full search on thirty-five
thousand triples without a single disagreement, after a first version
that mistook a sufficient case for the criterion and was caught by
the same check.


## 566. A WRONG DISPLACEMENT EQUATION IN 564 AND 565, AND THE
## CORRECTED RESULT: ONE LAP SUFFICES EVERYWHERE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Chasing the last
congruence class of 565 turned up an inconsistency between the parity
theory and the tally that was supposed to confirm it. The theory was
right and the programs were wrong: they solved for TWO laps. With the
equation corrected the result is stronger, not weaker. Machine:
scratch (trace, soundness check, corrected scan).

### 566.0 THE BUG (CORRECTED, 374.1, LOUDLY)

In the scripts behind 564.2 and 565.0 the variable n holds the number
of VERTICES, that is 2N. The one-lap condition is

    P - M  =  2N - k s  =  n - k s ,

and every one of those scripts wrote 2*n - k*s. THEY THEREFORE
SOLVED FOR TWO LAPS, w = 2, and a two-lap walk is not simple, so the
family they scanned was not the family 564.0 proves.

  HOW IT SURFACED. 565.2 proved that for s congruent to 3 modulo 4
  with D congruent to 2 modulo 4 the quantity k - M is ODD for every
  k, so the choice m = k can never have the right parity. The tally
  meant to confirm this reported m = k used 18697 times and m = k-1
  never - flatly contradicting a proof. Tracing one instance,
  s = 7 and 2N = 34, gave M = 0 at k = 6 where the correct formula
  gives M = 3k - 1 = 17. The discrepancy was the factor of two.

  SO 564.2's COVERAGE FIGURES AND 565.0's VERIFICATION ARE VOID.
  Both compared programs that shared the same error, so they agreed
  with each other while both computing the wrong family. 565's
  claim of "0 disagreements over 35424 triples" is exactly that: two
  wrong things agreeing.

### 566.1 THE CORRECTED COMPUTATION

With P - M = n - k s and P + M = L - k:

  SOUNDNESS. Over the uniform ladders at spans 5, 7, 9, 11 with 2N
  from 2s+6 to 4s+2, the construction claims 295 lengths and EVERY
  ONE of them is a genuine cycle length of the ladder - 0 false
  claims, checked against the transfer matrix.

  COVERAGE. Over all 111870 uniform ladders with odd span 5 to 201
  and girth-legal even 2N up to 24s:

      pairs admitting a power of two by the ONE-LAP construction
          111870  of  111870      -   100.00 per cent,
      residuals                   -   NONE .

  So the corrected construction is both sound and, on this range,
  complete. The 21 span-5 exceptions of 564.2 were an artefact of the
  two-lap equation; 560.2's universal octagon is not needed as a
  fallback at all.

### 566.2 WHAT STANDS AND WHAT DOES NOT

  STANDS: 564.0's SKIPPED-INTERVAL LEMMA, which is a geometric
  argument and never mentioned the displacement equation - k forward
  chords, odd runs, every backward run shorter than s, total exactly
  one lap, gives a simple cycle. Also 565.0's algebra, which used the
  correct M = (k(s-1) - D)/2 throughout; it was only 565's
  VERIFICATION that ran on the faulty code.

  DOES NOT STAND: 564.2's coverage table and its 21 residuals;
  565.0's "0 disagreements" verification; and 565.2's case analysis
  as a description of what the programs did - though as a statement
  about the correct M it must now be re-derived and re-checked, since
  the tally that appeared to confirm it was measuring something else.

### 566.3 STATUS

CORRECTED here (374.1), loudly: the scripts behind 564.2 and 565.0
wrote 2*n - k*s where the one-lap condition is n - k*s, with n the
vertex count 2N. They solved for two laps. The error was invisible
because the closed form and the full search shared it, so their
agreement confirmed nothing; it surfaced only when 565.2's parity
theorem contradicted the tally meant to illustrate it.

COMPUTED, with the corrected equation: the construction claims 295
lengths across the test ladders and all 295 are real; and over 111870
uniform ladders with odd spans 5 to 201, EVERY ONE admits a
power-of-two cycle by the one-lap construction - 100 per cent, no
residuals.

STANDING: 564.0's skipped-interval lemma, and 565.0's reduction of
the conditions to a single parity requirement with
M = (k(s-1) - D)/2.

WITHDRAWN: 564.2's coverage figures and its 21 residuals; 565.0's
verification; and the confirmation status of 565.2's case analysis.

NOT PROVED: that the one-lap conditions are satisfiable for every s
and 2N rather than on the scanned range; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime
open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER
BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five
statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The last
congruence class did not need closing, because the case analysis that
produced it was checked against programs solving a different problem.
Those programs asked for two laps where the construction needs one,
and they all shared the mistake, so the closed form and the full
search agreed with each other and confirmed nothing - the error
announced itself only when a proved parity statement contradicted the
table meant to illustrate it. Corrected, the picture is better than
before: the one-lap construction never claims a length the ladder
does not have, and it produces a power of two for every one of the
hundred and eleven thousand uniform ladders scanned, with no
exceptions and no need of the span-5 octagon. What is still owed is
what was owed at 564.4 - a proof that the conditions are satisfiable
in general rather than on a finite range - and it must now be

## 567. THE PRESCRIBED CHORD COUNT: k_0 OR k_0 + 1 ALWAYS WORKS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 566 corrected the
displacement equation and left the general satisfiability of the
one-lap conditions to be re-derived. It is derived here, the choice
of k is explicit, and it is checked against the transfer matrix
rather than against another closed form. Machine: scratch (matrix
check on 38 ladders, arithmetic scan on 443770 pairs).

### 567.0 THE PRESCRIPTION

With L a power of two at most 2N and D = 2N - L, put

    k_0  =  ceiling( D / (s-1) ) ,      M(k) = ( k(s-1) - D ) / 2 ,
    P(k) =  L - k - M(k) .

  k_0 is the least k with M >= 0, and by minimality
  k_0(s-1) - D < s-1, so

      M(k_0)  <  (s-1)/2  <  s - 2       for s >= 5 ,

  whence ceiling( M/(s-2) ) is 0 or 1 and the lower end of the
  m-interval is essentially 2k - L + M, which is at most k exactly
  when P >= 0.

  THE THREE BRANCHES.
    (i)  M <= k : take m = M. Valid because the upper end of the
         interval is then M itself and 2k - L + M <= M is 2k <= L.
    (ii) M > k and k = M (mod 2) : take m = k.
    (iii) M > k and k /= M (mod 2) : take m = k-1, which needs
         k >= 2 and P >= 1.

  AND THE PARITY MOVES PREDICTABLY. Raising k by one raises M by
  (s-1)/2, so the parity of k - M shifts by 1 - (s-1)/2:
  for s = 1 (mod 4) it ALTERNATES, so one of k_0, k_0+1 lands in
  branch (ii); for s = 3 (mod 4) it is FROZEN, and one takes k_0 + 1,
  which is at least 2, into branch (iii). The condition P >= 1 there
  amounts to L >= about (s+1)(s-1)/(s-2), that is L >= about s+3,
  which holds because L exceeds N and girth-legality forces
  N >= s + 2.

### 567.1 CHECKED AGAINST THE TRANSFER MATRIX

Per 566's lesson - a closed form checked against a search sharing its
helper confirms nothing - the prescription is checked against the
transfer matrix, an independent computation of the true spectrum.

  Over the uniform ladders at spans 5, 7, 9, 11 with 2N from 2s+6 to
  5s: 38 ladders, a valid k found for EVERY one, and the length it
  claims is a genuine cycle length in EVERY case - 0 failures, 0
  unreal claims. All three branches are exercised: m = M twenty-one
  times, m = k nine times, m = k-1 eight times, so none is vacuous.

### 567.2 THE ARITHMETIC SCAN

Taking the prescription alone, over every uniform ladder with odd
span 5 to 401 and girth-legal even 2N up to 24s:

    443770 pairs,   FAILURES 0 ,   elapsed 3.3 seconds,
    branches: m = k 230581,  m = k-1 192720,  m = M 20469 .

  k_0 or k_0 + 1 suffices every time; the search never had to look
  further.

### 567.3 WHAT IS STILL OWED

The prescription is proved to work whenever branch (i) or (ii)
applies, and branch (iii) is proved to work whenever P >= 1 and
k >= 2. What is not written out is a clean bound showing P >= 1 at
k_0 + 1 for every admissible (s, 2N) rather than asymptotically -
the estimate L >= (s+1)(s-1)/(s-2) is comfortable but the edge
cases where N is close to s + 2 deserve to be checked by hand rather
than absorbed into an approximation. Until that is done the family is
settled on the scanned range and not as a theorem.

  A NOTE ON A STALE JOB. The criterion check launched before 563
  returned after 4787 seconds with 55 mismatches, all of the form
  "predicted 4, not real" - the spurious 4-cycle that 563.1 already
  identified and removed. It is reported here only so the record
  shows it was read and is superseded.

### 567.4 STATUS

PROVED here: that k_0 = ceiling(D/(s-1)) gives M < (s-1)/2 < s-2, so
the lower end of the m-interval is governed by P >= 0 alone; that the
three branches m = M, m = k, m = k-1 cover the cases M <= k, and
M > k with k congruent or not congruent to M modulo 2; and that
raising k by one shifts the parity of k - M by 1 - (s-1)/2, so that
for s congruent to 1 modulo 4 one of k_0 and k_0+1 lands in branch
(ii), while for s congruent to 3 modulo 4 the frozen parity is
handled by k_0+1 in branch (iii) provided P >= 1.

VERIFIED against the TRANSFER MATRIX, not against another closed
form: on 38 uniform ladders at spans 5, 7, 9, 11, the prescription
finds a valid k every time and every length it claims is real - 0
failures, 0 unreal claims, all three branches used.

COMPUTED: over 443770 pairs with odd spans 5 to 401, the prescription
succeeds on all of them in 3.3 seconds, using m = k 230581 times,
m = k-1 192720 times and m = M 20469 times.

NOT PROVED: the bound P >= 1 at k_0+1 in the edge cases where N is
close to s+2, hence the uniform family remains settled on the scanned
range rather than as a theorem; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open
ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*);
