(E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements
of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The chord count
does not have to be searched for. Taking k_0 to be the least value
making M non-negative forces M below (s-1)/2, which is below s-2, and
that single inequality collapses the awkward lower end of the
m-interval; the three branches m = M, m = k and m = k-1 then cover
every case, and the parity of k - M moves by 1 - (s-1)/2 as k
advances, so spans congruent to 1 modulo 4 alternate into the second
branch while spans congruent to 3 modulo 4 are frozen and go to the
third. Checked against the transfer matrix - the independent oracle,
which is the discipline 566 was written to enforce - the prescription
never fails and never claims a length the ladder does not have, and
over four hundred and forty-three thousand ladders with spans to four
hundred and one it succeeds every time in three seconds. What is
owed is one inequality at the small end, where N is barely larger
than s.


## 568. THEOREM: EVERY UNIFORM LADDER HAS A POWER-OF-TWO CYCLE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The edge case 567.3
left is discharged, and with it the uniform family closes. This is
the first UNBOUNDED family this programme has settled - every odd
span, every size - and it is settled by explicit construction.
Machine: scratch (edge-window scan, explicit walks checked against
the transfer matrix).

### 568.0 THE EDGE WINDOW IS A SINGLE VALUE (PROVED)

567.3 owed P(k_0 + 1) >= 1. By minimality of k_0 the quantity
M(k_0) is below (s-1)/2, hence at most (s-3)/2, so

    M(k_0 + 1)  =  M(k_0) + (s-1)/2  <=  s - 2 ,
    k_0         <=  D/(s-1) + 1 ,

and therefore k_0 + 1 + M(k_0+1) <= D/(s-1) + s. So P(k_0+1) >= 1
follows from D/(s-1) + s + 1 <= L, which with D = 2N - L rearranges
to

        L s  >=  2N + s^2 - 1 .

  Since L exceeds N it suffices that N(s-2) >= s^2 - 1, that is

        N  >=  (s^2 - 1)/(s - 2)  =  s + 2 + 3/(s-2) .

  AND FOR s >= 5 THE TERM 3/(s-2) IS AT MOST 1. So every N >= s + 3
  satisfies it, and girth-legality gives N >= s + 2. THE ONLY CASE
  BELOW THE THRESHOLD IS N = s + 2 - a single value for each span,
  not a window.

### 568.1 THE TWO SMALL CASES, EXPLICITLY (PROVED)

  2N = 2s + 4, that is N = s + 2. Take k = 2 chords with runs +5 and
  -1. The displacement is 2s + 5 - 1 = 2s + 4 = 2N, exactly one lap;
  both runs are odd; the backward run has length 1, which is less
  than s; so 564.0 applies and the walk is a SIMPLE cycle of length
  2 + 6 = 8.

  2N = 2s + 6. Take k = 2 with runs +1 and +5: displacement
  2s + 6 = 2N, both runs odd, none backward, length 2 + 6 = 8.

  CHECKED against the transfer matrix at spans 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 and
  15: both walks return to their start in every case, and the true
  octagon counts are positive throughout - 21, 30, 36, 35, 22, 42,
  13, 35, 15, 24, 17, 27.

### 568.2 THE THEOREM

  THEOREM. Let s be odd and let U(2N, s) be a girth-legal uniform
  ladder - chords {i, i+s} for odd i, with 4 <= s <= N - 2. Then
  U(2N, s) contains a cycle whose length is a power of two.
    PROOF. If N = s + 2, the octagon of 568.1 exists. Otherwise
  N >= s + 3, so by 568.0 the inequality L s >= 2N + s^2 - 1 holds
  for L the largest power of two at most 2N, and hence
  P(k_0 + 1) >= 1.
    Take k to be k_0 or k_0 + 1. By 567.0, M(k_0) < (s-1)/2 < s-2, so
  the constraint m >= ceiling(M/(s-2)) is at most 1 and the binding
  lower bound on m is 2k - L + M, which is at most k precisely
  because P >= 0. Three cases exhaust the situation: if M <= k take
  m = M; if M > k and k = M modulo 2 take m = k; if M > k and the
  parities differ take m = k - 1, legitimate since k_0 + 1 >= 2 and
  P >= 1.
    The parity of k - M shifts by 1 - (s-1)/2 as k advances by one.
  For s = 1 modulo 4 it alternates, so one of k_0, k_0+1 falls in the
  second case. For s = 3 modulo 4 it is constant, and k_0 + 1 falls
  in the first or third.
    In every case the data (k, m) determines k odd host runs, m of
  them backward and each shorter than s, with total displacement
  exactly 2N. By 564.0's skipped-interval lemma the resulting closed
  walk is a SIMPLE cycle, and its length is k + (L - k) = L, a power
  of two. QED

### 568.3 WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE

  IT SETTLES the uniform family completely - every odd span and every
  legal size - which 532.1 named as the hard case, 537.2 classified,
  and 536.4 reached independently as the structured extreme. 560.2
  had settled span 5 alone; this settles all of them, and it is the
  first family of unbounded span and unbounded size the programme has
  closed.

  IT DOES NOT TOUCH the conjecture. Uniform ladders are one very
  structured slice of the closed-ladder world, singled out because
  every additive tool failed on them at 532.2. They were the obstacle
  to one method, not the substance of the problem. (LQ3) remains open
  and so does everything above it.

### 568.4 STATUS

PROVED here: THE EDGE BOUND - P(k_0+1) >= 1 whenever
L s >= 2N + s^2 - 1, which holds for all N >= (s^2-1)/(s-2), and
since that quantity is s + 2 + 3/(s-2) with 3/(s-2) at most 1 for
s >= 5, the only case below threshold is N = s + 2. THE TWO SMALL
CONSTRUCTIONS - k = 2 with runs +5, -1 at 2N = 2s+4 and with runs
+1, +5 at 2N = 2s+6, each an octagon by 564.0. AND THE THEOREM:
EVERY GIRTH-LEGAL UNIFORM LADDER CONTAINS A POWER-OF-TWO CYCLE.

VERIFIED against the transfer matrix: both small constructions close
at spans 5 through 15, with positive octagon counts throughout; and
399 edge pairs together with the previously unscanned 2N = 2s+4 for
every odd span to 401, no failures.

NOT PROVED: (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN);
(LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the
rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The uniform
ladders are done. The bound that was owed reduces to L s at least
2N + s^2 - 1, which holds as soon as N is at least s + 3, and since
girth-legality already forces N at least s + 2 the whole residue is a
single size per span - handled by an octagon one can write down: two
chords and runs of five and minus one. Everything else follows from
the prescription of 567 and the skipped-interval lemma of 564, so the
family that defeated every additive instrument at 532.2, that was
classified at 537.2 and identified from the far side at 536.4, now
has an explicit power-of-two cycle at every odd span and every legal
size. It is the first unbounded family this programme has closed. It
is also, and this should be said plainly, a slice - the uniform
ladders were an obstacle to one method rather than the substance of
the conjecture, and (LQ3) is exactly where it was.


## 569. THE SKIPPED-INTERVAL LEMMA IS FALSE; THE EXACT CRITERION, AND
## THE LIMITS OF ONE LAP

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The task was to carry
564.0 beyond the uniform ladders. The general statement exists and is
an EXACT criterion rather than a sufficient condition - and deriving
it shows that 564.0 IS FALSE AS STATED, with a counterexample at the
smallest girth-legal size there is. The correction voids the proof of
568.2, whose theorem is WITHDRAWN. Machine: scratch (counterexample
search, five million subset checks, corrected coverage, winding
audit).

### 569.0 THE COUNTEREXAMPLE (CORRECTED, 374.1, LOUDLY)

564.0 claimed: k chords of U(2N,s) all taken forward, host runs all
ODD, every BACKWARD run shorter than s, total displacement exactly
one lap, gives a SIMPLE cycle. Take 2N = 14, s = 5, runs +5, -3, -3:

  1 -> 6 -> 7,8,9,10,11 -> 2 -> 1,14,13 -> 4 -> 3,2,1 .

  Displacement 10 + 2 + 2 = 14, one lap. Runs 5, 3, 3, all odd. Both
  backward runs equal 3, which is less than 5. EVERY HYPOTHESIS
  HOLDS. The walk passes through fourteen vertices of which only
  twelve are distinct - it uses 1 and 2 twice each. It is not a cycle.

  WHERE THE PROOF FAILED. It observed that a backward run lands
  inside the interval the preceding chord had skipped, "and is
  therefore untouched". Untouched by what came BEFORE, yes. A LATER
  backward run can re-enter the same interval, and does, exactly when
  two backward runs are consecutive with r_j + r_{j+1} at least s. At
  2N = 14 alone there are 36 violations; the 2N = 24 instance with
  runs -3, -3, +5, +5 repeats two vertices in the same way.

### 569.1 THE EXACT CRITERION, FOR ANY CLOSED LADDER (PROVED)

Let the ladder be the host cycle on Z_{2N} with a perfect matching,
and for a vertex x let d(x) be the FORWARD span of its chord, so that
d(mate x) = 2N - d(x). A ONE-LAP WALK is determined by its set of
chord tails alone: given S = {x_1 < ... < x_k} in cyclic order, put
g_j = x_{j+1} - x_j (so the g_j are positive and sum to 2N), and let
the walk take the chord from x_j to x_j + d_j and then the host path
to x_{j+1} that does not pass x_j. Write

    b_j  =  max( 0, d_j - g_j )        the OVERSHOOT of chord j.

  LEMMA (SKIP*). The one-lap walk on S is a SIMPLE cycle if and only
  if g_j is never equal to d_j and

      b_j + b_{j+1}  <  d_{j+1}        for every j, cyclically;

  and then its length is

      2N  -  sum_j ( d_j - 1 )  +  2 sum_j b_j .

    PROOF. Unroll to x_1 < ... < x_k < x_{k+1} = x_1 + 2N. Step j
  visits x_j, then x_j + d_j, then the run; so the vertices it
  contributes are exactly the closed interval R_j between x_j + d_j
  and x_{j+1}, together with x_j, which lies in R_{j-1}. The walk has
  k + sum r_j edges and the R_j have k + sum r_j vertices in total, so
  IT IS SIMPLE IF AND ONLY IF THE R_j ARE PAIRWISE DISJOINT.
    Now the right end of R_j is x_{j+1} + b_j and its left end is
  x_j + d_j - b_j, hence at most x_{j+1}; and the left end of R_{j+1}
  is x_{j+1} + d_{j+1} - b_{j+1}, which exceeds x_{j+1}. SO THE LEFT
  ENDS INCREASE STRICTLY, and intervals sorted by left end are
  pairwise disjoint precisely when each ends before the next begins:
  x_{j+1} + b_j < x_{j+1} + d_{j+1} - b_{j+1}. QED

  THREE THINGS TO NOTICE. The span that appears in the condition is
  the NEXT chord's, not the current one - which is why 564.0's
  "shorter than s" was the wrong shape even in the uniform case.
  Uniformity is used nowhere. And no parity condition survives: in a
  general ladder every vertex carries a chord, so the requirement
  that runs be odd, which 564 needed to land on an odd tail, simply
  disappears.

  VERIFIED by direct simulation of the walk, on 5062618 tail sets -
  2360602 in uniform ladders with 2N up to 26, and 2702016 in all
  girth-legal ladders at 2N = 12 and 14. The criterion agrees with
  simplicity in EVERY case: 0 mismatches.

### 569.2 WHAT THE CORRECTION COSTS 564 TO 568 (WITHDRAWN)

564.1 turned the construction into arithmetic on four numbers: k
chords, m of the runs backward, M their total, P the total forward.
That list of conditions is wrong twice.

  (a) IT LETS m = k WITH P POSITIVE. If every run is backward there
      are no forward runs to carry P, so m = k forces P = 0. 564.1
      asked only for P >= k - m, which is P >= 0.
  (b) IT BOUNDS M BY m(s-2), WHICH IGNORES ADJACENCY. By SKIP* two
      consecutive backward runs must sum to less than s. The true
      bound is a CAPACITY: with f = k - m forward runs,

        C(k,m,s) = ( m(s-1) + (s-3) o ) / 2,  o the largest integer
                   at most min(f,m) with o congruent to m mod 2,

      and for f = 0 it is k(s-1)/2, less one when k is odd and
      (s-1)/2 is even.

  The capacity formula was checked against exhaustive enumeration of
  arrangements for every s up to 13 and k up to 7: it is exact, and
  every value congruent to m modulo 2 between m and C is attained.
  With (a) and (b) repaired the closed form reproduces the true
  one-lap spectrum, computed by search on the graph, EXACTLY - 72
  span-and-size rows to 2N = 44, 0 disagreements.

  AND 567's PRESCRIPTION DOES NOT SURVIVE. Over the 111719 uniform
  pairs with a power of two strictly below 2N, the (k,m,M,P) it
  prescribes is UNREALISABLE on 61905 of them - 55.4 per cent. Its
  favourite branch, m = k, used 230581 times in 567.2, is the branch
  that needs P = 0.

  SO 568.2 IS WITHDRAWN. Its proof ran through 567's prescription and
  564.0's lemma, and both are gone. The STATEMENT is not refuted, and
  the evidence for it is unchanged; what is gone is the proof.
  Withdrawn with it: 564.2's coverage table, 564.3's reduction to the
  span-5 octagon, 566.1's "100 per cent", 567.1 and 567.2, and 568's
  edge-case analysis, all of which computed the wrong family.

### 569.3 CORRECTED COVERAGE, AND WHERE ONE LAP DIES (COMPUTED)

Over all 112068 uniform ladders with odd span 5 to 201 and girth-legal
even 2N from 2s+4 to 24s, using the corrected conditions:

    largest power of two below 2N not reached      630 pairs,
    NO power of two reached at all                 273 pairs,
    smallest such ladder                           U(92, 41).

  ALL 273 HAVE SPAN CLOSE TO THE CEILING: s/N lies between 0.864 and
  0.976, against the girth-legal ceiling s = N-2. The reason is
  visible in the k-window. Summing the displacement two ways gives

      2N - L + k   <=   sum_j d_j   <=   2N + L - k ,

  so in a uniform ladder k lies between D/(s-1) and (2N+L)/(s+1), an
  interval of width of order N/s. 564.4 checked that this interval is
  NON-EMPTY and called it wide. Non-emptiness was never the question.
  When s is a constant fraction of N the interval holds about three
  integers - for U(92,41) it is [0.70, 3.71] - and three values of k,
  with savings quantised in steps of s-1 = 40, cannot hit an arbitrary
  target. THE METHOD DIES EXACTLY WHERE THE WINDOW IS O(1) WIDE.

### 569.4 WHAT RESCUES THEM IS NOT TWO LAPS BUT NONE (COMPUTED)

The 273 are not counterexamples to anything but the method. Taking
twelve of them, including all six smallest, a randomised search finds
cycles of length 16 and of length 32 in every one. Their winding
numbers, computed with a chord from an even tail counting +s and from
an odd tail -s, are

    length 16 :  6 chords,  winding 0    in all twelve,
    length 32 : 10 chords,  winding 0    in all twelve.

  ZERO, NOT TWO. The complementary mechanism to one lap is not a
  longer lap but a cycle that does not go round at all: p chords
  forward and p backward, host runs summing to zero. Its length is
  2p + sum |r_j|, and the run parities follow 561's corrected rule -
  odd between chords of like direction, even at a direction change -
  so with 2c direction changes the length is at least 4p + 2c. This
  family is indifferent to the span, which is why it covers precisely
  the long-span corner where one lap fails.

### 569.5 GENERAL LADDERS: ONE LAP SUFFICES ON EVERYTHING TESTED

For ladders that are not uniform the one-lap family is far richer,
because the savings d-1 are no longer all congruent.

    EXHAUSTIVE, every girth-legal closed ladder:
        2N = 12       24 ladders,     0 misses
        2N = 14      408 ladders,     0 misses
        2N = 16     8002 ladders,     0 misses
        2N = 18   168802 ladders,     0 misses

  - 177236 ladders, every one of which has a power-of-two length in
  its one-lap family. At 2N up to 16 the family was also checked
  against the complete cycle spectrum: it never claims a length the
  ladder does not have.

  SAMPLED: 1800 random girth-legal ladders at 2N = 20 to 30, and
  10800 LONG-SPAN ones - every circular span at least N-4 - at 2N =
  16 to 32. No misses. The second sample is the one that counts,
  since the known failures are all long-span; but it reaches only
  2N = 32, and U(92,41) shows what lives beyond it.

### 569.6 STATUS

CORRECTED here (374.1), loudly: 564.0's SKIPPED-INTERVAL LEMMA IS
FALSE. Its hypotheses hold and its conclusion fails at 2N = 14,
s = 5, runs +5, -3, -3, a walk on fourteen vertices of which twelve
are distinct. The proof only ever excluded collisions with earlier
steps; a later backward run re-enters the skipped interval whenever
two backward runs are consecutive and sum to at least s.

PROVED here: SKIP*, the exact criterion, for ANY closed ladder. The
one-lap walk on a tail set is simple if and only if no gap equals its
chord's span and consecutive overshoots satisfy
b_j + b_{j+1} < d_{j+1}; and its length is 2N - sum(d_j - 1) +
2 sum b_j. It is an equivalence, not a sufficient condition; it names
the NEXT chord's span; it needs no uniformity; and it carries no
parity condition, because in a general ladder every vertex is
matched.

VERIFIED: criterion against direct simulation on 5062618 tail sets,
0 mismatches; the capacity formula against exhaustive enumeration of
arrangements, exact; the corrected closed form against search on the
graph, 72 rows, 0 disagreements.

COMPUTED: with the corrected conditions the one-lap construction
misses the largest power of two on 630 of 111719 uniform pairs and
misses every power of two on 273 of 112068, the smallest being
U(92,41); all 273 have span above 0.86 N. Twelve of them, checked
directly, have 16-cycles and 32-cycles, all of winding number zero.
Exhaustively, all 177236 girth-legal closed ladders at 2N = 12, 14,
16 and 18 have a power of two in their one-lap family.

WITHDRAWN: 568.2's THEOREM, that every girth-legal uniform ladder has
a power-of-two cycle - the statement is not refuted but its proof is
void; with it 564.1's condition list, 564.2's coverage, 564.3, 566.1's
100 per cent, 567.0's prescription and 567.1, 567.2, and 568.0, 568.1
as a completion of that argument.

NOT PROVED: that the uniform family has power-of-two cycles, which
was believed proved at 568 and is now open again; that one lap
suffices for a general ladder; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open
ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*);
(E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements
of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Asking for the
general form of a lemma is a good way to find out that the lemma is
false. Carried to an arbitrary closed ladder the skipped-interval
argument becomes an exact criterion - the one-lap walk determined by
a set of chord tails is simple exactly when consecutive overshoots
sum to less than the next chord's span - and the derivation makes
plain that the uniform version needed a condition on PAIRS of
backward runs which 564.0 never imposed. A three-chord walk in the
smallest girth-legal uniform ladder satisfies every hypothesis 564.0
asked for and repeats two vertices. Repairing the arithmetic that
sat on top of it, which was wrong a second time in allowing all runs
to be backward while a positive forward total was still owed, the
construction covers 111795 of 112068 uniform ladders and not all of
them, so the theorem of 568 is withdrawn: the family it claimed is
back open. The 273 exceptions are all of nearly maximal span, which
is exactly where the number of admissible chord counts collapses to
three, and each one that was examined turns out to have its power of
two anyway - in a cycle that winds round the host not twice but zero
times. That is the honest state: one lap is a real and exactly
characterised family, it settles every girth-legal closed ladder up
to 2N = 18 without exception, and it is not by itself enough.


## 570. THE WINDING-ZERO CRITERION, AND THE UNIFORM FAMILY CLOSED
## AGAIN - BY THREE EXPLICIT CYCLES

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The winding-zero analogue
of SKIP* is not merely available, it is EASIER, because a winding-zero
cycle lifts to an infinite ladder whose host is a tree. The criterion
that comes out re-proves the theorem 569 withdrew, in a STRONGER form
and in three explicit cycles: every girth-legal uniform ladder has a
cycle of length 8 or 16. Machine: scratch (criterion against brute
force, construction built and walked on 444168 ladders).

### 570.0 THE LIFT (PROVED)

A cycle of U(2N,s) of winding number zero lifts to a cycle of

    L(s):   vertices Z,  host edges i ~ i+1,  RUNGS {m, m+s} for m even,

and conversely a cycle of L(s) descends to U(2N,s) as soon as its
vertices have distinct residues modulo 2N - automatic when it fits in
an interval shorter than 2N. So the whole family is a statement about
ONE infinite object, with no dependence on N.

  AND L(s) IS EASY, BECAUSE ITS HOST IS A TREE. The host is the path Z,
  a spanning tree; so the cycle space has as a basis the fundamental
  cycles of the rungs, one per even m, each of length s+1. HENCE AN
  ELEMENT OF THE CYCLE SPACE IS DETERMINED BY ITS RUNG SET S ALONE:
  the host edge (t, t+1) belongs to it exactly when an ODD number of
  the intervals [m, m+s), m in S, contain t.

### 570.1 (WIND0) THE CRITERION (PROVED)

Let S be a finite set of even integers, |S| = k. Its 2k endpoints
m and m+s are all DISTINCT - m_i - m_j = s is impossible with both
even and s odd - so write them in order e_1 < e_2 < ... < e_{2k}.

  The coverage parity at t is
  #{m in S : m <= t} - #{m in S : m+s <= t}, which modulo 2 is just
  #{endpoints <= t}. SO THE HOST EDGES USED ARE EXACTLY THE PATHS

      [e_1, e_2],  [e_3, e_4],  ...,  [e_{2k-1}, e_{2k}] :

  consecutive endpoints, paired off from the left. Every vertex then
  has degree two automatically, and

      LENGTH  =  k  +  sum_{i=1..k} ( e_{2i} - e_{2i-1} ) .

  (WIND0). Form the PAIRING GRAPH: k nodes, one per rung, and k edges,
  one per consecutive pair, joining the rungs that own its two
  endpoints. Every node has degree 2, so it is a union of cycles, and

      THE CONFIGURATION IS A SIMPLE CYCLE  <=>  THE PAIRING GRAPH IS A
      SINGLE CYCLE.

  Compare SKIP*. One lap needed an inequality between consecutive
  overshoots; winding zero needs only that a graph on k nodes be
  connected. There is no arithmetic condition at all - the displacement
  equation that dominated 564 to 568 has simply gone, because a cycle
  of L(s) closes by construction.

  VERIFIED: for 2N = 14 to 20 and every legal span, the lengths (WIND0)
  produces are EXACTLY the winding-zero lengths found by enumerating
  every cycle of the graph and computing its winding number - equal
  sets in every case, and every configuration built and walked.

### 570.2 THE TWO MECHANISMS ARE COMPLEMENTARY (PROVED)

Call a pair TIGHT if its gap is 1. A tight pair joins a start to an end
- starts are even and ends odd - and start_i = end_j + 1 or
end_j = start_i + 1 both force m_j = m_i - s -/+ 1. SO A START ALWAYS
PAIRS WITH AN END ONE LEVEL BELOW IT. Entering a rung at its start one
leaves at its end, one level up; so an ALL-TIGHT configuration ascends
forever and CANNOT close in L(s).

  All-tight configurations are precisely 564's construction with every
  run of length 1: they close only modulo 2N, which is winding one or
  more. Conversely a winding-zero cycle must contain a TURNAROUND, a
  start-start or end-end pair, and those are the pairs one lap cannot
  use. The two families meet only in the empty configuration.

  TWO CHAINS OF a RUNGS joined by a turnaround at each end give

      length  =  4a - 2 + g_top + g_bot ,  |g_top - g_bot| <= 2(a-1),

  with both gaps even. a = 2 and gaps 4 and 6 give SIXTEEN.

### 570.3 THE THEOREM (PROVED)

  THEOREM. Let s be odd and let U(2N,s) be a girth-legal uniform ladder,
  4 <= s <= N-2. Then U(2N,s) contains a cycle of length 8 OR 16.

  PROOF. Girth-legality gives 2N >= 2s+4. Three cases exhaust it.

  (A) s = 5. Take S = {0, 2, 4}. Endpoints 0,2,4,5,7,9; pairs (0,2),
      (4,5), (7,9); the pairing graph on the rungs {0,5}, {2,7}, {4,9}
      is a triangle. Length 3 + (2+1+2) = 8, and the eight vertices lie
      in [0,9], inside the circle since 2N >= 14. [This is 560.2's
      universal octagon, now explained rather than found.]

  (B) 2N = 2s+4, s >= 7. Take the ONE-LAP walk with tails 0 and s+5,
      that is runs +5 then -1. The gaps are s+5 and s-1, so the
      overshoots are 0 and 1, and 0+1 < s, so SKIP* applies. Length
      2N - 2(s-1) + 2 = 8; the vertices are 0, 1 and s to s+5.

  (C) s >= 7 and 2N >= 2s+6. Take S = {0, 4, s-1, s+5}. The endpoints
      in order are 0, 4, s-1, s, s+4, s+5, 2s-1, 2s+5, so the pairs are
      (0,4), (s-1,s), (s+4,s+5), (2s-1,2s+5) with gaps 4, 1, 1, 6. The
      pairing graph on A={0,s}, B={4,s+4}, C={s-1,2s-1}, D={s+5,2s+5}
      has edges A-B, C-A, B-D, C-D: a single 4-cycle. Length
      4 + 12 = 16, and the sixteen vertices lie in [0, 2s+5], an
      interval SHORTER THAN THE CIRCLE, so no two coincide. QED

  VERIFIED, not by an invariant but by the object (569's rule): for
  every one of the 444168 girth-legal pairs with odd span 5 to 401 and
  2N from 2s+4 to 24s, the prescribed cycle was BUILT, every edge
  checked against the graph, and the walk traversed - a simple cycle of
  length 8 or 16 in every case, 0 failures. Case A 54 times, case B
  198, case C 443916. Cross-checked against complete cycle enumeration
  for 2N up to 26: the claimed length is in the true spectrum every
  time.

### 570.4 WHAT THIS RESTORES, AND WHAT IT MEANS

  IT RESTORES 568.2, in a stronger form and by a shorter argument. Not
  "some power of two" but ONE OF THE TWO SMALLEST, uniformly over span
  and size. 569's 273 exceptions all fall to case (C). The entire
  apparatus of 564 to 568 - the chord count k_0, the quantities M and
  P, the three branches, the parity of k - M, the edge window - is
  UNNECESSARY. It was all an attempt to solve a displacement equation
  that winding-zero cycles do not have.

  AND IT SAYS SOMETHING ABOUT THE FAMILY. A ladder with a bounded
  power-of-two cycle is not near being a counterexample; it is not in
  band 3 at all. 532.1 named the uniform ladders the hard case because
  every additive tool failed on them. They were hard for the additive
  tools and easy for a drawing: four chords in a window of length
  2s+5. The lesson is 517's in another dress - the difficulty was in
  the instrument.

  THE CASE (C) CYCLE NEVER WRAPS. It is a theorem about L(s), the
  infinite ladder, and the finite ladders inherit it. That is why one
  configuration serves every size at once, and it is the shape an
  argument must have if it is to beat an unbounded family.

### 570.5 STATUS

PROVED here: THE LIFT - winding-zero cycles of U(2N,s) are the cycles
of the infinite ladder L(s) that fit in an interval shorter than the
circle; and since the host of L(s) is a spanning tree, such a cycle is
determined by its RUNG SET alone.

PROVED: (WIND0). With the 2k endpoints sorted, the host edges used are
exactly the paths between consecutive pairs e_1e_2, e_3e_4, ...; the
length is k + sum(e_{2i} - e_{2i-1}); and the configuration is a SIMPLE
cycle if and only if the pairing graph on the rungs is a single cycle.
No arithmetic side condition survives.

PROVED: the two mechanisms are disjoint. A gap-1 pair always joins a
start to an end one level below, so an all-tight configuration ascends
and can only close modulo 2N - that is 564's family. Winding zero
requires a turnaround, which one lap cannot use.

PROVED: THE THEOREM - every girth-legal uniform ladder U(2N,s) contains
a cycle of length 8 or 16, by S = {0,2,4} when s = 5, by the one-lap
octagon with runs +5, -1 when 2N = 2s+4, and by S = {0, 4, s-1, s+5}
otherwise, the last living inside an interval of length 2s+5.

VERIFIED by construction and simulation on all 444168 girth-legal pairs
with spans to 401, 0 failures, and against complete cycle enumeration
for 2N up to 26.

RESTORED: 568.2, which 569 withdrew, now in the stronger form "length 8
or 16" and by a different argument.

NOT PROVED: that one lap suffices for a general ladder; the
winding-zero analogue for ladders that are not uniform; (LQ3-3);
(OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently
(K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation;
J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The mechanism
that rescued 569's exceptions turns out to be the easier of the two.
A cycle that does not wind lifts to the infinite ladder, whose host is
a path and therefore a spanning tree, so the cycle is nothing but a set
of rungs; sort the 2k endpoints, pair them off consecutively, and the
host edges are the paths between the pairs. The length is immediate and
the only condition is that a k-node graph be a single cycle - there is
no displacement equation, which is exactly why the family covers what
one lap could not. Four rungs at 0, 4, s-1 and s+5 pair up with gaps
4, 1, 1, 6, close into a 4-cycle, and give a SIXTEEN-cycle inside an
interval of length 2s+5, shorter than any girth-legal circle except
2N = 2s+4, where two chords and runs of five and minus one give an
octagon, and s = 5, where three rungs give one. So the uniform family
is closed again, by three cycles one can draw, in the stronger form
that the power of two is always 8 or 16. Everything the withdrawn
argument computed was in service of an equation the right cycles never
had to satisfy.


## 571. (WIND0) FOR ANY CLOSED LADDER, THE ALTERNATING-SUM FORMULA,
## AND WHY NO WINDOW CAN BE BOUNDED

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Two questions were open
after 570: does the winding-zero criterion survive varying spans, and
does its bounded-window construction. The first survives VERBATIM - the
proof used exactly one fact, and that fact holds for every perfect
matching. The second does not survive, and what kills it is GIRTH, not
arithmetic. Machine: scratch (criterion against brute force, 54911
crossing configurations, census, high-girth search).

### 571.0 THE COVER OF A GENERAL LADDER

For each chord {u,v} choose a LEFT endpoint and a span: the short side,
so that the span is at most N, with the tie at span exactly N broken by
taking the smaller residue. Girth-legality makes every span at least 4.
Lifting to Z gives an involution mu with mu(x + 2N) = mu(x) + 2N and
|mu(x) - x| <= N, and the COVERING LADDER

    L :  vertices Z,  host edges i ~ i+1,  rungs {x, mu(x)} .

Put R = { x : mu(x) > x }, the rung positions. Then

    R  and  mu(R)  PARTITION  Z ,

because mu is an involution with no fixed point. That single sentence is
the whole difference between 570 and the general case.

  A cycle's winding number is (sum of displacements)/2N, and it depends
  on the choice of lift; the short-span choice is the canonical one and
  is the one meant here. Winding zero means the cycle closes ALREADY IN
  L, and any cycle of L descends to the ladder as soon as its vertices
  have distinct residues mod 2N.

### 571.1 (WIND0-GEN), UNCHANGED (PROVED)

  Let S be a finite set of k rungs of L. Its 2k endpoints - the x in S
  and the mu(x) - are all DISTINCT, since R and mu(R) are disjoint. Sort
  them e_1 < ... < e_{2k}. Then the coverage parity at t is
  #{endpoints <= t} mod 2, so the host edges used are exactly the paths
  between CONSECUTIVE PAIRS, and

      LENGTH = k + sum_i ( e_{2i} - e_{2i-1} ) ,

      SIMPLE CYCLE  <=>  the pairing graph on the k rungs, with one edge
      per consecutive pair, is a SINGLE CYCLE.

  Nothing in 570's proof used the equality of spans, the parity of the
  positions, or the value of s. It used the disjointness of R and mu(R)
  and nothing else.

  VERIFIED: on every girth-legal closed ladder at 2N = 12 and 14 - 24
  and 408 of them - the set of lengths (WIND0-GEN) produces is EXACTLY
  the set of lengths of winding-zero cycles found by enumerating every
  cycle of the graph and computing its winding number. Equal sets in
  every case, with no false claims and no omissions.

### 571.2 THE ALTERNATING-SUM FORMULA (PROVED)

Call k chords PAIRWISE CROSSING if their left endpoints all precede all
their right endpoints: x_1 < ... < x_k < y_1 < ... < y_k, where
y_i = x_i + sigma_i.

  PROPOSITION. For k ODD the pairing graph is the single k-cycle
  1-2-3-...-k-1, and

      LENGTH  =  k + sigma_1 - sigma_2 + sigma_3 - ... + sigma_k .

  For k EVEN the pairing graph is k/2 doubled edges, never one cycle.

    PROOF. The sorted endpoints are x_1,...,x_k,y_1,...,y_k. For k odd
  the consecutive pairs are (x_1,x_2), (x_3,x_4), ..., (x_k,y_1),
  (y_2,y_3), ..., (y_{k-1},y_k). Their gaps telescope: every position
  cancels and only the alternating span sum remains. Pair (x_{2i-1},
  x_{2i}) joins rungs 2i-1 and 2i, pair (x_k, y_1) joins k and 1, and
  pair (y_{2i}, y_{2i+1}) joins 2i and 2i+1, which is the k-cycle. For
  k even the pairs are (x_{2i-1},x_{2i}) and (y_{2i-1},y_{2i}), giving
  each edge twice and k/2 components. QED

  THE POSITIONS DO NOT APPEAR. Only the spans do, alternately signed.

  k = 1 : length sigma + 1. SO ANY CHORD OF SHORT SPAN 2^j - 1 GIVES A
          POWER-OF-TWO CYCLE OUTRIGHT - its fundamental cycle.
  k = 3 : length 3 + sigma_1 - sigma_2 + sigma_3.
  uniform: every span is s, the alternating sum is s, and the length is
          k + s - which is 570's count and, at k = 3 and s = 5, exactly
          560.2's universal octagon.

  VERIFIED on 54911 random pairwise-crossing configurations with
  distinct endpoints: the pairing is a single cycle and the length is
  the alternating sum in every case, 0 mismatches. (Configurations with
  two endpoints coinciding fail, as they must; they cannot occur in a
  ladder, where distinct chords have distinct ends.)

### 571.3 WHAT VARYING SPANS BUY (COMPUTED)

In a uniform ladder the alternating sum is always s, which is why 570
had to leave the crossing family and build a turnaround. As soon as the
spans differ the sum is TUNABLE, and three chords are usually enough.

    2N = 12 :     24 ladders, winding-zero with at most 3 rungs
                  settles all 24 .
    2N = 14 :    408 ladders, settles all 408 .
    2N = 16 :   8002 ladders, settles 7994 . The 8 exceptions all have
                the same span multiset {4,4,6,6,6,6,8,8}; each has an
                octagon of winding zero using six rungs, so the
                winding-zero family settles all 8002 .

  Sampled at 2N = 18, 20, 22 and 24, 120 girth-legal ladders each: at
  most three rungs settle EVERY ladder drawn. So the answer to "do four
  chords in a bounded window still work when the spans differ" is that
  three usually do, and 571.2 says exactly which three.

### 571.4 BUT NO WINDOW CAN BE BOUNDED (PROVED)

  A construction that uses k rungs inside a window of w positions
  produces a cycle of length at most w + k, since the host edges all lie
  between the extreme endpoints. And EVERY cycle has length at least the
  girth. So a bounded-window construction can only work on a family of
  BOUNDED GIRTH.

  AND THE GIRTH IS NOT BOUNDED AT 8. A girth-legal closed ladder on 140
  vertices with GIRTH 9 was constructed; it has no 8-cycle whatever -
  confirmed twice, by the girth computation and by an independent search
  for an 8-cycle - while 16, 32 and 64 are all present. The largest
  girth the greedy search reached was

      2N =   20   30   40   60   80  100  140
      girth   6    7    7    8    8    8    9 .

  SO 570's THEOREM IS SHARP TO ITS FAMILY. "Length 8 or 16" is a fact
  about uniform ladders, whose girth is 6; the moment the girth exceeds
  8 the 8 is gone, and if the girth of closed ladders is unbounded - it
  is expected to be, and it is NOT proved here - then no constant bound
  on the length can survive either.

  THIS IS THE HONEST SHAPE OF THE OBSTRUCTION. The difficulty of E-G on
  closed ladders is not that the arithmetic inside a fixed window is
  hard. It is that no fixed window can serve: the target length must
  grow with the girth, and a construction must grow with it.

### 571.5 STATUS

PROVED here: (WIND0-GEN). For any closed ladder, with a left endpoint
and a short span chosen for each chord, the rung positions R and their
images mu(R) partition Z; hence the 2k endpoints of any k rungs of the
covering ladder are distinct, the host edges of the corresponding
element of the cycle space are the paths between consecutive sorted
endpoints, the length is k + sum(e_{2i} - e_{2i-1}), and it is a simple
cycle exactly when the pairing graph on the rungs is a single cycle. The
proof of 570 goes through word for word; uniformity was never used.

PROVED: THE ALTERNATING-SUM FORMULA. For k pairwise crossing chords with
k ODD the pairing graph is a single k-cycle and the length is
k + sigma_1 - sigma_2 + ... + sigma_k, independent of the positions; for
k even the pairing graph is disconnected. In particular a chord of short
span 2^j - 1 yields a power-of-two cycle by itself.

PROVED: no bounded-window construction can settle the general closed
ladder, since such a construction yields a cycle of length at most
window plus rung count, while every cycle is at least as long as the
girth - and a girth-legal closed ladder on 140 vertices with girth 9,
having no 8-cycle at all, is exhibited.

VERIFIED: the criterion reproduces the winding-zero spectrum exactly on
all 432 girth-legal ladders at 2N = 12 and 14; the alternating-sum
formula on 54911 crossing configurations, 0 mismatches.

COMPUTED: winding-zero configurations with at most three rungs settle
all 24 ladders at 2N = 12, all 408 at 2N = 14, and 7994 of 8002 at
2N = 16, the eight exceptions being settled with six rungs; and every
one of 480 sampled ladders at 2N = 18 to 24.

NOT PROVED: that the girth of girth-legal closed ladders is unbounded,
which is what would turn 571.4 into an unbounded lower bound on the
window; that either mechanism settles a general ladder; (LQ3-3); (OPEN)
for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4);
(LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the
five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The criterion
generalises for free. Choose a left end and a short span for each chord;
then the rung positions and the rung ends partition the integers, which
is the only thing 570's argument ever needed, so for any closed ladder a
winding-zero cycle is a set of rungs, the host edges are the paths
between consecutive sorted endpoints, and simplicity is the connectivity
of a graph on k nodes. What varying spans add is tunability: for k odd
pairwise crossing chords the length is k plus the ALTERNATING SUM of the
spans, with the positions cancelling entirely, so three chords give
3 + sigma_1 - sigma_2 + sigma_3 and one chord of span 2^j - 1 gives a
power of two on its own. Three rungs settle every girth-legal ladder up
to 2N = 14 and all but eight at 2N = 16. What does not generalise is the
bounded window, and the reason is not arithmetic but girth: a window of
w positions cannot produce a cycle longer than about w, every cycle is
at least the girth, and a closed ladder on 140 vertices with girth 9 has
no octagon at all. The window must grow with the girth. That is the real
obstruction, and it is the first time in this programme it has been
stated as a lower bound on the method rather than as a difficulty in it.


## 572. WHAT GIRTH FORCES ON THE CHORD DIAGRAM, AND WHY FOUR RUNGS
## HAVE ALWAYS BEEN ENOUGH

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The task was to make the
window scale with the girth. The measurement says the opposite of what
was expected: THE RUNG COUNT NEVER HAD TO SCALE - four rungs settle
every ladder tested, including the adversarial ones - and it is the
WINDOW that grows. On the way, girth's exact grip on the chord diagram
comes out, and the reason the uniform ladders were hard turns out to be
a congruence modulo 4. Machine: scratch (formulas on 218196
configurations, constraints on 74 ladders, min-rung census on 8434).

### 572.0 WHAT GIRTH FORCES (PROVED)

(WIND0-GEN) gives the length of every small configuration outright:

    one chord        sigma + 1
    nested pair      2 + sigma_1 - sigma_2          (1 the outer)
    crossing pair    2 + 2(x_2 - x_1) + (sigma_2 - sigma_1)

the last because the two gaps are x_2 - x_1 and
y_2 - y_1 = (x_2 - x_1) + (sigma_2 - sigma_1). Every one of these is a
cycle, so every one is at least the girth:

    sigma >= g - 1 ,
    sigma_1 - sigma_2 >= g - 2                     for a nested pair,
    2(x_2 - x_1) + (sigma_2 - sigma_1) >= g - 2    for a crossing pair.

  TWO CONSEQUENCES. A NESTED CHAIN has length at most
  1 + (N - g + 1)/(g - 2), since its spans drop by g-2 at every step and
  live in [g-1, N]. And along a PAIRWISE CROSSING family the spans grow,
  sigma_{i+1} >= sigma_i + (g-2) - 2(x_{i+1} - x_i), so a crossing family
  inside a window of width w has at most 1 + (N + 2w)/(g-2) members.
  HIGH GIRTH FORCES THE SPANS TO BE BOTH LARGE AND SPREAD OUT.

  VERIFIED: the two pair formulas on 136866 crossing and 81330 nested
  configurations, 0 mismatches; the three constraints on 74 girth-legal
  ladders including high-girth ones, 0 violations.

### 572.1 SLIDING, AND WHY HIGH GIRTH HELPS (PROVED, COMPUTED)

  SLIDING LEMMA. Fix two of the three chords of a crossing triple. The
  length is then a constant plus, or minus, the span of the third:
  fixing (1,2) it is 3 + (x_2-x_1) + (y_1-y_2) + sigma_3, fixing (2,3)
  it is 3 + (y_3-y_2) + (x_2-x_3) + sigma_1, and fixing (1,3) it is
  3 + (y_3-x_1) + (y_1-x_3) - sigma_2.
  SO THE CROSSING-TRIPLE LENGTH SET IS A UNION OF TRANSLATES OF SPAN
  SETS, and the fuel of the mechanism is SPAN DIVERSITY.

  AND GIRTH SUPPLIES THE FUEL. Triple lengths on high-girth ladders:

     2N =  40, g = 7 :  27 values, filling [7,33] exactly,  gap 1
     2N =  80, g = 8 :  58 values, filling [8,65] exactly,  gap 1
     2N = 100, g = 8 :  76 values in [9,86],                gap 2
     2N = 140, g = 9 :  107 values in [10,119],             gap 3

  - a near interval reaching about 0.85 of 2N, containing three or four
  powers of two in every case. SO THE HYPOTHESIS THAT PROMPTED THIS
  SECTION IS CONFIRMED WHERE IT WAS AIMED: large spans do not defeat the
  crossing triple, they feed it.

### 572.2 THE HARD CASE IS FEW SPANS, NOT LARGE ONES (COMPUTED)

Ladders whose spans take only two or three distinct values starve the
triple: of eight such ladders constructed, THREE CHORDS FAILED ON SEVEN,
the triple length set collapsing to three to ten values - exactly what
the alternating-sum formula predicts, since with two spans s, s' the
three-fold alternating sums are only s, s', 2s-s', 2s'-s.

  AND THE UNIFORM LADDER IS THE EXTREME CASE, with a clean reason. All
  its left ends are even and all its spans equal, so a crossing pair has
  sigma_2 = sigma_1 and x_2 - x_1 even, whence

      length  =  2 + 2(x_2 - x_1)  ==  2  (mod 4)  ALWAYS.

  Checked for U(30,11), U(40,17) and U(92,41): the crossing-pair lengths
  are congruent to 2 mod 4 without exception. THAT is the obstruction
  570 had to route around with a turnaround, and it is 2-adic, which is
  the coordinate 516 said to name before opening a target.

### 572.3 THE MEASUREMENT (COMPUTED)

Minimum number of rungs in a winding-zero configuration whose length is
a power of two, over EVERY girth-legal closed ladder:

     2N = 12 :     24 ladders     k=2 : 24
     2N = 14 :    408 ladders     k=1 : 252   k=2 : 112   k=3 : 44
     2N = 16 :   8002 ladders     k=1 : 6832  k=2 : 1020  k=3 : 142
                                  k=4 : 8

  - 8434 ladders, none needing more than FOUR. Beyond the exhaustive
  range: 24 further ladders - random to 2N = 70, high girth to 2N = 140
  at girth 9, two- and three-span ladders to 2N = 80, and uniform
  ladders up to U(92,41) - all settled with at most four rungs; and 14
  ADVERSARIAL ladders whose spans were forced to avoid every 2^j - 1,
  killing the one-rung mechanism outright, ALL SETTLED AT k = 2.

  THE WINDOW, BY CONTRAST, DOES SCALE. For k = 1 it is the length minus
  one, a constant; for a random ladder at 2N = 70 it was 7, a tenth of
  the circle; for U(92,41) it was 85, over nine tenths. So 571.4's
  conclusion stands and is sharpened: it is the WINDOW that must grow,
  not the number of chords.

### 572.4 THE LADDER OF MECHANISMS

    k = 1              sigma + 1              dies iff no span is 2^j-1
    k = 2, crossing    2 + 2dx + Dsigma       runs on POSITIONS, so span
                                              poverty does not starve it
    k = 2, nested      2 + Dsigma             needs Dsigma = 2^j - 2
    k = 3, crossing    3 + alternating sum    needs span diversity
    k = 4              570's turnaround       needs neither

  Each mechanism dies on a thin, explicitly describable set, and the
  next one covers it. A counterexample would have to defeat all of them
  simultaneously: no span equal to 2^j - 1, no crossing pair with
  2dx + Dsigma = 2^j - 2, no nested pair with Dsigma = 2^j - 2, no
  crossing triple whose alternating sum is 2^j - 3, and no turnaround -
  a system of order N^4 conditions on N spans and N positions. THAT IS A
  HEURISTIC AND NOT A PROOF, and it is the same first-moment shape as
  517; but it is now attached to explicit mechanisms with exact length
  formulas rather than to an expectation.

### 572.5 STATUS

PROVED here: the length of every one- and two-chord winding-zero
configuration - sigma+1 for a single chord, 2 + sigma_1 - sigma_2 for a
nested pair, 2 + 2(x_2-x_1) + (sigma_2-sigma_1) for a crossing pair -
and hence GIRTH'S EXACT GRIP ON THE CHORD DIAGRAM: sigma >= g-1;
sigma_1 - sigma_2 >= g-2 for nested pairs; 2dx + Dsigma >= g-2 for
crossing pairs. Consequently nested chains have at most
1 + (N-g+1)/(g-2) members, and a pairwise crossing family in a window of
width w has at most 1 + (N+2w)/(g-2).

PROVED: THE SLIDING LEMMA - fixing two chords of a crossing triple, the
length is a constant plus or minus the third span; so the triple length
set is a union of translates of span sets and the mechanism runs on span
diversity.

PROVED: the uniform obstruction. All left ends even and all spans equal
force every crossing-pair length to be 2 modulo 4, so no crossing pair
of a uniform ladder can have power-of-two length.

VERIFIED: the pair formulas on 218196 configurations and the girth
constraints on 74 ladders, 0 failures.

COMPUTED: over all 8434 girth-legal closed ladders at 2N = 12, 14 and
16 the minimum rung count is 1, 2, 3 or 4 - never more; over 24 larger
and structurally varied ladders and 14 adversarial ones whose spans
avoid every 2^j - 1, at most four rungs again. High-girth ladders give
crossing-triple length sets that are near intervals reaching about 0.85
of 2N, with maximum gap 1 to 3.

NOT PROVED: that four rungs suffice in general - this is a measurement,
not a theorem; that the crossing-triple lengths form an interval; that
the girth of closed ladders is unbounded; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open
ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*);
(E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements of
451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. Girth turns out
to grip the chord diagram very tightly and in exactly three places, one
for each small configuration: a chord's span is at least g-1, a nested
pair's spans differ by at least g-2, and a crossing pair satisfies twice
the position gap plus the span difference at least g-2. From these the
nested chains and the crossing families are both short, and the spans of
a high-girth ladder are forced to be large and spread. Spread is exactly
what the crossing triple eats, because fixing two of its three chords
makes the length a constant plus the third span; so at girth 7, 8 and 9
the triple lengths fill a near interval up to about 0.85 of the circle
and catch three or four powers of two apiece. The hard case is therefore
not large spans but FEW spans, and the extreme of few spans is the
uniform ladder, where all left ends are even and all spans equal and
every crossing pair has length 2 modulo 4 - one congruence, which is the
whole of what 570 needed a turnaround to escape. Measured across every
girth-legal ladder to 2N = 16 and a spread of larger and adversarial
ones, the number of chords needed has never exceeded four; the window is
what grows. The window scales, the mechanism does not.


## 573. THE WINDOW IS BOUNDED BELOW BY THE SPAN, NOT THE GIRTH; AND
## THE POSITION SUM IS THE COORDINATE THE PAIR MECHANISM READS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 572 measured the scaling
but did not answer the question that was asked, which was whether a
power-of-two cycle can be found with O(g) rungs inside a window of
O(2^g) positions. Both halves are settled here. THE RUNG HALF IS
ACHIEVED AND BEATEN - four rungs, proved for the family that matters.
THE WINDOW HALF IS IMPOSSIBLE, and the same family proves it. Machine:
scratch (4930 crossing pairs, 6156 uniform ladders).

### 573.0 THE WINDOW LOWER BOUND (PROVED)

Call the WINDOW of a cycle the length of the shortest arc of the host
circle containing all its vertices. There are two lower bounds and they
are independent.

  (a) A cycle of length L has L distinct vertices, so its window is at
      least L - 1, hence at least g - 1. This is 571.4's bound.

  (b) A cycle that uses ANY chord contains both ends of that chord, and
      those lie at circular distance equal to its span. So its window is
      at least sigma_min, THE SMALLEST SPAN IN THE LADDER.

      window  >=  max( g - 1 ,  sigma_min ) .

  AND (b) IS THE STRONGER ONE, BY AN UNBOUNDED MARGIN. In U(2N,s) every
  span equals s, and the girth is at most 6 for every s - the chords at
  m and m+2 together with two host steps at each end give a hexagon. So
  U(2N,s) has girth 6 and window at least s, and s runs up to N-2.
  (Checked: all 6156 girth-legal uniform ladders with s <= 59 and
  2N <= 600 have girth exactly 6.)

  SO NO FUNCTION OF THE GIRTH CAN BOUND THE WINDOW. The uniform ladders
  sit at girth 6 forever while their windows grow linearly in N. THE
  O(2^g) WINDOW ASKED FOR IS IMPOSSIBLE - not merely unachieved.

  This also corrects the emphasis of 571.4, which attributed the growth
  of the window to girth. Girth is one obstruction; the span is another,
  and the second is unbounded even when the first is frozen at 6.

### 573.1 THE RUNG HALF IS ACHIEVED (PROVED)

570.3 proves that every girth-legal uniform ladder has a power-of-two
cycle using at most FOUR rungs: S = {0,2,4} at s = 5, the two-chord
octagon at 2N = 2s+4, and S = {0, 4, s-1, s+5} otherwise. Four is O(1),
hence certainly O(g).

  So ON THE VERY FAMILY THAT REFUTES THE WINDOW BOUND, THE RUNG BOUND IS
  ACHIEVED WITH ROOM TO SPARE. And 572.3's census found at most four
  rungs on all 8434 girth-legal ladders to 2N = 16, on 24 larger and
  structurally varied ones, and on 14 adversarial ones whose spans avoid
  every 2^j - 1.

  THE TWO HALVES OF THE QUESTION ARE THEREFORE NOT SIMULTANEOUSLY
  SATISFIABLE, and a single family witnesses both: uniform ladders meet
  the rung bound with four and violate any window bound in g.

### 573.2 THE POSITION SUM IS THE PAIR COORDINATE (PROVED)

Write phi = x + y for the POSITION SUM of a chord - 545's phi - and
sigma = y - x for its span. For a crossing pair,

    length  =  2 + (x_2 - x_1) + (y_2 - y_1)  =  2 + ( phi_2 - phi_1 ) .

  So THE CROSSING-PAIR LENGTHS ARE 2 PLUS THE DIFFERENCE SET OF THE
  POSITION SUMS, and girth says exactly

      phi_2 - phi_1  >=  g - 2      for every crossing pair.

  Verified on 4930 crossing pairs drawn from random, high-girth and
  uniform ladders: 0 violations, and 128 pairs attain equality, so the
  bound is sharp.

  THE CHANGE OF COORDINATES (x,y) -> (phi, sigma) SPLITS THE MECHANISMS.
  The pair reads phi ALONE - length 2 + Dphi - and the triple reads
  sigma ALONE - length 3 + sigma_i - sigma_j + sigma_k, positions
  cancelling by 571.2. That is why 572's adversarial ladders, built to
  starve the span coordinate, fell to pairs at once: they had not
  touched phi. It is 516's factorisation into two coordinates, realised
  on the chord diagram rather than on the target.

### 573.3 WHY THE DENSITY ROUTE CANNOT WORK (PROVED)

To reach L = 2^m with a crossing pair one needs two chords with
Dphi = 2^m - 2. The standard way to force a prescribed difference T in a
set A inside an interval of length W is the pigeonhole on A and A + T:
if 2|A| > W + T + 1 they must meet.

  BUT GIRTH FORBIDS THE DENSITY. Every two crossing chords have Dphi at
  least g-2, so a pairwise crossing family whose position sums span W has
  at most W/(g-2) + 1 members, and

      2( W/(g-2) + 1 )  >  W + T + 1

  is false for every g >= 5 once W exceeds a constant. THE HYPOTHESIS OF
  THE PIGEONHOLE IS EXCLUDED BY THE HYPOTHESIS OF THE PROBLEM.

  So no counting argument on the size of the phi-set can produce the
  power of two; only the ARITHMETIC of that set can. This is 517's
  barrier in its sharpest form so far: girth simultaneously supplies the
  structure the mechanisms need and removes the density any counting
  proof would need.

### 573.4 STATUS

PROVED here: the WINDOW LOWER BOUND. Every cycle has window at least
max(g-1, sigma_min), the second because a cycle using a chord contains
both of its ends. And the second is unbounded independently of the
first: U(2N,s) has girth at most 6 for every s, by the hexagon on the
chords at m and m+2, while its window is at least s, which runs to N-2.
HENCE NO BOUND ON THE WINDOW IN TERMS OF THE GIRTH EXISTS, and the
O(2^g) window asked for is impossible.

PROVED (570.3, restated as the answer to the rung half): every
girth-legal uniform ladder has a power-of-two cycle with at most four
rungs, so the O(g) rung bound is met with room to spare on the same
family that refutes the window bound.

PROVED: for a crossing pair, length = 2 + (phi_2 - phi_1) with
phi = x + y the position sum of 545; hence girth forces Dphi >= g-2 for
every crossing pair. The coordinates (phi, sigma) split the mechanisms:
pairs read phi alone, triples read sigma alone.

PROVED: the density route is self-defeating. Girth's own constraint
Dphi >= g-2 caps a crossing family at W/(g-2)+1 members in a phi-range
W, which is too sparse for the pigeonhole that would force a prescribed
difference, for every g >= 5.

VERIFIED: the position-sum constraint on 4930 crossing pairs, 0
violations, 128 tight; girth exactly 6 on all 6156 girth-legal uniform
ladders with s <= 59 and 2N <= 600.

NOT PROVED: that four rungs suffice for a general ladder; that the
crossing-triple lengths form an interval; that the girth of closed
ladders is unbounded; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2);
(RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the
rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The question was
whether O(g) rungs inside a window of O(2^g) can always produce a power
of two. The rung half is already a theorem: 570.3 does it with four, and
four is O(1). The window half is impossible, and the proof is one line -
a cycle that uses a chord contains both of the chord's ends, so its
vertices cannot fit in an arc shorter than that chord's span; the
uniform ladders have girth six for every span, so their windows grow
linearly in N while the girth does not move. What 571.4 read as a girth
obstruction is two obstructions, and the span one survives when the
girth is frozen. The compensation is a clean coordinate. Writing phi for
the position sum x+y, a crossing pair has length exactly 2 + Dphi and
girth says Dphi >= g-2; a crossing triple has length 3 plus an
alternating sum of spans and no dependence on position at all. Pairs
read one coordinate, triples the other, which is why ladders built to
starve the spans fell immediately to pairs. And the same inequality that
gives the mechanisms their structure is what denies a counting proof its
density: a crossing family in a phi-range W has at most W/(g-2)+1
members, far too sparse for the pigeonhole that would force the
difference 2^m - 2. The arithmetic cannot be avoided by counting.


## 574. THE WINDOW LAW: O(1) RUNGS IN A WINDOW OF THETA(SPAN)

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 573 proved that the window
cannot be bounded by any function of the girth. That refuted the
parameter, not the question. In the right parameter - THE SPAN - both
halves hold at once, with a two-sided bound, and on the uniform family
they are a theorem rather than a measurement. Machine: scratch (444168
uniform pairs, 18 varied ladders).

### 574.0 WHICH PARAMETER CONTROLS THE WINDOW (COMPUTED)

Three candidates, measured as the ratio of the smallest window of a
power-of-two winding-zero cycle to the parameter:

    girth       REFUTED at 573.0 - the uniform ladders sit at girth 6
                for every s while their windows grow linearly in N.
    cutwidth    ratio ranged from 0.47 to 4.11 over 18 ladders. Not it.
    SIGMA_MIN   ratio ranged from 1.00 to 2.25 over the same 18, and
                573.0 bounds it below by 1.

  The eighteen were random ladders to 2N = 70, high-girth ones to
  2N = 140 at girth 9, ladders whose spans were forced to avoid every
  2^j - 1, and uniform ladders to U(120,55). Rung counts 1 to 4.

### 574.1 THE WINDOW LAW FOR THE UNIFORM FAMILY (PROVED)

Take 570.3's three configurations and read off their windows, the window
being the shortest arc of the host circle containing every vertex.

  (A) s = 5, S = {0,2,4}. Vertices [0,2] + [4,5] + [7,9]; window 9,
      which is 2s - 1.
  (B) 2N = 2s+4, the two-chord octagon. Vertices {0,1} and [s, s+5]. The
      two cyclic gaps are both s-1, so the window is 2N - (s-1) = s+5.
  (C) otherwise, S = {0, 4, s-1, s+5}. Vertices [0,4] + [s-1,s] +
      [s+4,s+5] + [2s-1, 2s+5]; window 2s+5.

  THEOREM (WINDOW LAW). Every girth-legal uniform ladder U(2N,s) has a
  cycle of length 8 or 16 using AT MOST FOUR CHORDS, all of whose
  vertices lie in an arc of length at most 2s + 5. And by 573.0 no cycle
  except the host cycle lies in an arc shorter than s. So

      s   <=   window   <=   2s + 5 ,      rungs <= 4 .

    PROOF. The three cases are exhaustive because girth-legality forces
  2N >= 2s+4; the cycles are 570.3's and the windows are the arcs just
  computed; the lower bound is 573.0. QED

  VERIFIED on all 444168 girth-legal pairs with odd span 5 to 401: the
  prescribed cycle was built, walked in the graph, and its window
  measured - length 8 or 16, at most four chords, and s <= window <=
  2s+5 in every case, 0 violations. The largest ratio window/s is 2.714,
  at s = 7, 2N = 24.

### 574.2 THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION AS ASKED

The question was whether a power of two can be reached with O(g) rungs
inside a window of O(2^g) positions.

    RUNG HALF   -  YES, and better: FOUR, which is O(1). Proved for the
                   uniform family at 570.3, measured at most four on all
                   8434 girth-legal ladders to 2N = 16 and on every
                   larger and adversarial ladder tried (572.3).
    WINDOW HALF -  NO in g, and the failure is not an accident: a cycle
                   using a chord contains both of its ends, so the
                   window is at least sigma_min, which is unbounded with
                   the girth frozen at 6.
    CORRECTED   -  O(1) RUNGS IN A WINDOW OF THETA(SIGMA_MIN). Both
                   halves hold simultaneously, and both are optimal: the
                   rung count cannot be zero and the window cannot go
                   below sigma_min.

  So the shape the question was reaching for is right - a bounded number
  of chords in a window that scales - but the thing the window scales
  with is the SPAN, not the girth. The two are independent: girth 6 with
  span N-2 is the uniform ladder, and girth 9 with span 8 was found at
  2N = 140.

### 574.3 A REMARK ON THE PARAMETER

That the window is Theta(s) for the uniform ladders is the same number
562 met from the other side, where the transfer matrix's state width for
U(2N,s) is s and made the computation infeasible. THE SAME PARAMETER
BOUNDS THE LOCALITY OF THE CYCLE AND THE COST OF FINDING IT BY MACHINE.
That is worth remembering when choosing a family to compute on: a family
with small spans is cheap to compute and easy to solve; the expensive
ones are expensive for the same reason they are hard.

### 574.4 STATUS

PROVED here: THE WINDOW LAW for the uniform family. Every girth-legal
U(2N,s) has a cycle of length 8 or 16 using at most four chords inside
an arc of length at most 2s+5, and no cycle but the host cycle fits in
an arc shorter than s; so the window is Theta(s), between s and 2s+5.
The three windows are 2s-1 at s=5, s+5 when 2N = 2s+4, and 2s+5
otherwise.

PROVED (restating the answer to the question): O(g) rungs is achieved
with four, which is O(1); a window of O(2^g) is impossible; and the
corrected law - O(1) rungs in a window of Theta(sigma_min) - holds with
both halves at once and is optimal in both.

VERIFIED: on all 444168 girth-legal uniform pairs with spans to 401 the
cycle was built, walked, and its window measured: 0 violations of
s <= window <= 2s+5, largest ratio 2.714. Across 18 structurally varied
ladders the ratio window/sigma_min ran from 1.00 to 2.25 with at most
four rungs, while window/cutwidth ran from 0.47 to 4.11.

NOT PROVED: the window law for a general closed ladder - that four rungs
and a window of O(sigma_min) always suffice - which is a measurement
here and a theorem only for the uniform family; that the crossing-triple
lengths form an interval; that the girth of closed ladders is unbounded;
(LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3),
equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2
cancellation; J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The question asked
for a bounded number of chords inside a window that grows with the
girth. The number of chords is four and that half was already proved at
570.3; the window half cannot be done in the girth, because a cycle
through a chord holds both of the chord's ends and so cannot fit in an
arc shorter than that chord's span, and the uniform ladders keep girth
six while their spans run to N-2. Changing the parameter fixes
everything: the same three configurations that close the uniform family
sit inside arcs of length 2s-1, s+5 and 2s+5, so the window is between s
and 2s+5, and both halves of the question hold together. Measured on
four hundred and forty-four thousand uniform ladders the law never
failed and the worst ratio was 2.714; measured on eighteen varied
ladders, random, high-girth, span-restricted and uniform, the window
never exceeded 2.25 times the smallest span and the chord count never
exceeded four. The right statement is O(1) rungs in a window of
Theta(sigma_min), it is optimal on both sides, and the parameter is the
span - which is also, from 562, exactly what makes such a ladder
expensive to compute with.


## 575. TWO NOTIONS OF WINDOW; IN THE INTRINSIC ONE THE BOUND HOLDS,
## AND IT IS O(1) RATHER THAN O(2^g)

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 573 and 574 refuted a
window bound in the girth. That refutation is correct but it is about
the ARC window, which is not an invariant of the graph - it depends on
which Hamiltonian cycle was used to present the graph as a ladder. In
the INTRINSIC window - the vertices the cycle actually occupies - the
bound asked for holds, and holds by a wide margin: not O(2^g) but O(1).
Machine: scratch (20 varied ladders, 444168 uniform pairs).

### 575.0 THE TWO NOTIONS

  THE ARC WINDOW of a cycle is the length of the shortest arc of the
  HOST CIRCLE containing all its vertices. THE GRAPH WINDOW is the
  number of vertices the cycle occupies - equivalently, up to the usual
  exponential, the size of the smallest ball of the graph containing it,
  since a cycle of length L lies in a ball of radius ceiling(L/2), which
  holds at most 3*2^(L/2) - 2 vertices of a cubic graph.

  THE ARC WINDOW IS NOT AN INVARIANT OF THE GRAPH. A cubic Hamiltonian
  graph is a closed ladder in as many ways as it has Hamiltonian cycles,
  and the spans - hence sigma_min, hence 573.0's lower bound - change
  with the choice. The sixteen vertices of a 16-cycle are the same
  sixteen vertices whichever presentation is used; the arc they span is
  not. SO A LOCALITY STATEMENT ABOUT A GRAPH MUST BE MADE IN THE GRAPH
  WINDOW, and 573.0's refutation, though correct, refutes a statement
  about a presentation rather than about a graph.

### 575.1 IN THE GRAPH WINDOW THE BOUND HOLDS (PROVED)

  THEOREM. Every girth-legal uniform ladder U(2N,s) has a cycle of
  power-of-two length occupying AT MOST SIXTEEN VERTICES and using AT
  MOST FOUR CHORDS.
    PROOF. 570.3: the cycle has length 8 or 16, and a cycle of length L
  occupies L vertices and uses at most L chords - here at most four, by
  the configurations themselves. QED

  Since every girth-legal uniform ladder has girth 6 and 2^6 = 64, this
  is FOUR RUNGS IN A GRAPH WINDOW OF SIXTEEN, against an allowance of
  O(g) and O(2^g) = 64. The bound asked for is met with a factor of four
  to spare, and met by a constant rather than by a function of g.

### 575.2 THE SAME HOLDS ON EVERYTHING ELSE MEASURED (COMPUTED)

Smallest power-of-two cycle length L_min, with the rung count, over
twenty ladders chosen to be as different as possible:

    random, 2N = 20 to 90, girth 5 and 6      L_min = 8,  1 rung
    high girth, 2N = 40, 80, girth 7, 8       L_min = 8,  1 rung
    high girth, 2N = 140, girth 9             L_min = 16, 1 rung
    spans avoiding every 2^j - 1, 2N to 100   L_min = 8,  2 rungs
    uniform, U(30,11) and U(40,17)            L_min = 8,  <= 4 rungs
    uniform, U(60,25) to U(200,95)            L_min = 16, 4 rungs

    LARGEST L_min OVER ALL TWENTY:  16 .    L_min <= 2^g in every case.

  And L_min >= g always, since every cycle is at least the girth. So on
  everything tested the graph window sits between g and 16, while the
  question allowed 2^g. THE TRUE STATEMENT IS EXPONENTIALLY STRONGER
  THAN THE ONE ASKED FOR.

### 575.3 THE QUESTION, ANSWERED IN BOTH READINGS

    RUNGS, O(g) ASKED     -  met with FOUR, which is O(1). Proved for
                             the uniform family at 570.3; at most four
                             on all 8434 girth-legal ladders to
                             2N = 16 and on every larger and adversarial
                             ladder tried (572.3).
    GRAPH WINDOW, O(2^g)  -  MET, with sixteen vertices. Proved for the
                             uniform family; at most sixteen on all
                             twenty varied ladders measured, against an
                             allowance of 2^g >= 32.
    ARC WINDOW, O(2^g)    -  IMPOSSIBLE (573.0), because a cycle through
                             a chord holds both its ends and so spans at
                             least sigma_min, which is unbounded while
                             the girth stays at 6. But the arc window is
                             a property of the presentation, not of the
                             graph.
    SPANS FORCED LARGE    -  the crossing triple does keep reaching a
                             power of two: at girth 7, 8 and 9 its
                             lengths form near intervals up to about
                             0.85 of the circle, with maximum gap 1 to 3
                             and three or four powers of two apiece
                             (572.1). Large spans feed the mechanism;
                             what starves it is FEW spans.

### 575.4 STATUS

PROVED here: every girth-legal uniform ladder has a power-of-two cycle
occupying at most SIXTEEN vertices and using at most FOUR chords - the
O(g) rungs and O(2^g) window that were asked for, met by constants,
since the girth of these ladders is 6 and 2^6 = 64.

PROVED: the two notions of window are different in kind. The arc window
depends on which Hamiltonian cycle presents the graph as a ladder; the
graph window does not. 573.0's refutation applies to the arc window
only, and 574's law - arc window between sigma_min and about 2.25
sigma_min - is a statement about the presentation.

COMPUTED: over twenty ladders - random to 2N = 90, high girth to 2N =
140 at girth 9, ladders whose spans avoid every 2^j - 1, and uniform
ladders to U(200,95) - the smallest power-of-two cycle has length at
most 16 and uses at most four chords, and L_min <= 2^g in every case,
with L_min >= g always.

NOT PROVED: that the graph window is bounded for a general closed ladder
- sixteen is a measurement outside the uniform family; that the girth of
closed ladders is unbounded; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open ladders;
(COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at
girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements of 451.2;
the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The refutation in
573 was of the wrong statement, though it is itself correct. There are
two windows. One counts positions on the host circle, and it is bounded
below by the smallest span, which is unbounded while the girth stays at
six - so no function of the girth can bound it. But that window is a
property of the presentation: a cubic Hamiltonian graph is a ladder in
as many ways as it has Hamiltonian cycles, and the spans change with the
choice while the vertices of a cycle do not. The other window counts the
vertices the cycle occupies, and it is intrinsic. In the intrinsic one
the answer is not merely O(2^g) but sixteen: every girth-legal uniform
ladder has a power-of-two cycle on at most sixteen vertices using at
most four chords, by 570.3, and across twenty deliberately dissimilar
ladders - random, girth nine, spans forbidden to be one less than a
power of two, uniform up to a span of ninety-five - the smallest
power-of-two cycle never exceeded sixteen and never needed more than
four chords. The question asked for a bounded number of chords in a
window growing exponentially in the girth; what is there is a bounded
number of chords in a bounded window.


## 576. THE INTRINSIC BOUND IS FALSE: L_MIN IS UNBOUNDED, AND THE
## SHARP REPLACEMENT IS L_MIN = THETA(GIRTH)

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 575 measured the INTRINSIC
window and found it bounded - at most 16 vertices and 4 chords on every
ladder it reached. The question was whether that O(1) holds in general,
or whether there is a family where the smallest power-of-two cycle
grows. IT IS THE SECOND, and one line settles it: a power-of-two cycle
is at least as long as the girth. The family is the high-girth closed
ladders; their existence is in the literature and is verified verbatim
below; and what replaces the refuted bound is sharp on both sides.
Machine: scratch (8434 ladders exhaustively, uniform to U(120,55)).

### 576.0 THE LOWER BOUND, WHICH IS TRIVIAL AND DECISIVE (PROVED)

Write L_min for the length of the shortest power-of-two cycle of a
ladder, and P(g) for the least power of two that is at least g. A cycle
cannot be shorter than the girth, so

    L_min  >=  g ,   and being a power of two,   L_min  >=  P(g) .

  HENCE "L_min = O(1)" IMPLIES THE GIRTH OF CLOSED LADDERS IS BOUNDED.
  The whole question reduces to one about Hamiltonian cubic graphs,
  since a closed ladder is exactly a Hamiltonian cubic graph.

  IN PARTICULAR 575's MEASURED CONSTANT CANNOT BE A THEOREM. It found
  L_min at most 16 on every ladder it reached; any ladder of girth 17
  or more has L_min at least 32.

### 576.1 THE GIRTH IS UNBOUNDED (LITERATURE, VERIFIED VERBATIM)

From N. C. Wormald, "Models of random regular graphs", read from the
PDF directly rather than from memory (388.1). Three statements, quoted:

  INTRODUCTION. "Results on random regular graphs can of course be used
  to show that there exist graphs with particular combinations of
  properties; for instance d-regular graphs which are d-connected, have
  arbitrarily large girth, are Hamiltonian and have no non-trivial
  automorphisms."

  THEOREM 2.5 (Bollobas; Wormald). "For d fixed, let X_i = X_{i,n}
  (i >= 3) be the number of cycles of length i in a graph in G_{n,d}.
  For fixed k >= 3, X_3, ..., X_k are asymptotically independent Poisson
  random variables with means lambda_i = (d-1)^i / 2i."

  THEOREM 2.26 (Robinson and Wormald). "For fixed d >= 3, G in G_{n,d}
  is a.a.s. Hamiltonian."

  THE DERIVATION, at d = 3. By Theorem 2.5 the probability that a random
  cubic graph has no cycle of length at most g tends to
  exp( - sum_{i=3}^{g} 2^i / 2i ), which is POSITIVE. By Theorem 2.26
  the probability of being Hamiltonian tends to 1. For events with
  P(A_n) -> 1 and P(B_n) -> c > 0 one has P(A_n and B_n) -> c, so for
  every g and all large even n there is a cubic graph of girth exceeding
  g that carries a Hamilton cycle. That is a girth-legal closed ladder
  of girth exceeding g. The introduction quoted above states this
  consequence outright.

  AND NOTE WHAT SUPPLIES IT. The means (d-1)^i/2i are exactly 517's
  first-moment law, already in this programme. What Theorem 2.5 adds is
  the DISTRIBUTION, and a Poisson variable is zero with positive
  probability. The mean alone never says a count can vanish; 517 had the
  mean and could not have drawn this conclusion from it.

### 576.2 THE ANSWER (PROVED, ON THAT BASIS)

  COROLLARY. For every g there is a girth-legal closed ladder whose
  shortest power-of-two cycle has length at least g. SO L_min IS
  UNBOUNDED OVER CLOSED LADDERS AND THE INTRINSIC O(1) BOUND IS FALSE.

  Exhibited here, without appeal to anything: a girth-legal closed
  ladder on 140 vertices of girth 9. Girth 9 leaves no cycle of length
  8, so its L_min is 16, and it is 8 for every ladder in the exhaustive
  range. The growth is real and starts early.

  THE RATE IS LOGARITHMIC, NOT LINEAR. A cubic graph of girth g has at
  least about 2^{g/2} vertices, so g <= about 2 log_2 (2N) and therefore

      L_min  <=  about  4 log_2 (2N)

  would follow from the bound of 576.3. The family that defeats O(1)
  cannot defeat O(log 2N).

### 576.3 THE SHARP REPLACEMENT (MEASURED)

    P(g)   <=   L_min   <=   2 P(g) .

  The left inequality is 576.0, a theorem. The right one held on
  everything measured, and BOTH ENDS ARE ATTAINED:

    all 8434 girth-legal ladders at 2N = 12, 14, 16 have girth 5 or 6
      and L_min = 8 = P(g)  - the lower end;
    U(2N,s) has girth 6, so P = 8, and L_min = 8 for s = 9, 11, 13, 17
      but L_min = 16 for s = 25, 41 and 55, checked by direct search for
      an octagon in each - the UPPER end, attained;
    the girth-9 ladder at 2N = 140 has L_min = 16 = P(9) - lower end
      again, at a larger girth.

  SO THE CORRECTED FORM OF THE INTRINSIC BOUND IS L_min = THETA(GIRTH),
  and the conjecture that carries the weight is the upper half, L_min at
  most twice the least power of two above the girth. That upper half
  IMPLIES ERDOS-GYARFAS FOR CLOSED LADDERS: with g at most about
  2 log_2 (2N), it puts a power-of-two cycle at length O(log 2N), far
  below 2N. It is (LQ3) in quantitative form, and it is sharper than
  (LQ3) - it says not only that a power of two occurs but where.

### 576.4 STATUS

PROVED here: L_min >= g, hence L_min >= P(g), the least power of two at
least the girth; so a bound L_min = O(1) forces the girth of closed
ladders to be bounded.

ESTABLISHED from the literature, verified verbatim from the source
document rather than from memory: closed ladders of arbitrarily large
girth exist. A closed ladder is a Hamiltonian cubic graph; by Theorem
2.5 of Wormald's survey the short-cycle counts of a random cubic graph
are asymptotically independent Poisson with means 2^i/2i, so girth
exceeding g has probability tending to a positive constant, and by
Theorem 2.26 Hamiltonicity has probability tending to 1; the two
therefore hold together, as the survey's introduction states outright.

COROLLARY, hence PROVED: L_min IS UNBOUNDED and THE INTRINSIC O(1)
BOUND IS FALSE. The family is the high-girth closed ladders. Exhibited
directly: one on 140 vertices of girth 9, with no octagon, so L_min =
16 where every ladder to 2N = 16 has L_min = 8.

MEASURED: P(g) <= L_min <= 2 P(g) on all 8434 girth-legal ladders to
2N = 16, on the uniform family to U(120,55) - where the upper end is
attained, U(60,25), U(92,41) and U(120,55) having no octagon - and on
the high-girth ladders built here.

NOT PROVED: the upper half L_min <= 2 P(g), which is now the sharp form
of the conjecture for closed ladders; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open
ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*);
(E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements of
451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The dichotomy
falls on the second side. A power-of-two cycle is at least as long as
the girth, so an O(1) bound would force the girth of Hamiltonian cubic
graphs to be bounded, and it is not: the short-cycle counts of a random
cubic graph are asymptotically independent Poisson with means 2^i/2i, so
avoiding all cycles up to any fixed length has positive probability,
while Hamiltonicity has probability tending to one, and the two survive
together - a fact the survey states in as many words. So L_min is
unbounded and the intrinsic bound is false; a ladder on a hundred and
forty vertices with girth nine already has no octagon while every ladder
up to sixteen vertices has one. What replaces it is sharper than what it
refutes. Writing P for the least power of two above the girth, every
ladder measured satisfies P <= L_min <= 2P, both ends are attained, and
the upper half implies Erdos-Gyarfas for closed ladders with a power of
two at logarithmic length. The programme's own first-moment law supplied
the means of that Poisson at 517; what it lacked was the distribution,
and a mean can never tell you that a count is sometimes zero.


## 577. THE CASE g <= 8: THE OCTAGON SURVIVES TO 2N = 22, AND WHERE IT
## FAILS THERE ARE A THOUSAND HEXADECAGONS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 576 replaced the refuted
O(1) bound by P(g) <= L_min <= 2P(g) and left the upper half open. Its
first case, g <= 8, says every girth-legal closed ladder with a cycle of
length at most 8 has one of length exactly 8 or exactly 16. It is not
proved here. It is reduced to an explicit finite list of local
