  579's restatement of it should read: ABUNDANT IN ABSOLUTE TERMS - a
  hundred or ten thousand cycles, per 523.0's girth-7 graph on 36
  vertices with 12285 cycles of length 32 - BUT FAR BELOW (d-1)^k/2k.
  The conclusion those sections drew, that the large target cannot be
  dodged by a Poisson zero, is untouched, since it needs only that the
  count is large. What is corrected is the size claimed for it.

### 589.3 WHAT THIS CLOSES

The second attack line is now closed against both kinds of target. It
proves E-G for the cages, where the girth is large enough that the power
of two falls below 2g. It cannot reach band 3, by 452's own m < 2g. And
it cannot reach the large power of two, because there the trace is
dominated by non-simple walks in a ratio that grows with m.

  THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE SPECTRAL LINE. It works exactly where the
  target is below twice the girth and nowhere else, and no threshold
  argument changes that, because the failure is not one of size but of
  what the instrument counts.

### 589.4 STATUS

VERIFIED: tr(B^m) = 2 m c_m exactly for g <= m < 2g, on fifteen rows
across three ladders - confirming 452 and 555.2 and the arithmetic here.

COMPUTED: above 2g the simple-cycle share of the trace falls
geometrically, reaching 0.016, 0.009 and 0.002 at m = 2N for 2N = 14, 16
and 18. At 2N = 18 the trace is 261870, essentially 2^18, while twice m
times the cycle count is 504.

CONCLUDED: the trace frame cannot reach the large power of two. 518.0's
threshold 2^{m/2} > 2n holds with room to spare and is not the
obstruction; the obstruction is that the trace counts closed
non-backtracking walks, and at m of order 2N the non-simple ones
outnumber the cycles five hundred to one.

CORRECTED (374.1): the first-moment law E[c_k] = (d-1)^k/2k is asymptotic
for FIXED k and does not apply at k of order n. At 2N = 18 it predicts
7281 cycles of length 18 where there are 14. 554.1's and 579's
description of the large target as having exponential expectation is
wrong in its size; their conclusion, which needs only that the count is
large, stands.

NOT PROVED: (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN);
(LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank
>= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The trace frame
does exactly what it was proved to do and nothing more. Below twice the
girth the non-backtracking trace is two m times the number of m-cycles,
confirmed here to the digit on fifteen rows; above it the trace begins to
count walks that repeat vertices, and by the time m reaches the size of
the graph those walks outnumber the cycles by five hundred to one, so the
simple-cycle share is two thousandths and falling. The threshold that
worried 518 is satisfied with room to spare and is not what stops the
method; what stops it is that the instrument counts the wrong thing, and
by a margin that grows. The same computation corrects the reason the
attempt was made: the first-moment law is a statement about fixed
lengths, and at length equal to the size of the graph it overestimates by
a factor of five hundred - seven thousand predicted Hamilton cycles
against fourteen. The large power of two is still abundant enough not to
be dodged, which is all that 579 needed, but it is not abundant in the
way that was claimed.


## 590. THE CONTRACTION INDUCTION IS CAUGHT BETWEEN TWO CLASSES: THE
## STEP FAILS IN ONE, THE CONCLUSION FAILS IN THE OTHER

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The contraction is a clean
operation and the deficiency transforms exactly as hoped. The induction
still does not run, for a reason that is now precise and is the same
shape as 537's: girth-legality is not preserved by the operation, and
dropping it makes the statement false. Machine: scratch (exhaustive at
2N = 12, 14, 16).

### 590.0 THE OPERATION AND THE LIFTING (PROVED)

CONTRACTION. Delete a chord {u,v} and suppress its two endpoints, so that
u-1 becomes adjacent to u+1 and v-1 to v+1. The host cycle survives as a
cycle on 2N-2 vertices, and the remaining N-1 chords still form a perfect
matching of them, so THE RESULT IS AGAIN A CLOSED LADDER.

LIFTING. A cycle of length l in the contracted ladder lifts to a cycle of
the original of length

    l + (how many of the two suppressed host edges it uses) .

  Using an edge {u-1, u+1} means the lift passes through u.

### 590.1 THE DEFICIENCY TRANSFORMS AS PREDICTED (PROVED)

L is unchanged while 2N-2 >= L, so

    D_0  =  2N - L    becomes    D_0 - 2 ,

except at the crossing, where 2N = L and the contracted ladder's target
drops to L/2 with deficiency L/2 - 2. So the deficiency falls by two at
every contraction, and there are D_0/2 steps of room - which was the
attraction.

  AND THE LIFTING SAYS WHAT THE INVARIANT MUST BE. To reach length L in
  the original one needs, in the contracted ladder, either a cycle of
  length L avoiding BOTH suppressed edges, or one of length L-2 using
  BOTH. The second is the natural one, since at these lengths a cycle
  uses nearly every host edge; and it says the induction should carry the
  DEFICIENCY, not the length. That is consistent and encouraging.

### 590.2 BUT THE STEP FAILS (COMPUTED)

Girth-legality is not preserved. Counting, for every girth-legal ladder,
the chords whose contraction leaves a girth-legal ladder:

    2N = 12 :    24 ladders,   0 have any such chord
    2N = 14 :   408 ladders,  77 have none
    2N = 16 :  8002 ladders, 880 have none   - ELEVEN PER CENT

  The first line is not a defect: THERE IS NO GIRTH-LEGAL CLOSED LADDER
  ON 10 VERTICES AT ALL - enumeration gives 0 at 2N = 8 and 0 at 2N = 10,
  and 24 at 2N = 12 - so 2N = 12 is the base and cannot contract. The
  other two lines are the problem. For those ladders the induction has no
  step to take.

### 590.3 AND THE LARGER CLASS DOES NOT RESCUE IT (COMPUTED)

Drop girth-legality and ask only that no chord joins adjacent vertices.
Contraction is then almost always available - at 2N = 14 not one of the
44189 such ladders is stuck. BUT THE STATEMENT BECOMES FALSE:

    2N = 12 :  10 of  3326 have no cycle of length 8
    2N = 14 :  70 of 44189 have no cycle of length 8 .

  All ten at 2N = 12 have GIRTH 3 and all ten have a 4-cycle, so they
  satisfy Erdos-Gyarfas by the power of two below the target. They refute
  only the SHARPENED statement of 588 - a cycle of length exactly the
  largest power of two below 2N.

  SO GIRTH-LEGALITY IS ESSENTIAL TO 588's STATEMENT AND NOT DECORATIVE,
  and the induction is caught between a class where the step fails and a
  class where the conclusion fails.

### 590.4 WHY THIS IS 537 AGAIN

537 asked whether an induction was possible and on which parameters, and
found none. The reason is now explicit and it is not about the choice of
parameter: THE OPERATIONS THAT REDUCE A CLOSED LADDER DO NOT PRESERVE
GIRTH, and girth is what the statement needs. Any induction on closed
ladders must either carry a hypothesis strong enough to restore girth
after the reduction, or work in a class closed under the reduction - and
in the closed class the conclusion is false.

  That is a structural obstruction to induction on this object, and it is
  worth recording as one, since it applies to any reduction of this kind
  and not only to chord contraction.

### 590.5 STATUS

PROVED here: chord contraction - delete a chord, suppress its endpoints -
maps a closed ladder on 2N vertices to a closed ladder on 2N-2; a cycle
of the contracted ladder lifts to one longer by the number of suppressed
host edges it uses; and the deficiency D_0 = 2N - L falls by exactly 2
per contraction while 2N-2 >= L, so the natural induction invariant is
the deficiency and not the length.

COMPUTED: girth-legality is NOT preserved. Of the girth-legal ladders,
none at 2N = 12 admits a girth-legal contraction - correctly, since
enumeration shows there is no girth-legal closed ladder on 8 or 10
vertices - while 77 of 408 at 2N = 14 and 880 of 8002 at 2N = 16 admit
none either.

COMPUTED: in the girth-free class contraction is available - 0 of 44189
stuck at 2N = 14 - but the conclusion fails there: 10 of 3326 ladders at
2N = 12 and 70 of 44189 at 2N = 14 have no cycle of length 8. The ten are
all of girth 3 and all have a 4-cycle, so they satisfy the conjecture and
refute only 588's sharpening.

IDENTIFIED: girth-legality is essential to 588's statement, and the
obstruction to induction is structural - reductions of a closed ladder do
not preserve girth, and the class that is closed under them does not
satisfy the conclusion.

NOT PROVED: (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN);
(LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank
>= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The contraction is
everything one could ask of an operation: it takes a closed ladder to a
closed ladder two vertices smaller, the lifting of cycles is exact, and
the deficiency - which is the right invariant, since a long cycle uses
nearly every host edge and cannot avoid the suppressed ones - falls by
two at each step, giving as many steps of room as the deficiency has
halves. What it does not do is preserve girth. Eleven per cent of the
girth-legal ladders on sixteen vertices have no chord at all whose
contraction leaves girth five, so for those the induction simply has no
step; and enlarging the class until contraction always works destroys the
conclusion, since ten of the three thousand three hundred and twenty-six
closed ladders on twelve vertices have no eight-cycle - all of girth
three, all with a four-cycle, so they satisfy the conjecture and refute
only the sharpened target. The induction is caught between the two, which
is what 537 found without being able to say why. The reason is that the
reductions of this object do not preserve the hypothesis the statement
needs, and that is a structural fact about closed ladders rather than a
bad choice of parameter.


## 591. THE SHARPENED STATEMENT VERIFIED TO 2N = 28, AND WHAT THE SIZE
## OF THE SEARCH TREE SAYS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 588 verified to 2N = 24
that every girth-legal closed ladder has a cycle of length exactly the
largest power of two below its size. With the search rewritten it now
reaches 28, and the shape of the search is itself informative. Machine:
scratch (pruned enumeration, distance-bounded cycle detection).

### 591.0 THE ENUMERATION, REWRITTEN

Having a cycle of length exactly L is MONOTONE under adding chords, so
the ladders LACKING one can be enumerated by pruning: extend a partial
matching chord by chord, and abandon a branch the moment an L-cycle
appears. Two changes to 588's version:

  - the search for an L-cycle through the newly added chord is bounded by
    the BFS distance to its far endpoint, so a partial path is abandoned
    as soon as it cannot return in the edges remaining;
  - the first chord is fixed up to reflection.

  VALIDATED against 588: the same zeros at 2N = 12, 14, 18, 20, 22 and
  24, with 2N = 24 taking ten seconds where the first version took
  minutes.

### 591.1 THE RESULT

    2N        12    14    18    20     22      24      26       28
    L          8     8    16    16     16      16      16       16
    lacking    0     0     0     0      0       0       0        0
    nodes      6    31  1433  1155   3102   16118   95200   228819

  and 2N = 16 and 32 are trivial, since there L = 2N and the host cycle
  serves.

  SO EVERY GIRTH-LEGAL CLOSED LADDER ON AT MOST 28 VERTICES HAS A CYCLE
  WHOSE LENGTH IS EXACTLY THE LARGEST POWER OF TWO BELOW ITS SIZE.

### 591.2 WHAT IS BEING CERTIFIED, AND WHAT THE TREE SIZE MEANS

This is not a sample. The pruned search visits every girth-legal ladder
that could lack such a cycle, so a count of zero is a proof for that
size, over populations that are far too large to list - 168802
girth-legal ladders at 2N = 18 alone.

  AND THE TREE IS TINY AGAINST THOSE POPULATIONS. At 2N = 18 the search
  visits 1433 nodes against 168802 ladders; at 2N = 28 it visits 228819
  nodes against a population in the many millions. THE PRUNE FIRES ALMOST
  IMMEDIATELY: an L-cycle appears after a handful of chords, long before
  the matching is complete, so the overwhelming majority of partial
  ladders are already committed to having one.

  That is worth stating as a fact about the object rather than about the
  program. The largest power of two is not reached by a delicate
  construction that a ladder might avoid; it is forced early, by whatever
  few chords have been placed.

### 591.3 WHAT IT WOULD TAKE TO GO FURTHER

Node counts roughly quintuple per step - 16 thousand, 95 thousand, 229
thousand at 2N = 24, 26, 28. 2N = 30 closes the L = 16 band, since 2N =
32 is trivial. Beyond that a new band opens at 2N = 34 with L = 32, where
each node costs more because the cycle to detect is twice as long, and
the distance bound helps less.

  So the enumeration is near its natural limit, and the limit is the
  detection of a 32-cycle rather than the size of the tree.

### 591.4 STATUS

COMPUTED: no girth-legal closed ladder on 12, 14, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26 or
28 vertices lacks a cycle of length exactly the largest power of two
below its size - zero in every case, by exhaustive pruned enumeration,
not by sampling. 2N = 16 and 32 are trivial. This extends 588's range
from 24 to 28.

OBSERVED: the search tree is minute against the populations it certifies
- 1433 nodes against 168802 ladders at 2N = 18 - because the prune fires
after a handful of chords. The largest power of two is forced early
rather than achieved delicately.

NOT PROVED: the statement itself, at any size beyond the enumerated
range; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3),
equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2
cancellation; J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The sharpened
statement - a cycle of length exactly the largest power of two below the
size, not merely some power of two - now holds for every girth-legal
closed ladder on at most twenty-eight vertices, by an enumeration that
visits every ladder which could fail and finds none. The rewrite that
made this possible bounds the cycle search by distance and fixes the
first chord up to reflection, and it reproduces the earlier range in
seconds. What the enumeration shows beyond its own range is how the
statement fails to fail: the search tree is minute against the
populations it certifies, because a partial ladder acquires a cycle of
that length after a handful of chords and the branch dies there. The
target is forced early and by very little structure, which is the
opposite of how the small powers of two behaved at 579, where they could
be dodged entirely. The enumeration is near its limit - the next band
needs a thirty-two cycle detected at every node - so what it can settle
it has nearly settled.


## 592. "FORCED EARLY" IS FALSE - THE PRUNE FIRES LATE, AND THE MARGIN
## IS THREE OR FOUR CHORDS

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 591 read the small search
tree as saying the target is forced after a handful of chords, and
proposed a lemma on that basis. The reading was wrong and the lemma is
false: the tree is small in COUNT, not in DEPTH. What the measurement
does give is a sharp quantity - the margin by which the sharpened
statement holds. Machine: scratch (maximum-depth search).

### 592.0 THE CORRECTION (374.1)

591.2 said the prune fires "after a handful of chords, long before the
matching is complete". MEASURED, IT FIRES ALMOST AT THE END. The largest
number of chords in a girth-legal partial matching carrying NO cycle of
length L:

    2N      12   14   18   20   22   24   26
    N        6    7    9   10   11   12   13
    L        8    8   16   16   16   16   16
    max      3    4    6    6    7    8    9
    N - max  3    3    3    4    4    4    4

  A girth-legal partial matching can reach WITHIN THREE OR FOUR CHORDS OF
  COMPLETION while still having no cycle of length L. The branches of
  591's tree are nearly as deep as they can be; the tree is small because
  the branching factor collapses, not because the branches are short.

  Explicitly, at 2N = 22 with L = 16, the seven chords
  (0,4) (1,6) (2,20) (3,8) (5,19) (7,21) (9,17) are girth-legal and carry
  no 16-cycle, leaving eight vertices unmatched; only the last four chords
  force one.

### 592.1 SO THE PROPOSED LEMMA IS FALSE

No bounded number of chords in general position forces a cycle of length
L. The threshold is N - 3 or N - 4, LINEAR IN N. The route sketched at
the end of 591 - a bounded forcing number, hence the statement for all
large 2N - IS CLOSED.

  And the failure is not marginal. A bounded forcing number would have to
  be a constant; the measurement gives 3, 4, 6, 6, 7, 8, 9 across the
  range, tracking N.

### 592.2 WHAT THE MEASUREMENT DOES GIVE: THE MARGIN

Define the MARGIN of a size as N minus the largest number of chords a
girth-legal partial matching can carry without a cycle of length L. Then

    THE SHARPENED STATEMENT HOLDS AT THAT SIZE  <=>  THE MARGIN IS
    POSITIVE,

since a complete matching has N chords and must therefore pass the
threshold. Measured, the margin is

    3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4     at 2N = 12, 14, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26.

  THE STATEMENT IS TRUE BY THREE OR FOUR CHORDS, and the margin is
  growing - slowly, and by one step in the range measured, but growing
  rather than shrinking.

  THIS IS THE FIRST QUANTITY IN THIS STRETCH WHOSE BEHAVIOUR WOULD
  PREDICT A COUNTEREXAMPLE. A size at which the margin reaches zero is
  exactly a girth-legal closed ladder with no cycle of length L. Every
  other instrument in the last twenty sections could only fail to exclude
  one; this one would announce it, and it can be computed one size at a
  time.

### 592.3 STATUS

CORRECTED here (374.1): 591.2's reading of its own search tree. The
prune does not fire after a handful of chords. The maximum girth-legal
partial matching with no cycle of length L has 3, 4, 6, 6, 7, 8 and 9
chords at 2N = 12, 14, 18, 20, 22, 24 and 26 - that is N-3 or N-4, within
a few chords of a complete matching. The tree is small because the
branching collapses, not because the branches are short.

REFUTED: the lemma proposed at the end of 591, that a bounded number of
chords in general position forces a cycle of length L. The forcing number
is linear in N.

IDENTIFIED: the MARGIN - N minus that maximum - is positive exactly when
the sharpened statement holds at that size, and it measures 3, 3, 3, 4,
4, 4, 4 over the range. The statement is true by three or four chords and
the margin is not shrinking.

EXHIBITED: at 2N = 22 the seven chords (0,4), (1,6), (2,20), (3,8),
(5,19), (7,21), (9,17) are girth-legal with no 16-cycle, so only the last
four chords of any completion force one.

NOT PROVED: that the margin stays positive; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime
open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER
BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five
statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The previous
section misread its own computation. A search tree that is small in the
number of nodes is not a search tree that is shallow, and this one is
nearly as deep as it can be: a girth-legal partial matching can carry
nine chords out of thirteen on twenty-six vertices without ever
containing a sixteen-cycle, and the same margin of three or four chords
holds across the whole range measured. So no bounded number of chords
forces the target, the lemma proposed last section is false, and the
route it opened is closed. What replaces it is better posed than what it
replaces. The margin - how many chords short of a complete matching one
can stop and still avoid the target - is positive exactly when the
sharpened statement holds, it is three or four everywhere measured, and
it is drifting upward rather than down. It is also the only quantity this
programme has produced that would announce a counterexample rather than
merely fail to rule one out, and it can be computed one size at a time.


## 593. THE L = 16 BAND IS COMPLETE, A WRONG SHORTCUT AT THE BAND
## BOUNDARY, AND THE BOUNDARY TESTED EXACTLY

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The enumeration at 2N = 30
returned zero, which closes the whole band in which the target is 16, so
the sharpened statement now holds for every girth-legal closed ladder on
at most 32 vertices. Attempting to reach the next band cheaply produced a
false characterisation, recorded here; done exactly, the boundary is
clean. Machine: scratch (pruned enumeration, exact detection on 1768
ladders).

### 593.0 THE BAND IS COMPLETE (COMPUTED)

2N = 30, L = 16: zero ladders lacking the cycle, 474674 search nodes,
1282 seconds. With 591's table that gives

    2N = 12, 14        L =  8    zero lacking
    2N = 16                      trivial, L = 2N
    2N = 18 ... 30     L = 16    zero lacking, every even size
    2N = 32                      trivial, L = 2N

  EVERY GIRTH-LEGAL CLOSED LADDER ON AT MOST 32 VERTICES HAS A CYCLE OF
  LENGTH EXACTLY THE LARGEST POWER OF TWO BELOW ITS SIZE. The L = 16 band
  is closed with no exceptions anywhere in it.

### 593.1 A FALSE SHORTCUT (CORRECTED, 374.1)

To reach the next band cheaply I characterised a cycle of length 2N-2 as
follows: it omits two vertices, each omitted vertex removes its two host
edges, so exactly four host edges are unused and hence exactly two chords
are used, which must join the four boundary vertices - giving the test
"two chords {a,b} and {a+2, b+2}, or {a,b} and {a+2, b-2}".

  THE STEP "EXACTLY FOUR HOST EDGES ARE UNUSED" IS FALSE. More host edges
  may be unused, with more chords compensating; the chord count k is not
  forced to 2. Checked against brute force on 160 girth-legal ladders at
  2N = 14 to 20: 31 DISAGREEMENTS. The sampled figures the test produced
  are discarded.

  THE CORRECT STATEMENT comes from 581's formula: deficiency 2 means that
  over the k pairing intervals, either one has length 3 and the rest
  length 1, or two have length 2 and the rest length 1. The k = 2 case is
  the shortcut; there are others.

### 593.2 THE BOUNDARY, TESTED EXACTLY (COMPUTED)

2N = 34 is where the target doubles to 32 while N moves by one, so the
deficiency drops to 2 and the statement is at its most fragile - the
cycle must omit only two of the thirty-four vertices.

  Exact detection, distance-pruned, on girth-legal ladders sampled across
  the whole L = 32 band:

      1768 ladders, 2N = 34 to 62,  WITHOUT a 32-cycle:  ZERO.

  And the detection is fast - forty ladders a second at 2N = 34 - because
  a cycle omitting two vertices is easy to find when it exists. THE BAND
  BOUNDARY DOES NOT SQUEEZE THE STATEMENT on any ladder sampled.

### 593.3 WHAT REMAINS

The exhaustive pruned enumeration at 2N = 34 with L = 32 is the natural
next certificate and did not finish in the time given. It would extend
the verified range from 32 to 34, across a band boundary, which is worth
more than the same effort spent inside a band.

  And the margin of 592 has not been computed in the new band. Inside the
  L = 16 band it drifted upward, 3 to 4; the question that band boundary
  poses is whether it drops back when the target doubles.

### 593.4 STATUS

COMPUTED: 2N = 30 with L = 16 has zero ladders lacking the cycle, closing
the band. EVERY GIRTH-LEGAL CLOSED LADDER ON AT MOST 32 VERTICES HAS A
CYCLE OF LENGTH EXACTLY THE LARGEST POWER OF TWO BELOW ITS SIZE.

CORRECTED (374.1): the characterisation of a (2N-2)-cycle as requiring
two chords {a,b} and {a+2, b+2} or {a,b} and {a+2, b-2} is FALSE - it
assumed only four host edges can be unused, whereas more may be, with
more chords. 31 disagreements in 160 ladders. The sampled figures it gave
are withdrawn.

COMPUTED, exactly: over 1768 girth-legal ladders sampled across the L =
32 band from 2N = 34 to 62, not one lacks a 32-cycle.

NOT PROVED: the statement beyond the enumerated range; (LQ3-3); (OPEN)
for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4);
(LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the
five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The band in which
the target is sixteen is now closed: every even size from eighteen to
thirty returns zero ladders lacking a sixteen-cycle, and sixteen and
thirty-two are trivial, so the sharpened statement holds for every
girth-legal closed ladder on at most thirty-two vertices without

## 594. THE MARGIN RECOMPUTED: 592'S SEARCH COULD NOT SEE HALF THE
## CONFIGURATIONS, AND THE MARGIN IS NOT A DISTANCE TO A COUNTEREXAMPLE

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The task was to carry 592's
margin into the band where the target is 32. The margin turned out to be
wrong where it had already been measured, and then to be the wrong
quantity. Both are recorded here, with the repaired definition, what it
measures, and the first values in the new band. Machine: scratch
(exhaustive search, brute force, two independent cycle oracles, iterated
local search).

### 594.0 WHAT 592 ACTUALLY SEARCHED (CORRECTED, 374.1)

592 computed its maximum with a recursion that, at every node, took the
LEAST UNMATCHED VERTEX and matched it. That recursion cannot reach a
partial matching which leaves a low vertex unmatched and carries a chord
above it: to place such a chord it would first have had to match the
vertex below.

  Precisely, the configurations it enumerates are exactly those in which
  every chord's lower endpoint precedes every unmatched vertex - so with
  k chords and least unmatched vertex u, necessarily k <= u. THE REST
  WERE NEVER VISITED, and the maximum it reported is a lower bound on the
  true maximum, hence the margin it reported is an UPPER bound on the
  true margin.

  The corrected search decides each vertex in turn - MATCH it or SKIP it
  - and normalises by rotation: a partial matching that is neither empty
  nor perfect can be rotated so that vertex 0 is matched and vertex 2N-1
  is skipped, since somewhere on the circle a matched vertex follows an
  unmatched one. Skipping is what 592 could not do. What makes the
  corrected search finish is that with f vertices still undecided no
  branch can exceed depth + f/2 chords, so near the top of the range only
  a handful of skips are affordable.

### 594.1 THE MARGIN, EXACTLY

    2N        10   12   14   18   20   22   24
    L          8    8    8   16   16   16   16
    N          5    6    7    9   10   11   12
    max        2    3    4    7    6    7    9
    MARGIN     3    3    3    2    4    4    3

    592 said max                6         8      at 18 and 24
    592 said margin             3         4

  TWO OF 592'S SEVEN ENTRIES ARE WRONG. At 2N = 18 a girth-legal partial
  matching can carry seven chords with no 16-cycle, not six; at 2N = 24
  it can carry nine, not eight. 12, 14, 20 and 22 are confirmed
  unchanged.

  Checked three ways. Brute force over ALL partial matchings on the
  circle - no ordering assumption of any kind - gives 2, 3, 4 at 2N = 10,
  12, 14, agreeing. The same search driven by a completely different
  cycle oracle, the GF(2) cycle-space sweep in place of the path search,
  returns the same maxima at 12 and 14 AND the same node counts, 118 and
  1055, so the two oracles agree at every node of the tree. And each
  witness was re-verified from stored data by the (S,eps) dual detector
  of 581, which shares no code with either search; on the seven-chord
  witness at 2N = 18 it reports the full spectrum 5,6,...,15,17,18 -
  every length from the girth to the circle EXCEPT 16.

  SO THE UPWARD DRIFT REPORTED AT 592 DOES NOT EXIST. The corrected
  sequence 3, 3, 3, 2, 4, 4, 3 is not monotone.

  591'S AND 593'S ENUMERATIONS ARE UNAFFECTED. They build complete
  matchings, where matching the least unmatched vertex forbids nothing,
  so every girth-legal closed ladder is still reached and their zeros
  stand.

### 594.2 THE EXTREMAL OBJECT AT 2N = 18 IS RIGID

Counting rather than maximising: in the normalised frame there are
EXACTLY FOUR girth-legal partial matchings with seven chords and no
16-cycle, and NONE with eight. All four contain the same six chords,

    (1,6) (4,9) (7,12) (10,15) (13,0) (16,3),

that is (i, i+5) for i = 1 mod 3 - THE SPARSE UNIFORM LADDER: one span,
placed on every third position. The seventh chord is any of (2,8),
(2,14), (5,11), (8,14), all four inside the residue class 2 mod 3 that
the sparse ladder leaves free.

  So at the size where the margin is smallest, the avoiding
  configurations are one structured object plus one free chord.

### 594.3 THE MARGIN IS NOT A DISTANCE TO A COUNTEREXAMPLE

At 2N = 30 the margin is EXACTLY 1: iterated local search finds
girth-legal partial matchings with fourteen of the fifteen chords and no
16-cycle, and fifteen is impossible because 593 enumerated that size
exhaustively and found no closed ladder lacking one. On 592's reading
that is the statement one chord from failing.

  IT IS NOT. Two independent such configurations were found,

    (0,5)(1,10)(2,7)(3,28)(4,9)(6,27)(8,29)(12,26)(13,21)(14,18)
    (15,23)(16,20)(17,22)(19,24)                unmatched 11, 25
    (0,25)(1,6)(2,27)(3,24)(4,29)(5,26)(7,21)(8,16)(9,13)(10,18)
    (11,15)(12,17)(14,19)(23,28)                unmatched 20, 22

  and in BOTH the single missing chord is blocked by GIRTH, not by the
  target: 11 and 25 are three apart through the chord (12,26), and 20 and
  22 are two apart on the host. Neither configuration extends to a
  girth-legal closed ladder at all.

  THE MARGIN CONFLATES TWO OBSTRUCTIONS. A configuration can be deep
  because every legal addition creates the target, or merely because its
  leftover vertices are too close together to be joined. Only the first
  says anything about Erdos-Gyarfas, and at 2N = 30 the value 1 is
  entirely of the second kind.

  The maxima at 2N = 14, 18, 20, 22, 24 and the deepest configurations
  found at 28 and 34 were audited the same way and are of the first kind:
  each extends to a girth-legal closed ladder. At 18 all four legal
  additions create a 16-cycle.

### 594.4 THE REPAIRED QUANTITY

  DEFINITION. The COMPLETABLE MARGIN of a size is N minus the largest
  number of chords in a girth-legal partial matching that has no cycle of
  length L AND extends to a girth-legal closed ladder.

  Zero exactly when some girth-legal closed ladder has no L-cycle, so
  zero is still exactly a counterexample to the sharpened statement; and
  since the completable configurations are a subset, it is never below
  the margin of 592.

  EQUIVALENTLY, since the completable avoiding configurations are exactly
  the sub-matchings of girth-legal closed ladders and deleting chords
  only destroys cycles,

    completable margin = min over girth-legal closed ladders C of the
    minimum number of chords of C whose deletion destroys every L-cycle
    of C

  - a minimum hitting set, computable exactly per ladder: enumerate every
  L-cycle by the (S,eps) dual, then branch and bound on the hitting set.

  Measured:

    2N                    12   14   18   20   22   24   28   34
    completable margin     3    3    2    4    4    3   <=3  <=4

  At 12 and 14 by enumerating every girth-legal closed ladder (13 and 228
  up to the reflection cut) and taking the minimum hitting set; from 18
  on because the exact maximum of 594.1 is itself completable, which pins
  the value between the margin below and that witness above.

  ONE CAUTION, worth stating because it nearly produced a wrong entry: at
  2N = 12 the maximum the search returns, (0,6)(3,7)(4,10), is a girth
  dead end - and yet the completable margin is still 3, because a
  DIFFERENT maximum of the same size is completable. A non-completable
  maximum does not by itself raise the completable margin.

  AT 2N = 30 IT IS NOT DETERMINED. Both margin-1 configurations are
  girth dead ends, so the completable margin there is at least 2; over 60
  random girth-legal ladders, each carrying between 444 and 926
  16-cycles, no single chord lies on all of that ladder's 16-cycles,
  which is what a completable fourteen-chord configuration would need.
  Sampling, not proof.

### 594.5 THE FIRST VALUES IN THE L = 32 BAND

    2N = 34, L = 32:  thirteen of the seventeen chords, MARGIN <= 4

    (0,24)(1,28)(2,19)(3,7)(4,17)(6,16)(8,13)(11,15)(14,33)
    (21,31)(22,27)(23,29)(25,30)      unmatched 5,9,10,12,18,20,26,32

  girth 5, no 32-cycle by the dual detector, and COMPLETABLE - so the
  completable margin at 34 is at most 4 as well.

  THE MARGIN DOES NOT COLLAPSE WHEN THE TARGET DOUBLES. At the first size
  of the new band it is at most 4, against 2 at the corresponding size of
  the old one; the question 592 posed - drop or drift - is answered
  "neither" in the only sense the corrected quantity supports.

  The random-ladder route to the completable margin is too weak to
  extend the table: over 400 ladders it returns 5 at 2N = 24, where the
  true value is 3, and 6, 6, 7 at 26, 28, 30. Those are recorded as
  bounds only.

### 594.6 STATUS

CORRECTED (374.1): 592's maximum-depth search matched the least
unmatched vertex at every node, so it visited only the partial matchings
in which every chord's lower endpoint precedes every unmatched vertex.
Its maxima are lower bounds and its margins upper bounds. Two of its
seven entries are wrong: at 2N = 18 the true maximum is seven chords, not
six, and at 2N = 24 it is nine, not eight. 591 and 593 are unaffected,
since they enumerate complete matchings.

REFUTED: the upward drift of 592. The exact margins are 3, 3, 3, 2, 4, 4,
3 at 2N = 10, 12, 14, 18, 20, 22, 24, which is not monotone.

COMPUTED: at 2N = 30 the margin is exactly 1, by two witnesses against
593's exhaustive zero.

REFUTED: 592's reading of the margin as a distance to a counterexample.
Both witnesses at 2N = 30 are saturated by GIRTH - the one missing chord
would close a four-cycle - and neither extends to a girth-legal closed
ladder, so the value 1 there records nothing about the target.

IDENTIFIED: the COMPLETABLE MARGIN, the same maximum restricted to
configurations that extend to a girth-legal closed ladder, equivalently
the minimum number of chords whose deletion from some closed ladder
destroys every L-cycle. It is zero exactly at a counterexample, it
dominates the margin, and it is 3, 3, 2, 4, 4, 3 at 2N = 12, 14, 18, 20,
22, 24.

COMPUTED: in the L = 32 band, a girth-legal partial matching on 34
vertices with thirteen of its seventeen chords, no 32-cycle, and a
girth-legal completion - so both margins at 34 are at most 4, and the
margin does not collapse when the target doubles.

EXHIBITED: at 2N = 18 there are exactly four maximum configurations and
all four contain the sparse uniform ladder (i, i+5) for i = 1 mod 3.

NOT PROVED: that either margin stays positive; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime
open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER
BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five
statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The instruction was
to carry the previous section's margin into the band where the target is
thirty-two. It could not be carried as it stood, because it was wrong
where it had already been taken and because it was not measuring what it
was said to measure. The search that produced it always matched the
lowest unmatched vertex, which silently forbids every configuration that
leaves a low vertex free and reaches over it with a chord; run without
that restriction, two of the seven published values change, and the
sequence reported as drifting upward is not monotone at all. Worse, the
quantity itself does not do the job it was given. On thirty vertices a
girth-legal partial matching can carry fourteen of its fifteen chords
without a sixteen-cycle, which on the old reading is the statement one
chord from failing; but the one absent chord is absent because it would
close a four-cycle, and the configuration cannot be completed to a closed
ladder at all, so the near miss is a fact about girth and not about
powers of two. What survives is the definition with completability
imposed, which is zero exactly at a counterexample, equals a minimum
hitting set of the target cycles, and is three, three, two, four, four,
three across the sizes where it has been pinned. Carried into the new
band it gives four at thirty-four, on a configuration that is girth-legal
and completable and misses the thirty-two cycle - so the target doubling
neither drops the margin nor lifts it, and the quantity that would
announce a counterexample is still positive everywhere it has been
measured.


## 595. THE DEFICIENCY-2 TELESCOPE: THE TARGET DESCENDS TWO VERTICES AT
## A TIME, AND GIRTH SURVIVES THE DESCENT

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. A new route, assembled from
three facts the archive already held and never combined: a cycle of
length exactly L omits exactly 2N - L vertices; the ladder presentation
is a free choice (575); and girth is monotone under taking subgraphs -
which is precisely what 590's contraction induction lacked. The route
survives every test this section could throw at it, including the
adversarial ones. Machine: scratch (telescope DFS, exhaustive
enumeration, two cycle oracles).

### 595.0 THE TELESCOPE

To find a cycle of length L in a girth-legal closed ladder on 2N
vertices, do not aim at L. Find a cycle omitting just TWO vertices,
re-present the graph with that cycle as the new host, and repeat. Each
step shrinks the size by two; after (2N - L)/2 steps the size IS L, and
the host circle itself is the target.

  The power of two enters nowhere except as the size at which the
  descent stops. Every step is the same power-free statement: a cycle
  through all but two vertices. The 2-adic coordinate of 516, which
  every direct attack had to carry, collapses into the stopping rule.

### 595.1 THE STEP IS AN INDUCED SUBGRAPH (PROVED)

Let G be a closed ladder on vertex set V, C' a cycle omitting exactly
u and v, and H the re-presentation: host C', chords = the surviving
third edges.

  LEMMA. H = G[V - {u,v}], the induced subgraph. Proof: G is cubic, so
  each vertex of C' has two edges on C' and one third edge; H contains
  C' plus every third edge with both ends on C'; and the induced
  subgraph contains exactly the C'-edges plus those same third edges,
  since a vertex has no other edges to offer. QED.

  Three consequences, each doing real work:

  - GIRTH IS INHERITED. A subgraph only loses cycles, so girth-legal
    stays girth-legal all the way down. Contraction (590) failed
    exactly here; deletion cannot.
  - CYCLES OF H = CYCLES OF G AVOIDING u AND v. So anything the
    telescope finds is a cycle of G, and the final host is a cycle of
    G of length exactly L.
  - THE TELESCOPE IS A CHAIN OF INDUCED HAMILTONIAN SUBGRAPHS,
    V = V_0 > V_1 > ... , |V_(i+1)| = |V_i| - 2, each G[V_i]
    Hamiltonian (the next host). "G has an L-cycle" is trivially
    "some induced subgraph on L vertices is Hamiltonian"; the telescope
    refines this to steps of size two, each locally characterised.

### 595.2 GIRTH FORCES EVERY STEP TO USE AT LEAST TWO CHORDS (PROVED)

A deficiency-2 element using one chord has pairing interval of length
3: the chord plus a host arc of three edges, a 4-cycle. Girth >= 5
forbids it.

  So under girth every (2M-2)-cycle uses at least two chords, and the
  two-chord witnesses are exactly 593.1's local patterns: sorted
  endpoint intervals (2,2) - two chords parallel at host-distance two -
  or (3,1). Verified: over every girth-legal closed ladder at 2N = 14,
  the minimum number of chords on a (2N-2)-cycle is exactly 2.

  AND EVERY DEFICIENCY-2 CYCLE HAS ONE NORMAL FORM, the CHAIN: take the
  host circle, delete k disjoint arcs (the SITES), add k chords, one
  chord bridging each consecutive pair of sites. The site lengths are
  all 1 except one site of length 3 (its two interior vertices are the
  omitted pair) or two sites of length 2 (each omits its one interior
  vertex). Machine-checked: all 7520 + 240247 deficiency-2 cycles over
  every girth-legal ladder at 2N = 14 and 16, and 3427 more over forty
  ladders at 18 - ZERO violations of the form.

  This makes (T1) a statement about the CHORD-ADJACENCY MULTIGRAPH A:
  vertices = the N chords, one edge (ch(v), ch(v+1)) for every host
  edge, so 2N edges, 4-regular and connected (the host walk visits
  every chord). (T1) asks for a closed alternating chain in A - enter
  each used chord at one endpoint, leave at the other - with exactly
  one defect site of length 3, or two of length 2. Existence is a
  statement about A; girth never appears, which is why 595.5's
  girth-free census comes out clean.

### 595.3 THE LEDGER

Chords are spent twice per step: the chords the new host C' uses become
host edges of the next level (converted, not lost), and the chords
incident to the omitted u, v dangle away. By 595.2 the conversion costs
at least 2; on a full ladder u and v are matched, so the first step
costs at least 4; deeper, when the omitted pair is already unmatched,
a step costs as little as 2.

  Measured trajectory at 2N = 30 (chords per level, one run):
  15 -> 11..12 -> 8..10 -> 5..8 -> 3..6 -> 1..5 -> 2..5, reaching 16.
  And the branching (number of deficiency-2 cycles per level) collapses
  in step: roughly 970 at the full ladder, 30-110, 5-25, 0-5, 0-4,
  0-3, 0-2. THE TREE IS WIDE EXACTLY WHERE THE STEPS ARE EXPENSIVE AND
  THIN WHERE THEY ARE CHEAP; single branches die at the bottom (a
  partial with two or three chords often has no deficiency-2 cycle),
  and the descent survives by backtracking one level.

  The width at the top grows geometrically with the size. Deficiency-2
  cycles per FULL girth-legal ladder (12 random ladders per size):

    2N        16    20    24    28    32
    median    54   131   302   651  1431

  - a factor of about 1.5 per two vertices. This is the resource the
  second pillar spends: each extra band size adds steps to the descent
  but multiplies the branches available to survive them.

  And the minimum is never near zero: over EVERY girth-legal ladder
  (exhaustive), the count of deficiency-2 cycles ranges 25-56 at
  2N = 14 and 42-144 at 16. The starved ladders exist only far down
  the descent, never at the full matching.

### 595.4 THE TELESCOPE REACHES THE BOTTOM ON EVERYTHING TESTED

  - Single step at 2N = 20: every sampled ladder has 114-156
    deficiency-2 cycles, and 96-100 percent of them land on an induced
    subgraph that still contains a 16-cycle.
  - Full descent, random girth-legal ladders: 10/10 at 2N = 24, 8/8 at
    26, and 6/6 at 30 - the top-of-band deficit, 2N - L = 14, seven
    steps - with DFS trees of 15 to 208 nodes.
  - The uniform family, the archive's standing hard case: U(2N,5)
    reaches the bottom for every even 2N from 20 to 30. It is
    measurably the hard case: U(30,5) needs 308 nodes where random
    ladders at 30 need 15-208, and its descent dies repeatedly at
    levels 22-24 before finding the path.
  - ADVERSARIAL HUNT: with unlimited backtracking and randomised
    branch order, over 300 ladders at 2N = 22, 150 at 24 and 100 at
    26: ZERO ladders on which the telescope fails. Every girth-legal
    ladder tested admits a full chain of induced Hamiltonian subgraphs
    down to the power of two.

### 595.5 THE POWER-FREE PILLAR, CERTIFIED EXHAUSTIVELY

The first pillar is (T1): EVERY GIRTH-LEGAL CLOSED LADDER HAS A CYCLE
THROUGH ALL BUT TWO VERTICES. This is new territory: the enumerations
of 588-593 only ever tested the length 2N - 2 at the two sizes where it
coincided with the power of two (18 and 34). As a statement about every
size it contains no power of two at all. By pruned exhaustive
enumeration (the (2N-2)-cycle is monotone under adding chords; at 24
the oracle is a hybrid - budgeted path search, then the bounded dual
scan restricted to eps = 1, whose misses only cost work, with every
surviving leaf re-verified by the full oracle):

    2N        12   14   16   18   20   22     24
    lacking    0    0    0    0    0    0      0
    nodes     11   55  272 1433 8012 48818  317813

  ZERO girth-legal closed ladders lack a (2N-2)-cycle at any size up
  to 24; the run at 26 is in progress. The node counts at 18-22 are
  identical between the path oracle and the hybrid, a whole-tree
  agreement of the two detectors.

  AND (T1) NEEDS NO GIRTH AT ALL. Over every closed ladder of every
  girth - all 293 + 3326 + 44189 perfect matchings with span >= 2 at
  2N = 10, 12, 14 - zero lack a (2N-2)-cycle. So the first pillar is
  plausibly a theorem about ALL Hamiltonian cubic graphs: every one on
  2N >= 10 vertices has a cycle through all but two vertices. The
  classical neighbour is Smith's theorem (every edge of a cubic graph
  lies on an even number of Hamiltonian cycles, so a Hamiltonian cubic
  graph has at least three Hamiltonian cycles); whether the (2N-2)
  statement is in the literature has NOT been checked verbatim (388.1)
  and nothing here leans on it.

  A self-check worth recording: the Mobius-Kantor graph GP(8,3) -
  Hamiltonian, girth 6, hence a girth-legal closed ladder at 2N = 16 -
  was suspected of a spectrum gap at 14 and would have broken the
  table. Computed directly: spectrum {6: 24, 8: 30, 10: 96, 12: 100,
  14: 144, 16: 6}. The 14-cycles exist and the table stands.

### 595.6 WHERE GIRTH ENTERS, PRECISELY (COMPUTED)

Run the telescope on the ten girth-FREE 12-vertex ladders that lack an
8-cycle (exactly 590's census: 10 of 3326). It must fail, and where it
fails is the information: ALL TEN have deficiency-2 cycles - eight or
twenty-four 10-cycles each - and in all ten every branch dies at
retention. The failure is never in existence, always in landing.

  So the pillars separate cleanly: (T1) existence does not need girth
  (595.5 confirms it exhaustively on the girth-free class); girth is
  the hypothesis of the second pillar only.

### 595.7 THE SECOND PILLAR, STATED HONESTLY

(T2): the descent tree has a surviving branch. This is NOT a per-step
statement - thin partials genuinely die (trails show levels with two or
three chords and zero deficiency-2 cycles) - and any proof must be a
potential argument about the tree, not a lemma about one step: the
width at the top must be shown to outlast the deaths at the bottom.

  This is where the whole content of the conjecture now sits. The
  telescope repackages (LQ3) sharpened as: THE DESCENT FROM 2N TO L
  CANNOT BE STARVED AT EVERY BRANCH SIMULTANEOUSLY. What is gained by
  the repackaging: every quantity in it is local (deficiency-2 cycles
  are 593.1's interval chains), girth is carried for free, and the
  power of two appears only as the floor.

### 595.8 STATUS

PROVED: the re-presented object after omitting two vertices is the
induced subgraph G[V - {u,v}]; hence girth is inherited at every level
and the telescope's output is a genuine L-cycle of G. Under girth >= 5
every deficiency-2 cycle uses at least two chords.

COMPUTED: the telescope reaches the power of two on every ladder
tested: 10/10 at 2N = 24, 8/8 at 26, 6/6 at 30, U(2N,5) for all even
2N in [20, 30]; adversarial exhaustive-DFS hunts find 0 failures in
550 ladders at 2N = 22, 24, 26.

COMPUTED, exhaustively: (T1) - no girth-legal closed ladder on up to
24 vertices lacks a cycle through all but two vertices; and no closed
ladder of ANY girth on up to 14 vertices lacks one (47808 ladders), so
the pillar needs no girth hypothesis at all.

COMPUTED: on the ten girth-free 12-ladders with no 8-cycle, the
telescope fails always at retention, never at existence - girth is the
hypothesis of the branch-survival pillar only.

IDENTIFIED: the two pillars. (T1) existence, power-free and local;
(T2) branch survival, a potential argument about the descent tree.

NOT PROVED: (T1) beyond 2N = 24; (T2) anywhere; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for
prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4);
(LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the
five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The observation
is that a cycle of the target length omits a known number of vertices,
so the target can be approached by omitting two vertices at a time: a
cycle through all but two vertices becomes the host of a smaller
ladder, and the descent stops exactly at the power of two, where the
host is the answer. The step is an induced subgraph, so girth - the
hypothesis the statement needs, and the one every previous reduction
destroyed - is carried downward for free. The descent reaches the
bottom on every ladder it has been tried on, including the uniform
family at its hardest size and six ladders at the maximal deficit,
and an adversarial hunt over five hundred and fifty ladders found not
one on which it fails. What remains is two lemmas. The first, that
every closed ladder has a cycle through all but two vertices, contains
no power of two - and, on all the evidence, no girth: it holds
exhaustively to twenty-four vertices in the girth-legal class and to
fourteen with no girth restriction at all. The second, that the
descent tree cannot be starved at every branch at once, is where the
conjecture now lives; it is a statement about the width of a tree
whose nodes are local configurations, and the failure of the
girth-free counterexamples shows it is exactly girth that must feed
it.


## 596. (T1) AND (T2): THE LITERATURE FRONTIER, THE GENERATORS
## CLASSIFIED, A SUPPLY LEMMA CORRECTED AND PROVED, AND WHERE BOTH STAND

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The goal was the two
pillars of 595. Neither is proved in full; this section records what
was settled: (T1) is absent from the literature and past its frontier;
its two-chord generators are classified exactly; avoidance of them is
impossible at 14 and rare at 16; the existence threshold does not grow,
so (T2) cannot be a counting argument; and a supply lemma for (T2) was
stated wrongly, corrected, proved, and found to explain which ladders
are hard. Machine: scratch; literature verified from fetched PDF and
abstract per 388.1.

### 596.0 (T1) IS NOT IN THE LITERATURE, AND SITS PAST ITS FRONTIER

Fetched and read (PDF text layer; glyphs lost by extraction restored
in brackets): Matija Bucic, Lior Gishboliner and Benny Sudakov,
"Cycles of many lengths in Hamiltonian graphs", Forum of Mathematics
Sigma 10 (2022) e70, doi 10.1017/fms.2022.42, abstract:

  "In 1999, Jacobson and Lehel conjectured that, for [k >=] 3, every
  k-regular Hamiltonian graph has cycles of [Theta(n)] many different
  lengths. This was further strengthened by Verstraete, who asked
  whether the regularity can be replaced with the weaker condition
  that the minimum degree is at least 3. Despite attention from
  various researchers, until now, the best partial result towards
  both of these conjectures was a [sqrt(n)] lower bound on the number
  of cycle lengths. We resolve these conjectures asymptotically by
  showing that the number of cycle lengths is at least
  n^[1-o(1)]."

And a note of June 2026 (arXiv 2607.01738, read in the served HTML
rendering): for a simple graph on n vertices with minimum degree at
least 3 containing a Hamiltonian cycle, there is another cycle of
length at least n - c n^(2/3), improving the earlier bound
n - O(n^(4/5)) of Girao, Kittipassorn and Narayanan.

  SO THE FRONTIER IS: many lengths, without naming one (Bucic et al.),
  and a second cycle near the top, without an exact length (the 2026
  note). (T1) - a cycle of length EXACTLY 2N - 2 in every Hamiltonian
  cubic graph - is in neither, and for cubic graphs specifically
  nothing stronger was found. If true it is a new theorem; the
  exhaustive evidence below and 595's make it the programme's most
  exportable open statement.

### 596.1 THE TWO-CHORD GENERATORS, CLASSIFIED EXACTLY (COMPUTED)

A machine sweep over ALL two-chord configurations on a 22-circle -
both spans girth-legal, both chords required on the cycle, the
single-chord case (span 3 or M-3, which alone gives an (M-2)-cycle
and is girth-forbidden) excluded - gives:

  A (M-2)-CYCLE USING EXACTLY TWO CHORDS EXISTS IFF THE SECOND CHORD
  IS A TRANSLATE OF THE FIRST BY (2,2), (3,1) OR (1,3) - the same
  sign in both coordinates. In matching language: some x has
  mu(x + d) = mu(x) + d' with (d, d') in {(2,2), (3,1), (1,3)}, read
  in either orientation around the circle. In every case d + d' = 4.

  THE SIGN CONDITION IS THE CONTENT: a translate by (2,-2) does NOT
  generate - in the chain form its crossed pairing falls into two
  components. This sign is what breaks the naive supply lemma below.

### 596.2 AVOIDANCE: IMPOSSIBLE AT 14, RARE AND STARVED-PROOF AT 16

    2N = 14:   0 of  228 girth-legal ladders avoid all three patterns
    2N = 16:  12 of 4410 avoid them

  So at 2N = 14, (T1) holds THROUGH THE k = 2 PATTERNS ALONE: no
  girth-legal matching can dodge every generator. At 16 the twelve
  avoiders have span multisets {4,4,5,5,5,5,6,6} and
  {4,4,4,4,5,5,5,5} - near-uniform, span-poor - and each still
  carries 54 to 60 deficiency-2 cycles through chains with k >= 3.

  And avoidance CANNOT scale, on the first-moment dichotomy of 579:
  a target with O(1) expected count can be dodged outright (the
  octagon was); the (2N-2)-count GROWS with N (times 1.5 per two
  vertices, 595.3), so it sits on the same non-dodgeable side as the
  large power of two itself.

### 596.3 CERTIFICATES EXTENDED (COMPUTED)

Girth-free, over ALL closed ladders of any girth (pruned enumeration,
hybrid oracle, survivors re-verified):

    2N        10    12    14    16    18    20
    lacking    0     0     0     0     0     0

  EVERY HAMILTONIAN CUBIC GRAPH ON AT MOST 20 VERTICES HAS A CYCLE
  THROUGH ALL BUT TWO VERTICES (nodes 1738, 8930, 48416 at 16, 18,
  20). Girth-legal remains zero through 24 (595.5), with the 26 run
  still in progress.

### 596.4 THE EXISTENCE THRESHOLD DOES NOT GROW - (T2) IS NOT A COUNT

Define margin2(M) = M/2 minus the largest number of chords in a
girth-legal partial matching on M vertices with no (M-2)-cycle
(the exact search of 594, aimed at the deficiency-2 target):

    M          12   14   16   18   20
    margin2     2    3    3    2    3

  NOT growing - it oscillates between 2 and 3 across the whole range.
  (At M = 18 the extremal witness is exactly 594's
  seven-chord object - at a band edge M - 2 IS the power of two, so
  the two extremal problems coincide by definition.)

  CONSEQUENCE: no chord-count ledger can prove (T2). A telescope step
  costs at least two chords, and a partial can lack the deficiency-2
  cycle while only two chords short of perfect, so counting chords
  cannot certify survival past two steps. Branch survival is about
  WHICH configurations remain, not how many chords.

### 596.5 THE SUPPLY LEMMA: WRONG ONCE, THEN PROVED (374.1)

Stated first: "a generator footprint-disjoint from the one being
stepped on survives the step". MEASURED: 14 of 25 - FALSE.

  THE STEP IS A 2-OPT. The new host traverses one of the two regions
  between the sites REVERSED, so a generator with one side in each
  region has its offset flipped to (2,-2), which by 596.1 is not a
  generator. The naive lemma ignored orientation.

  CORRECTED LEMMA (PROVED). Let A be a (2,2)-generator, with
  footprint its six site vertices plus the mates of its two omitted
  vertices. If a generator B is footprint-disjoint from A and all
  four endpoints of B lie in ONE region (one arc of the circle
  between A's two sites), then after stepping on A, B is a generator
  of the induced partial. Proof: within one region the new host
  preserves adjacency, and preserves orientation up to wholesale
  reversal, which maps a (2,2)-translate to a (-2,-2)-translate -
  the same pattern read from the other end; and B's chords are not
  among the four the step consumes. Measured: 21 of 21.

  COROLLARY (LAMINAR SUPPLY). A laminar family of t generators -
  each nested inside a single region of the previous - sustains t
  telescope steps, so the sharpened statement holds at that ladder
  for every target L >= 2N - 2t.

  AND IT EXPLAINS THE HARD CASE. Nesting needs a generator whose
  whole span fits inside one region of another; a single-span ladder
  cannot do this (a span-s chord cannot fit in an arc shorter than
  s), so U(2N, s) receives NOTHING from supply - precisely the
  family where 595's telescope search worked hardest (308 nodes at
  U(30,5) against 15-208 for random ladders). SPAN DIVERSITY IS THE
  FUEL OF SUPPLY; the uniform ladder is span-poor by construction,
  which is its whole economy of blocking (578) seen from the new
  side.

### 596.6 WHAT (T2) NOW NEEDS

(T2) restated: from every girth-legal closed ladder, the tree of
deficiency-2 descents has a branch reaching the power of two. What
this section adds: at deficit 2 it IS (T1); laminar supply proves
depth t where t nested generators exist; the count route is closed
by 596.4; and the residual hard class is span-poor - near-uniform
ladders where chains of k >= 3, not generator pairs, must carry the
descent. The 12 avoiders of 596.2 are the smallest members of that
class, and every one of them still holds 54-60 deficiency-2 cycles.

  So both pillars now point at the same object: the k >= 3 chains of
  span-poor matchings. (T1) needs them to exist (they do, richly, in
  every case measured); (T2) needs them to survive a step. The
  next lever is the k >= 3 analogue of 596.1: classify the
  three-chord generators and their step-survival, in the span-poor
  class where pairs are absent.

### 596.7 STATUS

COMPUTED, exact classification: the two-chord (M-2)-generators are
the translates by (2,2), (3,1), (1,3), same sign both coordinates
(sweep of all two-chord configurations at M = 22).

COMPUTED: 0 of 228 girth-legal ladders at 14 avoid the generators;
12 of 4410 at 16, all span-poor, each with 54-60 deficiency-2 cycles.

COMPUTED, exhaustively: (T1) girth-free to 2N = 20 - every
Hamiltonian cubic graph on <= 20 vertices has a (2N-2)-cycle.

COMPUTED: margin2 = 2, 3, 3, 2, 3 at M = 12..20; the existence
threshold does not grow; no counting ledger can prove (T2).

CORRECTED (374.1): the naive supply lemma (14/25). The step is a
2-opt; orientation matters.

PROVED: the region-coherent supply lemma, and the laminar-supply
corollary: t nested generators give t telescope steps.

VERIFIED verbatim (388.1): Bucic-Gishboliner-Sudakov 2022 (cycle
lengths at least n^(1-o(1)), resolving Jacobson-Lehel and Verstraete
asymptotically); the June 2026 note (another cycle of length at
least n - c n^(2/3), improving Girao-Kittipassorn-Narayanan). (T1)
is in neither: the exact length 2N - 2 is past the frontier.

NOT PROVED: (T1) beyond the enumerated ranges; (T2) beyond laminar
supply; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN);
(LQ3), equivalently (K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the
rank >= 2 cancellation; J7; the five statements of 451.2; the
conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The two
pillars of the telescope were the goal, and neither fell, but both
changed shape. The first pillar is now known to be absent from the
literature - the best published results give many cycle lengths
without naming one, or a second cycle within n to the two-thirds of
the top without landing on an exact length - so a proof of it would
be a theorem worth having outside this programme. Its local
mechanism is now exact: two chords make a cycle through all but two
vertices precisely when one is a translate of the other by (2,2),
(3,1) or (1,3) with matching signs, no girth-legal matching on
fourteen vertices can avoid all three patterns, and the twelve
avoiders on sixteen vertices are all span-poor and all rescued by
longer chains. The second pillar lost its cheapest route - the
existence threshold measures two to three chords and does not grow,
so no counting of chords survives the descent - but gained its
first theorem: a generator that avoids the footprint of the step
and keeps to one side of it survives, because the step is a two-opt
and reverses one region wholesale; nested families of generators
therefore sustain the telescope for as many steps as they are deep.
What that theorem cannot cover is exactly the span-poor class where
generators are scarce, which is the same class where the first
pillar leans on longer chains; the two pillars have converged on
one object, and the next section of this programme should classify
the three-chord chains and their survival where the pairs are
absent.


## 597. THE THREE-CHORD GENERATORS CLASSIFIED, A SIGN BUG IN 596
## CORRECTED, AND THE CHAIN DEPTH MEASURED

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The k = 3 layer of the
telescope's local machinery, as 596.6 prescribed. On the way there a
measurement contradicted 596.2, and the contradiction traced to a sign
error in the avoider test; the correction turns two mismatched counts
into an exact equivalence. Then the section's own sharpest question
answered itself: the chain depth GROWS - eleven ladders on eighteen
vertices need four-chord chains - so no finite catalogue proves (T1).
Machine: scratch.

### 597.0 CORRECTION TO 596.2 (374.1)

596.2 counted "avoiders" with a test that accepted the translate
relation in BOTH signs - mate(x+d) = mate(x) + d' AND
mate(x+d) = mate(x) - d'. By 596.1's own classification the
mixed-sign translates are NOT generators. The counts are wrong, and
so is an inference:

  - At 2N = 14 the avoider count is 15 of 228, not 0 of 228. The
    sentence "at 2N = 14, (T1) holds through the k = 2 patterns
    alone" is WITHDRAWN: fifteen girth-legal ladders on 14 vertices
    have no two-chord generator at all, and are rescued by
    three-chord chains. Witness, with its only relation instances
    being mixed-sign: (0,4) (1,6) (2,8) (3,10) (5,11) (7,12) (9,13).
  - At 2N = 16 the count is 216 of 4410, not 12 of 4410, and the
    span-multiset remark about "the twelve avoiders" described the
    both-sign avoiders; it is superseded.

  What exposed it: the chain-depth measurement of 597.3 found ladders
  at 14 whose every deficiency-2 cycle uses three chords, which the
  "zero avoiders" claim forbids.

### 597.1 RELATION AND GENERATOR ARE EQUIVALENT UNDER GIRTH (PROVED)

  LEMMA. In a girth-legal closed ladder, a same-sign translate
  relation always yields a valid two-chord (2N-2)-cycle - the sites
  cannot be degenerate. Proof: for the (2,2) pattern the sites are
  {v..v+2} and {w..w+2}; if they met, the cyclic distance from v to w
  would be at most 2, making the chord (v, w) a span-<= 2 chord,
  which girth >= 5 forbids. The (3,1) pattern is identical with sites
  of lengths 3 and 1. QED

  So under girth: SAME-SIGN RELATION <=> k = 2 GENERATOR. And the
  corrected counts confirm it exactly: the same-sign avoiders number
  15 at 2N = 14 and 216 at 16, and the ladders whose minimum chain
  size is 3 number 15 and 216 - THE SAME SETS, measured two
  independent ways (relation scan; exhaustive cycle decomposition).

### 597.2 THE THREE-CHORD GENERATORS, CLASSIFIED (COMPUTED)

By the chain normal form (595.2) a k = 3 deficiency-2 element is:
three disjoint sites with gap profile a placement of (3,1,1) or
(2,2,1), six boundaries, and a perfect matching of the boundaries by
three chords, no chord inside a site - eight inter-site pairings per
profile. Sweeping ALL placements and positions at M = 30:

  EXACTLY FOUR OF THE EIGHT PAIRINGS ARE VALID - the same four for
  every one of the six profile placements - and validity NEVER
  depends on where the sites sit (zero mixed verdicts). Labelling
  each site's boundaries (left, right) in host order as site 1 =
  {0,1}, site 2 = {2,3}, site 3 = {4,5}:

      (0,2) (1,4) (3,5)
      (0,3) (1,4) (2,5)
      (0,3) (1,5) (2,4)
      (0,4) (1,3) (2,5)

  So there are 6 x 4 = 24 valid three-chord generator types, all
  position-free, and the k <= 3 generator catalogue is FINITE AND
  EXPLICIT. The set of four is closed under reflection (boundary i
  maps to 5 - i): the first two are self-mirror, the last two swap -
  which is what the survival lemma below needs.

### 597.3 THE CHAIN DEPTH GROWS - NO FINITE CATALOGUE PROVES (T1)

Define the CHAIN DEPTH of a size as the maximum over girth-legal
ladders of the minimum number of chords on any of its deficiency-2
cycles - the k that (T1) genuinely needs at that size. Computed by
enumerating the same-sign avoiders directly (pruning the moment a
relation appears, which is monotone) and decomposing only those:

    2N              12    14     16     18
    ladders         13   228   4410  168802
    avoiders         0    15    216    4877
    of which k=3     -    15    216    4866
    of which k=4     -     0      0      11
    CHAIN DEPTH      2     3      3      4

  ELEVEN LADDERS ON 18 VERTICES NEED FOUR CHORDS: every one of their
  deficiency-2 cycles uses at least four. Witness, checked by the
  independent cycle-space oracle - girth 5, 78 sixteen-cycles, chord
  counts over all of them {4,5,6,7,8}:

      (0,4) (1,8) (2,13) (3,9) (5,16) (6,12) (7,14) (10,17) (11,15)

  So the question this section was built to pose is ANSWERED: THE
  DEPTH IS NOT BOUNDED AT 3, and on this evidence not bounded at
  all - it has the shape of 587's law that the chord count tracks
  the target, not the mechanism. No finite catalogue of local
  patterns proves (T1); any proof must produce chains whose length
  grows with the ladder.

  And at 2N = 18 the deficiency-2 target IS the power of two, so
  these eleven ladders are extremal for the conjecture's own target:
  girth-legal ladders where every 16-cycle needs at least four
  chords.

### 597.4 THE SUPPLY LEMMA GENERALISES TO THE WHOLE CATALOGUE (PROVED)

  LEMMA. Let A be any generator being stepped on, and B any valid
  generator type instance - two- or three-chord - that is
  footprint-disjoint from A's consumed set (sites, used chords, and
  the mates of A's omitted vertices) and has ALL its vertices in one
  region between A's sites. Then B is a valid generator of the
  induced partial after the step.

  Proof: within one region the new host preserves adjacency, and
  preserves orientation up to wholesale reversal; B's chords are not
  consumed; so B's sites and pairing reappear intact, or mirrored,
  in the new presentation. By 597.2 validity is position-free, and
  the valid pairing sets at k = 2 and k = 3 are closed under
  reflection, so the mirrored instance is again a valid type. QED

  Verified: 21/21 for a k = 2 generator under a k = 2 step (596.5)
  and 20/20 for a k = 3 generator under a k = 2 step. The laminar
  corollary of 596.5 now runs on the full catalogue: t nested
  generators of ANY types sustain t telescope steps.

### 597.5 STATUS

CORRECTED (374.1): 596.2's avoider counts (a both-signs test; the
mixed-sign translates are not generators). 15 of 228 at 14, 216 of
4410 at 16; the "through k = 2 alone" inference at 14 is withdrawn.

PROVED: under girth >= 5 the same-sign relation and the two-chord
generator are equivalent - sites cannot degenerate - and the
corrected avoider sets coincide exactly with the min-k = 3 sets,
measured independently.

COMPUTED, exact and position-free: the three-chord generator
catalogue - six profile placements times the same four of eight
boundary pairings, closed under reflection. The k <= 3 catalogue is
finite and explicit.

COMPUTED: chain depth 2, 3, 3, 4 at 2N = 12, 14, 16, 18 - GROWING.
Eleven ladders on 18 vertices need four-chord chains (witness
verified by the independent oracle: 78 sixteen-cycles, all on 4 to
8 chords). No finite pattern catalogue proves (T1).

PROVED: the generalised supply lemma - any catalogued generator,
footprint-disjoint and region-coherent, survives any generator step;
laminar families of mixed types sustain the telescope for their
depth.

REFUTED: bounded chain depth (hence the finite-catalogue route to
(T1)).

NOT PROVED: (T1) beyond the enumerated ranges; (T2) beyond laminar
supply; (LQ3-3); (OPEN) for
prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently (K4);
(LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation; J7;
the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The three-chord
layer is now as explicit as the two-chord layer: three sites, a gap
profile, and always the same four of eight ways to wire the
boundaries, wherever the sites sit. On the way to that catalogue a
measurement refused to match the previous section - ladders existed
whose every deficiency-2 cycle needs three chords, where the
previous section had said none could - and the mismatch traced to a
test that accepted translate relations of the wrong sign, which the
classification itself rules out. Corrected, the two measurements
agree to the ladder: the same-sign relation is equivalent to the
two-chord generator under girth, because girth keeps the sites from
touching. The chain depth - the number of chords the first pillar
genuinely needs - is two at twelve vertices and three at fourteen
and sixteen, and whether it stays bounded is now the sharpest form
of the first pillar: bounded depth makes (T1) a finite combinatorial
statement about a catalogue this section has written down; unbounded
depth makes it another instance of the programme's oldest lesson,
that the chord count tracks the target and not the mechanism. The
supply lemma survives the enlargement: any catalogued generator that
stays out of a step's footprint and keeps to one side of it comes
through intact or mirrored, and the catalogue is mirror-closed, so
laminar families of mixed types drive the telescope as deep as they
are nested. And the sharpest question the section posed answered
itself before it was recorded: the depth is two, three, three, FOUR
- eleven ladders on eighteen vertices force four-chord chains, at
the very size where the deficiency-2 target is the power of two
itself - so no finite catalogue closes the first pillar, and
whatever proves it must build chains that lengthen with the ladder,
the way the walk in the chord-adjacency multigraph does.


## 598. THE DEPTH-4 LADDERS DISSECTED: TWO ORBITS, A PROVABLE INFINITE
## AVOIDER FAMILY ON THE THIRDS LATTICE, AND THE DEPTH AT TWENTY

STATUS: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. 597 left the eleven
depth-4 ladders as the object to dissect and the chain depth's growth
as the open question. The dissection collapses the eleven to two
symmetry orbits, one of which extends to an infinite family whose
starvation of the two-chord generators is a three-line residue proof;
and the depth at twenty is exactly four - growth to four, no growth
past it. Machine: scratch.

### 598.0 TWO ORBITS

Under the dihedral group of the host circle the eleven depth-4
ladders at 2N = 18 are TWO orbits:

  - ORBIT A, size 9, stabilizer 2: spans {4,4,6,6,7,7,7,7,7}, no
    visible algebraic structure.
  - ORBIT T, size 2, stabilizer 12: spans {4,4,4,4,4,4,9,9,9} and
    delta-sequence (mate(x) - x mod 2N) EXACTLY PERIODIC with period
    three: 4, 14, 9, 4, 14, 9, ...

  Orbit T is an algebraic object: six span-4 chords on the thirds
  lattice plus three diameters. The thirds lattice appears AGAIN -
  594.2's margin-extremal configuration at the same size was the
  sparse uniform ladder (i, i+5) on i = 1 mod 3. Both extremal
  problems at 18 are solved by residue systems mod 3.

### 598.1 THE T-FAMILY

For every 2N = 0 mod 6 define

    T(2N) = { (3j, 3j+4) : j } union { (3j+2, 3j+2+N) : j },

six-to-2N/3 span-4 chords joining class 0 to class 1, and N/3
diameters pairing class 2 with itself. Measured at 2N = 18, 24, 30,
36, 42, 48: girth 5 at every size; NO two-chord generator; NO
three-chord generator; four-chord chains PRESENT at every size. So

    min-k( T(2N) ) = 4   at all six sizes measured:

  AN INFINITE FAMILY OF SAME-SIGN AVOIDERS, of chain depth four
  everywhere it has been measured.

### 598.2 THE k = 2 STARVATION IS A RESIDUE ARGUMENT (PROVED)

delta is constant on residue classes mod 3: delta = 4 on class 0,
2N - 4 on class 1, N on class 2. The three generator relations of
596.1 each demand a coincidence:

  (2,2): delta(x+2) = delta(x). x and x+2 lie in different classes,
  so this needs two of {4, 2N-4, N} equal: each equality forces
  2N <= 10.
  (3,1): delta(x+3) = delta(x) - 2. Same class, so 0 = -2: never.
  (1,3): delta(x+1) = delta(x) + 2. Consecutive classes, so one of
  2N-4 = 6, N = 2N-2, 4 = N+2: each forces 2N <= 10.

  So for every 2N >= 12, 2N = 0 mod 6, THE T-FAMILY HAS NO TWO-CHORD
  GENERATOR. QED. (The three-chord starvation is measured at the six
  sizes, not proved; the girth likewise.)

### 598.3 THE PLATEAU, AND WHAT RESCUES T

T certifies chain depth >= 4 for infinitely many sizes - but does
not certify growth: its own minimum stays at four. The rescue at
k = 4 is structurally forced: a typical four-chord element of T(24),

    chords (1,21) (6,10) (8,20) (11,23),  spans {4,4,12,12},
    sites (6,2) (10,1) (20,1) (23,2),

uses two span-4 chords and two diameters - an EVEN number of
crossings between the residue classes, which is exactly what the
delta bookkeeping permits at k = 4 and forbids at k <= 3.

  Against the POWER target the family is soft: at 2N = 30 its
  diameters have span 15 = L - 1, so a single chord plus its host
  arc is a 16-cycle - ten of them for free. The family starves the
  deficiency-2 machinery, not the conjecture.

### 598.4 THE DEPTH AT TWENTY IS FOUR

By the avoider-first method (prune the instant a same-sign relation
appears; then scan masks by popcount, so the k = 3 test costs
C(10,3) masks per ladder):

    2N                    12    14     16     18      20
    same-sign avoiders     0    15    216   4877  154340
    of which min-k = 3     -    15    216   4866  154102
    of which min-k = 4     -     0      0     11     238
    of which min-k >= 5    -     0      0      0       0
    CHAIN DEPTH            2     3      3      4       4

  And the avoider-first method is independently confirmed at 18: the
  full sweep over the reflection-reduced census - 91651 ladders, every
  one decomposed - returns min-k counts {2: 86774, 3: 4866, 4: 11},
  the same 4866 + 11 split and the same deepest ladder.

  ZERO DEPTH-5 LADDERS ON TWENTY VERTICES. The sequence 2, 3, 3, 4,
  4 tempers 597.3's reading: the growth to four is real and the
  finite-catalogue route stays dead, but growth PAST four has not
  been observed - the depth at 22 (or the T-family's own depth at
  some larger size, if it ever leaves 4) is where "bounded or not"
  will be decided. Note the proportion collapses: 11 of 4877
  avoiders at 18, 238 of 154340 at 20 - the deep ladders are
  vanishing within their own class.

### 598.5 STATUS

COMPUTED: the eleven depth-4 ladders at 18 are two dihedral orbits,
sizes 9 and 2, the latter with stabilizer 12 and period-3
delta-sequence (4, 14, 9).

IDENTIFIED: the T-family T(2N) for 2N = 0 mod 6 - span-4 chords on
the thirds lattice plus diameters. Girth 5 and min-k exactly 4
measured at 2N = 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48.

PROVED: T(2N) has no two-chord generator for any 2N >= 12 - delta
is constant mod 3 and each generator relation forces 2N <= 10.

COMPUTED: chain depth at 2N = 20 is exactly 4 (154340 avoiders: 238
at depth 4, none deeper). The depth sequence is 2, 3, 3, 4, 4.

OBSERVED: the k = 4 rescue of T uses two span-4 chords and two
diameters - an even number of residue-class crossings, the exact
degree of freedom the mod-3 bookkeeping denies to k <= 3; and
against the power target T(30) is trivial (diameter span = L - 1).

NOT PROVED: T's three-chord starvation and girth beyond the measured
sizes; that the chain depth is bounded (or that it is not); (T1)
beyond the enumerated ranges; (T2) beyond laminar supply; (LQ3-3);
(OPEN) for prime open ladders; (COVER-2); (RUN); (LQ3), equivalently
(K4); (LADDER BOUND*); (E_3) at girth 5; the rank >= 2 cancellation;
J7; the five statements of 451.2; the conjecture.

STATUS RESTATED: Erdos-Gyarfas UNPROVED, J7 UNPROVED. The eleven
ladders that force four-chord chains turn out to be two objects, and
the smaller orbit is the better teacher: a period-three matching -
span-four chords on the thirds lattice and diameters on the class
they leave free - whose starvation of the two-chord generators is
three lines of residue arithmetic, valid at every size divisible by
six. It extends to an infinite family measured at depth exactly four
out to forty-eight vertices, rescued at four by chains that cross
the residue classes an even number of times, which is precisely the
move the arithmetic denies to shorter chains. The thirds lattice has
now produced the extremal object for the margin, for the existence
threshold, and for the chain depth; whatever proves the first pillar
must in particular defeat residue systems, and the walk it needs
must be allowed to cross classes as often as the system demands. At
twenty vertices the depth is exactly four - a hundred and fifty
thousand avoiders, two hundred and thirty-eight of them deep, none
deeper - so the growth stands at two, three, three, four, four, and
whether it ever leaves four is now the sharpest open measurement in
the programme.
